What?! You refuse to help your brother knight? And you call yourself a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous? It's no wonder the Realm is in such a bad state and God turned his face away from us when people like you do not fulfill their mission. Yes, go your way if you wish so. But know that God sees your actions and will judge you accordingly!
I found your companion, brother. But I could not help him. Trolls killed him.

What did you say? You're telling me Scott is dead? My God... no, it's not possible... we were friends for so long! We fought so many battles together... He must not leave me now. Nevertheless, you said you could not help him. I curse those monsters of hell! I curse them all! I won't stop fighting them until I fall dead or until the last of those hellspawns leaves this world for good! I will redeem Scott's death with their slaughtered bodies, so I swear! Here, brother—accept this gift. You deserve it for your courage. But now please leave me with my sorrow... and with my revenge!
I sympathize with you, brother. I'm sorry. Farewell.
If you're a friend, help me! My companion, Scott de Ormand, was overcome and dragged away by trolls. My wounds forbid me to set forth tracking those monsters and save Scott...
Are you a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?
Yes, it is so. Knight Rieven d'Ardrieaux at you service, brother.
Well, it seems more likely I'm here at your service, brother, judging by your appearance.
Yes, you're right, brother...
What happened?

We were returning from a campaign against orcs when we were deceitfully ambushed by a band of those infernal trolls. We killed several of them, but there were too many of them. We had to retreat, or we would have died there. But they chased us, caught my companion and dragged him away. I managed to escape, but I'm unable to fight, and I cannot help Scott myself. So I'm trying to get someone to help me. My I ask you, brother? Will you help me to rescue my companion?
Alright, I'll help you.

I thank you sincerely, brother. I'm happy there is still someone who obeys God's laws in this wicked world full of sin and evil. Find Scott and save him from the clutches of those man-eating monsters. Save him before it is too late!
Yes, I will help you. That is to say if there is something in it for me...

You want gold or some other reward for your help? Can't you see there's a human life at stake? If it is so, I do not care for your help. And remember that God sees you and judges your actions! Farewell!
I'm sorry, but I can't help you, brother.
You said trolls? I surely do not want to mess with them. You will have to find someone else to help you.
Oh, how I'm pleased to see you, brother! Have you found my companion, Scott de Ormand?
Not yet, brother.
In that case hurry, brother, before it's too late! I beseech you, find him while there is still some hope!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even God's knights rob innocent people! Go away, you disgusting thief!

And you call yourself a man of God, Father? It should be you who steps in the place of others when they are no longer able to carry their burden. It's no wonder the realm is in such a bad state and God turned his face away from us when people like you do not fulfill their mission. Yes, go on your way if you so wish. But know that God sees your actions and will judge you accordingly!
I found your companion, knight. But I could not help him. Trolls killed him.

What did you say? You're telling me Scott is dead? My God... no, it's not possible... we were friends for so long! We fought so many battles together... He must not leave me now. Nevertheless, you said you could not help him. I curse those monsters of hell! I curse them all! I won't stop fighting them until I fall dead or until the last of those hellspawns leaves this world for good! I will redeem Scott's death with their slaughtered bodies, so I swear! Here, Father—accept this gift. You deserve it for your courage. But now please leave me with my sorrow... and with my revenge!
I sympathize with you, knight. I'm sorry. Farewell.
Yes, it is so. Knight Rieven d'Ardrieaux at you service, Father.
Well, it seems more likely I'm here at your service, knight, judging by your appearance.
Yes, you're right, Father...

We were returning from a campaign against orcs when we were deceitfully ambushed by a band of those infernal trolls. We killed several of them, but there were too many of them. We had to retreat, or we would have died there. But they chased us, caught my companion and dragged him away. I managed to escape, but I'm unable to fight, and I cannot help Scott myself. So I'm trying to get someone to help me. My I ask you, Father? Will you help me to rescue my companion?

I thank you sincerely, Father. I'm happy there is still someone who obeys God's laws in this wicked world full of sin and evil. Find Scott and save him from the clutches of those man-eating monsters. Save him before it is too late!
I'm sorry, but I can't help you, knight.
Oh, how I'm pleased to see you, Father! Have you found my companion, Scott de Ormand?
Not yet, knight.
In that case hurry, Father, before it's too late! I beseech you, find him while there is still some hope!
Inquisitor of the Holy Office steals?! I can't believe it! It's no wonder this world is in so bad state when even priests are thieves! Get lost, you disgusting creep!

And you call yourself a noble, sir? Shouldn't you lead others by acting as an example in the protection of the Realm? It's no wonder the Realm is in such a bad state and God turned his face away from us when people like you do not fulfill their mission. Yes, go your way if you wish so. But know that God sees your actions and will judge you accordingly!

What did you say? You're telling me Scott is dead? My God... no, it's not possible... we were friends for so long! We fought so many battles together... He must not leave me now. Nevertheless, you said you could not help him. I curse those monsters of hell! I curse them all! I won't stop fighting them until I fall dead or until the last of those hellspawns leaves this world for good! I will redeem Scott's death with their slaughtered bodies, so I swear! Here sir, accept this gift. You deserve it for your courage. But now please leave me with my sorrow... and with my revenge!
Yes, it is so. Knight Rieven d'Ardrieaux at you service, sir.
Yes, you're right, sir...

We were returning from a campaign against orcs when we were deceitfully ambushed by a band of those infernal trolls. We killed several of them, but there were too many of them. We had to retreat, or we would have died there. But they chased us, caught my companion and dragged him away. I managed to escape, but I'm unable to fight, and I cannot help Scott myself. So I'm trying to get someone to help me. My I ask you, sir? Will you help me to rescue my companion?

I thank you sincerely, sir. I'm happy there is still someone who obeys God's laws in this wicked world full of sin and evil. Find Scott and save him from the clutches of those man-eating monsters. Save him before it is too late!
Oh, how I'm pleased to see you, sir! Have you found my companion, Scott de Ormand?
In that case hurry, sir, before it's too late! I beseech you, find him while there is still some hope!
A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! Go away you disgusting thief!

Halt, intruder! Argh the Gate Guard commands you to immediately tell him your name. Who are you who dare to trespass on Emperor Rashgar's lands? Argh does not know your smell and thinks you should not be here!
Do not force me to complain to Emperor Rashgar on you not allowing me to pass. Step out of my way immediately!

You won't fool Argh. Although Argh doesn't know who you are and how have you managed to get to the Gate, you surely do not bear the mark of the Beast. So you have no right to command Argh. No, you surely haven't. And so Argh will kill ya and stick yer head on the pole! Aaaaarrrggghhhh!
No way, orc. You and your miserable breed have no business here and now you are going to pay for it!

Argh laughs at you, you poor human. You're a fool if you think you can beat down Argh. You are the same as others of your race—good only as meat. And that's why Argh is going to kill ya! Aaaaarrrggghhhh!
I don't want to fight you, Argh. I'll pay you well if you let me pass!
Keep your gold, worm. Argh will kill ya! Aaaaarrrggghhhh!
I laugh at your empty threats, mortal. You will die and all your progeny with you! Your souls will be thrown into the eternal fire and will burn until eternity is ancient and time itself stops!
Not so fast, demon. I've come to thwart your plans.

You, stop me? Your words make me laugh, you human shit. Do you know who I am? I'm Fallen Angel Arthamon, the Cursed flame. I wield powers of destruction so powerful that you would go mad had I shown you all of them in one moment. Now get out of my way!
I won't step aside till you are back in hell!
I bow before your savage greatness, oh mighty Arthamon!
You may bow, human worm, but it won't help you. I'm going to destroy you, and then I will burst into the world and do with it the same as I'm going to do with you now!
I banish thee, demon, return back into the burning hell!

Banishing won't help you, mortal. Nobody will banish me out of this world. I will crush you like a worm and all of your progeny with you. Your souls will be thrown into the eternal fire and will burn until eternity is ancient and time itself stops!
Mercy, Arthamon!
I'm deaf to your pleas, mortal. You will die and all of your progeny with you. Your souls will be thrown into the eternal fire and will burn until eternity is ancient and time itself stops!

Welcome to my kingdom, mortal. You've arrived at the right moment. Soon I will move with all my court to the world's surface to unleash unimaginable destruction there. All will fall to complete ruin and doom. Towns will be reduced to dust, flaming spires will scar the earth and sky will go ablaze with terrible fire. The world will become a part of Hell!
Oh my God... Fallen Angel Arthamon! So it's really true. Fallen Angel has entered our world!

Yes, it's true. Gates have been opened and I again walk the earthly kingdom of God. And there will be the time of great ruin, a time of destruction and death. Nations will fall under steel-clad hooves of my armies, people will scream with terror and bow before me.
Oh my God... Fallen Angel Arthamon!
Yes, mortal. I have entered this world to make it part of the domain of Hell. Borders between Hell and the World will be erased forever!
What do you think of the charge of heresy raised against you, Master?

Charges brought against me are nothing more than blatant lies. I'm a humble servant of God and not some damned heretic. When those green skins attacked the town I had not even been in Hillbrandt. I was lured out of the town and tricked to be bound by dark magic to make it possible to plot this shocking conspiracy against me!
I found Bishop Quentinus, Master. He is being held in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains.

You have found Bishop Quentinus! In that case you have to free him as soon as possible, brother. His testimony is presently the only evidence we have against Baroness Linda van Gallagan! Act promptly, brother!
I managed to free Bishop Quentinus, Master. He was being held in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. I suppose he is already back in Hillbrandt by now.
In that case go and talk with him as soon as possible. You will assure yourself of my innocence. Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic and has to be proven guilty together with her accomplices!
I found and freed Bishop Quentinus, Master. And based on his testimony it seems Baroness Linda van Gallagan really committed the crime you told me about.
See? I told you so. Now, when you have the testimony of Bishop Quentinus, you may start gathering more evidence against Baroness van Gallagan. You have to prove her guilty. You just have to!

Baroness Linda van Gallagan pleaded her sins before dying, Master. She confessed she committed all those crimes in order to prepare a Sabbath of witches. And during that Sabbath Fallen Angel Arthamon was supposedly summoned. Furthermore she said that judge Vallarian masterminded all that villainy! What do you think about it?

You have taken me aback, brother! I've never doubted Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic. But I can not believe judge Vallarian would be behind all that. I've heard enough about Vallarian to know he is a willful man persisting on his first opinion—be it whatsoever—but it seems quite odd to me to think he is a heretic.

Furthermore, I'm shocked by the mention of Fallen Angel Arthamon. It has to be some mistake, because it's unthinkable to summon Fallen Angel Arthamon. Fallen Angels can not be summoned into this world, because it would disprove all what the Holy Scriptures teach us. But no matter what's the truth, in my opinion it proves the heretics that gathered around Baroness Linda van Gallagan are not simple charlatans. They are a real danger for the Realm. If I were you, I would quickly find out what's the truth behind all those speculations and who have their hands in it!

Based on the denunciation made by Linda van Gallaghan I decided to arrest Sam Riemann. When tortured, he confessed he helped Baroness Linda van Gallagan to prepare that heretical Sabbath at which Fallen Angel Arthamon was reputedly summoned. And much like Baroness he asserted that Judge Vallarian masterminded that crime. What do you think about it, Master?

Your investigation exceeded my expectations, brother. I have to say I'm almost taken by surprise. I've never doubted Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic. And also I'm not taken aback by Sam Riemann helping her. But it's queer that confessions of them both accord in the matter of judge Vallarian. If I were you, I'd quickly find out what's the truth behind all those speculations!
I'm going to accuse judge Vallarian of heresy, Master. Facts speak against him. What is your opinion about it?

You want to charge judge Vallarian with heresy... I hesitate to speak about it. It is really... beyond imagination. But if facts speak clearly... I hope you made no mistake. It would probably have fatal consequences for you. But do as you see fit.
Judge Vallarian pleaded guilty of all crimes he was charged with, Master. What do you think about it?

Judge Vallarian pleaded guilty? It is unbelievable. In that case it had to be him who tried to falsely accuse me of heresy and get me sentenced. And it was him who ordered Bishop Quentinus to be kidnapped...
Yes, just so.

Now it's starting to make sense! Vallarian wanted to cover up the tracks of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. So he persuaded the green skins to kidnap Bishop Quentinus and contrived it so the blame would fall on me. Oh my God, I would have never thought all the crimes would lead us so high. It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals!
What do you think about the treachery of judge Vallarian, Master?

It's unbelievable that judge Vallarian, the highest ranking inquisitor in this region, was behind all these crimes. It was he who tried to falsely accuse me of heresy and to get me sentenced. And it was he who devised the kidnapping of Bishop Quentinus. He did it to cover up the tracks of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. I would have never thought all the crimes would lead us so high. It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals!
What can you tell me about Bishop Trevorius?

Monsignor Trevorius is diocesan Bishop in Glatzburg. I've known him for some time and I may tell you with certainty he is a man of utmost faith and of unbelievable devotion to his mission. Furthermore, he is very scholarly and his knowledge in many different areas is admirable. He is very interested in everything concerning the faith and the fight for its greater power, so I'm hopeful he will help you with your investigation—that is, if you decide to seek him.
What do you think about the recent crisis the Realm has been dragged into, Master?

What do I think of the recent crisis? Well... I wouldn't use the term crisis. It seems like the end of the world to me, brother. I don't want to sound like a demagogue, but I'm deeply faithful man and I can sense when the faith is in danger. The events, which started after the Star of Doom has risen on the sky, are endangering the faith more than anything we have faced before. I do not know if the Visions of Saint Ezekiel in the Scriptures really speaks about the end of the world, but it seems so by all accounts. We have to step against it and stop it at all costs!
I'm sorry, but I won't talk with you about that!

Monsters are in abundance in the surroundings of the town, brother. It has always been a barbarous region, because it rests in the shadow of the Moonshine Mountains, which have been home to all sorts of beasts and horrors of Hell since long ago. But never has this country seen something like those creatures that have been debouching from the bowels of Earth over the last two years. It's hard to say which breed of monsters is the most dangerous, but wherever you go you will surely meet trolls. They are abominable beasts living among the highest mountain peaks. This year they have descended to lowlands in particularly numerous bands and now they plunder homesteads in the foothills. It's hard to kill them because they have stone instead of skin. They are terribly bloodthirsty. If you happen to meet them, brother, run for you life.
Is it possible to get any reward here in Hillbrandt for killing monsters?

Duke Weinberg announced a reward for orcish heads. Ask sheriff Contemburry for further details. He also pays the rewards—just bring him a head or a scalp from a green skin and the gold is yours. But it's a very dangerous to make a living on it. Many adventurers tried to make money that way, but nobody has seen them since. I'm afraid Duke's plan has failed—people are scared to go behind the town walls, let alone to hunt the orcs.
Has something unusual happened in Hillbrandt lately?
You ask me if something strange happened in Hillbrandt... I suppose you mean aside from all we talked about.
Yes.

Some time ago a terrible storm raged above the town. It was in the middle of one of those moonless nights and I openly admit I've never experienced anything more frightful. The storm caught me on my way back from one of my frequent crusades against hellspawns, when nightfall forced me to stay overnight out of the town walls. I've seen much in my life, but nothing like that. Cruel wind came, whipping the land as if the very sky started to fall down. Then thunders begin to stroke, rumbling like thousands of drums, and they deafened even the wailing of the tempest. And then it happened...

Each stroke of lightning resounded the night sky with a terrible roar and in a twinkling blinding flare I saw demons dancing in the sky. At first I thought it might be an illusion, but later I became certain. It was horrible, brother. They swirled in a mad dance, screamed and mutually scarified themselves, falling to the earth and flying up again. That entire infernal whirl culminated in a torrent of their bodies disappearing somewhere above the Dragon Rock. Then all became silent and only damaged countryside bore witness to the horrors that occurred in Hillbrandt and its surrounding.
What evoked that storm?

I do not know, brother, but whatever it was, everything has been going worse and worse since that moment. Orcs have crept from the depths of Earth and massacred Asherbalt. Wild monsters descended from the mountains and infested the foothills. All beasts and hellspawns started to be yet more aggressive... I do not know exactly what happened, but that storm has not brought anything good, that is for sure!
What do you know about Fallen Angel Arthamon, Master?

What do I know about Fallen Angel Arthamon? My knowledge of the Scriptures isn't too good, brother, but I know he is one of the most powerful demons ever serving Satan the Tempter. At the beginning of the days Arthamon has been thrown down from Heavens along with other Fallen Angels for crimes against God. Arthamon is the ruler of fires and the master of the ruin. His powers lie in the Kingdom of destruction. Now and then some heretics appear who worship him as a god of war.
The monstrance of saint Orthenius has disappeared from the town, Master. Do you know anything about it?

Yes, I heard the monstrance of saint Orthenius has disappeared. I wanted to investigate it, but now I have other concerns. It is a terrible shock not only for the town, but also for the Realm as a whole. It is one of a few saintly relics, which supposedly were consecrated by Saint Orthenius himself. Regrettably I haven't a slightest idea where it could went to.
Are there some legends or myths connected to Hillbrandt or its surrounding?

Hillbrandt is emblazoned with legends and myths, brother. It is a town with a long history, although it doesn't seem so. Take for example the tale of the Tree of Death, which grows near the Dragon Rock in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. It is told that it contains imprisoned souls of barbarian women, children and old men, hanged there by Duke Welliar in the year 988 after the last remnants of barbarian warriors were slaughtered. It was at the end of the Barbarian wars. The unified holy army was winning on all the fronts and the barbarian hordes were fleeing back to the Moonshine Mountains from where they had invaded the Realm. Majority of them was slaughtered on the run.
Well... continue.

The same happened here. Duke Welliar with his cavalry surrounded a decimated tribe and killed all the warriors in a night assault. Legend says barbarian women and children pleaded for mercy in the morning, but Duke refused to take them as prisoners and ordered them to be hung on a spreading old oak tree they were hiding under. It is told that when people from the town came the other day to bury the dead, they found only empty ropes. And the tree was lifeless as if dead for hundreds of years...
Dreadful...

Yes, it is. Since then people avoid that area, because they believe the tree is possessed by unclean sprits of never christened barbarian children, which entered it to wait inside for the day of their revenge. During unquiet windy nights you really may hear some groans and shrieks from afar. People from the town say dead barbarians come out of the tree once a year and ride into the country to have revenge.
What do you think about landsknecht Olfghard, the alleged murderer of Natalia Reichmann?

I knew Natalia Reichmann very well. She was pretty and merry girl. Her father was rightly proud of her. It's a mystery what happened to her. I do not know for sure Olfghard killed and robber her, as it is told. It may be so. Regrettably I had no time to investigate the case. But whatever the truth is, Olfghard has absconded and that for sure means something.
I'm searching for soldier named Jullian. By all accounts he has deserted. Do you know anything about it?
I'm sorry, brother, but I know nothing about soldier Jullian. He probably ran somewhere to the south, as most of deserters do.

What do you think about the accusation that the Brotherhood of the Righteous has been conspiring against the Holy Inquisition and tries to curtail its powers to stop it from revealing criminals inside the Brotherhood?

Brotherhood of the Righteous never committed itself to any wrongdoings, less so to a conspiracy! All these are only shameful lies. Whoever spreads such delusions should realize the facts first. Brotherhood of the Righteous was given an exclusive domain for administering justice as far back as in 1115, more than hundred years ago. The knightly order was established with the blessing of King Archibald I and always has been the bastion of true faith and righteousness.
Well... but what about your wealth? And your power?

It's true the power of our order has expanded greatly in the process and our wealth is innumerable, but all that serves to the benefit of our holy quest! Attempts of Holy Inquisition to curtail our power and subject us to its jurisdiction clearly prove that it's in fact the Holy Office that is pursuing its own interests and trying to intrigue against the justice. And we cannot permit that!
Do you regard Bishop Trevorius as trustful? I asked him for help, but his goodwill was quite limited...

Well... it is strange. I do not remember Bishop Trevorius to ever hesitate to lend a helping hand in a fight against darkness in human souls. I'd thought he will immediately assist you to the greatest extent possible. It's really odd! But I hope the situation will clear up somehow...
Do you know Bishop Trevorius is dead, Master?
What are you telling me? Bishop Trevorius is dead? My God! How comes it? What happened to him? Speak, brother!
He was murdered, Master. It was impossible to help him.

A Murder?! I should have though that! Vile murderers do not detest even to lay their hands on the God's legate on earth! His death must be avenged, brother! Those heathens and heretics won't get away with this; it's as sure as there is God above us! You must to do all you can not to let this death unpunished!
You can rely on me, Master.
I have every confidence in you, brother!
We have already found his murderers, Master. They are heretics from the cult named the Children of the New Order.

It's very grave news indeed, brother. Just the fact that the cult is still in existence is worrying me, let alone that they dared to commit such a terrible act as the murder of diocesan Bishop certainly is. You have to uncover all who are connected to those Children of the New Order and stop them in their rampart spree!
Who rules Hillbrandt and surrounding areas?

Hillbrandt and surrounding areas are ruled by Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. Vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. Duke Weinberg is the right man at the right place, I think. But Baron van Gallagan rules mostly with the aid of his wife...
I do not want it gratis, of course...
I'm sorry, but you won't bribe me! I firmly adhere to the principles of morality!
Answer me immediately, Master, or you will bear grave consequences for your reluctance!
You have to answer me. A man like you surely understands significance of my mission!
I do not believe that your great wisdom and judgement would restrain you from answering my question, Master.
I will look for your sword, Master. That thief will be smitten by rightful punishment.
Thank you, brother. I will be greatly indebted to you—if you succeed.
You are welcome. May I talk with you some more?
Certainly, brother. What do you need to know?
You are welcome, Master. Farewell.
What will you offer me for my service, Master?

What?! A knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous cares more about his personal benefit than about administering justice and catching criminals? In that case I'm not surprised God turned his face away from the Realm. You're making me sick, brother!
I'm sorry, but it does not seem to me as the best idea to help a man suspicious of heresy to obtain a weapon...
I understand, brother. It makes some sense. But I'm sorry you do not believe me, your own superior. Farewell.

I think I know where to find your sword. I had infiltrated the orcish caverns in Moonshine Mountains and met a creature from hell confusingly similar to you. And it wielded probably just the sword you are searching for.

Really? But this would mean I was right! Theft of my sword is connected with that man—I mean with that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among green skins during the orcish attack on the town. It's almost sure the heretics have stolen my sword just to summon a hellspawn that would be indistinguishable from me. And then put him among the green skins to make me suspicious of high treason! Yes, I'm starting to understand it. Thank you, brother, you helped me greatly. Although I would appreciate it if you could bring me my sword back. I need it badly!
All right, Master, I will bring you your sword.
Sure, brother. Ask your questions.
I may consider doing that... What will you offer me in exchange for this service, Master?

Well... so it is like this? Inquisitors of the Holy Office care more about their personal benefit than about administering of justice and catching criminals? In that case I'm not surprised God turned his face away from the Realm.

I'm sorry, but it does not seem to me as the best idea to help a man suspicious of heresy to obtain a weapon. Moreover, existence of a magic double does not necessarily prove anything of what you just deduced.
I understand, brother. It makes some sense. In that case, may the God be with you.
Wait, Master. I'd like to talk to you some more.
Really? And about what?
Farewell.
I think I've found your sword, Master. Is it this one?
Really, that is my sword! The First prophet himself bless you, brother. Where did you found it?
Deep in the orcish caverns under the Moonshine Mountains. It was wielded by a hellspawn looking exactly like you.

So I was true! The theft of my sword is connected with that man—I mean with that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among green skins during the orcish attack on the town. It's utterly probable the heretics have stolen my sword just to summon a hellspawn that would be indistinguishable from me. And then to put him among the green skins to make me suspicious of high treason! Thank you, brother, you helped me greatly. Now it's starting to make some sense. I'm greatly indebted to you. Accept, please, this little reward as an expression of my thanks for your hard work.
Than you. May I speak with you a little bit more?
Thank you, Master. Farewell.
Thank you, Master.
You're welcome. Is there something I can do for you now, brother?
It's a rather sensitive matter. Can you vow me you won't tell anyone?
Sure, brother. I vow by all that is dear to me I will not speak a word about anything what will be told here. What is the matter?
Bishop Quentinus suspects that judge Vallarian belongs to an ancient cult called the Children of the New Order. Have you heard anything about that cult?

It reminds me something. If I remember correctly, it was a cult of demonists established in the Empire several centuries ago by a heretic named Lucius. He declared himself the Dark prophet of Satan and started to proclaim speedy fall of the God's earthly realm. He gathered numerous fanatics, which pinned their faith to him and supposed that before long the world will end. Eventually all were caught and burned, even though many of them were of high status. Why do you think judge Vallarian would be a part of the long dead cult? I'm sure there is plenty of new ones these days.
Judge Vallarian told me strange things when I was arresting him. He said the day will come soon when some new order arises and its children will rule the world. That, he said, was foretold long ago.

Well... yes, you are right, it sounds weird. But I'm positive it is not related. Regrettably I hear such talking quite often. Or do you have any other evidence connecting Vallarian with that dead cult of Satan's worshippers?

I'm not sure if it is related, but Bishop Quentinus found this strange scroll written by unknown letters among judge Vallarian's belongings. He supposes that if we could decipher it we would get a lead for uncovering plans of judge Vallarian. And it may clarify his possible connection with the Children of the New Order.

Let me see... Yes, it really is quite strange writing. I've never seen anything like that. It almost resembles a code. You say it was amongst Vallarian's belongings? Well... To tell the truth it gives me the jitters just to look on that scroll. Whatever it is surely no good will come out of it. I'm sorry, but I can't help you with it, brother. I've told you all I know about the Children of the New Order, and I even can't say if this scroll proves Vallarian's connection to them.
Well... what a pity.

But I can help you another way, brother. I know a person, which for sure knows more about the Children of the New Order. I speak about Monsignor Trevorius, diocesan Bishop in Glatzburg. He is very educated man and fiercely fights against all that endanger true faith, and so I presume he could be able to give you some advice. I will write you a letter for him asking him to cooperate. Give it to him and you'll see he'll gladly assist you.

You're welcome, brother. Our goal is the same. These strange events have to be thoroughly investigated. It may show judge Vallarian was only a moonstruck heretic without a connection to any cult, but we have to know it for sure. Here is the letter for Bishop Trevorius. And give him my best regards. It's been some time since we met.
Than you. May I speak with you a while longer?
But of course. What interests you?
Farewell, brother. And good luck.
May I talk with you for a moment?
But of course, brother. What interests you?
In the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. It was wielded by your magic twin, summoned by heretics to make you suspicious of heresy.

Really? So I was right! Theft of my sword was connected with that man—or that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among the green skins during the orcish siege of the town. I would have never believed judge Vallarian was behind it. I sincerely thank you once more, brother. I'm greatly indebted to you. Accept, please, this item as a token of my deep gratitude.
Thank you. May I speak with you for a while more?

Well... it seems I have not convinced you of my innocence. I'm really sorry to hear that. You are making a terrible mistake. Somewhere outside there are heretics capable of anything and no one knows what they are up to. I doubt murders and robbing the dead will be enough for them. They pursue something greater. Something that sends shivers down my spine. And you've come to arrest me for a suspicion of heresy. Me, the only man trying to find real culprits in this labyrinth of villainy. I appeal to you to reconsider this, if you are trying to act in the name of justice. Reconsider while there is still time!
The time is out already. Moreover, if you are really innocent, you have nothing to fear. Will you go with me peacefully?

Don't worry, brother, I won't resist, although I'm confident I could stop you. I will go with you consentingly. I just wanted you to realize you are making a grave mistake. Well, let's go. I have nothing to fear because I'm in God's hands.
You may be right, Master. It will be better for me to look into this matter once more in order to be sure.
It's a wise decision, brother. Thank you.
Who are you, brother? You must be new here in Hillbrandt. I don't remember having the privilege of meeting you before.
Just so, brother. I'm new in Hillbrandt. And who are you?
My name is Edmond d'Arvias and I'm the superior of the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
You are a Master of the order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

Yes, you are right. My mission is to lead the local chapter and administer justice here in Hillbrandt and its surroundings. Along with my brothers we are of service to God and to the King, just as our order was entrusted to do when established. And you may believe me it is not an easy service—especially these days!
What do you mean?

Since the Star of Doom has risen on the sky and the Realm was struck by the Scourges of God our service is like an endless bloody fight with hordes of hellspawns and their human henchmen. And numbers of those monsters do not dwindle—in fact they rise. And moreover there are those conflicts between our Brotherhood and the Holy Inquisition. One would think that under such circumstances all who wish to fight common danger would unite, but it is just opposite. Instead of broad help the Holy Office tries to blacken our name and subject us to its jurisdiction. It is scandalous!
What if you're mistaken, Master? What if the Holy Inquisition is just trying to administer justice?

In that case enlighten me, brother, why are the highest representatives of the Holy Office trying to procure the largest possible restriction of our Brotherhood's time-proven jurisdiction and of our other privileges?
Maybe they have a strong argument for doing that. What if we abuse our powers? Would anyone be able to stop us?

I see your point, brother. You may even be right. These are evil times. We cannot believe anything and anyone. All that has been sacred is changing into a foul-reeking heresy and atheism. But I won't allow the Brotherhood of the Righteous to be accused of such shameful crimes that are being blamed on us. Of course nothing of that is true—it's just the opposite. The Holy Inquisition is the one that does everything in its power to become suspicious of pursuing its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction?
I do not have the slightest idea...

So I will tell you, brother. They are trying to destroy us! You surely heard tidings about the Brotherhood of the Righteous being a breeding place of hellish heretical conspiracies against God and the King. About heretical Sabbaths practiced in our quarters, during which we secretly worship Satan and his underlings. About our efforts to limit the powers of the Holy Office said to be based on fear of our terrible crimes being discovered. Of course nothing of that is true—it's just the opposite. The Holy Inquisition is the one that does everything in its power to become suspicious of pursuing its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction?
You thing it's just because the Holy Inquisition is pursuing its own interests?

Just so, brother. They are trying to blacken and scandalize us. All those tidings about the Brotherhood of the Righteous being a breeding place of hellish and heretical conspiracies against God and the King originate from the efforts of the Holy Office to break the power of the Brotherhood. None of these terrible accusations is true. And so all indicates the Holy Inquisition pursues its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction?
Why do you thing the Holy Office is trying to do something like that?

Because they are trying to destroy us! You surely heard tidings about the Brotherhood of the Righteous being a breeding place of hellish heretical conspiracies against God and the King. About heretical Sabbaths practised in our quarters, during which we secretly worship Satan and his underlings. About our efforts to limit the powers of the Holy Office said to be based on fear of our terrible crimes being discovered. Of course nothing of that is true—it's just the opposite. The Holy Inquisition is the one that does everything in its power to become suspicious of pursuing its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction?
Do you know you are suspected of heresy and conspiring against God and the King?
Yes, I am perfectly aware of that. And I presume you too have been entrusted to find evidence against me and prove me guilty of heresy?
You could say that.

In that case I must repeat to you what I already told to inquisitorial prosecutor Jeremiah when he came to interrogate me. I'm innocent. I committed no crime, which I could confess before God, or before any other secular or ecclesiastical court. So I swear by all which is sacred to me!
So how could it happen you are suspected of heresy? Allegedly it was you who let the orcs into the town during their assault on Hillbrandt...

My defense against this false allegation is simple, brother, although hardly believable. At the moment of that insidious attack of green skins on the town I was not in Hillbrandt. Hence the person sighted when allowing orcs to enter the town could not be me. It had to be someone just pretending to be me.
And where were you, then? What happened?

The day before that night attack on Hillbrandt I got an anonymous message. Someone told me to come to the Dragon Rock in the evening. The message promised me I would learn some information about heretics that I have been searching for in vain for some time. It should have struck me it is a trap, but I really needed a hint for my investigation as I was in a deadlock. So I carelessly went to the place of the meeting. I was ready for all things possible, but the web of infernal magic had devoured me before I could do anything. Only then I realized my error and when I fell into a devilish world of nightmares it was already too late. I will not try to convey to you what I had dreamed during that deep and corrupted sleep. It was a terrible nightmare full of cruelty and bizarreness of the worst sort. When I awoke I was sick and exhausted. I had no idea I spent full three days there!
What do you think happened to you, Master?

It's certain I fell victim to a conspiracy. First I had no idea why the heretics didn't kill me outright, if they made such an effort to lure me out of the town and bind me with magic. But I found out shortly after I returned into the town. People were afraid of me, crossed themselves and closed their doors before me. In no time I was met by an inquisitorial prosecutor and told I'm suspected of conspiring against God and the King. He asked me to surrender willingly to the Inquisition and subject myself to investigation. I knew that had he enough evidence against me he would just seize me. So I refused, although in doing so I made myself disreputable. It's not a good idea to let oneself be enquired by the Inquisition. I, Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, authorized by God and the King to prosecute and combat all evil and unjust, was accused of conspiring with the powers of Hell in order to overthrow the King's rule in Hillbrandt!
Why would someone try to defame you in such way?

Defame? No, brother, someone is trying to destroy me! He tries to bring me to the court, so I can be executed for heresy and for high treason. And I know very well the reason. When all those strange things started happening in Hillbrandt I immediately conceived there would be some connection. First it was the murder of Kurt Ollmier the merchant. He was quite an eccentric man and traded everything possible, maybe even occult items strictly forbidden by the Church. I think he was murdered because of some item he possessed and didn't want to sell. Or the murderer wanted to stop him from telling something that should not be told. Not long after that young Baroness Gwenn von Weill died. I've never concealed my suspicion she did not die a natural death. She was young, fresh as a flower and vigorous, I liked her very much. Despite of that she died under unexplainable circumstances and in the twinkling of an eye her body vanished from the grave!
Why should have these two crimes anything common?

Call it an intuition, brother. During those long twenty years I've been serving in the Brotherhood I learned to trust my intuition. Those two crimes are connected. I can swear on it. And that's why I investigated both cases together. Although in the case of the merchant Ollmier's murder I was clueless, when searching for thieves of Gwenn von Weill's body I managed to find a witness. It was Bishop Quentinus and he contacted me himself. He told me that one night in the graveyard he witnessed a group of heretics stealing the body of young Baroness. And he even recognized one of them.
Really? And who was it?

I could not believe it at first, but Bishop Quentinus was positive he recognized Linda van Gallagan, wife of the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt, Baron Robert van Gallagan. I decided to question her, but she refused to cooperate and moreover threatened me that if I would bother her with such nonsense she would complain to her husband and through him to Duke Weinberg. It reassured me in my intent to find out what has Baroness to do with this matter. But then the things I have already told you about happened—it was before I managed to advance with the investigation. Moreover, Bishop Quentinus disappeared without a trace during the orcish assault on the town and I became suspicious of his kidnapping as well. It's all slowly beginning to fit together. Surely the Bishop was kidnapped so he could not bespeak against Baroness Linda van Gallagan. And I was to be accused of heresy just because I revealed the heretics. Don't you understand, brother? It is a conspiracy!
It very well might be so, Master. The only question is who is the culprit. What if you are lying and trying to send me on a false trail?

In that case I do not doubt you will soon make it out yourself. But if you really care about justice, find out who is behind all those crimes which took place in Hillbrandt and which even may not be all known to me. I'm sure that the murder of Kurth Ollmier the merchant, the obscure death of poor Gwenn von Weill, the theft of her body and the kidnapping of Bishop Quentinus are connected and that Baroness Linda van Gallagan is mixed up in them. If you could find the real culprit behind all these impieties, you would also purge my name. If I may advise you, go talk to beggar Flitz. He hangs about the town tavern all the time and so he could see something important the night Ollmier the merchant was murdered. Though he told me he saw nothing, you may have better luck.
Culprits of the crimes in Hillbrandt will be uncovered, I will take care of that. And thank you for the advice.

Excellent, brother. I hope your investigation will have better results than mine. But I'd like to ask you for one more favor. When I was lying by the Dragon Rock bound by the infernal magic of the heretics my paladin sword disappeared. It's an unspeakable dishonor to me and I want it back at any cost. Could you look for it, brother?
The man suspicious of heresy won't tell me what to do.
As you wish, brother. But I told you the truth. Remember one thing: if this is a conspiracy, then you are in the same danger as I am. Take care!
You are probably right. Thank you for the advice.

You are welcome, brother. But I'd like to ask you for one more favor. When I was lying by the Dragon Rock bound by infernal magic of heretics my paladin sword disappeared. It's an unspeakable dishonor to me and I want it back at any cost. Could you look for it, brother?
Do not care, Master. I can take care of myself even without your advice. And if I will find out all those terrible crimes are your work, you may be sure you will regret it!
Yes, I'm sure you can. May God be with you, brother.
I found Bishop Quentinus in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains, Master. He is being held there.
In that case you have to free him as soon as possible, brother! The only testimony we can presently get is his.
I found Bishop Quentinus in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains, Master. I succeeded in freeing him. I suppose he is already back in Hillbrandt.
If it is so, go and talk with him as soon as possible. You will assure yourself of my innocence. Baroness Linda van Gallagan has to tell the truth!

I found and freed Bishop Quentinus, Master. He was held in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. On the basis of his testimony it seems Baroness Linda van Gallagan really committed the crime you told me about.
See? I told you. Now, when you have the testimony of Bishop Quentinus, you may start gathering more evidence against Baroness van Gallagan.
Master Edmond d'Arvias, I arrest you for heresy and high treason on the basis of reasonable suspicion.
Welcome, brother. Do you bring me my sword of the Brotherhood? I trust you managed to find it. It is an unspeakable dishonor to me to let it be stolen from me.
I'm sorry, but I do not have it yet. May I speak with you, Master?
Ask your questions, brother. What do you need to know?
I don't have your sword yet. But I've found out who has it.
Who? Who is that foul thief?

In the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains I met a creature of Hell, whom I at first considered to be you. It was indistinguishable from you. But consequently I found out it was not a human being. And just that creature wielded your sword.

Really? That explains a lot. Yes, I'm starting to understand it! The man seen amongst the green skins during the assault on Hillbrandt was not me. It was that creature of Hell you told me about! Heretics had stolen my sword just to be able to summon my unclean twin! Thank you, brother. This is a grave news indeed. You did me a great favor. But I have to get that sword back! I won't allow it to be wielded by some monster!
You may rely upon me, Master. I will bring it to you.
Thank you, brother. Can I do something for you?
I'd like to ask you some questions.
But of course, brother. Ask right away. What do you need to know?
No, Master. Farewell.
Here is your sword, Master.
In the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. It was wielded by creature indistinguishable from you.

Really? That explains a lot. Yes, I'm starting to understand it! The man seen amongst the green skins during the assault on Hillbrandt was not me. It was that creature of Hell you told me about! Heretics had stolen my sword just to be able to summon my unclean twin! Thank you, brother. You did me a great favor. Accept, please, this item as a token of my deep gratitude!
Thank you, Master. May I ask you several more questions?
Thank you, Master. And may God be with you.
Welcome, brother. How is your investigation going? Have you found something new?
Maybe. May I talk with you?
Welcome, brother. Thank you again for returning my stolen sword. I hope I will be able to repay this debt someday. How is your investigation going?
Quite well. May I talk with you?
Welcome, Master. I owe you my deepest apology for that regrettable error...

Do you mean that incident when you arrested me and accused me of heresy? Yes, I think I deserve an apology for that. But nay, let's forget about it. Now I know you tried to act righteously—although I was absolutely innocent. I hope it has opened your eyes and you will think more about things before you decide to act. Furthermore, who would think that the culprit of all those crimes was judge Vallarian, am I right?
Welcome, Master. I'm glad you finally proved to be innocent.

I'm glad too, brother. These times are desperate and one may be sure of nothing. And above all you may not trust anything and anybody, which is proven by the case of judge Vallarian. To tell the truth I still haven't been able to overcome it. I've known there are heretics hidden amidst us, but I would have never guessed judge Vallarian is one of them. You have my appreciation for uncovering him, brother.
Welcome, brother. I'm glad to see you again. What can I do for you?
Good day, brother. I'm glad to see you again. How is your investigation going?
Quite well, Master. I'd like to talk to you for a moment, if it's possible.
But of course, brother. I'll gladly talk with you. What's on your heart?

It's harder and harder. Sometimes I have a feeling I can't go on, that it's more than I can handle. So much evil, filth, hypocrisy, disguises, intrigues, trickery and death... I'm really bone-tired by all that!

I'm not surprised, brother. There is far more on you shoulders than any man can bear. But do not lose your heart! As the Holy Scriptures say, have faith and faith will strengthen you... And if not the faith then these potions surely will. Take them, I'm sure they will help you in your worst moment. And accept also some gold, I gladly present it to you from the coffers of our chapter. I know these are only humble gifts, but believe me I do not have anything else! You will surely succeed, brother!
Thank you, Master. I gladly accept your gifts. May I ask you some questions now?
It's noble of you, Master. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. And good luck. You will need it, I guess.
Sursum corda, brother. Our destiny is in God's hands! I'm sure you will again find the strength to continue in your mission. Can I do something for you?
May I speak with you?
Thank you, Master, but I don't need anything now. Farewell.
It could be better. But I do not lose my faith. Goodbye for now.
Farewell, brother. And when you are passing by, be sure to drop in. I will be glad to see you.
What conditions must I meet to be declared a commander of the order, Master?

Only a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous may become a commander of the Brotherhood, and only if he proves his loyalty to God and the King and completes a task that's assigned to him. Moreover, he has to prove his courage in fighting and kill more than a hundred infernal enemies!
I would like to become a commander of the Brotherhood, Master.
Really? And do you deem yourself sufficiently loyal to God and the King? Do you believe you're ready to sacrifice yourself for the justice we're sworn to defend even at the price of our lives?!
Yes, Master, I'm ready.

Then I will charge you with a quest that should prove your devotion to our mission. For ages, Hillbrandt was protected by a holy relic, which shielded it from all evil. It was the Monstrance of St. Orthenius. According to an ancient legend the monstrance was consecrated by the patron saint of the Realm, St. Orthenius himself, in 221. It was carried to Hillbrandt by its first Bishop Albertinus in 339 and it became the most valued treasure of the Holy Mother Church in this part of the Realm. The monstrance was kept in the Church of St. Orthenius. Not a long time ago it mysteriously disappeared. Your task will be to find the relic and to find out who was the perpetrator of that heinous crime.

By a lucky coincidence, I've already solved the case, Master. The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen by priest Romius. He was serving the undead Bishop Herbertius who apparently had risen from his grave. I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Unbelievable! Are you telling me that Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? That's infernal! And as if it was not enough, according to your words priest Romius was commanded by that spawn of darkness to steal the monstrance. A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers... I find it hard to believe, nevertheless I can't doubt your words. It is obvious that heresy has rooted itself deep in this town—it has infected even the ranks of the Church. Nevertheless I am glad to say that you completed your task with excellence! The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed. That means I'm free to declare you a commander of the Brotherhood. That is if you've already proven your courage in fighting and killed more than a hundred enemies...

By a coincidence, I've already solved a part of the case, Master. I found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on undead Bishop Herbertius who apparently rose from his grave and somehow managed to get the monstrance. Anyway, I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Indeed?! Are you telling me that former Hillbrandt Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? And that you found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on him? Diabolical indeed! Nevertheless it's good that the monstrance is back. Hopefully it will help Hillbrandt to rest once again under the divine protection. Have you managed to find out who stole the monstrance? Because it's obvious that Herbertius could not do that—such an infernal abomination could not have set its foot on the holy ground...
No, Master, I've not yet managed to find out that.
Then keep on searching till you find him, brother. I am sure you will find the perpetrator eventually.
Of course, Master.
I will do my best to apprehend the perpetrator as soon as I can and to return the relic to its rightful place, Master. Farewell.
I have retrieved the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Master. Undead Bishop Herbertius had it on him. It turned out he rose from his grave.
I found out who stole the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Master.
Really? And who was that? What treacherous sinner could have handed over the most valued relic of this town to such an infernal monster?
It was priest Romius. He testified that he served Bishop Herbertius as a slave.

What?! A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers? I find it hard to believe... though I believe your words, brother. It is obvious that heresy has rooted itself deep in this town—it has infected even the ranks of the Church. In any case I am glad to say that you completed your task with excellence! The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed which means I'm free to declare you a commander of the Brotherhood. That is if you've already proven your courage in fight and killed more than a hundred enemies.
I have proven my courage in fighting and killed more than a hundred infernal enemies, Master.
I have proven my courage already. More than a hundred infernal enemies are back in Hell or on their way there...
I am afraid, I haven't killed so many enemies yet...
Never mind. In that case return to me when soil under your feet is red with blood of infernal minions.

Excellent. By your courage in fight you've proven you deserve to be declared a commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Congratulations, brother! Accept this item as a symbol of your new office. And herewith I give you the key of the Hillbrandt chapter where you're now allowed to enter!

A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even God's knights are thieves! You have greatly disappointed me, brother. I'll beware of you!
What do you think of the charge of heresy raised against you, master?
I found Bishop Quentinus, master. He is being held in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains.

You have found Bishop Quentinus! In that case you have to free him as soon as possible, Father. His testimony is presently the only evidence we have against Baroness Linda van Gallagan! Act promptly, Father!
I managed to free Bishop Quentinus, master. He was being held in the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. I suppose he is already back in Hillbrandt by now.
I found and freed Bishop Quentinus, master. And based on his testimony it seems Baroness Linda van Gallagan really committed the crime you told me about.

Baroness Linda van Gallagan pleaded her sins before dying, master. She confessed she committed all those crimes in order to prepare a Sabbath of witches. And during that Sabbath Fallen Angel Arthamon was supposedly summoned. Furthermore she said that judge Vallarian masterminded all that villainy! What do you think about it?

You have taken me aback, Father! I've never doubted Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic. But I can not believe judge Vallarian would be behind all that. I've heard enough about Vallarian to know he is a willful man persisting on his first opinion—be it whatsoever—but it seems quite odd to me to think he is a heretic.

Your investigation exceeded my expectations, Father. I have to say I'm almost taken by surprise. I've never doubted Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic. And also I'm not taken aback by Sam Riemann helping her. But it's queer that confessions of them both accord in the matter of judge Vallarian. If I were you, I'd quickly find out what's the truth behind all those speculations!
I'm going to accuse judge Vallarian of heresy, master. Facts speak against him. What is your opinion about it?
Judge Vallarian pleaded guilty of all crimes he was charged with, master. What do you think about it?

Now it's starting to make sense! Vallarian wanted to cover up the tracks of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. So he persuaded the green skins to kidnap Bishop Quentinus and contrived it so the blame would fall on me. Oh my God, I would have never thought all the crimes would lead us so high. It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals—no offense, Father.
What do you think about the treachery of judge Vallarian, master?

It's unbelievable that judge Vallarian, the highest ranking inquisitor in this region, was behind all these crimes. It was he who tried to falsely accuse me of heresy and to get me sentenced. And it was he who devised the kidnapping of Bishop Quentinus. He did it to cover up the tracks of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. I would have never thought all the crimes would lead us so high. It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals—no offense, Father.
What do you think about the recent crisis the Realm has been dragged into, master?

What do I think of the recent crisis? Well... I wouldn't use the term crisis. It seems like the end of the world to me, Father. I don't want to sound like a demagogue, but I'm deeply faithful man and I can sense when the faith is in danger. The events, which started after the Star of Doom has risen on the sky, are endangering the faith more than anything we have faced before. I do not know if the Visions of Saint Ezekiel in the Scriptures really speaks about the end of the world, but it seems so by all accounts. We have to step against it and stop it at all costs!

Monsters are in abundance in the surroundings of the town, Father. It has always been a barbarous region, because it rests in the shadow of the Moonshine Mountains, which have been home to all sorts of beasts and horrors of Hell since long ago. But never has this country seen something like those creatures that have been debouching from the bowels of Earth over the last two years. It's hard to say which breed of monsters is the most dangerous, but wherever you go you will surely meet trolls. They are abominable beasts living among the highest mountain peaks. This year they have descended to lowlands in particularly numerous bands and now they plunder homesteads in the foothills. It's hard to kill them because they have stone instead of skin. They are terribly bloodthirsty. If you happen to meet them, Father, run for you life.

Each stroke of lightning resounded the night sky with a terrible roar and in a twinkling blinding flare I saw demons dancing in the sky. At first I thought it might be an illusion, but later I became certain. It was horrible, Father. They swirled in a mad dance, screamed and mutually scarified themselves, falling to the earth and flying up again. That entire infernal whirl culminated in a torrent of their bodies disappearing somewhere above the Dragon Rock. Then all became silent and only damaged countryside bore witness to the horrors that occurred in Hillbrandt and its surrounding.

I do not know, Father, but whatever it was, everything has been going worse and worse since that moment. Orcs have crept from the depths of Earth and massacred Asherbalt. Wild monsters descended from the mountains and infested the foothills. All beasts and hellspawns started to be yet more aggressive... I do not know exactly what happened, but that storm has not brought anything good, that is for sure!
What do you know about Fallen Angel Arthamon, master?

What do I know about Fallen Angel Arthamon? My knowledge of the Scriptures isn't too good, Father, but I know he is one of the most powerful demons ever serving Satan the Tempter. At the beginning of the days Arthamon has been thrown down from Heavens along with other Fallen Angels for crimes against God. Arthamon is the ruler of fires and the master of the ruin. His powers lie in the Kingdom of destruction. Now and then some heretics appear who worship him as a god of war.
The monstrance of saint Orthenius has disappeared from the town, master. Do you know anything about it?

Hillbrandt is emblazoned with legends and myths, Father. It is a town with a long history, although it doesn't seem so. Take for example the tale of the Tree of Death, which grows near the Dragon Rock in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. It is told that it contains imprisoned souls of barbarian women, children and old men, hanged there by Duke Welliar in the year 988 after the last remnants of barbarian warriors were slaughtered. It was at the end of the Barbarian wars. The unified holy army was winning on all the fronts and the barbarian hordes were fleeing back to the Moonshine Mountains from where they had invaded the Realm. Majority of them was slaughtered on the run.
I'm sorry, Father, but I know nothing about soldier Jullian. He probably ran somewhere to the south, as most of deserters do.
Do you know Bishop Trevorius is dead, master?
What are you telling me? Bishop Trevorius is dead? My God! How comes it? What happened to him? Speak, Father!
He was murdered, master. It was impossible to help him.

A Murder?! I should have though that! Vile murderers do not detest even to lay their hands on the God's legate on earth! His death must be avenged, Father! Those heathens and heretics won't get away with this; it's as sure as there is God above us! You must to do all you can not to let this death unpunished!
You can rely on me, master.
I have every confidence in you, Father!
We have already found his murderers, master. They are heretics from the cult named the Children of the New Order.

It's very grave news indeed, Father. Just the fact that the cult is still in existence is worrying me, let alone that they dared to commit such a terrible act as the murder of diocesan Bishop certainly is. You have to uncover all who are connected to those Children of the New Order and stop them in their rampart spree!
Answer me immediately, master, or you will bear grave consequences for your reluctance!
I do not believe that your great wisdom and judgement would restrain you from answering my question, master.
I will look for your sword, master. That thief will be smitten by rightful punishment.
Thank you, Father. I will be greatly indebted to you—if you succeed.
Certainly, Father. What do you need to know?
You are welcome, master. Farewell.
What will you offer me for my service, master?

So it is like that?! Inquisitors care more about their personal benefit than about administering justice and about catching criminals? In that case I'm not surprised God turned his face away from the Realm.
I understand, Father. It makes some sense. Farewell.

Really? But this would mean I was right! Theft of my sword is connected with that man—I mean with that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among green skins during the orcish attack on the town. It's almost sure the heretics have stolen my sword just to summon a hellspawn that would be indistinguishable from me. And then put him among the green skins to make me suspicious of high treason! Yes, I'm starting to understand it. Thank you, Father, you helped me greatly. Although I would appreciate it if you could bring me my sword back. I need it badly!
All right, master, I will bring you your sword.
Sure, Father. Ask your questions.
I may consider doing that... What will you offer me in exchange for this service, master?
I understand, Father. It makes some sense. In that case, may the God be with you.
Wait, master. I'd like to talk to you some more.
I think I've found your sword, master. Is it this one?
Really, that is my sword! The First prophet himself bless you, Father. Where did you found it?

So I was true! The theft of my sword is connected with that man—I mean with that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among green skins during the orcish attack on the town. It's utterly probable the heretics have stolen my sword just to summon a hellspawn that would be indistinguishable from me. And then to put him among the green skins to make me suspicious of high treason! Thank you, Father, you helped me greatly. Now it's starting to make some sense. I'm greatly indebted to you. Accept, please, this little reward as an expression of my thanks for your hard work.
Thank you, master. Farewell.
Thank you, master.
You're welcome. Is there something I can do for you now, Father?
Sure, Father. I vow by all that is dear to me I will not speak a word about anything what will be told here. What is the matter?

Let me see... Yes, it really is quite strange writing. I've never seen anything like that. It almost resembles a code. You say it was amongst Vallarian's belongings? Well... To tell the truth it gives me the jitters just to look on that scroll. Whatever it is surely no good will come out of it. I'm sorry, but I can't help you with it, Father. I've told you all I know about the Children of the New Order, and I even can't say if this scroll proves Vallarian's connection to them.

But I can help you another way, Father. I know a person, which for sure knows more about the Children of the New Order. I speak about Monsignor Trevorius, diocesan Bishop in Glatzburg. He is very educated man and fiercely fights against all that endanger true faith, and so I presume he could be able to give you some advice. I will write you a letter for him asking him to cooperate. Give it to him and you'll see he'll gladly assist you.

You're welcome, Father. Our goal is the same. These strange events have to be thoroughly investigated. It may show judge Vallarian was only a moonstruck heretic without a connection to any cult, but we have to know it for sure. Here is the letter for Bishop Trevorius. And give him my best regards. It's been some time since we met.
Farewell, Father. And good luck.
But of course, Father. What interests you?

Really? So I was right! Theft of my sword was connected with that man—or that creature of hell you're speaking about—which people had seen among the green skins during the orcish siege of the town. I would have never believed judge Vallarian was behind it. I sincerely thank you once more, Father. I'm greatly indebted to you. Accept, please, this item as a token of my deep gratitude.

Don't worry, Father, I won't resist, although I'm confident I could stop you. I will go with you consentingly. I just wanted you to realize you are making a grave mistake. Well, let's go. I have nothing to fear because I'm in God's hands.
You may be right, master. It will be better for me to look into this matter once more in order to be sure.
It's a wise decision, Father. Thank you.

Who are you, Father? You have to be new here in Hillbrandt. You are probably one of judge Vallarian's men—one of his inquisition vultures, am I right? Under the normal circumstances I would approve. I might even be happy the Holy Inquisition has visited Hillbrandt. But in this state of affairs...
Who are you, sir?
You are one of the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

Yes, you are right. My mission is to lead the local chapter of the Brotherhood and administer justice here in Hillbrandt and its surroundings. Along with my brothers we are of service to God and to the King, just as our order was entrusted to do when established. And you may believe me it is not an easy service—especially in these days!
Carefully, master. You are speaking to the representative of the Holy Inquisition. I won't allow you to speak in such a way in my presence!
In that case enlighten me—why are your highest representatives trying to procure largest possible restriction of the Brotherhood time-proven jurisdiction and of our other privileges?
They sure have valid reason for doing that. What if you abuse your powers? Would anyone be able to stop you? What if you are really driven by sin and have conspired against God and the King?

I see your point, Father. You may even be right. These are evil times. We cannot believe anything or anyone. All that has been sacred is changing into a foul-reeking heresy and atheism. I'm sorry if I offended you. I'm irritated by this entire situation just like you. But I won't allow the Brotherhood of the Righteous to be accused of such shameful crimes that are being blamed on us. Of course nothing of that is true—it's just the opposite. The Holy Inquisition is the one that does everything in its power to become suspicious of pursuing its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction? I do not want to offend you, but you should open your eyes... We live in times too dark to allow us to blindly believe all what is said.
Well... I do not have a slightest idea...

So I will tell you, Father. They are trying to destroy us! You surely heard tidings about the Brotherhood of the Righteous being a breeding place of hellish heretical conspiracies against God and the King. About heretical Sabbaths practiced in our quarters, during which we secretly worship Satan and his underlings. You had to notice that people say our efforts to limit the powers of the Holy Office are based on fear of our terrible crimes being discovered. Of course nothing of that is true—it's just the opposite. The Holy Inquisition is the one that does everything in its power to become suspicious of pursuing its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction? I do not want to offend you, but you should open your eyes... We live in times too dark to allow us to blindly believe all what is said.

Just so, Father. You are trying to blacken and scandalize us. All those tidings about the Brotherhood of the Righteous being a breeding place of hellish and heretical conspiracies against God and the King originate from efforts of the Holy Office to break the power of the Brotherhood. None of those terrible accusations is true. And so all indicates the Holy Inquisition pursues its own interests, which surely do not align with the interests of the Realm. Why else would the Inquisition make such efforts to subject the Brotherhood of the Righteous to the inquisitional jurisdiction? I do not want to offend you, but you should open your eyes... My defense against this false allegation is simple, Father, although hardly believable. At the moment of that insidious attack of green skins on the town I was not in Hillbrandt. Hence the person sighted when allowing orcs to enter the town could not be me. It had to be someone just pretending to be me.
What do you think happened to you, master?

It's certain I fell victim to a conspiracy. First I had no idea why the heretics didn't kill me outright, if they made such effort to lure me out of the town and bind me with magic. But I found out shortly after I returned into the town. People were afraid of me, crossed themselves and closed their doors before me. In no time I was met by inquisitorial prosecutor and told I'm suspected of conspiring against God and the King. He asked me to surrender consentingly and subject myself to investigation. I knew that had he enough evidence against me he would just seize me. So I refused, although in doing so I made myself disreputable. It's not a good idea to let oneself be enquired by the Inquisition—no offence, Father. I, master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, authorized by God and the King to prosecute and combat all evil and unjust, was accused of conspiring with the powers of Hell in order to overthrow the King's rule in Hillbrandt!

Defame? No, Father, someone is trying to destroy me! He tries to bring me to the court, so I can be executed for heresy and for high treason. And I know very well the reason. When all those strange things started happening in Hillbrandt I immediately conceived there would be some connection. First it was the murder of Kurt Ollmier the merchant. He was quite an eccentric man and traded everything possible, maybe even occult items strictly forbidden by the Church. I think he was murdered because of some item he possessed and didn't want to sell. Or the murderer wanted to stop him from telling something that should not be told. Not long after that young Baroness Gwenn von Weill died. I've never concealed my suspicion she did not die a natural death. She was young, fresh as a flower and vigorous, I liked her very much. Despite of that she died under unexplainable circumstances and in the twinkling of an eye her body vanished from the grave!

Call it an intuition, Father. During those long twenty years I've been serving in the Brotherhood I learned to trust my intuition. Those two crimes are connected. I can swear on it. And that's why I investigated both cases together. Although in the case of the merchant Ollmier's murder I was clueless, when searching for thieves of Gwenn von Weill's body I managed to find a witness. It was Bishop Quentinus and he contacted me himself. He told me that one night in the graveyard he witnessed a group of heretics stealing the body of young Baroness. And he even recognized one of them.

I could not believe it at first, but Bishop Quentinus was positive he recognized Linda van Gallagan, wife of the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt, Baron Robert van Gallagan. I decided to question her, but she refused to cooperate and moreover threatened me that if I would bother her with such nonsense she would complain to her husband and through him to Duke Weinberg. It reassured me in my intent to find out what has Baroness to do with this matter. But then the things I have already told you about happened—it was before I managed to advance with the investigation. Moreover, Bishop Quentinus disappeared without a trace during the orcish assault on the town and I became suspicious of his kidnapping as well. It's all slowly beginning to fit together. Surely the Bishop was kidnapped so he could not bespeak against Baroness Linda van Gallagan. And I was to be accused of heresy just because I revealed the heretics. Don't you understand, Father? It is a conspiracy!
It very well might be so, master. The only question is who is the culprit. What if you are lying and trying to send me on a false trail?

Excellent, Father. I hope your investigation will have better results than mine. But I'd like to ask you for one more favor. As you wish, Father. But I told you the truth. Remember one thing: if this is a conspiracy, then you are in the same danger as I am. Take care!

Welcome, master. I'm glad you finally proved to be innocent.

You have my appreciation for uncovering him, Father.
Welcome, Father. I'm glad to see you again. What can I do for you?
Good day, Father. I'm glad to see you again. How is your investigation going?
Quite well, master. I'd like to talk to you for a moment, if it's possible.
But of course, Father. I'll gladly talk with you. What's on your heart?

And accept also some gold, I gladly present it to you from the coffers of our chapter. I know these are only humble gifts, but believe me I do not have anything else! You will surely succeed, Father!
