Sursum corda, Father. Our destiny is in God's hands! I'm sure you will again find the strength to continue in your mission. Can I do something for you?

Inquisitor of the Holy Office tries to steal? I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in so bad state when even priests are thieves! I'm very disappointed with you, Father. I will watch out for you!

You have found Bishop Quentinus! In that case you have to free him as soon as possible, sir. His testimony is presently the only evidence we have against Baroness Linda van Gallagan! Act promptly, sir!

You have taken me aback, sir! I've never doubted Baroness Linda van Gallagan is a heretic. But I can not believe judge Vallarian would be behind all that. I've heard enough about Vallarian to know he is a willful man persisting on his first opinion—be it whatsoever—but it seems quite odd to me to think he is a heretic.

If I were you, I'd quickly find out what's the truth behind all those speculations!

It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals!

It's unbelievable that judge Vallarian, the highest ranking inquisitor in this region, was behind all these crimes. It was he who tried to accuse me falsely of heresy and get me sentenced. It's really shocking! It proves the Holy Inquisition is not faultless and that some of its members really pursue their own goals!

The events, which started after the Star of Doom has risen on the sky, are endangering the faith more than anything we have faced before. I do not know if the Visions of Saint Ezekiel in the Scriptures really speaks about the end of the world, but it seems so by all accounts. We have to step against it and stop it at all costs!

Monsters are in abundance in the surroundings of the town, sir. It has always been a barbarous region, because it rests in the shadow of the Moonshine Mountains, which have been home to all sorts of beasts and horrors of Hell since long ago. But never has this country seen something like those creatures that have been debouching from the bowels of Earth over the last two years. It's hard to say which breed of monsters is the most dangerous, but wherever you go you will surely meet trolls. They are abominable beasts living among the highest mountain peaks. This year they have descended to lowlands in particularly numerous bands and now they plunder homesteads in the foothills. It's hard to kill them because they have stone instead of skin. They are terribly bloodthirsty. If you happen to meet them, sir, run for you life.

At first I thought it might be an illusion, but later I became certain. It was horrible, sir. They swirled in a mad dance, screamed and mutually scarified themselves, falling to the earth and flying up again. That entire infernal whirl culminated in a torrent of their bodies disappearing somewhere above the Dragon Rock. Then all became silent and only damaged countryside bore witness to the horrors that occurred in Hillbrandt and its surrounding.

I do not know, sir, but whatever it was, everything has been going worse and worse since that moment. Orcs have crept from the depths of Earth and massacred Asherbalt. Wild monsters descended from the mountains and infested the foothills. All beasts and hellspawns started to be yet more aggressive... I do not know exactly what happened, but that storm has not brought anything good, that is for sure!

At the beginning of the days Arthamon has been thrown down from Heavens along with other Fallen Angels for crimes against God. Arthamon is the ruler of fires and the master of the ruin. His powers lie in the Kingdom of destruction. Now and then some heretics appear who worship him as a god of war.

It is told that it contains imprisoned souls of barbarian women, children and old men, hanged there by Duke Welliar in the year 988 after the last remnants of barbarian warriors were slaughtered. It was at the end of the Barbarian wars. The unified holy army was winning on all the fronts and the barbarian hordes were fleeing back to the Moonshine Mountains from where they had invaded the Realm. Majority of them was slaughtered on the run.
I'm sorry, sir, but I know nothing about soldier Jullian. He probably ran somewhere to the south, as most of deserters do.
What are you telling me? Bishop Trevorius is dead? My God! How comes it? What happened to him? Speak, sir!

A Murder?! I should have though that! Vile murderers do not detest even to lay their hands on the God's legate on earth! His death must be avenged, sir! Those heathens and heretics won't get away with this; it's as sure as there is God above us! You must to do all you can not to let this death unpunished!
I have every confidence in you, sir!

Just the fact that the cult is still in existence is worrying me, let alone that they dared to commit such a terrible act as the murder of diocesan Bishop certainly is. You have to uncover all who are connected to those Children of the New Order and stop them in their rampart spree!
Thank you, sir. I will be greatly indebted to you—if you succeed.
Certainly, sir. What do you need to know?

Well, so this is what it's all about? The gentry care more about their personal benefit than about administering justice and catching criminals? In that case I'm not surprised God turned his face away from the Realm.
I understand, sir. It makes some sense. Farewell.

I understand, sir. It makes some sense. In that case, may the God be with you.
Really, that is my sword! The First prophet himself bless you, sir. Where did you found it?

Call it an intuition, sir. During those long twenty years I've been serving in the Brotherhood I learned to trust my intuition. Those two crimes are connected. I can swear on it. And that's why I investigated both cases together. Although in the case of the merchant Ollmier's murder I was clueless, when searching for thieves of Gwenn von Weill's body I managed to find a witness. It was Bishop Quentinus and he contacted me himself. He told me that one night in the graveyard he witnessed a group of heretics stealing the body of young Baroness. And he even recognized one of them.

I could not believe it at first, but Bishop Quentinus was positive he recognized Linda van Gallagan, wife of the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt, Baron Robert van Gallagan. I decided to question her, but she refused to cooperate and moreover threatened me that if I would bother her with such nonsense she would complain to her husband and through him to Duke Weinberg. It reassured me in my intent to find out what has Baroness to do with this matter. But then the things I have already told you about happened—it was before I managed to advance with the investigation. Moreover, Bishop Quentinus disappeared without a trace during the orcish assault on the town and I became suspicious of his kidnapping as well. It's all slowly beginning to fit together. Surely the Bishop was kidnapped so he could not bespeak against Baroness Linda van Gallagan. And I was to be accused of heresy just because I revealed the heretics. Don't you understand, sir? It is a conspiracy!

Excellent, sir. I hope your investigation will have better results than mine. But I'd like to ask you for one more favor. When I was lying by the Dragon rock bound by the infernal magic of the heretics my paladin sword disappeared. It is an unspeakable dishonor to me—the sword symbolizes the paladin's rank in the Brotherhood. It's unthinkable anyone would let himself be deprived of it, the less so the master of the order. Therefore I want it back at any cost. Could you look for it, sir?
As you wish, sir. But I told you the truth. Remember one thing: if this is a conspiracy, then you are in the same danger as I am. Take care!

You are welcome, sir. But I'd like to ask you for one more favor. When I was lying by the Dragon rock bound by infernal magic of heretics my paladin sword disappeared. It is an unspeakable dishonor to me—the sword symbolizes the paladin's rank in the Brotherhood. It's unthinkable anyone would let himself be deprived of it, the less so the master of the order. Therefore I want it back at any cost. Could you look for it, sir?
Yes, I'm sure you can. May God be with you, sir.
In that case you have to free him as soon as possible, sir! The only testimony we can presently get is his.
Welcome, sir. Do you bring me my sword of the Brotherhood? I trust you managed to find it. It is an unspeakable dishonor to me to let it be stolen from me.
Ask your questions, sir. What do you need to know?

Really? That explains a lot. Yes, I'm starting to understand it! The man seen amongst the green skins during the assault on Hillbrandt was not me. It was that creature of Hell you told me about! Heretics had stolen my sword just to be able to summon my unclean twin! Thank you sir. This is a grave news indeed. You did me a great favor. But I have to get that sword back! I won't allow it to be wielded by some monster!
Thank you, sir. Can I do something for you?
But of course, sir. Ask right away. What do you need to know?

Really? That explains a lot. Yes, I'm starting to understand it! The man seen amongst the green skins during the assault on Hillbrandt was not me. It was that creature of Hell you told me about! Heretics had stolen my sword just to be able to summon my unclean twin! Thank you, sir. You did me a great favor. Accept, please, this item as a token of my deep gratitude!
Welcome, sir. How is your investigation going? Have you found something new?
Welcome, sir. Thank you again for returning my stolen sword. I hope I will be able to repay this debt someday. How is your investigation going?

I'm glad too, sir. These times are desperate and one may be sure of nothing. And above all you may not trust anything and anybody, which is proven by the case of judge Vallarian. To tell the truth I still haven't been able to overcome it. I've known there are heretics hidden amidst us, but I would have never guessed judge Vallarian is one of them. You have my appreciation for uncovering him, sir.
Welcome, sir. I'm glad to see you again. What can I do for you?
Good day, sir. I'm glad to see you again. How is your investigation going?
But of course, sir. I'll gladly talk with you. What's on your heart?

I'm not surprised, sir. There is far more on you shoulders than any man can bear. But do not lose your heart! As the Holy Scriptures say, have faith and faith will strengthen you... And if not the faith then these potions surely will. Take them, I'm sure they will help you in your worst moment. And accept also some gold, I gladly present it to you from the coffers of our chapter. I know these are only humble gifts, but believe me I do not have anything else! You will surely succeed, sir!
Farewell, sir. And good luck. You will need it, I guess.
Sursum corda, sir. Our destiny is in God's hands! I'm sure you will again find the strength to continue in your mission. Can I do something for you?
Farewell, sir. And when you are passing by, be sure to drop in. I will be glad to see you.
A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! You dissapointed me gravely, sir—I will be watching you!
Hmm... it seems that I have revealed someone's hideout. However, who would hide in a wilderness full of dangerous monsters?!
Anyways, there is nobody in sight. Perhaps I should come back later...
What do you think of the crisis that is spreading throughout the Realm?

All the disasters that have happened in Ultherst in recent years are nothing other than the Scourges of God bestowed upon us to punish our sinful lives. I'm not talking only about heretics—although splinters and cultists have major part in all that wrongness. I mean the whole life of faithful people. Look around yourself and tell me, is this how God's earthly realm should be like?
Well... probably not.

I agree. Sin and debauchery are everywhere—murders, robberies, violence, sacrileges, incest, gossip, sins, slough and unworthiness. What else could our Lord do than to impose penance on us to make us show him we are worthy of his love?! Yes, we must walk this thorny path through the vale of tears and drink bitter wine till the last drop. Only then we shall be purified and our Lord shall accept us again to his warm bosom!
I'm sorry, but I won't speak with you about that!
What do you think about Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert? Is he really a heretic as some people say?

I'm sure Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is innocent and unblemished by sin. He is like an eternally blooming lily, shining with purity even amidst the dirt and human filthiness. It's a judicial error. Those who brought such a disgusting accusation against him will be smitten by the thunderbolt of God's wrath. But it's true many people do not share this opinion of mine... It's hard to believe something firmly these days when heresy flourishes like some malign disease.
Have a fierce storm accompanied by unnatural spectacles occurred here in Alvaron in recent days?
I do not remember any fierce storm, son. And I doubt something could elude my attention, even if it would have happened in the midst of the darkest night. I'm a light sleeper.
What do you know about the Fallen Angels?

The Fallen Angels are the very essence of the dark side of faithful religion, son. Their names should not be uttered aloud. Don't you know heretics constantly repeat their names when summoning hellspawns? But do not be afraid—you will get your answer. The Fallen Angels are four supernatural beings, which together with Satan were thrown down from heaven by God's wrath into the infernal flames for crimes against the God's order. They are Arthamon, the ruler of infernal fires, Baphomet, the destroyer of order and the sower of madness, Cerdie, the mistress of debauchery and of bodily sin, and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the most dreadful of Satan's champions and the emissary of the ultimate evil.
I'm sorry, but I do not have any suspicions of heresy. If I had, I would immediately let you know, you may be sure about that!
Did something noteworthy happen in Alvaron lately?

I heard that paladin Richwald d'Blazier was found in Schwarzwald some time ago, completely turned into stone. A witch named Corin is suspicious of that crime; Richwald supposedly met her several times in the deepest regions of Schwarzwald. I do not know if there's any truth to that, but if the paladin let himself become bewitched it's his and only his fault. Witches have to be treated as they deserve—with flame and hammer!
I'm investigating the murder of paladin Richwalda d'Blazier. Do you know anything about it?

I know about the d'Blazier's murder only what the locals say. And they say he was murderer by a witch named Corin; she turned him into stone. If it is true, it was his fault. Witches have to be treated as they deserve—with flame and hammer!
I'm looking for a way to break the curse of stryx. Could you give me some advice?

Break the curse of stryx you say? Well... in that case I won't give you any advice. In my opinion that infernal creature should be killed and burned and you should not try to break it's curse. You may never be sure how it can end...
I'm looking for the members of the Cult of Pagan Night, especially for their leader, Juhasz Gotherr alias Zan Dremo. Do you happen to know where he could be hiding?

To tell the truth I know Juhasz Gotherr personally—although I wish I never met him. Because of that I'm convinced that he stays here in Alvaron. Several times I had a feeling I see him creeping through the city at night. But although I always reported it both to the Inquisition and to the town guard, he was not captured. He is devious like Satan himself!

Brother Nicolas says he is innocent, and Grand Duchess Liana Lambert says she has been raped. Sadly I must say the word of the royal governor's wife weights more than the word of young priest. I wish it could be settled down somehow and I wish Nicholas could be proven innocent, but I have no proof...
I hope you're just joking, son.
I must warn you that if you deny to answer my question, your fate is going to be very gruesome indeed!
I beg you with all my heart, Father, to overcome your possible aversion to me and answer my question. Believe me, it will help to administer God's justice!
I heard you are very wise and experienced. So I would be honored if you could answer my question.

Well... It's a serious crime for sure, but in my eyes it's not so outrageous as the other crime which I have on my mind. I'm sure the worst offence against the dead is the robbing of graves. Those who commit such crimes are the worst scavengers and disdain the most basic principles of true faith. To disturb the peaceful rest of the dead by stealing their property is really monstrous and deserves the strictest punishment!
You may be right... But why are we discussing it in the first place?

Because I'm very worried—lately there have been too many graves robbed here in Alvaron. Well, I should explain myself, I'm Augustin and I'm in charge of the city cemetery and the sepulcher. So you surely can imagine my grievance about the crimes which some unknown heretics commit by robbing the graves and disturbing not only the remembrance of the deceased, but also their eternal peace. Only God knows how many dead have risen just because of those sacrilegious thieves!
I will help you with your problem if you wish. I'll find who robs those graves...

Really? To tell the truth I did not dare to ask you for help because I know how very busy you paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are these days... And this problem of mine involves only a few robbed graves but no worshipping of demons and infernal forces. Though, as I said, in my eyes it is a crime equally serious to any other! So I greatly appreciate your help. Those disgusting villains must be burned!
May I talk to you for a moment?
Sure, as you wish, son. I'm at your disposal.
Tell me, has someone already done something in the matter of those robbed graves? Are there any suspects or at least any evidence?
No, son. I'm sorry, but you're the first who investigates that case. But if I may advise you: search the city cemetery. You will surely find a trace there.
Thank you. May I ask you some more questions?
Sure, son, as you wish. I'm at your disposal.
Thank you and goodbye.
Thanks, goodbye.
God be with you, son. And God bless you for your generosity...
I might be able to help you with your problem. If I would be somehow rewarded, of course.
I see. You wish me to say mass if you help me. All right, you may rest assured I will.
I hope someone will stop that grave-robbing ghouls' spree. I am afraid I can't deal with it myself.
I understand. I too hope there will be someone who could take care of those villains once and for all...
Sure. May I speak with you for a moment?
Yes, let's hope someone will. Farewell.
Farewell, son. God be with you...
Do you really view it as a worse sin than necrophilia? But intercourse with dead...
Yes, I think so! Fortunately there has been no crime of this sort in this country...
Could you heal me, Father?
Sure, sure, son. In exchange for a little gift to our diocese, let's say $$getmoney150$$ gp.
All right, son. Come closer and let the power of God heal your wounds...
Which crime against the dead do you think to be the worst, son?
Defamation of the remembrance of deceased?
Abuse of a dead body during a heretical Sabbath?
Necrophilia?
Have you found those foul grave-robbers, son? Have you managed to convict them and turn them over to God's justice to be punished?
Not yet, Father.
I see. But I pray you soon will. I'm scared to even think of the harm they may yet do by their shameful deeds...
Trust me.
I have complete confidence in you. What can I do for you?
Could I talk to you for a moment?
Of course, son. I'm fully at your disposal...
I have good news for you, Father. Perpetrators of those crimes were seized and executed.
Really? That's great! At last we will be free of those thievish villains! I'm so grateful to you, son! I will say a ceremonial mass for you, that's for sure!
Thank you. May I speak with you for a while?
Of course, son. I'm at your disposal!
Farewell, son. And God bless you for your merits...

Welcome, son. It's rather gloomy today, isn't it? I don't remember as damp Spring as this. It is as if the very air were heavy with something ominous... But enough gloomy talking—I'm sure you've come because of something important. What can I do for you?
I need to talk with you, Father.
In that case I'm at your disposal.
I must admit I do not have any important matters. I just came by...
I see. It is nice of you to stop by. God be with you.
God be with you, son.
I'm glad to se you again, son. I hope you are well—you certainly do deserve it for you great deeds in that matter with those grave robbers. Can I do something for you?
I'd like to talk to you.
In that case I'm fully at your disposal.
Just stopping by. God be with you.
It's nice of you to come by. May God be with you.
I would like to see your goods, Father.
As you wish, my son...

I hope you're just joking, brother.
I sincerely ask you, brother, to overcome your possible aversion to me and answer my question. Believe me, it will help to administer God's justice which is dear to both of us!

So I greatly appreciate your help. Those disgusting villains have to be burned!

Sure, sure. Come closer. Let the power of God heal your wounds...
Thank you.
You are welcome. I gladly help fellow believer in need.

Though, as I said, in my eyes it is a crime equally serious to any other! So I greatly appreciate your help. Those disgusting villains must be burned!

Grrrrrrrhhhh! How could you dare to endanger my plans, you paltry worm?! How could you dare to lay your hands on the executor of my will? For that you shall taste my wrath! Dark prince of Hell demands revenge for the insult rendered to him by that act! No one may step between the wolf and his prey!
No creature of hell will tell me what I shall do and what I shall not. I administer the will of God!
Your God is nothing to me, poor man! And soon he won't mean anything to anyone. But first, I will wash off the terrible insult you have caused me by your blood! You will die!
Have mercy, mighty Azrael! I will correct my faults...
It's too late for that, mortal! You should have decided betimes. You have infuriated me and Hell knows no mercy! Your life is forfeit.
I doubt that, demon. I shall stop you in your abominable endeavor and shall send you back from whence you came!
Fool! Do you really think your powers can stop me? Your human kind is even more wretched than I have ever imagined. Your worthless souls are barely fit to decorate my palaces!
Enough talking, demon. Soon, the wrath of God shall be upon you! You shall be cast back to hellish sufferings in no time!
Stay your hand, oh noble Baphomet! I have come to bow before you...

I already have enough human followers, you fool! Your trifling meekness does not affect me at all. Your body shall burn in the unholy flame and your soul shall stay with me, forever trapped as a cobblestone within the walls of this palace of madness!
I banish thee, demon, leave this world, for there is no place for your kind!

Banish as you will, human worm, though it shall do you no good. I shall destroy your soul and then I shall rampage upon your world to bring it the same fate as I am going to bring to your soul! You shall be forever trapped as a cobblestone within the walls of this palace of madness!

You despicable nobody! Nameless maggot! Puny worm! How could you have dared to enter my realm? There is nothing other than madness, chaos and unleashed depravity! And all this shall rampage upon the face of the earth when the gates of my palace open wide and my charioteers of doom and terror shall bring their demonic steeds forth to the whole of the world.
Goodness Gracious... Baphomet, the Fallen Angel! So it is indeed true?! One of the Fallen Angels has entered into our world!

So it is! The gates were torn down, hell unleashed and I have entered into the mortal realm to squeeze all the chaos and madness from the souls of men. You shall witness confusion beyond imagination, terror and rupture of all things orderly. You shall witness the mighty Word of Baphomet!
Goodness Gracious... Baphomet, the fallen angel!

Yes, it is me! The gates were torn down, hell unleashed and I have entered into the mortal realm to squeeze all the chaos and madness contained in the souls of men. You shall witness confusion beyond imagination, terror and rupture of all things orderly. You shall witness the mighty Word of Baphomet!
I'm trying to find out how I could remove the curse from the House of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. Any advice?

I remember Baron Dawn von Blutenreich very well, knight. He was a chubby reserved man—a decent fellow—at least so it seemed. But in fact he was a pervert and a sadist who in the course of his baleful life tortured all his twelve wives and countless children to death. He always managed to arrange it so cleverly that nobody suspected him. Divine providence crossed his villainous path when he married his thirteenth wife. She defied his bestial cruelty and being helpless, she decided to poison him. Of course, as a poisoner, she was sentenced to death, which was even more undeserved, as all the heinous crimes of her husband came out during the process. But law is above us all and so the poor woman was executed.
Go on...

Of course. As I've told you, the thirteenth Baron's wife was executed, but before she breathed her last, she uttered a terrible curse. The Baron was not to find peace unless all of his innocent victims did. Nobody suspected the curse to take effect on the very same night—it forced the Baron's tarnished spirit to the residence of the von Blutenreich family and made it a house of horrors.
Very interesting... Thank you.
You're welcome, knight. Even though it happened half a century ago I still remember it as if it were yesterday…

If my memory serves me—and it should, right? Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert, who acts here as the royal governor. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. She's a very genteel dame, I must say.
Where can I buy some equipment in Alvaron?

Well, it depends on what you want to buy. Leon van den Brooks has his famous armory in Alvaron. Apothecary Thelma Ulthraum and master alchemist Alberto Kelley can provide you with potions and various magic stuff. Landlord William Burton and innkeeper Salena Flock sell just about everything.

You ask me whether Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert belongs to the heretics? Hmmm... it's hard to say, knight. But the truth is that Grand Master de Malamert is not exactly popular among people—lots of them think he's a heretic who has betrayed God to serve Satan. That makes people even more afraid of the future, because if such a high ranking man can be a heretic, whom can we trust?

If my memory serves me well, Grand Duke Drake Lambert offered a huge reward for hunting down werewolves who are pestering not only the woods around the city but the city streets as well. The reward will be paid by Sheriff Henry Portmann for every trophy, that means for every werewolf head.

If I remember correctly, not a long time ago there were some rumors about stallholder Sandra Ullmann. She tried to get the attention of noble paladin Richwald d'Blazier by rather indiscrete means. People say she was like a bitch in heat. Nevertheless the paladin kept ignoring her, though not because of his status or because of his oath of purity, but because of some witch from Schwarzwald with whom he fell in love. Sandra Ullmann was supposedly pale with fury.
I'm investigating the murder of paladin Richwald d'Blazier. Do you know anything about it?

Well, according to what I've heard, paladin Richwald d'Blazier was found dead in Schwarzwald. Turned to stone, at least so people say. I'd bet that the Schwarzwald hag who bewitched him has something to do with that!

I have absolutely no idea where you should start looking for Juhasz Gotherr, knight. Some say he fled from the city and is now hiding somewhere at the northern outskirts of the Realm, others would swear that he's stalking the streets of the city at night.

I think that Grand Duchess Liana lies. I remember her when she was a child—she was a vain spoiled girl, who had to have everything she imagined. Well and she has not changed a little bit. Moreover, people say she's a passionate strumpet, who would not hesitate to commit any wickedness to satisfy her insatiable lust for bodily pleasures. I can easily imagine that she wanted to seduce Father Nicolas and when he refused her she, in her vanity, came out with that false accusation. Well, I don't have any evidence and of course I won't tell anybody else about this idea of mine. I'm glad I still have my tongue where it's supposed to be...
Are there any legends or rumors connected with Alvaron?

Have you heard about Joan the cursed girl of the netherworld? It's a very sad story—and it's even sadder when you realize that it might be true. People say that there's a girl named Joan living at the graveyard who was turned into a stryx by a terrible curse. She's now a being coveting blood and vengeance. People say that it was her own mother who cursed her—she was a priestess of the Order of St. Bethesda who was defiled and impregnated by a certain lewd priest. Joan's mother could not bear such a disgrace and went mad. When she gave birth to her daughter she cursed her not to rest until the blood of her father sprinkles her lips. Then she committed suicide and Joan died soon after her—at least everybody thought so. Though even in the grave the curse was changing her for thirteen years until she transformed into a stryx who came to life and has started stalking the city streets in search of her father. She wants to deliver the curse of her mad mother from the netherworld...
Answer me at once, old man, or you will regret your reluctance!
I urge you, good man, answer my question, please.
A wise man such as you could certainly provide me with useful information. That's why I've asked you. Please, answer me now.
Yes, quite possibly.
It is so. But tell me, knight, you are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, aren't you?
Yes, I am.
Well, then I would like to draw your attention to something, knight. Did I say draw attention? To be correct I would like to make a denunciation. But it's all the same these days, right?!
No, I'm certainly not.

No kidding, you are. One can tell just by looking at you, knight. I would like to draw your attention to something, knight. Did I say draw attention? To be correct I would like to make a denunciation. But it's all the same these days, right?!
Well, as you wish. Go on.

Well... to be honest I tried to tell your brothers from the local... ehm... er... chapter—that's the name. But the problem was that... ehm... I have forgotten what I wanted to tell them. Your brothers were not gifted with enough patience to let me remember. They were talking about wasting their time and such things. So I would like to tell you about my denunciation.
And have you already remembered what your denunciation is about?
No. That's the problem—I've not remembered yet. But it's really terribly important, I'm sure of it. Otherwise I would have forgotten it completely.
Is there a way to help you remember the event you would like to tell me about?

I don't know, knight. But it's just the thing I was going to ask you about. If you could find some way—maybe some magical potion or a powerful spell—to get my memory back, at least for a moment, I could make the denunciation.
Very well then, I'll try to find a way to restore your memory.
God bless you for your help, knight. I promise that with my testimony you will be able to cope with the heresy which is rampant all around.
I hope so. Now, could I ask you some more questions?
Of course, knight. Ask me about whatever you want. By the way what have we been talking about till now?
Hmm... Guess my questions can wait.
We shall see. Goodbye for now.
Goodbye, knight. I hope we will meet again soon, so we can talk about… well, what have we been talking about till now?
What can you offer me for restoring your memory?
Well, knight, my testimony, of course. Have you forgotten what were we talking about?!
I am sorry but I don't have time for such errands. You will have to remember on your own.
Well... I'll keep trying, knight, but I don't think my chances are very high. Once I forget it's lost forever.
Well, that's too bad. Now, could I ask you some more questions?
Of course, knight. What have we been talking about till now?
If your testimony is really that important you'd better remember.
Easier said than done, knight—you are young and your memory serves you well. Mine is not serving too well. Well, it's not serving at all.
If you can't remember what you want to tell me, you are wasting my precious time.

Ratbags! Crooks! Brigands! Fornicators! Killers! Sinners and Beelzebubs! Devils and fibbers! Licentious pagans... may plague and pox get them for all the evil they've done to us! May our Lord strike them down with lightning or may Archangel Gabriel slash their asses with his flaming sword. May those dirty bastards taste His justice!
What happened, good man? Why are you lamenting so much? And who are you, anyway?

No, knight, this is a whorehouse and a cesspit reeking of hellish sulphur coming from sin and evil! And you ask me who's responsible? Heretics! Heinous henchmen of the Devil, who lick the tails of goats and make love to demons at their unholy Sabbaths.
Yes, it's a likely explanation. But anyway, could you tell me who you are?
Who am I? Well, of course... ehm... well... dash it, what's that bloody name? Darn it, how do they call me? It was on the tip of my tongue!
Calm down, take your time, good man. I'm sure you will remember in time. Years often bring forgetfulness...
Yes, right. That's exactly... er... what they bring. Oh, I remember now! The name is Balthazar, knight. At least people call me like that, well, it's quite natural anyway—it's my name, isn't it...
If you even don't remember your name I should not be wasting my time on you, good man. Goodbye.
Balthazar! Yes, that's my name—Balthazar. People call me that way, which is quite natural—it's my name, isn't it...
Why do you think that nowadays the situation in the Realm has been caused by heretics?

Why? Because they have undermined the foundations of the faith! They have damaged the only thing that seemed unfaltering—the faith in our Lord. Who would think a few years back that heresy and fallacy would be so widespread? Just peek into the houses of your neighbors and you'll see that only sin flourishes there instead of virtue. And their excuse? They say God has left us anyway, so there's no need to live in accordance with Holy Scripture and with the Commandments. Why bother with something that can't grant you eternal life in the Kingdom of Heaven? So they say.

Such lowly thinking! When I was young, they would have been hanging from the trees for saying something like that. That's why I think God is punishing and testing us at the same time. But heresy has already spread like some malignant disease and the henchmen of devils are corrupting the souls of people, so everything is only going to be worse—not better. That's why I think that heretics are behind all the filth that's suffocating us!

I hope I'll get lucky soon. We can't keep talking like that... Goodbye for now.

Really? May the angels in Heaven praise you, knight. Well, if the potion works... give it to me, I'll drink it at once!
So, is it any better? Do you remember something?
I do remember, knight! Yes, I remember! The potion worked!
I'm glad to hear that. It was no easy task to acquire it for you. Tell me now, what was the deed you witnessed?
Witnessed? Did I witness something?
It can't be...
I'm sorry, knight, I've just dared to make a little joke. The potion restored not only my memory, but my good mood as well. I can't remember feeling so good, ha, ha.
Excellent. Could we now get back to the topic? To the denunciation you wanted to make.

Well then... it was several days back—It was already dark and I was returning home through the streets of the city. I was passing by a tavern and suddenly there was some fuss at the door. I wanted to get away at first, because when there's such a fuss in a pub it might cost you a tooth or two—if not the head. But it was different this time, instead of weapon clangor and groans of the wounded I heard laughter. So I stopped to watch what was to follow.
What happened then?

They were booting out Downay, the former gardener, out of the tavern. I don't know if you've met him, but he's a wicked midget, he is as foul-mouthed as he is mischievous. The runt is willing to do any kind of gleeful mischief or slander—anytime. He used to be the gardener in the Royal Gardens, though since the Scourges our Lord bestowed upon us he hasn't anything to do. He spends all his time in pubs and taverns, even though he can't pay the bills. And when he gets sottish he attacks the patrons—using both mouth and hands. And this is exactly what happened that evening I was talking about.
To the point, please. I don't have time to listen to pub stories.

Just getting there. As I've told you, Downay the Gardener probably bothered the patrons so they threw him out. He flew through the door and landed on his head in the slop filling the street. Everybody was laughing, but I shuddered because I saw his eyes. Never in my life have I seen such a cruel gaze. And then it happened. The gardener started shouting at the people around him that they would all serve him soon, because he would become a noble lord and they would be just the wretched thralls of his. They all started laughing even more, but I knew it was no laughing matter. I heard him snarling something about the coming of a new order and about its children ruling far and wide. He also murmured some words in a strange language, which ensured me that he must be a real heretic. So I didn't hesitate and ran to report it to the Brotherhood of the Righteous. But before I got there I forgot what I wanted to tell them and the paladins just laughed at me. Well, you know the rest.
Thank you, good man. Your witness was a great help.
Yes, thought it could help. It's a shame it took me so long to remember. I hope Downay didn't manage to commit some crime meanwhile…
The investigation will show. Could I ask you some more questions now?
Of course, knight. What would you like to know?
Yes, I hope so too. I better go and check it myself. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. And thanks again for the potion.
Do you know any people who would meet Downay on a regular basis? If he's really a heretic, he will certainly have accomplices.

No, I don't know about any such people. Downay is a loner and a weirdo—he lives in a small house at the edge of the Royal Gardens. I wonder why some of the monsters, which have been living there for the last few years, didn't eat him.
Did Downay really talk about a New Order and its children who will rule the world? Perhaps you misheard.
No, knight, I didn't mishear. That's why it made me so nervous. I have no idea who those children are, but it gives me chills. It sounds like... a heresy!

Then I recommend you remember quickly. But before you do, I have some more questions for you.
Yes, of course. About what have we been talking?
Let me know, when you remember. Goodbye till that day.
Well, I haven't promised you anything like that, but on second thoughts I think it will be easier if I help you.
Of course, knight. Ask me about whatever you want. By the way, what have we been talking about till now?

Sure. Could I have a minute of your time, good man?
Of course, knight. What's on your mind?
Yes, it is so. If you have any suspicion in the future, do not hesitate to tell me, ok?
As you wish, knight.
Excellent. Now, could you answer some more questions?
Certainly, knight. What do you need to know?
Deal. Goodbye for now.

You're welcome, Father. Even though it happened half a century ago I still remember it as if it were yesterday…

That makes people even more afraid of the future, because if such a high ranking man can be a heretic, whom can we trust?

A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even nobles are thieves! Shame!
I am Bartholomeus the Keeper of Secret. You have disturbed my eternal rest… and I see you have my Testament which holds my secret. You shall be stricken by just punishment!
I am sorry, wandering soul—I did not want to disturb your eternal rest. I'll return your Testament at once!
The secret has been already revealed—you must die. I'll take your soul, thief! Kill him, brothers!
No hellspawn will disgrace God's name by its presence in His Kingdom on Earth. Die, demon!
The secret has been already revealed—you must die! I'll take your soul, thief! Kill him, brothers!
Shut up, old man! As dead you don't have any property rights, so the testament in fact isn't yours, but it is a part of the heritage. Therefore you may consider me your beneficiary heir!
If I read correctly, this must be the grave of Saint Bartholomeus, the first head of the Saint Orthenius Order.
Let's see what's inside...
Hmmm, a scroll. It might be Bartholomeus's testament... It describes certain locations where the Angelic Statuettes of the Holy Trinity were hidden... Hmm... interesting!

Hmmm, a scroll. It might be Bartholomeus's testament... It describes certain locations where the Angelic Statuettes of the Holy Trinity were hidden... Could those statuettes be the same as those described in the Killian's Chronicle? I could open the Tomb of Saint Orthenius with them. Guess it really might be them...
I think it's better to leave the dead to their rest...

Ron Burton is missing? Well, it's a pity... He stopped by here on his way from Glatzburg—he was there to conduct some business, at least he said so. A storm hit him and he was glad to find a safe shelter here. We dined together and the next day he continued to Alvaron. I can't believe that he was not to return there...
Isn't there anything else you could tell me? Wasn't he followed? Didn't you see anything suspicious?

Hmm... when I think about it, I do remember something—there were some werewolf howling that morning. I think that it was quite strange, because the werewolves usually rage only at night. Is it possible that they got Ron Burton?!
Thanks.
You're welcome, knight. I'd be really sorry if something bad happened to him.
I won't tell you anything about it!
Hey, innkeeper, is there any gambling in your inn whereat one may pocket some money?
You could play Devil's Emissary.
I don't recall any recent storm. But if it was at night it's quite likely I didn't notice—I sleep like a log after a good meal.
What monsters can you meet around? You mean in my pub?!
No, in the vicinity of Alvaron.

Oh... I would be surprised if you didn't meet werewolves, knight. Take my advice—don't travel at night if you don't have to. Neither in the evening nor soon after sunrise. Their hunting ground includes most of the Schwarzwald and also the vicinity of the city—and sometimes even its streets. I suppose you've heard that when the moon is full they always somehow manage to get inside the city to kidnap an innocent, whom they then bring to their lair deep in Schwarzwald.
Are there any rewards for killing monsters in Alvaron?

I heard that Grand Duke Drake Lambert offered a huge reward for hunting down werewolves who are pestering not only the woods around the city but the city streets as well. The reward is paid by Sheriff Henry Portmann for every trophy, that means for every werewolf head. You could make a fortune selling them!

I heard that one of the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous went mad and attacked innocent people. I think the name was Minfred von Siegel or something like that. Supposedly he has recently returned from a quest against some great evil. I heard he went berserk and slaughtered several innocent people in a fit of rage, then he fled into Schwarzwald to kill anybody who is unlucky enough to cross his path. He chops his victims to pieces!

As far as I know paladin Richwald d'Blazier was found dead in Schwarzwald not far from here. People say he has been turned into stone. That's all I know. I'd bet that some warlock or witch is responsible, because even my boar ragout couldn't do that—and it's really something!

Juhasz Gotherr? I know him. If I recall correctly he used to be the city librarian and archivist. I had no idea that he's a heretic and a cultist until inquisitors of judge Gregorius came here to search for him. He used to stop by from time to time when he was traveling. Well, when I think about it, he really traveled a lot. Perhaps he was trying to get some heretical writings, right? But I have no idea where he could be. Guess he got himself into trouble...
I'm looking for certain magic ingredients—Betheal Temporarum blossom, sun crystal and troll bile. Have you any idea where I could get them?

Just a moment, knight, I'll take a look into my pantry. I might have some of them... Well, what have we here—some troll bile. You can have it if you want—I don't think I'll need it. Troll paste is not exactly popular with my customers, so it doesn't sell like hot cakes, ehmm, goulash in my case...
Thanks I'll gladly take it.
You're welcome, knight. I had no idea that troll bile could be magical, but nowadays everything's possible, right?
No, thanks, I'm not interested.
It's your choice, knight...

I've heard stories about priests who did not take the oath of purity very seriously and sinned a bit. Guess it's normal. Nothing personal, knight, but we are all men and as such we have certain needs, don't we? I can't imagine giving it all up. That's why I can understand why Father Nicolas did what he did—that he had some fun with Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. Well, maybe he went too far, it would have been better for him if he got just some street whore, but I guess he was a victim of circumstances, if you know what I mean. Well, that's all I can tell you for myself. I've never heard that he could be innocent!

Have you ever heard the legend of Wolfenburg—the lair of wolf-prince Wulfhyrr? According to old chronicles, Wolfenburg became the seat of the Lords of Wolfenburg in the seventh century. The Wolfenburg family was infamous for their cruelty and violence towards their subjects. The rumor is that wolf-prince Wulfhyrr was the last of their line. Though his name was Ronald then and as regards cruelty, none of his ancestor could match with him. One day he kidnapped a young beautiful seeress who lived near his castle and raped her terribly.
That's horrifying! What happened next?

The ravished seeress threatened Ronald to turn him in to the Holy Mother Church. But it was a mistake, because the atrocious Duke blatantly killed her. The seeress managed to curse her murderer before she died and Duke turned into an abhorrent wolfish beast. When Ronald's serfs got to know what happened to their Lord, they did not hesitate to grab pitchforks and sharpen broadaxes and soon they overran Wolfenburg. Though they did not get rid of their Duke. After some time, first people got missing and their bloody scraps were to be found far and wide. The rumor is Duke Ronald returned as wolf-prince Wulfhyrr to take bloody revenge for what happened to him. Since then he and his werewolf pack pester the country...
I suggest you answer my question, innkeeper. You don't want to cross the path of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, do you?!
It's obvious that you are an experienced trader. It would be an honor for me if you could answer my question.
What would you like, knight?
A tankard of beer. Its golden sparkle will surely refresh me.
As you wish, knight. It will be one gp.
Thanks, innkeeper.
You're welcome, knight. Enjoy your drink... It's getting dark. What else can I do for you?
I don't have that much money.
I'm sure you understand then that I can't get you anything to drink. I'm sorry but I can't give it to you on the house. Is there anything else I can help you with?
A cup of wine, innkeeper.
Here you go, knight. It will be one gp.
Mead.
Mead? As you wish, knight... Here you go, knight. It will be one gp.
I'd like a cup of pure water.
I'm sorry but water's not on the tap. I can offer you beer, wine or mead. Is there anything else I can offer you?
Do you want to start playing or do you want me to explain you the rules?
We may start.
Excellent. How many cards?
Two.
All right. The bet is 10 gp, knight.
Here you go.

Let's start. Here's our card—the Devil's Emissary. I'll turn it and I will add a second card. Now I'll shuffle them and move each of them to and fro, shuffle again, and which of them could it be? Is it still on the left or is it now on the right? Shuffle them one more time and here we go. So, knight, which of them is the Devil's Emissary? I'm sure you watched it vigilantly...
It's the first one.
It's the second one.
I'm sorry, knight. You know what? Gambling without money ain't much fun. Come back when you have at least 10 gp.
Three.

All right, let's start. Here's our card—the Devil's Emissary. I'll turn it and add two more cards. Now I'll shuffle them and move each of them to and fro, shuffle again, and which of them could it be? Is it still in the middle or is it on the left or perhaps on the right? Now, let's switch the side cards for the last time... and we're finished. Which of them is the Devil's Emissary? I'm sure you watched it vigilantly...
It's the third one.
Four.

All right, let's start. Here's our card—the Devil's Emissary. I'll turn it and add three more cards. Now I'll shuffle them and move each of them to and fro, switch the second and the third, shuffle again, and which of them could it be? Switch the third and the fourth... is it still on the left or on the right? Or perhaps one of those in the middle? What do you think? I'll shuffle the cards for the last time and here we go. Which of them is the Devil's Emissary? I'm sure you watched it vigilantly...
It's the fourth one.
Five.

All right, let's start. Here's our card—the Devil's Emissary. I'll turn it and add four more cards. I'll shuffle them just like that. See? Now let's move them around a bit, switch the first and the fifth, shuffle again. Where could that emissary be? Let's switch the second and the fourth and of course the third with the first... The last shuffle and last switching... and here we go. Which of them is the Devil's Emissary? I'm sure you watched it vigilantly...
It's the fifth one.
Yes I would like to hear the rules once more—just to be sure.

I'll draw several cards from the deck—the number depends on you, but five is the maximum. One of them always is the Devil's Emissary. Then I'll put the chosen cards face down on the table and will shuffle them just before your eyes. Well and your task is to guess which of them is the Devil's Emissary. The bet is always 10 gp; we can play with two, three, four or with five cards, so you can win 20 gp, 35 gp, 50 gp or 65 gp accordingly.
I'm sorry, knight, I won't play with you any further. You've cost me lots of money, so I will stay away from gambling for awhile. Is there anything else I can help you with?
I'll try another game. Let's go.
Excellent. The bet is 10 gp.
I'm sorry, knight, I can't play on. I've lost enough to stay away from gambling for some time. Goodbye.
I don't have enough money to continue.
In that case come when you have at least 10 gp, knight. Farewell.
I would like to change the number of cards.
As you wish, knight. How many cards would you like?
That's enough for now. But maybe I'll come another time. Farewell.
As you wish, knight. Farewell.
You're right, knight! You guessed it! Here's your 20 gp.

Well, I will try your famous goulash...
Great, knight. I'm sure you'll like it. Wait a moment—I'll be right back with it...
Here you go. Smells good, doesn't it? Dig in, knight, don't let it get cold. Bon appetit.
Thanks... tastes great. Can I ask you what's the recipe? I think that I've never tasted meat like that...
I'm sorry, but it's my secret. My culinary specialty—hope you understand. But on the second thought it's quite likely I might tell you one day. Who knows what will future bring us?
Yes, you're right. Thank you for the goulash. How much do I owe you?
Nothing, knight. The first serving is free; you know to make it easier for customers to decide if they should come back. Well, tell me if there's anything else I could do for you?
Actually, I'm not hungry at all.
I see, I won't insist. Maybe you'll change your mind later. How else could I be of service?
So you'd like to talk... What's the matter?
I'd like something to drink.
I'd like to play Devil's Emissary.
I'd like to see what you're selling.
Is there any truth to the rumors that people can get missing in your inn?

Hmmm, again those darn slurs?! I'm getting tired of them. I don't know who's spreading those lies, but I'm sure they want to ruin my honest business. They must be jealous so they are at least trying to compromise, calumniate, besmirch and to finally remove me. But that's not gonna happen, because as long as I live I'll provide my customers only with the best services.
I hope you don't listen to such mud-slingers, knight. A man like you surely knows what kinds of lies can people spread. Well, anyway, what about a plateful of goulash?
So it is true that you butcher people and cook their meat as if they were cattle...

Yes, you're right. But you have it wrong—people ARE cattle. They're just a herd waiting to be slaughtered. You can tell yourself how delicious goulash can be made of their meat. Take it as a proof that there's no other use for them. You must cut their throats, disembowel them, souse them like venison, and carve them—only then are they useful. Otherwise, they are useless...
Heinous cannibal!

You must be kidding me, knight. Even you would like to taste human meat, I'm sure of it. Why withholding the truth from people? Meat is meat! Forget about the morals—there's nothing like that in people. You can see for yourself—look around and tell me exactly where are the morals hiding? In the stomach? In the kidneys? In that pitiful little brain? No, knight, you can't find any morals, because there are none!
Enough blasphemy—you are coming with me!
And you know what—I'm not going. I've just invented a new delicious recipe. Paladin in wine. Yes, it's gonna be a luscious dish. I wonder if I'll be able to cook you well. I hope you'll be edible...
Stay away from me! Lay down that cleaver!
I'm sorry, knight, but I really need the cleaver. Otherwise I wouldn't be able to carve you!

I hope you'll stay overnight; our rooms are hospitable and cozy, you won't find any flea-ridden pallets there. And of course we will gladly provide you with food and drink—the best we have. I don't want to sound too boastful, but my meals are well known far and wide.
Are you the innkeeper?

I'm glad to see you again, knight. Hope you're back for a plateful of my delicious goulash.
I'm glad to see you again, knight. I'm sure you came to get a second helping of my excellent goulash, didn't you?
Yes, I would like your goulash. Last time it was really excellent!
Here you go, knight. I'm glad you like it.
Thank you. Could you share the recipe with me?
I'm sorry. But maybe the time will come when you'll get to know it. Is there anything else I could help you with?
No, I don't want your goulash.
No problem. How else could I then be of service?
Are you Bates the innkeeper? I hereby arrest you on the basis of justified suspicion for the murder of Ron Burton. You are coming with me to face a fair trial!
Yes, I'm Bates the innkeeper. And I suppose you are coming to arrest me—of course if it's not a stupid joke, right?
I assure you that I'm not joking. You're coming with me!
Why the hell should I? I've not committed any crime. Or is it a crime to slaughter cattle? Does it matter what kind of cattle you butcher—it's all the same: cow, calf, pig, shoat, lamb or human...
Bates the innkeeper, I hereby arrest you on the basis of justified suspicion for the murder of Ron Burton. You are coming with me to face a fair trial!
Well, knight. The problem is you did not want my delicious goulash. Otherwise you would have known that nothing beats soused human meat. Talking about Ron Burton—the man tasted great!

I don't say that it's the most interesting event of these days, but I was in Salena Flock's pub and I overheard a conversation between that odd trader Ihman ab Sahab and priest Gilbert. The trader was persuading the priest to get him a copy of the Legend of Saint Orthenius from the ancient Killian's Chronicle which is stored in the archiepiscopal archives.
Hmm.. thank you.

No problem, knight. I don't want to get involved, but I myself don't believe a single word Sahab utters. Did you know he comes from Jad-Habaal, the kingdom of pagan dogs? One would think that no pagan could set his dirty foot on the holy ground of our pious Realm and now there's one not only living, but also trading. Well, he's baptized, but anyway I don't believe him. There's a saying that a pagan will remain pagan till his death...
Well, pardon me, knight, but my memory has just failed me...
I'm not going to give you that much.
Well, it's gonna cost you $$getmoney10$$ gp.

Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert, who acts here as the royal governor. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. Grand Duke Drake Lambert is a very distinguished lord, very prudent, but also stern—but it's quite normal in higher ranking nobles. Grand Duke's worst weakness is his wife, Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. Well, the rumor is that she's... ehm... a slut. People say she's cheating on him and that she's insatiable as regards sexual pleasures. But it's his problem, not mine, right? Well, Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth is a very foppish and conceited dame. She would do anything to stop the time and prevent herself from aging. It's said that each new wrinkle makes her mad. That's why she remained single despite the efforts of her family. She didn't want to have any children so she could keep her youthful freshness...

Well, it depends on what you want to buy. Leon van den Brooks has a famous armory in Alvaron, so if you want some weapons or any armor pay him a visit. Well, I've heard that he's in some financial troubles, so his prices might be even more steep than usual. Apothecary Thelma Ulthraum and master alchemist Alberto Kelley can provide you with potions and various magic goods. Landlord William Burton and innkeeper Salena Flock sell just about everything. Well, then there's Bates the innkeeper and his King's Road Inn, but I would stay away from there, because of all the rumors surrounding his establishment.

The truth is people talk a lot about war. And there's more than talking—horses and drought animals are requisitioned, granaries are being filled, new recruits are conscripted... Still there's one thing missing—an enemy. You won't find anyone who could threaten the Realm and stand against his mighty royal armies in the field. It's really strange... I've recently seen the First Knight Rodrigo de Velacor several times and I can tell that his troubled face was quite unsettling. I'm sure you realize that after King Edward's death he's the supreme commander of the royal armies so he's likely to know more than the others...
What monster can you meet here in Alvaron?

Whatever quest brought you to Alvaron, knight, stay away from the cemetery—it's crawling with evil! And when I say evil, I mean real EVIL! Living dead are feasting on the graves and coffins at night, still night air is chilled by floating ghosts and dark shadows are stalked by nameless horrors. It's rumored that everybody who enters won't be seen again, unless as one of them...

Grand Duke Drake Lambert offered a huge reward for hunting down the werewolves who are pestering not only the woods around the city but unfortunately the city streets as well. The reward is paid by Sheriff Henry Portmann for every trophy, that means for every werewolf head. The highest reward will be paid for the head of wolf-prince Wulfhyrr himself, but who would be foolish enough to hunt down the werewolf leader, right? I think that the hunter would become his prey pretty fast...

The rumors that Christoffer de Malamert—the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous—is a heretic and a traitor are spreading among the people. It's said he's behind many heinous crimes—most importantly behind the murder of our King, Edward II. Moreover he has not been seen in public for some time, which only supports all the rumors. It's said that there is enough convincing evidence to arrest him at any moment.
I'm looking for a heretic cult named The Children of the New Order. Have you heard about it?
Well, to tell the truth I have a feeling that I might have heard somebody talking about that cult. But I don't recall who it was.
You better remember, for I've already paid you.
Yes, you're right. I think it was Downay the Gardener, that ugly midget who's wandering through the city streets—always drunk. Guess it was him, but I can't be completely sure.
Really, I'm not sure, knight. Well, perhaps I was drunk as well when I heard him... sorry.
Well, it's gonna cost you $$getmoney30$$ gp.

It's rumored that the paladin was charmed by a witch from Schwarzwald. People say her name's Corin, but I have no idea if it's her real name. Well, there's an interesting thing, there was another skirt wooing our paladin. Sandra Ullmann, a local stallholder. She's rather good-looking I must say, but the paladin refused her. But not because of celibacy or his holy mission—he refused her because of Corin. People say he wanted to leave the Brotherhood and wed Corin. So I think that maybe Sandra Ullmann could be behind the murder—there's nothing worse than a woman scorned...
I need to get a testimony from a dead person. I suppose you couldn't help me with that?

Well, I once heard Alberto Kelley, the master alchemist, talking about heretics who professedly can contact the Netherworld and make the dead talk. They use the other side of the Power, which offers possibilities undreamed of, but also paves the path to the scaffold—at least it's what he said. So I think that you might ask Kelley if you are interested in such things.
I need to get some information about this strange arrow. Could you help me with it?

Hmmm, doesn't ring the bell—I'm not very good with weapons. Well, try asking master smith Leon van den Brooks—I think it could be his work. Look at the arrowhead—it seems like very fine craftsmanship. By the way... whose blood is it? Oh... well, sorry for such a stupid question...
I'm looking for the murderer of His Highness Edward II. Do you happen to know any details about that crime?
Well, it's gonna cost you $$getmoney65$$ gp.

To tell the truth there are dozens of rumors concerning that murder spreading among the people, but I doubt any of them to be true. People often spin a yarn when they don't know what to do. Liar!
I'm not a liar, knight. It really happened as I've told you—I swear! Go ask Gilbert where he got that pouch. He's the heretic, not me!
Well, I believe you—at least for now. But be assured that I'm going to check your story...
Yes, please do it, knight. I'm really innocent. Well, I admit I stole the pouch, but divine providence punished me, so in fact I've already atoned for my sins.
Are you a beggar, good man?
Nope, I'm Saint Elizabeth! Do I look like a noble? Of course I'm a beggar, what have you thought? And by the way my name is Beckham—if you'd like to know...
I would like to have a little talk with you, good man.
Well, if you say so, knight. But it's going to cost you something... You know, I must earn my living.
Beckham? Were you named after that famous hero and lover of dames?
No the name Beckham is after my bloody grandfather—he was a fractious madcap. May black death get him for beating me when I was a little brat...
Oh, I see...
Oh!
Well, then accept this modest gift to help you in your unfortunate fate.

Sorry for bothering you, knight. Goodbye.
Well, here's something.
Thanks, knight! God bless you... I'll have a toast to your health! What can I do for you?

Well, pardon me, Father, but my memory has just failed me...

You came to kill me, didn't you? They sent you to find me and punish me for all my crimes. I know it, believe me—you are not the first one to try. What did they tell you about me? That I kill on sight? That I have no mercy? That my hands are stained with blood of countless men, women and children? They were right, soldier! Indeed, I killed multitudes of people without a single quiver of what you call humanity. But there is no other way. It's divine justice! And the only tool which can enforce it is might!
And what about right? And laws?

Right is powerless and dull. Laws are clumsy and judges are corruptible. But might is clear! Might is power that can shatter everything to dust! Blade of sword is above all laws and mighty arm is above all judges. Don't you understand it, soldier? You're a witness to so many crimes and still refrain from punishing them—don't you listen to the voice of God? Don't you hear Him crying at your every step? Life is a sin! Life is a fornication which intoxicates mankind and it's time to put an end to it! Don't you see that the Scourges of God were His sentence for the crime of living?
You can't be serious...

Can't I? Then why did my wife die—my young beautiful wife longing to live—and why did my wonderful children die? Because they sinned, soldier! They offended God by enjoying life and so he punished them. It was how the Lord showed me the right path! I became a soldier of divine justice, general of the army of the righteous! There are so many of us that we will soon be able to embark on a crusade against mankind! Against all mankind! We must kill them. We must burn them. Pig after pig. Cow after cow. Village after village. Army after army...
Enough! I won't listen to such madness! Life is the most precious gift God granted us. It's not a sin!

You are mistaken, soldier. You are blinded by your own sin. You must open your mind and your heart to hear the divine voice. He's talking all the time, you just need to listen. And as soon as you understand, it will strike you like a glistering diamond, like a brilliant of divine wisdom. You will understand that life—as you know it and live it—is a sin. We were not destined to live but to execute divine justice to each other. God was so kind to show us the way. The Scourges of God struck us so nobody could doubt divine justice. That which lives sins and must be punished. And we, the soldiers of divine justice, are here to punish them!
You are mad. I don't want to have anything to do with you. Goodbye.
Do you really think that... that life is a sin? That it's divine will to let them all die? I've never heard such opinion...

Yes, soldier, it is really so. Understand the truth and it will be as if you were imbued with the Holy Ghost. Understand and the manacles shackling you will break at once. It was the same with me when I was watching my family die—I understood. It was as if I was hit by a glistening diamond! Divine justice! Of course, life is a sin and God punishes us for it! I became His divine soldier. General of the Army of divine justice. We are many. And our numbers will grow. Every day more and more recruits come. I will build the army fearing no adversary. The army of soldiers knowing neither fear nor mercy. The army of soldiers deprived of all humanity. The humanity makes you imperfect and corrupt. You must shed your humanity and then you will truly become a soldier of divine justice!
That's... fascinating. I've never perceived life this way...

I've told you. When you understand it's as if you were struck by light... Join us, soldier. Become the executor of divine justice! Join the army of your equals and at last you will become really useful!
Yes, you're right. Life is a sin and that who lives should be punished!

Excellent, soldier. It seems you understood. But first you must prove that you are worthy to become a soldier of divine justice. You must shed your humanity and dispose of your emotions—pity, mercy, love, friendship, hatred, anger... You must become an executor of divine justice who is not hindered, neither by humanity nor by morals. Go and prove that you are able to do it. Go and bring me the head of Baroness Helen von Hunth, who is being held in my prison!
As you wish!
Wait a moment—I would never do anything like that! It's perverted!
Then you've sinned and I will execute your punishment. Defend yourself, soldier!
It's madness! Somebody must stop you!
Benthley of Welshrem, I came to bring you justice for murdering Lothard Luisse's mother and sisters!

I've performed many deeds in the name of divine justice—you may consider them murders—but I didn't kill Lothard Luisse's mother and sisters. Lothard Luisse is my lieutenant in the army of divine justice—he has never seen his mother and he has no sisters!
You're lying and it proves your guilt! I'm going to send you to face divine justice, sinner!

You leave me no other option!
You must be mad!
Once I observed a snail slithering along a blade of a sharp razor... That's my dream... And my nightmare...

Then I choose death. Though it won't be me who will soon be judged by God!

I'm sorry for the death of the ones you loved, but you can't ascribe such mad motives to our Lord!
Their death was a sign, soldier! Only a blind man can say it was not a sign from above! My eyes saw it so clearly, as blind Peolius did when the First prophet restored his sight!
I've been waiting for you, soldier. Come closer, so I can see you better. I want to see the face of my killer.
You are Benthley of Welshrem, right?

No, I am not. That name is no longer mine. Perhaps I used it once, but it was a long time ago. Names have no meaning. Only deeds do. Benthley of Welshrem is dead. Now a divine soldier stands here! A divine soldier does not need names, although he is given many.
Why have you said that you're waiting for me?
Who are you?
Names have no meaning. Only deeds do.
Were you always nameless?

No, once I had a name. A long time ago. Benthley of Welshrem... it was my name. But the person of that name is dead. Now a divine soldier stands here! A divine soldier does not need names, although he is given many.
I'm not a soldier...
We are all soldiers of divine justice when we have weapons in our hands, soldier! It doesn't matter who we are or who we think we are.
So, soldier. Do you have the head of Baroness Helen von Hunth? Were you able to shed your shackling humanity? Have you awakened?
Yes, general—here's her head. I'm waiting for your orders!

Indeed you did it... Now you are the soldier of divine justice! But it's not me who will give you orders! Only God commands us to do what we must do in His name. Go and pursue your holy quest for which you were chosen. Know that life is a sin and that who lives must be reformed! To help you in your holy quest take this sacred relic which will help you enforce divine justice when facing the mightiest of foes.
Thanks. Could I ask you a few questions?
Talking detains you, soldier. You have your duty! Go and perform divine justice.
Thanks. Goodbye.
Now when my task is finished, it's your turn Benthley of Welshrem. God requests your life!
Do you really feel that way? Then let's match our might so we can see whose life God requests in His infinite righteousness. Defend yourself, soldier!
No, I don't have the head of Baroness Helen von Hunth—yet.
Don't hesitate, soldier. You must prove that you are able to shed your humanity!
Sure. Could I ask you a few questions?
I won't disappoint you. Goodbye.
I've decided not to commit that crime! Instead, I'm going to send your soul to face divine justice!
Really? Then let's match our might so we can see whose life God requests in His infinite righteousness. Defend yourself, soldier!
I'm not going to do the task. I've decided to save the Baroness and bring her back to her husband.

Then you've failed me, soldier. A grave failure, indeed. It seems that you have not understood what it means to perform divine justice. I will have to redeem you of your sins. Defend yourself, soldier!
I'm not going to do the task. I've decided to save the Baroness and bring her to soldier Harph.
What do you need, soldier?
I would like to have a little talk with you.
Nothing. Just passing by. I should be on my way.
Go, soldier. And don't forget that your quest is to spread divine justice!
I want to bring you justice, Benthley of Welshrem. It's your turn, God requests your life!
Are you trying to steal, soldier?! You wanted to enrich yourself at the expense of others. Remember that theft is a crime as well as desire for riches. Your life is forfeit!
Nostrus Bhelfelix! Wuestrus da marghot morthum!
No matter what you say, foul demon, my answer will always be the same—I'll send you back to burning hell! God save us from the monsters of the ancient times!
Go back where you came from this instant, demon!
Nostrus Bhellfelix! Wuestrus da marghot morthum!
Then I'll send you there myself! God save us from the monsters of the ancient times!
I'm Ghorth-Baghor, guard of the God Bhelfelix. You are going to die for daring to touch him without my permission, mortal.
No foul, abhorrent monster is to threaten me with death. I'll send you back to burning hell where you belong!
You're going to pay for your impudence, mortal! You're going to die!!!
Wait Ghorth-baghor, I didn't mean to offend you. I brought a statue of your god to one of the Bhelfelix's cult priests!
You're lying and I'll punish you for your insolence! You're going to die!
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. I'll leave immediately!
You're not going to leave alive, mortal. Only death can redeem the disgrace of touching God Bhelfelix! You're going to die!!!
If Hulph Rechtzwurther's map is correct, there should be a treasure of the barbarian priests of the Bhelfelix's cult somewhere here.

Yes! I found it! Oh, my God... Look at all the gold and the gemstones! But where's the statue cardinal Severtinus wanted from me? Oh, here it is. By the Saint Eleiah, it's gross! Whatever, I'll just get it and leave.
Weird... Why is it so cold here all of the sudden? By Saint Ludmila... am I having delusions or is it fog rising from the ground? Oh god... This isn't fog, it's ghosts! The First Prophet save me!!!

This was all for the moment... However, my task hasn't been finished yet. The remains of all of the innocent victims of Blutereich's terror must be buried in a grave!

I came to free this house of the evil which resides here!
