I came to remove your curse, Baron von Blutenreich. I'm giving you an opportunity to leave this world!

My house is my world; I am the lord and the ruler here. And you are an intruder who has no right to be here. You are going to be punished for trespassing—you set your foot where you were not supposed to be!
The atrocities that were happening in this God-forgotten place! The terrible crimes done here! The culprit must be punished. This goes beyond human understanding!
You can almost hear the weeping of the women and the children who were tortured to death here, and buried in unholy graves without a proper funeral...
I came to free this house of the gold which resides here! Erm... I wanted to say of the EVIL!
Who isss it? A fresssh meat? I haven't bathed in the human blood for a long time. I'd love to feel the blissss again! Come closssser, mortal. I wasss looking forward to thisss moment!
Who are you, infernal monster?! What unholy powers have brought you to this world. You're not supposed to be here!

You're wrong, human. I came here to do what I had ssssworn before I died. There were ssssix men responsible for my exxxecution. Five of them are already rotting in the ground asss I had done before I returned. I'm Issstwan de Bragho and I came to try those who had tried me. The time of my revenge hasss come!
I will not let you, monster! I'll send your soul back to the burning hell where it came from uninvited.
You're sssso pathetic, mortal! Nobody can kill me. Nobody can sssstand between a revenant and hisss victim; nobody! And anybody who triess—diess. Jusssst like you!
Sssee, mortal? You cannot kill me. Nobody can asss long asss my victimsss live! Hahaaaaa!
We'll see, devil!
You're wrong! The holy water will strip you of your immortality! In the name of omnipotent God I sanctify your body so it can find peace in its grave forever.
No! You can't! No... I cursssse you! I cursssse you a thoussssand timesss, mortal! Nooooo!
Amen!
Who's the ruler of Glatzburg and the surrounding lands?

Glatzburg and the surrounding domains are ruled by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick who is the royal governor of the city. He's important, knight. The Heidrick family is one of the ancient families who were supposed to be here when the Realm was founded. The vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin. He claims his family to be ancient as well but it is probably not the case. His status comes mostly from the money his grandfather made by business. And Duke Heidrick is a pain in Leerin's neck—he thinks he should be the governor and not Heidrick. You know politics—it's crap. God knows there's nothing like being an honest beggar.
Then I'm really sorry, knight. My memory's as bad as my teeth...
Where can I get some supplies here in Glatzburg?

It depends on what you wanna buy, knight. If you need weapons, armor and things like that go to Hans von Drichtmaul's armor shop. At the seeres Enrie Jungwirdt's and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus's places you can get potions and all kinds of magic stuff. The tavern owner Wanda Gielwitch and the innkeeper Ludwig sell all sorts of things. And Alphons DiCerbio will barter anything as long as you don't care where it came from.
That will cost you $$getmoney20$$ gp.

I think that this crisis is a real pain. Couple years ago one would think that nothing like that could ever happen and puff—here it is. I tell you something, knight, life never was a rose garden, definitely not. But the things that are happening now are beyond all the ideas of hell I ever had. Soon devils will be running in the streets fornicating with us like at the judgment day and we'll have hell on Earth. But I know exactly who's behind all this!
Really? Who?

The heretics, knight! It was them who started to worship Satan and his servants so they could enjoy their despicable pleasures. They have poisoned the minds of people and plagued the country with apostasy! It was because of them that God turned away from us and punished us by disasters. It's a punishment for running away from his herd! And the worst thing is that you can never be sure who is a heretic and who's not. There's no way to tell. I always thought they looked like wild beasts with shaggy hair and beards, dirty nails and the look of a lunatic... But It's the other way around. People say that the nobility, the townspeople and—oh my god—even the clerics are joining heretic cults! How else could it end than in a disaster. And it will end in a disaster, knight, believe me. Because since I can remember, nothing has ever ended well.
Hmm... And do you suspect anyone in particular? Your testimony could be very valuable.

Um... sorry, knight, but I don't know anything about any suspicion. And even if I did, I'd keep it to myself because I like my head to stay right where it is now. You must understand, knight, that if they find a miserable beggar with his throat cut open in a gutter, nobody makes much fuss about it...
All right, thank you.
I heard that there is a war coming. Have you heard anything about it?
Maybe I have. It depends whether you are willing to pay $$getmoney25$$ gp.

You heard right when you heard about the war. They talk about it a lot amongst the royal garrison. They are worried, that's understandable. Nobody knows any details but it's not hard to guess that something's about to happen. The whole Glatzburg regiment is on standby. They take new recruits, requisition horses and cattle... And besides all this Rodrigo de Velacor, the First Knight and the Royal Marshal, is coming to Glatzburg. Innkeeper Weintraum is anxious about that because Duke Velacor is probably going to stay at his inn. This doesn't look good at all.

And the biggest mystery is who is the damn war going to be against. There's chaos everywhere, the heretics show their asses at every corner, the demons and beasts feed on everyone they see—or at least they tear their hands off; and their legs and balls—but this isn't something you could send an army against, is it? The Pagans from the far east stay at a respectful distance—why would they come here anyway with all the shit that's going on here—and there's no other enemy. I think there's politics behind it.
What monsters and devils can be encountered here?
Interesting question. It will cost you $$getmoney20$$ gp, if you are interested.

I'm no expert in monsters and other stinking devilish minions around Glatzburg or in the Realm. I think you should try to ask Sheriff Smith or, even better, one of the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous. They are always out on their quests so they have a good grasp. If I should speak for myself I must say that Glatzburg is not safe. At night there are undead appearing in the streets, knight! Living corpses, abhorrent zombies, damn returnees, revenants... They just appear out of nowhere, stagger in the streets and God save those who they come across. Not even the watchers dare to show up even when there's less than a dozen of them. And nobody knows where they come from—they simply appear in the streets and with the dawn they disappear again. Who would follow them when people are scared like shit.
Are there any rewards offered here in Glatzburg for killing monsters?
Maybe there is, maybe not. If you give me $$getmoney10$$ gp, I might recall something.

Grand Duke Heidrick offered a reward for hunting down the rogues who rob people on the roads. He thought it would chase them away from the vicinity of the city but from what I've heard nobody's too interested in the rewards. It's easier to rob somebody than to catch the robbers. But if you ever captured a villain just bring his head to Sheriff Smith and the reward in gold is yours.
I'm looking for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone? Have you heard anything?

Uh-oh, heresy? I don't wanna have anything to do with it, I don't wanna end up at a stake or eating hospital food. Sorry, knight, but this isn't something I would wanna talk about—even if I knew something. I'd rather bite my tongue off than get into some kind of trouble...
Have you by any chance heard about a heretic cult called The Children of the New Order?
Maybe. It depends whether you are willing to pay $$getmoney25$$ gp.

Nope, never heard about any Children of the New Order. I don't suppose there's anyone like that in the city. Or they are well hidden so they don't make a party talk. That's quite possible. But anyway, I've never heard of them.
Has anything worth mentioning happened in Glatzburg lately?

Do you know Francessca Gulvardi, knight? She's a nice girl, pleasure to look at. Really pretty I must say. She's one of our Grand Duke's servants. Well, she was—until that thing happened. She tried to kill bishop Trevorius, can you believe it?! It was right in the church in the middle of confessionals! She hurled herself at him like some kind of wild beast, probably wanted to dismember him with her teeth. The bishop, fortunately, is no wisp, so he could deal with her, with all his luck, however. Francessca has been held in the local jail since. They say she's possessed by an unholy spirit, an incubus or something. She must be totally out of her mind. How dreadful!
I'm investigating the assassination of bishop Trevorius. Do you know anything about it?
Maybe. It depends whether you are willing to pay $$getmoney30$$ gp for the information.

It's a tragedy, the death of our bishop, I mean. He was a good and decent person. He wouldn't give any alms but at the big religious holidays he would throw a feast where everybody could get a good dinner. Now that he's gone the archbishop will definitely put some ogre in the place, I bet. About the murder... the strange thing is that it was a second attempt in such a short time. There are many people who think that there is a connection between the two attacks. After it didn't work out with the girl—Francessca Gulvardi—they tried again. And this time, unfortunately, they were successful...
Who do you think is behind the murder?

Who? Well, that's a difficult question. It could have been the heretics 'cause the bishop was a pious person, did everything to spread the faith—and he was successful in that. But then, one would think, if it was the heretics, why didn't they kill someone from the Inquisition? Like Judge Welfhar—he's sent so many of them to the stake that the potential avengers would make a long line. It's simply a mystery...

It's a tragedy, the death of our bishop I mean. He was a good and decent person. He wouldn't give any alms but at the big religious holidays he would throw a feast where everybody could get a good dinner. Now that he's gone the archbishop will definitely put some ogre in the place, I bet. But to the point... To tell the truth, there are many people who think it was you. Well, don't be surprised... the rumors spread quickly. They say they found you bent over the bishop's corpse before it had the time to stiffen. I'd be careful if I were you. You know what they say: Ubi suspicio, ibi etiam argumenta—where there is suspicion there is evidence.
I'm looking for the tomb of an Elenian noble named Fae'Darlion. Do you have any idea where it could be?

Of course I don't know anything about the tomb, I'm not a treasure hunter or an adventurer, but I've heard that most of the Elenian—whomever they were—things were found in the woods around the Hunth family house. So you might be able to find your tomb there...
Do you know anything confidential about Father Frederick?
Maybe. It depends whether you are willing to pay $$getmoney20$$ gp for the information.

I remember him well enough even though there wasn't really anything exceptional about him. He was an elderly priest, skinny as a goat, but his sight was so penetrating that when he looked at you, you had to cast down your eyes and go to the confession because you suddenly remembered all your sins. I also heard he used to be an exorcist. But I don't think he has been performing any exorcisms recently. He was little too old for another skirmish with the devil. He died two years ago when there was the plague epidemic. Just like many other people of different ages and statuses...
I heard there were some undead wandering around the streets at the night. Is it true?
Maybe. It depends whether you are willing to pay $$getmoney50$$ gp for the information

Yes, you heard correctly, knight. There really are zombies appearing at night and hurling themselves at anyone they come across during their bloody riots in the streets. And before dawn they disappear as mysteriously as they appeared after sundown—it's as if they returned to hell they came from. You can certainly imagine the panic spreading among the people in the city. Nobody dares enter the city at sundown. They're afraid they might be the next victim of the rage of those undead monsters...
And how about the city guards? Why don't they do anything about it?

Sheriff Smith and his men were trying to, but a lot of them suffered a very unpleasant death. It's no pleasure to be torn to pieces by a zombie. And there was no outcome anyway—the zombies they killed one night reappeared the second night. So they gave up and now they only guard the most important buildings and people in the city. Somebody should do something about it...
And where do these living corpses come from, anyway? Hasn't anybody ever seen them materializing?

No, knight. I personally think there is some connection with the legends of the ancient sewers under the city. I don't know whether you heard about it but there is a rumor saying that there is a sewer dungeon underneath the city. It was probably built by the Erebornian captives right after the city was founded. It was the time when Ereborn was defeated and Saint Orthenius would beat seven shades out of the pagans. That's when Glatzburg was founded and they used the pagan captives to build an orthodox city.
So the sewers are still here?

Well... Nobody knows. The thing is that before a century passed everything touched by the pagans was being destroyed and rebuilt again—supposedly because of the purity of the faith. The sewers being an invention of the pagans were filled up, the canals and the entrances walled in and there went all the fun... and the hygiene. All kinds of crap has been lying scattered on the streets since then and nobody's doing anything about it. But the sewers... well, everybody thought that they have been buried for good and don't exist anymore, not even in the minds of the people. But I know of at least a dozen of holes the rats run to when something is going on. I was investigating the local junkyard the other day and I came across a strange opening leading deep under the ground. So I think the sewers underneath the city still exist and the zombies found an asylum there. From there they crawl up every night to kill...
Thank you. Your information was very interesting.
You're welcome, knight.
No problem, knight
Somebody's stolen Knight Commander Ethien de Pasque's Chain of the Brotherhood. Do you know anything about it?

I know nothing about the commander's Chain of the Brotherhood. That means I didn't steal it, I promise and God is my witness. But if I were you I'd ask performer Tinthan—he can steal the nose from between your eyes without you noticing. I wouldn't be surprised if stealing a chain of a knight from the Brotherhood of the Righteous who are known for persecuting the criminals was his work.
I'm investigating the disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch. Do you know anything about her?

I heard she was missing together with few other girls. I believe they were all virgins—which is significant for our times, if I can say it that way. I remember hearing the trickster DiCerbio with some other regulars talking about the virginity of the local girls and women in Wanda Gielwitch's tavern... But it probably doesn't have to do anything with your problem. I myself get involved in such discussions now and then, heh-heh.

You've been extremely helpful and that's why I'll tell you everything you might find useful. I was in a tavern the other night and I heard undertaker Dietrich boasting that he knew exactly who was behind all the evil things happening in Glatzburg. It was supposed to be someone of high status but he didn't want to say who because then he'd have to be hiding for the rest of his life!
Well... thanks for the information, good man.
I am a humble servant of God, valiant knight, the humblest of all!
Now I would like to ask you a few questions if I can.
But of course, knight. For a little gold I will tell you anything you'd like to know...
Very well. I finished my job and I'll get going. And next time be more careful about your belongings—and you debts as well.
I'm going to, valiant knight, I promise. Goodbye.

Knight, give a little gold to a poor, tormented soul. I'm a humble servant of God, the humblest of all. All my life I've been living in accordance with the commandment of Saint Baudolinus—be modest so there's more left for those who need it. I humbly lower my head before God Almighty and the Brotherhood of the Righteous—eternal glory to the Grand Master De Malamert and all his brothers...
What is your name?
Braham, knight. Braham of Ullstadt, that's my name.
Braham of Ullstadt? Are you a noble?

Oh no, knight. They started to call me that when I was a little kid because they found me at the gate of Ullstadt. I don't even know who my goddamn parents were, they left me bare naked on the street and didn't care whether wild dogs ate me...
Have you always lived by begging? Never tried to work?

And who'd give me work, knight? Who would trust a tramp and a beggar? Once you are a hobo everybody closes their door. They'd rather give you a coin than having to watch out for you if you are not stealing anything. And you can swear by the name of Saint Baudolinus and by all the angels that there are in the heaven, and it still doesn't move anyone. That is the fate God has chosen for me and I'm trying to live in accord with that. So if you could spare a coin, I'd be grateful...
Take these alms, Braham. Use it wisely.

Thank you very, very much, valiant knight! But wait a moment. I wanted to ask you something. I couldn't have missed that you're a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous... You see to the assertion of justice in the Realm and such, don't you?
Yes, that's right. Why are you asking?
I know I'm just a beggar but anyway... I'm a victim of a crime and I seek justice!
What kind of crime? What's happened to you?
I have been robbed, valiant knight! Robbed in full daylight! And nobody did anything to help me!
What did they steal from you, good man? You don't seem to have much...

They stole my silver amulet. I had it since I was little. They found it on me at the gate of Ullstadt where my parents left me as soon as I was born. It's a magic amulet which protects me against all the evil of this world. It must have been sanctified by the Saint Baudolinus personally, I'm sure about that!
And who stole it from you?

It was the bitch, Wanda Gielwitch! Or, to be precise, one of her bullies who knock out all your teeth before you have the time to say "sorry". He came to me and before I could say anything I was lying in the mud and the lout was walking away with my amulet. But I'm not going to leave it that way. I want it back because it's mine. I know my rights, really!
I can help you, good man. I'll bring your amulet back.
Really? Then I'd be really grateful, valiant knight!
All right, all right. Now, can you answer a few questions for me?
Whatever you wish, knight. For a little gold I'm gonna tell you what you need to know. I know the city and the people in it pretty well, really!
Goodbye, valiant knight. And thanks for promising to bring back my amulet. The bitch Gielwitch cannot get the idea that she can get away with anything just because... because... well, really.
What can you offer for my help?
Well... I don't have much, but I know the city like the palm of my hand. So if you need some information, I could recall many things. And for a reasonable price, really!
I'm sorry, I can't distract myself with trivialities like that. I have an important mission.
Ah, understood. Well, what can one do.
I need to talk to you for a moment. Could you answer a few questions?
Whatever you wish, knight. For a little gold, of course. You know, my memory needs a little stimulation, really!
Goodbye, valiant knight. God bless you for your helpfulness, really!
I'm sorry, I don't have time right now. Goodbye.
Well, goodbye, knight. I was thinking... well... nevermind, really.
I'm not giving you any alms, Braham. You're not a friar or a victim of an accident or of a misfortune. You are responsible for your situation. Goodbye.
Well... then... goodbye, knight. And live happily as long as you have something to live on.
Hello, valiant knight. How about my silver amulet. Did you get it from that bitch Wanda Gielwitch?
No, not yet, good man. Be patient.
All right, knight. I hope you are successful. Is there anything I can do for you?
I'd like to talk to you about something.
But of course, valiant knight. What do you need to know. For a little gold I will tell you anything, really!

I didn't. And to tell you the truth, I probably never will. Wanda Gielwitch admitted she sent one of her bullies to take it from you, but she only did it to have an enormous debt you have with her paid up. Is that true?
Well, if you wanna hear it, yes, it's true. I am in debt with her. Are you happy now? But it doesn't change the fact, that she has taken my amulet!
She did but she had the right to do it. Pay off your debts and she will give it back.
I knew it was going to end like this—she shook her boobs in front of you and you changed your mind immediately, right? Well, whatever, just get yourself going, I'm not interested in your preaching!
Not so fast. I wanna ask you some questions.
Well, if it has to be... But it will cost you some gold, remember that! My memory's not what it used to be...
Be careful, what you're saying. You might be sorry for that later!
But I... well... I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you, valiant knight. I'm just a meek servant of God, really... Farewell, knight.
Farewell. And repent of your sins, sinner!
Farewell and God bless you, knight!
I didn't bring your amulet, good man. But I promised Wanda Gielwitch, that I would pay off you debts she took the amulet for.

You... you found out? That she took it because of the money I owed. Well... I could have expected that... Thank you very much, valiant knight. I didn't want to lie to you but the amulet is the most precious thing I've ever had...
I figured that out. That's why I agreed to pay off you debt. As soon as I get the money, I'll bring you back your amulet.
Thank you, valiant knight. I'm forever indebted to you, really!
In that case, will you answer a few questions, good man?
I'd be happy to, knight. I'm ready!
Yes, I brought your the amulet. Here it is.

Oh my God, it is my amulet! You did it, valiant knight! I wish I could have seen the Gielwitch bitch, when you were taking it from her. She must have been shaking with anger. But it serves her right, bitch. Thank you once more, knight.
You're welcome...
Hello, knight. Could I possibly ask you whether you have paid off my damn debt to Wanda Gielwitch and brought back my amulet?
Yes, good man, your debt has been paid off and here is your amulet.
Oh my God, it really is my amulet! You did it, valiant knight! Thank you very much. I'll be extremely careful never to lose it because of drinking again!
That would be wise...
No, good man. I'm not bringing the amulet yet.
Nevermind. I'm sure you will bring it next time. What can a poor beggar do for you?
I'd like you to give me some answers, good man.
Whatever you wish, valiant knight. You wouldn't mind giving a little gold for my answers, would you?!
Hello, revered knight. What can an old beggar like me do for you?
I'd like to speak with you for a moment.
As you wish, valiant knight. You will definitely find me useful, really...
Nothing, just a mistake. Goodbye.
Hello, valiant knight. What can I do for you?
Whatever you wish, valiant knight. I'll be happy to tell you anything you'd like to know.
Nothing today, good man. Goodbye.
Do you have any idea, where I could find the residence of rogue knight Benthley of Welshrem?
Maybe. It depends whether you are ready to pay $$getmoney500$$ gp.

If you are looking for the residence of rogue knight Benthley of Welshrem you've come across the right person. I was there once! You can find it in the deep woods near the Von Hunth's residence and you can get there by an almost invisible pathway from the Royal road. I'll show you on the map where it is—right here, see? But be careful—it's a well protected place!

Glatzburg and the surrounding domains are ruled by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick who is the royal governor of the city. He's important, noble sir. The Heidrick family is one of the ancient families who were supposed to be here when the Realm was founded. The vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin. He claims his family to be ancient as well but it is probably not the case. His status comes mostly from the money his grandfather made by business. And Duke Heidrick is a pain in Leerin's neck—he thinks he should be the governor and not Heidrick. You know politics—it's crap. God knows there's nothing like being an honest beggar.
Then I'm really sorry, noble sir. My memory's as bad as my teeth...

It depends on what you wanna buy, noble sir. If you need weapons, armor and things like that go to Hans von Drichtmaul's armor shop. At the seeres Enrie Jungwirdt's and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus's places you can get potions and all kinds of magic stuff. The tavern owner Wanda Gielwitch and the innkeeper Ludwig sell all sorts of things. And Alphons DiCerbio will barter anything as long as you don't care where it came from.

I think that this crisis is a real pain. Couple years ago one would think that nothing like that could ever happen and puff—here it is. I tell you something, noble sir, life never was a rose garden, definitely not. But the things that are happening now are beyond all the ideas of hell I ever had. Soon devils will be running in the streets fornicating with us like at the judgment day and we'll have hell on Earth. But I know exactly who's behind all this!

The heretics, noble sir! It was them who started to worship Satan and his servants so they could enjoy their despicable pleasures. They have poisoned the minds of people and plagued the country with apostasy! It was because of them that God turned away from us and punished us by disasters. It's a punishment for running away from his herd! And the worst thing is that you can never be sure who is a heretic and who's not. There's no way to tell. I always thought they looked like wild beasts with shaggy hair and beards, dirty nails and the look of a lunatic... But It's the other way around. People say that the nobility, the townspeople and—oh my god—even the clerics are joining heretic cults! How else could it end than in a disaster. And it will end in a disaster, noble sir, believe me. Because since I can remember, nothing has ever ended well.

Um... sorry, noble sir, but I don't know anything about any suspicion. And even if I did, I'd keep it to myself because I like my head to stay right where it is now. You must understand, noble sir, that if they find a miserable beggar with his throat cut open in a gutter, nobody makes much fuss about it...

I'm no expert in monsters and other stinking devilish minions around Glatzburg or in the Realm. I think you should try to ask Sheriff Smith or, even better, one of the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous. They are always out on their quests so they have a good grasp. If I should speak for myself I must say that Glatzburg is not safe. At night there are undead appearing in the streets, noble sir! Living corpses, abhorrent zombies, damn returnees, revenants... They just appear out of nowhere, stagger in the streets and God save those who they come across. Not even the watchers dare to show up even when there's less than a dozen of them. And nobody knows where they come from—they simply appear in the streets and with the dawn they disappear again. Who would follow them when people are scared like shit.

Uh-oh, heresy? I don't wanna have anything to do with it, I don't wanna end up at a stake or eating hospital food. Sorry, noble sir, but this isn't something I would wanna talk about—even if I knew something. I'd rather bite my tongue off than get into some kind of trouble...

Do you know Francessca Gulvardi, noble sir? She's a nice girl, pleasure to look at. Really pretty I must say. She's one of our Grand Duke's servants. Well, she was—until that thing happened. She tried to kill bishop Trevorius, can you believe it?! It was right in the church in the middle of confessionals! She hurled herself at him like some kind of wild beast, probably wanted to dismember him with her teeth. The bishop, fortunately, is no wisp, so he could deal with her, with all his luck, however. Francessca has been held in the local jail since. They say she's possessed by an unholy spirit, an incubus or something. She must be totally out of her mind. How dreadful!

Yes, you heard correctly, noble sir. There really are zombies appearing at night and hurling themselves at anyone they come across during their bloody riots in the streets. And before dawn they disappear as mysteriously as they appeared after sundown—it's as if they returned to hell they came from. You can certainly imagine the panic spreading among the people in the city. Nobody dares enter the city at sundown. They're afraid they might be the next victim of the rage of those undead monsters...

No, noble sir. I personally think there is some connection with the legends of the ancient sewers under the city. I don't know whether you heard about it but there is a rumor saying that there is a sewer dungeon underneath the city. It was probably built by the Erebornian captives right after the city was founded. It was the time when Ereborn was defeated and Saint Orthenius would beat seven shades out of the pagans. That's when Glatzburg was founded and they used the pagan captives to build an orthodox city.
You're welcome, noble sir.
No problem, noble sir

I know nothing about the commander's Chain of the Brotherhood. That means I didn't steal it, I promise and God is my witness. But if I were you I'd ask performer Tinthan, he can steal the nose from between your eyes without you noticing. I wouldn't be surprised if stealing a chain of a knight from the Brotherhood of the Righteous who are known for persecuting the criminals was his work.
I am a humble servant of God, noble sir, the humblest of all!

Braham, noble sir. Braham of Ullstadt, that's my name.

Oh no, noble sir. They started to call me that when I was a little kid because they found me at the gate of Ullstadt. I don't even know who my goddamn parents were, they left me bare naked on the street and didn't care whether wild dogs ate me...

And you can swear by the name of Saint Baudolinus and by all the angels that there are in the heaven, and it still doesn't move anyone. That is the fate God has chosen for me and I'm trying to live in accord with that. So if you could spare a coin, I'd be grateful...

Do you have any idea where soldier Jullian could be hiding?

I've never liked Jullian. He's cute, that I must admit, but he has never cared for anything but my property. He was courting me, you know. It's been some time now but I haven't forgiven him yet. What a nerve, trying to get rich through my skirt. No wonder that he's deserted. He had no disposition to become a good soldier. He joined the army because he thought it meant receiving a good mercenary pay for doing nothing. What a fool!

What do I think about all the evil things that have been happening to us in the past few years? I don't know, knight... I'm desperate. Business is terrible. They should seize them and burn them all, as soon as possible!

Sheriff Contemburry offers rewards in gold for every orcish scalp or head you bring him. But even though the reward is pretty high for our measures, there haven't been too many of them paid out. Many of those who went for an orc hunt to get rich, haven't returned.

Hillbrandt and the surrounding lands are ruled by Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. The vice governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. About Duke Weinberg, I can't say anything other than that he's a noble and classy gentleman who's good at governing the town. But Baron Robert van Gallagan is a sissy who lets his wife Linda rule instead.
I heard that master Edmond d'Arvias is a heretic suspect. What do you think about it?

I heard that lunatic Thomas Reitdorf saying that he'd seen master Edmond d'Arvias letting the orcs into the town during their last attack on Hillbrandt. I don't know if it's true but I'm still shaking when I'm reminded of the greenoes—I saw them from my window running around the town and killing everyone they saw. It was horrible. If it was Edmond d'Arvias's work he should be locked up and executed as soon as possible...
The monstrance of Saint Orthenius was stolen, do you know anything about it?

I heard somebody broke into the church and stole the monstrance. They didn't leave any tracks. The priests who were guarding the monstrance that night were found deeply asleep among the pews. The thief must have used some unclean powers to overcome the priests and get the monstrance. What are we going to do without it?
Do you know anything about the disappearance of bishop Quentinus?
They say bishop Quentinus disappeared during the attack of the greenoes on the town. Nobody's seen him since. He was probably killed by the orcs and his body trashed somewhere. Terrible fate!
Do you happen to know anything about Paul Hammerhand being missing?

Paul Hammerhand is the wildest brat I've ever seen in my life. You wouldn't believe he's a son of smith Victor Hammerhand. He was left a widower when Paul was only a boy and obviously wasn't able to bring him up properly. Paul became a rogue with no respect for anything. He's an obstinate lout and runs away from home. You know, to tell you the truth, there was a time when I was interested in Victor. He would make a good match—he has a well established trade, makes good money... But that brat Paul totally put me off. When I realized I'd have to be his mother I changed my mind. And I'm happy for it. Look at Paul now—he's growing up for the scaffold. You say he's been missing again? That's like him. He got into a trouble somewhere. He's always sticking his nose in where he's not supposed to.
Do you know anything about the disappearance of Linda van Gallagan?

What a nerve, doubting the quality of what I sell. What do you think, knight?
What do you think of the murder of Natalia Reichmann, which is supposed to have been done by landsknecht Olfghard?

And the scum Olfghard—let his soul burn in hell—killed her for a little jewelry. Could you believe he tried to sell it to me? As soon as I found out whose jewels they were I went to Sheriff Contemburry and told him. Olfghard was immediately detained and it looked like he would be sentenced soon but the rogue managed to escape. I hope they will capture him soon and execute him. That's what he deserves!

Do you know any details about it?

Well... I've heard that they found him with his throat cut. There were gallons of blood. And they also cut off his... well... genitals, and shoved it up his mouth. From that I would guess it was done by one of those succubus, who fornicate at night with men and do all kinds of perverted stuff as well...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick of Glatzburg is looking for a wife and you are single, aren't you?

His ex-wife has met her maker.
Ah, well it makes more sense now, but if you thought that I and the Duke... that's nonsense, knight. A duke wouldn't marry a simple stallholder. It's a nonsense—no offence.

It's supposed to be a treasure of immeasurable value which would make anyone, who finds it, stinking rich. Lots of people tried looking for it but nobody was successful. They say it's hard to find because it's well hidden and because it's protected by a terrible pagan curse!

Interesting. Do you believe in astrology?

Of course. You don't? Astrology is a science like any other, it has its own rules and all manner of secrets, which a man can reveal and through understanding them he can come to a deeper knowledge of space and of the world around us. It is not my problem that the church doctrine hasn't fully reconciled modern observation of the space bodies positions and their influence on human beings yet. We live in revolutionary times. Old dogmas collapse and new directions, working with the scientific knowledge, are emerging. Astrology allows us to understand the influence of space on the events in the surrounding world. Each movement of any space body is projecting to the processes here, in our kingdom and in the whole world. It is wise to examine these influences and to use them.
Why exactly do you deal with alchemy? Isn't it too dangerous?

Dangerous? What do you mean? Oh so... you mean the cases of those alchemists who were convicted of heresy and of invocations of hellspawns. I can say only one thing to that matter—there is a substantial difference between alchemy and black magic. But I can't exclude that someone will start practicing both. In that case it is my duty to search out and remedy such a mountebank. But anyone who obeys the strict rules of the Royal Alchemist Guild cannot be accused of sorcery not even with a single word. And that's right in my case.
Do you think God exists?
If God exists? What kind of question is that, knight?! Of course God exists!
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of St. Orthenius' monstrance?
I am sorry, but I don't know anything about the St. Orthenius' monstrance theft. However, I have heard it disappeared.

You ask me what do I think about the events that have been happening in our Realm since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky? I'm not a theologist, knight, so I'm not able to tell whether it is a sign of the End of the World, or it isn't. In my opinion people believe too much in what they see, without trying to find some explanation for it. They just accept the first thing which comes on their little minds and start to lament immediately. The science is different, the science proceeds systematically and searches for the facts to separate superstitions from reality. But hardly anyone acts like that. That is why so many people believe that the End of the World is coming.
Well... I understand. Thanks.
And what do you think about it?
As I have said—I observe and evaluate the facts. But I haven't come to any conclusions yet. We will see how this situation will develop...

The abundance of monsters in these regions may surprise you. Local people say that earlier only some types of hellspawns and unrighteous creatures were found around Hillbrandt, like for example Plecotus Giantus or Araneus Diabolicus, and from time to time some Trollus Vulgus came down from the Moonshine Mountains. But since the Scourges of God and the appearance of the Star of Doom in the sky various types of godless monsters are bustling here, some of them I would recently call rare or even completely unknown or forgotten—Orcus Cursius, Homoablus Bulkus and many others. Their presence in such quantities proves that the equivalence of Power has been violated recently for some reason.
Oh... thanks.
I'm searching for heretics here in Hillbrandt. Do you suspect anyone?

I don't suspect anyone of heresy, knight. At least, I do not have any reasonable suspicion. I'm not interested in other people much, because it distracts me from my research, and there is so little time! Of course, I have heard the rumors about master Edmond d'Arvias; he is supposed to be the one who let the orcs to the town when they attacked lately. But I haven't seen him myself doing anything of that kind, so I cannot judge him.
Has anything unusual happened in Hillbrandt lately?

Has anything unusual happened recently? Yes, something... very strange... happened. Not long ago, when I did regular measurements of the Power around Hillbrandt, I registered a sharp increase. I was totally astonished, although substantial fluctuations in the Earth magic aura have occurred several times over last few years. But I haven't seen such a sharp increase of Power yet. And during the following night a wild storm was unleashed, no one in this city remembers such a powerful storm. Originally, I wanted to go out and try to draw a part of the unleashed Power for my needs, but I changed my mind in the end.
Why?

Actually, so much dark side Power was unleashed that it would have dismembered me to pieces, should I have tried to grasp it. People believe that the gates of the Hell itself were opened that night and the hellspawns capered about in the sky in wild unhallowed dances. I am a scientist, so I hesitate to believe such rumors, but something very dangerous occurred out there. I wonder what unleashed such a storm. And above all—what unleashed such an incredible increase in Power.
Well... thank you.
What is the Power you are talking about?
Have you read the book by Albierto Morray, Tractatis de la Peiora Materia?
Sure.
Then you don't need me to tell you anything else about it.
Regrettably not...
Then come after you have studied it in detail. Until you understand that excellent work and all it deals with, I won't be able to tell you my opinion on what the Power is.
What do you know about the Fallen Angel Arthamon?
Fallen Angel Arthamon? Why... why do you ask me about him, knight?!
Because I'm interested in him, good man. Is there any problem in it?!

Oh no, surely there isn't... So—according to the Scriptures he was one of the three Fallen Angels, who were thrown down from God's Realm of Heaven together with Satan for the sins committed against God's Commandments. Arthamon constitutes total physical destruction and annihilation, the end of the whole existence. According to my research, his analogy exists also in other religions—for example Elene and Throne pagan nations called him Damned Flame, because they likened him to a fire, which burns both live and dead into the dust!
Well... do you think that it is possible to invoke Arthamon? Bring him into this world?

I don't think so—after all the church tenet says that the invocation of the Fallen Angels is impossible through the protective shield of our true faith in God the Almighty. Because of that the Fallen Angels cannot get into the world of mortals, and so they send lower demons and various hellish minions and tempters instead of themselves.
I'm searching for the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias, do you happen to know anything about it?

Master d'Arvias lost his sword? It is a big surprise for me. That is to say, there aren't many people able to wield it. Although I haven't had an opportunity to study it in detail, I know for sure from what I have observed during casual meetings with master d'Arvias, that it is a mighty artifact, spellbound so that only the master himself can hold it. The touch of sword causes unbearable pain to the others. Thus it surprises me that someone stole the sword from him. It would be of no use to the thief.
I ran into a case of curse here in the Hillbrandt. Do you happen to know how to remove it?

How to remove a curse from a person? Well... I'm not sure I can help you with something like that, knight. I am an astrologist and an alchemist, not a cleric or an exorcist. I'm afraid you will have to ask someone else.
Are there any legends or myths connected to Hillbrandt or its surrounding?
I am a scientist, knight, not a folk poet or a wandering minstrel. So I'm not interested at all in legends and myths. Such things are a waste of time.

I give you best regards from your former colleague, master Alberto Kelley, and ask you to be so kind and pay him a visit. By the way... I wouldn't guess that you are a former master of the Royal Alchemist Guild...

So, you have found it out? Well... after all, why not, it is not a secret. Yes, I am the former master of the Royal Alchemist Guild, but it's the past for me now, and I don't want to have anything in common with them. I left for Hillbrandt, to concentrate fully on my work. What does that incompetent ignoramus Kelley want from me anyway?
He needs your advice concerning the work you left unfinished in Alvaron...

I should have known that those bunglers will be unable to make any progress in any field without me. But it is their problem. They are just a band of clodpoles and good-for-nothings, the whole Royal Alchemist Guild. I don't want to hear anything about them, let them squabble with their petty troubles... I have no time for useless discussions with incapable numskulls! I left for Hillbrandt to be able to concentrate fully on my work, and I want to be left to do it in peace!
What work did you came here to create? And why so far to the North, away from all civilization?

I'm not going to tell you! Sorry, but it is the alchemist secret. Even if I told you, you wouldn't be able to understand anyway—it is too abstract, inadmissible for a common human mind. But the whole world will see the results of my work!
I understand. Goodbye.
Do you happen to know anything about the death of merchant Kurth Ollmier?
I don't know anything about that inauspicious case of merchant Ollmier's murder, knight. Only that it all happened some time ago in the attic of Joseph Truthorn's tavern.
I found this piece of a very bizarre rock. Do you know what it could be? Seems magical...
Piece of a strange rock you say, knight? Show it to me... But yes, this is a Philosopher's stone!
What is it, this Philosopher's stone?

It is a rustic name for a rare mineral Astratus Lungis. The secret of the origin of this mineral hasn't been discovered yet, but it is true that with a dash of craftsmanship it can be turned into any other metal—gold is most popular, of course, but smiths like to use it for forging weapons and armor. It depends on the smelting temperature and on the way of processing. I could turn each Philosopher's stone you bring me into gold for you, if you wish—for a small remuneration, of course.
Thanks for the offering.
Not at all, knight. You are really lucky to get something like that into your hands...
Could you process the Philosopher's stone, if I bring you some?
Can I process the Philosopher's stone? But of course, knight—I revealed that secret long ago. Each Philosopher's stone you bring me I can turn into gold for you. For a remuneration, of course.

Duke Weinberg rules in Hillbrandt and surrounding domains as the royal governor of town. The royal vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. I won't say a bad word about Duke Weinberg, although I must admit his disbelief in alchemy causes me a lot of problems. But Baron van Gallagan rules more through the help of his wife, I'd say...
Of course I don't want it free of charge...
In that case I'm unable to help you...
Don't you realize who I am? It is a heinous crime to oppose me!
I really need to know it, Brechthold. Realize the urgency of the situation, please.
I can't believe that someone so wise and educated would refuse to help me...
Eagle.
Knight.
Aries.
King.
Rider.
Taurus.
Unicorn.
Virgin.
Messiah.
Raven.
Arrow.
Wolf.

Well... really interesting. When I take into account the influence of Tanaris and Menis orbit, the location of Gion and Rethis and bring it all to the astrologic map, remarkable things come out. I haven't seen such a constellation for a long time, by my troth...
So, what do the stars say about my destiny?

It seems that you will live very short, knight. I am really sorry, but Ethel lies in the shadow of the moon Zunnt, and that predicts early death. On the other hand, the planet Centhres is in the Sage constellation, which means that your deeds are able to influence surrounding world, fundamentally I might add.
In what sense?

That depends on you. You will either follow the orbit of Deneris—and that means good, or you set out for the orbit of Allherm, and that means evil. In both cases I can see you will meet many important personalities, which ordinary people cannot meet, even in your short lifetime. Thanks. Do the stars tell you something else about my destiny?
No, knight—that's all.
Interesting. Thank you, good man. I wonder to what extent will your horoscope come true.
Is there any possibility to escape from one's destiny?

From the astrologic point of view? Yes, of course. Astrology doesn't say what will come true, but what can happen, if your deeds intersect the star constellations. If you want not to run into anything I told you, you can do a simple thing—change your way of life.
How?
Enter a monastery and spend the rest of your life there. Usually it helps.
Well... thanks for the advice. I will think about it.
I have one Philosopher's stone here, alchemist. I'd like to have it turned into gold.
Of course, knight. I'll get on it immediately...
Not for much. So, here you are. And with your permission I will keep 50 gp as my reward.
Of course. Thank you.
Do you need anything else from me?

I must open my heart to you in one matter, knight. Do you know that all the people around here, even the eldest townsmen, has known herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt as an old, wizened woman, for all their life? She was already looking ancient when the elders were born. Doesn't she age? I asked the question myself many times, but I didn't know the answer till lately...
I'm sorry, but can I ask you first, who you are, good man?

But then I caught her out one night collecting strange herbs at full moon in the foothills of Moonshine Mountains. Later, I read in an ancient book that these herbs had been used for a production of a potion, which can extend a natural human life! So, this explains her age. I thought that it wouldn't be bad to have one such potion, and so I wanted to buy it from her. But not only that she didn't sell it to me, she even denied all of that and declared that she couldn't prepare any such potion. But I need it! Old age is already knocking at my door and I am only at the beginning of epochal inventions, which will change the character of our world. I need that potion, knight!
One moment. Who are you in fact?!
What? Oh so... excuse me, knight, I forgot to introduce myself in the excitement. It's hard for me to concentrate on something else now. I must have that potion!
But who are you? You still haven't told me!

My name is Theil Brechthold, but that is not important. I'm an astrologist and alchemist. If you need any potion or magic goods, don't hesitate to turn to me. But now you must tell me... the potion of the herbalist Würtenrodt—will you help me to get it?
If you really need that potion, I will obtain it for you.
You will not regret it, knight. You will see, this service will pay off for you!
Can I speak to you a bit more?
Of course. What's the matter?
If I bring you the potion, what will you offer me for it?
Don't be afraid, knight, I'll repay you for it gladly. I have gold, and I am able to read the stars. Man of your kind sure appreciates both of that, doesn't he?
What epochal discoveries are you trying to achieve?

That I cannot reveal to you, knight. But sure you know, that alchemy hides unsuspected possibilities... There are so many discoveries I'd like to turn up, and meanwhile my eyesight is fading and my body refuses to obey me...
I'm absolutely not going to help you in something like that!
Well... what can I do. Your misfortune. I'll say you goodbye in that case.
One moment, could I speak to you a little longer?
If you must... but try to be brief, because I have a lot of work to do, do you understand?!
Wait, I'd like to see your goods.
If you must... but if you break something, you will pay for it!
Hello, knight. How do you do? Did you bring me that potion from herbalist Würtenrodt which I asked you for?
No, not yet, good man.
What can I do. But I hope you will be successful. I need it badly!
What can I do for you, knight?
I need to talk to you for a moment.
Of course, as you wish. What do you need to know?
Yes, I brought you that potion. Here it is.

Great! Finally I do not have to be afraid of old age and I can go on with my discoveries. My thanks to you, knight! Apart from the pouch of gold as a sign of my respect I can offer you also a horoscope compilation for your services, if you are interested.
That sounds interesting. I accept.

In that case let's see, what does the stars say about your destiny... We have year 1223, there is a strong position of Aprion in the constellation of Dragon. This predicts nothing good on it's own. Now, tell me, in what sign are you born, knight?
I don't believe in horoscopes, thanks.
As you think, knight. Can I do something else for you?
But of course. What would you like to know?
Can I see your goods?
What would such a horoscope present?
Horoscopes would reveal to you something about your destiny...
The herbalist says she doesn't have any such potion. You must have got it wrong.

Do as you wish.
Do you want anything from me, or are you leaving already?!
I'd like to talk to you a little longer.
Really? And do you think that I have something I want to tell you?!
I'd like to exchange some goods.
If you insist...
Sorry, I'm not going to deal with you. Farewell.
What do you want, knight? Don't you see I'm very busy?
And what do you want to know? I have no time to exchange pleasantries with you all day long.
Nothing indeed, thanks.

Do you know, master armorer, to whom could this strange arrow belong?

Show me the arrow, knight... But this is my work, after all! Sure, I recognize it. I made a whole dozen of them for one of my customers. Yes, I'm sure it is that arrow. Look, at that smart design—the hit means certain death!
In that case I must ask you to reveal to me the name of your customer. That is to say, this arrow was used in a premeditated murder!

Oh, really? I'm sorry about that... if I can tell something about that matter, that was what the arrow was created for—to kill. Of course I don't know anything about the murder—the customer I made those arrows for didn't tell me what he needed those arrows for.
That is not important now, master. I want his name.
That will be a little bit complicated, knight. I'd like to tell you the name, but I'm bound by a business secret. I cannot afford to lose the faith of my customers.
I understand. But you may change your mind, if I offer you some money for it...

Well... money, you say? Yes, that might rather change the situation. Don't misunderstand me, knight. I'm not some greedy man who will betray the trust of others for a few gold pieces. But I must admit I have certain... financial inconveniences and in case I won't be able to gather certain amount of money, I could lose my workshop—or at least my independence, which is in fact the same for me. Maybe even worse.
To whom do you owe the money?

To Duchess Vanessa of Kentworth, the royal vice-governor. She has lent me a fat sum of money several times already. This is all the fault of my desire for better and more efficient technologies of steel hardening, which should have brought me new earnings. Regrettably I didn't manage as well as I supposed and too late I realised I'm in a great debt. And it seems that I cannot count on a release from the debt or on deferring its repayment, because the Duchess wants to get my shop under her control. The idea that I'm close to becoming her serf and to work for her haunts me day and night...
Maybe there will be something I could do about that. How big is your debt to her?
Well, that's the problem, Father. I owe her 30,000 gp. If you help me with repaying the debt, I'll be more than disposed to reveal to you the identity of the customer I made the arrow for.
So that is really a FAT sum of money, that's right. I'll see what I can do in this matter...
Thank you, knight. Thank you with all my heart. Let the Lord redeem it to you...
Tell me immediately who did you make that arrow for, or you will know the wrath of God!
I am sorry, but there's nothing you can accomplish with threats, knight. My position is high enough to be sure that your threats will come to nothing.
I beseech you, master armorer, tell me the name. It is very important!
Yes, I'm sure it is. But the business secret is similar to the confessional secret—you cannot reveal it, even if you want to. I'm sorry.
I found this piece of a very bizarre rock. Do you know what could it be, master armorer?
Show me what you have, knight... But yes, this is a Philosopher's stone!

It is a rustic name for a rare mineral. Nobody knows where the mineral comes from, but the truth is it is very magical. With a dash of craftsmanship it can be turned into any other metal and still it retains its magical properties. I could forge you one magical item from each Philosopher's Stone you bring me, if you wish.
Not at all, knight.
Of course I could process the Philosopher's Stone. If you bring me some, I can forge you one magical item from it.
Grand Duke Drake Lambert rules in Alvaron as the royal governor of town and Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth is the royal vice-governor.
I have heard some rumors that the war is about to start. Do you happen to know any details about it?
Yes, the war is about to start, I'm sure about that!
How can you know for sure?

Because I'm the most renowned weaponsmith far and wide, knight. So I know what it means when I get an order for three hundred lances, two hundred cavalry armor, three threescores of longbows and for countless numbers of other military equipment. But that's not all—horses and draught cattle are being requisitioned, granaries are being filled, new recruits gathered... so there will be a war! There's just one essential thing missing—that is to say, the enemy. There's no sign of any outer enemy endangering the Realm, which our army could confront in the field. Really strange, isn't it...

I'll tell you without diffidence, knight—beware of women! They are the most terrible monsters ever born in this world. And you don't have to lie with them at all to get into trouble. Thus, take my advice to heart—avoid them like the devil eschews the holy cross!
Are there any rewards announced here in Alvaron for monster killing?

Grand Duke Drake Lambert announced big rewards for catching werewolves, who are rampaging not only outside the city, but who even dare to enter our streets. Henry Portmann, the Sheriff, disburses the rewards in exchange for trophies brought to him—heads of dead werewolves.

It happened to me several times that a customer paid me for my goods with money which seemed good at first glance. But later the coins turned into dirty human excrement. At first I wanted to hunt and kill those wretches, but then I found out this occurs in the whole city and it affects all other citizens. It seems that some heretics use the forces of hell to turn human excrement into gold for some time, and introduce those fake gold coins into circulation like real ones. I'm sure you can imagine, knight, that mistrust and worries are spread among the people...
I'm searching for criminals who let the werewolves enter the city every full moon. Do you happen to know anything about them?

I'm sorry, but I don't know much about that werewolf case. I just wonder what damned heretic could be so stupid and do something as crazy as to make a pact with werewolves?! After all, they are just uncontrollable beasts, skirmishing with each other when it comes to a piece of human meat...
I'm searching for the missing Ron Burton. Do you happen to know anything about him?

Well, the last time I saw Ron Burton, he was entering the King's Road Tavern in Schwarzwald. We ran into each other that day—we were both returning from business trips back to Alvaron, and so we rode part of the journey together. The night caught us in Schwarzwald, the storm was getting closer and we could even hear the howling of werewolves from the distance. Ron Burton decided to stay overnight in the pub of innkeeper Bates. I tried to talk him out of it, for the facility has a very doubtful reputation, but he said he would rather face the intrigues near the burning fireplace and with a full stomach, than to race with a pack of werewolves through the night. So he stayed there and I went on. I haven't seen him since then...
Priest Nicolas claims he was wrongfully accused of ravishing Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. Do you happen to know anything about it?

I have heard about that case of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert's violation, but I can't tell you anything substantial about it. Only that Father Nicolas had hellishly bad luck. When a man entangles himself with a woman, nothing good can arise from that. Men should avoid them, like a devil obviates the holy cross...

Alvaron is pretty rich with myths and legends, knight. Especially with the stories about various treasures and fairy-tale riches—maybe due to the fact there's a lot of money-grubbers among the people here. Have you heard, for example, the tale about the treasury of Baron Decard of Longhorn? The Baron was obsessed with magical and sorcerous items and dedicated his life to collecting such things. Unfortunately for his neighbourhood, his passion turned to an obsession soon and he succumbed to the forces of darkness, merely to get as many of those sorcerous things as possible. He gained those riches with the help of hellspawns who committed murders, deceptions, robberies, thefts and many other villainies for him. All those deeds were as far from righteousness as his soul was far from the salvation.
Well... what was the ending of his story?

And when the Baron tried to rob Bishop Benedictius, he ended up in chains and even his hellspawns were unable to help him out of the claws of the Inquisition. He pleaded all his crimes during the torture—with a fair-sized dose of pride, they say — but even the Inquisition interrogators were unable to squeeze the location of the stolen treasures out of him. He was executed in 1210, but nobody was able to find that treasure since.
I would advise you, master armorer, to answer my questions. Because the wrath of God will not stop for anything...
I ask you frankly, master armorer—answer my question, please.
You are a wise and skilled man, master armorer. Your reputation precedes you. Because of that, I would be honored if you answered my question.
I've got one Philosopher's Stone here. I'd like to have something forged from it.
Thanks, master armorer. No need to hurry. Be careful about it.
Don't worry, knight... So, here you are. It is a perfect piece—as usual, when forging a Philosopher's Stone. I hope you will be satisfied. Can I do something else for you?

Welcome, knight, to my humble steel kingdom. Everything you see around can be yours. Just tell me—and pay for it, of course. No matter if you are looking for something in particular or you just came to look at the goods, I'm sure you will find something! After all, weapons and armor from master Leon van den Brooks' armory are renowned—even famous!
I'm glad to meet you, master armorer. Could I speak with you for a moment?
Certainly, knight. Although I admit I thought you came to choose some of my excellent pieces of work. But we can get to it later, can't we...
What do you produce in your workshop, master?

Everything the art of war requires, knight. Infantry weapons, cavalry weapons, attack and defense weapons, pure war or hunting weapons, fighters' and decorative shields, armor and kirtles for all the brave... simply everything that comes in your mind. Just look around yourself and we will surely come to an agreement about the price.
Well... in that case I won't resist and will look through your goods, master.
I will surely look at your goods sometime, master. However, I need to talk to you now.
As you wish, knight—my door is always open to you. What do you need to talk to me about?
It is good to know whom to address in the case I lack some armament or equipment. Maybe I'll stop by sometimes. Farewell for now.
As you wish, knight—my door will be always open to you.
To tell the truth, I've never heard about your renowned workshop, master armorer.

Surely not? Peculiar... why, the van den Brooks family line has been supplier of weapons and armor for the royal army for several generations. Nobody has been able to take this primacy from us and as long as I live, nobody will. Look around you, knight—what you see is the best quality! Steel brisk as wine, as a poet would say.

Yes, that's true. But tell me, is there severe competition in your profession? I have already talked with several blacksmiths and armorers, who extolled their art above all others. For example Hans von Drichtmaul...

I know Hans von Drichtmaul well, knight. He's a skilled armorer and blacksmith, but—with all respect—he's neither as skilled nor he possesses as much knowledge of metals as me. But you are right otherwise, there has always been a great demand for warriors' equipment in the Realm—as well as in any other country, for that matter. Moreover armorers in the Empire and in other faithful countries compete with us. We shall see where it will lead, as the times are so hard... But tell me, knight, what can I do for you? Some weapon, as you please? Or maybe a suit of armor?
I'm not interested in shopping now, master—maybe later. However, I need to talk to you for a moment.
We'll see. First of all, I'll look at your goods.
Nothing this time, master. But surely I'll stop by sometimes. Farewell for now.
As you think, knight—my door will be always open to you. Farewell.
Hello, knight. Did you come to buy something from me? You will find something in my shop for sure—there's nothing better to get in the whole Realm!
To tell the truth, I'd rather ask you a few questions...
Well, ask the questions then, knight. But feel free to look at every single item you see exhibited in my workshop. Maybe you will find something you'd like...
I'd like to see your goods, master.
I have good news for you, master armorer. I paid all the debts you owed to Vanessa of Kentworth.

Sure? You paid her all the 30,000 gp, including interests? My God... you have my deepest admiration, sir knight. It is quite a hard task to get together such a large sum of money. I'm in your debt, let the lightning strike me down if I'm not!
In that case tell me for whom did you created that arrow, which I showed you.

Sure, knight—that was the agreement. So, I made those arrows for a man named Sven Larsen. He stops by from time to time and wants me to fix something special for him. He's an expert. I found that out when we first met. He knows a lot about weapons, as if he were an experienced landsknecht, but he has never told me what he does for a living. Probably nothing a man would boasts about in the public, I'd say.
Thank you, master. It's very interesting information.

You are welcome, knight. I'm glad I could help you. It's nothing in comparison with how much you helped me. So I would like to offer you this piece from my workshop as a token of my gratitude. I hope it will be useful to you. And even if it won't, I'm sure you can sell it anytime.
Thank you, master armorer.
Really, there's no need to thank me, knight. Is there anything else I could do for you?
I'd like to ask you several questions, master armorer.
In that case, ask your questions, knight. I'll tell you all I know.
I'd like to look at your goods, knight. Maybe I'll buy something else.
I don't think so—at least at this moment. Farewell.
Farewell, knight. And God be with you.
My way just led me around here—I'm leaving already.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick rules in Glatzburg, knight. He's the royal governor of the city. His vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin.

Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned armory in Glatzburg. You can get potions and various magic items from Enrie Jungwirdt, the wise woman, and from Paolus Ventimus, the alchemist. Wanda Gielwitch, the tavern owner, and Ludwig Weintraum the innkeeper have both variety of goods for sale. And you can barter anything at Alphonso DiCerbio's, if you don't mind the origin of the goods.

What do I think about the present crisis? You mean what I think about all these Scourges of God that struck upon us? About all those beasts running around the woods? And about godlessness, which plagues human minds like some sort of infection? I think, knight, that the End of the World is coming! At least, the end of the world as we know it. I know the Holy Inquisition tries hard to do all it can, but when gangrene gets into an open wound on your leg, you can't do anything but cut the leg off. And that's exactly what will happen to our Realm. Nothing will be like before. It has gone too far. God knows what—or who—is responsible. Maybe it really is God's punishment, for we lived lives of sinners and offended God's Laws of submission. But no matter what the truth is, it does not look like it's going to get better soon.
There's going to be a war, they say. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Yes, I've also heard the war will come. Imagine, knight, they came to me and tried to recruit me. I was nearly petrified from that. Me a soldier? Of course I refused, but I couldn't resist to think about it. It has to be really bad, when even scrubs like me are recruited. I can't even pick up a halberd without hurting someone...
What monsters and hellspawns can people meet here in Glatzburg and around?

I personally think that the worst are brigands and highwaymen, who rage around Glatzburg and assault and kill everyone they meet. There's nothing they fear, they spare no one—women, children, old men, clerics, nobles... they rob and kill all. And the most terrible is that self-appointed leader of them, Knight Benthley of Welshrem. He's said to be a real monster, who has made cups from the skulls of people he killed and now drinks human blood from them at feasts!
I'm looking for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone?
I've already told you about the only suspicion of heresy I have—the one about Jeanette the maid, that she tried to bewitch me with the help of dark sorcery. That's all.

Has anything worth mentioning happened lately? Well... you know, knight, I'm not a very superstitious man. I'd love to say I don't believe anything I can't see with my own eyes. But I must admit that what happened in Glatzburg some time ago scared me so much I hid under my bed with my teeth clattering from fear.
What did scare you so much?

A storm, knight. Such a terrible storm drifted to Glatzburg one night, nobody remembers anything like that—not even Enrie Jungwirdt or Guss Halworth, they say, and those two are pretty old people. It came out of nowhere. When I ended my work in the evening, the sky was cloudless, as if swept with a brush. But at midnight wind came so strong that my shutters were torn away. Clouds came together with the storm, and looked like they wanted to crush all on the ground below. Then came myriads of lightning bolts, one after another, and the thunder deafened me. And then it happened, knight. I heard some voices in the tempest. First it seemed to me like someone got caught out in the rain, so I risked to look out. And I won't forget that view as long as I live!
And what did you see, good man?

There were demons dancing in the sky, knight. I had never seen one before, but I'm sure they were demons. They lamented, cried, laughed, it was so bad I nearly lost my mind. I dragged myself back into the bed, as if hoping it would be able to save me from them, and I was afraid to show my face till the morning!
Well... interesting. Thank you.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible tragedy. I can't imagine who could do such an awful thing! Regrettably I won't help you with the investigations, because I don't know anything about it. But I'm sure bandits or heretics are responsible. Or maybe some hellspawns.

Do I know anything about the Bishop Trevorius murder? Oh... with all due respect, knight... I would hate to offend you... but when you're asking about that... I... have heard, that Trevorius was murdered by you. People say you were found above his body, when it was still warm... But sure it is just slander!
What can you tell me about those undead, killing in the city streets during the night?

Those things that occur after dusk, they're a true hell, knight. I have always thought that we were safe within the city walls, that the hellspawns can't get to us and that one should be careful only when going out of the city gate. But now... since those living dead started to appear right in the streets, it is no longer safe to be anywhere. Damn, those caught in the streets after dusk—they probably won't live to see the next morning. And the city watch is helpless against them—they can slaughter dozens of them in the night, but the next day it seems that for each destroyed undead another one crept to the city. Heaven knows how they get into the city—probably Satan brings them on his flaming wings...
If something was lost or stolen, go and ask Tinthan the performer. He's a very bad actor, but he can even steal the nose between your eyes.
I'm looking for missing Raquel Gielwitch. Do you happen to know anything about her?

I'm sorry, knight, but I haven't heard about Raquel Gielwitch since she disappeared without a trace from the house of her sister. I'm afraid that Satan took her—at least this is what her sister Wanda says.
Are there any myths or legends connected with Glatzburg or its surroundings?

Have you heard the legends about pagan city Galibornium, knight? Not that all of them were legends, because most of what I'd like to tell you really happened, but it was so very long ago... There's a place near Glatzburg, where a pagan city called Galibornium used to be. It was a proud and mighty city, maybe the largest in the whole Filkland peninsula, which then belonged to Ereborn. And of course in the memorable year 223 that city became the target of the attack of faithful armies led by saint Orthenius himself—who haven't heard about it, after all? It was a really atrocious massacre, the pagans knew it was the end for them, with nowhere to run, so they defended themselves like rabid dogs. But it didn't help them anyway, they were captured and the city burnt to the ground.
Interesting. And what happened then?

When all that bloodshed settled down, it was found out that there are no lodgings for many faithful people. Thus, the nobles and clerics decided that a new town will be founded and will be called Glatzburg. They decided to build the town on the ruins of Galibornium and to use the stones of that pagan nest to build the town of faithful. People set out to build, but they stopped almost before they started, because evil pagan ghosts and various demons overwhelmed the town. So the people went and founded Glatzburg at the place where it stands now. And Galibornium was left to the ghosts of the past, who have been guarding forgotten pagan treasures since then. At least, that's what people say...
Thanks, I've already heard about it...
Your answer is necessary, Brookwelt. If you will hesitate to answer, I'm sure it will bring you some VERY unpleasant consequences...
Look, good man—I can see you are a decent and righteous man. In that case, why do you refuse to answer me, although it would help a good cause? Answer me, please.
Seldom have I the honor of talking to someone as clever and sharp as you, Brookwelt. I'm sure nobody would be able to provide me a better-founded answer!

Knight, you must put an end to her evil-doings. You cannot let her go free and wait till she tries to bewitch me again! I have been resisting her successfully for the time being, but who knows when that crazy wench really stumbles upon some working magic formula?! After all, it is a blatant heresy!
First of all, good man, tell me, who you are?

Who am I? Haven't I introduced myself? Excuse me, I'm so angry that it muddles my mind. My name is Brookwelt, Hans Thomas Brookwelt. I work as a carpenter here in Glatzburg. You wouldn't imagine what a good living I can make thanks to the Scourges of God, really. I'd rather do something else than more and more coffins, but when I count out how much have I already earned on them, well... I don't mind so much. It's a nice stack of gold, by my troth. And she knows it very well, that treacherous old witch! That's why she has chosen me as her first victim! God is my witness, were it not for a rosary my departed mother gave me at her death-bed, I would already be an obedient slave of that evil witch! Someone must stop her, knight!
Well, who are you talking about? And what happened to you?

But still waters run deep, that you can believe me. I don't know what devil set me to that, but I talked to her several times when she did some shopping in the city market with Baroness Helen von Hunth. Once, after I mentioned how good living these times brought to me, she suddenly looked like she had awoken from sleep and started to be interested in me. I was glad, as I didn't recognize any bad intents in her. But... Well, I was awfully mistaken. One day I invited her for a walk beyond the city walls, to the place the royal gazebo is—or rather what was left of it. And there it all happened!
What exactly do you have in mind?

I wanted to cuddle her—with honest intentions, of course—but she pushed me away swiftly and laughed at me. She said I was a weakling she wouldn't touch if only I hadn't saved up quite a lot of gold. And that she does need it and that she'll take it. This time I laughed at her and asked her, how does she want to do that. But then... she told it to me, and suddenly, it wasn't funny any more. She told me she had found a secret magic formula, which will help her to take control over the mind of any man. That she would enslave all men in the city and that we would blindly fulfill her every command.

And thereafter she started to recite some strange formulas in a language I didn't understand. I nearly passed out, there was only darkness, everything was dark and muddy, except Jeanette's figure. She stood there and shined like the sun at noon and I wanted to obey her every word. But then I fell down and struck my head. It awakened me and in the same moment I had a knob-stick in my hand to defend myself from the witch. But she ran away from me and I let her go, because I started to be really scared.
So you say that she tried to bewitch you?

You are right, good man. Her wicked bluster must be put to end. I'll take care of it.

But of course, knight. Ask the questions.
Don't worry, good man—I'll return good sleep to you. Trust me. Farewell.
Maybe something could be done in this matter... But it depends on what you would offer me for that.

What do you think about it?

Well... if you think so, knight.

What is it?

Yes, you're right. I'll take care of it.

Now I'd like to ask you several questions, if I may.
Of course, knight. What's the matter?

Yes, you're right. I'll take care of it!

To the prison?! To the inquisition jailhouse? No, never! I've heard enough about it to know whoever steps inside will never come out alive! You'll never get me there! Never! I'm innocent and I won't let you force me to confess, as you do with others!
If you resist, I'll have to force you, Brookwelt. I warn you, that's something you really don't want! You have a chance to stand a fair trial!
