It's easy for you to say that, noble lord. You are a noble and God favors you. But who will pray for the common people? Who will guarantee them that God will accept them into his herd again? Nobody...
We must stop it, noble lord! We must stop it once and for all!
I would donate all my belongings to the gentry so that they could use them to improve the situation of the Realm.

Do not be too modest, knight. People everywhere speak about you killing that hellspawn in a fierce fight. Surely the Almighty has sent you to save us from the bloody rage of werewolves. God bless you, knight!
Oh my God, what will we do, sir knight?! What will we do now, when our King is dead?!
What are you talking about, dear man?!

What?! Haven't you heard about the murder? His Majesty King Edward is dead! He was assassinated in his private chambers! Not even the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor could protect him. What will we do now? With the King and his son prince Louis the royal house died out... the Realm will fall into trouble. Oh My God...
Assassination of a king? Unbelievable! I must learn more about it...

Do not be too modest, Father. People everywhere speak about you killing that hellspawn in a fierce fight. Surely the Almighty has sent you to save us from the bloody rage of werewolves. God bless you, Father!
Oh my God, what will we do, Father?! What will we do now, when our King is dead?!
Don't be afraid, the Grand Duke will take care of that!
Hmm... the Grand Duke Drake Lambert is surely omnipotent, but can it really cope with all those packs of werewolves? But maybe you are right...

Do not be too modest, noble lord. People everywhere speak about you killing that hellspawn in a fierce fight. Surely the Almighty has sent you to save us from the bloody rage of werewolves. God bless you, noble lord!
It's easy for you to say that, noble lord. You are ritch and God favors you. But who will guarantee the common people that God will accept them into his herd again? Nobody...
I would sell all my belongings and then donate all the money to the nobles so that they could better administer justice in the Realm.
Oh my God, what will we do, noble lord?! What will we do now, when our King is dead?!
It's told that you single-handedly killed Benthley of Welshrem, the Bloody Butcher, knight. Is it true?
It's told that you single-handedly killed Benthley of Welshrem, the Bloody Butcher, Father. Is it true?
It's told that you single-handedly killed Benthley of Welshrem, the Bloody Butcher, noble lord. Is it true?
Who rules Hillbrandt and the surrounding areas?
Hillbrandt is ruled by Duke Weinberg the royal governor. His deputy is Baron Robert van Gallagan the royal vice-governor.
I would like to know if there are any rewards for killing monsters in Hillbrandt.
Duke Weinberg declared that there's a reward for the head of any orc who gets in the vicinity of Hillbrandt. Bring me a green skin scalp or head and I'll give you cash on the barrelhead.
That's none of your business!

Well, the word is that heretics are behind the crisis. They caused God to turn away from us and so the good believers suffer for the sins of others. I'll be honest with you, knight—if it's really so, the only thing that can solve the crisis is force. The royal power must be upheld no matter the cost. The Inquisition is good, but it's too inefficient and slow, because it must respect laws. Gimme a regiment of the royal army and I'll scour the Realm, city after city, town after town, village after village... believe me the crisis would be over in no time! All we need is a quick decisive strike and heretics will be demoralized before they can say their false prayers! Long story short, we need another Saint Berthold Night...
If you think so...
I'm right, knight. Believe me.
What is Saint Berthold's Night?

How is it possible you've never heard about Saint Berthold's Night? Well, it all happened in the Empire in 1215 on Saint Berthold's Day. Prince Henry, an orthodox believer and heir to the throne, was supposed to marry Kathryn de Valion, a daughter of reformist King Hugo III. Prince Henry's mother wanted to prevent the wedding at any cost, so she exploited growing animosity between the orthodox believers and the reformists to initiate a huge nightlong massacre in which almost ten thousands reformists were slaughtered. It was the end of the Saint-Generiel religious reconciliation and the start of schism in all the faithful world. Nevertheless it purged the Empire of reformists—thoroughly.
I won't discuss such issues with you!
Where can I buy some goods in Hillbrandt?

You can buy lots of stuff in Hillbrandt—well, if you know what you're looking for. If weapons and armor are concerned, go see our local blacksmith—Victor Hammerhand. His goods are the best you can get in Hillbrandt. Potions and other magic stuff can be obtained from Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist or from Theil Brechthold the astrologist. Father Dominicus could help you with such things as well. Well, then there's inkeeper Joseph Truthorn and stallholder Suzan Brauchner—they'll sell you almost anything.
I've heard that you pay rewards for killed orcs, Sheriff. Is it true?

Yes, I pay rewards for dead orcs. Bring me some orc scalp or head and the reward in gold is yours. The bigger the orc, the bigger the reward, knight. Well, but to be honest, I haven't paid many rewards so far. There are not many who went hunting orcs and returned. It's simply too dangerous.

Hillbrandt is nowadays surrounded by hordes of infernal vermin, knight. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, there has been too many damn bastards crawling from the bowels of the earth. But to tell the truth, knight, orcs are the most frightening of them all. Green skins. I don't know if you've already heard about them... Those infernal fiends have appeared in the early spring in the Moonshine Mountains, nobody knows through what hellholes they got there. Before anybody could react they ransacked entire mining village Asherbalt, including nearby iron mines. And to make it even worse it seems that the orcs have settled there to do some mischief, because since they got into the mines a thick black smoke has been fuming from the bowels of the mountains. They raid the entire region, so we are almost cut off from the rest of the Realm—no merchant dares to travel to the town. I'm afraid they will swarm in front of the walls and will storm us—as they did one night several days back. But this time there will be hundredfold more of those bastards...
What can you tell me about orcs, Sheriff?

So you wanna hear about the green skins, knight? I don't know how is it with you, knight, but I first heard about them in the legends regarding old pagan kingdoms populated by inhuman races. Well, but it was a long time ago. The rumor is that the orcs were summoned by some infernal being called Cursed Flame from the forsaken place called Accursed Depths. God knows what it means. Anyway, they were summoned to crush a proud and powerful empire called Thron which lied below the mountains. And they did their job well. They reduced the barbarian empire to ashes. And with Thron wiped out, the mysterious pagan race living there vanished as well.

All my life I believed that it was just a legend and that the orcs were just a myth. But this spring opened my eyes—they suddenly swarmed from the depths of the Moonshine Mountains and attacked Asherbalt and iron mines slaughtering all the locals. Since then they've been controlling the entire foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Nobody knows from where they came. And why. Maybe the heretics summoned them to bring total despair to the Realm. Though the sure thing is that Hillbrandt has been constantly in danger since then. The recent night attack proves it.
I'm looking for heretics in Hillbrandt, Sheriff. Do you have any suspicions?

To be honest, knight, I don't suspect anyone in the town of being a heretic. I'm a soldier and so I believe only things I can see. And if I see a heretic threatening God or the King I kill him. It's my job. I've heard some rumors about master Edmond d'Arvias, but I won't comment at it. I haven't seen him doing anything bad and as far as I know he's a man who has destroyed good many hell spawns! I don't think he would be a demon hunter and a demon servant at the same time...

Lots of things happened, so I don't know about which I should tell you first. Well, probably the worst thing that befell Hillbrandt was that night attack of the green skins—they managed either by some ploy or betrayal to get inside the town. Hell broke lose—It was a terrible bloodbath! I lost almost quarter of my men before we managed to push them behind the walls. Well, to be honest, I don't think that it was their main attack. I have a feeling that there are many more hiding beneath the mountains. I think they're waiting for something and that attack was just a harbinger of terrors to come. Anyway they mustn't get into the town again. We can hold them behind the walls for quite some time.
Tell me, Sheriff, do you happen to know anything about the theft of the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius?

The theft the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius is a terrible loss, knight. I can't imagine who could have done that—the Holy Mother Church valued and guarded it above all else. I'm sure it was some licentious heretic proficient in unclean infernal powers, because he managed to put to sleep all the priests praying in the church for the salvation of mankind. In the morning they found them sleeping on the floor among the pews. There's no doubt that they were lulled to sleep by the culprit who then seized the monstrance. Well, I was ordered to look into it, but I wasn't successful. We didn't find a single trace leading to the culprits.
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus?

I'm sorry, knight, but I don't know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus. He disappeared the night when the orcs attacked the town—nobody has seen him since. Well, if it were up to me I'd add him to the casualties of the orcs, but Father Dominicus won't allow—he's probably waiting for the body to be found. Well I doubt it can be found—as far as I know orcs are cannibals who eat their fallen foes.
What do you think about the alleged murder of Natalia Reichmann which was supposedly committed by landsknecht Olfghard?

Poor Natalia, it's a terrible fate, don't you think? To be murdered for a few pieces of jewelry... I've known landsknecht Olfghard for some time and I had a feeling that I knew him well—obviously I was mistaken. He was trying to sell her jewelry when we arrested him. I put him in jail at once, but before Duke Weinberg could sentence him, he managed to escape. Since then he's not been seen. He probably fled to the south to get as far from Hillbrandt as possible. He would have to dance on air if we captured him.

Well it's a tricky case, that with merchant Ollmier, I can't deny it. We had to adjourn the case, because there was little evidence—all in all it was a dead end. It happened some time ago... one morning innkeeper Truthorn rushed into my office, he could barely catch his breath, and dragged me to the attic of his pub—Kurt Ollmier was renting it. The merchant was lying on the bed and he looked very dead. Well, I immediately knew that he was dead—there was blood all around—real slaughter. The murderer cut his throat and stuffed his mouth with his privates. Not a very nice sight.
Do you have a suspect?

If I had one I wouldn't hesitate to bust him, believe me, knight. But there were no leads to help us in the investigation. The murderer entered the room, killed the merchant and then left without being noticed. No witnesses, no traces.
What can you tell me about the merchant himself?

He was kinda weird. Well, he was not that much of a merchant—you could say that he was an adventurer, treasure hunter and profiteer—he had the goods which can't be bought in normal shops. Various artifacts from the pagan times, which he dug up in ancient ruins and tombs; potions, which normal alchemists can't brew; maps of the places nobody heard of... and other things like that. To be honest I'm not surprised that he did not die a natural death—people like him usually die violently.
When I was in the south I heard some rumors that there might be a war coming. Do you know anything about it?

Rumors about a coming war? You heard right, knight. Not too long ago we got the orders from the First Knight Don Rodrigo de Velacor to mobilize the Hillbrandt regiment and to reinforce the town defenses. We were also ordered to requisition horses and draft cattle, to fill granaries and to build up supplies of provisions. So it really seems a war is at hand. Well, but it's not sure against whom. Monsters pestering Hillbrandt can't be defeated on the battlefield...

Since I was a little boy I've been hearing legends about a pagan treasure which was thought to be buried in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains—somewhere near the Dragon Rock. People say it was hidden there by barbarians four hundred years ago, when they were fleeing through Hillbrandt back to the north. The Barbarian Wars were almost over then and Duke Welliar's cavalry caught up with the shattered fleeing barbarian hordes and massacred them. But before they were destroyed, they managed to bury their treasures which have been hidden there since. It's rumored that the treasure is invaluable and well hidden—moreover supposedly there is a terrible pagan curse guarding it.
Answer at once! You know who I am, don't you?!
Sheriff, I'm sure you know that information is a key to success in any endeavor. Now, please, answer my question.
You are an intelligent and perceptive man, Sheriff. I'm sure you know that you can speak absolutely freely in my presence.
Linda van Gallagan, Sheriff.

You have arrested Baroness Linda van Gallagan! Damn! Well, if you think so... But I hope that there won't be any complications. You know, her husband is kinda... my superior. He's the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt. You should better have a word about it with judge Vallarian.
Edmond d'Arvias, Sheriff.
What? You have arrested Edmond d'Arvias! The Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, superior of the local Chapter? It will cause lots of problems, believe me, knight. But if you insist...
Bishop Vallarian, Sheriff.
WHAT?! Are you insane, knight? You have arrested an Inquisitorial judge! And you want me to put him into a cell and keep him there?
Ehm... Well, fine, if it's not going to be any more daring—like asking me to imprison Archbishop Laurencius or His Majesty Edward... After all the responsibility is yours. I just obey your orders.
Edmond d'Arvias.
Edmond d'Arvias? Oh my... Well, it's your call, knight. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack or strappado?
Linda van Gallagan.
Linda van Gallagan? Well, knight, I'm afraid you can't do that...
Why? Why couldn't I do it? She's been arrested and as such she's a subject to the right of torture.

Well, the problem is she isn't, knight. You know, I'm not very good with these legal issues, but from my work I know that the Inquisition Codex forbids torturing pregnant women and children. And Baroness van Gallagan is pregnant—there's no doubt about that. Before she disappeared she met with Würtenrodt the herbalist and she confirmed her story. So I'm sorry, knight, but you can't use torture in the interrogation.
Hmm... thanks for the info. I didn't know that.
Bishop Vallarian.
My god. Are you really absolutely sure that you want to do it, knight? I can lively imagine what would happen if judge Vallarian were proven innocent.
Yes, I am sure!
As you wish. I'll tell my boys to get ready. But you must attest that I did it only because I was bound by the law!
You're right. Forget about it...
Yes, it's reasonable...
Rack!
Fine. I'll tell my boys to get ready. You may proceed down to the torture chamber.
Strappado!
So you have managed to kill some green skins, knight. That's good news. The more will be sent back to hell the less people will die when they attack us again. Well, show me what you have...
I have an orc scalp.
Excellent, knight! It's a valuable trophy, no kidding. A dead orc is a good orc. Here's you reward.
I have an orc warrior head.
Excellent, knight! It's a worthy trophy. Those bastards are so strong that they can chop a man in half with a single blow—as if he were just a withered stick. Here's your reward.
I have an orc shaman's head.
That's great, knight! It's quite a worthy trophy. Those beasts are more dangerous than anything I can imagine. Here's your reward.
I have the head of Rashgar the Orc Khan.
Wait a moment, knight. Are you trying to tell me that this... that this is the head of Rashgar the Orc Khan?! Legendary ruler whose armies destroyed Thron the pagan Empire?
It is so, Sheriff. Is there a reward for his head?

Damn me! He's asking me about a reward for the Khan's head. You just killed the Orc Khan, a terrible beast from terrifying legends who ruled all the bloody green skins below the mountains and you just ask me as if nothing happened if there's a reward? The Duke will endow you with gold when he hears about it! Go see him and show him the head of that beast. I guarantee you won't be able to carry that sack of gold! Good Lord... I'm sure it will cheer up all my men, you can bet! Khan Rashgar is dead! Oh yes...!
That's all for now.
Very well, knight. What else can I do for you?
I have arrested someone, Sheriff. I would like to imprison the suspect in the jail, until proven guilty or innocent.
Of course. Who's that?
I would like to interrogate one of the imprisoned in the torture chamber.
And who would it be?

The hordes of green skins occupying the Moonshine Mountains can attack us any day now. Nobody knows exactly where they came from and how many of them are hiding there. It seems the old legends came to life and the evil, which once walked the earth, has returned. Something must be quickly done about it. Duke Weinberg asked Glatzburg for reinforcements several times, but nobody listens to his pleas. They say there are problems in the south as well and they can't spare any soldiers. Unbelievable.
It seems you're rushed off your feet, Sheriff. Can I help you with anything?

Help me? Well, it's hard to say. You're a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous and I'm sure you have your own tasks. But thinking about it, I might need your help. It concerns the soldier Jullian. He has been avoiding duty for several days, which is obviously desertion. Unless he's quickly found and punished, my men will start disappearing like ghosts. And that is the last thing I need. Could you find him and bring him back?
Of course, Sheriff. I'll do what I can.
Really? I'm really thankful, knight. I didn't hope to get any help. Thanks again. Bring him to me when you find him.
Of course. Could I ask some more questions, Sheriff?
Sure, go ahead, knight.
You can count on me, Sheriff. Goodbye.
And what about a reward? Is there a reward for capturing him?
Well, if it would satisfy you, I could offer you a pouch of gold. What do you say? Deal?
What are you going to do with him if he's captured?

What am I going to do with him? Well, of course I'll lock him up until he rots. If he's not going to be hung straightaway. Undermining morale of my men like that! And it seemed he might be a great soldier one day. I have no idea what led him to leave the army.
Chasing deserters? I'm sorry, Sheriff, but I don't really have time for that.
Thought so. I'm sure you have more important things to do than helping the defensiveness of the town. God bless you, knight.
Wait a moment, Sheriff. Could I ask some more questions?
As you want, knight. But make it quick, I have my duties and they won't wait.
You're absolutely correct, Sheriff. Goodbye.
I met that soldier of yours—Jullian. He's hiding in an abandoned chapel in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains—not too far from the Dragon Rock.
Well, then escort him into the town at once, knight. We can't let him stay loitering around the town without punishment.
Right, Sheriff, I'll do it.
Thanks, knight. I knew we could make a deal!
Could I ask some more questions?
I must leave, Sheriff. Goodbye.
Have you got a feeling that I'm a military patrol so I should take care of your deserters?
Well, you're right, knight. Obviously I mistakenly got a feeling that you could help me. Well, nevermind, I'll send some of my men there.
Of course, knight. But make it quick, I have my duties and they won't wait.

I met that soldier of yours—Jullian. He was hiding in an abandoned chapel in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains—not too far from the Dragon Rock. I was forced to kill him because he attacked me.

Really? You say he attacked you... well, then it's good you killed him. Originally I thought I could discipline him, but obviously I was mistaken. Thanks, knight. Here's some gold for the problems Jullian caused you. I must watch my men better.
What are the powers of a Sheriff?

Any town Sheriff has only as much power as the royal governor allows—but the powers are always connected only with military service and public order. Well, as for me, I administer the entire Hillbrandt military garrison. I do everything—from getting supplies to recruitment and training. And I also manage the town jail, which is probably the most interesting for you, am I right? If you arrest somebody, you can put him in jail with my permission. And if you'd like to rack him, just ask. Well, I hope there won't be too much torture—I'm damn busy even without it. Damn orcs and other infernal maggots are giving us hell!
Greetings, knight. Do you have any news about Jullian? If we don't capture him fast, it could undermine the morale of all my men. And it's the last thing I could afford these damn days.
No I haven't found anything yet.
Well, I can't blame you. Do you need something?
Could I have a minute of your time?
Alright, knight. But make it short, I don't have much time.
I would like to get my reward for the killed orcs.
Well, just passing by. Farewell.

I found Jullian, Sheriff. He was hiding in an abandoned chapel near the Dragon Rock. He kidnapped Natalia Reichmann so he could blackmail her father. I tried to convince him to come with me, but he attacked me. I had to kill him.

Huh? Are you telling me that he kidnapped Natalia Reichmann? And that he attacked you? Then it's good he's dead. Originally I thought the boy could be disciplined, but obviously I was mistaken. Thank you, knight. Here's some gold for the troubles he caused. I must watch better over my men.
Greetings, knight. Do you need my assistance? If not, please leave me to do my job.
Please make it quick, knight. I don't have much time.
Well, in fact I'm just passing by, farewell.
Greetings, knight. Do you need something?
Of course, knight. Please try to make it brief, I don't have much time.

I've met the soldier Jullian, Sheriff. He was hiding in the deserted chapel in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains near the Dragon Rock. Do you know he had kidnapped Natalia Reichmann? Anyway, I frightened him so much he's never going to show himself here again...
You say he had kidnapped Natalia Reichmann? Then it's a pity you didn't arrest him, knight. But what can we do? Maybe the arm of the law will find him somewhere.

I've found Jullian, Sheriff. He was hiding in the deserted chapel near the Dragon Rock. He had kidnapped Natalia Reichmann to blackmail her father. I didn't arrest him but I frightened him so much he's never going to show himself here again...
What? You say he had kidnapped Natalia Reichmann? In that case it's a pity you didn't arrest him, knight. But what can we do? Hopefully the arm of the law will find him somewhere.
Sam Riemann.
Alright, I'll put him into a cell.
As you wish, knight. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack or strappado?
Release Edmond d'Arvias—he was found innocent.
As you wish, knight. I'll set him free immediately.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! Shame!

Not too long ago we got the orders from the First Knight Don Rodrigo de Velacor to mobilize the Hillbrandt regiment and to reinforce the town defenses. We were also ordered to requisition horses and draft cattle, to fill granaries and to build up supplies of provisions. So it really seems a war is at hand. Well, but it's not sure against whom. Monsters pestering Hillbrandt can't be defeated on the battlefield...
What? You have arrested Edmond d'Arvias! The Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, superior of the local Chapter? It will cause lots of problems, believe me, Father. But if you insist...
WHAT?! Are you insane, Father? You have arrested an Inquisitorial judge! And you want me to put him into a cell and keep him there?
Edmond d'Arvias? Oh my... Well, it's your call, Father. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack or strappado?
Linda van Gallagan? Well, Father, I'm afraid you can't do that...

Well, the problem is she isn't, Father. You know, I'm not very good with these legal issues, but from my work I know that the Inquisition Codex forbids torturing pregnant women and children. And Baroness van Gallagan is pregnant—there's no doubt about that. Before she disappeared she met with Würtenrodt the herbalist and she confirmed her story. So I'm sorry, Father, but you can't use torture in the interrogation.
My god. Are you really absolutely sure that you want to do it, Father? I can lively imagine what would happen if judge Vallarian were proven innocent.
So you have managed to kill some green skins, Father. That's good news. The more will be sent back to hell the less people will die when they attack us again. Well, show me what you have...
Excellent, Father! It's a valuable trophy, no kidding. A dead orc is a good orc. Here's you reward.
Excellent, Father! It's a worthy trophy. Those bastards are so strong that they can chop a man in half with a single blow—as if he were just a withered stick. Here's your reward.
That's great, Father! It's quite a worthy trophy. Those beasts are more dangerous than anything I can imagine. Here's your reward.
I have the head of Rashgar the orc Khan.
Wait a moment, Father. Are you trying to tell me that this... that this is the head of Rashgar the orc Khan?! Legendary ruler whose armies destroyed Thron the pagan Empire?

Damn me! He's asking me about a reward for the Khan's head. You just kill the orc Khan, a terrible beast from terrifying legends who ruled all the bloody green skins below the mountains and you just ask me as if nothing happened if there's a reward? The Duke will endow you with gold when he hears about it! Go see him and show him the head of that beast. I guarantee you won't be able to carry that sack of gold! Good Lord... I'm sure it will cheer up all my men, you can bet! Khan Rashgar is dead! Oh yes...!
Very well, Father. What else can I do for you?

Hello, Father. I'm Jacob Contemburry the local Sheriff. I must admit that you're coming to the town in rather troubled times. The hordes of green skins occupying the Moonshine Mountains can attack us any day now. Nobody knows exactly from where they came and how many of them is hiding there. It seems the old legends came to life and the evil which once walked the earth has returned. Something must be quickly done about it. Duke Weinberg asked Glatzburg for reinforcements several times, but nobody listens to his pleas. They say there are problems in the south as well and they can't spare any soldiers. Unbelievable. So I hope the inquisitors such as you might help us.

Help me? Well, it's hard to say. You're a priest and also an inquisitor, so I'm sure you have your own tasks. Well, now that I think about it, I might need your help. I have a problem with one of my soldiers—Jullian. He has been avoiding duty for several days, which is obviously desertion. Unless he's quickly found and punished, my men will start disappearing like ghosts. And it's the last thing I need. Could you find him and bring him back?
Really? I'm really thankful, Father. I didn't hope to get any help. Thanks again. Bring him to me when you find him.
Sure, go ahead, Father.
Thought so. I'm sure you have more important things to do than helping the defensiveness of the town. God bless you, Father.
As you want, Father. But make it quick, I have my duties and they won't wait.
Well, then escort him into the town at once, Father. We can't let him stay loitering around the town without punishment.
Thanks, Father. I knew we could make a deal!
Well, you're right, Father. Obviously I mistakenly got a feeling that you could help me. Well, nevermind, I'll send some of my men there.
Of course, Father. But make it quick, I have my duties and they won't wait.

Really? You say he attacked you... well, then it's good you killed him. Originally I thought I could discipline him, but obviously I was mistaken. Thanks, Father. Here's some gold for the problems Jullian caused you. I must watch my men better.

Any town Sheriff has only as much power as the royal governor allows—well but the powers are always connected only with military service and public order. Well, regarding me, I administer the entire Hillbrandt military garrison. I do everything—from getting supplies to recruitment and training. I also manage the town jail, which inquisitors, such as yourself, find the most interesting, right? If you arrest somebody, you can put him into jail with my permission. And when you'd like to rack him, just ask. Well, but I hope there won't be too much torture—I'm damn busy even without it. Damn orcs and other infernal maggots are giving us hell!
Greetings, Father. Do you have any news about Jullian? If we don't capture him fast, it could undermine the morale of all my men. And it's the last thing I could afford these damn days.
Alright, Father. But make it short, I don't have much time.

Huh? Are you telling me that he kidnapped Natalia Reichmann? And that he attacked you? Then it's good he's dead. Originally I thought the boy could be disciplined, but obviously I was mistaken. Thank you, Father. Here's some gold for the troubles he caused. I must watch better over my men.
Greetings, Father. Do you need my assistance? If not, please leave me to do my job.
Please make it quick, Father. I don't have much time.
Greetings, Father. Do you need something?

As you wish, Father. I'll set him free immediately.

Well, the word is that heretics are behind the crisis. They caused God to turn away from us and so the good believers suffer for the sins of others. I'll be honest with you, noble lord—if it's really so, the only thing that can solve the crisis is force. The royal power must be upheld no matter the cost. The Inquisition is good, but it's too inefficient and slow, because it must respect laws. Gimme a regiment of the royal army and I'll scour the Realm, city after city, town after town, village after village... believe me the crisis would be over in no time! All we need is a quick decisive strike and heretics will be demoralized before they can say their false prayers! Long story short, we need another Saint Berthold Night...
I'm right, noble lord. Believe me.

Yes, I pay rewards for dead orcs. Bring me some orc scalp or head and the reward in gold is yours. The bigger the orc, the bigger the reward, noble lord. Well, but to be honest, I haven't paid many rewards so far. There are not many who went hunting orcs and returned. It's simply too dangerous.

Hillbrandt is nowadays surrounded by hordes of infernal vermin, noble lord. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, there has been too many damn bastards crawling from the bowels of the earth. But to tell the truth, noble lord, orcs are the most frightening of them all. Green skins. I don't know if you've already heard about them... Those infernal fiends have appeared in the early spring in the Moonshine Mountains, nobody knows through what hellholes they got there. Before anybody could react they ransacked entire mining village Asherbalt, including nearby iron mines. And to make it even worse it seems that the orcs have settled there to do some mischief, because since they got into the mines a thick black smoke has been fuming from the bowels of the mountains. They raid the entire region, so we are almost cut off from the rest of the Realm—no merchant dares to travel to the town. I'm afraid they will swarm in front of the walls and will storm us—as they did one night several days back. But this time there will be hundredfold more of those bastards...

So you wanna hear about the green skins, noble lord? I don't know how is it with you, noble lord, but I first heard about them in the legends regarding old pagan kingdoms populated by inhuman races. Well, but it was a long time ago. The rumor is that the orcs were summoned by some infernal being called Cursed Flame from the forsaken place called Accursed Depths. God knows what it means. Anyway, they were summoned to crush a proud and powerful empire called Thron which lied below the mountains. And they did their job well. They reduced the barbarian empire to ashes. And with Thron wiped out, the mysterious pagan race living there vanished as well.

To be honest, noble lord, I don't suspect anyone in the town of being a heretic. I'm a soldier and so I believe only things I can see. And if I see a heretic threatening God or the King I kill him. It's my job. I've heard some rumors about master Edmond d'Arvias, but I won't comment at it. I haven't seen him doing anything bad and as far as I know he's a man who has destroyed good many hell spawns! I don't think he would be a demon hunter and a demon servant at the same time...

Lots of things happened, so I don't know about which I should tell you first. Well, probably the worst thing that befell Hillbrandt was that night attack of the green skins, they managed either by some ploy or betrayal to get inside the town. Hell broke lose. It was a terrible bloodbath! I lost almost quarter of my men before we managed to push them behind the walls. Well, to be honest, I don't think that it was their main attack. I have a feeling that there are many more hiding beneath the mountains. I think they're waiting for something and that attack was just a harbinger of terrors to come. Anyway they mustn't get into the town again. We can hold them behind the walls for quite some time.

The theft the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius is a terrible loss, noble lord. I can't imagine who could have done that—the Holy Mother Church valued and guarded it above all else. I'm sure it was some licentious heretic proficient in unclean infernal powers, because he managed to put to sleep all the priests praying in the church for the salvation of mankind. In the morning they found them sleeping on the floor among the pews. There's no doubt that they were lulled to sleep by the culprit who then seized the monstrance. Well, I was ordered to look into it, but I wasn't successful. We didn't find a single trace leading to the culprits.

I'm sorry, noble lord, but I don't know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus. He disappeared the night when the orcs attacked the town—nobody has seen him since. Well, if it were up to me I'd add him to the casualties of the orcs, but Father Dominicus won't allow, he's probably waiting for the body to be found. Well I doubt it can be found, as far as I know orcs are cannibals who eat their fallen foes.

If I had one I wouldn't hesitate to bust him, believe me, noble lord. But there were no leads to help us in the investigation. The murderer entered the room, killed the merchant and then left without being noticed. No witnesses, no traces.
You're welcome, noble lord.

Set the stake afire already! I'm waiting here just to see the treacherous heretics burn in infernal flames! Death to the heretics!
Death to the bloody heretics! Burn the witches at the stake! Burn the misbelievers. Burn the idol worshippers!
Execution at stake is terrible. But no death is terrible enough when it comes to punishing heretics! I'm glad that the Inquisition did its homework. Finally we can have some fun...
May all the devil's lackeys burn. May they burn in infernal flames. May they burn!
I'm glad there are the executions. There would be no fun in the world without them...
Are they going to set the stake afire soon?! I'm waiting here just to see the treacherous heretics burn in infernal flames!
Death to the heretics! Burn the witches at the stake! Burn the misbelievers. Burn the idol worshippers! I wanna see them burn!
Execution at stake is terrible. But no death is terrible enough when it comes to punishing heretics, right?!

I'm glad there are the executions. There would be no fun in the world without them... I attend executions whenever I can—I think that burning is the most fun. Especially if the executioner is skilled and can build the stake at which the sentenced roasts for a long time before they give up the ghost.
Klael'eprah edwaar sterneal arte des leehwa'est!
Aeern'thal ruth estre santi'ediomo rweenshal Kae'saar etheal morthum est!
I won't allow such a hellish monstrosity to walk the face of earth! Die, unclean spirit!
I don't understand you, wandering soul. Your language is unknown to me.
Wait, lost soul. If you are Elenian Grand Duke Fae'Darlion, I ask you for forgiveness for desecrating your grave. I had no other option, please hear my plea!
Greetings, knight. How is it going? Could I have a little talk with you?
What is it, soldier, do you need to confide something to me?

Just that, knight. It concerns my friend Jullian, a Hillbrandt soldier just like me. He hasn't been on duty for several days now. It's too bad because Sheriff Contemburry noticed he was missing and proclaimed him to be a deserter. But I'm not sure that he deserted. You know, lately he was very interested in Natalia Reichmann, the daughter of the merchant Stefan Reichmann. I don't know what she thought about it, but when her father got the word he went mad and told Jullian that if he even looks at his daughter again he's gonna kill him.
Do you think he really did it?
I don't know, knight. I just needed to tell it to somebody. I thought it to be quite a coincidence.
Thank you, soldier.
I find it hard to believe that a merchant would do something so low.
I don't know, knight. But I needed to tell it to somebody. I thought it to be quite a coincidence.
I heard that Natalia Reichmann was murdered by a certain Olfghard. Do you think it might be somehow connected?
I'm sorry, but I don't have time.
Sorry for intruding then. Didn't know you're in such a hurry. Farewell.
Greetings, soldier.

Greetings, knight. It's a bad duty, if you ask me. Danger all around, beasts behind every corner, and as if that was not enough, we have those damned heretics. A few years back, one would not think that things could end up like this.
Have faith, soldier. The days are not over yet.
Who is that Stefan Reichmann?

Merchant Stefan Reichmann is one of the richest men in the town, knight. Well, it's true that the Scourges of God took away most of his wealth, but compared to the locals, he's still a rich man. He owns several houses in Hillbrandt, but if you'd like to talk to him, you can probably find him in the local tavern—he spends most of his time there. It is said he's waiting there for better days. Try asking him if he doesn't know something about Jullian, maybe he'll slip...
Greetings, Father. How is it going? Could I have a little talk with you?
What is it, my son, do you need to confess?

Confess? Well, no, Father, I don't need to confess. It's something else. My friend Jullian, a Hillbrandt soldier just like me, hasn't been on duty for several days now. Baron Decard of Longhorn's Ghost
My treasure... someone has taken my treasure! Filthy thief... you'll pay for the crime with your life!
I am sorry, wandering soul—I did not want to disturb your eternal rest. I'll return your treasure to the last gold coin!
I will take not only my treasure, but your soul as well, thief! Sssaaaahhhh!
I declare your treasure confiscated! You may regard it as escheat property!
If werewolf Kenthwarr spoke the truth, the treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn should be under this stone. I hope that it's not some infernal trap.

Goodness gracious... the treasure is really there! The werewolf didn't lie... All the possessions of Baron of Longhorn are here! Gold, precious stones, magic items... If I take them I'll be a rich man!
Goodness gracious... the treasure is really there! The werewolf didn't lie... Well, I think that I'll leave the treasure be. God knows why Kenthwarr didn't take it himself. It might be cursed...
The treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn is still hidden here...
I'll take it—I want to be rich!
I'd better leave it be. God knows why Kenthwarr didn't take it himself. It might be cursed...
Enough of those abominations! May righteous divine wrath delivered by my hand will punish your blasphemous presence in the Kingdom of God on Earth!
You are mistaken, my dear—it's you who will be punished for daring to hinder the wheel of inevitability. You are not supposed to be here. Prepare to meet your new close friend—Death!
You will never know, my dear. The Plan will remain hidden from you forever. You are not supposed to be here. Prepare to meet your new close friend—Death!

Lo, who is coming there?! Who has entered the place where no one is supposed to be?! No mortal is supposed to disrupt the magnificent work of the Dark Lord and of those who bear the Mark of the Beast. What are you doing here, fool? The only thing you can find here is death—I am sure you are aware of it...
Who are you, fallen soul? By what right are you trying to stop me? Isn't this a holy place where the dead should slumber in their eternal rest?

Obviously, they are rather restless, my dear. I am Princess Diana and I was given new undead life to fulfill the will of my spiritual Father. My sisters and many of my ancestors were raised as well—I believe you had the honor of meeting them on your way here. I hope you regarded them with due respect—after all they are members of the royal family!
Who raised you, Princess? Who committed such a heinous crime?!

Does it really matter who raised me and my family? The only thing that matters is that we are here and that we are part of the Great Plan which will soon be accomplished. I can feel His presence here in this dungeon. Yes, I can feel his hot breath. Soon, he will be among us! Soon, that what is supposed to be will come to pass!
What infernal abominations are you talking about? What are you trying to do, you shameless hellspawn?!
I urge you, Princess, if there's at least a little spark of faith left in your soul, please tell me, who raised you and what is your mission here? I must know!

Glatzburg is ruled by that cunning bastard Grand Duke Heidrick. You seem surprised to hear how I'm talking 'bout him, right? Don't you think—it's damn fitting. If I've ever met a man who cares just about himself and who doesn't detest to use any means to ensure his plans go well, then it's Grand Duke Heidrick, the royal governor of the city. His vice Govenor is Duke Rowan van Leerin—a very fair gentleman, though I don't agree with some of his opinions. If only he could replace that fat pig Heidrick... But it's high politics, so I'd better keep my mouth shut.
Then I can't help you, knight.
Believe me, knight, the best goods in the city can be bought only in my shop! You can chop my hand off if I'm lying!
What do you think about the crisis that is spreading throughout the Realm?
Well, it will cost you $$getmoney5$$ gp.

Look, knight, I'm a merchant—it's a job our Lord has given to me and I'm sure that in his endless wisdom he wants me to do it well. So I'm trying to do his will. And as regards this crisis, those Scourges of God, the religious unrest and the political skirmishes—it's all good for business. Every time things like that happen the prices soar high—and it's good. I don't wanna tell you that I like the crisis—Heaven forbid! Who would want to live in constant danger that some beast will tear his heart from his chest at night, or that a fanatical crowd sent by some self-proclaimed prophet, who thinks that you're Satan himself, beats you to death. But on the other hand, business flourishes—who can blame me for liking it?!
I heard that there's a war coming. Do you know anything about it?
Yep, you heard right, there's gonna be a war. It's brought me both good and bad things.

Every time there's going to be a skirmish, the royal army tries to acquire every piece of military stuff they can get. And smith Hans von Drichtmaul can't fully satisfy their demands, though I must admit that he's a skillful and quick guy. So they wanted my goods as well. They came to me, I offered them a good price and the deal was made. Two threescores halberds, five dozen longswords, three dozen bows... it was lotsa stuff. They wouldn't do it if they had no reason. Guess the only reason can be war. You can chop my hand off if I'm wrong!
So you made a profit...

Well, yep, that deal was profitable. But then they came and told me that I had three geldings in my stables—they requisitioned them for military purposes. That bloody royal edict allows them to requisition draft cattle and horses in the time of war. Damn the bastards and their stupid war.
In that case I can't help you, knight. My memory isn't what it used to be, you know...

I've never seen them with my own eyes, but people say that from time to time there are hellspawns in the woods—they live in the Devil's Caverns near the ruins of Galibornium. People say they are devils who crawl straight from hell to feed on fresh human flesh. Grand Duke Heidrick offered a reward for killing brigands who pester the roads. It's paid by Sheriff Smith. But there aren't many volunteers—certainly less than rogues, I'd say.

If you did you'd be hung before you could say amen. Anyway there are some rumors... And if you put all the pieces together you'll get a really interesting picture.

Just look at all those atrocities which happen all around and then look at the Grand Duke and his family—obviously, nothing happened to them. Many people lost their homes or families, but not the Grand Duke. And what is he doing to improve things for all of us? Not much... It almost seems as if the situation were not that bad for him. Or maybe even... Well, enough talking—I don't wanna get into trouble. I just wanted to answer your question...
Have you ever heard about the Children of the New Order? It's a heretic cult.

Hmm... I don't recall hearing about them. But I'm no expert on heretic cults, knight. They seem all the same to me. All the heretics rumble about the end of the world, love sin, have sex at Sabbaths, desecrate the Hosts, blaspheme and most importantly don't do any business. Why are you asking about that cult anyway?
I'm looking for its members here in Glatzburg.

I heard something about them and now I would like to know some details.

Maybe. It depends on if you are willing to pay me $$getmoney25$$ gp.

During his years in the office, lotsa girls, boys and even little children disappeared. Nobody found them—or better to say nobody found them in one piece. The case was investigated by several paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous—five, if I remember right—and in the end the Duke became their prime suspect. But there was no hard evidence, so he just kept laughing at the paladins. And the girls kept on disappearing.

But then one of the girls managed to escape. She told the paladins about all the perversities the Duke committed. No need to go into details; guess you can imagine what he was doing to them. The paladins didn't hesitate and chased down the Duke who meanwhile tried to escape and brought him back to the city in chains. His execution was quite a show, people came from far and wide to see it. But the Duke seemed to be in quite a good mood, he was laughing madly all the time and just before he perished he uttered a terrible curse.
What curse, If I may ask?

That he will one day return from Hell to get all his murderers. The people lost the mood at once, you know, such a curse can affect anybody. Anyway, the execution was finished—executioner Yan Flemberg did his job well and the Duke's remains were then decorating the city gates for quite some time. The curse was completely forgotten. But imagine what happened! This spring all five paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous responsible for capturing the Duke suddenly died. And believe me, it had to be quite a painful death—their bodies were almost impossible to identify. So it seems that the laughing Duke has really returned to wreak vengeance on those responsible for his death. And the only one who still lives is Yan Flemberg who then led the execution. I'm not surprised that he's scarred shitless.

I'm sorry, knight, but I don't know anything about the murder of bishop Trevorius. Well, they found him at the Grand Duke's gazebo. I guess rogues or maybe hellspawns are responsible—they are flocking to the city these days as if it were the Sabbath. The only thing I don't get is what was the bishop's business there. Nobody goes there these days...

I heard that you were discussing the virginity of local girls and women in Wanda Gielwitch's pub. Is it true?

Is it a crime or what?!
All those girls who have recently disappeared in Glatzburg were virgins...

What can you tell me about the undead who kill people in the city streets at night?

I can certainly tell you one thing 'bout those zombies stalking the streets at night—it's really strange that their victims are always completely looted to the last gold coin, to the smallest earring or to the thinnest necklace. Chop my hand off if it weren't that bastard Tinthan. He steals everything he sees. And he sees lotsa things! So if you meet him, try to clamp down on him, knight, and he might just hand it over...

People say they are devils who crawl straight from hell to feed on fresh human flesh. They look a bit like normal people, but they have tails, fiendish maws, long paws and snake scales instead of skin. If you get into their grip, you're as good as dead.
Grand Duke Heidrick offered a reward for killing brigands who pester the roads. It's paid by Sheriff Smith. But there aren't many volunteers, certainly less than rogues, I'd say.

Just look at all those atrocities which happen all around and then look at the Grand Duke and his family, obviously nothing happened to them. Many people lost their homes or families, but not the Grand Duke. And what is he doing to improve things for all of us? Not much... It almost seems as if the situation were not that bad for him. Or maybe even... Well, enough talking I don't wanna get into trouble. I just wanted to answer your question...

Hmm... I don't recall hearing about them. But I'm no expert on heretic cults, noble lord. They all seem the same to me. All the heretics rumble about the end of the world, love sin, have sex at Sabbaths, desecrate the Hosts, blaspheme and most importantly don't do any business. Why are you asking about that cult anyway?
I could have guessed that. Anyway, I've never ever heard about such a cult. Sorry, but it seems I can't help you with that, noble lord.
Yes, I see. Though you're not going to hear much about them from me, because I've never heard about such a cult. I'm sorry, noble lord.
Well, you're right, noble lord. You're the one asking the questions, I get it. Anyway, I've never ever heard about such a cult. So I can't help you, noble lord.

Have you ever heard the name Istwan de Bragho? Used to be the royal vice-governor. You know, he was a Duke, aristocrat, blue blood. But in fact he was a damn son of a bitch, lecher and sodomite. During his years in the office, lotsa girls, boys and even little children disappeared. Nobody found them, or better to say nobody found them in one piece. The case was investigated by several paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous five, if I remember right, and in the end the Duke became their prime suspect. But there was no hard evidence, so he just kept laughing at the paladins. And the girls kept on disappearing.

I'm sorry, noble lord, but I don't know anything about the murder of bishop Trevorius. Well, they found him at the Grand Duke's gazebo. I guess rogues or maybe hellspawns are responsible, they are flocking to the city these days as if it were the Sabbath. The only thing I don't get is what was the bishop's business there. Nobody goes there these days...

With all respect, noble lord, I heard that you were involved in it. I heard that they found you kneeling over the body which was yet warm. If I didn't know you... Well, it's probably a mistake, but it must be a damn bad feeling to be a suspect. You can never know when they are going to bust you telling you that they have enough evidence to use the right of torture. Dark torture chamber, you on the rack, no witnesses, just you and an interrogating Inquisitor. It's giving me goose bumps, what 'bout you?

What? What are you talking about? Are you kidding? It goes without saying that I don't discuss Holy Scripture in pubs. It's possible, well, almost sure that I was talking about things like that with somebody. And I guess we were having a damn good time discussing it. Maybe I'll discuss it again soon. Is it a crime or what?!

Oh I see, you came here to make up an accusation, right? But you've chosen damn weak evidence, noble lord. I discussed almost everything in the pub, and believe me, the virginity of the local women is the least interest of it. Accusing somebody of kidnapping just because he's discussing woman treasures is not a good path to take. So I'm sorry, noble lord.
You're welcome, noble lord. But I must say that sometimes you ask really strange questions...

I can certainly tell you one thing 'bout those zombies stalking the streets at night, it's really strange that their victims are always completely looted to the last gold coin, to the smallest earring or to the thinnest necklace. Sometimes even their buttons are missing... It's damn strange for a bunch of killing zombies!

Chop my hand off if it weren't that bastard Tinthan. He steals everything he sees. And he sees lotsa things! So if you meet him, try to clamp down on him, noble lord, and he might just hand it over...

There're lotsa suspicions like that nowadays. People are blaming heretics and their black magic for almost everything, poor crop, bloated cow, dead hen, cough, blackheads... whatever. It's so easy to get rid of somebody you don't like just by accusing him. I don't wanna say that it's the same with Hans Thomas Brookwelt, but if you ask me, I don't think that he's a philanderer, let alone sorcerer. He's a hard working guy, no doubt, after all carpenters are in high demand nowadays, especially those who can make coffins...

Chateau de Trebrechette, you say? Hmm... It's a problem. Times are bad, merchants are afraid to even peek out of the city gates and Chateau de Trebrechette is exclusively imported goods. You might be able to get it in Alvaron, but the price would be extremely steep. After all it's the most renowned wine of the Empire. I'm sorry, noble lord, that I couldn't help you. Well, unless you wanna go to Alvaron to buy there the wine yourself.

Yes, I heard that Raquel Gielwitch is missing. Well to be honest, it's no wonder. She was kinda... weird. She had such a strange look in her eyes as if she were absent-minded but also as if she saw to the depths of your soul. If you ask me, she was possessed by Devil, noble lord! So it's quite likely he took her to him so they could cavort together in his infernal bed...

Dead serious, noble lord. There are lotsa events like that nowadays. People consort with the dark powers and they think that's like in a whorehouse, that they get what they've paid for. But they're mistaken—Devil's damn usurious!

Nice to see you, noble lord. So what brings you here? Do you wanna buy something? Or maybe you have some stuff to sell. Whatever you want, I'm sure we'll make a good deal. Maybe you're interested in information, right? Even information can have its price nowadays, am I right? And what fortune brought you to Glatzburg, noble lord? I don't know you and I doubt that you've been in the city for a long time. I assure you that I get to know 'bout everyone who passes through the city gate!

Are you asking me who I am? Ha! An interesting question. Haven't heard it for ages. You know, noble lord, everybody knows me here. Even those who have never heard 'bout me... The name is Alphonso DiCerbio, all arounder when it comes to serving customers! Chop my hand off if I can't get you anything you need!

But of course, noble lord, I'd love to have a little chat with you. Nevertheless I must warn you in advance that it's not gonna be for free... Well, some of my information is kinda expensive—depends on whom it's concerning. But I don't think it's so unusual—rare stuff is expensive. And you can chop my hand off if any of my information won't satisfy you.

Of course I know who you are, noble lord! My name is DiCerbio, isn't it? DiCerbio knows everything... But don't be mistaken, noble lord. Even the Holy Inquisition buys my information, so don't be upset and don't think that I'm denying to tell you something, I'm just asking for a little benevolence. You know, I have seven mouths to feed!
As you want, noble lord. But keep in mind DiCerbio is here just for you. If you need anything you know where to find me. And you can chop my hand off if I'm lying!
Of course, noble lord. DiCerbio is here just for you!

As you wish, noble lord... Please come in and take a look around DiCerbio's humble shop. Everything we have is just waiting for you and you can chop my hand off if I can't get you anything you need in a few days!
As you wish, noble lord... Farewell. Please keep in mind that if you need anything you know where to find me. DiCerbio bids you goodbye!
Nice to see you, noble lord. Are you here for some goods? Or do you want to sell something? Maybe you are here for some questions, right?
But of course, noble lord. I'll tell you everything you need to know for a few gold coins—and maybe I'll even add a bonus!

I'm sorry, noble lord, but I don't know anything about it. Somebody has mistaken me for someone else, it happens. So take your accusation and leave my shop. Of course it would be different if you had a warrant of arrest. But I'd bet you don't have it!

So it seems that luck is no longer on DiCerbio's side... I didn't expect it to end like this... I thought... to hell with what I thought. The situation is exactly as you say, noble lord. I'll confess. But I have one condition...
Great, noble lord. I'm glad you're so wise. When I'm finished you'll agree that my skin is damn worthless compared to the skins of the others involved.

So... I'm not exactly a saint, noble lord. That's for sure. I had a sorrowful childhood—my parents died when I was still very young and I had to manage for myself. I tried studying and becoming a priest, but I didn't have enough money to graduate the seminary.

All right, all right... Well, anyway I just wanted to say that I've committed enough crimes to make any priest grey during a confession. But I've also met certain people... Compared to them I was just a naughty child. And I met one of those just here in Glatzburg. He told me that he was chosen to do something really big and that Fallen Archangel Azrael himself told him to find me and allow me to serve him. I was kinda surprised by it, but in the end I told myself why not? I would go straight to hell for all the treasures that guy offered me. Moreover it was obvious that he had everything well calculated and that I wouldn't make a mistake if I join him to do his biding. I was also sure that if I refused my head would be soon found in some bloody gutter. He was really an influential and powerful guy, noble lord. Too powerful!
Yes, noble lord, just so.
Excellent, noble lord. I'd take my leave then. And to be honest, I hope we won't meet again. Don't take it personally. Farewell.
If it's the God's will... But hear my warning, DiCerbio, if you lied to me, you won't escape the wrath of God and just punishment!
I told you the truth, noble lord. Farewell.
If you want it the hard way, noble lord, you'll get it. Nobody has ever managed to capture DiCerbio!

It's really nice of you, noble lord. But I don't have anything to confess. Moreover, do you think me to be as stupid as to wait here for you until you get it? I know the methods of investigation well enough to be sure that by torturing me you can make me confess to absolutely anything, regardless if it's the truth or a lie. I just have a feeling that we see each other for the last time, noble lord. Farewell!
As you want, noble lord—you asked for it! Nobody has ever managed to capture DiCerbio!

Enough, noble lord, I give up. I don't wanna die as a filthy dog. I'd rather lie at your mercy than die here in this dirt. I've been trying to get away from this mess all my damn life, but to no end. So I don't wanna sign out my soul in it!
Very reasonable words, DiCerbio. However, for an assault on a member of the nobility I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!

I won't pretend that I'm glad to see you, noble lord. I hope that our agreement still holds good—I confessed to all the stuff I did for that madman Rowan van Leerin and you agreed to leave me be. Right?
Sure, noble lord, don't worry. Farewell.
As you want, noble lord, you're leaving DiCerbio no other option than to quickly dispatch you up there. And you can chop my hand off if I'm lying!
As you want, noble lord, you're leaving me no other option than to quickly dispatch you up there. And you can chop my hand off if I'm lying!

A noble steals?! It's unbelievable! I've always thought that if the nobles want to come by wealth they raise new levies or such. But I've never heard they just come and take money from people. Isn't it called theft? And you may get your hand cut off for a theft, at least that's what I've heard. So beware, noble lord!
What?! Do you really expect me to believe that? No way. They will come at night hammering at my door, I know it!
I'm telling the truth, good man. All the undead from the cemetery have been destroyed. If you don't believe me, you can look around!

Holy gosh... by the Saint Baudolino, if it is true... then I'm finally going to get a good night sleep! No more guarding the door with a spade in my hand in case one of those undead beasts managed to get inside!
Exactly. So are you going to come out or not?
Well... I can now. All right, I'm coming out. But no tricks, all right? If you are a zombie, I'm going to hit you over the head with my spade before you can say 'I want your brains!'
Hello, anybody there?
Begone, demon! Begone, away from my door. You'll return no more... or... whatever the damn formula was!
You are mistaken, good man. I'm not a demon. I'm a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

Really? Well, anybody could say that—even a demon! Maybe you are one of those zombies which roam around my house each night trying to smash my door open so they can eat my brains. Don't think I'll open—I'm not a fool!
I told you who I was. If you don't believe me, come out and you see for yourself.
I'm not buying this nasty trick. I'm staying in. Go away!
In the name of justice open the door and come outside! It's the Brotherhood of the Righteous here!
No!
What if I offered you some gold for coming out?
Then I would send you where you came from. Nobody's going to fool me with tricks like that! Don't even try or else the pastor is going to hang himself after my next confession!
If you don't open the door voluntarily, I'll smash it open and drag you out!
I don't think so! I barricaded it. And if a bunch of zombies which comes here every night can't smash my door, you definitely won't.
Who are you, good man?

It's none of your business. Was I asking you who you were and what were you doing out there? And besides—who do you think I am when I live at the cemetery and make my living digging the graves? I'm Dietrich, the local gravedigger. But why should I tell you anything...
Open the door. I just want to ask you few questions.

Questions? Shove your questions up your ass, whoever you are. I have corpses here hanging around each night trying to break into my house and eat my brains and you want to ask me some goddamn questions? Oh no. Shut up and get out of here.
So if I understand correctly you are afraid of the undead who hang around the cemetery, is that right?

Oh, you must be a really smart person to have figured that out in such a short time. Of course I'm afraid of the undead. Wouldn't you be afraid if you were awoken by hammering at your door in the middle of the night and found out it was your undead granny coming for a visit and expecting you to treat her with you brains? You must be a tough person.
All right, enough of that. This isn't getting anywhere. If I help you get rid of those undead monsters, will you come out of your house and answer my questions?
Well... if you could do that, it would radically change the situation, that's true. All right, we have a deal. But no tricks, understand? I'm not going to get my brain eaten by a rotten zombie.
You don't have to be afraid anymore, good man. All the undead monsters from the municipal cemetery are back in the hell they came from. You can come out of your house now.
Are you there, Dietrich?
Of course I'm here, where did you expect me to be. Did you do all the devilish beasts around here in?
No, not yet.
Then leave me alone. Until there are no more zombies around, I'm not going anywhere! Goodbye.
You don't have to be afraid of the undead anymore. I destroyed them all.
You are mistaken, good man. I'm not a demon. I'm a priest from the Holy Office
In the name of the Holy Inquisition open the door and come out!
You are mistaken, good man. I'm not a demon. I'm a man and a noble on top of it. You don't need to be afraid of anything.

Really? Well, anybody could say that, even a demon! Maybe you are one of those zombies which roam around my house each night trying to smash my door open so they can eat my brains. Don't think I'll open the door, I'm not a fool!
In the name of justice open the door and come outside!
You were heard at Wanda Gielwitch's inn saying that you knew who was behind all the evil things happening in Glatzburg. I would like to know who's that. Can you tell me?
Ech... what did you say I was saying? That I knew who was behind all the evil in Glatzburg? I must have been drunk... I was talking nonsense.
Are you testing my patience, Dietrich? I wouldn't do that if I were you!

Well... All right, all right... The pittance she gave me... Some time ago somebody knocked at my door. First I thought it was the zombies coming to eat my brain but then I found out it was HER. I was shocked, believe me. I'm just a simple gravedigger, I don't normally have visitors like that. Especially not at night. And when she told me what she wanted from me I was totally perplexed.
What did she want from you?

She gave me a pouch of gold and asked me to get her a corpse from the cemetery. That would be scary enough—especially because it was someone like her. But it wasn't everything. She said it must be a corpse of an insane girl who wasn't a virgin and she mustn't have been lying in the holy ground for more than thirteen days. Completely crazy. But I could use the money, of course... and I was also afraid to decline her offer. She looked like she would thrust a dagger into my heart any instant. So I did it for her. I watched who was being buried and in time I got what she wanted. So she was happy and gave me another pouch of gold to be silent.
Who was the person?
You wouldn't believe it, knight. It was Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. I swear! Let my soul burn in hell, if I'm lying.
I don't believe you. I think you're lying!
I knew you wouldn't believe me, knight. That's why I didn't want to tell you. But you insisted so now you have what you wanted. And now leave me alone.
How much money did she give you all in all?
I don't know exactly. I didn't count it.
Well... nevermind. Anyway, give it to me. It is an exhibit and I confiscate it for the investigation's sake. And if you decide to resist I will have you arrested.
But... that's theft! Oh my god, this is a terrible world. Here's your gold and you can choke to death on it!
This is dirty money, Dietrich. You should donate it to the church or to a charity.
But I... uhm... maybe you're right. I'll do it. I'll get rid of the money before it brings me bad luck...
Who's the ruler here in Glatzburg? Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, of course. He is the royal governor of the city. And the vice-governor is duke Rowan van Leerin.
Where can you buy some goods in Glatzburg?

Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned armory in Glatzburg. You can get potions and various magic items from Enrie Jungwirdt, the wise woman, and from Paolus Ventimus, the alchemist. Wanda Gielwitch, the tavern owner, and Ludwig Weintraum the innkeeper both have a variety of goods for sale. And you can barter for anything at Alphonso DiCerbio's, if you don't mind the origin of the goods.

What do I think of these miserable times? The same as the people in the city. It's the end of the world. It's not good when corpses walk around the cemetery as if they were on parade trying to catch you and eat you. I definitely think it's not normal. I don't think too much about it, I'm not the thinking type. But I agree with what the people in the city say. The end of the world is coming. The Heavens will be flooded with blood of the faithful and Satan leading his devilish legion will come up to the Earth to trample down those who still believe in God with his fiery hooves.
Supposedly, there is a war brewing. Do you know anything about it?
A war, you say? Well... I've heard something but I don't care too much about it. I'm a gravedigger, not a soldier. But if there is a war, I might make some money—God forgive me.

What monsters and devils can you encounter here in Glatzburg? Are you kidding me, knight? You can tell at first sight what kind of devilish bastards hang around the city. There are living corpses square-dancing in front of my house each night and you are asking whether I have by any chance seen a monster around here? Look around and see for yourself, knight.
I'm sorry, knight, but I don't suspect anyone of heresy. You know, times are bad, one is trying to stay alive... It's better not to see and hear anything.
Except for Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, I don't suspect anyone of heresy, knight. And about her, I told you everything. I swear by my dead granny.

I think one thing worth mentioning would be that a few young girls went missing recently. For example Raquel, the sister of innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch. She wasn't fifteen yet. She disappeared together with a few others without any trace. I hate to think of what might have happened to them.

No, knight, I don't know anything about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. I only heard they found him murdered at the Grand Duke's gazebo behind the city. It must be a great loss for the Mother Church..
I heard something about the murder, that's right. But you probably won't be happy to hear that...
Could you tell me why?
Well... they say it was you. It feels weird to be telling you... Because if it was you, you must know so you don't have to be asking me, do you?

I don't know anything about Ethien de Pasque's chain. But I'd bet my granny that it was that trickster Tinthan. He pretends to be an actor, a big artist but all he can really do is steal things. That's what he's famous for here in Glatzburg rather than for being a real actor. So I'd recommend you ask HIM about the paladin's chain.
I heard that Hans Thomas Brookwelt is possessed by dark powers which help him to seize Glatzburg women and girls. What do you think about such a suspicion?

It's true that they say strange things about Brookwelt. He's supposed to be a wizard who possesses women with the help of dark powers and ravishes them. I don't know if this is true but I'd make sure whether the gossips are not spread by women who were caught cheating on their husbands so they blame it on a wizard rather than confessing that they voluntarily spread their legs and let their lover enjoy the joys of marriage.
I've heard that servant girl Jeanette was a witch performing dark rituals. Do you know anything about it?

Servant Jeanette a witch? I don't think so... I don't know her very well but she is a quiet type, I can't imagine her on a broomstick flying to Sabbath. It sounds quite unlikely. But the times are weird, that's true.
Do you have any idea where the legendary hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul could be found? They say Bonhart hid it before he went to war...

You're looking for Bonhart von Drichtmaul's hammer? I've heard many stories about it. If there is at least some truth to them, then he must have hidden the hammer somewhere near the city. Some people say it was at the place of execution but I've searched for it high and low and didn't find anything. Others say it was somewhere near the Grand Duke's gazebo but I didn't find anything there. And it's quite possible that it's someplace completely different.

There are many legends and tales being told here in Glatzburg, knight. Most of them concern Ereborn, the pagan Empire which was here before Saint Orthenius chased them away with his orthodox army. There is a legend about a coliseum from those times, which was in the middle of Galibornium, a pagan city you can visit its ruins even nowadays—if you are brave enough.
Interesting... Go on.

The coliseum was like a huge theater except they didn't play dramas and comedies there but they would fight to death. At the beginning they would put the convicts and the prisoners of war there so they could be torn to pieces by beasts so it was a kind of execution. But then, one of the convicts would defend himself so bravely that he killed all the beasts and somebody thought it would be more interesting if all the convicts were fighting with weapons in their hands—and amongst themselves. The winner was to get a few more days of life. It became a popular entertainment when the Erebornians set the prisoners against each other and they would fight like dogs with swords in their hands.
Barbaric...

Yeah, I agree with that. In the end these fights became so popular that they stopped using slaves and the coliseum turned into a fighting place of bold heroes of the whole region. Those who won, would become famous and popular with the crowd. Many gladiators—that's what they would call the warriors—gained more fame than many of the Erebornian Emperors. And those fights—they were called gladiator fights because of the sword called gladius, which was very popular at the time—became a symbol of the pagan Empire. Or at least our ancestors who conquered them thought so. And that's why Saint Orthenius, after defeating Galibornium, in 223 went to destroy the coliseum as a symbol of the pagan Empire. But he didn't do it by force, as one would expect, but by a curse.
Really?

Yes, knight, really. There was supposed to be a deep and complicated dungeon where gladiators were being trained and were spending all their free time. And also pagan magicians would perform all kinds of rituals in there, creating new monsters to be sent against the gladiators. Simply a pagan vice anywhere you looked. And Saint Orthenius locked the dungeon by a terrible curse so nobody could get in or out. All those who were hiding in there from the orthodox army were imprisoned. For weeks you could here cries, wails and moans from the various openings of the colosseum but Orthenius was unyielding and let them all die of hunger. They say that since then, ghosts of those who died there dwell in the dungeon!
I've heard that, thanks.

You can choose, Dietrich—either you answer my question or else something terrible happens to you... I think I know a place where they would find your rotting corpse long after anyone would be able to tell who you were!
You don't like me and you have every right not to. Still I think you could answer my question because you know, in the end it will not hurt you...
One can tell from first sight that you must be very intelligent, good man. That's why I thought you would answer my question.
I'm glad we could make a deal in the end, Dietrich.

Well... me too. Anyway, thanks for the help with the zombies. You know, the guards stopped coming to the cemetery long time ago. They left it to the mercy of the infernal powers and didn't care that one could lose a brain here. And their life of course.
The times are bad... Could you answer some questions now?
Well... go ahead, ask, knight. I guess, I owe you that. Go ahead...
I'm glad I was able to help you. Clearing the cemetery of the monsters was my holy duty. Now, excuse me I must go. But we will certainly see each other again.
Goodbye, knight. And stop by any time, if you can. Just in case more living corpses show up here. One never knows, these are terrible times...
Hello, knight. How are you? Hunting for the undead again?
Well, good luck. Is there anything I can do for you?
Yes, I would like to ask you some questions.
If it makes you happy...
No, thanks. I was just passing by so I stopped to see whether you were still alive.
That's SO nice of you, knight. Really. See you soon. Goodbye.

A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! You surely are quite desperate, aren't you? I almost can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! Shame!
You wouldn't believe it, Father. It was Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. I swear! Let my soul burn in hell, if I'm lying.
I knew you wouldn't believe me, Father. That's why I didn't want to tell you. But you insisted so now you have what you wanted. And now leave me alone.

There are living corpses square-dancing in front of my house each night and you are asking whether I have by any chance seen a monster around here? Look around and see for yourself, Father.
I'm sorry, Father, but I don't suspect anyone of heresy. You know, times are bad, one is trying to stay alive... It's better not to see and hear anything.
Except for Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, I don't suspect anyone of heresy, Father. And about her, I told you everything. I swear by my dead granny.

That's SO nice of you, Father. Really. See you soon. Goodbye.
