Except for Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, I don't suspect anyone of heresy, noble sir. And about her, I told you everything. I swear by my dead granny.

No, noble sir, I don't know anything about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. I only heard they found him murdered at the Grand Duke's gazebo behind the city. It must be a great loss for the Mother Church..

There are many legends and tales being told here in Glatzburg, noble sir. Most of them concern Ereborn, the pagan Empire which was here before Saint Orthenius chased them away with his orthodox army. There is a legend about a coliseum from those times, which was in the middle of Galibornium, a pagan city you can visit its ruins even nowadays—if you are brave enough.

Yeah, I agree with that. In the end these fights became so popular that they stopped using slaves and the coliseum turned into a fighting place of bold heroes of the whole region. Those who won, would become famous and popular with the crowd. Many gladiators, that's what they would call the warriors, gained more fame than many of the Erebornian Emperors. And those fights, they were called gladiator fights because of the sword called gladius, which was very popular at the time became a symbol of the pagan Empire. Or at least our ancestors who conquered them thought so. And that's why Saint Orthenius, after defeating Galibornium, in 223 went to destroy the coliseum as a symbol of the pagan Empire. But he didn't do it by force, as one would expect, but by a curse.

Yes, noble sir, really. There was supposed to be a deep and complicated dungeon where gladiators were being trained and were spending all their free time. And also pagan magicians would perform all kinds of rituals in there, creating new monsters to be sent against the gladiators. Simply a pagan vice anywhere you looked. And Saint Orthenius locked the dungeon by a terrible curse so nobody could get in or out. All those who were hiding in there from the orthodox army were imprisoned. For weeks you could here cries, wails and moans from the various openings of the colosseum but Orthenius was unyielding and let them all die of hunger. They say that since then, ghosts of those who died there dwell in the dungeon!

You can choose Dietrich, either you answer my question or else something terrible happens to you... I think I know a place where they would find your rotting corpse long after anyone would be able to tell who you were!
Well... go ahead, ask, noble sir. I guess, I owe you that. Go ahead...
Goodbye, noble sir. And stop by any time, if you can. Just in case more living corpses show up here. One never knows, these are terrible times...
Hello, noble sir. How are you? Hunting for the undead again?
That's SO nice of you, noble sir. Really. See you soon. Goodbye.
A noble man steals?! You must be quite desperate, aren't you? I almost can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the nobles are thieves! Shame!
I would like to ask you one more time about the circumstances of the kidnapping of Bishop Quentinus.

Bishop Quentinus disappeared the night the goddamn green skins attacked the town. It looks like they managed to get into the church where the Bishop probably clashed with them. We can tell because of the many corpses found at the place. The Bishop, however, disappeared. That's why we think he was—unlike most of the other people—kidnapped, not murdered. If they wanted to kill him why not just let his corpse lay at the place?
Forgive me, son, but I don't want to talk about that anymore.
What do you think about the crisis that is spreading across the Realm, Father?

In the Holy Scripture they talk in the Revelation of Saint Ezechiel about the terrors of the three seals and the Scourges of God that are going to befall on the Realm. Of course I can't stay calm in the times when the three Scourges seem to have befallen on us. The Star of Doom has appeared in the sky, the three Angels blew their clarions and the beasts are hammering at the door of their prison to free themselves, after a thousand years of divine rule on Earth, and to seduce all the nations of the world. God save us, son, if the time of the end of the world has come! We must do everything we can to prevent that!
Sorry, son, but I don't have to talk to you about things like that.
I'm looking for heretics here in Hillbrandt, Father. Do you suspect anyone?

I don't suspect anyone in particular from the crimes against faith, son. I've heard all kinds of rumors and people say all kinds of things at the confessionals, but I have myself never witnessed anything what would prove anyone guilty of heresy. I'm sorry.

Besides the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus there are many other events, son. People are talking about ex-Bishop Herbertius who is said to have risen from his grave and walked around the town at night. It's true that there was unspoken suspicion during Herbertius's life, that he had sold his soul to Satan in return for perverted bodily pleasures. Young girls would disappear, and later even young boys, and their crippled bodies were found from time to time in the woods not far from the town.

Whatever the truth was, one day the Bishop was found dead in his bed. It seemed he died sleeping. Since then, there has been peace and people believed they would never hear about the Bishop again. Until now. They say he's returned from the underworld to do evil to fulfill his part of the infernal contract. And even I have seen a shape crawling in the shadow of the city walls. The look of it made me shudder.
Judge Vallarian suspects master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy, Father. What do you think about it?

I heard master Edmond d'Arvias was suspected of heresy. Namely judge Vallarian believes him to be guilty. It looks like he was seen letting the orcs into town during their recent night attack. God be my witness that if I believed him guilty I would be the first to testify against him. But I'm sure he would never do anything like that. I've known him for several years and as far as I can tell, I've never seen a more zealous defender of faith among the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I believe, he's innocent.
What do you know about Fallen Angel Arthamon?

The Holy Scripture says that the Fallen Angel Arthamon is one of the three angels who were cast down from Heaven, together with Satan, for their sins against God's Commandments. He embodies total destruction, nothingness and the opposite of being. They nickname him the Lord of Fire and the Ruler of Destruction. In the infernal pantheon he has many legions of demons who serve him.
Do you think he could be summoned?
Not, that's absolutely impossible. It denies all the teachings of the church about the divine kingdom on Earth.
The Monstrance of Saint Orthenius disappeared. Do you know anything about it?

Unfortunately, I don't know much about the robbery. Coincidentally it was me, who in the morning, found out that the brothers on duty were put to sleep by a dark spell and the monstrance disappeared. We went to search the whole town with the help of the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous immediately but without result. The monstrance just vanished. It's a terrible loss. If we don't manage to find it and bring it back, I hate to think of the consequences.
Do you know anything about the disappearance of Baroness Linda van Gallagan, Father? Her husband has been missing her for some time now.

I've heard Linda van Gallagan went missing mysteriously. It was supposed to happen the same night Bishop Quentinus disappeared. It's probably those damn green skins' doing. God save her soul if those unholy beasts have done something to her!
What do you think about Natalia Reichmann being murdered by Olfghard?

The murder of Natalia Reichmann is a very unfortunate event. Natalia was a deeply faithful girl with an optimistic mind who would please the whole town. I don't understand why it was her who became a victim of a cold-blooded murderer. And that bastard Olfghard managed to escape from the prison where he was put after trying to sell some of her jewelry. I don't blame merchant Reichmann for falling into a deep depression.
I came across a case of curse here in Hillbrandt. Do you know how to remove it?

Are you saying you came across a case of curse here in Hillbrandt, son? That's serious... Cursing somebody requires a deep knowledge of dark, forbidden teachings. Unfortunately my powers don't include removing a curse from someone. But try to ask herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt. She's a layperson but she has knowledge of many teachings and she might be more helpful than me. Well, if she's in a good mood and willing to talk to you.

There are many legends and tales concerning this region. When I came to Hillbrandt a couple of years ago, I took some time studying this phenomena. My favorite was the legend of Saint Orthenius who also happens to be the patron of this town, as well as of the whole Realm. He was a great advocate of true faith here in the Filkland Peninsula at the time of the downfall of Ereborn—the pagan Empire. It was the time when the fundamentals of our Realm were laid, although it had taken several centuries before Ultherst was founded.

According to a contemporary chronicler named Killian, the armies of saint Orthenius won thanks to his powerful relic, against which the pagans had no means of defense. Before he died few years later he had prophesied that in the time of the greatest danger for the true faith it will come into the hands of a new protector who will use it to defeat the enemies of the faith. I must say that the legend is very popular with the people nowadays. They say that the time has come and the new savior will come to stand against those who want to destroy the true faith.
I saw priest Romius and I'm worried about his health. Has he come to you for advice lately?

Brother Romius's condition worries me lot as well. I offered him help but he refused it fiercely, which I didn't expect because he always seemed to be a calm and quiet man. I don't know what's causing his illness. Until recently he was full of strength and energy and all of a sudden he has started to fade. And he determinately refuses any examination or treatment. What a strange attitude for a servant of God who should keep himself in good condition to stay fit for his uneasy duty.
Do you know anything about the death of merchant Kurth Ollmier, Father?

I don't know anything more than what people say about the murder. He was murdered in Truthorn's Inn where he was renting an attic room. I also heard that after he was killed—or maybe even before—he was mutilated. His penis was cut off and put in his mouth. That could mean it was an attack of a succubus or a demon of lechery, but it's only a theory. I don't know any other details except that Sheriff Contemburry has adjourned the case for a lack of evidence.
Do you know who I am, Father? You better think twice before you defy me!
I really need to know, Father. I'm sure you don't want to keep me from doing my duty.
You are of great benefit to the whole Hillbrandt diocese, Father. That's why I'm in no doubt that you will answer my question.
I'd like to buy some potions and scrolls, can I?
Could you heal me?
Oh, sure, son. Come closer and let divine power heal your wounds...
Can I talk to you?
Of course, son. What do you need to know?
Goodbye, son. And God bless you...

The crimes that occured in our diocese are horrible. Even though we live at the very borders of the Realm, our Bishop Quentinus was always able to set things right. His sincerity and determination could open the hearts of the most stubborn sinners. And now we have to witness people being seduced by infernal forces and throwing away what our poor Bishop was trying to establish here.
Oh, I'm sorry, I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Dominicus and I belong to the local diocese. I help Bishop Quentinus in his difficult job.
What is your mission here, Father?

Thanks to my powers, given to me by our gracious Lord, I can heal both body and soul. I can also make a lot of various potions. Did you say poor Bishop Quentinus? What did you mean? Did anything happen to him?

You don't know, son? Oh, of course, you are new here. Bishop Quentinus—heaven have mercy with him—has been missing. He disappeared during the recent orc attack on the town. Everybody thinks the beasts killed the Bishop but I don't believe it because his body was never found. They found blood in the church where he was attacked but that doesn't prove anything. It looks like the Bishop was fighting hard with the orcs.
Do you think they kept him alive?
Yes, I'm positive, unlike the others. If they wanted to simply kill him, they would probably leave his body at the place. I think the Bishop was kidnapped and he must be helped.
If he's still alive I'm going to get him back. If he's not I will avenge his death.

Is it so, son? Would you do it for him? Blessed be your name then, son. You are an example of a true faithful. I'm confident your deeds will be rewarded with success. I know Bishop Quentinus hasn't passed away.
We'll see.
Yes, you are right. Can I do anything for you now? Do you need healing? Can I make you a potion or a scroll?
I might try to find him. It depends how much you value Bishop Quentinus's life...

I'm sorry about what's happened to the Bishop. But anyway, there's nothing I can do to help.
I'm sorry. I thought... I believed you were the person who could do something for him. But you must have more important things to do.
I found Bishop Quentinus deep under the Moonshine Mountains in the orc caves. They keep him there.

All right, I'll try to free him.

So you deny it?

But I wasn't talking about the cult of the Children of the New Order. You said that!
Uh... what? You said the old man Balthazar heard me talking about the cult of the Children of the New Order...

Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is Satan himself! He is the devil in a human body, a wolf in God's herd. He must be put to the stake and pay for his sins!

The priest said so at the last sermon. And he's right—the Grand Master is a heretic and a traitor and must be burned! People are scared of him and he's been hiding for some time now. Has a fierce storm accompanied by unnatural spectacles occurred here in Alvaron in recent days?
I don't remember any violent storm.

Do you want to know what kind of hellspawns can bump you off? It could be a good idea to find out before you get your bum somewhere. So listen—wherever you go, be careful about the werewolves of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr's pack. People of Alvaron have been exposed to their attacks from time immemorial but in the past few years the beasts have multiplied so much that you're not safe even during the day. It even looks like each full moon they manage to breach into the city and kidnap somebody and drag him to their hideout somewhere in Schwarzwald.
No, I've never heard about the cult of the Children of the New Order.
Uhm... but beggar Beckham says something different. He's heard you talking about the cult in a pub the other day.
Beckham is a liar and a drunk!

I'm searching for Ron Burton who is missing. Do you happen to know anything about him?
I don't know anything about Ron Burton. But if he's disappeared, I'd bet, it's the werewolves' doing. As well as with many others.
No matter what Father Nicolas says I think he had some fun with the lady. When a man is on heat it doesn't matter whether he's a priest or not. I think they did it whether she agreed or not.

Answer me, good man. Believe me, you have no idea what could happen to you if you didn't obey me!
If you for some reason don't like me, good man, I'm really sorry. But your answer would be of a great use to me.

All right, whatever you wish. I don't want to prevent you in the administration of justice...
In that case, will you excuse me, sir? Goodbye.

I'm glad to see you again, sir. And thank you for the help with the forgery case. If it weren't for you, who knows how long priest Gilbert could go on putting into circulation human excrements turned to gold...
Who has the authority to bestow a title of a Grand Duke, now when King Edward the second is dead?

Coincidentally it's me. Although most of the duties were taken over by the First Knight after the death of the King, putting new records into the Gold Book of the Realm is the duty of the governor of the royal seat, and that's me.
I'd like to get the title of a Grand Duke. I trust I'm worthy of it!

Really? In fact... why not? In these hard times we have to do all that's in our powers to strengthen the ranks of the gentry. I'll bestow upon you the title of a Grand Duke if you find the murderer of King Edward the second. I have a feeling our Holy Office isn't exercising all due care to apprehend the culprits.
You're welcome, Duke. Personally I sincerely wish you success, it's a crime that CANNOT stay unpunished in any circumstances! The murder of the King of the Realm... that's unimaginable!

If my information is correct, King Edward was found dead by his chamberlain Trisstan in the evening several days ago. Apparently there was a fight because the furniture was scattered all around the room. It's obvious the King fought back against his murderer. That's all we've managed to find out.
I've exposed the murderer of His Majesty Edward II, Grand Duke. May I inform you about the result of my investigation?
But certainly, Duke! That's great news, the murderers of His Majesty are exposed! Tell me, who's the culprit? Who has the death of our leader on his conscience?
It is the First Knight Rodrigo de Velacor.

The First Knight? I really didn't expect that... Why, the main task of the First Knight has always been to protect the Crown and the Realm! How could he? I'm really shocked. It seems Satan is able to worm into the thinking of every man... It's terrible to imagine that! But tell me what evidence have you got against the First Knight?

The royal chamberlain Trisstan has witnessed the murder and identified the First Knight with certainty. Moreover I got the testimony of Cardinal Gustapho Letti whom the First Knight confessed his terrible secret to. Furthermore, I managed to find out that the King wounded his murderer in the last fight. The First Knight has some scratches on his face and he's silent about how he got them. And finally, under the weight of all those proofs Rodrigo de Velacor has confessed to the crime.

Fascinating! You managed to prove him guilty and force him to confess in a really admirable way! You've carried out your task Duke, and with excellence! I'll be honored to record you into the Gold Book of the Realm as the Grand Duke of Asherbalt. That is, if you have 15 000 gp.
I bring 15 000 gp. to get my name written into the Gold Book of the Realm, Grand Duke. I hope you may bestow a title of a Grand Duke upon me now.
I have the money. Here it is.
Regrettably I don't have that much money on me...
Never mind, Duke. Return to me when you have 15 000 gp. and the title of a Grand Duke will be yours.

Great! On paying 15 000 gp. your name will be written into the Gold Book of the Realm. Herewith I bestow upon you the title of the Grand Duke of Asherbalt! Congratulations, Grand Duke! Accept this item as a symbol of your new office.
Thank you, Grand Duke. Farewell.
Has anything unusual happened in Glatzburg lately?

Do you know Tom Clifford, knight? He's the son of Johaness Clifford—Duke Rowan van Leerin's valet. He's a good boy. He liked watching me work since he was little—he's been lured to smithery. He's gifted, there's no doubt about that. He's a born smith and an armorer, I know it. I grew to like him and since I'm single and childless I even started to think of bequeathing him my craft—when the time comes.
That's very nice of you, master armorer. But what's unusual about it? I was asking whether something unusual has happened in the city...

Exactly, knight. Tom had persuaded his father in the end, that if he was not needed in Duke van Leerin's house, he could come here to learn smithing. So he would spend all his free time here. But then he didn't show up for some time. And that was strange. In the end I went to his father to ask him if he was ill or something and he brushed me off saying that his son was not my problem. And that was even stranger because we've always been on good terms.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to talk about that.
Glatzburg is ruled by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick who is the royal governor of the city. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor.
Who can sell me some supplies here in Glatzburg? Except for you, of course.

Do you want to replenish your supplies? If you are looking for potions and magic items, go to seer Enrie Jungwirdt or to alchemist Paolus Ventimus. At Wandy Gielwitch's inn and Ludwig Weintraum's inn you can buy or sell anything. At Alphonso DiCerbio's you can barter for anything as long as you don't care where it comes from.

What do I think of the crisis? Why should I lie to you, knight, it's bad. But the Realm has been through several disasters in the past and—with the help of God—it always brought itself back to its feet, so I don't think this should be the end of the world. Not that it doesn't look exactly like the end of the world they describe in the Holy Scripture—the Star of Doom has appeared, the Scourges of God have stricken us, beasts and monsters leave the underworld, people are turning to false prophets... But I still think there's no reason to be pessimistic. All our problems can still be solved with a blow of a hammer on the head. No matter if it's a beast or a heretic, a blow on the head will get all the evil thoughts out of them—together with their brain of course, but that's the point of it, isn't it?
There is supposed to be a war brewing. Have you heard anything?

Yes, it's very likely. Grand Duke Heidrick ordered a lot of war gear. Horseshoes, cuirasses, pikes, longswords, all kinds of stuff. The order was so big that I had to hire some extra hands to be able to finish it on time.

Of all devil minions I've seen around here or I've heard about, I consider the biggest nuisance the highwaymen and rogues. They are human and not some Beelzebubs who smell of brimstone, but they're worse than anything that comes from hell. When a devil is holding you by your neck, you can be sure, he just wants your life, but the rogues would cut your throat for a few coins. They only care about mammon and killing, torture and rape is their fun. The group of this Benthley of Welshrem is the worst. They kill on sight and only a few were lucky enough to get out of their claws alive. They don't respect anything and they despise human life.

Sheriff Gendriel Smith pays a reward for heads and scalps of bandits. The rewards were offered by Grand Duke Heidrick in an attempt to put an end to the killing but it wasn't a huge success. But if you manage to catch a bandit, the reward in gold is yours.

I don't suspect anyone of heresy, knight. I'm a faithful person and I know my duty, but on the other hand I don't snoop and grass up—I don't need that. But if I found out about anything, I would definitely let you know. You don't have to tell me that the misery we're in is the heretics' doing.

I learned that Istwan de Bragho rose from his grave to wreak vengeance on those who were behind his capture and execution. It seems he's immortal now. Do you have any idea what might help me against him?

You saw Istwan de Bragho? So it's true what they say, that he's returned to take revenge on his executioners... who would think of that. And you say he's immortal. That scares me. Are you sure about that?
Yes, I have first-hand experience of it.

Well... that doesn't look good. Especially for executor Flemberg. If Bragho comes for him, he's dead. I can make powerful magic swords but not against immortals. There must be some unholy powers and I can't help you against them. Try asking seer Jungwirdt, she knows more about these things than I...
To tell you the truth, knight, the murder wasn't unexpected. Ever since Francessca Gulvardi's attack I thought the poor man was on somebody's list. And I was right.
Do you know of any enemies he might have?
No, knight, sorry. I don't know of any enemies.
You're welcome, knight. I hope you catch the murderer soon. Bishop Trevorius was a good person.

An Elenian noble's tomb, you say? Uhmm... can't help you, I've never heard of anything like that. But it's true that I've met some people a couple times who would say they found remnants of an ancient civilization in the woods around Glatzburg. Who knows, maybe they come from those—Elenian.

Undead in the streets of the city... yeah, that's a real disaster. As long as they stayed behind the walls we at least had hope. But now that they appear right in the streets after it gets dark, people panic. There's nowhere to run, nowhere to go. Terrible. Who knows where they come from? As soon as the sun goes down there are loads of them everywhere. And if they get somebody, not even his mother recognizes him after they're done with him.
Is there anything more you can tell me?

I heard there was one strange thing about the dead. They have been robbed of anything precious. They are even missing copper buttons and all kinds of shiny pieces of their clothing. That's strange with living corpses, isn't it? I've never heard they'd care about anything else but brain and fresh blood...
I'm looking for missing Raquel Gielwitch. Have you heard anything about her?

So you're looking for Raquel Gielwitch. Yes, I've heard she's been missing... Her sister says she was taken by Satan. But I'm afraid it wasn't Satan, it was rather some damn heretic who used her for some kind of a disgusting ritual... I hate to think of what could happen to a young girl these days!!
There are many legends about Glatzburg, knight. Have you heard of Devil's Caves?
Yes, I have heard about Devil's Caves...
Really? Well... could have expected that... well, nevermind.
Tell me the story.

They say that in the ruins of Galibornium there is an entrance to deep caves which lead to Hell itself. That's why people started to call it Devil's Caves—because they believe it's the way the devils take to get to our world. The truth is that the caves are full of devils. It's the way the gross, sly, scaly devils with long tails and big claws come here. From time to time they come in huge gangs and rampage around. Those are the times when all of the wanderers are in peril of their lives!

I didn't know Knight Commander Ethien de Pasque was robbed. That must be a really delicate situation for him—having the Chain of the Brotherhood stolen is a great dishonor for a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. To tell you the truth, I'd bet it was that crook Tinthan. He pretends to be a performer, an artist and an actor but he really is an ordinary thief. So if you happen to see him, make sure to ask him. But be careful, he can play tricks. Last time he was stealing in my shop he confused me with his chit-chat so much that I gave him the dagger he had stolen...
Let me see, knight... but that's the Philosophers' Stone!

That's what they call this extremely rare piece of rock which nobody knows where it comes from but it's very magic. With some skill you can turn it to any metal and it still keeps its magic properties. If you want, I can make one magic item of each stone you bring.
Of course, knight. Of each Philosophers' Stone you bring I can make one magic item.
I'm warning you, master armorer. If you don't answer, you might get yourself into serious trouble. You better think twice before you refuse to answer my question.

You probably don't like me master armorer and that's why you refuse to talk to me. Your behavior is not very rational although you do look like a rational man. And so you must be realizing that your answer will benefit a good thing.
I knew from first look that you were a very wise man, master armorer. And I don't understand why you wouldn't want to answer my question...
I would like to ask you some questions, master armorer.
Well, I should have expected that since you are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. So ask away, knight.
Yes, I would like to exchange some goods here.
No, I don't need anything. Thank you. Goodbye.

Don't worry, knight... So, here you go. I wasn't able to make anything else out of the stone. The problem with this strange metal is that it changes in front of your eyes as if it had its own free will. But I hope you'll be satisfied. If not, I can buy it from you. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Is there anything else I can do for you?
Of course, knight. No problem. What do you want to know?
Nothing could be easier, knight.
I don't need anything, thanks.
Then don't forget, knight, that the next time you come, there will be a little present for you. Goodbye. And thank you!

I sell anything you can name—from knives to plate armor. And I also buy those things. Remember, my workshop is the best around. Our family didn't gain the title of Baron for nothing!
Baron title, you say? What did your ancestors gain it for?

For their service to the Realm of course! The Drichtmauls rule the hammer and the steel since time immemorial. And nobody compares to us—except for the royal armorers in Alvaron, of course. Since 745, when my ancestor Eugen Drichtmaul settled here in Glatzburg, we've been supplying first class weapons and armor far and wide. It was, however, my grand-grandfather Bonhart von Drichtmaul who gained the title of Baron for a plate armor made for the then governor of the city Grand Duke Gerhard. It was a powerful magic armor which saved the Grand Duke's life in many battles with the barbarian raiders.
I'm pleased to meet you, master armorer. Can I talk to you for a minute?
But of course, knight. Although I'd prefer that you bought something from my stock. But we might get to that. What troubles you?
But of course, knight—that's why I'm here. Choose what you like and we can agree upon a good price.
Pleased to meet you, master armorer. I don't need anything this time. Goodbye.
Hello, knight. How are you? Do you need to buy or sell a weapon or armor? If yes, you've come to the right place.
No, master armorer, I'm not interested in your goods this time. I came to ask you a few questions.
Go ahead and ask, knight. Maybe, as we talk, you'll remember that you do need something from my stock. What did you want to know?
Yes, I'd like to see your goods. Maybe I will like something.

I'm sure about that. But before we start talking about business, I'd like to ask you something. You're a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, aren't you? Your work is to investigate various suspicions, search for evidence and things like that, is that right?
Yes, that's right. What's your point, master armorer?

You know, it's a complicated problem... My great grandfather, thanks to whom the Drichtmauls are now Barons, became famous mainly thanks to a magic hammer made for him by his friend André Juliano Vestrennio, one of the most famous alchemists of his time. With that hammer he could make armor and weapons with which no other could measure. The problem is that when the war with the barbarians started my great grandfather decided to go to that war. Before he went, he buried all his property including the hammer at an unknown place and then he died as a hero in the battle of the Hallaworth Fields. And the hammer has been lost since. You know, knight, I'm not a bad armorer. In fact, I'm one of the best in the Realm. But I still can't make anything my great grandfather could with his hammer. If I got hold of if, I could do great things, you see?
Yes, I see. You want me to find your great grandfather's hammer, is that right?
Exactly, knight. I thought you could find the place where my great grandfather's treasure was buried and bring me the hammer.
Today's your lucky day, master armorer. I found your grand grandfather's hammer. Here it is.

Damn it, that's a miracle! It does look like the hammer my father and my grandfather described. You found it! I can't believe it! I'm forever indebted to you, knight. If you want, I can make you a magic item with this hammer.
That would be very nice of you, master armorer. Thank you.
No, knight, I thank you. Next time you stop by, there will be a little present for you. In the mean time, you can look at my stock and see if you like something.

That won't be necessary, master armorer. I'm happy to have been able to help you and my help will benefit the whole Realm. Your weapons and armor will be of much use in the fight against the evil that has stricken us.
Well, as you wish, knight. Man, that was unexpected. But modesty is a virtue, of course.
Exactly. Can I see what you have in stock, now?
All right, I accept. I will try to find the place your great grandfather has hidden his treasure.
Thank you, knight. I knew we could come to an agreement. And now we can do some business.
What exactly would I get out of it, master armorer?
As I said—I only want the hammer, I don't care about the money, I have plenty of it. But I must have the hammer! So if you find the treasure, you can keep it—except for the hammer.
I'm sorry, I'm not a treasure hunter. If you want your great grandfather's hammer, you'll have to find it yourself. Now I would like to see your goods.
Of course, knight. As you wish.
Thank you, master armorer, but I don't need anything. Goodbye.
Hello, knight. What can I do for you? Would you like a weapon or armor? Or do you have anything to sell?
I have your great grandfather's hammer, master armorer.
No, knight, I thank you. Next time you stop by, there will be a little present for you.
Hello, knight. What can I do for you? Would you like a weapon or an armor? Or do you have anything to sell?
Hello, knight. You came quite early. But your reward is ready. I'm sure you will find it useful in your quests. And if not, you can always sell it for a nice sum of gold.
You're welcome, knight. With my great grandfather's hammer I can make these things with one eye closed.
I'm really happy for you. Could you spend some more time answering my questions?
As you wish, knight. What do you want to know?

Hello, noble lord. What can I do for you? Would you like a weapon or armor? Or do you have anything to sell?
No, noble lord, I thank you. Next time you stop by, there will be a little present for you.
Hello, noble lord. What can I do for you? Would you like a weapon or an armor? Or do you have anything to sell?
Hello, noble lord. You came quite early. But your reward is ready. I'm sure you will find it useful in your quests. And if not, you can always sell it for a nice sum of gold.
You're welcome, noble lord. With my great grandfather's hammer I can make these things with one eye closed.
As you wish, noble lord. What do you want to know?
Goodbye, noble lord. And thank you one more time.

We meet again, knight! You didn't expect that, did you? You thought you had sent me to burning hell for eternity. But you were mistaken! I didn't spend too much time in hell. The time of darkness is coming, the dead are leaving their graves and walking the Earth. And I came to take what you owe me. You are going to pay dearly!
I don't think so, unclean ghost. I will not allow an unholy monster to dispraise God's name by its presence in this world!
We will see who's going to be burning in hell sooner!
What is it like in hell?
It's hell, knight. But don't worry, soon you will see for yourself.
In the name of Archangel Gabriel, I curse you, unholy ghost. Go back to burning hell!
I will, but I'm going to take your soul with me!
God have mercy with this lost soul and kindly embrace it so it can't disturb the peace of the living anymore.
I don't think God would have mercy with me—he didn't have it the last time I faced him, he won't have it this time. And to tell you the truth, I don't even want him to. Prepare to die!

We meet again, Father! You didn't expect that, did you? You thought you had sent me to burning hell for eternity. But you were mistaken! I didn't spend too much time in hell. The time of darkness is coming, the dead are leaving their graves and walking the Earth. And I came to take what you owe me. You are going to pay dearly!
It's hell, Father. But don't worry, soon you will see for yourself.

We meet again, sir! You didn't expect that, did you? You thought you had sent me to burning hell for eternity. But you were mistaken! I didn't spend too much time in hell. The time of darkness is coming, the dead are leaving their graves and walking the Earth. And I came to take what you owe me. You are going to pay dearly!
It's hell, sir. But don't worry, soon you will see for yourself.
Go back to burning hell, unclean spirit!
I will, but I'll take your soul with me!
This must be the gate that leads into the Realm of the fallen angel Arthamon...
It's closed! I must find the way to open it...
Fortunately I've already found the key that unlocks it!
The Gate is opened!
You must die! Everybody must die!
Oh God... you're not human! You are an infernal apparition who took the form of a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I won't let a monster like you walk this world!
Death! Death to all! All must die! None can be spared!
Master Edmond d'Arvias, is that you?

Oh God... you are not master Edmond d'Arvias. You have his face, his sword but you are not master d'Arvias. You are an infernal creature who looks like him. Die, infernal monster. I won't let a monster like you walk this world!
Who are you, sir? Tell me your name and what you're doing at this damn place?
Attacking a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous has never paid off for anyone!
Attacking an inquisitor is the most serious crime, sir!
Attacking a noble is the highest crime, sir!
Aaaaahhhh! Finally free! Thank you mortal for setting me free. What do you ask as a reward from me?
I need healing.
As you wish, mortal—your wish is my command! Do you ask for something else, before I return to my native sphere?
I need shopping.
As you wish, mortal—your wish is my command! Choose whatever you want. And then I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
I need aid against my enemies—help me!
As you wish, mortal—your wish is my command! I will rip to pieces any of your enemies that may cross my path. And then I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
I don't need anything, thank you.
Really nothing? That's weird... then at least take this gold as a token of my gratitude. And now I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
Really nothing? That's weird... then at least take this magical item as a token of my gratitude. And now I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
Really nothing? That's weird... then let me make you more powerful at least. And now I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
Really nothing? That's weird... then let me make you more skillful at least. And now I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
Who are you, unclean spirit?!
Unclean?! I am definitely not unclean! You just set me free from a hermetically closed astral cube!
Well... then—who are you, spirit?!
Spirit?! I am not a spirit, because I am not dead. I am unsubstantial—but not undead!
Stop playing with words. Could you finally tell me who you are?
It would take a very long time. And I doubt you would understand it. It would be much easier to tell you that I am a genie who can fulfill one of your wishes.
Interesting. What can I wish for? Anything?

Unfortunately I am not such an all-round expert. But I can heal you, you can visit my shop right here, I can transfer you to any outdoor place you have already visited, or I can rip your enemies to pieces. So make a wish, mortal.
That is all for now, thank you.
Then I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!
I want to get out of here!
As you wish, mortal—your wish is my command! Choose your destination. And then I shall finally return to my native sphere... Aer karth moarmm kal-ebhor!

Who's the ruler of Glatzburg? Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor of the city, of course. He's my liege lord, and I'm obliged to obey him. I will not say a bad word against him. Towards the Royal Vice-Governor Duke Rowan van Leerin, I don't feel the same. He's too ambitious to spend time solving the problems our city is overwhelmed with. But it's not up to me to judge him—he's a higher noble and I'm only a poor Baron.
Where can you buy goods in Glatzburg?

You need to do some shopping? Well, that depends what you need. Hans von Drichtmaul has a famous armor shop in Glatzburg. The seer Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus sell potions and all kinds of magic items. The innkeepers Wanda Gielwitch and Ludwig Weintraum buy and sell assorted gods. At Alphonso DiCerbio's you can exchange anything, and he doesn't care how his goods are sourced.

To tell you the truth, knight, even I am losing faith when I hear what the people in the city are saying. Sometimes I'm thinking that God has turned away from us—that the end of the world is coming and we all are going to end up chained in Hell. But then I find peace again in a prayer. I think people in the city have no idea what real poverty is. Glatzburg has always been a rich city and people here have always lived well. Nobody was hungry or thirsty, the business was going well and every night you could hear music coming from countless balls and parties all over the city. And now that it's gone people think it's the end of the world. If they had spent their whole lives in hunger and poverty, as the poorest of the poor do, they would have known that this is no end of the world.
An interesting attitude...

I don't know, knight... to tell you the truth even though I'm pretty worried. We've had the signs of the end of the world that the Holy Scripture describes—the Star of Doom appeared, the Scourges of God struck... but I'm even more worried by the behavior of the people. Heresy is spreading like a disease, people are worshiping false idols everywhere and everything is getting worse. Once people lose faith it will be the end of the world, whatever that truly means.
I heard that there was a war brewing. Do you know anything about it?

I've heard some rumors. I even heard that Grand Duke Heidrick was thinking of introducing some extra taxes, even though in the beginning of the spring he promised there was not going to be more taxes. One can make plans, but life plans otherwise. If that happens I have no idea where I'm going to get the money. They've already requisitioned our horses although it was just two old nags.
What monsters and hellspawns can people meet in and around Glatzburg?

There's all kinds of monsters and hellspawns, knight. Many have crawled up from their lairs lately. But I'm more frightened of the bandits around the royal roads. Not many businessmen and travelers are so lucky as to get to the city without a scratch earned on the highway. There are many bandit groups, but the worst is the Benthley of Welshrem's company. That bastard has united the worst scum that walks our land. They have no respect for life and they kill on sight. They hold Glatzburg in their deadly grip, striking here and there.

To tell you the truth, I'm suspicious about what Duke Rowan van Leerin has been doing lately. He's my liege lord so speaking against him is almost a crime but I can't help it. He's been acting strange lately. There's nothing surprising about him criticizing the rule of Grand Duke Heidrick. One could expect it—that's politics. But from time to time he hints at truths that make me shiver. As if he was certain Grand Duke Heidrick would soon be out of his way...
Maybe he knows something about the Grand Duke and he's going to use it.

Yes, that's possible. And if it was just a political fight I'd be relieved. But there is something else about the Duke... I don't know, maybe I'm just imagining things, but he seems to be too self-assured. Yes, that's the word—self-assured. No politician can afford that.
Uh... but I can't arrest the Duke for being too self-assured, Baron.
Yes, I know. It's just a suspicion and I have no evidence about anything bad the Duke does. It'd probably be best if you forgot it.

Anything worth mentioning? You mean except the kidnapping of my wife by the bloodthirsty monster Benthley of Welshrem, knight? Well, then I must mention the madman that rages around Glatzburg these days. It's Henry de Montreaux, an ex-paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. If what they say is true, he used to be an honest and just man who went crazy and started to murder innocent people. He stays in the woods around the city and challenges anyone he meets to a duel. And since he's still there one can tell that he hasn't been beaten yet. Some say that he's made a contract with the devil but I don't think so. The paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are trained to kill. They are supposed to watch over the execution of justice and defend it, but many times all they actually do is kill monsters. And that's what they train for from the novitiate until death. No wonder one of them goes mad and makes such a mess.
I'm investigating the murder of Bishop Trevorius. Do you know anything about it?

Monsignor Trevorius's death is a great loss for all of us. Only few dioceses have the pleasure of having such an excellent person as bishop Trevorius. God save his soul. As far as the circumstances of his death are concerned there's not much I can say about it. Some suspect the heretics, the bandits or the hellspawns, but if I was investigating it I'd search different places. Perhaps amongst the high ranking clerics...
Really? That's a daring suggestion. Can you explain it?

Of course, knight. I don't know whether you've heard about it, but Bishop Trevorius was one of the radical clerics. He believed the Holy Mother Church needed healing from the many maladies it's been suffering for centuries. He wanted to return it to its original form and an aim. He would preach of a great faithfulness and loyalty of the clerics, of the service to God and the people and mainly about poverty and humility. He stood against the church leaders getting involved in politics. He had some radical ideas which, according to the higher clergy, sounded like heresy. That's why the two attacks—one of which was unfortunately successful—were made against him. That's my opinion, knight.

Actually... I heard it was you who killed Bishop Trevorius, knight. Not that I believe it, what strange rumors one hears... Anyway, the loss of monsignor Trevorius is a terrible thing. Only a few dioceses ever have the pleasure of having such an excellent person as Bishop Trevorius. God save his soul!
I'm looking for the tomb of an Elenian noble named Fae'Darlion. Do you know where I could find it?

I don't know of any Elenian tomb, knight. But it's true that in the woods around my mansion there are remains from the pagan times. I'm not a history expert, so I can't tell whether they come from the times of the Elenians, but I imagine they do. So maybe if you look around a bit you might find some luck. But beware of the bandits!
Do you know anything about Father Frederick?

Father Frederick? Yes, I remember him, I talked to him couple of times. He was an old melancholic priest. As far as I know he died of mortis negra two years ago. They say he used to be a famous exorcist but I don't think he performed any exorcisms in Glatzburg. He had done a lot of traveling, and I think he came to Glatzburg to die in peace. Well, he did manage to die, but the part with the peace didn't work out.

To tell you the truth, I don't know much about the Fallen Angels. I only know what the Holy Scripture says and what you hear at mass. There's four of them—Arthamon—the lord of Destruction, Baphomet—the lord of madness, Cerdie—the queen of sin and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the devil's first servant. They were cast out from heaven together with Satan for the sins and crimes they committed in the name of God. They've dwelled in hell since trying to take control of the divine kingdom on Earth and in Heaven. They can never do this because they are being held in hell by the chains of the true faith and love of God, the savior.
I'm looking for Bonhart von Drichtmaul's hammer. Do you have any idea where it could be? Bonhart is said to have hidden it somewhere before he went to war...
I heard that Bonhart von Drichtmaul buried all his property somewhere near the city before he left. That's all I can say about it, knight. It's all I know. Many tried to find it in vain.
I need to get some of the wine called Chateau de Trebrechette. Do you have any idea where I could get a few bottles?
Interesting question, knight. The other day I found a dusty crate in my cellar and there were a few bottles of that wine. I have no idea which of my ancestors got it and where—but it's a treasure!
And could you sell me some?
I'm sorry, knight, I can't. I need money, that's true, but I want to keep the wine for a special occasion. I'm sorry.
I understand.
You don't understand Baron—I really need that wine!
I understand, knight, but I simply can't give it to you. I want to keep it for the time there will be something to celebrate—if such a time ever comes.
I'm looking for missing Raquel Gielwitch. Do you know anything about her, Baron?

I heard that Raquel Gielwitch disappeared. Her sister Wanda is completely wretched. She thought she would manage to arrange a better future for Raquel but it wasn't meant to happen... But Raquel is not the only one who disappeared lately. There have been a few cases of young girls who disappeared in Glatzburg. God knows where could the girls have gone. Sheriff Smith spent some time investigating it but he didn't find any evidence. The girls are now in the hands of God.

The popular legend nowadays is the legend of Saint Orthenius. It says that a new protector of the Realm should come at the times of the greatest need and that he would find the lost Saint Orthenius's relic called the Inquisitor. He will use the Inquisitor to defeat the enemies of true faith with it, as Saint Orthenius did in 223 when he destroyed the pagan empire of Ereborn. To think that Ereborn stood here in the Filkland Peninsula. That was the first step to the foundation of Ultherst, the first independent faithful empire, a few centuries later.
So, do people think it's time the Saint Orthenius's heir came?

Exactly, knight. And I don't blame them—I mean, look around. If this is not the times of the greatest need then what is it? But I personally don't believe the legend. It is true that Saint Orthenius owned a relic called the Inquisitor supposedly brought to him by the Archangel Gabriel, but I don't believe a hero is going to appear and drive demons and heretics out of the Realm. It clearly mixes historical facts with folk fantasies. Unfortunately.
And has the relic of Saint Orthenius really been lost?
Yes, knight. They say that Saint Orthenius hid it somewhere before he died and declared that only the new protector will be able to take it. I think it's been lost forever.
You better answer, Baron. You never know how much trouble a bad decision will cause.
Please, Baron, can you answer my question?
If I didn't know I'd hardly find a wiser and smarter person to answer my question I wouldn't insist so much. So please, can you answer my question?

By the First Prophet, Helen! Is it really you? My God, you saved her, knight. God must have heard my prayers. Thank you, knight. I'm infinitely grateful. You deserve a big reward for your help but I have nothing to give you. But wait, I might find something. I was cleaning my cellar the other day and I found this old, dusty crate I didn't even know was there. And there I found a few bottles of Chateau de Trebrechette. It's 1048, the best year! It must be worth a lot of gold.
Uh... thanks, Baron.

I thank you, knight. I'm forever indebted to you. Without Helen my life would have no meaning at all. I'd be the last of the Hunth family since I have no children or any other relatives. Until recently my father was living here with me but few days ago God took him to his Realm. We couldn't even bury him because of what's happening at the cemetery these days...
I'm sorry about your father. But now that your wife is back you will definitely be happier.
Yes, of course. Is there anything I can do for you in return?
Yes, I'd like to ask you a few questions, if it doesn't bother you.
Sure, knight. Ask your questions.
No thanks, Baron. Goodbye.
What do you mean Baron? What's happening at the cemetery?

Haven't you heard about it? The corpses return to life at nights, raise from their graves to kill everything living they come across. It makes me shiver when I think about it. I can't imagine burying my father there.
What kind of things do you mean, Baron? Do corpses return to life in there?
Exactly, knight. It's horrifying. It makes me shiver. I can't imagine going there and burying my father.
What? Helen is dead? I don't believe that. What happened? Where did you find her? Who... who killed her?!
I killed her. It was God's will!
You?! Did you go crazy?! You're gonna pay for that. Murderer! I'll kill you! Kill you!!!
I have no idea who killed her. It was probably the... well... bandits.

Oh my God... Helen... Why did this have to happen? Why?! What am I going to do without her? She was the light of my life... No, I can't stand it. Life has no meaning without you. I'm leaving this world to be with my love. God can see me and he will understand.
Don't do that, Baron. Suicide is a sin!
Well then, it's going to be my last sin. Goodbye, knight! Ahhhhh...
May your soul rest in peace, Baron...
Leave in peace, Baron. I'm giving you the absolution.
Thank you, knight. Goodbye. Ahhhhh...
If you are afraid to bury the remains of your father, I'd be happy do it for you. If I sanctify the sarcophagus it will prevent your father from returning as an undead monster.

Would you do it for me? Knowing that my treasury is empty... It's very kind of you. Here is the coffin with the remains of my father. You will find the family sarcophagus in the secular tomb under the cemetery. May all the saints protect you...
Thank you. Can I ask you a few question before I go?
Thank you. Goodbye.
How terrible. I totally agree with you. Can I now ask you something?
I understand your concerns, Baron. A corpse should lie in a grave. But under these circumstances... I must leave now, I have an important mission. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. And stop by if you ever have time. Me and my wife will be happy to see you.
The bastard! The scumbag! May the black death get him. I wish his mother had died in terrible pains before welping him. If I got hold of him I'd kill him in ways too atrocious to speak of!
What's going on, good man? Why so much cursing?
Why? Because I'm mad like I've never been in my life. The bastard has taken my wife! My beloved wife is in the hands of a madman who despises all humanity. Can you imagine it, knight?
Calm down and tell me what happened.

I'm Baron Edger von Hunth. And this is my land in case you didn't notice. I know it's not a fancy place. It rather resembles an old shack but I'm glad I have a roof over my head. I'm not ashamed of being poor!
You don't have to be, Baron. But tell me, what has happened to your wife? You mentioned a bastard who took her...
Oh yes, the bastard! My beloved wife Helen was on her way from Glatzburg when she was attacked by the bandit group of that servant of Satan and they took her God knows where!
What servant of Satan are you talking about? Who kidnapped your wife?

The Bloody Butcher, knight! The brigand Benthley of Welshrem. It was his men who took my wife! An old servant the bastards beat up and left lying in his own blood on the ground told me. The good old man spent several days crawling through the woods with broken limbs so he could tell me her fate.
Baron, I could help you find her and free her.
Really? Then I'd be infinitely grateful, knight. The problem is that nobody knows where the scumbag lives. I have searched every single valley around Glatzburg myself but without any success.
Don't worry, Baron. If your wife is alive I'm going to bring her back.
God bless you, knight.
Thank you. Can I talk to you for a moment?
Thank you. Good bye.
Maybe I could help you find your wife, Baron. It depends what would you give me for that.

In that case I must fail you, knight. My treasury is empty. I have nothing left. I even had to sell my cattle. If you're looking for a reward for a good deed you came to a wrong person. And I'm quite surprised that a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous haggles to get a reward for his services like a horse trader. Where's your knightly honor?
I hope your wife is found alive and well. Can I now ask you something, Baron?
Go ahead, knight. But hurry up, I want to go looking for my wife soon. I'm not leaving her in the hands of the son of a bitch!
I hope everything ends up well. Goodbye.
You don't have to, Baron. But you were talking about the kidnapping of your wife. I'm happy to be able to tell you that she's alive and well. Actually, you can see for yourself—here she is!
That's very noble of you, Baron. Unfortunately, I don't know anything about your wife. I need to ask you a few questions...
Go ahead and ask, knight. But hurry up. I would like to go look for my wife as soon as possible.
Poverty is not a sin, Baron. But you were talking about your wife and... unfortunately I must tell you that she is dead.
That's alright. As far as your wife is concerned, I freed her. But I took her to the soldier Harph, he paid well for her.

What did you do? Who did you take her to? Harph? My God, that's the animal who tried to rape her... and you took her to him! Why did you do it? What kind of person are you? I'm going to kill you for thatd! DIE!!!
Hello, Baron. How are you?
Not very well, knight. I'm still looking for my wife, you see? If something's happened to her I'd be the death of me. I can't imagine living without her.
You don't have to worry about your wife, Baron. Here she is—alive and well.
I understand. Can we talk?
Your wife is dead, Baron.
I freed your wife, Baron. But then I took her to the soldier Harph who paid a nice sum for her.

What did you do? Who did you take her to? Harph? My God, that's the lecher who tried to rape her... and you took her to him! Why did you do it? What kind of person are you? I'm going to kill you for that! DIE!!!
Hello, knight. I'm happy to see you. Did you find my wife? I haven't been successful yet...
Yes, Baron, I found her and freed her. Here she is—alive and well.
No, Baron, I haven't found your wife yet.
Well then, maybe you'll be luckier next time. We can't stop looking for her until there is the faintest hope that she's still alive. I can't imagine what would I do if she died...
I understand. Can I talk to you?
Sure. What is it?
Goodbye, knight. Please don't stop looking.
If you want to know what happened to your wife I can tell you. I freed her. But then I took her to the soldier Harph who paid a nice sum for her.

What did you do? Where did you take her? Soldier Harph? The lecher who tried to rape her some time ago... and you took her to him? Why did you do that? What kind of person are you? I'm going to kill you for that, bastard!
What a pleasant surprise, knight. I'm pleased to see you. How are you? Is there anything I can do for you?
I would like to ask you something, if you don't mind.
Of course not, knight. Go ahead. What's on your mind?
Nothing right now, Baron. I was just passing by. Goodbye.
What a pleasant surprise, knight. I'm pleased to see you. Can I ask you how the burying of my father's remains went? Is he resting in peace in the family sarcophagus?
Yes, Baron. The remains of your father are in the family sarcophagus, which I have sanctified.
Oh, thank God! I was already losing faith that my father would ever reach the eternal peace. I'm forever indebted to you, knight. Forever.
That's alright, Baron. Now, please, can you answer a few questions?
I'd be more than happy to answer. What do you need to know?
Yes, I agree. It wasn't easy to fulfill the task.
Yes I know. I wish there was something I could give you in return. But unfortunately I have nothing.
Well then, can you at least answer a few questions?
Of course, knight. What do you need to know?
Well then, maybe you will find something later. Goodbye.
You don't owe me anything, Baron. It was my Holy duty. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. May all the saints protect you!
No, Baron, not yet.
Well then, what can I do, knight. But please don't lose any time, knight. You never know what will happen to a corpse that hasn't been buried in time.
Of course, Baron. Don't worry. Could you answer a few questions?
Of course, knight. Go ahead. What's on your mind?
I will do all I can, Baron. Goodbye.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe it! You're disgracing your whole Brotherhood, knight! You should be ashamed of yourself!

That bastard has united the worst scum that walks our land. They have no respect for life and they kill on sight. They hold Glatzburg in their deadly grip, striking here and there.

The paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are trained to kill. They are supposed to watch over the execution of justice and defend it, but many times all they actually do is kill monsters. And that's what they train for from the novitiate until death. No wonder one of them goes mad and makes such a mess.

He stood against the church leaders getting involved in politics. He had some radical ideas which, according to the higher clergy, sounded like heresy. That's why the two attacks—one of which was unfortunately successful—were made against him. That's my opinion, sir.

Maybe I should examine his body... It's possible I'll find some clue to lead me to his murderers.

In that case I win!

Who rules in Glatzburg and over the surrounding domains, Your Grace?
My husband Duke Rowan van Leerin rules in Glatzburg. He is the royal vice-governor of the city. He's a very wise man, knight.
But your husband is dead after all, Your Grace.

Is he? I don't know anything about that... my husband is a kind man and because of his wisdom he's the royal vice-governor of the city, by the grace of God... that's all I know. It is beyond woman's cognizance to talk into the politics.
Well, all right then...
Well... I thought the royal governor rules the city more than the royal vice-governor, right?

I'm not shopping much, knight. My husband says I'd spend all money. He's a very wise man, you know.

What do I think about the current crisis? Oh, knight, all those things afflicting us are so terrible! I pray so much for all those things to be already behind us and we could live like before again. This isn't the End of the World after all, knight, is it?
Of course it isn't, Your Grace.
Oh, I'm so glad to hear that!
I don't know, Your Grace. It's beyond my cognizance to judge that. I've another mission.
Oh yes, sure. We are in the hands of God!
Regrettably yes, Your Grace. It's just a question of time...
What do you think by that, knight? You really scared me. I... why should it be the End of the World? Do you now anything about it?
I'm sorry, I was just trying to make a joke.
Oh, now I can breathe again, knight!
Of course. Just look around and remember the Revelation by St. Ezekiel in the Scriptures...
Oh yes, sure... you are right. I thought, that... but no, how stupid I've been. Of course, the Scriptures mention all this as a coming of the Judgment Day. But I believe firmly that it won't come!
The war is said to be coming, Your Grace. Do you happen to have heard anything about that?

I've heard nothing about the war, knight. My husband hadn't mentioned it at all. Against whom should be the war waged? Did the pagans from the Far East start to endanger us? Or did some hellish army stepped out from the bowels of the Earth?
No, Your Grace, nothing of that kind happened—the more strange it is, isn't it?!
Yes, it is, for sure.

If I suspect someone from heresy? Oh... God save us! I don't know anything about the heretics! Should my husband found out I know anything about them, surely he would be angry. And when my husband is angry, he... oh God, I don't know anything about the heretics!

Oh, knight, of course something terrible happened in Glatzburg lately! You can't imagine the horror when that terrible storm stroke the city several days ago. It was such a foul weather, that even my husband stayed at home overnight—and he's used to go working in the night often. Right at midnight, just when the sound of temple bell faded, horrible rumpus started. At some moments I was afraid it would destroy our house completely! Lightning followed another lightning, thunders rumbled, the tempest crooned... and those voices! They cried and thundered, laughed and lamented... as if hell itself were swirling outside our windows. The other day people in the city whispered to each other that they glimpsed demons dancing in the sky. But I haven't seen them, because I was huddled in my bed all the time. I was scared so much, you know.
Bishop Trevorius passed out? My God... that's terrible! I'll pray for the salvation of his soul...
So you don't know anything about that murder?
About what murder?
The murder of Bishop Trevorius, of course...
Forget it, Your Grace...

Father Frederick? Isn't he that old, somber cleric? Yes, it must be him. But I haven't seen him for a long time... Maybe he's ill. I must ask my husband, he always knows everything. He's a very kind and wise man, you know.
I've heard that Hans Thomas Brookwelt is possessed by dark powers, and with the help of them he can lay his hands on women and girls in Glatzburg. What do you think about that suspicion?

My God, Hans Thomas Brookwelt is a heretic? I'd have never thought that... He always looked like a decent man—although a low-born. Who would have thought he was a lecher, who tried... well, that what you said... That's terrible! I'll have to beware of him. If he did me that... well, that what you said, my husband would be probably very angry. And when my husband is angry, he... but good heavens, what have I told, my husband is a good man, after all! They should catch this Brookwelt and do something about him, not to let him do any harm to someone else.
I've heard rumors that the maid Jeanette is a witch practicing dark rituals. What do you think about it?

My God, the maid of Baron Edger von Hunth is a witch? Who would have thought that... she always looked like a decent young girl, although a low-born. One should start to be afraid of his own underlings! When my husband will get to know about this...
I need to get the wine called Chateau de Trebrechette. Do you have any idea where I could get a few bottles?

Raquel Gielwitch disappeared? That's terrible! And by the way, who was she?
She was a sister of Wanda Gielwitch.

But of course we can talk to each other, knight. Sure my husband would agree with that.

An honor to meet you, Your Grace. Could I talk to you for a moment?
But of course you can talk to me, knight. Sure my husband wouldn't mind that. He's a very kind man, you know.
Why did you say a while ago, that we had a nice day today? Does this gloomy day seem nice to you?
But of course, knight! My husband told me in the morning that we have a nice day today, so this is a beautiful day. My husband is a very wise man, you know.
Oh yes, sure he is... Could I ask you some questions?
But of course you can talk to me, knight. I'm sure my husband wouldn't mind that. He's a very kind man, you know.
No offense to you husband, but I don't think today is a nice day at all...
Hush! You can't talk like that, knight! He could hear you and he would think that I opposed him. You can't talk like that about my husband. He's a very kind man, you know. And he loves me a lot.
Is there something wrong with your eye, Your Grace? Did someone hurt you, maybe?
With my eye? What eye? Nobody did hurt me... my husband is a very kind man!
Well... as you wish. Let's not talk about it any further. Could I ask you some questions?
Don't be cross with me, Your Grace, but it seems like someone did strike you. Maybe even beat you up. You're trying to hide it under the face powder, but I can see it clearly. What happened to you?
Quietly, knight! Don't talk so loud, or he will hear you and he'll think I've told you everything. My husband is a very kind man!
It seems that your husband beat you up, is that true?
No, it isn't! It's an awful lie! My husband loves me and he's a very kind man. I'm his duteous, devoted wife! He would have never hurt me!
So what about those bruises and contusions, Your Grace? And why do you insist your husband is a good man? Does your husband maltreat you?
Oh my God, what have I done? Why did I say something like that? My husband is a kind man, yes he is! He would never hurt me. He loves me and I love him. He's a kind man!
If your husband hurts you, Your Grace, you better open your heart to me. I'll see what could I do in that matter.
My husband is a kind man! Yes, a very kind man. He tells me he loves me. He's a good, kind, noble man.
Tell me the truth, Your Grace. NOW!

Oh my God... this is so terrible... after all, how could I tell a bad word about my husband?! He will find out and he'll beat me again... He's a kind man, so why does he such a terrible things? Why does he behave so strangely? And where does he spend all those nights? Oh my God, forgive me my sins...
Does your husband beat you often? When did he start to do it?
No no no... for the God Almighty, what have I said?! My husband is a good man! Forget what I've told you, please!
You mentioned that your husband is often out of home at night. What will you tell me about that?
No, no... he's at home every night, I swear! I must have been daydreaming, I'd never say something like that about my husband!
Look, Your Grace—I can help you, if you tell me the whole truth. Denying brings you no good!
I'm not denying anything! My husband is a good man, he would never hurt me. Forget what I've said, I must have been out of my mind! Please, knight!
Are you Duchess van Leerin? I'm sorry what happened to your husband. But there was nothing else I could do.
Hail to you, Your Grace. How do you do?
Great, knight. We have such a beautiful day today...
Well... if you think so. Could you spare some time to have a little talk with me?
But of course, knight. My husband would surely approve it.
Do you still consider this day beautiful?
But of course, knight! My husband told me this day is beautiful, and he has to be right! Just look around you...
Haven't you changed your mind, Your Grace? Don't you want to tell me the truth about your husband?
Leave me alone! I won't tell you anything! My husband is a kind and gracious man. He loves me and he's a good husband to me, you know!
I'd better go, Your Grace. Farewell.
Hail to you, Your Grace. I'm sorry for what happened to your husband.
Hail to you, Your Grace. Are you better already?
Of course I'm better, knight. My husband takes care of me so nicely and gently! He's a very kind man, you know.
Your Grace, your husband is dead! He was a debauched heretic who died as he deserved! Stop living in that lie—your husband is dead!

Why do you say ugly things like that, knight? Such a joke isn't nice of you. But don't worry—I'm not going to tell him you talked about him like this. Surely he would be offended by it. My husband is a very kind man, you know.
Oh so... sure. Could I talk to you, Your Grace? If it won't distress you, of course.
Sure we can talk, knight. I believe my husband will be delighted when I tell him we talked to each other.
Sorry to have bothered you, Your Grace. I'd better go. Farewell.
Oh, knight, you should better leave. I'm not sure it's a good idea to stay in my husband's house right now...
Why do you think so, Your Grace? What happened?

My husband was here before a while and he's very angry about you. He said you had done something very unpleasant to him. He was very angry. Do you know anything about that? Have you really done something to him?
Yes. I killed him.

Surely not, knight. After all, I told you he was here just a moment ago. You should better leave before he returns. He's a very kind man, you know. But sometimes... Oh my God... have you heard that? He's already here! Quickly, knight, go away! If he gets angry, he...
Stop that already, Your Grace. Your husband is dead!
My husband is not dead, knight. On the contrary—he's coming. You must go away immediately. He is very angry!
First of all, please, answer some questions.
Don't you understand, knight? My husband is here! You must leave immediately. He's very angry at you!
All right, Your Grace, I'll go. Farewell.
Oh, knight, I'm so glad to see you. Good that you left so quickly last time. My husband was very upset. But he's no longer angry, so everything is all right.
Your Grace, during my last visit I met the ghost of your deceased husband. It nearly cost me my life!
Really? That's terrible... Thanks to God nothing happened to my husband. I'd tax myself with that as long as I live. My husband is a very kind man otherwise, you know?
Yes, of course he is. Could I talk to you for a moment? If your husband won't mind—I'd really want not to make him angry once again.
But of course we can talk, knight. My husband did forgive you long time ago for sure.
Well, I'd rather go. I don't want to meet your husband once again. Farewell.
Hello, knight. How are you this beautiful day?
Thanks for asking, Your Grace. Could I talk to you for a moment?
But of course, knight. Shall I call my husband? Surely he would like to see you.
No, thanks, that's not necessary. I'll be better off without him.
All right, as you wish, knight.
Why not? I'll be glad to see him again. He still has a lot to explain to me!

All right, wait a minute. I'll send for him. Oh, my most beloved spouse, I'm sorry to bother you from your surely very important work, but there is somebody here who'd like to talk to you. Could you come to us? My spouse? Well... strange, he's not here. There's nothing I can do, probably his duties called him. He's a very busy man, you know... You'll have to do without him. I'll tell him later you were here.
Well enough. Farewell.
But of course, knight. My husband surely will be glad when he finds out we talked to each other.
Not bad, thanks. Haven't your husband showed up somewhere around here?
Oh, far from it, knight, I'm sorry. Probably he's somewhere out of the city. But sure he will come back soon.
Your Grace, you really don't know your husband is dead and his ghost tried to assassinate me here in your house, do you?

I wonder, knight, where do you get all those stories from? Even a wandering minstrel wouldn't think up something like that. But you better stop it, or my husband will find out about it. And he's not fond of such jokes very much.
Could I ask you some questions, Your Grace?
Of course, knight. Since my husband is out of the city, I have almost no one to talk to.
Farewell, Your Grace.

Oh... it seemed to me just now as if you tried to take something from me! Oh my God, I'm terrible—to suspect a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous of theft! My husband mustn't find out about it! Please, don't tell him, knight! He would be very angry...
My husband Duke Rowan van Leerin rules in Glatzburg. He is the royal vice-governor of the city. He's a very wise man, Father.

Sure, is he? I... I don't know, Father. My husband is a kind man and by the grace of God he's the royal vice-governor of the city... that's all I know. It is beyond woman's cognizance to talk into the politics.
I'm not shopping much, Father. My husband says I'd spend all money. He's a very wise man, you know.

What do I think about the current crisis? Oh, Father, all those things afflicting us are so terrible! I pray so much for all those things to be already behind us and we could live like before again. This isn't the End of the World after all, Father, is it?
What do you think by that, Father? You really scared me. I... why should it be the End of the World? Do you now anything about it?
Oh, now I can breathe again, Father!

I've heard nothing about the war, Father. My husband hadn't mentioned it at all. Against whom should be the war waged? Did the pagans from the Far East start to endanger us? Or did some hellish army stepped out from the bowels of the Earth?

Oh, Father, of course something terrible happened in Glatzburg lately! You can't imagine the horror when that terrible storm stroke the city several days ago. It was such a foul weather, that even my husband stayed at home overnight—and he's used to go working in the night often. Right at midnight, just when the sound of temple bell faded, horrible rumpus started. At some moments I was afraid it would destroy our house completely! Lightning followed another lightning, thunders rumbled, the tempest crooned... and those voices! They cried and thundered, laughed and lamented... as if hell itself were swirling outside our windows. The other day people in the city whispered to each other that they glimpsed demons dancing in the sky. But I haven't seen them, because I was huddled in my bed all the time. I was scared so much, you know.

If you're looking for wine, try asking in the innkeeper Truthorn's tavern, Father. My husband has been buying wine from him for years. Sure he will have some wine. Or beer at least, if not wine. My husband likes also beer very much, you know.

The slums? I'm not frequenting such places, Father. My husband doesn't want it. He says I could catch some disease there, or I could be attacked by some devious villain. He says I should stay away from the indigents.
All right, as you wish, Father. What were we talking about?

What? That's nonsense. Are you crazy, Father? I'm a married woman, after all! My husband would be very angry if he found out that I'm a widow. No, no, Father, you must be mistaken. I'm not a widow, but a happily married woman!
It will be nice to see you again, Father. Sure my husband would not have any objections against it. He's a very kind man. Farewell.
I seriously doubt that, Father. I can hear him working in his study. In a while we'll go for a walk to the city. He's very nice to me. He's a kind-hearted man, you know.
But of course we can talk to each other, Father. Sure my husband would agree with that.
Farewell, Father. And come to visit us again sometime. Both me and my husband will be glad to see you.
