Grand Duke Robert Heidrick rules in Glatzburg by the grace of God—let the heaven bless his rule. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the royal vice-governor of the city.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to talk about that with you, son!

As far as I know, Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned armory in Glatzburg. You can get potions and various magic items from Enrie Jungwirdt, the wise woman, and from Paolus Ventimus, the alchemist. Wanda Gielwitch, the inkeeper, and Ludwig Weintraum the landlord both have large selections of goods for sale. And you can barter anything at Alphonso DiCerbio's, if you don't mind the origin of the goods.

What do I think about the current crisis? That's a strange question, son. You know as well as me that we are in the hands of God. All that is happening here is His will and if He decided in His infinite wisdom to put us to trial, He has the right to do that and nobody can change it. We must hold and stand the test!
But what if we won't stand it? Don't you see how weak is the faith of the people around you?

In that case, if God turns His face away from us, we deserve it. But it won't happen, son. Aren't both of us here to prevent it? Me with my prayers and with my service to Lord and you with your determination and with the sword in your hand?
Thanks, Father. It's pleasant to hear such opinion.
You're welcome, son. If you're missing the faith, you will find it in prayer.
War is said to be coming, Father. Do you happen to know some details about that?
War, you say? I've heard no rumors of that kind... But if it is as you say, surely it is a just war, because a just war is the will of God.

Lots of hellspawns and devils have appeared in the area around Glatzburg in the recent years, son. There were always some infernal powers here, because Satan is lurking everywhere. However, since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, their numbers have been increasing so much that even my mind was seized with horror. And not only around the city—creatures of hell started to manifest even here within the city walls. It always occurs after dusk. Living dead are arising from dark corners, wandering through the city and tearing all living creatures that come in their way. No one knows where do they come from—maybe Satan himself brings them on the wings of darkness. All of them disappear again just before sunset, as if they sink into the ground. I'm sure you can imagine, son, how scared are the people in the city. And the royal garrison is helpless—no matter how many creatures they succeed to slaughter, the monsters come to kill and maim the next night regardless!
I'm looking for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone, Father?
I don't have any suspicion of heresy I could confide to you with, son. However, I know what my holy duty is and if I find out something wicked, I'll inform you immediately.
Do you happen to know anything about the heretic cult of The Children of the New Order?

The cult of The Children of the New Order? It rings a bell to me, but I'm not quite sure... Wasn't it one of those heretic cults that defiled the Faith in the Empire during the restless times of Hundred Years War? I don't remember exactly... try asking honorable cardinal Truncquillius, the local curial inquisitor. He will know about it for sure.

A very bad thing happened, son. Francessca Gulvardi, the maid of the Grand Duke, a pleasant and obedient girl, tried to assassinate Bishop Trevorius during the confession! But the worst is the way she tried to do so, son—with her teeth and finger nails, like a rabid animal. She charged at him through the confessional, crushed the wood to pieces and made an attempt on his life so vehemently that she left him with a lot of bruises and lacerations. Luckily he was able to defend himself, because he's strong not only of mind, but also of body. God save him for the missions he has already accomplished. Francessca Gulvardi was thrown into the local prison after that; she was struggling and kicking like a wounded horse. There was no doubt some unclean demon possessed her! We live in terrible times, my son.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible event, son! Maybe it's the worst thing that could have happened to us these times. That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all!

That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all! Because of that I feel very bad about the fact that people say you have something to do with that murder, son. It's utter nonsense, of course, but even so the clergy is losing its credibility, when people venture that a servant of God assassinated the Bishop.

I'm not interested in pagan relics, son. And you should not be interested in them either. Those filthy things contravene the true faith. You should spend your time serving the Realm, not searching for pagan devilments. Maybe you should confess as soon as possible...

Of course I know something about Father Frederick, son. That is to say, I was with him during the last years of his life, before he left us forever two years ago. He was a very strange servant of God. His interpretations of church rule, as well as of the Laws of God and of the Scriptures, were... unorthodox. But I can't say a bad word about him, nothing of the kind. After all, the ways of God are enigmatic and only God can judge our deeds. Father Frederick had a reputation of a successful exorcist, but I must say that he didn't performed any exorcism during his stay here in Glatzburg.
How could it be? Was there nobody possessed by some evil demon here?

Nothing of the kind, son, we had several possessed people here during that time. But Father Frederick claimed that he's already too tired, too weak and that Satan would have only laugh at him. It seems to me that he wanted to live the rest of his years in peace here in Glatzburg. And he was successful in the end, because mortis negra took him two years ago.

So, those rumors about the return of Istwan de Bragho from the Netherworld were true. I don't even want to believe that... but on the other hand, no wonder—the times are so hard! However, I'm afraid I can't help you much, son—my strongest weapon against the powers of darkness is prayer. And I doubt a prayer would stop Istwan de Bragho.

So, you're interested in the Fallen Angels, son. That's a rather dark side of the orthodox religion, to tell the truth. But it is an inherent result of the divine equanimity of power—where there's light also darkness must exist. A counterweight must exist to everything—even to the all-embracing love of God the Redeemer. And the Fallen Angels represent such a counterweight.
I understand, go on.

The Scriptures mention them as angelic beings that were, together with Satan, thrown down from the sky for their sins. So they were the angels in the beginning, but the wrath of God made them condemnable hellspawns, who must linger in hell. Together, they are four—Arthamon, the Master of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Mistress of Fornication and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the first of the servants of Satan. Every faithful man should beware of the Fallen Angels and at the same time also of their henchmen and of all the infernal signs and seductions. Despite their banishment, these angels may still get into human minds and this is the way the sin comes to this world.
I'm sorry, son, but I don't know anything about Raquel Gielwitch that could help you to save her. I pray for the salvation of her soul.

Father, you're making a grave mistake when you're denying me the answer to my question. You must know very well what happened to Ulpian of Erbrett according to the Scriptures, when he refused to provide a shelter to the First Prophet? He disappeared and his name was forgotten forever...

It seems you don't like me for some reason, Father. You have the right to do so, but I believe that if you think properly about the whole matter, you will surely find out that your answer won't make any harm to anyone.
There are only few people as well-read and educated as you, Father. I assure you that your answer would help me a lot.

I fulfill various assignments the Bishop charges me with, but most of all I devote myself to the healing of both bodies and souls. I studied herbalism and medicine from renowned Abbot Malabert before our Lord recalled him to Eternity in my native Trimoli monastery.
Where is the Trimoli monastery located? I've never heard about it.

No wonder you haven't heard about it. It is a small monastery in Bellamond Mountains, several days of ride from Alvaron, the capital of the Realm. Ways leading there are almost forgotten, as almost no one visits the place these days. However, it became renowned exactly because Abbot Malabert retired there in his declining years.
Who was that Abbot Malabert?

Don't you know Abbot Malabert? I'm really surprised... It was him who healed King Edward I—father of our ruler—from that evil illness he had nearly succumbed to. The Abbot taught the medicine at the Alvaron University of St. Orthenius. However, before the end of his life he chose seclusion, Trimoli monastery to be exact, where I had the honor of being his last pupil. What a shame he didn't live to see these days. Maybe he could help His Majesty King Edward who's weaker every day since his children died...
When did King Edward actually lose all of his children?

Don't you remember? Two years ago, when the first Scourge of God was raging in the form of plague. Though apparently not mortis negra had their deaths on its conscience—the forces of hell had. At least that's what people were saying. Anyway, it was a terrible tragedy. No wonder it broke King's heart completely.
What do you mean by that?
People say he shut himself away and he almost doesn't talk at all. All the time he drowns his sorrow in wine and his health is worse and worse every day.
Well... May God protect their souls—and King Edward!

Amen, son. That's why I'm so sorry Abbot Malabert passed out in Trimoli sooner then he could do something in this matter. Surely he would find some wonder drug to rescue the King from his disinterest and to give him strength to perform brisk actions which would benefit the people of the Realm...
But of course, son. For a little gift to our diocese, let's say $$getmoney100$$ gp.
Could you answer me some questions, Father?
But of course. It will be a pleasure for me.
I have to go, Father. Farewell.
Farewell, son. Go in peace.
Hello, son. If I'm not mistaken, you must be that paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous who came from Hillbrandt not long ago, am I right?
Yes, that probably would be me. Why do you ask?

I was curious who was behind those events that occurred in Hillbrandt. The burning of Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian and so on. It caused quite an upheaval in the curia. That is, Judge Vallarian was a member of the local curia and he was sent to Hillbrandt at his own request.
Really? I didn't know that.

Yes, it was as I said. He made a great effort to be allowed to set out for Hillbrandt and clean it from the heretic proliferation. He said Satan is sleeping there and it's only a matter of time when he will wake up. In the end cardinal Truncquillius named him a commissioned judge and sent him to Hillbrandt in the name of Glatzburg Inquisitorial Curia. It was early in the spring, as soon as the snow melted.
Interesting. Anyway, could I ask you, who you are?
Excuse me for not introducing myself immediately. Curiosity prevailed over etiquette. My name is Erbert of Trimoli and I'm the deacon of the local diocese.
I'm glad to meet you, Father. Tell me what is your mission here.
Maybe. Depends on who and why is asking.

Oh so... I understand. My name is Erbert of Trimoli and I'm the deacon of the local diocese. I didn't want to snoop around, I was just interested, if it's really you who was involved in those strange Hillbrandt events related to the burning of Bishop Vallarian.
Yes, that would be me.
I'm glad to meet you, son. My name is Erbert of Trimoli and I'm the deacon of the local diocese.
Nice to meet you, Father. What is your mission here?
No, that's a mistake.
Forgive me then, mea culpa. Anyway, you're new to the city, I've noticed that immediately. You definitely don't belong to the local chapter because I would remember you if you did.
You are right, Father. However, tell me, what's your mission here?
No, that must be some kind of mistake.

Oh... excuse me, I made a hasty conclusion. That is to say, I've heard that a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous came to the city, the same one who caused quite an upheaval in Hillbrandt in connection with that case of the Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian. They say he even got him burned! But if you say it's not you, I won't bother you with that. In any case, you're new to the city, I've noticed that immediately. You definitely don't belong to the local chapter because I would remember you if you did.
You are right, Father. Actually, can I ask you who you are?
God bless you, son. What can I do for you?
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! You should be ashamed of yourself, son!
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to talk about that with you, brother!

What do I think about the current crisis? That's a strange question, brother. You know as well as me that we are in the hands of God. All that is happening here is His will and if He decided in His infinite wisdom to put us to trial, He has the right to do that and nobody can change it. We must hold and stand the test!

In that case, if God turns His face away from us, we deserve it. But it won't happen, brother. Aren't both of us here to prevent it? Me with my prayers and with my service to Lord and you with your inquisitorial vesture and with flaming torch?
Thanks, brother. It's pleasant to hear such opinion.
You're welcome, brother. If you're missing the faith, you will find it in prayer.
War is said to be coming, brother. Do you happen to know some details about that?

Lots of hellspawns and devils have appeared in the area around Glatzburg in the recent years, brother. There were always some infernal powers here, because Satan is lurking everywhere. However, since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, their numbers have been increasing so much that even my mind was seized with horror. And not only around the city—creatures of hell started to manifest even here within the city walls. It always occurs after dusk. Living dead are arising from dark corners, wandering through the city and tearing all living creatures that come in their way. No one knows where do they come from—maybe Satan himself brings them on the wings of darkness. All of them disappear again just before sunset, as if they sink into the ground. I'm sure you can imagine, brother, how scared are the people in the city. And the royal garrison is helpless—no matter how many creatures they succeed to slaughter, the monsters come to kill and maim the next night regardless!
I'm looking for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone, brother?
I don't have any suspicion of heresy I could confide to you with, brother. However, I know what my holy duty is and if I found out something wicked, I would inform you immediately.

A very bad thing happened, brother. Francessca Gulvardi, the maid of the Grand Duke, a pleasant and obedient girl, tried to assassinate Bishop Trevorius during the confession! But the worst is the way she tried to do so, brother—with her teeth and finger nails, like a rabid animal. She charged at him through the confessional, crushed the wood to pieces and made an attempt on his life so vehemently that she left him with a lot of bruises and lacerations. Luckily he was able to defend himself, because he's strong not only of mind, but also of body. God save him for the missions he has already accomplished. Francessca Gulvardi was thrown into the local prison after that; she was struggling and kicking like a wounded horse. There was no doubt some unclean demon possessed her! We live in terrible times, my brother.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible event, brother! Maybe it's the worst thing that could have happened to us these times. That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all!

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible event, brother! Maybe it's the worst thing that could have happened to us these times. That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all! Because of that I feel very bad about the fact that people say you have something to do with that murder, brother. It's utter nonsense, of course, but even so the clergy is losing its credibility, when people venture that a servant of God assassinated the Bishop.

I'm not interested in pagan relics, brother. And neither you should be interested in them. Those filthy things contravene the true faith. You should spend your time serving our Lord, not searching for pagan devilments. Maybe you should confess soon...

Of course I know something about Father Frederick, brother. That is to say, I was with him during the last years of his life, before he left us forever two years ago. He was a very strange servant of God. His interpretations of church rule, as well as of the Laws of God and of the Scriptures, were... unorthodox. But I can't say a bad word about him, nothing of the kind. After all, the ways of God are enigmatic and only God can judge our deeds. Father Frederick had a reputation of a successful exorcist, but I must say that he didn't performed any exorcism during his stay here in Glatzburg.

Nothing of the kind, brother, we had several possessed people here during that time. But Father Frederick claimed that he's already too tired, too weak and that Satan would have only laugh at him. It seems to me that he wanted to live the rest of his years in peace here in Glatzburg. And he was successful in the end, because mortis negra took him two years ago.

So, those rumors about the return of Istwan de Bragho from the Netherworld were true. I don't even want to believe that... but on the other hand, no wonder—the times are so hard! However, I'm afraid I can't help you much, brother—my strongest weapon against the powers of darkness is prayer. And I doubt a prayer would stop Istwan de Bragho.

So, you're interested in the Fallen Angels, brother. That's a rather dark side of the orthodox religion, to tell the truth. But it is an inherent result of the divine equanimity of power—where there's light also darkness must exist. A counterweight must exist to everything—even to the all-embracing love of God the Redeemer. And the Fallen Angels represent such a counterweight.
I'm sorry, brother, but I don't know anything about Raquel Gielwitch that could help you to save her. I pray for the salvation of her soul.

Brother, you're making a grave mistake when you're denying me the answer to my question. You must know very well what happened to Ulpian of Erbrett according to the Scriptures, when he refused to provide a shelter to the First Prophet? He disappeared and his name was forgotten forever...

It seems you don't like me for some reason, brother. You have the right to do so, but I believe that if you think properly about the whole matter, you will surely find out that your answer won't make any harm to anyone.
There are only few people as well-read and educated as you, brother. I assure you that your answer would help me a lot.

Amen, brother. That's why I'm so sorry Abbot Malabert passed out in Trimoli sooner then he could do something in this matter. Surely he would find some wonder drug to rescue the King from his disinterest and to give him strength to perform brisk actions which would benefit the people of the Realm...
But of course, brother. Come closer and let the power of God heal your wounds...
No problem, brother. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Could you answer me some questions, brother?
I must go, brother—call of duty to God. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. Go in peace.
Hello, brother. If I'm not mistaken, you must be that cleric who came from Hillbrandt not long ago, am I right?

I was curious who was behind those events that occurred in Hillbrandt. The burning of Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian and so on. It caused quite an upheaval in the curia. That is, Judge Vallarian was a member of the local curia and he was send to Hillbrandt at his own request.
I'm glad to meet you, brother. Tell me what is your mission here.
I'm glad to meet you, brother. My name is Erbert of Trimoli and I'm the deacon of the local diocese.
Nice to meet you, brother. What is your mission here?
Forgive me then, mea culpa. Anyway you're new to the city, I've noticed that immediately. Surely you belong neither to the local diocese of the Holy Church nor to the curia of the Holy Office.
You are right, brother. However, tell me, what's your mission here?

Oh... excuse me, I made a hasty conclusion. That is to say, I've heard that a priest came to the city, the same one who caused quite an upheaval in Hillbrandt in connection with that case of Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian. They say he even got him burned! But if you say it's not you, I won't bother you with that. In any case, you're new to the city, I've noticed that immediately. Surely you belong neither to the local diocese of the Holy Church nor to the curia of the Holy Office.
You are right, brother. Actually, can I ask you who you are?
God bless you, brother. What can I do for you?
The Inquisitor of the Holy Office and he's a thief?! I don't want to believe that! What can you expect from the world as a whole, when even clerics are stealing! What a shame, brother!

In that case, if God turns His face away from us, we deserve it. But it won't happen, son. Aren't both of us here to prevent it? Me with my prayers and with my service to Lord and you with your standing and God's favor?
I don't have any suspicion of heresy I could confide to you with, son. However, if I find out something wicked, I'll inform you immediately.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible event, son! Maybe it's the worst thing that could have happened to us these times. That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in the deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of a diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all!

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible event, son! Maybe it's the worst event that could have happened to us these times. That is to say, monsignor Trevorius was a flame in the deep darkness for us! Who could ever do such a thing? What kind of animal, what monster? The one who can cause the death of a diocese Bishop can't be a human being at all! Because of that I feel very bad about the fact that people say you have something to do with that murder, son. It's utter nonsense, of course, but even so the nobility is losing its credibility, when people venture to say that a noble man assassinated the Bishop.

I'm not interested in pagan relics, son. And neither should you be interested in them. Those filthy things contravene the true faith. You should spend your time serving the Realm, not searching for pagan devilments. Maybe you should confess as soon as possible...
Hello, son. If I'm not mistaken, you must be that noble who came from Hillbrandt not long ago, am I right?
Maybe. Depends on why and who is asking.
Forgive me then, mea culpa. Anyway you're new to the city, I've noticed that immediately. You definitely don't belong to the local gentry because I would remember you if you did.

Oh... excuse me, I made a hasty conclusion. That is to say, I've heard that a noble came to the city, the same one who caused quite an upheaval in Hillbrandt in connection with that case of Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian. They say he even got him burned! But if you say it's not you, I won't bother you with that. In any case, you're new to the city, I noticed that immediately. You definitely don't belong to the local gentry because I would remember you if you did.
A noble man steals?! I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! You should be ashamed of yourself, son!
Wait, Fathor! I'm sure we can agree on something...
You want to make a deal with Fathor, little human?! Fathor is too hungry for a trade. And more, what on earth do you think you could offer him?!
I could bring you so much food you could load yourself up for a couple of weeks!
Well... sounds interesting, but Fathor smells a dirty trick, little human. He let you go and you flee—or you come back with soldiers. No, Fathor better eats you up immediately!
Wait, I'll do anything for you! Do you understand?! Anything!

Anything I want, you say, little human?! Well... it is true. Fathor hasn't had any good meat for a long time. Fathor eats those scraggy human worms all the time and there's hardly any meat on them—only some skin and sinew. But, Fathor would like to have some mutton... All right, I agree—bring a fat sheep to Fathor and Fathor not only won't eat you up, but he'll even give you some of his glorious gold. Do you agree, little human?!
Yes, I agree. Farewell.
I won't do anything like that! I won't steal the remaining pieces of cattle from the people because of the gluttony of some hellish monster!
NO?! In that case, Fathor will eat your meat and spit out your bones, little human! Muheeehaaahaaa!
What about some money?
Fathor eats neither gold nor gemstones—he's not a troll, after all!
I assure you this bite will turn bitter in your mouth, you beast!
Fathor eats bitter things as well, little human! Muheeehaaahaaa!
Fathor smells fresh meat! Who dares to enter Fathor's cave?! Hah, a human! What reason do you have to be here?! You came to feed Fathor with your meat voluntarily, little human?!
I came to purge this place of the presence of hellish monsters such as you!
Fathor thinks you are a madman, little human. Fortunately, Fathor eats madmen too, so he will enjoy you as a meal.
No... that's a mistake... I apologize... I better go!

It's a mistake, you say?! Bah... a human coming to Fathor's cave because of a mistake?! Fathor doesn't think so... Fathor thinks you are a thief... or a madman. Fortunately, Fathor eats both thieves and madmen, so he will enjoy you as a meal!
What, little human—do you bring Fathor that mutton he wanted from you?! Fathor would eat a horse... if you won't bring him at least that sheep, he will eat you instead!
I bring you a sheep, as you wanted, Fathor. Here you are.
Excellent! Fathor's mouth waters at the sight of the juicy meat! Here is your gold, little human—you deserve it. Now Fathor can see not all humans are good only to be put in my mouth. Muheeehaaahaaa!
What would you say about this sheep I have with me? Would it be enough?
Do you mean that smallish weakling, little human?! No, it wouldn't be enough for Fathor. Fathor wants a good sheep, or he will eat you instead, do you understand?!
Now, I'm fed up—I won't let some monster make me his flunky!
In that case Fathor will make you his dinner, little human! Muheeehaaahaaa!
I haven't come by any sheep yet...
So you'd better hurry, little human, or you will end up in Fathor's stomach! Go!
I've changed my mind—I won't fetch food for some wicked monster!
In that case Fathor will make you his food, little human! Muheeehaaahaaa!
What's the matter?! Don't you see Fathor is eating?! Gulp...
Oh... sorry then.
I'm here to purge this place of your presence, you infernal monster!
Huh...?! But that's a BETRAYAL! In that case Fathor will make you his dessert, little human! Muheeehaaahaaa!
This must be the gate that leads to the royal burial chamber...
It's closed! I have to find out how to open it...
It seems I have found the way to open it!
The gate of the royal burial chamber is opened!
The gate of the royal burial chamber is closed!
Well... to tell you the truth, knight, I do really have one suspicion of heretical godlessness but I'm not entirely sure if I should mention it to you...
You better tell me about your suspicion, good man. You never know what detail can lead to revealing of heretics!

You are right, knight. Now then—I saw something pretty strange. To tell you the truth, a shiver ran down my spine and you would say that considering my occupation I shouldn't fear even Satan himself. It happened that night when that terrible storm was raging above the city. I knew something would happen but I had so much work at the scaffold I was delayed there 'til dusk. When I finally set on my way to the city, the fog was falling down all around and occasionally I had a feeling I was already lost. Suddenly, a group of people came out of nowhere. I wanted to join them but what I saw in that fog and darkness made me think otherwise...
I won't urge you, good man. You will decide on your own what's good for you...

You're right... just because of that I think I should tell you. In short... I saw something pretty strange. A shiver ran down my spine, and you would say that considering my occupation I shouldn't fear even Satan himself. It happened that night that terrible storm was raging above the city. I knew something would happen but I had so much work at the scaffold I was delayed there 'til dusk. When I finally set on the way to the city, the fog was falling down all around and occasionally I had a feeling I was lost already. Suddenly, a group of people came out of nowhere. I wanted to join them but what I saw in that fog and darkness made me think otherwise...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of Glatzburg, knight. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor.

Hans von Drichtmaul has a reknowned armory in Glatzburg. You can get potions and various magic items from Enrie Jungwirdt, the wise woman, and from Paolus Ventimus, the alchemist. Wanda Gielwitch, the innkeeper, and Ludwig Weintraum, the landlord, both have large selections of goods for sale. Also, you can barter anything at Alphonso DiCerbio's, if you don't mind the origin of the goods.

I'll tell you frankly, knight—people in the city are scared to death and they believe the end of the world will come soon. All this misery lasts too long for the people to believe in something else and it is constantly getting worse. I know that it's a trial and we must come through it but it seems there's too much of that. All those signs from the Scriptures, hellspawns lurking above the ground, heretic sects multiplying like flies on a piece of dung... this is not right and people are becoming hopeless, even desperate. Someone should do something about it very quickly, otherwise it will end pretty grim.
The war is said to be coming. Do you happen to know anything about that?

You're right, I've heard something about the war. Sheriff Smith recruits new men. He can forget about me though, as according to the royal edict, all members of the Executioners' Guild are dispensed from the duty of serving in the army—because they are very busy both in peace and during the war, if you understand me.
What monsters and hellspawns can people meet here in and around Glatzburg?

Ungodly vermin are lurking here around the scaffold, knight. They are attracted by the smell of death and human suffering. I've already spotted almost every species I have ever heard about... For example, those hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns. People say they're devils moving out to the earths surface to feed on human meat and take victims back to hell. I don't know to what extent this is true, but the fact is, whenever they attack they leave a bloody havoc behind. They always hide themselves in those caves near the ruins of Galibornium and there's no hide nor hair of them for some time. Lately, their attacks are increasing. As if frenzy, rage and daring were rising in them...
Are there any rewards announced in Glatzburg for killing monsters?
Yes, there are, I've heard about it. Grand Duke Heidrick announced the reward for capturing the bandits pestering the roads near Glatzburg. Sheriff Smith pays the reward in gold.
If we could get back to those heretics for a moment...

I've already told you about my suspicion of heresy, knight. I mean that event here at the scaffold where I saw Raimond Ventano—if it was him—and some other hooded figures draw something somewhere in the dark. I don't know about anything else.

Aside from Duke Istwan de Bragho rising up from his grave and is out for my life, I must mention that also several young girls are missing. Very young girls, from what I understand. I'd say that damned Istwan de Bragho is responsible, as he also had a taste for young girls and it appears he used them in a way which would make you throw up, knight. Not only the girls—before his rampage was finally ended, even some boys went missing. However, this year, only several young girls got lost. Without a trace. Without a witness. It is as if the horned reaper himself took them away.

I don't know who killed Bishop Trevorius, knight. Although, no matter who the murderer was, I hope frankly to get my hands on him. I will use every scrap of my knowledge of the executioners art so his execution may last several days. I will break his limbs so artfully he will bleed very little. I'll pull the skin away from his body in such a way he won't faint from pain, not even once. I'll cut strips of flesh from him so that he...
Ahem... thank you, Master Executioner.

Excuse me, knight, I was carried away by my emotions; it hasn't happened to me for a long time. I just wanted to say that I'm deeply sorry about what happened and I hope the murderer will be punished. No matter who it is!
Somebody has stolen knight Commander Ethien de Pasque's Chain of the Brotherhood. Do you know anything about it?
I'm sorry, but I don't know a word about the necklace of Commander Ethiene de Pasque. Could he have lost it somewhere?
I'm looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Do you happen to know where it could be located? Bonhart was said to hide it somewhere before he left for the war...

Of course I've heard about the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Bonhart was said to be able to make real wonders with it. I've also heard that he buried it somewhere before he went to the Barbarian Wars in 977—to keep it from falling in the hands of some thieving mongrel but nobody knows where he buried it...

You're interested in local legends, right? I was always fascinated by the tales about the coliseum that was located in the pagan city of Ereborn. It was something like a theatre, but executions occurred there instead of acts. At least, in the beginning. People convicted to death were executed there. They were herded to the arena and wild animals or soldiers were sent to kill them. One day, one of the convicts killed all the fierce beasts with bare hands and people were so excited that they started to give weapons to the convicts and those who survived were pardoned. It was during this time that those fights became very popular and, in the end, it became pure entertainment where courageous volunteers called gladiators performed in the coliseum instead of convicts. They fought not only against fierce beasts, but also against each other and against various monsters abundant in the world in that era.
Interesting. Go on.

It used to be like that until the year 223, when St. Orthenius and his righteous armies captured Galibornium. The coliseum was ruined and all its underground—where the gladiators prepared for the fight—was entombed. All who were hiding there from the war starved to death. It's said that people still can hear moaning and howling of ghosts from the depths under the coliseum.
Of course, I don't want it for free...
In that case, I can't help you...
Answer me immediately, or I'll have to force you to cooperate by means you no doubt won't like!

It seems you don't like me for some reason, good man. There's nothing I can do; you have the right to do so. But, I'd like you to think properly about the whole matter once again and change your mind. Your answer could help the cause of God greatly.

I could see from my first sight of you that you're a wise man, Flemberg. Wise and experienced, at least it seems to me. So, you can't be surprised I'm trying so hard to get your answer. That is to say, I'm sure it would help me a lot.
And what was that, if I can ask you?

It was such a large gray sack, knight. Long enough to hide a human body inside, if you get me. As soon as I saw it, I knew that something was very unpleasant about it. Who on earth would drag a dead body near the scaffold after dusk? So I hid in a nearby bush and tried very hard not to make a sound. Don't get me wrong, knight. I could oppose a bunch of bandits easily, but this was something else. It made my hair stand on end, although in fact I didn't know exactly why.
That's all right, good man. Did you recognize some of those people?

That's the problem, knight. I'd say Raimond Ventano was one of them but I'm not quite sure about that and also... it was dark and there was a heavy fog... but he was the only one who talked. I think I recognized him by his voice.
Thanks for the information, good man.
You're welcome, knight. I only hope I didn't cause any trouble to anyone by that. At the same time I didn't want to keep it for myself, if you get me...
Can you tell me when exactly that meeting occurred?

Well... in fact I can tell you that exactly. It was that night when that terrible storm took place above our city. It started even before I walked from the scaffold to the city. As for I can tell, I don't remember worse weather here in the city, and I've been living here since I was born...

Well... you may be right, knight. So... it concerns Istwan de Bragho. He was the royal vice-governor of the city many years ago but he wasn't a very good man. Well, in fact he was a true son of a bitch possessed by dark powers and he did things so terrible that peoples hair turned gray from the horror. He organized hunts for people, brought sacrifices to dark demons, bathed in the blood of non-baptized children... Simply the worst filth you can imagine but at the same time he was very clever. He never left any traces after his crimes, so no one could declare him guilty. He openly laughed at the authorities and boasted that they were no match for him. They were though. After several years of precise investigation, five paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous accused him of various crimes and proved him guilty at the trial. He was executed in quite a brutal way—quartering. Before he breathed his last breath he uttered a terrible curse saying he would come back from the Other World to take revenge on those who were behind his execution. Now, it seems that Bragho's curse really came true!
Why? What happened?

All five of the paladins who participated in the apprehending of Istwan de Bragho were found dead, one after another. Assassinated. Such a grim way was their demise that even my hair stood on end from horror! One of them was recognized only thanks to the equipment he had with him. Not much left from him. Just the blood, entrails and some flesh. It was terrible!
That's really scary but what does it have to do with you?
Don't you understand, knight? It was I whom executed Istwan de Bragho! Now I'm the next in his terrible afterlife revenge!
Yes, now it makes sense to me.

Of course! That's why I approached Judge Welfhar to ask him if he could do anything about that matter but nothing has happened since and I can't sleep in the night. My fear won't let me. Once it even seemed to me as if someone was walking around my house... I really fear for my life, knight! I fear that the revived body of Istwan de Bragho will come for me in the dark of night and take my soul to hell, as he did with all those paladins!
I'll help you, good man. I won't let a beast from the Other World lay a hand on you!
That would be very nice of you, knight. Really very nice.
That's right. You better answer me a couple of questions.
Gladly, knight. What do you need to know?
I'll start the investigation immediately, good man. Farewell.
Farewell, knight. Hurry, please. I don't think I'd like it if that bastard dragged me to a burning hell...
Maybe I could help you somehow in this matter but it depends on what you offer me for my help.
Offer? Do you mean a reward, knight?

I'm afraid I won't help you in this matter. But I'm sure that God will protect you as carefully as he protects every true faithful.
I hope so too. Otherwise it's quite probable I'll be found soon hanging by my own entrails!
Perhaps it won't come to that. Could I ask you a couple of questions to carry our discussion a bit further?
Sure, knight. What exactly are you interested in?
I hope so too. Farewell.
I've got good news for you—Istwan de Bragho is back in his grave. You don't have to worry about him anymore.

May our gracious Lord bless you, knight! I was already thinking that the devil will take me to hell as well as those five poor paladins who convicted him many years ago! Thanks, good man. Could I ask you a couple of questions now?
Sure, knight. What would you like to know?
Thanks. Farewell, good man.

I don't know what are you talking about, good man.

You could start by telling me your name.

Thanks, knight, but Judge Welfhar has already promised to take care of the whole matter. At least I hope so.
Good. However, could I talk to you for a moment?
Sure, knight. What can I do for you?
Judge Welfhar is a very busy man. You better open your heart to me, or you might regret it.
As you wish. Farewell for now.
I'd like to talk to you for a moment, if I can.
So, you are the Executioner? In that case it's an honor for me to get to know you. It seems to me we will work together a lot.
That can be, knight. There's a lot of work for people like you here in Glatzburg. We'll surely meet again.
Yes, I'm certain we will. Farewell for now.
Good news? Oh yes, sure... I bring you good news. Of course.
So is the curse broken? Does Istwan de Bragho lie dead in his grave? I don't have to fear for my life anymore, right?
I see, you meant THAT good news... No, I have to disappoint you. Istwan de Bragho is still alive. If that could be said about him, of course.

Then do something about that, knight! As a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous you have only one simple mission—to protect honest and innocent people from injustice. Better hurry then, or you'll probably find me tomorrow hanging on my own entrails!
Don't worry, we'll take care of it. By the way, why are you so afraid of this Istwan de Bragho?

Why? Because, before he breathed his last breath he uttered a terrible curse. He said he would come back from the Other World to take revenge on those who stood behind his execution. All five paladins who participated in the apprehending of Istwan de Bragho have already bit the dust... if they still have a jaw to bite. One of them was recognized only thanks to the equipment he had with him.
That's terrible but why are you personally afraid of the revenge of Istwan de Bragho?

Don't be afraid, good man. I'll protect you from that curse.
I'm glad to hear that, knight. To tell you the truth, my fear won't let me close my eyes at night. Each night I have a feeling that something is walking around my house.
I'll take care of everything but now you answer a couple of questions for me.
I'm at your service, knight. What's on your mind?
I believe firmly that all will be well in the end. Farewell for now.
Don't be afraid, good man. I'm sure that Judge Welfhar will take care of it.
I hope so. I should hate to end up as bad as those paladins. I'm the city Executioner, after all—how could someone expect I'd defend myself against the curse of a dead Duke?
I agree with you. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Sure. What's on your mind, knight?
Who is this Istwan de Bragho?
What? You're asking me who Istwan de Bragho is?! Didn't Judge Welfhar send you to tell me what progress he made? I am relying upon the Holy Office in this matter.
Well... no, I'm sorry. Judge Welfhar did not send me. If you tell me what the matter is, maybe I could help you more than he could?
Yes, Istwan de Bragho is back in his grave. You can live in peace.

Not yet, good man. Have patience.
Patience? How could I be patient when a dead hand can grasp my neck at any moment?! Easy for you to say...
Can I speak to you for a moment?
Sure, knight. What's the matter?
Your sleep will no longer be haunted, good man. The curse of Istwan de Bragho is broken and his body rests in the grave again.
Hello, knight. How do you do? Probably much better than I. Is there something you want from me?
I'd appreciate answers to my questions.
Ask then, knight, as you are here anyway...
How are you feeling?

How do you think I'm feeling? Bad, of course! Every night I awake with the feeling that a dead hand is grasping my neck but why would I tell you about it? Do you want anything from me? Or did you just come to see whether I'm still alive?
I don't need anything this time, good man. I just came by. Farewell.

Is that you, knight? I'm glad to see you again. I'll be grateful to you as long as I live for saving me from the curse of that damned Istwan de Bragho. May he rest in peace forever. Can I help you somehow?
Yes, you can. I'd like to ask you some questions.
I'll answer you gladly, knight. Just ask...
Not this time, good man. Farewell.
Farewell, knight. God bless you.
Well... to tell you the truth, Father, I do really have one suspicion of heretical godlessness but I'm not entirely sure if I should mention it to you...

You are right, Father. Now then—I saw something pretty strange. To tell you the truth, a shiver ran down my spine and you would say that considering my occupation I shouldn't fear even Satan himself. It happened that night when that terrible storm was raging above the city. I knew something would happen but I had so much work at the scaffold I was delayed there 'til dusk. When I finally set on my way to the city, the fog was falling down all around and occasionally I had a feeling I was already lost. Suddenly, a group of people came out of nowhere. I wanted to join them but what I saw in that fog and darkness made me think otherwise...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of Glatzburg, Father. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor.

I'll tell you frankly, Father—people in the city are scared to death and they believe the end of the world will come soon. All this misery lasts too long for the people to believe in something else and it is constantly getting worse. I know that it's a trial and we must come through it but it seems there's too much of that. All those signs from the Scriptures, hellspawns lurking above the ground, heretic sects multiplying like flies on a piece of dung... this is not right and people are becoming hopeless, even desperate. Someone should do something about it very quickly, otherwise it will end pretty grim.

Ungodly vermin are lurking here around the scaffold, Father. They are attracted by the smell of death and human suffering. I've already spotted almost every species I have ever heard about... For example, those hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns. People say they're devils moving out to the earths surface to feed on human meat and take victims back to hell. I don't know to what extent this is true, but the fact is, whenever they attack they leave a bloody havoc behind. They always hide themselves in those caves near the ruins of Galibornium and there's no hide nor hair of them for some time. Lately, their attacks are increasing. As if frenzy, rage and daring were rising in them...

I've already told you about my suspicion of heresy, Father. I mean that event here at the scaffold where I saw Raimond Ventano—if it was him—and some other hooded figures draw something somewhere in the dark. I don't know about anything else.

Aside from Duke Istwan de Bragho rising up from his grave and is out for my life, I must mention that also several young girls are missing. Very young girls, from what I understand. I'd say that damned Istwan de Bragho is responsible, as he also had a taste for young girls and it appears he used them in a way which would make you throw up, Father. Not only the girls—before his rampage was finally ended, even some boys went missing. However, this year, only several young girls got lost. Without a trace. Without a witness. It is as if the horned reaper himself took them away.

I don't know who killed Bishop Trevorius, Father. Although, no matter who the murderer was, I hope frankly to get my hands on him. I will use every scrap of my knowledge of the executioners art so his execution may last several days. I will break his limbs so artfully he will bleed very little. I'll pull the skin away from his body in such a way he won't faint from pain, not even once. I'll cut strips of flesh from him so that he...

Excuse me, Father, I was carried away by my emotions; it hasn't happened to me for a long time. I just wanted to say that I'm deeply sorry about what happened and I hope the murderer will be punished. No matter who it is!

It was such a large gray sack, Father. Long enough to hide a human body inside, if you get me. As soon as I saw it, I knew that something was very unpleasant about it. Who on earth would drag a dead body near the scaffold after dusk? So I hid in a nearby bush and tried very hard not to make a sound. Don't get me wrong, Father. I could oppose a bunch of bandits easily, but this was something else. It made my hair stand on end, although in fact I didn't know exactly why.

That's the problem, Father. I'd say Raimond Ventano was one of them but I'm not quite sure about that and also... it was dark and there was a heavy fog... but he was the only one who talked. I think I recognized him by his voice.
You're welcome, Father. I only hope I didn't cause any trouble to anyone by that. At the same time I didn't want to keep it for myself, if you get me...

Well... you may be right, Father. So... it concerns Istwan de Bragho. He was the royal vice-governor of the city many years ago but he wasn't a very good man. Well, in fact he was a true son of a bitch possessed by dark powers and he did things so terrible that peoples hair turned gray from the horror. He organized hunts for people, brought sacrifices to dark demons, bathed in the blood of non-baptized children... Simply the worst filth you can imagine but at the same time he was very clever. He never left any traces after his crimes, so no one could declare him guilty. He openly laughed at the authorities and boasted that they were no match for him. They were though. After several years of precise investigation, five paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous accused him of various crimes and proved him guilty at the trial. He was executed in quite a brutal way—quartering. Before he breathed his last breath he uttered a terrible curse saying he would come back from the Other World to take revenge on those who were behind his execution. Now, it seems that Bragho's curse really came true!
Don't you understand, Father? It was I whom executed Istwan de Bragho! Now I'm the next in his terrible afterlife revenge!

Of course! That's why I approached Judge Welfhar to ask him if he could do anything about that matter but nothing has happened since and I can't sleep in the night. My fear won't let me. Once it even seemed to me as if someone was walking around my house... I really fear for my life, Father! I fear that the revived body of Istwan de Bragho will come for me in the dark of night and take my soul to hell, as he did with all those paladins!
That would be very nice of you, Father. Really very nice.
Gladly, Father. What do you need to know?
Farewell, Father. Hurry, please. I don't think I'd like it if that bastard dragged me to a burning hell...
Offer? Do you mean a reward, Father? Are you not a cleric, who should help his neighbors without question? No offense, of course.
Although I am a priest, I'm not a mendicant. I'll gladly work for my alms. So?
I'm afraid I won't help you in this matter. I'm sure that Judge Welfhar will take care of it.
Sure, Father. What exactly are you interested in?

Sure, Father. What can I do for you?
That might be, Father. You're an Inquisitor and there's a lot of work here in Glatzburg. I'm sure we'll meet again.

You must do something about that, Father! This whole glorious Inquisition of yours has only one simple mission—to protect honest people from evil and hellspawns. You better hurry or you'll probably find me hanging by my own entrails by tomorrow!

People say that landsknecht Olfghard assassinated Natalia Reichmann. What do you think about it?
So, it will cost you $$getmoney10$$ gp.

I have also heard that, knight, but that's nonsense. Olfghard would never do such a thing. To tell the truth, he's hard enough to do that. He's experienced a lot and life was never very kind to him, believe me, but he would never do something so terrible like murdering a young girl. I've known him long enough to be able to say that.
I've heard that Bishop Quentinus is missing. Do you happen to know anything about it?
Maybe I do. It depends whether you would be willing to pay $$getmoney30$$ gp for it.

What you've heard is right. Bishop Quentinus disappeared that night when those devilish green skins attacked the town. They're said to get into the town due to treachery, but I don't know anything specific about it. Fortunately, the royal guard is constantly on standby these days or our throats would be cut in our sleep.
What has this to do with Bishop Quentinus?

I'm getting to that, knight. I was near the church when a scuffle burst out. I tried to get somewhere safe but the place was swarmed by green skins. I rather quickly climbed the wall of the church cemetery and stayed there. I saw a group of orcs burst into the church. Bishop Quentinus opposed them and killed quite a few before they had time to do something but there were too many of them for him to overcome. Even a priest as mighty as our Bishop was unable to defend himself. There were also those shamans they have, you know? They pulled him down to the ground with their unclean spells; stunned him and took him, tied, somewhere to the darkness.
You're said to be prowling around town taverns. Did you happen to see something unusual the night merchant Kurth Ollmier was murdered?
No, I don't remember. My memory doesn't serve me well, you know. But, maybe I would recall something for $$getmoney250$$ gp.

Well, in fact, I did see something. It was an awful night. It was snowing heavily and I was looking around for some place to hide myself. When I passed by the tavern, I spotted someone climbing out of the window where the guestrooms are located. I quickly hid myself not to let him see me—it's never good to catch someone doing something wrong and let him see you, after all.
Who was he? Did you recognize him?
Eh... no, knight, I didn't. It was too far away and it was dark.
You didn't help me much. I want my money back!

Calm down, knight, I'm not finished yet. When the person climbed down to the street, he wanted to escape quickly through an alley leading to the city walls. In that moment, a soldier whom I guess was Millward, came up from the dark. He was on guard that night and I was frankly surprised to see him trudging outside in such bad weather. In any case, he caught up to the person and was talking to him for a while. I can't say exactly about what, but as I know Millward, he probably wanted money. After some haggling they parted their ways and the person disappeared somewhere in the dark.
Well, that's much better. Thank you.
Where can I exchange some goods here in Hillbrandt?

What type of goods do you have in mind, knight? As for weapons and armor, you can buy them most expedient from the blacksmith Hammerhand. He's experienced in buying and selling of almost everything for a price. Also, he's not looking twice who he's trading with. He sells to the royal army, to the nobles, but also to persons of dubious nature. If you're interested in potions and spells, ask the herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt or Theil Brechthold, the astrologist. But, they're both quite temperamental and they even might simply deny dealing with you. In that case, go to Father Dominic. As for various goods of any origin and quality, you can go to Joseph Truthorn, the innkeeper, or to Susan Brauchner, the stall holder. They sell almost anything, but they don't have so much to choose from.

It's a disaster. I've never had so little alms as during the last few years. It's a misery. Someone should do something about that as soon as possible. If it continues the same way, I'll starve to death before long.

Yes, there is. Sheriff Contemburry will pay you a reward in gold when you bring him an orc trophy—either a scalp, or a head. To tell you the truth, I don't think the Duke's treasury will lose much money from these rewards.
I'm searching for the heretics here in Hillbrandt. Do you suspect anyone?
It will cost you $$getmoney35$$ gp.

To tell the truth, knight, I suspect Sam Riemann. Too often have I seen him returning home in the early morning hours. Where on earth could he be all night long? Most of all, why, knight? A decent man is at home in such a godless hour and doesn't show his face outdoors. He quietly walks through the dark, no matter what danger might lurk there. He's probably not afraid at all... which smells of infernal forces to me!
It will cost you $$getmoney10$$ gp.

So many bad things happened lately, knight, that I don't know what to tell you first. The orcs, murders, mysterious disappearances... What really makes me scared are those rumors about Bishop Herbertius. He was a former Hillbrandt Bishop, knight. People didn't say many good words about him during his life, you can believe me. He was said to sell his soul to Satan and that he received forbidden bodily pleasures in exchange. I don't know to what extent it was true, but what was true—young girls started to go missing. Later, boys of various ages as well. They were either never found, or their maimed bodies were found here and there. People whispered to each other that it weighed heavily on Bishop Herbertius' conscience. No matter what the truth was, the Bishop was found dead lying in his bed one day. He was said to have died naturally in his sleep, but I wouldn't believe that much. No matter how it really was, kidnappings and murders stopped. Time went on and all of that was mostly forgotten, until people started to whisper again during this spring that Bishop Herbertius returned from the Other World.
How could that be? What happened?

Town cemetery, knight. It seems like the dead left their graves and started to wander around. It's horrible! Bishop Herbertius is one of them. People say several witnesses saw him walking near the town! People are really scared about it and they think the Bishop returned from the Other World to uphold his part of the pact with Satan. Several people disappeared without a trace, that's true, but I'm not sure if it was the work of undead Bishop Herbertius.
The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen from the town church, do you happen to know anything about it?

One thing I know for sure—I didn't steal it. According to the rumors I've heard, it had to be someone who knows a lot about witchcraft. Those clerics who prayed that night for the redemption of mankind were found sleeping on the floor in the morning—at least people say so. It took some time to wake them up. There were dark spells for sure, believe me, knight. The Monstrance was away. Without it, the city didn't have a proper defense any more. If the Monstrance was where it belonged, the orcs would have never been able to get inside!
Perhaps. It will cost you $$getmoney15$$ gp.

To tell the truth, knight, I don't know much about the disappearance of Paul Hammerhand. I'd say he ran again—like many times before, after all. Try asking Ruphert the shepherd. They were close friends. He surely will know where Paul is or where he could be.
Perhaps. It will cost you $$getmoney20$$ gp.

Baroness Linda van Gallagan disappeared the same night Bishop Quentinus disappeared—during the attack of the green skins. If I were you, knight, I'd ask the guards. Maybe they noticed orcs drawing her away from the city. It's the only possible explanation. The orcs kidnapped her, I mean. I don't even want to think what unrighteous things can happen to a young woman among those monsters. What do you think, knight?!
It seems the soldier Jullian probably deserted. Do you happen to know where he could be hiding?

It's hard to say, knight. He can be anywhere. Maybe on the way to Glatzburg or anywhere else. However, in case he's still somewhere around Hillbrandt he will need lodging. Thus, if I were looking for him, I'd go through the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains—he could be hiding in some abandoned shepherd's chalet.
Perhaps. It will cost you $$getmoney10$$ gp.

I've heard the legend about King Harlior, the last King of the pagan Thron empire that was situated at the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains a very long time ago. When the Empire was attacked by the armies of Orc Emperor Rashgar and stood at the edge of obliteration, Harlior declared before the last battle that he wouldn't leave his land as long as emperor Rashgar was threatening it. The Thron armies lost that battle and Harlior himself was killed. His oath became his curse and since then the ghost of the King has been staying there waiting for somebody to save him. According to the old miners from the iron mines a man was able to hear his thundering voice full of anger from time to time in the heart of the mountains. The legends say that the one who succeeds in setting him free will get his entire treasury as a reward.

Duke Weinberg rules Hillbrandt and the surrounding domains as the royal governor of the town. Baron Robert van Gallagan is the royal vice-governor. Duke Weinberg is a typical representative of high aristocracy, but unlike the others, he doesn't have the brains of a mouse. Sadly, I can't say the same about Baron van Gallagan, who is so stupid that it hurts. In fact, his wife Linda rules in his stead.
Alms, knight. Don't let a lame beggar die from hunger. Alms, please.
I won't give you any money. Rather tell me your name so I know who I am talking with!
Unfortunately I don't remember my name any more, knight. I never used it much. Everyone calls me Flitz.
But of course, knight. For a little gold I'll tell you everything you want.
Here you are, take this, good man.
Thank you, valiant knight, thank you a hundred thousand times!
You're welcome. After all, it's my duty to split my money with a neighbor in need. What's your name?
Unfortunately I don't remember my name any more, knight. I never used it much. One and all call me Flitz.
Hail to you, sir knight. What can an old, lame beggar do for you?
But of course, knight.

I have also heard that, Father, but that's nonsense. Olfghard would never do such a thing. To tell the truth, he's hard enough to do that. He's experienced a lot and life was never very kind to him, believe me, but he would never do something so terrible like murdering a young girl. I've known him long enough to be able to say that.

I'm getting to that, Father. I was near the church when a scuffle burst out. I tried to get somewhere safe but the place was swarmed by green skins. I rather quickly climbed the wall of the church cemetery and stayed there. I saw a group of orcs burst into the church. Bishop Quentinus opposed them and killed quite a few before they had time to do something but there were too many of them for him to overcome. Even a priest as mighty as our Bishop was unable to defend himself. There were also those shamans they have, you know? They pulled him down to the ground with their unclean spells; stunned him and took him, tied, somewhere to the darkness.
Eh... no, Father, I didn't. It was too far away and it was dark.

Calm down, Father, I'm not finished yet. When the person climbed down to the street, he wanted to escape quickly through an alley leading to the city walls. In that moment, a soldier whom I guess was Millward, came up from the dark. He was on guard that night and I was frankly surprised to see him trudging outside in such bad weather. In any case, he caught up to the person and was talking to him for a while. I can't say exactly about what, but as I know Millward, he probably wanted money. After some haggling they parted their ways and the person disappeared somewhere in the dark.

What type of goods do you have in mind, Father? As for weapons and armor, you can buy them most expedient from the blacksmith Hammerhand. He's experienced in buying and selling of almost everything for a price. Also, he's not looking twice who he's trading with. He sells to the royal army, to the nobles, but also to persons of dubious nature. If you're interested in potions and spells, ask the herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt or Theil Brechthold, the astrologist. But, they're both quite temperamental and they even might simply deny dealing with you. In that case, go to Father Dominic. As for various goods of any origin and quality, you can go to Joseph Truthorn, the innkeeper, or to Susan Brauchner, the stall holder. They sell almost anything, but they don't have so much to choose from.

To tell the truth, Father, I suspect Sam Riemann. Too often have I seen him returning home in the early morning hours. Where on earth could he be all night long? Most of all, why, Father? A decent man is at home in such a godless hour and doesn't show his face outdoors. He quietly walks through the dark, no matter what danger might lurk there. He's probably not afraid at all... which smells of infernal forces to me!

So many bad things happened lately, Father, that I don't know what to tell you first. The orcs, murders, mysterious disappearances... What really makes me scared are those rumors about Bishop Herbertius. He was a former Hillbrandt Bishop, Father. People didn't say many good words about him during his life, you can believe me. He was said to sell his soul to Satan and that he received forbidden bodily pleasures in exchange. I don't know to what extent it was true, but what was true—young girls started to go missing. Later, boys of various ages as well. They were either never found, or their maimed bodies were found here and there. People whispered to each other that it weighed heavily on Bishop Herbertius' conscience. No matter what the truth was, the Bishop was found dead lying in his bed one day. He was said to have died naturally in his sleep, but I wouldn't believe that much. No matter how it really was, kidnappings and murders stopped. Time went on and all of that was mostly forgotten, until people started to whisper again during this spring that Bishop Herbertius returned from the Other World.

Town cemetery, Father. It seems like the dead left their graves and started to wander around. It's horrible! Bishop Herbertius is one of them. People say several witnesses saw him walking near the town! People are really scared about it and they think the Bishop returned from the Other World to uphold his part of the pact with Satan. Several people disappeared without a trace, that's true, but I'm not sure if it was the work of undead Bishop Herbertius.

But of course, noble lord.
What was your relationship with Hans Falkner? Suzan Brauchner thinks you were lovers. Is it true?
That mangy bitch! How could she dare to slander me like this? I'll gouge the harlot as soon as I meet her...

Oh, sorry, knight, I let my feelings get the better of me. The harlot uses such slanders to take revenge on me, for I took a lover from her several years ago. I've nothing to do with that murderer Falkner. It's good they executed him. Something should be done also with that wanton Brauchner. She shouldn't be allowed to slander decent people like this!
Where can I buy some goods here in Hillbrandt?

Do you want to do some shopping? Go to the local blacksmith, Hammerhand—if weapons and armor are what you want. You can get magic items from Würtenrodt the herbalist, Brechthold the astrologist or from Father Dominic. Truthorn the innkeeper and Brauchner the stall holder have all sorts of goods for various prices.
I don't know much about the crisis, knight. I'm just a simple maid. It must be a terrible disaster, because the Duke seems to be very troubled.
I'm afraid I don't know any heretics, knight. I'm sorry.
Has something unusual happened here in Hillbrandt lately?
Bishop Quentinus disappeared during that terrible attack of the orcs at the town. I'm so sorry to hear it. He was a very good man!
Master Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of heresy. What do you think about it?

I've heard that Master Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of letting the orcs into the town before their recent attack, but I can't tell for sure. I was locked in my room the whole evening. I didn't see anyone.
I'm afraid I haven't the slightest idea what might have happened to poor Baroness Linda van Gallagan. I hope she will be all right.
I'm convinced that Olfghard really killed poor Natalia. He was found with her jewelry on him, after all. He must have robbed and murdered her somewhere. May they catch him soon and execute him!

People say that there is a piece of rock near the scaffold, called Death Stone. The lament of the tortured souls of the sinners struck by divine justice for their terrible deeds is said to be heard from the stone.

I don't know anything about the murder of Kurth Ollmier, knight. Only that it happened in the attic of Truthorn's tavern, where the merchant had a room rented. People say some lecherous succubus killed him because he was found with his own... well... limb in his mouth.
If I'm single? Yes, I'm single... and single I will stay, knight. I don't know what you want to propose to me, but whatever it is, I can tell you in advance that you're trying in vain.
Duke Weinberg rules in Hillbrandt as the Royal Governor of the town. Baron Robert van Gallagan is the royal vice-governor, although the one who makes decisions is in fact his wife Linda...
Answer me, good woman. I wouldn't like to force your cooperation. But if you won't give me any other option...
I ask you frankly, good woman, to answer my question.
I must admit I'm very pleased to speak with someone as beautiful and clever as you. Thus, could you please answer my question?
Lotti Frankmüller, I'm taking you into custody for a well-grounded suspicion of the attempt to murder Friedrich Raubsticht. You will come with me.
I'm arrested? But how could it be so... It must be some kind of mistake. I haven't done any harm to Master Raubsticht, after all.

Raubsticht the Executioner was cursed by somebody. I have a reason to think it was you. Suzan Brauchner testified she caught you with Hans Falkner. You were lovers. Thus, you have a reason to hate the executioner, as it was he whom executed your lover.

So you did find out? That surprises me quite a lot. I mean, usually you look like you're putting two and two together to get five. Yes, I cursed that bastard. He deserved that. He executed Hans, my only true love. Nobody could understand Hans, only I. They all thought he was just a pervert and murderer, but I loved him. Nobody can return him to me. But at least I was able to take my revenge. The executioner will die—you can rely on it! And you won't keep me from doing that, because I'll kill you! Summorium dathmorum morseth via porthor unghoth!!!
Hail to you, good woman.
Hello, knight. Welcome to the house of Duke Weinberg. I'm Lotti Frankmüller, his maid. What can I do for you?
You look a bit sad, has anything bad happened to you?
Pardon? No, I'm all right. And leave me alone, do you understand?! Mind your own business!
Well, excuse me, it's not my business of course. Farewell.
Be careful, girl. You won't talk to me like that. Do you know who I am?!
I... I'm sorry. I had no right to shout at you like that. It's because of those hard times weighing on us so heavily. Let us hope that good times will return soon.
That's right. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Talk to me? You? About what? I don't know much.
I'm sorry. I just wanted to help.

No, no need to excuse yourself, knight, that's alright. Everything is all right. It's just those hard times weighing on us so heavily, nothing else, knight. That's the reason I might look sad to you. It's nothing personal. Let us hope that good times will return soon. All that ruination, all that disaster... they're taking a cruel toll on us.
You're right. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Talk to me? About what? I don't know much...
You're right. Maybe all will turn to the good. Farewell.
I came to see the Duke.

He's been very busy lately, but I'm sure he'll see you. It's too much for him. All those disasters that happened here during the last years turned life here in Hillbrandt into a true hell. The Duke does as much as he can though.
Hello, knight. It's nice of you to visit us again. How do you do?
As you wish, but I don't know much...
Could be better. Farewell.

Who disturbs me from my eternal sleep? Who doesn't allow the dead to sleep?
God Almighty, what forces of hell brought the body of this priest back from the Other World?! Cease and desist, you unclean abomination, and let this body resume its rest in the sarcophagus!
Forgive me, poor soul, I didn't want to disturb your eternal sleep!
I didn't want to disturb your eternal sleep, Father Frederick. I only needed your diary!
Wait, poor lost soul. If you are Father Frederick, I ask you to forgive me the desecration of your sarcophagus. I had no other choice, after all! Please listen to me!
Hello, valiant knight. How do you do? I see you came for a walk with a beautiful young lady. She's so very young... I'm sure she is also innocent yet, isn't she?!

Well... I'd rather say that's none of your business, valiant knight. But all right, I'll tell you. All the people here call me Fritz. Now can you tell me what the name of the maiden traveling with you is?
Don't mind that girl, good man. I assure you that it's not your business whether she's innocent or not.

I'd say it is, knight. I must tell you I like her very much. So, I will probably take her—at least for some time, before I get bored with her. I'll play with her, pretty much to let her know a real man. You lead her to the monastery anyway, so let her have some fun, what do you think?
I'm afraid I can't satisfy your claim. Excuse us for now, we're in a hurry.
No way, knight. I told you I want that whore, so I'll get her, too. And you better get out of my sight quickly, unless you want to taste the blood from that knightly nose of yours!
I think your manners need some improvement, good man. Your threat lead me to an idea how to do so!
I'm sorry, but I definitely can't give you the girl. Farewell!
In that case I'll take her myself—and I'll beat your face to a pulp at the same time!
Behave yourself, neighbor, or I'll teach you good manners!
No way, knight. You're not telling me how to behave. It seems to me that you need a lesson—I'll teach you one—gladly. At the same time I'll take the young lady who is here with you!

What are you talking about? What help for a neighbor do you have in mind?

I'm talking about our brother in arms, Minfred von Siegel. He was a devoted servant of God who, as well as all of us, was going every day to fight against the hellspawns scourging our homeland. He was a firm pillar of faith and a faithful defender of the Realm. But, something happened to him. Something that none of us are able to understand...
How can it be? What happened?

One day he attacked and killed several innocent people in an unexpected fit of rage. It happened during the daytime, just a few days after he had returned from a long-time quest to seek and destroy the settlement of an ancient evil somewhere in Schwarzwald. After his act of insanity he immediately fled from the city and since then he has been strolling aimlessly around Alvaron and killing everyone he meets. None of us knows what had happened to him, but we would like to help him. However, our investigation led us nowhere. That is why we came to ask the Holy Office, but we were told that the paladin would be immediately executed in case he is caught alive. And we won't allow that!
What do you want to do? Do you think there's a hope of saving that man?

I firmly believe there is, brother. He was our fellow warrior for many years—we supported each other and went through many bloody battles together. Thus, I'm not going to leave him in time of his greatest need—although he probably doesn't realize he needs help. I want to help him, release him from the powers that made him to do such terrible deeds and then let him decide on his own what he will do with his future...
I'll try to help you, brother. What do you ask from me?

If you really want to help me, brother, find Minfred von Siegel and try to bring him back to reason. I don't know if it's possible, but try to do it. We must find him before someone else catches him and either kills him or hands him to the Inquisition!
All right, I'll try to find a way to show Minfred von Siegel reason.
Thank you, brother!
You're welcome—it's my duty.
Yes, I've noticed that. I'll pray to the Archangel Gabriel for your early return.
Why are you so sure that you will be able to bring your brother in arms to reason?
I'm not sure, of course, but I must try!
What will you give me for my help?
I hope you are joking, brother!
The man is lost, brother. I'm not going to risk my life to bring a killing maniac to reason!
Then we are getting back to that matter of helping a neighbor in the time of need. I'm very disappointed by your attitude. You're a selfish and ignorant utilitarian, nothing more. Farewell!
Death is the only thing the heretic deserves. He killed several innocent people, after all!
I thought you would answer otherwise, brother. But I was mistaken in you. Farewell!
I bring bad news, brother—I killed paladin Minfred von Siegel. It was self-defense. He attacked me. Apparently he was mad...
What?! Minfred is dead?! Oh my God... I tried to help him all this time! This is not fair—decay comes to places where people struggle to otherwise prevent it! This is not fair...
Justice is a privilege of our Lord God, brother. I'm sorry about that, but there was nothing else I could do.
I understand, brother. It will be better for both of us if you go away now and leave me alone with my sorrow...
All right, but first I'd like to ask you several questions.
As I've said, brother—you better go away now and leave me alone with my sorrow...
As you wish. Farewell.

What an awful item... I can almost smell spilled blood from its aura. It pains me when I realize this thing has caused death to so many innocent people. Now it's important to destroy the devil's work. Thank you, brother—for all you have done for me.
I'm glad to have helped you, brother.
