You better not say such things and destroy the chain—it's cursed!

Oh yes, sure... I must destroy it... but after all... maybe the curse can be broken somehow? The First Prophet was said to cure deadly diseases with the power of his mind and to return sight to people. Why couldn't I break the dark power of this item? I'll put it on and I'll take control over it. It will commit good, to atone for all the evil it ever committed!
Don't do it, brother. Destroy the item—IMMEDIATELY!
No, brother, I'm not going to destroy it. On the contrary, I'll put it around my neck. Like this, as you can see!
Oh my God...

What happened...?! I can see some red fog around me... but at the same time I'm feeling so relaxed... As if I were released from shackles weighing me down until now. I'm so... strong! I feel so... powerful. Yes, I'm so strong and powerful I could kill a man with a single blow. Yes, I must kill all. KILL THEM ALL!!!

You did a reasonable thing, brother. I'm frankly glad the thing didn't get into my hands. Who knows how many deaths the thing had on its conscience? I'm glad it all ended like this... although I'm sorry for the death of Minfred von Siegel. Thank you, brother—for all you have done for me.
I'm glad to help you, brother. Farewell.
Welcome, brother. What do you ask of Commander Hector de Froix?
Nice to meet you, brother.

You won't speak with me that way, brother!

I don't understand? What happened? Where is Minfred?

The misfortune of your brother in arms was caused by an ancient cursed chain Minfred put on his neck due to lack of caution. Beyond doubt it's bewitched by fearsome dark spells...

In that case give it to me immediately, brother. It must be destroyed today at once!
Here it is.
I destroyed the chain, brother. I didn't want anyone else to be exposed to the temptation to put it on...
I don't have the chain with me.
In that case you must bring it to me as soon as possible, brother. We mustn't allow it to commit any more evil!
All right, I'll bring it to you.
That's not important—it won't return Minfred his life...
You're right, brother. I'm deeply sorry it had to end like this. I wanted so much to help Minfred... However, thank you very much, brother. You did all you could do. I'll never forget that!
I understand. I didn't run into Minfred. Let's hope we'll do better in the future.
Go away, brother!
One moment, I need to talk to you!
But I don't need to talk to you. Farewell, and don't try to persuade, urge or threaten me—I'm not going to exchange even one word with you!
As you wish... goodbye!
Thank you for your help, brother. I'm deeply sorry for the death of our brother Minfred von Siegel, but his was the fate of most warriors.
I'll pray for the salvation of his soul, brother. Farewell.
Do you bring me that cursed chain which turned brother Minfred von Siegel into a killing beast, brother?
Yes, here it is.
Unfortunately, I haven't brought it yet.

In the place that awful crime was committed, of course. We didn't dare to even touch the statue, not to let the deadly sin stain us!

Do as you think, brother. I was hopping you would stay here and oversee the trial, but never mind. God be with you!
What? What do you mean by that? This ungodly harlot bewitched our fellow Richwald d'Blazier, after all, and turned him into stone! How could she be innocent? She deserves death!

On the basis of presented proofs she confessed that she cursed Paladin Richwald d'Blazier for resisting her infernal temptation and for refusing to become her lover!

I'll do penance!

...and then the First Prophet said: The one who committed a sin and disorderly insisted upon his heresy shall be stricken by the Punishment of God and the Wrath of Heaven shall fall down on his head! Because of that we, brothers, the protectors of justice by the Will of God, are now judging this woman called Corin for the sins she committed. For that terrible disgrace and lecherousness that dwell in her soul and... what? Who are you, sir? What do you need? Why are you interfering with this trial?

No need to apologize, you're a noble and so your mission is similar to ours... in a way. Please take part in this trial as an independent witness. At least you can testify the horror and nastiness of this bitch's heresy...
Is that you, sir? What do you need? To tell the truth I don't have much time for you as I must put my mind into the trial with the accused witch Corin.
I'm sorry, sir, but there's really no time for that. The trial must be held as soon as possible, as punishment of the evil must be swift and just.

You've decided to defend the witch?! Against the servants of God? That's betrayal! What a hellishness! My fist is grasping the hilt of my sword when I hear such words from the mouth of an ordinary noble! We are the Justice, we are the Law! But as you wish, gather the proofs of her innocence as long as you want—the girl will be hanged, because she's a heretic! And now get away from here, you better go and gather some proofs!
God be with you, sir.

Is that you, sir? That witch's advocate? So what proofs did you gather about the innocence of that hellish fornicatrix? I doubt you ran into any, because that Satan's whore is guilty without any doubt!

I've heard certain rumors about one of our former brothers in the Order, Master. His name is Henry de Montreaux and it seems he's killing whoever he meets around Glatzburg. What can you tell me about him?

Henry de Montreaux, you said? Yes, it's really a terrible case... I'd never think such madness was hidden in his mind. I accepted him into the Order myself and I was the one who named him paladin. He was an excellent swordsman. The best of all of us, in my opinion. Nobody was a match for him. I supposed he would be a really firm supporter of our local chapter. I don't know what went wrong with him. Suddenly, he started to behave like a madman. He started challenging his brothers and killed anybody who stood against him. He was expelled from the Order for that. He's been wandering around Glatzburg since then and whoever he meets, he challenges him and kills him. Me and my brothers have been searching for him, but our search has been fruitless so far.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of Glatzburg. Nobles from the Heidrick House have been named the royal governors of the city for many generations already—it nearly became a hereditary title, although it could be given to someone other land holder, of course. Rowan van Leerin is the royal vice-governor—he was named to the office eight years ago and he's been trying to get higher since then. But he doesn't seem to have enough political power to eliminate the Grand Duke. However, one never knows in politics...

What do I think about the current crisis? It depends on which crisis you have in mind, brother—the one of the clergy or the one concerning power? The clergy crisis is very bad, but I'm sure it's only the beginning of the real crisis which is purely power-related. Of course I'm devotedly faithful and the Law of God is above all for me, but I can't avoid the feeling that power is the most important thing here. Of course there are all those signs St. Ezechiel described in his Apocalypse around, but it only created the hub for the conflict of powers—not that I'd like to spread rebellious or maybe even heretic opinions.
And what exactly do you mean?

Can't you see it, brother? The Inquisition is haggling with the Brotherhood of the Righteous for the jurisdiction and competence, the nobles scream they want more rights because royal power is falling away, and the struggle concerns common people as well, though they are immediately inclined to the "End of the World" idea. However, it's possible the Day of Judgment is really coming soon, it's possible that Satan will be released from his jail and the Final Judgment will be done.
I've heard some rumors about the war being about to begin. Do you happen to know anything about that?

I've heard some rumors about the war too, brother. And because the mission of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is closer to the warrior issues than to anything else, I can put two and two together. Yes, it really seems to me that the war is about to start. And I even have a certain suspicion against which opponent the war should be waged. But because of the fact it could be considered treason—not to mention heresy—I'd rather keep it for myself. For the sake of safety, brother. Both my and yours safety.
You can open your heart about your suspicion to me, Master. I won't breathe a word of it.
I'm sorry, brother, but that's not possible. The theory is too outrageous and unsubstantiated at the same time—I can only guess. I'm sorry. There's nothing personal in it.
Tell me about it, Master. Now!
What monsters and hellspawns can people find here in Glatzburg and around?

I'm glad to hear you're interested in the opponents you may face in Glatzburg, like a good paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous should be. It's always a good idea to get to know opponents before you meet them. If you travel any of the royal or country roads, you will surely run into some robber baron and his minions. They're a great trouble for the whole city, as both the trade and the transport stagnate. Deeper in the woods you can find those horned beasts from the Devil's Caverns. Some call them devils, but personally I'd say they're some kind of lizards walking upright like people. Though they are bloodthirsty and very dangerous. Beware of the living dead in the city after dusk—they appear in the streets and kill anybody they meet. There are also a lot of them in the cemetery. Only a few dead bodies remained lying in their graves when the Scourges of God stroke the Realm...

Grand Duke Heidrick set some rewards for the brigands pestering the roads. He did so thinking it will help to get rid of them. But it doesn't seem to help at all. However, if you were as lucky as to do away with a brigand in the course of your holy mission, Sheriff Smith will pay you some gold as a reward. If a modest and humble servant of God is taking any rewards at all, of course.

So, you're asking me if I suspect anybody of heresy. Well... maybe I do and maybe I don't. In any case I'm not going to open my heart to you about it at the moment. And don't try to persuade me, it would be useless.
I've already told you about my suspicion, brother. That thing about the secret meeting of cardinal Truncquillius in the Bishop's Garden. I don't know anything else.
Do you happen to know anything about the cult of Children of the New Order, Master?

I do know something about the cult of the Children of the New Order. If I remember it well, it was a rather numerous and quickly spreading cult of the demon-invocators that was created in the Empire during the restless times at the end of the tenth century. The cult was founded by a self-appointed Dark Prophet named Lucius who foretold the End of the World and the release of Satan from his one thousand years imprisonment. Soon the cult found some members also among the gentry and nobles and then it became a really dangerous movement, which was a hard nut to crack for the Inquisition. Fortunately for Ultherst the cult of the Children of the New Order didn't spread into the other faithful countries and because of that we were spared from the grim raging of the Holy Office. What came to pass in the end was what had to come to pass—all members of the cult were caught and executed, including the members of the Emperor's family. Several hundred heretics were burned in the Emperor's Square in Bonorium in 1021. And that was the end of the cult of the Children of the New Order.
So you think the cult doesn't exist nowadays? You think it didn't have any followers who escaped from the Pope's Inquisition?

Yes, that's exactly what I think. The Pope's Inquisition is very precise, as you yourself must know very well. They don't hesitate to extirpate the seed of heresy together with the lump of healthy ground, if you understand me. They act according to the principle that in the case an innocent man is executed, God will take care of his soul. Thus, I firmly believe the Children of the New Order belong to the past, as well as many other cults of those times. Several hundred years have passed since, after all. And if I can give you some advice, you better pay attention to the groups existing nowadays that are much more dangerous for our Realm than some long time abandoned cult.

It's worth mentioning that Tinthan the actor was—and I'm very glad he was—accused at least of theft and will be hanged. That is, he stole a golden monstrance in the Bishop's Cathedral. There are witnesses. He was able to escape from the city, but I'll find him anyway! I've been longing to punish him for several years already, but the bastard just kept laughing in my face. But now he made a fatal mistake. He was pretending to be a great artist, a renowned wandering actor, but the only thing he was very good at was crime. Thefts, burglaries and many other things. I believe I could prove he also committed some murder or robbery, if I could push him to the rack. But you will see that when I catch him!

Unfortunately I don't know much about the murder of poor Bishop Trevorius. I've heard he was found near the Grand Duke's gazebo, nobody comes there these days. I wonder what he was doing there. From first view it looks like the brigands killed him, but things may not be what they seem to be at all.

I'm not surprised you're asking me about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. That is to say, you yourself are a suspect and now you must find the murderer at all cost, or the case will turn against you. And who will be interested in innocence, if you yourself confess you committed the murder? After a long and painful torture, of course. But I hope it won't come to that, it would be a shame—or I think it would. Unfortunately I won't help you with that case, because I don't know much about it. Only that Bishop Trevorius was murdered near the abandoned Grand Duke's gazebo. But you should know that better than me...
I'm looking for the burial chamber of an Elenian noble named Fae'Darlion. Do you happen to know where it could be located?

I've heard that quite a large number of ancient relics are located in the woods around von Hunth's mansion. I rode through that country many times and I can say that from time to time I ran into the ruins of stone buildings much older than the Erebornian ones you can see everywhere around. I suppose those ruins are from that Elenian civilization, no matter who the Elenians were. So if you really want to find that burial chamber you talked about and you know for sure it is located somewhere near Glatzburg, try to search in the woods around von Hunth's mansion.

I don't know much about Father Frederick, although he lived here for several years before the Black Death killed him. He was an old crazy strange man, it's quite possible he wasn't right in the head in his old age. But people said he used to be a successful exorcist, expeller of Satan. Reputedly he implemented several dozen successful exorcisms... But he didn't perform any of them here in Glatzburg. I think it was not so great with those exorcisms—I don't want to do him injustice, but I've personally met several false exorcists of Satan, who became very famous this way without banishing any evil ghost even once.

I've found out that Istwan de Bragho came out of his grave to take revenge on those who caused his apprehension and execution. And it seems he's immortal. Do you happen to have any good advice for me?

Did Istwan de Bragho really come back from the Other World? I never thought about it... If it is as you say, I certainly wouldn't get in his way, brother. A curse is no fun at all, especially when it brings the dead back to life. If weapons and spells don't do any harm to him I can't imagine any other way to get rid of him other than to let him finish his posthumous revenge! And God will surely take care of the souls of his victims.

The Fallen Angels are the minions of Satan and the most powerful demons who have ever lived in Hell. Sources other than the Scriptures mention them, thus we can expect they were known already in pagan times. They impersonate the antithesis of God Almighty, just as darkness is the opposite of light. There're four of them: Arthamon, the Master of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Mistress of Fornication and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the first of the servants of Satan. Each of the Fallen Angels controls one of the Chaos elements—destruction, madness and lechery. Since the Dawn of Time, when they were thrown down from the sky together with Satan for the crimes they committed, they've been imprisoned in Hell. Only their lesser servants can get into our world directly, but they can affect our world with their power, by affecting human minds—and this is the way that sin and misdemeanor come into this world. And they are very successful in their effort! Tell me frankly, brother—do you think there has been any lack of destruction, madness and of lechery in the world in recent years?
Do you think the Fallen Angels can get to our world on their own? That the heretics can invoke them?

No, I don't think so. It's written in the Scriptures that none of the Fallen Angels will come back to our world as long as the people will believe in God Almighty. True faith prevents the powers of Hell from making God's Kingdom on Earth their domain.
What can you tell me about the undead who kill people in the streets of the city during night?

There's only one thing I can tell you about the undead, brother—they're a really awful lot. When the hellspawns were kept at bay behind the city walls, the situation wasn't so bad. That is to say, people were scared and depressed, but still there was no threat to their lives. Thus, when the undead started to show themselves in the streets of Glatzburg after dusk, people panicked at once and the city started to look a lot like a Black Death village. I've met those living dead personally several times and I cut them with my men like barley, but if you meet the same ones every day—well, every night in fact—you will lose your vim quite soon. So they walk the streets mostly unpunished these days...
And from where do these undead come really?

That's a good question, brother. I racked my brain about it too and I have a suspicion it's somehow related to those tales about the ancient underground sewers that should be probably located under the city. It's possible the sewers really exist—that they weren't filled up as the sources from the beginnings of the city history say—and that the undead settled down there. But it's just my opinion. In addition to that I haven't found one entrance which could be used to get into those sewers.
Somebody stole the Chain of the Brotherhood from the commander Ethiene de Pasque. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Commander Ethiene de Pasque lost his Chain of the Brotherhood? Well, that's very bad for him. As you must know, symbols of our rank are counted among the relics in our Brotherhood, because they were anointed by the Grand Master of the Order himself in the name of the First Prophet and of the Archangel Gabriel. Commander de Pasque will now have to make a great effort to get his chain back—and to get back his honor at the same time. However, if you're going to help him in his effort, brother, ask Tinthan the actor first of all whether he doesn't know anything about it. Because when something disappears without anybody noticing it, Tinthan usually has a hand in it!
I'm looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Do you happen to know where it could be located? Bonhart is said to have hidden it somewhere before he left for the war...

You're not the first and neither the last who's looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. And the one who finds it will get very, very rich. Because if only a half of what people say about the hammer is true, a nifty blacksmith would be able to make real wonders with it. But first someone would have to find it. Bonhart is said to have buried the hammer somewhere—just before he went to the Barbarian wars in 977 when the land was attacked. But he took the knowledge of where he hid it with him to the grave. Some people say he hid it somewhere at the scaffold, then others declare it must be buried at some place near the Devil's Caverns. Who can say where it really is?
If you really want to know that, brother, it will cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
If you won't answer my question, Master, I'll have to enforce your cooperation with the use of very unpleasant methods!
You're the Master of the knightly Order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Because of that I believe you'll take your principles into account and answer my question.
You're a wise and deliberate man, Master, I saw that the moment we met. Thus I wonder if you wouldn't give one answer to someone like me.

Sure, brother. I don't know whether you've already familiarized yourself with the situation in Glatzburg, but I can assure you that the situation is serious, although it doesn't look like that at first sight. I feel brimstone is boiling and the smoke of hell is fuming under this quite and calm surface. Since the Scourges of God struck, people are different, very different. They either lock themselves inside their houses, as if the stone walls could protect them from what did affect the Realm, or... the others... they treacherously hatch plots and serve the idols in an attempt to save themselves from the coming End of the World. You wouldn't believe what people are able to commit. As if they went totally mad.
I can agree with that. But what's the matter, Master?

I'm getting to the point. As I've already said, we've faced many terrible crimes here in Glatzburg since the Scourges of God struck. But I assure you, brother, that it's not the same here as in Hillbrandt. No matter what you have met there, it's one hundred times worse here in Glatzburg. Hillbrandt is situated in a wild area far in the north of the Realm and people there are ruder and simpler since their birth—no offense intended. On the other hand, Glatzburg is the second largest city in the Realm! Deadly intrigues, falsehood and dissimulation rule here. Crime is much more sophisticated; our criminals are more dangerous and cunning.
Yes, that's probably true. But what does it have to do with me?

I was just about to explain it to you. Several girls went missing in Glatzburg and around not long before your arrival. Very young girls, to be exact. They disappeared without a trace and nobody has heard of them since. You can imagine what upheaval this unfortunate event caused among the people. They immediately started talking about a heretic cult rooted deeply in the Glatzburg community. Members of the cult were said to drink the blood of innocent virgins during the night. Simply said—panic is rising through the city which is rather undesirable at the moment. Can you imagine the bloodshed if the people went out to the streets? Because of that my superiors from the Alvaron Chapter believe that it's necessary to get the situation under control as soon as possible at all costs. They think that it's necessary to find out the wrong-doer in a short time and to deliver him to justice.
I think I get your meaning, Master. You want me to find the kidnapper, don't you?

Yes, brother, you are right. I'm confident a man like you will have the best opportunity to find out how the things really are without attracting too much undesirable attention. Thus I decided to wait for your arrival when the Hillbrandt Chapter notified me that you were coming. I want you to clear up those mysterious disappearances of several young girls I told you about. Gather affirmative proofs and present them to me.
Pardon me?! You want me to give the results of my investigation over to you? But it would look like as if you revealed those crimes...

Yes, exactly. If you've mentioned it, I won't withhold it from you—it wouldn't make sense. My heart craves to present this case—if successfully solved, of course—as my own success. Thanks to that the door of the Main Chapter of our Order in Alvaron, the capital of our Realm, would be opened to me. Probably I would be promoted to the Seneschal of Order, and it does mean everything for me at the moment! Understand, brother—I have nowhere to rise here in Glatzburg. And thus my only chance of getting a better position is to solve this case which is under the solicitous scrutiny of my superiors.
I can't believe my own ears. You want to buy your own promotion from me? What kind of man are you? Where are your moral principles and your Code of the Knight? This is a nasty barter!

Call it as you want, but it's a fair trade. And please leave my personal qualities and my conscience to someone more qualified—that is, to myself. They're not your business. In any case you'd better realize that you can't lose in this bargain. Be sure about that! As I told you at the beginning, this little trade between us will bring you a great reward. It's linked to your investigation... To tell the truth, I'm not completely sure what the reason of your coming to Glatzburg is, but I believe it has something to do with the Hillbrandt case. You're probably searching for the accomplices of Judge Vallarian or something like that. In that case I assure you that I have certain information which would make your investigation much easier. In other words—I have straight convincing evidence against one person here in Glatzburg that is almost drowning in heresy. I'm sure that convicting that person would mean another great jump in your career.

You seem to be a very ambitious man, Master. There's nothing bad about it—only a dumb man wouldn't use the possibility if he were in your situation. There's only one question about it—what's in it for me?

I'm glad you take it like this, brother. You can't lose in this bargain, be sure about that! As I told you in the beginning, this little trade between us will bring you great reward. It's linked to your investigation... To tell the truth, I'm not totally sure what is the reason of your coming to Glatzburg, but I believe it has some connection to your Hillbrandt case. You're probably searching for the accomplices of judge Vallarian's murder or something like that. In that case I assure you that I have certain information which would make your investigation much easier. In other words—I have straight convincing evidence against one person here in Glatzburg that is nearly drown in heresy. I'm sure that convicting that person would mean another great jump in your career.

That, of course, I'm not going to tell you, brother. At least, not now. First I want to hear the name of those girls' kidnapper and to have evidence against him in my hands. Then of course I'll testify to you all that I witnessed some time ago.
Withholding information borders with heresy these days, Master. If you have any proofs that could lead to proving a heretic guilty, give them to me immediately!

No, brother, I'm sorry. If you would like to take it like this, let's pretend our dialogue never happened. However I believe you will change your attitude. Believe me—the information would be more than interesting for you!
Why don't you use that information to blame that person of heresy yourself? Surely it would help your career as well...

Not necessarily, brother. You surely know that to mess up with the things of the Inquisition is quite a risky matter even for the Brotherhood of the Righteous. And in addition to that—I'm not sure how my superiors would react to the fact I lead the investigation against that person! It's a politically sensitive matter. Therefore I think it would be more suitable for you to manage. Just find out who had kidnapped the girls and gather enough evidence and testimonies against him so that he can be put on trial.
Your proposition sounds interesting, Master. I think we have an agreement.
Great! I knew you were a man who can be reasonable! So I await the results of the investigation as soon as possible, brother. God bless us.
Thanks. Could I talk to you a little longer?
Gladly, brother. What do you need to know?
Your proposition sounds interesting, Master. If you add some gold to it, I'll gladly start the investigation immediately.

Are you asking me to bribe you with gold? And you call yourself a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous! But you may be right—what does a few gold coins mean in this case in comparison to what I can gain? So we have the agreement.
Great. Now I'd like to ask you some questions, if I can.
You can't traffic in justice, Master. Your proposal is amoral and it goes against my belief!

Well... do what you want, brother. But I assure you that you will return to me. As I say—find out who is behind those kidnappings and give me some evidence so he can be put on trial. In exchange I'll give you my testimony about what I saw and heard with my own eyes and ears.
Well... we'll see. But now I'd need to talk to you for a moment.

Sure, brother, of course I'll keep my part of the agreement. I'm sure my testimony will be useful to you—no matter which way your investigation leads. Well... from time to time I used to go to the Bishop's Garden in the evening, to rest there peacefully and quietly, which is something all of us miss so much these days. It may sound like a lie from me, but it is as I say, brother. I like to enjoy the moments I don't have to hold a sword in my hand or to think about thousand and one thing of my office.
Very poetic. Go on, please. You haven't told me anything interesting yet—without offense.

Sure, brother, I'll get to the point soon. I'm sure you know that the relationships between the Holy Mother Church and the Brotherhood of the Righteous aren't very good since the Decretum Inquisitorium was declared. Also here in Glatzburg malice rules between our Knights and the clerics. Because of that I'm always trying not to be seen in the Bishop's Garden. And exactly like that it was also that evening. I was just in the middle of a deep contemplation, when two persons' coming distracted me. They were quite far from me but not far enough to prevent me from hearing them. And I'll tell you—I held my breath. That is, they were talking about some heretic mass they were going to hold rather soon! It looked like one of them gave the other some kind of instruction on how to prepare that witchlike Sabbath! I was trying hard to recognize both conspirators in the deepening dark, because I knew I became a witness of something very wicked and surely it would be of some use to me in the future.
Interesting. Have you recognized those men?
Not both of them, brother. But one of them I recognized for sure. I swear by God Almighty that the one who gave the orders was Cardinal Truncquillius!
Cardinal Truncquillius? The Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg? Are you sure, Master? Do you have any idea what you have just told me?! It is absolutely unthinkable...

Sure I realize it, brother. Maybe you understand now why I didn't do anything about the information until now. What would I tell them? That I spotted the Cardinal hatching a plot against God and preparing a Black Sabbath? Everybody would laugh at me... No, brother, this information is too dangerous for me to dare to use it. Because of that I decided to exchange it with you for the revealing of those girls' kidnappers. And so I've done. I tell you it was Cardinal Truncquillius, as there's God in Heaven above me!
What exactly were those two heretics talking about, Master? What were they planning after all?

As I told you—they were talking about some heretic ritual—one of those heretics was to prepare it. They were talking pretty quiet, so I didn't hear many details, but several times I heard clearly that they were mentioning some Chaos Sanctuary. But I don't know at all what it means.
When did it in fact all happen?
Not long ago, brother. I don't remember the days exactly, but for sure it was before that terrible storm which raged above the city several days ago. I haven't been to the Bishop's Garden since then.
Thank you, Master. I don't know yet how I will dispose of your testimony, but I'm glad you told me about it.

Yes, I'm sure you are. But let me tell you one more thing—if you would like to summon me as a witness and you would not have everything prepared properly, I'd deny everything I've just said. Do you understand me? Farewell, brother.

Hail to you, brother. I'm glad to meet you at last. I've heard so much about you that I prayed dearly to be able to get to know you personally. Seldom has a man had the opportunity to talk with someone who was able to figure out crimes as heinous as those that were committed in Hillbrandt this spring.
Who are you, if I can ask?

Excuse me for not introducing myself immediately. I forgot my decent manners being so excited from our encounter. My name is Master Dieter von Gelbendiel and I'm the highest Magister of the local Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Nice to meet you, Master. I've met your companion, Master Edmond d'Arvias in Hillbrandt. Do you know him?

Of course I know Edmond, brother. We were serving together for many years as commanders and together we were also promoted to Masters. I'm glad you were able to prove his innocence in the end. It was irrational from the beginning to accuse him of such crimes. Edmond would never do something like that—even if some evil demon possessed his soul, brother. You can believe me about that!
It seems to me that you're informed in detail about what happened in Hillbrandt.

Oh yes, I know more than enough, brother. You know how it is—we're living in times when information is worth more than gold. He, who doesn't know what's happening in the other part of the Realm will very probably meet something unpleasant during his journeys. And our Order keeps appropriate information about all that is important for us. You must admit that your investigation in Hillbrandt was more than important. The sole fact that you, as a completely unknown paladin, led the investigation against the Inquisitorial Judge and you got him to the scaffold in the end is something that can't be left unnoticed.

Well... You may be right. However I'm discomforted by the fact so many people were informed about that Hillbrandt case even before I came to Glatzburg. After all, it all happened only a few days ago...

You know, brother, certain information can spread very quickly. But I can assure you that I'm one of a few people who know that you're on a mission here in Glatzburg. And in addition to that—the information will be absolutely safe with me. Rest assured that nobody will get to know anything from me. And I don't have slightest idea what your mission is here in Glatzburg. But I can say I'm very glad I could have met you personally thanks to it.
Why did you want to meet me so much?
Do you think that the exposure and conviction of an Inquisitorial Judge isn't enough?
I'm not sure if we can count this as a success, Master. It was more of a tragedy...

Yes, no doubt you're right—the Inquisitorial Judge convicted of heresy! What a wicked time we live in! But it doesn't lessen your merit, brother. On the contrary—your modesty proves that you are able to do great deeds without being blinded by self-praise. And just because of that I'd like to ask you for something. And I believe you won't refuse my offer.
Can you be a little bit more specific?
You are right. I haven't realized what a wonderful thing I managed to do!

You can see it! No need to be humble without a reason—after all, the exposure of judge Vallarian's crimes wasn't anything simple, I'm sure about that. You had to put forth all your strength, wits and intuition to solve that complicated case. And just because of that I'd like to ask you for something. And I believe you won't refuse my offer.
Can you tell me what's the matter?
According to your words it seems to me that you want to tell me something, don't you?
You're very keen, brother! It's really unbelievable—you've completely overcome my expectations!
Could you then move to the point?

Hail to you, brother. Have you solved that case already? Time is running out quickly and I'm getting a little bit impatient. The sooner you hand me over the criminal and convincing evidence, the better—both for me and, of course, for you.
I'm sorry, Master. I haven't solved that case yet. However, I'd need to talk to you, if it would be possible.
But of course, brother. I only ask that you not waste time too much and pay attention to that case. What do you need to know?
No, not yet. Farewell.
Yes, that case is solved already. But I'm not sure you will be satisfied...
Great, brother! You haven't disappoint me. So who was the perpetrator of all those kidnappings? And what evidence have you gathered against him?

Duke Rowan van Leerin was the perpetrator, Master. He kidnapped all those innocent girls to perform a dark ritual using their blood. He wanted to bring the statue of King Edward to life and to introduce it instead of the real King whom he was going to assassinate.

What...?! Duke Rowan van Leerin? But how could that be... Oh my God... The royal vice-governor of the city? I've always considered him my friend... He had contacts even at the royal court... Are you sure he was the one who stood behind those kidnappings? And do you have enough evidence against him to bring him to court to put him on trial?
Well... there's a little problem with that, Master. To tell the truth, he's dead.
WHAT? How did that happen? Who killed him? Did you?!
Yes, that was me. There was nothing else I could do. He assaulted me when I caught him performing that disgusting ritual during which he sacrificed all those innocent girls.

God Almighty... what reasons could I give for that? This is not how I envisioned it at all... Did I want you to execute justice on your own? You should have brought me some evidence instead of swooping at the perpetrator alone... But I should have known you would do it like that—you have already murdered Bishop Vallarian this way, so why wouldn't you do it again. I won't get promoted because of that; there will be an investigation instead! What evidence did you have against him? Tell me about it—I need to know everything. If you acted contrary to the Law, you will be held responsible for that!
Alphonso DiCerbio testified that he accomplished several wicked crimes for Duke Rowan van Leerin, including kidnapping of several innocent girls and little Tommy Clifford.
Well... good. And further? DiCerbio can deny everything—in the case you've left him alive, of course.
Johaness Clifford testified that Duke Rowan van Leerin imprisoned several young girls in a secret shrine under his house and threatened them with being sacrificed.
Interesting. But somebody could object that you forced Clifford to this testimony! Do you have any other evidence?

The Duke himself pleaded that he commanded the kidnapping of several innocent girls he needed for a perverse heretic ritual, during which he would bring the statue of King Edward II to life, because he wanted to usurp the power in the Realm into his hands by means of that statue.

Was anybody else present during that testimony, brother? Nobody, I suppose. In that case you could be accused you made it all up. And even in the case anybody else was there with you, people could say he was in conspiracy with you. Some sound proof is needed to silence all prospective fault-finders—and you can believe me tens of them usually appear in such cases... Do you have any more evidence?

I found a secret diary of Duke Rowan van Leerin, in which the monstrous plan for the displacement of His Majesty King Edward II is described in detail. There's no doubt that the mad Duke wanted to usurp the might of the Realm into his hands with the help of infernal forces.
You really did? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, brother. Although I believe somebody could even doubt the authenticity of that diary... Do you have some other evidence?
That's all, Master. I haven't come by more evidence.

Excellent, that should be enough. In the end it doesn't look as bad as I thought at the beginning. I was worried both of us will be in really big trouble. Many people will probably ask many questions about many things even now, but with this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, brother. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!
I'm glad you're satisfied, Master. Now I'd ask you in return for your prospective testimony you promised to tell me.

Damn it, brother, I hope this is just a bad dream! With this evidence—although they're direct and clear—we could be accused that we constructed the whole case against Duke van Leerin. That we made a plot against him! We must prevent that at all costs, brother. Go and find some other proof that will give evidence against Duke van Leerin. Without it our lives would be forfeit, you can believe me of that!

Hail to you, brother. Have you changed your mind about that proposition I gave you? I believe firmly that you did. I'm sure you are interested in what I witnessed here in Glatzburg... And it will cost you nothing at all—well, if you don't count bruising your ethical codex a little, in case you have any...
Yes, I've changed my mind. I'll find out who's behind those girls' kidnappings.
Excellent, brother! I know you would become reasonable. Find out who the perpetrator is, and I'll tell you what I witnessed. You will see you'll thank me very much for that!
That's what we will see. Could I talk to you for a moment?
We'll see. Farewell.
No, I haven't changed my mind. I'm not going to accept your strange proposal. However, I need to ask you several questions.

As you wish, brother. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you. What do you need to know?
No, Master, I haven't changed my mind. Farewell.
As you wish, brother. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you.
Hail to you, brother. Have you already found something proving Duke Rowan van Leerin guilty?

Yes, Master, I have. I found a secret diary of Duke Rowan van Leerin, in which a monstrous plan for the displacement of His Majesty King Edward II is described in detail. There's no doubt that the mad Duke wanted to usurp the might of the Realm into his hands with the help of infernal forces.

Really? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, brother. With this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, brother. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!
No, Master, I haven't. However, I'd need to talk to you for a moment.

As you wish, brother, I'm at your service. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...
No, Master, not yet. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...

Hail to you, brother. What brings you to me? I'm awaiting a courier from Alvaron impatiently, as he should bring me news from my superiors. Sure I'll be promoted to the Seneschal status and be transferred to the Citadel of the Brotherhood...
I'd need to ask you a couple of questions, Master.
At you service, brother. What do you need to know?
I just happened to come by, nothing more. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. May God protect you!
What conditions do I have to meet to be declared a master of the Order?

Only a Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous may become a Master of the Brotherhood, and only if he proves his utter loyalty to God and the King and completes a task that's assigned to him. Moreover, he has to prove his courage in fighting and kill more than a quarter of a thousand infernal enemies.
I would like to be declared a Master of the Order.

Really? And do you deem yourself sufficiently loyal to God and the King? Do you believe you're ready to sacrifice yourself for the justice we're sworn to defend even at the cost of our lives, et cetera et cetera... My Goodness, those lengthy phrases are annoying!
Ehm... Yes, I'm ready!

In that case listen carefully, brother. I'm not sure if you've heard about it already, but the undead are walking the streets of the city at nights. You surely can imagine the panic those monstrous creatures have caused. Nobody dares to leave his house after dark and he who does risks a very unpleasant death. I personally have put my mind to the case and I found out several things that alarmed me more than the presence of the undead inside the city walls. I especially noticed that they're not usual murders, committed by infernal monsters led only by an urgent lust for fresh blood. All the victims were robbed of all their valuables including brass buttons and gold teeth. At first sight it seems the undead murdered for money. But that's pure nonsense—undead bodies are led only by their murderous instinct and by nothing else.
Hm...

That's why I've been so surprised by that. At first I thought the robberies are—in contrast to the murders—the work of someone else, but the testimonies of the witnesses speak otherwise. I couldn't believe there are some undead monsters who would intentionally collect valuables. And then I finally caught on to it. It's not the will of the undead that makes them steal, but the will of the one who summoned them into this world! There are many forbidden necromantic rites by which heretics are able to compel dead bodies to a new unclean life. The undead brought to life in this way obey their creator and may perform certain easy tasks for him. Fortunately that devilish ability of theirs is limited to the most basic orders, otherwise we couldn't be sure of anything. And that's why I'm sure there is a heretic standing behind the undead in the city streets and behind their attacks on the citizens. This way the heretic tries to get wealthy!
I understand. And my task is to find the heretic, get enough evidence against him and turn him over to justice.
Just so, brother. If you manage to do that, it'll be clear evidence you're worthy to become a Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Alright, I'll accomplish the task. The culprit will be caught and punished!
Very well, brother. Definitely you don't lack courage...
By chance I've already occupied myself with that case and I believe I've uncovered the culprit of all those crimes.
Really? That's great! So, who is it?
It's the soldier Harph of the Royal Garrison of Glatzburg.
Hmm... and by what evidence will you back up this accusation, brother?

I found Harph's diary—it was hidden in his disgusting den deep in the deserted sewers under the city. In the diary he confessed to all his crimes. Moreover I've heard a witness who told me he saw Harph descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of undead monsters.

Great! I didn't dare hope you would manage to solve the case so quickly, brother. There's nothing more to say. I'm free to declare you a Master of the Brotherhood. That is if you've already proven your courage in fighting and killed more than a quarter of a thousand enemies...
I've found out who stands behind all the robberies perpetrated by the undead monsters wandering in the city streets at night.
I have proven my courage in fighting and killed more than a quarter of a thousand infernal enemies, Master.
I have proven my courage already. More than a quarter of a thousand infernal enemies are back in Hell or on their way there...
Regrettably, I haven't killed so many enemies yet...
You can rely on me, Master. Farewell!

Excellent. By your courage in fighting you've proven you deserve to be declared a Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Congratulations, brother! Accept this item as a symbol of your new office. And herewith I give you the key of the Glatzburg chapter where you're now allowed to enter!

A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even God's knights are thieves! You greatly disappointed me, brother—I'll have to be more careful when dealing with you in future!

I've heard certain rumors about one of your former brothers in the Order, Master. His name is Henry de Montreaux and it seems that he's killing everybody he meets around Glatzburg. What can you tell me about him?

What do I think about the current crisis? It depends on which crisis you have in mind, Father—the one of the clergy or the one concerning power? The clergy crisis is very bad, but I'm sure it's only the beginning of the real crisis which is purely power-related. Of course I'm devotedly faithful and the Law of God is above all for me, but I can't avoid the feeling that power is the most important thing here. Of course there are all those signs St. Ezechiel described in his Apocalypse around, but it only created the hub for the conflict of powers—not that I'd like to spread rebellious or maybe even heretic opinions.

Can't you see it, Father? The Inquisition is haggling with the Brotherhood of the Righteous for the jurisdiction and competence, the nobles scream they want more rights because royal power is falling away, and the struggle concerns common people as well, though they are immediately inclined to the "End of the World" idea. However, it's possible the Day of Judgment is really coming soon, it's possible that Satan will be released from his jail and the Final Judgment will be done.

I've also heard some rumors about the war, Father. And because the mission of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is closer to the warrior issues than to anything else, I can put two and two together. Yes, it really seems to me that the war is about to start. And I even have a certain suspicion against which opponent the war should be waged. But because of the fact it could be considered treason—not to mention heresy—I'd rather keep it for myself. For the sake of safety, Father. Both mine and your safety.
I'm sorry, Father, but that's not possible. The theory is too outrageous and unsubstantiated at the same time—I can only guess. I'm sorry. There's nothing personal in it.

Are you interested in monsters, Father? Well... it's always a good idea to get to know opponents before you meet them. Although I suppose you've already met quite a lot of them. If you travel any of the royal or country roads, you will surely run into some robber baron and his minions. They're a great trouble for the whole city, as both the trade and the transport stagnate. Deeper in the woods you can find those horned beasts from the Devil's Caverns. Some call them devils, but personally I'd say they're some kind of lizards walking upright like people. Though they are Bloodthirsty and very dangerous. Beware of the living dead in the city after dusk—they appear in the streets to kill anybody they meet. There's also a lot of them in the cemetery. Only a few dead bodies stayed laying in their graves when the Scourges of God struck the Realm...

Grand Duke Heidrick set some rewards for the brigands pestering the roads. He did so thinking it will help get rid of them. But it doesn't seem to help at all. However, if you were so lucky to do away with some brigands in the course of your holy mission, Sheriff Smith will pay you some gold as a reward. If a modest and humble cleric is taking any rewards at all, of course.
I've already told you about my suspicion, Father. That thing about the secret meeting of cardinal Truncquillius in the Bishop's Garden. I don't know anything else.

Did Istwan de Bragho really come back from the Other World? I never thought about it... If it is as you say, I certainly wouldn't get in his way, Father. A curse is no fun at all, especially when it brings the dead back to life. If weapons and spells don't do any harm to him I can't imagine any other way to get rid of him other than to let him finish his posthumous revenge! And God will surely take care of the souls of his victims.

The Fallen Angels are the minions of Satan and the most powerful demons who have ever lived in Hell. Sources other than the Scriptures mention them, thus we can expect they were known already in pagan times. They impersonate the antithesis of God Almighty, just as darkness is the opposite of light. There're four of them: Arthamon, the Master of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Mistress of Fornication and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the first of the servants of Satan. Each of the Fallen Angels controls one of the Chaos elements—destruction, madness and lechery. Since the Dawn of Time, when they were thrown down from the sky together with Satan for the crimes they committed, they've been imprisoned in Hell. Only their lesser servants can get into our world directly, but they can affect our world with their power, by affecting human minds—and this is the way that sin and misdemeanor come into this world. And they are very successful in their effort! Tell me frankly, Father—do you think there has been any lack of destruction, madness and of lechery in the world in recent years?

There's only one thing I can tell you about the undead, Father—they're a really awful lot. When the hellspawns were kept at bay behind the city walls, the situation wasn't so bad. That is to say, people were scared and depressed, but still there was no threat to their lives. Thus, when the undead started to show themselves in the streets of Glatzburg after dusk, people panicked at once and the city started to look a lot like a Black Death village. I've met those living dead personally several times and I cut them with my men like barley, but if you meet the same ones every day—well, every night in fact—you will lose your vim quite soon. So they walk the streets mostly unpunished these days...

That's a good question, Father. I racked my brain about it too and I have a suspicion it's somehow related to those tales about the ancient underground sewers that should be probably located under the city. It's possible the sewers really exist—that they weren't filled up as the sources from the beginnings of the city history say—and that the undead settled down there. But it's just my opinion. In addition to that I haven't found one entrance which could be used to get into those sewers.

Commander Ethiene de Pasque lost his Chain of the Brotherhood? Well, that's very bad for him. Symbols of our rank are counted among relics in the Brotherhood of the Righteous, because they were anointed by the Grand Master of the Order himself in the name of the First Prophet and of the Archangel Gabriel. Commander de Pasque will now have to make a great effort to get his chain back—and to get back his honor at the same time. However, if you're going to help him in his effort, Father, ask Tinthan the actor first of all whether he doesn't know anything about it. Because when something disappears without anybody noticing it, Tinthan usually has a hand in it!

Sure, Father. I don't know whether you've already familiarized yourself with the situation in Glatzburg, but I can assure you that the situation is serious, although it doesn't look like that at first sight. I feel brimstone is boiling and the smoke of hell is fuming under this quite and calm surface. Since the Scourges of God struck, people are different, very different. They either lock themselves inside their houses, as if the stone walls could protect them from what did affect the Realm, or... the others... they treacherously hatch plots and serve the idols in an attempt to save themselves from the coming End of the World. You wouldn't believe what people are able to commit. As if they went totally mad.

I'm getting to the point. As I've already said, we've faced many terrible crimes here in Glatzburg since the Scourges of God struck. But I assure you, Father, that it's not the same here as in Hillbrandt. No matter what you have met there, it's one hundred times worse here in Glatzburg. Hillbrandt is situated in a wild area far in the north of the Realm and people there are ruder and simpler since their birth—no offense intended. On the other hand, Glatzburg is the second largest city in the Realm! Deadly intrigues, falsehood and dissimulation rule here. Crime is much more sophisticated; our criminals are more dangerous and cunning.

Yes, Father, you are right. I'm confident a man like you will have the best opportunity to find out how things really are without attracting too much undesirable attention. Thus I decided to wait for your arrival when the Hillbrandt Chapter told me about your deeds. I want you to clear up those mysterious disappearances of several young girls I told you about. Gather affirmative proofs and present them to me.

Yes, exactly. If you've mentioned it, I won't withhold it from you—it wouldn't make sense. My heart craves to present this case—if successfully solved, of course—as my own success. Thanks to that the door of the Main Chapter of our Order in Alvaron, the capital of our Realm, would be opened to me. Probably I would be promoted to the Seneschal of Order, and it does mean everything for me at the moment! Understand, Father—I have nowhere to rise here in Glatzburg. And thus my only chance of getting a better position is to solve this case which is under the solicitous scrutiny of my superiors.

Call it as you want, but it's a fair trade. And please leave my personal qualities and my conscience to someone more qualified—that is, to myself. They're not your business. In any case you better realize that you can't lose in this bargain. Be sure about that! As I told you in the beginning, this little trade between us will bring you great reward. It's linked to your investigation... To tell the truth, I'm not totally sure what the reason of your coming to Glatzburg is, but I believe it has some connection to your Hillbrandt case. You're probably searching for the accomplices of Judge Vallarian or something like that. In that case I assure you that I have certain information which would make your investigation much easier. In other words—I have straight convincing evidence against one person here in Glatzburg that is nearly drown in heresy. I'm sure that convicting that person would mean another great jump in your career.

I'm glad you take it like this, Father. You can't lose in this bargain, be sure about that! As I told you in the beginning, this little trade between us will bring you great reward. It's linked to your investigation... To tell the truth, I'm not totally sure what is the reason of your coming to Glatzburg, but I believe it has some connection to your Hillbrandt case. You're probably searching for the accomplices of judge Vallarian's murder or something like that. In that case I assure you that I have certain information which would make your investigation much easier. In other words—I have straight convincing evidence against one person here in Glatzburg that is nearly drown in heresy. I'm sure that convicting that person would mean another great jump in your career.

That, of course, I'm not going to tell you, Father. At least, not now. First I want to hear the name of those girls' kidnapper and to have evidence against him in my hands. Then of course I'll testify to you all that I witnessed some time ago.
Withholding of information from the Inquisition borders with heresy, Master. If you have some proof that could lead to proving a heretic guilty, give it to me immediately!

No, Father, I'm sorry. If you would like to take it like this, let's pretend our dialogue never happened. However I believe you will change your attitude. Believe me—the information would be more than interesting for you!

Not necessarily, Father. To mess with the things of Inquisition is quite a risky matter even for the Brotherhood of the Righteous. And in addition to that—I'm not sure how my superiors would react to the fact I lead the investigation against that person! It's a politically sensitive matter. Because of that I think it would be more fitting for you. Just find out who kidnapped the girls and gather enough evidence and testimonies against him so he can be put on trial.
Great! I knew you are a man who could be reasonable! So I await the results of the investigation as soon as possible, Father. God bless you.
Are you asking me to bribe you with gold? And you call yourself a cleric! But you may be right—what does a few gold coins mean in this case in comparison to what I can gain? So we have an agreement.

Well... do what you want, Father. But I assure you that you will return to me. As I say—find out who is behind those kidnappings and give me some evidence so he can be put on trial. In exchange I'll give you my testimony about what I saw and heard with my own eyes and ears.

Sure, Father, of course I'll keep my part of the agreement. I'm sure my testimony will be useful to you—no matter which way your investigation leads. Well... from time to time I used to go to the Bishop's Garden in the evening, to rest there peacefully and quietly, which is something all of us miss so much in these times. Maybe it sounds like a lie from me, but it is as I say, Father. I like to enjoy a moment I don't have to hold a sword in my hands or to think about a thousand and one thing of my office.

Sure, Father, I'll get to the point soon. I'm sure you know that the relationships between the Holy Mother Church and the Brotherhood of the Righteous aren't very good since the Decretum Inquisitorium was declared. Also here in Glatzburg malice rules between our Knights and the clerics. Because of that I'm always trying not to be seen in the Bishop's Garden. And exactly like that it was also that evening. I was just in the middle of a deep contemplation, when two persons' coming distracted me. They were quite far from me but not far enough to prevent me from hearing them. And I'll tell you—I held my breath. That is, they were talking about some heretic mass they were going to hold rather soon! It looked like one of them gave the other some kind of instruction on how to prepare that witchlike Sabbath! I was trying hard to recognize both conspirators in the deepening dark, because I knew I became a witness of something very wicked and surely it would be of some use to me in the future.
Not both of them, Father. But one of them I recognized for sure. I swear by God Almighty that the one who gave the orders was Cardinal Truncquillius!

Sure I realize it, Father. Maybe you understand now why I didn't do anything about the information until now. What would I tell them? That I spotted the Cardinal hatching a plot against God and preparing a Black Sabbath? Everybody would laugh at me... No, Father, this information is too dangerous for me to dare to use it. Because of that I decided to exchange it with you for the revealing of those girls' kidnappers. And so I've done. I tell you it was Cardinal Truncquillius, as there's God in Heaven above me!
Not long ago, Father. I don't remember the days exactly, but for sure it was before that terrible storm which raged above the city several days ago. I haven't been to the Bishop's Garden since then.

Yes, I'm sure you are. But let me tell you one more thing—if you would like to summon me as a witness and you would not have everything prepared properly, I'd deny everything I've just said. Do you understand me? Farewell, Father.

Hail to you, Father. I'm glad to meet you at last. I've heard so much about you that I prayed dearly to be able to get to know you personally. Seldom has a man had the opportunity to talk with someone who was able to figure out crimes as heinous as those that were committed in Hillbrandt this spring.

Excuse me for not introducing myself immediately. I forgot my decent manners because of that excitement from our encounter. My name is Master Dieter von Gelbendiel and I'm the highest Magister of the local Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. At your service, Father.

Of course I know Edmond, Father. We were serving together for many years as commanders and together we were also promoted to Masters. I'm glad you were able to prove his innocence in the end. It was irrational from the beginning to accuse him of such crimes. Edmond would never do something like that—even if some evil demon possessed his soul, Father. You can believe me about that!

Oh yes, I know more than enough, Father. You know how it is—we're living in times when information means more then gold. The one who doesn't know what's happening in the other part of the Realm will very probably meet something unpleasant during his journeys. And our Order keeps appropriate information about all that is important for us. You must admit that your investigation in Hillbrandt was more than important. Alone the fact that you, as a completely unknown priest, led the investigation against the Inquisitorial Judge and you got him to the scaffold in the end is something that can't be left unnoticed.

You know, Father, certain information can spread very quickly. But I can assure you that I'm one of a few people who know that you're on a mission here in Glatzburg. And in addition to that—the information will be absolutely safe with me. Rest assured that nobody will get to know anything from me. And I don't have slightest idea what your mission is here in Glatzburg. But I can say I'm very glad I could have met you personally thanks to it.

Yes, no doubt you're right—the Inquisitorial Judge convicted of heresy! What a wicked time we live in! But it doesn't lessen your merit, Father. On the contrary—your modesty proves that you are able to do great deeds without being blinded by self-praise. And just because of that I'd like to ask you for something. And I believe you won't refuse my offer.
You're very keen, Father! It's really unbelievable—you've completely overcome my expectations!

Hail to you, Father. Have you solved that case already? Time is running out quickly and I'm getting a little bit impatient. The sooner you hand me over the criminal and convincing evidence, the better—both for me and, of course, for you.
But of course, Father. I only ask that you not waste time too much and pay attention to that case. What do you need to know?
Great, Father! You haven't disappoint me. So who was the perpetrator of all those kidnappings? And what evidence have you gathered against him?

Was anybody else present during that testimony, Father? Nobody, I suppose. In that case you could be accused you made it all up. And even in the case anybody else was there with you, people could say he was in conspiracy with you. Some sound proof is needed to silence all prospective fault-finders—and you can believe me tens of them usually appear in such cases... Do you have any more evidence?
You really did? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, Father. Although I believe somebody could even doubt the authenticity of that diary... Do you have some other evidence?

Excellent, that should be enough. In the end it doesn't look as bad as I thought at the beginning. I was worried both of us will be in really big trouble. Many people will probably ask many questions about many things even now, but with this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, Father. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!

Damn it, Father, I hope this is just a bad dream! With this evidence—although they're direct and clear—we could be accused that we constructed the whole case against Duke van Leerin. That we made a plot against him! We must prevent that at all costs, Father. Go and find some other proof that will give evidence against Duke van Leerin. Without it our lives would be forfeit, you can believe me of that!

Hail to you, Father. Have you changed your mind about that proposition I gave you? I believe firmly that you did. I'm sure you are interested in what I witnessed here in Glatzburg... And it will cost you nothing at all—well, if you don't count bruising your ethical codex a little, in case you have any...
Excellent, Father! I know you would become reasonable. Find out who the perpetrator is, and I'll tell you what I witnessed. You will see you'll thank me very much for that!

As you wish, Father. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you. What do you need to know?
As you wish, Father. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you.
Hail to you, Father. Have you already found something proving Duke Rowan van Leerin guilty?

Really? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, Father. With this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, Father. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!

As you wish, Father, I'm at your service. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...
Farewell, Father. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...

Hail to you, Father. What brings you to me? I'm awaiting a courier from Alvaron impatiently, as he should bring me news from my superiors. Sure I'll be promoted to the Seneschal status and be transferred to the Citadel of the Brotherhood...
At you service, Father. What do you need to know?
Farewell, Father. May God protect you!

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of Glatzburg. Nobles from the Heidrick House have been named the royal governors of the city for many generations already, it nearly became a hereditary title, although it could be given to someone other land holder, of course. Rowan van Leerin is the royal vice-governor—he was named to the office eight years ago and he's been trying to get higher since then. But he doesn't seem to have enough political power to eliminate the Grand Duke. However, one never knows in politics...

What do I think about the current crisis? It depends on which crisis you have in mind, sir—the one of the clergy or the one concerning power? The clergy crisis is very bad, but I'm sure it's only the beginning of the real crisis which is purely power-related. Of course I'm devotedly faithful and the Law of God is above all for me, but I can't avoid the feeling that power is the most important thing here. Of course there are all those signs St. Ezechiel described in his Apocalypse around, but it only created the hub for the conflict of powers—not that I'd like to spread rebellious or maybe even heretic opinions.

Can't you see it, sir? The Inquisition is haggling with the Brotherhood of the Righteous for the jurisdiction and competence, the nobles scream they want more rights because royal power is falling away, and the struggle concerns common people as well, though they are immediately inclined to the "End of the World" idea. However, it's possible the Day of Judgment is really coming soon, it's possible that Satan will be released from his jail and the Final Judgment will be done.

I've also heard some rumors about the war, sir. And because the mission of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is closer to the warrior issues than to anything else, I can put two and two together. Yes, it really seems to me that the war is about to start. And I even have a certain suspicion against which opponent the war should be waged. But because of the fact it could be considered treason—not to mention heresy—I'd rather keep it for myself. For the sake of safety, sir. Both mine and your safety.
I'm sorry, sir, but that's not possible. The theory is too outrageous and unsubstantiated at the same time—I can only guess. I'm sorry. There's nothing personal in it.

Are you interested in monsters, sir? Well... it's always a good idea to get to know opponents before you meet them. Although I suppose you've already met quite a lot of them. If you travel any of the royal or country roads, you will surely run into some robber baron and his minions. They're a great trouble for the whole city, as both the trade and the transport stagnate. Deeper in the woods you can find those horned beasts from the Devil's Caverns. Some call them devils, but personally I'd say they're some kind of lizards walking upright like people. Though they are Bloodthirsty and very dangerous. Beware of the living dead in the city after dusk—they appear in the streets to kill anybody they meet. There's also a lot of them in the cemetery. Only a few dead bodies stayed laying in their graves when the Scourges of God struck the Realm...
I've already told you about my suspicion, sir. That thing about the secret meeting of cardinal Truncquillius in the Bishop's Garden. I don't know anything else.

Did Istwan de Bragho really come back from the Other World? I never thought about it... If it is as you say, I certainly wouldn't get in his way, sir. A curse is no fun at all, especially when it brings the dead back to life. If weapons and spells don't do any harm to him I can't imagine any other way to get rid of him other than to let him finish his posthumous revenge! And God will surely take care of the souls of his victims.

The Fallen Angels are the minions of Satan and the most powerful demons who have ever lived in Hell. Sources other than the Scriptures mention them, thus we can expect they were known already in pagan times. They impersonate the antithesis of God Almighty, just as darkness is the opposite of light. There're four of them: Arthamon, the Master of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Mistress of Fornication and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the first of the servants of Satan. Each of the Fallen Angels controls one of the Chaos elements—destruction, madness and lechery. Since the Dawn of Time, when they were thrown down from the sky together with Satan for the crimes they committed, they've been imprisoned in Hell. Only their lesser servants can get into our world directly, but they can affect our world with their power, by affecting human minds—and this is the way that sin and misdemeanor come into this world. And they are very successful in their effort! Tell me frankly, sir—do you think there has been any lack of destruction, madness and of lechery in the world in recent years?

There's only one thing I can tell you about the undead, sir—they're a really awful lot. When the hellspawns were kept at bay behind the city walls, the situation wasn't so bad. That is to say, people were scared and depressed, but still there was no threat to their lives. Thus, when the undead started to show themselves in the streets of Glatzburg after dusk, people panicked at once and the city started to look a lot like a Black Death village. I've met those living dead personally several times and I cut them with my men like barley, but if you meet the same ones every day—well, every night in fact—you will lose your vim quite soon. So they walk the streets mostly unpunished these days...

That's a good question, sir. I racked my brain about it too and I have a suspicion it's somehow related to those tales about the ancient underground sewers that should be probably located under the city. It's possible the sewers really exist—that they weren't filled up as the sources from the beginnings of the city history say—and that the undead settled down there. But it's just my opinion. In addition to that I haven't found one entrance which could be used to get into those sewers.

Commander Ethiene de Pasque lost his Chain of the Brotherhood? Well, that's very bad for him. Symbols of our rank are counted among relics in the Brotherhood of the Righteous, because they were anointed by the Grand Master of the Order himself in the name of the First Prophet and of the Archangel Gabriel. Commander de Pasque will now have to make a great effort to get his chain back—and to get back his honor at the same time. However, if you're going to help him in his effort, sir, ask Tinthan the actor first of all whether he doesn't know anything about it. Because when something disappears without anybody noticing it, Tinthan usually has a hand in it!

Sure, sir. I don't know whether you've already familiarized yourself with the situation in Glatzburg, but I can assure you that the situation is serious, although it doesn't look like that at first sight. I feel brimstone is boiling and the smoke of hell is fuming under this quite and calm surface. Since the Scourges of God struck, people are different, very different. They either lock themselves inside their houses, as if the stone walls could protect them from what did affect the Realm, or... the others... they treacherously hatch plots and serve the idols in an attempt to save themselves from the coming End of the World. You wouldn't believe what people are able to commit. As if they went totally mad.

I'm getting to the point. As I've already said, we've faced many terrible crimes here in Glatzburg since the Scourges of God struck. But I assure you, sir, that it's not the same here as in Hillbrandt. No matter what you have met there, it's one hundred times worse here in Glatzburg. Hillbrandt is situated in a wild area far in the north of the Realm and people there are ruder and simpler since their birth—no offense intended. On the other hand, Glatzburg is the second largest city in the Realm! Deadly intrigues, falsehood and dissimulation rule here. Crime is much more sophisticated; our criminals are more dangerous and cunning.

Yes, sir, you are right. I'm confident a man like you will have the best opportunity to find out how things really are without attracting too much undesirable attention. Thus I decided to wait for your arrival when the Hillbrandt Chapter told me about your deeds. I want you to clear up those mysterious disappearances of several young girls I told you about. Gather affirmative proofs and present them to me.

Yes, exactly. If you've mentioned it, I won't withhold it from you—it wouldn't make sense. My heart craves to present this case—if successfully solved, of course—as my own success. Thanks to that the door of the Main Chapter of our Order in Alvaron, the capital of our Realm, would be opened to me. Probably I would be promoted to the Seneschal of Order, and it does mean everything for me at the moment! Understand, sir—I have nowhere to rise here in Glatzburg. And thus my only chance of getting a better position is to solve this case which is under the solicitous scrutiny of my superiors.
