I'm glad you take it like this, sir. You can't lose in this bargain, be sure about that! As I told you in the beginning, this little trade between us will bring you great reward. It's linked to your investigation... To tell the truth, I'm not totally sure what is the reason of your coming to Glatzburg, but I believe it has some connection to your Hillbrandt case. You're probably searching for the accomplices of judge Vallarian's murder or something like that. In that case I assure you that I have certain information which would make your investigation much easier. In other words—I have straight convincing evidence against one person here in Glatzburg that is nearly drown in heresy. I'm sure that convicting that person would mean another great jump in your career.

That, of course, I'm not going to tell you, sir. At least, not now. First I want to hear the name of those girls' kidnapper and to have evidence against him in my hands. Then of course I'll testify to you all that I witnessed some time ago.

No, sir, I'm sorry. If you would like to take it like this, let's pretend our dialogue never happened. However I believe you will change your attitude. Believe me, the information would be more than interesting for you!

Not necessarily, sir. To mess with the things of Inquisition is quite a risky matter even for the Brotherhood of the Righteous. And in addition to that, I'm not sure how my superiors would react to the fact I lead the investigation against that person! It's a politically sensitive matter. Because of that I think it would be more fitting for you. Just find out who kidnapped the girls and gather enough evidence and testimonies against him so he can be put on trial.
Great! I knew you are a man who could be reasonable! So I await the results of the investigation as soon as possible, sir. God bless you.
Gladly, sir. What do you need to know?
Are you asking me to bribe you with gold? And you call yourself a noble! But you may be right, what does a few gold coins mean in this case in comparison to what I can gain? So we have the agreement.

Well... do what you want, sir. But I assure you that you will return to me. As I say—find out who is behind those kidnappings and give me some evidence so he can be put on trial. In exchange I'll give you my testimony about what I saw and heard with my own eyes and ears.

Sure, sir, of course I'll keep my part of the agreement. I'm sure my testimony will be useful to you no matter what your mission is. Well... from time to time I used to go to the Bishop's Garden in the evening, to rest there peacefully and quietly, which is something all of us miss so much these days. It may sound like a lie from me, but it is as I say, sir. I like to enjoy the moments I don't have to hold a sword in my hand or to think about thousand and one thing of my office.

Sure, sir, I'll get to the point soon. I'm sure you know that the relationships between the Holy Mother Church and the Brotherhood of the Righteous aren't very good since the Decretum Inquisitorium was declared. Also here in Glatzburg malice rules between our Knights and the clerics. Because of that I'm always trying not to be seen in the Bishop's Garden. And exactly like that it was also that evening. I was just in the middle of a deep contemplation, when two persons' coming distracted me. They were quite far from me but not far enough to prevent me from hearing them. And I'll tell you—I held my breath. That is, they were talking about some heretic mass they were going to hold rather soon! It looked like one of them gave the other some kind of instruction on how to prepare that witchlike Sabbath! I was trying hard to recognize both conspirators in the deepening dark, because I knew I became a witness of something very wicked and surely it would be of some use to me in the future.
Not both of them, sir. But one of them I recognized for sure. I swear by God Almighty that the one who gave the orders was Cardinal Truncquillius!

Sure I realize it, sir. Maybe you understand now why I didn't do anything about the information until now. What would I tell them? That I spotted the Cardinal hatching a plot against God and preparing a Black Sabbath? Everybody would laugh at me... No, sir, this information is too dangerous for me to dare to use it. Because of that I decided to exchange it with you for the revealing of those girls' kidnappers. And so I've done. I tell you it was Cardinal Truncquillius, as there's God in Heaven above me!
Not long ago, sir. I don't remember the days exactly, but for sure it was before that terrible storm which raged above the city several days ago. I haven't been to the Bishop's Garden since then.

Yes, I'm sure you are. But let me tell you one more thing—if you would like to summon me as a witness and you would not have everything prepared properly, I'd deny everything I've just said. Do you understand me? Farewell, sir.

Hail to you, sir. I'm glad to meet you at last. I've heard so much about you that I prayed dearly to be able to get to know you personally. Seldom has a man had the opportunity to talk with someone who was able to figure out crimes as heinous as those that were committed in Hillbrandt this spring.

Excuse me for not introducing myself immediately. I forgot my decent manners because of that excitement from our encounter. My name is Master Dieter von Gelbendiel and I'm the highest Magister of the local Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. At your service, sir.

Of course I know Edmond, sir. We were serving together for many years as commanders and together we were also promoted to Masters. I'm glad you were able to prove his innocence in the end. It was irrational from the beginning to accuse him of such crimes. Edmond would never do something like that—even if some evil demon possessed his soul, sir. You can believe me about that!

Oh yes, I know more than enough, sir. You know how it is, we're living in times when information is worth more than gold. He, who doesn't know what's happening in the other part of the Realm will very probably meet something unpleasant during his journeys. And our Order keeps appropriate information about all what is important for us. You must admit that your investigation in Hillbrandt was more than important. The sole fact that you, as a completely unknown noble, led the investigation against the Inquisitorial Judge and you got him to the scaffold in the end is something that can't be left unnoticed.

You know, sir, certain information can spread very quickly. But I can assure you that I'm one of a few people who know that you're on a mission here in Glatzburg. And in addition to that—the information will be absolutely safe with me. Rest assured that nobody will get to know anything from me. And I don't have slightest idea what your mission is here in Glatzburg. But I can say I'm very glad I could have met you personally thanks to it.

Yes, no doubt you're right—the Inquisitorial Judge convicted of heresy! What a wicked time we live in! But it doesn't lessen your merit, sir. On the contrary—your modesty proves that you are able to do great deeds without being blinded by self-praise. And just because of that I'd like to ask you for something. And I believe you won't refuse my offer.
You're very keen, sir! It's really unbelievable—you've completely overcome my expectations!
Very sharp. Could you then move to the point?

Hail to you, sir. Have you solved that case already? Time is running out quickly and I'm getting a little bit impatient. The sooner you hand me over the criminal and convincing evidence, the better—both for me and, of course, for you.
But of course, sir. I only ask that you not waste time too much and pay attention to that case. What do you need to know?
Great, sir! You haven't disappoint me. So who was the perpetrator of all those kidnappings? And what evidence have you gathered against him?

Was anybody else present during that testimony, sir? Nobody, I suppose. In that case you could be accused you made it all up. And even in the case anybody else was there with you, people could say he was in conspiracy with you. Some sound proof is needed to silence all prospective fault-finders—and you can believe me tens of them usually appear in such cases... Do you have any more evidence?
You really did? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, sir. Although I believe somebody could even doubt the authenticity of that diary... Do you have some other evidence?

Excellent, that should be enough. In the end it doesn't look as bad as I thought at the beginning. I was worried both of us will be in really big trouble. Many people will probably ask many questions about many things even now, but with this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, sir. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!

Damn it, sir, I hope this is just a bad dream! With this evidence—although they're direct and clear—we could be accused that we constructed the whole case against Duke van Leerin. That we made a plot against him! We must prevent that at all costs, sir. Go and find some other proof that will give evidence against Duke van Leerin. Without it our lives would be forfeit, you can believe me of that!

Hail to you, sir. Have you changed your mind about that proposition I gave you? I believe firmly that you did. I'm sure you are interested in what I witnessed here in Glatzburg... And it will cost you nothing at all—well, if you don't count bruising your ethical codex a little, in case you have any...
Excellent, sir! I know you would become reasonable. Find out who the perpetrator is, and I'll tell you what I witnessed. You will see you'll thank me very much for that!

As you wish, sir. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you. What do you need to know?
As you wish, sir. But believe me—you're making a big mistake. But I hope you will change your mind sooner or later. And the sooner you will, the better—both for me and for you.
Hail to you, sir. Have you already found something proving Duke Rowan van Leerin guilty?

Really? Well, this is what I call sound evidence. Excellent, sir. With this evidence I can stand out with a clear conscience and say that I revealed the truth about Duke Rowan van Leerin and that I put him to death in self-defense, as he resisted me during the apprehension. Thank you, sir. I think my promotion to the Seneschal position is only a matter of time. Great!

As you wish, sir, I'm at your service. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...
Farewell, sir. But if I can give you an advice, go and find some other evidence quickly, before somebody starts asking questions about Duke van Leerin. We can't keep it secret for too long...

Hail to you, sir. What brings you to me? I'm awaiting a courier from Alvaron impatiently, as he should bring me news from my superiors. Sure I'll be promoted to the Seneschal status and be transferred to the Citadel of the Brotherhood...
At you service, sir. What do you need to know?
Farewell, sir. May God protect you!

I'm sorry, but my master don't like me to talk to his guests. He says I'm too stupid for that. And he's probably right. I think my mother wasn't very clever because she married my father. And my father definitely wasn't clever, at least according to what my mother used to say about him...
I see. In that case I'd better go and talk to your master. Farewell.
Hello, knight. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city. I'm Geoffrey, the Grand Duke's butler.
Nice to meet you, good man. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Nice to meet you, good man. How do you like working for Grand Duke Lambert?
The work is good, knight, thank you.
I see. Could I talk to you for a moment?
The work is good? That's all you'll tell me about that?
Eh... the work is very good?
Hello, knight. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city.
Hello, Father. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city. I'm Geoffrey, the Grand Duke's butler.
The work is good, Father, thank you.
Hello, Father. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city.
Hello, noble sir. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city. I'm Geoffrey, the Grand Duke's butler.
The work is good, noble sir, thank you.
Hello, noble sir. Welcome to the house of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this city.

Duke Drake Lambert rules in Alvaron as the royal governor of the city. Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth is the vice-governor. I can tell you we are very lucky that the woman is more interested in what she wears than in how to rule. Because should this woman be the royal governor I'd have to leave the city as I wouldn't suffer such a disgrace. What a terrible age we live in that a woman can keep such an important office?!
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to talk to you about that!

I don't remember any recent fierce storm. It's true that sometimes the sky above Alvaron is going wild and you can see things man would not believe to exist, but recently? No, I don't remember any fierce storms.

It is said that people sometimes disappear in the Royal Road Inn in Schwarzwald, especially lonely travelers. And to tell you the truth, the place makes me shiver every time I'm so unlucky to ride around. Neither Bates, the innkeeper, nor his hostler Norman make a good impression...
I'm investigating the case of the paladin Richwald d'Blazier's murder. Do you happen to know anything about it?
The only thing I know about that case is that he was killed by a witch named Corin who lives somewhere in Schwarzwald—she bewitched the poor paladin. I don't know any details.
I'm looking for the members of the Cult of the Pagan Night, especially for their leader Juhasz Gotherr called Zan Drem. Do you happen to know where he could be hiding?

You're not the only one looking for Juhasz Gotherr, knight. I've heard that Judge Gregorius is truly obsessed with his apprehension—maybe because they were very good friends and Gregorius considers the fact he wasn't able to recognize the heresy of the city librarian as his personal failure. But I really don't have an idea where that tricky heretic could be hiding...
I'm looking for several magic ingredients—for the Betheal Temporarum blossom, sun crystal and troll bile, to be specific. Do you happen to know where some of those ingredients can be found?

As for magical additives and various ingredients, try asking Thelma Ulthraum the gallipot or Alberto Kelley, the Master Alchemist. I won't help you with that personally. Only, as for that troll bile, I'd look for it in the gallbladder of some hunted troll. I've heard some of those creatures appeared again in the northern areas of the Realm...
I'm searching for the criminals who rob the graves in the city cemetery and around the city. Do you happen to know anything about them?

To tell the truth, I saw that rogue Steinger one evening heading towards the cemetery. It seemed very strange to me as there aren't many people bold enough to go alone even near the cemetery during the day—and that was at night. I wonder what that slacker was up to.

Grand Duchess Liana Lambert's lies are second only to Satan, the king of lies. Everybody knows she's a very passionate and lecherous woman, who has already tempted as many men as she could. She's said not to have a lack of lovers and she's always willing to spread her legs to anyone. Thus, I'd be surprised if someone was able to lay hands on her before she would be able to say yes, hahaha...

Alvaron is full of tales and legends, knight. Especially, there's a lot of tales about various treasures and hidden fairy-tale riches—probably because the people are so greedy here. For example, look at the legend about Baron Decard of Longhorn's treasure. This wicked heretic gathered great fortune during his sinful life, especially a lot of magic items. To get it he committed murders, frauds, thefts, robberies and many other deeds that were as far from fairness as his soul was from that of salvation.

But he made a fatal mistake in the end; he tried to rob Bishop Benedictius and he ended up in chains. He admitted all of his crimes during torture—with a lot of pride, they say—but even the Inquisitors were unable to make him tell them where he had hidden the treasure he had gathered. He was executed in 1210, but nobody has been able to find the treasure since.
I need to find out some details about this special arrow. Do you happen to have some advice for me in this matter?

Show me the arrow, knight. Well... it's really good work. I'd say it's from the workshop of Leon van den Brooks. Have you already asked him about that? In the case you haven't, you should do that for sure. And by the way... what about the blood on the arrow? I see, I understand... that was a silly question.
In that case I can't help you anyhow...
Answer me, sir Baron. I promise you I'll make you wish you were never born!
If there're any problems between you and me, sir Baron, please be so kind and forget them for a moment. Your answer will help a good cause!
I can't believe a man as wise and educated as you would refuse me the answer to my question...

Hail to you, knight. You seem to be in a good mood—that's what I like. Because I must say that not a single day passes here in Alvaron without meeting a whole army of pale chicken-hearts lamenting about everything they have already met or they have been afflicted by. I'm sick of all that never-ending mumbling of requests to Heaven and of lamenting their fate!
And what do you suggest, sir Baron?

What do I suggest? Well, to grab a sword or a bow and go and face the evil lurking around us! All the people here are complaining that they are in real trouble, but to do something about it, well, that's not their cup of tea. As if it wouldn't concern them at all. I'll tell you what happened to me once. We were hunting with King Edward and one moment we were alone, only two of us, facing a raging wounded bear. The King went pale from terror—well, no doubt he did—and he started to pray devotedly to the Archangel Gabriel. How do you think it ended up?
How could I know? But I suppose you'll tell me...

Exactly. The Archangel Gabriel didn't come, of course, neither did any other Angel. Instead of them, I jumped between the King and the bear and brought the bear down with my own hands. Well, to tell the truth... I had my spear, the Bearkiller, in my hands, but except for that it was all exactly as I said. Prayers didn't help the King, neither did any of the Saints and Angels he called. I helped him, putting the ell-long blade into the bear's belly. And this is how all the things should be treated—we must fight, fight for our lives and not to give up even if it all looks as if the grim reaper is already sharpening his scythe.
The Archangel Gabriel appeared there and he brought the bear down with his flaming sword?

Not at all—instead of the Archangel Gabriel I jumped between the King and the bear and brought the bear down with my own hands. Well, to tell the truth... I had my spear, the Bearkiller, in my hands, but except for that it all was exactly as I said. Prayers didn't help the King, neither did any of the Saints and Angels he called. I helped him, putting the ell-long blade into the bear's belly. And this is how all the things should be treated—we must fight, fight for our lives and not to give up even if it all looks as if the Grim Reaper is already sharpening his scythe.
Could I ask you who you are, good man?

I'm Baron Gerbert of Rowington, valiant knight. I used to be the Head of the royal hunters... but the hunts were stopped three years ago. Because of that I know what I'm talking about, when I say it won't help even the tiniest bit to lament your bad fate. You must take the spear and put it into the bear's belly, or he eats you. And it's the same with life—the bear will eat those who give up and surrender!
What an interesting bear philosophy...

That's what I think, too. But enough of this talking, it only brings the idleness. You better tell me, knight, if you think you are courageous enough to help me with one problem that has been troubling me for a long time already.

I don't know if you've heard about it, but if you have stayed in Alvaron for some time already, this cause must have reached your ears. It's about Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. I mean, about the mansion he left us. The Baron was the last descendant of an ancient House that lived in Alvaron for many hundred years. He was very a rich man and pretty reputable in the community, but—as it was found out later—he was a terrible pervert and deviant from an ethical point of view—keen on cruelty and torture since babyhood. However, during his first marriage he turned into a complete bloodthirsty monster, who tortured his wife and three children to death.

But that was only the beginning. Later, he got married twelve times in a row during the years 1144–1175, whereas none of those wives and children had a better fate. The Baron turned the large cellars under the family mansion into torture and burial chambers for his poor women and children, whom he buried or immured there without any anointment. In the end the last—thirteenth—wife was able to resist his monstrosity and she simply poisoned our dear Baron. However, she was convicted of his murder and hanged because the Baron's crimes stayed hidden to the public and the people believed he was an orderly and believing man. But the poor woman cursed the Baron before her execution never to rest in peace and to stay imprisoned in the mansion together with those he murdered there!
God save the souls of those innocent victims...

God has nothing to do with that, knight—it's probably Satan who had a hand in what happened after. That is, the Baron's spirit stayed imprisoned in the family mansion that became a real house of terror and everybody started to avoid it. Of course, tales about inexhaustible riches hidden in the dungeons under the Blutenreich mansion appeared soon, but nobody of those who decided to go there was ever seen again. Terrible laughter can be heard from that house in the dead of night, as well as laments of women and of children. I'm sure you can imagine what probably takes place there...
If I understand all of that well, you want me to remove the curse from the mansion, don't you?

Yes, that's exactly what I want, knight. I want you to find the spirit of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich and to banish him from his house and completely out of this world. I would have it done on my own.. well, supernatural powers I can't handle, but what I can handle are bears. Moreover my health isn't what it used to be any more. I'm not the fighter I used to be since that hunt when a black bear broke my knee...
All right, I'll help you, Baron. I'll banish the spirit of Baron von Blutenreich from his mansion.
I'm glad you've decided to do that, knight. And no doubt you will be successful!
We'll see. Could I talk to you for a moment?
If you consider it necessary... why not?
Farewell, knight. Or better, see you soon. And don't forget—whenever there is a problem, the best solution usually is to put a spear or two into a bear's belly...
What can I expect as a reward for fulfilling this quest?

I'm glad you have asked, sir knight. I always settle all my debts. If you are able to banish all the unclean spirits from the Blutenreich mansion, I'll give you one magical item from my large collection and a purse of gold with some magical elixirs.
I'm sorry, but I don't have time for such cases.
Don't you? Well, that's a surprise to me. When I saw you for the first time, I said to myself—behold, this is a real spirit killer! But if you think so...
If you consider it necessary...

Hail to you, knight. You seem to be in a good mood—as always. Does it mean you have already succeeded in removing the curse from the mansion of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich? Have you exorcised the spirit of the mad Baron away from his mansion?
Regrettably I haven't, sir Baron.

Never mind. You surely will be successful one day. It's like bear hunting—he's running away from you in the beginning and he tries to escape, but after some time he's bored with that and he charges at you...
Well... could I talk to you for a moment?
Yes, the curse was removed from the mansion of Baron von Blutenreich. His erratic soul found the eternal peace—well, more likely it is back in Hell where it belongs!

You have really succeeded to do that! You exorcised the soul of Baron von Blutenreich away from this world. In that case you have my deepest admiration, knight! This is just like fronting a cave bear in the time of mating with just bare hands! Well done, you have done a great deed! Now I'll be able to sell the mansion at last!
Eh?! The mansion belongs to you?!

But of course, knight. You didn't know about it, did you? When Baron Dawn von Blutenreich died without leaving any heir, all his belongings were given to my House according to royal decision. The price of the mansion is very high but because of that curse I wasn't able to sell it unless someone banished the Baron's spirit away from this world. And you succeed to do that. Thus, yours is not only my thanks, but also the reward I promised you—take this magic item from my large collection. Perhaps you'll find it useful. A purse of gold and these miraculous elixirs are yours as well.
Not at all, knight. Today all the thanks belong only to you... What a shame King Edward didn't live to see that, surely he would be glad... He was so troubled about the von Blutenreich mansion!
There's nothing we can do about it. Could I talk to you a little longer, sir Baron?
Farewell, knight. And thank you again for your help. If you happen to come by again, you must visit me—I'll tell you how I ran into a really big cave bear one night...
Hail to you, knight. You seem to be in a good mood—and that's nice. I'm already getting sick from all those injured looks the other people have here.
I agree with you. Farewell.

Hail to you, knight. You seem to be in a good mood—as always. I really admire you for being able to remove the curse from the mansion of Baron von Blutenreich. It was bolder than facing a hungry cave bear!
If you think so... Could I talk to you for a moment?
Why not? I'm not very talkative in fact, but that's not important now, is it?
Thanks. Farewell, sir Baron.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! You should be ashamed of yourself!

You're not the only one looking for Juhasz Gotherr, Father. I've heard that Judge Gregorius is truly obsessed with his apprehension—maybe because they were very good friends and Gregorius considers the fact he wasn't able to recognize the heresy of the city librarian as his personal failure. But I really don't have an idea where that tricky heretic could be hiding...

Alvaron is full of tales and legends, Father. Especially, there's a lot of tales about various treasures and hidden fairy-tale riches—probably because the people are so greedy here. For example, look at the legend about Baron Decard of Longhorn's treasure. This wicked heretic gathered great fortune during his sinful life, especially a lot of magic items. To get it he committed murders, frauds, thefts, robberies and many other deeds that were as far from fairness as his soul was from that of salvation.

Show me the arrow, Father. Well... it's really good work. I'd say it's from the workshop of Leon van den Brooks. Have you already asked him about that? In the case you haven't, you should do that for sure. And by the way... what about the blood on the arrow? I see, I understand... that was a silly question.

Hail to you, Father. You seem to be in a good mood—that's what I like. Because I must say that not a single day passes here in Alvaron without meeting a whole army of pale chicken-hearts lamenting about everything they have already met or they have been afflicted by. I'm sick of all that never-ending mumbling of requests to Heaven and of lamenting their fate!

I'm Baron Gerbert of Rowington, reverend Father. I used to be the Head of the royal hunters... but the hunts were stopped three years ago. Because of that I know what I'm talking about, when I say it won't help even the tiniest bit to lament your bad fate. You must take the spear and put it into the bear's belly, or he eats you. And it's the same with life—the bear will eat those who give up and surrender!

That's what I think, too. But enough of this talking, it only brings the idleness. You better tell me, Father, if you think you are courageous enough to help me with one problem that has been troubling me for a long time already.

God has nothing to do with that, Father—it's probably Satan who had a hand in what happened after. That is, the Baron's spirit stayed imprisoned in the family mansion that became a real house of terror and everybody started to avoid it. Of course, tales about inexhaustible riches hidden in the dungeons under the Blutenreich mansion appeared soon, but nobody of those who decided to go there was ever seen again. Terrible laughter can be heard from that house in the dead of night, as well as laments of women and of children. I'm sure you can imagine what probably takes place there...

Yes, that's exactly what I want, Father. I want you to find the spirit of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich and to banish him from his house and completely out of this world. I would have it done on my own.. well, supernatural powers I can't handle, but what I can handle are bears. Moreover my health isn't what it used to be any more. I'm not the fighter I used to be since that hunt when a black bear broke my knee...
I'm glad you've decided to do that, Father. And no doubt you will be successful!
Farewell, Father. Or better, see you soon. And don't forget—whenever there is a problem, the best solution usually is to put a spear or two into a bear's belly...

I'm glad you have asked, Father. I always settle all my debts. If you are able to banish all the unclean spirits from the Blutenreich mansion, I'll give you one magical item from my large collection and a purse of gold with some magical elixirs that you will certainly appreciate.

Thus, yours is not only my thanks, but also the reward I promised you—take this magic item from my large collection. Perhaps you'll find it useful. A purse of gold and these miraculous elixirs are yours as well.

Inquisitor of the Holy Office is a thief?! I don't want to believe that! What could we expect from the world when even the clerics steal! What a shame, Father!

A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! You should be ashamed of yourself, sir!
Really? That's great news, brother! I was beginning to think that he managed to escape. It was great luck that you came into his way. Thanks, brother—you have my recognition!
Yes, that would be right. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. Let the power be with you. That is to say... the power of the Archangel Gabriel—if you understand me.
It seems to me I helped you in your effort. Thus, I should get some reward!

What?! You request a reward for performing your holy mission?! How awful! As I can see, some of our brothers are interested more in their own goals and benefits than in their true mission. What a shame for all of us!

Death to the hellspawns! I, Gerhard de Blanc, paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, swore that I would not stop my fight till there were no more infernal monsters walking this world! And I'm going to fulfill my oath!
That's a right decision, brother.

I also think so. Did you happen to see a wounded werewolf somewhere around, brother? We've been looking for him since the morning, but we lost his scent. We almost succeeded in killing him, but he was able to escape and hide somewhere. But he couldn't have crept too far away, as he was badly wounded!
If the name of that werewolf was Kenthwaar, you don't have to take care about him any longer—I've finished him.
No, I haven't met any wounded werewolf, brother. But if you want, I'll help you in looking for him, and if I'll find him, I'll kill him!
Excellent, brother. Find him and finish him. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
No, I haven't met any wounded werewolf, brother. And I don't have time to look for him.
Farewell in that case, brother. We must go on searching. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
I promised to get some healing potions for one wounded werewolf, brother.
What?! I must have heard wrong. Have you promised to heal an infernal monster? That's a betrayal! That's a conspiracy! What a heresy! Charge, brothers! Kill this minion of Hell!
I've helped a wounded werewolf, brother. I brought him some healing potions...
What?! I must have heard wrong. Have you really helped that infernal monster? That's a betrayal! That's a conspiracy! What a heresy! Charge, brothers! Kill this minion of Hell!
I'm not interested in your mission, brother—I've my own one. Farewell!
What a shame! How arrogantly and haughtily can some of our brothers behave these days! Search your conscience, brother, and take the way of expiation before it's too late! Farewell!
Hello, brother, have you caught that wounded werewolf? We had no luck...
Yes, I've found and killed that werewolf. The act of God's Justice is finished!
I'm sorry, but I haven't killed that wounded werewolf yet.
Never mind, brother. We must go on in our effort. The werewolf must die!
To tell the truth, I found that werewolf. However, I decided to help him...
What?! I must have heard wrong. Have you really decided to help that infernal monster? That's a betrayal! That's a conspiracy! What a heresy! Charge, brothers! Kill this minion of Hell!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe it! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even regular brothers rob one another!

Really? That's great news, Father! I was starting to think he managed to escape successfully. It was great luck that you came across his path. Thanks, Father—you have my recognition. I'll have to reassess my relationship to the members of the Holy Office—or at least to some of its members.
Farewell, Father. Let the power be with you. That is to say... the power of the Archangel Gabriel—if you understand me.

What?! You request a reward for performing your holy mission?! How awful! As I can see, the members of the Holy Office are interested more in their own goals and benefits than in their true mission. What a shame for all of you!
That's a right decision, sir Knight.

No, I haven't met any wounded werewolf, sir Knight. But if you want, I'll help you in looking for him, and if I'll find him, I'll kill him!
Excellent, Father. Find him and finish him. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
No, I haven't met any wounded werewolf, sir Knight. And I don't have time to look for him.
Farewell in that case, Father. We must go on searching. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
I promised to get some healing potions for one wounded werewolf, sir Knight.
I've helped a wounded werewolf, sir Knight. I brought him some healing potions...
I'm not interested in your mission, sir Knight—I've my own one. Farewell!

What a shame! What an arrogant and haughty behavior can be seen these days in the members of Holy Office! Scrutinize your conscience, Father. Leave the way of expiation before it's too late! Farewell!
Hello, Father, have you caught that wounded werewolf? We had no luck...
Never mind, Father. We must go on in our effort. The werewolf must die!

Really? That's great news, noble lord! I was beginning to think that he managed to escape. It was great luck that you came into his way. Thanks, noble lord, you have my recognition! I'll have to reassess my opinion of the aristocracy, or at least of some nobles who haven't forgotten yet what their holy duty is.
Farewell, noble lord. Let the power be with you. That is to say... the power of the Archangel Gabriel, if you understand me.

What?! You request a reward for performing your holy duty?! How awful! As I can see, the aristocracy is interested more in their own goals and benefits than in the wellbeing of the Realm. What a shame for all of you!

I also think so. Did you happen to see a wounded werewolf somewhere around, noble lord? We've been looking for him since the morning, but we lost his scent. We almost succeeded in killing him, but he was able to escape and hide somewhere. But he couldn't have crept too far away, as he was badly wounded!
Excellent, noble lord. Find him and finish him. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
Farewell in that case, noble lord. We must go on searching. Let the Justice of our Lord be done!
What a shame! How arrogantly and haughtily can the aristocracy of the Realm behave these days! Search your conscience, noble lord, and take the way of expiation before it's too late! Farewell!
Hello, noble lord, have you caught that wounded werewolf? We had no luck...
Never mind, noble lord. We must go on in our effort. The werewolf must die!
Ghurr hungry! Ghurr eat nobody long time! Ghurr smell fresh meat! Ghurr eat you, human!
I won't allow a monster as awful as you to walk this land freely! Die, you infernal demon!
Ghurr very unlucky today, 'cause Ghurr go to hell with empty stomach!

I'm sorry, but I don't think I know any heretics, knight. And even if I knew somebody, I mean somebody who is a really wicked heretic bathing in the blood of innocent children and keen on various awful things and stuff, I'd rather not talk about that too much, you know? The justice's very strange these days, you know, and so I could get myself into really big trouble.

Well, while you're talking about it... once I heard Dietrich, the city grave digger, saying that he knows very well who's behind all the evil afflicting Glatzburg. Someone very distinguished, he said. But he didn't want to tell me the name, because he was afraid he would get in trouble, so he said he'd rather take the secret to the grave with him.
A beggar, Braham was the name I believe, accused you of stealing a silver amulet from him. What can you tell me about that?

What? I'm supposed to steal something from Braham?! Is that what that wicked nasty creature has told you? It's like him. Rubbish! I'll tell you how it was. That drunkard was soaking here for quite some time and he owed me quite a heap of gold! And do you think he bothered to pay me his debts? No way! Whenever I wanted money from him he quibbled, lied and dodged. Because of that I sent one of my goons to get the amulet from him. I took it as a partial payment for the debt he has in the tavern.
Oh so... In that case I'm sorry for bothering you. I was deceived.
You better be careful when talking to him, knight. You never know what lies he will tell you right to your face...
The circumstances are not important. The amulet belongs to Braham. Hand it over immediately or you will face the consequences of your ill-judged deeds!

What?! Are you threatening me?! I'd never say such a thing could happen... Debtors hire paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous to protect their property from the creditors... But as you wish, knight—here is the amulet, take it. I'm not going to get into trouble because of it, you can bet on that. But you should be ashamed.

It seems that Braham misses the amulet very much. He's had it since he was born and it's the only link to his parents who left him when he was a baby. I'd be very grateful to you if you'd return it to him.

You don't expect me to cry for him, valiant knight, do you? Braham is a drunkard and a notorious liar; you can't believe a word he says. But I'm willing to return the amulet to him—when he pays me my 500 gp.
I'll pay the debt. Here is the money.
Well... as you wish, knight. Here is the amulet. But I frankly wonder why you waste time and money on that beggar.
I'd pay the debt for Braham, but I don't have enough money myself just now.
Oh, really? Well, when you have the money, you know where you find me, knight. But I frankly wonder why you'd waste time and money on that beggar.
You want it the hard way, good woman, let it be as you wish—give me the amulet immediately or you will face the consequences of your ill-judged deeds!
I want to pay Braham's debt according to the agreement. Here's your 500 gp.
All right, venerable knight. Here is Braham's amulet. But I frankly wonder you waste time and money on that beggar.
Is there any gambling performed in your tavern a man can use to earn some money?
We play dice here and the Devil's Emissary. You can try it if you have the balls.

Who rules here in Glatzburg? Why, Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of city. His vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin. But don't you want me to tell you my opinion about their relationship to their subjects, especially as for tax collection... The're a couple of sharks when it comes to money!
Who can sell you some supplies here in Glatzburg? Except for you, of course.
Where can you do some shopping in the city? Why do you ask? Isn't my shop good enough for you, knight? In that case you go somewhere else!

I'm sure that when the crisis ends, the only thing we'll have will be the tears in our eyes. Well, maybe not even that. Maybe we'll die—all of us. Why should the common people hope their miserable lives will be saved somehow? Go for a walk in the city and you'll see most of the people don't hope anymore. Sure, you can judge us and tell we don't have enough faith. But even the Grim Reaper can't take anything that you don't have from you. If this is not the End of the World, what the Hell is it then?
I've heard some rumors that the war is about to start. Do you happen to know any detail from your guests here?

Some rumors about the war, eh? Well... you know, my customers sometimes talk much more then they should. Especially when strengthened by spirits, you should see them, knight. They scream one nonsense rumor after another here. Yes, the war is also what they talk about. Mostly the drunkards from the royal army do. I'll tell you, when I see them drunk here under the tables, I'm scared about the fact our fate would be in their hands in the time of war. May Satan take all those stupid wars to Hell! Ehm, excuse me, knight...
Do you happen to know anything about the cult of Children of the New Order from your guests here?

No, I haven't heard anything about the cult of Children of the New Order. Not even about any other heretic cult. I refuse to listen to this talking deliberately, because when you don't know anything, you can't talk about it when interrogated. Not even when tortured.

It's worth mentioning that Tinthan the actor was accused of theft. Some witnesses saw him steal the monstrance from the Bishop's Cathedral. He'll be hanged, that's clear. I think he's on his way to Hillbrandt already, or to some other rat hole at the northern border of the Realm. I say it because he was stealing and swindling here for many years. He pretended to be a renowned actor, but the only acts that really made him famous were thefts and frauds. He owes me a nice amount of gold too.
I'm investigating the assassination of Bishop Trevorius. Do you know anything about it?

Death is always a sad thing. And it's even sadder in the case of monsignor Trevorius. He was the best of the local clerics. He dwarfed the others like a mountain peak. While most of the local clerics, as well as the nobles, roistered and sinned all the time, Bishop Trevorius adhered firmly to the Scriptures and to the Commandments—to all of them. He tried to change things, that's it. He also wanted other priests to behave according to the Scriptures and to the Prophets' sermons. But it's all gone now... I don't know much about his murder, knight. Only, I have heard he was murdered near the Grand Duke's gazebo outside the city walls. What on Earth was he doing there? It's such a lonely place...

I'm sorry about the death of monsignor Trevorius. He was the best from the local clerics. He dwarfed the others like a mountain peak. While most of the local clerics, as well as the nobles, roistered and sinned all the time, Bishop Trevorius adhered firmly to the Scriptures and to the Commandments—to all of them. He tried to change things, that's it. He also wanted other priests to behave according to the Scriptures and to the Prophets' sermons. But it's all gone now... no offense, knight, but the people say you had a hand in that. They say they found you over the Bishop's dead, but still warm body. I don't believe it of course, but such tales can be dangerous...

Undead in the streets of our city are a real disaster. It surprises me the living dead haven't murdered all of us yet. They had more than enough opportunities and nobody does anything about them—like always, to tell the truth. Who cares about the common people? The nobles and burghers are firmly locked in their houses so they don't have to be afraid the living dead would kick their door in during the night and eat their brains. Unlike we poor people have to. But why would I take the trouble to talk about it...

Considering that almost everything gets stolen these days I'm not truly surprised that someone shaved the Commander of Brotherhood of the Righteous. He should have been more careful. What a shame for him—and very bad luck, too.

Hans Thomas Brookwelt being a pervert and a sorcerer as well? I don't want to believe that. But almost anything is possible these days... He has tried nothing on me one way or another—with the help of witchery or without it. That was very lucky for him, I must say. I'd have driven him away from here like a lousy cattle...
I need to get some Chateau de Trebrechette wine. Any ideas where could I get a few bottles?
I don't have any Chateau de Trebrechette wine, knight. And that's all I'll tell you about this matter.
I've heard a suspicion that the maid Jeanette is a witch practicing dark rituals. What do you think about that?

To tell the truth, knight, I think the maid Jeanette really must be hiding something. She came to my inn one day and asked me to get various strange stuff for her—bat wings, serpent skin, moonshine crystal and God knows what else. So I had her thrown out of here, as I don't want to deal with anything smelling of occult wretchedness. And she was glaring at me in so weird a way that shivers were running down my spine. When she was out, she made some sign before she left and—I swear by God I'm telling the truth—not even one customer came to my inn the whole day. She must have bewitched it here. May pox and Black Death get the loathsome witch!
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is looking for a wife. You're single, aren't you?
I haven't heard a word about Grand Duke Heidrick looking for a new wife. And I don't know why I should be interested in it—no matter if I'm married or not.
That's not a very clever decision, good woman. You can't imagine how much pain a human being experiences when tortured. Thus, I'd recommend you to think once more about the answer to my question...
I can't force you to answer my questions, good woman. But I believe there's in fact nothing that could be preventing you from answering me.
You're a clever and also very good-looking woman, Wanda. I assure you that your answer will really help me a lot!
And what will you have? Beer, wine or mead?
A tankard of beer.
One gp, please.
You're welcome, knight. Enjoy your drink. I think it's the most reasonable thing a man can do in these times. Is there anything else I can do for you?
I won't give you the drink in that case. Come when you have some money to spend for drinks. Is there anything else I can do for you?
A chalice of wine.
I won't give you the drink in that case. Come when you have some money to spend on drinks. Is there anything else I can do for you?
We don't offer it here. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Do you want to start playing right away, or would you like to hear the rules first?
In that case you should come when you have at least 10 gp.
I would like to hear the rules—just to be sure.

Several cards will be taken from the pack—it's up to you how many of them it will be, but the highest number is five—whereas one of the cards always is the Devil's Emissary. I'm sorry, knight, but I'm not going to continue any more. I've lost enough money to stay away from gambling for some time. Farewell.

Great.

Let's see, what number I will have...

It seems it's a tie.
It seems I won.
It seems I lost.
What can I do?

What can I do? You won 40 gp.
What can I do? You won 50 gp.

I hoped her premonition wouldn't come true this time, but I was wrong... I returned home one night and my sister was gone... Everything in the room was trashed, it looked like she was desperately trying to defend herself, and there were even traces of blood here and there...
And nobody really started to look for your sister? Neither the Holy Office nor the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous?

He indeed promised to deal with the case immediately, because it's not the first case of kidnapping here in the city, but I haven't heard a word from him since.

No, I don't—I've just noticed those cases are very similar.
I hope nothing happened to her... I tried so hard to get her out of this slum...
Thank you for the information, good woman.
