She came to my inn one day and asked me to get various strange stuff for her—bat wings, serpent skin, moonshine crystal and God knows what else. So I had her thrown out of here, as I don't want to deal with anything smelling of occult wretchedness. And she was glaring at me in so weird a way that shivers were running down my spine. When she was out, she made some sign before she left and—I swear by God I'm telling the truth—not even one customer came to my inn the whole day. She must have bewitched it here. May pox and Black Death get the loathsome witch!
You're welcome, noble lord. Enjoy your drink. I think it's the most reasonable thing a man can do in these times. Is there anything else I can do for you?
All right. The bet is 10 gp, noble lord.

Let's start. Here's our card—the Devil's Emissary. I'll turn it and I will add a second card. Now I'll shuffle them and move each of them to and fro, shuffle again, and which of them could it be? Is it still on the left or is it now on the right? Shuffle them one more time and here we go. So, noble lord, which of them is the Devil's Emissary? I'm sure you watched it vigilantly...
I'm sorry, noble lord, I won't play with you any further. You've cost me lots of money, so I will stay away from gambling for awhile. Is there anything else I can help you with?
I'm sorry, noble lord, but I'm not going to continue any more. I've lost enough money to stay away from gambling for some time. Farewell.
In that case come when you have at least 10 gp, noble lord. Farewell.
As you wish, noble lord. How many cards would you like?
As you wish, noble lord. Farewell.
You hit it, noble lord. Here is your 20 gp.
You didn't guess it right, noble lord. Those 10 gp belong to me.
You're right, noble lord! You guessed it! Here's your 35 gp.
You're right, noble lord! You guessed it! Here's your 50 gp.
You're right, noble lord! You guessed it! Here's your 65 gp.
I'm afraid you can't play then, noble lord. Come when you have at least 10 gp. Farewell.

The game is simple, noble lord. We'll take two dice, each of us will roll one and the one who has the highest number wins. You'll roll your dice first, I'll follow you. There's nothing complicated about it. You can bet 10 gp, 20 gp, 30 gp, 40 gp or 50 gp and you can win the same amount of money. In the case we have the same numbers nobody loses, but also nobody wins anything.
As you wish, noble lord. How much do you want to wager?
So take the dice, noble lord. You roll first.

It was Satan, noble lord! Satan took her and carried her away, to the entrails of the Hell! That is, my sister used to have quite vivid dreams... Premonitions, as someone could say... All she dreamt about came true later in some way. And she had a dream some time ago that Satan appeared in her room in the middle of the night and he took her to the entrails of the Earth, where he chained her to the wall and started to boil her heart in a large cauldron... I hoped her premonition wouldn't come true this time, but I was wrong... I returned home one night and my sister was gone... Everything in the room was trashed, it looked like she was desperately trying to defend herself, and there were even traces of blood here and there...

No, noble lord, nobody did. I even told Master Dieter von Gelbendiel himself about it—he's the local Magister of the Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He indeed promised to deal with the case immediately, because it's not the first case of kidnapping here in the city, but I haven't heard a word from him since.
Yes, noble lord, she was... as far as I can say. But I'm pretty sure she was. O my God... Do you think something terrible might have happened to her because of that?
It's me who should thank you, noble lord. You've returned hope to me. Is there something I can do for you? To bring you a drink or something like that?
But of course, ask your questions, noble lord. What are you interested in?
Farewell, noble lord. And please forgive me my behavior. I had no hope I'd find somebody willing to help me...

Don't you try to look like you're interested in that, noble lord. Nobody wanted to hear about that, although I hurt my knees black and blue when I was begging on them to everybody around to help me find my sister! She was so young... she had all her life before her, she could leave the slum and start to live differently, not like me... I saved some money for her, to give to her dowry; I wanted her to marry well and to get out of this slum our mother tossed us in without mercy. But nobody took pity on me, they even didn't move an eyebrow. They told me my sister is in the hands of God. They put my testimony on record and filed it into a thick file together with dozens of other unsolved cases. Should this be that so-called justice for all? Is that the help to a neighbor in their time of need? Oh my God...

Well, I should have thought that! You want to know how much you will be paid for your services! But as you wish, let's do it your way. I'll give you all the gold I saved for my sister in case you find out what happened to her! Take it or let it be, because there's nothing more I could give you...

I should have thought right away that my money won't smell well to you. What is the price of your justice, noble lord? How much should common people like me pay you to get the attention of someone of your standing?
But of course, noble lord, I'm keeping my mouth shut. Why should I bother to say anything? What can I do for you?

Oh yes, sure... Our Lord in his generosity and grace will bring her back into my house. As well as he brought all those victims that disappeared here and nobody has seen them since. But as you wish, noble lord—don't pay any attention to that. She's only a stupid village girl, after all. Ask your questions then, I'll give you your answers. I'm sure they are very important. Much more important than the life of a young girl unimportant to everybody. So, what can I do for you?

Oh yes, sure... Our Lord in his generosity and grace will bring her back into my house. As well as he brought all those victims that disappeared here and nobody has seen them since. But as you wish, noble lord—don't pay any attention to that. She's only a stupid village girl, after all. Come see my goods. I'm sure it's much more important than the life of a young girl unimportant to everybody.
I... thank you, noble lord. I'd never thought I would see my sister again...

I know there was nothing I could do, noble lord. But it doesn't help me to know that... However, thanks for your prayers. Maybe my sister will find peace in the grave at least. Is there anything I can do for you?
No, noble lord. Ask whatever you want to know. Just excuse me for the tears... I can't stop it...
Excuse me, noble lord, but I'm not in the mood for games. Maybe next time, but I don't want to play just now for sure. Is there anything else I can do for you instead?
Thank you, noble lord. Farewell.
Thank you, noble lord, thank you one hundred times for forgiving me. What can a poor stupid woman do for you?
As you wish, noble lord. What do you need to know from such a poor woman like me?
Farewell, noble lord. And don't be afraid—I won't say a word to anyone, you can be sure about that!

Oh, look who did the devilry bring here. A gentle lord. So, what will you have? What can we do for you in these great times, eh? That is to say, you deserve to be treated like a king for all that the aristocracy have done for us in recent years!
I thought the aristocracy was the best informed of them all... But if you want to know, my name is Wanda Gielwitch. And this is my inn, if you want to know that, too.
Do you think something happened to me? All seems to be in good order, doesn't it? Just look around yourself, noble lord, and tell me, whether I have some reason for hatred and grief!

Sure, this is the speech of a true deputy of the aristocracy, property, property and property again! How right are all those who declare the world is wicked and the aristocracy is rotten to the core, living in wealth and taking care only for their domains! Where is the protection of common people against injustice? Everything is connected to property and people can perish quietly, because nobody cares! Where were the authorities with their helping hand when my sister disappeared without trace? Where were the noble rulers with their laws? Where has all their justice gone, that they so perseveringly enforce with the aid of their soldiers? Down to the mud with many other things not related to their power and their property...

Sure, this is the answer you have always ready. There's something I don't like, so let's put the poor defenseless woman to the stake because she dared to open her mouth and tell something about the splendid aristocracy! But, let it be as you wish, noble lord. I'm a humble sheep in God's herd after all. Forgive a stupid sinner who doesn't know what she's saying...

No, noble lord, you don't understand at all. You just think you know almost everything, but in fact you don't. You have no idea how deep is the despair of losin family! You can't understand how it hurts when your only sister is torn out of your life and nobody cares. I'd wish you'd experience it—both you and all the others who should help the people in need and who rather gather riches instead of that and take care of the goals not being in connection with love to your neighbors!

Not very comfortable for you to hear the truth, eh? But don't be afraid, I won't say anything more. I don't want to give you a handle to use me as an example and show the people what happens to those who oppose the aristocracy. I'm just a poor stupid woman asking you humbly to forgive her.

As you wish, noble lord, I'll shut up. After all—who would be interested in the fate of a poor miserable woman? Please, come in, noble lord. Welcome. I ask you humbly to forgive me. What can I do for you in such an awful rat hole like this tavern is?
Just ask, noble lord. I'll humbly give you all the answers.
Farewell, noble lord. I'm sure all the Saints will protect you, no matter where you go.
Hello, noble lord. Have you already found out what happened to my sister? I'm so trembling here...
I AM patient, noble lord. But it's been such a long time since she disappeared... And hope is getting smaller and smaller day after day! What can I do for you?
Of course, noble lord. What do you need to know?
What do you want, noble lord? I thought I wouldn't see you again. What brings you around to such a rat hole like our place is? What can we do for you?
If you think so, noble lord. I'm a humble sheep in the Lord's herd. So, ask your question.
Farewell, noble lord. Maybe we won't see each other again. Of course it would be Our Lord's will—you must be sick of looking at someone like me.
My best greetings to you, noble lord. What can a poor miserable woman like me do for you? What can I serve to such a precious guest?
Of course you can, noble lord. Ask any question you want. I'll answer all of them gladly.
Farewell, noble lord. Let all the Saints protect you... more than they protected my poor sister.
Duke Drake Lambert rules in Alvaron as the royal governor of city. Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth is the vice-governor.

It's terrible what has happened in the Realm during recent years. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky we have been affected by famine, Black Death, rain of fire, death of the whole royal family, tragic decrease in the number of inhabitants, a flood of monsters and by countless other disasters. To tell you the truth, no doubt people are inclined to believe in delusions and heresy in whatever form. It's bad, of course, and it shouldn't happen, but I understand it...

Yes, quite probably things are as people say—Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is a heretic and a traitor. When I think about what he has done to increase the power of the Brotherhood of the Righteous at the expense of the Inquisition... yes, it makes sense now. Only our Lord knows for sure how many other members of this Order are heretics or heathens! And most of the people here in Alvaron think the same thing. The more they are afraid of what the future will bring to them, because how far can heresy reach when it has already infected the soul of the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?

If you go to the city cemetery, son, you'll find that it's flooded by evil! Living dead feast there on the graves and coffins during the night, ghosts fly through the air of the graveyard and a nameless horror is lurking in the darkest shadows. None of those who decided to go there was ever seen again—only as one of the living dead... The cemetery should be a holy place, where dead should be resting in peace forever!

Grand Duke Drake Lambert set high rewards for killing the werewolves raging not only around the city, but unfortunately also in the streets. Sheriff Henry Portmann pays a reward to those who bring him trophies—the heads of dead werewolves. But I don't think that the measure has any significant influence on the situation...

Baron Mansfeld died some time ago. That wouldn't be so important alone if he weren't a renowned rich noble who gathered a great property thanks to several good decisions—many high noble Houses can only dream about such riches. And even more interesting is the fact that the Baron buried all his riches—a treasure of gold—somewhere around Alvaron not to let it get into the hands of his naughty heirs. I'm sure you can imagine, son, that many people turned every stone around here several times in the effort to find the treasure...
Do you think the Royal Counselor Verenicus could be involved in the murder of Prince Louis?

Do you think the Royal Counselor was involved in the murder of Prince Louis? No, that's nonsense. He was very loyal to King Edward and he was grateful for everything, so why should he attempt to kill the King's only son and the heir to the throne? No, it doesn't make sense...
Do you think the Inquisitor General Commendoni could be a leader of a heretic cult endangering the stability of our Realm?
Cardinal Commendoni being a heretic? No, it doesn't make sense at all... He's the Inquisitor General after all, the head of the Holy Office!

Unfortunately I don't have the slightest idea what deviant heretic lets the werewolves into the city each full moon. I wish I knew something that would help you reveal those criminals, son. However, the only thing I can do is to pray for the success of your effort... Yes, I'll surely do that!
I'm trying to find a way to cure a human from lycanthropy. Do you happen to know something?
I'm convinced there's only one thing you can do for a lycanthropy-infected human to help him—to kill him and pray for the salvation of his soul. Yes, I'd surely do that, if I were you...

Really scary legends are passed on about the mansion of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. Maybe you've already seen it when you walked through the city—it's an awful looking mansion on the edge of Alvaron. People say that an unclean ghost of the Baron lives there as he stayed imprisoned there when Baron von Blutenreich was poisoned and cursed by his thirteenth wife for prospective crimes he committed on a dozen of women he married before and on their children. The Baron was said to be a really strange man, but he was an orderly faithful noble who went to church for mass each week and gave rich charities and contributions to the Church. However, many people wondered how can it be that his wives died one after another, twelve of them in a row. All in all he married thirteen wives and had countless children with them, but none of them lived much longer.

It was very similar with his latest wife—the thirteenth one—but contrary to the others she was executed as the murderer, because she poisoned the dear Baron. She was saying he was a monster who had killed all his previous wives and children and buried them in the cellar of his mansion, but who would listen to the woman who had poisoned her husband? However, the unhappy woman cursed the Baron before her execution so he would never rest in piece. And it seems the curse came true, because really terrible noises can be heard coming from the Baron's mansion, laments and moaning, so nobody goes closer to the mansion neither at day light nor during the night. And those who decided to go there and look for the Baron's riches have never come back.
Heed my advice, Father Gilbert—give me the answer to my question, or you will be very sorry about that. I really mean it!
I ask you frankly, Father—answer my question, please.
You're a wise and experienced man, Father Gilbert. The answer from a person like you would really help me a lot.
Father Gilbert, you're arrested for a well-founded suspicion of the adoration of dark powers and of counterfeiting gold. You'll come with me to be put on fair trial!
What...?! You... you have found out?! But that's impossible... I was so careful! Nobody could know it was me who... oh my God, how is it possible?
You can't hide yourself from the justice, Father. Let's go.
Let's go? But where do you want to go? You can't arrest me like a criminal, like some dirty murderer. I did no harm to anyone. In fact, I'm almost innocent...
And how did you change human excrements into the gold? With the help of infernal powers! You're a heretic!

But... I made no harm to anyone! It was a funny thing for me in the beginning... But when I've found out the powers of Hell serve me, I've decided to use them. Not to do harm to anyone, just to have a little fun. I have neither a lot of resources, not many opportunities for entertainment as a Church scribe... And they told me they will bring me a lot of joy and a real fun if I start to worship them. They tempted me to the bad ways...
Who? The powers of Hell?

Yes, Father! It was them who made me do what I've done... It came out of my hands! Please, don't arrest me. Let me go. I'll run away from the Realm and nobody will ever hear about me again... I'll pay you for that!
I'm sorry, Father, but you're arrested. Let's go!
I'm not interested in money that turns into human excrements after some time. Let's go!
How much would you give me?
All that's left... and it's quite a lot of money! It can be all yours if you let me go!
Hail to you, son. What can a humble servant of our Lord do for you?
I'd like to know who you are.
I'm Father Gilbert, the scribe in the Archbishop's library.
Could I talk to you for a moment? If there's nothing more important you must do, of course...
At your service, son. Ask your questions.
You are a scribe. What is it that you have to do?

Nothing as exciting as fighting murderous monsters and bloodthirsty hellspawns every day, son. A Scribe's work is never-ending copying of various books, scrolls and letters—from the liturgical texts to everyday Church correspondence.
As you wish, son. What's on your mind?
Fare thee well then, son. May the Archangel Gabriel protect you on your way of pursuing divine justice...
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! You should search your conscience, son!

If you go to the city cemetery, brother, you'll find that it's flooded by evil! Living dead feast there on the graves and coffins during the night, ghosts fly through the air of the graveyard and a nameless horror is lurking in the darkest shadows. None of those who decided to go there was ever seen again—only as one of the living dead... The cemetery should be a holy place, where dead should be resting in peace forever!

Baron Mansfeld died some time ago. That wouldn't be so important alone if he weren't a renowned rich noble who gathered a great property thanks to several good decisions—many high noble Houses can only dream about such riches. And even more interesting is the fact that the Baron buried all his riches—a treasure of gold—somewhere around Alvaron not to let it get into the hands of his naughty heirs. I'm sure you can imagine, brother, that many people turned every stone around here several times in the effort to find the treasure...

Unfortunately I don't have the slightest idea what deviant heretic lets the werewolves into the city each full moon. I wish I knew something that would help you reveal those criminals, brother. However, the only thing I can do is to pray for the success of your effort... Yes, I'll surely do that!
Heed my advice, brother Gilbert—give me the answer to my question, or you will be very sorry about that. I really mean it!
I ask you frankly, brother—answer my question, please.
You're a wise and experienced man, brother Gilbert. The answer from a person like you would really help me a lot.
Brother Gilbert, you're arrested for a well-founded suspicion of the adoration of dark powers and of counterfeiting gold. You'll come with me to be put on fair trial!
You can't hide yourself from the justice, brother. Let's go.
I'm sorry, brother, but you're arrested. Let's go!
Hail to you, brother Inquisitor. What can a humble servant of our Lord do for you?
At your service. I know the holy mission of you Brothers Inquisitors depends on questions and especially on answers. Ask your questions then.

Nothing as exciting as searching for the perpetrators of those awful crimes against God and the King, brother. A Scribe's work is a never-ending copying of various books, scrolls and letters—from the liturgical texts to everyday Church correspondence.
As you wish, brother. What's on your mind?
Fare thee well then, brother. May the Archangel Gabriel protect you on your way of pursuing divine justice...

The Inquisitor of the Holy Office and he's a thief?! I don't want to believe that! What can you expect from the world as a whole, when even the clerics steal! You should search your conscience, brother!

Nothing as exciting as administering a vast domain and protecting its safety, son. A scribe's work is a never-ending copying of various books, scrolls and letters from the liturgical texts to everyday Church correspondence.

Aaaahhhh! I'm free at last! So long I've been waiting in the infernal cauldrons for this moment. For the moment when some thief comes and desecrates my grave. That was the only way I could enter this world again. And nobody will stop me now. How can I be executed again when I'm already dead? The time has come to settle the score!
Who are you, creature of Hell?

Who am I? That's hard to tell. I used to be Duke Manfred Gotfried... But it was a long time ago. Now I'm something greater. I'm death personified. I'm the revenge from the beyond. I'm the anger of the cursed ones. And you, mortal, you are going to die.
Wait, wandering soul. Surely there is a possibility of how to send you back to where you came from.
Back to Hell? No, it doesn't seem a good idea to me when I've finally gotten away from there. I have a better idea—I will kill you and will feed on your entrails! You are going to die!
I won't allow such an unholy monster as you are to walk this world!

And what are you going to do about it, you wretched weakling? Are you going to pray so hard that I will die? No, I have a different plan for the following seconds—I will feed on your entrails. You are going to die!
How come you've managed to stay alive for so long here in the underground?

How did I manage to stay alive here for so long? Because I know it better than anybody else does. I know where to get water from and how to obtain some food. I know how and where to hide before the orcs and other monsters. All that I was taught by my father, and he learnt it from my grandfather. I know it here better than on the surface, why, I've spent most of my life here.
Tell me something about this mine.

The iron mine is very old, knight. It has been operating for more than hundred years. My grandfather was one of the first miners that came here to dig for iron ore. Maybe that's why I know it here like the back of my hand. But the last few years mining here has been quite a dangerous job. You have had to dig deeper and deeper for the ore. Now and again the ceilings collapsed and the walls tumbled down. I can't even count how many men died here because of cave-ins. And so I advise you, knight—watch your step! I know what I'm talking about. One wrong step and nobody will ever find you. Not even the orcs, ho, ho.
What do you know about the orcs?

Those orcs are ugly beasts, believe me. I hate them, I hate them all down to a single orc! God damn them for all they've done! If I could I would cut their throats by myself and would spit on them till their damned souls vanish in Hell. Who would have thought they are hiding there in the depths, locked away from the outside world, waiting for somebody to set them free? In the end all those legends and myths about the pagan realms have turned out to be true. Too bad we have lived to see such bad times when the legends are coming to life and changing into the nightmare.
All the time you've been hiding here you spoke to no one?

Yes, I spoke to no-one for all the time I've been hiding here. That is, aside from Joachym, of course. But the truth is that I heard human voices here several times. At first I thought they were soldiers from town fighting against the orcs, but it was not so. Whoever it was, he had to be hand in glove with the orcs. They talked and it seemed the orcs treat them with great respect. I've beaten my brains out vainly over who they could be. Who could do something so vile like collaborating with those infernal monsters? One would think something like that is not even possible!
Are there some legends or myths about the iron mine?

Since my childhood I've heard legends about the pagan realm of Thron that was to be found somewhere underneath the Moonshine Mountains. It's told it was a rich realm full of palaces built of gold and gemstones. But then the Cursed Flame came from somewhere deep and dark and with him the orcs came and conquered Thron. Since then the orcs supposedly have been waiting under the mountains till the Cursed Flame rises again and they follow him to destroy the world. Don't you think, knight, that this legend is scaringly similar to the present reality?
What is that Cursed Flame?
I dunno. The legends are silent about that. But it has to be some ancient evil. Several legends from long ago refer to it...
The realm of Thron? Aren't those only stories for children?

I don't think so. I found some things here in the iron mine that aren't the creation of any man. Ancient things forgotten here long before we came. I believe the realm of Thron existed and is buried somewhere deep.
I have no use for money here in the underground, knight. I'm sorry.
Disobeying the Brotherhood of the Righteous is worse than a crime, Graubner—it's stupidity. Do you know what could happen to you if you behave like this? You had better answer me!
I have to know it, Graubner. I believe you understand my reasons. You will help a good cause if you tell me.
I understand you, Graubner. You are wise and so you don't speak with everyone you meet. But you may trust me. Please, answer me.
Who is that Joachym you speak about?

Joachym is a friend of mine. We have worked here in the mine since we were young. That's one of the reasons why I know it here like the back of my hand and why I've been able to keep out of sight of the orcs. But we've started to run out of supplies lately and Joachym decided to try to steal something from the orcs or hunt down some bats. But he never returned. I greatly fear something has happened to him. Could you look for him, knight?
Alright, I will try to find out what has happened to Joachym.
Thanks, knight. I hope he is just delayed and didn't get into some sort of trouble.
We will see. May I speak with you for a moment?
If you want...
We will see. Bye for now.
We will see. What would you offer me for doing that?
Ehm... I probably have nothing you could need, knight. But maybe you could use the key from the old gate leading to the deepest levels of the iron mines...
I'm sorry, but I have no time to search for your companion. I have an important mission.
What a pity. But well, there's nothing I can do about it. Farewell.
I have bad news for you, good man. Your companion perished and has become a living dead.
What?! No, I do not believe that. Nobody could kill Joachym, he is able to hide in shadows like nobody else.
I'm sorry but it's true. I had to kill him, otherwise he would have killed me.
Alas! What happened to poor Joachym? He had to be found and murdered by the orcs. I curse them a thousand times! But I thank you anyhow. Joachym surely wouldn't want to... live as a damned monster.
May his soul find eternal peace.
Amen! I sincerely thank you again for your help, knight. Take this key as a reward, you can surely use it... It's from the old gate leading to the deepest levels of the iron mine...
Thank you. May I speak with you for a moment?
Thank you. Farewell.

Is that you, Joachym? You have been away for quite a long time. I almost started to worry about you... But wait! You aren't Joachym. You look like a knight. Blood and thunder! How did you find me here?
I'm sorry for frightening you. I didn't expect to find a man living here.

For goodness sake, you scared me to death. I feared those cursed orcs had found me. I thought nobody could discover this secret passage, but it seems I was wrong. Joachym and me have to find somewhere safer. You know, hiding from the orcs means being wary all the time.
Tell me, who are you and what are you doing here when the whole mine is full of the orcs.
Name's Graubner, knight. I'm a miner, or at least I used to be until the orcs came from the depths of the Earth. Since then me and Joachym have been hiding here.
That's not important. Better tell me what you are doing here when the whole mine is full of the orcs.
Name's Graubner, knight. I'm a miner, or at least I used to be until the orcs came from the depths of the Earth. Since then Joachym and me have been hiding here.
I don't believe you. No man can stay alive in the mines for such a long time without being detected by the orcs.

Are you trying to suggest I'm a spy for the orcs? That I band with the orcs? Are you telling me this? No, it's not like that. I deeply hate the orcs. They have taken everything I had from me. They changed my life into a hell on Earth. And then you come and start to accuse me of conspiring with them!
I'm sorry, I didn't really mean it. I'm just surprised you've managed to live here for so long without being caught by orcs.

I know it here better than on the surface, knight. Why, I've spent most of my life here. And when the orcs poured out from the depths of the Earth and started killing on sight, Joachym and me hid in one of the secret passages and then waited to see what would happen. When we found out that orcs have spread throughout the mine, we understood nobody would come from Hillbrandt to help us. We didn't know what happened and so we've rather stayed here. And we have been hiding here with Joachym since that.
You are not going to deceive me. You are conspiring with the orcs and you will die for that!
Have you found what happened to Joachym, knight? I must know what happened.
Not yet, good man. But do not fear, I will find out.
I'm sorry, but it is true.
May I speak with you for a moment?
About what?
I'm glad to hear that...
What do you want, knight? Buzz off and let me be.
It concerns your friend Joachym. I've found him. But regrettably he is a living dead now.
What?! No, I do not believe that. Nobody could kill Joachym, he is able to hide in the shadows like nobody else.
I have nothing to tell you. Go away, I have no time for you!
Hardly so. I've decided to kill you!
Poor Joachym. We had been hiding from orcs together for so long, and now he met so terrible fate. But I thank you anyhow, knight, for not letting him to his own ill-fated destiny.
You are welcome. Farewell.
You may rely upon me. Farewell.

The iron mine is very old, Father. It has been operating for more than hundred years. My grandfather was one of the first miners that came here to dig for iron ore. Maybe that's why I know it here like the back of my hand. But the last few years mining here has been quite a dangerous job. You have had to dig deeper and deeper for the ore. Now and again the ceilings collapsed and the walls tumbled down. I can't even count how many men died here because of cave-ins. And so I advise you, Father—watch your step! I know what I'm talking about. One wrong step and nobody will ever find you. Not even the orcs, ho, ho.

Since my childhood I've heard legends about the pagan realm of Thron that was to be found somewhere underneath the Moonshine Mountains. It's told it was a rich realm full of palaces built of gold and gemstones. But then the Cursed Flame came from somewhere deep and dark and with him the orcs came and conquered Thron. Since then the orcs supposedly have been waiting under the mountains till the Cursed Flame rises again and they follow him to destroy the world. Don't you think, Father, that this legend is scaringly similar to the present reality?
I have no use for money here in the underground, Father. I'm sorry.
Disobeying the Inquisition is a high crime, Graubner. Do you know what could happen to you if you behave so? It's better that you should answer me!

Joachym is a friend of mine. We have worked here in the mine since we were young. That's one of the reasons why I know it here like the back of my hand and why I've been able to keep out of sight of the orcs. But we've started to run out of supplies lately and Joachym decided to try to steal something from the orcs or hunt down some bats. But he never returned. I greatly fear something has happened to him. Could you look for him, Father?
Thanks, Father. I hope he is just delayed and didn't get into some sort of trouble.
Ehm... I probably have nothing you would need, Father. But maybe you could use the key from the old gate leading to the deepest levels of the iron mines...
Amen! I sincerely thank you again for your help, Father. Take this key as a reward, surely you can use it... It's from the old gate leading to the deepest levels of the iron mine...

Is that you, Joachym? You have been away for quite a long time. I almost started to worry about you... But wait! You aren't Joachym. You look like some priest. Blood and thunder! How did you find me here?
Name's Graubner, Father. I'm a miner, or at least I used to be until the orcs came from the depths of the Earth. Since then me and Joachym have been hiding here.
Name's Graubner, Father. I'm a miner, or at least I used to be until the orcs came from the depths of the Earth. Since then Joachym and me have been hiding here.

I know it here better than on the surface, Father. Why, I've spent most of my life here. And when the orcs poured out from the depths of the Earth and started killing on sight, Joachym and me hid in one of the secret passages and then waited to see what would happen. When we found out that orcs have spread throughout the mine, we understood nobody would come from Hillbrandt to help us. We didn't know what happened and so we've rather stayed here. And we have been hiding here with Joachym since that.
Have you found what happened to Joachym, Father? I must know what happened.
And about what?
What do you want, Father? Buzz off and let me be.
Poor Joachym. We had been hiding from orcs together for so long, and now he met so terrible fate. But I thank you anyhow, Father, for not letting him to his own ill-fated destiny.

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Downay, who is accused of heresy, of congress with the devil and of conspiring against God and the King. I hereby ask the prosecutor to speak. Please, my son.
Thank you, Your Honor. With your leave I'd like to present the evidence against the defendant.
Very well, present your evidence. Let the truth be told!

Investigation has shown that the defendant Downay was led astray and has sold himself out to dark powers to be their humble servant. This was attested by the old man named Balthazar, who heard Downay boasting about a new order coming soon and its children ruling the world. This proves beyond reasonable doubt that the gardener belongs to the cult of the Children of the New Order.

Really a terrible case of heresy! Belonging to the cult that seeks to overthrow the Earthly Kingdom of God is the most disgusting crime. But this evidence is not enough to prove the guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Does the prosecution has any other evidence?

Yes, Your Honor. During the interrogation with the use of torture Downay confessed he actually was in the service of the cult of the Children of the New Order and did many terrible crimes in their name. He assisted with preparing of a mass celebrating Hell this spring. All the dark priests of that cult have met on that mass.

Appaling! Look at all the terrible atrocities the foul heretic perpetrated! It's not necessary to present any other evidence. His guilt has been proven beyond reasonable doubt. And since the heresy is rooted really deep in the heart of this unfaithful man I don't see any other choice than to ignite the flames of justice and let them purify the soul of his sinful body and purge it of all the abhorrence he committed. This is the mercy the Holy Mother Church may bring to the people who have sinned. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence defendant Downay to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Sven Larsen, who is accused of murdering paladin Eradim d'Chambrie. I hereby ask the prosecutor to speak. Please, my son, come forward.
Yes, present your evidence to the court. Let the truth be told!

Paladin Eradim d'Chambrie was insidiously murdered by an unknown shooter hiding not far away from the place where I had just been talking with the paladin. The master armorer Leon van den Brooks identified the arrow that killed the paladin as the arrow he custom-made per order of the defendant Sven Larsen.

Hmm... It seems the defendant really is an assassin. If he had obtained the murderous weapon in order to commit such a disgusting crime as the assassination, then there remains not much to resolve. But tell me, my son, does the prosecution have any other evidence?
Yes, it's just so, Your Honor. After being arrested and put to torture the defendant Sven Larsen confessed that he actually committed the murder, and even that he did it for a payment.

Really? How disgusting case of a hideous treachery! Disgusting in the same way the First Prophet was betrayed by cursed Malachiah, who denounced him to the Erebornians for 33 gold pieces. There is enough evidence for the court to pass a sentence. And I don't see any other choice of how to free the soul of Sven Larsen of the mortal sin than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Sven Larsen to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Duke Verenicus, who is accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. I hereby ask the prosecutor to speak. Please, my son, come forward.

Duke Verenicus is accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King based on the confession of two persons who saw him two years ago when he willfully allowed unknown men into the royal palace and then performed an unclean rite with them in the chambers of Prince Louis. Everyone knows the results of their terrible acts—Prince Louis was found dead the other day, lying in his bed without signs of life.

Appaling! Look at that man; look at those terrible crimes he committed while His Majesty King Edward II was fostering him. See how he abused confidence of our good monarch and how he betrayed him. How he sold his soul to Hell and with his shameful deeds contributed to the passing of Crown Prince Louis and King Edward himself. God sees this man and is angry with him for letting his soul to be stained by so many mortal sins. Nevertheless he wishes the man to return into the God's herd and his sins to be forgiven—through the executioner's stake. But in order to accomplish that additional evidence must be shown. Tell me, my son, has the prosecution any other evidence?

Yes, it is so. Your Honor, allow me to present the highest proof which will show the guilt of the defendant beyond all doubt. The defendant pleaded guilty to all his crimes and acknowledged that all that has been spoken against him is the truth and nothing else.

How wicked! That shameless heretic committed a really disgusting treason. And not only against the royal family whom he should have faithfully served, but also against God himself, when as a cunning counselor conspired with the powers of darkness and brought the soul of Prince Louis to their dark altar. There was enough evidence of the guilt of the royal counselor Verenicus presented to this court. And I don't see any other choice how to relieve his soul of the mortal sin than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence the royal counselor Verenicus to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Father Gilbert, who is accused of heresy, worshiping the powers of darkness and of the forgery of gold. I hereby ask the prosecution to speak. Please, my son.
Yes, present your evidence. Let the truth be told and nothing to be hidden before the God's sight!
The shadow of the suspicion first fell on a beggar named Beckham. But during the interrogation he confessed he stole the forged gold from Father Gilbert.
Continue, my son.
On the basis of this evidence Father Gilbert was arrested and immediately and voluntarily pleaded guilty of his crimes.

Did he really plead guilty? I'm glad to hear that. Hardly any heretic finds the courage to voluntarily commit himself to God, to expiate and thus to find the way to the eternal kingdom of Heaven through purgatory. And we won't disappoint our brother. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Father Gilbert to be burned to death. Let the flames of justice be ignited and his soul purified of the sinful body. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger, who is accused of grave robbing. I hereby ask the prosecutor to speak. Please, my son.
Yes, present your evidence to the Inquisitorial court. Let the truth be told!

Well... It's beyond all doubt that Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger committed the crimes he is accused of. His boots have incriminated him, being muddy with clay, which can be found at only one place—at the city cemetery near one of the robbed graves.

That's disgusting! Look, all you good people, at this man and tell me, if there is any worse crime against the dead than to defame their graves and steal their belongings. It's a terrible work of Satan, the seed of sin and of moral degeneration. Even this evidence alone is enough for God to condemn the actions of this man. But I have to satisfy laws of God and Church and ask the prosecution if he has any other evidence against the defendant, which would prove him guilty. Well, son, do you have any other evidence of the defendant's guilt?
Certainly, Your Honor. I have the highest proof—the defendant's confession! When arrested, Steinger confessed he really committed those terrible crimes in an effort to obtain unjust enrichment.

Really? I'm glad to hear that the defendant voluntarily confessed to his crimes. It shows that his soul is not lost yet and yearns for redemption. And in this case I'm willing to give the defendant a chance to relieve his soul of all sins—to ignite the flames of justice that will burn his sinful body and let his soul enter purgatory. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!

All stand up, the Court of the Inquisition is about to start. I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Vick Length, who is accused of grave robbing and of grave desecration. I hereby ask the prosecution to speak. Please, my son.
Well... Based on the confession of Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger it was possible to find out it was Vick Length who made him rob the graves at the city cemetery in the vicinity of the city.

Really? In that case we now look in the face of a man who detests nothing, because as the First Prophet said—ever so little a sin is like a murder. We face the man who doesn't detest to decry a remembrance of the deceased by destroying their graves, disturbing the peace of the dead and by stealing the belongings of their consecrated bodies. How monstrous! How foul! How depraved! Nevertheless I have to ask the prosecutor if he has any other proof supporting the charge. Do you have any other evidence on which basis we might find the defendant Vick Length guilty?

Certainly, Your Honor. The prosecution has managed to get the tradesman Imam ab Sahab's confession. He testified that Vick Length tried to sell him some jewelry stolen from the grave of Baron Mansfeld.

In that case there is no doubt about the guilt of the defendant. Evidence submitted by the prosecutor proves Length's guilt beyond reasonable doubt. And I don't see any other choice how to free the soul of Vick Length of so many sins than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, judge Gregorius, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Vick Length to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, my son!
Can the court see that malicious arrow?
Of course. Here it is!
Unfortunately, I don't have it with me.
I ask the prosecution, if they've brought to the court the deadly arrow of Sven Larsen?
In that case I suspend the trial until the prosecution brings the deadly arrow. Otherwise I can't accept the arrow as an evidence against Sven Larsen.

I completely agree with the contention of Cardinal Commendoni. He is convinced this is not a crisis, but an ordeal to try our loyalty and faith, which the people of Ultherst have been subjected to, similar to that of Saint Benedict when the Devil tempted him on the Mount of Makrabij. We have to stand the test and prove we deserve the love of our Lord. And that's the task of the Holy Office, my son. We are to carry the banner of God's justice; we have the power to cleanse those who have gone astray with the purifying flames of justice. If the inquisitors administer their holy mission with the verve and diligence of true servants of God, I do not fear for the Realm. I know you as a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous think differently, but it's true.
I've heard some rumors the war is going to start. Do you know anything about it?
I'm sorry, but military affairs are not my concern, my son. Hence I can't answer your question. Try to ask someone more competent.
What do you think of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert? Is he really a heretic as they say?

The truth is there are not many people here in Alvaron that would believe the Grand Master is innocent. Many a person thinks he's mixed up in a conspiracy against God and the King. Whatever the truth is, I think he has earned it mainly by his great efforts to suppress the jurisdiction of the Inquisition. It may be that he has acted out of honest reasons, but it also may be quite opposite. I can't judge that. In any case if evidence speaks against him, there's nothing to discuss.

To take interest in the Fallen Angels is somewhat dangerous these days, my son. You never know whose attention you will attract. But to answer you—the Fallen Angels are the most dreadful servants of the Dark Prince of Hell. They are the former angels, punished by God for their sins when they along with Satan the Tempter plotted treason against God Almighty. The Holy Scripture says they were stricken down and bound in Hell to suffer there forever for their sins. Since then they have been trying to get back to seize rule over the world and the heaven. There are four—Arthamon, Lord of defeat, Baphomet, the master of madness, Cerdie, the wanton succubus, and Archangel Azrael, the devil's emissary and evil's advocate. Be on the watch for them, because they are the archenemies of the Holy Mother Church, my son!
Do you think it possible, Your Honor, to summon the Fallen Angels? To bring them into this world?
No, it's impossible, my son. It's impeded by all that the earthly kingdom is built on. It would deny all that the church doctrine teaches us!
Thank you, Your Honor.
You're welcome, my son.
If I suspected someone from heresy I wouldn't hesitate to investigate that suspicion immediately and support it by appropriate evidence. But anyhow, I commend you for your zeal.

So, you are searching for the cult of the Children of the New Order, my son. I'm greatly alarmed to hear this. Why, that cult was destroyed several centuries ago. And moreover, it had never acted in the territory of the Realm, but only in the Empire. I hope your suspicion will eventually prove false. It would be really dreadful.

I'm greatly grieving for what has happened to the city cemetery, my son. And especially to the royal crypt. For several years nobody has been able to get inside because its entrance is sealed by an infernal sigil of evil. It happened not long after Prince Louis was entombed there, along with his royal daughters, princesses Diana, Raphaela and Theresie. I shudder to think what infamies may be going on inside.

No, I don't think Verenicus is mixed up in the murder of Princ Louis. Two young servant girls from the royal palace were proven guilty of that crime and convicted of witchcraft and heresy. It's true that one of them said at first the murderer was in fact Verenicus, but when put to torture, she took her confession back and pleaded guilty. The case is closed and it's useless to put mind to it any more.
What? You ask me if the Inquisitor General is a heretic? Is it some bad joke?
No, it's not a joke. I'm serious.

Have you gone mad, my son? I advise you to consider such questions carefully before you ask them. You could get into serious trouble. I've heard about your achievements in Hillbrandt and Glatzburg. But the Inquisitor General? No, it can't be!
I need to get the confession of a dead person. You wouldn't be able to advise me, would you?
I surely won't help you to get the confession of a dead person, my son. And I recommend you warmly to stay away from such thoughts, because they could get you beyond the border of lawfulness.
Do you know any way to improve a man's memory?

I personally suggest iron maiden for improving the memory, my son. When the iron prickers start to pierce the body of the interrogated, the memory returns to him quite fast. But you may also effectively use the rack or strappado, apart from pillory.
In the case of a stryx I wouldn't exert myself with removal of the curse, son. Stryxes are cursed beasts concerned only with blood and nothing else. You would do best if you burnt it to dust.
I'm searching for a way to cure a man of lycantrophy. Would you be able to help me?

I wouldn't care for saving the soul of a man infected with lycantrophy and I would give up its salvation to God. You have only to remove the tainted body away from the unfortunate soul and leave the rest to Divine Providence. Believe me, my son—that is the best way.
That's all. Farewell.

Wait a moment, my son. I'd like to ask you for help with a case. It concerns a certain Juhasz Gotherr, who is the city librarian and the keeper of the records. He was accused of heresy because it turned out he is the high priest of the cult of the Pagan Night. That cult struggles for the return of the pagan gods. When arrested, Gotherr killed the Inquisitor and ran away. Now he's hiding at some unknown place.
And you want me to find him and to put him in chains, am I right?

Yes, my son, you are right. We have to find him at any cost and bring him to justice. We cannot allow anyone to blaspheme this way and at the same time to insult the Inquisition. Juhasz Gotherr must be caught and punished.
All right, I'll take care of it. Juhasz Gotherr will be caught.
I thank you for the help, son. I knew I could rely on you. God bless you.
Will I be somehow rewarded for catching Juhasz Gotherr?
Certainly, my son. You will have the honor to serve God and you will do a good deed which will surely help your sinful soul. What more could a humble faithful man want, am I right?
I'm sorry, but I have no time for that.
I understand. Well, what can I do? I won't trouble you with it any more. Farewell.
In that case I have good news for you, Your Honor. I've already found Juhasz Gotherr.
Really? That's great news, son! I've almost lost all hope that justice will be served to the fallen soul. Is he in chains?
Regrettably not, Your Honor. I had to kill him. He resisted me when I tried to arrest him.

Oh no... Another soul has fallen without hope for purity and eternal redemption. It greatly grieves me, because God lost another sheep that was unable to return to his herd. But there's nothing we can do about it now. I thank you anyway, my son. You did really well.
You are welcome, son. I should thank you instead. God be with you.
Farewell, son.
Come on, son. Bribery is a mortal sin.
Better answer me, Your Honor. You will avoid great trouble, believe me!
I ask you sincerely, Your Honor, to overcome any possible aversion to me and answer my questions. You will help a good cause!
You're renowned for your wisdom far and wide, Your Honor. I would be honored if you would answer my question.
I'd like to charge the gardener Downay with heresy, Your Honor.
Do you have enough evidence for that, my son?

Yes, I do. The old man Balthazar confessed he saw Downay one evening threatening people with a speedy coming of some new order, whose children shall rule the world—supposedly he's one of them. That's clear proof that he belongs to the heretical cult of the Children of the New Order!

Hmm... It surprises me such a common man should declare his support for the cult dead for several centuries. But the proof is clear. In that case I bring the charge of heresy against Downay. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
Thank you, Your Honor. Farewell.
I'd like to charge Sven Larsen with the murder of Paladin Eradim d'Chambrie, Your Honor.
Murder, you say? And do you have enough evidence for that?
Yes, I do. Paladin Eradim d'Chambrie was killed by a treacherous arrow, identified by the master armorer Leon van den Brooks as the arrow he custom-made for Sven Larsen.
Hmm... It seems this proof is clear. In that case I bring the charge of murder against Sven Larsen. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge the First Knight Rodrigo de Velacor with murder of His Majesty King Edward II, Your Honor.

What did you say? You want to accuse Don Rodrigo de Velacor of murdering King Edward? That's a very serious allegation. Don Rodrigo is one of the foremost men in the Realm and moreover he is presently the provisory head of the kingdom. Do you have enough evidence for your claim, my son?

Yes, I do. I have the confession of the chamberlain Trisstan, who saw Rodrigo de Velacor in the act. Moreover, I found out that the King wounded his murderer during their fight. Rodrigo de Velacor has scratches on his face conforming to that. And then I got the testimony of Cardinal Gustaph Letti, whom the First Knight confessed to with his secret.

That's very alarming. It seems the evidence presented by you speaks clearly. But I cannot imagine any motive that could move the First Knight to murder. Why, he was the protector of the King! But there's nothing we can do about it now. In the light of your evidence I bring the charge of murdering His Majesty King Edward II against Don Rodrigo de Velacor. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge brother Gilbert with heresy and forgery of gold, Your Honor.

So, you'd like to bring the charge against brother Gilbert from the archiepiscopal library. Hmm... That's alarming. We must be cautious and very careful when accusing a priest. The Holy Mother Church may suffer for it in the eyes of the faithful. Do you have enough evidence for your claim, my son?
Yes, I do. Beckham the beggar was caught trying to use the forged gold. But when interrogated he confessed that he'd stolen the gold from brother Gilbert.

Hmm... It seems the evidence speaks clearly, although it may not be absolutely convincing. All right, I bring the charge of heresy and of forgery of gold against brother Gilbert. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger with grave robbing, Your Honor.
I'm glad to hear that. But do you have enough evidence for your claim, my son?
Yes, I do. Steinger's boots are stained with an unique clay which can be found only at one place in the vicinity of Alvaron—at the city cemetery near one of the robbed graves.
Hmm... It seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring the charge of robbing and desecrating graves against Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Vick Length with grave robbing, Your Honor.
Yes, I do. Vick Length has been denounced by his accomplice Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger. He confessed that they both partook in grave robbing to an equal extent.
Hmm... It seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring the charge of robbing and desecrating graves against Vick Length. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
Yes, I do. The tradesman Ihman ab Sahab confessed that Vick Length tried to sell him some jewelry with which Baron Mansfeld was entombed.

Yes, I do. The tradesman Ihman ab Sahab confessed that Vick Length tried to sell him some jewelry with which Baron Mansfeld was entombed. Moreover, his accomplice Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger has denounced Vick Length and confessed that they both partook in grave robbing to an equal extent.
I'd like to charge Norman the butcher with murdering Ron Burton, Your Honor.
Yes, I do. Salena Flock confessed she bought some items from the butcher Norman, and William Burton maintains those items belonged to his missing brother.
Hmm... It seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring the charge of murder against the butcher Norman. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Bates the innkeeper with murdering Ron Burton, Your Honor.
Bates the innkeeper? From the King's Road Inn? He makes a great goulash... What evidence do you have against him, my son?

When I tried to arrest him the butcher Norman confessed that he along with the innkeeper Bates had been killing customers of Bates' inn and that they had been making various dishes from their meat then... For example the famous goulash!
My God! Goulash you say? That great goulash I ate in his inn was made of human meat?! My God, it makes me sick.
You look somewhat pale, Your Honor. Breathe deeply. Shall I assume I have your consent with arresting Bates the innkeeper?
Yes, for goodness sake! Of course! I bring the charge of murder against Bates. Arrest him! My God, I feel so sick...
Thank you, Your Honor. You should better go get some fresh air.
Yes, I'll do it. My God! I won't touch any meat as long as I live...
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against the gardener Downay.
It's my duty as an Inquisitorial judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment, my son.

Yes, I do. Downay boasted about a new order coming soon and its children ruling the world. This proves beyond a reasonable doubt that the gardener belongs to the cult of the Children of the New Order. Moreover, Downay pleaded guilty of heresy when arrested.
It seems the evidence speaks clearly, son. Thereby I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Downay the Gardener.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Sven Larsen.

Yes, I do. It's beyond reasonable doubt that Sven Larsen perpetrated the murder of Paladin Eradim d'Chambrie. The results of the investigation suggest he killed him by an arrow, custom-made for him by Leon van den Brooks. After Sven Larsen was arrested and put to torture, he confessed he really committed the crime.
It seems the evidence speaks clearly, son. Thereby I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Sven Larsen. The court is going to sit immediately.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against the royal counselor Verenicus.

Yes, I do. I've managed to get the confession of two persons who testified that two years ago Duke Verenicus had allowed two unknown men into the royal palace and then performed a heretical rite with them in the chambers of Prince Louis. That rite led to the tragic death of the Crown Prince, as is commonly known.

Really? But that's a terrible case of heresy! I'd never thought that the royal counselor Verenicus... But your evidence speaks clearly, son. Thereby I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Duke Verenicus. The court is going to sit immediately.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against brother Gilbert.

Yes, I do. It's beyond reasonable doubt that brother Gilbert had used infernal powers to change human ordure into gold and then paid with it as if it were real gold in an effort to obtain unjust enrichment. He pleaded guilty to his crime when arrested.

Your evidence speaks clearly, son, even if it is somewhat shocking news. I myself have borrowed some money from brother Gilbert... In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant brother Gilbert. The court is going to sit immediately.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger.

Yes, I do. It's beyond reasonable doubt that Steinger partook in the grave robbing at the city cemetery in the vicinity of Alvaron. His boots have incriminated him, being stained with clay, which can be found only at one place—at the city cemetery near one of the robbed graves. Moreover Steinger pleaded guilty to his crimes when I arrested him.

It seems your evidence speaks clearly, son. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger. The court is going to sit immediately.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Vick Length.

Yes, I do. It's beyond reasonable doubt that Vick Length had organized and masterminded the robbing of graves at the city cemetery in the vicinity of the city. He has been incriminated by the confession of his accomplice Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger and the confession of the tradesman Ihman ab Sahab, to whom Vick Length tried to sell some jewelry stolen from the grave of Baron Mansfeld.
It seems your evidence speaks clearly, son. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against the defendant Vick Length. The court is going to sit immediately.
I've captured Juhasz Gotherr as I promised to you.
Really? That's great news, son! I'd almost lost all hope that justice would be served on the fallen soul. Is he in chains?
Regrettably not, Your Honor. I had to kill him. He resisted arrest.

Oh no... Another soul has fallen without hope for purity and eternal redemption. It greatly grieves me, because God has lost another sheep that was unable to return to his herd. But there's nothing we can do about it now. I thank you anyway, my son. You did really well.
Your're welcome, son. I should thank you. May I reward you somehow for your service and help you in your holy mission?
And who might you be, my son? I don't remember seeing you here before. But by all accounts it seems you are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. To which chapter do you belong?
Presently I'm on a special mission, Father. I've arrived in Alvaron quite recently.

Then I understand. I'm pleased to meet you, son. I'm Father Gregorius, the curial judge of Alvaron. If your mission is connected with administering justice, then I think we will cooperate very closely, because I give orders to arrest people accused of heresy and on the basis of submitted evidence I order a trial to be held in particular cases. Tell me, what is your mission here?
I am searching for members of the cult of the Children of the New Order, Your Honor.

The Children of the New Order? That's a very ancient cult, my son. It was supposed to have been wiped out entirely during the Hundred Years War. Moreover, the history of this cult does not touch the history of Ultherst. All the more I'm surprised by your words. It seems heresy knows no bounds—neither in geography nor in time. It exists independently of the place and time and spreads as sickness. You do well to fight that cult, my son. You have my blessing and all the help possible.
You are welcome, my son. Is there something I may do for you now?
I'd like to ask you several questions, Father.
Certainly, my son. Ask about anything you are interested in. I will gladly satisfy your curiosity by proper answers—as far as I can.
I don't think so, Your Honor. But we will surely meet again. Farewell for now.
Farewell, my son. And take care of yourself. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself guard you.
If you wouldn't be offended, I'd like to keep silent about my mission. The less people know about it the better.
Maybe you are right, son. After all it's your case, not mine—at least for now. But regardless of what your mission here is, I bless you and offer you all the help I'm capable of giving.
Thank you, Your Honor. I'm sure your offer will be of great help.
Do not thank me, son. Is there something I may do for you just now?
Yes. I'd like to ask you several questions.
Thank you, Your Honor. We will surely meet again. Farewell for now.
Farewell, my son. And take care of yourself. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself guard you as you perform your holy duties.

Is it you, my dear son? I'm glad to see you again. How is your search for the members of the cult of the Children of the New Order going? I hope you are being successful. Heresy has to be weeded out and uprooted entirely. May I be of help somehow?
I'd like to speak with you, Your Honor.
Well then, speak, my son. I will be glad to give you your answers, if it's in my powers.
No, I don't think so. Farewell.
Is it you, my dear son? I'm glad to see you again. How is your investigation going? I hope you are being successful. Heresy has to be weeded out and uprooted entirely. May I be of help somehow?
Well then, speak my son. I will be glad to give you your answers, if it's in my powers.
I'd like to accuse Seneschal Jean de Guise of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King, Your Honor.

You want to accuse Seneschal Jean de Guise of heresy? Hmm... I won't conceal that it will surely kindle the flame of struggle between the Holy Inquisition and the Brotherhood of the Righteous even more. Do you have enough evidence for such an accusation, son?

Yes, I do. According to the confession of Sven Larsen Seneschal Jean de Guise ordered the murder of the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie because the paladin decided to denounce the Seneschal to the Inquisition. Then I managed to get the confession of Seneschal's underling Downay who confessed he perpetrated many disgusting crimes at Seneschal's bidding. And finally I have the confession of the royal counselor Verenicus who pleaded he threw a dark curse upon Prince Louis together with Jean de Guise two years ago!
Dreadful! If all you have just told me is really true, then Seneschal Jean de Guise is the fiercest heretic I've ever met. You have my permission to arrest him. The truth must come to light!
I'd like to accuse Duke Verenicus of Khentt of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King, Your Honor.
You want to accuse the royal counselor Verenicus of heresy? I won't conceal I regard him as my friend. What evidence of heresy do you have against such a blameless man?!

According to the confessions of the former royal chamber-maids Kathryn Winhold and Corin Morray Duke Verenicus has displeased God and the King when he together with Jean de Guise threw a dark curse upon Prince Louis!
I can't believe that, son. I'm well aware Corin Morray herself was accused of the crime you're speaking about on the basis of the confession of Kathryn Winhold...
But in fact it happened exactly the other way round, Your Honor. The confession was forced from her by torturing her.
Even if it was true, I couldn't accept the confession of Kathryn Winhold as a proof—she's dead!
The Codex of Inquisition doesn't say a confession of a dead person can't be used as a proper evidence. Or does it?

Well... you're right, brother. If I didn't accept that evidence I would be committing a procedural error. You have my permission to arrest Duke Verenicus of Khentt, then. But I firmly trust your evidence is based on truth.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I'm shocked! Go confess your sins immediately, son! I won't allow this!

I wholly agree with the contention of Cardinal Commendoni. He is convinced this is not a crisis, but an ordeal to try our loyalty and faith, which the people of Ultherst have been subjected to same as Saint Benedict was when the Devil tempted him on the Mount of Makrabij. We have to stand the test and prove we deserve the love of our Lord. And that's the task of us, the inquisitors, my son. We are to carry the banner of God's justice; we have the power to cleanse those who has gone astray by the purifying flames of justice. If we administer our holy mission with verve and diligence of true servants of God, I do not fear for the Realm.
Certainly, my son. You will have the honor to serve God and you will fulfil your holy mission. What more could a priest want?
And who may you be, my son? I don't remember seeing you here before. But by all accounts it seems you are an inquisitor. To which curia do you belong?
Presently to the local curia, but I've arrived quite recently.

Then I understand. I'm pleased to meet you, son. I'm Father Gregorius, the curial judge of Alvaron. I think we will cooperate very closely. I give the curial inquisitors orders to arrest persons accused of heresy and on the basis of evidence submitted by the prosecutors I order a trial to be held in the particular case. Tell me, what is your mission here?
Farewell, my son. And take care of yourself. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself guard you in your holy mission.
As a Curial Inquisitor I ask you for one inquisitorial investigator to help me with my holy mission.
As you wish, my son. I will call one of our brothers immediately.
The Inquisitor of the Holy Office steals? I'm shocked! Go and confess your sins immediately, brother. I will not allow this!

I completely agree with the contention of Cardinal Commendoni. He is convinced this is not a crisis, but an ordeal to try our loyalty and faith, which the people of Ultherst have been subjected to, similar to that of Saint Benedict when the Devil tempted him on the Mount of Makrabij. We have to stand the test and prove we deserve the love of our Lord. And that's the task of the Holy Office, my son. We are to carry the banner of God's justice; we have the power to cleanse those who have gone astray with the purifying flames of justice. If the inquisitors administer their holy mission with verve and diligence of true servants of God, I do not fear for the Realm.
And who may you be, my son? I don't remember seeing you here before. But by all accounts it seems you are a noble. Where is your domain?
Farewell, my son. And take care of yourself. May the Archangel Gabriel himself guard you.
A noble man steals?! I'm shocked! Go confess your sins immediately, son! I won't allow something like that!

Did You really manage to do it? You really killed all those infernal monsters out there, right? In that case please accept my humblest apology. I wronged you and behaved in a way no real servant of God should behave. I'm sorry.
That's all right, my son. We all sin now and then.
You are right, brother. I'm going to do penance immediately. You proved to me that not all our brothers forgot their real mission—which is to fight evil in all its forms. Farewell.
Brother, you are bleeding! May I ask you what happened to you and what mission has led you to this desolate place?

You ask me what has led me here, brother? Then know that I've been led here by the mere Holy Mission of Divine Justice that many of our brothers cast aside the instant they started to fear for their life. Oh God, what a shame—paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous fear for their life! You and your likes hide in the safety of the Brotherhood's fortresses rather than stand in the face of infernal monsters with sword in your hand, although hellspawns are sprawling around like a disease!
Why such sharp words, brother? Do you know me that you dare to judge my deeds?

I don't know you personally, brother, but I do know your kind. Don't try telling me that you are different from all those brave brothers hiding inside the town walls when our Realm stands on the verge of destruction! Don't tell me you are the shining exception and that you struggle for killing all infernal minions!

Don't you think it is quite a biased opinion? I admit that some of the Brotherhood of the Righteous don't behave too bravely, but that doesn't mean that every one of our brothers is a coward. If you want, I will prove to you my devotion to God and the King!

Well, you want to prove to me you are devoted to your Holy Mission. All right. There are ruins of an old pagan watchtower not far from here. I incidentally found a forgotten cellar under the watchtower that has become the refuge of infernal monsters of all sorts that walk the earthly kingdom of God. I tried to cleanse the place of the unholy presence of those monsters, but failed and was lucky just to get away with my life. If you contend your honor with the mission of Divine Justice, then go and prove your words. Destroy all the infernal beasts dwelling under the watchtower and prove you are worthy of my trust.
All right, I'll do it.

Really? I... ehm... you've surprised me, brother. I didn't expect you... I regret speaking in such a way about you. I was... biased. I sinned and I will do penance for it. Accept, please, my humblest apology. It seems that there are still true knights in our ranks.
There surely are many of them. But tell me something about that watchtower of yours.

It probably was a part of the former guard and defense system of the pagan realm of Ereborn. According to the chronicles from that period the watchtower was captured in the year 223 by the faithful armies and since then it hasn't been rebuilt. It has been deteriorating since and because it is situated away from civilization it was forgotten. But then the people from the surrounding villages started to go missing this year and thus we started looking for the cause and I had the luck to find out the terrible truth. There is a hidden dungeon under the remains of the watchtower and it has become the refuge of infernal monsters. And it's them who have on their conscience all the disappearances in the surrounding villages. I decided to cleanse the place, but as you can see, I caught a Tartar. It will be some time until I can again wield the sword.
Thank you. And now I bid you farewell. I'm going to fulfil my Holy Mission. Wait for my return.
I apologize once more, brother. Farewell. And good luck down there. You will need it.
Yes, you are right. And now I bid you farewell. I'm going to fulfil my Holy Mission. Wait for my return.
It's done already. The hellspawns from the dungeon under the ruins of the pagan watchtower are back in Hell.
What would be in it for me?
Do you see? You are bargaining. You want to profit when there is place only for faith in God. Go away, brother. I'm sick of you.
I won't risk my life in vain. My mission does not consist of killing hellspawns but of prosecuting their human henchmen!
I knew you would refuse. Go away then and yield the Holy Mission to those who are truly called to it—to the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
In that case I had better go away. I don't want to disgust you any more.
Yes, go away, brother. There is no place for cowards here!
As you wish. Goodbye.
Watch your words, brother!

Can you see? Arrogance and superiority is burning in your eyes! Instead of honoring the principles of humility, modesty and self-denial important for a true faithful as the First Prophet and all his followers preached. But the Brotherhood of the Righteous flourishes with cowardice which slowly consumes one and all. Instead of fulfilling their holy mission the knights of God hide behind safe walls of their fortresses. But God sees that and everyone will be rightly punished!
Enough! I won't listen to such flippancy. I demand your apology immediately, brother!
What should I apologize for? For telling the truth? Never!
In that case you will meet the rightful punishment!
Your arrogance and heedlessness won't force me to waste any more time with you. Farewell.
Yes, go away, brother. There is no place for cowards here.
I'm sorry you see it this way, brother. I had better go because clearly I'm not welcome here.
Hello, brother. How are you going? Have you managed to kill those infernal monsters?
Not yet, brother. Have patience.
