Do not tarry with it, brother. The longer the monsters dwell there the bigger the danger is that they'll claim more innocent victims.
Yes, brother. The hellspawns from the dungeon under the ruins of the pagan watchtower are all dead.
Go away, brother. I do not want to set my sight on you. It is a shame someone like you may belong to the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even regular brothers are thieves! Shame!
You are right, Father. I'm going to do penance immediately. You proved to me that not all inquisitors have forgotten their real mission—which is to fight evil in all its forms. Farewell.
Knight, you are bleeding! May I ask you what happened to you and what mission has led you to this desolate place?

You ask me what has led me here, Father? Then know that I've been led here by just the Holy Mission you and your brothers in the Holy Inquisition cast aside the instant you started to pursue your own goals. The mission of Divine Justice has led me here! But such ideas mean nothing to you! So mind your own business!
Why such sharp words, knight? Do you know me that you dare to judge my deeds?

I don't know you personally, Father, but I do know your kind. Don't try telling me that you are any different than all those esteemed inquisitors shouting wicked words and raising fists against our order. Don't tell me you are the shining exception and that you understand the reasons why the Brotherhood of the Righteous refused to submit itself to the jurisdiction of the Holy Office!

Don't you think it is quite a biased opinion? I admit there are some divergences of opinion between the Holy Office and your order, but that doesn't mean that everyone who is from the opposite camp is a rascal and an intriguer, if not something worse. If you want, I will prove to you my devotion to the Holy Mission.

Well, you want to prove to me you are devoted to your Holy Mission. All right. There are ruins of an old pagan watchtower not far from here. I incidentally found a forgotten cellar under the watchtower that has become the refuge of infernal monsters of all sorts that walk the earthly kingdom of God. I tried to cleanse the place of the unholy presence of those monsters, but failed and was lucky just to get away with my life. If you contend you honor the mission of Divine Justice, then go and prove your words. Destroy all the infernal beasts dwelling under the watchtower and prove you are worthy of my trust.

Really? I... ehm... you've surprised me, Father. I didn't expect you... I regret speaking in such a way about you. I was... biased. I sinned and I will do penance for it. Accept, please, my humblest apology. It seems that even in the ranks of the Holy Inquisition all is not as it seems at first sight.
It surely is not. But tell me something about that watchtower of yours.
I apologize once more, Father. Farewell. And good luck down there. You will need it.
Do you see? You are bargaining. You want to profit when there is place only for faith in God. Go away, Father. I'm sick of you.
Yes, go away, Father. There is no place for intrigues and ruses here!
Watch your words, knight!

Do you see? Arrogance and superiority is burning in your eyes! Instead of that you should honor the principles of humility, modesty and self-denial as the First Prophet and all his followers preached. But the Church flourishes with indecency and the drive for power, which slowly consumes one and all. It's no wonder the Brotherhood of the Righteous has become a thorn in your side, when it opposes your arrogant efforts to seize absolute control over the Realm. As long as any of our brothers is alive you won't be able to get away with your intrigues!
Enough! I won't listen to such flippancy. I demand your apology immediately, knight!
Yes, go away, Father. There is no place for intrigues and ruses of the Inquisition here.
I'm sorry you see it this way, knight. I had better go because clearly I'm not welcome here.
Hello, Father. How are you going? Have you managed to kill those infernal monsters?
Not yet, knight. Have patience.
Do not tarry with it, Father. The longer the monsters dwell there the bigger the danger is that they'll claim more innocent victims.
Yes, knight. The hellspawns from the dungeon under the ruins of the pagan watchtower are all dead.
Go away, Father. I do not want to set my sight on you. It is a shame someone like you may belong to the Church.
That's all right, sir knight. We all sin now and then.
You are right, noble lord. I'm going to do penance immediately. You proved to me that not all nobles forgot their real mission, which is to protect the Realm against evil in all its forms. Farewell.

You ask me what has led me here, noble lord? Then know that I've been led here by my Holy Mission. But you surely know nothing of that... You nobles rather pursue your own shameful goals than try to protect the Realm against the evil that's flooding it! So mind your own business!

I don't know you personally, but I do know your kind. Don't try telling me that you are different from all those noble aristocrats fighting for power while our Realm stands on the verge of destruction! Don't tell me you are the shining exception and that you struggle for restoring the power of the King in the Realm!

Don't you think it is quite a biased opinion? I admit that some nobles aren't very suportive of the King's power, but that doesn't mean that every noble is a rascal and plotter. If you want, I will prove to you my devotion to the Realm and the King!

Well, you want to prove to me you are devoted to the Realm and the King. All right. There are ruins of an old pagan watchtower not far from here. I incidentally found a forgotten cellar under the watchtower that has become the refuge of infernal monsters of all sorts that walk the earthly kingdom of God. I tried to cleanse the place of the unholy presence of those monsters, but failed and was lucky just to get away with my life. If you contend you're devoted to the Realm and the King, then go and prove your words. Destroy all the infernal beasts dwelling under the watchtower and prove you are worthy of my trust.

Really? I... ehm... you've surprised me, noble lord. I didn't expect you... I regret speaking in such a way about you. I was... biased. I sinned and I will do penance for it. Accept, please, my humblest apology. It seems that there isn't all as it seems to be in the ranks of aristocracy.
Thank you. And now I bid you farewell. I'm leaving to banish evil from the place where it should not be. Wait for my return.
I apologize once more, sir. Farewell. And good luck down there. You will need it.
Yes, you are right. And now I bid you farewell. I'm leaving to banish evil from the place where it should not be.Wait for my return.
Do you see? You are bargaining. You want to profit when there is place only for faith in God. Go away, sir. I'm sick of you.
I won't risk my life in vain. My mission does not consist of killing hellspawns.
I knew you will refuse. It's not possible to trust gentry. The administering of God's Justice will rest only on the shoulders of the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Yes, go away, noble lord. There is no place for aristocratic intrigues and trickery here!

Can you see? Arrogance and superiority is burning in your eyes! Instead of honoring the principles of humility, modesty and self-denial important for a true faithful as the First Prophet and all his followers preached. But the aristocracy flourishes with cowardice which slowly consumes one and all. It's no wonder the power of the King is a thorn in your side because you'd like to usurp it for yourselves in your arrogant effort to gain absolute power in the Realm. But God sees that and you'll never be sure those intrigues of yours will bear fruit!
Hello, sir. How are you going? Have you managed to kill those infernal monsters?
Do not tarry with it, sir. The longer the monsters dwell there the bigger the danger is that they'll claim more innocent victims.
Go away, noble lord. I do not want to set my sight on you. It is a shame someone like you may have a title.

What? A man in Gubring's territory? What an insult! How dare you come here, you miserable worm? Gubring does not know you and does not think he should let you wander his territory. Gubring does not grasp how you have managed to get here when his guards are all around, but Gubring does think it is showing your utter stupidity. Gubring thinks he will soon be finished with you. Your presence here irritates Gubring greatly.
Wait, Gubring, I'm your ally. I travel to Emperor Rashgar with an important mission. Let me pass.

What? Do you regard Gubring as a fool, you wretch? Have you thought you can bluff Gubring? That Gubring is as stupid as an orcish digger who digs in the dirty earth all day? No, man, you won't fool Gubring. You are an intruder and Gubring will feed on your meat!
You are right, Gubring. Enough talking. The time has come to consecrate this place with your blood.
Wait, Gubring. We still may be able to make a bargain. What if I give you some gold?
Gubring will take your gold anyway when you are lying dead. You're gonna die!
Have mercy, Gubring, and let me go away. I've gone astray.
Don't whimper for your life, you human worm. The Cursed Flame asks for your blood and will get it!
I don't think so, miserable orc.
Don't you happen to miss a worker named Wrang, Gubring?
Huh... oh... How do you know that, you worm? Did you meet him? Speak!
Yes, I met him. And not only that—I've promised to bring him your head.
What have you done? You scabby worm! Gubring will cut off all your arms and legs for such a hardihood and then he will tear your skin from you while you still breathe. Arrrhhhh!
Yes, I met him. He asked me to kill you and bring him your head. But instead I killed him. Are you pleased by it?

Oh yes... Gubring is pleased by the death of that arrogant worker. No one may disobey Gubring's will. No one! You deserve a reward for killing defiant Wrang, human. And so Gubring promises to kill you fast and painlessly.
Yes, I met him. And if you let me pass I will tell you where to find him.
WHAT?! You want to bargain with Gubring, you human worm? You want to irritate Gubring with your terms? No, you won't do it. Gubring will kill you and then he finds that arrogant Wrang himself.
God sees this place and his anger is great. He wishes me to relieve the world of such unholy monsters as you, Gubring.

God? No, human, you won't shock Gubring by your god. He has no power in this place. The Cursed Flame rules here and neither you nor your god can do anything about it, you fool. Get ready to die by Gubring's axe!
Who are the members of the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition?

The head of the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition is an Inquisitor General, at present time Cardinal Commendoni, who is also the permanent papal legate. Besides him other members of the tribunal are three Inquisitorial judges, Cardinals Gustapho Letti, Severtinus and Giovanni Timore.

You're welcome, brother. It's important for you to get to know those men. They are the most powerful inquisitors in the Realm. It's a shame one of them is a henchman and accomplice of Christoffer de Malamert. It's Gustapho Letti, who acts as the confessor of the King and as his spiritual guide. He is a very dangerous man, brother—beware of him. His words are sweet as honey, but deadly as poison!
I'd like to ask you about one thing, Seneschal. The former gardener Downay branded you as a heretic and a member of the cult of the Children of the New Order. What can you tell me about it?

Am I regarded as a heretic and a supporter of some infernal sect?! That's a foul lie! I've never in my life heard such a wicked offense. I will punish that insolent liar in such a way he will never forget it. But on the other hand... It seems this scheme is part of the intrigues of the Children of the New Order. Grand Master de Malamert surely has decided to destroy me. But he mustn't be allowed to succeed, brother. You have to arrest him no matter the cost and bring him to justice. Then the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition will be able to sentence him. I depend on you!
Yes, I understand.
So you deny the accusation?

What? What do you mean by that? Do you really consider the possibility the information would be true? Do not make fun of me, brother. There's no time for such jokes. Attend to your mission so as to get those damned heretics to the stake.
The assassin Sven Larsen pleaded guilty to the murder of paladin Eradim d'Chambrie. And he confessed it was you who hired him to kill the paladin. What can you tell me about it?

The second allegation against me? I'm starting to fear. It seems the intrigues of Grand Master de Malamert are thoroughly prepared. But do not let yourself be fooled, brother. The Grand Master plays for his life and knows it well. Arrest him at once or he may get an advantage and destroy us before we can do anything. And that would be the absolute end...

It's rather embarrassing for me, but there is another accusation against you. The royal counselor Verenicus confessed he belongs to the Children of the New Order and specified you as one of the supporters of this heretical cult. What can you tell me about it?

Do you realize Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert has managed to put up three false proofs against me already? And exactly that number is necessary for my indictment and arrest. This is beyond all bounds. Arrest Grand Master de Malamert at once or we all end up at the stake. It's only a matter of time before some evidence against you comes up!

The entire grave crisis the Realm has been dragged into is the work of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert and his wicked heretical followers, I'm sure of it! Just look around yourself, brother, what damage they've managed to do. I wouldn't be surprised if it showed during the investigation that they have their hands in the murder of His Majesty Edward II. All the more it's important to arrest Grand Master de Malamert as soon as possible.

Tidings about a war have been circulating around the town for some time already, but only after the death of His Majesty King Edward II they got more realistic outlines. The First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor was ordered to ready the royal regiments in the entire Realm for the fight. It can mean only one thing—war. But it sort of eludes my understanding against whom it should be waged. There are no accounts of any army advancing on Ultherst. And you can't send an army against the hellspawns—they don't attack in close battle formations and it's hardly conceivable they would accept a challenge and fight us on the battlefield.

I don't remember any fierce storm with unnatural spectacles recently. It's true there is occasionally quite a tumult above Alvaron, brought here by winds from the seashore, and then you can see things a man would not believe to exist, but nothing like that has happened recently.
What do I know about the Fallen Angels? Hmm... Why are you asking, brother?
Because it interests me. Is there some problem with it?

No, certainly not. I'm just surprised you're asking me about that and not about a priest or so. But to answer your question—the Holy Scriptures mention the Fallen Angels as the most dreadful servants of the Dark Prince of Hell. They are former angels, struck by God's punishment for their sins when they along with Satan the Tempter plotted treason against God Almighty at the dawn of days. The Holy Scriptures say that they have been thrown down from Heaven and bound in Hell to suffer there for their sins. Since then they have been trying to get back to seize the rule over the world and over Heaven. They are four—Arthamon, Lord of the Defeat, Baphomet, the Master of Madness, Cerdie, the Wanton Succubus, and the Archangel Azrael, the Devil's Emissary and Advocate. Lots of lesser demons and infernal henchmen serve them and the Fallen Angels send them to the world to cause harm and to sow seeds of ruin and disruption.

If I were you I'd be cautious not to be caught at night outside of the city walls. It could happen you become a game for the werewolves from Schwarzwald. People from the town surroundings far and near have been at their mercy from time immemorial, but over the last few years it has been really terrible. Everybody who falls into their claws is dead for sure. Moreover, at each full moon they somehow manage to get inside the city, abduct some innocent victim and drag him or her away into their den somewhere in Schwarzwald. None of the abducted has returned alive.

There were quite a lot of people brutally murdered in Alvaron and its vicinity recently. And at least the same number has gone missing without a trace. People usually blame wolf-prince Wulfhyrr and his packs of werewolves for it, but I'd say that other hellspawns have their hands in it too. I wouldn't be surprised if it is a part of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert's plan to disrupt the Realm and to seize control of it.

The death of our companion Richwald d'Blazier has hit me hard, brother. He was a good soldier of God and true defender of faith. But he couldn't resist the wiles and temptations of certain infernal witch, hiding before the world in the dark woods of Schwarzwald. That witch completely bemused him with her dark magic and then in some lascivious turn of mind she turned him into stone. I wish the witch ends up at the stake as soon as possible!
I'm searching for the criminals who let the werewolves enter the city every full moon. Do you happen to know anything about them?

You are not the only one who's trying to find out which treacherous heretic—or even a group of them—allows the werewolves into the city on full moons. But no one has been able to discover anything yet—and neither have I. So I can't help you in any way, I'm sorry.

I'll give you some good advice, brother—don't try to help people tainted with lycantrophy. It's more of a damnation than a disease, it's the Mark of the Beast, it's the brand of being forsaken by God. He who gets diseased is destined to eternal perdition and all have to put up with it. The only act of kindness we may do for lycanthropes is to free their souls of their tainted bodies and let our Lord to bless their souls through purgatory.

It is said that there is a stryx dwelling in the city cemetery and that it has arisen from a cursed girl named Joan. The legend says her own mother, a nun of the order of Saint Bethesda, cursed Joan. Some goatish priest raped the nun, she lost her mind then and wandered helplessly around the Realm until she gave birth to her daughter in the Alvaron cemetery.
Well... and what else does the legend say?

The instant she gave birth to her daughter the poor soul cursed her newborn child and then committed suicide. The girl was found lifeless in the morning by priests and put into a nameless grave. Years went by and no one suspected the curse was slowly changing Joan into a dreadful stryx that would hunt her father. And then it really happened—the stryx awoke and since then she has been stalking the city to get her father. It's said she will kill anyone she meets.
You had better answer me, Seneschal. I wouldn't advise you to conceal anything. That would be very unwise of you, if you understand me.
It seems there are some problem between us. Nevertheless I hope that if you think about it you would admit there isn't any reason not to answer me.
You are wise and powerful man, Seneschal. Your answer would be of the greatest help to me.
I knew I might rely on you, brother. I've known it since the beginning. It was a good choice to entrust you with investigation of this case.
We will see, Seneschal. Now please present to me all the evidence against Grand Master de Malamert you've managed to get.

Of course, brother. First and foremost it is the testimony of neophyte Petrier de Duby, Grand Master's minion, who served as his messenger. He denounced Malamert and revealed a secret safe where the Grand Master had been hiding heretical books and letters from his wicked accomplices. On the basis of the letters from the Grand Master's safe we got another two pieces of evidence necessary to arrest the Grand Master. In those shameful letters the Grand Master conveys to other conspirators his orders how they should proceed in their joint plan to disrupt the Realm. By all accounts all the conspirators had consorted with dark powers and planed to use them in their plan. But only you were able to discover the fact that they belong to the cult of the Children of the New Order, brother.
Thank you, Seneschal. I will present this evidence to the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition.

Great, brother. I knew I could rely on you. Grand Master de Malamert has to be brought to justice! Accept this pouch of gold, brother. Take it as a deposit on the necessary costs related with the investigation of this case.
Thank you. But before I put my mind to the case, I'd like you to answer a few questions, Seneschal.
As you wish, brother. What would you like to know?
Thank you. I will turn my attention to this case. Farewell for now.
Farewell, brother. And act promptly, because the enemy is not sleeping. I would hate to get some unpleasant surprise.
Seneschal Jean de Guise, I hereby arrest you on the basis of reasonable suspicion of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. You will come with me to be put to justice.

Hmm... it's interesting how the situation has evolved. Instead of catching Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert you accuse me of heresy. I won't pretend being surprised, it's not suitable to my status. But I know the Inquisitorial law as well as you do, brother. So I ask—what evidence do you have against me?

Sven Larsen confessed you recruited him to murder paladin Eradim d'Chambrie. Downay the Gardener stated that he along with you perpetrated many a shameful crime because you both belong to the cult of the Children of the New Order. And then there is the confession of the royal counselor Verenicus with whom you undertook the heretical rite two years ago. During that rite you'd put a curse on Prince Louis.
You've managed to find out so much, brother. But you don't realize one thing.
That if you try to arrest me I will kill you!
Is that you, brother? My goodness... yes it is you! I've never thought I would see you again. Heaven has sent you to me in these hard days.
I'm sorry, knight, but who are you?

No, I'm sorry for not introducing myself. My name's Jeane de Guise and I'm a Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. But my name probably doesn't mean anything to you, and neither does my face. Nevertheless I know you and you know me, because we met once. You surely remember two men who visited you this spring and asked you to investigate strange events in the town of Hillbrandt...
Yes?

Just so, brother. It was I and one of my companions who sought you out that day and asked you for help. We needed a stranger, who wouldn't be too visible to all and who would be able to find out what's going on without raising suspicion. And because of that we came to you, brother.
I'm glad we meet again. But I have to say I was vainly waiting all the time for you to visit me again or to send me some message of what to do next.

Of course I wanted to do that, but I couldn't. I'm sincerely sorry, but the situation we had to face here after that day forbade us to contact you in any way. If we did so we would endanger not only your life but also the mission which has been entrusted to you and which is—no offense—much more important than the life of any of us.
I think the time has come for you to tell me all, Seneschal. I've risked my life to get here.

Yes, I believe that. And I agree you should get to know the whole truth. Well... The reason why we decided to seek you out this spring and ask you for your help was simple. We've found out something very obscure and wicked is going on in the Realm and that it endangers the very existence of the Kingdom. We ran into intrigues aimed at undermining the power of the King, at the destruction of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, at spattering the faith in the Holy Mother Church and at disrupting society. But we didn't know anything more than that it's the work of some heretics trying to carry out their plans with the aid of infernal powers.
Continue, please.

Thanks to a lucky coincidence we got wind of Kurth Ollmier, notorious for grave robbing. He was reportedly heard to say that he got his hands on something that should have provided him with enough money to live the rest of his life as a nobleman, but that very thing also endangered him mortally and forced him to hide before the Inquisition. We understood it had to be some artifact or a scroll of great worth to heretics and that with the utmost probability it was linked to the events starting to appear all over the Realm. That's why we started to hunt for Ollmier immediately. But it happened that our trusty companions following his track were murdered or went missing without a trace. We understood the enemy was aware of our existence and tried to stop us.
I understand. And then you decided to entrust the case to someone who was little known and who would thus evade the enemy more easily. Am I right?

You surely are, brother. We chose you out of dozens of suitable adepts and then we visited you in utmost secrecy to charge you with the investigation of the case of the merchant Ollmier. We wanted to contact you after some time and take over the result of your investigation, but we couldn't. Our allies started to die one after another, usually very violently, and we figured out the enemy was after us. We didn't want to endanger you, hence we left you to your own fate and hoped you would manage to survive even without our help and maybe eventually get here to Alvaron to help us to step in against the conspirators.
You use the plural, Seneschal. In whose name do you speak and who are your enemies? What do you know about them?

I represent a group of royalists, brother, sworn to defend the Realm against any danger, be it from the outside or from the inside, even if it would cost them their lives. We are wholly devoted to the Crown and everything we do is in its best interest. Several years ago we were many, but many of our supporters have died recently. In fact only a few of us are left and consequently we cannot keep our influence even in Alvaron, the capital of the Realm! Contrary to our enemies—by all accounts, their numbers have been rising all the time. We don't know which group of heretics it is, but their contacts reach into the highest circles of society, there's no doubt about that.

In that case I may greatly enhance your knowledge, Seneschal. The heretics you fight against belong to the cult of the Children of the New Order. Kurt Ollmier got the book Libre Daemonium for them, which describes rites for summoning the Fallen Angels. And that's precisely what the heretics are trying to do—to summon those infernal demons.

Oh my God! But in that case it all starts to make sense! If it really is the cult of the Children of the New Order, Christoffer de Malamert is its dark High Priest and the number one enemy we face here in Alvaron.
What are you talking about, Seneschal?

I talk about the treason of Christoffer de Malamert, the Grand Master of the order of Brotherhood of the Righteous. He is the leader of the enemy trying to disrupt the Realm. He is behind the intrigues that have brought Ultherst to the very edge of destruction. He thought he managed to get an advantage over us, that he could crush us. But he overreached himself greatly. We managed to catch one of his messengers he used to send orders and the messenger confessed to everything when put to torture. He denounced Christoffer de Malamert and some of his other henchmen. Exactly because of this lucky coincidence, surely brought to us by Divine Providence, the balance of power has shifted. Until now we have been the hunted game, but now it's just the opposite.
Are you telling me that Christoffer de Malamert, the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, is the dark High Priest of the cult of the Children of the New Order?

Exactly, brother. I myself couldn't believe it, but the evidence spoke clearly. We could do nothing but put up with the idea of my highest superior, friend and mentor being the traitor. And on top of it the dark High Priest of the cult of the Children of the New Order, as you've just said. Now I understand why he has been trying to disrupt the Realm and set us all against each other. At first I thought he was trying to seize power, but the destruction he was inflicting all around mismatched this conclusion. No one wants to rule a disrupted and destroyed land. But with what you've just told me it makes sense. He strives to summon the Fallen Angels!
It seems so. What do you suggest, Seneschal?

We have to gather all the evidence possible against Malamert and render it to the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition. Because only it may accuse the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous of heresy. This may bear no delay, brother, because Grand Master de Malamert already suspects something. We mustn't allow him to prepare a counterstrike. We have to act immediately. Do you think you'd be able to undertake this task, brother? Would you come forward before the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition as the chief prosecutor? I've no doubt that with the results of your investigation you will be able to convince the Tribunal to accuse the Grand Master of heresy, so we may consequently arrest him.
All right, I agree. I will come forward before the Tribunal and will bring the charge against the Grand Master.
I don't like it. I'm not used to taking over judgments of others. I'd like to investigate all this by myself first.

There's no time for that, brother. Under other circumstances I would certainly agree, because I know that direct experience is better than anything else, but presently it's impossible to continue with the investigation any longer. We need to accuse Grand Master de Malamert of heresy as soon as possible and to arrest him. Otherwise he might rise against us or run away and all our efforts would end up in smoke. Hence I have to urge you to act, brother. If you really want to help us, do it now!
I'm not sure if I'm the right person, Seneschal. Nobody knows me in Alvaron.

Don't worry about it, brother. This is not about connections but about justice. And the fact that you managed to solve the case of such proportions and to stay alive predestines you for such great things as this one.
How am I going to be rewarded if I decide to help you?

You deserve your reward, there's no doubt about that, brother. You may count with the generosity worthy of noblemen of the highest rank. Gold, magic jewelry, weapons... Whatever crosses your mind. And of course you will get something in advance.
I won't come forward before the Tribunal before I personally investigate this case.
I'm sorry, brother. But I understand. Attend to the case of Grand Master de Malamert then and decide for yourself. Remember, though, that time is our enemy. When you decide, come to me immediately.
All right. May I ask you some questions now?
As you wish, brother.
Agreed. Farewell.
What if I would say I don't know what you are talking about, Seneschal?

I understand. It's wise to be cautious these days. If you really don't believe me, I'll gladly give you proof of my words. In the spring we asked you to investigate the case of Kurt Ollmier the merchant, because we suspected he gained possession of some rare heretical relic or text. Now you see it was really me who sought you out then.
Welcome, brother. Have you made any progress in the case of Grand Master de Malamert? Time is our enemy. Have you managed to find him and arrest him?
Not yet, Seneschal. You have to be patient.
I am patient, but there's too much at stake now for us to hesitate. But I trust you will succeed. Is there something I can do for you now?
I'd like to ask you a few questions, Seneschal.
Certainly, ask your questions, brother. What do you want to know?
Would it be possible to get another advance payment to cover my costs associated with this case?

Certainly, brother. Take this pouch of gold. I hope it will be enough for now. But remember that gold is not omnipotent and it's necessary to do more in this case than just expend funds. But you surely know that well.
You're welcome, brother. The service to God demands sacrifices. May I do something else for you?

I'm glad to see you, brother. May I ask you how your investigation of Grand Master de Malamert's heresy is going? Are you ready to take your place as the prosecutor in his case? Time is working against us and nobody can tell what the Grand Master might do to avert the threat we pose.

I am patient, but there's too much at stake now for us to hesitate. But I trust you will soon take heart to come forward before the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition and present the evidence of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert's treason and heresy there.
Yes, maybe. But now I'd like to ask you a few questions, Seneschal
Ask away, brother. What exactly would you like to know?
Certainly. Thank you.
Yes, I investigated the case and decided to act for the plaintiff.
Nooooo!! Darn it! The pain! Whose blood is this? My God, I'm bleeding! Help me, brother! I can't stop it. My sight dims! I'm so cold... What has happened? It shouldn't have ended this way. Ahhh...
I can't help you, Seneschal. Nobody can heal such serious wounds. You should have given up!
But I... I should have killed you. Nobody can defeat me in a single combat! How could it happen? I'm so cold... I'm shivering... I don't feel my body, I can't move. Won't someone help me?!

Your life is forfeit, Seneschal. But your soul has hope for salvation. Make confession. Open your soul to God and admit your sins. As you can see, the infernal powers have forsaken you. They've let you to fall and haven't helped you. But God may forgive you. Don't deprive yourself of the chance of eternal life!

My God! How could it happen? How could I... forsake You? The Dark Prince has betrayed me... he condemned me... left me to die! Although he promised me so much! Aaah! The pain! I can hardly talk now. Listen carefully, brother... Cardinal Commendoni... he is behind all the evil that has befallen the Realm. Earlier this year he restored the cult of the Children of the New Order and summoned dark priests to participate in the conspiracy that... that should contribute to the execution of the Plan. He is the dark High Priest of this cult!
Cardinal Commendoni? Inquisitor General of the Holy Office? Why should I believe you, Seneschal?

It's up to you, brother. I... am not lying to you. Listen carefully, I won't be able to resist death for too long... He sent his dark priests to search for the book Libre Daemonium, describing the rite of summoning of the Fallen Angels. He entrusted Vallarian and Truncquillius with summoning of Arthamon and Baphomet. He prepares to open the gates of Hell and to free the Prince of Darkness from his thousand-year prison. He... My God... aaaah...
Seneschal, do you hear me? Have Arthamon and Baphomet been really summoned? Where are they? Is it possible to stop them somehow? And who was charged with summoning the Fallen Angel Cerdie? Seneschal?
He is dead. But all the same he said much. Let God judge his soul justly.

You're welcome, Father. It's important for you to get to know those men. They are the most powerful inquisitors in the Realm. It's a shame one of them is a henchman and accomplice of Christoffer de Malamert. It's Gustapho Letti, who acts as the confessor of the King and as his spiritual guide. He is a very dangerous man, Father—beware of him. His words are sweet as honey, but deadly as poison!

Am I regarded as a heretic and a supporter of some infernal sect?! That's a foul lie! I've never in my life heard such a wicked offense. I will punish that insolent liar in such a way he will never forget it. But on the other hand... It seems this scheme is part of the intrigues of the Children of the New Order. Grand Master de Malamert surely has decided to destroy me. But he mustn't be allowed to succeed, Father. You have to arrest him no matter the cost and bring him to justice. Then the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition will be able to sentence him. I depend on you!

What? What do you mean by that? Do you really consider the possibility the information would be true? Do not make fun of me, Father. There's no time for such jokes. Attend to your mission so as to get those damned heretics to the stake.

The second allegation against me? I'm starting to fear. It seems the intrigues of Grand Master de Malamert are thoroughly prepared. But do not let yourself be fooled, Father. The Grand Master plays for his life and knows it well. Arrest him at once or he may get an advantage and destroy us before we can do anything. And that would be the absolute end...

The entire grave crisis the Realm has been dragged into is the work of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert and his wicked heretical followers, I'm sure of it! Just look around yourself, Father, what damage they've managed to do. I wouldn't be surprised if it showed during the investigation that they have their hands in the murder of His Majesty Edward II. All the more it's important to arrest Grand Master de Malamert as soon as possible.
What do I know about the Fallen Angels? Hmm... Why are you asking, Father?

I knew I might rely on you, Father. I've known it since the beginning. It was a good choice to entrust you with investigation of this case.

He entrusted Vallarian and Truncquillius with summoning of Arthamon and Baphomet. He prepares to open the gates of Hell and to free the Prince of Darkness from his thousand-year prison. He... My God... aaaah...

You're welcome, sir. It's important for you to get to know those men. They are the most powerful inquisitors in the Realm. It's a shame one of them is a henchman and accomplice of Christoffer de Malamert. It's Gustapho Letti, who acts as the confessor of the King and as his spiritual guide. He is a very dangerous man, sir—beware of him. His words are sweet as honey, but deadly as poison!

Am I regarded as a heretic and a supporter of some infernal sect?! That's a foul lie! I've never in my life heard such a wicked offense. I will punish that insolent liar in such a way he will never forget it. But on the other hand... It seems this scheme is part of the intrigues of the Children of the New Order. Grand Master de Malamert surely has decided to destroy me. But he mustn't be allowed to succeed, sir. You have to arrest him no matter the cost and bring him to justice. Then the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition will be able to sentence him. I depend on you!

What? What do you mean by that? Do you really consider the possibility the information would be true? Do not make fun of me, sir. There's no time for such jokes. Attend to your mission so as to get those damned heretics to the stake.

The second allegation against me? I'm starting to fear. It seems the intrigues of Grand Master de Malamert are thoroughly prepared. But do not let yourself be fooled, sir. The Grand Master plays for his life and knows it well. Arrest him at once or he may get an advantage and destroy us before we can do anything. And that would be the absolute end...

The entire grave crisis the Realm has been dragged into is the work of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert and his wicked heretical followers, I'm sure of it! Just look around yourself, sir, what damage they've managed to do. I wouldn't be surprised if it showed during the investigation that they have their hands in the murder of His Majesty Edward II. All the more it's important to arrest Grand Master de Malamert as soon as possible.
What do I know about the Fallen Angels? Hmm... Why are you asking, sir?

No, certainly not. I'm just surprised that a noble is asking a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous about the fallen angels, rather, you should ask some priest. But to answer your question, the Holy Scriptures mention the Fallen Angels as the most dreadful servants of the Dark Prince of Hell. They are former angels, struck by God's punishment for their sins when they along with Satan the Tempter plotted treason against God Almighty at the dawn of days. The Holy Scriptures say that they have been thrown down from Heaven and bound in Hell to suffer there for their sins. Since then they have been trying to get back to seize the rule over the world and over Heaven. They are four, Arthamon, Lord of the Defeat, Baphomet, the Master of Madness, Cerdie, the Wanton Succubus, and the Archangel Azrael, the Devil's Emissary and Advocate. Lots of lesser demons and infernal henchmen serve them and the Fallen Angels send them to the world to cause harm and to sow seeds of ruin and disruption.

The death of our companion Richwald d'Blazier has hit me hard, sir. He was a good soldier of God and true defender of faith. But he couldn't resist the wiles and temptations of certain infernal witch, hiding before the world in the dark woods of Schwarzwald. That witch completely bemused him with her dark magic and then in some lascivious turn of mind she turned him into stone. I wish the witch ends up at the stake as soon as possible!

I'll give you some good advice, sir—don't try to help people tainted with lycantrophy. It's more of a damnation than a disease, it's the Mark of the Beast, it's the brand of being forsaken by God. He who gets diseased is destined to eternal perdition and all have to put up with it. The only act of kindness we may do for lycanthropes is to free their souls of their tainted bodies and let our Lord to bless their souls through purgatory.
You should answer me, Seneschal. I wouldn't advise you to conceal anything. That would be very unwise of you, if you understand me.
I knew I might rely on you, sir. I've known it since the beginning. It was a good choice to entrust you with investigation of this case.

Of course, sir. First and foremost it is the testimony of neophyte Petrier de Duby, Grand Master's minion, who served as his messenger. He denounced Malamert and revealed a secret safe where the Grand Master had been hiding heretical books and letters from his wicked accomplices. On the basis of the letters from the Grand Master's safe we got another two pieces of evidence necessary to arrest the Grand Master. In those shameful letters the Grand Master conveys to other conspirators his orders how they should proceed in their joint plan to disrupt the Realm. By all accounts all the conspirators had consorted with dark powers and planed to use them in their plan. But only you were able to discover the fact that they belong to the cult of the Children of the New Order, sir.

Great, sir. I knew I could rely on you. Grand Master de Malamert has to be brought to justice! Accept this pouch of gold, sir. Take it as a deposit on the necessary costs related with the investigation of this case.
As you wish, sir. What would you like to know?
Farewell, sir. And act promptly, because the enemy is not sleeping. I would hate to get some unpleasant surprise.

Hmm... it's interesting how the situation has evolved. Instead of catching Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert you accuse me of heresy. I won't pretend being surprised, it's not suitable to my status. But I know the Inquisitorial law as well as you do, sir. So I ask—what evidence do you have against me?
You've managed to find out so much, sir. But you don't realize one thing.
Is that you, sir? My goodness... yes it is you! I've never thought I would see you again. Heaven has sent you to me in these hard days.

Just so, sir. It was I and one of my companions who sought you out that day and asked you for help. We needed a stranger, who wouldn't be too visible to all and who would be able to find out what's going on without raising suspicion. And because of that we came to you, sir.

You surely are, sir. We chose you out of dozens of suitable adepts and then we visited you in utmost secrecy to charge you with the investigation of the case of the merchant Ollmier. We wanted to contact you after some time and take over the result of your investigation, but we couldn't. Our allies started to die one after another, usually very violently, and we figured out the enemy was after us. We didn't want to endanger you, hence we left you to your own fate and hoped you would manage to survive even without our help and maybe eventually get here to Alvaron to help us to step in against the conspirators.

I represent a group of royalists, sir, sworn to defend the Realm against any danger, be it from the outside or from the inside, even if it would cost them their lives. We are wholly devoted to the Crown and everything we do is in its best interest. Several years ago we were many, but many of our supporters have died recently. In fact only a few of us are left and consequently we cannot keep our influence even in Alvaron, the capital of the Realm! Contrary to our enemies—by all accounts, their numbers have been rising all the time. We don't know which group of heretics it is, but their contacts reach into the highest circles of society, there's no doubt about that.

Exactly, sir. I myself couldn't believe it, but the evidence spoke clearly. We could do nothing but put up with the idea of my highest superior, friend and mentor being the traitor. And on top of it the dark High Priest of the cult of the Children of the New Order, as you've just said. Now I understand why he has been trying to disrupt the Realm and set us all against each other. At first I thought he was trying to seize power, but the destruction he was inflicting all around mismatched this conclusion. No one wants to rule a disrupted and destroyed land. But with what you've just told me it makes sense. He strives to summon the Fallen Angels!

We have to gather all the evidence possible against Malamert and render it to the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition. Because only it may accuse the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous of heresy. This may bear no delay, sir, because Grand Master de Malamert already suspects something. We mustn't allow him to prepare a counterstrike. We have to act immediately. Do you think you'd be able to undertake this task, sir? Would you come forward before the Supreme Tribunal of Inquisition as the chief prosecutor? I've no doubt that with the results of your investigation you will be able to convince the Tribunal to accuse the Grand Master of heresy, so we may consequently arrest him.

There's no time for that, sir. Under other circumstances I would certainly agree, because I know that direct experience is better than anything else, but presently it's impossible to continue with the investigation any longer. We need to accuse Grand Master de Malamert of heresy as soon as possible and to arrest him. Otherwise he might rise against us or run away and all our efforts would end up in smoke. Hence I have to urge you to act, sir. If you really want to help us, do it now!

Don't worry about it, sir. This is not about connections but about justice. And the fact that you managed to solve the case of such proportions and to stay alive predestines you for such great things as this one.

You deserve your reward, there's no doubt about that, sir. You may count with the generosity worthy of noblemen of the highest rank. Gold, magic jewelry, weapons... Whatever crosses your mind. And of course you will get something in advance.
I'm sorry, sir. But I understand. Attend to the case of Grand Master de Malamert then and decide for yourself. Remember, though, that time is our enemy. When you decide, come to me immediately.
As you wish, sir.
Welcome, sir. Have you made any progress in the case of Grand Master de Malamert? Time is our enemy. Have you managed to find him and arrest him?
Certainly, ask your questions, sir. What do you want to know?

Certainly, sir. Take this pouch of gold. I hope it will be enough for now. But remember that gold is not omnipotent and it's necessary to do more in this case than just expend funds. But you surely know that well.
You're welcome, sir. The service to God demands sacrifices. May I do something else for you?

I'm glad to see you, sir. May I ask you how your investigation of Grand Master de Malamert's heresy is going? Are you ready to take your place as the prosecutor in his case? Time is working against us and nobody can tell what the Grand Master might do to avert the threat we pose.
Ask away, sir. What exactly would you like to know?
Nooooo!! Darn it! The pain! Whose blood is this? My God, I'm bleeding! Help me, sir! I can't stop it. My sight dims! I'm so cold... What has happened? It shouldn't have ended this way. Ahhh...

My God! How could it happen? How could I... forsake You? The Dark Prince has betrayed me... he condemned me... left me to die! Although he promised me so much! Aaah! The pain! I can hardly talk now. Listen carefully, sir... Cardinal Commendoni... he is behind all the evil that has befallen the Realm. Earlier this year he restored the cult of the Children of the New Order and summoned dark priests to participate in the conspiracy that... that should contribute to the execution of the Plan. He is the dark High Priest of this cult!

Several weeks ago my army service ended and I ran like a madman to be home as soon as possible and to see my mother and sisters again. But when I came to Jaegermoor I found it burned to the ground and all its citizens staked. Including my mother and my sisters. They killed even the little Kim, and she was only six! It was easy to find out it's the work of that bastard Benthley of Welshrem, dubbed the Bloody Butcher. And I will kill that mongrel for it, I surely will. Before I'm finished with him he will be sorry he was ever born.
Are you really sure Benthley of Welshrem is responsible for killing your family?

I know it for sure, knight. It was him! I found a villager who had survived that killing spree. He told me about Benthley and the others bursting into the village, killing all who resisted, raping all the women and girls and then sticking them on stakes to a man.
How old did you say your youngest sister was?
Ten, knight. But even she was raped! Can you imagine that horror?!
Hmm... That's strange. At first you said your youngest sister was six.
Really? Oh shit...
You are lying to me! Tell me the truth this instant!
I see your cause is just. If you accept, I would help you to execute the judgment against Benthley of Welshrem.

Really? God bless you, knight! Only when Benthley of Welshrem is dead will my family find its peace. Bring me his head, knight, for only then I'll be sure it's all over with him. If you do it I will give you all my soldier's pay that I saved during my service.
Maybe I could help you with your revenge. What would you offer me for it?
I would give you all my soldier's pay that I saved during my service, knight. There's nothing important in my life anymore but to avenge my family.
In that case I wish you luck. Farewell.
You won't help me, knight? Damn! Why, it's told you can cope with anything, so don't tell me you don't have the courage to beat Benthley. I've taken such pains over this!
What are you speaking about? What have you taken pains over? What's going on here?
I... ehm... oh shit!
Tell me what's going on here immediately!
In that case I have good news for you, good man. Benthley of Welshrem is dead!
Dead? Benthley's dead? I don't believe that. How did it happen? Who killed him?
I killed him.
You? But anybody could say that. I won't believe you until you bring me his head.
In that case—here it is!

Honestly, it's him! Benthley of Welshrem is dead! You really killed him, knight. Now there's nothing preventing me from taking his place I've been pining for. I'm going to become the general of his Army of Divine Justice!
I already gave over his head to Grand Duke Heindrick in the town.
So you really killed him, knight? That's great news! Now there's nothing preventing me from taking his place I've so pined for. I'm going to become the general of his Army of Divine Justice!
I will bring you his head, no fear!
All right, we have a deal, knight. Bring me the head of Benthley and I will give you all my saved soldier's pay for it.

Well... as you wish, knight. It doesn't matter anymore. Well... I've heard you can cope with almost anything. So I told to myself that you could help me to kill Benthley of Welshrem. Why get my hands dirty when other can do it for me, am I right?
Why did you lie to me? Why didn't you tell me the truth?

Because you surely wouldn't help me then. I'm Benthley's lieutenant. And if Benthley were to die I would became the captain of his personal army. And that would give me some choices, wouldn't it? But it seems it wasn't a good idea. Now I have to kill you!
What are you talking about? What does it mean?

What does it mean? Only that you've helped me to become one of the most powerful people round Glatzburg! I'm the first lieutenant in Benthley's army. I wanted to kill him somehow to step into his place. And I've done it! So thank you. But now I have to kill you because you know it. I don't want it to get about, you surely understand it. So adieu, knight. And give my kind regards to that God of yours!
Halt! Not a step more! Just one more move and I'll kill you. I won't let anybody to thwart my plans!
Peace, good man. I do not mean you any harm. Tell me who you are and what is you business in this backcountry?
Nobody will threaten me and stay unpunished! Give your weapons away—now!
I'm sorry, knight. I didn't know you were a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I thought you were one of those perfidious footpads of Benthley of Welshrem.
That's what I am definitely not, as you can see. But tell me who are you and what is you business in this backcountry?
Do you bring me the head of Benthley, knight?
Yes, I do bring you the head of Benthley—here it is!
Honestly, it's him! You really killed him, knight. In that case there's nothing preventing me from taking his place. I'm going to become the general of his Army of Divine Justice.
No, not yet. Have patience.
So hurry up, knight. I can't wait to see that mongrel dead!
I didn't bring you the head of Benthley. To tell the truth I gave it over to Grand Duke Heindrick in exchange for the reward offered for it.

So Benthley really is dead? You really killed him, knight? In that case there's nothing preventing me from taking his place I've been pining for so much. I'm going to become the general of his Army of Divine Justice!
Let's put Benthley's head aside for now. I've found you don't have any sisters and you've never known your mother. You faked the entire story about the revenge. You are Benthley's lieutenant!

Not much, knight. But it's all really horrible. I remember going to confession... to Father Trevorius, as always. And then, when kneeling in the confessional... I suddenly ran amok against the Bishop... I crashed the confessional open till the wood chippings started flying and then I bit the Bishop's throat. The first taste of blood on my lips made me drunk and blissful... But the Bishop didn't die... he parried my attack... bound me by a spell... I fought and at the same time I wanted to die, as if I was split in two persons... I screamed in horror because of what I'd done but in doing so I heard myself spiting one swear after another... Oh my God, what have I done? And why? Then my vision dimmed, I fell unconscious and awoke here in this filthy cell. Holy Mother of God... I... tempted all around me... I showed them my thighs... and they took hold of me... They were like wild animals... and I screamed and cried in horror, but instead I heard only wanton groans of delight... Oh, our Lord Merciful, forgive me!
What do you remember from the time before that foul spirit gained control over your body?

I was returning home... it was late in the evening... I had to deliver a letter of my mistress Yulliette Heidrick somewhere. The night was falling, so I quickened my steps to be home sooner. And then I heard those steps. I thought it is some passer-by and didn't even look back. But the steps drew nearer, there were two people. I started to run and the steps followed me... I was running but someone's hands pulled me down... They gagged me, hit my head hard and then... then I remember awaking at some dreadful place...
And then?

I was lying naked on a stinking stone floor, there were bowls with strange things inside all around me, there were strange lights burning... And those walls, Archangel Gabriel protect me, those walls were full of souls, trapped and imprisoned souls! And then three persons came from somewhere... they wore cloaks with deep hoods so I didn't see into their faces... They started to discuss something and one of them went to check if I was already conscious. And then I looked in his face... and I realized I know him!
Who was the person you saw? I have to know it!

It was the tradesman Raimond Ventano! I couldn't believe it... I begged him to free me, but he laughed at me and told me not to fear anything. He told me I was going to experience something beautiful and delightful... He spoke something about enlightenment, about a mission... And then they started the rite. Oh my God... They sacrificed a lamb and drew some foul signs on my body by its blood. And my body was burning, I tried to get free from the chains, but my body twisted with pain and then there was He. I didn't see him, but I felt him... He was there, he lay upon me so I smelled his foul breath... He scarified my body, torn my breasts and bit my lips... He took me... He violated me... We became one body... And that's the last thing I remember. God Almighty, why me? What have I done to deserve this?
What was the place you were dragged into? Could you recognize it?

I don't know what place it was, knight. But it stunk of brimstone. Those walls... they were full of trapped souls! They might look as stone, but I know they were alive! Those souls put their eyes on me... their faces looked at me as if they knew what was going to happen. There were complex ornaments and writings there... Maybe runes or some code... It was shocking.
You told me that He came. Who was Him?

I don't know, knight. I don't know His name. But when he came I suddenly knew who he was... I can't describe it, but I just knew it was Him and that he was going to take me. Never before had I felt so much evil. It was terrible!
Thank you, Francessca. That's all I needed to know.

Oh my God... I... All that happened to me! All that I did! I... can't... Can't bear the burden! So much sin, so much filth, so many atrocities... I can't bear it. God Almighty, forgive me my sins! I must take my own life!
No, Francessca, don't do that! Suicide is a sin! NO!!
Aaaahhhh! Gabrath sinect acturis devororum behardos gebell! So begone to burning hell, you damned sucker!
So it's really true. The soul of that girl is possessed by a foul spirit!

Rabathor estreductar! Thorat baentheat! It's just as you've said, you wretch. I've possessed the body of this innocent whore to do with it anything I want. And just that I've been doing. I took her, raped her mind and enslaved her body. Her pain and her grief are so sweet! So, what are you going to do about it? You can't help her now, because I'm here!
Get out of the body of this innocent girl, you foul spirit!

Yuck... I'm all quivering with fear, brave knight. You nearly frightened me, muhehe. But I have to disappoint you, sucker. The bitch is mine and mine she will stay. And moreover, she's no longer as innocent as you think. You can't even begin to apprehend what I've been doing with her. She was so delightful! I'd let her stay conscious for a while for her to helplessly watch all that can be done with what she has between those indecent thighs of hers! The bitch is mine!
We shall see!

God Almighty, who spoke to me through this Holy Scripture, lend me your power so that I may free the body of this innocent girl of the evil powers!

Sahaath aghad! Stop that show, sucker. You can do nothing here and you know it well. Or are you so blind? You won't get the whore even if you kissed my hairy ass at full moon. You won't get her! Nihaard kebr'seth dotorum est!
Archangel Gabriel, who wields the sword of justice, lend me your power and guard me against all the infernal wiles through this rosary!

You will never get her, do you understand? Never! I won't give over what I've gotten the possession of. That sinful whore is mine! I will lead her onto the executioner's stake and will let her watch the flames licking her legs like wanton tongues of infernal tempters! I'll let her scream with pain and horror, I'll let her burn in her own hell!
I sprinkle you with this decoction of magical mandrake root, you foul spirit, to loosen your pestilent roots and force you to leave the body of this poor girl!
