Presently the ruler of this town is Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, son of Grand Duke Danworth Heindrick. King Edward II inducted him into the office of the royal governor of Glatzburg in the year 1213. His deputy is Duke Rowan van Leerin, who got the title of vice-governor two years later thanks to his wealth—no one knew where he had gotten it from.

Hans von Drichtmaul has his renowned armory in Glatzburg. Enrie Jungwirdt the Wise Woman and Paolus Ventimus the Alchemist can sell you potions and various magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum sell just about everything. And Alphonso DiCerbio can get you many a thing, if you don't mind the origin of his goods.

What do I think about this crisis? I will tell you, knight. It's the curse of this era. Nothing like that was possible in my younger days. Nothing of what has befallen us recently could happen then. The faith was strong as the best of steels, men's hearts were unspoiled and God's law was above all things. But now? I'm not surprised God punishes us for all what's happening here.
Could you explain it to me?

So much filth, obscenities, smallness and debauchery I've never seen in my life. Mortal sin everywhere. Heretics walk the world in sheep's clothing and secretly destroy all what our ancestors and fathers created. During last few years so much has been destroyed that our ancestors surely are turning in their graves. I wish I could take the sword in my hand and try to correct what I can. But what a poor old man can do?

Yes, I've heard tidings about a war. Men are being recruited, horses and cattle are being requisitioned and granaries are being filled with supplies, forges are working day and night... who could overlook it? But there's no one to fight against, that's the trouble. There are no rumors about any progressing armies of an enemy. Strange, isn't it? But the truth is there have not been many reports about what's going on behind the borders of the Realm since the Scourges of God struck us.
Yes, that's right. Let's hope it will clear up somehow.
Maybe. Who knows what will happen tomorrow?

The worst monsters of all are the footpads, knight. Let plague and pox get them. They have no respect for anything, those accursed curs. If I were several years younger, I'd beat them like a drum. I'd cut their heads, break their bones, drag them behind a horse and spit on their dead bodies. I wonder why nobody has done it already.

I'm sorry, I allowed myself to be carried away. But the truth is the bands waiting along royal roads and main roads are countless. And the worst of all are the ruffians of that brigand Benthley of Welshrem. Some say that the madness of that man was caused by an unfortunate fate that befell him, but I don't care. He became a castaway, a renegade and a murderer, so he deserves no mercy. His lot kills at sight, nothing interests them, and often they even don't carry away the booty. They just kill. That's crazy!

If there are any rewards announced for killing monsters? Sure there are, knight. Our gracious Grand Duke Heidrick has offered rewards for catching the footpads assaulting people at the roads. If you bring a head or a scalp to Sheriff Smith, he will pay you corresponding reward in gold.

I have a suspicion, but I'm not sure if it has something to do with heresy. I don't like what Duke Rowan van Leerin is doing. He capers about too much for my liking considering that he's only a royal vice-governor. He's starting to behave as if all around belonged to him. Strange. But I'm unable to say whether it has its roots in heresy.

It's said Istwan de Bragho has returned. From the Other World. Have you heard about him, knight? He used to be the royal vice-governor, came here straight from Alvaron from the royal court. He had a recommendation from someone powerful, whose name regretfully stayed hidden from me. But no matter who had established him here, the Duke turned out to be quite a rowdy during those few years he was in his office. What did I say? Rowdy? Filthy pervert he was!

Yes, just so. Not long after his installation young girls began to vanish in the vicinity of Glatzburg. Firstly they were lowborn girls, shepherdesses, charwomen and such, but then daughters of merchants and townsmen started to go missing, and even noble ones. At that time several paladins set out to investigate—they were tirelessly searching like hunting dogs until they really torn the mask off the Duke's face and proved him guilty. He tried to run away but was caught and handed over to the executioner.
So, a happy ending?

But not at all! During his execution the mad Duke uttered a terrible curse: His death shall not stay unrevenged and he shall return and take to Hell with him the souls of all who orchestrated his execution. And it happened so that all the five paladins who caught him are rather cold already. They were all murdered this spring. And they died in quite disgusting ways. Only the headsman Flemberg who executed him is still alive.

The death of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible thing, knight. I'm very sorry our Lord allowed something like that. The criminals must be caught and executed as soon as possible! But otherwise I regretfully don't know a thing about it. I have no idea why the Monsignor went to such a lonely place as the Grand Duke's Gazebo. Nobody goes there anymore.

I've heard the murder of Monsignor Trevorius is the work of a paladin! They found him just above the Bishop's still warm body near the Grand Duke's Gazebo. It's a good place for murder—nobody goes there anymore so the murderer didn't have to concern himself with inconvenient witnesses. But I wonder how the knight managed to lure the Bishop out to such a lonely place...

Fae'Darlion? Hmm... The name doesn't ring a bell. As well as most of the names coming from the ancient Elenian civilization. I've never studied history in such a degree to get deeper knowledge about that ancient era. But people say there are ancient ruins from the times before Ereborn in the vicinity of Baron Edger von Hunth's homestead. So you should direct your search in that direction.
Do you happen to know anything about priest Frederick?

I don't know much about Father Frederick. I exchanged a few words with him now and then, that's true, but he was quite an eccentric man, he kept aloof from people, even from other priests of the Holy Mother Church. I think he was a former mentor and teacher of Judge Welfhar—maybe that's why he selected Glatzburg as the place where he would spend the rest of his days. I've heard all kinds of things about him—supposedly he was a renowned exorcist. I didn't personally see him do any exorcism, but that means nothing. It has been almost two years since his death. The mortis negra took him—the black death. The plague!

The undead in the town streets are really disastrous for whole Glatzburg. If nobody does anything about them the town will turn into a town of ghosts soon. All the remaining life will fade away and only death, fear and despair will stay. And that's just what the chaos worshippers want. To feaze and to demoralize people and to undermine their morals. But I'm certain it will not happen. Although the attacks of the living dead in the streets are alarming, they don't have the character of a targeted attack. They are not so numerous as to endanger the citizens on a larger scale.
But they represent a threat, don't they?

That's true. The question is where do the living dead come from and how many are they. Speaking about it, I have to tell you something. I have a suspicion. Taking into account that the undead don't like daylight, they have to hide somewhere during the day. And I think they've found refuge in the ancient and almost forgotten sewers, built in the days of early Glatzburg and walled up and filled soon after. But what if they were not filled completely? What if the sewers have been surviving for centuries to offer a refuge to the undead? I believe it's just so. Moreover, I found a strange hole at the town dumping ground that leads God knows where. It's quite possible it's one of the forgotten entrances into the city sewers...

There are dozens of myths circulating about Bonhart von Drichtmaul and his miraculous hammer. He made such amazing armor and weapons that even now you can hardly find better—although it's been almost three hundred and fifty years since Bonhart fell in the battle at the Fields of Hallaworth. Because of the barbarian wars he was forced to end the career of a blacksmith and go to fight the pagan invaders.

It's told that before leaving home he buried most of his belongings together with the hammer somewhere near the Devil's Caverns, although the tales tell us about a dozen other probable places. The hiding place is told to be covered by a large stone enchanted so that nobody can roll it away. But people say that once in a year the stone itself rolls away for a while—in the day of Bonhart's death anniversary. Supposedly, the reason is to allow Bonhart to assure himself his hammer is still at its place.

No, knight, I don't know a thing about the abduction of Raquel Gielwitch. It's an unfortunate incident. Several other young girls have gone missing along with her. I shudder to think what could happen to them. They've disappeared without a trace and no one has demanded any ransom. In these days there is not much hope a missing person will be found again. At least not alive.
Have you heard the legend about the Devil's Caverns, knight?
Yes, I have.
No, I haven't. Go on...

It gives me shivers. It's told that near the ruins of Galibornium there is an entrance into deep caverns, leading maybe as far as the very Hell. That's the reason they are called the Devil's Caverns—and also because they're inhabited by devils. Hellspawns looking like giant lizards with a long tails, their bodies covered with scales and their vicious mouths full of sharp teeth. They must have been dwelling there from time immemorial, because even grandfathers of our great-grandfathers talked about them.
Hmm...

There's not much talk about them till they set out on a bloody hunt around their den once in a while. Then they wreak havoc everywhere they go—dead cattle, burned farmhouses, slaughtered hamlets and of course murdered people. But it's told they drag some of the captured away with them and imprison them in Hell. So if I may advise you, knight, stay away from the vicinity of Galibornium!
You should better answer me, good man, or you will, despite your old age, get to know pain you've never dreamed about!
You have the right to dislike me, good man. I don't object to it. But I don't understand why don't you want to answer my question. Surely it won't do any harm.
You are very wise, good man. Only rarely I meet someone so studied as you are. That's why I would be glad if you answered my question.

My God! By Saint Orthenius and the Archangel Gabriel, it's really it! You've returned my honor to me, knight! I've already given up all hope of getting my ring back. Oh, tell me how could I reward you?
Forget about it, good man.
No, knight, I can't forget about it. I... My God... I forgot it! I completely forgot it! How could I?
I don't understand you much, good man. What have you forgotten?
I forgot to report it to Sheriff Smith!
See, eventually you've remembered. You only needed some time.
No, knight, you don't understand. I completely forgot it! I wanted to go and report it to Sheriff Smith immediately, but my damned head...
What did you want to report? Did you witness a crime?

Just so, knight! Several days ago I was returning home in the evening. In a small street near the house of the master armorer Hans von Drichtmaul I sighted several men fighting with someone. I shouted at them and wanted to face them, but they ignored me. They thought I presented no danger to them. And well, they were probably right.
Who were those men? Did you recognize them?
They were masked so I couldn't see into their faces. But despite of it I recognized one of them. By his voice. My hearing is still quite good.
And who was he?
That middleman rascal Alphonso DiCerbio. I've always suspected him of foulness and so seeing him there didn't surprise me. He evidently thought I haven't recognized him, but he was greatly mistaken.
Do you know whom the men were fighting?

Yes, knight. They were fighting young Tom Clifford, son of Johaness Clifford, who is the Chamberlain of Duke Rowan van Leerin. I found his cap on the ground there then. I'm sure the rascals were abducting him!
What happened next?

Those rascals ran away with poor Tom into the evening haze of the rampart district. It would be pointless to go after them, because my old body can hardly walk. I wanted to go and report it to Sheriff Smith and tell it to Chamberlain Clifford, but my memory failed me... A while or two later I didn't remember anything and thought that it was just some daydream or something.
Thank you, good man. You did good to mention it to me.
You're welcome, knight. I hope nothing wrong has befallen the boy because of my forgetfulness...
I hope so too. May I ask you a few questions now?
Certainly, knight. Ask away.

Oh... so it came to trafficking of good turns, knight? People didn't do that in my younger days. Honor was regarded as the greatest virtue. But I see that the times have changed. Regrettably I have nothing to offer you for your so-called goodwill. I don't have anything, I have nothing left. So it's up to you, knight.
In that case I can't help you.
Well, what can I do? I couldn't expect people helping me for free, could I? Farewell.
Wait, I'd like to ask you a few questions.
Really? Well... ask away, then, knight. Maybe you'll learn something...
You're right, it would be dishonorable. I'll get you your ring without demanding any reward.
Thank you, knight. It's very noble of you.
May I ask you a few questions now?
Don't despair, good man. I've found your ring. Here it is.
What would you offer me for bringing you back your ring?
You mentioned being robbed of your ring by footpads. I will bring it back to you!
I would be very grateful to you if you did so, knight. Let the Archangel Gabriel guard you with his angelic shield!

Thieves! Lowbred robbers they are and nothing more! Cutthroats! Wicked footpads! May God forsake them all! I wish somebody would catch them all and execute them to a man! They reinlessly rob and murder as they like and nobody does anything about it! This wasn't possible in the days of King Vilhelm. The roads were safe and footpads were hanging along them like pears.
Who are you, if I may ask?

My name is... oh, my memory... Gusstapho Halworth. Yes, that's right. But everyone here calls me Guss, knight. At least I hope you are a knight—my eyes are not too good anymore, same as my memory. But you should have seen me in the days of King Vilhelm's rule—I was a gem of a man. Well-built, sharp sight... God, now it seems as if it were never true.
What has happened to you, good man, that you are wailing so much about these times?

What else should a helpless old man do, knight? At least I hope you are a knight, my eyes are not too good anymore, same as my memory. Well, listen, knight, what happened to me. I was attacked and robbed! I was returning from a visit to Baron Edger von Hunth—I had paid a visit to him to express my condolences to him in the matter of his deceased father Liam—when I was attacked by some footpads. If I were several years younger I might have been able to defend myself with the sword in my hand. But that's long gone, so they easily overcame me, made fun of me and instead of killing me and granting me a fast death they took my ring and let me live. What a shame! Former First Knight overcome and robbed by some lowbred damned footpads! Now I can just hate myself.
You are the former First Knight?!
Yes, knight, just so. I'm Gusstapho Halworth, the former First Knight of King Vilhelm the Bold.
Forgive me for not being able to hide my discomposure, but it's hard to believe your words. King Vilhelm died more than seventy years ago.

I understand what you mean, knight. Who would think such a feeble old man is the defender of the Realm, am I right? Maybe it really wasn't me. Maybe it was just some dream or a delusion. What really is our past, when no one remembers it and is able to remind or testify it to you? Maybe we all are living in lies...
Well, forget about it. But you mentioned a ring being stolen from you by footpads...
Yes, that's true. Those rascals have robbed me of the most valuable item I've ever had—the ring of the knights of the Archangel Gabriel, given to me by King Vilhelm himself not long before his death.
Eh?! You were the First Knight of King Vilhelm? But that's incredible! I've met the former highest defender of the Realm and the personal confidant of King Vilhelm!

Yes, yes, those and many other honors appertain to the office of the First Knight. And all those honors I was holding for a long twenty years. I have to admit I liked King Vilhelm quite a lot, even if he were stubborn and hardened man. His death has broken my heart. There was no place for me at the knightly court after that. I've backed away to seclusion, changed my name and left the Realm for many years. All that was linking me with my shiny past was the ring of the order of the Knights of the Archangel Gabriel, given to me by King Vilhelm himself not long before his death. And now I've been robbed even of it.
You told the life was better in the days of King Vilhelm. How can you know it? King Vilhelm died more than seventy years ago.
What? That's utter nonsense, knight. It has to be only several winters since King Vilhelm has left us for a better world. I have to know it, because I attended his funeral!
You attended his funeral? How did you get there? Only a limited circle of the highest-ranking nobles may be present at a funeral of a member of the royal family.
If I'm not mistaken I've already told you I was the First Knight of King Vilhelm the Bold, knight.
The First Knight? Forgive me for not being able to hide my discomposure, but it's hard to believe your words.

You are probably right, knight. Who would think such a feeble old man is the defender of the Realm, am I right? Maybe it really wasn't me. Maybe it was just some dream or a delusion. What really is our past, when no one remembers it and is able to remind or testify it to you? Maybe we all are living in lies...
Well, forget about it, good man. Better tell me why were you wailing about your fate so much when I came. Has something evil befallen you?

Sure it has! I was returning from the visit of Baron Edger von Hunth—I had paid a visit to him to express my condolences to him in the matter of his deceased father Liam—when I was attacked by some footpads. If I were several years younger I might have been able to defend myself with the sword in my hand. But that's long gone, so they easily overcame me, made fun of me and instead of killing me and granting me the fast death they took my ring and let me live. What a shame! Former First Knight overcame and robbed by some lowbred damned footpads! Now I can just hate myself.
What?! You were the First Knight of King Vilhelm? But that's incredible! I've met the former highest defender of the Realm and the personal confidant of King Vilhelm himself!

Yes, yes, those and many other honors and duties appertain to the office of the First Knight. And all those honors I was holding for long twenty years. I have to admit I liked King Vilhelm quite a lot, even if he were stubborn and hardened man. His death has broken my heart. There was no place for me at the knightly court after that. I've backed away to seclusion, changed my name and left the Realm for many years. All what was linking me with my shiny past was the ring of the order of the Knights of the Archangel Gabriel given to me by King Vilhelm himself not long before his death. And now I've been robed even of it.

I'm glad to see you again, knight. Have you managed to get back my ring?
Yes, I have, good man. Here it is.
Not yet. But I'd like to ask you a few questions if I may.
Not yet. Farewell.
What do you need, knight?
I've found your ring, good man. Here it is.
I've thought better of it and I decided to get you your ring back. I won't let those footpads to lawlessly steal whatever they wish.
Thank you, knight. Thank you with all my heart. I've misjudged you. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself bless you!
Thank you. May I ask you a few questions now?
Certainly, knight. I'll be glad to answer all your questions.
I'm glad to see you again, knight. Thank you so much for returning my ring to me. It's my only memory of the past. What can I do for you?
May I ask you a few questions?
Nothing right now. Farewell.

What do I think about this crisis? I will tell you, Father. It's the curse of this era. Nothing like that was possible in my younger days. Nothing of what has befallen us recently could happen then. The faith was strong as the best of steels, men's hearts were unspoiled and God's law was above all things. But now? I'm not surprised God punishes us for all what's happening here.

The worst monsters of all are the footpads, Father. Let plague and pox get them. They have no respect for anything, those accursed curs. If I were several years younger, I'd beat them like a drum. I'd cut their heads, break their bones, drag them behind a horse and spit on their dead bodies. I wonder why nobody has done it already.

If there are any rewards announced for killing monsters? Sure there are, Father. Our gracious Grand Duke Heidrick has offered rewards for catching the footpads assaulting people at the roads. If you bring a head or a scalp to Sheriff Smith, he will pay you corresponding reward in gold.

It's said Istwan de Bragho has returned. From the Other World. Have you heard about him, Father? He used to be the royal vice-governor, came here straight from Alvaron from the royal court. He had a recommendation from someone powerful, whose name regretfully stayed hidden from me. But no matter who had established him here, the Duke turned out to be quite a rowdy during those few years he was in his office. What did I say? Rowdy? Filthy pervert he was!

The death of Bishop Trevorius is a terrible thing, Father. I'm very sorry our Lord allowed something like that. The criminals must be caught and executed as soon as possible! But otherwise I regretfully don't know a thing about it. I have no idea why the Monsignor went to such a lonely place as the Grand Duke's Gazebo. Nobody goes there anymore.

I've heard the murder of Monsignor Trevorius is the work of a priest, even worse, of an inquisitor! They found him just above the Bishop's still warm body near the Grand Duke's Gazebo. It's a good place for the murder—nobody goes there anymore so the murderer hadn't to be concerned with inconvenient witnesses. But I wonder how the priest managed to lure the Bishop out to such a lonely place...

No, Father, I don't know a thing about the abduction of Raquel Gielwitch. It's an unfortunate incident. Several other young girls have gone missing along with her. I shudder to think what could happen to them. They've disappeared without a trace and no one has demanded any ransom. In these days there is not much hope a missing person will be found again. At least not alive.
Have you heard the legend about the Devil's Caverns, Father?

There's not much talk about them till they set out on a bloody hunt around their den once in a while. Then they wreak havoc everywhere they go—dead cattle, burned farmhouses, slaughtered hamlets and of course murdered people. But it's told they drag some of the captured away with them and imprison them in Hell. So if I may advise you, Father, stay away from the vicinity of Galibornium!

My God! By Saint Orthenius and the Archangel Gabriel, it's really it! You've returned my honor to me, Father! I've already given up all hope of getting my ring back. Oh, tell me how could I reward you?
No, Father, I can't forget about it. I... My God... I forgot it! I completely forgot it! How could I?
No, Father, you don't understand. I completely forgot it! I wanted to go and report it to Sheriff Smith immediately, but my damned head...

Just so, Father! Several days ago I was returning home in the evening. In a small street near the house of the master armorer Hans von Drichtmaul I sighted several men fighting with someone. I shouted at them and wanted to face them, but they ignored me. They thought I presented no danger to them. And well, they were probably right.

Yes, Father. They were fighting young Tom Clifford, son of Johaness Clifford, who is the Chamberlain of Duke Rowan van Leerin. I found his cap on the ground there then. I'm sure the rascals were abducting him!
You're welcome, Father. I hope nothing wrong has befallen the boy because of my forgetfulness...
Certainly, Father. Ask away.

Oh... so it came to trafficking of good turns, Father? People didn't do that in my younger days. Honor was regarded as the greatest virtue. But I see that the times have changed. Regrettably I have nothing to offer you for your so-called goodwill. I don't have anything, I have nothing left. So it's up to you, Father.
Really? Well... ask away, then, Father. Maybe you'll learn something...
Thank you, Father. It's very noble of you.
I would be very grateful to you if you did so, Father. Let the Archangel Gabriel guard you with his angelic shield!

My name is... oh, my memory... Gusstapho Halworth. Yes, that's right. But everyone here calls me Guss, Father. At least I hope you are a priest—my eyes are not too good anymore, same as my memory. But you should see me in the days of King Vilhelm's rule—I was a gem of a man. Well-built, sharp sight... God, now it seems as if it were never true.

What else should helpless old man do? You are a priest, aren't you? At least I hope you are a priest, my eyes are not too good anymore, same as my memory. Well, listen, Father, what happened to me. I was attacked and robbed! I was returning from the visit of Baron Edger von Hunth—I had paid a visit to him to express my condolences to him in the matter of his deceased father Liam—when I was attacked by some footpads. If I were several years younger I might have been able to defend myself with the sword in my hand. But that's long gone, so they easily overcame me, made fun of me and instead of killing me and granting me a fast death, they took my ring and let me live. What a shame! Former First Knight overcame and robbed by some lowbred damned footpads! Now I can just hate myself.
Yes, Father, just so. I'm Gusstapho Halworth, the former First Knight of King Vilhelm the Bold.

What? That's utter nonsense, Father. It has to be only several winters since King Vilhelm has left us for a better world. I have to know it, because I attended his funeral!
If I'm not mistaken I've already told you I was the First Knight of King Vilhelm the Bold, Father.

Cease thy steps, mortal, may thy pace be none. I see thou are no orc, I hereby ask thee, what dost thou seek in the domains of mine? These domains are my realm and thou lackest the privilege to enter, lest I allow it!
Who are you, unclean spirit? What infernal spell brought you into our world?

I am neither unclean spirit nor a phantom, mortal. I am a soul cursed to wandering after death of its body. I have been dwelling here in my domain for more than five millennia; struggling in vain to escape and to get to the Ancestral Halls. Lo, my megalomania bound me here, to this world, where neither I nor my kin belong—all my brethren were gone millennia ago. Wot! I am Harlior the last great King of Throns beneath the mountains.
The last King of Throns?

Indeed, mortal. I was the King of the great Thron Empire, which was spreading deep at the roots of these mountains. It was in the time of yore when the ancient gods walked this very earth and fought their battles by our side. Lo! Such magnificent days they were when my nation flourished. Those were the days of building, abundance and of glory. Woe! Then fire and despair came from the bowels of the Earth in the wake of Cursed Flame being followed by slaves of his. Orcs. May their kin in its entirety be cast out to the Halls of Damnation and may the body of their cursed Khan Rashgar be laid down into the Rift of Eternal Torment. They came being commanded by their Lord to destroy everything my people had built. Nothing remained. Only my hatred in which I swore not to leave this domain of mine unless it is liberated from the bondage of Rashgar and his accursed orcish kin.
Did you say 'Cursed Flame'?

Indeed, mortal. Cursed Flame brought his orcish slaves from the Accursed Depths wherefrom he himself hails. Many a name has he in various tongues as he is eternal. Even now I can feel presence of his as he lurks beneath in the depths. Beware of Cursed Flame, human. Beware, as he is coming again; being accompanied by slaves of his!
Isn't there a way how to remove your curse, King?

Indeed, there is a way how to remove my curse. If and only if Rashgar dies. Then and only then would I be liberated from my curse and I could embark on the journey to the Ancestral Halls, as its gates has remained closed to me after death of mine.
I'll do it, King Harlior. I'll kill Rashgar and will liberate your soul from the bondage of this world. You have the right to rest in peace, even though you're a pagan.
May thy name be carved in gold into the Wall of Fame, mortal. Go now and take the life of Rashgar away thus allowing me to be released from the millennia long torment of mine.
If I kill Khan Rashgar, what reward would I get for it?
Certainly thou wouldst find a reward for the help of thine, mortal. There are still many treasures hidden in this domain which have not been found by those orcish filths...
I can't make an agreement with a wandering soul of a pagan king.

It saddens me greatly, mortal. Indeed it seems that I shall not be released from the burden of the curse of mine. Thou cannot imagine the greatness of my suffering, mortal. Go now and leave me to the eternal suffering of mine.
I won't allow an infernal pagan monster, who should have been burning in hell by now, to wander these halls! Die!

Thou dost not understand, mortal. I do not belong into this world, I do not know what is the hell you are talking about. Nonetheless, whatever it is, thou canst dispatch me. I am already dead, mortal! Even though thou managed to destroy me, I would appear again being tortured by my curse. Nonetheless the choice is thine!
We shall see, cursed spirit!
I don't believe you! You're just another infernal plot set to set me astray. You shall die!

Thou dost not understand, mortal. I do not belong into this world, I do not know what is the hell you are talking about. Nonetheless, whatever it is, thou canst dispatch me. I am already dead, mortal! Even though thou managed to destroy me, I would appear again being tortured by my curse. Still, the choice is thine!
Then I'm glad I've found you, Harlior. I've promised an orc leader, Horth, to eliminate you.
What?! Thou art an orcish lackey?! Then I must take thy life, mortal, for I cannot stand the shame of talking to one plotting with the servants of Cursed Flame. You shall die!
Kill Khan Rashgar, mortal, so the soul of mine can the Ancestral Halls enter. Release me from my curse...
Hold on, King Harlior. Your soul is going to be in peace soon.
I must disappoint you, Harlior. Your days are over. An orc leader, Horth, will reward me with gold and magic items if I eliminate you.
What?! Thou art an orcish lackey?! Then I must take thy life, mortal, for I cannot stand the shame of talking to one allying with the servants of Cursed Flame. You shall die!

Thou wast successful, mortal! I can feel my curse is shattering and my soul starts ascending up the endless stairs to the Ancestral Halls. Thy name shan't be forgotten, mortal. For your courage take this reward as the last gift of King Harlior from beneath the mountains. Farest thou well, mortal. May your gods bless the steps of the paths thou walkst...
May you find eternal peace, wandering soul. Farewell.
Go away, mortal, and leave the soul of mine to its damn faith.
Not so fast, Harlior. Your days are over. An orc leader, Horth, will reward me with gold and magic items if I eliminate you.

I can feel my curse is weakening and shattering into pieces. The Soul of mine starts floating to the Ancestral Halls. That means Rashgar the Khan is dispatched and the domain of mine is released of his gruesome yoke. Now I can finally enter the Ancestral Halls...
What?! Darest thou to steal?! I shall not suffer that! Thou shalt be punished for thine insolence, thief!
The Orcish king Rashgar is dead. I slayed him!
I've heard that people are wondering about the riches you've gained recently. How did it happen that you managed to get so much money?

Well, gossip is spreading damn fast, right?! Bad mouths are doing the best they can. Well, they can say anything they want—I don't give a damn. It's true that I've gained some money recently. Nevertheless, how I've gained it is none of their business. If everybody knew how to get it, there wouldn't be any poor, right?
So you're not going to tell me where you got the money, right?!
Should I? I don't think so. No offense, knight.
Hmm... thanks.

The royal governor of the City is Robert Heidrick. His deputy, the royal vice-governor, is Duke Rowan van Leerin. They are both thieves in noble disguise—anyway, anybody guarding a treasury is. Well, as the Scripture says—everybody's gonna get what he deserves!
Nothing, knight. Just what I said. Everybody's gonna get what he deserves.

Hans von Drichtmaul runs his famous armory in Glatzburg. He makes really great stuff—I bought some of his specials myself. Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus can provide you with potions and various magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum offer various wares. Last but not least, I like shopping at Alphonso DiCerbio's best. You can buy there almost anything... of course if you don't mind from where he got the goods.
What do I think about the crisis of these days? Hmmm... nothing at all. That's none of my business. I'm just a soldier following orders. I leave thinking to those who were chosen to think.
I heard that there's a war coming. Is it true?
Yep, there are some rumors about a war. It's a flaming job to be a soldier, don't you think? The nobles just invent a damn conflict and a poor footman has to risk his neck...

I've fought lotsa vermin—both human and infernal. Living dead, bandits, infernal lizards from the Devil's Caverns... there are tons of them, damn 'em all. One can never know if it isn't his last day, right? So carpe diem, as they say...

Rewards? Yep, there are some rewards—I think that there's something for bandits pestering the roads. Anyway, I doubt anybody would have the balls to go against brigands. It's much easier to rob than to catch robbers, don't you think?

To tell the truth, I might have a suspicion. It regards a certain very high ranking person. So high ranking that there's nobody above him in Glatzburg. That person behaves as if there were nothing going on—as if there were no Scourges of God, no infernal monsters slaughtering innocents and no brigands threatening travelers. That person wasn't affected by any of the disasters that struck the Realm; moreover his treasury is teeming with gold and his health is just perfect. If I were an inquisitor, I'd have investigated him for sure. You know, there is no smoke without fire.
If I got you right, you're accusing the royal governor of Glatzburg of heresy, right?
You said that, knight. Though I must admit that my description fits Grand Duke Heidrick rather well. But it can still be just a mere coincidence, right?!

I've heard that the madman Henry de Montreaux is wandering around the city. Be careful not to meet him, knight. He's a former paladin who was cast out from the Order because he had killed several of his brothers in duels. He's said to be completely out of his mind and he challenges anybody he meets. He has not lost so far. So take care, knight!
I don't know anything important about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. Just that they found him at the Grand Duke's gazebo.

Well, knight, the rumor is that you bumped off Bishop Trevorius yourself. If I didn't know you, I'd say it's quite likely. At least you can see how blind the justice is—one can be completely innocent and still people can be talking bad about him.

Why are you interested in that case of the murdering undead, knight? It's just another display of infernal powers which you can nowadays see at every corner. Everybody was thinking that it's safe inside the city as if the walls were protected by an army of angels led by the Archangel Gabriel himself. Well, it seems they were awfully wrong. There's nothing anybody can do about it...

Why should I know what has happened with the chain of Commander Ethien de Pasque? He should have taken better care of it. He must know better than others that crime is on a sharp rise every year and that what was sacred once is sacred no more. The times are bad...

Do you know what I'm going to tell you regarding that suspicion? That it's quite likely Brookwelt consorts with the dark powers and uses them to ravish women in the city and in its surroundings. I'm ready to believe it. Still waters run deep... And tell me, who's not soaked with sinful thoughts these days?

It's quite probable that Jeanette really performs black magic. I wouldn't be too surprised if she would be convicted to be a witch. Those watery eyes of hers—they can hide anything, even crime and heresy!
I've heard some legends, but I don't remember them. Why should I? They are good just for fools and dreamers...
Let me make myself clear, soldier—you'll either answer me or you'll be regretting not to for the rest of your life!
I'm not biased against you, soldier. So I hope you're not biased either and will answer my question.
I can't understand why would somebody as strong and brave as you deny a knight his answer...
What would it be?

Well, knight... I've realized that even gold can't grant you all your earthly desires. One could think otherwise, but in fact it is not so. Some human desires just can't be satiated with gold. Let's say desire for women. Well, of course you could say that—there're lots of loose women, but it's not exactly what one could have meant. They give themselves for a handful of coins and for another they'll give you few emotions—as in that song, you know. Well, but overpowering a woman who's not pretending anything and is fighting with you to her last breath to protect her chastity... that's different.
I have a feeling that you might be asking me to help you to take a woman by force.
Well... maybe one could agree with what you've just said.
About whom are we talking?

About Baroness Helen von Hunth, knight. She's the source of my uncontrollable lust. I tried to seduce her, but she fiercely refused. She only fueled the flame of passion in me by that. I must have her! No matter the cost, she must be mine!
I'm afraid, soldier, that your desire will remain unfulfilled. You didn't know Baroness Helen von Hunth is dead, did you?
What?! Helen is dead? That's impossible... Bloody hell, who killed her?!
It doesn't matter, soldier. Anyway, I have a feeling that this information concludes our discussion, because I'll not borrow any money with such high interest rates. Farewell.
It's your lucky day, soldier. By coincidence, Baroness Helen von Hunth is here with me. Well, I promised to return her to her husband, but I think that I'll make a deal with you anyway. Here she is!

By the powers, you're Satan himself, knight! I would've not imagined that heavenly Helen would fall in my lap so easily! I've been longing for this moment so much—and now she's in my grasp! Here's your reward, knight. And as regards this matter, we've never met! Farewell.
Very well, it's a deal. I'll kidnap Baroness Helen von Hunth for you.
Excellent, knight. It's a pleasure doing business with you. Here is your money!
So if I understand you well—if I kidnap Baroness Helen von Hunth, I can keep the money you lend me?
Exactly. Bring me Baroness Helen von Hunth and all the money is yours...
I am sorry, but I can't accept such a deal. Farewell.

Weapons and armor can be bought from Hans von Drichtmaul. Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus can provide you with potions and magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum offer various wares. Alphonso DiCerbio will also sell you almost anything—if you don't mind the origin of his wares.

I don't know what to think about the crisis. Guess it seems bad enough. There are rumors spreading. Bad and disturbing rumors. It seems that the monsters in the Realm are on the rise. There's news from Hillbrandt concerning orcs—the monsters from legends and myths. Here in Glatzburg, there are those scaly devils living in the Devil's Caverns—at least according to the locals. The people are afraid of their own shadows and to make it worse there are the rumors about a war...
Yes, I've heard them too. Thanks!
You're welcome, knight. I wish there were a miracle, like the Archangel Gabriel coming down from the Heaven correcting all wrongs. But, of course, that's not gonna happen...
War, you say? I've not heard about it. Do you know any details about it?

I don't know much, knight, but I've been serving in the army long enough to realize that there's something going on. The entire garrison is on alert and no soldier can leave the city. New recruits are drafted, granaries are filled with supplies... well, something's brewing and what else than war could it be? Well, but against whom it should be waged remains rather unclear.

I don't wanna scare you, knight, but you can meet living dead right here in the city streets after dusk. It is really as I say—I swear on my dead mother. Nobody knows where they come from; all of a sudden the streets are crawling with them and anyone who gets within their claws is done for. Have you ever seen a mob of living dead tearing a screaming victim into pieces? I have and I must tell you that I almost crapped my pants—even though I was in that slaughter at Rottenheim in 1215. As suddenly as they appear they disappear just at cockcrow—as if they went to Hell itself.
Sheriff Smith pays gold for heads or scalps of brigands you bring him. The reward was declared by Grand Duke Heidrick in an attempt to suppress robbery. If you ask me, I don't think he succeeded.

The murder of monsignor Trevorius is a very serious problem, knight. One can feel the shiver running down his spine when he thinks about it. People say he was murdered near the royal gazebo. What could he be doing at such a deserted place? Some say he was there to meet with hellspawns whom he secretly served. But I don't believe it much.

I've heard that Bishop Trevorius was murdered by a paladin. Can you imagine something that dreadful? A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, instead of serving God and fighting hellspawns, is killing servants of God. He must have been completely possessed by dark powers because he mutilated the Bishop's body just after he had sodomized it!
Look, soldier, you're going to answer me, or...!
You don't like me, it's clear. But it doesn't mean you won't be talking with me, does it?
You're a strong and brave man, soldier. That's why I don't believe you would refuse to answer a knight a simple question...
Hello, knight. Have you come to perform the last rites on me?
Why? Do you think you need it?
One can never know, as people say... Especially these days. I would not have imagined that one day I'll be guarding here and everything around me will be falling apart.
Perhaps it won't be that bad...
Well... I could argue about that, but I'd hate getting into trouble, you see. After all—I can do my job and those few gold coins I get for it I can spend as I see fit...
I see, so your discontent stems from your low pay, right?
Could be so, knight. But not necessarily. It would depend on how high the pay would be...
I see. Nonetheless I can't help you with that.
Well, you're right, knight. Can I do something for you or have you come just to boost my spirit?
In fact I'd like to ask you some questions, if I can.
Go ahead, knight. Maybe I can be useful to you...
I don't need anything in particular, soldier. Farewell. And don't lose heart, everything will turn good eventually.
Of course, of course, knight. I'm looking forward to it!
Do you really need it already?
Well... one can never be sure. I'd hate to miss something. Can I do something for you or have you come just to gratify me with your presence?
Well, go ahead, knight. Maybe I can be useful to you...
I don't need anything in particular, soldier. Farewell.

If you are looking to buy weapons and armor, knight, I recommend that you visit Hans von Drichtmaul's armory shop. You can get magic items and potions at the seer Enrie Jungwirdt or the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. The innkeepers Weintraum and Wanda Gielwitch buy and sell all kinds of things. And then there is Alphonso DiCerbio, who is said to be selling stolen goods.
What do you think about the current crisis affecting our Realm, Lady Baroness?

I'm scared to death by the disasters that have happened in the past few years, knight. I'm not a hysterical woman and I know how it feels to live in poverty—me and my husband have lived in it long enough. But still it scares me what I see around me. The true faith is failing, there's no doubt about that. People no longer believe things could get better and they're looking for a solution—a way to escape. No wonder the heretic sects are so successful—they are offering what people have lost—the faith. I don't know whether this is the end of the world but many think so. They say God has turned from us and left us to the mercy of the beasts which not only want our lives but souls as well.
I heard some disturbing rumors about a war, Lady Baroness. Do you know anything about that?
I heard that there was a war brewing. They requisitioned our only horse so there must be some truth in it. God save us.

I don't know if it has something to do with heresy but I think Duke Rowan van Leerin beats his wife. She has bruises everywhere, whip wounds and sometimes even a black eye or a sore lip. She tries to hide it by make up or by telling everybody that she fell of a horse but she can't deceive me. Duke van Leerin tortures his wife both physically and psychically. Have you ever spoken with her? She's completely absent-minded, she speaks as if dazed.

I don't know if you heard about it but a few young girls have disappeared in Glatzburg without a trace lately. It's a mystery, it looks as if they vanished because of some evil spell or as if they were taken by monsters. That's what people in the city think but I think they became victims of lecherous desires of some heretics who don't believe in the sacrament of marriage and praise lechery and sin instead. I'm afraid nobody will ever see the girls again.

I'm praying for the salvation of Monsignor Trevorius's soul, knight. He was a great person. Talented, considerate, wise, kind and full of understanding. But at the same time he was strict and unyielding when it came to the protection of the faith. He was trying to change some of the oldest traditions of the Holy Mother Church. In other words he was rather listening to the Holy Scripture and the sermons of the prophets than to the church doctrine. He was one of those controversial radical priests that are trying to return the Church to its roots. I just hope the murder had nothing to do with his opinions. That would mean that the disputes inside the Holy Mother Church were so serious the priest would even be willing to kill because of it!
Do you know anything about the priest Frederick?

Father Frederick? The old priest who died of plague two years ago? Yes, it must be him you mean. I don't know much even though people talked a lot about him. He was supposed to be a famous exorcist. Came to Glatzburg couple of years ago, probably wanted to live the rest of his years in peace which he managed to do, in a way... Try asking Judge Welfhar, I think they used to spend a lot of time together.

I know Hans Thomas Brookwelt, he is the local carpenter. It is strange that he hasn't married yet considering his age, but I don't think he's a rapist and a heretic. I mean, he could be, of course, but my female instinct tells me that even though he might be sexually starved he wouldn't lay his hands on a woman.
I heard a rumor that your servant-girl Jeanette was a witch practicing dark rituals. What do you think about it?

Our Jeanette a witch? That's a complete nonsense! I absolutely trust her—she's a decent young girl, very quiet, there have never been any problems with her. Not a single conflict, she always does what she's told. So whoever spreads gossip like that is a filthy liar and should be punished!
I'm looking for missing Raquel Gielwitch. Do you know anything about her?

The disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch and of few other young girls is a terrible case, Father. It proves that danger waits everywhere you turn these days. You never know which shadow can Satan or his servants be hiding in to take you and drag you right to Hell!
So you think the girls have been kidnapped by Satan, Lady Baroness?

Yes, knight. I think demons came and took them to Hell to feed on their bodies and torture their souls. Where else could they have disappeared without a trace? I'm not a superstitious person but I've learned not to underestimate infernal powers. There is more of them than Monsignor Trevorius would admit during his sermons.

They tell many legends and stories here in Glatzburg, knight. Did you hear about the ancient sewers underneath the city? According to the legend there should be ancient sewers underneath Glatzburg built by Grand Duke Harold at the foundation of the city in 223. He used pagan Erebornian builders he captured during the war and their lives were spared because of their skills. They are said to have built an intricate complex of tunnels and corridors which would take the sewage out of the city. But few years later the Church Council decided that everything pagan was cursed and it must have been destroyed. So the sewers were filled up, the entrances walled in and the city has been suffering of terrible dirt since.
Interesting. And do you think the sewers have been filled in completely?

People say that the sewers still exist, knight. That they haven't been filled in completely and parts of them still are underneath the city. From time to time somebody gets lost without a trace falling into a hole which all of a sudden opens in a street. Or we get huge crowds of sewer rats and everybody wonders where does such a huge crowd comes from. All in all, it's quite possible that the sewers still exist underneath the city although they don't serve the purpose they were originally built for.
You better answer, Lady Baroness. You never know how much pain a wrong answer could cause.
Please, Lady Baroness, answer my question. I'm sure you understand how important it is.
There's no doubt that you are a wise and educated woman, Lady Baroness. An answer of such a person would be extremely helpful, believe me. Please answer my question.
Oh God, please, help me. Help me out of this hell! I beg you, good man, have mercy with me!
I'm Baroness Helen von Hunth. The servants of the psycho Benthley of Welshrem kidnapped me and since then I've been held at this terrible place. I beg you, get me out of here, whoever you are.
Tell me more about your kidnapping.

Couple days ago I left to Glatzburg to deliver a dress I made for one of my clients. I make my living by sewing, you see? When I was on my way back me and my old servant were attacked by the brigands of Benthley of Welshrem. I thought they were going to kill me right there but they took me to this terrible place instead. You can smell death here everywhere you turn. Please, knight, get me out of here!
You don't have to be afraid anymore, Lady Baroness, I promised your husband I was going to bring you back.
Good heavens, I'm saved! Thank you, Saint Gabriel—I knew you were going to answer my prayers! And thank you, knight! I'll never forget that!
Let's go.
I didn't come to save you, good woman. I came to kill you. It's a way to prove Benthley of Welshrem that there was nothing human left in me. God wants you dead—as well as all the others!
Let me live... I beg you, please, let me live... Noooooo!
I'm glad I found you, Lady Baroness. I'm taking you away from here. I promised the soldier Harph that I'd bring you to him. And don't try to resist me!
God, what's happening? Why do you want to take me to Harph? He's a lecher who tried to rape me some time ago! Please, knight, help me get back to my husband!
No way! I got paid from Harph to bring you to him and that's what I'm going to do. Let's go!
Is there anything I can do for you, Lady Baroness?
Oh yes, knight. Please, take me to my husband baron Edger von Hunth.
Of course, Lady Baroness. I won't refuse help to a neighbor in need. Let's go.
Thank you, knight. Thank you thousand times!
You're welcome, Lady Baroness. Let's go.
Can I count with a reward of some kind, Lady Baroness?
Oh, my God... I'm not sure whether there is a single gold piece left in my husband's treasury, knight...
Hello, knight. I'm happy to see you. I'll be forever grateful for freeing me from the madman Benthley of Welshrem! Me and my husband don't have much but still we are happy. What's bringing you here?
Can I talk to you, Lady Baroness?
Of course, knight. No problem. What do you need to know?
I'd like to ask you something, Lady Baroness. I heard you were a skilled seamstress and many Glatzburg ladies wore a dress made by you. So I decided to ask you for help.
I'd be happy to help, knight. What exactly do you need?
I need you to make a wedding dress for Baroness Elisabeth van Singier.

But of course, knight. I'm going to make the prettiest dress for what you've done for me. I know Lady Baroness Elisabeth van Singier—she used to be my friend when I lived in Glatzburg. So I'm going to do my best. You can pick the dress up anytime it's convenient.
All right, thank you. Can I ask you something else?
Of course, knight. I'll be happy to answer anything you ask. What is it?
I'll stop by soon. Goodbye.
I wanted to ask whether the dress I asked you to make is finished.
You came early, knight. But fortunately, I'm almost finished. Hold on a moment...
Of course. There's no hurry. Take your time, Lady Baroness.

Don't worry, knight. The dress will be beautiful... just the few last stitches and I'm finished. Here you go, knight. I wish it brought Lady Baroness Elisabeth van Singier good luck. And say hello for me. We used to be good friends...
Thank you, Lady Baroness. May I talk with you some more?
You're going with me, Lady Baroness. I promised the soldier Harph that I'd bring you to him. Don't try to resist!
What do you mean, knight? I don't understand... why do you want to take me to Harph? He's a lecher who tried to rape me some time ago!
That doesn't matter. He paid me to bring you and that's what I'm going to do. Let's go!
Are you crazy, knight? This is kidnapping! Don't touch me! Heeelp!
Nobody's going to help you here, Lady Baroness!
I came to kill you, Lady Baroness. It's God's will that you die!
What are you saying, knight? Is that some kind of a bad joke?
Of course not, Lady Baroness. Pray for the last time!
My God, you must have gone mad! Leave me alone! Get your hands of me! Heeeeelp!
No one's going to help you here, Lady Baroness!
I was passing by so I stopped to see how you were doing. But I'll be going now. Goodbye.
Farewell, knight. And God bless you.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe that! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights are thieves! Shame!

If this is the only way to help you, Father Herbertius, then take my blood!

Fool! You are so stupid, you are making me sick. A curse is exactly what I want from my new existence. Your blood will make me stronger, as well as anyone's blood would and you gave it to me freely. How hilarious. Your life belongs to me now!

Welcome to my undead kingdom of fear. Look into my eyes and you will see the emptiness death is to bring you. As soon as your soul leaves its cooling body I will imprison it with my powers between Purgatory and Hell and you will be my miserable slave until your flesh rots and your bones turn to dust.
Who are you? You look like a human but I can feel such deadly coldness emanating from you...

I'm Bishop Herbertius... or at least I used to be him, when I was still alive. But, thanks to the Beast, I've become the ruler of the undead. I'm the Duke of the night and the shadow of death. I hunt for life and rule helplessness. Nothing living I touch survives. Not even you!
Stop it, Father Herbertius. I know you are under a terrible curse and maybe there is a way to help and save your poor soul!

Oh... you surprise me, fool... I wasn't expecting any help from someone summoned to destroy all evil. The terrible curse I myself called upon me could be removed. A mortal has to offer me his blood freely. Then I will be released from the terrible world of living corpses and the Beast will have no power over me!
Is there no way the terrible curse could be removed from your lost soul?
Actually, there is a way, son. It's so sinister though that no mortal will be willing to do what's necessary. Not even you who has shown more bravery than anyone by coming here.
What way could it be removed?
My curse could be removed if a mortal offered me his own blood freely. Then my soul would be free and I could go on to the hereafter.
Your death will remove the evil from this holy place, monster!
Death cannot stop me for it has no power over me. It cannot kill that which is not living anymore. You will see for yourself, my slave!
Can you tell me of the crusade you were in?

You want to hear the story of my life? Well, sit down then—it's going to be a long story. It all started when I was at the dangerous age, knight. You know, when you start liking girls and you feel like the king of the world thinking nothing can ever happen to you. Well, something happened to me. I was caught by Baron Trow von Ulbracht having fun with his only daughter in a barn. He got furious and it almost cost me my life. He started yelling that I had dishonored his only daughter, slashing his sword around so violently that he almost hit his naughty daughter. I managed to run away to my village but the next day the Baron came, resolved to have me executed. Things were getting tough—as the son of a poor peasant I had no means of defending myself so I took the only chance I had at the time. I joined the party of Paul Wachthremm. At the time, he believed he would be the person to free the Holy Grave of the First Prophet from the dirty pagan hands of the Jad-Habaal Empire and answered Pope Pius' call for a crusade. I accepted the cross and ended up in the Duke's army.

We marched across the whole Realm to Alvaron, where I and a thousand others boarded a ship which took us to the Kingdoms of Calmariland. There we joined King Bert of Tenerick's army and marched to the holy mountain Estroppel at the borders of the Empire. It was here that Pope Pius the Sixth personally performed a mass blessing all the crusaders and pronouncing us the knights of God. Then I got a sword and some armor. They put me in a saddle and for a couple of months we traveled across the Empire to the borders of the pagan Empire Jad-Habaal. It wasn't a pleasant journey. Some parts of the Empire are a complete wasteland and we were starving so the army was half destroyed before we met the first pagan bastards. I survived though and I saw true hell. Have you ever been to Jad-Habaal, knight? It's a desert. Sand and heat and little shade anywhere. The pagan bastards knew how to survive there but we didn't. The people who died in the last crusade didn't know it and those who died after us didn't figure it out either. It was simply hell.
And what happened next?

First, the war was going well, I must say. With King Bert of Tenerick, who was already called the Iron King at the time, at the head of the army, we fought our way to Jevaran. We managed to conquer it after several months and thus we freed the Holy Grave of the First Prophet. At that time we thought nothing could stop us and nothing could stop the victory of the true faith over the pagans. So we went on to the center of Jad-Habaal. The pagans would only send small untrained units who didn't stand a chance against our cavalry. We were crushing them under the hooves of our horses and conquering miles. We defeated some of their cities and many strongholds and we were positive the final victory was at hand. But, we were awfully wrong. After conquering Nafrat we found out about a huge army of pagans coming from the south. Before we could do anything we were cut off. The land we had conquered. including Jevaran, fell back to the hands of pagans and we were under siege in Nafrat. The three years I spent there made me thirty years older, knight. The situation was desperate. We were able to hold the walls but the numbers of the Jad-Habaal bastards were infinite. It was like looking at an endless sea.
How did you get out of the siege? Did you defeat them?

No, knight. After three years they defeated us. Murdered most of us and made slaves of those who survived. Me and King Bert of Tenerick were amongst them. An owner of a galleon bought us at a slave market and I spent the next two years rowing at the Southern Ocean together with the King and a few other comrades. You wouldn't believe how much landmass lies there, knight. All our maps of the known world are just tiny bits compared to the pagan lands. I saw worlds which I'd never thought could exist. Islands with people black as coal and all naked. Countries where dark people with black hair built temples taller than mountains. Simply unbelievable but we also had to bear the terrible labor and torture of our master.
How did you manage to escape?

A violent storm carried our galleon far north. The first ship we met was coming from Tenerick. What a coincidence! A fight started during which we managed to free ourselves and take revenge on our cruel masters. We thought we were saved but we were wrong. King Bert had been declared dead meanwhile, and his brother Edgar took his place. When the captain of the ship found out it was King Bert, he had us all locked up into metal crates and transported to the court of Tenerick. Edgar apparently wasn't willing to give up his throne and it looked like we had returned just to be executed quietly. But a noble lady, who found out about everything from the prison guards, helped us out. King Bert gathered his loyal vassals in the country, defeated his brother in a single battle and got his throne back. He gave a generous reward to all who got through the six-year hell with him. Before I returned back to the Realm I'd spent all of it. I was spending money like water. Who'd blame me—I almost wasn't alive the previous six years.
How did it end?

When I came back to Hillbrandt, nobody recognized me. They didn't believe it was me. I kept my crusader name Herminus and went to fight in all kinds of wars. I became a mercenary soldier because the only thing I knew was killing and staying alive. The years passed and one day I found out that I couldn't lift a hand-axe anymore. I quit my craft and went back to Hillbrandt. I've been living here since and waiting for Death to come for me.
That's... an amazing story, good man. You've done so many great things!

It must have been God's will, knight. I haven't told the story to anyone for quite some time. I'll give you something for your willingness to listen to an old veteran. I brought it from my travels. I don't need it anymore but you might find it useful.
Do you really think I'm going to believe something like that, good man?
I'm not going to make you, knight but you will see for yourself how unpredictable fate can be.
I've heard enough, good man. Can I ask about something else?
Of course, knight. I just thought you were interested.
Strange worlds, you say? They burn people for saying things like that in the Empire, good man. You're lucky we are in the Realm and you are talking to me. Can you answer a few questions?
Whatever you wish, knight. I did live through what I said and I have no reason to lie and make up stories though.
Must have been terrible but I'm sure it ended well. Could I interrupt you there and ask you something else?
Of course, knight.
Interesting observation. It looks like a long story and I don't have time to listen to it further, good man. Can I ask you something else?
It looks like a long story, good man. Unfortunately, I don't have time for it.
I'm sorry, I don't remember.

Where can you buy supplies? Supplies? What supplies? Ah you mean supplies... Well, if you're looking for war gear, you should see the blacksmith Hammerhand. He's an expert. At the herb healer Würtenrodt's you can get all kinds of magic potions, if you don't make her mad—she won't deal with you then. The same applies to astrologist and alchemist Theil Brechthold. But at Father Dominicus' you will be welcome anytime. The innkeeper Joseph Truthorn and the stead-holder Suzan Brauchner buy and sell all kinds of things but their prices aren't very good.

The times have never been so bad as they are now, knight. Even the crusades were a piece of cake compared to what's happening now. I know the local people pretty well. They are mostly stubborn and brave because living in a land like this they can't afford to be oversensitive like those who live in the big cities to the South. Yet they are turning hopeless and desperate. All the monsters out there, the heretics amongst us and death everywhere you look... it makes them lose faith and determination to fight for their destiny.

You can encounter all kinds of devilish monsters here in Hillbrandt, knight. I was fighting against many things during the crusades but I never saw so many monsters in one place. At night, watch out for giant bats. They come down from the sky and bite through your neck before you can say 'amen'. Most of them can be encountered at the Dragon Rock but the whole Moonshine Mountains are full of them. You can also find giant spiders there, some of them big as a cow. They carry deadly poison—one bite and you're dead...

I can't help you with the heretics, knight. My eyesight is not what it used to be, I'm almost deaf and when I limp, my knees creak so loud that even if I caught somebody performing a heretical ritual, he'd run away long before I'd get there. Sorry.

What's happened here lately? Natalia Reichmann is dead, knight. I've known her family since the time her grandmother was a young girl. Very decent people—even though they're mostly business people. I can't believe she's no longer with us. It looks like she was murdered by landsknecht Olfghard, because her jewelry was found on him. He said he was innocent but nobody believed him. He was arrested and put in prison. Unfortunately, he managed to escape and nobody knows where he is now.

I heard he had opened the gate for the orcs during their recent attack on the town but to tell you the truth I don't believe it. I don't know him well but I think he's dedicated to his duties. I don't think he's a heretic. There's not many of us here in Hillbrandt who think so.
The Monstrance of Saint Orthenius has disappeared. Do you know anything about it?

I don't know anything about the theft, knight. I heard it must have been someone with dark powers because it took a whole day to wake up the priests who were praying for the salvation of humanity at the church that day.
I'm searching for the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Master Edmond d'Arvias losing his sword? That's strange... A sword is a symbol of the order of the Brotherhood of Righteous. It's their symbol. Losing it is a great disgrace. I suppose it was stolen from him. If I find out who it was, I'll let you know, knight.

My favorite is the one about the Tree of Death. It says that at the end of the wars with the barbarians in 988, when the barbarians were running from the victorious orthodox armies back north, Duke Welliar's cavalry laid siege to a barbarian clan. It had more women and children than effective fighters but Welliar still attacked. The remaining fighters were killed and the women and the children hid at the top of a hill at an old spreading oak. They wanted to surrender but the Duke had them all hanged right on the tree.

The next day some Hillbrandt people came to bury the dead but the nooses were empty and the tree dead. It's believed that the souls of the barbarians entered the tree to await the time of their revenge. It's true that in restless windy nights. you can hear a strange moaning and howling from that direction. Nobody dares to go there anymore.

He would sell all kinds of strange items. As far as I know he did a lot of searching for various pagan artifacts and relics because there has always been a great demand for those. He came to Hillbrandt often, because the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains were inhabited by many civilizations, even by the ancient empire of Thron.
I see. Go on.

Of course, knight. I would sit with him in Truthorn's Inn now and then. He was interested in what I had to say because I did a lot of traveling and saw many places and therefore could give him much useful information. But he would never talk about the business; that he kept to himself. The last time I saw him he mentioned getting this great job which could get him a lot of money. It concerned some book he had managed to find after years of searching and now he had a buyer. I'd say if it was such a special book, he could have been murdered because of it. But of course, this is just my opinion.
Hillbrandt and the surrounding lands are ruled by Duke Weinberg who is the royal governor. The vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. God help them in their difficult duty...
Answer now, Herminus, or I'll have you arrested and racked for!
I know I'm not your favorite, Herminus, but that doesn't mean you can avoid my question, does it?
You're a wise and experienced person, Herminus. I think you can judge what to tell me and what not. That's why I don't understand why you hesitate to answer my question.
My name is Herminus. It's not my true name, I've forgotten that. This name was given to me by my comrades when we first went against the pagans to free the Holy Grave from Jad-Habaal rule.
Wait, good man... you mean you were in the first crusade?

Of course, knight. As a truly faithful person, I did everything I could to free the Holy Grave of the First Prophet from the hands of the filthy Jad-Habaal pagans. There were terrible fights. The blood was up to our knees sometimes. They were great times full of heroism and brotherly love.
But the first crusade ended more than a hundred years ago...
Has it been so long already? It seemed to me as if it had been just few years since I've come back. A hundred years you say?
Forget it, good man. Can I talk to you for a moment?
But of course. I don't have much to do today anyway. What do you want to know?
Well then, Goodbye.
Pleased to meet you. Goodbye.
Who are you, knight? I don't know you... you must be new to Hillbrandt.
You're right, good man. Who are you?
It's not your business. You tell me who you are!
But we've talked already...
Really? Well, that's possible. What can I do for you?
Oh, nevermind. Goodbye.
