Of course, noble sir. As a truly faithful person, I did everything I could to free the Holy Grave of the First Prophet from the hands of the filthy Jad-Habaal pagans. There were terrible fights. The blood was up to our knees sometimes. They were great times full of heroism and brotherly love.
Who are you, noble sir? I don't know you... you must be new to Hillbrandt.
A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! Something like that could never happen in my younger days!
Aaaahhh! Finally some fresh meat. I've been waiting so long for a good piece of raw meat. Come here, mortal!
Who are you, lost soul?

Who am I? Well... that's hard to say. Call me what you want, it doesn't matter anymore. I used to be Honoricus Flavius. Yes, I remember the name. It's been so long... since I was still mortal. I was ruling Galibornium, one of the richest Erebornian provinceshere in the Filkland Peninsula. As I said—it's been so long... It's not true anymore. Fortunately!
What brought you back amongst the living? You must know there's no room for creatures like you.
You're wrong, mortal. More fallen souls will come soon. There's not enough room for them in Hell and the infernal gates are opening but enough of talking. I'm hungry for your flesh. Die!
Die, spawn of darkness! Begone back to the infernal abyss you came from!
I'm sorry, mortal, but it won't be me who will leave for hell in a moment. I didn't spend such a long time lying in my grave to be sent back by the first mortal I encounter. Die!

Ahhhh... fresh meat! I can feel the heady taste of hot blood running from a lacerated, cooling body. I can almost hear the screaming of the dying—the desperate hopelessness in it—while his bones are cracking and his flesh disappears in my mouth. There will be a feast today. We'll finally have plenty to eat. The terrible hunger is ruining me!
Who are you, monster? What kind of infernal powers have brought with you to this world?

Who... me? Nobody. Death, but I used to be... somebody. I had a name. Horathius... Yes, that was my name. I used to be... alive. That was before though. After, I was taken to Hell and hunger has been ruining me ever since! I can't stand it. My body... it's rotting, falling apart. I don't feel the pain, just terrible hunger. It's consuming me, I can't resist it. I want to... I have to... kill you!
Wait, maybe there is a way to remove the curse from your soul?

No... That's impossible. The hunger's burning my insides. I have to kill you. I wasn't allowed to rest in a proper grave. None of us were. They left our bodies to the mercy of demons and to eternal damnation. I must kill you!
What are you talking about? Who left your bodies to the mercy of demons?

Who? The orcs, of course! They came and made me... what I'm now. They are responsible for the hunger which makes me kill. I don't feel anything, my heart isn't beating, my body's falling apart. The hunger's ruining my mind. When I feed on your flesh I might be able to rest in peace for a while!
Don't count on that, monster!
You're right. You are an infernal monster and you belong to hell!

Yes... I am a monster. My heart's not beating and my body's falling apart. The hunger is ruining me. It's tearing my insides apart and it's making me kill every living thing. That's why I'm going to kill you too. Your warm blood and fresh meat will help me satisfy the hunger for a while!
Look what terrible evil's walking this world. God, give me the strength to carry the heavy burden of justice!

There's no other way... you must die. I will feed on your flesh and satisfy the hunger burning in my insides for a moment. I must hear you giving a death rattle because only then will my hunger be satisfied. There's no other way for me!
In that case, only death can free you!
My name is Horst. And my father always told me not to talk to paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. So I'm not going to talk to you!
Who is your father?
Why are you not supposed to talk to paladins?
Because my father said they were stupid and you know what, knight? Looking at you, I see he was right!!
Well... do as you think. Goodbye.
I'm afraid you're going to have to talk to me, boy. You are suspected of being in congress with infernal powers...
What? I'm not in any congress! Leave me alone or I will tell my father and he'll deal with you!
You were seen using black magic to put the guards at the city gate to sleep and let a gang of werewolves in. What do you say about that?
I hate you! I hate you all! As my father says—you're not good for anything but food. When I grow up, I'll eat all of you!

You really want to know? I'll tell you then! Wulfhyrr, the terrible Prince of the Wolves is my father. It was he and his gang that I opened one of the city gates for, every full moon—so they can capture a human victim and bring it to the altar of our bloody God, Urrm! You people are like sheep. It's so easy to get rid of you!
Oh my God... You're coming with me, boy. You must be tried for your crimes—no matter what your age is!
I'm not going anywhere with you, whhhhhhgggrrrrr! I'm strong enough to hunt on my own! I'll kill you. I will! Whaaaauuuuuu!
Hello boy.
Jeez, are you a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?
Yes, I am a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. But who are you?
It's impolite to answer a question with a question. First, tell me who you are.
You again? I told you I wasn't going to talk to you!
I was hoping you'd changed your mind.
I didn't! I don't see any reason to!
I think you should think twice about such a decision, boy. Do you know who I am?
Don't try to threaten me. If you do, I'll tell my father and he'll deal with you. I'm not going to talk to you, no matter what!
Goodbye then!
They say that the best punishment for thieves is to chop off their hands at the wrists, knight. So be careful or you might spend the rest of your life begging somebody to feed you!
My name is Horst. My father always told me not to talk to priests so I'm not going to talk to you!
Why are you not supposed to talk to the clergy?
Because my father said they were stupid and you know what, Father? Looking at you, I see he was right!!
Jeez, are you a priest?
Yes, I am. Who are you?
They say that the best punishment for thieves is to chop off their hands at the wrists, Father. So be careful or you might spend the rest of your life begging somebody to feed you!
My name is Horst. And my father always told me not to talk to nobles. So I'm not going to talk to you!
Why are you not supposed to talk to nobles?
Because my father said they were stupid and you know what, sir? Looking at you, I see he was right!!
Jeez, are you a noble?
Yes, I am a noble. But who are you?
They say that the best punishment for thieves is to chop off their hands at the wrists, sir. So be careful or you might spend the rest of your life begging somebody to feed you!
Really? The King under the Mountains finally dead? But then... The Horth's clan can go look for the Thron treasure under the Mountains! Very good, mortal. Horth's happy.
Give me the reward you promised then, and I'm leaving.
Oh no, mortal. Horth doesn't think it be a good idea giving you gold or artifacts. On the contrary, Horth thinks he kills you and then eats your flesh. Yes, that be much better!
A betrayal? You will pay for it, orc!

So, you are the human who comes to the place where the orcs rule, huh? Then you must be a great warrior or a powerful shaman. Horth praises people like that, even if they come from a lower race. Horth is not stupid. Horth is well aware that not all from your race believe in God. Many of them have the Mark of the Beast on their soul which the orcs have carried since the time they were lead out of the Eternal Damnation by Cursed Flame at the dawn of ages. Maybe you carry the Mark of the Beast as well!
Who is that Cursed Flame, you've just mentioned?

Cursed Flame? He lord of the Orcs. Our ruler. At the dawn of the ages he freed the race of Emperor Rashgar from the Eternal Damnation and brought them here to destroy the Thron kingdom under the Mountains. Then, after a long time, he brought them orcs here again. This time to destroy the low race of people! With the exception of those who carry the Mark of the Beast, of course.
Let's say I have the Mark. What would that mean?
It would mean that you're a friend of the orcs, human and a friend of Horth! In that case, Horth endows you with gold and weapons.
But there is a catch, isn't there?

Of course. Horth endows you with gifts if you kill the ghost of the Thron king who has been appearing in the orc caves for ages. Many Horth's orcs died by his hand. You kill him, human, and Horth will give you presents none of your race has ever dreamed of.
We have a deal, Horth. I'll take care of the ghost.
Good. Go and destroy him, so that he never shows up in our kingdom again.
What presents in particular are you talking about, monster? Uhm... I meant to say Horth.
Gold, magic weapons, armor, rings, helmets, necklaces... anything human heart desires!
I'm not making a dirty deal like that!
In that case, Horth will feed on your insides, worm!
I killed the ghost of King Harlior, Horth.
I have no Mark of the Beast. On the contrary, I follow the word of the First Prophet.
Really? What is your First Prophet telling you?
He's telling me to clean this place of all evil!
So? Did you destroy the damn ghost of the King under the Mountains, human?
Not yet, Horth. Have patience.
Hurry, then, so that Horth can endow you with gold!
No, Horth, I didn't kill him. To tell you the truth, I've changed my plans.
Huh? Really? What are your plans now, human?
To kill you!
I will not kill him. I will not undertake that task.
Then Horth is going to kill you, worm!
Yes, Horth, I killed him. If you can call it that.
What? A disgusting human worm stealing in Horth's residence?! He's gonna pay for that with his life!
According to the name carved in the tombstone the sarcophagus belongs to Father Frederick. I'll see what's hidden in there...
Hmm... There's nothing but remains of the deceased. It looks like Father Frederick lived humbly and modestly as appropriate for a God's servant.
But wait, what's this? A book! Father Frederick is grasping it tightly even though he's been dead for many years now. I'm going to take it, it might be useful.
The grave belongs to the Gotfried family.
I'll see what it's hiding...
I'd rather not disturb the eternal peace of the deceased...

Since I have a bottle of holy water on me I can sanctify the grave immediately—just like the apothecary Thelma Ulthraum told me to. In the name of omnipotent God and the First Prophet I sanctify the grave so Joan's mother can rest therein in peace and her soul may find eternal repose forever. Amen.
As soon as I have holy water I can sanctify the grave just like the apothecary Thelma Ulthraum told me to.
Another grave which hasn't been sanctified and the souls of the deceased cannot reach salvation. The suicides, the convicts, the mad... their way to God was forever lost.
If I'm correct, this must be the grave of Joan's mother—just like Cardinal Timore said.
I'm going to pray for them... so they don't succumb to the Mark of the Beast and come back.
The grave of Joan's mother... a poor suicide.
If I'm not mistaken, the grave belongs to ex-archbishop Martroiani whose ring I'm supposed to bring brother Marcius. I'm lucky it's the right grave. Lets see if the ring is still in its place.
My God... the smell! But the ring... yes, it's here. It's still on the cadaver's finger. I hope I'll be able to take it off carefully.
Good heavens... it looks like I've disturbed Martroiani from eternal sleep... This doesn't look good!
If I'm reading it correctly, the grave belongs to ex-archbishop Martroiani. He died in 1215...
I'd rather not disturb his eternal peace.
I'll see what's hidden inside.
My God... the smell! But the ring... yes, it's here. It's still on the cadaver's finger. I hope I'll be able to take it off carefully. But wait... what's happening?
This is the grave of ex-archbishop Martroiani. I hope he's still wearing the ring I'm supposed to bring brother Marcius.
According to the inscription on the tombstone Kathryn Winhold lies here.
I'll look what's inside. Hmm... as far as I can see, there's nothing of any value. The scorched remains of the girl show that she has been burnt.
According to the inscription on the tombstone Kathryn Winhold lies here. I have to find her skull to be able to perform the necromantic ritual and summon her to this world...
I'm lucky, here it is—among the remains of the girl. I'm shaking at the thought of her terrible fate!
Here lies Kathryn Winhold. This is where I have to summon her to hear her testimony.

According to the book Libre Necronomicon I need to put on the Necklace of the Living Dead, hold the skull of Kathryn Winhold in my hand and start reading from the Necronomicon to perform the necromantic ritual... So, if the book is correct, I'm ready.
All right, let's start...
By the dark lord of the underworld Aghatosh, By the foursome of demons guarding the river Styx, by the black wings of Azrael, I open the gates of the underworld!
Kathryn Winhold, I summon thee for the first time, come back to this world!
By the power of demons Anthra and Bhutha, I summon thee for the second time, Kathryn Winhold, come back to this world and answer my questions!

Guarded by demons Hemiel, Thusmail and Kepthonus, I summon thee for the third time, Kathryn Winhold, come back to this world and answer my questions truthfully for you cannot lie to he who is holding your remains!
My God... it works!
However, I better not do it now...

According to the book Libre Necronomicon I need to put on the Necklace of the Living Dead, hold the skull of Kathryn Winhold in my hand and start reading from the Necronomicon to perform the necromantic ritual... So I have to get ready before I start the ritual.

The inscription on the tombstone says 'Here lies Saint Orthenius, the Holy Father of the Realm; angels Gabriel, Raphael and Michael are guarding his eternal peace and won't let anyone disturb his sleep'.
It looks like the tomb entrance is locked tight. It's not in my power to open it...
It looks like the tomb entrance is locked tight but if the Killian's Chronicle tells the truth, I should be able to open it using the statuettes of angels Gabriel, Raphael and Michael.
Yes! It works! It's opening. I can descend to the Orthenius' tomb...
But I must have all three statuettes on me to be able to open the entrance...
This looks like the von Hunth family sarcophagus. This is where I have to lay the remains of Baron Liam von Hunth.
In the name of merciful God I sanctify this sarcophagus by the holy water to protect it from the forces of evil. Let the body of deceased Baron Liam von Hunth rest in peace. Amen.
Unfortunately, I have no holy water on me to sanctify the sarcophagus. Without doing so, I'd risk dark forces affecting the body of the deceased.
In that case I'm going to take it by force!
I seriously doubt that. Get him, guys. Teach the scum a lesson!
Really? I don't like that... what's going on? Get on with it, knight, and hurry up.
According to my well informed sources you have a map leading to a certain barbarian treasure buried somewhere near Hillbrandt. Is it so?
Somebody was talking, right? Well... I won't be lying then, I have it. It's not a crime, is it?
No, it's not and I'm not accusing you of anything. I'm just interested in the map.

Really? Uhm... interesting. I thought paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous were not interested in anything pagan—the less in treasure hunting. But anyway, one thing is sure—the map is not for sale! I've decided to find out myself what was buried in there, you see?
I really need the map. I'll give you 100 gp.
Well... it's a nice sum. But I'm not selling.
I really need the map. I'll give you 200 gp.
I really need the map. I'll give you 500 gp.
I really need the map. I'll give you 1,000 gp.
I really need the map. I'll give you 1,500 gp.
Well... that's a nice sum. All right, we have a deal. Give me 1,500 gp and the map is yours.
Thank you, knight. Here's your map. Enjoy it. Now that we've finished, you should leave so nobody sees you here!
May I ask who you are and what you are doing here?

It's not your business who I am, knight. When I want to confess I'll go to church, heh-heh. Likewise, it's not your business what I'm doing here either. To tell you the truth I'd rather be doing it alone; without company. So go mind your own business, knight. Now!
You're mistaken, neighbor—it IS my business who you are and what you're doing here. And if you don't want to have problems, you better answer my questions.
Well... if you insist. My name is Hulph Rechtzwürther. As to what am I doing here? I'm taking a walk. Satisfied? So can you leave me alone now?
Not so fast, good man. It's you who I'm looking for!
All right, whatever. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. Hope I'll never see you here again.
What are you doing here again, knight. Got lost? Let me help you find your way then—turn around and follow your nose. Mind I don't kick your butt meanwhile!
I didn't get lost, I'm looking for you, good man.
Then I will take your advice and leave. Goodbye.
What do you want here again, knight? You're wasting your time. I'm not giving you the map. Turn around and follow your nose. Mind you I don't kick your butt meanwhile!
Really? I don't like that... what's going on? Get on with it, Father, and hurry up.

Really? Uhm... interesting. I thought priests were not interested in anything pagan, unless it was heresy of course. I also thought they were especially not interested in hunting for treasures. Anyway, the map is not for sale! I've decided to find out myself what was buried in there, you see?
Thank you, Father. Here's your map. Enjoy it. Now that we've finished, you should leave so nobody sees you here!

It's not your business who I am, Father. When I want to confess I'll go to church, heh-heh. Likewise, it's not your business what I'm doing here either. To tell you the truth I'd rather be doing it alone; without company. So go mind your own business, Father. Now!
You're mistaken son—it IS my business who you are and what you're doing here. Likewise, if you don't want to have problems with the Inquisition, you better answer my questions.
Goodbye, Father. Hope I'll never see you here again.
What are you doing here again, Father. Got lost? Let me help you find your way then—turn around and follow your nose. Mind I don't kick your butt meanwhile!
What do you want here again, Father? You're wasting your time. I'm not giving you the map. Turn around and follow your nose. Mind you I don't kick your butt meanwhile!
Really? I don't like that... what's going on? Get on with it, noble lord, and hurry up.

Really? Uhm... interesting. I've heard that the nobles are interested in anything that could help them obtain some money. But anyway, I'll have to disappoint you, noble lord, the map is not for sale! I've decided to find out myself what was buried in there, you see?
Thank you, noble lord. Here's your map. Enjoy it. Now that we've finished, you should leave so nobody sees you here!

It's not your business who I am, noble lord. When I want to confess I'll go to church, heh-heh. Likewise, it's not your business what I'm doing here either. To tell you the truth I'd rather be doing it alone; without company. So go mind your own business, noble lord. Now!

Goodbye, noble lord. Hope I'll never see you here again.

What do you want here again, noble lord? You're wasting your time. I'm not giving you the map. Turn around and follow your nose. Mind you I don't kick your butt meanwhile!
What? An intruder? Kill him! Quick! Kill him!
Hold it, orc, I'm your friend!

Do you think Hurgh is a stupid orc who doesn't know anything and can be easily fooled, huh? But you're wrong. Hurgh knows very well which of your low race is a friend of the orcs and which is not. You're an enemy because Hurgh doesn't know you. That's why we kill you and eat your flesh!
I really am your friend, Hurgh. Here is some gold for you, see?
Uh oh... you really are a friend of the orcs if you give gold so generously. Hurgh was wrong. Go on, noble sir, there's nothing for you to be afraid of.
Thank you, orc.
Let me pass, orc, or you'll know my wrath. I'm beginning to lose my patience!
Are you trying to threaten Hurgh? Do you think you'll scare him? You asked for it. You're dead already!
You're wrong, orc. It won't be me who dies today!
Enough of playing. Prepare to die, monsters!
No infernal monster is to prevent me from going into a place where the flame of divine justice must be lit!
You're dead already, human! You're even more impudent than stupid. You cannot fight Hurgh. Hurgh is looking forward to decorating his lair with your skull. You're dead!
I didn't come to fight you. Leave me alone and nothing will happen to you. I promise.
You can't scare Hurgh, human. Kill him!
You can pass, noble sir!
I changed my mind, orc. I'm going to kill you all!
A treachery! Kill him! Quick!
What? A theft? Oh no! Nobody's going to be stealing from Hurgh! Death to the disgusting thief!
I'm doing pretty well, thanks.
I'm happy for you, son. Nevertheless don't forget that God sees all our actions...
How do you know I'm looking into this case?
I heard about it. Don't forget son that I belong to the Holy Office! God help you...
It could be better...
Don't give up, son. Remember that where the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous cannot cope, the job of the Holy Office starts!.

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the Children of the New Order cult case. I would have never guessed that the ancient cult could ever reappear. Especially here in Ultherst where they've never operated before. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking for a potion able to return one's memory. I suppose you need it to get a testimony of some kind. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the witch Corin. I give you credit for trying to prove her innocent, although it's clear from the first sight that she's bewitched a paladin from the Brotherhood of the Righteous and turned him into stone. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you decided to pay up master armorer Leon van den Brook's debts. It's really commendable of you. You certainly do it from some noble reason, don't you?
Yes, I do. Goodbye.
How do you know?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of Grandmaster Christoffer de Malamert's heresy. I must admit that I would never think that someone from your Order could be as impartial as to investigate the Grandmaster himself. You have my deepest admiration! Can I ask you how is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you promised your fellow knights to recover one of their relics—the Decapitator sword. It's very noble of you. It's admirable how you paladins keep together these days. But it's true that any precious weapon that falls into the hands of the enemies means a loss to all the faithful. How is your investigation advancing?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the Cult of the Pagan Night case. It's absolutely vital that the heretics end up at stake. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you promised to find the unknown heretic who lets the werewolves into the city every full moon. It's a very dangerous case. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of missing William Burton. It looks like he disappeared returning from a business trip to Glatzburg. Can I ask how your investigation's going on?

Hello, son. I heard you promised the innkeeper Salena Flock to help her husband who seems to have been bitten by a werewolf. I recommend you to be extraordinarily careful in your noble effort—you can never judge how much rotten the soul of the infected is. Anyway, I'd like to know how your investigation's going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the money forgers who turn... well... human excrements into gold. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you promised master Kelley to help with deciphering of some kind of a mysterious scroll. I think you should be extremely careful—mysterious scrolls attract attention of many lost, fallen souls these days. Can I therefore ask you how your investigation's going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the cursed house of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. It's really brave of you—the house really is an ulcer on the face of the city. Can I ask how your investigation is going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of grave looting. It's really noble of you. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard some rumors saying that you were looking into the case of brother Nicolas. I must admit, I admire your courage to stand against the accusations of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert herself. It's admirable. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the murder of King Edward the Second. It's probably the most serious event these days—nobody was able to get to the bottom of it and it's absolutely vital that the murderers are discovered quickly otherwise the stability of the Realm collapses! How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you initiated a trial against the Curial Inquisitor, Cardinal Truncquillius and that you actually convicted him and had him executed at a stake. Is it true?

Hmm... very interesting. I must admire your courage to look for the evil amongst the members of the Holy Office—even if it was as high as in the office of the Curial Inquisitor. Not many would have the courage. But on the other hand, as an executor of divine justice you have undermined the faith in the infallibility and purity of the Inquisition. But who am I to judge your deeds...
No, it wasn't me.

Well... I heard different. If your soul is free of sin, there's nothing to be afraid of. I must admire your courage to look for the evil amongst the members of the Holy Office—even if it is as high as in the office of the Curial Inquisitor. Not many would have the courage. But on the other hand as an executor of divine justice you have undermined the faith in the infallibility and purity of the Inquisition. But who am I to judge your deeds...

Hello, son. I heard you had arrived in town. It seems the Brotherhood of the Righteous is strengthening its ranks. I wonder what's the reason for that... I trust there's nothing sinister in it—I would hate to be forced to investigate you!
Don't worry, Father.
Theft is a mortal sin, son. Remember that the next time you touch something which doesn't belong to you!
I'm happy for you, brother. Don't forget that it's God's will you are executing!
I heard about it. Don't forget, brother, that I belong to the Holy Office as well as you. God help you...
Don't give up, brother. Don't forget that it's God's will you are executing!

Hello, brother. I heard you initiated a trial against the Curial Inquisitor, Cardinal Truncquillius and that you actually convicted him and had him executed at a stake. Is it true?
Hello, brother. I heard you were doing great. I'm glad you've joined our curia. God bless you!
Theft is a mortal sin, brother. Remember that the next time you touch something which doesn't belong to you!
I've heard about it. Don't forget, son, that I belong to the Holy Office! God help you...
Don't give up, son. Remember that as a noble of the Realm you're favored by God!.
Hello, son. I heard you decided to pay up master armorer Leon van den Brook's debts. It's really commendable of you. You are certainly doing it from some noble reason, aren't you?
Yes, I am. Goodbye.

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of Grandmaster Christoffer de Malamert's heresy. I must admit that I would never dare to investigate among the people of such a high status—I admire your resolve! Can I ask you how is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you promised the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous to recover one of their relics—the Decapitator sword. It's very noble of you but your resolution to help seems striking to me. But it's true that any precious weapon to fall into the hands of the enemies means a loss to all the faithful. How is your investigation advancing?
Hello, son. I've heard you had arrived to the town. I'm glad you decided to strengthen the ranks of local faithful people. God bless you!
Head up, son! Should paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous fall, the Holy Office will come!

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the missing girls. To tell you the truth, I was trying to find the mysterious kidnapper myself, but had no success. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you've promised the seer Enrie Jungwirdt to get her an ancient pagan relic. It's strange what various things paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous engage in. But I presume you have a reason for that. How is your search going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were trying to perform exorcism on Francessca Gulvardi. I must say that your determination to free the soul of the poor innocent girl from the grip of infernal powers is fascinating. How is it going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of Bonhart von Drichtmaul's lost hammer. I admire your dedication—it's really noble to help even the mundanes. With the hammer the blacksmith will be able to make great armor and weapons for royal regiments. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking for the kidnapped Baroness Helen von Hunth. I pray for you to find her alive and in good health. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the Hans Thomas Brookwelt's case. As far as I know he was accused of heresy and of rape of servant girl Jeanette and of some other women. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were working on the case of Master Edmond d'Arvias' heresy. It's really commendable that you are willing to investigate even your superior. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of missing Baroness Linda van Gallagan. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the executioner Raubsticht's disease. I must say that it would be really unpleasant if Hillbrandt lost its executioner. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of the desertion of soldier Jullian. It's vital that we catch him and punish him, because his escape could corrupt the morale of the whole garrison. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of missing Paul Hammerhand. The boy was a real scamp. I wouldn't be surprised if he fell a victim to his own prank. How is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of master Edmond d'Arvias' stolen sword. Can I ask you how is your investigation going on?
Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of missing Bishop Quentinus. I'm glad you're still convicted you can help him. How is your investigation going on?

Hello, son. I heard the executioner Raubsticht's disease had an unnatural cause—maybe it's even a curse. I'm glad it was you who's investigating the case. Can I ask you how your investigation is going on?

Hello, son. I'm glad you've come to strengthen the ranks of the faithful here in the north of the Realm. It's a god-forsaken place, but even it deserves the gentry of the Realm and the Inquisition too, of course, to protect its people here. God bless you.
I am here to serve you, my lord! God bless our holy mission!
Who dares to bother me while I'm working? I don't have time for anyone! By tonight I have to have tortured to death ten more heretics!
My God, you must be crazy!
So what? Are you going to draw any conclusions? Out of my way, worm!
In that case I'm not going to disturb you...
You aren't going anywhere, traitor! I arrest you and sentence you to death by slow torture. A very slow torture... I promise.

How can you think of shopping after the Realm has been stricken by a disaster as terrible as the death of our leader?! Well, whatever... Leon van den Brooks has a famous armory here in Alvaron. At the apothecary of Thelma Ulthraum's and master alchemist Alberto Kelley's you can get potions and all kinds of magic items. And the innkeepers William Burton and Salena Flock deal in all kinds of goods.

A rumor of war has been spreading for some time here in Alvaron. It does look like a war might be coming—horses and draft cattle is being requisitioned, the granaries filled, recruits recruited... the mystery remains however, against whom the war should be waged. The first time I noticed something was going on was when King Edward asked me a strange question not long before he died—he asked whether I would defend my Realm with a weapon in my hand, if I were a king who's lost everything he ever cared for and who considered all the people around him traitors, opportunists and scoundrels.
What did you tell him?

I told him I was a fool and a clown but I had my honor, so I wouldn't defend anything which doesn't have any value for me. That was the last moment he smiled at me, although it was a smile full of pain and of suffering. He said he agreed with me and that was all.

Grand master Christoffer de Malamert a heretic? Well... they say so. It's true that many people in Alvaron believe him to be a heretic and a traitor. And yet more they're afraid what future has in store for them because if such an important person is a heretic, whom we can still trust, you know?
I'm looking for heretics here in Alvaron. Do you suspect anyone?
No, I have no suspicion. These are not the affairs a fool like me would want to get involved in...

What else could be worth mentioning besides the murder of His Highness King Edward the Second? What else did you expect me to say but the fact that the Realm has lost its beloved King? How is it even possible that the King is murdered in the middle of the palace in his private quarters surrounded by loyal servants? It's terrible...
Do you think Royal Counselor Verenicus could be involved in the murder of Prince Louis?

Royal chancellor Verenicus involved in the murder of prince Louis? No, I don't believe that. Louis was almost like his son. Spent so much time teaching him and I don't think he could ever think a false thought. No, that can't be true!

Cardinal Commendoni a heretic? That sounds as if somebody of the Brotherhood of the Righteous made it up. They would do anything to change the Inquisition Decree concerning the authority of the Holy Office over the Brotherhood...
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to discuss that with you!

I sincerely wish your investigation was successful and you managed to discover the King's murderer. Nobody would see him in the hands of an executioner more gladly than me. Unfortunately there is no way I could help you, because I don't know anything about the murder.
How is it possible that you don't know anything? You were his personal clown. I thought you were always with him...

You are wrong, knight. Even though I was trying hard to cheer him up, he would often send me away; sometimes quite rudely. He did it the night the murder took place. He sent me away claiming that he wanted to be alone. But he wasn't alone—I'm sure of it—because shortly after that I heard him quarreling with someone in his quarters.
Unfortunately, I have no idea. I came back to the King's quarters together with other servants after we had heard the terrible news of his murder.

Whatever Father Nicolas says, without evidence it will always be his word against the word of the governor's wife. So it's clear, how it must end—whatever the truth is. Don't say anything about justice...

Have you heard the legend about Duke Manfred Gotfried? He was a big villain, I bet. They say he was a determined heretic even though it's never been proved. The Inquisition spent five years guarding his house, but no result. Still he was able to use his necromantic Necklace of Death to summon the souls of the dead making them do all kinds of errands for him. Corpses were serving at his table, ghosts sweeping his house and in bed he had some undead whores. He died under mysterious circumstances couple years ago—I think it was 1213—and he was buried in a noble's crypt as if nothing had ever happened.
Answer, clown, or I'll have you tortured!
I beg you, good man—answer my question.
I don't mean to flatter, good man, but an answer of someone as wise as you could be extremely helpful.
Who disturbs me in my grief? What do you want from me, knight? Don't you see I'm suffering? Are you going to ask me to joke or to make a roll in my current state?
My name is Jolliah Jackmar, but everybody calls me Jolly Jack. I am—well, I was—the King Edward's clown.
What are you going to do now that the King is dead?

I'm going to die of grief. Isn't that ironic? A clown, a happy creature always joking and doing tricks is going to die of grief because there's nothing but pain in his heart. With the King dead I lost the meaning of my life!
You will certainly be able to find other work. There's such a need of laughter these days...

Who would want a sad clown with the heart torn to pieces? Who would wanna see a wreck with no light in his heart? Who? I tell you, knight—nobody. I lost the meaning of my life. You won't understand that because your mission lasts till you die, but I'm as empty as a drunk bottle of wine. What do you want from me? Why have you come and filled the emptiness which—I hoped—would soon kill me?
I wanted to talk to you.
All right, knight. I don't wanna talk to anybody—except to Death. But if you wanna talk...
I don't want to bother you, good man. I'll leave you to your grieving.
Goodbye, knight. We might never meet again, because my heart will soon break with grief. Pray for me.
Were you King Edward's personal clown?

Yes, as I said. King Edward got me as a gift from Lochland Emperor Friedrich the Third on his coronation journey to Pope. He took me in and loved me like a son he hasn't had yet. I wasn't just an amusement to him, I was his company and a person he loved. And when prince Louis was born, his feelings didn't fade away and neither did mine. We were a family.
What do you want, knight? What do you want from this wrecked person?

You are wrong, Father. Even though I was trying hard to cheer him up, he would often send me away; sometimes quite rudely. He did it the night the murder took place. He sent me away claiming that he wanted to be alone. But he wasn't alone—I'm sure of it—because shortly after that I heard him quarreling with someone in his quarters.

Goodbye, Father. We might never meet again, because my heart will soon break with grief. Pray for me.

You won't understand that because the meaning of the life of a nobleman is to heap up riches, and you're gonna do that till you die, but I'm as empty as a drunk bottle of wine. What do you want from me? Why have you come and filled the emptiness which, I hoped would soon kill me?
All right, noble lord. I don't wanna talk to anybody—except to Death. But if you wanna talk...
Goodbye, noble lord. We might never meet again, because my heart will soon break with grief. Pray for me.
What do you want, noble lord? What do you want from this wrecked person?
Who's the ruler of Glatzburg? It's Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, of course. Although I heard that duke Rowan van Leerin, the royal vice governor was interested in his position.
Sorry, knight, I'm not going to talk about that!
Me and Baroness Helen von Hunth usually go shopping at the city market. You must go there and take a look when there is a fair.
I hope the situation in the Realm goes back to normal soon and everything is as it used to be. I pray for it..
There is a war coming. Have you heard about it?
Sorry, I don't know anything about a war. I don't like wars...

I told you about my suspicion of heresy, knight! Have you forgotten? About Hans Thomas Brookwelt, the dangerous wizard who tried to bewitch me and to force me to do his bidding. Thank the Archangel Gabriel that it didn't happen. Somebody must stop the monster!

Few days ago there was a terrible storm, knight, I don't remember a worse one. It was in the middle of the night. Windstorm started to blow, sky was lit by lightning bolts and thunder was roaring. Then a cloudburst started and I was so scared I hid my head the deepest under the straw I could. Still I saw shapes floating in the sky. First I thought they were clouds but then the clouds started to scream, moan, whine and shrill. I figured it must have been an infernal parade, hellixarum devilicum. Demons were dancing and romping in the sky. It must have been the heretics. They must have summoned them by a dark mass with human sacrifices on their Sabbath.
I heard Bishop Trevorius was murdered somewhere at the Duke's gazebo. Have no idea what he was doing there. Such a deserted place...
To tell you the truth, knight, I heard it was you who murdered the Bishop. But it must be just gossip...
I'm looking for the missing Raquel Gielwitch. Do you happen to know anything about her?

The kidnapping of Raquel Gielwitch must be the wizard Hans Thomas Brookwelt's doing! I'm sure about that—he kidnapped her with the help of black magic to rape her and to satisfy his lowly bodily drives!

I haven't heard of anybody stealing the Ethien de Pasque's Chain of the Order. It must be a big loss for him. It's quite possible that it is the nasty wizard Brookwelt's doing—maybe he sent demons who serve him to steal the chain!

I heard that close to the ruins of Galibornium there are caves called the Devil's Caverns. That's because they lead to Hell itself and infernal creatures can use them to come to our world. And they really do so. From time to time the surroundings of the city are flooded with bloodthirsty devils, sly beasts with long tails, scaly skin and huge maws full of sharp fangs. Then it's not advisable to leave the house because those they catch will never be seen again. They are said to be summoned by the heretics who let them feed on the bodies of the faithful...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is looking for a wife. You are single, aren't you?
Am I single? Yes, knight, I am. Why are you asking?
Because the Grand Duke told me to find him a new wife.

And you think, that I... oh my God, that's a complete nonsense. The Grand Duke would never marry a mere servant. Of course it's every single girl's dream, but it wouldn't work. The Grand Duke would throw you out with such a proposition. No, knight, that would be useless.
I'd answer if I were you. You can never know what terrible things could happen to you.
Your answer would be extremely helpful, Jeanette. Please answer my question.
It's very pleasant to speak with someone as pretty and intelligent as you, Jeanette. It makes your unwillingness to answer my question even more devastating...

Is this what the bastard has told you? Does he really think I care about his few pieces of gold? No, the fool has no idea what he could have become to me. I'd enslave his mind and make him obey my every word. He'd be the first puppet in the great theater I'd start here in Glatzburg. But I still can. Oh yes, my time will come. The men of Glatzburg will be crawling at my feet... I just have to finish the right spell. It's going to be soon, I can feel it. I almost got Brookwelt... it was only a bad coincidence that he was able to avoid my spell. The next time he won't manage, muhaehaehaeh!
So you confess to your crimes?

What? Oh, the heck, I confess. But it won't matter anymore, knight. You should have minded your own business. But it's good that you're here. I'm going to try my new spell on you. Maybe it's the right one and I'll manage to enslave your mind! Amnar hepraes, gothismeil enwhaar, dochrab gethor... Eaaahhhbaaar!
Enough! Your spell has no power over me. You're coming with me!
Aaaaahhhhh! Never, you bastard. I'm going to kill you. Poke your eyes out, cut your legs off, eat your entrails! Slay him, my sisters! Aaaaahhhhh!
Knight, Heavens sent you! I must confess, I can't take it any longer... the shame! Hurt me so bad... the devil! I wish he rotted alive!
Calm down, good woman. Who are you and what has happened to you?

My name is Jeanette and I'm Baron Edger von Hunth's and his wife Helen's servant girl, knight. I used to be quite happy here, knight, you see? I was saving up my dowry and looking to get married one day and be happy... but everything went south. Now I have nothing but grief, pain and shame left. I can't get married. Not after that what that devil's done to me!
Who are you talking about? What happened?

I'm talking about Hans Thomas Brookwelt, knight. He works as a carpenter but in reality he's a devil in human form! A monster who knows black magic and brews infernal potions and with their help does villainies such as the one he did to me. I must admit I used to like him, but once I went for a little walk outside the city with him and he hurled at me as if possessed. I would normally be able to defend myself but he cast a terrible spell on me which bound me so I couldn't move. I was just lying there watching the devil taking me... It was horror, knight. The obscenities! Oh my God. And the pain... I couldn't see anything through the tears. I was begging him to leave me alone, but he was just laughing at me... Somebody must punish him! Somebody must stop his evildoings. As far as I've heard I'm not the only one whom he took using unholy powers! He must be put to trial for what he's done!
If it's really true, I'll make sure Brookwelt is punished!

Would you do it for a poor servant girl, knight? I'd be forever grateful. Nobody cares about justice when a victim is a poor village girl... But somebody must stop the monster! Thank you, knight! From the bottom of my heart!
You're welcome, good woman. Can I ask you a few questions now?
Of course, knight, go ahead. What do you want to know?
You're welcome, good woman. Await divine justice. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. And God bless you. I'll be looking forward to seeing you again when Brookwelt is in chains and on his way to the stake.
I might be able to help you enforce justice. What would you give me for that?
Well, it depends on what you want, knight. I don't have much I could give you, but I know how to be grateful, knight. I could give you everything you've ever wanted. You don't think I'm ugly, do you?
Your offer smells of sin and seduction! Don't count on my help!
Then go to hell, knight! Brookwelt is going to pay for what he's done—with or without your help!
Well... you really are pretty, I must say. All right, I'll do it for you—for the agreed price!
Yes, knight—punish Brookwelt, so he can never hurt anybody again and my body is all yours...

Inquisitorial Court is hereby called to order! I, Inquisitorial Prosecutor Jeremiah, temporarily authorized to assume the office of the judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor, and as such authorized in the name of God, Our Merciful Lord, and in the name of The Church, Our Holy Mother, to prosecute and punish the crimes against God and Faith, hereby institute proceedings against Bishop Vallarian who is charged with heresy, murder planning, sacrilege and with the conspiracy against God and the King. I hereby ask the prosecution to begin.

Thank you, Your Honor. Bishop Vallarian was sent to Hillbrandt by the Glatzburg Inquisitorial Curia to remedy the multiplying occurrences of heresy in these parts. Nevertheless soon it became apparent that it was him who was behind the most of the heinous deeds that happened in the last few months.
Those are very bold allegations. Do you have any cogent evidence for your claims? Please, keep in mind that you are accusing a man who was chosen to fight heresy himself using all means necessary.

Of course I do have evidence, Your Honor. First of all, I have the confession of Baroness Linda van Gallagan who testified that Bishop Vallarian planned the murders of Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill.
Why would Judge Vallarian do anything like that? Why would he seek the death of two innocent people? I see neither motive nor connection.

Their motive is simple—they wanted to summon a certain demon, Your Honor. The Demon was nobody else than the infamous Fallen Angel Arthamon—the Master of Despair, the Cursed Lord of Unholy Flame. The murders of the merchant Ollmier and Baroness von Weill were conspiring in connection to the preparation of the Dark Sabbath at which the Fallen Angel was summoned.

That's outrageous! Are you trying to tell me that you suspect Judge Vallarian of summoning Fallen Angel Arthamon?! Do you want me to believe that he's responsible for opening the Gates of Hell and for releasing one of the Fallen Angels? That he's guilty of such heinous crimes?!

You are absolutely correct, Your Honor. Sam Riemann testified as well and confirmed the testimony of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. I don't know whether the Fallen Angel was summoned, though Judge Vallarian definitely tried to summon him!
Does the prosecution have any more evidence to support its claims? I do not want to impeach the credibility of your witnesses' testimonies, though as they were convicted as heretics...
Yes, I do have more evidence proving the guilt of Bishop Vallarian.
Then go on. I cannot wait to see if your evidence is any good!

I managed to find a broken dagger blade at the town cemetery—it belonged to Judge Vallarian. It was lying next to the coffin of Baroness Gwenn von Weill—it was forced open. It clearly proves that Judge Vallarian participated in the theft of the body of the young Baroness.
And how do you know that this dagger belonged to Judge Vallarian?!
Shepherd Ruphert one morning saw how Vallarian threw away a dagger with a broken edge. Both parts of the dagger match perfectly!
And can you show these corpus delicti to us?!
Yes I can—here they are!
Hmm... It really is a dagger of Judge Vallarian, I recognize it for sure. This evidence proves clearly the guilty of Judge Vallarian. Does the prosecution have any other evidence?
Unfortunately I don't have it with me...

What?! The prosecution doesn't have the corpus delicti that serves as an evidence of guilt?! In that case come back later when you collect both parts of the dagger. Until then I suspend this pleading.
Well... I ask the prosecution, whether they can show us the missing parts of the dagger that is believed to be Vallarian's property?
Unfortunately I still don't have it...
The patience of this court is not exhaustless—I ask the prosecution to stop testing it. Come back later, when you collect the missing parts of Vallarian's dagger!
My final evidence is Vallarian's confession he made when he was being arrested!

I am astonished, Father. To tell the truth, till now I did not believe that the evidence against Judge Vallarian could be convincing. Nevertheless you proved beyond doubt that he is guilty. I must confess, although it fills me with terror and dread, that I believed the man whose moral principles, faith and determination to fight evil were just pretence, lies and treachery. He conducted all the investigation in Hillbrandt to blame Master Edmond d'Arvias for all the crimes that happened in the town. I most sincerely regret ever believing him.
The betrayal of Judge Vallarian is a terrible blow indeed...

Yes, it is so. Though in the end the truth was revealed and it was proven that the Holy Inquisition can fight heresy even in its own ranks. Bishop Vallarian, on the basis of the evidence presented this court finds you guilty. Thus I, Inquisitorial Prosecutor Jeremiah, temporarily authorized to assume the office of the judge in the name of God, Our Merciful Lord, and in the name of The Church, Our Holy Mother, to prosecute and punish the crimes against God and Faith, hereby sentence you to death at the stake. The sentence will be carried out immediately. Fire up the flames of justice. May God have mercy with his soul!

Inquisitorial Court is hereby called to order! I, Inquisitorial Prosecutor Jeremiah, temporarily authorized to assume the office of the judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor, and as such authorized in the name of God, Our Merciful Lord, and in the name of The Church, Our Holy Mother, to prosecute and punish the crimes against God and Faith, hereby institute proceedings against Sam Riemann who is charged with heresy, sacrilege, murder complicity and with the conspiracy against God and the King. I hereby ask the prosecution to begin.

Thank you, Your Honor. Baroness Linda van Gallagan testified on oath that it was Sam Riemann, who had helped her to murder and steal the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill. According to her testimony Sam Riemann also took part in a Dark Sabbath that led to the alleged summoning of Fallen Angel Arthamon.
Those are horrible allegations! Do you have any cogent evidence for your claims? The court cannot find him guilty on the basis of one single testimony.
Yes, I do. Sam Riemann, while tortured, confessed that all what Baroness Linda van Gallagan had said is true!

How disgusting! Until now the accused seemed like modest and respectable person, but in fact he is a perverse heretic, who is attracted by having intercourse with hellish powers! If God wouldn't be so merciful, Riemann's soul would surely be lost forever. Fortunately, God forgives our sins and that's why he will forgive also this sinner—as soon as his soul is purified from the sinful body! Thereupon I hereby sentence Sam Riemann to death at the stake. The sentence will be carried out immediately. Fire up the flames of justice. May God have mercy with his soul!
I met with Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian. He told me that we are going to work together a lot.

Yes, regrettably he was right. I won't hide that I disagree with His Excellency's decision to involve a secular person in the investigation process of the Holy Office, but I'm not here to judge his decisions. Your task is to conduct an investigation and to gather evidence against heresy suspects. As soon as you have enough evidence to charge someone, come to me and I'll hear your cause. If I find the evidence convincing enough, I'll issue a warrant of arrest, which will enable you to arrest the suspect and to hand him over to Sheriff Contemburry—he'll imprison him then. If you'd like to make the imprisoned suspect subject to the right of torture, tell the Sheriff and he'll prepare everything.
How long have you been in Hillbrandt, Father?

Not too long. I arrived just after snow thawed and the roads became at least a little bit passable. Though it was still a perilous journey. Only those who travel the Realm in these difficult times can fully understand the depth of the crisis which is upon us. There are swarms of hellspawns who no longer try to hide from the daylight. Heretics are plotting to carry out their unholy plans everywhere and heretic cults thrive as much as the hope of those still believing fades. It's terrible!
Judge Vallarian suspects Master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy. He charged me with acquiring incriminating evidence. What do you think about such a suspicion?

I agree with Judge Vallarian—I think that Master Edmond d'Arvias committed the crimes of which he's suspected. It really seems that it was him who opened the gates to the orcs during their late attack against the city. I myself called upon him to fully cooperate with the Holy Inquisition, but he fiercely denied me. I am afraid that his soul is corrupt, although till now I've never heard anything but praise for him. But the times are dire and people can easily lose their faith. Try asking the people of our town—they could be able to provide you with their testimonies. The truth must be revealed!
I would like to become an inquisitorial prosecutor. What are the requirements?

In view of the fact that inquisitorial prosecutors bring charges against those suspected of heresy, it is absolutely necessary for them to have perfect knowledge of both the canon and secular law. Knowledge in itself would not be enough, though. Just a perfect knowledge of the law does not make you a suitable candidate for the position of an inquisitorial prosecutor. It is also necessary to find out whether the adept is capable of independent work on the most difficult cases. That's why every adept is also given a specific case to solve. Moreover he must be also able to devise a charge against a potential perpetrator. Only then can his superior Inquisitorial Judge decide to appoint the adept an inquisitorial prosecutor.

What do I think about the crisis? I think that God bestowed indeed a difficult test upon us. Maybe the most difficult since the defeat of pagans—and it happened a millennium ago. Sometimes, I really don't know what to think about it. If I rigidly interpreted the Holy Scriptures I would have to conclude that the Day of Judgment is coming just as was prophesized in the Revelations of St. Ezechiel—the Beast is pounding upon the gate of its prison to set itself free and to mesmerize all the nations of the world. The Star of Doom has risen in the sky, Angels blew their clarions and three Scourges of God fell upon us. Famine came first, year later came plague and this year fire rained from the skies. Evil monsters are rising everywhere and evil spreads its webs. What else could it be than the signs of the end of the world? Although I still do hope that it is just an unfortunate coincidence. The only thing we should be concentrating on is the fight against heresy. The Decline of faith awakens sinful thinking in people and we must stop it no matter the cost!
What monster have you met here in Hillbrandt, Father?

There's indeed monsters and hellspawns galore, son. I've myself battled only orcs and giant bats, though there ale rumors about bands of half-ogres and mountain trolls who came down from the Moonshine Mountains. Moreover the surrounding forests are crawling with lethally poisonous giant spiders. And thus be very careful, my dear son, should divine providence lead you behind the stockade of the town.
Has something uncommon happened here in Hillbrandt lately?

Recently, there have been many events in Hillbrandt which would deserve the attention of the Holy Inquisition, son. I am certain that most of them is connected with the reason we are here. Let's say that terrible storm which befell Hillbrandt not a long time ago. I've discussed it with several people and everybody agrees that they've never seen anything as terrible as that. All of them concordantly swear that they saw demons dancing in the sky and that they heard crying and screams as if the gates of Hell itself were swung open. I myself don't believe rumors like that, though I must admit that I spent that terrible night praying. That what was happening out there was really terrible. I am sure that it has something to do with the activities of the local heretics who made a pact with infernal powers to destroy the true faith and to gain control of the town.
I heard that the Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen. Do you know anything about it, Father?

The loss of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius is a terrible blow not only for Hillbrandt but for the entire Holy Mother Church as well. According to an ancient legend from the third century, the monstrance was consecrated by St. Orthenius himself and was carried to Hillbrandt by its first Bishop Albertinus in 339. It became the most valued ecclesial treasure in this part of the Realm. It is rumored that as long as the Monstrance of St. Orthenius stays in the town the town cannot be conquered by any army. That's why the majority of the locals loses even the last remnants of hope of survival.
I don't think the monstrance to be that powerful. In the ninth century, when the Realm was conquered by the barbarians, Hillbrandt was overtaken, am I right?

Yes, you're right, son. Though I've read in the diocesan chronicle that the monstrance was taken out of the town when the Barbarian Wars began. It was meant to be taken to Alvaron to help protect the Capital of the Realm. Unfortunately it never arrived there and it was believed lost to the barbarians. Nevertheless after the Barbarian Wars it was miraculously found in an abandoned hermitage and returned to Hillbrandt.
What do you know about Fallen Angel Arthamon, Father?

Fallen Angel Arthamon? It's a reincarnation of one of the three infernal elements Satan commands. Arthamon represents destruction and despair. His symbol is all-destroying and all-consuming fire. At least the Holy Scripture reads so. At the dawn of ages he was together with Satan, other two angels and with Archangel Azrael thrown down from Heaven for the crimes against the divine laws. Since then they have been waiting in Hell till they can storm into our world and unleash their infernal fury there.
Do you think it's possible for the Fallen Angels to enter our world if summoned?

Hmmm... It's a difficult question. A few years ago I would say it's absolutely impossible. But I'm no longer sure. Though I still believe with all my heart that it's not possible—just imagine the consequences of such a possibility!

According to the testimony of witnesses, Bishop Quentinus disappeared during the last attack of the orcs against the town. His body was not found, thus I assume that he was taken by those infernal monsters. But to tell the truth I don't believe that it gives us any hope of his rescue. Orcs are most likely cannibals eating flesh of their victims... God protect the soul of Bishop Quentinus!
I came across a curse here in Hillbrandt, Father. Do you happen to know how to remove it?

What? Are you telling me that there's someone cursed in Hillbrandt? By Saint Michael, who could have done something as dreadful as that? It only proves how treacherous and dangerous the local heretics are, son. We must stop them no matter the cost, before it's too late. Though I am really sorry to tell you that I don't have a slightest idea how to remove the curse. Try asking brother Dominicus, he's very experienced in curing various maladies.

There are legends among the people concerning Saint Orthenius who at the dawn of our Realm defeated all the pagans with the help of a powerful relic. According to the legend the relic should find its way to the hands of a new protector of the faith in the times most dire. He will then stand against all the enemies and will defeat them. It is an obvious example of folk creativity to which common people resort in difficult times.

Although it is true that Saint Orthenius led the faithful armies here in Filkland peninsula in 223 and defeated pagan empire Ereborn and that its ruins served as foundation stones of Ultherst and all the faithful kingdoms; it would be foolish to think that the victory was achieved thanks to some relic, even if it were a mighty one. I don't want to question the existence of such an item, but I think that its power was indeed far from the power ascribed to it by folk legends.

I am rather familiar with the case of the murder of Kurth Ollmier—I've been investigating it myself. Kurt Ollmier was suspicious of heresy and thus the Holy Office was indeed interested in him. Unfortunately somebody acted faster than us and killed the merchant. I must say that it is very unsettling for the Holy Office—the Inquisition doesn't like its heresy suspects being removed before they can be investigated.
Who could have committed the murder?

I don't know, son. It's possible that it was some self-proclaimed holy avenger who believes his deeds to be divine will. Though I doubt it. I'm sure that his heretical colleagues are behind the murder—they were simply afraid he might reveal them. Perhaps they somehow got to know about the suspicion and expected us to interrogate Ollmier and thus they removed him. Yes, it seems very likely. That's why we must quickly capture the Ollmier's murderers and interrogate them!
Do you have any suspicions?

No, unfortunately not. The investigation ended in a deadlock. There are no witnesses and no traces which would explain the circumstance of the murder. Though I think that it is only a matter of time before we apprehend the perpetrator and question him!
Tell me. Now!
Look, Father—I don't care about your opinion of me, but I really need you to answer me. It will be for the good of the investigation.
I understand that your difficult and selfless mission requires vigilance and that you can't tell everything to everybody you meet. Though I'm sure it won't hurt you to answer my question.

Greetings, son. I heard you had arrived in Hillbrandt to bolster the ranks of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. It seems that we will have to put all the efforts in the fight with heresy that is spreading through the town. My name is Jeremiah and I am an inquisitorial prosecutor.
It was a pleasure meeting you, Father. Nevertheless I must take my leave now. Duty calls.

Farewell, son. Stay vigilant. You can never know where hellish minions or devilish plots lurk. I have a feeling that you will have to face many trials here in Hillbrandt which will put your faith and abilities to a test. Always keep in mind though that there is only one right way leading to your goal—the one which is the most perilous. Should you need anything, you know where to find me. God bless you.
Greetings, son. I hope your investigation is going well. What can I do for you?
Could I talk to you for a minute?
But of course, son. What do you need to know?
I would like to accuse Edmond d'Arvias of heresy.
Do you have enough evidence for that, son?

Yes, I do. Edmond d'Arvias was seen by soldiers Millward and Thomas Reitdorf as he was opening the gates to the orcs the night they managed to get into the town. Moreover, Sam Riemann avowed that he saw Master d'Arvias ordering the orcs how to attack the church.
Hmm... It seems that your evidence speaks for itself. I hereby accuse Master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy and of conspiracy against God and the King. You have my consent to arrest him, son.
I would like to accuse Linda van Gallagan of heresy.

Yes, I do. Linda van Gallagan was seen by Bishop Quentinus at the local graveyard—she was, together with several other heretics, taking away the once buried body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill. Moreover, soldier Millward saw Baroness van Gallagan climbing down from the window of the merchant Ollmier's rented room the night he was murdered.
Hmm... It seems that your evidence speaks for itself. I hereby accuse Linda van Gallagan of heresy and of Kurth Ollmier's murder. You have my consent to arrest her, son.
I would like to accuse Sam Riemann of heresy.
Yes, I do. Linda van Gallagan called Sam Riemann an accomplice in all the crimes she committed.
Hmm... It seems that your evidence speaks for itself. I am hereby accusing Sam Riemann of heresy. You have my consent to arrest him, son.
I would like to accuse Judge Vallarian of heresy.
I'm sorry, son? I'm sure I've misheard.
I would like to accuse Judge Vallarian.

Oh, then I've heard well. Hmmm... to tell you the truth, son, I'm rather confused. Do you really want me to let you arrest my superior inquisitor? It is unusual INDEED—and especially because it's a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous who suggests that. Well I will do it after all; it is your right—and your responsibility. I'm sure you know what fate awaits you if the accusation is proven unjust—you will spend the rest of your days behind bars. Providing that the Tribunal will show you mercy. What evidence against Judge Vallarian do you have?

Baroness Linda van Gallagan confessed that Judge Vallarian ordered her to murder the merchant Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill. Moreover stonemason Sam Riemann testified that he stole the body of Gwenn von Weill from the graveyard with the help of Baroness van Gallagan and of Judge Vallarian. I also found the broken blade of Judge's dagger near Gwenn's coffin which had been forced open.

Your evidence is not very convincing, my son. Baroness Linda van Gallagan could have lied to you as Sam Riemann could. The broken blade could have been foisted near the looted grave to blame Judge Vallarian for the crime. Nevertheless, you have my consent to arrest him, my son. The truth must be revealed!

According to the Inquisitorial Codex it is also my duty to temporarily assume the office of the judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor which cannot be performed by Judge Vallarian, as he is accused of heresy, unless he is proven innocent.
Congratulations.

I don't think it's a reason for congratulations. I personally believe that we are in a rather unfortunate situation which will be soon explained. I don't know how you came to believe Judge Vallarian is behind all the crimes that happened in the town because I consider him the most honorable and the most just man I have ever met. His faith is unshakable and his service to God is flawless.
It seems from your tone as if you didn't believe me.

To tell the truth, I don't believe Judge Vallarian is involved in the case. Instead, you come here with so-called convincing evidence asking me to formally accuse him. You, a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Well, enough speculations. Prove your allegations or take your accusation back.

Yes, I do. It's probable beyond doubt that it is she who cursed Friedrich Raubsticht the town executioner. She was a lover of Hans Falkner who was executed by Raubsticht not a long time ago. The curse could be a revenge for the death of her murderous lover.
Hmm... Your evidence seems convincing. I am hereby accusing Lotti Frankmüller of heresy. You have my consent to arrest her, son.
I would like to submit a proposal to start court proceedings in the case of Linda van Gallagan.
As an inquisitorial prosecutor I am obliged to ask you whether you have enough evidence for court proceedings, son.
I do.
Then go to Judge Vallarian and pass him the indictment against Linda van Gallagan.
I would like to submit a proposal to start court proceedings in the case of Sam Riemann.
Then go to Judge Vallarian and pass him the indictment against Sam Riemann.
Nothing for the moment, thanks.
I would like to submit a proposal to start court proceedings in the case of Judge Vallarian.

Your restless determination to put Judge Vallarian on trial puzzles me, son. Have you really lost your commonsense? Though as an inquisitorial prosecutor I am obliged to ask you whether you have enough evidence for court proceedings in the case of Judge Vallarian, son.

I thought so. In that case I, as a prosecutor of the Holy Office temporarily authorized to assume the office of the judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor, order the trial to begin. There's no point in prolonging the agony. Let the truth be revealed!

Please, accept my deepest apologies, son. I didn't believe that Judge Vallarian could be guilty and thus I considered your accusation to be false. I wasn't able to accept the fact that the infernal powers can corrupt anyone. You taught me a valuable lesson which I'm going to remember till the day I die. I sincerely thank you for that!
There's no need to apologize, Father. I'm not surprised you didn't believe Judge Vallarian to be guilty.

Yes, it was indeed difficult to accept the fact that the man I looked up to and from whom I learned so many things should be just a shameless heretic besmirching His name and plotting against the royal power.
What are you going to do now, Father?

I'm going to wait for inquisitors from the Glatzburg Curia to arrive. I'm sure they will send someone soon enough to investigate the situation and to decide what should we do. Nevertheless, although Judge Vallarian and his accomplices were captured, there is much work left to be done yet. We live in evil times that constantly spawn new renegades who deserve our attention!
I'm glad you are able to admit your mistake, Father. As you can see, I was right about everything!
Yes, I admit my mistake. I believe with all my heart that I will take a lesson from it and that it will allow me to better carry out my holy duty.

I'm going to wait for inquisitors from the Glatzburg Curia to arrive. I'm sure they will send someone soon enough to investigate the situation and that they will decide then what should we do. Nevertheless, although Judge Vallarian and his accomplices were captured, there is yet much work left to be done. We live in evil times that constantly spawn new renegades who deserve our attention!
Keep your apologies for yourself—nobody is interested in them!

I understand your anger. My attitude was prejudiced and biased... In any case I'm going to wait for inquisitors from the Glatzburg Curia to arrive. I'm sure that curial inquisitor Cardinal Truncquillius will send someone soon enough to investigate the situation and decide what should we do. Although Judge Vallarian and his accomplices were captured, there is yet much work left to be done. We live in evil times that constantly spawn new renegades who deserve our attention!
I thought so. Thereby I, as the prosecutor of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Sam Riemann. The court is going to sit immediately.
I am sorry, but I can't talk to you righ now, knight. Talk to judge Vallarian first and then come back to me...

I can't believe my eyes, son—have you just tried to steal from me?! How could you dare to do something like that! You are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous! Go to the confession at once and beg our Lord for forgiveness for your momentary lapse of judgment!

Yes, he was absolutely right. As an inquisitorial investigator you will be obliged to conduct investigation and to gather evidence against heresy suspects. As soon as you have enough evidence to charge someone, come to me and I'll hear your cause. If I find the evidence convincing enough, I'll issue a warrant of arrest which will allow you to arrest the suspect and to hand him over to Sheriff Contemburry—he'll imprison him then. If you'd like to make the imprisoned suspect subject to the right of torture, tell the Sheriff and he'll prepare everything.
How long have you been in Hillbrandt, brother?
What monster have you met here in Hillbrandt, brother?

There's indeed monsters and hellspawns galore, brother. I've myself battled only orcs and giant bats, though there ale rumors about bands of half-ogres and mountain trolls who came down from the Moonshine Mountains. Moreover the surrounding forests are crawling with lethally poisonous giant spiders. And thus be very careful, my dear brother, should divine providence lead you behind the stockade of the town.

Recently, there have been many events in Hillbrandt which would deserve the attention of the Holy Inquisition, brother. I am certain that most of them is connected with the reason we are here. Let's say that terrible storm which befell Hillbrandt not a long time ago. I've discussed it with several people and everybody agrees that they've never seen anything as terrible as that. All of them concordantly swear that they saw demons dancing in the sky and that they heard crying and screams as if the gates of Hell itself were swung open. I myself don't believe rumors like that, though I must admit that I spent that terrible night praying. That what was happening out there was really terrible. I am sure that it has something to do with the activities of the local heretics who made a pact with infernal powers to destroy the true faith and to gain control of the town.
I heard that the Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen. Do you know anything about it, brother?

Yes, you're right, brother. Though I've read in the diocesan chronicle that the monstrance was taken out of the town when the Barbarian Wars began. It was meant to be taken to Alvaron to help protect the Capital of the Realm. Unfortunately it never arrived there and it was believed lost to the barbarians. Nevertheless after the Barbarian Wars it was miraculously found in an abandoned hermitage and returned to Hillbrandt.
What do you know about Fallen Angel Arthamon, brother?
I came across a curse here in Hillbrandt, brother. Do you happen to know how to remove it?

What? Are you telling me that there's someone cursed in Hillbrandt? By Saint Michael, who could have done something as dreadful as that? It only proves how treacherous and dangerous the local heretics are, brother. We must stop them no matter the cost, before it's too late. Though I am really sorry to tell you that I don't have a slightest idea how to remove the curse. Try asking brother Dominicus, he's very experienced in curing various maladies.

You're wrong, brother. An inquisitorial prosecutor can decide to investigate any case himself and perform all the investigatory actions on his own. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Yes, an inquisitorial prosecutor can decide to investigate any case himself and perform all the investigatory actions on his own.
You're right, brother! Excellent!
Yes, he can, but only if there's no inquisitorial investigator at his disposal or only if his superior Inquisitorial Judge allows it.

You're wrong, brother.
