Also, there's no need for the consent of his superior Inquisitorial Judge, because it would be an unnecessary burdening of the judges of the Holy Office. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Is an inquisitorial prosecutor completely independent in his investigation?
No, brother. He's obliged to follow the orders issued by his superior Inquisitorial Judge.
You're right! Excellent!
Of course. He wouldn't be able to perform his tasks otherwise.

No, it is not so, brother. Any inquisitorial prosecutor is always obliged to follow the orders of his superior Inquisitorial Judge. Judge's opinions are binding for him. Opposing the will of a judge is a transgression any inquisitorial prosecutor should strive to avoid. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
In case an inquisitorial prosecutor is also ordained as a bishop, then he is completely independent. Otherwise he must follow the orders of his superior Inquisitorial Judge.

You are mistaken, my son. Crosier is not relevant in such a case. You must distinguish between our Holy Mother Church and the Holy Office. Although inquisitors were born in the womb of the Church and are still its part, we have a different hierarchy which is not affected by the Church hierarchy. The prosecutor who is a bishop must follow the orders of his superior judge, although he's just a priest. It's true that there are not many cases like that, but it doesn't change anything. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Who can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor?
Everybody who will demonstrate his practical and theoretical knowledge of both canon and secular law and who will solve a real case given to him.

No, brother. Only a priest and moreover a member of the Holy Office who is already an inquisitorial investigator can strive to achieve the position of an inquisitorial prosecutor. Can you imagine what it would be like if the Inquisition became secular and merchants, burghers, and, God forbid, common people, riff-raff and the rabble were appointed inquisitors? The Inquisition's holy mission is to fight heresy and only clergy is capable of recognizing it and of finding an appropriate cure. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Every priest who will demonstrate his practical and theoretical knowledge of both canon and secular law and who will solve a real case given to him.

No, brother. Only a priest and moreover a member of the Holy Office who is already an inquisitorial investigator can strive to achieve the position of an inquisitorial prosecutor. Can you imagine what it would be like if the Inquisition became open to all the clergy? The Inquisition's holy mission is to fight heresy even among the clergy and thus only an inquisitor of the Holy office is capable of recognizing it and of finding an appropriate cure. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Every inquisitorial investigator who will demonstrate his practical and theoretical knowledge of both canon and secular law and who will solve a real case given to him.
Decretum Inquisitorium states several principles which affect the work of an inquisitorial prosecutor. Can you tell me what do you know about the accusatory principle?
The accusatory principle states that any person accused of heresy can choose his own attorney.

No, brother. The accusatory principle states that only those accused by an inquisitorial prosecutor can stand inquisitorial trial. It prevents possible arbitrary behavior which could have otherwise occurred. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
The accusatory principle states that only those accused by an inquisitorial prosecutor can stand inquisitorial trial.
The accusatory principle states that an inquisitorial prosecutor charged with a crime cannot perform duties connected with his office unless he's acquitted.
Is it possible for the jurisdiction of the Holy Office to overlap with the jurisdiction of either the nobility or of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?
No, brother. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office and the jurisdiction of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are mutually exclusive.
Yes, it is possible. Some crimes can be prosecuted both by the Inquisition and by the Brotherhood of the Righteous and by the nobility.

No, brother, you are mistaken. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office was designed to be exclusive to the jurisdiction of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

It depends on who is accused. If a noble is accused, then he's tried by his liege lord. If a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is accused, then he's tried by his Order. All the remaining come under the jurisdiction of the Holy Office.

No, brother, you are mistaken. It does not matter who is accused. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office was designed to be exclusive to the jurisdiction of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. You have much to learn yet before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

Excellent, brother! It seems that you are quite proficient as regards law—you've correctly answered all my questions. Thus all the requirements prescribed for being appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor of the Holy Office are met. It is my pleasure to appoint you to the office of the inquisitorial prosecutor. Sancte fedicius ave Domini procurator de Inquisitorium suffratheses. Please, accept this item as a symbol of your new office. Congratulations, brother!
Thank you, brother. It's a great honor!

Greetings, brother. I'm glad you've arrived to Hillbrandt to bolster our ranks. It seems that we will have to put all the effort we can into the fight with the heresy that is spreading through the town. My name is Jeremiah and I am an inquisitorial prosecutor.
It was a pleasure meeting you, brother. Nevertheless I must take my leave now. Duty calls.

By a coincidence, I've already solved the case, brother. The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen by priest Romius who was a servant to undead Bishop Herbertius. According to my investigation Bishop rose from his grave as the undead Lord of the Night. I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Unbelievable! Are you telling me that Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? That's infernal! And as if it were not enough, according to your words brother Romius was commanded by that spawn of darkness to steal the monstrance. A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers? The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed which means the practical part of the test is complete. When you feel you are ready, come to me and we will complete your endeavor.

By a coincidence, I've already solved a part of the case, brother. I found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on undead Bishop Herbertius who, according to my investigation, rose from his grave and somehow managed to get the monstrance. I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Indeed?! Are you telling me that Hillbrandt Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? And that you found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on him? Diabolical indeed! Nevertheless it's good that the monstrance is back. Hopefully it will help Hillbrandt to rest once again under the divine protection. Have you managed to find out who stole the monstrance for Herbertius? It is obvious that such an infernal abomination could not have set its unholy foot on the holy ground...
No, brother, I've not yet managed to find out that.
Then keep on searching till you find him. I am sure you will find the perpetrator eventually.
Of course, brother.
Is there anything else I could help you with?
I will do my best to apprehend the perpetrator and to return the relic to its rightful place.
I have retrieved the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, brother. Undead Bishop Herbertius had it on him. It seems he rose from his grave.
I have found out who stole the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, brother.
Really? Who was that? What treacherous sinner could have handed over the most valued relic of this town to such an infernal monster?
It was brother Romius. He testified that he served Bishop Herbertius as a slave. He confessed to all his sins.

I hope that you've prepared yourself very thoroughly. I am sorry, but I can' talk to you right now, brother. Talk to judge Vallarian first and then come back to me...

I can't believe my eyes, brother—have you just tried to steal from me?! How dare you do something like that! You are an Inquisitor! Go to the confession at once and beg our Lord for forgiveness for your momentary lapse of judgment!

Yes, regrettably he was right. I won't hide that I disagree with His Excellency's decision to involve a secular person in the investigation process of the Holy Office, but I'm not here to judge his decisions. Your task is to conduct an investigation and to gather evidence against heresy suspects. As soon as you have enough evidence to charge someone, come to me and I'll hear your cause. If I find the evidence convincing enough, I'll issue a warrant of arrest, which will enable you to arrest the suspect and to hand him over to Sheriff Contemburry, he'll imprison him then. If you'd like to make the imprisoned suspect subject to the right of torture, tell the Sheriff and he'll prepare everything.
Look, Father, I don't care about your opinion of me, but I really need you to answer me. It will be for the good of the investigation.

Greetings, son. I heard you had arrived to Hillbrandt to take over your new domain. It seems that we will have to put all the efforts in the fight with heresy that is spreading through the town. My name is Jeremiah and I am an inquisitorial prosecutor.

Oh, then I've heard well. Hmmm... to tell you the truth, son, I'm rather confused. Do you really want me to let you arrest my superior inquisitor? It is unusual indeed, and especially because it's a secular person who suggests that. Well I will do it after all; it is your right, and your responsibility. I'm sure you know what fate awaits you if the accusation is proven unjust, you will spend the rest of your days behind bars. Providing that the Tribunal will show you mercy. What evidence against Judge Vallarian do you have?

To tell the truth, I don't believe Judge Vallarian is involved in the case. But it is very likely that someone is trying to destroy him and in such case we, as faithful men, should do all we can to purge his name and to expose the real perpetrator. Instead, you come here with so-called convincing evidence asking me to formally accuse him. Well, enough speculations. Prove your allegations or take your accusation back.
I am sorry, but I can' talk to you right now, son. Talk to judge Vallarian first and then come back to me...

I can't believe my eyes, son, have you just tried to steal from me?! How could you dare to do something like that! You are a highborn man! Go to confession at once and beg our Lord for forgiveness for your momentary lapse of judgment!
Brains... we want your brains!
Do you? Then you're going to die, monster!
Wait, Joachym, your friend Graubner sent me.
Don't you dare to lay your unholy paws on me, fiend!
Stop, wandering soul! I offer you redemption from your curse!
Eat! Yum-yum... eat!
Hold on, girl—I'll tell your father to take you in.
I came to release you from you curse, Joan. It's going to hurt—a lot actually, but it should help you, you'll see...
Hurt? No... no hurting me! Don't want hurt... Want my father... want his blood!
That's exactly what I've brought you, Joan. Do you see this flask? You must drink—there's Giovanni Timore's blood in it—your father's blood...
No, not like thissss... wanna kill! Kill father! Sssssssssssss...
I thought so. Then I'll have to force you to drink that flask of blood!

I'll help you, Joan. I'll help you to get rid of your course. You will be a human being again... I just need you to drink your father's blood and then I must consecrate the grave of your poor mother. Hold on, I'll be back soon!
Want my father! Want... his blood. Sssssss...
Father? Father, dear... where are you? Want your blood! Sssssssss... your blood!
Who are you, infernal abomination?
Want my father! Ssssssss... want his blood! Where is he? I want him...
I can't allow you to make an attempt on anybody's life! I'm going to send you back to burning hell!
Who is your father, wandering soul? Why do you ask his blood?
My father... Sssssssss... want him! Want his blood... Yesss, his blood...
I'd better be going. I don't think that it's a wise idea to interfere. May you find eternal peace, cursed soul...
Father? Father, dear... where are you? I want your blood! Sssssssss... your blood!
I can't allow you to make an attempt on anybody's life! I'm going to send you back to the burning hell!
Ssssaaaaaaaahhhhh!!!
Excellent! Finally I've managed to overpower her. Now I must give her the flask of her father's blood... I wonder if it's going to work.
Gulp... gulp... gulp... Aaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhhhh!!!
By Archangel Gabriel... it seems to work! That monster is beginning to change! My God... It's a miracle!
Eat... yum-yum... eat!
If it's not a piece of her father what she'd like to eat then the curse is broken! Blessed be the First Prophet! I'm going to tell Cardinal Timore, to take her in.
Excellent! Finally I've managed to overpower her. Now I must give her the flask of her father's blood... But where is it? Damn, I don't have it on me! I have to find it and do it all again...
I was told by the master armorer Hans von Drichtmaul that he had not seen your son recently. Is there anything wrong with him?

My son is none of von Drichtmaul's business! I told him clearly enough that there's nothing wrong with my son and that he can't serve him as an apprentice for some time. He's been ill so I had to send him out of town so he could get better. That's all. I hope I answered your question.
Yes, it's enough. I'm sorry for interfering with your domestic affairs.
Well, no harm done. But could you please tell Drichtmaul to leave my son alone? He's not going to help anyone by sticking his nose into other people's matters.
Hmm... It would depend...
What? On what would it depend?!
Whether you told me the truth!

But of course I told you the truth, knight! Why would I lie to you? I had to let him go to my brother, because nobody could help him here in Glatzburg. That's all. There's nothing mysterious about it, see?
Weintraum the bartender is afraid about you, good man. According to him you've been acting as if you were not yourself. Is anything troubling you?

It's none of Weintraum's business how I'm acting! He better keep to himself and don't try to set people against me. I'm fine and nothing's troubling me. Why shouldn't I be fine? Tell Weintraum that I appreciate his concern but it's misplaced.
Alright, thanks.
Hmm... Am I mistaken or are you trying to hide something from me?

What? What do you think I'd be hiding? If Weintraum thinks that I'm not in a good mood or something like that tell him to look around! I think that he'll see more than enough reasons to be down, don't you think?
Alphonso DiCerbio confessed that he kidnapped your son Tom. Is it true?

Alphonso DiCerbio confessed that he kidnapped my son?! I don't know anything about that! What an absurd confession. My son had to travel to my relatives to recover from a disease that had suddenly stricken him. I don't know anything about kidnapping. It's absurd!
You're welcome!
Strange indeed... Aren't you trying to hide something from me?

Why do you think I should be hiding something from you? You've just come here to ramble about the kidnapping of my son who is in fact far from Glatzburg safe with my relatives... I don't think it's necessary to comment on it!
The royal governor of the city is Robert Heidrick, knight. The royal vice-governor is my master, Duke Rowan van Leerin.

If you want to sell or buy weapons or armor, just visit Hans von Drichtmaul in his armory shop. Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus can provide you with potions and magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum offer various wares. Well, and Alphonso DiCerbio will also sell you almost anything—if you don't mind the origin of his wares.

I don't know what to think about the crisis, knight. People are talking about the end of the world, about coming of Satan to our world and about Judgment Day. If I look around I think that it is really so. You don't feel it's different do you? No wonder people are melancholic and that they don't believe everything will turn out good in the end. Countless heretics were burnt at the stake, dozens of rogues and murderers were executed and still nothing has changed so far—instead it is as if there were more and more of them.
Supposedly there is a war coming, did you hear anything about it?
Yes, people are talking about a coming war. If it's true then may God and all His saints protect us. The war is the last thing we need! As if there were not enough grief without the war...

I've heard that the cemetery is plagued by living dead who raise from their graves to feast on the living venturing near. I believe it's true, though I haven't been there myself for some time. It's possible that even my father, may God grant him eternal glory, rose from his grave as an infernal undead monster. Terrible idea.
His Grace Duke Robert Heidrick offers a bounty for apprehending rogues plaguing the roads. Just bring a head or a scalp to Sheriff Smith and he'll immediately hand you your reward.
No I... I don't suspect anybody of heresy. I don't know anything. And I don't want to know anything like that. Nothing good can come out of such an involvement.
Am I mistaken or are you trying to hide something from me?
Why should... why should I hide anything, knight? There's no reason... I don't know anything—that's all!
I'm sorry, good man. I was just asking
That's alright, knight. If I knew something I'd have certainly told you—you can count on me. But I don't know anything. Really!
Well I've already told you about my master Duke Rowan van Leerin, knight. I don't know more.

I was scared to death by that storm that struck the city a few days ago. It was in the middle of the night. I was awoken by a loud thunder—it was so loud that it would have awoken even dead. And maybe it did because that what I saw in the night sky then will haunt me till the day I die. Knight, I saw... I saw demons and beelzebubs flying and frolicking all over the sky—God be my witness. It was mad. I couldn't avert my eyes from that scene, even though I knew that they could have stolen my soul if they saw me. I needed all my strength to get away from the window—then I just cowardly crawled under my bed. Well, what would you do if you were me and if you were surrounded by whirling hellspawns?! I'm just a simple valet.
Monsignor Trevorius was a great support for entire Glatzburg, knight. His death will have terrible consequences for us. Unfortunately I know absolutely nothing about his death, so I can't help you.

I'm not sure if you know about it, knight, but the word on the streets is that you committed that murder. Well, that you and the Bishop... well that you did it because you were jealous. Anyway, I don't believe that. I knew Bishop Trevorius long enough to know that it's just a dirty slander. Anyway, if I were you, knight, I'd better be careful. If somebody becomes suspicious of a crime he has a hard time proving his innocence.

Father Frederick? Hmmm... wasn't he that cranky priest who came to Glatzburg a few years back and died during that plague in 1221? Yep, it should be him. Unfortunately, I don't know any details about him, knight. I don't recall ever talking to him. Try asking Judge Welfhar, they used to spend a lot of time together.

It is a very tricky situation those murdering dead roaming the streets of Glatzburg. People are freaking out—and who could blame them? Just imagine that anytime at night you can get ambushed by a horde of undead reeking of graveyard and of death. Well, they don't threaten you only in the streets—they can even kill you at home! They will tear the door down and will storm in to shred anybody inside. You're dead before you can say a word. Really appalling. Somebody should quickly do something about it!

If you are looking for anything stolen, just go straight away to that buffoon Tinthan. He's the one responsible for almost all the thefts in the city. Well, nobody has proven anything yet, but everybody knows that it's him who stole their stuff. He claims to be a great actor, but in fact he's just a sticky-fingered bastard. Nevertheless he's a very skillful thief—there's no doubt about that.
Your answer is necessary for my investigation, Clifford. If you won't provide me with the answers I need voluntarily I have more than enough means to make you talk...
If you don't like me for some reason, Clifford, I accept it because it's your right. Though I don't see any reason why you couldn't answer my question.

It's obvious you know how to deal with people, Clifford. I sincerely admire you—it requires quite a courage to defy a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Nevertheless I hope that you'll answer my question anyway...

Oh my God... Goodness Gracious, is it really you, Tom? Blessed be Our Lord for returning you to me! I prayed so much for your safe return and now you are here—alive and well! Tell me, knight, how could you manage to find him? I thought that damn Duke van Leerin ordered him to be dragged to some infernal place...
Well, in fact you're right, Clifford. I found him in the Devil's Caverns. Now I would like to hear, what happened!

Well, knight... Now when Tom's back I will gladly tell you everything—I believe Archangel Gabriel himself will protect me. When my son was being held by those monsters I didn't dare to speak, because they threatened me to do him terrible things if I mention anything I saw down there...
Who threatened you? Tell me your story, Clifford. I promise that neither you nor your son will come to any harm.

I will tell you everything, knight. In fact I'm not sure how it all began... it happened so quickly. One night strange sounds awoke me. The sounds were coming from somewhere in the house—I went through it twice but I didn't find anything. But then... in the light of my lantern I saw a secret trapdoor—a small passage leading deep into the bowels of the earth. I was very surprised because I thought I knew the house through and through. I was really worried, but in the end my fear was overwhelmed by my curiosity and I entered the stairs...

I was frozen by fear. It became obvious to me that the Duke is insane—his voice was like a chorus of thousand demons. I staggered away as fast as I could. That discovery jolted me and made me feverish. I wanted to forget all I had seen there, but I couldn't. I couldn't do that. Naturally, the next day my master noticed my behavior. I tried hard to avoid answering him but in the end he managed to make me talk. I told him about everything I saw down there and that I would report it to the Inquisition. But he just kept on laughing and told me that if I told anyone he would kill my son. That monster ordered him kidnapped to ensure my silence! I couldn't do anything... He promised me to return my son when he performs the task he was chosen for... I couldn't do anything, knight. Please, believe me!
Are you sure that it was really Duke van Leerin?

Yes, knight, I'm absolutely sure. I've been serving Duke van Leerin all my life and so I'd be able to recognize him even in complete darkness. Moreover he had a lantern illuminating his face. I must tell you, knight, I almost started screaming. The Duke must be Satan himself!
Where is the secret entrance into that cellar, good man?

It's here on the first floor. I guess it's a derelict cellar or something, but I have no idea when exactly it was built. I'd bet though it was in the pagan times—I'm sure about it. There are more relicts like that around. Well, I'd have never imagined that one of those relicts is just under the house in which I live.
So the cellar is accessible?
Well, no, knight. There's a big lock as I found out after that terrible experience down there.
Well and you wouldn't happen to have the key, would you?

I would, knight. Some time ago I made copies of all Duke's keys just in case some of them gets broken or lost. Later I realized that there was one key among them which did not fit into any lock in the house. After I found the secret trapdoor I realized that the key fits its lock. Here you go, knight. I suppose that it will come in handy.
Thank you for telling me everything, good man.
You're welcome, knight. In fact I'm in your debt! I will be thankful to you for saving my son till the day I die, knight. God bless you.
Could you answer me a few more questions?
Sure, knight. I'll gladly answer all your questions.
Hail to you, good man.
May I ask you who you are?
Of course, knight. My name is Johaness Clifford. Can I help you somehow?
I would like to have a talk with you.
Have a talk? About what do you wanna talk? I don't know much, I'm just a simple valet...
May I ask you what are you doing here?
I am the valet of my master—Duke Rowan van Leerin, knight. You're in his house. Now, may I ask you what are you doing here?
A good question, good man. I came to visit Duke Rowan van Leerin.
Then I welcome you here, knight. I'm sure you'll find the Duke without my help...
Yes, I think so. Nevertheless I'd like to ask you a few questions, if I may.
What questions? I don't know much, I'm just a simple valet...
You're right, Clifford. Farewell.
I investigate crimes against God and faith here in Glatzburg. Do you happen to have any suspicion?

A suspicion? Heaven forbid! I don't know about anything. And even if I knew, who would believe me—I'm just a simple valet. I don't know anything, God is my witness. Would you please stop asking questions like that? It's no good neither for my ears nor for my stupid head.
I am sorry, good man, I didn't mean to scare you. I'd better be going.
Very well. Nevertheless I'd like to ask you a few questions.
Aren't you hiding something from me? I think that your reaction suggests you know something.
I don't know anything, I've just told you that! So leave me be, please. If you want to talk with the Duke, go to him. If not, please leave.
I was just passing by, good man. I don't want to hold you up any longer. Farewell.
Hello, good man. Do you know this boy next to me? It seems he might be your son Tom...
I wanted to ask you if you know this boy next to me. It seems he might be your son Tom...
About what do you want to talk? I don't know anything, I'm just a simple valet...
Nothing, just passing by. Farewell.

Welcome, knight. I'm so glad to see you again. I'll praise you again and again for returning my son to me. For wrestling him out of the claws of those infernal lackeys! How can I ever repay you? What can I do for you?
Nothing this time, good man. Farewell.

Stumbling in the darkness I cautiously headed in the direction from which those sounds were coming and then I arrived to the point where the corridor was opening into a small chamber. It was a jail or something like that—there were three small cells with several girls inside. They were scared, huddling together and sobbing in terror. Just opposite to them was my master Duke Rowan van Leerin and he was muttering to them in a low voice. He was telling them that he was chosen for a mission or something like that and that he needed to sacrifice them in order to complete it... It was terrible!

Of course, noble sir. My name is Johaness Clifford. Can I help you somehow?
I am the valet of my master—Duke Rowan van Leerin, noble sir. You're in his house. Now, may I ask you what are you doing here?
Then I welcome you here, noble sir. I'm sure you'll find the Duke without my help...
What do you need, noble sir?

Welcome, noble sir. I'm so glad to see you again. I'll praise you again and again for returning my son to me. For wrestling him out of the claws of those infernal lackeys! How can I ever repay you? What can I do for you?
Natalia Reichmann? I've heard that the landsknecht Olfghard killed her. Some of her jewelry was found on him...

So that's what the people say? A good one! Well, but it's not true! That jewelry found on Olfghard—I gave it to him. That nosy bastard caught me taking this Reichmann bitch outta the city, so I had to give him some of her precious stuff to shut his bloody mouth.
So, the landsknecht Olfghard's testimony is true, right?

Yep, guess so. That jewelry found on Olfghard—I gave it to him. That nosy bastard caught me taking that Reichmann bitch outta the city, so I had to give him some of her precious stuff to shut his bloody mouth.
Have you kidnapped Natalia Reichmann?!
Yep, it is so. Wanna make some conclusions cuz of it?! I'm gonna send a message to her papa—if he wanna see his nice gal alive he's gonna send me lotsa gold damn fast!
Kidnapping is a deadly sin, neighbor. Drop that weapon at once and come with me.
Just forget about that, knight. Nobody's gonna ruin my plans. I'll get her father's money even if it means sending her in pieces to him. You're not gonna stop me!
Do you know what kidnapping means under secular law, soldier? Kidnapping expresses your intention to marry this woman in the eyes of the King and of God!
What are you babbling about, knight?! I don't wanna marry her—just wanna have some fun with her and get some money from her damn father!
I am sorry, but due to your ignorance you got yourself into a delicate legal situation—instead of committing a crime you made the first legal step towards marriage!
Bullshit! I'm telling you I just want cash—I'll get lost as soon as I get it! I don't wanna marry this woman, I'm not gonna take her with me. Wanna get her cash, nothing else!

I'm sorry. By your deeds you've expressed the will to marry Natalia Reichmann as your legal wife. In the view of the fact that I am a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous imbued with the power to carry out marriage rituals I hereby declare you husband and wife.
WHAT?! Never! I don't wanna marry this bitch! NEVER! Take her yourself, I'm gone! I'm not gonna get enslaved—I have no need to do that...
Hmm... It's interesting how a vision of marriage can put an atrocious criminal to flight! Men...
It seems you're going to get your money, soldier. Anyway, do you have a plan how to get them? You can't keep guarding the girl and go to the city to ask her father for ransom at the same time.
Well... er... you're right, knight. Didn't think 'bout that. Damn, it's getting kinda complicated! May plague and cholera eat it all...
Maybe I could help you. I'll visit her father to tell him your conditions.
You? Why the hell would you do something like that? You wanna outsmart me, right? Careful with that, man, or I'm gonna introduce you to my blade.
Give me half of the ransom and we have a deal.

Hmm... an interesting idea. While you're gone to her father for the gold I could have some fun with this bitch. Then we'll spit the ransom and I'll be gone. Well... Sounds like a good deal to me. So, you go to her father, that bloody merchant Reichmann, and tell him that if he wanna see his daughter alive he's gonna pay 2,000 gp.
I don't want you to harm the poor girl.
Then I'll have to kill you, knight, cuz I'm gonna have lotsa fun with that bitch.
There's still time to save your soul, soldier. Drop that sword and come with me.
Go to hell, knight. I told you that nobody's gonna thwart my plans! Gonna kill you!

Stop right there! One more step and you're gonna know how deep I can sink my sword into your damn belly, knight. How the hell did you find me here?! Just snooping around? Or was it somebody from the city who sent you?!
Well, who are you?
It's none of your bloody concern! You shouldn't have stayed away from my business. If you kept to yourself we wouldn't be in this mess now. A wrong move and you're dead meat!
I don't have a slightest idea what is going on here. And I can't understand why are you threatening me with your weapon?!
Coz nobody's gonna thwart my plans. I've gone too far to be stopped by anyone.
What plans are you talking about? And who's that scared girl behind you? What is going on here?

Don't play an ignorant fool, knight. You look far too intelligent. I'd bet the Sheriff or someone else sent you to get me. Cuz I kidnapped this bitch Natalia Reichmann. If her father weren't such an ass, I could have gotten under her skirt and could have gotten her papa's gold. Well, but that old fool threatened to kill me if I looked at her again. Doubt that. Well, anyway, I needed the gold. I said to myself that he's gonna pay me well if I return her alive... of course, after I have some fun with her.
It wasn't my intention to cross your path, soldier. I'd better be on my way.

Do you think I'm crazy? I'll let you go and you'll bring the entire Hillbrandt garrison to bust my ass. I'm sure Sheriff Contemburry has declared me a deserter. I guess that he even might have asked you to spy on me. Don't you play a fool, knight. You look far too clever. I'm damn sure the Sheriff or someone else sent you to find me and get me. Cuz I kidnapped this bitch—Natalia Reichmann. If her father weren't such an ass, I could have gotten under her skirt and could have gotten her papa's gold. Well, but that old fool threatened to kill me if I looked at her again. Doubt that. Well, anyway, I needed the gold. I said to myself that he's gonna pay me well if I return her alive... of course, after I have some fun with her.
Kidnapping is a deadly sin, my son. Drop that weapon at once and come with me.
Just forget about that, knight. I'm not gonna let you spoil my plans. I'll get her father's money even if it means sending her in pieces to him. You're not gonna stop me!
Hmm... well if I think about it you'll be the soldier Jullian, am I right?
So you know me?! Kinda surprises me, cuz I dunno your face. You must be new here. But why the hell do you need to know?
Because I promised Sheriff Contemburry to bring you back. You are a deserter.

So that old tyrant hired you to find me, right? That's typical of him. He's hiding his ass in the safety of the garrison and asks others to do his job. I tell you, knight, it's not bad to be an officer. Well, that's not for people like myself. For the poor who are on the breadline and have no chance to get any better. Couldn't stand that anymore. Had to get away from that dirt. I had to do something. That's why I became interested in this bitch Natalia Reichmann. First I thought I could get under her skirt and get the money of her papa then. Well, but that old fool Stefan Reichmann threatened to kill me if I looked at her again. Doubt that. Well, anyway, I needed the gold. I said to myself that he's gonna pay me well if I return her alive... of course, after I have some fun with her.
Because I met Olfghard—he told me very nasty things about you...

So that snitch told you about me... What the hell did he told you? That I was fed up with the damn military life? That I couldn't stand it anymore? That I had to get away from that social dirt? Yeah, right, it's exactly like that! I had to do something to get away from it. That's why I became interested in this bitch Natalia Reichmann. First I thought I could get under her skirt and get the money of her papa then. Well, but that old fool Reichmann threatened to kill me if I looked at her again. Doubt that. Well, anyway, I needed the gold. I said to myself that he's gonna pay me well if I return her alive... of course, after I have some fun with her.
Hello.
Have you delivered my conditions to Reichmann, knight?
Not yet, soldier. Could I ask you a few questions?
Don't wanna talk, knight. Get the money, we'll split it and I'm gone. Done. No talking needed.
Yes, I did. And he paid me the required amount.
Great. So gimme my half and I'll be on my way. I'm gonna be lucky with money like this. Farewell, life of a fucking soldier. I'm gonna live as a lord now.
Here's the gold. I'm going to take Natalia back to her father.
You can do anything you want with her—she's none of my concern now. I've had a good time with her already. See you, knight. Guess you've improved my opinion 'bout the Church.
Farewell. It'll be better if we never meet again...
I doubt that, soldier. You're not going to get a single coin from it. I'm going to keep the money myself.
What?! You betrayed me. You cheated me. Gonna kill you for that!
Regrettably I don't have the money on me by now...
What?! And I'm to believe that? Are you trying to cheat me?! I'm gonna kill you for that!
According to canon law, kidnapping is a deadly sin, my son. Drop that weapon at once and come with me.
Just forget about that, Father. Nobody's gonna ruin my plans. I'll get her father's money even if it means sending her in pieces to him. You're not gonna stop me!
What are you babbling about, Father?! I don't wanna marry her—just wanna have some fun with her and get some money from her damn father!

I'm sorry. By your deeds you've expressed the will to marry Natalia Reichmann as your legal wife. In the view of the fact that I am a priest imbued with the power to carry out marriage rituals I hereby declare you husband and wife.
Well... er... you're right, Father. Didn't think 'bout that. Damn, it's getting kinda complicated! May plague and cholera eat it all...
Then I'll have to kill you, Father, cuz I'm gonna have lotsa fun with that bitch.
Go to hell, Father. I told you that nobody's gonna thwart my plans! Gonna kill you!

Cuz nobody's gonna thwart my plans. I went too far to be stopped by a damn priest.
