I found out that Istwan de Bragho have risen from his grave to wreak vengeance upon those who were behind his capture and execution. It seems that he's immortal. Could you help me with that?

Woe! Woe and despair echo in your words! So the rumors about the return of the cursed Vice-Governor Istwan de Bragho are true! There will be nothing good coming out of it. Moreover you're telling me that he's immortal, right?
Yes, he is, good woman. I myself heard him boasting that he cannot be killed unless he takes the lives of those because of which he came from the Underworld. He considers himself to be a revenant.

Revenant you say? Then it's really bad, knight. Bad indeed... If Istwan de Bragho really is a revenant like he claims, then he cannot be harmed neither by weapons nor by spells. Revenants are those who have returned—people sometimes mistake them for zombies—they are undead monsters brought to our world to fulfill vengeance they swore to wreak upon someone while they lived. After they return they cannot be stopped or destroyed unless all their victims are dead. Then they descend back to the Underworld never to return.
I don't believe it's possible to battle them. They are immortal, aren't they?

Yes, in their essence they are immortal, knight. No weapon, no spell, no man, no animal can harm them. There's only one way to affect them—to sanctify their dead bodies. If somebody manages to sprinkle a revenant's body with holy water it should sunder all the ties between this world and the Underworld. It should remove his curse and return him to eternal rest. At least ancient tomes mention that. I've never heard somebody would manage to do it.
Thanks. I must try everything.
Be careful, knight. Revenants are particularly ill tempered—anybody standing between them and their prey is in mortal danger...
What do you know about the Fallen Angels, good woman?
Oh my God... why are you asking me about such terrible things, knight?
Because we live in terrible times. Go on, what do you know about them?

Woe, knight! The visions of the Fallen Angels haunt me in my dreams these days... Surely it is not by chance that you're asking. The Archangel Gabriel himself came to me in my dream and prophesized terrible news. The judgment is at hand—the inevitable is coming. I fell upon my knees in my dream and then I saw the Earth crack open—infernal flames burst out revealing the three Fallen Angels—Arthamon, the ruler of despair and the cursed lord of fire; Baphomet, the demon of madness and the creator of chaos; and Cerdie, the lascivious mistress of fornication and of eternal sin. And the world was flooded with beasts and monsters dancing gruesome dance celebrating the end of the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. The fallen angels rose and the earth and the heavens trembled under the blast of their infernal powers. And then came despair and chaos and all the people were drown in eternal sin. The end of all things came. Kingdoms were crumbling, people were fornicating, murdering, dying... and the False Prophet was walking the Earth demonically laughing.
Are you trying to tell me that the Archangel Gabriel heralded you the end of the world?

No... no, I don't think so, knight. In my visions, I don't always see what will really happen. Sometimes, their meaning is hidden. I'd think that those nightmares herald a great movement in the mechanism of the history of the world. It is just a grain of sand blown into my dreams from the endless desert of destiny. Something is going on and it surely has to do something with the Fallen Angels. I'm sure you know the Scripture, knight. In the Revelations of Saint Ezechiel there's exactly what I see in my dreams—the liberation of the Fallen Angels and their coming to this world which will end the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. I am absolutely sure that it is just what would happen if the Fallen Angels were to enter our world.
You mentioned that you can foretell future. Could you tell me what the future has in store for me?
I didn't tell I can foretell the future. I said that I can foresee the events that might happen. There's a difference.
Very well then—what can I expect? What can have the future in store for me?
Do you really want to know, knight?
Yes, I do. It could help me in my quest.
Well then. I'll look into your heart. But I need you to bring me a thorn apple. It's very difficult to call visions without it...
Then you can begin your work, good woman. I happen to have a thorn apple right on me—here you go.
All right, I'll get a thorn apple for you.
As you wish, knight, it's your decision...
You're right, I don't want to know.
A wise decision. Just believe that your life is in the hands of God and be content with it.
I'm sorry but I'm not going to tell you that!

Secular rule is insignificant, knight. It's just a passing affair—it comes and leaves as spring snow does. Well, but if you really want to know... the royal governor is Robert Heidrick, he has a Grand Ducal title I believe. His deputy is Rowan van Leerin, a proud bearer of a Ducal title.

If you're looking for weapons, armor and for other war-gear, knight, go visit the Armory of Hans von Drichtmaul. Potions and magic goods can be obtained either here or at the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. Then there are two shops with all kinds of goods run by the landlord Ludwig Weintraum and by the inkeeper Wanda Gielwitch. And if you're not interested in the origin of the goods, you can visit that rogue Alphonso DiCerbio.

God is punishing us for our sins! He turned away his divine sight because we were living in sin and lecherousness, forgetting about the divine laws teaching humility and obedience. We descended at the level of pagans from whom we once originated. We turn our attention to idols and demons asking them to satisfy our sinful lust. God sees it all and judges us for our crimes!
And how do you think we could amend this gruesome state of things, good woman?
It's clear, knight—there's no going back. We're halfway on the road to Hell. There's no going back from Hell. It's too late, the Judgment Day is at hand!
I've heard various rumors about a coming war. Do you know anything about it?

War... yes, the war is coming. Every day I meet men—they are laughing, drinking, loving their women and they do not know that many of them have the sign of death on their foreheads. They are already dead. Oh those dreams of mine... those fields covered with corpses... those black ravens feeding on the eyeballs of the fallen men... Two armies of brothers face each other—man against man. Yesterday they drank together, today they lash out with their swords one against another. In the name of God, in the name of justice—kill Ultherst heretics, kill them all! In the name of God, in the name of Saint Orthenius, stand by my side the knights of Ultherst, kill those Lochland dogs! Brother rose against brother, blood was shed on the immaculate canvas of the righteous realms. No more serenity, no more peace. And the big black tomcat is lying at the doorstep, his head bearing the crown with seven diamonds... he's waiting for he knows that his time shall come. There's no other way.

What are you talking about? What's the meaning of your dreams? And what about Lochland Empire? What has the Empire to do with all that? Lochland is a firm supporter of the true faith and a time-honored ally of Ultherst!
I don't know, knight. I don't know what it means. Something terrible is at hand—something inevitable. Woe shall plague all of us who have lived to witness these cruel and pitiless times.

Hmmm, I see, heretics is that what you seek... You're trying to find the snake, but he's hidden too well in a deep dark crevice—he sees everything and everyone from his lair. He's walking around and still he's staying at one place, he's hiding and still everybody can see him. The snake who is guilty of biting and poisoning, the snake who is firmly grasping his victim...
What are you speaking about, good woman?
I... I don't know, knight. Suddenly I saw it all before my eyes... the words were flowing like a river. I don't know, I'm sorry...
What do you know about a heretic cult named The Children of the New Order?

The Children of the New Order? Yes, I know who they are. They were acting in the dark ages at the end of the Hundred Years War, that's in the tenth century. They were led by certain Lucius—he was a Dark Prophet and the High Priest of the cult. That was him who prophesized the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth and the release of Satan from his prison. He was preaching about the end of the Old World and about coming of a New Order—Its children were supposed to rule the enthralled souls of the righteous who were to be killed by sword and fire in the process. Although the cult infiltrated the highest social ranks of the Empire it met a gruesome end. All the cultists—including Lucius—were executed. Burnt. And that was their end.

The Children of the New Order? Yes, I know who they are. Why are you asking? It has something to do with that cursed scroll I translated, right? Oh yes, I can see it in your eyes, I can see it in your soul... the shadow of that scroll hinders your soul as a heavy boulder. It crushes you, it suffocates... You shall never get rid of it. Never! It should have never gotten in your hands, knight. Woe shall befell the one who caused his bad luck by his thoughtless acts. Blessed be the one who does not yearn for secrets. Though death gruesome indeed awaits the one who uncovers that what should have remained hidden, the one who brings to the light of our worlds the shadows of things meant to lay in darkness for eternity!
You are mistaken, good woman. Not all secrets are meant to remain hidden. Some secrets must be revealed. Nevertheless, tell me, what do you know about the cult of the Children of the New Order?

They were acting in the dark ages at the end of the Hundred Years War, that's in the tenth century. They were led by certain Lucius—he was a Dark Prophet and the High Priest of the cult. That was him who prophesized the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth and the release of Satan from his prison. He was preaching about the end of the Old World and about coming of a New Order—Its children were supposed to rule the enthralled souls of the righteous who were to be killed by sword and fire in the process. Although the cult infiltrated the highest social ranks of the Empire it met a gruesome end. All the cultists—including Lucius—were executed. Burnt. And that was their end. Well, but it seems now that it wasn't quite true. What did you discover, knight? Why are you looking for that cult? That scroll I translated mentioned summoning of the Fallen Angels. Whose scroll was it? How did it come into your possession?

The scroll belonged to Bishop Vallarian, the judge of the Holy Office who was sent to Hillbrandt by the local curia to reveal and punish heretics. Though in the end it became apparent that he himself was a heretic. According to my investigation it seems he managed to summon one of the Fallen Angels—Arthamon. Unfortunately I lack evidence.

Goodness Gracious, have mercy with us... Arthamon the Fallen Angel in our world! But that would mean... that Judge Vallarian strived to carry out the deeds mentioned in that scroll. Once summoned the Fallen Angels would cause the end of the world—just as Saint Ezechiel prophesized in the Revelations. My vision... oh God!
I can't answer your questions, good woman. It's for your own safety.

My safety was jeopardized the moment you entered my house for the first time. I told you then to leave and to leave me alone, but you just had to look into the face of death. Though it's your choice—leave your answers to yourself. I can knit together many a thing even without them. And to be honest with you, I'm not going to sleep well after your visit. You are indeed deep in troubles, knight. There's no other way left than that running forward—you have to get to the point where it ends and drink the wormwood potion of fate to the last drop. I wish you good luck, though I have a feeling that luck has nothing to do with your mission.

So you want to know what happened... Roses in their prime withered. Petals of fresh buds were torn apart. Blood spoiled the lily-white purity. Desecrated they were and revenge is not to come. Lo, the murdering one easily avoids the hand of justice! People will never turn a suspicious eye to him—the murderer is daringly staring at them, waving his hand from his lofty window. The Beast disguised as a lamb. God's wrath is mighty, though even He is helpless. What justice is it? The time of revenge will come, though maybe too late to change anything. Everything is shrouded in darkness deep underneath the surface... through the hidden passage... opened with a key stolen without knowing...
What are you talking about, good woman? Don't speak in riddles.

Those are no riddles, knight. It's the reality. It's not my fault that you see no meaning in my words. Maybe the time will show... maybe the time will prove me right. And maybe not. It is yet to be seen.

There's a black shadow clouding the murder of Bishop Trevorius, knight. The shadow of betrayal, hypocrisy and of deceit. You are indeed deep in troubles, knight. Avoid mistakes, for they may cost you life. The murder stirred the motionless surface of a deep dark pool having a deadly mire at the bottom. The one who sinks into it shall not come back.

What exactly do you want me to tell you about Father Frederick, knight? It was an aged man who came to Glatzburg several years ago. Even then Grim Reaper was following in his wake, though he took him only during the plague two years ago. I think that he went peacefully—he must have been tired by the sins of this world. No longer could he stand against the evil—he was too old and broken. No wonder after all those trials he had to suffer...

He was a highly regarded exorcist, knight. A demonbane, if you want. He encountered good many soul devouring demons in his life. He was able not only to face them, but also to defeat them. He was able to banish them from the body of a possessed and to send them to burning hell whence they came. I admired him greatly. It's a pity he was not inclined to tell about his vast experience—I'd have loved to learn more about demonology. But such is our fate—as soon as you find a treasure somebody snatches it away and spits into your face.
I understand. Thank you.

Beware of darkness luring to the forgotten depths underneath the city! Beware of shadows lurking at the places where sun never shines. Beware of death stalking the places long forgotten! There's yet one place you should avoid...
Never ever visit the junkyard!
I'll try to heed your warning, thank you.
I wonder why, good woman.
I don't know, knight. But if I were you I'd heed my advise!

I... I know what happened to Raquel Gielwitch, knight. I had a vision... I saw her slumbering. In the house of her sister. She looked so innocent... almost a child. She was sleeping with a rag doll in her bosom. So silent and beautiful. Then came Satan...
Are you trying to tell me that Raquel Gielwitch was kidnapped by Satan?

Yes, knight, exactly. Satan is behind all evil deeds! That night he took the form of two men. Strong and very evil men. They floated into her room through the window as two bats, black cloaks swirling around them as the wings of death! They took Raquel. They disrupted her lovely dream and plunged her into the hell of waking. She resisted. Blood was spilled. Rag doll fell down to be trampled by their heavy boots. Darkness is shrouding the innocent girl—she's praying to the Archangel Gabriel and all the Saints. Though her prayers fall on deaf ears. The men are taking her away—she's limp like a puppet on strings. The night city is quickly floating around them. The darkness is impenetrable. Then the sinners stop to quickly knock on a splendid door. A flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!
Who were those men? Have you recognized them?
No, knight. I did not. But I do know the house where they took her. It is the house of Duke Rowan van Leerin!
I don't have time to chat about Satan, good woman. I'm investigating a crime.

I am well aware of that, knight. Though, know that Satan is behind all the evil being committed throughout our world. You should be aware of it, as a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. That night he took the form of two men. Strong and very evil men. They floated into her room through the window as two bats, black cloaks swirling around them like the wings of death! They took Raquel. They disrupted her lovely dream and plunged her into the hell of waking. She resisted. Blood was spilled. Her rag doll fell down to be trampled by their heavy boots. Darkness is shrouding the innocent girl—she's praying to the Archangel Gabriel and all the Saints. Though her prayers fall on deaf ears. The men are taking her away—she's limp like a puppet on strings. The dusky city is quickly floating around them. The darkness is impenetrable. Then the sinners stop to knock hastily on a splendid door. A flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!

Glatzburg is literarily soaked with legends and stories, knight. And if not the city itself then its surroundings. The local people are clinging to legends and stories even more these days because they offer them at least some consolation and even hope. The Legend of Saint Orthenius is especially popular among the people. It says that in the times of the direst peril a new hero will rise from the people to defend the faith as once Saint Orthenius did. He is supposed to protect the Realm against all the enemies.
Interesting. Is there any way how to tell who's that hero?

He will be readily recognized, knight, for he will wield a mighty relic called Inquisitor, a powerful weapon that helped Saint Orthenius to defeat the Erebornian pagans and to release the Filkland peninsula from their grip. That relic will shine with mighty light, blinding all enemies. A single command will make it decapitate all the enemies and strike the sinners with heavenly lightning bolts. At least so it is said in the legend circulating among the people.
Do you think there's any truth to that legend?

Of course, knight. There some truth to all things. I am sure that the relic does exist. It is rumored that Orthenius hid it before he died and prophesized that it would be retrieved by his heir—the new protector of the Realm. Though the legend does not mention where it should be hidden.
I brought you that thorn apple you asked for. Can you divine the future for me now?
I would like to ask you to decipher this scroll for me—the Royal Master Alchemist, Alberto Kelley, gave it to me.

Another mysterious scroll? You're keeping me busy alright, knight. Do you have any ideas what it should contain? I suppose that it will again be some dark prophecy about the end of the world... I'd not expect anything less from you.
Don't be waspish, good woman. Master Kelley supposes that it could be a powerful magic formula...
Hmm... well. But it's not going to be free. I want $$getmoney1250$$ gp.
Very well, here you go.
I don't have that much right now.
So come when you have enough, knight.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to translate anything for you!
I'd like you to translate the scroll I told you about. Hopefully I have enough money this time—here you go.
I've found a very weird root of some herb unknown to me. Can you tell me what it is?
Show me that root, knight... Oh my! It's a Radix Diaboli root, people call it Devil's Root! It's very rare and very magic. I can make you a rather powerful power-up potion of it.
Thank you, I'll remember that.
Are you able to brew magic potions from the devil's root, good woman?

But of course, knight! It's not very difficult to make magic potions using Devil's Root. The difficult part is to find some. It usually grows at rather dangerous places—hence the name. If you find a Devil's Root, I can make you a magic potion of it for a few gold coins.
You're either going to answer my question or I'm going to introduce you to the right of torture!
You probably don't like me for some reason, good woman. It's your right to dislike me, though if you think about it you'll certainly realize that there's no point in avoiding answering my question.
You are a very wise woman, Enrie. Your answer would really help me. I beg you, answer my question.

Woe and despair befell me, a poor old woman! Hellish snares of death are binding me to the bosom of eternal damnation! That scroll is the purest evil, knight! Any one who touched it shall never be safe again! That scroll should have never come to this city, it should have never crossed my threshold!
What are you talking about, good woman? You've not yet read the scroll...

I don't have to touch it to know that it's the scroll my premonition forewarned me about. It is the source of all woe which now dwells in the walls of my house. Take it away, knight. I don't want to touch it.
I need to know what's written there, good woman. I need it really bad. Help me, please. I know that you're adept in many occult arts, maybe you could recognize the writings.

I said no, knight! I'm not going to touch that scroll, even though I know that it is already too late. Even mentioning its existence has put my life into a mortal danger. Things like this should remain hidden and forgotten.
I hate to insist, but I really do need that scroll translated. If I have to, I'll force you to do it. Believe me that I have enough rather violent means at my disposal!
I really do need your help, good woman. If you help me, you can ask anything in return!
Oh? Hmm... anything you said?
Yes, I said that. If you help me, you can ask anything in return.

Hmm... very well, I'll help you then. Your presence here is an omen that I shall not escape my grievous fate anyway... I'll examine that scroll of yours. But first you must do me a favor. Have you ever heard about the Elenian race?
I might have. Why are you asking?

The Elenians were a pagan non-human race living where now the Realm is—it was long before the arrival of man. It was a very advanced and flourishing civilization with a great talent for magic and alchemy. Although it might seem heretical to you, the most of our knowledge of magic and of nature comes from their teachings. The Elenians believed in afterlife. Though it was different from the afterlife described in the Scripture. The Elenians believed that their dead travel into the different world which resembles our own. That's why they buried their dead into tombs with all their belongings that might come in handy on their journey to the afterlife. Thanks to that many remnants of their culture have been preserved to our times—they can serve as a repository of knowledge and of understanding. Well, but why am I telling you all this? Thanks to an ancient Elenian scroll I found out that the tomb of Fae'Darlion, an Elenian noble, is located somewhere near Glatzburg. It seems that he was a very powerful man who was buried with various artifacts.
Well, I suppose I know what are you getting at. You want me to bring you something from that tomb. What exactly do you need?

I want his spellbook. Fae'Darlion was a mage. It seems he managed to fathom the most intriguing secrets of pagan magic and for me it would be a great repository of information regarding Elenian views of the world and of magic. Bring me Fae'Darlion's spellbook and I will help you with the translation of that accursed scroll!
Do you have any idea where should be the tomb located? "Near Glatzburg" is a bit too general description...
I'm sorry but I can't help you with that. The scroll was not very specific as regards the tomb location. I think you'll have to search around the city.
Deal. I don't think haggling would help. I'll bring you the book.

Be very careful, knight. Elenian tombs are renowned for their intricate traps preventing the attacks of tomb raiders. Take this scroll with the transcription of the Elenian runic alphabet, it might come in handy. You can never know what might happen.
Deal. Could we talk a little bit more?
Very well. I would like to trade some goods now.
Oh, Lord Almighty... My worries came true. I won't escape my punishment. That writing of the scroll is the forbidden diabolic script, the writing of the Dark Prophets!
Are you sure?

Yes, I am. When I was young I succumbed to temptation and deciphered the writing with the help of several scrolls which supposedly were word-for-word partial transcripts of the work of one of the Dark Prophets. Although I have not seen the writings since then its image was burnt deep into my mind—as if with branding iron.
So you can decipher the scroll, right?

Yes, knight, I can do it. There is no going back. Bad omens came true and we must bear the burden of our destiny as the First Prophet bore his cross. Give me a moment to look through the text. I'll make you a verbatim translation.

Don't thank me, knight. I'm not doing you a favor—on the contrary. I'm paving your way to the depths of the cursed abyss! Here's the translation of the scroll. Now leave me alone, please. Go and know that betrayal, death and eternal damnation follow in your footsteps!
What?! You've read the scrolls of the Dark Prophets?! It's the most severe of all the sins!

I know, knight. I've not let a day pass without begging God for forgiveness since. I always believed that one day I could be able to redeem my sin somehow... I had no idea that it would happen in such a gruesome way!
I have a Devil's Root. Could you make me that magic potion of it, please?
Of course, knight. It will cost you $$getmoney1000$$ gp.
I will need just a moment, knight...
Thank you, there's no need to hurry. Better make it perfect.
Here you are, knight. One miraculous potion. Do you want anything else?
Very well, knight. I'll make the potion at once. Just wait a moment...
Of course. Take your time...

It's finished, knight. Smells great... I've not tasted thorn apple in years... Show me your hand. No, don't worry, it's no palm reading like at a fair, I just need a contact with your aura. Aaah... that's... hmmm... interesting. Golden color... It apparently corresponds with the way you earn your living as a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I see many violent deeds scarring your soul... but it's not for me to judge. You are who you are. There's the path you're walking... You see what is there to be seen and hear what you want to hear... You are the Wanderer and Death walks in your wake. You are the beast and the lamb... a cocoon which will give birth either to the tiger or to the butterfly...
What's there? What do you see then?

I hear the sound of horns... No! Those are the infernal horns... Doomed is the one who enters the maw of Hell. Though thrice shall you enter and thrice shall you fall to face your very own self—to decide. Three evils shall you face and the victory shall be your defeat. I see you walking through the vale of tears to the gate leading nowhere. I see you travel places which do not exist. I see you walking the streets of the cities long forgotten, talking to the people long dead. You are Malus Victideus, Alpha and Omega of the eternity, who is being reborn to perish again. I see... no, I don't see anything more. Just blood, nothing other than blood. And graves. Nothing other than graves. Endless fields dotted with graves. Oh, there is something more... Beware of false people with friendly faces and deadly daggers. You are the Wanderer who walks alone. The only one following you is Death and Death cannot be trusted!
Hmm... thank you. Whatever may your prophecy mean.
Oh... do not thank me, knight. I did nothing to deserve your thanks. On the contrary!

Well, show me the scroll... It's the Elenian moon script—it's obvious, though the words are unclear. It's probably coded in some way... The Elenians obviously enjoyed mysterious codes. Reading was a game to them, see?
Didn't know that...

Got it! It is very primitive... the words are written the other way around. Well, did you say that it should be a powerful magic formula? The scroll reads: three threescores of nuts, five ells of cloth, six carafes of wine... It doesn't seem like a magic formula to me, knight. It almost seems... as if it were a shopping list! I think that it's probably a shopping list of some merchant embarking on a business trip.
Hmm... Thank you anyway, good woman.
You're welcome, knight. I was afraid that it'd be another dark prophecy. Farewell.

My God... the signs were right! Behold, the Wanderer is coming and Death is following in his wake lurking to overwhelm all who would welcome the Wanderer with a kind word. Begone, knight! Begone at once! You are bringing me great woe! Begone!
What? What are you talking about, good woman? And who are you, anyway?

My name is Enrie Jungwirdt, if you must know it. And it's all you are going to hear from me. Go away—your shadow hides threat. The signs did not lie—the Wanderer is coming... Terrible woe befell me, a poor servant of the angel Raphael! Go away as fast as you can and leave me be!
I'm sorry you feel it this way. I assure you that I pose no threat to you. I've sought you because I need to talk with you about a certain matter.
I've told you to begone at once! Your presence alone puts me in great danger. I don't want to have anything to do with you. Begone!
You cannot tell me where I can or cannot stay! I do require your cooperation and if I see fit I can force you to do what I ask by any means necessary!

Oh... forgive me, knight. I implore you to forgive me, it was not my intention to oppose you... Just... I just know that you are bringing me gruesome fate indeed. I was afraid of it, but it's inevitable. Man proposes, God disposes. Very well, what can I do for you?
Looking at the furnishings of your house I'd say that you are an adept in the art of alchemy...

My art has nothing to do with alchemy—at least as the Royal Alchemist Guild perceives it. My knowledge stems from the nature and from its understanding. I can make not only various potions and elixirs supporting both body and mind, but also miscellaneous items imbued with supernatural spiritual powers. Everything in accordance with the Holy Scripture, of course!
People say that you're a seer. That you can perceive things others cannot see. How can you explain it?

Yes it is so—I can perceive things others cannot see. I can see places and people hundred miles away. I can see what was and what could be. It's a gift from God, knight. Or a curse, if you wish. It's been inherited by the first born daughter in our family since time immemorial. Though people do not look kindly at such a gift—they consider it a diabolic omen. Fortunately, the Holy Mother Church tolerates it, especially thanks to the efforts of Bishop Trevorius. Women in our family were not always that lucky. I remember old stories about my great-grandmother who prophesized the barbarian invasion of the Realm—when she tried to warn the people they accused her of witchcraft and wanted to burn her. Fortunately, they had no time to do it because that very moment the village was overrun by barbarian raiders coming from the Moonshine Mountains to the south...
I would like to ask you whether you could decipher this scroll. It is an imperative to keep absolute silence about everything you might learn from it!
But of course, knight. What do you need to know?
Welcome, knight. What brings you here?
I would like to have a little talk with you, if I can.
Nothing for the moment, good woman. Farewell.
Well, knight, how is going your search for the tomb of Fae'Darlion?
I was able to make a certain advance, good woman. I probably found the entrance to the tomb.

Really?! That is... that is the greatest discovery of this century, knight! We're to embark on the journey to knowledge undreamt of. Nevertheless judging from the absence of Fae'Darlion's spellbook in your hands I'd say that there were certain complications, right?
Exactly. The writing I managed to find and decipher mentioned a Sunlight Charm of a god named Ael'Erthen. It's the only way how to get inside the tomb.

Hmm... But of course, it makes sense... The Elenians considered the afterlife to be the Realm of Shadows and thus only priests serving Sun God Ael'Erthen could enter. It seems that their charms had the power to open otherwise imperviously sealed tombs of the Elenians.
Well, it's very a interesting theory, but I can't get inside without such a charm.

A good observation, knight. Well, I have an ancient Elenian amulet in my possession, but I was not able to find out any details about it, thus I have absolutely no idea whether it could be the Sun Charm of priests serving Ael'Erthen. Well, anyway it can't do any harm to lend it to you. But you must promise me to return it when you're finished—it's very precious to me!
You're welcome, knight. It's in the best interest of both of us. Is there anything else I can do for you?
I have the spellbook you asked for, good woman. Here it is!

Heavens... Isn't my sight playing tricks on me? It really looks like an Elenian spellbook. And here's the name—Fae'Darlion... You did it, knight! Can you even imagine the knowledge I will be able to gain from that spellbook? It can't be compared to anything I've studied so far! Thank you again, knight.
I'm glad you're pleased. Now, in exchange, I would like you to translate the scroll I told you about.

Oh yes, of course. I must hold my end of the bargain. Show me the scroll, I'll take a look at it. Though I must warn you, knight, once translated there shall be no going back. Do you really want to know what's its message?
Of course. I wouldn't be bothering you otherwise.
Well then. Show me that cursed scroll.
I don't have it on me right now.
Very well, then bring it to me when you want it translated. Not even my ability to see things others cannot see allows me to read other people's letters.
Of course, I understand. Could I talk to you a bit more then?
Of course, knight. What troubles you?
All right. I'd like to barter some goods.
It's a deal. Farewell.
Well I've not made much progress so far.

No wonder, knight. Looking for remnants of the Elenian culture is like looking for a needle in a haystack. Though I believe you'll eventually succeed. You need me to translate that cursed scroll, needn't you?
I knew there will be more questions. Go ahead, ask me, knight.
I'll continue my search. Farewell.
Greetings, knight. Thank you again for bringing me the spellbook. What can I do for you?
I brought the scroll I need translated. Here it is.
Could I have some more questions?
Are you able to brew a potion from the magic mandrake root?

A potion from the magic mandrake root? Are you aware it's used during magic rituals?! Well... it's none of my business, of course. Yes, I can brew the potion, but it's quite an expensive job. It will cost you $$getmoney1000$$ gp.
Great. In that case I will start distilling immediately. But it's going to take a while...
I'm not in a hurry. Take your time.

Of course. First we crush the root in the Petri dish and pour it into the flask. Then we spill in some crushed stardust and a Gautieria fungus, add some clean water and let it stand for a while. Then we'll pour the solution into the boiler and let it distill... Well, it's done. Here's the potion from the magic mandrake root. Use it cautiously, knight—it's a powerful essence alluring evil powers!
Thank you, I'm well aware of that. Farewell.
Regrettably I don't have that much money.
In that case stop by when you have enough, knight.
I'd like you to brew me the potion of the magic mandrake root. I've brought you the money—here it is.

Revenant you say? Then it's really bad, Father. Bad indeed... If Istwan de Bragho really is a revenant like he claims, then he cannot be harmed neither by weapons nor by spells. Revenants are those who have returned—people sometimes mistake them for zombies—they are undead monsters brought to our world to fulfill vengeance they swore to wreak upon someone while they lived. After they return they cannot be stopped or destroyed unless all their victims are dead. Then they descend back to the Underworld never to return.

Yes, in their essence they are immortal, Father. No weapon, no spell, no man, no animal can harm them. There's only one way to affect them—to sanctify their dead bodies. If somebody manages to sprinkle a revenant's body with holy water it should sunder all the ties between this world and the Underworld. It should remove his curse and return him to eternal rest. At least ancient tomes mention that. I've never heard somebody would manage to do it.
Be careful, Father. Revenants are particularly ill tempered—anybody standing between them and their prey is in mortal danger...
Oh my God... why are you asking me about such terrible things, Father?

Woe, Father! The visions of the Fallen Angels haunt me in my dreams these days... Surely it is not by chance that you're asking. The Archangel Gabriel himself came to me in my dream and prophesized terrible news. The judgment is at hand—the inevitable is coming. I fell upon my knees in my dream and then I saw the Earth crack open—infernal flames burst out revealing the three Fallen Angels—Arthamon, the ruler of despair and the cursed lord of fire; Baphomet, the demon of madness and the creator of chaos; and Cerdie, the lascivious mistress of fornication and of eternal sin. And the world was flooded with beasts and monsters dancing gruesome dance celebrating the end of the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. The fallen angels rose and the earth and the heavens trembled under the blast of their infernal powers. And then came despair and chaos and all the people were drown in eternal sin. The end of all things came. Kingdoms were crumbling, people were fornicating, murdering, dying... and the False Prophet was walking the Earth demonically laughing.

No... no, I don't think so, Father. In my visions, I don't always see what will really happen. Sometimes, their meaning is hidden. I'd think that those nightmares herald a great movement in the mechanism of the history of the world. It is just a grain of sand blown into my dreams from the endless desert of destiny. Something is going on and it surely has to do something with the Fallen Angels. I'm sure you know the Scripture, Father. In the Revelations of Saint Ezechiel there's exactly what I see in my dreams—the liberation of the Fallen Angels and their coming to this world which will end the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. I am absolutely sure that it is just what would happen if the Fallen Angels were to enter our world.
Do you really want to know, Father?
As you wish, Father, it's your decision...

Secular rule is insignificant, Father. It's just a passing affair—it comes and leaves as spring snow does. Well, but if you really want to know... the royal governor is Robert Heidrick, he has a Grand Ducal title I believe. His deputy is Rowan van Leerin, a proud bearer of a Ducal title.

If you're looking for weapons, armor and for other war-gear, Father, go visit the Armory of Hans von Drichtmaul. Potions and magic goods can be obtained either here or at the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. Then there are two shops with all kinds of goods run by the landlord Ludwig Weintraum and by the inkeeper Wanda Gielwitch. And if you're not interested in the origin of the goods, you can visit that rogue Alphonso DiCerbio.
It's clear, Father—there's no going back. We're halfway on the road to Hell. There's no going back from Hell. It's too late, the Judgment Day is at hand!
I don't know, Father. I don't know what it means. Something terrible is at hand—something inevitable. Woe shall plague all of us who have lived to witness these cruel and pitiless times.
I... I don't know, Father. Suddenly I saw it all before my eyes... the words were flowing like a river. I don't know, I'm sorry...

The Children of the New Order? Yes, I know who they are. Why are you asking? It has something to do with that cursed scroll I translated, right? Oh yes, I can see it in your eyes, I can see it in your soul... the shadow of that scroll hinders your soul as a heavy boulder. It crushes you, it suffocates... You shall never get rid of it. Never! It should have never gotten in your hands, Father. Woe shall befell the one who caused his bad luck by his thoughtless acts. Blessed be the one who does not yearn for secrets. Though death gruesome indeed awaits the one who uncovers that what should have remained hidden, the one who brings to the light of our worlds the shadows of things meant to lay in darkness for eternity!

They were acting in the dark ages at the end of the Hundred Years War, that's in the tenth century. They were led by certain Lucius—he was a Dark Prophet and the High Priest of the cult. That was him who prophesized the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth and the release of Satan from his prison. He was preaching about the end of the Old World and about coming of a New Order—Its children were supposed to rule the enthralled souls of the righteous who were to be killed by sword and fire in the process. Although the cult infiltrated the highest social ranks of the Empire it met a gruesome end. All the cultists—including Lucius—were executed. Burnt. And that was their end. Well, but it seems now that it wasn't quite true. What did you discover, Father? Why are you looking for that cult? That scroll I translated mentioned summoning of the Fallen Angels. Whose scroll was it? How did it come into your possession?

My safety was jeopardized the moment you entered my house for the first time. I told you then to leave and to leave me alone, but you just had to look into the face of death. Though it's your choice—leave your answers to yourself. I can knit together many a thing even without them. And to be honest with you, I'm not going to sleep well after your visit. You are indeed deep in troubles, Father. There's no other way left than that running forward—you have to get to the point where it ends and drink the wormwood potion of fate to the last drop. I wish you good luck, though I have a feeling that luck has nothing to do with your mission.

Those are no riddles, Father. It's the reality. It's not my fault that you see no meaning in my words. Maybe the time will show... maybe the time will prove me right. And maybe not. It is yet to be seen.

There's a black shadow clouding the murder of Bishop Trevorius, Father. The shadow of betrayal, hypocrisy and of deceit. You are indeed deep in troubles, Father. Avoid mistakes, for they may cost you life. The murder stirred the motionless surface of a deep dark pool having a deadly mire at the bottom. The one who sinks into it shall not come back.

What exactly do you want me to tell you about Father Frederick, Father? It was an aged man who came to Glatzburg several years ago. Even then Grim Reaper was following in his wake, though he took him only during the plague two years ago. I think that he went peacefully—he must have been tired by the sins of this world. No longer could he stand against the evil—he was too old and broken. No wonder after all those trials he had to suffer...

He was a highly regarded exorcist, Father. A demonbane, if you want. He encountered good many soul devouring demons in his life. He was able not only to face them, but also to defeat them. He was able to banish them from the body of a possessed and to send them to burning hell whence they came. I admired him greatly. It's a pity he was not inclined to tell about his vast experience—I'd have loved to learn more about demonology. But such is our fate—as soon as you find a treasure somebody snatches it away and spits into your face.
I don't know, Father. But if I were you I'd heed my advise!

I... I know what happened to Raquel Gielwitch, Father. I had a vision... I saw her slumbering. In the house of her sister. She looked so innocent... almost a child. She was sleeping with a rag doll in her bosom. So silent and beautiful. Then came Satan...

Yes, Father, exactly. Satan is behind all evil deeds! That night he took the form of two men. Strong and very evil men. They floated into her room through the window as two bats, black cloaks swirling around them as the wings of death! They took Raquel. They disrupted her lovely dream and plunged her into the hell of waking. She resisted. Blood was spilled. Rag doll fell down to be trampled by their heavy boots. Darkness is shrouding the innocent girl—she's praying to the Archangel Gabriel and all the Saints. Though her prayers fall on deaf ears. The men are taking her away—she's limp like a puppet on strings. The night city is quickly floating around them. The darkness is impenetrable. Then the sinners stop to quickly knock on a splendid door. A flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!
No, Father. I did not. But I do know the house where they took her. It is the house of Duke Rowan van Leerin!

I am aware of that, Father. Though, know that Satan is behind all the evil being committed throughout our world. You should be aware of it, as a priest. That night he took the form of two men. Strong and very evil men. They floated into her room through the window as two bats, black cloaks swirling around them as the wings of death! They took Raquel. They disrupted her lovely dream and plunged her into the hell of waking. She resisted. Blood was spilled. Rag doll fell down to be trampled by their heavy boots. Darkness is shrouding the innocent girl—she's praying to the Archangel Gabriel and all the Saints. Though her prayers fall on deaf ears. The men are taking her away—she's limp like a puppet on strings. The night city is quickly floating around them. The darkness is impenetrable. Then the sinners stop to quickly knock on a splendid door. A flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!

Glatzburg is literarily soaked with legends and stories, Father. And if not the city itself then its surroundings. The local people are clinging to legends and stories even more these days because they offer them at least some consolation and even hope. The Legend of Saint Orthenius is especially popular among the people. It says that in the times of the direst peril a new hero will rise from the people to defend the faith as once Saint Orthenius did. He is supposed to protect the Realm against all the enemies.

He will be readily recognized, Father, for he will wield a mighty relic called Inquisitor, a powerful weapon that helped Saint Orthenius to defeat the Erebornian pagans and to release the Filkland peninsula from their grip. That relic will shine with mighty light, blinding all enemies. A single command will make it decapitate all the enemies and strike the sinners with heavenly lightning bolts. At least so it is said in the legend circulating among the people.

Of course, Father. There some truth to all things. I am sure that the relic does exist. It is rumored that Orthenius hid it before he died and prophesized that it would be retrieved by his heir—the new protector of the Realm. Though the legend does not mention where it should be hidden.

Another mysterious scroll? You're keeping me busy alright, Father. Do you have any ideas what it should contain? I suppose that it will again be some dark prophecy about the end of the world... I'd not expect anything less from you.
So come when you have enough, Father.
Show me that root, Father... Oh my! It's a Radix Diaboli root, people call it Devil's Root! It's very rare and very magic. I can make you a rather powerful power-up potion of it.

But of course, Father! It's not very difficult to make magic potions using Devil's Root. The difficult part is to find some. It usually grows at rather dangerous places—hence the name. If you find a Devil's Root, I can make you a magic potion of it for a few gold coins.

Woe and despair befell me, a poor old woman! Hellish snares of death are binding me to the bosom of eternal damnation! That scroll is the purest evil, Father! I know, Father. I've not let a day pass without begging God for forgiveness since. I always believed that one day I could be able to redeem my sin somehow... I had no idea that it would happen in such a gruesome way!
Of course, Father. It will cost you $$getmoney1000$$ gp.
Just a moment, Father. Wait, please...
Here you are, Father. One miraculous potion. Do you want anything else?
Very well, Father. I'll make the potion at once. Just wait a moment...

But of course, Father. What do you need to know?

Revenants are those who have returned—people sometimes mistake them for zombies—they are undead monsters brought to our world to fulfill vengeance they swore to wreak upon someone while they lived. After they return they cannot be stopped or destroyed unless all their victims are dead. Then they descend back to the Underworld never to return.

Yes, in their essence they are immortal, noble lord. No weapon, no spell, no man, no animal can harm them. There's only one way to affect them—to sanctify their dead bodies. If somebody manages to sprinkle a revenant's body with holy water it should sunder all the ties between this world and the Underworld. It should remove his curse and return him to eternal rest. At least ancient tomes mention that. I've never heard somebody would manage to do it.
Be careful, noble lord. Revenants are particularly ill tempered—anybody standing between them and their prey is in mortal danger...
Oh my God... why are you asking me about such terrible things, noble lord?

Woe, noble lord! The visions of the Fallen Angels haunt me in my dreams these days... Surely it is not by chance that you're asking. The Archangel Gabriel himself came to me in my dream and prophesized terrible news. The judgment is at hand—the inevitable is coming. I fell upon my knees in my dream and then I saw the Earth crack open—infernal flames burst out revealing the three Fallen Angels—Arthamon, the ruler of despair and the cursed lord of fire; Baphomet, the demon of madness and the creator of chaos; and Cerdie, the lascivious mistress of fornication and of eternal sin. And the world was flooded with beasts and monsters dancing gruesome dance celebrating the end of the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. The fallen angels rose and the earth and the heavens trembled under the blast of their infernal powers. And then came despair and chaos and all the people were drown in eternal sin. The end of all things came. Kingdoms were crumbling, people were fornicating, murdering, dying... and the False Prophet was walking the Earth demonically laughing.

No... no, I don't think so, noble lord. In my visions, I don't always see what will really happen. Sometimes, their meaning is hidden. I'd think that those nightmares herald a great movement in the mechanism of the history of the world. It is just a grain of sand blown into my dreams from the endless desert of destiny. Something is going on and it surely has to do something with the Fallen Angels. I'm sure you know the Scripture, noble lord. In the Revelations of Saint Ezechiel there's exactly what I see in my dreams—the liberation of the Fallen Angels and their coming to this world which will end the millennium lasting Kingdom of God on Earth. I am absolutely sure that it is just what would happen if the Fallen Angels were to enter our world.
Do you really want to know, noble lord?
As you wish, noble lord, it's your decision...

Secular rule is insignificant, noble lord. It's just a passing affair—it comes and leaves as spring snow does. Well, but if you really want to know... the royal governor is Robert Heidrick, he has a Grand Ducal title I believe. His deputy is Rowan van Leerin, a proud bearer of a Ducal title.

If you're looking for weapons, armor and for other war-gear, noble lord, go visit the Armory of Hans von Drichtmaul. Potions and magic goods can be obtained either here or at the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. Then there are two shops with all kinds of goods run by the landlord Ludwig Weintraum and by the inkeeper Wanda Gielwitch. And if you're not interested in the origin of the goods, you can visit that rogue Alphonso DiCerbio.
It's clear, noble lord—there's no going back. We're halfway on the road to Hell. There's no going back from Hell. It's too late, the Judgment Day is at hand!
I don't know, noble lord. I don't know what it means. Something terrible is at hand—something inevitable. Woe shall plague all of us who have lived to witness these cruel and pitiless times.
I... I don't know, noble lord. Suddenly I saw it all before my eyes... the words were flowing like a river. I don't know, I'm sorry...

Oh yes, I can see it in your eyes, I can see it in your soul... the shadow of that scroll hinders your soul as a heavy boulder. It crushes you, it suffocates... You shall never get rid of it. Never! Though death gruesome indeed awaits the one who uncovers that what should have remained hidden, the one who brings to the light of our worlds the shadows of things meant to lay in darkness for eternity!

They were acting in the dark ages at the end of the Hundred Years War, that's in the tenth century. They were led by certain Lucius—he was a Dark Prophet and the High Priest of the cult. That was him who prophesized the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth and the release of Satan from his prison. He was preaching about the end of the Old World and about coming of a New Order—Its children were supposed to rule the enthralled souls of the righteous who were to be killed by sword and fire in the process. Although the cult infiltrated the highest social ranks of the Empire it met a gruesome end. All the cultists—including Lucius—were executed. Burnt. And that was their end. Well, but it seems now that it wasn't quite true. What did you discover, noble lord? Why are you looking for that cult? That scroll I translated mentioned summoning of the Fallen Angels. Whose scroll was it? How did it come into your possession?

My safety was jeopardized the moment you entered my house for the first time. I told you then to leave and to leave me alone, but you just had to look into the face of death. Though it's your choice—leave your answers to yourself. I can knit together many a thing even without them. And to be honest with you, I'm not going to sleep well after your visit. You are indeed deep in troubles, noble lord. There's no other way left than that running forward—you have to get to the point where it ends and drink the wormwood potion of fate to the last drop. I wish you good luck, though I have a feeling that luck has nothing to do with your mission.

Those are no riddles, noble lord. It's the reality. It's not my fault that you see no meaning in my words. Maybe the time will show... maybe the time will prove me right. And maybe not. It is yet to be seen.

There's a black shadow clouding the murder of Bishop Trevorius, noble lord. The shadow of betrayal, hypocrisy and of deceit. You are indeed deep in troubles, noble lord. Avoid mistakes, for they may cost you life. The murder stirred the motionless surface of a deep dark pool having a deadly mire at the bottom. The one who sinks into it shall not come back.

What exactly do you want me to tell you about Father Frederick, noble lord? It was an aged man who came to Glatzburg several years ago. Even then Grim Reaper was following in his wake, though he took him only during the plague two years ago. I think that he went peacefully—he must have been tired by the sins of this world. No longer could he stand against the evil—he was too old and broken. No wonder after all those trials he had to suffer...

He was a highly regarded exorcist, noble lord. A demonbane, if you want. He encountered good many soul devouring demons in his life. He was able not only to face them, but also to defeat them. He was able to banish them from the body of a possessed and to send them to burning hell whence they came. I admired him greatly. It's a pity he was not inclined to tell about his vast experience—I'd have loved to learn more about demonology. But such is our fate—as soon as you find a treasure somebody snatches it away and spits into your face.
I don't know, noble lord. But if I were you I'd heed my advise!

I... I know what happened to Raquel Gielwitch, noble lord. I had a vision... I saw her slumbering. In the house of her sister. She looked so innocent... almost a child. She was sleeping with a rag doll in her bosom. So silent and beautiful. Then came Satan...

Yes, noble lord, exactly. Satan is behind all evil deeds! That night he took the form of two men. Strong and very evil men. They floated into her room through the window as two bats, black cloaks swirling around them as the wings of death! They took Raquel. They disrupted her lovely dream and plunged her into the hell of waking. She resisted. Blood was spilled. Rag doll fell down to be trampled by their heavy boots. Darkness is shrouding the innocent girl—she's praying to the Archangel Gabriel and all the Saints. Though her prayers fall on deaf ears. The men are taking her away—she's limp like a puppet on strings. The night city is quickly floating around them. The darkness is impenetrable. Then the sinners stop to quickly knock on a splendid door. A flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!
No, noble lord. I did not. But I do know the house where they took her. It is the house of Duke Rowan van Leerin!

I am well aware of that, noble lord. Though, know that Satan is behind all the evil being committed throughout our world. You should be aware of it, as a true faithful. Then the sinners stop to knock hastily on a splendid door. The flame of a candle illuminates the entrance and a ghost appears to let them in. The innocent virgin is once again shrouded in darkness. Never to return!

I'd like to ask for your help, Master Alchemist. A certain pagan spell is concerned; or better to say its side effects...

Have I heard correctly? Did you experiment with pagan spells, knight? I thought such procedures were forbidden by the Inquisition... Well, what happened? What spell was it? And how did you come to know it?

Well, the spell does not concern me, but Grand Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. She asked me to get her some magic ingredients which she needed for a pagan spell which should have given her proverbial freshness, beauty and vigor of Elenians... Nonetheless, something went wrong and she became a hideous hag.
I wonder why she even tried something that foolish. Elenian magic is unattainable for us... well, we don't know much about it. What ingredients were it?
A Betheal Temporarum blossom, a Sun crystal and some troll bile. I acquired everything for her and still the spell misfired...
You have managed to get the flower of Trollus Bilealius!? Congratulations! Troll Bile is a very rare herb, even I hear about it only once or twice in dozens of years...
No, you don't understand—it was real troll bile. From a dead troll.

Are you trying to tell me that the Grand Duchess used bile from a dead troll in her spell?! No wonder then that the spell misfired—bile from dead trolls is used in neither spells nor in alchemical experiments. It's a harmful substance without any real use. Obviously, it was a mistake. The Grand Duchess thought she needed real troll bile, but instead she needed Trollus Bilealius—the herb.
Hmm... yes, that's possible. Do you think you would be able to remove the spell from her?

I could try. It is necessary to make a reconstruction of the spell; nevertheless with the original substances. I have both the Betheal Temporarum blossom and the Sun crystal, but I don't have any troll bile—and I mean Trollus Bilealius. It grows in the shadow of Wolfsburg and that's very dangerous place. If you bring me some, I could be able to distill substance which turned the Grand Duchess into the hag.
I understand. I'll look around for the herb. Thank you.
I found this very strange mineral, Master Alchemist. Do you happen to know what it could be?
Let me take a look at it, knight... But of course, it's a philosopher's stone!
What is philosopher's stone?

It's how people call Astratus Lungis—it's a very rare mineral. It has not been discovered yet how the mineral originated, nevertheless it's extremely magical. If you're skilled, at least a little bit, you can transmute it into any metal—gold is of course the most popular choice, though smiths don't hesitate to use the mineral when forging weapons and armor. If you'd like me to, I could transmute any piece of philosopher's stone you bring me into gold—of course for a little commission.
Would you be able to process philosopher's stone if somebody brought you some?
Of course I'd be able to process philosopher's stone, knight. If you bring me a piece of it I can transmute it into gold. For a little commission, of course...

As a scientist I'm trying to look at the current situation of the Realm through empirical eyes, knight. I'm trying to objectively asses the facts and conclude logical inferences which could be handled and utilized.
Great. What have you discovered?

I've discovered that our situation is not very good, knight. Too much Power has been unleashed and thus the situation cannot be unimportant. To tell the truth, I'm surprised that the Realm hasn't crumbled down yet. Nonetheless, until recently many people in Alvaron did not believe that the Realm could be in such a dire situation as was rumored in other places. Though after the murder of King Edward II the situation changed and the city has been in the state of nervous anticipation since.
Do you think it's possible to solve it somehow?

Well... you tell me, knight. You're a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous and the vocation of your order is to change the course of events, right? Though personally I think that not everything is lost yet and that a miracle or two could put the things back into order...

No, knight, I don't remember any fierce storm with unnatural aspects to it. According to some theories big storms are accompanied with great Power discharges, thus it's quite possible that strange things might happen. Nonetheless I don't remember anything unusual happening lately.

I doubt that I'd be able to tell you about the Fallen Angels more than you already know... According to the Scripture they are former angels who were stricken down from the Heaven together with Satan for the crimes they had committed. There are four of them—Arthamon, the Lord of Despair, Baphomet, the Ruler of Chaos, Cerdie, the Vile Succubus, and the Archangel Azrael, the advocate of Evil and the first of Satan's emissaries. To tell you the truth, some of my colleagues perceive the Fallen Angels rather metaphorically as personifications of the negative aspects of the Power, although one might consider such a teaching modern and plausible, I must stress that I'd refrain from adhering to it as it borders on heresy.

To be honest, I'd rather not answer this question. Perhaps the worst event that has happened recently was the murder of His Highness King Edward II. Can you imagine how dreadful it is, knight? The leader of the Realm murdered—straight in the chambers of the Royal Palace—amidst all those servants and guards! Nobody knows neither why he was murdered nor who was his murderer. A tragedy! I can't predict what will happen to the Royal Alchemist Guild when its patron and protector is gone. It might very well happen that after a new King is elected by the Counsel of Lords we would be dismissed or even arrested as some lowly heretics...
I am investigating the case of the paladin Richwald d'Blazier's murder. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Yes, I've heard that paladin Richwald d'Blazier was murdered. Supposedly he was turned into stone. To be honest with you, knight, transubstantiation of living matter into stone is an unattainable phenomenon in alchemy. Some unclean sorcery had to be involved!

To get a testimony from a dead person? I'm afraid that I'm not able to help you with that. Alchemy can't do anything like that, knight. Nevertheless, I must admit that I've heard some rumors about heretics who might be able to use dark forbidden rituals to contact the Netherworld and to commune with dead. And even to bring them back to our world! Well, anyway, I'm sure that it is a one way trip to a scaffold, regardless how noble your intentions may be...

To tell you the truth, knight, the issue of improving memory by the means of magic potions has always been quite a challenge for me. I've already spent several years studying it, unfortunately I must admit that I've not achieved any tangible results so far. Nevertheless, it is possible that one day I'll discover something...
I'm looking for a way to remove a stryx curse. Would you offer a piece of advice?

Well, knight, removing a stryx curse is a rather spiritual problem—not alchemical. Alchemy deals with the material aspect of the Power, not with its immaterial component. That's why I'm sorry to say that I must disappoint you.
I'm trying to find out how I could remove the curse from the mansion of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. Could you help me with it?

The cursed mansion of Baron von Blutenreich has been an ulcer on the face of the city since time immemorial. It's rumored that it's haunted by Baron's ghost who kills anybody who steps through the door. Anyway, anybody who went searching the house for Baron's legendary treasure didn't come back. And in the dead of night truly sinister sounds can be heard from there. Nonetheless, I have no idea how to cleanse the house of the presence of evil spirits. It might be good to find out the cause of the curse and try to remove it...
I'm investigating the case of fake gold. It seems that some heretics are able to temporarily turn human excrements into gold. Do you happen to have any information regarding the case?

I must admit, knight, that although it's a heinous crime I must admire those forgers. They succeeded in the task entire generations of alchemists have been vainly trying to succeed in—that means to transmute any substance into gold. The fact that the wicked criminal succeeded, though temporarily, in utilizing human excrement in the process just emphasizes the talent he has been given. Unfortunately, I don't know any details that might help you apprehend him. I'm sorry.

There are certain indications in folk rumors that some of those afflicted by lycantrophy were cured by drinking a potion containing certain herb called wolfbane among the people. Well, I don't believe much in those rumors. No herbal extract can prevent the immaterial aspect of the Power from manifesting. After all, lycantrophy is just a type of a curse.
I suggest you answer my question, master alchemist. You're an educated man, so you must know what could happen to you if you resist to cooperate with me...
I sincerely urge you to answer my question, Master Alchemist. I'm sure you can see yourself that there's no reason to deny to answer.
You're renowned for your wisdom, Master Alchemist. It would be quite an honor for me if you could answer my question.
No, I'm sorry, knight. I've not met any man of that name.
I understand. No problem. I'll just have to keep looking for him. Nevertheless, allow me, please, to ask for your help in a certain matter which has been causing me quite some distress lately...

It concerns a certain scroll which I acquired thanks to a lucky coincidence. During one of my trips outside the city I managed to find ruins of an ancient temple and this scroll was there. It's very old and I myself would date it into the times of the ancient Elenian Empire. Nonetheless, it's not written in moon runic script which the Elenians used, but in some other script which is absolutely unknown to me. It seems to me as a code or some secret language. It led me to a conclusion that the scroll must contain a magic formula or a magic potion recipe which the author intended to be protected from being comprehended by any unauthorized reader.
Why do you need him? What happened that he left?

Well, it's a mystery of sorts, knight. Theil Brechthold used to be a very ambitious man, totally absorbed in his work. He had unbelievable results. It seemed that he was born for alchemy. Nonetheless, a few years back he resigned from his position of the Master of the Royal Alchemist Guild and disappeared somewhere. Nobody has heard about him since. There are rumors that he has been seen in the Northern parts of the Realm, but nobody has been able to confirm them personally. All that unfinished work he has left behind... Well, that's why I need to find him and try to persuade him to return no matter the cost. Haven't you, by any chance, met him?
I've met a man of that name in Hillbrandt, Master Alchemist.

Really? That's great news, knight! I was starting to despair. I thought he went abroad... I'd need to discuss so many of his discoveries he left us here—nobody can understand them. Very well, I can help you. I'll give Theil Brechthold your best regards.

I am sorry but I don't have time for such a long journey. I'm sorry.

Very well, I'll help you to decipher the scroll. The Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt of Glatzburg is most proficient in those matters...
Thank you, knight. If you manage to decipher it I'll make sure to repay you splendidly.
Could I now finally ask those questions?
Could I take a look at your wares, Master Alchemist?
Of course, knight. You can buy whatever you need...
Goodbye for now.

And I thought that I'm standing on the threshold of colossal discoveries that would make Theil Brechthold green with envy...
Pride comes before the fall, Master Alchemist. Well, don't be low, your days aren't over yet.

You're welcome, knight. Could I do something for you for that?

Oh, you mean a reward, don't you? But of course, noble lord. If you'll give my regards to master Brechthold, I'll be glad to compensate for your troubles by a pouch of gold and by a magic item. There's absolutely no problem with that!

Of course, noble lord. But first let me ask you for a favor. It concerns a certain scroll which I acquired thanks to a lucky coincidence. During one of my trips outside the city I managed to find ruins of an ancient temple and this scroll was there. It's very old and I myself would date it into the times of the ancient Elenian Empire. Nonetheless, it's not written in moon runic script which the Elenians used, but in some other script which is absolutely unknown to me. It seems to me as a code or some secret language. It led me to a conclusion that the scroll must contain a magic formula or a magic potion recipe which the author intended to be protected from being comprehended by any unauthorized reader.

You're absolutely correct, noble lord. Maybe you know someone skilled in secret languages who could help me in this matter... Anyway I'd like to ask you to treat the scroll carefully and to show it only to reliable people. It contains a secret which must not fall into wrong hands. Moreover, I have a feeling that there's somebody else trying to get it. Since I got it I've had a feeling that I'm being followed...
Thank you, noble lord. If you manage to decipher it I'll make sure to repay you splendidly.
Of course, noble lord. You can buy whatever you need...

You're absolutely correct, noble lord. The very day I brought the scroll home I heard somebody stalking under my windows trying to glimpse inside my rooms. Maybe it was just a coincidence or my paranoia, but one can never be careful enough, right?
I see, noble lord. I'm sorry for bothering you with that.

Pity. Well, I can't blame you. I'll spread the word to the other members of the Royal Alchemist Guild. Thank you, noble lord. Take this pouch of gold and this magic item as an expression of my gratitude.
You're welcome, noble lord—in fact it's me who should thank you. Well, anyway, tell me if there's anything I could do for you.
You're welcome, noble lord. I'm myself curious if it'll work. Is there anything else I could help you with?
As you wish, noble lord. There's nothing mightier than a big chest full of gold, right? Please, just a small moment...

That's no ordinary stone, noble lord—just to the contrary. It's an extremely precious substance which is renowned for its ability to be turned into almost any other unliving substance. The only limitation is to find new substances to turn it into. Well... it's finished, noble lord. Here's your gold. If you wouldn't object, I'd just take my share as a reward.
Greetings, noble lord. I've not seen you around yet. I think you're not one of the locals, right?

The pleasure's mine, noble lord. Nevertheless, back to that matter I wanted to ask you about. The fact that you're not one of the locals inspires a hope in me that you travel throughout the Realm—even in these difficult times. Am I right?

I'm really flattered by your interest, noble lord. I'll be glad to tell you about it. A Guild Master is the head of each Guild—whether it's a royal guild or not. He represents his guild and is its supreme representative, he acts on its behalf and supervises the proper performance of the craft, which is carried out by journeymen, apprentices and trainees. My position is even more renowned, because our guild is royal and thus privileged, hence it has many exclusive rights—but it also has certain duties. It's a great responsibility, you can believe me that!
Greetings, noble lord. Can I ask you if you've already deciphered and brought me the scroll I lent you?

Really? That's splendid, noble lord! I'm sure that it will help us to make great discoveries in the field of alchemy! That it will allow us to unveil some of the secrets of Elenian mages and will reveal a bit of the mystery shrouding the Elenian civilization. Entire generations will be learning from my discoveries...

Thank you, noble lord. Maybe you're right... there is still a chance that I'll get my hands on a REAL treasure—being represented by an ancient Elenian formula. Here's the promised reward. I'm sorry to have drawn you into that.
You're welcome, noble lord. Could I do something for you for that?
Greetings, noble lord. Thank you once more for your help with that mysterious scroll. I'm sorry that it all was just one big hoax. What can I do for you to repay you?
Greetings, noble lord. How is it going? Is there anything else I could help you with?
You bastard! Burn in hell... Whhrrraaaauuuu...

Thanks, knight. I'd have never thought that a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous would save my life... For that I'm gonna tell you where's the treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn. I'm sure you've heard 'bout him, he was mighty rich and a scrooge, too. He used to collect treasures like any other man, but unlike others he did not hesitate to murder, cheat and commit any sin an experienced devil would be ashamed of. But as they say there's a butcher waiting for every swine, so he was finally convicted and executed. Well, the point is that before he died he managed to bury the treasure at a secret place in Schwarzwald. It's under an ancient oak split by the lightning in two—not far from here. Just roll aside the boulder under it and the treasure's all yours.
If you knew where the treasure was hidden why didn't you claim it?!
Well, knight, what would I do with it?! Rest assured that it'd be of no use to me. You don't think that I could just walk to a city and buy something for it, do you?!
No problem, knight. I thank you—if it were not for you I would have died in this bush as a filthy dog. I'd better be going—would hate to meet those bloody paladins...
Farewell. Be more careful next time.
Not so fast, hellspawn. I've decided to end your miserable life which offends God himself!
What?! A betrayal?! You bastard! Burn in hell... Whhrrraaaauuuu...

What are you waiting for, knight? Finish me... Perform God's will! Thrust your sword into my bowels and burn my body! That's exactly you've been chosen to do, haven't you? It's so easy to finish a wounded hellspawn crawling to get to the safety of his den. Come one, kill Kenthwaar the Messenger of Death—don't hesitate and strike!
Yes, you're right—God cannot abide a monstrosity such as you to walk the face of Earth!
What has happened to you, godless hellspawn? How did you get your wounds?

Knights of the Brotherhood of the Righteous ambushed me. May god Urr strike them down with his lightning so I could feast on their flesh. They were on my tail like a pack of hounds smelling blood—they almost killed me. I survived only thanks to Urr's help... but my wounds are too serious. I can't make it back to my den... I need to be healed... to lick my wounds. Otherwise I'm gonna die as a filthy dog!
I will help you. What do you need me to do? To get you some healing potions?

You would help a hellspawn, knight?! I can't believe that... well, I'm not in a situation where I could afford to be choosy, right? Very well, if it's really so, I'd need a Potion of Cure Disease and a Potion of Healing...
It's your lucky day, I have both potions on me. Here you go.
Very well, I'll bring you the potions.
If it's really so you better hurry, knight. I'm on my death bed here and, moreover, those knights of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are wandering throughout the forest...
Maybe I could help you. What would be in it for me?
I'd tell you where to find the treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn. It's a rather good offer considering all the treasures the Baron acquired during his filthy life...
My brothers were doing the right thing when they were trying to take your life. I'll finish their righteous work!
Hard luck—I've promised paladin Gerhard de Blanc that I'll find you and that I'll finish his righteous work!
Are you bringing me the potions, knight? I'm at Death's door and the paladins are at my heels...
Yes, I have the potions. Take them.
No, I've not acquired the potions yet.
You damn better hurry up, knight...
I've changed my mind and I'm going to send you to Hell where you belong!
What?! A betrayal?! You bastard! Burn in hell, you scab... Whhrrraaaauuuu...
Filthy thief! Get lost! Do you hear me? Get lost!

Why such a restriction?
Only those authorized by Cardinal Truncquillius himself may enter the heart of the archdiocesan dungeons. You're not one of them. I'm sorry...
Very well... farewell.
Cardinal Truncquillius is accused of severe crimes. I'm here to arrest him. Let me enter!
I'm sorry, but I'm not obliged to accept orders from you. I'm subordinated exclusively to Cardinal Truncquillius!
Then I'll have to enter using force!
