Get your dirty hands off, sir. Can you hear me?! Once more you try to steal something from me and I promise you I'll introduce a ten-inch steel blade to your guts! And don't think that your nobility won't let me do that, holy shit!
I'll help you to find your amulet.
Oh, really? In that case you would pay a part of the debt your people owe to the noble race of Elenians. All right, go and bring me my necklace, human!
I was able to get your necklace by chance. Here it is.

You bring me back my amulet? By the Gods... it really is the right one. At last I can return back to the land of shadows for eternal oblivion. Thank you, human. You've rendered a service to a member of the long dead race and your deeds won't ever be forgotten! The Gods of Al'Bienth can see them... But I won't let you leave empty-handed, take this item as an expression of my gratefulness. And now... Ael'Esther Niamiseal!
Farewell, wandering soul.
If I return the necklace to you, what reward will I get?
I'll let you live.
I'm afraid I can't let you stay in this world a moment longer. Your presence here is an offense to God himself...
In that case you will die as well as the thieves, who brought me to this world!
My necklace... where is it?! They stole it from me... Awful thieves... Awful people! Let the Gods of Al'Bienth come out from their graves and sweep that trash off the surface of the Earth!
Who are you, godless creature?
I'm En'Lenius, Grand Duke of Gnom'Ethers gilliad, the patron of Hu'Chien sanctuary and the guardian of The'Brieaes flame.
And what do you seek in this place? There's no place here for those who have returned from the Other World...

I know that well, human. But remember it was not my intention to return from the land of shadows to this world from where my people were banished by your poor race millennia ago. I returned because the dirty hands of human thieves stole my precious amulet Zun'Triam. A terrible deed of those people whipped me out of sweet dreaming and non-existence in the land of shadows and brought me back here. Without my amulet, I can't return to the land of shadows. I must have it, at all costs!
That sounds exotic... and very ancient. What civilization do you belong to?

I belong to the noble race of Elenians. I belong to a nation that was exterminated by your ancestors as soon as they arose from the barbarism. I belong to the race building beautiful cities at the time when the human breed lived in caves with other animals. But all of that belongs to the past. Now the Elenians dwell in the land of shadows, where they indulge in a sweet—and merciful—sleep and dreaming. And I want to return there!
I won't let such an awful pagan creature like you walk this world!

It's you people who is the trash that must be swept from the face of Ael'Kaela, Mother Earth! You slaughtered our people millennia ago and banished us to the land of shadows, but even there you won't let us rest in peace. Your greed forces you to disturb the peace of the dead and capture their property, like the scavengers seize a dead body! Daeph'Ethel Mi'Proclits Fanae!
I exorcise you, you awful memory of ancient times, return back to Hell from where you came to us!
Who disturbed your peace, wandering soul?

Who? The awful thieves, that's what I say. Their dirty greedy hands seized the thing that kept my soul in peace and quiet. My magic amulet Zun'Triam, my treasure, the light of my life, the well of my knowledge. I want it back, because I can't sleep comfortably without it in the land of shadows. I must have it back, because it's mine!
Do you bring me my amulet, human? I hate this world... there's nothing for me to seek here but my amulet. I want to go away from here, but I can't leave without my amulet!
I really brought you your amulet. Here you are.

Excellent! At last I can return back to the land of shadows for the eternal oblivion. Thank you, human. You've rendered a service to a member of the long dead race and your deeds won't be forgotten forever! The Gods of Al'Bienth can see them... But I won't let you leave empty-handed, take this item as an expression of my gratitude. And now... Ael'Esther Niamiseal!
I'm sorry, but I haven't brought your amulet yet.
In that case you'd better hurry, human. The thieves must he punished for what they've done!
I've changed my mind—I decided to free the world of your presence by the means of sheer force.
In that case you will suffer the same punishment as those who violated my grave—death!

Well... you say you need the testimony of a person that is no longer alive? That's a serious issue, son. Very serious. You can cross the border of feasibility, you know. The end justifies the means, indeed, but this is the way to perdition. As the First Prophet said—what is dead, should rest in the grave forever!
So there is some way to do it?

Yes, there is. Maybe you've already heard about the heretics who were unable to resist the temptation to talk to the dead. The thirst for the knowledge of the dead—knowledge long forgotten and very valuable—brought many renowned scholars and sages to the edge of faith. Just remember the case of doctor Gregoriades who longed for the invention of an almighty cure so much that he sold his soul to Satan and gained the ability to talk to the dead. However most of the attempts to establish contact with the Other World ended tragically or were a complete failure. The Other World can't easily be made to do what one desires.
But there is a way, isn't there?

Yes, there is one way that was found and described. One excommunicated cleric did so, a man named Martinicus—what a big sorrow for the Holy Mother Church. He found a way how to establish contact with the Other World and how to talk to the dead. Unfortunately his mistake was revealed and further developed by a heretic author of the book Libre Necronomicon who exploited and elaborated the ways of communication with the Other World even further—in the most terrible way, of course. And this book—Libre Necronomicon—could help you, son. You could study it and find out what to do to make the Other World give out its testimony. Nevertheless you should realize that even thinking about the use of Libre Necronomicon is a wicked heresy and thus you're committing a crime you should fight yourself!
Do you happen to know where could I get either the book or a copy of it?

I don't have the slightest idea, son. If I had, I'd have proceeded a long time ago and I would have that book burnt. But it's true that during my stay in the office of the judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition I've heard some suspicions several times that one copy of that wicked book could be located in Alvaron or somewhere around. But I firmly believe it was nothing but lies.
To tell the truth, Your Excellency, I've already found the book.

Oh, really? That must be a Satan's plot and nothing else! Be very careful when dealing with that book, son. I'm afraid for your soul. Nevertheless, if you could succeed... Well, heed the voice of conscience. You could make yourself believe that you're to perform a task given to you by God, although it could easily lead you to your damnation.
Not at all, son. It's not exactly the service I'd like to do for you, but only God can judge our deeds...
You're right, Your Excellency. I'd rather not do that.

Wait, son. I didn't want to discourage you from taking this course of actions—I just wanted to warn you. The decision you will make in this matter will be only yours so you should know what could happen to you and what you risk...
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to talk to you about that, son!

I'd like to ask you for your opinion, Your Excellency. During my investigation I've run into the proof according to which the Inquisitor General, Cardinal Commendoni, could be also involved in the plot of the Cult of the Children of the New Order. And worse—he could even be their High Priest! What should I do?

Cardinal Commendoni? Oh my God... it's a terrible suspicion! Good Heavens save us if it's found to be true! All the power of the entire Inquisition is concentrated in the hands of Cardinal Commendoni. It's nearly impossible to accuse him of heresy—the other members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition would have to agree with it—that is me, Cardinal Severtinus and Cardinal Giovanni Timore.
But what shall I do? Should I investigate the suspicion or refuse it? The proof could be fake...

Yes, it's true. Nothing and nobody can be trusted. But just because of that I'd verify the suspicion and would find out whether it's true or not. And in the case it's true... I'd adopt appropriate measures to accuse Cardinal Commendoni of heresy and of conspiracy against God and the King!
I've found three affirmative proofs against Cardinal Commendoni, Your Excellency. What do you suggest I do next?

So the suspicion regarding the Inquisitor General was really found to be true. I grieve for that a lot, son. Not that I was afflicted by your results, but because it's another proof of how rotten the Holy Office, to which I myself serve, is. But there's nothing to grieve for—the evil must be uprooted no matter in what soil it grows. Thus we must accuse the Inquisitor General of heresy. We need to get the approval of the other members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. I give you my approval of course. Now go and try to get the approval of Cardinal Severtinus and of Cardinal Giovanni Timore.

I tried to convince the other members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition to accuse Cardinal Commendoni of heresy and I failed, Your Excellency. How should I proceed? I can't arrest the Inquisitor General without their approval...

Well... it's as I've feared. I've had a suspicion for some time already that the Cardinals Timore and Severtinus haven't been acting to the best of their knowledge and ability and now I'm sure about it. No doubt they were corrupted by the Cult of the Children of the New Order—otherwise they wouldn't hesitate so much to approve the accusation of Commendoni. But we must break it. I've known both Cardinals long enough to know how we could circumvent them!
What do you suggest?

We'll have to commit a sin, son. You must make them cooperate by threatening them. Blackmailing is what I mean. You must make them feel you know absolutely everything about them and that you wouldn't hesitate to reveal their secrets if they wouldn't come to terms. They will surely give up. They must. There isn't any other way. We're lost without their approval!
I killed Cardinal Commendoni, Your Excellency. He refused to be arrested, opposed me and defended himself to the very end...

Oh my God... I'm sorry about that, son! How could I know it would end up like that? Cardinal Commendoni lost the chance to be purged of his sins and his soul will be damned forever... What a terrible fate for a man! Nevertheless, tell me, did he confess all the sins we suspected him of before he died?

Yes, he confessed everything. And he also confirmed that all the three Fallen Angels were invoked and that they dwell in the realms of Earth now, preparing the release of Satan from his thousand-year imprisonment...

Good Heavens... I was afraid of that! I don't know how this could be possible, but if it's really true... Did you manage to get any details from Cardinal Commendoni that could either confirm or disprove his statement? Anything...
He told me that the Kingdoms of the Fallen Angels on Earth can be entered only by the means of a ritual described in the book Libre Daemonium, written by Lucius, the Prophet of the Cult.

Well... in that case we must get that book, son. I don't see any other way than to try to enter the Kingdoms of the Fallen Angels on Earth with the help of that infernal book and prove this way whether the Fallen Angels were really summoned or not. And if they were, then...

...then we're all in the hands of God, son! But I'm convinced they weren't. For if they were it would mean the threat for the balance of God's Kingdom on Earth and that's unthinkable! Thus, we must gain that infernal book!
But how could we get it? Commendoni told me he had hidden it somewhere...

I believe he hid it among his possessions. Surely he didn't hide it in some place far away—it would be of no use to him there. He had to hide it in the Archbishop's palace. Thus I suggest you ask the Archbishop Laurencius to let you look through the Cardinal's possessions. It's the only way to get to them.
All right, I'll try to do it.
Excellent, son. God bless you for all you've been doing in His name!
Tell me, Your Excellency, who will be the acting Inquisitor General now?

You see, I've nearly forgotten about that... I'll be the acting Inquisitor General till a new Inquisitor General is appointed—that's because I'm the oldest judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition.
Well, that's what I've thought...
Excuse me, did you say something, son?
Oh, no...
I see... it just seemed to me like you did.

As you wish, son. I hope you're prepared well enough. I won't hide from you that a very difficult tasks is ahead of you—that is, to find out and to prove guilty the murderer of His Majesty King Edward the Second. If you succeed—and if you also pass the theoretical part of the exam—I'll name you a Curial Inquisitor personally.
Do you know any details about the circumstances of His Majesty's death?

I'm afraid I do, son. That is, I know the murderer's name. He's a long-time friend of mine and he was my good companion in many difficult times. I even know the incentives that made him do what he did—and unfortunately I must say I agree with them.
How is it possible you know the murderer's name? And why do you assign me the mission to prove him guilty when you could do it on your own?

There's nothing I can do in this matter, son. That is, I'm bound by the confessional secret—the murderer of His Majesty confessed to me and asked me for absolution. I couldn't do it, but I promised him I wouldn't do anything against him personally. I've been waiting for someone to deal with the case of the murder of His Majesty. And here you are. I want to tell you the truth, although I know I'll break the sacrament of the confessional secret because of that.
I'm listening, Your Excellency.

Well... The murderer of His Majesty is the First Knight Don Rodrigo de Velacor. He committed the murder for the reason I don't want to tell you, but if you are able to urge Rodrigo to confess, I'm sure he will tell you about his reasons. He committed the murder in affect, although it doesn't lessen his guilt anyhow. It saddens me, but there's nothing I can do—murder is still murder, although his incentives were exalted.
Not at all, son. I wish you were able to fulfill this quest—it's a crime that MUSTN'T be left unpunished—no matter the cost, no matter who the murderer is!
I was able to prove Rodrigo de Velacor guilty of the murder of His Majesty Edward the Second, Your Excellency. Can I show you the results of my investigation?

Oh my God... so you really accomplished it? Poor Don Rodrigo... I'm so sorry about what happened. But there's nothing we can do—murder is still murder! Tell me about the results of your investigation then. What proof have you find against Don Rodrigo de Velacor?

And do you think you are prepared? Remember that the knowledge of Law is absolutely necessary for a Curial Inquisitor of the Holy Office. Without the knowledge you won't be able to fulfill your mission right and you would be not an asset, but a burden to the Holy Inquisition. Can we start?
Ita, Vestre Excellentissime Vire, paror. Yes, Your Excellency, I'm ready.
Because of the fact that you're the acting Inquisitor General at the time I'd like you to let me finish fulfilling the quest on the basis of which I could be named a Curial Inquisitor.

So, you're thinking about a curial post, son. That does you credit. Nevertheless the positions of a Curial Inquisitors must be occupied by the most competent judges of the Holy Office, son. Do you believe you belong to them?
In that case tell me, what quest my predecessor gave to you. What crime should you have revealed?
I was charged with revealing and proving guilty the murderer of King Edward the Second.

Oh... so this is how the things are. Convicting poor Don Rodrigo de Velacor should bring you the post of Curial Inquisitor? What a dramatic irony of fate... But we're all in the hands of God. So tell me what proof have you found against Don Rodrigo de Velacor?
Because of the fact you're the acting Inquisitor General at the time I'd like you to let me finish the tests for the position of a Curial Inquisitor, Your Excellency.
Because of the fact you're the acting Inquisitor General at the moment I'd like you to let me repeat the tests for the position of a Curial Inquisitor, Your Excellency.

Do you think you are well prepared? Remember that the knowledge of Law is absolutely necessary for a Curial Inquisitor of the Holy Office. Without the knowledge you won't be able to fulfill your mission right and you would be not an asset, but a burden to the Holy Inquisition. Can we start?
I'm looking for the murderer of His Majesty King Edward the Second. Do you happen to know any details about this crime?

I'll be frank with you, son. For a long time I've been considering what I should do about this case and in the end I couldn't do anything else but reveal to you a terrible secret. That is, I know the murderer's name. He's a long-time friend of mine and he was my good companion in many difficult times. I even know the incentives that made him do what he did—and unfortunately I must say I agree with them. However, he is still a murderer!
How is it possible you know the murderer's name? And why haven't you moved against him yet?

Well... The murderer of His Majesty is the First Knight Don Rodrigo de Velacor. He committed the murder for reasons I don't want to tell you, but if you are able to urge Rodrigo to confess, I'm sure he will tell you about his reasons. He committed the murder in affect, although it doesn't lessen his guilt anyhow. It saddens me, but there's nothing I can do—murder is still murder, although his incentives were exalted.
Thank you, Your Excellency. I know this had to be hard for you.

That's a very hard question, son. Were it not for the Scourges of God and all those other unhappy events, I'd rather say this entire crisis is only a power struggle. Nevertheless the plans of the Cult of the Children of the New Order aim too high. Combined with those Scourges of God... I'm really scared there could be the End of the World coming! Thus, we must do our best to stop the Cult of the Children of the New Order. The roots of evil must be destroyed!
I've heard some rumors that war is going to start. Do you know anything about it?

I know what you have in mind—horses and draft animals are requisitioned, granaries are filled, new recruits are gathered... It seems that the soldiers will be drawn to the field soon. You ask the same question as the others—where's the enemy to fight the war against? That is, there isn't the slightest indication of an apparent enemy threatening the Realm; no army which would strive to defeat ours. Despite all of that I assure you the danger is very real!
How do you know about that? Who is endangering the Realm? Who's going to lead an army against us?

No, don't ask me how do I know and don't urge me to tell you more. But there's one thing I can tell you: Whether there will be a war or not depends a lot also on the results of our efforts. Thus let's not waste any time and try to reveal the heretics leading our land to the edge of total perdition as soon as possible!

I don't remember any really wild storm over Alvaron lately. It's true that sometimes winds bring really bad weather from the coast, and there are things seen and heard that puts fear into a man, but nothing of that kind has happened lately.
What can you tell me about the Fallen Angels?

The Fallen Angels are the most terrible servants of the Dark Prince, the ruler of Hell. They're former Angels that were cast down by the wrath of God for their sins, because they plotted betrayal together with Satan the Tempter against God Almighty. The Scriptures said they were thrown down from the sky and chained in Hell to suffer there for their sins. They've been trying to get out of there since, to be able to rule both the world and the sky again. Together there are four: Arthamon, the Master of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Wanton Succubus and Fornicatress and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, Satan's Emissary, the Advocate of the Evil. Whole regiments of lower demons, imps, tempters, devils and other hellspawns serve them, being sent to our world to harm and seduce wherever they come.
Do you suspect anyone of heresy, Your Excellency?

We've already talked about Jean de Guise, the seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, son. I must express again my sorrow about the matter—the situation his treachery led us into and the fact that so many people perished because of his betrayal are grave indeed. I hope we will be able to judge the heretic as soon as possible and at least partly rectify the damage he committed!

Not long ago it was found out that the Cult of Pagan Night appeared here in Alvaron and—according to the results of the actual investigation—it's been striving to return paganism and the ancient Elenian Gods. They have dozens of terrible crimes on their conscience and it seems they committed them to get surviving Elenian texts. Probably the cult is looking for a particular document and we know nothing about its content. Despite the intensive effort of our curia we haven't succeed in catching and judging any member of this cult yet.

To tell the truth, the cure for lycantrophy is beyond my abilities. It's a disease that attacks not the body but the soul of the infected person; and it is resistant to all healing spells, blessings and sacraments. People say that there's a plant called Wolfbane and that the tea from this plant can help infected people. Nevertheless I think Thelma Ulthraum the apothecary would know more about that. I've never seen such a plant.

A stryx, you say? Well... Try asking Thelma Ulthraum the apothecary—she's the most informed about things like that. I could only advise you to kill the stryx without mercy and leave her soul to our Lord God, but obviously it isn't what you want to hear from me...

I fear for brother Nicolas, son. Although I believe him, the statement of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert can't be impeached without good reason—she's the wife of the royal governor of the town, after all, and the member of one of the most noble Houses in the Realm. At the same time, her moral qualities are considered really poor. She's said to be a coquette keen on whatever love adventure she can get—outside of her husband's bed, of course. I wish we had some evidence to dispute her false accusation of brother Nicolas...
Wait a moment, son... There's one thing I wanted to ask you about. The man that accompanies you... that one looking like a landsknecht, where did you run into him?
You mean Olfghard? He joined me in Hillbrandt when I saved him from being hanged. I was lucky and I succeed in proving he was innocent. Why do you ask?

You know, son... I'll be frank with you. I know the man. And you can't imagine how glad I am to hear you saved him from the gallows. I know very well what kind of life he lives and that he has a wonderful gift of getting into various problems very easily...
You know Olfghard, Your Excellency? He never mentioned that...

It's not so easy, son. I know Olfghard quite well, that's true. But he doesn't know me—that's why he has never talked about me with you. He doesn't even know we're relatives... he's my younger brother!
Olfghard is your brother?!

Right as I said, son. He's my younger brother—third child of our late parents. Nevertheless, unlike my older brother and me he never knew his parents. He was an unwanted child. The mistake that should have never happened. You know, son, we stem from a distinguished House in the Realm. Our parents couldn't have more than two sons—they wanted to avoid shattering the House fortune. All their fiefs were inherited by my older brother and by me. As the second son I was sent to seminary, to become a priest. When Olfghard was born, our parents decided to put him away, so he couldn't lay claim for the heirdom.
They simply got rid of him?

Not completely. They were looking after him for the rest of their lives, they were defending and helping him in many ways—anonymously, of course. It was very hard work, because soon it was found out that Olfghard is rather wild and that bad luck is following in his wake. From time to time I wonder he's still alive... When my dear parents died, I continued to keep an eye on Olfghard. Several times I visited Hillbrandt, where he settled down for a while, and I hired some people to send me news about him.
It was very kind of you. But after all you weren't informed that he was accused of the murder, were you?

Yes, that's right. Because of that I'm so grateful to you for helping him without knowing any details about him. And I hope you won't be offended if I give you a pouch of gold and this relic as an expression of my gratitude for your help. And at the same time I ask you not to tell Olfghard anything you've heard from me.
It's me who must thank you, son. Farewell.
No need to give me presents, Your Excellency. I didn't help him with greedy intentions...
I know that well, son. Because of that you deserve it much more then anybody else!
I think bribery is a very awful crime!
If I can advise you, sir Cardinal, give me the answer. Even your position won't save you from the wrath of God in case you hide something!
It's obvious you don't like me, Cardinal. Despite that I ask you to think once more about your answer, as it could help a rightful cause...
You're a very clever and world-wise man, Cardinal. I assure you there's nobody who could give me a more detailed answer for my question than you could.

I came to you as to a member of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. I'd like to show you the proof about heresy of a person that can be accused only by this Supreme Court Tribunal of the Holy Office.

Oh, really? That's a very important issue... The Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition is here to judge the most distinguished persons in the Realm. Who does your proof concern? Who is the person you want to start proceedings against? Who do you want to accuse of heresy? I advise you to choose your words very carefully, because premature trials and false accusations are crimes the Inquisition punishes very strictly—no matter who commits them!
I'd like to bring forward proof of guilt of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert, Your Excellency. There's a reasonable suspicion he's a heretic and traitor.

So, you want to bring forward the proofs of heresy of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert. What madness is that? Grand Master de Malamert is a solid pillar of both the Realm and the Crown! Moreover he's your highest superior!
The proofs are clear, Your Excellency.
Come, bring forward your proofs of heresy of Grand Master Malamert. I'm listening carefully!

Petrier de Duby, a neophyte of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, confessed that Grand Master de Malamert attempts to disrupt the Realm with help of the powers of Hell whom he serves. Moreover we found two of the Grand Master's letters in which he gives instructions to his minions how they should proceed in their joint plot to disrupt the Realm.

This is more than funny, son. And very suspicious at the same time... The neophyte Petrier de Duby disappeared under still unclear circumstances several weeks ago. Because of that, his sudden testimony is more than strange. And the letters from the Grand Master could be a fake, as it's quite common in these wonderful times. No, son, I'm sure these proofs wouldn't stand a chance before the Supreme Tribunal.
Are you trying to tell me you won't give me the approval to accuse and subsequently arrest the Grand Master?

Yes, exactly, son. And not only that—I'll be very careful about you. I'll be watching your every step and in the case of the slightest sign of reasonable doubt I'll let you be arrested and interrogated thoroughly! Now go away and consider whether you shouldn't confess your sins!
If you think so, Your Excellency.

Think about it once more, Your Excellency. Grand Master de Malamert is a very dangerous criminal and it's necessary to accuse and interrogate him as soon as possible! And in the case we'll find he's innocent during the interrogation, the better for all of us, don't you think?

I certainly disagree with that. The Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition can't use the trial and error method. This is a very naive approach. No, I can't agree with that on principle. Moreover, the proofs you have against Grand Master de Malamert are pretty poor.
If I can't get your approval voluntarily, Your Excellency, I'll try to get it with the use of all means possible!
Don't you ever try to threaten me, son. It's completely useless, and at the same time it's a sin. Well, I could let you be arrested and strictly punished for that!
What is the price of your approval, Your Excellency? I'm sure we can come to an agreement...

Don't try to bribe my, son! If there's something in the world I really hate, it's corruption. Hide your pouch immediately and start to behave yourself according to your position. I already fear for your soul!
Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert told me that I could turn to you without doubt whenever I need help...

You talked to Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert, son? About what matter? And who are you in fact? I don't know you... And your talk is very suspicious. What kind of help should I offer you? What do you want to achieve by all this?
No need to fear, Your Excellency. I'm not your enemy—it's more to the contrary. I'm in the service of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert. Read this letter he's sending to you.

A letter from Grand Master de Malamert, you say? Show it to me, I'll look at it. Well... the seal doesn't seem broken and this really is the handwriting of Grand Master de Malamert... But the things he writes here... Good Heavens... this is... terrible! The Cult of the Children of the New Order? Invocation of the Fallen Angels? Releasing Satan from his underground prison?! Jean de Guise a traitor? Let the Archangel Gabriel protect us from such evil! This is the worst news I've ever heard. I'm sorry, son, for not trusting you at first. But if you knew the situation here in Alvaron a bit, you would agree with me that one can't be cautious enough these days. Especially in the case if all you found out during your investigation, as I've just read in Grand Master de Malamert's letter, is true...

No need to fear, Your Excellency. I'm not your enemy—it's more to the contrary. I'm in the service of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert. He gave me a letter for you in which he clears up everything in detail.
And where is the letter?
Well... I don't have it on me at the moment.
In that case come when you have the letter. In case it really exists, of course, and I doubt it quite a lot. And if I can warn you—be careful about what you do and what you say to me!
I bring the letter Grand Master de Malamert sent to you, Your Excellency.

Show it to me, I'll look at it. Well... the seal doesn't seem broken and this really is the handwriting of Grand Master de Malamert... But the things he writes here... Good Heavens... this is... terrible! The Cult of the Children of the New Order? Invocation of the Fallen Angels? Releasing Satan from his underground prison?! Let the Archangel Gabriel protect us from such evil! This is the worst news I've ever heard. I'm sorry, son, for not trusting you at first. But if you knew the situation here in Alvaron a bit, you would agree with me that one can't be cautious enough these days. Especially in the case if all you found out during your investigation, as I've just read in Grand Master de Malamert's letter, is true...
I'm sorry to bother you, Your Excellency. I'm leaving already. Farewell.
Farewell, son. Go in peace...
I'm glad I've gained your confidence, Your Excellency.

So am I, son. There are so few of us left... I'm glad that the Grand Master's intent to entrust you with the investigation of the case of Kurth Ollmier's murder proved to be right. The information you've retrieved is going to expand the safe borders of the Realm by miles. I agree completely with the opinion of Grand Master de Malamert—we must act immediately and try to reveal the Dark High Priest of the cult sooner than they'll try to carry out that monstrous Plan.
I agree with you.
Excellent. I'm glad to have you on our side, son. Tell me, what can I do this time to help you in your so difficult mission?
I need your advice, Your Excellency.
But of course, son. What's on your mind?
I need some money, Your Excellency.

All right, I'll help you. Take this pouch, it should be enough for various expenses concerning the investigation. However I must ask you to use the money reasonably, as we don't have too much in fact.
Of course, Your Excellency. Farewell.
I don't know about anything, Your Excellency.
No problem, son. Whenever you need my help in the future, don't hesitate to ask me—that's why I'm here. God be with you!

Besides your testimony, I gained the testimony of the royal chamberlain Trisstan who became a witness to the murder and who identified the First Knight reliably. I also found out that the King injured his murderer during the deadly fight and the First Knight had some scratches in his face and refused to talk about where he got them. Under the weight of all those proofs Rodrigo de Velacor confessed his crime in the end.

Precise work, son. Although I'm sorry it happened like this. Don Rodrigo de Velacor was a great man. However, you fulfilled your mission, son—and you did really well! Thus, you got over the practical part of your trial. Nonetheless to be named a Curial Inquisitor you must also pass the test regarding church and civil law. Are you ready to start the test?
Yes, I'm ready, Your Excellency.
Who are you and what do you want from me, son? I'm very busy and I don't think I have an appointment with you.
Can I know first who is the person I have the honor of speaking to?

My name is Gustapho Letti and I'm a Pope's legate at the Archbishop's cathedra of the Holy Mother Church of the Ultherst Nation. At this time I also act as a judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. You can conclude from that I'm really very busy. Thus, what do you need from me?
Nice to meet you, Your Excellency. Could I bother you for a moment and ask you several questions?
I'm very sorry, son, but I haven't time for you. I must address myself to very important tasks. Nevertheless you can come a little later.
If you think so, Your Excellency. Farewell.
What do you need, son? I'm very busy...
What do you want, son? I won't hide from you that this dialog spoils my precious time and I'd like to address myself to something useful. My work, for example.
I need to ask you several questions, Your Excellency.
I'm sorry, son, but I haven't time for you. Come another time!
In that case I won't bother you. Farewell.
I'm glad to see you, my dear son. I hope your investigation goes on well. Tell me, how can I help you in your effort?
That's why I'm here, son. What's on your mind?
I don't need anything this time, Your Excellency. I just happened to come by.
All right, son. But if you need anything in the future, come to see me. God be with you.

I'm glad to see you, dear son. I hope your investigation goes on well. Were you able to get the book Libre Daemonium and to use it to confirm or to disprove the suspicion the Fallen Angels had been invoked?
No, Your Excellency, I haven't found the book yet.
You had better hurry in that case and go to see Laurencius as soon as possible. Time is against us!
I know. But I need your advice now, Your Excellency.
Farewell, son. And if you need anything in the future, come to see me. God be with you.
I've got the book, Your Excellency. But I haven't been able to confirm the presence of the Fallen Angels yet—neither to disprove it.
It doesn't matter, son. I'm sure you'll succeed in the end. But remember that time is against us!
I realize that well. Farewell.
Farewell, son. If you need anything in the future, come to see me. God be with you.
Unfortunately yes, I have, Your Excellency. The presence of the Fallen Angels was proved beyond reasonable doubt. They're here, in our world!

What terrible news, son! Nothing worse could happen to us. The presence of the Fallen Angels ruins all the knowledge about God's Kingdom on Earth. It is... unimaginable! But we must somehow deal with that anyway. Maybe there still is some way to remedy the crimes of the heretics. The Fallen Angels must be banished back to where they came from!
I know. It's my mission!

Your determination is admirable, dearest son! I wish the Realm was full of men like you! You look towards your fate as undaunted as the First Prophet. Here, take this magic item, maybe you'll find it useful in your holy mission.
Thank you, Your Excellency. Could you give me brief advice?
Thank you, Your Excellency. Farewell.

I'm so glad to see you alive and healthy, dear son. I was so afraid for your life—and also for your soul! When I think about the danger you are facing... Tell me, have you tried to face the Fallen Angels?
Never mind, son. I'm sure you'll do it soon. Remember, time is against us!
Yes, I've sent some of the Fallen Angels back to burning Hell.

That's... that is unbelievable, son! I'd never believe a single mortal can do such a thing! There's nothing I can say... you have my deep respect! If someone is able to return the order to the Realm, it's you!
Don't laugh before breakfast, as people say. The work hasn't been finished yet...
Yes, we mustn't forget it. As long as even one Fallen Angel dwells in our world we risk the ruination of the entirity of God's Kingdom on Earth! But now tell me, is there something I can do for you?
Yes, I need brief advice from you.
I don't think so, Your Excellency. Farewell.
Farewell, son. And if you need anything in the future, come to see me. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you!
How do you do, son? I pray for the success of your effort. The Fallen Angels must return to the place from which they came!
I'm afraid I haven't been able to destroy all of them yet, Your Excellency.
Never mind, son. You're doing more than a common mortal can. I'm sure you will be successful in the end. Tell me, how can I help you in your mission?
I need brief advice from you.
I don't need anything just now, Your Excellency. Farewell.

Thank God you've finally returned, son! Something terrible happened! You must go to the royal burial chamber immediately! You must stop him! I'd never think he's a heretic... It's horrible! We thought we were able to stop the members of the Cult of the Children of the New Order, but it seems we weren't at all!
What are you talking about, Your Excellency? What happened? I'm coming to tell you that all the Fallen Angels were destroyed...
It's good, son... very good! However, I'm not sure whether it's the most important matter at the time. That is, something happened that none of us could presume...
What's the matter? Tell me about it at last!

The Archbishop Laurencius! Thanks to Providence I asked my informants once to keep an eye on him! Because of that I've just found he's a wolf in a sheepskin! A restless old man at first sight, but a heretic in fact, hiding his real face of a beast!

My informants told me that Archbishop Laurencius left the city and went to the royal graveyard, where he performed—God help me—some necromantic ritual, after which he closed himself in the Royal Burial Chamber! Do you know what it means, son?
I think it means I'll go to the Royal Burial Chamber and blow the lid off the plots of Archbishop Laurencius—no matter what he is doing there!

Thank God we have you, son! I've a bad feeling Archbishop Laurencius is trying to commit some terrible crime... Take this key, it should unlock the Royal Burial Chamber no matter how it was sealed by Archbishop Laurencius. You must stop him at all costs!
I'll do my best. Could you give me brief advice first?
You better hurry, son. Laurencius must be stopped! Anyway, what's on your mind?
I'll take care of it, Your Excellency. Farewell.
Farewell, son. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you!
Were your successful in your mission, son? Did you stop the wicked plans of Archbishop Laurencius? Did you find out what he was trying to do?
I'm afraid not yet, Your Excellency.
In that case you'd better hurry, son. Although you're doing more than a common mortal can do, the Archbishop must be stopped, because he's surely going to do something very wicked!
I'll do all I can. But now I'd need brief advice from you.
All members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition agreed to accuse cardinal Commendoni of heresy. Do you know where he could be hiding?
Great job, my son! Now you must arrest him. I suppose he has hidden himself in the underground beneath the Archbishops' palace. This place is heavilly guarded, so be very careful!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous can't succumb to temptation, son. You must fight it. I know you long for riches, but it's not the right way for you. Remember your mission!
So, you want to bring forward the proof of heresy of Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert. What madness is that? Grand Master de Malamert is a solid pillar of both the Realm and the Crown!
I know. It's my holy mission!

Your determination is admirable, dearest son! I wish the Holy Mother Church were full of clerics like you! You look towards your fate as undaunted as the First Prophet. Here, take this magic item, maybe you'll find it useful in your holy mission.
All members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition agreed to accuse cardinal Commendoni of heresy. Do you happen to know, where he could be hiding?
Great job, my son! Now you must arrest him. I suppose he has hidden in the underground beneath the Archbishop palace. That place is heavily guarded, so be very careful!
Inquisitor of the Holy Office can't succumb to the temptation, son. You must fight it. I know you long for riches, but it's not the right way for you. Remember your holy mission!

Thank God we have you, son! I've a bad feeling Archbishop Laurencius is trying to commit some terrible crime... Take this key, it should unlock the Royal Burial Chamber no matter how it was sealed by Archbishop Laurencius. You must stop him!
All members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition agreed to accuse cardinal Commendoni of heresy. Don't you know, where could he be hiding?
Great job, my son! Now you must arrest him. I suppose he has hidden himself in the underground beneath the Archbishop palace. This place is heavilly guarded, so be very careful!

A highborn man can't succumb to temptation, son. You must fight it. I know you long for riches, but it's not the right way for you. If you want to steal lawfully, raise the taxes. But otherwise remember your mission!
I'd like to ask you about that accusation of the violation you brought against Father Nicolas, Grand Duchess. What really happened?

What do you mean, what really happened?! I don't know what you've heard, but that devil laid his dirty hands on me! He's a dark sorcerer who decided to get a hold of me and he really did so with the help of infernal tricks. You can't imagine how terrible it was... when he tore off my clothing, when he tortured my body, when he entered me and violated my honor... Oh my God, it was terrible! I wish I could forget it...
Well, brother Nicolas says he's innocent. He says you fabricated the whole story as a revenge, because he refused to become your lover.

And you believe that, knight? What kind of human being are you when you don't believe a woman that was violated, raped and defiled by such an awful criminal? The devil has been lying to you all the time and you can't see it?! What a shame!
No matter what really happened, I want you to take your accusation back.
Are you kidding? I'd never do such a thing. Never, do you understand?! NEVER!
I don't believe brother Nicolas violated you, Grand Duchess. Why, you flirted even with me and pretended you wanted to seduce me...
No matter what happened, I'll never take back my accusation. Never. Do you understand?! NEVER!
I consider your attitude absolutely shocking, knight. I'll tell my husband about it. He keeps an eye on my honor and he would never stand such a disgrace!
I want you to take back your accusation of Father Nicolas, Grand Duchess.
I already told you I'd never do such a thing. Never. Do you understand?! NEVER!
Not even in the case that I otherwise reveal to your husband that you have a forbidden relationship with Father Marcius?
Wh... what?!
Yes, you heard well. If you don't take back your false accusation, I'll reveal to your husband that you've indulged in monstrous debauchery in the city graveyard together with the priest Marcius!
But that's blackmail! And you call yourself a knight?!
Yes, I do. Well, how will you decide, Grand Duchess?
You don't have any proof against me! Nobody will believe you. Both me and Marcius will deny everything!
I doubt he will, Grand Duchess. Marcius confessed to your disgusting relationship. And he agreed to make it public in the case you refuse to take back your accusation of Father Nicolas!
I don't believe that! Marcius would never betray me! He's a real man—in contrast to you, you poor cipher!
I don't think so... He stated that you had tempted him and he was very sorry about that. He told me you were a reinless fornicatress and nothing was sacred to you.

That bastard! To cast me away so easily! May the stupid swine never get a hard on! All right, let's do it your way—I'll take back my accusation of Nicolas. Anyway, he's a poor wretch... I wonder why I tried to have an affair with him after all!
Excellent. I'm glad we have an agreement.
You... lousy ferret!

Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert a heretic... it's an exciting idea, don't you think? To tell the truth people think he's a heretic. At least most of the people. It causes the people to be afraid of what the future will bring them, because when such a distinguished man can be a heretic, who can we trust? As for me, I can imagine quite well the Grand Master to indulge himself in perverse bodily pleasures with kidnapped virgins in his impregnable Citadel. Imagine how he's catering his lowest disgraceful instincts that urge him further and further, until he enters with his... well... sorry, my imagination carried me away a bit...
I'm sorry, but I really hate talking about weather! Perhaps we could talk about something more interesting.

The only heretic I was so unlucky to meet personally was the priest Nicolas! He's Satan himself! He violated me, spattered me, defiled me and yet he laughed at my tears! He's a dark sorcerer, who decided to get a hold of me and he really did so with the help of infernal tricks. You can't imagine how terrible it was... when he tore my clothing off, when he tortured my body, when he entered me and violated my honor... Oh my God, it was terrible! I wish I could forget it... He must go to the stake for what he did!
No, I don't!

I've heard that Nina Monthreass disappeared without a trace last full moon. It seems that the werewolves of wolf-prince Wulfhyrr kidnapped her, as well as all the previous victims. I'm full of fear when I imagine what they could do to her in their awful lair. Surely they'd rape her roughly. They'd tear her clothes off, stripping it away like animals, they'd strangle and scar her and at the same time they'd enter her with their ugly... oh... what am I saying...

I've heard that paladin Richwald d'Blazier was turned into stone by some witch of Schwarzwald, because the poor paladin had fallen in love with her like a fool. I'm sure he also fornicated with her. The image of a wild untamable mystic woman must be fascinating for men, don't you think? Imagine that you'd hunt her like a wild beast, you'd flirt with her, tempt her, try to master her and when she finally surrendered you'd feel like the hunter with a valuable trophy in your arms... Yes, I think that's exactly how you would feel!
I found this golden earring. Do you happen to know to whom it could belong?

Show me the earring, please. Well... it's gold, that's true, but otherwise it's a trinket of no value. A noble woman wouldn't wear something as plain-looking as this. It's good only for the low-born...
I'm sorry but I don't know any details about His Majesty's death. I can only ask myself how such a thing could be committed in the very royal chambers? There was magic involved, I'm sure about it!

I've heard that the brother of William Burton was missing. But I wouldn't fear for him too much if I were you. He's a man, he has his needs and he probably ran into some beautiful maid or house-girl... Or I'd look for him in the bed of some salacious harlot girl—those are rather available to merchants...

Maybe you know that there's a place near Alvaron where St. Orthenius, patron of our Realm, himself was buried in 233. It used to be one of the most sacred pilgrimage places for a thousand years and legions of faithful people came there year after year to bow to the relics of our Realm's patron. During the reign of King Henry the Third the beautiful gardens called the King's Gardens were planted around the crypt. The place was full of flowering bushes, evergreen grass, exotic trees and wooden gazebos attracting people to rest—and to indulge in erotic adventures! For the last several generations of nobles the Gardens became a place to spend most of their leisure time. But now... better not to talk about it.

When the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, the Gardens were one of the first places that were ruined. During several years when the Scourges of God struck the Realm the Gardens changed beyond recognition—and they're called Garden of Sorrow now. It's really regrettable that such a lovely place became a nest of evil and the hiding place of hellish monsters. Thus the burial chamber of St. Orthenius is located in the middle of a wicked land, where even the most desperate lovers looking for a place to please each other don't dare to come!
You had better answer voluntarily, Grand Duchess. Do you think I couldn't make you answer the hard way?
I ask you frankly, Grand Duchess, answer me, please.
You're beautiful and at the same time a wise and educated woman, Grand Duchess. Your answer would mean a lot to me...

Oh, you joker! I'm so glad to meet somebody with similar sense of humor like my own. My husband has no understanding of this type of joke—and maybe I understand him. But I would die without a bit of excitement and entertainment!
Well... If you think so.

But enough of these jokes, I'm sure you didn't come to me to have some fun. I guess your holy mission brings you to me, right? How can I help you? You can be sure I'll do all I can to help a knight as handsome as you are!
Come on, dear knight, it was only another joke. I didn't really mean it. Calm down and take a deep breath, it'll help you.
But sure... let's talk openly about all that's teasing our hearts, dear knight!
I'd better go. Farewell.
You're leaving already, dear knight? We've talked just for a short time. All right, here's a farewell kiss for you. Au revoir mon amour!
Hello, knight. I'm sure we don't know each other yet—I'd certainly remember a man as handsome as you are. I'm Grand Duchess Liana Lambert, wife of Drake Lambert, the royal governor of the city.
Nice to meet you, Grand Duchess.

I'm the one who's pleased, dear knight. You must certainly be a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, mustn't you? Yes, there's no doubt about it. I recognized it from your behavior—you're self-confident, vigorous, proudly upright, your face is determined and there's a glow in your eyes. It's really nice to look at you. I'm feeling so... safe with you! You must be very courageous when you're able to face infernal monsters that lurk at every corner every day. Oh, every night I'm so afraid that a vampire or werewolf will come for me and lay hands on me! My heart is skipping a beat—here, can you feel it?
Yes, your heart really beats very quickly.

Can you see how hard is it for me to breath? My breath is so shallow—can you feel it? And my heart is beating so feverishly—can you see? It's because of the horror that some infernal monster would lay its dirty hands on me in the middle of the night. It would tear the clothing from me and would scar my skin with its sharp claws, and my blood would pour down my naked body. I'd be crying from the horror when it would get a hold of me lecherously and violate me like some bitch... Ehm... it became quite hot here, dear knight, don't you think? Please help me to loosen the corset a little bit, I can't breathe...
Is it just my imagination, Grand Duchess, or are you seducing me?

And if I am? What if I told you I haven't met a man as attractive as you in my life, that I fell in love with you at the first sight, that the idea of never seeing you again makes me suffer... what would you say to me about that?
Grand Duchess, you're a married woman! Behave yourself, please—such talking is a sin!
I would tell you I've never met a woman as beautiful as you are!

You flatterer! I'd never think that although you're a cleric you will be able to blandish a woman like that	. But think about what would happen to us if we abandoned ourselves to passion! Public interdict, excommunication from the Church, banishment from home... Oh, are you willing to risk all of that for the love of a woman?
Enough of that game... it's not entertaining any more!
I'll do anything for you, Grand Duchess!
If you give me a pouch of gold, your husband will never know what you have just told me!
The question is what would your husband say to that...
Is that you, my dear knight? I'm so glad to see you... I missed you! Do you come to please my heart with your presence?
What do you want, knight? I'm not in the mood to talk to you...
That's not important. I need to talk to you, Grand Duchess!
You... boorish savage! What do you want from me?
In that case I'll leave you. Farewell.

And you believe that, Father? What kind of human being are you when you don't believe a woman that was violated, raped and defiled by such an awful criminal? The devil has been lying to you all the time and you can't see it?! What a shame!
I consider your attitude absolutely shocking, Father. I'll tell my husband about it. He keeps an eye on my honor and he would never stand such a disgrace!
But—this is intimidation! What kind of a priest are you?
I'm a humble servant of God... So, what about your decision, Grand Duchess?!

But enough of those jokes, I'm sure you didn't come to me to have some fun. I guess your holy mission brings you to me, right? How could I help you? You can be sure I'll do all I can to help a cleric as handsome as you are!
Come on, dear Father, it was only another joke. I didn't really mean it. Calm down and take a deep breath, it'll help you.
But sure... let's talk openly about all that's teasing our hearts, dear Father!
You're leaving already, dear Father? We've talked just for a short time. All right, here's a farewell kiss for you. Au revoir mon amour!
Hello, Father. I'm sure we don't know each other yet—I'd certainly remember a priest as handsome as you are. I'm Grand Duchess Liana Lambert, wife of Drake Lambert, the royal governor of the city.

I'm the one who's pleased, dear Father. You must certainly be an Inquisitor, mustn't you? Yes, there's no doubt about it. I'm feeling so... safe with you! You must be very courageous when you're able to face heresy and wicked delusions every day—not to talk about infernal monsters. Oh, I'm so afraid every night that some vampire or werewolf will come for me and lay hands on me! My heart is skipping a beat—here, can you feel it?

I'd be crying from the horror when it would get a hold of me lecherously and violate me like some bitch... Ehm... it became quite hot here, dear Father, don't you think? Please help me to loosen the corset a little bit, I can't breathe...

And if I am? What if I told you I haven't met a man as attractive as you in my life, that I fell in love with you at first sight, that the image of a terrible obstruction dividing us, because you're a priest, makes me suffer... what would you say to that?
Grand Duchess, you're talking to a cleric! Behave yourself, please!
Is that you, my dear Father? I'm so glad to see you... I missed you! Do you come to please my heart with your presence?
What do you want, Father? I'm not in the mood to talk to you...

And you believe that, sir? What kind of human being are you when you don't believe a woman that was violated, raped and defiled by such an awful criminal? The devil has been lying to you all the time and you can't see it?! What a shame!
I consider your attitude absolutely shocking, sir. I'll tell my husband about it. He keeps an eye on my honor and he would never stand such a disgrace!
But that's blackmail! And you call yourself a noble?!
But enough of these jokes, I'm sure you didn't come to me to have some fun. How can I help you? You can be sure I'll do all I can to help a man as handsome as you are!

Oh, every night I'm so afraid that a vampire or werewolf will come for me and lay hands on me! My heart is skipping a beat, here, can you feel it?
