It's because of the horror that some infernal monster would lay its dirty hands on me in the middle of the night. It would tear the clothing from me and would scar my skin with its sharp claws, and my blood would pour down my naked body. I'd be crying from the horror when it would get a hold of me lecherously and violate me like some bitch... Ehm... it became quite hot here, dear sir, don't you think? Please help me to loosen the corset a little bit, I can't breathe...

And if I am? What if I told you I haven't met a man as attractive as you in my life, that I fell in love with you at first sight, that the idea of never seeing you again makes me suffer... what would you tell me to that?
Is that you, my dear sir? I'm so glad to see you... I missed you! Do you come to please my heart with your presence?
What do you want, sir? I'm not in the mood to talk to you...
Tell me once more about your kidnapping, Lady Baroness.
So you want to hear again about my kidnapping. I mean, do you really want me to recall those terrible events again?
The question was asked, Lady Baroness...

All right... I was lying in bed, and I heard some noise from the street. I didn't know what was happening, so I went to look there. And I saw a bunch of those infernal green skins running along the street directly to our house. I cried in horror and that probably was what attracted them to me, because they ran to me immediately and caught me before I was able to lock myself in my house. I fainted from fear and awoke in some orcish cell.
You're right, I won't bother you with that any further.
Thank you, knight. You're a very sensitive man.
Tell me how you were kidnapped, Lady Baroness.

I was lying in bed, and I heard some noise from the street. I didn't know what was happening, so I went to look there. And I saw a bunch of those infernal green skins running along the street directly to our house. I cried in horror and that probably was what attracted them to me, because they ran to me immediately and caught me before I was able to lock myself in my house. I fainted from fear and awakened in some orcish cell.

I fear for the fate of our Realm, knight. Several times I had a terrible dream that the entire Kingdom was blazing with fire. All was burned to ashes, overwhelmed and suffocated. Flames licked the Cathedral of the Holy Trinity like a wicked harlot licks her lover's body. The walls of the royal palace laid in ruins and hordes of hellspawns rushed over them. It was terrible!
I'm sorry but I'm definitely not going to talk to you about it!

Has anything uncommon happened lately? You mean except for all that what happened to me. I've heard that the daughter of Stephan Reichmann the merchant is dead. It seems she was assassinated by landsknecht Olfghard who seized her jewels. Poor Natalia, she was such a flowering bud... How is it possible that those royal army wretches were unable to keep Olfghard safely under lock and key when they arrested him? How is it possible that he escaped and nobody knows where he is hiding? If my husband were the royal governor of the town, nothing of that kind would have happened! It's just another sign of Duke Weinberg's incompetence.
The Monstrance of St. Orthenius is missing; do you happen to know anything about it?
I've heard that the Monstrance of St. Orthenius is missing. What a terrible loss for the entire town. Who on Earth could do such a thing?
Poor Bishop Quentinus! I've heard he disappeared the same night I was kidnapped. I'm afraid his fate was terrible. If you didn't save me, knight, I'm sure I'd also be dead already.
Do you happen to know anything about the missing Paul Hammerhand?

Paul Hammerhand is the most terrible child I've ever met. He's a real little devil, knight! He runs away from his home, doesn't go to confession, opposes his father... I'm not surprised he disappeared. Surely the devils took him to burning Hell. It was the only destiny awaiting him.
Do you happen to know where the soldier Jullian could be hiding, Lady Baroness?
Are you asking me where the soldier Jullian is hidden? How would I know, knight? Do you think I should know where runaways are hiding?
If there're some legends tied to Hillbrandt? I don't know, knight. I'm too noble and educated to be interested in folk tales and superstitions. These things belong to the low-born.

I don't like to ask you about that, Lady Baroness, but Bishop Quentinus testified that he had seen you one night in the town graveyard together with other masked people carrying away a dead body you had recovered from a grave. What can you tell me about it?

Oh my God, that funny accusation of heresy returns to me again? As I have already told that godless Edmond d'Arvias, when he came to me and asked me the same question—Bishop Quentinus had to make a mistake. For it definitely wasn't me. I really don't know why I should dig up some bodies in the graveyard and why I should carry them anywhere. You can ask my husband if you don't believe me. He'll tell you that I lay in my husband's bed every night like a good faithful wife and I don't get up until the cockcrows. And he'll also definitely tell you that if you won't stop that absurd investigation IMMEDIATELY, he'll use all his authority of the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt to destroy you! Do you understand?

I'm sorry to be so daring to ask such a question, but the soldier Millward testified he saw you the night the merchant Kurth Ollmier was murdered climbing out of the window of his room in a Hillbrandt tavern. What can you tell me about that?

I think this is a bad dream! What nasty story is that? What are you trying to accuse me of? I have had enough of this—I'll tell my husband to put a stop to your investigation. I've never climbed out of any window, it's irrational! And if some drunken soldier told you so, you should better investigate him, for it's evident he's lying. And that's all I'm going to tell you about that!
Do you happen to know anything about the death of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, Lady Baroness?

I don't know any details about the death of Kurth Ollmier. He was weird and didn't keep company with many people. And I also wouldn't call him merchant—he was sort of an adventurer and treasure hunter. If he traded something, it was nothing good—you can believe me of that. Why else would the Inquisition be interested in him? I've heard he was suspected of heresy. No wonder he ended up so bad. Playing with fire brings the risk of getting burnt sooner or later—or being burned.
I was told that you had a short talk with the merchant Kurth Ollmier in the bar of Truthorn's inn the night he was murdered. Is it true?
What? Who told you such a thing?
That's nothing you should be interested in, Lady Baroness. Answer my question, please.

I didn't talk to Kurth Ollmier that night. In fact I doubt I've ever said more than few words to him when he met my husband and me in the streets. The person who told you such a nonsense is a nasty liar trying to discredit me!
It was your sister-in-law, Baroness Elisabeth van Singier. She also told me that after your talk with Ollmier she didn't see either of you in the bar again.

Oh, now I see which way the wind is blowing. I should have thought that! My sister-in-law has been always trying to discredit me; she told my husband lies and nasty fabrications about me and slandered my name wherever she went. And all of that just because of the fact Robert and me didn't want to move to her in Glatzburg when her husband was alive. Now when she herself must take shelter at our place she continues in her disgraceful slander instead of being grateful to me for not ordering to whip her away from our door-step!
So you didn't talk to Kurth Ollmier the night before his murder?
Of course I didn't. I've got nothing in common with that man!
Oh, I see now. Thanks.
Not at all, knight. And be careful about Elisabeth van Singier—she's a dangerous plotter!
I'm looking for heretics here in Hillbrandt, Lady Baroness. Do you happen to have any suspicions of heresy?

I believe that all those infernal monsters are lurking around Hillbrandt these days because of Master Edmond d'Arvias and his wicked heretic plans. Whatever those plans are. I'm sure it's true what the people say—that it was him who opened the gate for the orcs when they attacked the town! He's a heretic and should be burnt at the stake as soon as possible...

Who rules in Hillbrandt and around? Why, my husband does—Baron Robert van Gallagan. He's the royal vice-governor. He takes care of very important issues regarding the town administration. However officially—and totally unearned—Duke Weinberg rules the town as the royal governor. I don't understand at all how King Edward could entrust him with the rule of the town—that is to say, he's totally incompetent and without the outstanding qualities of my husband he would have lost the domains entrusted to him long time ago because of some rebellion!
Think twice about your decision, Lady Baroness. I don't mean to threaten you, but can you even imagine what terrible things could happen to you if you chose to oppose me?
You may not like me, Lady Baroness, but I believe you don't want to refuse me your so much needed help without good reason.
Someone as beautiful and intelligent as you, Lady Baroness, shouldn't hesitate to answer my question...
Oh, thank God I'll get out of this terrible place. Thank you, knight. No doubt my husband will reward you handsomely. I nearly gave up all hope of being rescued!
Who are you talking about, Lady Baroness? You had better tell me all you know before it's too late!

What you have found during your investigation is really true, knight. I really killed both the merchant Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill. And it was also me whom Bishop Quentinus saw in the city cemetery when we were carrying the body of Baroness von Weill away.
Why did you kill Kurth Ollmier?

Because he had a book we needed for the preparation of the summoning ritual. I killed him to cover all the tracks. Nobody was to know what book we gained from him. And beyond that, the fool wanted to extort me! He said that the Inquisition would be surely interested in what books I was interested. He wanted my body; he wanted to fornicate with me. But I didn't grant him that pleasure. I killed him.
Why did you assassinate Baroness Gwenn von Weill and why did you later steal her body?

Because we needed the body of an innocent girl that had been lying in the holy ground for thirteen days for the Ritual. It was sort of a problem, as the local girls are rarely innocent since childhood—I know it well myself, knight, trust me! In the end Baroness Gwenn von Weill seemed to be the most suitable one, despite the fact she was noble. She lost her entire family, being left lonely in the entire world and without any assets. It wasn't hard to win her favor and later to poison her. The thirteenth night after the burial we unburied her body and carried it to the Ritual place. She was so sweet!
What about the summoning Ritual you mentioned?
It's a ritual allowing you to summon the most powerful hellish being, knight. The ritual to summon a Fallen Angel!
What? Oh my God... are you trying to tell me, Lady Baroness, that you've summoned a Fallen Angel?

Exactly, knight. It was the aim of all our efforts and in the end we were successful. The gates of Hell were opened and the Fallen Angel Arthamon entered our world. Soon he'll be walking the surface of Earth, ruling the world. There's no way to stop him!
If you've really told me the truth and the Fallen Angel was summoned, where does he dwell in our world? How can it be that no one else saw him?

He dwells in the Kingdom of Despair on Earth. I don't know exactly where that place is located, but it's somewhere deep underground, close to the borders of Hell. After the summoning he departed there to gather his armies of hellspawns and wait for the day he'll resurface and will destroy all that will stand in his way.
Armies of hellspawns? What armies are you talking about, Lady Baroness?

I'm talking about destroyer armies of hellspawns and monsters lined up under his command. I'm sure you've already met some of them. The orcs, for example. But there are many others creeping through dark holes in the ground to the surface to await the day when the sun will turn red from human blood and human kingdoms will be shattered to dust one after another.
What can you tell me about that Fallen Angel?
He's the demon of ruination and the damned Lord of Fire. He spreads total destruction; he's the general of the armies of Hell. He's the all-devouring flame that cannot be extinguished.
You're talking in plural, Lady Baroness. Who are your accomplices? Bishop Quentinus testified he saw you at the graveyard accompanied by other heretics...

Most of the crimes I committed together with Sam Riemann. He was good only for the dirtiest jobs that would even the most stupid orc do better, but he was handy after all. It wasn't hard to get him on our side—he's obsessed by the idea of the world ruled by terror.
Who else was with you? Who are you afraid of so much that you're telling me such a terrible confession?

It's Judge Vallarian, knight. It was he who came to Hillbrandt with the idea of summoning the Fallen Angel Arthamon. He revealed to me what my future would be in case I'd help him, and I succumbed to his temptation. It was too alluring to resist. I even didn't want to resist. That is to say, all my life I was waiting for something like that!
Judge Vallarian? I don't believe that!
It is as I've told you, knight. I've not lied to you. Ask Sam Riemann. He's a weakling, and when you put the squeeze on him, he'll tell you everything!
Judge Vallarian, you say? And can you prove it somehow?

I doubt it, knight. I've got nothing to prove it was Vallarian who thought it all up and prepared it. But you can ask Sam Riemann. He's a weakling, and when you put the squeeze on him, he'll tell you everything!
Yes, I'll do that. But tell me, why do you think Vallarian wants to kill you? You're his accomplice, after all, if not something worse...

I know people well, knight. He's interested in nothing else than what he wants for himself. And to tell the truth, I was never really sure what his aim was. He told us that the fall of God's Kingdom on the Earth was near and it was time to decide on which side we wanted to stand. And that if we would choose the right side, we could live in forbidden pleasures to our tastes forever. But he never told us what would really happen in fact. When you arrested me and put me into jail, he helped me out of prison immediately, but he was... different. He was hiding something—I saw it immediately. He regaled me with assurances that there was nothing to fear, that all was managed and would be solved soon. But I knew something wasn't right. His smile filled my heart with fear. He had such a dead face. Thus I decided to tell you everything. I'm so scared of him!
But I'm sure you know that for heresy—especially such a great one—you'll be sentenced to death. What do you want from me? Why did you decide to confess to me?

Because we can have an agreement, knight. All can be managed, I'm sure you know it well. I'll testify against Vallarian at the trial and in exchange for that I'll be able to escape under strange circumstances... I saved some money... I can get away... quickly... I can... ahhhh!
Are you ok, Lady Baroness? You look terribly pale. Do you feel well?

I'm... not feeling well at the moment... my head swims... my neck is lame, it's hard to talk for me... Oh, the pain... What's happening to me? Oh my God, I can hear judge Vallarian... he's whispering something to me... I don't understand it... go away, you devil! Go away, can you hear me? Leave me alone!
Lady Baroness, you are delirious! What has happened to you? Lady Baroness!

I don't want to die... God forgive me... I don't want to die! I'm so young... I can start somewhere else... again... The wine! He had to give something into the wine he offered me... He... poisoned me! The pain... I can't stand it... I don't want to die! Help me, knight! I beseech you, help me, please! Don't let me die... I don't... want... to die... I don't want... ahhh...
Lady Baroness...
My God... she's dead!
There was nothing I could do to help you. I couldn't prevent it, the poison was too strong. May your soul rest in peace, Lady Baroness. Amen.
Linda van Gallagan, I arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. You'll come with me!
Pardon? That must be some mistake, knight. I was kidnapped by the orcs from my home, dragged into their lair and you accuse me of heresy? That's irrational!
Irrational? I don't think so. Irrational or not, you're arrested.

You will be sorry for that, knight. My husband is a very powerful man. You will pay a lot for your impertinence, you can bet on it! You will be glad if you spend the rest of your life in murus strictus!
We'll see. Let's go.
Maybe you really are innocent, Lady Baroness. However, I must investigate every suspicion. Please, come with me.

All right, as you wish. But you will be sorry for that, knight. You will pay a lot for your impertinence. My husband is a very powerful man and he won't let you unpunished, you can bet on it! You will be glad if you spend the rest of your life in murus strictus!
Good Heavens, I'm saved!
Who are you, good woman? And how did you get here, to the depths of orcish caverns?

My name is Linda van Gallagan. My husband is Baron Robert van Gallagan, the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt. I was kidnapped by the orcs the night they attacked the city. Since then I've been kept here, in this awful place. Without you, knight, I'd surely loose my life. No doubt those hellish monsters would sooner or later torture me to death. You can't imagine what terrible things they made me do, and what they did to me! Oh my God, I can't even think about it...
How were you kidnapped, Lady Baroness?

I was lying in my bed, and I heard some noise from the street. I didn't know what was happening, so I went to look there. And I saw a bunch of those infernal green skins running along the street—directly to our house. I cried in horror and that probably was what attracted them to me, because they ran to me immediately and caught me before I was able to lock myself in our house. I fainted from fear and awakened in this terrible place.
Well, you say you were at home at the time of kidnapping, but your husband said you were missing sooner...

Oh, really? Eh... no doubt he did, knight. You know, my husband is a great man, but he has several weak spots. Spirits are among them. He can sleep drunken whole days without knowing what's happening around him. I've been trying to force him not to drink so much, but I've not been very successful.

Landsknecht Olfghard is not sure, but he thinks he saw you that night the orcs attacked the town to go together with a group of green skins in the direction of the iron mines. And he said it didn't look like those green skins kidnapped you at all. What can you tell about it?

Oh... what an audacity! Not only that I had to suffer such terrible things; but some poor sod also dares to accuse me of such a nonsense like cooperation with the orcs! I wonder you listen to such people, knight. Do you know he's said to kill Natalia Reichmann? That's terrible.
It had to be a really terrible experience.
Yes, it was terrible, knight. I won't forget it as long as I live.
What did those monsters do to you, Lady Baroness?
Such terrible things, knight... I can't even say it aloud... But I'm sure you can imagine... oh my God!
There's nothing to be afraid of anymore, Lady Baroness. I'll escort you back to the town.
There's nothing to be afraid of anymore, Lady Baroness. I promised your husband to escort you back to the town.
Hello, knight. Thank you once more for saving my life. No doubt those hellish monsters would sooner or later torture me to death if you hadn't found and saved me. What can I do for you?
I'll talk to you gladly, knight. What's on your mind?
Nothing, Lady Baroness. I just wanted to know if you are all right.
Oh... really? It's very nice of you. You're a very sensitive man, knight. I'm glad we're friends!
Knight? Please, listen to me. I know you don't like me, but I must... I want to confess to you. I have to do it. I'm so scared...
You surprise me, Lady Baroness. What's the matter? I mean, you were released from prison. So what are you afraid of?

I'm afraid of HIM. I fear he's going to kill me. I'm an unwanted witness for him, a witness that you held in your hands and he's not going to let you find out the truth. When I talked to him after my release from prison, there was something strange about him. He was trying to hide something; I can recognize such efforts. He hides some terrible secret, or maybe a plan...
What are you trying to do, Lady Baroness? Telling me another pack of your lies? I don't believe you!
No, knight, I assure you I don't lie. Not this time. I fear for my life. I'm afraid that he'll try to kill me!
Thank you, Father. You're a very sensitive man.

I fear for the fate of our Realm, Father. Several times I had a terrible dream that the entire Kingdom was blazing with fire. All was burned to ashes, overwhelmed and suffocated. Flames licked the Cathedral of the Holy Trinity like a wicked harlot licks her lover's body. The walls of the royal palace laid in ruins and hordes of hellspawns rushed over them. It was terrible!
Poor Bishop Quentinus! I've heard he disappeared the same night I was kidnapped. I'm afraid his fate was terrible. If you didn't save me, Father, I'm sure I'd also be dead already.

Paul Hammerhand is the most terrible child I've ever met. He's a real little devil, Father! He runs away from his home, doesn't go to confession, opposes his father... I'm not surprised he disappeared. Surely the devils took him to burning Hell. It was the only destiny awaiting him.
Are you asking me where the soldier Jullian is hidden? How would I know, Father? Do you think I should know where runaways are hiding?
If there're some legends tied to Hillbrandt? I don't know, Father. I'm too noble and educated to be interested in folk tales and superstitions. These things belong to the low-born.
Not at all, Father. And be careful about Elisabeth van Singier—she's a dangerous plotter!

Think twice about your decision, Lady Baroness. I don't want to threaten you, but I'm sure you know it's a serious crime to oppose the Inquisition. Can you imagine what terrible things could happen to you?
Oh, thank God I'll get out of this terrible place. Thank you, Father. No doubt my husband will reward you handsomely. I nearly gave up all hope of being rescued!

What you have found during your investigation is really true, Father. I really killed both the merchant Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill. And it was also me whom Bishop Quentinus saw in the city cemetery when we were carrying the body of Baroness von Weill away.

Because we needed the body of an innocent girl that had been lying in the holy ground for thirteen days for the Ritual. It was sort of a problem, as the local girls are rarely innocent since childhood—I know it well myself, Father, trust me! In the end Baroness Gwenn von Weill seemed to be the most suitable one, despite the fact she was noble. She lost her entire family, being left lonely in the entire world and without any assets. It wasn't hard to win her favor and later to poison her. The thirteenth night after the burial we unburied her body and carried it to the Ritual place. She was so sweet!
It's a ritual allowing you to summon the most powerful hellish being, Father. The ritual to summon a Fallen Angel!

Exactly, Father. It was the aim of all our efforts and in the end we were successful. The gates of Hell were opened and the Fallen Angel Arthamon entered our world. Soon he'll be walking the surface of Earth, ruling the world. There's no way to stop him!

It's Judge Vallarian, Father. It was he who came to Hillbrandt with the idea of summoning the Fallen Angel Arthamon. He revealed to me what my future would be in case I'd help him, and I succumbed to his temptation. It was too alluring to resist. I even didn't want to resist. That is to say, all my life I was waiting for something like that!
It is as I've told you, Father. I've not lied to you. Ask Sam Riemann. He's a weakling, and when you put the squeeze on him, he'll tell you everything!

I doubt it, Father. I've got nothing to prove it was Vallarian who thought it all up and prepared it. But you can ask Sam Riemann. He's a weakling, and when you put the squeeze on him, he'll tell you everything!

I know people well, Father. He's interested in nothing else than what he wants for himself. And to tell the truth, I was never really sure what his aim was. He told us that the fall of God's Kingdom on the Earth was near and it was time to decide on which side we wanted to stand. And that if we would choose the right side, we could live in forbidden pleasures to our tastes forever. But he never told us what would really happen in fact. When you arrested me and put me into jail, he helped me out of prison immediately, but he was... different. He was hiding something—I saw it immediately. He regaled me with assurances that there was nothing to fear, that all was managed and would be solved soon. But I knew something wasn't right. His smile filled my heart with fear. He had such a dead face. Thus I decided to tell you everything. I'm so scared of him!

Because we can have an agreement, Father. All can be managed, I'm sure you know it well. I'll testify against Vallarian at the trial and in exchange for that I'll be able to escape under strange circumstances... I saved some money... I can get away... quickly... I can... ahhhh!

I don't want to die... God forgive me... I don't want to die! I'm so young... I can start somewhere else... again... The wine! He had to give something into the wine he offered me... He... poisoned me! The pain... I can't stand it... I don't want to die! Help me, Father! I beseech you, help me, please! Don't let me die... I don't... want... to die... I don't want... ahhh...

It's him! He is the godless monster dealing with hellspawns and bringing human sacrifices to them! This is the heretic who doesn't mind kidnapping innocent people and throwing them down to monsters from the depths of Hell! Arrest him and let us purify his soul from deadly sins!
One moment, please, what's happening here? What are you talking about?

Don't keep denying that you're a heretic, you scoundrel! We have clear proof! Witnesses testified that they saw you talking to people who disappeared later without a trace! You will confess your sins! Arrest him!
None of that is true. I'm innocent!
The trial will judge that. Arrest him! Tie him! And if he opposes you, let the will of God be done!
Wait, Father—I think we can come to an agreement. Take my money and stop the investigation.
You thought you can bribe me? Well, you thought wrong, you heretic. Arrest him! Tie him! And if he opposes you, let the will of God be done!
If you think you can stop me, you're wrong! Let me go or I'll send all of you to Hell!
You think you can threaten me? Well, you thought wrong, you heretic. Arrest him! Tie him! And if he opposes you, let the will of God be done!
Wait, brother—I think we can come to an agreement. Take my money and stop the investigation.
Wait, Father, I think we can come to an agreement. Take my money and stop the investigation.
Prince Louis
In the name of Angels Raphael, Michael and Gabriel I call upon you, powers of Hell, release the body of Prince Louis from your damned grip!
In the name of God Almighty I exorcise you, powers of Hell, give back what doesn't belong to you! Now, Prince Louis is under God's protection!
Third time I dispraise your name, powers of Hell—leave this place and stop your plots in God's Kingdom on Earth!
Oh... What is... What happened to me?
Your Highness...?

I had a terrible dream... I had a dream that I died, my father was assassinated and the Realm was threatened by destruction. I saw the faces of a thousand demons eager for the blood of innocent people... It was terrible!
Thanks to God, I succeeded! The evil work of the powers of Hell was staved off!
What are you talking about, knight? Where are we? How did I got here? Oh my God... this looks like a burial chamber! And I don't know who you are. Where is my father?
I'm sorry, Your Highness, but your father is dead. You're the heir of the Ultherst throne!
Oh my God, so it wasn't just a dream, was it? My father really was assassinated and the Realm is on the verge of destruction.
Correct. However, you bring new hope to all of us! Let's go, Your Majesty, I'll accompany you to the Royal Palace. The Realm has it's leader again!
I don't understand. I'm so confused... Please help me stand up... and let's go out of here. According to your words I don't have time to waste. I have to build a new order!!!
In the name of the three powers of Hell—Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie—I summon you, Dark Prince of Hell; enter the body of this mortal I'm humbly offering you!

The gates of the powers of Hell were opened and the world is awaiting you, my Lord! Rise up from your prison and sit on the throne of the World that rightfully belongs to you! Come among us, ruler of Hell!
I praise your name and three times spit at the cross on which the First Prophet died! Come among us, my Lord! I INVOKE YOU FOR THE LAST TIME—COME AMONG US, SATAN!
You Highness...? My Lord?

I had a dream... a dream that I died, my father was assassinated and the Realm was threatened by destruction. I saw the faces of thousand demons eager for the blood of innocent people. I saw the ruination, chaos and fornication spreading throughout the world... What a beautiful dream. And now I'm back and it's time to make our dreams true. At last!
It is done! The quest is accomplished! Let's go, Your Majesty. I'll accompany you to the Royal Palace. You must build a new order!
Do not anticipate the future, knight. Help me to stand up and let's go out of here. I've got a lot of work to do. I have to build a new order!!!
What are you talking about, Father? Where are we? How did I got here? Oh my God... this looks like a burial chamber! And I don't know who you are. Where is my father?
Do not anticipate the future, my son. Help me to stand up and let's go out of here. I've got a lot of work to do. I have to build a new order!!!
What are you talking about, sir? Where are we? How did I got here? Oh my God... this looks like a burial chamber! And I don't know who you are. Where is my father?
Do not anticipate the future. Help me to stand up and let's go out of here. I've got a lot of work to do. I have to build a new order!!!
As you wish—I'm only fulfilling the will of God!
Wait! I arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of heresy! You will come with us to stand a fair trial and to confess your sins!
Pardon? This must be a mistake. That is to say, I haven't done anything wrong...
You're lying! We've just caught you doing an unholy occult ritual; you've summoned the dead and disturbed their eternal peace—and that's a sin against God Almighty himself! You're arrested!
I haven't done anything like that, you must have made a mistake. You should leave immediately!
Are you trying to oppose us? In that case I have to use force against you. Take him, brothers! To jail with this awful heretic! Or even better—to Hell with him! We'll spare executioner some work!
That's true, but I did so in the interest of Higher Goals, for the protection of the faith and God Almighty!
What a nasty lie! Nobody can commit a crime in the interest of our Creator! Take him, brothers! To jail with this awful heretic! Or even better—to Hell with him! We'll spare executioner some work!
Pardon? There must be some mistake. That is to say, I'm an Inquisitor! And beyond that, I've done nothing wrong...

I knew betrayal was hidden in you, brother! I've known it from the very first moment we met. Thanks to the Providence that my intuition didn't disappoint me and I ordered spies to watch you. Thanks to that I caught you right in the act! You deserve death for your betrayal! The sentence will be carried out immediately!
I doubt it, Grand Master! You will pay with your life for your arrogance!
Hold, Grand Master—this is a misunderstanding! That was a part of my plan how to stop Archbishop Laurencius!
You're a liar, and as a liar you will be punished!
Mercy, Grand Master! Forgive me my mistake... I'll atone for my sins!

Aaaaahhhhh... no... No! NO! This can't be the end... My God... I disappointed you... I wasn't able to stop him... Archangel Gabriel, my Lord, you can see that! You can see what a terrible injustice is happening to Lord God... God, forgive me my weakness... I wasn't able... aaaahhhh...

I knew a betrayal was hidden in you, Father! I've known it from the very first moment we met. Thanks to the Providence that my intuition didn't disappoint me and I ordered spies to watch you. Thanks to that I caught you right in the act! You deserve death for your betrayal! The sentence will be carried out immediately!

I knew a betrayal was hidden in you, sir! I've known it from the very first moment we met. Thanks to the Providence that my intuition didn't disappoint me and I ordered spies to watch you. Thanks to that I caught you right in the act! You deserve death for your betrayal! The sentence will be carried out immediately!
What were the first manifestations of the cult you noticed? How did you find the trace of the enemy?

I think it was the events that occurred before the Scourges of God. That means in the times when nobody comprehended how serious troubles would soon get in the the Realm. First of all, there were several seemingly accidental deaths that brought certain people, I've almost never heard about, into high positions in the Realm. The news was surprising to me, but not surprising enough to pay bigger attention to. Nonetheless, when the Archangel Gabriel himself appeared before me and heralded the arrival of a great evil I began to suspect that something wicked was happening. And the suspicion became much stronger when several of my brothers I entrusted with the investigation of those deaths were assassinated.
Cardinal Commendoni told me you were his friend, Grand Master. Was that true?

Commendoni? That lousy dog in a cleric robe? No, he isn't a friend of mine at all—more to the contrary. He preaches devotedly against the sovereignty of the Brotherhood and is ready to do anything to restrain or to even totally destroy our Order!
Well... interesting.

I must say you surprised me, brother. It's hard to give you any advice in such a case... It seems to me that it's not possible to get the testimony of a dead person. Unless one wants to descend to heresy. Although the idea itself is terrible, I've heard about some cases of heretics being able to talk to the spirits of dead people. But I'm really not the one to help you, brother. But try asking Cardinal Letti, he has better knowledge of those things and has also the necessary insight...
Thank you, dear Grand Master.
Not at all, brother. It's me who must thank you for dealing with the case of the Cult of the Children of the New Order.
Who rules in Alvaron and around?

Grand Duke Drake Lambert is the royal governor of Alvaron. I must say he's probably the best person for that position, although mostly because there's nobody better around. That is to say, nowadays the nobles are very good only in disagreeing with each other and in raising objections against almost anything—especially against the actions of other noble Houses. Fortunately, Drake Lambert is sort of exceptional man, although I have some objections against him too. On the other hand, the chair of the royal vice-governor is totally catastrophically seized by Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. If the Duchess looked after the Realm administration half as much as she looks after her beauty, all of us would live much better...

There's no doubt the Cult of the Children of the New Order is responsible for the most of the crisis. The Realm is so disrupted because of the Cult. Nonetheless, we must do all we can to prevent its blustering. However, I must say that considering all the circumstances including the Star of Doom, Scourges of God and the things written in the Revelation of St. Ezekiel, shiver is running down my spine. I smell the breath of Hell here, by my troth!
I've heard some rumors about preparations for a war. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Yes, I've heard some rumors too. The royal regiments in the whole Realm were put on the alert. Thus, I expected that also the Order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous would be asked to prepare to fight and that some further details would be passed to me. Unfortunately, in the meantime King Edward the Second was murdered and the whole situation became much more complicated because our Order is bound to military duty only to the leader of the Realm and to nobody else. Because of the current situation I don't expect somebody would tell me about current military plans...

The Fallen Angels are the most fearful legionaries of Satan you can imagine, brother. They're the generals of his infernal hordes, the rulers of destructive infernal powers and the devourers of all that's clean. The Scriptures say they're former Angels affected by the God's punishment for their sins, as they had been plotting to betray God Almighty together with Satan the Tempter at the Dawn of Time. The Scriptures further state that they were thrown down to the Earth from the sky and chained in Hell to suffer there for their sins. Since that time they've been trying to get back to seize the rule in both the world and Heaven. Together they're four—Arthamon, the Master of Ruination, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the succubus and fornicatress and the Archangel Azrael, the Satan's Emissary and the Advocate of Evil.

Humans are the most terrible monsters, brother. Be careful who you talk to, what do you say into what ears and to whom do you turn your back. You can be never sure a human won't betray you, stab you in the back or even murder you. When I remember how blindly I trusted Jean de Guise, I can't avoid tears in my eyes...

What has happened in Alvaron lately? Both the city and the whole Realm were shattered by the murder of His Majesty King Edward the Second. I believe most of the people don't realize how terrible the event really was. Now when the King is dead and so is the Royal Heir Prince Louis, the Realm is without the leader. It would be necessary to gather the Realm Assembly and to elect a new ruler among the Nobles. But because of the current state of the Realm I doubt the Assembly would be able to meet in council and that the members would come to an agreement to whom should be given the Scepter. I don't understand at all how the murder could have been committed. It happened in the middle of the royal palace, in the private chambers of His Majesty—and those are the most guarded rooms in the whole Realm!

Prince Louis was murdered two years ago and two royal chamber-maids were accused of the crime. They were charged of witchcraft and consequently burned, at least one of them, because the other one succeed to escape. Nonetheless, there was something very strange about the case—one of the maids accused Royal Advisor Verenicus of the murder. Nobody paid much attention to it at the time because the girl took her accusation back at the torture and confessed she had committed the crime. But since then I can't get rid of the feeling there was something wrong with that case. Maybe it would be good to investigate all those events once more...

Yes, I could imagine quite well that lousy dog in cleric's robes to be a heretic. I've never trusted him too much and when Decretum Inquisitorium was issued and he started to preach against the Brotherhood of the Righteous, I felt betrayal in him. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to get a single ounce of proof. If you have any, brother, don't hesitate to grab him by the throat—no matter if he's the Inquisitor General!
I'm looking for a way how to remove the curse from a stryx. Do you happen to have some advice for me?

How to remove the curse from a stryx? Well... I don't have the slightest idea. I've fought several of those monsters, yes, but I've never tried to remove the curse from any of them. I believe the result can never be as excellent as the legends and tales say. But if you really want to try that, ask the apothecary Thelma Ulthraum—she's wrathful, but still more learned than anybody else!

I know about the case, but I don't know many details. And it seems very strange to me that someone would cooperate with the werewolves. Lycanthropes are known to have a straight, aggressive nature and trying to plot with them usually means certain death. Suddenly somebody—some heretic—willingly opens the city gates for them each full moon and they won't tear him apart. This is very strange...
I'm sorry, but I can't help you, brother...
You should tell me about it, Grand Master. It's not good to hide any facts. Your decision could have serious consequences!
It seems to me there's some problem between us, Master. But I hope you'll think about the matter once again and will see your answer won't bring any harm to anyone.
You're a wise and powerful man, Master. Your answer would really help me a lot...
Oh, really? And who was that man?
I'm not going to tell you.
You don't have to tell me, brother. I know exactly who he was—Jean de Guise, the Seneschal of our Order, my long-time companion in arms and a true friend. Is it true?
Yes, it is. How could you know?

Because it was me who visited you together with him that spring. We decided to entrust you with that case of the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier because we knew the enemy was watching us. We couldn't afford to address the matter ourselves, because we'd show the enemy that way how much we knew and where our steps were headed. For you, the situation was completely different, brother. Nobody knew you; nobody could know what you plan and what were you going to do. Exactly because of that we entrusted you with the case. The only thing I don't understand is why you have come in bad faith instead of joining our forces and trying to stop the enemy whom you probably know better than me now...
Seneschal Jean de Guise.

Yes, I was sure about it. Jean de Guise, the Seneschal of our Order, my long-time companion in arms and a true friend. It was he who visited you together with me that spring. We decided to entrust you with that case of the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier because we knew the enemy was watching us. We couldn't afford to address the matter ourselves because we'd show the enemy that way how much we knew and where our steps were headed. For you the situation was completely different, brother. Nobody knew you; nobody could know what you plan and what were you going to do. Exactly because of that we entrusted you with the case. The only thing I don't understand is why you have come in bad faith instead of joining our forces and trying to stop the enemy whom you probably know better than me now...

The explanation is simple, Grand Master. Jean de Guise told me you were a heretic, gave me the results of his investigation and entrusted me with taking the case to the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition.
WHAT?! What are you talking about, brother? What accusation of heresy? What proofs? And how is Jean de Guise involved in that? Tell me!

Jean de Guise introduced himself to me as the man who had visited me in the beginning of this spring and had entrusted me with the investigation of Kurth Ollmier's death. The Seneschal also told me that he believes you are a member of some plot aiming to disrupt the Realm and gave me the proof that I put forward to the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. The tribunal accused you of heresy and ordered to arrest you.

I don't believe that! I don't believe that my friend and comrade Jean de Guise would do anything even resembling that you've just told me. Sure, it was he who visited you with me in spring, but that's all. I don't understand it at all...
Since I'm not a liar, there're only two possibilities left—either you're a heretic and you're trying to confuse me, or Seneschal Jean de Guise is a traitor. What do you think to be more probable?
Seneschal Jean de Guise and a traitor? No, I don't believe that... what did he tell you?

He told me that he was the leader of a secret group of royalists who swore to defend the Realm against all enemies and that they revealed a plot and that according to their evidence it seemed you were the head of it. I'm sure, you know the rest well enough yourself.

All of that is true, brother. Except for one thing—I'm the head of those royalists, not Seneschal Jean de Guise! He tricked me... betrayed me. He dishonored our Order. There's no doubt about it now. He's the traitor—I've been suspecting for some time that there's a traitor among us. It was him who revealed all our plans to the enemy and who betrayed the names of our helpers. He's guilty of the deaths of a great many people, who were found and slaughtered without mercy. He's the treacherous traitor!
And it seems I trusted him blindly!

There was nothing else you could do, brother. Nobody would be able to see through that falsehood and delusion. That is, the damned traitor knew all that I knew! No doubt he decided deliberately to use you to destroy me. It seems to me the conspirators don't feel strong enough to come out against me openly...
What is really going on here? What of that Seneschal de Guise told me is really true?

I don't know what exactly he told you, brother, but I suppose he didn't have to lie too much. He only changed some facts. Some time ago, when nobody apprehended into how serious troubles the Realm will get soon, a group of royalists faithful to the Crown was created in Ultherst. Some nobles and gentry belonged to the group, as well as the representatives of my Order and also selected priests including some Inquisitors. I formed the group, because the Archangel Gabriel himself appeared before me in his infinite mercy and heralded the arrival of a great evil. Not long after that I found small clues pointing to intrigues spreading throughout the highest political strata. Because of the fact the intrigues concerned all the strata of the society of the Realm I decided to ask some people I fully trusted for help. Thus was formed a group sworn to protect the Crown from any danger irrespective of consequences; even at the cost of the lives of its members.
Go on, Grand Master.

At first we thought somebody was trying to get the power in the Realm into his hands through those intrigues. But soon we started to suspect there was more than a political fight here. The smell of brimstone and heresy was to be scented behind the strange events that seemed to happen without a mutual connection. Meanwhile, the Scourges of God affected the Realm and interrupted the investigation of the plot for some time. Unfortunately, the Scourges of God also overwhelmingly influenced our group—many of our members died, the others disappeared without a trace. Too late did I realize it wasn't an accident but the work of plotters who were precisely organized and well prepared. It was obvious they got to know about us, even though I'm still shocked to realize that it was Seneschal Jean de Guise who betrayed our plans to the enemy and informed him about our comrades. Simply put, the enemy knew everything about us and we knew almost nothing about him.
Apparently. Then you found the trace of the merchant Kurth Ollmier...

Exactly, brother. Thanks to the hand of Providence our spies were able to catch that trace. Kurth Ollmier, renowned adventurer and treasure hunter, was said to be heard talking about a contract that should have brought him fairy-tale riches—in the case the Inquisition wouldn't be able to get him first. It was clear to us that he ran into a powerful item or into a text somebody distinguished was interested in and that the item could be probably turned into a powerful weapon in wrong hands. Thus, we had to find out who was behind that matter at all costs. But we couldn't afford to start looking for Ollmier openly, because we had known the enemy was watching us. At that time I started to suspect there was a traitor among us, because more and more of our followers were dying.
Thus you entrusted me with the case not knowing that Seneschal Jean de Guise was the traitor.

Yes, that's exactly how it was. I thought that if someone unknown dealt with the case and if he acted carefully, our enemy wouldn't notice him an we'd be able to find out to whom Kurth Ollmier sold the item that should have made him so rich. Nevertheless, Kurth Ollmier was murdered in Hillbrandt before we managed to assign you the quest and that's why you went right there. I couldn't have known all my efforts were useless due to the betrayal of Jean de Guise. I dragged you into a dangerous game without the slightest idea the enemy knew about you from the beginning. I'm sorry about that, brother. Frankly, I'm sorry!
No need to apologize, Master. Things are not so bad in the end—I'm here, after all, and I have much information that could help you to finish the general picture of the whole matter.

You're right, brother. The situation is not so bad to give up without a fight. In that case tell me all you were able to find out. As for me, I think I know quite well what's happening in the Realm, but still there're some things I can only guess. For example—whom do we face; who are those damned plotters? And also I'm not sure what exactly they want to achieve with all those intrigues and infernal tricks.

You're facing the Cult of the Children of the New Order, Grand Master. You needn't believe that, but it's true. The Cult wasn't destroyed, as everybody thought, but prevailed to these days to carry out certain Plan—I found a copy of the Plan in Hillbrandt, it belonged to Judge Vallarian.

The Cult of the Children of the New Order, you say? I've heard a lot about it, but to tell the truth only in connection with the history of the world heretic movements and cults. I thought the Pope's Inquisition completely uprooted it and moreover that it was never established firmly in Ultherst. Nonetheless, obviously the Cult has survived till nowadays, strengthened by many hundred years of preparations and merged into all the strata of the society of the Realm. What a scary image. But you have mentioned the Plan of that cult. What's the matter with it?

The aim of the Plan—and at the same time the goal of the efforts of the entire Cult—is releasing Satan from his thousand-year imprisonment. It should be achieved through the summoning of the Fallen Angels—Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie!

Oh my God! The summoning of the Fallen Angels? Releasing Satan from his imprisonment? This is much worse than I anticipated! I'd never think we face someone so wicked, someone with such a terrible goal! And how did you get to know about the Plan?
I found Judge Vallarian's copy—was found out to be a member of the Cult of the Children of the New Order. Later, together with Glatzburg Bishop Trevorius, we deciphered the text...

I've heard about the case. Judge Vallarian was sentenced as a heretic and burned. But I'd have never thought you were behind it, brother. I must admire you because you were able to deal with such a terrible case without the slightest help from us and in addition to reveal the Plan of our enemy. I bow deeply before you! How was you able to investigate the case?

Through Kurth Ollmier, or better to say through his murderers. I found out that the item the poor merchant wanted to sell was the book Libre Daemonium—it had been written by the Cult founder Lucius himself. The rituals necessary to summon the Fallen Angels were described in the book.

So I was right—there really was an item that could become a powerful weapon in the hands of the Cult. However' I'd never think it was something so terrible. It means that the Cult can try to summon the Fallen Angels now and thus to fulfill its Plan! Maybe that's why the heretics decided to go for an open attack on me—they thought they had all the trumps in their hands...

Maybe they really have, Grand Master. There's a suspicion that the two Fallen Angels were already summoned—that is Arthamon and Baphomet. At least the results of my investigation in Hillbrandt and Glatzburg indicate so...

By all the Saints... this is very bad news. I'd have never thought it is possible to summon the Fallen Angels themselves! But if it's really true... in that case not only our Realm is endangered, but the whole faithful world! The true faith is threatened! We must avoid it at all cost, brother. We can't allow the heretics to do such a terrible thing. We must stop them!
I agree. What do you suggest?

We must find out who's the leader of the Cult, the dark High Priest. The one who leads all the actions of the Cult and stands behind its efforts. Only he can tell us the truth about the Fallen Angels. And we could get to him through Jean de Guise. We know he belongs to the Cult and we must use that knowledge. He thought he'd abuse us for his wicked intrigues and instead of that he revealed himself. We must start with him. I believe that if you focus on him, brother, you'll find out the proofs necessary to arrest him. And during the torture he'll testify all, even if you had to squeeze his soul from him! No mercy for that lecherous heretic traitor!
I agree. However, I have one more trace—I learned about it in Glatzburg from Curial Inquisitor Truncquillius...

Cardinal Truncquillius was also a member of the Cult? Oh my God... I wouldn't have guessed it! Should I suppose you were also behind his sentence, brother? You were able to find the proofs of his heresy and to hand him over to justice? Although he was a Curial Inquisitor and Pope's legate? That's admirable... I don't know what to say! I thank the Heavens it was exactly you whom I entrusted with the investigation of the case of Kurth Ollmier. However, could you tell me about the clue? What did you learn from Cardinal Truncquillius? Can we use it for our purposes?
I hope we can, Grand Master. That is, Cardinal had some letters addressed to him from someone here in Alvaron with the instructions how to proceed in the implementation of the Plan.

That's a great news, brother. It's better than I hoped. Those letters are straight proof against a high-ranking member of the Cult. I'm sure they'll help us to find the Dark High Priest himself. But first of all we must find out who wrote those letters. I know one man here in Alvaron who could help us with this problem. The priest Marcius, Archbishop's scribe and illuminator, knows well the handwriting of all the members of Archbishop's diocese including Inquisitor General, Cardinal Commendoni, and most of the nobles of the Realm sitting in the Royal Court. If the author of the letters you've found belongs to these people, Father Marcius will surely recognize his handwriting.
Excellent. I'll start to investigate the case immediately.

Thank you, brother. Unfortunately, I can't help you much with your investigations because my hands are bound by the accusation that was brought against me. But if I could advise you in any way, don't hesitate to turn to me. You'll always find me here in the Citadel, the ancient seat of our Order. It's probably the only safe place where I can take shelter. Furthermore you can always approach Cardinal Gustapho Letti—he's my trusted friend and ally standing by my side from the very beginning. I believe firmly I'm not mistaken in him as I was in Jean de Guise. Give him this letter in which I explain all in detail. And one last thing—if Seneschal Jean de Guise asked you about the progress of the investigation of my person, don't tell him about our meeting and say I'm still avoiding you. We'll circumvent unnecessary troubles this way...
I agree. Farewell for now.

One more thing, brother—if you need someone to help you, ask Father Nicolas. He's an Inquisitorial prosecutor who has bee also standing by my side from the very beginning. And I trust him as well as you or Cardinal Letti.
Could I ask you a few questions before I start the investigation?

But of course, brother. Unfortunately I can't help you much with your investigation, because my hands are bound by the accusation that was brought against me. But if I could advise you in any way, don't hesitate to turn to me. You'll always find me here in the Citadel, the ancient seat of our Order. It's probably the only safe place where I can take shelter. Furthermore you can always approach Cardinal Gustapho Letti—he's my trusted friend and ally, standing by my side from the very beginning. I believe firmly I'm not mistaken in him as I was in Jean de Guise. Give him this letter in which I explain all in detail. One last thing—if Seneschal Jean de Guise asked you about the progress of the investigation of my person, don't tell him about our meeting and say I'm still avoiding you. We'll circumvent unnecessary troubles this way...

One more thing, brother—if you need someone to help you, ask Father Nicolas. He's an Inquisitorial prosecutor who has been also standing by my side from the very beginning. I trust him as well as you or Cardinal Letti. And now ask your questions, brother. I don't want to restrain you from your mission...

I don't believe that! It's impossible! That would mean... denial of the whole doctrine regarding the God's Kingdom on Earth! Are you sure it's really true? Maybe it's some nasty trick or an infernal delusion that was supposed to lead you astray.
No, Grand Master—I can confirm it personally.

In that case the fate of the whole faithful world is in your hands, brother. Do you realize that? You're the only one who stands between this world and Hell! You must stop the Fallen Angels at all costs. You must make them return to the place where they came from!
I'll see what I can do. Could I ask you a few questions now?
We'll see. Farewell for now. Maybe we'll meet again...
Farewell, brother. I'll be praying for you!
Yes, I'd need to talk to you for a moment.
Ask your questions, brother. All my knowledge is at your disposal...
I don't think so, Grand Master. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. I won't stop praying for you!

In the name of the Archangel Gabriel, stand at my side, my faithful ones! Stop this minion of Hell who dared to lay hands on our Order! Punish this unfaithful misbeliever who arrogantly threatens what we swore to protect! May the wraith of God strike him, let him understand the horror of heresy! CHARGE!

Enough of this talking, Grand Master de Malamert. I'm here to put you on trial. I arrest you for the reasonable suspicion of heresy and of conspiring against the King... why are you looking at me this way?
Oh my God, this is impossible! Is that you, brother? Are my eyes betraying me or is it some heretic fabrication?
I don't remember that we've already met, Grand Master.
Sure, of course. I didn't want to tell you who I was that time, to avoid prospective revelation of both you and me...
What are you talking about?

I'm talking about the secret meeting that took place at the beginning of this spring; two men asked you to travel to the town of Hillbrandt in the north of the Realm to investigate there some very strange events regarding the merchant Kurth Ollmier. I suppose you remember the meeting.
And what do you have to do with that?

It was me who approached you that time. Me and one of my companions. It was me who asked you to put your mind into the case of the merchant Kurth Ollmier. I selected you among the dozens of adepts and entrusted you with the case...
I don't believe a word from what you've told me!
You don't believe me?! In that case tell me how I could know what was that meeting about. And how I could know you if we never met each other.
I don't know, I'm at a loss a bit. That is to say, not long ago I met a man who told me he was the one who approached me that time in spring...
To tell the truth I'm at a loss a bit. That is to say, not long ago I met a man who told me he was the one who approached me that time in spring...

I'm so glad to see you, brother! You're the only hope left for our Realm. I hope you made some progress in the searching for the Dark High Priest of the Cult of the Children of the New Order. Can I offer you some advice or can I otherwise help you in your mission?
I'd need to talk to you, Grand Master.
But of course, brother. I'll gladly answer all your questions. Just ask.
No, I don't think so. I just happened to come by.
I'm glad you came to see me, brother. Stay in the Citadel as long as you want, you need some rest. You're safe here... at least for now.
I found out that the Dark High Priest of the Cult is Cardinal Commendoni, Grand Master.

Cardinal Commendoni? The Inquisitor General of the Holy Office? By all the Saints, this is terrible news! Can you imagine, brother, what terrible crimes could he have committed in his position? What did you do with him? Is he arrested?
He's dead. He refused to give up and I had to kill him.

Zounds... I didn't expect that. You're really... well... effective, I must say. You've reached admirable results. I'm glad you're on our side. I wouldn't like to oppose you one day. But tell me; was that the end of the whole Cult? Was it crushed to the last man? Is the Realm in no more danger?

It's hard to say, Grand Master. According to the results of the investigation the Cult of the Children of the New Order might have summoned the Fallen Angels who could be now dwelling in our world. At this time I'm investigating that suspicion.

I can't believe that! It's impossible! That would mean... denial of the whole doctrine regarding the God's Kingdom on Earth! I'll be praying for you to be successful to disprove that suspicion, brother!
I believe you can accomplish it! I have faith in you. But now tell me, is there something I could do to help you? Maybe answer some questions?
Yes, that would be great.
In that case ask your questions, brother. What do you need to know?
No, I don't think so.
Farewell in that case, brother. May God protect you!

I can't say that, Grand Master. It seems the Cult of the Children of the New Order summoned the Fallen Angels who are now dwelling in our world and threaten to release Satan from his thousand-year imprisonment!

Hail to you, brother. Have you done some progress in the investigation of the Fallen Angels? Were you able to disprove the suspicion about their invocation by the Cult of the Children of the New Order?
No, not yet, Grand Master.
Never mind, brother. I'm sure you'll be successful soon. Till that time we must pray it isn't true. Is there something I can do for you?
I have a bad news for you, Grand Master—the Fallen Angels were really summoned!
I'm so glad to see you alive, brother. I've been praying for the success of your efforts. The Fallen Angels must return to the place they came from!
I agree with you, Grand Master. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to destroy all the Fallen Angels yet.
Never mind, brother. I'm sure you're doing everything that a common mortal can do. Certainly you'll be successful in the end. Is there something I could do to help you in your effort?
The Fallen Angels are back in Hell, Grand Master. I succeeded in destroying all of them!

By the Archangel Gabriel... you'll never stop to amaze me, brother! You simply come and tell me that you faced the Fallen Angels and sent all of them back to burning Hell! Brother, I bow before you. You deserve the deepest respect. Again and again you've proven the Realm has a steady reliance in you!
I'm glad it had such a good ending. Thus, all the plans of the Cult of the Children of the New Order should be thwarted, right?
I wish it were so. The Realm could never gain its former grandeur if the plans for its ruination still existed. But now tell me, can I help you somehow?

The Fallen Angels are back in Hell, Grand Master. However, I've a bad news for you—the spies of Cardinal Letti spotted Archbishop Laurencius entering the Royal Burial Chamber. It seems the Archbishop was hiding his true face from the world!

What do you want to say? Archbishop Laurencius and a heretic? Oh my God! This damned plot seems to be rooted much deeper than we expected... Where will be the end of this all? Isn't there anybody but heretics living in the Realm?
It's hard to say, Grand Master. However, as for Archbishop Laurencius, I'll find out what he is trying to achieve...
Thank you, brother. You've done so much for the Realm and for the God's Kingdom on Earth that I'll never be able to pay make it up to you. Could I help you somehow in your efforts?
I'm so glad to see you, brother! Your heroic deeds returned the hope of quick recovery to the Realm. What can the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous do for you?
That's why I'm here, brother. What's on your mind?
Nothing at the moment, Grand Master. Thank you.
If you think so, brother. Farewell. May the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you on your journeys!
I've a bad news for you, Grand Master. The spies of Cardinal Letti spotted Archbishop Laurencius entering the Royal Burial Chamber. It seems the Archbishop was hiding his true face from the world!

What do you want to say? Archbishop Laurencius and a heretic? Oh my God! This damned plot seems to be rooted much deeper than we expected... I thought the whole matter ended by the defeat of the Fallen Angels. Isn't there anybody but heretics living in the Realm?
I'm so glad to see you, brother! Tell me, have you succeeded in stopping Archbishop Laurencius and his wicked plans already? Have you found out what was he trying to do?
Unfortunately not yet, Grand Master.
In that case you should better hurry, brother. Although you're doing more that a common mortal could do, Archbishop Laurencius must be stopped, no matter what he is trying to achieve!
I'll do all I can. But now I'd need your advice.
You can rely on me, Grand Master. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. May the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you!
What conditions do I have to meet to be appointed a Seneschal of the order, Grand Master?

Only a Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous may become a Seneschal of the Brotherhood, and only if he proves his utter loyalty to God and the King and completes a task that is assigned to him. Moreover, he has to prove his courage in fighting and kill more than half a thousand infernal enemies!
I would like to become a Seneschal of the Brotherhood.

I'll be glad to appoint you a Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, brother. I hope you're sufficiently ready for the task I have to assign to you as a test. I won't hide that it will be a very demanding task. You'll have to clarify the murder of His Majesty King Edward II. If you manage to find his murderer and prove your exceptional bravery by killing more than half a thousand hellspawns, you'll become a Seneschal of the Order.
You're welcome, brother. Personally, I sincerely wish you success—it's a crime that CANNOT be left unpunished in any circumstances! The murder of the King of the Realm... that's unimaginable!

If I am informed correctly, King Edward was found dead by his chamberlain Trisstan in the evening several days ago. Apparently there was a fight because the furniture was scattered all around the room. It's obvious the King fought back against his murderer. That's all we've managed to find out.
I've exposed the murderer of His Majesty Edward II, Grand Master. May I inform you about the result of my investigation?
But certainly, brother! That's great news—the murderers of His Majesty are exposed! Tell me, who's the culprit? Who has the death of our leader on his conscience?

The First Knight? I really didn't expect that... Why, the main task of the First Knight has always been to protect the Crown and the Realm! How could he? I'm really shocked. It seems Satan is able to worm into the thinking of every man... It's terrible to imagine! But tell me what evidence have you got against him?

The royal chamberlain Trisstan has witnessed the murder and identified the First Knight with certainty. Moreover I got the testimony of Cardinal Gustapho Letti to whom the First Knight confessed his terrible secret. Furthermore, I managed to find out that the King wounded his murderer in the last fight. The First Knight has some scratches on his face and he's silent about how he got them. And finally, under the weight of all those proofs Rodrigo de Velacor has confessed to the crime.

Fascinating! You managed to prove him guilty and force him to confess in a really admirable way! You've carried out your task, brother—and with excellence! But to be appointed a Seneschal you also have to prove your exceptional qualities in fighting. Did you kill more than half a thousand hellspawns?
I've proven my courage in fight and killed more than a half thousand infernal enemies, Grand Master.
I have proven my courage already. More than a half thousand infernal enemies are back in Hell or on their way there...

Excellent! By your courage in fighting you've proven you deserve to be appointed a Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Congratulations, brother! Accept this item as the symbol of your new office. And herewith I give you the key of the Alvaron chapter where you're now allowed to enter!
What are you doing, brother—you're not going to steal from your own friends, are you?!

I must say you surprised me, Father. It's hard to give you any advice in such a case... It seems to me that it's not possible to get the testimony of a dead person. Unless one wants to descend to heresy. Although the idea itself is terrible, I've heard about some cases of heretics being able to talk to the spirits of dead people. But I'm really not the one to help you, Father. But try asking Cardinal Letti, he has better knowledge of those things and has also the necessary insight...
Not at all, Father. It's me who must thank you for dealing with the case of the Cult of the Children of the New Order.

The Fallen Angels are the most fearful legionaries of Satan you can imagine, Father. They're the generals of his infernal hordes, the rulers of destructive infernal powers and the devourers of all that's clean. The Scriptures say they're former Angels affected by the God's punishment for their sins, as they had been plotting to betray God Almighty together with Satan the Tempter at the Dawn of Time. The Scriptures further state that they were thrown down to the Earth from the sky and chained in Hell to suffer there for their sins. Since that time they've been trying to get back to seize the rule in both the world and Heaven. Together they're four—Arthamon, the Master of Ruination, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the succubus and fornicatress and the Archangel Azrael, the Satan's Emissary and the Advocate of Evil.

Humans are the most terrible monsters, Father. Be careful who you talk to, what do you say into what ears and to whom do you turn your back. You can be never sure a human won't betray you, stab you in the back or even murder you. When I remember how blindly I trusted Jean de Guise, I can't avoid tears in my eyes...

Yes, I could imagine quite well that lousy dog in cleric's robes to be a heretic. I've never trusted him too much and when Decretum Inquisitorium was issued and he started to preach against the Brotherhood of the Righteous, I felt betrayal in him. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to get a single ounce of proof. If you have any, Father, don't hesitate to grab him by the throat—no matter if he's the Inquisitor General!
I'm sorry, but I can't help you, Father...

No mercy for that lecherous heretic traitor!

Together they're four—Arthamon, the Master of Ruination, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the succubus and fornicatress and the Archangel Azrael, the Satan's Emissary and the Advocate of Evil.

All right, I'll help you to find your grave, wandering soul. What was your name during your life?
Baron Martin Mansfeld, if I remember it correctly. Yes, I was Baron Mansfeld.
In that case let's go, Baron. We'll find your grave and put you to eternal sleep again. But don't you try to betray me, do you understand?
You can rely on me, knight. And thank you. I'm looking forward to be dead again. It's good to be dead, when you've already died...
Maybe I could help you to find your grave, wandering soul. Nonetheless it depends on what you would give me for my help.

It's hard to say... I don't have much to give you because I'm dead and dead can't have any estates—it's an ancient legal principle. But I could tell you where I buried most of my belongings during my life. Well, I didn't want it to get into the hands of my relatives, as they were a bunch of freeloaders and idlers.
Did you expect me to believe you this devilish trick, you hellspawn? Well, you expected wrong! I'll send you back to the Other World!
Oh... really? That would be very nice of you. And I mean it.
I'm sorry, but you will have to solve your problem on your own, Baron. I've more important mission than to look for your grave. Farewell!
Well, what can I do... I'll try to find it myself in that case. I was so well in my grave...
Hello, is there anybody there? Could you help me, please? I can't get back...
Oh my God... who are you, you monster of Hell?

It's hard to say... because I don't recognize myself. My body is decaying, white bones can be seen everywhere, my clothing turned into moldering rags... But I used to be a noble! I prided myself with an aristocratic title, I had a large manor and everybody worshiped me. But it was a long time ago... When I was alive... I remember very well that I died. I was laying in my bed and all of a sudden there was light at the end of a tunnel and nothing after it. And then at once I awoke—lying in my coffin and I didn't feel well at all. When I succeeded to get out of it, I was terrified, because I found out I was... dead!
Yes, it seems so. It looks like you have returned from the Other World...

Yes, I probably did. But I don't like it. You know—it wasn't so bad to be dead. Except for the fact that I was... dead, of course. I don't know why I was awakened. But I don't like it at all. I want to get back to my grave. But I don't know which one is mine. My eyes aren't what they used to be. Probably because I don't have any.
What a trick of Hell is that? Are you trying to outwit me? I can see from the first sight that you're undead!

Yes, probably I am. But I'm not going to trick you, knight. I'm trying to... find my lost peace again. Eternal peace, if you understand me. It wasn't bad—except for the fact I was dead, of course. I don't know why I was awakened. But I don't like it at all. I want to get back to my grave. But I don't know which one is mine. My eyes aren't what they used to be. Probably because I don't have any.
You can rely on me, Father. And thank you. I'm looking forward to be dead again. It's good to be dead, when you've already died...

You can rely on me, dear sir. And thank you. I'm looking forward to be dead again. It's good to be dead, when you've already died...
