I don't know why I was awakened. But I don't like it at all. I want to get back to my grave. But I don't know which one is mine. My eyes aren't what they used to be. Probably because I don't have any.

I'm so glad... I've been already afraid I'd never return back. For your effort I'll tell you where you can find most of the money I saved during my life. I decided to hide it to prevent my relatives from inheriting it—they were a bunch of freeloaders and idlers! You'll find the treasure in a big old stub near the place of execution. I'll draw you a map, it'll help you to find it.
Thank you, Baron.

You're welcome, knight. It would be of no use to me anyway. And now—if you will excuse me—I'm going to lie down in my grave again and I'm going to sleep... and sleep... and sleep... Good night, sir knight...
May nobody disturb your eternal sleep, Baron. Rest in peace. Amen.
I think we have found it, Baron Mansfeld. This should be your grave.
Oh, really? Oh yes, it seems so. But the gravestone is missing... someone must have stolen it! Those nitwits! I can't rest in peace without my gravestone, knight. We must find it!
Calm down, Baron, I have the stone with me. I'll place it on your grave... Well, it's ready!
Calm down, Baron, we'll find the stone.
We must find it, knight. I can't fall asleep without it...
Well, Baron Mansfeld, we're near your grave and we have also that lost gravestone. I'll place it at your grave... Well, it's ready! Our common journey ends here.
You're welcome, Father. It would be of no use to me anyway. And now—if you excuse me—I'm going to lay in my grave again and I'm going to sleep... and sleep... and sleep... Good night, Father...
Oh, really? Oh yes, it seems so. But the gravestone is missing... someone must have stolen it! Those nitwits! I can't rest in piece without my gravestone, Father. We must find it!
We must find it, Father. I can't fall asleep without it...
You're welcome, sir. It would be of no use to me anyway. And now—if you excuse me—I'm going to lie down into my grave again and I'm going to sleep... and sleep... and sleep... Good night, sir...
Oh, really? Oh yes, it seems so. But the gravestone is missing... someone must have stolen it! Those nitwits! I can't rest in peace without my gravestone, sir. We must find it!
We must find it, sir. I can't fall asleep without it...
If what the zombie of Baron Mansfeld said was true, his money should be located under this stone where he decided to hide it from his heirs. I only hope there isn't any infernal trap set here.
By all the Saints... the treasure is really here! Baron didn't lie... all his belongings are here! Gold, gems, magic items... Thanks, Baron—this is quite a worthy reward!
I've learned that you were a secret lover of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. Is that true?

What are you saying, son? That I'm a lover of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert? The wife of Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of the city? Are you mad? I'm a priest—I'm committed to celibate because of my service to God! How could I descend to something as awful as fornication? You've offended me. And the one who told you that is a foul liar!
So you've never committed wild pervert fornication with the Grand Duchess in the city cemetery? Although an eye-witness saw you there...
In the city cemetery...? Well... an eye-witness, you say? Whom exactly do you have in mind, son?
That's none of your business—I'm not going to tell you the name.

Damned! I knew I'd get into troubles because of that... But she urged me so much that I succumbed to her. She's a mad insatiable nympho, and all the time she's avid for new perversities! I couldn't... I wasn't able... It was stronger than me! Please, swear, son, that you won't tell anybody! Please! That would destroy me, and I have such far-going plans...
Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth.

I should have thought that! That woman would do anything to do harm to Grand Duchess Liana. Damn! I knew I'd get into troubles because of that... But she urged me so much that I succumbed to her. She's a mad insatiable nympho and she's always avid for new perversities! I couldn't... I wasn't able... It was stronger than me! Please, swear, son, that you won't tell anybody! Please! That would destroy me, and I have such far-going plans...

It depends on what you want to buy, son. Leon van den Brooks has his renowned armory here in Alvaron. Thelma Ulthraum the apothecary and Alberto Kelley, Master Alchemist, will sell you potions and various magic goods. Both William Burton the landlord and Salena Flock the innkeeper have shops with various goods to sell.

No doubt Christoffer de Malamert really is a heretic and godless man as most people think. So all of us are afraid of the future, because when the highest representative of the Brotherhood of the Righteous can be a heretic, how far can this matter go?

I'm afraid I don't know about the Fallen Angels more than you already know yourself, my son. That is, I know they're former Angels who were struck down by the God's punishment for their sins which they committed at the Dawn of Time—together with Satan the Tempter they plotted to betray God Almighty. The Scripture says they were thrown down to the Earth and chained in Hell to suffer there for their sins. Since then they've been trying to get back to seize the control over the world and over the Heavens. If I remember correctly, there's four of them—Arthamon, the Master of Ruination, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Succubus and Fornicatress and the Archangel Azrael, the Devil's Emissary and the Advocate of Evil.
I'm very sorry, son, but I don't suspect anybody of heresy at the time.

I don't know if you've heard about it, but no doubt the cases of grave and burial chambers robberies have been recently multiplying. Unfortunately, nobody knows what sacrilegious fools dared to commit something as woeful as that, but surely it's the work of some infamous heretics. And in addition to that their diablerie has horrible consequences—many living dead who make trouble at the cemetery were woken up right because of them!
I'm really sorry, but I don't know anything about the case that could help you to capture the offender. I've only heard that his death was caused by some unknown witch living in Schwarzwald...

I'm sorry, but I really don't have any idea where could Juhasz Gotherr or some of his minions be hiding. People say that from time to time some of them have been seen in the streets of this city—during dark nights, of course. But it's possible he's been far behind the frontier for a long time already...

If someone has been missing lately around Alvaron, surely it's because of the werewolves. They tear to pieces anybody they run into. And if the werewolves are not responsible, surely it is some other infernal vermin, as there's a lot of them in every corner of the Realm nowadays...
I've heard about the violation of Grand Duchess Liana, but there's nothing I can tell you about it, because I don't know any information proving or disproving her statement.

Have you heard the tale about Wolfenburg, the mansion of wolf-prince Wulfhyrr? According to the ancient chronicles Wolfenburg has been a House residence of Lords of Wolfenburg since 7th century. Members of the House were infamous for the cruelty with which they treated their tenants from the beginning. It's said that wolf-prince Wulfhyrr is the last member of that House. Though in those times his name was Duke Ronald and his cruelty was even greater than that of his ancestors. One day he reputedly violated certain young beautiful witch, who lived in the neighborhood of his mansion, and raped her brutally.
I'd advise you to think again about your negative approach, Father. You can never know what kind of accident could happen to you...
Answer my question, please. I'm being honest with you.
You're one of the wisest and most experienced clerics in the archdiocese, Father. Your answer would help me a lot.
I understand. Could I help you somehow in this matter?

No, that won't be necessary. I'm sure brother Sefrenius is coming any moment. Please, once again accept my apology for the misunderstanding. How can I help you? I don't recognize your face, so you probably don't belong to our diocese, do you?
Yes, that's true. However, if I can ask something from you, I'd like to know who you are.
But of course, it should have crossed my mind immediately that you wouldn't know who I was. My name is Marcius and I'm Archbishop's scribe and illuminator.
Archbishop's scribe and illuminator? What do you do in you function?

I work for Archbishop Laurencius as his personal scribe and I'm also entrusted with the administration of the Archbishop's Library and Archive, and at the same time I'm a notable illuminator of newly created books. It means that I decorate the books by hand-painted pictures. The highest quality, of course—I'm a pupil of the Masters of the Pope's Office—of Framonico de Giorno and of Machiavellius Tenerrius!
I'm glad that I've found you, Father. I'd like to approach you with a certain issue...
Nice to meet you, Father. I'm honored to meet someone as important as the Archbishop's scribe.

Oh, really? I'm glad you say it... It's true that my work is very important and in a way I'm crucial for the Archbishop's Office. Without me and my abilities neither the Archbishop's correspondence nor the Archive would be in such a good order.
I'm sure about that. Could I ask you some questions now, Father?
Of course, ask your questions. I'll answer you gladly—if I'll be able to answer.
Yes, I'm sure about that. But now excuse me, please, I'll have to go. Nice to have met you.
I'm glad to have met you too, son. Farewell.
Here they are. As I said, I need to find out who's the author. And as for the content of those letters, you should better forget about it immediately after you recognize the handwriting...
I don't have them on me at the moment.
Well... in that case bring them to me when you'll have them.
Surely, I will. Now answer some question for me.
As you wish, son. But be brief, I'd like to devote myself to that ring you brought to me. I must examine the powers with which it is blessed.
All right. Farewell for now.
What's the matter? What exactly do you have in mind, son? Do you need my help?

Just so. Certain incriminating letters got into my hands and I need to find out who wrote them. I know for sure the letters were sent from the city. And I've heard that you know the handwriting of all the distinguished people here in Alvaron...
Well... you've heard right. However, I'm not sure if I should deal with your letters. Times are bad and I could happen to expose myself to certain... danger.
It's a service to God, Father. And as a servant of God you can't deny a request from a humble faithful.

Yes, I know it well. But I know as well that the service to God would be of no use to my dead body. However, I don't want to get you angry, dear son, and I'll look at your letters. But, well, you know... scratch my back and I'll scratch yours...
All right, I agree. What would you want in return?
Have I heard well? Do you really want something in return? Do you really want to traffic in the duties to which we're committed through the service to God?
Call it as you want, son—service, favor, tithe, bribe... whatever. But one thing is sure—if you won't do what I want you to do I won't even look at your precious letters.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to traffic in anything like that. If necessary, I'll make you to cooperate another way!
If you think so, son. However, I'm sure that you won't succeed. So when you change your mind, come to me and I'll tell you what I want you to do. Farewell for now.

What? You want to tell me you really... found that ring? My God, it's really that ring! Good Heavens... with the help of this ring I'll surely be able to rise and to become a Bishop! I can't believe it...
As you can see, Father, I've fulfilled my part of our agreement. It's your turn now.
No, son, I don't think so. I got the ring and that's enough for me. I'm not going to be involved in the things that aren't my business!
Wait a moment! We had an agreement!
Oh yes, sure... I was just kidding, I'm sorry. It's because I'm so glad the ring of Archbishop Martroiani came to my hands. Well, show me your letters.
What? This is a betrayal! You'll pay for it with your life!
Wait, calm down, son... I was just kidding, I'm sorry. It's because I'm so glad the ring of Archbishop Martroiani came to my hands. Well, show me your letters.

Maybe you've heard, son, that before our current Archbishop Laurencius came to the Office, Archbishop Martroiani was the head of the Holy Mother Church of the Ultherst Nation here. He died under relatively unclear circumstances, but that's not important for our business. He was buried in a sepulcher in the Royal cemetery with all the symbols of his office. Among those symbols was also a mighty ring-like relic, renowned in the whole Realm for giving Martroiani the knowledge of all the world languages. And I can't deny I need such knowledge too.
All right, I'll bring you the ring, although it's an awful grave robbery.

Excellent! I knew we'd come to an agreement, son. But be careful when fulfilling this assignment. The sepulcher is full of planted traps, the Royal Cemetery has been under the control of dark powers for several years, and nobody can say what could be hiding in the sepulcher itself. I don't want anybody to blame me for your death.
Don't be afraid, I can take care of myself. But now answer me a few questions, please.
But of course, ask your questions. I'll answer you gladly—in the case I'm able to answer.
We have an agreement. Farewell.
Farewell, son. I hope you'll bring me soon what I wanted from you. The sooner you will, the sooner I'll tell you who was the author of those letters.
Have I understood correctly you want that ring from me? In that case you can have it—here you are! I wrenched it free from the dead grip of Archbishop Martroiani himself.
I knew it! I knew I'd get into troubles because of that! I wish I've never met you!
Do you know the handwriting? Do you know who's the author of those letters?
Of course I know the handwriting! That is to say, I'm the Archbishop's scribe. How could I not know it?
Who is the author then? Who wrote those wicked heretic texts?
When I take account of the elegant style of the handwriting, its slope, the way how the capitals are written... there's no doubt the author is—God forgive me—Inquisitor General Commendoni!
Do you really mean it? Are you sure? Couldn't you make a mistake?

No, son, I'm sure. This is the handwriting of the Inquisitor General, unless it's a really perfect fake, but I doubt it is. The illustrative way of capital writing, handwriting of a lefthander, the same slope in all rows... it is as I've just said. Oh my God... Cardinal Commendoni is a heretic! Good Heavens... what will we do now?
It's my problem what I'll do, Father. But you should better forget immediately what you've witnessed here and don't allude even to a single word when speaking with anybody else. Do you understand?

No need to tell me twice about that, son. I know well what could happen to me in the case I'd let it out. You should better leave immediately and we'd better try to look like we have been only praying here together for the salvation of our Realm.
I agree. But before I leave, answer a few questions for me, please.
All right, ask your questions. But try to be brief, the less people can see us together the better.
I agree. Farewell.
I won't speak my mind, you can trust me. Though only in the case that Grand Duchess Liana Lambert will take back her accusation of Father Nicolas!

I understand. In that case—tell her that if she won't take back that funny accusation, I'll go myself straight to her husband and I'll tell him everything... that his beloved wife tricked him behind his back...
Yes, that's EXACTLY what I'll do. But if she will refuse, well...
She won't refuse, believe me. She would rather die than lose her position; she's been working for many years to achieve it.
I hope so.
You're here at last, son. Have you brought those books I asked you for from the scriptorium? I've yet some work planned for today...
This is probably a mistake, Father. You didn't ask me for any books.

Not yet, Father. What books should I have brought?
You forgot what books I wanted? Well, of course I wanted... but wait a moment, you're not brother Sefrenius!
No, really I'm not him.
In that case I'm sorry, son. I thought you were brother Sefrenius. I asked him to bring me several books from the Archbishop's scriptorium and he haven't brought them yet...
I'm not your servant to bring you any books!
What?! What do you mean by that!? I didn't... but wait a moment, you're not brother Sefrenius!
Oh, son, it's you again. What do you need?
I'd like to ask you for help in a certain matter...
I thought I'd ask you a few questions, Father.
A few questions? Well... we'll see. Ask your questions.
Nothing in fact, I just happened to come by. Farewell.
Hail to you, son. Do you bring me what I asked you for? Were you able to get that ring?
No, I haven't brought the ring yet. Hold on.
I understand. Why do you seek me then?
I happened to come by so I decided to go to see you...
That's nice of you. But it would be much nicer if you'd bring me that ring. Go and try to get it. It's in your interest too...
I brought you the ring. Here you are.
Hail to you, son. Have you changed your mind as regards that favor we talked about?
No, there's nothing to talk about!
I understand. I understand that. However, I don't understand why have you sought me then?
I happened to come by so I thought I could ask you whether you didn't change your mind as regards providing of your services to me voluntarily...
I'll provide my services to you voluntarily, son—as soon as I'll get your service. Go away and think about it. It's in your interest too...
Yes, I've changed my mind. What's the matter?
Hail to you, son. Have you brought me those letters, whose author you need to identify so urgently?
No, I haven't brought the letters yet. Hold on.
Well, it's neither my problem nor my business. You are the one who wants to identify those letters. Why have you sought me then?
That's very nice of you. If there's nothing else on your mind, leave me and let me study the ring of Archbishop Martroiani.
I brought those letters. Here they are.
Welldicore, tuther. Sinquer doen, giorme. Canthelum, fuirmoso. Biendicone, aminni. Al haab djinhaad, uthoor!
What? I don't understand you, Father. What foreign language is this?

Not one foreign language, son, but several of them. Lochlandish, Aquitanian, Salmondish, ancient Lateran and even Jad-habaalish. As you can see, the ring of Archbishop Martroiani provided me with the knowledge of many foreign languages—I would have to spend the rest of my life to learn them all otherwise. However, you're probably not interested in that. Tell me then, why did you come to me? Haven't you caused enough trouble to me already?
As you wish. But be brief. You can never know who's watching you right this moment.
Well, I don't have any good reason, Father. I just happened to come by.
I understand. In that case please excuse me, I must address my issues. And next time you better think if you really need to talk to me. Farewell.
What do you need, son? Why have you decided to pay me a visit? I don't think you want to hear about my improvement in Baldorian. Well, what do you want?
I came to ask you a few questions. And answer me in Ultherst, all right?
As you wish, son. But be brief. You never know who's watching you right this moment.
Nothing in fact. I'd be better going...
Yes, that will be the best. And next time you better think if you really need to talk to me. As the Baldors say: Bismen dix alfoatium de werdis, frasmoni! Farewell.

A noble man steals?! It's hard to believe that! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry are thieves! Shame!
You will die! You are going to die, fool, for awaking me from my eternal sleep! Your death will be my deliverance! You will die!
I'm sorry, Your Excellency. I didn't want to wake you up from your eternal sleep. I'm sorry!
There's no place for being sorry now, sinner! You will die for your daring!
Wait, Your Excellency. We surely can come to some agreement!
You can't bargain with death, sinner! You will be punished for your arrogance and sky-high impudence!
No infernal monster from the Other World will be trying to take my life!
Your life is long forfeit, sinner! You will be punished for your arrogance and sky-high impudence!
The name carved into the tombstone suggests this is the grave of late Archbishop Martroiani.
I'd rather not disturb his eternal peace...
I'll look what is hidden inside his grave...

Oh, look at that! There's a beautiful ring with a large gemstone on the Archbishop's finger. I should better take it to custody or someone might steal it. These times are so desperate that thieves would not hesitate to do absolutely anything...
In that case I'm lucky—I need his ring for brother Marcius. I hope the deceased Archbishop wouldn't mind me taking it for the good cause...
Baroness?
What Baroness?
You've just said you didn't see the Baroness that night. What Baroness didn't you see?
Oh shit...
So you have two choices, good man. Either you'll tell me all you know, or I'll arrest you and put you to torture. What seems better to you?

Damned! All right, I'll tell you everything, knight. No need to torture me. The night when the merchant Ollmier was murdered I caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan climbing down from the window of his room in the town inn. I didn't know what to say, but before I could open my mouth and ask what was going on she gave me a pouch of gold coins. And I was to get much more soon if I were silent about her nightly affair. I thought she was just cheating on her husband, Baron Robert van Gallagan. It didn't cross my mind that there could be something worse going on. The merchant Ollmier wasn't found dead until the next day.
I'm glad you told it to me, soldier. And go make a confession as soon as possible.
I'm glad the truth has come out at last, soldier. But do you realize you lied to a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?
Oh... I... I didn't mean it. I was confused!
And you will be much more because you are going to spend the rest of your life in a musty cell. That will wean you off lying to the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
Mercy, knight! I won't lie any more! I'll change my ways!
Alright, I believe you. Farewell.
In that case give me the gold given to you by Baroness Linda van Gallagan. It will be a token of your penance!
But that... You can't... Oh my God... Alright, here it is. Just leave me alone, please!
From that old rummy? What did he tell you? I doubt anything of it is true.
He confessed that you caught a person climbing out of the window of the merchant Kurth Ollmier's room in the Hillbrandt inn just the night when the merchant was murdered. Is it true?
What? It's the first time I hear something like that. I don't know what Flitz pursues by this, but when I meet him I will break those crippled legs of his.
I don't know... It seems strange. Don't lie to me! Did you really see anyone that night?
I don't lie, knight, I swear! I didn't see the Baroness that night!
So you didn't see anyone that night?
Why, I'm telling you I didn't see the Baroness that night!

Good day, knight. I heard you've arrived in the town. I hope you will soon catch all those heretical mongrels who have all that mess around here on their conscience. And you will be surprised how many of them are here in Hillbrandt.
Do you suspect someone?
Well, I wouldn't like to harm anyone, but I've seen what I've seen. I can't change that.
And what was it you saw?

The night the orcs broke into the town during their insidious attack I stood guard at the Upper gate. It was terribly cold, so I went to the fire from time to time to warm myself up a little. Perhaps because of it I didn't see anyone sneaking along the stockade and stealthily opening the gate. And behind it there were hordes of green skins ready to attack. Before we were able to recover from the shock and raise an alarm they burst inside and were running through the town.
Did you recognize the person who opened the town gate?
Yes, knight. It was Master Edmond d'Arvias. Although he disappeared in darkness immediately, I was able to recognize him. It was him—I would put my shirt on it!
So you're telling me Master Edmond d'Arvias is a heretic and an idolarer?!
I know well what I saw, knight. Although it was night I was looking at him in the firelight for a while as clearly as I see you now. I'm telling you, it was him!
Thank you, soldier. It's a helpful testimony.
You're welcome, knight. Farewell
Wait a moment. I'd like to ask you one more thing. I need to verify an information I have from a beggar named Flitz...
Tell me more about Master d'Arvias. What do you know about him?

He is the superior of the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He really is somebody. I've always thought him to be a devout man pursuing only his mission—which is to keep an eye on justice. I thought he was that sort of a pious man with a clear mind. I'd never thought he might be a heretic, knight. But these are strange times, then why strange things couldn't happen even among the knights of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, am I right? No offense, knight...
Hello, knight. I hope all orcs will soon be hanging on the trees all around. And those damned heretics sticking together with them as well.
May I speak with you for a moment? I need to verify an information I have from a beggar named Flitz...
Tell me again, soldier, what did you witness the night the merchant Kurt Ollmier was murdered?

How many times do I have to repeat it to you? I'd rather forget it once and for all. I caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan climbing down from the window of the merchant's room in the town inn. I didn't know what to say, but before I could open my mouth and ask what was going on she gave me a pouch of gold coins. And I was to get much more soon if I were silent about her nightly affair. I thought she was just cheating on her husband, Baron Robert van Gallagan. It didn't cross my mind that there could be something worse going on. I didn't get to know the merchant Ollmier was murderer until the next day.
Could you repeat what you saw during the night the orcs assaulted the town?
As I've already told you—I saw Master Edmond d'Arvias when he stealthily opened the town gate and allowed the green skins inside. How many times do I have to repeat it to you?
Watch your words when speaking with me!
Eh... sorry. But it's not easy to repeat such a testimony again and again when it concerns a man able to behead three men with a single strike of his sword.

Damned! All right, I'll tell you everything, Father. No need to torture me. The night when the merchant Ollmier was murdered I caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan climbing down from the window of his room in the town inn. I didn't know what to say, but before I could open my mouth and ask what was going on she gave me a pouch of gold coins. And I was to get much more soon if I were silent about her nightly affair. I thought she was just cheating on her husband, Baron Robert van Gallagan. It didn't cross my mind that there could be something worse going on. The merchant Ollmier wasn't found dead until the next day.
I'm glad the truth has come out at last, soldier. But do you realize you lied to the inquisitor, son?
And you will be much more because you are going to spend the rest of your life in a musty cell. That will wean you off lying to the Holy Inquisition!
Mercy, Father! I won't lie any more! I'll change my ways!
I don't lie, Father, I swear! I didn't see the Baroness that night!

Good day, Father. I heard you've arrived in the town. I hope you will soon catch all those heretical mongrels that have on their conscience all that mess around here. And you would be surprised how many of them are here in Hillbrandt.
Yes, Father. It was Master Edmond d'Arvias. Although he disappeared in darkness immediately, I was able to recognize him. It was him—I would put my shirt on it!
Are you really sure it was master Edmond d'Arvias?
Although it was night I was looking at him in the firelight for a while so clearly as I see you now. I'm telling you, it was him!
You're welcome, Father. Farewell

He is the superior of the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He really is somebody. I've always thought him to be a devout man pursuing only his mission—which is to keep an eye on justice. I thought he is that sort of pious man with clear mind. I'd never think he might be a heretic, Father. But these are strange times, so why strange things couldn't happen even among the knights of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, am I right?
Hello, Father. I hope all orcs will soon be hanging on the trees all around. And those damned heretics sticking together with them as well.

Damned! All right, I'll tell you everything, noble sir. No need to torture me. The night when the merchant Ollmier was murdered I caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan climbing down from the window of his room in the town inn. I didn't know what to say, but before I could open my mouth and ask what was going on she gave me a pouch of gold coins. And I was to get much more soon if I were silent about her nightly affair. I thought she was just cheating on her husband, Baron Robert van Gallagan. It didn't cross my mind that there could be something worse going on. The merchant Ollmier wasn't found dead until the next day.
I'm glad the truth has come out at last, soldier. But do you realize you lied to a noble?
And you will be much more because you are going to spend the rest of your life in a musty cell. That will wean you off lying to the gentry!
Mercy, noble sir! I won't lie any more! I'll change my ways!
I don't lie, noble sir, I swear! I didn't see the Baroness that night!

Good day, noble sir. I heard you've arrived in the town to take over the domain of Asherbalt. I hope you will soon drive all those mongrels out of the Moonshine Mountains who have all that mess around here on their conscience—and their human henchmen too. And you will be surprised how many of them are here in Hillbrandt.
Yes, noble sir. It was Master Edmond d'Arvias. Although he disappeared in darkness immediately, I was able to recognize him. It was him—I would put my shirt on it!
You're welcome, noble sir. Farewell

He is the superior of the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He really is somebody. I've always thought him to be a devout man pursuing only his mission—which is to keep an eye on justice. I thought he is that sort of pious man with clear mind. I'd never think he might be a heretic, noble sir. But these are strange times, so why strange things couldn't happen even among the knights of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, am I right?
Hello, noble sir. I hope all orcs will soon be hanging on the trees all around. And those damned heretics sticking together with them as well.
Stone Face

Oh so... I understand. In that case I'll answer that you are Yrrmaxius, the High Priest of the Cult of the Creators, holder of the Chalice of Metamorphosis and the favorite of god Pearin. And among others you are also my creator, who has created me to protect the Temple of the Cult of the Creators.
What is that Cult of the Creators?

The Cult of the Creators is the foremost cult of god Pearin, the great Creator and space fisherman. It is concerned with the mystery of the existence of things and beings, studies their creation, transformation and demise. Since the year 29 of the rule of Trinius, when the cult was named an imperial warden of wisdom and genesis, it has resided in the underground of the Coliseum and with the help of the Chalice of Metamorphosis found in the ruins of the town of Khulu it has been slowly unfolding the mystery of creation.
How can I enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators?
Do you want to know how to enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators? Well, use the secret passage you personally ordered to be built.
If I am the High Priest of the cult, I surely have all my gold and magic items hidden somewhere, am I right?
Certainly, my master. You keep all your treasures in the very heart of the Temple of the Cult of the Creators.
What would I have to do if I want to descend down to the Temple of the Cult of the Creators?
Nothing at all, my master. You just say the password and I will open the way—just as you wished.
I see. And when I don't remember the password?
For that case you ordered me to give you a riddle with its correct answer being the password.
Alright. I will hear the riddle now.
Great. In that case tell me the password.

I'm sorry, but I can't tell you that, High Priest. You are Yrrmaxius and you know the password. No one but you and your priests, which know the password too, may enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators!
Well... so you're telling me I am some Yrrmaxius?
Who else could you be, my master? I don't understand you.
Enough of this ugly game! I've come to wrest this place from the infernal claws and you, daemon, I will send back to burning Hell from whence you came!
I don't understand you, my master. What are you talking about? I'm your faithful servant, as you surely know.
I've said enough! Apage, demon! I exorcise you—return to burning Hell. In the name of God Almighty leave this world!
I don't understand you, my master. What are you talking about? I 'm your faithful servant, as you surely know.
If I say I've lost my memory and don't know who I am, what would you tell me about myself?
I don't understand you, master. These are strange questions. Is it some form of a test?
No, this is no test. Just tell me who I am!
I understand. In that case I wish you good day!
So then: I'm no vampire but blood I do drink; I'll forbid you all though law I'm not; Even if you love me nothing you will gain; But if you betray me I'll give you much pain. Who am I?
Mother-in-law!
Sister!
Wife!
Sister-in-law!
Mother!
I'm sorry, but your answer is wrong. According to the order you gave me I have to stop you now as an intruder!
Your answer is correct, High Priest Yrrmaxius. You may enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators.
Well... what about some indicia?
I'm sorry, Jacque, but this is not the Fort Boyard!

Welcome, High Priest Yrrmaxius. You've not been here for long time. I almost started to fear something happened to you. Last time you spoke about a rebellion of religious fanatics shaking very foundations of Ereborn. I'm glad you're alright!
Well... yes, I'm all right. And who are you?!
Who am I? What a strange question it is, my master! Why, you yourself have created me... How could you forget about your monumental creation that has no equal in whole Ereborn?!
I'm sorry, my memory is quite bad lately...

No, no, it's me who must apologize. I'm not to judge your motives. You may ask whatever you wish—I'm your humble creation. You've made me to guard the Temple of the Cult of the Creators of which you are the High Priest. I protect the Chalice of Metamorphosis, the most valuable relic of the Cult.
Answer my question!

I apologize for my improper behavior, my master. I'm not to judge your motives. You may ask whatever you wish—I'm your humble creation. You've made me to guard the Temple of the Cult of the Creators whose you are the High Priest. I protect the Chalice of Metamorphosis, the most valuable relic of the Cult.
What are you talking about, infernal demon? I'm no Yrrmaxius!
Welcome, High Priest Yrrmaxius. What can I do for you?
I'd like to enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators.
Then say the password, my master.
I don't remember the password. Give me your riddle.
Your answer is wrong. As an intruder you have to be stopped!
He who wishes to enter must say the password!
And what if I don't remember it? Will you give me a riddle?
Alright, do your part...

So then: You can't hear it, you can't see it, neither catch or merely feel it, it gapes under hills, 'hind stars, in empty pits and behind bars, it was here first—and will restore, stifling all life to its core, it makes every sun die, as the time goes slowly by. What is it?
Emptiness!
Disease!
Forbidden love!
Death!
Darkness!
Your answer is correct. You may enter!
You may enter!

So then: It follows your footsteps like a hound, led by you as you walk round, without you it couldn't be, sunshine makes it sharp to see, darkness overcomes it fast—in its embrace it can't last. What is it?
Blind man!
Shadow!
Ghost!
Dog!
Life!
I'm sorry, but Father Fourat has left the Fort Boyard!
So then: Possesses your soul or house, non-invited like a louse, he enslaves you with his will never confessing it still, he can doom you or let go, what he'll do you cannot know! What is it?
Husband!
Virus!
Bacteria!
Uninvited guest!
Demon!
I'm sorry, but Father Fourat has given us no indices.
So then: Turn me to my back, if you lust for me: just open me wide and enjoy what you see. I will give you all, happy to do so. Gain Wisdom from me and let your Reason grow. Who am I?
Wise prostitute!
Book!
Hen from whose enviscerated entrails future is foretold by the heretics!
Shahrazad!
I'm sorry, but Jacque has not returned from Father Fourat yet.
He who wishes to enter must say the correct passwords to me and my brothers.
So then: Heat softens my solid body, my hot glance spreads light and shine, if I'm slim I must die early, thickness means long life of mine. Who am I?
Torch!
Sunshine!
Fire woman!
Goldbrick in a melting stove!
Candle!
Your answer is right. If you answer correctly to my brothers too, you will be allowed to enter.
Your answer is right. Because you answered rightly to my brothers too, you may now enter!
In that case Father Fourat awaits you in his tower. Jacque will escort you.

So then: Banish me and you'll be dead, so you'll be, if you don't do that, some say I'm a gift of Gods, others beat me out with rods, many people long and bother to destroy me in each other. What am I?
Riches!
Motivation!
Faith!
Will!
Go for it, Jacque! Allez allez allez!

So then: You must know you really want me, going after me so dour, yes, I'm needed for your living, without me you would be poor. I am neither love nor might, but you need me to be bright. If you get me, you'll be glad, if you fail to, you'll be sad. What am I?
Beautiful woman!
Wise woman!
Rich woman!
Beautiful, wise and rich woman!
Knowledge!
I'm sorry, but Father Fourat is not here today, Jacque.

So then: It pigs whole worlds and all living, trees, birds, flowers not forgiving, gnaws at iron, steel it chews, fighting with it is no use, it grinds rocks and defeats kings, mountains to the ground it brings. What is it?
Time!
Acid!
God!
Satan!
Here lies the entrance into the Temple of the Cult of the Creators. He who wishes to enter must say the password!
So then: Throat of fire, hair of smoke, thunder of mine dark clouds cloak. I'll burn all that's in my way, I'm no dragon though I got flame.
Fire!
Fire golem!
Volcano!
Yes, your answer is correct. You may enter the Temple of the Cult of the Creators.
Phoenix!
Well... maybe some other day. Farewell.
Damned! I will have to find a way to get out of here...
This is the Temple of the Cult of The Creators. No one will leave it without the consent of the High Priest of the Cult!
But High Priest Yrrmaxius is dead!
Yrrmaxius is dead—I order you to open the gate!
I'm telling you Yrrmaxius is dead—there's no High Priest now!!
Let's try it the other way. I'm the High Priest of the Cult. I order you to open the gate!
As you wish, High Priest!
What do you think about master Edmond d'Arvias being suspected of heresy?

It certainly is utter nonsense to believe master Edmond d'Arvias could be in any way allied with infernal powers and could strive for the town to fall into the hands of Satan. He has to be the victim of some terrible plot against him. He's the most honorable man I've ever met in my life. And I won't change a word of this opinion of mine even if there's not many people now who would agree with me.

Duke Weinberg offered a reward for killing any orc who gets anywhere near Hillbrandt. You just give his head or scalp to sheriff Contemburry and he pays you the reward in gold. But not many people have got rich this way so far, you can believe me. Hunting for orcs is a very dangerous business. You never know if you are a hunter or hunted game.
What do you think about the present crisis the Realm has been dragged in, brother?

It's necessary to brave any crisis, brother, much like the one we are in now. I don't know if it really is the end of the world, as the Holy Scriptures tell us in the Revelations of Saint Ezekiel. But we have clear objectives we have to pursue, and that's all what should concern us now. Our holy mission has to be fulfilled. There's no other way. The heresy has to be uprooted and trampled on by the steel boots of justice.
What monsters is it possible to meet in Hillbrandt, brother?

You should beware mainly of the orcs, brother. Maybe you don't believe yet they are really here, but it's true. They've appeared early in the spring. Some tells they came from Hell itself. The truth is they've come from some deep holes in the iron mines and before anybody managed to do anything they murdered all the miners and destroyed the mining village Asherbalt. Now their hordes spend nights plundering the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains and they assault all the merchant caravans daring to venture there. On the top of it seems they've settled down in the iron mines, because there is thick black smoke hovering over the area. Only God knows what rogueries they are preparing there.
Do you know anything in particular about the orcs, brother?

The orcs are monsters from the ancient times, brother. It's not sure from where they came, but it's a race of hellspawns first seen in the age of old pagan wars between inhuman races. At that time the armies of orcish Khan Rashgar were the cause of the fall of the ancient realm of Thron. But subsequent fate of the inhuman nations was not influenced by the orcs, because the orcs disappeared as fast as they came. Legends are totally silent about that, but it's accredited to an interference of the pagan gods against the orcs as they were an infernal race. But who can tell how much truth is in those ancient stories?

The truth is the orcs have come early this spring from the depths under the Moonshine Mountains and left such bloodshed behind them that there's no doubt about their existence. During single night they massacred everybody in the iron mines and the mining village Asherbalt. Since then they along with the half-ogres and trolls have been controlling entire foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Hillbrandt is almost besieged due to that. Business was bad even before, but now it drags even worse because merchant caravans are being assaulted and no one dares to go here.
Do you suspect someone in connection to the crimes master Edmond d'Arvias is charged with?
I don't suspect anyone, brother. If I did, I would be the first who would crash his door open and drag him by his hair to the executioner's stake.

Some sinner stole the monstrance of Saint Orthenius, brother. That may be one of the reasons the orcs managed to get inside the town during their recent attack. Monstrance has magic power to guard the town against dark powers and preventing them from getting in. People are very nervous because of it, because they think there's nothing left what would protect them against the blustering hellspawns.

The Fallen Angel Arthamon? You make me nervous, brother. Such names are not to be spoken aloud, you know? But if you want to hear it... Arthamon is one of the three terrible Fallen Angels. He is the master of fire and ruler of utter destruction. He is the antipode of life, the negation of all existence. Let God and the Archangel Gabriel guard us against him—and against his infernal minions too!
Do you think, brother, that Arthamon may be summoned?
You mean summoned into this world? No, that's impossible. That would mean the end of all!
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus, brother?
I don't know a thing about that unfortunate disappearance, brother. I shudder to think what might have happened to the poor Bishop. He is probably long dead. Let God guard his soul.

Master Edmond d'Arvias' Sword of the Brotherhood was stolen? That's impossible. I can't believe that. Swords of the Brotherhood are the symbols of our position for us, the paladins. If the master's sword was stolen, it had to be the work of some infernal intrigues. If I knew who has such a dirty trick on his conscience I would punish him by cutting both his hands off as the law prescribes.

Have you heard the legend of Dead Man's Stone, brother? Not far from the gallows there is a piece of rock dubbed the Dead Man's Stone. It's told that the voices of lost souls can be heard from it, the voices of people who found their death on the gallows. They are supposed to be imprisoned in it for all the sins they committed during their lives, and for which they are not allowed to leave this world. I don't know how true is that, but it's certain I heard strange sounds several times when passing by that stone.
Do you know anything about the death of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, brother?

Of course I've heard about the case of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, brother. I personally didn't know Kurth Ollmier well, and if I'm right, he hadn't many friends here in Hillbrandt. He was proclaiming himself to be a merchant, but he dealt only in very strange items. Pagan artifacts and relics, lost scrolls, ancient grimoires... All kinds of strange goods. And only per order, certainly. So no one ever knew for whom he chased all those strange items. Just that by itself is suspicious. If what is told is true, even the Inquisition itself became interested in him. But the merchant was murdered before the Inquisition was able to indict him and hear him out. He was found in the attic of Truthorn's inn. His throat was cut and his genitalia stuffed in his mouth. Disgusting crime. But as they say—they who live by the sword...

Hillbrandt is ruled by Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. The royal vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. Both of them should meditate about the meaning of the word humbleness, but excluding that flaw of theirs people don't repine them much. But in truth it's told about Baron van Gallagan that his wife rules in his stead.
Answer me, brother, lest I lose my patience!
I sincerely ask you to answer my question, brother.
I see a brave brother knight before me, fully devoted to his holy mission. And that is why I don't believe you wouldn't want to answer my question.
AAA
I won't need your services any more, brother. Our ways part here.
Have you considered it thoroughly, brother? It seemed to me we complement each other well...
Yes, I've considered it well. I won't need your help any more.

If I really can't persuade you to think it over, brother, I'll have to part with you. But if you reconsider someday, don't hesitate to seek me out. You'll find me in Hillbrandt. Farewell and good luck!
Actually you're right. Forget it.
That's all. Let's go.
Your offer seems interesting. Alright, join me.
I don't care for your help. I can manage without you.
Brother, I offer you my sword, my shield and my life. I don't doubt you would find it helpful when fulfilling your noble mission. Let me go with you!
You may be right, brother. Alright, join me.
As I've said, I don't need your services. Farewell.
Well, brother, it seems I won't persuade you. But you may be persuaded later by the circumstances. In that case you know where you'll find me. Good luck, brother. You will need it.
Thank you, brother! You'll see our joined forces will be enough to stand against all what the infernal powers may put in our way.
I hope so too. Let's go.

Thank you, brother! You'll see our joined forces will be enough to stand against all what the infernal powers may put in our way. But if you really want me to join you, dismiss from your services Jacques de Pulein, whose presence I've necessarily noticed. I don't know how the nefarious man has deluded you to insinuate himself into your favor, but I have to warn you against him. There is a despicable man hiding behind the mask of God's servant. I've managed to see through his disguise no sooner than we acquainted during the novitiate. I advise you well, dismiss him while there is still time. If you do, my sword will be yours.
If it is really true I'd rather dismiss Jacques de Pulein.
Great, brother. I'm glad you've listened to my advice. You'll see my services to be much more helpful to you than the services of that good-for-nothing who fouls the name of our Order!
I hope so. Let's go.
As I can see you quite dislike one another with Jacques de Pulein. But his services have been helpful to me. Would you be able to overcome your grudge against him? Two swords are better than one.
I'm afraid I can't. My holy mission must not be disgraced by anything and joining forces with someone like Jacques de Pulein would be a sin! Dismiss him and my sword will be yours that very instant.
I understand. In that case I'm going to dismiss him immediately.
Great, brother. I'm glad you've listened to my advice. You'll see my services will be much more helpful to you than the services of that good-for-nothing who has fouled the name of our order!
I'm sorry but I won't dismiss Jascquese de Pulein for now. Farewell.
I'm sorry, but the services of the knight Jacques de Pulein have been helpful to me until now. I don't see any reason for dismissing him now.

What a shame, brother. I hoped you would take my advice to the heart. It's a risk to rely on people like Jacques de Pulein to help you in your holy mission. Remember my words—the man may betray you at any moment. Anyway, if you ever reconsider, I will be always ready to offer you my services.

Thank you, brother! You'll see our joined forces will be enough to stand against all that the infernal powers may put in our way. But frankly, I can't abide the presence of a certain priest in your company. And that's an unsurpassable obstacle for me now. Because of the efforts of the Holy Office to do away with our Brotherhood I cannot ally with someone like him.
Alright, brother. I need your services, so I will dismiss Father Nicolas.
Great, brother. I'm glad you listened to my advice. You'll see my services will be much more helpful to you than the services of that priest.
I understand your ill feelings for the inquisitors of the Holy Office, brother. But the services of Father Nicolas have been helpful to me. Would you be able to overcome your grudge against him?
I'm afraid I can't, brother. I'm unable to overcome this obstacle. I don't know Father Nicolas and I don't know if I may trust him. Dismiss him and my sword is yours that very instant.
I'm sorry, but Father Nicolas will stay in my service for now. Farewell.
I'm sorry, but the services of Father Nicolas have been helpful to me until now. I can't see any reason for dismissing him now.

What a shame, brother. I hoped you would understand my reasons. I can't ally with someone who may be openly standing against the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Anyway, if you ever reconsider, I will be always willing to offer you my services.
Brother, we must stop this madness! We must stand against it and stop it at any cost! It's the will of God!!!
What are you talking about? What do we have to stop?

We must clear master Edmond d'Arvias of the suspicion of heresy! It's a blatant lie by which someone tries to scandalize our honorable master along with our whole Brotherhood. And we must not allow that!
First tell me who you are.
My name's Hugo Montesque and I'm a commander of the knightly order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I hold the office of the second protector of justice in the local chapter of the Brotherhood.
I was charged to gather convincing evidence against master d'Arvias, not to clear him of suspicion.

What have you to say, brother?

Traitor! You'll be rightly punished for this!
I don't think so. Unlike you I stand on the right side. Victory shall be ours! Farewell!

Thank you, brother! You'll see that our joined forces will be enough to stand against anything that the infernal powers may put in our way. But to be honest I can't join you unless you dismiss Olfghard who is following you. I don't know, why you trust him, but I warn you against him. You can't trust him. If you want me to follow you, dismiss Olfghard first!
You can trust Olfghard, brother. He has shown his loyalty in furious combats.
Maybe he convinced you, but I don't have any reason to trust him! If you want me to follow you, dismiss Olfghard!
All right, join me. I'll need your help more than that of Olfghard's.
Very well, brother. I'm glad you followed my advice. You'll find my services more handy than services of this miscreant.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to dismiss Olfghard.
In that case we can't join our forces. I'm sorry. And I warn you—watch Olfghard carefully. Your trust can doom you...

I see you've recruited Jacquese de Pulein. If you want me to follow you, dismiss him from your services. I don't know how the nefarious man has deluded you to insinuate himself into your favor, but I have to warn you against him. There is a despicable man hid behind the mask of God's servant. I've managed to see through his disguise no sooner than we acquainted during the novitiate. I advise you well, dismiss him while there is still time. If you do, my sword will be yours.

I can't abide the presence of certain priest in your company. And that's an unsurpassable obstacle for me now. I believe you, because I can see good in your heart, but I don't know the other man. I see you've recruited Olfghard. I don't know, why do you trust him, but I warn you against him. You can't trust him. If you want me to follow you, dismiss Olfghard first!
Help yourself, brother. All you find on me is yours. You surely need it more than I.
What do you think about the present crisis the Realm has been dragged in, sir knight?

It's necessary to brave any crisis, Father, much like the one we are in now. I don't know if it really is the end of the world, as the Holy Scriptures tell us in the Revelations of Saint Ezekiel. But we have clear objectives we have to pursue, and that's all what should concern us now. Our holy mission has to be fulfilled. There's no other way. The heresy has to be uprooted and trampled on by the steel boots of justice.
What monsters is it possible to meet in Hillbrandt, sir knight?

You should beware mainly of the orcs, Father. Maybe you don't believe yet they are really here, but it's true. They've appeared early in the spring. Some tells they came from Hell itself. The truth is they've come from some deep holes in the iron mines and before anybody managed to do anything they murdered all the miners and destroyed the mining village Asherbalt. Now their hordes spend nights plundering the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains and they assault all the merchant caravans daring to venture there. On the top of it seems they've settled down in the iron mines, because there is thick black smoke hovering over the area. Only God knows what rogueries they are preparing there.
Do you know anything in particular about the orcs, sir knight?

The orcs are monsters from the ancient times, Father. It's not sure from where they came, but it's a race of hellspawns first seen in the age of old pagan wars between inhuman races. At that time the armies of orcish Khan Rashgar were the cause of the fall of the ancient realm of Thron. But subsequent fate of the inhuman nations was not influenced by the orcs, because the orcs disappeared as fast as they came. Legends are totally silent about that, but it's accredited to an interference of the pagan gods against the orcs as they were an infernal race. But who can tell how much truth is in those ancient stories?
I don't suspect anyone, Father. If I did, I would be the first who would crash his door open and drag him by his hair to the executioner's stake.

Some sinner stole the monstrance of Saint Orthenius, Father. That may be one of the reasons the orcs managed to get inside the town during their recent attack. Monstrance has magic power to guard the town against dark powers and preventing them from getting in. People are very nervous because of it, because they think there's nothing left what would protect them against the blustering hellspawns.

The Fallen Angel Arthamon? You make me nervous, Father. Such names are not to be spoken aloud, you know? But if you want to hear it... Arthamon is one of the three terrible Fallen Angels. He is the master of fire and ruler of utter destruction. He is the antipode of life, the negation of all existence. Let God and the Archangel Gabriel guard us against him—and against his infernal minions too!
Do you think, sir knight, that Arthamon may be summoned?
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus, sir knight?
I don't know a thing about that unfortunate disappearance, Father. I shudder to think what might have happened to the poor Bishop. He is probably long dead. Let God guard his soul.

Master Edmond d'Arvias' Sword of the Brotherhood was stolen? That's impossible. I can't believe that. Swords of the Brotherhood are symbols of our position. If the master's sword was stolen, it had to be the work of some infernal intrigues. If I knew who has such a dirty trick on his conscience I would punish him by cutting both his hands off as the law prescribes.

Have you heard the legend of Dead Man's Stone, Father? Not far from the gallows there is a piece of rock dubbed the Dead Man's Stone. It's told that the voices of lost souls can be heard from it, the voices of people who found their death on the gallows. They are supposed to be imprisoned in it for all the sins they committed during their lives, and for which they are not allowed to leave this world. I don't know how true is that, but it's certain I heard strange sounds several times when passing by that stone.
Do you know anything about the death of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, sir knight?

Of course I've heard about the case of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, Father. I personally didn't know Kurth Ollmier well, and if I'm right, he hadn't many friends here in Hillbrandt. He was proclaiming himself to be a merchant, but he dealt only in very strange items. Pagan artifacts and relics, lost scrolls, ancient grimoires... All kinds of strange goods. And only per order, certainly. So no one ever knew for whom he chased all those strange items. Just that by itself is suspicious. If what is told is true, even the Inquisition itself became interested in him. But the merchant was murdered before the Inquisition was able to indict him and hear him out. He was found in the attic of Truthorn's inn. His throat was cut and his genitalia stuffed in his mouth. Disgusting crime. But as they say—they who live by the sword...
Answer me, sir knight, lest I lose my patience!

I can only suppose what you think of me, sir knight. Just the same I believe your prejudice against me won't hinder you from helping me in my holy mission, which is in fact not much different from yours. Please, answer my question.
I see a brave man before me, devoted to his holy mission. I do believe you wouldn't want to refuse a poor priest's question.
I won't need your services any more, sir knight. Our ways part here.
Have you considered it thoroughly, Father? It seemed to me we complement each other well...

I'm not surprised Grand Duke Heidrick is looking for a new wife. I've heard his previous one was convicted of heresy and burned to death. I tell you, it had to be a hard blow for the Grand Duke. People say the scandal will break his neck—and I wouldn't be surprised if it does. There are many people in Alvaron who would like to get the office of the royal governor of Glatzburg.
And that's exactly why Grand Duke Heidrick is looking for a new wife who would at least partially sweep away the shadow of doubts cast upon him. I've thought you might be interested.

I'm sorry, knight, but you've thought wrong. Although the vision of marrying the royal governor is tempting, I'm of the opinion the Grand Duke will be withdrawn soon. And then he will lose his standing, his wealth and all his honor and respect. Then he will be named governor of some sleepy hollow at the frontier in the middle of nowhere. No, knight, I don't envision my future in that way!

The only one whom I suspect of heresy is that brat Horst. In fact it's more than a suspicion, because I witnessed his wrongdoing during my kidnapping. I hope his soul will burn in Hell for all he has done.

Maybe you've heard it already, but one of the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous went mad after one of crusades against evil and started to murder innocent people! His name's Minfred von Siegel and he had to run away after killing several innocent men and women in the city in broad daylight. Now he hides somewhere in the vicinity of the city and kills on sight. Someone should do something about it. As if there aren't enough of hellspawns!

You ask me if Royal Counselor Verenicus could have his hands in the murder of Prince Louis? To tell the truth after my kidnapping and the murder of His Majesty I'm willing to believe anything. And moreover, one of the King's servant girls, Kathryn Winhold, at that time accused Verenicus of murdering poor Princ Louis.
The Inquisitor General a heretic? God forbid! I really can't imagine that. It would be the end of all our hope!
I'm sorry, but I don't know a thing about the murder of paladin Richwald d'Blazier. I've only heard a witch from Schwarzwald killed him. Someone should catch her and execute her.
I found this gold earring. Do you happen to know whose it might be?

Show me the earring... Why, that's my earring I've been given by my departed father. Yes, I recognize it! I even didn't know I lost it. But wait a minute, my earrings had small notches on this side. I'd better check it out.
Yes, I'd recommend you to do so!
So I've been mistaken, knight. My earrings are a little bit different, do you see? And moreover, none of them are missing. I'm sorry.
I'm trying to find a way to cure a man of lycantrophy. Would you be able to give me some advice?

Are you making fun of me, knight?! You pull me out of the mouth of werewolf-god Urrm where his infernal minions put me and now you are asking me how to help one of them? They don't deserve any help! Only thing they deserve is fifteen inches of hard steel into their belly, as my departed father used to say.

Since my kidnapping by the werewolves I have no heart for any wrongdoing to women. If Father Nicolas is innocent he should prove it quickly, because in that case God stands on his side. But if he is guilty, then he have to stand before court and bow before justice.

People say there is a horrible stryx lurking at the city cemetery, born from a cursed girl named Joan. The legend says Joan was cursed by her own mother, who was a nun of the order of Saint Bethesda, violated by some goatish priest. She lost her mind then and wandered the realm aimlessly until she gave birth to her daughter at the Alvaron cemetery.

Immediately after giving birth to the child the poor soul cursed her newborn baby and committed suicide. The girl was found lifeless in the morning by priests and put into a nameless grave. Years went by and no one suspected the curse was slowly changing Joan into a dreadful stryx that would hunt her father. And then it really happened—the stryx awoke and since then she has been stalking the city to get her father. It's said she will kill everyone she meets...
You should answer me, good woman, or you will meet the fate of people who reject to cooperate with the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
I ask you sincerely, good woman, to answer my question. I'm sure it will do you no harm.
I don't believe such a wise and beautiful woman would deny me an answer to my question.
Alright, I'll help you. I'll escort you back to the city.
Thank you, knight. It's so noble of you! My home is in the southwestern part of Alvaron, not far from the city gate.
Let's go, we have a long way ahead of us.
Will I be somehow rewarded for helping you?
I have a little money saved at home. I thought it would be my dowry, but if you insist on helping me only for a reward, then I will certainly pay you.
I'm sorry, but I have no time. Farewell.

My name's Nina Monthreass, knight. At the last full moon the werewolves of the infernal wolf-prince Wulfhyrr kidnapped me and have kept me here since then. They want to sacrifice me to their bloody god! You have to get me out of here!
How the werewolves kidnapped you? How did they managed to break into the city?

It was that brat Horst—he allowed them to enter the city by the small gate after luring the guards to sleep by some dark magic! He's been surely doing that for a long time, because merely this year several people went missing already, always at the full moon. He is the son of Wolf-Prince Wulfhyrr himself! I saw Wulfhyrr when he commended him for the work well done. Such a villainy!
How did it happen?

I had a date with a young soldier. We were to meet under the city walls in order to avoid being disturbed. But when I went by the small gate I saw the guards falling to the ground. I didn't know what was happening and so I stood still. Then that brat Horst appeared in the torchlight and opened the small gate. Suddenly there were werewolves all around and I heard that damned Wolf-Prince Wulfhyrr commending Horst for what he just done. He told him he is proud to have a son such as him. I wanted to run away, but they scented or heard me and before I managed to do anything they were dragging me out of the city. Please, knight, help me to get back!
I'm glad to see you again, knight. How are you? Thank you once again for saving me. Can I help you somehow?
I need to talk with you, good woman.
It will be a pleasure. What do you want to know?
I don't think so. Farewell.
Farewell, knight. Have a good time. And God bless you!
Oh God, save me, knight. I implore you, help me to get away from here, lest those werewolf beasts kill me!

No, Father, I don't envision my future in that way!
So I've been mistaken, Father. My earrings are a little bit different, do you see? And moreover, none of them are missing. I'm sorry.

Are you making fun of me, Father?! You pull me out of the mouth of werewolf-god Urrm where his infernal minions put me and now you are asking me how to help one of them? They don't deserve any help! It was a test I've passed and now I can at last do what God Almighty wishes me to do—to challenge to fight everyone the fate sends in my way. And now it is you, brother. Well, en guard!
Alright, as you wish. May the better of us win.
That's madness! To challenge wayfarers to the fight isn't a service to God, but an infernal fallacy. Fall down on your knees and pray to God Almighty to forgive you the sins you've committed!

No, brother, you're wrong. It's my mission, I know it! I have to challenge you, same as anybody else. I'm the best swordsman in the world and it's the will of God for me to live my life in deathmatches. En guard!
I refuse to fight you, brother. You are evidently out of your mind. Maybe some unclean spirit has possessed you and dimmed your sanity. Come with me, we must find a cure for you.

My mind is absolutely sharp, brother. My thinking is as clean as water in a highland stream. I know what is expected of me. I know what God expects of me. I'm the best swordsman in the world and challenges are my mission. En guard!
I don't accept your challenge. I've done you nothing wrong and I don't see any reason to fight you. Farewell.
I'm sorry, brother, but I can't let you go. I challenged you to a duel and that means we will cross our swords. It's the will of God. En guard!
A duel, you say? All right, as you wish. I'm at your service. En garde!

I've heard about you, brother. They say you used to be a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, but you were expelled because of frequent duels. Since then you have been murdering everyone on sight. There's a high reward offered for you.

Murdering? What crossed your mind, brother? That's only a slander—I've never murdered anyone. Everyone I fought had a chance not only to defend, but of course also to kill me. I can't help it that God has chosen me as his champion and that I'm the best swordsman in the world. But enough of talking, brother. We have to fulfil the will of God. En guard!
Alright, as you wish. Justice has to be satisfied.

Someone is coming at last! The waiting almost started to tire me. There's nothing worse than to waste time by waiting while such a difficult divine mission rests on my shoulders. Clashing of swords, furious shouting of the duelists and the cry of the defeated... Yes, that's my way and my mission. Duels to the death. So let's look whom has fate sent my way today? A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous? Wow, I'm really honored! Welcome, brother in arms. You've come right in time.
What are you talking about, good man? And who are you?
Are you asking me who I am, brother? Then know that my name's Henry de Montreaux. And what am I doing here? I'm waiting for you! I'm here to challenge you to a duel.
No matter who you are, tell me what's your business here at once!
I'm Henry de Montreaux, brother. The best swordsman in the world. What am I doing here? I'm waiting for you! I'm here to challenge you to a duel.
You look like a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, but something tells me your present actions have nothing to do with the service to God.

You're right, brother. My name's Henry de Montreaux and I really used to be a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. But then my eyes opened and I understood God has given me a different mission. And that's why I'm waiting for you. I'm here to challenge you to a duel.

You have... you have beaten me, brother! That's... incredible! That means... I'm not the best swordsman in the world! And all what I did wasn't the will of God, but... Oh my God, what did I do? What happened to me? Why did I do all this? Good gracious, I'm a serial killer of innocent people!

See, I've freed you from your delusion. Under the presumption you are administering the will of God you were committing evil in the worst of forms. The time has come for you to atone for your terrible deeds. Go and do good anywhere you set your foot. There's a long way before you to redress all injustice you perpetrated.

Yes, you're right, brother. I have to set forth on the way of penance and to remedy all what I did in my blindness. Thank you, brother. I know my soul has no hope for salvation, but I'll hope I can at least partly atone for all the wrongs I caused. Here, brother—take all my possessions. I do not need them anymore. I forsake them as a token of my purity. I will wander the world as a poor pilgrim because I at last know that's my destiny. Farewell, brother. And thank you.
Yes, you're a murderer and you'll pay for your crimes with your life.
Yes, you're right, brother. Let's end this to allow the just judgment to be delivered to me. May I burn in Hell for all what I did! Farewell!
May God forgive you, brother!
