You're a knight, aren't you? Yes, you certainly are a knight. I see a strong personal aura around you. It glitters like a thousand diamonds. It's like brisk air in the midst of a musty swamp. I entreat you, knight, hear me out. I didn't murder my beloved Richwald. No, I could have never committed such a terrible crime, believe me! My soul slumbers and listens to the silence of eternal loneliness, I open my eyes to the deepest darkness and drink the cup of bitterness to the last drop, although I'm innocent.
Tell me more about yourself, girl. Who are you and how could you get charged with the murder of paladin Richwald d'Blazier?

You shouldn't want to know who I am, knight. My name has the brand of death, the shadow of perdition hovers above it. Of God's damnation. I'm a memory of the yesterday's night full of nightmares. I'm a forgotten sin forcing to eternal vigilance. I'm... fear and in fear I live.
Stop speaking in riddles and tell me who you really are.
Why, I've just told you, knight!
And how came it you were accused of murdering Richwald d'Blazier?

He... he led me back into the light, knight. He reached for me and his touch... healed me. At least partly. He brought me comfort, understanding and lot of other feelings that I had thought died forever when... when I... Oh my God! No, not again! Please! It returns again! Those dreams... they were gone for so long, but now they're back! No, let me be! I mustn't cry, lest they hear me. Silence, Kathryn, silence, for goodness sake! Those men are dangerous! They are going to the chamber of Prince Louis. We have to go away. It's a matter of life and death. If they see us we are doomed! Let him be, oh my God, let him be, he is only a child! Oh my God... he's dead, they killed him!
What are you talking about, girl? What has happened to you? You're in a trance.

What? What happened? I had... I don't know, I dreamed about something. It's gone now. I hope so. I don't remember. I don't remember anything. Richwald allowed me to forget, he gave me happiness and... love. Yes, he gave me love, as great as a soul is capable of to another. When we met for the first time, I was... wild animal. I lived like a wolf, I tore flesh by my bare hands and teeth... I dug in the earth, drank from springs. But when I saw him I awoke from that nightmare. I started to live again. He cleaned my face, caressed my hair, gave me his loaf of bread and some cheese. I feared him because he allured me. I knew he posed danger to me, because I couldn't return. But I couldn't do otherwise. I loved him and he loved me.
How it was next with knight Richwald d'Blazier? What happened?

Something... terrible happened. For some time we were meeting and getting to know one another. He always came for me to certain place in Schwarzwald, brought me flowers and lavished me with gifts. He tried to get me to return. I hesitated, but maybe I would eventually agree. But one day, when I came to the place we were usually meeting, I found him... heavens... turned into stone. He stood there motionless, as if waiting for me, he had flowers in his hand, but his heart wasn't beating, his chest didn't move. He was turned into stone. Somebody had to enchant him. But not I, knight. I swear! Please, help me to find the real culprit. Avenge Richwald's death. I implore you!
Alright, I'll help you. If you're innocent, I'll set you free.
Thank you, knight. Thank you thousand times. I don't ask it for myself, God condemned me long ago. But I ask it in the name of my Richwald. He didn't deserve such a fate.
What could you offer me in the case I decide to help you?

How can you ask something from me, knight? Can't you see I have nothing to give you? Maybe only... my body. Alright, take my body in exchange for your services if you wish so. I will yield to you if only the murderers of my Richwald will be caught.
I'm sorry, but I have no time to occupy myself with your case.
Oh... in that case my beloved Richwald won't find peace. God, why are you so cruel?
Why did you live like an animal? What made you do it? Who were you before?

I don't know, knight. I don't remember. I swear I don't remember. Sometimes nightmares are returning to me, bringing terrible visions, but the next morning I never remember a thing. My home is Schwarzwald, it provided me shelter from the whole world. It's dangerous and cruel, but honest. At least compared to the world around it. Only Richwald was different. He understood me, he loved me. And I loved him.
I pray for the success of your efforts, knight. The murderers of my Richwald must be uncovered. Their souls must burn in Hell!
I have good news for you, girl. I've caught the murderer of Richwald d'Blazier. It was Sandra Ullmann.
Sandra Ullmann? The town stallholder Sandra Ullmann? But I know her! She is my friend... at least she had been, before... before...
Before what? What occurred to you, girl? What happened to you so evil that you ran into the woods and lived there like a wild animal

Oh my God, I can remember now! I remember all! I know how it happened. They killed Prince Louis! They accused me of heresy when Kathryn told what we witnessed. They forced me to run into the woods and live like an animal.
Tell me all, Corin. Who are you and what did you witness? And who is that Kathryn you're talking about?

My name's Corin Morray and I'm... or I was... royal chamber maid of His Majesty Edward II, just like Kathryn Winhold. Two years ago—at least I think it was two years ago, because I've lost the concept of time—we witnessed a terrible event in the royal palace. In the middle of the night a group of men intruded into the palace. They all wore black cloaks with deep hoods and without hesitation they headed to the chamber of Prince Louis. Kathryn and I sighted them by chance and secretly followed them. And that was our fatal mistake. I wish we didn't do anything and rather pretended that nothing happened.
What happened in the royal palace?

Those hooded men entered the chamber of Prince Louis and performed there—God forgive me—some dreadful ritual. They lighted ugly black candles around the bed of the young Prince, started to utter some awful words and gesticulated wildly with their hands. The body of Prince Louis flew up a little and hovered above the bed. And then shadows began to appear around it, like some ancient ghosts awakened and scrambled to enter this world. The shadows reached for the Prince and melted into his body. The young Prince turned deadly pale and slowly sank back to the bed where he then lied absolutely still. And he remained so forever. Because he was dead! But we didn't get to know that until the next morning when all the court was upside down. Prince Louis was murdered!
What did you do next? Haven't you tell anyone what you witnessed

I advised Kathryn to hold her tongue, not to tell anyone. I knew well that if those men got to know about us we would end up dead. And I was right. Kathryn eventually didn't keep her mouth shut and told it all at a confession. The same day the Inquisition arrested her. She was accused of murdering Prince Louis and of witchcraft. And she denounced me when put to torture. But I didn't wait for them to come for me, and I ran away. They hunted me like a wild animal, they were chasing me restlessly for several weeks. Until at last I took shelter in Schwarzwald, in that ancient dreadful forest. It embraced me, although only as a cruel stepfather. It made me its child. It taught me how to survive. And there the merciful shadow of forgetfulness fell upon me. I didn't know who I was and from where did I come. I became a witch, a fairy and a nymph.
Did you recognize some of the men who performed the ritual? Try to remember, please. It's really very important.

Yes, knight. We recognized one of them. It was the one who let the others into the royal palace by the side entrance. And it was the one who led them to the chamber of Prince Louis and who performed the mad ritual there with them. We recognized him because we were meeting him almost every day. It was the Royal Counselor Verenicus!
Thank you, Corin. Your testimony is very important for me. But tell me, what happened with Kathryn Winhold? If I could get her testimony too, it would help me greatly.
I don't know. I ran away from Alvaron even before the trial took place. I don't know what was her fate. I hope it was not so bad as mine was. But I feel I hope in vain.
Thank you, Corin. You've helped me a lot.

I'm glad I was able to repay you somehow what you did for my Richwald. I have no other choice now than to return back to Schwarzwald. To my Richwald. He is waiting for me there to come to him. We will be together again. I can't live among people, they would treat me as a witch and a wild animal. They would kill me, I know it. I'll return back to my Richwald. To the forest. It's my destiny. I will lay fresh flowers at his feet every day till God unites us again. Farewell, knight!
I think I have good news for you, Corin. But I have to speak with paladin Brian de Gawais first.
Really? Then hurry, knight. I can't wait to hear your news. My stomach gripes in anticipation of the murderers of my beloved Richwald being disclosed.
Yes, it's true. But I don't have any evidence yet.
I'm sure you'll get some soon, knight. I believe you. Your aura shines like the midday sun. It completely dazzles me. You surely won't disappoint my Richwald.
I beseech you, knight, find the murderers of my beloved Richwald. His death must be avenged! Surely there is some justice left in the world.
Alright, I will pursue this case. You have my word.
Thank you, knight! Thank you thousand times! Your aura didn't lie—it shines like the sun at midday.
Justice is in God's hands. I believe our Lord will look after us. Farewell.
The world is much more beautiful when the murderer of my Richwald is rightly punished. I hope I too will be called to God's kingdom soon to be with my beloved again. Yes, I wish nothing else.
May I ask you some questions, Corin?
I don't know answers to your questions, knight. The life is worthless for me. Don't be angry. I've told you all I could. I don't know any more and I don't want to.
The ways of God are beyond our comprehension. God be with you.

Thank you, Father. Thank you thousand times. I don't ask it for myself, God condemned me long ago. But I ask it in the name of my Richwald. He didn't deserve such a fate.

How can you ask something from me, Father? Can't you see I have nothing to give you? Maybe only... my body. Alright, take my body in exchange for your services if you wish so. I will yield to you if only the murderers of my Richwald will be caught.

He understood me, he loved me. And I loved him.
I pray for the success of your efforts, Father. The murderers of my Richwald must be uncovered. Their souls must burn in Hell!

Wise decision, my son. You saved yourself lots of useless toil by it. Why don't you go to brother Jeremiah and bring the accusation against me? Alright, that's enough for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the next interrogation. Guards, take him away!
Alright, I think it's enough for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the next interrogation. Guards, take him away!

I've told you all I know. But if you want to let me taste the life once more, I won't resist.

I've told you everything, knight. I've concealed nothing, I swear!
A swear of a traitor and heretic has no weight before law. Executioner, do your duty!

Bishop Vallarian, you are accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. Along with Baroness Linda van Gallagan and the stonemason Sam Riemann you were to invoke the Fallen Angel Arthamon. For this purpose you designed the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill. You also committed sacrilege and grave desecration. Do you want to express your opinion on these accusations?

Yes, I'd like to. I really perpetrated all those proud and noble deeds, my son. But you won't hear anything more from me. I've told you all I wanted to say. From now on I'll be silent about what I did for the benefit of those who have understood.
What wicked purposes did you pursue by the alleged invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon?
As I said, I won't tell you anything more, my son. You may spare yourself the effort. And I won't grant you the pleasure of hearing me scream. Pain has no power over me.
Was the alleged invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon your own decision or did the disgusting idea originated in the head of another?

You're wasting your time, my son. I will tell you nothing more, however long you would torture me. If you are so clever and keen as you think you are, you surely will find it yourself and so it's useless for me to help you in any way.
Did you arrive in Hillbrandt for the purpose of committing the crimes you are accused of? Or did you decide to perpetrate them only during your stay here?

Your efforts are really quite useless, my son. I won't tell you more, however long you would torture me. You have to look elsewhere for the answers for your questions—if you are clever enough to find them.
How did you manage to entice Baroness Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann to your infernal purposes? Had you known them even before arriving to Hillbrandt?

I have nothing more to say about it, my son. Spare your time and end this show. You know well that my will is unbreakable. I endure this all only because I want it so. Death will close my mouth forever.
Do you want to renounce your delusions before God Righteous and confess your sins to clear your soul and have hope for salvation?

Thank you very much for you offer, son, but I'm really not planning to confess. Furthermore the Lord whom I serve plays by different rules and your rites don't interest him. I'm his chosen one and when the time comes I'll return no matter what you do with my dead body.
If you cooperate you may save your life. I will personally push for your death sentence to be changed to lifetime mulus strictus, or even to mere exile. What do you say to that?
My life is worthless compared to that what will arise from my death. Your offers are pointless, my son. But I'd like you to know I greatly appreciate your efforts.
In that case you don't give me any other choice than to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!
Well... It seems it is really useless to further interrogate you. I already have all the evidence needed for your conviction.
Bishop Vallarian, I exhort you one more time to start answering my questions. I'm asking you here before God Almighty. Will you confess?
As I've already told you, I really perpetrated all those proud and noble deeds I'm accused of, my son. But you won't hear anything more from me. I won't say a word.
Alright. After due consideration I'm of the view that it's pointless to interrogate you any further. I already have all the evidence needed for your conviction.

Master Edmond d'Arvias, you've been accused of conspiring with infernal powers for the purpose of the genocide of innocent people and for the purpose of usurping the rule over Hillbrandt. I'm asking you, do you plead guilty of your crimes?

I have nothing to plead guilty of. I'm innocent as sure as there are stars above us. I haven't conspired with anyone for any purpose. And you surely won't force me by torture to confess to something I didn't do. Free me and you'll save much time that you may dedicate to searching for the real culprit.
I don't believe you. You'll be interrogated as long as it is needed for you to confess to your sins! Executioner, do your duty!
Do you really want to endure long hours of torture, master? Confess and you'll feel no pain. None of the instruments you can see here will touch you.
I'm sorry, I can't confess to that what I didn't do. God knows I'm innocent. You've got a wrong man, knight.
If that's your last word, there's nothing I can do about it. May pain make you speak. Executioner, do your duty!
I'm asking you again, master Edmond d'Arvias, do you confess to the crimes you are accused of?

Oh my God, why do you put me to such trials? Didn't I serve you well? I have nothing to confess, knight. I... didn't do anything you charge me with. I've become a victim of... deadly intrigues. I'm innocent, God knows that.
In that case we will continue with the interrogation until you think better of it. Executioner, do your duty!
Soldier Harph, you've been accused of heresy and of conducting necromantic rites for the purpose of perpetrating willful murders. Do you confess to those sins?
No, I'm innocent. I never did a thing even slightly resembling what you charge me with. It's all made-up.
In that case you don't give me any other choice than to put you to the torture. Executioner, do your duty!

If you don't confess, soldier, I will be forced to use torture. You should better think it over while there is still time. You can't even imagine the pain the instruments you can see here will give you.
Go to Hell, knight!
Soldier Harph, I'm asking you again—will you confess to the crimes you are charged with?
I've already told you I'm innocent. Never did I anything even remotely like what you charge me with. It's all made-up.
Alphonso DiCerbio, you're charged with kidnapping Tom Clifford, son of the chamberlain Johaness Clifford. Do you confess to this crime?

Yes, knight, I confess, I did it! Just don't put me, for the love of God, to the torture. I've been always frightened to death of pain. Please, knight... I'll tell you everything, just don't torture me!
We will see. Speak.
Stop that show, DiCerbio. You're looking into the face of God here. Confess, or I will be forced to use torture.

Alright, alright... Well, I just wanted to say my sins are so numerous that a priest would turn gray if I should confess them all. But all my wrongdoings are mere trifles in comparison to those of some people I've met. And one such man I've met here in Glatzburg. He declared he was chosen to do something great and that the Fallen Archangel Azrael himself told him to go and enlist me to his services. I was quite surprised, but then I said to myself—why not? I would gladly give my ass to Hell for all that man offered me. Moreover it was clear he had thought out everything well, so it seemed I couldn't make a mistake if I joined him and did whatever he wanted. And besides it was obvious that if I refused my head would soon end in some stinking sewer. The man was really a big shot, knight. Really big!
Maybe you won't believe me, but it was Duke Rowan van Leerin, the royal vice-governor of the town.

So let's sum this up. Duke Rowan van Leerin came to see you, told you he was chosen for something terrible and that you shall be at his disposal, for which he promised you some adequate reward. Am I right?

Eh... well, you know... they were no innocent matters. But I had to obey him, what else could I do? He told me he needed several innocent gals no matter the costs. I mean virgins, if you understand me. Chicks who have never had a man. And I was to get them for him, or else he would disembowel me and stuff my bowels into my... well, you know where. So I did his bidding. One after one I kidnapped three girls who, based on my findings, were pure. Secretly and without any witnesses I carried them into the basement under his house.
Well, alright, that's enough. I don't need any more information of you. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the decision of the court. Guards, take him away!
I don't believe your confession, DiCerbio. You are lying to me and hence you will be interrogated until you tell the truth. Executioner, do your duty!
Well, Alphonso DiCerbio, I'm asking you once more—for what purpose did you kidnap Tom Clifford?

I've told you already, knight—Duke Rowan van Leerin ordered me to kidnap the boy. He is completely crazy. He thinks he was chosen to do something and I was to help him with it. I kidnapped several gals and Tom Clifford, because he promised me everything you can imagine for it. I thought I would get some fortune at last... I'm telling you the truth, knight. Nothing but the truth.
You are lying and hence you'll be interrogated until you tell the truth. Executioner, do your duty!
Well... alright, I believe you. You will be escorted back to you cell where you'll await the decision of the court.

Release me! I order you, release me at once!
Do you know what will follow if you don't confess voluntarily? I'll have to use torture, though I'll feel great regret doing so.
I'm innocent. And you are making a great mistake, knight. Release me at once!
Alright, I've heard enough for now. Escort him back to his cell.
I'm asking you once more, Raimond Ventano: Do you confess to the crimes you're charged with?
No! It's all bullshit! I did nothing! Release me at once, or you'll be terribly sorry! My standing...

Commander Ethien de Pasque. Are you surprised, knight? As you can see, my allies are powerful. Don't think you'll get away with this. You are playing with greater fire than you are able to imagine! Even now you may count yourself dead, you bastard. Worms will eat your entrails before you can open your mouth and tell someone what you've just learnt.
Whose idea was it to kidnap Francessca Gulvardi?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick's. Yes, you've heard well, knight. She's the High Priestess of the Lord Baphomet's Cult of Chaos. She was the one who devised the way to summon Baphomet into our world. She is our holy leader who will sit next to Lord Baphomet, and I will get my reward then.
Have you really invoked the Fallen Angel Baphomet? When? How? Speak!

It's been some time. It was easier than I thought. But much crazier. I nearly lost my sanity because of it. To summon Baphomet it was needed only to get a body of a dead girl who was mad when she lived, but who had already lost her virginity. Moreover she had to lie in her grave in the graveyard exactly for thirteen nights. Once we managed to get such a corpse, we performed the rite of summoning in an ancient temple of Chaos. We eviscerated her rotting entrails and inserted a poisonous snake into the emboweled body. Then we ravished the dead bitch good. You can't imagine what happened next!
Continue. Tell me all.

I thought it would make me crazy. The snake started to grow, it twitched and writhed, it changed before our eyes and started to take a monstrous shape... It lashed with slimy tentacles, bone spikes were growing from it... it was becoming Baphomet. Eventually the temple was full of him, so big he was. A single look at him would mean losing my mind. Only Priestess Yulliette could rise her sight to him and speak to him. I think they fornicated, at least it seemed so judging from the sounds, although Grand Duchess screamed in great pain. I pressed my face into the ground not to see what was going on. And then he was gone. He went away through the gateway that was there on the wall. As if Hell itself has devoured him.
Where is that temple of Chaos you're speaking about?

It's not far away from the gallows. It must have been there for many centuries because it stank like Hell. But you will search in vain for the entrance to the temple, that's for sure. You will never get there! Only he who believes in our master, Lord Baphomet, can see it.
Who murdered Bishop Trevorius?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. It was she who murdered him when the plan to use Francessca Gulvardi didn't work. She gave him a poisoned drink that killed him. It served him right, damned friar. He shouldn't stick his nose into the things that were none of his business.

You think you've managed something, you bastard? You're mistaken, and greatly. Soon your entrails will be hanging from trees and your brain will be lying at my feet. Lord Baphomet will destroy you. Do you hear me, you wretch? He will destroy you!
That's enough, Raimond Ventano. I've heard what I needed. Guards, escort him back to his cell.
I feel you didn't tell me all, Raimond Ventano. Tell me the whole truth or I will continue with the interrogation.
I feel you've concealed something, Raimond Ventano. Tell me the whole truth or I will continue with the interrogation.
You're charged with high crimes, knight Ethien de Pasque. By all appearances you committed the crimes of kidnapping, heresy, high treason and of sacrilege. Will you confess to these sins?

No, knight. I have nothing to confess. I did nothing and I don't understand how it is possible you're accusing me of something so awful. Most likely I've become a victim of some mistake—or even an intrigue—and that has blinded your eyes. I'm totally innocent, as sure as there's God above me.
If you don't plead guilty voluntarily, sir knight, I will have to—although I would hate to do it—put you to torture.
I'm innocent. I won't confess to anything I didn't do. And you're making a grave mistake not believing me.
Alright, I've heard enough for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell, sir knight, where you'll be waiting during the rest of the investigation.
I ask you once more, sir knight: Will you confess to the crimes you were charged with?
No. I can't confess to something I didn't do. It would be against all I'm sworn to protect—even at the price of my own life.

Aaaaaaaaahhhhhhh! The pain! Lord Baphomet, my master, why have you left me at the mercy of these disgusting minions of the dead god? What did I do that you've lost all love for me? Didn't I serve you well? Why don't you rescue me and bring me away from here on the wings of madness? Where are you, Baphomet, when I need you?
Do you see, sir knight? You're pleading. Tell me all and your suffering will end at once. Confess your sins!
I can't resist any more. My Lord has abandoned me. He has left me to pain and death. I was betrayed!
Did you participate in the preparing of the heretical rite and the invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet?

Yes I did. We summoned the Fallen Angel Baphomet, really! He appeared before us in all his madness and we fell on our faces and cried bloody tears of joy because the ritual was successful and our Lord has descended among us.
With whom did you perpetrate that disgusting crime?
With Raimond Ventano and with Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick.
Whose idea was it? Who devised such a repulsive notion of invoking the Fallen Angel Baphomet into this world?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick! She led me astray. She seduced me, abused my body as well as my soul. She convinced me I would be the general of infernal armies when we would march the world and conquer one kingdom after another. The woman was mad, knight! Absolutely crazy! If you only could see her, what things she was able to do, all those nasty vulgarities and perversities...
What was the purpose of the alleged invocation of Baphomet?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick told us that when Baphomet entered this world he would unleash dreadful madness and chaos around him from which the new kingdom would rise that would be ruled jointly by us.
Where did you perpetrate that terrible crime? In the temple of Chaos, where I found your necklace?
Yes, exactly. Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick led us there and we performed the rite there during which our Lord entered this world.
Did you and Raimond Ventano kidnap Francessca Gulvardi?

Yes, we did. It was the idea of Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. She maintained we had to get rid of Bishop Trevorius because he was a danger to us. Because he could get us at the gallows. That's why she decided we would kidnap Francessca Gulvardi, whose confessor Bishop Trevorius was, and that we would let the Fallen Angel Baphomet possess her by an unclean spirit. The spirit inside the girl's body was to murder Trevorius without a shade of suspicion falling upon us. It should have been the work of another crazy heretic who would then be rightfully punished.
It was Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. It was she who murdered him when our plan to use Francessca Gulvardi didn't work. She gave him a poisoned drink that killed him.
Does the Cult of the Children of the New Order rings a bell to you, sir knight?
No, I've never heard about it.
You are lying, sir knight! You are its member, there's no doubt about it. What are you intending to achieve by carrying out that Plan of yours? Who is the head of the Cult?
I don't know what you are talking about, knight. I don't know of any Plan. And I don't belong to any cult. Grand Duchess plotted it all. She was mad!
I don't believe you. You will be interrogated until you confess. Executioner, do your duty!
Very well. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the trial.
Alright, that's enough. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the trial.

I ask you once more, knight Ethien de Pasque: Do you belong to the Cult of the Children of the New Order? Who is your leader? And what are you intending to achieve by carrying out that disgusting Plan of yours?
I don't know what are you talking about. I don't belong to any cult. I don't know anything about any Plan. Even if you tore the heart out of my body, I don't know what you are talking about.
Alright, I believe you. You'll be escorted back to your cell, knight, where you'll wait during the course of investigation.

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, you are charged with organizing the conspiracy against God and the Crown. According to the indictment you, as a fallen soul, prepared and along with other heretics performed the ritual of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet. Furthermore you ordered Francessca Gulvardi to be kidnapped. In the name of God Almighty I ask you: Do you confess to those sins?

No, I'm completely innocent. And I won't speak a word from this moment on. You won't hear a sound from me, I promise. The Archangel Gabriel and the First Prophet himself will give me the strength to resist the pain you in your perversity are going to inflict me. And sooner than you'd expect you'll be in my place. You'll be rightfully punished for what you will have dared to do to me. Remember my words!
If you don't confess voluntarily, Grand Duchess, I'll have—although I would really hate to do that—put you to torture.
As I said, I'm innocent and you won't hear a word from me.
Alright, I believe you for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell, where you'll be waiting during the course of the investigation.
I ask you again, Grand Duchess: Do you confess to the crimes you are charged with?
You won't gain anything by being silent, Grand Duchess. Plead guilty and the interrogation will end in an instant.
Nothing? In that case you don't give me any other choice. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright, Grand Duchess. I'll stop the interrogation for now. You'll be escorted back to the cell where you'll have time to think it all over. Guards, take her away!
As you wish, Grand Duchess. Interrogation will continue. Executioner, do your duty!

You bastard! You scabby cripple! You son of a treacherous bitch! I curse you, I curse you thousand times! May black worms eat your entrails while you still live, may your limbs be broken hundredfold, may ugly stinking festering ulcers appear on your body and may your cock never stop dripping blood. You'll be punished by Lord Baphomet, the master of chaos and the ruler of madness. The time will come soon when he rises out of the depths of the Earth into this world and you will be the first who he will make his drooling slave. And then all others will follow, until the world is in complete madness and brother will murder his brother for the eager wanton loins of his sister.
I assume this nice speech of yours is the confession, Grand Duchess.

You poor wretch! You're toiling here with all those petty charges of yours and don't understand you stand against something that exceeds human comprehension. Stop pretending at being a brave knight of God and admit that even now you're looking into the face of eternal despair. You'll suffer for laying your hands on me. On me, the first concubine of Lord Baphomet! Oh yes, you've heard well! I fornicated with the Fallen Angel himself! He fertilized me with the seed of madness and made me the mother of his cursed children of Chaos. Come to me, my children! Your mother calls you! Kill that disgusting minion of the dead god! Eat his entrails and gouge out his eyes! Tear him to pieces and take me back to your father, Lord Baphomet!
What... what is... Oh my God! They're all around us!
Your disgusting children are dead, Grand Duchess. As you can see, no one will help you.
Nooooooo! You murderer! You damned bastard! You killed my children, my beautiful, beloved children! You killed them...!
Yes, Grand Duchess, I killed them. They were spawns of Hell. And now confess all you sins!
You bastard... You killed my children!
Dietrich the gravedigger confessed he procured for you a dead girl's body from the city cemetery and you paid him for it. Is it true?

So the scabby bastard told you? Oh well... it doesn't matter now. Yes, he procured for us a corpse we needed. It was the corpse of a young girl, almost a child, but not a virgin any more. And also she was mad, just as we needed. It was told that she lost her mind when her own father raped her. She was so sweet... Those beautiful lips! Little hard breasts! And the shameless loins! Have you ever fornicated with a dead girl, knight? Have you ever sucked delightful breasts of a crazy woman dead for thirteen days?
What did you need the corpse of that poor girl for? To invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet?

Sure, for what else? Why do you ask so stupidly when you know it? I must tell you that God of yours looked with envy when I ripped out the entrails of the dead bitch and put the poisonous snake in their place. And I'm convinced that your God still only silently envied when the others violated the dead girl to give rise to the Lord Baphomet. I'm sure he would preferably join in. He made a mistake when he has bound himself with too absurd rules and restrictions. He can't even guess what delights he's missing because of it.
Blasphemer! Who were your accomplices? Who helped to prepare the perverse ritual?

Why, you know it, you poor wretch! So why do you ask me? You tortured the confession out of Raimond Ventano and Commander Ethien de Pasque, so what's your point here? You should have seen them when they in ecstasy took hold of the corpse of that scabby bitch down there in the ancient temple. They ripped off her shroud like wild animals and took her in such a way that they almost destroyed the corpse. It was a wonderful sight.
Whose idea it was to summon the Fallen Angel Baphomet? Who devised that madness? And what did you intend to achieve by doing it?

You still don't understand, do you? Your mind is unable to accept the fact that the glorious God's earthly kingdom is soon to end after having stinked here for thousand years, and that infernal powers will assume the reign of the world. You defend that what exists no more, you fool! Lord Baphomet entered our world and he will soon open the gate of his Temple of Madness in it. And then utter madness and chaos will overcome the world. Brother will kill brother, sister will perish by the hand of her own sister. Out of the flames of infernal madness the kingdom will rise, ruled by the Baphomet's chosen ones. I will be amongst them, because it was I who devised his resurrection! I knew that when Lord Baphomet walks the world again, the prophecy, in which I had been foretold a kingdom without borders, would fulfill.
In that case you will surely tell me where you found out how to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet into this world.
What? What do you mean by this, you wretch?
If it was your idea to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet, you can surely tell me how you found out what you need for the rite.
I had a dream in which Lord Baphomet appeared to me and ordered me what I must do. So it happened and I did his bidding then. And now he is amongst us and you're going to become his slave soon!
You're lying, Grand Duchess. You might have a dream, but to perform the rite you needed certain book that describes it. What was the name of the book? Do you know it?
Book? What book?
The book Libre Daemonium in which there's the description of the ritual of invocation of the Fallen Angels!
But...
So it wasn't your idea to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet. So, whose?
It was my idea! I devised it and...

No, Grand Duchess, you are lying. The book Libre Daemonium had to be sent to you by Bishop Vallarian from Hillbrandt after he got it from the merchant Kurth Ollmier. You don't know a thing about the book. So, who was it? Who led you astray and made you to do all those crimes? Who stands behind you? Whom do you cover? As you can see neither him nor the Fallen Angel Baphomet will help you.

It was... it was Cardinal Truncquillius. We had been lovers for years. He revealed to me the secrets of forbidden books and magic grimoires. He taught me like his disciple. We performed many forbidden rites. He always suggested to me that the time would come when we both are powerful, very powerful. That he knew something that would change the whole world. And this spring he came to me and told me the time had come. He promised me the place alongside Lord Baphomet who we were supposed to invoke. He declared that this world will perish and the new one will be born, ruled by the Fallen Angel And by us. He told it was needed only to invoke Lord Baphomet. So I did his bidding. He told me what I had to procure. A corpse of a crazy girl buried for thirteen days in holy ground, a poisonous snake, desecrated hosts, fresh blood of a lamb, ashes from the executioner's stake on which a heretic burned... I got it all and Lord Baphomet really came.
Cardinal Truncquillius? I don't believe you!

Are you surprised, knight? Yes, it was Cardinal Truncquillius. He planned it all in detail and entrusted me to implement it. At least he wanted me to think it was his idea. But I found out he probably acted at someone other's bidding. He had on him several letters, brought to him in the spring by a messenger from Alvaron. He thought I didn't know about them, but he underestimated me. I'm not so naive to believe everything he was telling me.
The letters? What letters are you speaking about?

As I said, Cardinal Truncquillius had letters on him that he guarded like the crown jewels. I'm sure there were instructions in them upon which he acted when preparing the rite of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet.
Who wrote those letters?

I don't know. A messenger brought them to him from Alvaron, the capital of the Realm. I don't have the slightest idea who wrote them. But I know Cardinal Truncquillius guarded them like the crown jewels.
What do you know about the Cult of the Children of the New Order?
What cult? I don't know what you are talking about, it doesn't ring a bell. Why should I know that cult?

Because that cult presumably plans something greater than just invoking the Fallen Angels. And if you don't know a thing about the Cult, then it's as plain as day that you were just exploited and that they never counted with you as a Baphomet's concubine! You were exploited and fooled!
I haven't heard a thing about any cult...!
Was it you who murdered Bishop Trevorius?

Yes, I killed him. I prepared a deadly poison and gave it to him. The trustful fool accepted it and even thanked me. I thought he would be more suspicious since the attack of Francessca Gulvardi. But I was surprised how long he endured the effect of the poison before falling dead. I was waiting for him by the Grand Duke's Gazebo, right where you were to meet him on that secret conspiratorial meeting of yours. Don't be surprised I know about it. I know many things. And there, by the old desolate gazebo, where no one goes these days, I gave him the drink. I'm just sorry I wasn't able to play with his dead body.
I don't believe that you don't know about the Cult of the Children of the New Order. You'll be interrogated until you confess!
I don't know a thing about any damned cult, you scabby bastard!
In that case I can do nothing but to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!

I don't believe you, Grand Duchess, that the Curial Inquisitor Cardinal Truncquillius is behind the invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet. You'll be interrogated until you reveal the name of the real culprit.
It beats you, doesn't it? But it's true, you wretch! Cardinal Truncquillius devised it and planned every detail. Provided he wasn't acting on behalf of somebody else, as I personally presume.
Very well. That's enough, Grand Duchess. You'll be escorted back to your cell, where you'll wait for the trial. Guards, take her away!

I ask you once more, Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, what do you know about the Cult of the Children of the New Order? Are you its member? What do you intend to achieve by carrying out that Plan of yours?
I've already told you, you wretch, that I don't know about any cult. And I don't know a thing about any plan.
I don't believe you, Grand Duchess. You don't give me any other choice than to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!
I ask you again, Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, who schemed the crime of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet?
I've already told you, you wretch, that it was Cardinal Truncquillius! Provided there isn't someone else standing behind the Cardinal, as I personally presume.
Alright, I believe you, Grand Duchess. Now you'll be escorted back to the cell where you'll wait for the trial. Guards, take her away!
Cardinal Truncquillius, you've confessed you're a member of the Cult of the Children of the New Order, and that you're its dark priest.
Save the effort, my son. You'll learn nothing from me. You'd do best to put me to the court straight away. My will is stronger than your tools, I assure you.

Cardinal Truncquillius, tell me, what exactly does the Cult of the Children of the New Order intends to achieve by carrying out its monstrous Plan? What infernal goal are you aiming to accomplish by those wicked doings of yours?
I'm sorry, my son, but you're not destined to get this information from me. But I trust you'll find it out someday, if it's your fate—probably in the instant of your death.
Cardinal Truncquillius, I'm asking you again: who stands behind all your disgusting crimes? Who sent you those letters in which he calls upon you to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet?
In that case I'm forced to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright, Cardinal, that's enough for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell, where you'll be waiting during the course of the investigation. Guards, take him away!

Gardener Downay, you're accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. According to the results of the investigation you were a follower of the Cult of the Children of the New Order. I'm asking you in the name of God Almighty: do you confess to those sins?
No, I'm innocent. Damned, let me go, I didn't do anything. You can't torture an innocent man. That's illegal! Knight, listen to me. I'm as pure as the driven snow!
If you don't plead guilty voluntarily, I'll have to—although it will grieve me to do so—put you to the torture. I'd like you to be aware of that.
I'm telling you that I'm innocent and I didn't do anything. Let me go, this is a mistake. God knows what that crazy old man Balthazar heard.
You're clinging to your sins and refuse to confess. In that case you don't give me any other choice. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright, I believe you for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell, where you'll be waiting during the course of the investigation. Guards, take him away!
I'm asking you again, Downay the gardener, do you confess to the crimes you're accused of? Do you belong to the Cult of the Children of the New Order?
You sadistic bastard! It amuses you to torture a cripple, doesn't it? You are excited by seeing the pain you inflict to people, am I right? But I'm innocent. Can you hear me? INNOCENT!
So you won't confess? In that case you don't give me any other choice than to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright, I'll end the interrogation for now. You'll be escorted back to the cell. I advise you to think it all over. Guards, take him away!

Enough! I'll confess. I belong to the Cult of the Children of the New Order. Yes, I'm its member and I'm awaiting the day the Earth will become part of Hell and we—the Children of the New Order—will rule here! And the day will come soon, don't worry about that. The gates of Hell will open, hundreds of thousands of beasts will come and all what will come into their way will perish under their hoofs. And I, I will get my revenge. All who've ever done me wrong or mocked me will be my slaves. You'll be one of them, knight. I promise!
Who introduced you to the Cult, sinner? Who told you about it and led you astray?

It was my master, Seneschal Jean de Guise. Only he was kind to me, he gave me helping hand and told me comforting words. Only he saw me as a powerful man, a man able to do everything others may do, and not only as a cripple hobbling around. He offered me to enter his service—and being in his strong loving embrace I was told about the secrets of the Cult. And I helped him in everything he wanted me to.
What horrible crimes did you perpetrate because of his perverse affection?

This spring I helped him to prepare the heretical mass attended by all the priests of the restored Cult—for the first time after several centuries. I stole a dozen of unbaptized newborns from cradles of their mothers and sacrificed them on the altar of the Dark Prince. From their entrails I cooked narcotic potions. From their skins I made parchments and from their skulls I carved ritual bowls. I found a suitable place for the Sabbath itself and prepared it in such a way as my master had instructed me.
That's disgusting! How could you...?! You'll be rightly punished for that.

You think you've won against me, knight? You're gravely mistaken! Sooner than you manage to do anything the New Order will come and the God's earthly kingdom will burn in infernal flames. Remember that the New Order is going to come soon! Soon!
Enough! You'll be escorted to the cell, where you'll wait for the rightful trial. Guards, take him away!
It seems to me there's something you're concealing from me. Tell me the whole truth or I'll continue with the interrogation.
Where is the place where that heinous black mass of the dark priests took place?
You'll find it in the Gardens of Grief, deep under the earth's surface. A fallen star has uncovered the entrance to that unholy place. There it all took place and I, Downay, have the greatest credit!
Do you know any other members of the Cult aside from Jean de Guise?
No, I don't. My master told me I don't need to know anyone else.
Sven Larsen, you're charged with the murder of the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie. In the name of God Almighty I ask you: Will you plead guilty of that crime?

What should I say now, knight? Naturally I can't confess—I would deprive myself of all the torture and would go straight to the gallows. No, knight, I won't plead guilty. I don't know what you're talking about. I've never seen that paladin. Did I say it right?
Enough of that perfidious game! If you don't plead voluntarily, I'll have to—although quite unwillingly—put you to the torture. You should understand that.

I'm aware of it, knight. More than you think. It's SO exciting for me. I've never experienced anything so exciting. In fact it's the first exciting thing what happened to me in all my boring life. You can't imagine how dull my life has been.
Oh yes, knight. Thank you... Oooooooohhhhhhhhh!
Alright, we'll stop for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the next interrogation. Guards, take him away!

It ends already? Why, we've hardly started, knight! This is really not nice of you. I was looking forward to experiencing the threshold of pain and instead you're gonna lock me away to that stinking cell again. But as you wish, I can wait. You surely will reconsider.

I'm asking you once more, Sven Larsen: Will you confess to the crime you are accused of? Did you murder the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie? What led you to that? Was it the calling of the powers of darkness? Are you a minion of Hell? Speak!

No, I'm afraid I can't confess—the pain hasn't been so unbearable so far to force me to want it to end. And as I think about it I doubt it is possible to inflict such pain to me. But it is definitely... fantastic. At least I feel I'm living, after many years of dullness. Last time I felt something similar was when I killed my stepmother and my father by these very hands. My life has been just a single working day since then. Only now I've awakened again!
So you won't confess? In that case you don't give me any other choice. Executioner, do your duty!
Yes, knight, let's continue! It's so... fascinating! Aaaaaaaaaaahhhhhhhhh!
Well... I'll stop the interrogation for now. You'll be escorted back to the cell. I advise you to reconsider it all while waiting for the next interrogation. Guards, take him away!
You want to end already, knight? Why, we've hardly started, knight! I must know how deep my pain can be. It's like being born again. But as you wish, I can wait.

That's... incredible. I feel such pain that the feeling pierces the very heart of my being! I can't... I can't endure it. Stop it! STOP! I'd never say something like this will happen to me. I'm LIVING! I feel pain, I feel fear... That's splendid! Thank you, knight. You let me feel the taste of life again.
So, do you plead guilty of murdering the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie? Was it you who sent the murderous arrow?

Yes, it was me, knight. And it wasn't the first time I murdered someone. I've been an assassin for years. In fact from my youth. You wouldn't imagine how dewy-eyed are people to children. But I won't tire you with talking about cruel childhood and about how my father beat me and my stepmother forced me to comply to wishes of wealthy strangers. We all have our own stigmata. The truth is that when I was standing above their dead bodies and was watching them getting cold, I was excited like never before. I thought that killing another person would give me similar excitement throughout my whole life. But it wasn't so. My life became an emotional desert then. I didn't feel anything. Fear, sorrow, pain, hate, love, friendship... shortly, nothing. I became completely lethargic and murdered for money without a trace of regret. I think I've become a perfect killer because of it. It wasn't possible to either bribe me or persuade me. I was merciless, but all the time I was yearning for human emotions. For any emotions.
Who hired you to kill Eradim d'Chambrie?

Who? That's easy. It was that coward Jean de Guise, the Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He pretends being a brave knight, but in fact he is a wretch unable to look into his own eyes. I'm almost sorry for that poor coward. My stomach rises every time I just think of him. But he paid and so my services were his.
Are you telling me that the murder of the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie was ordered by his superior, Seneschal Jean de Guise?

I've just told you so, knight. Listen carefully when speaking with me. I don't like to repeat myself. Yes, it was Jean de Guise who paid me for the murder. He came one evening and without much hesitation paid for the paladin's death. Do you see? I'm a death dealer. I sell the most raw goods in the world—death!
Do you know why Jean de Guise wished the paladin Eradim d'Chambrie dead?

No, I don't have the slightest idea. And I don't care—it's none of my business. I don't get paid for caring but for killing. I'm a death dealer, I sell the most raw goods of all. Motives of my unmanly clients are of no interest to me. How I'm sorry for them in their misery! It's making me vomit. They accept death, but don't want their hands to get stained by blood. Weaklings!
How many gold pieces did you get for murdering the paladin?
Is it so important? If I remember correctly, it was 666 gold pieces.
That's all I needed to hear. Now you'll be escorted back to your cell, where you'll wait for the court to pass the rightful judgment on you.

So is this the end? Will I be escorted to the cell of condemned now where I'll be waiting for the hour of my death? I'm not going to delude myself that the fear of dying is absent in me, but the experience was worth it. I felt all my life once again. Take me away, guardsmen, I'm ready to enjoy myself dying.
I'm not happy with your confession, Sven Larsen. It seems to me there's something you're concealing from me. Tell me the whole truth or I'll continue with the interrogation.

Duke Verenicus of Khentt, you're accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. According to the results of investigation you participated in the murder of Prince Louis by means of invoking powers of darkness. In the name of God Almighty I'm asking you: Will you confess to those sins?

Did you know, knight, that Erebornian lawyers from the school of Severinus struggled to enforce a principle that would ban forcing the defendant to confess using torture? As you can see, the inquisitorial law hasn't let itself to be influenced by the Erebornian legal principles in this matter. None the less I insist on not confessing.
Confess voluntarily, Duke, and nothing will happen to you. You'll avoid very unpleasant experience that way.
I'm sorry, knight. You should better forsake your vain efforts and find yourself some nice place from where you'll watch the New Order coming. Because it will start soon!
What? You're a member of the Cult of the Children of the New Order?!
I have nothing to tell about it, knight. But apparently you have a good general view, I must admit that. Regrettably soon it will be of no use to you.

Alright, we'll end for now. You'll be escorted back to your cell where you'll wait for the next interrogation. I advise you to think better of your position—think of the salvation of your soul. Guards, take him away!

Duke Verenicus of Khentt, I'm asking you again: Will you confess to the crimes you are charged with? Did you participate in the murder of the Crown Prince Louis? Are you a minion of dark powers? Speak!
I have nothing to tell you about it, knight. You're wasting your time here, believe me.
In that case you don't give me any other choice, Duke. Executioner, do your duty.
Alright, I'll stop the interrogation for now. You'll be escorted back to the cell. I advise you to think it all over—think of the salvation of your soul. Guards, take him away!
Enough! I'll confess... it's all true. I'll tell anything you want, just stop torturing me!
So, do you confess to taking part in the murder of Prince Louis? Are you a member of the Cult of the Children of the New Order? What did you intend to achieve by the murder? Speak!
Yes, I confess. I belong to the Cult of the Children of the New Order. But I didn't participate in the murder of Prince Louis.
You lie! I have the confession of Corin Morray and Kathryn Winhold. They told me you were personally present during the rite resulting in the death of Prince Louis.
It's true that I participated in the ritual. It even was me who at that time two years ago let my companions to the royal palace. But it's not true that Prince Louis was murdered.
What are you talking about?! He has been buried in the royal crypt for two years already!

Yes, that's true. But Louis is not dead. The ritual we performed in his chamber put him into a state near death, but he is still alive. So as you can see, it's not possible to speak about a murder. But all other is true. I really belong to the Children of the New Order. Once our Plan is finished the title of Infernal Prince will be bestowed to me and I'll rule the world along with my brothers and sisters. At last I'll go one step further. I almost started to become desperate about finishing my life in the services of that idiot Edward. I pined for getting higher, I wished to enforce some turning points in the society, to reign nations and dictate them my will. And with the Children of the New Order all that will become reality. I won't insist I like all the practices of the Cult, but as they say, the end justifies the means.
What plans does the Cult have with Prince Louis? Why did you performed the rite?

I don't know, knight. The Dark High Priest of the Cult ordered the rite to be performed without telling us anything about it. He doesn't have to explain anything to us—his word is a law for us. So we did his bidding without asking. Once the Prince was put in the royal tomb the High Priest cursed it by a powerful curse so no one could get inside and find out Prince Louis was still alive.
With whom did you perform that disgusting rite in the chamber of Prince Louis? Who are your accomplices and dark brothers?

The ritual was attended by the Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous Jean de Guise, and by Cardinal Commendoni, the Inquisitor General of the Holy Office. Are you surprised? Yes, I can see you are. Maybe you're starting to understand you stand on the wrong side. Surely you realize you can never defeat us, because our influence extends too high. We know all and nothing can evade our attention. And we're ready for anything. We will be one step ahead of you all the time.
What happened after you finished that disgusting rite?

Prince Louis was found dead and buried in the royal tomb. And King Edward sank deep into despair and melancholy—exactly according to our plan. It was easy for me to drown his sorrow in wine and advise him not to stop. He became a broken man whom I was able to control quite easily. That was why he signed Decretum Inquisitorium—the inquisitorial decree giving special jurisdiction in fighting heresy. And what can't you stamp as heresy these days?
But then the confession of the royal servant girl Kathryn Winhold appeared, am I right?

Yes, just as you said. It showed that the silly ninny witnessed all our actions. And not only she—the other servant girl, Corin Morray, saw it too. Luckily Kathryn was so stupid as to confess. We got to know it instantly and the next day she was arrested for murdering Prince Louis. We turned it all against her. She was so vulnerable... But the other one was more clever. She ran away from the city as soon as she found Kathryn was arrested. We were looking for her for some time, but eventually we stopped it because it was pointless. She was declared an escapee of the Inquisition so she was unable to get help from anyone. I didn't anticipate she would survive and reveal her testimony to you. I'm sorry now for not hunting her down and wringing her neck then.
Do you want to say Cardinal Commendoni is a member of the Cult of the Children of the New Order?

Yes, knight. And he's not only a member, he's the Dark High Priest of the Cult. Yes, you've heard well. It's him who has planned and governed it all, it's him who has been standing behind the intrigues of the entire Cult. He knows about everything and controls everything. He know who you are and it's only a matter of time before you appear in my position—as a defendant.
That's all I needed to hear. Now you'll be escorted to the cell where you will wait for the inquisitorial court that will pass the rightful sentence on you.
No, knight, you didn't understand. There will be no judgment—except maybe the final one—and I guarantee you it won't be very pleasant for you. But you're going to find out for yourself soon.
I feel you are keeping something from me, Duke. Tell me the whole truth or I'll continue with the interrogation.
Your confession didn't satisfy me, Duke Verenicus of Khentt. I feel you are concealing something from me. Tell me the whole truth or I'll continue with the interrogation.
Vick Lenght, you're accused of grave robbing in the city cemetery and in the vicinity of Alvaron. I ask you before God Almighty: did you perpetrated those crimes?
No, I'm completely innocent, knight. I don't know a thing about any graves. Who says otherwise is a foul-spoken liar.
If you don't confess voluntarily I'll be forced to put you to the torture. Do you realize what pain you may avoid?

The pain means nothing to me. I fell on my head in my youth and I haven't felt any pain since then. So you can't intimidate me by torture. Moreover I've told you several times that I'm innocent and that I didn't rob any graves.
As you wish. In that case you don't give me any other choice. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright, I believe you. You'll be escorted back to the cell where you'll be waiting during the progress of the investigation. Guards, take him away!
I ask you once more, Vick Lenght: Will you plead guilty of the crimes you're accused of? Did you rob graves in the city cemetery and in the vicinity of Alvaron?
So you refuse to confess? In that case you don't give me any other choice. Executioner, do your duty!

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, you're charged with heresy. Apparently you desecrated a grave at the city cemetery and stole a corpse from it. According to the charge you prepared a disgusting infernal Sabbath with the help of the felonious knight Benthley of Welshrem. Do you confess to those sins?

I think that I'll answer in the same way as most of the indictees who fell into your hands did. I'm innocent. I didn't do anything you're talking about. And if you actually have some evidence, it is forged. That's all I can tell you about it. I'm innocent and God sees it!
You deny? In that case you don't give me any other choice than to continue with the interrogation. Executioner, do your duty!
Alright. I'll end the interrogation for now. You'll be escorted back to the cell. I advise you, Grand Duke, think it all over well. Guards, take him away!
I suppose that evidence of your husband's heresy was false, wasn't it?!
Correct. Cardinal Truncquillius thought, that we could keep off the attention of the Holy Inquisition that way... and I would get rid of that loser who had annoyed me for the whole life!

Sam Riemann, you are accused of committing several horrible crimes together with baroness Linda van Gallagan, including participation on black Sabbath that allegedly led to invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon. Do you confess to your crimes?
I didn't do anything! I'm innocent! Baroness van Gallagan lies, she is a lying whore!
I ask you again, Sam Riemann, do you confess your crimes against God and the Crown?
God... enough! I curse baroness van Gallagan for revealing me! Many times I wished to grip her skinny neck and strangle her. I should have done it long time ago...
So do you confess?

Yes, I confess, if you need to hear it. It doesn't matter anyway. In a while you're gonna die! Yes, we summoned the Fallen Angel Arthamon! He came to us to become our new lord! And I'll command his armies! I will head his troops of hellish monsters and I'll let them ruin the Realm. I'll take whatever I want! And nobody will stop me from doing it, because I'll be invincible! I'll be the tyrant of the world!
Who has thought up this madness? Who has come up with the idea of invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon?

Who? It was judge Vallarian. He is the highest infernal priest of Arthamon's ancient cult! Surprised huh? I see you didn't expect it, uh uh! An inquisitorial judge planned this heresy you're investigating here! What do you thing you can do now, huh? Nothing! Absolutely nothing, you fool!
Was it you, who helped baroness Linda van Gallagan to steal the body of baroness Gwenn von Weill from the graveyard?
That's right, sir knight. It was me, who dig her body off and who helped to take it to the Dragon Rock, where we did the evocation and allowed Lord Arthamon to enter this world!
Are you saying that you really evoked Fallen Angel Arthamon?
Of course! This world will be destroyed and on it's ruins Kingdom of Hell with an undefeatable army will rise. And I will command this army!
That is enough, Sam Riemann. You will be escorted back to your cell, where you'll be waiting during the rest of the investigation. Guards, take him away!
I don't believe your testimony, Riemann. You're either lying or you're still hiding something.
Sam Riemann, I ask you again to tell the whole truth about crimes you confessed. Speak the truth and you will be spared from an agonizing pain caused by torture.
I've told you everything, Father. I've concealed nothing, I swear!
I'm sorry, I can't confess to that what I didn't do. God knows I'm innocent. You've got a wrong man, Father.

Yes, Father, I confess, I did it! Just don't put me, for the love of God, to the torture. I've been always frightened to death of pain. Please, Father... I'll tell you everything, just don't torture me!

Alright, alright... Well, I just wanted to say my sins are so numerous that a priest would turn gray if I should confess them all. But all my wrongdoings are mere trifles in comparison to those of some people I've met. And one such man I've met here in Glatzburg. He declared he was chosen to do something great and that the Fallen Archangel Azrael himself told him to go and enlist me to his services. I was quite surprised, but then I said to myself—why not? I would gladly give my ass to Hell for all that man offered me. Moreover it was clear he had thought out everything well, so it seemed I couldn't make a mistake if I joined him and did whatever he wanted. And besides it was obvious that if I refused my head would soon end in some stinking sewer. The man was really a big shot, Father. Really big!

I've told you already, Father—Duke Rowan van Leerin ordered me to kidnap the boy. He is completely crazy. He thinks he was chosen to do something and I was to help him with it. I kidnapped several gals and Tom Clifford, because he promised me everything you can imagine for it. I thought I would get some fortune at last... I'm telling you the truth, Father. Nothing but the truth.
I'm innocent. And you are making a great mistake, Father. Release me at once!

Commander Ethien de Pasque. Are you surprised, Father? As you can see, my allies are powerful. Don't think you'll get away with this. You are playing with greater fire than you are able to imagine! Even now you may count yourself dead, you bastard. Worms will eat your entrails before you can open your mouth and tell someone what you've just learnt.

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick! She led me astray. She seduced me, abused my body as well as my soul. If you only could see her, what things she was able to do, all those nasty vulgarities and perversities...
I don't know what you are talking about, Father. I don't know of any Plan. And I don't belong to any cult. Grand Duchess plotted it all. She was mad!

You poor wretch! You're toiling here with all those petty charges of yours and don't understand you stand against something that exceeds human comprehension. On me, the first concubine of Lord Baphomet! Oh yes, you've heard well! I fornicated with the Fallen Angel himself! It wasn't possible to either bribe me or persuade me. I was merciless, but all the time I was yearning for human emotions. For any emotions.

And the disgraced body is slowly starting to decay. No matter what happened here, it took place several days ago. Rain has washed away most of the trails since then.

Wait a minute, what have we here? Those are... shells of some strange black egg. Hmm... it seems it has entered into the body of the poor woman instead of her heart. And what's worse—it seems something hatched out of that egg. Strange. Really strange. And at the same time worrying.
Maybe I should take the body with me and find someone who could inspect it and tell me some details concerning the death of the girl. Every clue counts.
God Almighty... it seems as though some unholy rite took place here similar to the one performed by Judge Vallarian in Hillbrandt during which the Fallen Angel Arthamon was supposedly invoked.

Yes, there's every indication that I'm right. The body of the victim is disemboweled in a similar way as the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill was. But it seems the death didn't come before too long. The girl has been dead for about two weeks. God protect us from heretics able to do such things!

Yes, there's every indication that I'm right. The body of the victim is disemboweled in a similar way as the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill was. But it seems the death didn't come before too long. The girl has been dead for about two weeks. It means that it's really possible they attempted to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet here, as Raimond Ventano told me. God protect us from heretics able to do such things!
Have you already recovered from what happened to you?

I'm trying to forget it, knight. And I'm quite successful at it. After all nothing ultimately horrible happened to me thanks to your help. Though I'm sure it will still haunt my dreams as long as I live.

What do I think about the present crisis? Several years ago I was unable to imagine something so horrible, knight. All the death, suffering, pain, despair... Local people are stubborn, knight. They're hard to themselves and also to others. That's because life here is so difficult. It has never been easy here, knight. We are far to the north, almost at the frontier of the wilderness of the Moonshine Mountains. That's why we are quite hardened. Though in spite of that these bad times make us despair deeply. Where shall we find comfort and sustenance when all disintegrates around us?
I'm searching for any heretics here in Hillbrandt. Do you suspect anyone?

Pardon me, knight, but regrettably I have no suspicion of heresy. I can't help you in that. I'm sorry, I'd be so happy to be of any help to you for all that you've done for me. In any case if I get to know something I'll surely inform you.

It wasn't long ago when I was awakened in the middle of the night by a horrible windstorm. Wind was howling through the town streets like a pack of werewolves; its sound sent shivers down my spine. And that was only the beginning, because all hell broke lose then. I wasn't able to sleep because of the horror. None in the town remembers such a formidable storm. I swear I saw something prancing about in the sky. It was no illusion, I'm sure of it. They were demons, knight. Infernal creatures were flying in the air and were laughing at me frighteningly as if very Hell opened for a while and lost souls soared out of it. It was horrible.

The accusation of Master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy is absurd, knight! I've known master Edmond for long time and I can tell you for sure he's a man fully devoted to his holy mission. He would never entangle himself with infernal powers. I don't know where those fables of seeing him opening the gate to the orcs during their recent attack on Hillbrandt are coming from, but I decidedly don't believe them. Regretfully there are not many people who think of the Master the same way as I do. Most of the others blame him for almost everything that has befallen us in recent years without any real certainty he is in fact guilty. Try listening to that madman Reitdorf, he's a fomenter without a trace of common sense. But people give ear to him nonetheless.
Someone stole the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius from the church. Do you know anything about it?

I've heard about the disappearance of the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius. It's such a terrible event! Who could do something like that? Without the protection of the Monstrance, infernal monsters may attack us any time and nothing more than a handful of weary royal soldiers would defend us against them. The Monstrance protected us all against evil out there and now it is gone. That explains why the orcs managed to get through the walls during their recent attempt to capture the town. I wish I knew something that would help you to find the culprit.

I know nothing about the unfortunate disappearance of our diocesan Bishop Quentinus. I'm terribly sorry, knight. Bishop Quentinus was a great support for all of us. I pray for the salvation of his soul.

Regrettably I don't have a clue about where Paul Hammerhand could be, knight. I've heard of his disappearance and I must say it's not the first time it's happened. He is an unruly boy, his father just can't cope with him. I hope nothing terrible has happened to him, but frankly, I wouldn't be surprised if he broke his neck somewhere. He is really a troublesome child!
Do you know Baroness Linda van Gallagan? According to her husband she disappeared the night the orcs attacked the town. Do you happen to know anything about her?

I wasn't in touch with Baroness Linda van Gallagan much. But I was quite fond of her. She seemed so serene and austere all the time. I'm sorry such a bad fate befell her. She probably fell into the hands of those unholy monsters. I wish I could help her more than only praying for her.

Do I know anything about the death of the merchant Ollmier? Yes, I've heard something about the case. Reputedly he was found one morning in the attic of the Truthorn's inn with his throat cut. They say the murderer also cut his... ehm... manhood and stuffed it into his mouth. Disgusting... It had to be some demon.
Demon? Why do you think so?
Because it left no trace. As if it sank into the earth or if it vanished into thin air. That's why the investigation led to no conclusions.

Am I'm single? Yes, I am. But I trust that there will be someone sooner or later who will love me and whom I will love. And such a man I'll marry and we will live happily together. I believe in love more than in anything else, and should I ever marry I shall do so only out of love. Do you believe in love too, knight?
Certainly. I wish you good luck, child.
Thank you, knight. You're so sweet.
I believe in the love of God!
Oh yes, I certainly believe in it too. But I believe in love between people too. And such love will surely lead me to the altar.
I believe in love in the same way I believe in cancer.
Oh, knight, how can you be so cruel?
You want to know who rules Hillbrandt and the surrounding domains? That's easy, our rulers are Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town, and Baron Robert van Gallagan, the royal vice-governor.
Do you know how much pain one may experience when put to torture, Natalia? If you don't want to get to know, then you had better answer me.
I don't care how you think of me, Natalia. But you surely understand that your answer is very important not only to me. Please, answer my question.
You're young, beautiful and on top of it clever, Natalia. Don't force me to think you're closelipped.
You don't need to fear any more. I'll accompany you back to town—I promised it to your father.
Thank God. I'm so glad it all ended. I want to get out of here as soon as possible and to forget all those horrors.
Calm down, child. You have nothing to fear now.
I'm so grateful to you, knight. Will you accompany me back to the town to my father? Please? I'm sure he will reward you handsomely for all you've done for me.
Certainly. I can't leave you alone in the midst of the wilderness. Let's go, your father will surely be happy when he sees you again.
I'm sorry, I don't have time. Goodbye.
You will really leave me alone here in the midst of the wilderness? I beseech you, knight, help me. Get me back to the town. My father will surely pay you anything you'd ask.
Alright, let's go.
As I said, I don't have time. Goodbye.

Oh my God, the devil's dead! I almost lost all hope of ever being rescued from his dirty hands. I'd have never thought there's such a monster inside him. When he started to court me I even had a feeling for a short time that he loved me and that he was the right one. But when my father showed him out it became apparent that money was all he wanted. How lucky I was that you came before he managed to do me more harm.

Oh my God, you're so admirable, knight. It was so smart of you to force that devil to flee like a coward by that clever trick. I almost lost all hope of ever being rescued from his dirty hands.
