But when my father showed him out it became apparent that money was all he wanted. How lucky I was that you came before he managed to do me some harm.
Get away from me, you devil! You'd conspired with that vile man who harmed me so much. You're not a knight, you're a villain! They should execute you as soon as possible!

I advise you to be silent and not to say a word to anyone about what happened here. Now I'll escort you back to the town to your father and then it will be over for you—that is if you take my advice to heart. Or else you'll fare badly!

Be quiet you bitch! One more word and I'll wring your neck. Now I'll escort you back to the town to your father and it will be over for you. If you tell a word to anyone about this you'll end on the stake sooner than your father can pay again. Hold your tongue!
Welcome, knight. I must thank you again for saving my life. That devil Jullian surely wouldn't let me go away alive. What can I do for you?
Sure, knight. What do you want to know?
Go away, knight.
I promised your father to escort you back to the town.
Really? In that case forgive me, knight, I was wrong about you. I knew you wouldn't leave me here. Thank you.
I've decided to help you and accompany you back to the town.
Really? In that case forgive me, knight, I was wrong about you. I knew you wouldn't leave me here.
Get away, you devil. There's so much evil in you I can't even look at you. You've ruined my life!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I can't believe that! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even knights rob innocent people! Your behavior utterly dismays me!

I'm trying to forget it, Father. And I'm quite successful at it. After all nothing ultimately horrible happened to me thanks to your help. Though I'm sure it will still haunt my dreams as long as I live.

What do I think about the present crisis? Several years ago I was unable to imagine something so horrible, Father. All the death, suffering, pain, despair... Local people are stubborn, Father. They're hard to themselves and also to others. That's because life here is so difficult. It has never been easy here, Father. We are far to the north, almost at the frontier of the wilderness of the Moonshine Mountains. That's why we are quite hardened. Though in spite of that these bad times make us despair deeply. Where shall we find comfort and sustenance when all disintegrates around us?

Pardon me, Father, but regrettably I have no suspicion of heresy. I can't help you in that. I'm sorry, I'd be so happy to be of any help to you for all that you've done for me. In any case if I get to know something I'll surely inform you.

It wasn't long ago when I was awakened in the middle of the night by a horrible windstorm. Wind was howling through the town streets like a pack of werewolves; its sound sent shivers down my spine. And that was only the beginning, because all hell broke lose then. I wasn't able to sleep because of the horror. None in the town remembers such a formidable storm. I swear I saw something prancing about in the sky. It was no illusion, I'm sure of it. They were demons, Father. Infernal creatures were flying in the air and were laughing at me frighteningly as if very Hell opened for a while and lost souls soared out of it. It was horrible.

The accusation of Master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy is absurd, Father! I've known master Edmond for long time and I can tell you for sure he's a man fully devoted to his holy mission. He would never entangle himself with infernal powers. I don't know where those fables of seeing him opening the gate to the orcs during their recent attack on Hillbrandt are coming from, but I decidedly don't believe them. Regretfully there are not many people who think of the Master the same way as I do. Most of the others blame him for almost everything that has befallen us in recent years without any real certainty he is in fact guilty. Try listening to that madman Reitdorf, he's a fomenter without a trace of common sense. But people give ear to him nonetheless.

I know nothing about the unfortunate disappearance of our diocesan Bishop Quentinus. I'm terribly sorry, Father. Bishop Quentinus was a great support for all of us. I pray for the salvation of his soul.

Regrettably I don't have a clue about where Paul Hammerhand could be, Father. I've heard of his disappearance and I must say it's not the first time it's happened. He is an unruly boy, his father just can't cope with him. I hope nothing terrible has happened to him, but frankly, I wouldn't be surprised if he broke his neck somewhere. He is really a troublesome child!

Am I'm single? Yes, I am. But I trust that there will be someone sooner or later who will love me and whom I will love. And such a man I'll marry and we will live happily together. I believe in love more than in anything else, and should I ever marry I shall do so only out of love. Do you believe in love too, Father?
Thank you, Father. You're so sweet.
Oh, Father, how can you be so cruel?
I'm so grateful to you, Father. Will you accompany me back to the town to my father? Please? I'm sure he will reward you handsomely for all you've done for me.
You will really leave me alone here in the midst of the wilderness? I beseech you, Father, help me. Get me back to the town. My father will surely pay you anything you'd ask.

The ruler of Alvaron is Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of this town. Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth is the vice-governor.

The misery that has befallen us is really great, son. The truth is that until lately many people in Alvaron didn't think the situation of the Realm was so grave as it was told to be. But after the murder of King Edward II the situation has changed and the city has fallen into nervous expectation of things to come. But personally I'm sure we'll succeed in this test of our faith and that we'll prove to our Lord we deserve His favor.

The Holy Scriptures tell us they're the most formidable servants of the Dark Prince. They're former angels, punished by God at the beginning of days for their sins when they plotted treason against God Almighty together with Satan the Tempter. For that they were struck down from Heaven and bound in Hell to suffer there for their sins

They've been trying to get back here since then to usurp the reigns of the world and Heaven. There are four of them: Arthamon, the master of ruin, Baphomet, the master of madness, Cerdie, the wanton succubus, and the Archangel Azrael, Satan's champion and the emissary of evil. Each of them is served by regiments of lesser demons and all kinds of infernal underlings that they send to the Earth in their stead to do harm here and to destroy God's Creations.

Grand Duke Drake Lambert has offered high rewards for catching werewolves raging in the vicinity of the city and regretfully even in its streets. Sheriff Henry Portmann pays the rewards in exchange for trophies brought to him—heads of dead werewolves. I personally think, though, that it won't bring much success in the fight against the infernal pack of Wolf-Prince Wulhyrr.

I've heard some tidings about an awakened ancient evil walking around the city at nights and killing everybody who gets in its path. It tries to get back something that reputedly was stolen from it. Nobody knows neither what shape that evil has nor what exactly it seeks, but it's said it's maybe a ghost of some pagan nobleman or mage, whose eternal sleep has been disturbed by the desecrating and robbing of his tomb.

If you want to try to remove a curse, son, first you must find out exact reading of the curse, find out the words used by the person who uttered it. If it concerns the case of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich, the problem is that he died many years ago and none of his peers will probably remember how his wife actually cursed him.

I also devoted myself to that case of the werewolves' attacks on the city, but I didn't come to any tangible result. But most startling to me is that someone conspires with werewolves who are known to not being able to stand human scent because it arouses their thirst for blood in them. That's why I don't understand how some heretic is able to open the city gates for them without being attacked by them.

I personally suspect the vagabond by the name of Steinger of robbing those graves, because I saw him several times heading to the city cemetery in the early evening, although no one has dared to go there for years not even in daylight, let alone at night. But I have no evidence.
You can't bribe me, I'm sorry!
Better answer me, Father. You never know what evil may befall you, if you understand me...
You seem to be very wise and learned, Father. Your answer would be of great benefit to me.
I won't need your services any more, Father. You may leave.
Are you sure, son, that you'll need me no more? It seemed to me my services are quite helpful to you.
Yes, I'm sure about it.
Alright, I'll go. If you should reconsider you'll find me in the Citadel of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Farewell and good luck!
Actually, you're right. Forget it.
That's all. Let's get going.
Have you gotten into some trouble?
Yes, exactly. A certain woman accused me of seducing and disgracing her. And moreover with the help of infernal powers!
Who was the woman?

That's the problem. She's Grand Duchess Liana Lambert, the wife of the royal governor of the city, Grand Duke Drake Lambert. I know it sounds strange, but it seems she's quite a rakish hussy, who doesn't detest any moral offence. But what's worst, she's able to hide it behind a mask of a devoted and loving wife! She attempted to seduce me. I refused—and I think I did it very politely—but even so I felt I made her angry. And when I learned she accused me of disgracing her and with the help of dark powers on top of it, I knew I had no chance to explain anything to anyone. So I hid here in the Citadel to think out a way to clear myself of the accusation.
I'll help you—I'll clear you of that charge.
What reward would you offer me if I clear you of that charge?
I would be able to join you in your fight against conspirators threatening the Realm.
Grand Duchess Liana Lambert is of too high a standing for me to have the nerve to contravene her statements. I'm sorry.
You quite took me by surprise, son. I thought you... But as you wish. I can't do anything about it. But if you reconsider, I'll be glad.
Certainly, son. What have you to say?
I see. Tell me, did you commit that crime?
Son! Of course I'm innocent! How can you doubt it?!
I wanted to be sure.
Yes... I understand. My apologies.
Thank you, son. I knew I might rely on you. You must prove to Grand Duke Lambert I didn't do anything that I'm accused of. It will be hard work, I know, but you'll surely succeed, son.
Farewell, son. And thank you again.

Welcome, son. I'm so glad you've joined our side. There are so little of us... I'm the inquisitorial prosecutor Nicolas. I've stood by the side of Grand Master de Malamert since the very beginning, same as you. But I was lucky to be able to cooperate with him closely—unlike you, who have had to manage for yourself. I admire you for that.
Grand Master de Malamert mentioned I might ask for your help...
Yes, that's true. If you need something I'll be glad to join you.
We will see. Maybe later.
As you wish, son. It's your decision.
Sure—after all we're talking already.
Yes, I'll be glad if you join me.
I hoped you would say that, son. But to be frank there's a certain obstacle impeding me in going out of the safety of the Citadel...
I'm glad to meet you, Father. But frankly, I'm not sure if I trust you...
I understand your fears and so I won't persuade you about sincerity and serenity of my words, because only my deeds may demonstrate that.

I'm glad to see you, son. May I ask you if you've made any progress in my case? Have you managed to refute the accusation brought by Grand Duchess Liana Lambert who asserts I violated her with the help of infernal powers?
Never mind, you will surely succeed eventually. The truth must be revealed!
Certainly. What have you to say?
Yes, you may rely on me. Farewell.
Yes, I've managed to clear you of that false accusation.
You really did it? Glory to our Lord! My prayers were answered. Thank you, son. I'm much obliged to you. If you want, I'll join you at once in your fight against conspirators threatening the Realm.
Alright, join me. Your services will be of great help to me.
Great, son. Together we will light the flames of justice in the places where the brimstone and infernal fetidness are ruling.
No, it won't be necessary. Maybe later.
I understand. You'll find me in the Citadel, if you should so wish.
Certainly, son. What is it you want to know?
Hello, son.
Hello. May I speak with you for a moment?
I'd be glad if you could join me, Father.
So you've decided to help me and to clear me of that absurd accusation by which Grand Duchess Liana Lambert revenges upon me for her injured pride?
Welcome, son. How is your fight against conspirators threatening the Realm going? May I help you somehow in you efforts?
I need to talk to you, Father.
As you wish. What have you to say?
Join me. Your services will come in handy.
No, thank you. Farewell.
What is it, son?

My services are at your disposal, son—but only on the condition that you first send away the weird individual who's accompanying you. I can see at first sight that he's a mercenary. And we have to arm against such men because they cannot be trusted!
You mean Olfghard? You may trust him, Father. He has demonstrated his loyalty in fierce battles.
He might have persuaded you, but I don't have a single reason to trust him! If you want me as your companion you'll have to send him away!
Alright, join me. Your services will be more useful to me than Olfghard's.
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to send Olfghard away.
In that case we won't pull together, I'm sorry. And I advise you well—beware of that Olfghard. If you rely on him it may later become your doom. I feel it!
I would like to change some goods.

If you want me to follow you again, you must first send away the weird individual who's accompanying you. I can see at the first sight that he's a mercenary. And we have to arm against such men because they cannot be trusted!

Do you really need things I have on me, son? If so, ask for them directly—I'll be glad to share with you all I have. You don't need to derogate yourself by stealing like a lowbred thief. Although I believe some noble purpose unknown to me led your hands.

I would like to see your goods.
May I talk to you?
I'm sorry but I can't talk to you right now. Come back later. We can have a drink and a little chat in the tavern...
Goodbye.
And about what?!
About whatever interests me.
But I won't tell you anything!
Why don't you want to talk with me?
Because I don't like people like you!
Do you know who I am? If I must I'll make you to cooperate by force.
I love force. Just say and I'll show you some.
You won't tell me even your name?
Well... I could do that. Name's Norman. And now get lost, I've much to do!
And what exactly do you do, good man?
I work as a butcher in Mister Bates' Inn. And now get lost!
Salena Flock testified you sold her some items belonging to Ron Burton. What can you tell me about that?
Who's Ron Burton?
Brother of William Burton. He's been missing and moreover there's reasonable suspicion he was murdered.
I dunno anything about it. And all those pimps had better watch out—usually I wring the neck of such people till their neck breaks. And now get lost at last!
Humpf!
Norman the Butcher, I arrest you on the basis of reasonable suspicion for the murder of Ron Burton. You'll go with me to be put before rightful trial.

Norman won't go anywhere. He's a nice boy. He always minds his mother who loves him. And he'll always do what she tells him. And now she's telling him: don't go anywhere with that man, boy. He's evil and dangerous, he wants to harm you.
But yes, you'll go with me. You've just been arrested!
You've heard what my mother said: I won't go with you anywhere. My mother forbade it.
You're accused of murder! Inkeeper Salena Flock testified you sold her some items belonging to Ron Burton. There is a suspicion you murdered him.

Bully for you. You don't like it or what? He was neither the first nor the last. My mother was right when she told me people are just cattle, some cows, some pigs... I haven't found anything in them that would be different from animals—just entrails, blood, fat, meat, bones, sinews—but no values. Even faith I didn't find inside—although they are talking about it all the time. But when you disembowel a man, there's nothing that you couldn't fry on a pan, cook in a pot or smoke in the chimney.
So you plead guilty? Did you murder Ron Burton?

Yes, I and Mister Bates killed him, the same as many others. He even didn't twitch much when I hanged him by the feet on the flesh-hook down under the inn and left him to bleed to death with his throat cut. He will make very good roast meat when he is a little mellow. Or Mister Bates will make goulash out of him, our great specialty. And just the same he will dispose of you when I bring him your dead body.
My God... you're cannibals!

Do you see, Norman? I told you he's an evil man. Kill him, Norman. Do your mother's bidding and kill him. Or he'll find the entrance to Mister Bates' basement hidden in the kitchen and will tell everything to the people in the city. That mustn't happen, Norman. KILL HIM!
You have to stand before a rightful trial for your crimes, Norman!
I'm tired of you, knight. Mother's right. It'll be better if I kill you. Come here, I'll cut you down like a sheep!
What? What are you talking about?
Do you hear, Norman? Your mother tells you he's an evil man. Don't go anywhere with him. Listen to your mother—you know she loves you.
Who are you talking with, man? You're mad!
I won't go with you anywhere—you've heard my mother. She loves me and I'm gonna do everything she tells me.
What d'ya want?!
I just wanted to know who you are, good man.
And why d'ya wanna know that?!
Because I wanted to talk with you.
I'd like to talk with you.
What d'ya want again? Get lost, you're blocking my way!
I'd like to talk to you, good man.
But I don't. So get lost!
Alright, anything you say...
Get your dirty hands off, or I'll cut them off and stick them into your throat!!!

Put your dirty hands away, or I'll cut them off and stick them into your throat!!!
What have you done, you murderer? You killed my beloved Norman! My dear boy! I'll kill you for that. Do you understand? I'll kill you!
I'm the Norman's mother, you fool. And you'll be justly punished for killing my son. No one may do wrong to my Norman. I'll kill you!
I'll send you back to burning Hell from whence you came, fallen soul!
You'll be justly punished for killing my son. No one may do wrong to my Norman. I'll kill you!
Tsssk! Tsssk! Tsssk!
You must be the spider beast which has taken many innocent lives... Die, unholy monster!
Mysterious Voice
Hear my words, son. You are walking in darkness, your way is veiled. You are followed by death and damnation and wherever you go, betrayal and deceit rules. Beware!
What? What's going on? What is this strange voice?

Beware of false friends, good mentors and even of companions—you must not succumb to their lies and promises. Lies cover your eyes and foul acts tighten a noose around your neck. You must go on and not let them stop you.
Good heavens... is it the Savior himself talking to me? Or is it a deceitful voice of the Tempter?

Remember my words, dear son—if you believe you commit a crime. If you are blind you will get yourself killed. If you are obedient lions will dilacerate you. If you are careless you will step on a snake. If you fall asleep you will not wake up again!
Remember my words, dear son. Darkness is covering both the Earth and the Heavens... remember my words...
I investigate crimes against faith here in Hillbrandt. Do you suspect anyone?

Crimes against faith you say? You mean like catching heretics? I have seen many strange things in my life, you know. This has always been a wild region, but I don't remember anything like the things that have been happening since the Scourges of God struck. People just went crazy. Take For example Baroness Lind van Gallagan. Always seemed to be an orthodox faithful and now she's supposed to be colluding with Satan...

The night I ran away from town—it was the night of the green skins' attack—I hid here in Asherbalt. Before I could get some rest, I saw the light of torches through a window. I thought it was the guards who were after me but I was wrong. It was an odd parade—a bunch of green skins and Baroness van Gallagan with them. They were walking toward the Iron mines. And she didn't seem to be going with them against her will. It almost looked like they were protecting her. Really strange, I must say.
Are you sure it was Baroness Linda van Gallagan? It was dark, wasn't it?
Well... not totally sure, that's true. But most likely it was her!
Your suspicion was correct, Olfghard. Baroness Linda van Gallagan was accused of heresy and she confessed.
You see? I was right. You wouldn't believe what kind of people can fall to heresy, would you?

You wanna go shopping? Well, if you need weapons, go to Victor Hammerhand. I shop there myself and I can confirm that his services are great. When it comes to potions and spells, I'd recommend Ellisa Würtenrodt—if you don't make her mad. The same applies to the astrologist and alchemist Theil Brechthold. He's an old grouch when it comes to it. Father Dominicus, on the other hand, should be willing to help you anytime. But I don't go to him too often. He always wants to know what was the last time I confessed, and of course, there is the innkeeper Joseph Truthorn and the stall-holder Suzan Brauchner. I always got rid of everything I had on me and didn't need anymore with them. You can also buy all kinds of things there, but their prices aren't too good. But sometimes you have no choice.

The times are pretty rotten, that's true. God knows whether there is any truth in the talk about the end of the world, but it looks like it. Devils, heretics and all this filth everywhere you look... this is not good. I've never seen the locals so scared and desperate. Few believe that it can ever get better.
What kind of monsters can you encounter in Hillbrandt and in its surroundings?

You can find all kinds of monsters here, sir knight. From the overgrown spiders with deadly poison to huge trolls with skin made of stone and with beech logs instead of bones. Trolls are responsible for innumerable murders and disappearances because they wait at the roads and jump at you without giving you a chance to realize what's going on. They've always lived here but there weren't many of them. They are said to be living at the tops of the mountains and not coming down very often. But in the past few years there were crowds of them coming down and the foothills are not safe anymore. So I tell you, sir knight, beware the trolls!
Duke Weinberg offers good rewards for killed orcs. The scrooge Sheriff Contemburry pays them out.

What do you mean by asking if anything unusual have been happening in the past three years? The famine, the plague, the rain of fire, the heretic cults, monster worshiping, beasts everywhere you go, inquisition witch hunts... So many unusual things have happened that if I should sum it up in one sentence, I should say 'we're all in deep...'
Don't blaspheme!
...trouble!

Master d'Arvias a heretic? Who knows, what the truth is... and first of all—does it matter? They will execute him without any remorse even if he's completely innocent. Look at me, what I got into. Accused of a robbery with murder before I could say 'amen'. And I haven't done anything!
I don't know anything about the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius. And I really hope nobody tries to pin it on me. I wouldn't be surprised after what happened because of Natalia Reichmann...
Unfortunately I don't know anything about Bishop Quentinus. I didn't kidnap him, that's all I can say about it.
I'm investigating the theft of master Edmond d'Arvias's sword. Do you know anything about it?

You know, what's interesting, sir knight? Every time something gets lost the first person everybody asks about it is me. As if it was me, who steals things in the town. Other people steal as well, sir knight, believe me. Even the Duke steals because what else can you call taxes this high if not a theft? I tell you something, they should start hunting the thieves amongst the nobility, not amongst the poor who have nothing.
Do you know how to remove a curse?
I have no idea how to remove a curse. But I know of plenty of ways to deal with the one who cast the curse. But you're not interested in that I guess.

Of course there are some local legends connected to Hillbrandt, sir knight. And you know what? When the time is right, we'll make a fire, catch a deer, open a barrel of beer and I'll tell you a legend. But right now I'm not in a mood, sir knight—sorry.

Kurth Ollmier's murder is an ugly case. I knew him a little, we used to talk now and then in the Truthorn's inn where he rented the attic. He was interested in all kinds of stories from the time I was in the army. He said it gave him information useful in his business—whatever it was. I'm sorry about his death. They cut his throat like he was a hen... And I heard the murderers also cut off his dick and put it in his mouth! A bad ending, that's what I call it.
The murderers? There were more people? How do you know?

Of course I don't know how many murderers there were. I said murderers because Kurth was very careful and he wasn't a beginner who'd let somebody cut his throat in his sleep. He was good with blades. There must have been more of them... But it's just my opinion.
God forgive him his sins...
You said it really well, sir knight. Amen.
Hillbrandt is ruled by Duke Weinberg who is the royal governor. The vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan. What should I say about them—nobility will always be the same. Damn rich bastards!
Maybe you think, Olfghard, that you've been through a lot. But if you resist I assure you that I'm going to put you through things you've never dreamed of. And believe me, you won't like it!
I think I know your opinion of me, Olfghard. But I still think you are not as dumb as to refuse to cooperate with me...
Look, Olfghard, we both know that you are too intelligent and experienced not to know what you can say to whom. So why make so much fuss about it?
I don't need your services any longer, Olfghard. You can go now.
Are you sure, sir knight, you don't need me anymore? I thought you found me pretty useful...
All right, I'm going. If you changed your mind, you can most likely find me in Hillbrandt. Goodbye.
I know you're innocent. I found Jullian hiding with the kidnapped girl Natalia Reichmann in a deserted chapel at the Dragon Rock.
Really? Then I'm saved! If somebody told Duke Weinberg, that Natalia Reichmann was kidnapped by Jullian I would be acquitted. Could you do it for me, sir knight?
Why not? The truth should be uncovered. I'm going to tell Duke Weinberg that you are innocent.

Then I'd be indebted to you, sir knight. But I better stay here for a little while. Just until you arrange everything. I don't want to be hanged. I'd rather risk meeting with green skins than with the executioner Raubsticht.
We have a deal. Can I ask you some more questions?
All right. If you think, it might help you...
It depends what you'd give me for it.

And what should I give you? A sack of gold and the hand of my daughter? I don't have any gold and neither have I a daughter—at least not one I know of—so the only thing I can give you is a word of thanks.
I'm sorry, I don't have time for things like that.
Well, what can I do then, sir knight. If you're so busy you can't even help an innocent person prove his innocence, I won't keep you any longer. You'd better go.
If you are innocent, it will eventually come to light, so there's nothing to be afraid of.

Are you kidding, sir knight? Do you expect me to think that everything will turn out good? That somebody will come out of the blue saying 'leave him alone, he's innocent'? They will execute an old landsknecht as if they were killing a fly and will just keep laughing at it. And if they later find out he was innocent, they'll say that he's certainly committed many sins and crimes he deserved such punishment anyway, so why bother.
I'll prove you that you are wrong. I'm going to prove your innocence. But if you're lying to me...
I can't believe that you would be interested in proving my innocence. But if you propose it... I'm going to trust you. Prove me innocent. Find Jullian and tell Duke Weinberg.
We have a deal. Goodbye.
If you're innocent, I could help you. What would you give me for that?
And what should I give you? A sack of gold and the hand of my daughter? I don't have any gold and neither have I a daughter—not one I know of—so the only thing I can give you is a word of thanks.
Maybe you're telling the truth. Maybe you're lying. Anyway, It's not my problem. Goodbye.

You're right, sir knight, it'll be better if you go. You can't help me. If it goes well, we'll never see each other again. I'm going to try my luck in the Empire. I hope I will be able to get through the Moonshine Mountains. Goodbye!
Thank you, sir knight. You won't be sorry for you decision, I promise. Let's go!

Thank you, sir knight! You won't be sorry for your decision, you'll see. But I can see, that you already have company—Hugo de Montesque, the paladin. This might be a problem. I trust you, sir knight... but I can see no reason to trust Hugo de Montesque. Dismiss him and I shall follow you even to Hell.
All right, Olfghard, I'll dismiss him. I prefer your services.
I'm not going to dismiss anyone, Olfghard. If you don't like it, you can't stay in my party.
Hmm... it's a pity, sir knight. I wish you all the best. And if you changed your mind, you know where to find me. Goodbye.

Thank you, You won't be sorry for your decision, you'll see. But I can see that you already have company—a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous... This might be a problem. I trust you, sir knight; after what you've done for me... But I don't know him, and to tell you the truth, I don't see a reason to trust him. Dismiss him and I shall follow you even to Hell.
All right, Olfghard, I will dismiss Ethien de Pulein. I prefer your services.

Thank you, You won't be sorry for your decision, you'll see. But I can see, that you already have company—a priest... This might be a problem. I trust you, sir knight; after what you've done for me... But I don't know him, and to tell you the truth, I don't see a reason to trust him. Dismiss him and I shall follow you even to Hell.
All right, Olfghard, I will dismiss brother Nicolas. I prefer your services.
I promised merchant Reichmann to bring him your head!

Oh, my God, I must be dreaming! This world has gone crazy! No wonder it's going to the dogs. But you chose your fate yourself, sir knight—if you want it the hard way, you shall have it. I've never killed a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous before, but it won't be a sin in your case. You asked for it in your stupidity!
Stay right where you are, sir knight. One more step and I'm going to kill you. I don't care about anything anymore. I'm not going to be taken back to Hillbrandt!
Calm down and tell me who you are, and why are you raising your weapon?
My name is Olfghard. But why the hell do you care who I am. And I'm raising my weapon because I don't like you finding me here.
Are you hiding here?
Of course, I'm hiding here. What else would I be doing in a deserted village destroyed by green skins. Waiting for a miracle? I don't believe in them, sir knight. Not after what has happened.
What's happened so bad that it made you hate the whole world?

What's happened? What the hell has happened? Not much, sir knight. It's just that I was arrested for the murder of Natalia Reichmann, which I didn't commit and I was nearly executed because of it. If I didn't manage to escape during the attack of the green skins on the town, I'd be dead now. And I'm completely innocent, sir knight, because Natalia Reichmann was kidnapped by the soldier Jullian. How do I know? I caught him. He gave me some of her jewelry to keep me quiet. So I thought, why not—it's not my problem anyway—and I took the jewelry. But when I tried to sell it, somebody recognized it and they immediately put me into prison to wait for Duke Weinberg to deliver judgment. What do you say about that?
What are you going to do?

I'm going to try to get through the Moonshine Mountains to the Empire. It sounds crazy, but it's my only chance. They would hunt me down sooner or later here in the Realm. I think it's better to break my neck or be torn to pieces by monsters than to stay in this crazy country.
I don't believe your story. I think you are guilty. Otherwise you wouldn't be running from justice.
Believe whatever you want, but I told you the truth. I didn't murder Natalia Reichmann and I didn't rob her of her jewelry either.
You're lying, I can tell. You're going to answer for your crimes.
Never, sir knight. I'm not getting executed for something I didn't do! I didn't want to hurt you, but you made me!
Whatever the truth is, I'm not going to do anything about it. If you lower your weapon I'll leave. If not, you're going to die.

That sounds reasonable, sir knight. We'll part in peace, I'm not going to step in your way, if you leave me alone. If all goes well, we'll never see each other again. I'll try my luck in the Empire. I hope I can get there through the Moonshine Mountains. Goodbye!
So you are the Olfghard, who's supposed to have killed the merchant Stefan Reichmann's daughter?

Yeah, that's me. So you've heard about it, haven't you? And I suppose you believe it as well as everybody else... But I'm innocent, sir knight. I didn't touch a single hair on Natalia's head. She was kidnapped by Jullian, he probably wanted her father's money, I guess. I was just unlucky to catch him in the act. First it looked like he was going to try to kill me, but the girl was there, so he gave me some of her jewelry to keep me quiet. So I thought, why not—it's not my problem anyway—and I took the jewelry. But when I tried to sell it, somebody recognized it and they immediately put me into prison to wait for Duke Weinberg to deliver judgment.
Hello, sir knight. Have you proven my innocence to Duke Weinberg already?
Yes, Olfghard. Duke Weinberg cancelled the sentence. You're free now.

I can't believe it... Did you really do it? Is it some kind of trick? No? Then I'm saved! God forgive me ever doubting the justice. Thank you, sir knight. I'm forever indebted to you. What can I do to repay you? You can ask anything!!
I might need someone like you. Do you want to join me?

Are you serious? Would you really want to be accompanied by a landsknecht who's always having troubles with the law? You are a brave one. However, my services are not for free—they cost 500 gp for a hundred slain enemies. Do you still want me to join you?
As I said—I'd really need somebody like you.
You're right, that wouldn't be exactly appropriate.
I expected that. But still I'm indebted to you, sir knight. Goodbye.
I don't ask anything for my help, Olfghard. Executing justice is the best reward for me.

Then I'm not just grateful, I'm in awe. You don't find many people nowadays who don't ask anything for their help. Thank you one more time. And if you ever need me, you can find me in Hillbrandt. Goodbye for now.
It's you again, sir knight. I thought the last time we met we agreed on never seeing each other again. You better go now.
I want to talk to you.
But I don't want to talk to you. Goodbye!
Hello, sir knight. How are you? Thank you for your help one more time. If it weren't for you, I'd probably be hanging on a rope now. What can I do for you in return?
Of course, sir knight. I'll tell you everything—even what I don't know for what you did for me. What would you like to know?
I would like you to join me, Olfghard.
Nothing, I was just passing by. Goodbye.
Hello, sir knight. We haven't seen each other for quite some time. How are you? You don't look very well, you see? Is there anything I can do for you?
Can I talk to you, Olfghard?
Of course, sir knight. Just like in the old times. What do you need to know?
I'd be grateful if you joined me again, Olfghard.
What is it, sir knight?
Unfortunately not yet.
Hmm... nevermind. I'm sure you will eventually succeed. I just hope it's before they hang me!
Another hundred enemies back in hell, sir knight! Can I ask you for my money? I think I deserve it...
Of course, here is your money.
Thanks, sir knight. Let's go!
Unfortunately, I don't have enough money...
Hmm... Don't worry about that, sir knight. It happens to much better people than you AS well. Just give me the money you've got...
I'll pay you nothing!
Nothing? In that case I'll take my leave, sir knight. I don't work for free. If you change your mind, you'll find me in Hillbrandt. Good bye and good luck!

Oh, my God, I must be dreaming! This world has gone crazy! No wonder it's going to dogs. But you chose your fate yourself, noble lord—if you want it the hard way, you shall have it. I've never killed a noble but it won't be a sin in your case. You asked for it in your stupidity!
Stay right where you are, noble lord. One more step and I'm going to kill you. I don't care about anything anymore. I'm not going to be taken back to Hillbrandt!
Of course, I'm hiding here. What else would I be doing in a deserted village destroyed by green skins. Waiting for a miracle? I don't believe in them, noble lord. Not after what has happened.

What's happened? What the hell has happened? Not much, noble lord. It's just that I was arrested for the murder of Natalia Reichmann, which I didn't commit and I was nearly executed because of it. If I didn't manage to escape during the attack of the green skins on the town, I'd be dead now. And I'm completely innocent, noble lord, because Natalia Reichmann was kidnapped by the soldier Jullian. How do I know? I caught him. He gave me some of her jewelry to keep me quiet. So I thought, why not—it's not my problem anyway—and I took the jewelry. But when I tried to sell it, somebody recognized it and they immediately put me into prison to wait for Duke Weinberg to deliver judgment. What do you say about that?
Never, noble lord. I'm not getting executed for something I didn't do! I didn't want to hurt you, but you made me!

That sounds reasonable, noble lord. We'll part in peace, I'm not going to step in your way, if you leave me alone. If all goes well, we'll never see each other again. I'll try my luck in the Empire. I hope I can get there through the Moonshine Mountains. Goodbye!

Yeah, that's me. So you've heard about it, haven't you? And I suppose you believe it as well as everybody else... But I'm innocent, noble lord. I didn't touch a single hair on Natalia's head. She was kidnapped by Jullian, he probably wanted her father's money, I guess. I was just unlucky to catch him in the act. First it looked like he was going to try to kill me, but the girl was there, so he gave me some of her jewelry to keep me quiet. So I thought, why not—it's not my problem anyway—and I took the jewelry. But when I tried to sell it, somebody recognized it and they immediately put me into prison to wait for Duke Weinberg to deliver judgment.
Hello, noble lord. Have you proven my innocence to Duke Weinberg already?

I can't believe it... Did you really do it? Is it some kind of trick? No? Then I'm saved! God forgive me ever doubting the justice. Thank you, noble lord. I'm forever indebted to you. What can I do to repay you? You can ask anything!!
I expected that. But still I'm indebted to you, noble lord. Goodbye.
It's you again, noble lord. I thought the last time we met we agreed on never seeing each other again. You better go now.
Hello, noble lord. How are you? Thank you for your help one more time. If it weren't for you, I'd probably be hanging on a rope now. What can I do for you in return?
Of course, noble lord. I'll tell you everything—even what I don't know for what you did for me. What would you like to know?
Hello, noble lord. We haven't seen each other for quite some time. How are you? You don't look very well, you see? Is there anything I can do for you?
Of course, noble lord. Just like in the old times. What do you need to know?
What is it, noble lord?
Another hundred enemies back in hell, noble lord! Can I ask you for my money? I think I deserve it...
Thanks, noble lord. Let's go!
Hmm... Don't worry about that, noble lord. It happens to much better people than you as well. Just give me the money you've got...
Nothing? In that case I'll take my leave, noble lord. I don't work for free. If you change your mind, you'll find me in Hillbrandt. Good bye and good luck!

I see that you've recruited Hugo de Montesque, the paladin. This might be a problem. I trust you... but I can see no reason to trust Hugo de Montesque. Dismiss him and I shall follow you even to Hell.

I see that you've recruited Jacques de Pulein, the paladin. That might be a problem. I trust you... but I can see no reason to trust Jacques de Pulein. Dismiss him and I shall follow you even to Hell itself.
Freeze! Don't move! Who are you? Orghp thinks you are a human spy. Shouldn't be here!
You're wrong Orghp, I am your friend. Let me pass, I have an important message!
You—friend of the orcs? Do you think you can fool Orghp? You are risking your life! Tell us the message! Then we'll see what we'll do with you.
The message is not for you, Orghp. Let me pass or you'll have to deal with the consequences of your ill-considered deeds!
Oh no no no. You're not going anywhere until you tell the truth to Orghp. Maybe a little pain could help. What if we tortured you? Would that loosen your tongue?

You want to torture me, orc? How pathetic! Don't you see who I am? Let me pass or I'll make you suffer you've never even dreamed of. First I'm going to burn your eyes out with burning spikes. Then I'll peel the skin off your back and finally I'll crush your limbs and weave you in a wheel where you'll be dying slowly for three days...

Eh... uh... enough, noble sir. Orghp doesn't want to be put through anything like that. Orghp would be stupid not to let you pass. You can go and tell your message. Orghp is really sorry for making you mad.
Calm down, Orghp. If you let me pass, I'll give you a pouch of gold!

Are you trying to buy Orghp? Do you think your gold will cloud his mind? He knows that you are a spy who's not supposed to be here. You don't have the Mark of the Beast, you are trying to avert the destruction of your disgusting race. But you've come too far. You are not leaving alive. Kill him! Kill him!
All right, Orghp, I'm going to tell you what the message is. I must warn your Khan that he's in danger!

What? Khan Rashgar in danger? Are you trying to fool Orghp? Khan Rashgar is never in danger. Your race is in danger facing an unpleasant fate. What kind of danger should Khan Rashgar be expecting in his hall under the Mountains where your God cannot go, heh?
As I've said—Khan Rashgar is in danger. But you are in even bigger danger...
What? What is the human slave talking about? Tell Orghp everything immediately or you'll die like a worm.
The purgative flame of divine justice has come to your Empire!
Really? Is that true? And where is the flame?
Standing right in front of you! You'll all die now!
I was just kidding. Let me pass. I've lost enough time already!
So Orghp WAS right. You are a disgusting human spy who's trying to get somewhere he's not supposed to be! But you won't manage because Orghp's orcs will kill you!
Yes, he's in a mortal danger and it's important to warn him in time. Or do you want to risk your ruler's life?
Hmm... yes, Orghp better lets you pass. Go and tell Khan Rashgar your message. But if you are a human spy Orghp will find you and kill you—that promise!
I've told Hurgh already—the message cannot be delivered to anybody other than the recipient.
Huh, you talked to Hurgh, the old fleabag?
Yes, Orghp. He sends you word to let me pass, or he'll deal with you personally!
Ah—then you must be a friend of orcs. You can pass.
Yes I did. Just before I sent him to the burning hell!
Kill him! Kill him!
You are monsters who deserve eternal damnation. Die in the infernal flames, devils!
You asked for it, human worm. Kill him! Kill him!
You can pass, noble sir. We are not going to hold you.
I've changed my mind. I will kill all of you, you unholy monsters!
A thief! Kill him! A thief!
Scott de Ormand
Hmm... There's no way to help him. The poor man is dead.
God help your soul. Rest in peace, good man.
Who are you good man? And how did you get to this unholy place?

Oh my God, the pain... my body... I can't feel anything but the pain... I couldn't defend myself. There were too many demons... I can hear the angels coming for me... playing the golden hornets, announcing my end... the beautiful music! Please tell Rieven, that I hate to leave him here... alone... aaahhhh.
Hold on. good man! A healing potion will surely help you!
Who is Rieven, good man? And who are you?
Hold on, sir knight, I came to help you. Your comrade Rieven d'Ardrieaux sent me.

Rieven... Rieven sent you? He hasn't forgotten me? My dear Rieven! Please... tell him... that I hate to leave him alone... I have no choice. I can hear the angels coming for me... playing the golden hornets, announcing my end... the beautiful music!... aaahhhh.
I arrived too late, there's no way to help him. Rest in peace dear knight.
You must be Scott de Ormand, if I'm not mistaken. I talked to your comrade Rieven d'Ardrieaux...

Really? That's good... Please... tell him... that I hate to leave him alone... There were too many of them... I can hear the angels coming for me... playing the golden hornets, announcing my end... the beautiful music... aaahhhh.
Rest in peace, sir knight. God save your soul. Amen.
Saint Orthenius

I, Saint Orthenius, the harbinger of the faith and God's emissary, talk to you, mortal—there are just two reasons a human would be willing to risk his life and come to my grave. The first reason can be the concern for the true faith; the second a desire to seize something that cannot be seized. Speak, mortal—why did you come here and what are you asking from me?
The Realm of Ultherst, whose foundations you helped to lay a millennium ago, is in danger. I hoped that I could use your relic called the Inquisitor to face the enemies of the true faith.

Really? your words please me, mortal. I knew the time would come when the true faith would be in danger and it would be necessary to take up the weapon of divine wrath. But your words could be hiding deceit. If your soul is pure, the relic is yours. But if you're lying and your conscience is guilty of mortal sins, a terrible fate is awaiting you. Let me now see to your soul...
All right, there's nothing I'm afraid of.

Hmm... it seems your intentions really are pure. You can then take the sword Inquisitor to fight your battle. Trust that it shall never betray you and it shall lead you to victory as it has led me. Goodbye, savior of the true faith!
A betrayal! You lied to me. You're guilty of many a mortal sin! You're an ordinary thief and you are to be treated as a thief. Your life has no value at all!
Wait, I'm not going to undergo anything like that!
Then I will treat you like an ordinary thief. Your life has now no value at all!
I'm not asking anything, undead monster. You are not Saint Orthenius—you are a monstrous infernal demon who has no place in the Divine Kingdom. Die!
How can your dare to touch my relic! I'm going to punish you, for your life has now no value at all!
I came here to get your relic called the Inquisitor. I'm going to keep the reasons to myself.
Then you are an ordinary thief and you are to be treated as a thief. Your life has no value at all!
Tomb Guard

Wrong! Your answer is wrong! You can't be truly faithful if you don't know the answer to my question. You are going to be punished justly for your lies!
Correct! Your knowledge of the Scripture proves that you are truly faithful. You can enter!
Only he can enter who is truly faithful. Only true faith is the way to salvation and those who go astray from this path will face eternal damnation. Are you truly faithful?
Yes, I am!

Sepria.
Baktar.
Hepreth.
Kunkvas.
Hevlet.
Ibhar.

Trina.
Necra.
Jesmis.
Malchra.
Apocalypse.
Timoth.

Kalkimon of Effras.
Matheos of Iallos.
Balthazar of Trevion.
Farnius of Naorth.
Ezekiel of Effrat.
Etrick the Babtist.
Noah the Goth.
Vermin of Sahbara.
Barmus the Provident.
Trevor of Rabin.
Gusthus of Sivon.
Dermus of Heptar.
Victorius Eason.
Then you must know the Holy Scripture well. Tell me in how many days did God create the Earth??
In one day.
In two days.
In three days.
In four days.
In five days.
In six days and he rested the seventh day.
In seven days.
I'm... not sure. I'm always doubting myself.
Then turn around and leave or you'll burn in infernal fire! Go!
You can enter!
Only he can enter, who's devoted to God. Devotion brings God's favor and God's favor brings light in all human doings. Are you devoted?

Then you will surely do anything God would ask. Do you know the story of a father who was told by God to kill his only son to test his devotion? You must make a sacrifice to prove your devotion as well. You must give up all the property you now own. You'll have nothing left and you'll leave as a beggar.
All right, I'll make the sacrifice. I'm giving up everything I have!
There's no need to. I can see that you are able to make sacrifices... You've proven your dedication. You may enter!!
You can't ask a sacrifice like that!
It's up to you—only he may enter who's dedicated to God. And you must prove your dedication by making the sacrifice!
I'm not going to do that!
Then you are not dedicated enough. You're a liar and you are going to be punished as a liar deserves!
Wrong! Your answer's incorrect. You can't be wise since you don't know the answer to my question. You are going to be punished for your lie!
Correct! Your knowledge of history proves that you are wise. You may enter!
Only he can enter who is wise. Only wisdom enables us to see a deeper truth and truth is divine blood. Are you wise?

Then you surely know the history of this world of which you take lessons when walking the path of your destiny. Answer my question then—in what city was Kalkimon, the First Prophet and the son of God, born, crucified and buried?
In Methuzalem.
In Effrat.
In Jevaran.
In Alvaron.
In Babylon.

Then you surely know the history of this world of which you take lessons when walking the path of your destiny. Answer my question then—in what year was Kalkimon, the First Prophet and the son of God, born?
In the 33rd year of the old era.
In the 3rd year of the old era.
At the turn of the old and the new era.
In the 3rd year of the new era.
In the 33rd year of the new era.

Then you surely know history of this world of which you take a lesson when you decide about your way. Answer my question then—in what year was Kalkimon, the First Prophet and the son of God, crucified?
Only he can enter who is brave. Bravery is vital for the faithful to protect the true faith from its enemies. Bravery brings victory and strengthens the faith. Are you brave?
Than you can surely prove it. A terrible enemy will materialize now. If you defeat him, you'll prove yourself worthy of entering. Otherwise your life will lose its value.
Good, let him materialize!
Great! You've passed the test, you no longer need to prove your bravery. You may enter!!
Only he can enter, who is deliberate. Deliberateness prevents unwariness and unwariness seduces you to sin which breaks divine order. Are you deliberate?

Then you will surely answer my question correctly. Imagine you and your army are standing in front of a well fortified pagan city. The walls are full of pagan pikes and you can hear the sounds of their unholy rituals. God wishes to erase the place from His Kingdom because its existence offends his. Your army, however, is weakened by hunger and by disease of which many men are dying and the morale is failing. You're running out of supplies because the pagans attacked the supply lines on their way. Your army is not big enough to siege the city and to starve it. Moreover, your intelligence tells you that there is a big pagan army coming from another city to help their brothers and sisters. What will you do to fulfill God's will and defeat the pagans?
I will attack at sunrise! I will lead the attack myself and will take the city!

A wrong answer. An attack at sunrise could be fatal considering that you have no idea how many pagans are there in the city. You are not as deliberate as you said you were. You are going to be punished for the lie!
I would have a tunnel dug into the city and would pass through it during the night to open the city gates!

A wrong answer. Digging up a tunnel would take many days and surely would not pass unnoticed by the city guards. You are not as deliberate as you said you were. You are going to be punished for the lie!
I would surprise the pagans by an attack at night!

A wrong answer. A mindless attack at night could be fatal considering that you have no idea how many pagans there are in the city. You could lose the whole army without achieving anything. You are not as deliberate as you said you were. You are going to be punished for the lie!
I would pray to God and ask him to sweep the city out off the face of the Earth with his wrath!
A wrong answer. It's you who should be performing the creator's will, not him. You are not as deliberate as you said you were. You are going to be punished for the lie!
I don't know. I'd have to think about it...
Great! You've passed the test. You've proven your deliberation by not making hasty conclusions. You may enter!
Only he can enter who is unyielding. Persistence is vital for the truly faithful, because only he who can resist temptation can reach the eternal salvation in the Kingdom of God. Are you unyielding?
I don't believe you. I can smell falsehood in your words. Leave or you'll burn in infernal fire. Return when you really are unyielding!
I'm not leaving. I am unyielding!
I said leave, because you are not unyielding. Go or you'll burn in infernal fire!
Great! You've passed the test. You may enter!
Do you admit you are not unyielding? Then you didn't pass the test. You are not worthy to enter. You are going to be punished!
Come to me, little sheep—I've promised Fathor the giant I would bring him some mutton...
Baaah baaah!
You must be Betty, the sheep who ran away from the shepherd Ruphert. I arrest you on suspicion of desertion!
Bleet bleeet.
Oh... what am I saying?! It's a job thing. Come, lost sheep, I'm going to take you back to your herd.
What are you doing here, lost sheep? Ran away from your herd? Come, I'm going to help you find your way back to the shepherd—after all, it is my job...
Or I might sell your meat...

Exactly, brother.
Maybe we should submit to the authority of the Holy Inquisition after all—what if it's the will of God?!
Never! The Brotherhood of the Righteous will never recognize the unrestricted authority of the Holy Office! Get real, brother!

Hmm... I don't know. Farewell.
