The gentry are not allowed to enter the Glatzburg chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
Only the entitled are allowed to enter the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, brother. And you're not one of them yet.
Welcome into the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, brother!
The clergy are not allowed to enter the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
The gentry are not allowed to enter the Hillbrandt chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
I found this necklace, brother. Does it by any chance belong to you?

Oh yes, it is my necklace. You found it! Unbelievable... I was beginning to think that my honor was lost forever. My necklace is back. Thank you, brother. I'm forever indebted to you. Where did you find it anyway?

To tell you the truth, I found it in an abhorrent pagan shrine near the local place of execution. And I'm not going to keep silent about the fact that an unholy pagan ritual took place in there not a long time ago. I found a body of a young girl with lacerated innards in there!

What? You found it in such a horrible place! It seems it wasn't a simple theft. It was meant to cast suspicion of heresy on me, I'm sure about that! Because what else could you derive from finding my chain in such a place than that I took a part in the ritual. Disgusting!
Exactly. And that's why I think you'd appreciate if nobody found out about it. If you were willing to spend some gold, I'm not going to say anything!
But, brother! Do you realize what you've just proposed? It could be called blackmail!
That's an ugly word, brother. I'd prefer 'a friendly service to a neighbor in need'.
Well... if that's the way you look at it, I don't really have a choice. How much do you want for your silence?
All right, here you go. I hope you'll keep your promise.
What?! Are you out of your mind, brother? Not even the property of my father would be enough to satisfy you! I don't have that much. The most I can give you is 7,500 gp.
Either you will give me 10,000 gp, brother, or I won't be able to guarantee that the public doesn't find out about the place where your chain was found!
I'm sorry but that's unacceptable!
It was your choice, brother.
Yes, that sounds likely..
What else could it be, brother. I'm a Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, not a renegade who cuts bodies of young girls in cellars and gets satisfied by the sight of their innards.
That's a possible explanation, brother. But it's also possible that it was you who lost the chain during the ritual. What will you say about that?

That's ridiculous, brother. I'm a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, not a renegade who cuts bodies of young girls in cellars and gets satisfied by the sight of their innards. I'm telling you that somebody is trying to discredit me. And you should find out who, instead of suspecting me of all kinds of perversities!
Hmm... Maybe. We'll see.
I'm looking for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone? Maybe you've seen something on your journeys...

Me... well, I have, brother. I've seen something really disturbing. I'd be much happier if I hadn't seen anything, because it worries me sick, but there's nothing I can do about it. I haven't told anybody yet, because I'm afraid I could break the code of the Order.
You can say that to me. I'm your brother in arms!

I don't know, brother. You're my brother in arms, that's true, but each paladin is bound with loyalty to the crown and I can't disobey it. If I told you what I saw, I'd risk my honor and everything I swore to obey!

I understand your reasons, brother. But please think over what is more important—whether it's the faith you swore to protect or your honor. If you must make a choice, you must chose even at the cost of a self-sacrifice—just like the Holy Scripture says.
Yes, you're right. I'm going to tell you even if the consequences of my decision will probably be terrible!
If you saw anything that could help to discover any heretics and deal with them, tell me immediately. Otherwise I could take your behavior as being very suspicious!
You're right, brother. It's my duty to protect the true faith even if it means making sacrifices!
As you wish, brother. I'm not going to push you. Keep your testimony to yourself. You will certainly be able to justify yourself when you face God at the final judgment!
Wait, brother... you're right. It would be better if I told you—even if the consequences were terrible!
Thanks to the favor of God and the King, the ruler of Glatzburg is Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor. His deputy is Duke Rowan van Leerin.

You can get weapons and armor at the armorer Hans von Drichtmaul. At the wise-woman Enrie Jungwirdt and at the alchemist Paolus Ventimus you can get potions and magic items. The innkeepers Wanda Gielwitch and Ludwig Weintraum both sell all kinds of things. At Alphonso DiCerbio's you can exchange anything as long as you don't ask where it came from.

The cause of the crisis is obvious, brother. It's the heretics! They've poisoned the minds of people. Because of them God has punished us by His Scourges and cast this terrible malady on us. Because of the heretics we have crowds of beasts, of evil spirits and of devils in the Realm. There's only one way to stop this and return Ultherst to God's favor—cut off the heads of all that don't follow the word of God and fornicate with demons and phantoms—whether they do it with their minds or with their bodies!
I heard some rumors that there is a war brewing, brother. Do you know anything about it?

If there is a war, there's nothing we can do about it. It's God's will and no mortal can put a stop to it. Death to the enemies of faith, death to the heretics and all that don't live according to the word of God!!!

If you want to know about hellspawns, you came to the right person, brother. I have a lot of personal experience with them—the scars all over my body prove it. The biggest danger nowadays are the living corpses that appear in the streets of the city as soon as it gets dark. You can certainly imagine the panic it started amongst the local people. Until now everybody thought they were safe behind the city walls. If you go outside the city, beware rogues and all kinds of cutthroats waiting at the roads. They will kill for a few pieces of gold.

Wait, brother—it's not all. If you think you would be safer if you cut through the woods and the meadows instead, you are mistaken. Devils from the Devil's Caverns set out for their bloody feast more and more often. Nobody knows what exactly they are. Some think they are devils, some think they are humans turned to terrible scaly beast by a curse. The truth is, they look like a cross-breed of a human and a lizard. As if a basilisk raped a woman and she then gave birth to such a monster.

Grand Duke Heidrick offered a reward for catching the rogues who rob people at the roads. If you bring a scalp to Sheriff Smith the reward is yours. But of course, there hasn't been many that brought a scalp. There has been more of those who tried and lost their scalp instead.
Have you encountered any heretics who admitted to belong to the Cult of the Children of the New Order lately?
The Children of the New Order, brother? Where did you get that?
I found the first trace of them in Hillbrandt and it led me right here to Glatzburg.

Really? That's strange. I thought the Cult was dead. As far as I can remember it was one of the cults founded in the Empire in the 9th or 10th century. And I also thought its members were all burned at stakes by the Inquisition. That's why your news is so surprising to me. You must definitely tell that to Cardinal Truncquillius, the local Curial Inquisitor—if you haven't spoken to him already.
That's not important, brother. Please answer my question.

I've heard about the Cult. But I've never met anyone who'd belong to it. As far as I can remember, it was one of the cults founded in the Empire in the 9th or 10th century. It was crushed by the Inquisition in the end. I don't know anything else. You should try asking Cardinal Truncquillius, he knows a lot about things like that.

I don't know if you'd find it interesting, but the trickster Tinthan has finally been accused of theft. The rogue was evading justice for so many years laughing at us and now he's done for. He was stealing in the temple and there are witnesses who saw it. He's going to be hanging by his short, fat neck, I promise. His crooked legs will be fluttering in the wind and his body will be twitching. He deserves it. In the years he's spent here in Glatzburg he committed so many crimes that God must have condemned him a long time ago. Thefts, burglaries, frauds... and it's possible that there were even worse crimes. Robberies, murders... but the investigation will show. First we must catch him because he ran away—coward.

The merchant Raimond Ventano was accused of heresy, brother. At the third degree of torture he testified that he's committed some terrible crimes together with you. He testified that you together summoned the Fallen Angel Baphomet and that you kidnapped Francessca Gulvardi. What can you say about accusations such as these?

Where the hell did you get that!? It's a dirty lie spoiling my name! The man is lying, isn't that obvious? But I'm not going to leave it like that. I'm going to seek redress, he's going to pay with his life for that. Me, the protector of justice and a faithful servant of God, accused of something like that by filthy heretic who fornicates with cattle at Sabbaths and distills innocent virgins' blood at nights!

Did you expect me to confess to something like that, brother? Of course I deny it, it's a dirty lie! I haven't done anything like that. But you probably don't believe it. That surprises me. You know, it's not such a long time ago when a word of a knight was absolute. But the times have changed... a word of a simple merchant is more important to you than a word of a knight. Especially when it comes to heresy. That's unfortunate. But don't think I'm going to leave it like that!
Well, it probably is a false testimony...
You bet, brother. Nothing the son of a bitch has told you is true. I'm a servant of God, not a heretic and a traitor!
I'm looking into the murder of Bishop Trevorius. Do you know anything about it, brother?
No, I don't know anything about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. I just heard, they found him at the Grand Duke's gazebo. It's a great loss, not just for the church.

I heard that you were somehow involved, brother. They say they found you at the corpse before it had the time to get cold. Who would believe something like that is possible? Not that I'd ever suspect you of murder, but accusing a noble of such a terrible crime, that's unheard of!

I've never heard about Fae'Darlion, brother. I don't care about barbaric pagan history. Think they're devils and hellspawns. And you should leave them alone as well if you want your soul to stay pure. If God wanted us to care about places like that he wouldn't have let us forget them.
I'm sorry, I don't know much about Father Frederick. I only know that he died when the plague came. He was a feeble old man, he had no chance of surviving.

What did you say? That Istwan de Bragho rose from his grave? That's good news for a warrior! Happy to hear that, brother! The holy providence itself must have challenged me with a quest like that. It's clear that God wants me to stand up against him! And you say he's immortal? Nonsense. Everybody's mortal. You just need the right spell or to hit them with a sword hard enough! If you can't take him out, brother, you can leave him to me and my brothers!

The Fallen Angels are the highest demons ever to serve Satan. Together with him they were forced out of the Heavens for the crimes they had committed and for conspiracy against God. There's four of them and each of them controls one of the strong elements of chaos—Arthamon controls downfall and destruction, Baphomet rules madness, succubus Cerdie breeds lechery and the Fallen Archangel Azrael is the first emissary of Satan. It's a dangerous lot, brother, although nobody knows for sure whether they exist.
What? Are you trying to question the Holy Scripture?

No, brother, I'm not. But you know as well as I that you can't take the Holy Scriptures literally. You must interpret the texts, understand them and find their hidden meaning. So when it talks about heavenly or infernal creatures it doesn't necessarily mean that angels and devils walk the world just like ordinary people. Many church scholars admitted in their writings that we must primarily see the demonstration of higher powers—both infernal and heavenly—in those creatures, of which they are an essence. Therefore it's possible that when the Holy Scripture talks about the four Fallen Angels it really means the foursome infernal powers, although people picture them as devils with horns, hooves and tails.
That's heresy!
Well... maybe.
Uhm... an interesting opinion. Thank you.
You're welcome, brother. But remember that we'll never find out what the truth is—well, at least not why we're still alive.
I have no idea where the famous Bonhart von Drichtmaul's hammer could be found. And since I'm not a treasure hunter, I don't even care.
I've heard that Raquel Gielwitch has gone missing. But I don't know any details. Master of our order Dietrich von Gelbendiel is looking into it so maybe you could try asking him.
You probably think, brother, that there is no way to make you answer. But you are very wrong. You better answer or I'll be forced to use some very unpleasant methods to make you!
I'm probably not your favorite person, brother. But still I hope you'll answer my question.

I can see, brother, that over the years of fighting mortal enemies you've learned to be alert. That's quite understandable. But you will certainly agree that in a situation like this there's no need to be alert—your answer could be extremely helpful.
What has been stolen from you?

The Chain of my Order, a symbol of my status! What a shame! May a terrible punishment strike the one who dared to do something like that. I have no idea who it was but it must have been an extremely agile person. I didn't notice anything and than saw it was gone. What a disgrace! A knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous robbed of the symbol of his status. I was looking for it everywhere but without any success. Now that the providence has sent you I would like to take the chance and ask you to help me.
I will bring your chain back, brother. Trust me.
Would you really do that for me, brother? Then I'd be really grateful, believe me. God bless you.
God bless you too, brother. Can I talk to you for a moment?
Of course, brother. What troubles you?
Thank you, brother. Goodbye.
Goodbye, brother. And don't forget about my necklace!
Will there be any reward?
If it's not against your principles and the rules of your order then there surely will be some. I'm not greedy when my honor is at stake.
Do you suspect anyone, brother?

I do, brother. Considering that I didn't notice the chain disappearing, I'd bet it was the performer Tinthan! The rascal is such a skillful thief that he could steal the nose between your eyes and you wouldn't notice before you wanted to blow it. That's why I think it must have been him. There is no thief more skillful than him in Glatzburg.
All right, thanks.
Where can I find this Tinthan?
If I knew that, brother, I'd put the squeeze on him myself!
It doesn't seem like you have any real proof for your claim. Because Tinthan is known to be a skillful, it doesn't mean that it was him who stole the chain.
Of course not, brother. And I didn't accuse him of theft. I only said that I suspected him.
I'm sorry but I really don't have time for this.
I understand, brother. You don't need to say more.
Isn't it by any chance this chain, brother?
Why do you think I'm on a mission?
All of us are on a holy mission. And especially we, paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I suppose you're fulfilling a task here that was assigned to you by God—am I right?
Yes, you could put it that way.

That's what I thought. I hope you'll find what you're looking for here in Glatzburg. Whatever it is. But If you could spare some time, there's something I would like to confide to you. There is a certain... well, quite an unpleasant issue. Very unpleasant for me because it's a matter of honor, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!
I have no mission here in Glatzburg. You can say that I'm just passing by.

Oh, I understand. In that case I hope that you come to the end of your journey safely. But since the providence has led you in my way I would like to ask you to do me a favor. There is a certain... well, quite an unpleasant issue. Very unpleasant for me because it's a matter of honor, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!
I'm looking for members of a certain cult. I have a reasonable suspicion that they're planning to do something terrible!
What cult is it? Who's in it? What kind of things do the filthy heretics sell themselves out to?
The name is not important, but they will stop at nothing! Murders, sacrileges, conspiracies, fornicating with Satan, dark rituals, summoning demons...

Unbelievable! So many mortal sins at once... No wonder you're after them. I hope your investigation is successful. But if you could find some spare time, there's something I would like to confide to you. There is a certain... well, quite an unpleasant issue. Very unpleasant for me because it's a matter of honor, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!
I'd prefer if you kept that to yourself, brother. I don't want any scaremongering.

I understand. It looks like the cult is extremely dangerous. I hope your investigation is successful. But if you could find some spare time, there's something I would like to confide to you. There is a certain... well, quite an unpleasant issue. Very unpleasant for me because it's a matter of honor, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!
I'm investigating the origin of a certain mysterious scroll found on one of the heretics sentenced to death by burning in Hillbrandt.

A mysterious scroll, you say? There must be lot of them these days. Some heretic scribbles some kind of nonsense and then he starts to kill to get human innards or whatever. I wouldn't wanna be in your shoes, brother. But if you could find some spare time, there's something I would like to confide to you. There is a certain... well, quite an unpleasant issue. Very unpleasant for me because it's a matter of honor, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!
My mission is not your business, brother.
Yes, you're right, brother. I didn't want to be nosy, I was just curious about the reason for you coming to Glatzburg. From the first moment I knew that you did not belong to the local gentry.
That's right, brother.

But I was pleased to meet you. I would like to talk about something that happened to me. Something very unpleasant because my honor's at stake, you see? I was robbed, brother! I, the Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, called by God to protect and to carry out justice, robbed by a filthy thief who had no respect for my mission and status!

I found your chain in an abhorrent pagan shrine near the local place of execution. And it was obvious that there had been a dark ritual performed short time before, because I found a body of a young girl with prolapsed innards there!

What? My chain in such an abhorrent place? Unbelievable! It looks like the theft wasn't a simple theft. It was meant to make me a heretic suspect, I'm sure about that! What else could you deduce from finding my chain there, than that I took a part in the ritual? How disgusting!
But, brother! Do you realize what you've just proposed? It could be called blackmailing!
What a disgusting word, brother. I prefer a more accurate term—a friendly service to a fellowman in need.
All right, here you go. I hope you'll keep your promise. And now will you please excuse me, I have a lot of work!
Not so fast, brother. I want to ask you some more questions.
But hurry up, brother. My time is precious.
I hope you'll keep your word! And now, excuse me please, I'm too busy!
I'm sorry, but that's unacceptable. Goodbye!
All right, whatever. But now you have to answer some of my questions.
It was your decision, brother. Good bye.
Yes, you're right. Could I ask you few more questions?
Of course, brother. What do you want to know?
Well, then... goodbye.

That's ridiculous, brother. I'm a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, not a renegade who cuts up bodies of young girls in cellars and gets satisfied by the sight of their innards. I'm telling you that somebody is trying to discredit me. And you should find out who, instead of suspecting me of all kinds of perversities!
Hmm... maybe. Can I ask you something now?
Go ahead, brother. What do you want to know?
You found it, brother? I can't believe it... my chain is back. Thank you. I'm deeply indebted to you! Please accept some gold as a token of my gratitude.
Thank you, brother. I was happy I could help. Goodbye.
Thank you, brother. But I must tell you this—the circumstances under which I found your chain were... well... surprising.
Really? What do you mean? Could you be more specific?
I don't ask a reward for what I did, brother. You can give your gold to the poor or donate it to the Holy Mother Church. Goodbye.
You're right, brother. I'm going to do that. Thank you and have a nice day.
I don't ask a reward for what I did, brother. But I must tell you this—the circumstances under which I found your chain were... well... surprising.
That's a wise decision. And what did you see? What did you witness?

It was a dark night and I was returning from a campaign against the rogues, that were hassling the von Hunt residence, to the city. I decided to cut across the municipal cemetery; I don't really know why. The cemetery is full of the undead at night nowadays but that night it was empty. Then suddenly I heard a strange sound—as if somebody was digging in the ground. I followed the sound and then, in a faint light of a lantern, I saw somebody. Somebody was digging a grave. First I thought it was Dietrich, the gravedigger. But the silhouette didn't look like him. And then I found out that the person wasn't digging but opening a grave. I sneaked a little bit closer to see the face of the person. And when I finally saw it, my heart stopped. It was Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor!
The royal governor? I can't believe that...

But it's true, brother. Now you probably understand why I was so reluctant to tell anybody. Grand Duke Heidrick is the representative of royal authority here in Glatzburg and as a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous I'm supposed to be loyal to him and not oppose him!
The Grand Duke dug out a coffin and pried out the lid with a spade. Then he took out the corpse. It must have been a girl or a boy because the body was very slender.
Why didn't you do anything? Why did you stay behind?

What was I supposed to do, brother? As a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous I'm bound by loyalty to the royal authority which is represented by the Grand Duke here in Glatzburg. I can't take an action against him without breaking the code of the order.
You're welcome, brother. I hope my testimony helps, even though it won't bring anything good to me. I'm sure about that.
Ethien de Pasque, I arrest you on the suspicion of heresy and of conspiracy against God and the King. You're coming with me!
Excuse me, brother? There must a mistake.
There's no mistake, brother. You're coming with me.
Do you have any evidence against me? I know my rights—you cannot arrest me unless you have very good evidence!
I have all the evidence I need, brother! Surrender immediately!
Hmm... All right, I'm going to come with you. But you are making a huge mistake, brother, believe me. I'm completely innocent, trust me!
Let's go. And I take your necklace as a corpus delicti.

The first evidence is your chain found at the shrine near the place of execution. The second evidence is Raimond Ventano's testimony according to which you two kidnapped a girl named Francessca Gulvardi so she could be seized by an unholy spirit!
That's ridiculous. I have never heard a charge more absurd. No inquisition court would believe a charge like that, brother, sorry.
It's not up to you to decide, brother. Surrender and come with me!
Maybe you're right, brother. But anyway, I must ask you to come with me, because, as you surely understand, I must check every suspicion!

God is watching our deeds, brother. He's watching us and he's getting ready for Judgment Day when he'll pass his sentence. And that's why our faith must be stronger and our service more zealous than ever! As the First Prophet said: 'All that have hands must help in building the divine kingdom on Earth!' And that's why I say: 'let's raise our swords and shields to protect this holy work which is being destroyed by filthy heretics right before our eyes!'
You're right, brother. The time to protect what's in danger has come.

Exactly! The infernal monsters are lounging at the door yard of the house of God, heretics spit at the cross of the First Prophet and faith in the Dark Prince is stronger than true faith in God. It's time to set spurs to our horses and with their hooves crush all that went astray from the right path and ignored the call of the Lord for the return to his herd!

I personally think that you are exaggerating, brother. Of course God is watching us but it has nothing to do with what's happening in the Realm. Heresy has nothing to do with the way God is watching us.

I don't think so, brother. I think the time of a great trial has come and everybody must show now how strong his faith is! It's time to make sacrifices and time to protect what's most precious to us—our faith! And it's God who's watching us and trying us. And you know what, brother? I'm not letting him down.
May I ask who am I talking to?
Knight Ethien de Pasque, at your services! I am the Knight Commander of the local chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Pleased to meet you.
Pleased to meet you.

The pleasure's all mine, brother. I'm glad you've strengthened our ranks here in Glatzburg. The conflicts between our Order and the Holy Inquisition occur even here and we must be ready for anything. I realize that these are difficult times and many couldn't carry the heavy burden anymore and fell prey to an unjustified anger. But mutual incriminations in order to gain more power will not help. That's why I hope that the unfortunate dispute over the authority of the Brotherhood of the Righteous and the Holy Office will soon be resolved by an edict of his highness Edward the Second.
In whose favor do you think the King will decide, brother?

In whose favor? In the favor of justice, of course! What else should matter to the King but justice and peace for all the faithful. I'm sure his decision will follow such an aim and whatever it will be, it will contribute to stability and to victory over the heretics dancing on the grave of our faith!
Yes, I agree.
I'm pleased about that. Can I ask you what kind of mission has brought you to Glatzburg, brother?
I think the Brotherhood of the Righteous should submit to the authority of the Holy Office. In times such as these it's better if justice is executed by only one institution!

Hmm... maybe you're right, brother. The times require a change and tradition is not right anymore. We all must do everything to save what we have been fighting for. Even if it meant giving up our standards to the prosecutors of the Inquisition.
Exactly. I'm glad you agree with me, brother.
Thank you. However, can you tell me what kind of mission has brought you to Glatzburg, brother?
I can't believe that you agree with the proposal, brother.

Well, it is unusual for a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous but you must realize that what we are facing nowadays is the beginning of the end of everything we've ever known and loved. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, nothing has been as it used to be. And that's why I think the Inquisition should have a free hand if it can bring peace.
A good observation.
Thank you, brother. Can you tell me, however, what kind of mission has brought you to Glatzburg.
The Brotherhood of the Righteous should be allowed to keep all its present authority. It's always better if justice is executed by more independent institutions—then mutual control is guaranteed.

Exactly, brother. The Brotherhood has been tested by time in their fight for justice. The mission has been given to us by God and thus there is no reason to worry that we would ever use our influence to gain secular power or wealth..
I'm glad we can agree in such an awkward question. But can you tell me what kind of mission has brought you to Glatzburg?
Yes, I hope so. I doesn't help anything.
Exactly. It's not important who will have what authority and who will have to submit to the authority of the other. The important thing is whether we've all done enough to execute justice!
Hello, brother. How are you doing? Have you found out anything about my chain? I must get it back at any cost. It's a matter of honor!
I found some chain, brother. Here.
Unfortunately, I didn't find anything.
Never mind, brother, I didn't either. But hopefully we'll find it soon. I can't allow my reputation to be injured in such an inglorious way. Can I help you?
Of course, brother. What's the matter?
No, I was just passing by.
Hello, brother. How are you doing? Is there anything I can do for you?
I'd like to talk to you, brother. If it doesn't bother you.
About your stolen chain... I've changed my mind. I've decided to help you find it.
Really, brother? What a surprise! If you managed to succeed, I'd be infinitely grateful!
Good. Can I now ask you a few questions?
Sure, go ahead.
Hello, brother. Thank you for the chain—you helped me recover my honor. Is there anything I can do for you in return?
Is it you, brother? What do you need? I don't have much time...
Whatever. But be brief, all right?
I found this necklace, sir knight. Does it by any chance belong to you?

Oh yes, it is my necklace. You found it! Unbelievable... I was beginning to think that my honor was lost forever. My necklace is back. Thank you, Father. I'm forever indebted to you. Where did you find it anyway?
But, Father! Do you realize what you've just proposed? It could be called blackmail!
That's an ugly word, sir knight. I'd prefer 'a friendly service to a neighbor in need'.
1,000 gold pieces.
What?! Are you out of your mind, Father? Not even the property of my father would be enough to satisfy you! I don't have that much. The most I can give you is 7,500 gp.
Either you will give me 10,000 gp, sir knight, or I won't be able to guarantee that the public doesn't find out about the place where your chain was found!
It was your choice, sir knight.
What else could it be, Father. I'm a Knight Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, not a renegade who cuts bodies of young girls in cellars and gets satisfied by the sight of their innards.
That's a possible explanation, sir knight. But it's also possible that it was you who lost the chain during the ritual. What will you say about that?

That's ridiculous, Father. I'm a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, not a renegade who cuts bodies of young girls in cellars and gets satisfied by the sight of their innards. I'm telling you that somebody is trying to discredit me. And you should find out who, instead of suspecting me of all kinds of perversities!

Hello, sir. How are you doing? Have you found out anything about my chain? I must get it back at any cost. It's a matter of honor!
