According to the results of my investigation defendant Harph has sold himself out to dark powers and in exchange for his soul he obtained vicious necromantic abilities allowing him to raise dead people and to change them into awful tools for his dreadful plans. And the defendant's only ambition was to get as much gold as possible. Defendant Harph made his undead monsters murder the citizens of Glatzburg in its streets, and then robbed their dead bodies of gold and of other valuables.

The strongest evidence against the defendant is his own diary, found in a secret hiding place in his disgusting necromantic sanctum in the center of the city sewers. But that's not the only evidence. An eyewitness testified he saw defendant Harph entering the city sewers accompanied by several undead monsters. That's clear and unambiguous evidence.

We've heard an appalling case of heresy. It's not necessary to present any other evidence—the guilt has been proven beyond a reasonable doubt. And since the heresy is rooted really deep in the heart of this unfaithful soldier I don't see any other choice than to ignite the flames of justice and let them purify his soul of the sinful body and purge it of all the abhorrence he committed.

Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence defendant Joah Harph to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Alphonso DiCerbio, whom the prosecution charges with kidnapping, criminal conspiracy and with conspiring against God and the King.

Alphonso DiCerbio is accused of kidnapping Tom Clifford, the son of the chamberlain Johaness Clifford, on the basis of the testimony of Guss Halworth who witnessed the crime. Hence Alphonso DiCerbio was arrested and questioned to find out if he's really guilty of the crime.

When interrogated he confessed to his sins and pleaded he in fact kidnapped Tom Clifford. But that's not all. He confessed it was him who kidnapped several innocent girls in Glatzburg and its vicinity not a long time ago.

With regard to these facts I don't see any other choices to free his soul of so many sins than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Alphonso DiCerbio to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Raimond Ventano, whom the prosecution charges with the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi, heresy and with intriguing against the Faith, the Holy Mother Church, the King and even against God.

The investigation results have shown Raimond Ventano was one of the principal kidnappers who abducted Francessca Gulvardi in order to throw her body before infernal powers that possessed her by an unclean spirit. The aim of that devilish plan was to make her murder Bishop Trevorius. Fortunately the monstrous intrigue didn't come to fruition and the Inquisition was able to purify poor Francessca of the wanton infernal paws and to question her.

Based on the testimony of Francessca Gulvardi Raimond Ventano was arrested and put to torture. Then he confessed he in fact perpetrated the said crime. But that was not all. He also confessed he in his perversity partook in the preparation and subsequent alleged invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet.

Think of that awfulness—the man standing before us has the nerve to spit into the face of God and to defame His name by deliberately and willingly working on the staining of the God's Earthly Kingdom by the presence of a Fallen Angel. Such a chilling and staggering arrogance is unforgivable! All the evidence brought forth speaks clearly—the man, the monstrous harpy fetid with the smell of brimstone and of Hell, is really guilty. He doesn't deserve anything else but to perish by the most dreadful way. His remains should be tossed to fierce beasts so his soul would never find peace.

But in these hard times our Holy Mother Church is willing to accept even such hardened and unfaithful men back to our ranks. The heart of this sinful man may be purified by the purgative flames of justice that will relieve it from the sinful body. Then his soul will stand before the face of God without the brand of sin and it will be able to enter purgatory where the wisdom and reason of our Lord will grace it with immortality. Hence I sentence Raimond Ventano in the name of God Almighty to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Commander Ethien de Pasque, whom the prosecution charges with heresy, with complicity in the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi and with conspiring against the Holy Mother Church, God and against the King.

Just look at the evidence convincing the man standing before us. A necklace was found in a disgusting heretical sanctum near the gallows in Glatzburg, where, beyond a reasonable doubt, a rite to invoke dark powers took place. Subsequently the Inquisition managed to find out and to duly establish that it belonged to Commander Ethien de Pasque and that it proves his participation in enormities that took place in the damned sanctum.

But that's not all. After interrogating the merchant Raimond Ventano with the use of torture the Inquisition obtained his full confession. The malevolent merchant confessed it was Ethien de Pasque who assisted him in kidnapping Francessca Gulvardi and that they together participated in the alleged rite of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet.

And there's another evidence. Commander Ethien de Pasque was arrested on the basis of the suspicion of heresy and put to torture. Although he had been resisting for quite a long time, eventually he confessed he in fact perpetrated all the crimes I charge him with. He admitted he purportedly assisted with the invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet who has become his new master. He confessed that he, together with Raimond Ventano, kidnapped Francessca Gulvardi in order to let her get possessed by an unclean spirit and to use her as a living weapon against Bishop Trevorius.

You've just heard how awful the heresy of Commander Ethien de Pasque is. I can't help but to declare his guilt as proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Let's look at the monstrous disguise the man used to conceal his deeds. Behind the mask of a God's servant protecting justice and the Crown at every turn there was a beast hiding not hesitating to do evil of the worst kind. He didn't detest the most condemnable crimes in his disgusting pride.

But the Holy Mother Church has sympathy even for such renegades. I'm convinced that once his body is burned at the stake his soul will be able to stand before the face of our Lord and accept his judgment. Hence I sentence Commander Ethien de Pasque to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, whom the prosecution charges with heresy and intriguing against the Faith, the Holy Mother Church, the King and against God Himself.

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick was indicated as the mastermind of all the crimes perpetrated by Reimond Ventano and Ethien de Pasque. Their confessions clearly speak against the Grand Duchess. It was she who devised the idea of invoking the Fallen Angel Baphomet. It was she who ordered the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi and to use her for the attempted murder of Bishop Trevorius.

But those are not all her crimes. Dietrich the gravedigger confessed he purveyed the dead body of a mad girl for the Grand Duchess and her henchmen, and that he did it for payment. The heretics needed the corpse for invoking of the Fallen Angel Baphomet.

And if someone wishes to doubt the charges made, then he may listen to the supreme proof—the Grand Duchess' confession. She went even so far in her depraved pride as to plead guilty on all counts of the indictment. Moreover she confessed she reputedly fornicated with the invoked demon Baphomet and that she gave birth to infernal creatures arisen from that unclean union. And those creatures in fact came to help her during the torture.

Do you see how terrible the crimes Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick perpetrated are? Do you see of how disgusting offences of God's name and of all that's sacred the woman was capable of? We all had recognized her, believing in the purity of her soul and in the kindness of her heart. Instead she greedily drank from the stream of sin and fornicated with infernal powers!

But God in his mercy offers eternal salvation to people and the Holy Mother Church will gladly administer the purgative flame that will burn all the filth and retain only the essence of the human soul. Hence I, in the name of God and by virtue of the authority bestowed upon me, sentence Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to her soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Downay, whom the prosecution charges with heresy, consorting with dark powers and with conspiring against God and the King.

The results of the investigation are clear—defendant Downay was led astray and sold himself out to dark powers to be their humble servant. This was attested to by the old man named Balthazar, who heard Downay boasting about a new order coming soon and its children ruling the world. This proves beyond a reasonable doubt that the gardener belongs to the Cult of the Children of the New Order.

But that's not all—during the interrogation with the use of torture Downay confessed he actually was in the service of the Cult of the Children of the New Order and that he committed many terrible crimes in its name. He assisted in the preparations of a mass celebrating Hell this spring. All the dark priests of the Cult met at that mass.

Appaling! Look at all the terrible atrocities the foul heretic perpetrated! It's not necessary to present any other evidence. His guilt has been proven beyond a reasonable doubt. And since the heresy is rooted really deep in the heart of this unfaithful man I don't see any other choice than to ignite the flames of justice and let them purify his soul of the sinful body and purge it of all the abhorrence he committed.

Yes, the Holy Mother Church may bring such mercy even to the people who have sinned so terribly. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence defendant Downay to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately.

I, as a Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Sven Larsen, whom the prosecution charges with the murder of Knight Eradim d'Chambrie.

The evidence speaks clearly. Paladin Eradim d'Chambrie was insidiously murdered by an unknown shooter that was hiding not far away from the place where the Knight lingered at that time. The master armorer Leon van den Brooks identified the arrow that killed the paladin as the arrow he custom-made for the defendant Sven Larsen.

Based on this evidence defendant Sven Larsen was arrested and put to torture because he refused to plead guilty voluntarily. Only pain showed him the way back to God and he confessed he actually committed the murder, and even that he did it for payment.

Isn't it disgusting? How heinous a case of hideous treachery! It's the same as when the First Prophet was betrayed by cursed Malachiah, who denounced him to the Erebornians for 33 gold pieces. There is enough evidence for the court to pass the sentence. And I don't see any other choice how to free the soul of Sven Larsen of the mortal sin than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Sven Larsen to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Duke Verenicus, whom the prosecution charges with heresy and conspiring against God and the King.

Duke Verenicus is accused of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King based on the confession of two persons who saw him two years ago when he willfully allowed unknown men into the royal palace and then performed an unclean rite with them in the chambers of Prince Louis. Everyone knows the results of their terrible acts—Prince Louis was found dead the next day, lying in his bed with no sign of life.

Isn't it appalling? Look at that man! Look at those terrible crimes he committed while His Majesty King Edward II was fostering him! See how he abused the confidence of our good monarch and how he betrayed him! How he sold his soul to Hell and with his shameful deeds contributed to the passing of Crown Prince Louis and of King Edward himself!

God sees this man and is angry with him for allowing his soul to be stained with so many mortal sins. Nevertheless it's necessary to bring forward another evidence of his guilt. Hence I'll offer you now the highest proof which will show the guilt of the defendant beyond any doubt. The defendant pleaded guilty to all his crimes and acknowledged that all that has been spoken against him is the truth and nothing else.

How appalling! That shameless heretic committed a really disgusting treason. And not only against the royal family whom he should have faithfully served, but also against God himself, when he conspired with the powers of darkness and brought the soul of Prince Louis to their dark altar.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Gilbert, whom the prosecution charges with heresy, worshiping of dark powers and with the forgery of gold.
The truth is the shadow of suspicion first fell on a beggar named Beckham. But during the interrogation he confessed he stole the forged gold from Father Gilbert.

On the basis of this evidence Father Gilbert was arrested and immediately and voluntarily pleaded guilty to his crimes. By that he made it obvious he wished for redemption and was ready to make the highest sacrifice to allow his soul to be redeemed. Hardly any heretic finds the courage to voluntarily commit himself to God, to expiate and thus to find the way to the eternal kingdom of Heaven through purgatory.

And we won't disappoint our brother. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence priest Gilbert to be burned to death. Ignite the flames of justice that will relieve his soul of the sinful body. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger, whom the prosecution charges with the robbing of graves.

The results of the investigation has shown beyond a reasonable doubt that Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger committed the crimes he is accused of. His boots incriminated him, being muddy with clay which can be found only at one place in this entire region—at the city cemetery near one of the robbed graves.

Even this proof alone is enough to convict him. Look, all you good people, at this man and tell me, if there is any worse crime against the dead than to defame their graves and steal their belongings. It's the terrible work of Satan, the seed of sin and of moral degeneration. Even this evidence alone is enough for God to condemn the actions of this man. But I have to satisfy laws of God and Church and put forth yet another convincing evidence.

And that proof is the highest one—the defendant's confession! When arrested, Steinger confessed he really committed those terrible crimes in an effort to obtain unjust enrichment. God is glad the defendant confessed to his sins voluntarily. It shows his soul is not lost yet and is longing for redemption.

In that case I'm willing to give the defendant a chance to relieve his soul of all sins—to ignite the flames of justice that will burn his sinful body and let his soul enter purgatory. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Vick Length, whom the prosecution charges with grave robbing and with grave desecration.

The evidence is beyond a reasonable doubt. Based on the confession of Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger it was possible to find out it was Vick Length who made him rob the graves at the city cemetery and in the vicinity of the city. And so we're now looking into the face of a man who detests nothing, because as the First Prophet said—ever so little a sin is like a murder. We face the man who doesn't detest desecrating the remembrance of the deceased by destroying their graves, disturbing the peace of the dead and by stealing the belongings of their consecrated bodies. How monstrous! How foul! How depraved!

But that alone would not be enough to sentence the sinner. Fortunately the prosecution has managed to get the tradesman Imam ab Sahab's confession. He testified that Vick Length tried to sell him some of the jewelry stolen from the grave of Baron Mansfeld. Thanks to that there is no doubt about the guilt of the defendant.

All that has been told here proves Vick Length's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. And in that case I don't see any other choice as to how to free his soul of so many sins than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence Vick Length to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, commence this trial against defendant Joah Harph, whom the prosecution charges with heresy, dealing with dark powers, practicing of necromantic rites and with orchestrating of thefts and murders.

As you can see, many proofs of the guilt of the royal counselor Verenicus were presented. And I don't see any other choice as to how to free his soul of the mortal sin than to ignite the flames of justice that will purify his soul of the sinful body. Thereby I, Judge of the Holy Office, entrusted by the Holy Mother Church and merciful God to discover, prosecute and punish crimes against God and the Faith, sentence the royal counselor Verenicus to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.
If Inquisitor General Commendoni spoke the truth, this portal leads to the Kingdom of Eternal Sin where the succubus Cerdie resides...
The cursed book Libre Daemonium should be able to open the portal... May God's will prevail!
If the Fallen Angel Arthamon has really been summoned then this must be the portal leading to the Earthly Kingdom of Destruction.
If the Fallen Angel Baphomet has really been summoned this must be the portal leading to the Earthly Kingdom of Madness...
I've heard you are paying out rewards for killed werewolves, Sheriff. Is that so?
Yes, it is, boy. Grand Duke Drake Lambert authorized me to pay out a reward for each werewolf head you bring from Schwarzwald. You bring a head, I give you the gold.
Thank you, Sheriff.
You're welcome, boy. And by the way—the biggest reward is for bringing the head of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr.
I'm sorry but I'm not going to talk to you about that, boy.

Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert, the royal governor of the city. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. As far as Grand Duke Lambert is concerned, I can't say anything bad about him. He's a noble man who knows how to rule. It's just his marriage that is not too successful. His wife Liana is said to be rather flighty. But that's not my problem, is it?

It depends on what you wanna buy, boy. If it's weapons or armor you should try master armorer Leon van den Brooks, who has his famous workshop here in Alvaron. At the apothecary Thelma Ulthraum and the master alchemist Alberto Kelley you can get all kinds of potions and magic items. And the innkeepers William Burton and Salena Flock sell all kinds of stuff.

Have I heard rumors about war? Hoh! Who else but a Sheriff should know about war. And you're right, there is a war coming. I was authorized by the First Knight Rodrigo de Velacor to get the whole Alvaron regiment ready, and that means something. In a few weeks there will be five thousand men armed. Plus we are requisitioning horses, recruiting new men, filling the armories getting the war machines ready... there's just one important thing missing—an enemy. It doesn't seem there is anyone you could use an army against threatening the Realm. That's what I don't get.

Believe me, nothing has scared me as much in many years as the Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert's case. I've always believed him to be a bane of all human and non-human scoundrels and all of a sudden he's on the blacklist. I don't know what to think about it. Most people in the city believe him to be a heretic and a pagan who didn't hesitate to make a contract with Satan to gain more power. And yet more are they afraid of what the future has in store for them because if a superior of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is a heretic, where does it stop?!
No, I've never heard of Cult of the Children of the New Order, boy. We used to have the Cult of the Pagan Night here, but not the Children of the New Order. Sorry.

It's a two-year-old affair but I still cannot forget about it. I mean the death of Prince Louis and of his sisters. Two young chamber maids—Kathryn Winhold and Corin Morray were convicted of the murder. Kathryn Winhold, however, originally accused the royal advisor Verenicus of the murder. You can certainly imagine the scandal. But the witch took everything back and confessed in the torture chamber. Yet there are still people who don't trust Verenicus. Who knows what happened then.

If it's about weapons, you should ask Leon van den Brooks. He knows all about weapons. And as far as I can tell the arrow looks like his work. I suppose it's pointless to ask whose blood it is, isn't it? Yes, that's what I've thought...

There's been many who tried to remove the curse of Baron von Blutenreich's house. I think Baron Gerbert of Rowington has been trying as well although it's not quite clear why. But nobody has succeeded. People say that the curse was cast by the Baron's wife before she was executed and it cannot be removed. Maybe it's true.

As far as Father Nicolas is concerned I'm deeply sorry for him. I'm sure he didn't touch Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. You know, it's difficult to rape a woman who spreads her legs before you have the time to lay her down. But it will always be his word against the word of the wife of the royal governor, that means the word of one of the most important ladies in the Realm, so Father Nicolas has good reason to be worried... I, unfortunately, don't know about anything that could help him.
If you really want to know, boy, it will cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
I'm waiting for your answer, Sheriff! And I want it now, understood?
To tell you the truth—it seems to me that I'm not your favorite person. But still I would like you to answer my question.
If I hadn't heard about your deep knowledge of the world and your great experience I wouldn't insist on you answering the question. But in this case I must insist that you answer, Sheriff..
Can I talk to you for a moment? I'd like to ask you a few questions.
Go ahead, boy. Maybe you will find out something you need to know.
I'm going. Goodbye.
Nice to meet you, boy. And take care. I don't want the werewolf beasts to get another innocent.
Can I talk to you for a moment, Sheriff?
Sure, boy. What's on your mind? What do you need to know from old Henry Portmann?
Of course, son—that's why I'm here. Who is it?
I would like to interrogate one of the accused, Sheriff. In the torture chamber.
And who should that be, boy?
As a judge of the Holy Office I would like to take proceedings against a suspect, Sheriff.
As you wish. And who should that be, boy?
The gardener Downay.
All right, boy. I'll lock him up.
Sven Larsen.
All right, boy, as you wish. I'll lock him up.
The royal advisor Verenicus.
Duke Verenicus? I can see you are playing it high, boy. But all right, as you wish. I'll lock him up.
Father Gilbert.
That scribe from archbishop's library? As you wish, boy. I'll lock him up.
Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger.
Vick Length.
All right, boy. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? A rack, a strappado, a pillory or an iron maiden?
Do you want to torture the royal advisor Duke Verenicus?
Yes, exactly. Is there an estoppel to proceedings?
No, boy. I don't think so. I just wanted to make sure. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? A rack, a strappado, a pillory or an iron maiden?
A rack!
All right, boy. I will tell my assistants to get everything ready. You can descend to the torture chamber.
A strappado!
A pillory!
An iron maiden!
All right, boy. I'll have the prisoner taken to the place of execution. You can get ready for the trial.
Duke Verenicus.
Priest Gilbert.
Steinger.
Did you manage to get any of the beasts, boy? Good job! Come on, show me what you got.
I have a werewolf head.
Excellent! Good job! Here's your reward. Another cursed soul back in hell!
You're welcome, boy. Do you have anything else?
I have the head of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr, Sheriff.
You killed the wolf-prince Wulfyhrr, a murderer of many innocent including women and children! The Wulfhyrr everybody far and wide has been terrified of?
Yes, Sheriff. There is a reward, isn't there?

But... but of course, dear boy. This is a great news for all of us. Wulfhyrr is dead! Nobody's going to die by his claw anymore! He will not cause more chaos and grief! Here's your reward—God knows you rightfully deserve it.
All right, boy. You were doing great.

Hello, boy. It's a pretty busy day here. As well as any other day in fact. Damn—these are horrible times. The service in the army is harder and harder but I'm not going to bother you with that. What can old Henry Portmann do for you?

As I said—my name is Henry Portmann, boy. I'm a Sheriff here in Alvaron. That means that I get blamed for all the shit that happens here. But I've learned to live with that. You have to contend with that when you become a Sheriff—it's more of toil than a service, but you certainly know something about toil, don't you?
You obviously have a lot of work, Sheriff. Do you need any help?

Oh, I'll take that offer gladly, boy. There is a case which is within my jurisdiction you could help me with. I don't know how to deal with it and it's unfortunately a serious problem. A problem of the defense of the city. When you look at the walls you probably think where could be a problem here.

Well it's about the werewolf beasts that have been raging around Alvaron in the past few years. I don't know whether you've heard about them but I suppose you did because people have been talking about them a lot lately. The problem is that every full moon they manage to get into the city and kidnap some women.
How do they get over the walls?

That's the core of the problem. They always manage to get through one of the gates and in the morning we find the guards deep in an unnatural sleep. I don't have to be an inquisitor to recognize that there are some dark powers of some filthy heretic at work. The beasts must have an accomplice in the city who puts the guards to sleep and opens the gates. And I need to find him and get him hanged.
I'll take care of the case, Sheriff.
Really, boy? Then I'm glad. I hope you are successful.
What happens to the victims of the kidnappings? Was any of the women ever found?
Partly, boy. From time to time we find a part of one of them but it's difficult to identify, if you know what I mean.
Is there a reward for finding the heretic who cooperates with the werewolves?
Yes, boy. If you manage to find him, a reward is yours!
Unfortunately, I have more important work than this, Sheriff. I can't look into the case.
Really, boy? That's a pity. But what can I do? I'm gonna have to take care of it with my people.

A municipal Sheriff always has as much authority as the royal governor gives him—but only in the area of the army administration and of public order. I, for example, take care of the whole garrison here in Alvaron—from supplies to training and recruiting. I also take care of the municipal prison, which is probably what interests you. When you arrest somebody you can imprison him in the local jail with my consent. If you want to rack him, just tell me. But I hope there won't be much torture because I have a lot of work anyway!
I would like to point out that since I am a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous you should address me 'knight', not 'boy'.
All right, as you wish, boy.
Pleased to see you, boy. How is your investigation of the werewolf case getting on? Did you manage to discover the villain who lets them in the city at the full moons?
No, Sheriff, not yet. But I'm working on it...
I'm pleased to hear that. Sooner or later you will certainly manage to catch the heretic. Even though there is not much time left until the next full moon...
Yes, Sheriff, I found him. It was a boy named Horst. He really was a son of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr.
What? Horst? Good heavens... I would never think of that. I knew him pretty well, he was a lively boy, a little wild, but still...
Satan has a thousand faces and senses can be deceived... anyway, I finished the job and the case is closed.
Yes, that's true. No matter what, you did your job. Here is your reward. And thank you for your help. I'd have never exposed Horst myself.
You're welcome, boy. You did a good job!
Hello, boy. What can old Henry Portmann possibly do for you?
I would like to get my reward for killed werewolves.
Actually, I've changed my mind...

The punishment for a theft is cutting the right hand off, boy. So next time think twice before you touch something that doesn't belong to you. Of course you only did it by mistake. But I'd be unhappy if such a situation ever took place again.
I would like to point out that since I am a priest you should address me 'Father', not 'boy'.
I would like to point out that since I am a noble you should address me 'noble lord', not 'boy'.
So, how do I look? Do I look all right? I feel... strange.
To tell you the truth... you look like a skeleton!
Damn... it seems one body was not enough. It was enough for a skeleton but that's not sufficient. I can't walk amongst the people like this, I have nothing to wear. I need one more body, mortal!
All right, I'll get it for you.
Great! But hurry up—you never know when will another infernal servant appear to take me back to Hell!
I'm sorry but I don't have any more time.
I'm sorry. I thought we would make it to the end together... what can I do. But I can't let you leave—I can't risk you bringing back the ghost hunters!
Great! I can see you're bringing me another suitable body. I hope it will be enough this time... Guuuuuulp!
So, mortal, when are you going to bring me a suitable body? You better hurry up—you never know when will another infernal servant appear to take me back to hell!
Don't worry, I will bring you a suitable body...
I rely on you!
So, do I finally look like human?
It's better but still it's not right. You look like a few weeks old corpse!
Damn... you're right, mortal. And the smell... terrible! I can't walk amongst the people like that—with this body I wouldn't get too far. I need one more victim!
All right, I'll take care of it.
I'm sorry but I really don't have any more time.
Great! I can see that you've kept your promise and that you are bringing me another suitable body. I hope this time it will be enough... Guuuuuulp!
So, do I finally look like a human?
Yes, it's all right now... I think.
Really! I feel like I was born again. I'm gonna have to get used to having a new body and learn to use it, but I have a whole eternity, don't I?
Probably... wait, what was that? I've heard something...

Hmm... really. it looks like somebody's coming... But it's not an infernal servant—I'd smell it. It's mortals. What are they doing here? Damn! If they are the ghost hunters, we got a problem... I better disappear quickly. And thanks for your help, mortal!
Wait! What about my reward?
I'm sorry, but I have nothing to give you—but you must have expected that, haven't you? Goodbye... I hope you'll be able to get out of here somehow.
Help me, mortal! A fallen soul is asking your help! Will you listen?
Who are you, unholy spirit?
I'm Augustin Pteremon, a governor of the Alvaronium province. Or at least I used to be before I died and spent a thousand years in Hell. Only recently I've managed to run away...
WHAT?! You ran away from Hell?

Yes, exactly. You probably won't believe it, mortal, I'm telling the truth. Not all the fallen souls become the servants of the Dark Prince... Many of them are tortured and kept in eternal agony until the Dark Prince makes them his servants. But they've never broken me. I was waiting for an opportunity and it finally came. I returned and nobody can get me back! Not even the servants the Dark Prince sent after me and that are now at the door of my tomb...
What?!
Yes, they are here. They found me. I can smell them. They are supposed to bring me back. But I don't wanna return. No! Help me mortal. Kill them. Send them back to Hell instead of me!
All right, I will get rid of your pursuers.
Thanks, mortal. Kill them all!
If I help you what will I get out of it?
Nothing right now... I'm just a fallen soul without a body! But if you help me there will definitely be something for you...
And what did you do that you ended up in Hell for that?

What did I do? Nothing... some people call it bribery, blackmail, murders but I call it politics. I didn't do anything unusual for a governor of the Alvaronium province. To end up in Hell for that—what an injustice!
I'm not going to help such an unclean soul!
Then get lost, mortal!
I'm not going to listen to an infernal monster. Go back to burning hell!
That's exactly what I don't want to do—I've just managed to run away... so I'm gonna have to kill you!
Kill them, mortal. Kill them all! I don't want to go back to Hell. Never, understand? Never!
Don't worry.
Thank you mortal. Thank you for killing them all. I'm not going back to hell—it's worse than death!
What are you going to do now? It's only a matter of time before other infernal servants find you.
I have a plan... and you could help me with that, actually. If you are interested, of course...
What way is it?
I need to get a new body in which I could live amongst the mortal again. As you certainly see I can't show up looking like this anywhere. The ghost hunters would return me to hell immediately.
Do you want to become a human again? But that's impossible—you're undead!

Thanks for the information, I have noticed that myself. I don't want to become a human, I just wanna look like a human. That should be enough. And that's why I need a human body to control like a human controls his body. Understand?
Yes, I understand. It's smart and it might work—at least until the body doesn't rot.

Don't worry about that, mortal. I learned all kinds of things in Hell and I know how to deal with a body to make it resistant to pathological processes... but enough of talking, we're wasting time. What I want from you is simple—get me the body of a mortal. A man and somebody unimportant—I don't want to attract attention of the ghost hunters. A slave maybe.
I'm afraid slavery's been abolished after the fall of Ereborn.

Ereborn fell? Well... I can see some things have changed in the thousand years. But never mind. Get me the body of a simple peasant then. There are tons of them everywhere and they're good for nothing anyway...
All right, as you wish. I'll get you a simple peasant.
Great! I knew we could make a deal. You'll see that one day I'll give you a great reward for your help.

I'll be able to do all kinds of things with a new body... for example make you a magic weapon! As I've said—I learned all kinds of tricks in Hell. If you have a soul of a blacksmith who was cheating on his customers boiling in the next cauldron for half a millennium, you learn interesting things...
I'm not going to help you with anything like that!
No? What a pity... I thought we could make a deal. But considering you know my plans, I'm gonna have to kill you—what if you decided to set ghost hunters against me?
No thanks, I'm not interested. This has been enough. The farther I am from the infernal monsters, the better.
I see. That's quite understandable. But thanks for the help with the infernal servants anyway, mortal. And who knows—maybe we'll meet again, but you probably won't recognize me.
Great! I can see you kept your promise and you are bringing me a suitable body. Not too pleasant to look at but on the other hand, who'd miss someone like that.
What will you do with him?

I'll eat him. His living body will become a part of my undead and I will look like a human. It's similar as if you create a clay statue—take some clay and work it into a statue. The only difference is in the material—instead of clay I will use human flesh!
Disgusting!
Don't look then. Guuuulp!
So, mortal, when are you going to bring me a suitable body. Hurry up, you never know when will another infernal servant appear here to take me back to Hell!
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is in the position of the royal governor of the town. Royal vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin.

Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned armory in Glatzburg; if you want some warrior's equipment, you should pay him a visit—he has the best on offer. You can get various potions and the best quality magic items from Enrie Jungwirdt the wise-woman and Paolus Ventimus the alchemist. Wanda Gielwitch the innkeeper and Ludwig Weintraum the landlord have both shops with a lot of various goods to sell. And you can exchange a lot of things with Alphonso DiCerbio, if you don't mind the shady origin of those goods.
What do you think about the present crisis the Realm has been dragged into, brother?
Do you really want to know the truth, brother? Do you really want to know what I think about the current crisis?
Sure. That's why I ask you...

In that case know that what we're facing here is the total and irreversible end! It's a decay of all that seemed to be strong and stout till now. The faith is ruined, the Realm is falling apart, the dark times will soon rule the day! God punished us for our sins and put us on a trial. And as you can see—instead of repentance and submission people are looking up to wicked idols. Instead of the arms of the Holy Mother Church they run to the cults that offend God himself by their existence. To punish those who lack the faith, oh yes, that's what should be done. Because they committed sins and they don't want to find a way back, although a saving hand was offered to them. There's so few of us who are still trying to make things right... If only there weren't those conflicts between the Holy Office and my Order. I wish our powers could be combined instead of standing in opposition to each other. But this is all in vain...
Well... better not in fact.

But I don't mind telling you, brother. I think that what we're facing here is the total and irreversible end! It's a decay of all what seemed to be strong and stout till now. The faith is ruined, the Realm is falling apart, dark times will soon rule the day! God punished us for our sins and put us on a trial. And as you can see—instead of repentance and submission people are looking up to wicked idols. Instead of the arms of the Holy Mother Church they run to the cults that offend God himself by their existence. To punish those who lack the faith, oh yes, that's what should be done. Because they committed sins and they don't want to find a way back, although a saving hand was offered to them. There's so few of us who are still trying to make things right... If only there weren't those conflicts between the Holy Office and my Order. I wish our powers could be combined instead of standing in opposition to each other. But this is all in vain...
Some people say that a war is about to start. Do you happen to know anything about that?

I've also heard people talking about the war. Many things indicate it will start soon—men are being recruited, horses and cattle requisitioned, war armaments and equipment bought, granaries are filled, garrisons are on alert... Maybe it's just a preventive measure, but nobody believes it too much. The war is going to be, that's clear. But it's not so clear whom we will fight. An enemy that could be crushed with an army is nowhere to be seen. We can only wait. The King's marshals surely know well what they do—at least I pray for that.

If your life is dear to you, brother, beware of the neighborhood of pagan city Galibornium. The Devil's Caverns are situated there—it's a very deep complex of caves that leads to Hell itself. It seems that just those caverns are the place where a wicked kind of hellspawns lives—they look like bastards of a man and a basilisk. Those monsters have committed terrible crimes and bloodshed. From time to time a large bunch of them raid to kill in the neighborhood of our city. Maybe they long for human blood, nobody knows that for sure. However no one who got in their claws was ever seen again. So you better be careful about them, brother!

Grand Duke Heidrick set the reward for catching those brigands robbing people along the roads. You can bring a scalp or a head of a bandit to sheriff Smith and the reward is yours. But there aren't many head-hunters in the city, that's clear. It's much easier to rob than to catch the robbers...
I'm searching for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect anyone, brother?

I don't suspect anyone of heresy, brother. And if I had a suspicion, I'd follow his trail like a hound and I wouldn't lose the scent until the game would be caught. Because heretics are beasts that must be hunted and killed like vermin they are!

I don't know whether the name Henry de Montreaux would mean anything to you. He was my comrade in arms, a Knight of Brotherhood of the Righteous. Many times we fought alongside each other against the wiles of infernal powers, we spilled a lot of blood together when defending true faith and justice—just like our Order entrusts us to do. But something that I didn't understand happened and suddenly Henry de Montreaux wasn't my comrade any more; he's my enemy now. His mind must have been darkened by madness, because he killed several of our brothers in duels. When he was excommunicated from our Order for his deeds, he went totally mad, ran to the woods and now he kills everyone he runs into. I must stop him at all costs as I cannot stand that a servant of God became a tool of Satan.

Monsignor Trevorius was a good man. He knew where the place of the Holy Mother Church and of its servants is. His murderers must be punished, no matter who they are. Do you understand me, brother? No matter who committed the murder! He must pay for his crime. He must know what the Dies irae means!

I don't know anything about any burial chamber, brother. But it's true that during my journeys I several times ran into ruins of ancient buildings—they must have been even older than the Erebornian ones. Thus I think they were made by the ancient civilization of Elenians, but I could have made a mistake of course. However, I can't tell you whether any of the ruins was a burial chamber of some Elenian nobleman, brother.
And where are the ruins located, brother?

They're hidden in the woods surrounding the von Hunth's mansion, brother. In unapproachable places, where nobody goes. If you really want to find and investigate that burial chamber, you'll have to search very carefully.

Istwan de Bragho came out from his grave? And you say he can't be killed? Well... it's a serious problem. Very serious. I've heard about cases where the lust for revenge brought the dead back to this world and nobody was able to prevent him from doing that. People say that such undead creature can't be harmed by magic nor by sword and it won't stop committing its unholy deeds until its revenge is fulfilled—no matter if it was a just revenge or not.

However, I believe firmly that there must be some way how to make the lecherous Duke Istwan de Bragho return back to his grave. Try consulting Enrie Jungwirdt, brother—she knows pretty much everything about things like that. I often go to her for advice myself when I don't know what to do.

What do I know about the Fallen Angels? Well... you ask me about some very grim things, brother. So grim that it isn't a good idea at all to talk about it in these dark times. But I'll answer your question, although I doubt I'll tell you anything you don't know already. The Fallen Angels are former angelic beings who were thrown down from Heaven together with Satan for their crimes against God at the Dawn of Time. At least the Scriptures say so. Since that time they've been hellspawns, awful demons who live in Hell and try to make harm to anything of God's order. But because they're chained in Hell, they can only send their servants and minions to our world. They can also use their infernal powers due to which they spread the seed of sin among the people and thus hurt the Will of God.
And who are the Fallen Angels?

Fallen Angels are Arthamon, the Master of Ruination and Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Chaos and Madness, Cerdie, the Mistress of Fornication and of the Original Sin and Azrael, the Fallen Archangel, the first servant of Satan and the emissary of his will. Each of the Fallen Angels possesses unique infernal powers and with their help tries to destroy anything that was created by the God's Will—or thanks to the God's Will.
Do you think it's possible to bring the Fallen Angels to this world?
In the case the things described in Revelation of St. Ezekiel will come true it surely is!

The dead appearing in the streets of our city after dusk—this is a really dark and mysterious case, brother. And even more terrible is the fact that all those things have a corruptive effect on the city inhabitants, as they aren't used to living in the state of never-ending exposure to danger. They thought they'd be safe if they stayed within the city walls—away from the hellspawns raiding the woods and swamps. So when the living dead started to appear right in the streets of Glatzburg during the night, people panicked and long before dusk nobody dares show his face out of his door. On the other hand it's no wonder—in contrast to God's servants like us they don't perceive the jeopardy as a test in which we must hold out, but as another evil that affected them and can take their lives from them very quickly.
Maybe you're right, it's a test we were exposed to. However, I don't think anybody succeeded in the test—nobody has been able to deal with the undead yet...

Yes, unfortunately that's true. Nobody has been able to rid the city of the living dead—and I must say many tried to do so. Sheriff Contemburry used all the men he had to protect the city. But it was fruitless. Also my brothers and me looked for the enemy in the city every night and we slaughtered the undead like cattle in the slaughterhouse, but even that was ineffective. No matter how many we caught and killed during the night, all of them rose up again the next day. It's a futile fight. The only solution is to find the reason why they appear in the streets and burn this reason to the roots!
And don't you happen to know what this reason could be? Or maybe who?

No, brother, I'm afraid I don't. If I had any suspicion, surely I'd put this matter to its end. Now the only thing I can do is to watch with sadness in my eyes how one innocent man after another dies night after night...
I need to get Chateau de Trebrechette—it's an exquisite wine. Do you happen to know where I could get a few bottles?

I'm sorry, but I really won't help you with that. You can't expect me to help a knightly brother of mine with getting spirits. And if I can give you some good advice—stop your ungodly behavior, because nothing can be hidden from the sight of God and drinking is a sin!
No, the wine is not for me, of course...
This is what all people say to me, brother!
Well... yes, of course. You're right. Forget it.

Master Dieter von Gelbendiel from our Order is investigating the case of missing Raquel Gielwitch personally, so I'm not supposed to deal with the case in any way. However, to tell the truth, not only Raquel, but also several other young girls are missing. Very young girls, if you understand me, brother. So young that they doubtlessly were taintless virgins. In these times, when heresy is spreading out from every corner, godless people use virgin blood for various Black Sabbaths, pagan rituals, forgotten infernal rituals and witchlike goings-on. Because of that I personally think that whoever kidnapped the girl did so because he longed for her blood.
But that would mean, that...
Yes, exactly. That means the hope that those girls can be saved is negligible. Unfortunately. I wish with all my heart my conclusions were wrong...
As you wish, brother. However I must ask you whether you really thought well about your decision.
Yes, it's the final decision.
All right, farewell in that case, brother. If you need my services again in the future you'll find me in Glatzburg.
Well, you're right, brother. You had better stay with me. Forget about it.
I can guess what you think about me, brother. However I believe your prejudice against me won't hinder you in helping me in my holy mission, which is so similar to yours...
I can see a brave man devoted to his holy mission in front of me. You won't deny your help in the form of a single answer to your knightly brother, will you?
Maybe you're right, brother. Can I ask what you do for a living?

I'm fulfilling my holy mission, brother. I fight against injustice and subjection, because that's what I swore to do; that's where my lifes path leads. Whole neighborhoods of the city are infested by criminals who found shelter in dark underground holes and now they peer out like awful insects to destroy things and rob people. And they must be fairly punished for that!
Oh, really? In that case we have quite similar missions. What would you say if we combine our powers?
You mean to travel together and to fight all forms of evil?
Yes, I do. Or something like that...
What a great idea, brother! Two knights from the Brotherhood of the Righteous will be able to accomplish more than anyone else. I'm so glad God brought us together!
So am I, brother. Let's go.
On the other hand... maybe it wasn't such a good idea. Forget it.
The idea wasn't bad, brother. Two knights from the Brotherhood of the Righteous will be able to accomplish more than anyone else. If you change your mind, don't hesitate to approach me, brother!
All right, we'll see. Now I'd like to ask you several questions. Do you think I can waste your time for a moment?
Yes, I think such a waste is in accordance with God's order. Ask your questions, brother. What would you like to know?
You can rely on me. But I'll be going now, your mission surely makes you hurry. Farewell.
Farewell, brother. And God be with you.
It does credit to you. Could you interrupt your effort of setting the world right for a moment and answer several questions for me?
But of course, brother. I'll gladly contribute with my word to the success of your mission.
My mission? What do you know about my mission?
I don't know anything about your mission, but I suppose that as a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous you must have one, mustn't you?
Oh yes, sure.
Thus, ask your questions, brother. Time is passing quickly and injustice is spreading out from every corner.
I wish you a lot of luck in your effort, brother. I hope you'll catch and fairly punish as many brigands as man could find here. Farewell.

Thank you, brother! You'll see that with our forces combined we could oppose everything the forces of Hell will send to cross our way! However I can't leave unnoticed that there's a certain person traveling with you at the time. He doesn't seem to walk the way leading to the fulfillment of our holy mission. He seems much more like... landsknecht or maybe a wandering brigand.
You mean Olfghard, brother? It's true that his life isn't devoted to any holy mission, but his services have been fully satisfying till now.

I don't want to infirm your decision to use his services, nothing like that. However his... way of life is not acceptable for me. I'm a Knight of Brotherhood of the Righteous and I live only to fulfill my holy mission. This person here doesn't fulfill anything. Apparently he's a rover and rogue. If you really want to use my services, you must dismiss Olfghard first!
All right, brother. I'll dismiss Olfghard. I'm going to need your services much more than his.
I understand Olfghard isn't a man who raise a fair admiration in a Knight of Brotherhood of the Righteous. However, his services are useful. Could you overcome your indignation against him, brother?
I'm afraid I couldn't. My holy mission can't be violated by anything—and using services of a man who lives as an immoral sinner would be such a violation.
I'm sorry about that. Farewell.
I'm sorry, but Olfghard's services have been useful till now. I don't see any reason to dismiss him.

What a shame, brother. I hoped you'd understand my reasons. You're making a mistake when you rely on people like Olfghard in your holy mission. There is not a bit of honor in them and often also their faith could be successfully doubted. You take a risk he'll betray you sooner or later. Remember my words. However, if you change your mind, I'd always like to join you.

This is a great idea, brother! Two knights from the Brotherhood of the Righteous fighting alongside each other... However, if you really want to combine our powers, dismiss Hugo de Montesque, who accompanies you at the time, from your services. I don't know what this wicked person told you to gain your favor, but I must warn you not to trust him. A wild beast is hidden behind the mask of a true servant of God, which ignores the Commandments and follows goals that absolutely can't be called fulfilling a holy mission. He has tricked many people with his false mask, but I realized his true nature first when we served together during the novitiate. If I can give you a good advice, dismiss him, brother—it's not good to have such a man at your side. Dismiss him before it's too late. My sword is yours!
Your words are alarming. If it's really as you tell, I'd better dismiss Hugo de Montesque.
You made a good decision, brother. You'll see that my services will be of much greater use to you then the services of a person who violated his holy mission!
You don't like Hugo de Montesque too much, as I can see. However, his services are useful. Could you overcome your indignation against him, brother? Two swords are better than one.
I'm afraid I couldn't, brother. My holy mission can't be violated by anything—and combining powers with someone like Hugo de Montesque would be a sin. Dismiss him and my sword is yours!
I'm sorry, but I'm going to keep Hugo de Montesque for now.
Farewell in that case, brother. And God bless you!
I'm sorry, but the services of Knight Hugo de Montesque have been useful till now. I don't see any reason to dismiss him.

What a shame, brother. I hoped you'd take my advice to heart. You're making a mistake when you rely on people like Hugo de Montesque in your holy mission. Remember my words—you take a risk he'll betray you sooner or later! However, if you change your mind, I'd always like to offer you my services.

Thank you, brother! You'll see that with our combined forces we can oppose everything the powers of Hell will send to cross our path! But to tell the truth, I can't leave unnoticed that there's an inquisitor in your party. And he's an obstruction for me to join you—because of the fact the Holy Inquisition is trying to get rid of our Order I can't combine my powers with someone like him!
I understand your aversion to inquisitors, brother. But the services of Father Nicolas have been very helpful to me so far. Could you possibly overcome your grudge against him, brother?
I'm afraid I couldn't, brother. This obstacle is insurmountable for me. I can't have any objections to you, but I don't know Father Nicolas. Dismiss him and my sword is yours!
I'm sorry, but Father Nicolas will stay with me for now. Farewell.
I'm sorry, but the services of Father Nicolas have proven useful to me so far. I can't see any reason for dismissing him.

What a shame, brother. I hoped you'd understand my reasons. I can't fight alongside someone who might openly preach against the Brotherhood of the Righteous. However, if you change your mind, I'd always like to offer you my services.
Hail to God, hail to the King! Death to all enemies of true faith and of the Realm! Let the Beast die together with its false Prophet!
Could I know who am I honored to talk to?
Jacques de Pulein, Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. God bless our Order for ever!
It can be like that, brother. But who knows if there aren't falsehood and pretence hidden behind your words?!
How shall I understand that?

No offence, brother, but many of our brothers don't live as would beseem the Knights of God and they commit deeds of selfishness and sin. That is why my righteous anger turns against them as well as against all the others who offend God's order!
Yes, unfortunately that's true. I've experienced that too...
It's unimaginable... it's the utter end of all that has held our order together. We can't believe even one another anymore. But I hope we will succeed in reversing the unfavorable course of events!
But the same thing I could say about you!

I am afraid... you're right. I'd never think I'd be able to admit something like that, but contrary is the case. We can't trust even one another. But I hope we will succeed in reversing the unfavorable course of events!
I've heard of some conflicts between the Order and the Holy Office. What do you think about that?

What a disgusting plot against those who fight for the righteous cause! It's like a spit into the faces of those standing with swords in their hands at the bastion of faith, devoted to fight till the last breath! Politics is the most awful weapon of chaos worshippers and of minions of Hell whose powers taint the face of God's Kingdom on Earth like poisonous insects! It's necessary to crush them and trample them into the ground so they won't rise again. No matter where they belong. Those who spread ill will and feud must die in order to prevent them from doing harm in the flowering garden of the Kingdom of God on Earth!
Your words are wise, brother.
Those are words of wisdom, brother.
Now you talk mostly about our superiors, brother. They are the ones who deny the validity of the authority of the Holy Inquisition!

In that case I'm sure they have a good reason to do it! But on the other hand, I must say that I could not back up all the words and deeds of my superiors without asking God Almighty to forgive the sinners. However, it's not only the illness of my Order that those who have a holy mission forget their oaths and fall into the pettiness of profane life, or even into the deception of sinful life. Also in both the Holy Mother Church and the Holy Inquisition there're those who found out that the power entrusted to their hands can be used also as a tool of their personal welfare and thus as a tool of Satan!
Is there anybody particular in your mind, brother?

But of course! I have in mind all those who betrayed their holy missions—no matter what they were—and became the tools of Satan and succumbed to the temptations and seductions! It's exactly those depraved people I have in mind!
Well... what are you thinking about, brother?

What am I thinking about? I'm thinking about the fact that a thousand years passed by and the False Prophet, sent by the Beast itself from the entrails of Hell to the face of Kingdom of God on Earth, is walking our world to run down and destroy everything—nothing is sacred to him! I'm talking about the fact that soon he'll tempt all the Nations in the World to bow to the Beast!
Who is the Beast you're talking about? Satan?
But, brother! Hadn't you read the Scriptures? Because this is a part of the Revelations of St. Ezekiel!
These words are worthy of a devoted believer! Faith is so seldom found these days...

Yes, it is... and my heart is crying, when I think about it. Gone are the times when faith and justice ruled the world. Gone are the times when people gathered in churches for the mass and praised our Lord. Gone are the times people were frank and faithful to the sacrament of christening! Sins and falsehood sneaked into the hearts of many people and they walk the world with lack of faith, dressed in the robes of false righteousness!
Hail to God, hail to the King!
God protect the King!
Hail to you, brother. How do you do?
Not bad, but I believe it could be even better, brother. Do you think I won't hold you up for too long if I ask you a few questions for which I seek answers?
No, brother, I believe you won't hold me up at all—in the case you'll be briefer than a wandering minstrel.
I want to ask you, brother, whether you don't want to combine your powers with mine. At least for some time, before you'll find out that your holy mission leads you another way than mine leads me.

Yes, I think it would be possible. Both of us fight for the same thing, although each of us uses his own ways and fights together with different comrades. All right, let our steps go alongside from now on and let our enemies are enemies of both of us.
Thank you, brother. I wish you success in your mission. Farewell.
Fare thee well, brother. And God be with you!
Hail to you, brother. How are you? I hope you still carry the heavy burden of your holy mission with pride. Is there something I could do for you?
Yes, there is, brother. I'd appreciate if you answered a few questions for me.
Well, ask your questions. If my answers help you in your holy mission, it's not a waste of time!
Yes, there is, brother. I wanted to ask you to join me again. Your services would be more than welcome.
All right, I accept your offer. Let our steps go alongside again and let our holy missions be missions of both of us!
Nothing at the moment, brother. Farewell.

I can't leave unnoticed that there's a certain person traveling with you at the time. He doesn't seem to walk the way leading to the fulfillment of our holy mission. He seems much more like... landsknecht or maybe a wandering brigand.

I can't leave unnoticed that there's Hugo de Montesque traveling with you at the time. I don't know what this wicked person told you to gain your favor, but I must warn you not to trust him. A wild beast is hidden behind the mask of a true servant of God, which ignores the Commandments and follows his own goals. If I can give you a good advice, dismiss him and my sword is yours!

I can't leave unnoticed that there's a priest in your party. I trust you, because I can see deep into your heart. But I don't trust him. And because of the fact the Holy Inquisition is trying to get rid of our Order I can't combine my powers with somebody like him!

A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! You shocked me by trying that, brother. There's no excuse for it. I hope you regret having done such a shameful thing and that you're going to confess on the nearest occasion and pray to God for forgiveness! Or else I will take care of that myself!
What do you think about the present crisis the Realm has been dragged into, sir knight?
Do you really want to know the truth, Father? Do you really want to know what I think about the current crisis?

But I don't mind telling you, Father. I think that what we're facing here is the total and irreversible end! It's a decay of all what seemed to be strong and stout till now. The faith is ruined, the Realm is falling apart, dark times will soon rule the day! God punished us for our sins and put us on a trial. Forever, amen!

Did you know that your Master became a victim of dark powers? Someone bewitched him, there's no doubt about it.

The Monstrance of St. Orthenius is said to be missing from Hillbrandt. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Well, I don't want to make any harm to anyone, knight, but I saw something. The night the Monstrance disappeared I went around the town church by chance. Well... in fact I felt asleep there—near the graveyard wall—on the way home from the tavern. I woke up in the middle of the night. I just came to the decision that I should better go home when I briefly saw the priest Romius coming out of the church. It was pretty strange, because the church is closed during the night and nobody is allowed in or out—even the clerics aren't allowed to go as they will. And even more strange was that there was something visibly hidden under his frock. He also looked in all directions as if he was afraid somebody would see him. But nobody was there—that is, except for me.
Well... that's interesting. Are you sure it really was as you told me? You said you were drunk...
Drunk? Yes, drunk I was, that's true. But I know what I saw, knight.
Are you sure the person was the priest Romius?
Yes, knight, I am. He had a small lamp with him to light the way. Because it was pitch dark...
Did you see what was he hiding under his robe?
No, knight, unfortunately not. But he held it quite forcefully—it must have been something very valuable, so it pretty well could have been the Monstrance of St. Orthenius.
Not at all, knight. Maybe it will help you somehow...
Where could I buy some goods here in Hillbrandt?

Where could you buy some goods here? Well... it depends on what's on your mind. Weapons and such? In that case Victor Hammerhand the blacksmith will surely help you. Or you mean potions and various magic things? In that case go to Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist, Theil Brechthold the stargazer or to Father Dominic. And you can also buy any goods from Joseph Truthorn the innkeeper or from Suzan Brauchner the stallholder, or sell it to them as well.

And then suddenly, everything lied ruined in one moment. Even here in Hillbrandt people are driven to gloom and despair, and I would never thought it possible before. Nobody believes too much that good times will return—me neither.

There are various monsters here, knight. Personally I'm most afraid of orcs. Have you heard about them? Sure you have—there are plenty of them around here. Orcs are the very same green skins about which the tales are told. Monsters from the ancient times when pagan gods walked the Earth. Nobody knows how it's possible that the orcs appeared here. Someone must have summoned them, otherwise it'd be impossible. They appeared in the depths of the iron ore mines in the Moonshine Mountains and during one bloody night they killed all the miners and their families living in the nearby village of Asherbalt. Since that time the orcs have been going out on the robbing forays and smoke is coming out from the iron mines like if it was a hole to Hell itself. God knows what atrocities are those hellspawns committing there.

Do I suspect anyone of heresy? Well... I'm not sure, knight, whether I should even tell you about it, but it seems to me... that Duke Weinberg is somehow too quiet and satisfied about what happened here during last several years. To tell the truth, Scourges of God didn't affect him at all. He lives alone and thus he didn't lose anybody dear and near due to the Black Death. He has money and rich supplies, so he went through the famine without even noticing it. And the rain of fire bypass his property in a wide curve. One can't help thinking about how it's possible... But as I said, I don't want to cause any harm to the Duke, God knows I don't...

Because I'm the attendant of the Master Executioner, my duties often bring me to the city cemetery. The gravedigger died last year due to the Black Death and since that time the dead have been buried by anybody who needed to do so. I was put in charge of burying of those who hadn't any relatives and the Church didn't arrange their burial. So I went quite often to the town cemetery. But I don't go there any more.
Can you tell me why?

The place is crawling with living dead, knight. The dead are coming out of their graves all the time to wander around. And he who gets into their hands is torn to pieces. It's really dreadful—they're said to be half alive and half dead. They remember something from their lives, but are driven by restless need to kill. So you should be better careful about them, knight. People in the town believe that former Bishop Herbertius caused the entire ruckus. Have you heard about him, knight?

He was a diocese Bishop here before Father Quentinus. But nobody liked him much. It seems that people were afraid of him and told really unpleasant tales about him. Especially at the end of his life the people said he sold his soul to Satan in exchange for awful delights and forgiven pleasures he was given. In that time young girls started to be missing and after some time also young boys were kidnapped. From time to time someone found a mutilated body somewhere far from the town.

But no matter what the truth was, one day the Bishop was found dead in his bed. He was buried and people thought both them and he would have the peace forever. But now there's a rumor going around that Herbertius returned from the Other World and that he's lurking around the town to look out for new victims. He's said to come to fulfill his part of the pact with Satan.

It's hard to say what one should think about that suspicion of Master Edmond d'Arvias, knight. I always believed Master Edmond d'Arvias is a fair and honest man. But now I'm not so sure about it. I don't want to say he did what he is said to do. I don't know about it. But I want to say that we live in times when one can't be sure about even the simplest truths.
Do you know anything about the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus?

I don't know much about kidnapping of Bishop Quentinus, knight. I wasn't in the town that night so I can't help you. But I've heard Flitz the beggar was talking about something he saw, so you can try asking him. In the case you would have to give him some gold, of course...
I don't have the slightest idea where Paul Hammerhand could be. I'm sorry. Probably he again escaped somewhere and now works on some dirty tricks—no doubt as it wouldn't be for the first time!

The murder of Natalia must be a terrible thing for old Reichmann. Moreover when Olfghard succeeded to escape from the prison, he was so angry that he couldn't breathe when he yelled at Sheriff Contemburry. He told the Sheriff was incompetent and said that he'll pay a nice reward to a person who will bring him Olfghard's head.

I don't have the slightest idea where the soldier Jullian could be hiding, knight. I'm sorry. Probably he's already on his way to the East, maybe to Glatzburg. What would he wait here in Hillbrandt for? The rope?

The murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier? Well, it was a terrible murder, that's true. I didn't see it with my own eyes, but the people say he was cut like a piglet. In Truthorn's tavern, in the attic room he rented. And I've also heard they cut his cock off and stuffed it into his mouth. What a disgusting deed, valiant knight. One should be scared what terrible things could happen to him. But on the other hand, no wonder Ollmier ended like that. That is to say, he traded things you couldn't get easily on the market. Various residues from pagan times, strange artifacts and relics, maybe even some heretic goods... the devil knows what he took money for. Such a man can't end well.

Duke Weinberg rules in Hillbrandt as the royal governor of the town. Robert van Gallagan is the royal vice-governor. But as for Baron van Gallagan, it's hard to talk about ruling, because his wife Linda does all the decisions for him...
Answer me immediately, you scrub, or I'll order to put you on the rack!
Maybe you don't like me, Quarim; there's nothing I can do about it. But I assure you your answer will help a right cause. Please answer my question.
I'm sure you're very clever, Quarim. Clever and wise. So why don't you want to answer me?
Hello, hello, knight. I heard you had come to town. What happened? The Brotherhood of the Righteous strengthtens its numbers? Or is there open war looming between the Church and the Brotherhood?
Who I am? He he, that's a question. Everybody knows me here. I'm Quarim, Executioner's assistant. I learn the job from my Master, the Executioner Friedrich Raubsticht.
Of course you can, knight. I've so few opportunities to talk to somebody. All the people here think I'm a lousy cripple...

You're leaving already? But you just came here before a moment, knight... I thought we could talk to each other a little. Nobody here talks to me much, you know? All people here hate me and think I'm a lousy cripple...
Well, in fact there're a few things I'd like to ask you about, when I'm here.
Excellent, knight! What would you like to know? I'll tell you all I know...
I'm sorry, but I don't have time to talk to you. Farewell.
Watch your tongue, you scum. You don't know how dangerous is the fire you're playing with.

I don't think so. Death is always close to somebody like me and man gets to be used to it during the time, knight. In addition to that I don't think I offended you somehow or said something wrong. But I'm not surprised you're offended. Nobody likes me here so why should exactly you treat me better than the others? I'm just a cripple, scum, poor wretch or a lousy dog for anybody. Only my Master likes me. And keeps a protective hand above me.
Don't be afraid, all is going well. I came to investigate the crimes perpetrated here in Hillbrand.

I'm glad to hear that. It would be very good if all those awful crimes were cleared up as soon as possible. The idea that there are people among us who are really aiming at out lives makes me nervous. Damned heretics, may Black Death and pox get them.
What does bring you to me, knight? Do you long for my company?
Hail to you. Could I talk to you?
It depends on what you want to talk about...
Well... knight... It seems to me you have just looked into my pocket. I don't think you have the right to do that. You should better not try to do it again or I'll call the guards, all right?

Well, I don't want to make any harm to anyone, Father, but I saw something. The night the Monstrance disappeared I went around the town church by chance. Well... in fact I felt asleep there—near the graveyard wall—on the way home from the tavern. I woke up in the middle of the night. I just came to the decision that I should better go home when I briefly saw the priest Romius coming out of the church. It was pretty strange, because the church is closed during the night and nobody is allowed in or out—even the clerics aren't allowed to go as they will. And even more strange was that there was something visibly hidden under his frock. He also looked in all directions as if he was afraid somebody would see him. But nobody was there—that is, except for me.
Drunk? Yes, drunk I was, that's true. But I know what I saw, Father.
Yes, Father, I am. He had a small lamp with him to light the way. Because it was pitch dark...
No, Father, unfortunately not. But he held it quite forcefully—it must have been something very valuable, so it pretty well could have been the Monstrance of St. Orthenius.
Not at all, Father. Maybe it will help you somehow...

I'm glad to hear that. It would be very good if all get into the groove. I wish those awful crimes that have been perpetrated here in Hillbrandt lately were cleared as soon as possible.
