What does bring you to me, noble sir? Do you long for my company?
Well... noble sir... It seems to me you have just looked into my pocket. I don't think you have the right to do that. You should better not try to do it again or I'll call the guards, all right?
Could you tell me once more about your kidnapping?

It happened the night when those orcish demons attacked the town. I was in the church at the moment, absorbed in night prayers, and I heard the sound of fighting from the town. Immediately I figured out the hellspawns attacked the town so I hurried up to face them. But before I got to the church door, the door opened and there was a bunch of green skins there. They savagely charged at me, but I succeeded to destroy all of them before they could touch me with their dirty hands. But there were those wicked warlocks with them. They attacked me with some damned spells I wasn't able to resist long. The last thing I remember was a bunch of those bloodthirsty monsters attacking me and carrying me somewhere to the darkness. Then I awoke deep in their underground lair.
I brought that dead girl, Monsignor. Could you look at her?

Baroness Linda van Gallagan confessed all her sins before she died, Father. She testified that she committed all her awful crimes with a single goal—to accomplish a certain heretic Sabbath, during which the Fallen Angel Arthamon should have been summoned according to her words...
That's crazy! I suspected Baroness to be involved in terrible crimes, but I'd never expect something like that... You say she performed a ritual and invoked the Fallen Angel Arthamon during it?
Yes, exactly, Monsignor. But that's not all she said. She testified that the plotter of the whole crime was Judge Vallarian!

What? That sinful soul dared to accuse our good Judge Vallarian of heresy? This is inaudible... How could she do something like that? Father Vallarian is an Inquisitorial Judge and a Bishop of the Holy Mother Church. It's clear Baroness tried to blemish him and fault her own blame for her crimes on him! It's terrible what the heretics are able to do at these bad times! How did Baroness van Gallagan die in fact?

It's hard to say, Monsignor. She approached me voluntarily, probably she was afraid about her life. And during the confession she suddenly collapsed and died in horrible pains. Probably she was poisoned...

Oh, really? Well... that's bewildering. It seems that her own heretic comrades got rid of her. But why should she try to blemish the name of Judge Vallarian? This is very strange, my son. You should pay much more attention to this case!
What can you tell me about the death of the merchant Kurth Ollmier?

Oh yes, that was a terrible case. Kurth Ollmier was quite a strange person. He called himself a merchant, but nobody knew exactly what was he dealing in. He didn't spend much time in Hillbrandt; usually he was traveling. People said he was searching for ruins of ancient pagan settlements and then that he was selling the artifacts he found there for high prices to people who were interested in them. And there were more than enough such people—at least according to the income of money that the merchant evidently had.
Who do you think could have killed him?

I don't have the slightest idea, my son. Maybe it was just a robbery. But I wouldn't believe it too much. Maybe he died by the hand of some demon he set against himself because of his ill-considered deeds, but I also wouldn't believe it too much. I'd rather say it was a result of his unfortunate business. Maybe some unsatisfied buyer. Or somebody wanted to silence him. Who knows?

I arrested Sam Riemann on the basis of the testimony of Baroness Linda van Gallagan. When tortured, he confessed to all that the Baroness testified. That he prepared a heretic mass together with her during which the Fallen Angel Arthamon was reputedly summoned. What do you think about it, Monsignor?

I'm very concerned, my son. Those talks about summoning of the Fallen Angel Arthamon seemed to be pure madness at the beginning, but now we have a second testimony here confirming that. But I hesitate to believe it anyway! The Fallen Angels can't be summoned to our world! Sam Riemann had to lie—as well as Baroness van Gallagan lied. Another explanation doesn't exist!
And do you think, Monsignor, that Sam Riemann lied also about the fact Judge Vallarian was the plotter of the crime?

What? Sam Riemann claimed that Judge Vallarian prepared the crime? I have nothing to say, my son! That's awful! That's exactly what Baroness van Gallagan told you... You say Sam Riemann confessed it during the interrogation? That's really shocking... It's clear we have a large plot against Judge Vallarian here. I wish we were able to find out who's behind that plot... and how he was able to bewitch the others to declare Judge Vallarian to be the main planner of the crime.
I decided to accuse Judge Vallarian of heresy, Monsignor.

You decided to... what, my son? You don't really mean it, do you? I don't understand it. Judge Vallarian is the highest representative of the Holy Inquisition here in Hillbrandt; and you want to accuse him of heresy? That's total nonsense. I don't know where you got proofs for such an accusation, but I believe those proofs are false. You should change your mind before it's too late. It isn't a good idea to antagonize an Inquisitorial Judge delegated with the power of a curial inquisitor.
I accused Judge Vallarian of heresy, Monsignor.
I can see I didn't entice you not to do so. I hope the truth will be revealed soon. It's not good when there are any doubts about purity of the Inquisition.

Judge Vallarian confessed to all his crimes, Monsignor. If he tells the truth, the invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon really was his idea. And according to his words he really succeed to do so...

Unbelievable! I don't want to believe it's true. Judge Vallarian is a heretic? Good Heavens... Excuse me, my son, for not trusting you in the beginning. I'd never think that... somebody like Bishop Vallarian could do it. He was an Inquisitorial Judge! What times are we living in...
What do you think about the betrayal of Judge Vallarian, Monsignor?

It's a tragedy, my son. Such a distinguished representative of the Holy Inquisition... When the heretics were able to get so high in the Holy Office, how could we be sure about its true mission? If there were more such cases... I better don't want to think about it. We must oppose such people, my son. We must reveal the heretics and destroy them before they destroy us!
What do you know about Bishop Trevorius, Monsignor?

He's the Bishop of Glatzburg Diocese. It means that he's the highest representative of the Holy Mother Church in the whole Glatzburg diocese. From time to time we visit each other—or we used to do so before the Scourges of God stroke us. Now we have more than enough of our own troubles. However, all the time I've known him he seemed to me to be a man in the right place. Although a bit reserved, he's reasonable, well, sometimes he's stiff and stubborn, but he has great knowledge of faith and of politics.
What do you think about the current crisis that has affected our Realm, Monsignor?

I'm scared, my son. Cold hand of fear grips my heart, as I fear for the fate of our Realm and all of us. What we are facing is more than a common insurgence of confused heretics. You can almost feel the presence of evil. The Star of Doom, the Scourges of God, infernal beings around us... Something is happening, my son, and we don't know what it could be. We must find the source of all the evil and destroy it before it's too late. I've never seen the people from my diocese so terrified. They're drowning in despair, I can see it in their eyes. They used to be hard and firm, and now they experience feelings they never knew before. Only few of them really believe good times will return again. Thus, we must do all we can to change it.
Did something uncommon happen in Hillbrandt before you were kidnapped, Monsignor?

More things happened than you can imagine. But most terrifying was the storm which drifted over Hillbrandt one night some time ago. I felt some concern that evening before that terrible storm came. I knew something very bad was going to happen, but when a strong wind started to blow during the night and soon it became a tempest, I figured out something especially terrible was happening. I've been living in Hillbrandt for twenty years and I can tell with certainty that nobody here remembered such a storm. Some people even mentioned they saw demons dancing in the sky. I didn't see anything like that, because I was absorbed in prayers for the salvation of our town, but maybe I'd believe that.
How is that possible, Monsignor? What happened?

The tempest was worse every moment and torn to pieces everything it ran into. One lightning followed the other, as if the sky itself should collapse to the Earth and bury all of us under it. But what alarmed me were those voices. They were whispering and were hardly to be heard in the howling tempest. Voices that yelled and croaked like a thousand hellspawns. And voices that blamed the name of God and shamelessly tempted to commit sins. I don't know what kind of a terrible phenomenon that was, or whether it was a harbinger of something foul, but since then everything's been quickly turning worse. The orcs appeared, the dead came out of their graves, bunches of ogres and trolls came down from the mountains... God protect us from all the evil.
Master Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of heresy. What do you think about it, monsignor?

That's an absurd and nonsensical accusation, my son. I know Master Edmond d'Arvias very well and I'm firmly convinced about the purity of his mind and of his soul. I know Judge Vallarian is led by high-hearted thoughts and the proofs against Master seem to speak clearly, but it's obvious that this is nothing else but an attempt of hellspawns and of their heretic minions to get rid of Master d'Arvias. I also felt into their hands and without your help, my son, I'd have surely perished in the orcish prison.
Can you tell me once more what do you think about the confession of Sam Riemann and about the accusation of Judge Vallarian of the heresy?

It's clear there's a plot against Judge Vallarian here, my son. I don't know which mad mind came with that idea, but it's sure that both Baroness Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann acted with the aim to blemish good name of Judge Vallarian, or even the name of the whole Inquisition! We must find out as soon as possible who brought those two godless creatures to this idea and who made them to insist on their lie even when facing their death!
The Monstrance of St. Orthenius is said to be missing, Monsignor. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Unfortunately I don't have the slightest idea who could have committed such a terrible crime, my son. And I'm very unhappy about that. That nasty godless wretch who stole it must have been in a league with dark powers—or he was a hellspawn himself. Our brothers clerics who stayed in the church that night absorbed in prayers were found in the morning sleeping in a deep unholy rest and we were nearly unable to wake them up. Without the Monstrance of St. Orthenius our town is exposed to the attack of any enemy. Even that damned attack of the orcs at the town took place just after the Monstrance disappeared!
So you think these things are connected to each other?
I don't know, my son. It's possible, but it's not sure. There are several possible explanations here, each rotten to the core...
Do you happen to know anything about missing Paul Hammerhand?

I've heard the boy is missing. Probably he ran away from his home. It has happened several times before, if I remember well. He's a very naughty child. He opposes his father's authority, lies, runs from home, doesn't go to masses, the less to the confessions. I'm really afraid about him. How can a young human being tempted to idleness and heterodoxy face the temptation of Satan when he becomes adult? But I believe firmly I'll be able to amend him. Unfortunately I don't have any news about his whereabouts.
What do you think about the alleged murder of Natalia Reichmann that is said to had been committed by the landsknecht Olfghard, Monsignor?

That's a terrible case. I knew Natalia since she was born—it was me who baptized her. It seems to me as if it was yesterday. I saw her growing up, I absolved her after confessions and I believed firmly she would stand before the altar one day and I'd bless her marriage. But now she's away forever. It's really terrible that her life was wasted like that. And her murderer is free! I wish I could do something in that matter.
I found a case of bewitchment here in Hillbrandt, Monsignor. Do you happen to know how to dispel it?

Bewitchment you say, my son? That's really horrible... But on the other hand, I can't say I'm surprised much—after all those things that happened here in Hillbrandt. However, unfortunately I don't have any experience with that kind of dark power. Try asking Father Dominicus, he's the best healer in my diocese. And in case he doesn't have any advice for you, try asking Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist—but remember that her mood is as changeable as the spring weather.

Among the people, the legend of St. Orthenius is told now much more often then it used to be before. The people say that when the hardest time will strike the Realm, a new protector of the Realm will be found among the people, and he will defeat all who oppose the true faith—as well as St. Orthenius defeated the armies of the pagan realm Ereborn in 223 and thus he set our Filkland Peninsula free of many hundred years long dominion and brought the opportunity to freely worship God the Messiah to the people. Before St. Orthenius died several years later, he predicted that a new protector of the true faith would come in the time of the greatest need to defeat all the offenders and enemies. Common people hope the time has just come; because of that which affected our Realm during the last several years.
I found a place near the Dragon Rock where that witchlike Sabbath Baroness van Gallagan talked about probably took place.
Oh, really? Why do you think so, my son? Describe me the place.

I found some remnants of the blood-painted circle there on the ground and in the middle of the circle there was a young girl's body in an advanced stage of decay. It's highly probable it was Baroness Gwenn von Weill.
Terrible... I haven't heard anything so terrible in my whole life. We must inspect the body at all costs... maybe it'll help us reveal some more information about what happened at that place.
I've the body here, Monsignor. I thought I should better take it with me.
All right, I'll bring you the body.
Excellent, my son!
I found a place near the Dragon Rock—it's quite probable a witch Sabbath was held there, monsignor.
I found remnants of a ritual circle painted with blood there and in the middle of it there was lying a dead girl's body—it was in a advanced stage of decay.
All right, I'll bring it.
What do you know about the Fallen Angel Arthamon, Monsignor?

Quiet, my son...! Names like this should better not be pronounced aloud! Well, Arthamon is one of the Fallen Angels, who were together with Satan thrown down from the sky for their crimes against God. According to the Scriptures all of them have been chained in Hell since their fall, in the prison of Earth, as well as souls of all those who were damned by God's trial. They mustn't return from where they were banished, so they try to get to our world and to come to control it with their vicious powers. Arthamon is the symbol of total ruination, nonentity, complete destruction and of the non-existence of everything. He's called the Master of Ruination and the Ruler of Hellfire. According to the Scriptures he has plenty of minions among the awful pantheon of demonic creatures, as well as of the harbingers of his godless destructive powers.
And do you think it's possible that the heretics could have summoned the Fallen Angel Arthamon?

No, my son, it's definitely impossible. The Fallen Angels can't enter the God's Kingdom on Earth, because the Will of God prevents them from doing so. Our entire world would have to be on its way to Hell to let something like that be possible. No, it's not possible at all! I don't know whom—or what—the heretics really summoned, but surely it couldn't be the Fallen Angel Arthamon. Maybe they invoked some of the lower hellspawns and they thought it was Arthamon...
Can you tell me once more what do you know about the Fallen Angel Arthamon, Monsignor?

As you wish, my son. Arthamon is one of the Fallen Angels, who were together with Satan thrown down from the sky for their crimes against God. According to the Scriptures all of them are chained in Hell since their fall, in the jail of Earth, as well as the souls of all those who were damned at the God's trial. They mustn't return from where they were banished, so they try to get to our world and to come to control it with their vicious powers. Arthamon is a symbol of total ruination, nonentity, complete destruction and of the non-existence of everything. He's called the Master of Ruination and the Ruler of Hellfire. According to the Scriptures he has plenty of minions among the awful pantheon of demonic creatures, as well as of the harbingers of his godless destructive powers.
Excellent, my son. In that case we'll start the work immediately. It won't be pleasant, but there's nothing we can do about it. The service to God exposes us to difficult tests sometimes...

All right, put the body here on the bench. Excellent. Let's look at it. Well... despite the advanced stage of decay I can state this is the body of young Baroness Gwenn von Weill who died here in Hillbrandt some time ago. I personally held a requiem for her. I knew well that her body disappeared from the grave several days after it was buried, because I witnessed a group of heretics led by Baroness Linda van Gallagan carrying it away one night.

If I can say, she was a virgin at the time of ritual performance, or at least all seems that she was. I don't see any signs of concision on her body except the ruptured abdomen and the split chest. It seems like the cut in the chest was done by a sharp tool, because the edges of the wound are straight and non-tattered. On the contrary, the abdomen was torn by some blunt thing. But it's strange, because it seems as if the wounds were caused not from outside, but from inside. Well... it's really strange!

Let's look at the viscera. It seem that nothing is missing... All is where it should be—lungs, stomach, bowels, liver... Come here, son, hold this for me... What's the matter, son, are you feeling well? Yes, you are. Excellent, let's go on. Really, I can see all the viscera. Here's the spleen, kidneys... But wait a moment, what's this?
What do you see there, Monsignor?

Someone cut the heart of the girl, Father. The whole heart is missing. And instead of it there's... Oh my God... It looks like a shell of some large egg. The shell of rich black color... I've never seen anything like that! What a wicked devilment was that? What infernal ritual did they perform with that poor girl?
What do you conclude from it, Monsignor? What are the results?

I... don't want to make a mistake, but according to all I see here it seems that... God forgive me... something hatched from the girl during the ritual! And with the highest probability it emerged from the black egg of which we found the shell here. It can't mean anything good, my son. Although I'm not an expert in heretic rituals, I have a feeling that some hellspawn was really summoned during that Black Mass near the Dragon Rock. But I'm unable to tell what kind of hellspawn was invoked.
Thank you, Monsignor. Your knowledge is a great asset to me.

You are welcome, my son. If I were you, I'd focus my further investigations on finding out which hell forces were summoned there. Because it's clear now that what we're facing here is a group of heretics much more powerful than common quacks we were used to here in Hillbrandt...
Yes, you're right monsignor. If you excuse me, I'll prepare for the journey to Glatzburg now.

Excellent idea, my son. However, if I can give you good advice, remember that Glatzburg is very different from Hillbrandt. It's the second largest city in the Realm and although it wasn't spared from the Scourges of God, still it's a very large city in comparison to Hillbrandt. Thus, be careful, because you'll be surely exposed to thousands of temptations there. But you mustn't stray from your path, do you understand?
No need to be afraid for me, Monsignor. Farewell.
Do you have another advice for me?
No, my son. It seems to me you gained a lot of experience during the short time you spent here in Hillbrandt to be successful in Glatzburg too. Good luck to you!

Thanks to God, I'm saved! At least I'll be able to regenerate my magic abilities with the help of this potion and to return back to the town. Thank you, my son. God is my witness that you saved my life. You must come to see me when you return to Hillbrandt!
As you wish, monsignor.

I besiege you, help me to get out of here, my son. The only thing you have to do is to bring me a mana potion. I'll be able to get back to the town by the means of my magic abilities. Just bring me the potion, please. There's so much I have to do...
All right, I'll bring you the potion.
As I've already told you, I've other things to do. Farewell.
No doubt I'll do that, Monsignor. No need to be afraid. The truth will be revealed.
God bless you, my son. I'm sure you'll succeed in the end. Thank you again for saving my life. I wish I could do something for you in return... At least take this item as an expression of my thanks!
Thank you, Monsignor. And could I ask you a few questions?
Of course you could, my son! Ask questions about anything you want—I'll gladly answer all your questions.
Thank you, Monsignor. And now excuse me, please, I must carry on in my holy mission.

Hush... the orcs can be here any moment! Listen carefully, my son. My name is Quentinus and I'm a Bishop in Hillbrandt diocese. I was kidnapped by the orcs during the attack at the town. I don't even know how long I've been here... They tortured me, tried to break me, but they didn't succeed. I'm only tired to death. Please, bring me a mana potion to let me get away from here. Tired like this I can't focus my mind even on a simple spell. I must get out of here... There's so much I have to do... Please, help me!
Of course I'll help you, Monsignor. I won't turn you adrift to those monsters. I'll bring you what you asked me for.
Thanks to God you found me here... Without you those green skins would surely torture me to death... Please, bring me that potion so I could get back to the town. God bless you.
I'll save you, monsignor. But first you have to tell me what you'll give me for it.

I don't understand you, my son. You're trying to haggle with a man in need? With a man threatened by death from the hands of those damned monsters? I hope you told it just for fun, although I think your sense of humor is grossly impertinent...
I'm sorry, monsignor, but I've no time to help you. I'm on an important mission.
I have one such potion, Monsignor. Here you are.
I'm glad I found you, Monsignor. Father Dominicus asked me to look for you. I'll get the potion for you.
Thanks to God my faithful Dominicus believed so firmly I'm still alive. Thank you for your help, my son. Bring me the mana potion so I can get back to town. There's so much I have to do...
I'm glad I found you, monsignor. Father Dominicus asked me to look for you. Here is the potion you asked for.
So Father Dominicus was right when he believed you're still alive...

You talked to my faithful Dominicus? He's very devoted to his holy mission... I'm not surprised he believed firmly I'm still alive... Please, my son, bring me the mana potion so I can get back to the town. There's so much I have to do...
All right, I'll bring you the potion, Monsignor. You can rely on me.
I'm sorry, Monsignor. I don't have time to help you.
So Father Dominicus was right when he believed you're still alive... Here is the mana potion, Monsignor. I'm glad I was able to help you.
You don't have to be afraid of the orcs so much now, Monsignor. I killed their Khan Rashgar and a large group of his infernal minions.

You really did? So you must have been sent to me by Gracious Heaven itself. I didn't have the slightest idea such a hero would be found in these dark times who'd set on a way to the heart of the orcish caverns to fight there the leader of those devilish creatures. You have my deep admiration, son. However... please bring me the potion I asked you for. You can believe me that I'd find my way to the town on my own under different circumstances, but now I'm tired to death.
I'm sorry, but I can't do anything else for you, Monsignor. Farewell.
Here you are, Monsignor.
Do you bring the potion to me, son? It's only a matter of time before the orcs will come for me again...
Not yet, Monsignor.
In that case you should better hurry, my son. I don't want to urge you, but you can believe me nothing good awaits me in these infernal cells. If the orcs came for me again...
I besiege you, help me to get out of this terrible place. Bring me the mana potion. There's so much I have to do. And the orcs can come for me anytime...
All right, I'll bring you the potion, Monsignor.
Thanks to God! I knew you wouldn't leave me here...

I'm so glad you're back, my son. I already started to be afraid something happened to you. Although I knew the Archangel Gabriel protects you after all you've done already, I admit I was in a great fear. Only thanks to your help I can return to my duties here in Hillbrandt diocese. But now there's something of grave importance I have to talk to you about. I have some information about you and I trust you a lot. I want to talk to you about the circumstances of my kidnapping...
I'm listening, Monsignor.
If I knew who you really were, I'd have told you already in the orc prison. The matter is that I know pretty well why I was kidnapped and who ordered it!

It's just as I say! My kidnapping was an attempt to shut my mouth up, so I wouldn't be able to reveal before the Inquisition trial what I have witnessed! One night I caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan together with several other heretics carrying the dead body of buried Baroness Gwenn von Weill away from the town cemetery. You should have seen, my son, what nasty things the Baroness did during that crime! No doubt the woman is rotten to the core, full of sin and deviation! Only God knows what other crimes can that heretic have on her conscience... Heavens save us from such people!
Amen. And what happened after that?

I suppose that if I kept my witness for myself, nothing would have happened. But of course I didn't do anything of that kind. I told about it to my friend, Master Edmond d'Arvias, the superior of the local Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, and of course he started to investigate the whole matter immediately. And of course I reported all the facts to Judge Vallarian as to a representative of the Holy Office. And immediately after that I was kidnapped by the orcs during their unexpected attack at the town! Because of that I firmly believe my kidnapping was arranged by the very Baroness van Gallagan and her heretic comrades who were afraid of disclosure!
Yes, that's exactly what Master Edmond d'Arvias is saying... But I'm sure you noticed he's suspected of heresy and of high treason.

Yes, I couldn't left that unnoticed. Yes, I've already talked about it with Judge Vallarian and tried to convince him to stop the proceedings against Master d'Arvias. I wasn't successful, but no doubt the truth will reveal itself in the end and Edmond d'Arvias will be acquitted of that nonsensical accusation. That's one of the things I wanted to talk to you about. I've heard you're very talented, and so I hope you'll take care of the whole matter. You must reveal what a terrible secret is Baroness Linda van Gallagan hiding and who her accomplices are!
That is a very daring accusation, Monsignor. Are you sure it really was Baroness Linda van Gallagan?
Yes, I'm completely sure about it. There's no doubt it was her. Well, it was a dark night, but I know her voice more than well from the confessional!
We'll see, Monsignor. Of course I'll investigate your testimony.

Yes, do it, my son! And if I can give you a good advice, you should also find Master Edmond d'Arvias. I couldn't left unnoticed that he was proclaimed suspicious of heresy and high treason when I wasn't here. That's absolutely nonsensical! I've already talked about it with Judge Vallarian and tried to convince him to stop the proceedings against Master d'Arvias. I wasn't successful, but no doubt the truth will reveal itself in the end and Edmond d'Arvias will be acquitted of all the accusations. Seek him out and try to find out what he uncovered during his investigation. And be careful, my son—the heretics can be lurking everywhere around you!
Hail to you, my son. I'm glad to see you again. Is there something I could do for you?
I'd like to talk to you, Monsignor. If it's possible, of course.
But of course, my son. I'll gladly answer all your questions.
Nothing this time, Monsignor. Farewell.

I hadn't the slightest idea until today how far the heretics could have had gone, my son! I'd never think that the coquetry of godless people and of heretics with the powers of Hell could achieve so terrible and monstrous levels! They tried to summon the Fallen Angel Arthamon... God protect us! I firmly believe it was just an idea of mad minds, who believed to that heterodoxy and really thought they would be able to invoke the Fallen Angel Arthamon, but in fact they weren't. However we can't be not sure...
What do you suggest, Monsignor?

I'd like to ask you, my son, to find out if some of those rumors are true. I want you to disconfirm those lies about the Fallen Angel Arthamon before they make more harm than the Fallen Angel himself!
All right, Monsignor, I'll take care of it.
Excellent, my son. I knew you won't disappoint me!

It's really terrible what happened here in Hillbrandt. I'd never think that such a highly positioned member of the Holy Office could be a heretic involved in such a monstrous plot. And only God knows who's leading the plot, my son. I'm not sure Vallarian really was the one who thought it all up—although he said he was.
That's true, monsignor. Some information indicate that the whole matter is more complicated than we've already revealed.
What information do you mean, my son?

When I arrested judge Vallarian, he told me some strange things. He said that soon the day will come when some new order will be born and its children will rule the world—as it was foretold long time ago.
I don't want to make a mistake, but it sounds as if Vallarian talked about a heretic cult of the Children of the New Order...
Cult of the Children of the New Order? I've never heard about it...

No wonder you haven't, my son. It wasn't any of those heretic cults that have appeared in the Realm during last several years. The cult of Children of the New Order was a powerful group of fanatics certain Lucius gathered around himself in 9th century in the Realm. He claimed he was the Dark Prophet who came to reveal the ending of God's Kingdom in the Earth. The cult spread quickly, because the doctrine of Lucius was very captivating. Soon the heretics had many terrible crimes on their conscience, acting in the name of their ruler, the Dark Prince of Hell. But in the end the cult was destroyed and its members burned, all of them at the same time.
So it seems we're facing the cult that was destroyed more than four hundred years ago?

Yes, exactly. In addition to that all of it happened beyond the borders of our Realm—in the Lochland Empire. But nobody was really sure the cult was completely destroyed. Maybe some of its members were able to flee beyond the borders—for example here in Ultherst—and thus the doctrine of Dark Prophet Lucius has prevailed till nowadays.
Well, that's possible of course. But why should this cult represent more danger than those that are present in our Realm now?

I really don't know. Maybe I interpreted it wrong and it was just a coincidence of words. It was just an idea. Maybe Vallarian didn't belong to any cult at all. Or he thought he was the member of the cult, but the cult doesn't really exist. We must find out the truth at all costs. That is to say, there're some clues here indicating the contrary. During the inspection of things Bishop Vallarian left behind I found something what alarmed me indeed. I mean this scroll. It was among the things that belonged to Judge Vallarian. It's a kind of a map, or maybe a plan. Although I don't understand the written text, it brings about the worst apprehensions in me. As well as the material this scroll is made from. I don't know exactly how should a scroll of human skin look like, but I have such a feeling that it should look just like this!
Well... do you think it's something important?

I don't know. Maybe it's not important at all, but I'm sure it must have some value. Vallarian kept it hidden in a secret space in the double bottom of his chest. And he set a deadly trap there. Fortunately I'm not as naive as someone might think. However, I believe that if we were able to solve the mystery of the scroll it would give us a clue for the further investigation. Take the scroll and try asking Master Edmond d'Arvias if he couldn't help you with it. And come to tell me how successful you were.
All right, Monsignor.

Excuse me, Monsignor, but it seems to me that it isn't a good idea to possess a mysterious scroll from human skin someone kept hidden in a chest with a deadly trap. It could bring us troubles, you know?

It seems to me we're almost drowning in troubles, my son. And certainly I don't think it would help our cause if we decided to ignore the scroll I found. Take the scroll and try asking Master Edmond d'Arvias if he couldn't help you with it.
Are you sure you want to reveal this information to someone else?

I think that the loyalty of Edmond d'Arvias can't be doubted, my son. He's a true warrior of God, and if someone could help you, it would be him. I'm positive about it. Take the scroll and try asking the Master if he won't be able to puzzle it out or give us some other advice.
Well, my son, was Master Edmond d'Arvias able to advise you as for that scroll?
Partly he was, Monsignor. He wasn't able to translate it, but he recommended Bishop Trevorius in Glatzburg to me. He should be able to help us.

I know Trevorius. He's the Glatzburg diocese Bishop. From time to time we visit each other, but during the last years we didn't have many opportunities to do so. As far as I know he's a true and devoted servant of God—although I thought the same about Judge Vallarian. Anyway, if Master Edmond d'Arvias recommended you to seek him, don't hesitate to do so. Set on the journey to Glatzburg, my son, and try to reveal the secret of that scroll. I'm convinced it doesn't hide anything good, but it's our holy duty!

I'm glad you decided to take care of that damned case, my dear son. You must find out the truth about Judge Vallarian and his plans here in Hillbrandt at all costs. And at the same time it's also absolutely necessary to find out if the rumor about—God forgive me—the invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon was true. I pray that they were just lies and fantasies of those lost souls. Because if Vallarian really was able to summon the Fallen Angel, it would be not only the proof of his deep heresy, but also a sign of a very bad crisis the Realm fell into. Under normal circumstances nothing of that kind should be possible of course, because God protects His Kingdom on Earth, but these times are so bad that man can't be sure with anything. We really must find out what the truth is. We must find out if the demon Arthamon was really invoked!
As I've already promised once, I'll find out if it's true or not, Monsignor.
I know you'll do all what you'll be able to do. I fully trust you. And may God protect all of us from the Fallen Angels and their infernal powers!
I'll find out if it's true or not, Monsignor.
Yes, that's what we need now. God protect all of us from the Fallen Angels and their infernal powers!
I haven't spoken with him yet, Monsignor.
In that case you better don't waste any time, my son. I'm afraid time is working against us at the moment.
You can rely on me, Monsignor. Could I talk to you for a moment?
But of course, my son. What do you need to know?
Sure, Monsignor. Farewell.
Hail to you, my son. I hope your mission is going well. Is there something I could do to help you?
I'd like to talk to you for a moment, Monsignor.
I'll gladly fulfill your wish, son. What do you need to know from me?
I'd like to ask you for a favor, Monsignor. According to the information I was told you promised the royal chamberlain Trisstan to take care of his granddaughter Adeleida...

Yes, I promised it to him. I've known Trisstan since childhood and I won't deny any kind of help to him—especially when it comes to the protection of his dears and nears. Why do you ask me about that?
Because I brought Adeleida here, Monsignor. Here she is.

Good Heavens... hail to you, my child! So your grandfather decided to send you to me in the end? There's one thing I can tell you—he made the right decision. Hillbrandt might seem little bit rude and barbarous to you in comparison to the life in Alvaron, but I can assure you that you will be all right with me. I'll take care of you well. Thank you, son, that you brought her to me. I'll watch her as well as if she was my own!
I thank you, Monsignor. Could I talk to you for a moment again?
Of course you could, my son. What would you need to know?
Farewell, Monsignor.
Farewell, son. And if you'll talk to Trisstan, give him my best regards.
Nothing at the moment, Father. Farewell.
Farewell, my son. Let the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you under his wings!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even God's knights rob innocent people! You've greatly disappointed me, son!

You decided to... what, my son? You don't really mean it, do you? I don't understand it. Judge Vallarian is the highest representative of the Holy Inquisition here in Hillbrandt; and you want to accuse him of heresy? That's total nonsense. I don't know where you got proofs for such an accusation, but I believe those proofs are false. You should better change your mind before it's too late. It isn't a good idea to antagonize an Inquisitorial Judge authorized by the Holy Office itself.
I can see I didn't entice you not to do so. I hope the truth will be revealed soon. It's not good when members of the Inquisition stand against each other.
I'm glad I found you, Monsignor. Brother Dominicus asked me to look for you. I'll get the potion for you.
Thank God my faithful Dominicus believed so firmly I'm still alive. And thank you for your help, my son. Bring me the mana potion so I can get back to the town. There's so much I have to do...
I'm glad I found you, monsignor. Brother Dominicus asked me to look for you. Here is the potion you asked for.
So brother Dominicus was right when he believed you're still alive...
So brother Dominicus was right when he believed you're still alive... Here you are the mana potion, Monsignor. I'm glad I could help you.
An Inquisitor of the Holy Office is a nasty thief? I don't want to believe that! What should this world be like as a whole when even clerics are stealing! You strongly disappointed my faith, son!

You decided to... what, my son? You don't really mean it, do you? I don't understand it. Judge Vallarian is the highest representative of the Holy Inquisition here in Hillbrandt; and you want to accuse him of heresy? That's total nonsense. I don't know where you got proofs for such an accusation, but I believe those proofs are false. You should better change your mind before it's too late. It isn't a good idea to antagonize an Inquisitorial Judge delegated with the power of a curial inquisitor.
A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even gentry rob innocent people! You've greatly disappointed me, son!

And what's the matter? Do you think that because I'm dead you don't have to express appropriate respect to me, you stupid villager? In that case you're mistaken—I'll teach you good manners! Yeeeeaaarghhhh!
Oh good Heavens! At least someone's coming to entertain me. I'm so lonely here... How long is it since I spoke to somebody? I feel so lonely here... even my sisters are somewhere... God knows where!
Oh my God... who are you, wandering soul?
I'm Princess Raphaela, the Grand Duchess of Yorkheim and Regent of Woodlington—don't you recognize me? Oh yes, you wanted to imply that my youths beauty is irretrievably lost, didn't you?
No, I didn't want to tell anything like that. I just wonder...
What made you wonder? TELL ME!
I just wonder that you still take care of your beauty, although you've been dead for several years already!
You're Princess Raphaela? But that's impossible... she died several years ago!
Princess Raphaela has been dead for several years already. You're just an awful monster that desecrated her body. Die, you evil demon!
You dare to talk to me like this, you poor villager? You will be justly punished for such an offence. Nobody may offend the kingship like that. Yeeeeaaarghhhh!
Poor girl... How much had she to undergo before her death? What injuries had she to suffer during that crazy ritual before God Mercifully took her soul? Well, she was still almost a child...
In the case that copper chain she had around her neck really belonged to her, her name was Raquel Gielwitch... May God take care of her soul!

In the case that copper chain she had around her neck really belonged to her, her name was Raquel Gielwitch... Now I know the answer for the question as to what happened to the sister of Wanda Gielwitch. May God take care of her soul!
Don't think about it, Rashgar. You will be fairly punished for all your sins!
You are mistaken, Rashgar. I promised the ghost of King Harlior that I'd rid the world of you, and that's exactly what I'm going to do!
So this is how things are! You're just a minion of that Phantasm of the Past. In that case Rashgar must laugh at you, mortal. You'll die and Rashgar will let his lieges eat their fill!

Welcome to Rashgar's realm, crazy human. Did you come to see the beginning of the end or your mean race? Look at the stairs leading to the Depths of Damnation—soon the phalanx of infernal warriors will rise up from there and rivers full of blood will flow through your world. All old things will fall and the Kingdom of Evil will rise from the ruins, like the Cursed Flame predicted. And Rashgar's race is here to use its weapons and to do what must be done!
What are you talking about, you monster?

Once already—at the beginning of time—our Lord took the orcs out of the Depths of Damnation to join his army and crush the realm of Thron here under the Mountains. And it will be the same this time. We bring the bloody stigma of destruction and ruination. We were called on again. Now, the time has come to drown the world in the blood of its people. Soon the Legions of Death will come out of the Depths of Damnation!
I came to stop you, hellspawn!

You can't stop what is uncontrollable! Once already—at the beginning of time—our Lord took the orcs out of the Depths of Damnation to join his army and crush the realm of Thron here under the Mountains. And it will be the same this time. We bring the bloody stigma of destruction and ruination. We were called on again. Now the time has come to drown the world in the blood of its inhabitants. Soon the Legions of Death will come out of the Depths of Damnation!

It depends on what you want to buy, sir knight. Most often I go to Victor Hammerhand the blacksmith. He has a sense for metal in his hands and he makes really good swords. It never happened to me that a sword from Hammerhand was damaged during an execution. Of course you can get also other weapons from him, and even armor. As for other things, I usually buy at Truthorn's. I can get all I need from him—from food to healing salves for scabies. I don't go anywhere else.

Although I'm not a cleric, sir knight, and thus I can't tell you where the crisis came from, from the viewpoint of the town executioner I can tell you I've never seen anything so terrible before. It seems like people went totally mad and rushed into idolatry like wasps to spilt wine. And those who still believe are losing their hope slowly. I never saw so much despair in people like in the last few years. Nobody believes it could get better again.

If I were you, I'd be very careful about giant spider beasts lurking around Hillbrandt. You can find most of them on the edge of the Moonshine Mountains, where they're hidden in deep holes and glens. But sometimes they dare to go near the town too. Their poison is deadly, sir knight. One bite and you'll die in couple of minutes.
Thanks for the advice.

Not at all, sir knight. And if I can give you some more advice, be very careful during the night about what's going on in the sky. Because it could happen to you that a bunch of giant bats would attack you and bite you to the bones before you'd be able to call for help!
If there's any rewards? If I'm not mistaken, the orcs are on the list for now, sir knight. Because they're our biggest trouble and there's plenty of them. Ask sheriff Contemburry about the details.

To tell the truth, sir knight, there is one suspicion of heresy I have. I spend a lot of time around the scaffold, often also late in the evening. Because of that, some time ago I saw Suzan Brauchner walk around the common graves where we place the bodies of executed people to which the Church denied a proper burial. It seemed as if she was looking for something. She had a long cloak on her, and a hood, so I didn't recognize her at first, but when I went closer to find out what was happening, I saw her face for a short moment. Then she ran out and disappeared into the evening gloom. I don't know what I should deduce from it, but I doubt she was doing anything good there.

I think the strangest event recently is the fact that the orcs appeared in the Moonshine Mountains. They came from the depths of the iron mines without any reason or warning. As if they came straight out of the fairy tales about ancient non-human realms. They slaughtered every miner they ran into and killed all the people in the miners' village of Asherbalt. Men, women, even children. Only a few people were able to flee soon enough and get into Hillbrandt. The orcs hunted them down in surrounding woods like wild animals. Since that time, thick black smoke has been coming out from that place. Nobody knows what devilish things they're doing there, but it can't be anything good. I have a feeling that soon the hordes of iron-clad orcs will come out of the iron mines and attack Hillbrandt. They've already tried to attack it not long ago. Someone opened the gate for them in the dark and they entered the town. Many people were killed before the orcs retreated.

I've heard that Master Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of heresy, but I don't believe that. I know the Master quite well, because we cooperate often with each other, if you understand me. He catches criminals and I execute their sentence. Because of that I know he wouldn't be able to do such a thing he was accused of. There must be some other explanation.
I'd like to help you, but I don't know any more than anybody else could tell you about the theft of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius—that is, it disappeared and nobody knows who stole it.

The disappearance of the Bishop Quentinus is a tragedy. You know, Bishop Quentinus was a blessing for this diocese. Nobody knows why a man so wise and educated left for such a God-forgotten place like Hillbrandt. At first people whispered to each other about his dark past, about which nothing was known, and constructed various slanders. But during the time the Bishop got to their hearts and became a great support for them. It's sad he had such a bad fate.

Someone stole the sword from Master Edmond d'Arvias? It's really hard to believe. How could that happen? I don't know of anything that is more precious for the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous than their swords. The sword is more than just a weapon for them—it's a symbol of the Brotherhood. Some nasty heretic had to do that! I hope he'll be caught and punished soon. If I get to know any details about the case, I'll tell you about it.

It's possible that Olfghard killed Natalia Reichmann. I've had the honor of applying my art on him several times already—the Duke judged him to the pillory a few times and once he nearly lost his right hand. But I can't tell you if he really killed Natalia Reichmann. Some of her jewelry was found on him, that's true, but I don't think he would have to kill her because of that. He would be able to steal an eye from you without you noticing it.
Do you know the soldier Jullian? He's said to have deserted...

I know this Jullian. He's a young dandy thinking that the world lies at his feet. He has such an innocent face, but otherwise he's a really bad egg, as far as I can tell. And he's pretty violent. Once I saw him almost kill one villager in Truthorn's tavern for a worthless reason. Thus, I'm not surprised he decided he doesn't like his life in the army anymore and he ran away. But I don't have the slightest idea where he could be. Maybe on his way somewhere east...

Yes, sir knight, and there's a lot of them. But I am most worried about the tale about the Death Stone. Have you heard about it? There's a piece of rock not far away from here that remotely reminds one of the face of a dead man. It's said that all the souls of brigands, killers and ravishers executed here in Hillbrandt during the centuries are trapped in the stone. And that those wicked lost souls can't leave this world and must stay in the Death Stone till the End of Time. I don't know if there's any truth to that tale, but I'm sure that nobody dares go closer than one hundred steps to the stone, because some strange voices can be really heard from it...

The merchant Kurth Ollmier was assassinated some time ago in the attic of the Truthorn's tavern. His throat was cut and in addition to that his manhood was separated from him and inserted into his mouth. As far as I know, Sheriff Contemburry postponed the case, because he had neither any proof nor any clues. Thus, the murderer is still avoiding justice.
If you really want to know that, sir knight, it will cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
Answer me, Raubsticht, and I promise you any of those terrible things I'm just thinking about won't happen to you!
It's clear that we don't like each other, Raubsticht. But I assure you that your answer will help a righteous cause.
You're very intelligent and smart man, Raubsticht. Because of that I believe you could answer my question.
Thank you. Could I ask you a few more questions?
Of course you could, sir knight.
Thank you, good man. Farewell.

To be honest, I haven't felt well recently, sir knight. It seems to me I've caught some disease. A few days ago, moist ulcers appeared on my body and cruel pain assailed me. In addition to that I also have a fever now. I've already tried various salves and potions, but they didn't help. In fact it's getting worse. I fear that it is something serious. Could you help me, please?
I'll help you.
I'd be very grateful to you, sir knight. I fear it could bring me down. Go to see herbwoman Elisia Würtenrodt and ask her to prepare a cure disease potion.
You can count on me.
Thank you, sir knight. You surely will be rewarded!
It depends on what would you offer me for that.
If you won't take it as an offence, I'll pay you gladly for your service. My health is more important than my gold, and in these stirred times there's nothing to spend the gold on anyway.
I'm sorry, I'm not a doctor.
What can I do. I'll try to find some help myself. You now, in my profession I can't afford to lose strength.
I understand. Could I talk to you a little longer?
Sure, but be brief, please. I don't feel well at all...

I thank you warmly, sir knight. I hope I'll feel better thanks to it. Those last few days I really felt very bad. And in my profession I can't afford to lose strength. Here is the reward I promised you, you deserved it fully.
Could you answer a few more questions for me?
Yes, of course. What would you like to know?
You'd better hurry, please. I'm feeling worse and worse every moment...
Sure. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Sure. What do you need to know?
Sure. Farewell for now.
Hello, sir knight. You're new in the town, aren't you? I suppose the latest stirring events led you to our town. Maybe the Inquisition will be able to solve all our issues properly.
Excuse me for not introducing myself immediately, sir knight. My name is Friedrich Raubsticht. I'm the town executioner.
Sure, sir knight. But be brief, please. I don't feel well at all...
It seems to me you don't look well at all. Are you ill?
Don't be afraid, I won't keep you long.
That's considerate of you, sir knight.
Excuse me for my curiosity, but it couldn't be left unmentioned, that you look... not well at all. Are you ill?
Nice to meet you, good man. Farewell.
What stirring events do you have in mind?

Those heretic matters. I'd never think that heresy and godless thinking could spread in our town. Life has always been harder here than in other parts of our Realm and sometimes faith was the only reliance for the people. And now it was found out that there are heretics even among us. They commit dirty things and terrible atrocities.
Hello, sir knight. Have you already got the cure disease potion from Ellisia Würtenrodt? I feel worse and worse every moment.
I got it. Here you are. I hope it will help you.

Thank you once more for that healing potion you brought me, sir knight. But to tell the truth, it didn't help me even a bit. The fever didn't recede and the ulcers didn't heal up. Do you happen to know how is that possible?
What? That potion didn't help? In that case I'm afraid that your disease is of some unclean origin.
Of unclean origin? You mean... the effect of dark powers? A curse? Are you trying to tell me my disease was caused by someone's curse?
It seems more like a bewitchment.
But that's... an attempt to murder! Someone's trying to kill me! Would you help me, sir knight? If I don't get rid of the bewitchment, I'll die sooner or later!
All right, I'll help you. I'll find out who's trying to kill you.

God bless you, sir knight. I hope you'll be able to find out very soon. The pain is worse and worse every moment. Maybe Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist could give you some advice in that case, she knows more than anybody else about these supernatural matters.
Don't be afraid, the evil will be uprooted!
God bless you, sir knight!
It depends on what you would offer me for that.
Of course I won't spare any gold, sir knight. It's my life at stake, after all!
I'm sorry but I have no time to do that. Maybe someone else will help you.
Well... I'm not sure about it at all. But what can I do...
I really don't know, I'm not a doctor. Ask someone else to help you.
What can I do. However, thanks once more for the potion, although it was probably useless.
What do you need, sir knight? I'm not feeling well...
What do you need, sir knight? I'm not feeling well. And in addition to that I must find out, who's trying to kill me.
Hello, sir knight. How are you? Did you find out anything as to that bewitchment? To tell the truth, I feel worse and worse every moment.

Your assistant Quarim believes that your bewitchment could be someone's revenge because you executed somebody. I'd say you must have many enemies in your profession. Do you remember someone who would like to take revenge on you?

I don't know, sir knight. I've been the town executioner for ten years already and during those ten years many people whom I wouldn't like to meet in a dark alley became my enemies. But somebody who would try to kill me with the help of dark powers... I don't know, I don't think that about anybody. But now I remember that when I executed Hans Falkner he laughed at me and told me that he will take his own back after his death. Is it possible that the threat could come true in some dark way?
Who was that Hans Falkner?

Hans Falkner was a murderer and a rapist who committed several terrible crimes. Not long ago the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous caught him right in the city and I performed the execution. I don't think I've ever met a human being as bad as he was. He always killed in cold blood, no matter if the victims were men, women or children. I hope God damned him.
Well... interesting. Do you think it has some connection with your bewitchment?
Yes, it's possible. I'd investigate it if I were you...
I have good news for you. I found out that Lotti Frankmüller cursed you for executing her lover Hans Falkner.

Lotti Frankmüller? Maid of the Duke? Oh my God, that's unbelievable. I thought she's a quiet, modest girl, and here she revels in the powers of Hell and she even fornicated with that murderer Hans Falkner. That's terrible. However I'm glad you revealed her, sir knight. What will you do with that bewitchment now? How could it be canceled?
It's been canceled already, good man. I destroyed a cursed statuette which Lotti Frankmüller controlled you with. You will be completely healthy in a few days.
Oh, really? In that case I'm saved! Thank you, sir knight, I owe you a lot. I'll never forget what you've done for me. Here is the promised reward, you deserved it.
Thank you. I'm glad it ended like that, good man.
So am I, sir knight.
It seems to me that it's connected somehow with this statuette I found on Lotti.
Maybe you should ask Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist for advice. She knows more than anybody else about these supernatural matters.
Unfortunately that's what I don't know yet.
You should ask Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist for an advice. She knows more than anybody else about these supernatural matters.
It seems to me I'm on a good way. I'm investigating one suspicion now. Hold on.
Excellent, sir knight. But you had better hurry, please. I'm nearly at the edge. Ask Ellisia Würtenrodt the herbalist for advice, she knows more than anybody else about these things.
Not yet, good man.
Hail to you, sir knight. I'm so glad you helped me to get my health back! What can I do for you?

God put me to the trial and I passed it. He entrusted me with the mission—to open the eyes of the people and to prepare them for the End of the World, for Doom. Heretics destroyed both our faith and our land. They invoked demons and invited them into the Kingdom of God on Earth to fornicate with them on our white bones and rotten entrails. We must repent and seek redemption for our sins before it will be too late! Abandon all your things, knight, throw away all your belongings and walk the world naked like St. Millius, dressed for the righteous mission of God's mercy.
God doesn't want me to talk to you about it, knight!
Tell me once more what you witnessed that night when the hellspawns attacked the city.

I saw the treacherous Edmond d'Arvias sneaking around the stockade like a dark shadow in the dark and in a moment when tired guards rested by the fire he opened the gate to the hordes of green skins. It was him who caused that terrible slaughter! He's the source of all evil! I hate him!
Do you think that God will forgive us, if we purge the Realm of the heretics, like the flames of execution stake purge the heretics of their sins?

Whether God will forgive us? I don't know. Maybe he will. And that's why all the land must be put on fire, not to let a single heretic avoid this mercy that's prepared for them. Death to the heretics! Death to nasty godless creatures and false heterodoxies! Let flames eat their flesh, let their eyes come out of their heads, to Hell with those wicked cultists! God can see them and hates them all as much as I do!

This crisis is the work of heretic minions of the powers of Hell, knight. It's the wrath of God for what the heretics did to our faith. That's exactly why we must rise up, we must walk the Realm with the torches of Justice in our hands and light the purging flame at every corner. Those who contravened God's Commandments must be burned. The families the heretics came from should be burned too. As well as their friends and people they were in contact with. Let all the people who know those heretics be burned, because such people could be infected by the perverse seed of sin!

Gerrasian the Prophet said: Behold, you will see the wolf in the lamb skin, and he will be the most terrible beast. Lack of faith and falsehood are his teeth, beautiful face and rotten innocence are his shield. You will turn your back to him; he will bite your neck with his poisonous teeth!
And the First Prophet said: You will never long for golden mammon, because who longs for mundane belongings is damned forever and ever and the face of God is denied to him for eternity!

The Temple of Balaghar went down in flames, water was turned to blood, sky was glowing with infernal flames, lack of faith flooded the minds, three seals were broken and three Angels blew their trumpets, the eagle took his wings and heralded the wrath of God! Behold, the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth is coming and the Beast will be released from its prison to sit on the throne of Heaven. False Prophet walks the world and seduces the nations of all four quarters of the world!

...and the Fallen Angel Arthamon will spread his wings and fiery breath melting rocks into lava will come out of his nostrils. And he will walk the world and Destruction and Pain will follow him not to let anything more to exist...
All that was saintly to us will be taken away from us and we'll shed bitter tears, never to taste happiness again. So deep are our sins!
I saw Bishop Quentinus walking the Way of the Cross, having a crown of thorns on his head...

God called Kurth Ollmier to Him to kneel before His face. Everybody who will offend His Will must suffer for his sins and crimes and all who dishonor the name of our Shepherd by a single word or act will be burned to ashes!

Who rules Hillbrandt? Well, sin does! Sin and fornication! Because of that it's necessary to take torches and burn the town to ashes! Thus, we'll purge ourselves of all bad things and come before God Almighty naked in our purity!
Yes, I expected something like that...
Don't expect anything, knight, get a torch and start acting!
God wants me to tell you about it in exchange for some gold...
Well... I'm sorry then...
I won't give you that much. Here is 10 gold pieces.
In that case I can't help you in any way...
Answer me immediately, Reitdorf, or I'll lose my patience and order your arrest and torture!
I know how you feel, Reitdorf. All of us have lost something in these cruel times. But don't let the powers of Hell lead you on a wrong path. Your answer would help a rightful cause.
You're a real missionary! I wouldn't believe someone like you could be found in these hard times! Because of that I firmly believe you'll answer my question!

Alas! We are all doomed! The End of the World is coming! The Star of Doom blazed in the sky, three Angels blew their trumpets and three seals were broken! Famine, plague and fire from the sky tell us clearly that our time has come! God turned his face away from us. The Scriptures speak clearly—we will be damned and the thousand years of God's rule will be ended, Satan will be released from his jail! The end of the World is coming!

What? Who am I? Nobody. I'm nobody. I'm damned as well as you and all the others. God became angry with us and turned His face away from us. Disasters of Three Seals affected our world. And Satan is already knocking on Heaven's door.
You really don't have any name?

I had a name, but I lost it. Together with my family, they died of the plague. Together with my belongings which the rain of fire took away from me. My name was Thomas Reitdorf, but that name is gone forever. I used to be a farmer. I prayed to God, went to church for confessions and for Holy Mass. I paid the tithes. I paid my taxes and gave generous gifts to the Holy Mother Church. My family was god-fearing and faithful. And despite that God took all from me. And do you know why? Because our time is over already. The End of the Kingdom of God on Earth came. Those who threw away the faith and turned to the powers of Hell are already preparing the throne for their ruler. And God punished us for that!
You words are outright heresy! How do you dare to preach anything like that? You could be put to the execution stake for that!

Yes, let's ignite the stakes, let them burn with a purging flame! It's the only way to destroy the heretics, the awful helpers of the Prince of Hell. Let's ignite the fires of Justice in the whole Realm, let the heretics die a purifying death, their bodies flooded with painful agony of mercy! People, don't wait for anything and light the stakes for witches and sorcerers, because you're doing the will of God!
Be careful, good man. This is the work of the Inquisition, not a mission for common people.

So why doesn't the Holy Inquisition do anything about it? Why must we countenance when the heretics walk with impunity in full daylight without a single threat? Why doesn't that damned Edmond d'Arvias stand on the execution stake yet; why doesn't the purging flame lick his soul already?
Did you say Edmond d'Arvias?
Yes, Edmond d'Arvias. He's a wolf dressed in a lambskin. I curse both his name and his soul. I hope he'll turn black in the eternal cauldrons of Hell, I hope he'll never find peace!
Why do you think Edmond d'Arvias is a heretic?

Because he plotted with dark powers. He summoned monsters to this world, and he gives them orders. He consorts with them in the night during heretic Sabbaths; he drinks the blood of non-baptized children. He's a demon in a human body!
Do you have any proof of your statements?

Sure I have! Providence itself revealed to me the truth about the real spirit of Edmond d'Arvias. That night when the infernal orcs got to the town I saw the treacherous Edmond d'Arvias sneaking around the stockade like a dark shadow in the dark and in a moment when tired guards rested by the fire he opened the gate to the hordes of green skins. It was him who caused that terrible slaughter! He's the source of all evil! I hate him!
I don't believe it was Master Edmond d'Arvias! It was too dark for you to recognize him clearly, wasn't it?

Yes, it was dark like hell, but I recognized him. I was sitting in one of those sheds near the stockade. He didn't see me at all, but I saw him well. He waited till the guards went to the fire and then he sneaked to the gate and opened it. Before anybody was able to do anything, the hellspawns were in and terrible bloody slaughter began. It was Edmond d'Arvias who let them into the town. I swear!
I'm sorry about your family, Reitdorf, but even something like that hardly entitles you to preach such a rebellious heterodoxy!

Rebellious heterodoxy? No, knight, this isn't any rebellious heterodoxy. This is our faith. God gave me an omen that I should prepare all those who still believe for the Judgment Day, when the sins of mankind will be counted and the final bill will be paid!

Why, who's coming here? Stop and listen to the words of truth. The end of the world is coming! The Star of Doom blazed in the sky, three Angels blew their trumpets and three seals were broken! Famine, plague and fire from the sky tell us clearly that our time has come! God turned his face away from us...
I've already heard that from you. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Ask me and you'll see the truth. God enlightened me and entrusted me the Mission!
I don't have time for this. Farewell.
Yes, our time is over. God damned us because we diverted from Him. Death to the heretics! Death to all those who committed sins! And who's not guilty, throw the stone...

Why, God's emissary is coming! I bow to you, Chosen One. You were predestined by God to hold the Archangel Gabriel's Sword of Justice and do with it that what must be done. But alas! Whatever you'll do won't affect fate anyhow. The heretics are spreading through the whole Realm and wherever they come, they lay the seeds of sin. The whole Realm has to be put into the purging fire and those who are devoted to our faith will be raised to the Kingdom of Heaven.
What a pleasant imagination, but I don't think it's in accordance with the teachings of our Holy Mother Church.

Alas! I pity you if you rely on what seemed to be reliable yesterday. Where is my family, I ask you? Where is all I had in this world? And where was the Church when God took them from me? I was fairly punished for the sins of all the people. For the sins of heretics who tossed away all that's saintly to fornicate with the flames of Hell.
Eh... farewell.
You had better shut up, or you'll end at the stake!

Yes, I deserve to stand before the face of God purged from the sins of this world. God can see me and he promises me a place in the Kingdom of Heaven. Still I have a chance—before the flames of Hell devour everything!
This is heresy! I'll have you burned, Reitdorf. Unless you want to use gold to ransom yourself from your sins...
I mean that if you'll give me all your gold, I might forget about all your heretic blabbering. And don't try to look like a beggar—I'm sure you've something left!
You'll get nothing from me, lost soul. I'm a prophet of the truth and nothing more. I've got nothing except for my mission. Go away!
You poor creature!
You're a fool, Reitdorf. I don't have time for this. Farewell.
Ask me and you'll see the truth. God enlightened me and entrusted me with the Mission—to open the eyes of the people!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even God's knights rob innocent people! Shame!

God put me to the trial and I passed it. He entrusted me with the mission—to open the eyes of the people and to prepare them for the End of the World, for Doom. Heretics destroyed both our faith and our land. They invoked demons and invited them into the Kingdom of God on Earth to fornicate with them on our white bones and rotten entrails. We must repent and seek redemption for our sins before it will be too late! Abandon all your things, Father, throw away all your belongings and walk the world naked like St. Millius, dressed for the righteous mission of God's mercy.
God doesn't want me to talk to you about it, Father!

This crisis is the work of heretic minions of the powers of Hell, Father. It's the wrath of God for what the heretics did to our faith. That's exactly why we must rise up, we must walk the Realm with the torches of Justice in our hands and light the purging flame at every corner. Those who contravened God's Commandments must be burned. The families the heretics came from should be burned too. As well as their friends and people they were in contact with. Let all the people who know those heretics be burned, because such people could be infected by the perverse seed of sin!
Don't expect anything, Father, get a torch and start acting!
Are you really sure it was Master Edmond d'Arvias? It was dark, wasn't it?

Rebellious heterodoxy? No, Father, this isn't any rebellious heterodoxy. This is our faith. God gave me an omen that I should prepare all those who still believe for the Judgment Day, when the sins of mankind will be counted and the final bill will be paid!

Heretics destroyed both our faith and our land. They invoked demons and invited them into the Kingdom of God on Earth to fornicate with them on our white bones and rotten entrails. We must repent and seek redemption for our sins before it will be too late! Abandon all your things, sir, throw away all your belongings and walk the world naked like St. Millius, dressed for the righteous mission of God's mercy.
God doesn't want me to talk to you about it, sir!

This crisis is the work of heretic minions of the powers of Hell, sir. It's the wrath of God for what the heretics did to our faith. That's exactly why we must rise up, we must walk the Realm with the torches of Justice in our hands and light the purging flame at every corner.
