Let all the people who know those heretics be burned, because such people could be infected by the perverse seed of sin!
Don't expect anything, sir, get a torch and start acting!

Rebellious heterodoxy? No, sir, this isn't any rebellious heterodoxy. This is our faith. God gave me an omen that I should prepare all those who still believe for the Judgment Day, when the sins of mankind will be counted and the final bill will be paid!
Good Heavens, how could this statue get here? It's a masterpiece... I've never ever seen anything like that. So authentic lineaments, natural shirring of clothing... every detail is perfect!

Wait a moment... that's not a statue. That's... my God! That's a petrified man! What a terrible crime was committed here? What awful witchery was practiced here that the paladin was turned to stone? God save his soul.
This must be the paladin Richwald d'Blazier, turned to stone. Awful witchery... God save his soul.
Do you suspect anyone in the town of heresy? Except for Master d'Arvias, of course...
To tell you the truth, knight, I have one more suspicion. But I don't know if I should talk about it, because the suspected person is a child. But he's possessed by dark powers—no doubt about that!
Who are you talking about?

I'm talking about Paul Hammerhand. Ask the people in town, they'll confirm my words—the boy is a downright devil! Floundered by the powers of Hell since childhood. His father—and he's an orderly man—is no match for him at all. He's rebellious and runs away from his home to lurk around the city for days doing God knows what. He wasn't at confession all year and he's avoiding the church like the devil keeps away from the Holy Cross. He lies, renounces and steals everything he runs into. I tell you, knight, although he's a child yet, Hell devoured him a long time ago!

Children are under God's protection, good man. They can be prosecuted only under exceptional circumstances, if there are many affirmative proofs against them. They can't be questioned with the help of torture and they can be judged only to a lifelong stay in a monastery—to murus strictus.

I thought it's like that. That infernal whelp knows very well that justice doesn't apply to him and that the Law is no match for him! So he can perform his awful goings-on without fear for his life. It's really a nice justice, if I can tell you that!
Who are you talking about, good man?
I'm sorry, but it's as I've said. There's nothing I can do about it. Children are protected...
Yes, yes, children are protected by God, you've already told me that. So forget about it when you don't want to do anything about it!
Tell me once more what you saw that night when the orcs attacked the town.

I saw Master Edmond d'Arvias with my own eyes give orders to those awful green skins to attack the town church. I didn't want to believe that, but no doubt it was Master Edmond d'Arvias himself. First I thought the orcs attacked him, but later I figured out it's otherwise. He was giving orders to those monsters and then he disappeared in the dark before the guards came. I hope he'll be judged and executed soon!

You want to do some shopping? Well, if you want to buy some armaments, try asking the blacksmith Hammerhand, knight. Potions, spells and stuff like that can be bought from the herbalist Würtenrodt, astrologer Brechthold or from Father Dominic. And you can also buy various things from the inkeeper Truthorn or the stallholder Brauchner.

You call it a crisis? Well... you're probably right—it's a crisis, when you look at it like that. Life is much harder now than it was before. But on the other hand I've never had so many orders for gravestones like during the last three years. If I look at it from that point of view, I must say I'm doing well. On the other hand I know that soon all will be changed and all of us will have great times. Very soon!
How can you be so sure?
Aren't you sure things will turn for the good soon, knight? I'd be very surprised if a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous wouldn't believe that justice will prevail in the end...
Well... yes, I'm sure you're right.
I've heard that you often come back home late in the evening. Can you explain it to me somehow?
What? From whom have you heard that, knight?
From Flitz the beggar. He told me he saw you to return home early in the morning several times.
That lousy bastard! He lurks around my house, doesn't he? That mangy leper tries to slander me. Plague and pox on that nasty snake!
So it's the truth?

Yes, knight, it's true—from time to time I come home late in the night. But the reason isn't anything like you might think. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, knight. I swear!
All right, I believe you. If you promise me never to commit such a godless act again, I'll forgive you.
I promise, knight. I'll stop that immediately. Thanks.
I believe you. However, you must do penance for your terrible deeds. You'll pay a special gift to the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
What? A special gift? I'll be broke because of that... But if you won't let me otherwise... Here is all the gold I made on those stones.
That's not your business.

You're right, knight. But I don't want some untrue suspicion to fall on me. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, knight. I swear!

The worst thing that could happen to us during the last days was the betrayal of Master Edmond d'Arvias. I'd never think he was a heretic. He looked like a saint all those years and suddenly he was proven to be a heretic and a godless person, who offends God's name and hatches plots and intrigues against all that's saintly. I wish that the devil were at the stake soon!

I don't know anything about the theft of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius. But it seems to me someone had to get a lot of money for it. Holy relics are in high demand nowadays—people believe relics can save them from all evil, or at least guarantee eternal salvation to them...
Why should I know anything about the missing Bishop Quentinus? He was probably killed when the orcs attacked the town.

If I were you, knight, I wouldn't look for that hellspawn Paul Hammerhand. Surely he's back in Hell from where he came from. Dark powers possessed him, I'm sure about it. Probably he did some devilish things again and broke his neck somewhere!
I don't know anything about the missing Baroness Linda van Gallagan, knight. God knows what could have happened to her.
I'm investigating the theft of the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias. Do you happen to know anything about it?

Why should I know anything about the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias? And for the most part—why are you looking for the sword when it's as clear as day that Master d'Arwais is a heretic? He's trying to convince you 'bout something, isn't he? He'd like to escape justice. But he won't succeed!
Olfghard probably killed her. What else should I think about the murder of Natalia Reichmann? Natalia was the daughter of the richest townsman in Hillbrandt; no doubt someone killed her for money.
How should I know where that dandy Jullian could be? Probably he's on his way south. Maybe he believes he'll find a better fate there. What a fool!
Linda van Gallagan testified you helped her prepare a certain witchlike Sabbath and that you also took part in it. What can you tell me to this accusation?

How could Baroness van Gallagan testify such a barefaced lie? That's total nonsense, knight! I didn't commit anything of that kind, I swear! I'm a humble faithful believer... Well, I do something bad from time to time, I set too high a price for the gravestones to people, but I'm not a wicked heretic, knight, honestly! Baroness must have lied to you!
Why should I know anything about the death of Kurth Ollmier? I'm not interested in such things. Ask someone else!
Wait... you really don't know anything about it? It happened not too long ago.
Well... I've heard something, to tell the truth. His throat was cut here in town, in Truthorn's tavern. He rented a room in the attic. That's all I know about the matter.
If you won't cooperate, I promise you that you'll get to know many ways of torture before I finish your questioning!
I really need you to answer my question, good man. I'm sure you know the situation is urgent—although you seem not to like me.
I don't want to believe that a man as smart as you would deny to answer my question...
Sam Riemann, you're arrested for reasonable suspicion of heresy and of the participation in the plot against God and the King. You'll come with me!
Arrested? But why... What do you think I committed? Because I didn't do anything wrong!
You're arrested for a reasonable suspicion of heresy. You'll be arrested till the truth will be revealed!
If you're innocent, you've nothing to fear. Come with me so we can reveal the truth as soon as possible.
Give up immediately, or I'll take you to jail by any means of violence!
I'm not going anywhere with you, do you understand? You don't have any proof against me!

You're mistaken, Riemann. Baroness Linda van Gallagan testified you committed several terrible crimes together with her, including taking part in a dark ritual with the aim to summon the Fallen Angel Arthamon!
What did you say? That's bullshit! Do you hear me?! Bullshit! I'll kill you for such a slender!
So you confess?

Yes, I confess, if you want to hear it. It doesn't make any difference anyway, because you'll be biting the dust soon! Yes, we summoned the Fallen Angel! He came to us to become our new ruler! And I'll lead his armies! I'll command the legions of hellspawns and I'll let them devastate the Realm, I'll take what I want! And nobody will stop me, because I'll be invincible! I'll be the tyrant of the world!
Who thought this crazy thing up? Who came with the idea to summon the Fallen Angel Arthamon?

Who? Judge Vallarian did. He's the Highest Priest of Fire of the ancient cult of Arthamon! Surprised, are you? Not what you expected, ha ha! A Judge of the Holy Inquisition plotted all you're investigating here! What do you think you can do about it, heh? Nothing! Nothing at all, knight!
Were you the one who helped Baroness Linda van Gallagan to take the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill from the cemetery?
Yes, I was, knight. It was me who dug her body up and who helped to carry it to Dragon Rock, where we performed the ritual and thus let our ruler Arthamon enter this world!
Do you want to say you really summoned the Fallen Angel Arthamon?
That's enough, Sam Riemann. I arrest you for suspicion of heresy and of the plot against God and the King. You will confess your sins!
I doubt it, valiant knight! And if there's someone who should confess, it's you, because you'll be biting the dust at any moment. Die!

What do you want here, knight? I don't think I invited you to visit me. But I've heard about you. You are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, aren't you? In that case I hope you'll establish justice and help all the sinners to get where they should. To Hell!
Your concern for justice is admirable, good man.

I'm a humble servant of God. I've lived almost all of my life in the town and I've never seen so much atrocity and disgust as during the last few years. People I thought to believe firmly all the life turned into heretics before my eyes—they are worshipping the worst that's located in the entrails of Hell. And nobody does anything about it. It's awful!
My name is Sam Riemann, if you're interested in that. I'm a stonemason. If you need a gravestone, nobody around is better than me. You can look for inspiration at the town cemetery.
Eh, we'll see. Maybe later.
It's never too soon for something like that, knight. You never know when some heretic will send you to Him before your time. And there's a plenty of them lately!
Do you suspect anyone in particular, good man?
Yes, that's what I do. And it isn't only a suspicion. I've found out that Master Edmond d'Arvias is a heretic who sold his soul to Satan and started to plot with hellspawns!
Why do you think so?

It happened that night when those damned green skins got into the town. I was on my way back from the pub when I heard the sound of a fight from the Upper Gate. The sound was coming near quickly. I panicked and hid in the ruins of an abandoned house. From there, I could see the street leading to the church well. And I saw a bunch of green skins coming! I was completely dumbfounded for the moment. And just when they were passing by my hideout Master Edmond d'Arvias came out from the dark. It seemed like he was going to fight them. I saw him wielding his sword before. As for me, he's one of the best swordsmen in the Realm.
And what happened then?

Nothing! Nothing happened at all. I thought there'd be a terrible fight, but the orcs just stopped and waited. Master d'Arvias came to them, told them something, pointed at the church and the orcs ran that way howling wildly. The Master himself quickly looked around, whether someone's watching him, and disappeared in the dark.
Can you swear that what you have just said was true?
I cross my heart that what I've testified was true and nothing else, knight!
Thank you, good man. Can I talk to you for a moment?
Master Edmond d'Arvias, you say? Do you want to say that you suspect the Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous of heresy?
Exactly, knight. I know, maybe it seems strange to you, but I know what I've seen. Master d'Arvias is a heretic!
Enough... I give up. Mercy!
Hail to you, knight. What can I do for you? Are you interested in some gravestone? Or maybe you want to decorate your burial chamber?
Could you spare a moment to talk to me?
Thank you, but I don't need anything. Farewell.
Wise decision, Riemann. However, for assault on a member of the Brotherhood of Righteous I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!
To tell you the truth, Father, I have one more suspicion. But I don't know if I should talk about it, because the suspected person is a child. But he's possessed by dark powers—no doubt about that!

I'm talking about Paul Hammerhand. Ask the people in town, they'll confirm my words—the boy is a downright devil! Floundered by the powers of Hell since childhood. His father—and he's an orderly man—is no match for him at all. He's rebellious and runs away from his home to lurk around the city for days doing God knows what. He wasn't at confession all year and he's avoiding the church like the devil keeps away from the Holy Cross. He lies, renounces and steals everything he runs into. I tell you, Father, although he's a child yet, Hell devoured him a long time ago!

You want to do some shopping? Well, if you want to buy some armaments, try asking the blacksmith Hammerhand, Father. Potions, spells and stuff like that can be bought from the herbalist Würtenrodt, astrologer Brechthold or from Father Dominic. And you can also buy various things from the inkeeper Truthorn or the stallholder Brauchner.
Aren't you sure things will turn for the good soon, Father? I'd be very surprised if a cleric wouldn't believe that the time of trial is near to the end...
What? From whom have you heard that, Father?

Yes, Father, it's true—from time to time I come home late in the night. But the reason isn't anything like you might think. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, Father. I swear!
I promise, Father. I'll stop that immediately. Thanks.
I believe you. However, you must do penance for your terrible deeds. You'll pay the indulgence!
What? Indulgence? I'll be broke because of that... But if you won't let me otherwise... Here is all the gold I made on those stones.

You're right, Father. But I don't want some untrue suspicion to fall on me. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, Father. I swear!

If I were you, Father, I wouldn't look for that hellspawn Paul Hammerhand. Surely he's back in Hell from where he came from. Dark powers possessed him, I'm sure about it. Probably he did some devilish things again and broke his neck somewhere!
I don't know anything about the missing Baroness Linda van Gallagan, Father. God knows what could have happened to her.

How could Baroness van Gallagan testify such a barefaced lie? That's total nonsense, Father! I didn't commit anything of that kind, I swear! I'm a humble faithful believer... Well, I do something bad from time to time, I set too high a price for the gravestones to people, but I'm not a wicked heretic, Father, honestly! Baroness must have lied to you!
What did you say? That's bullshit! Do you hear me?! Bullshit! I'll kill you for such a slander!

Who? Judge Vallarian did. He's the Highest Priest of Fire of the ancient cult of Arthamon! Surprised, are you? Not what you expected, ha ha! Your superior plotted all you're investigating here! What do you think you can do about it, heh? Nothing! Nothing at all, reverend Father!
Yes, I was, Father. It was me who dug her body up and who helped to carry it to Dragon Rock, where we performed the ritual and thus let our ruler Arthamon enter this world!
I doubt it, reverend Father! And if there's someone who should confess, it's you, because you'll be biting the dust at any moment. Die!

What do you want here, Father? I don't think I invited you to visit me. But I've heard about you. You belong to the Inquisition, don't you? In that case I hope you'll help all the sinners to get where they should get. To Hell!
It's never too soon for something like that, Father. You never know when some heretic will send you to Him before your time. And there's a plenty of them lately!
I cross my heart that what I've testified was true and nothing else, Father!
Exactly, Father. I know, maybe it seems strange to you, but I know what I've seen. Master d'Arvias is a heretic!
Hail to you, Father. What can I do for you? Are you interested in some gravestone? Or maybe you want to decorate your burial chamber?
Wise decision, Riemann. However, for an assault on a member of the Holy Inquisition I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!

To tell you the truth, noble lord, I have one more suspicion. But I don't know if I should talk about it, because the suspected person is a child. But he's possessed by dark powers—no doubt about that!

I'm talking about Paul Hammerhand. Ask the people in town, they'll confirm my words—the boy is a downright devil! Floundered by the powers of Hell since childhood. His father—and he's an orderly man—is no match for him at all. He's rebellious and runs away from his home to lurk around the city for days doing God knows what. He wasn't at confession all year and he's avoiding the church like the devil keeps away from the Holy Cross. He lies, renounces and steals everything he runs into. I tell you, noble lord, although he's a child yet, Hell devoured him a long time ago!

You want to do some shopping? Well, if you want to buy some armaments, try asking the blacksmith Hammerhand, noble lord. Potions, spells and stuff like that can be bought from the herbalist Würtenrodt, astrologer Brechthold or from Father Dominic. And you can also buy various things from the inkeeper Truthorn or the stallholder Brauchner.
Aren't you sure things will turn for the good soon, noble lord? I'd be very surprised if a noble wouldn't believe that all will get rectified in the end...
What? From whom have you heard that, noble lord?

Yes, noble lord, it's true—from time to time I come home late in the night. But the reason isn't anything like you might think. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, noble lord. I swear!
I promise, noble lord. I'll stop that immediately. Thanks.
I believe you. However, you must do penance for your terrible deeds. You'll pay an exceptional tax!
What? An exceptional tax? I'll be broke because of that... But if you won't let me otherwise... Here is all the gold I made on those stones.

You're right, noble lord. But I don't want some untrue suspicion to fall on me. You know, I... well, I mostly make gravestones for a living nowadays. And I lack the material. So I go to the town cemetery and... Well, I take old gravestones there, I produce new ones from them and then I sell them. I know it's not honest, but it has nothing to do with heresy or something like that, noble lord. I swear!

If I were you, noble lord, I wouldn't look for that hellspawn Paul Hammerhand. Surely he's back in Hell from where he came from. Dark powers possessed him, I'm sure about it. Probably he did some devilish things again and broke his neck somewhere!
I don't know anything about the missing Baroness Linda van Gallagan, noble lord. God knows what could have happened to her.

How could Baroness van Gallagan testify such a barefaced lie? That's total nonsense, noble lord! I didn't commit anything of that kind, I swear! I'm a humble faithful believer... Well, I do something bad from time to time, I set too high a price for the gravestones to people, but I'm not a wicked heretic, noble lord, honestly! Baroness must have lied to you!

Who? Judge Vallarian did. He's the Highest Priest of Fire of the ancient cult of Arthamon! Surprised, are you? Not what you expected, ha ha! A Judge of the Holy Inquisition plotted all you're investigating here! What do you think you can do about it, heh? Nothing! Nothing at all, noble lord!
Yes, I was, noble lord. It was me who dug her body up and who helped to carry it to Dragon Rock, where we performed the ritual and thus let our ruler Arthamon enter this world!
I doubt it, noble lord! And if there's someone who should confess, it's you, because you'll be biting the dust at any moment. Die!

What do you want here, noble lord? I don't think I invited you to visit me. But I've heard about you. You are a noble, aren't you? In that case I hope you'll establish justice and help all the sinners to get where they should. To Hell!
It's never too soon for something like that, noble lord. You never know when some heretic will send you to Him before your time. And there's a plenty of them lately!
I cross my heart that what I've testified was true and nothing else, noble lord!
Exactly, noble lord. I know, maybe it seems strange to you, but I know what I've seen. Master d'Arvias is a heretic!
Enough... I give up, noble lord. Mercy!
Hail to you, noble lord. What can I do for you? Are you interested in some gravestone? Or maybe you want to decorate your burial chamber?
Wise decision, Riemann. However, for an assault on a noble lord I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!
I found out that the accusation of the trickster Tinthan of stealing the Monstrance of Saint Rhodric from the Bishopal temple was false. I would like to acquit him.

Excuse me? Did I understand you correctly, knight? You want to acquit Tinthan of the theft? You must be kidding! I must remind you that there was an eyewitness. Tinthan is probably going to be sentenced to death and the evidence is clear. There's no doubt about it!
As far as I know, the only evidence is the innkeeper Weintraum's testimony. And he took it back. He said he'd been mistaken.

I don't believe that... Did he really take his testimony back? But why would he do that? He has a score to settle with Tinthan and he must have been waiting for an opportunity like that for a long time...
But still he took it back—as I've already said. That's why I demand that Tinthan is acquitted and the proceedings against him stopped!

Well, then... If it's really true I must admit that further prosecution of Tinthan would be illegal. His guilt hasn't been proved and there's not enough evidence to justify further prosecution. But it's strange... Tinthan has such a bad reputation and I thought he was finally going to get what he deserved. But I must have made a mistake.
I would like to ask you, Grand Duke, whether you recognize this piece of rag. Does it come from any of your clothes?
Let me see... Yes, it looks like it. It seems it comes from my travel cloak. I don't use it very often anymore. Where did you find it?
That's not important. But please, tell me, when was the last time you wore it?
I really don't remember that. Probably in the winter.
Good, Grand Duke. Thank you.
You're welcome, knight. I really have no idea where I could have damaged the cloak...
I found it at the municipal cemetery, Grand Duke. It was hanging on a thorny bush close to a looted grave.
Is that all you can say about it, Grand Duke?
No... of course not. I'm just surprised. I haven't been to the cemetery lately and of course I have nothing to do with the grave, in case you want to imply something.
Good, Grand Duke. That's enough.
I'm not going to pretend that I'm not worried. How could the rag get there? Strange... really strange... I better deal with it personally!
So a rag coming from your cloak was found in the municipal cemetery close to a desecrated and looted grave and there's nothing you can say about it?

And what do you expect me to say? Of course I have no idea how the rag could have gotten there. I haven't worn it since winter, I haven't been to the cemetery lately and I have no idea what's going on here. Unless somebody's trying to discredit me. Yes, that would make sense... But who has access to my clothes? Really strange. I better start dealing with it.
Do you know that there is testimony according to which you desecrated a grave in the municipal cemetery and stole the body of the deceased?
What? What kind of nonsense is that? Who dares to spread gossip like that about me?
That's not important, Grand Duke. I'd like to know what you have to say about it.
What else can I say other than that it's a dirty lie?! An attack on me, gossip made to discredit me—if not something worse! Tell me who told you!
I'm sorry, Grand Duke, I can't do that. I'm bound by the vow of silence.
As you wish, knight. I'm going to find out myself.
It was Knight Commander Ethien de Pasque.
Knight Commander Ethien de Pasque?! Well then... I'll look into it!
What can you say about the accusation, Grand Duke?
What else can I say other than it's a dirty lie? It's an attack on me, dirty gossip made to discredit me—if not something worse!
All right. Thank you.
What do you think about the crisis that is spreading across the Realm, Grand Duke?

What do I think about the crisis? As an official of the Realm I must say that it's a disaster. A catastrophe. The Scourges of God that struck the Realm caused damage which will take years to repair. The population is decreasing, property is being damaged, the harvests are bad, the cattle are dying... and it's going to take years, maybe even decades to repair. People don't have the money to pay taxes so there is no money in the treasury. If there is no money the Realm is going down and it becomes an easy prey. I'll tell you something, knight, it will be primarily our children who will suffer the consequences of the Scourges of God—if they survive of course.
Do you see it only as an economic crisis, Grand Duke? What about faith?

I'm not a priest, knight, so I'll leave this part of the problem to the more competent. Of course I've heard people saying that this was the end of the world and the Scourges of God was just its forerunner. I know the Holy Scripture, the Apocalypse and saint Ezechiel—but still, who can say that this is the end of the world? It's not a question I am competent to answer. I have been authorized to administer this land and I can see the effect of the plague, the famine, the rain of fire, the coming of the beasts, the loss of faith and the heresy—and of course the constant decrease in tax revenues. Glatzburg treasury is completely empty and there is no hope it will get better anytime soon. That's what I call a crisis!
I've heard that there was a war brewing. Is that really so?

I have no idea, knight, whether there will be a war or not. As far as commanding the Glatzburg regiment is concerned I only obey the orders of the First Knight from Alvaron. The orders are speaking clearly—get the regiment ready, draft and train new recruits, prepare the cavalry and the charioteers, replenish supplies and wait. And that's exactly what I'm doing—even though I must admit that it's a difficult thing to do without introducing extra taxes. I can't take from people what they don't have... and still I have to obey the orders. The rumor has spread quickly and people are afraid. And I don't blame them—war is a terrible thing.
But who would the war be against, Grand Duke?
I have no idea, knight. I'd be happy if I could use the regiment against the brigands that torment Glatzburg. But the orders speak clearly—be ready. So all I can do is await more orders.

There are swarms of monsters around Glatzburg. And not just around Glatzburg—even in the city itself. You've probably heard about the corpses that appear in the streets at nights. Nobody knows where they come from and where they disappear to in the morning. But they leave dead behind and there's nowhere to bury them because the municipal cemetery has fallen to the shadow of the Beast and the dead raise from their graves and murder everyone they see. And unfortunately it's not just the living corpses that endanger my subjects.
And who else?

The rogues and the bandits who lurk by the roads and kill people on sight are much worse. I need to do something about them but I can't. There's too many of them and I'm not allowed to use the royal army. And there is no money and men to gather a local militia. I can't do anything but to look at their bloody rage. The bandits of Benthley of Welshrem are the worst. They don't really care for the booty but for the killing. They don't leave anybody alive—the merchants, the pilgrims, the nobles, the farmers, the priests, nobody.

At the end of the winter I started offering rewards for catching any brigand raging around both the royal and the local roads. I hoped it would help in the fight against the bandits and their bands. I thought it would turn them against their comrades, that the rewards would make some of them kill the others. But I was wrong. But the rewards are still offered so anyone who manages to catch a bandit and bring a scalp or a head to Sheriff Smith will get the reward in gold.

To tell you the truth I have a few suspicions of heresy. But I have no proofs so I'd rather not mention them for the sake of my own safety. I don't want to be accused of using the Brotherhood of the Righteous to reach my own aims.
Have you encountered the Cult of the Children of the New Order here in Glatzburg?

The Children of the New Order? No, I don't recall hearing anything like that. I'm not absolutely sure but I think I've never heard of the cult. It's rather a question to ask Cardinal Truncquillius or Judge Welfhar, they know more about the heretic cults and movements. After all, it's their mission.
So many things have happened in Glatzburg lately, knight, that I don't know where to begin.
What do you think is the worst?

The worst of all was, I think, the attempt to murder Bishop Trevorius. It was my own chamber-maid Francessca Gulvardi. I couldn't believe it because Francessca came from a good family, she was a quiet and modest girl, never did anything bad... and yet she hurled herself at the Bishop during the confessionals like a wild animal. She must have been possessed by an unholy spirit, that's the only explanation.

Fortunately, the Bishop was able to defend himself against the attack. I heard that when she was being taken to the prison, five men had to hold her so she couldn't escape. Even though she had handcuffs on her hands. The times are bad but we haven't had one attack on a high priest yet. And suddenly, a diocesan Bishop is attacked by a possessed girl. I don't know how this is going to end.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a tragic event. And it took me completely by surprise. I must admit that the Bishop's presence here in Glatzburg was making my life a lot easier. When my writs and decrees had no effect, one sermon of the Bishop did the job. His influence on the parishioners was unbelievable. But he had enemies, of course.
Really? Can you tell me what enemies?

Many didn't like the Monsignor Trevorius's radical opinions. His belief in poverty and modesty of the priests, their duty to serve God as well as the people. His attempts to change the Holy Mother Church, his demand that it lives according to the twelve holy prophets. I wouldn't be surprised if the murder had something to do with that. But that's just my opinion. It's quite possible that the heretics or some infernal powers are responsible. Monsignor Trevorius was an embodiment of the true faith!
Are you a history lover or is there another reason you are interested in the tomb?
It's a part of my... secret mission, Grand Duke.

Oh yes, sure... the secret mission. Well, who doesn't have a secret mission these days? But to answer your question, I must sincerely admit I've never heard of a noble named Fae'Darlion, which of course doesn't mean the tomb couldn't be hidden somewhere in my cellar. Glatzburg is surrounded by many relics of the past including some relics older than Ereborn. There are a few books in my library, which deal with the relics of the Thron and Elenian Empires, and they say that many of those relics can be found in Glatzburg and its surroundings.
And where exactly?

Can't help you with that, knight. You'll have to look around the city, search through the woods, meadows and swamps or climb the rocks. But be careful about the dangers you can encounter there. I don't want to be solving another case of a mysterious disappearance or of a brutal murder.

As far as I can remember, Father Frederic came to Glatzburg a couple years ago to live the rest of his days in peace. Unfortunately, he died of plague in 1221. That probably wasn't the death he was looking for but there was nothing he could do about it—we all are in the hands of God. That's probably all I know about him—oh yes, and that he was supposed to be a famous exorcist. Pity he died, maybe he could remove the curse from my servant Francessca Gulvardi who tried to kill Monsignor Trevorius in a sudden fit of madness a few days back.

The undead in the streets are a disaster for the whole city. I asked Sheriff Smith to look into the case with maximum effort. It's a duty of the governor of a city to make sure all his subjects including the poorest are safe. Unfortunately, we have had no success yet. The attacks continue although the royal army has killed hundreds of them. The Brotherhood of the Righteous lent their swords as well, but there was no result. The undead they kill at night raise again the next day after dusk.
Are there any suspicions as to where they come from or who's behind it?

Strangely, there are not many suspicions, knight. Of course they blame it all on the heretics and the infernal powers but that's a weak explanation. There are priest walking the streets of the city and their prayers and rituals should be banishing the hellspawns—as they did until recently. It's not clear why the undead appear. I believe, however, that Sheriff Smith will be able to deal with it. He's a person you can rely on.

I know which hammer you're talking about and of course I've heard that is was buried somewhere together with the rest of Bonhart von Drichtmaul's property. I found a few reports of the event in the municipal chronicle. But none of them gives any details as to where the hammer could be. So I can't help you in your investigation, knight.
I need to get some wine called Chateau de Trebrechette. Do you have any idea where I could get a few bottles?

Are you preparing a celebration? You've chosen a really exquisite wine, no mistake! But anyway, I haven't tried the excellent beverage for some time now. It's because you can only get it in Alvaron, the royal city, these days. The merchants are not willing to risk a loss of such precious goods by transporting it here. Thus I don't think you can get Chateau de Trebrechette here in the city.
I'm looking for the missing Raquel Gielwitch. Do you know anything about her?

The disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch is a sad event. And she's not the only one who has disappeared—there are a few more young girls missing in Glatzburg and its surroundings. To tell you the truth, I don't think we will ever find any of those girls alive. The times are too bad to rely on false hopes. But the kidnapper must be found, that's obvious. We must stop him. I can't allow crimes like that to go unpunished in my city. The investigation, unfortunately, hasn't revealed anything yet.
Why do you think the girls were kidnapped by someone, Grand Duke? Isn't it possible they were just killed? For example by some monsters?

Of course it would be easier to take the explanation involving some beasts killing the girls but I don't think that would help much. We must find out what really happened and I'm sure the girls were kidnapped and that there is a single culprit. The investigation will show.
Goodbye, knight. And be careful what you do here in Glatzburg—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?!
The fact that you are the royal governor of the city won't stop me, Grand Duke! Answer my question or you'll be sorry. I swear to God!
It's very important that you answer, Grand Duke. Please cooperate with me.
You are the wisest and the most important man in the city, Grand Duke. Your opinion is very valuable. Please answer my question.
Of course, knight. Ask Sheriff Smith. He'll tell you everything you need to know.
Thank you, Grand Duke. Can I now ask you a few questions?
As you wish, knight. But please remember that I'm very busy!
Thank you, Grand Duke. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. And be careful about what you do while you're here—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
Is there a reward offered for catching him?
When did he become such a brutal monster and a heretic?

As far as I can remember it was two years ago. It was the time the plague was almost over and his relatives were amongst the last victims. He lost them all—his father, sister, wife and two sons. I remember he brought them on a wagon in front of the Bishop's Temple and started to call on God to return his family to him because he was a true faithful.
What a dramatic fate. And what happened next?

The fourth day at dawn he awoke raving with madness and started to curse God in such a terrible way that we had to send guards after him. That's when he probably went mad because he killed all the guards and ran away from the city. We didn't hear of him for the next couple of weeks but then he attacked and slaughtered a settlement near the city.

Soon he became the self-appointed ruler of the bandits around here although I think they joined him on their own will without him summoning them somehow. His devilish charisma and complete disregard for any feelings and values made him the perfect leader worth admiration and following.
Thank you, Grand Duke. I'd like to ask you a few questions now.
As you wish, knight. But remember that I don't have much time.
I have to go now, Grand Duke. Pleased to meet you.

By Saint Zigmund, it's him! I'd recognize his face amongst thousand of others—I dream about him almost every night! You did kill him, knight! Unbelievable... I must bow to you. You did what the best fighters couldn't do! I'm sure the death of Benthley of Welshrem will be a big blow into the face of all the bandit gangs around Glatzburg. I hope we will be able to make at least the royal roads safe again... thanks to you, knight. The whole city is indebted to you. As a token of our gratitude please accept the reward offered for the head of Benthley of Welshrem.
Goodbye, knight. And thank you one more time! But still be careful about what you do—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city, all right?
As you wish, Grand Duke. We'll see who's right in this case.
Yes, that's put nicely, knight—we'll see! And you'll see you won't like what you'll see! Goodbye!
I'm sure your wife is innocent, Grand Duke. But I must examine all suspicions—even if they concern your wife.
Don't be hypocritical, knight. If you were sure my wife was innocent, you wouldn't have arrested her. I'm telling you one more time—you are not getting away with that!
You're wasting my time, Grand Duke. This dialog is over!
You arrogant bastard! You're going to pay for that, trust me!
I'm a humble servant of God, Grand Duke.
Yes, I'm sure about that, knight. The sad thing is that this case might end my days in the office of the royal governor of the city.
I'm sorry about that. But maybe there is a way to prevent that...

Yes, maybe... maybe the heresy of my wife could be forgotten... if I found a decent and noble woman who would become my wife and her good reputation could improve my badly hurt status, I could hope that the consequences wouldn't be that severe... yes, that's the answer! I need to find a new wife from a good family to prove that my estate still trusts me. Can you help me there, knight? I'm not saying that it is all your fault that I'm looking for a new wife but you played your part in it...
You want me to find you a new wife? Actually, why not. We have a deal.
Excellent, knight. And please, don't take too long. But still be careful who you chose because if I don't manage to win the respect back my days in the position of the royal governor are over!
Trust me, Grand Duke. Goodbye.
We have a deal. Can I talk to you for a moment?
What's in it for me, Grand Duke?
I'm glad you asked, knight. Of course I would spare some gold. Don't worry.
I'm not a marriage broker. Sorry.
Well, as you wish. I'm not going to beg you.
Fine. Goodbye.
That's all right. Can I talk to you for a moment?
As you wish, knight. But my time is precious. What do you want to talk about?
I'm going to take the job. I'll find you a good wife.
That'd be nice of you, knight. Is there anything I can do for you?
Yes, I'd like to talk to you.
What's on your mind?
I'm a humble servant of God, Grand Duke. But enough talking about the case. I did what you've asked me to do. I found you a wife. I think you know her—it's Baroness Elisabeth van Singier.

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course I know her, knight! How could I have forgotten about her? Why didn't I think of her earlier—I wouldn't have had to bother you. Her husband died of plague two years ago and their house was burnt down on the Night of the Falling Stars. Then she went to live to her brother in Hillbrandt and I haven't heard of her since. But she will make an ideal wife—she's a noble, well educated, sociable, easy-going... and pretty and with a sad past. I must say that I've always liked her. But I couldn't show it because of my social status. It's a great choice, knight. But are you sure she will agree with the marriage?
Yes, Grand Duke. She agreed already.

Great, knight. That's all I could have wished for. Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, knight.
I did already, Grand Duke. Here she is.

My God! Elisabeth, is it really you? I didn't think I'd see you again. Thank you, knight, for your kindness. Here is the reward for you. And now excuse me, I must talk to Elisabeth. We have so much to talk about...
Yes, I know. Is there anything I can do for you?
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, I arrest you on suspicion of heresy and conspiring with dark powers against God and the King. You're coming with me!
What? You're willing to come voluntarily?! Will you not say anything to defend yourself?
And would that help? No. So why waste words, knight?
I'm glad you decided to cooperate, Grand Duke. You'll see that It's going to be better for both of us. Let's go.
Yes, I'm sure about that!
I can see you didn't stop at my wife... All right, let's go.
Yes, I'm sure about that.
Seeing you investigate my wife I though you knew what you were doing, knight. But obviously, I was wrong. All right then, let's go.
Your wife was convicted of heresy and treason. You are accused of the same crimes. Isn't there anything you can say to defend yourself?
Greetings, knight. I'm Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor of the city. What can I do for?
Pleased to meet you, Grand Duke. As far as I know you are the most noble and most powerful man in the city, aren't you?
Yes, that's right. I've been holding my office since 1210 which is more than thirteen years. But tell me, what can I do for you?
The question is if there's anything I can do for you, Grand Duke.

To tell you the truth I have problems everywhere I look—I don't know what to deal with first. I'd be pleased if you helped me with the damn lizard race that lives in the Devil's Caverns close to the ruins of Galibornium. There are rumors that the devils are again getting ready for one of their bloody raids and this time they are going to attack the city itself...
Can I ask you something?
Of course, knight. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.
Goodbye, Grand Duke.
Goodbye, knight. And be careful what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city!
I'd like to talk to you for a moment, Grand Duke.
As you wish, knight. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.
Nothing really, Grand Duke.
Pleased to meet you, Grand Duke. It must be difficult to keep order in these difficult times...
What do you mean? What times?
Well, I meant the problems the Scourges of God have brought since the Star of Doom appeared...

Sorry, knight, but solving the problems is a part of my work. I can't imagine administration of the city without problems. And as far as the Star of Doom is concerned and the rumors about the end of the world... I don't believe that. I think we have to catch and hang many bandits, thieves, murderers, villains, false prophets and cultists, but that's all. And of course we have to clean the Realm of all the hellspawns that have come lately nobody knows from where. But that's all.
So you don't believe the Scourges of God means the end of the world? And that God has turned away from us? Do you really not believe that?

I believe that when I raise the taxes so that the treasury is not empty there will be many saying it's the end of the world. I believe that if regiments don't cruise the roads catching the bandits, they will multiply like rabbits. I believe that if a new star appears in the sky the astrologists and theologians have something to do, something to write books and essays about. That's all I wanted to say.
But that's a blasphemy!
I don't know, knight, I'm not an expert on religion and faith. Try talking to Cardinal Truncquillius about this topic—I'm sure his answer will make you happy.
You obviously are a pragmatic, Grand Duke.

I don't know, knight... hard to say. I just don't believe that if I start to run around with he Holy Scripture in my hands shouting that the end of the world was coming it'd help keep order in the city. That's all.
Are there more of you with similar... opinions, Grand Duke?
I don't know, knight, I don't care about the opinions of the others too much—as long as they're not illegal!
Can I talk to you for a moment, Grand Duke? I have a few questions.
Goodbye, Grand Duke. I have duties to attend to.
Me too, knight. And be careful about what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
If you are the governor of the city then you will probably be able to tell me about the problems you are facing here...
What do you mean, knight? What kind of problems do you mean?
You have to tell me, Grand Duke. The times are bad and I would like to know what torments the city. Maybe I would be able to help...

Well, you might, that's true... I don't know what exactly you want to hear about, but we've had lot of problems with the bandits lately. The so called Scourges of God took everything from some people and they now think it's right to take from those who have something left. And because the army is not big enough there's nothing we can do about them. They are hiding around the royal roads and even if we do all we can it's still not enough.

The worst thing is that they have joined a private army of a powerful brigand. His word is law they obey and they are willing to fulfill his craziest order without the wink of an eye. He lost his humanity. He doesn't kill for money but for killing. Sometimes I think he's not a human. He kills women, children and the elderly as well. He attacked a nearby convent and cut off the hands of all the priestesses so they couldn't pray. And then he drove them to the city walls to show us that praying was good for nothing. Can you imagine the horror, knight?
What's the butcher's name, Grand Duke?

Benthley of Welshrem the Bloody Butcher. He comes from a family of knights, they used to live near Glatzburg on a small, poor settlement. We've never had any problems with him—rather the other way around. He seemed to be a true faithful and a protector of the faith. But now...
I've heard of him, Grand Duke. It's Benthley of Welshrem, isn't it?
Exactly, knight. I can see that he has a reputation—unfortunately.
I know who you're talking about, Grand Duke. His name is Benthley of Welshrem. I talked to him.
Really? Then I'm surprised you are still alive! Didn't he try to kill you?
Yes, he did, Grand Duke. But fortunately wasn't successful.
At least you can see what a dangerous person we're dealing with here! It really is the bloody butcher they call him here.
Yes, you're right. Can I now ask you a few questions?
Is there a reward offered for killing him, Grand Duke?
I know who you're talking about, Grand Duke. His name is Benthley of Welshrem. Actually, it was his name, because he's not alive anymore. I killed him.
Are you kidding or are you serious, knight? Are you trying to tell me that you killed Benthley of Welshrem called the Bloody Butcher?
Yes, Grand Duke. This is his head as proof!
Yes, Grand Duke!
I don't believe that! I must see his head!
If you could really prove that you killed the worst bandit in the last three hundred years the whole of Glatzburg would be infinitely grateful, knight. Believe me!
Good. I would now like to ask you few questions, Grand Duke.
All right, as you wish, knight. But please remember that I really have a lot of work!
Greetings, knight. What brought you here. Is there anything you need?
I'd like to talk to you, Grand Duke.
As you wish, knight. Just remember that I have a lot of work. What's on your mind?
I brought you the head of Benthley of Welshrem as proof that he's never going to cause trouble again.
I killed Benthley of Welshrem, Grand Duke. Sheriff Smith told me to show you his head.
Did you kill Benthley of Welshrem called the Bloody Butcher? I can't believe my ears! The best fighters tried to kill him and we are still finding pieces of their bodies around the roads...
Here's his head, Grand Duke. Is it proof hard enough?
Nothing really, Grand Duke. Goodbye.
Are you mad, knight? What on Earth did you do? Arrested my wife and accused her of heresy... did you go out of your mind? What were you thinking? Can you explain that?!
Your wife has been accused of serious crimes, Grand Duke. I must look into all the circumstances of the case otherwise I won't be able to discover the truth.

Stop this expert talk, knight. You arrested her and made her, and me as well, look suspicious. Believe me, I'm going to destroy you before you have the time to say how sorry you are for that! Nobody's going to mess with my family. My wife is completely innocent!
Believe me, Grand Duke, it's nothing serious, it's just routine. Your wife will be back home soon.

Stop it, knight. You arrested her and made her, and me as well, look suspicious. Believe me, I'm going to destroy you before you have the time to say how sorry you are for that! Nobody's going to mess with my family. My wife is completely innocent!
Be careful what you're saying, Grand Duke. I could arrest you as well!

What an insolence! Nobody dares treat me like that. Believe me, I'm going to destroy you before you have the time to say how sorry you are for that! Nobody's going to mess with my family. My wife is completely innocent!

Knight, tell me that it's not true! Tell me that it's just a bad dream I'm going to wake up from in the morning and everything will be as it used to be! I can't believe my own wife could be a heretic!
Unfortunately it's the truth, Grand Duke. There's nothing we can do about it!

It's my fault that in all the years of my marriage I wasn't able to recognize that I was having a devil in my house! But it's too late to do anything about that. I must get over it somehow. To tell you the truth, I never really loved Yulliette. It was a political marriage as it usually is amongst the nobility. But still her death means terrible complications for me, knight. You can certainly imagine the consequences the scandal will have on my position as the royal governor of the city! I can already hear all the schemers and intriguers in the royal court making plans to get me out of their way as soon as possible...

Yes, maybe the heresy of my wife could be forgotten... if I found a decent and noble woman who would become my wife and her good reputation could improve my badly hurt status, I could hope that the consequences would not be that severe... yes, that's the answer! I need to find a new wife from a good family to prove that my estate still trusts me. Can you help me there, knight? I'm not saying that it is all your fault that I'm looking for a new wife but you played your part in it...
I'm glad you are considering it, knight. I wouldn't spare on gold, of course—be sure of that.
What are you doing here, knight? Get out of here or I'll have you kicked out like a rotten beggar!
Not so fast, Grand Duke. I want to ask you a few questions.
Go to hell with your questions, knight. I don't have to answer anything. And if you want to start with some legal talk I'm warning you that my dogs don't understand legal analyses and disputations!
In the case of your wife there was nothing I could do but arrest her, Grand Duke. The evidence speaks clearly. Please don't make it worse than it is.

Are you saying that I'm making it worse? Was it me who came to arrest my wife and accused her of heresy? Do you realize the situation I'm in? The wife of the royal governor of Glatzburg accused of heresy? I can already hear the slander spreading across the city! Go away, knight before I get really mad!
As you wish, Grand Duke. Goodbye!

Hello, knight. Have you found a good wife for me already? The longer it takes the bigger the chance is that they remove me from my office... You can't imagine how quickly they make their schemes in the royal court—especially now that the King is in... a difficult situation and gets influenced by the people around him easily.
I'm sorry, Grand Duke, I haven't found a wife for you yet.
Then keep trying, knight.
Of course, Grand Duke. Do you have time right now? I have a few questions...
Of course, Grand Duke. Goodbye.
Yes, Grand Duke, I think I found a good wife for you. I believe you know her—it's Baroness Elisabeth van Singier, the wife of the ex royal vice-governor.

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course I know her, knight. How could I have forgotten about her? Her husband died of plague two years ago and their mansion was burnt down on the Night of the Falling Stars. She lost everything so she left to go to her brother to the North of the Realm. I haven't heard of her since. It's true that she'd make an excellent wife—she's of a noble origin, well educated, sociable, easy-going, faithful... and pretty and she had a difficult past. I must say that I've always liked her. But my social position prevented me from showing it. It really is a great choice, knight. But do you think she'd agree with the marriage? She can still be mourning her husband as a decent woman from a good society should...
She's not mourning anymore, Grand Duke. And she agrees with the marriage.

Really? That's great, knight! That's all I could wish for. Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, knight, so we can get married as soon as possible.
I did already, Grand Duke. Baroness Elisabeth van Singier is here already.

Good heavens! Elisabeth, is it really you?! I didn't think I would ever see you again. Thank you, knight, for your help. Here is the reward for your work. And now please excuse us, me and Elisabeth must talk. We have so much to talk about...

What do you want, knight? I don't have much time... Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, knight.
As you wish, knight. But be brief, all right?
I was just passing by, Grand Duke. Goodbye.
Hello, knight. How are you doing? I want to thank you one more time for finding Elisabeth for me. She will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. Is there anything I can do for you?
I don't see a problem in it, knight. What do you need to know?

Hello, knight. I must say that the results of your investigation are worse than my deepest fears. I thought it would end with revealing and executing my wife but I was wrong—which doesn't happen too often. Who would think that the Curial Inquisitor Cardinal Truncquillius was a heretic too. Terrible...
I agree with you, Grand Duke. The times we live in are very difficult. There's not many things we can be sure about.
That's true. Anyway, the whole city is indebted to you. If it wasn't for you, who knows how it all would have ended...
Hello, Grand Duke. I wanted to excuse myself for the misunderstanding we had...
What misunderstanding do you mean, knight? I don't know about any misunderstanding. Not counting that you arrested me and accused me of heresy!
Yes, that's exactly what I'm talking about, Grand Duke. I'm deeply sorry!

I accept your excuse, even though it doesn't change what happened. But that's life and there's no point in believing that if you are a governor of a city you avoid problems like that. Not nowadays. After all, you were only doing your duty, RIGHT?!
I was just doing my duty. It was perfectly legal.
Yes, it certainly was. You can do this either well or badly or according to the law. But enough of that, it's over and there's no point in returning to it. After all, you were only doing your duty.
Don't complain. It could have ended up worse. You should be glad you are still alive!
Yes, you are certainly right, knight. I'm not going to return to it, if you wish. It's a closed chapter. After all you were only doing your duty.

Hello, knight. Did you manage to find me a good wife? The longer it takes the bigger the chance I'm removed from my office. You can't imagine how quickly they make their schemes in the royal court—especially now that the King is in... a difficult situation and gets influenced by the people around him easily.
I'm sorry, I haven't find any wife yet, Grand Duke.
Sure, Grand Duke. Do you have a minute? I'd like to as you a few questions...

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course, I know her, knight! How could I have forgotten about her? Why didn't I think of her earlier—I wouldn't have had to bother you. Her husband died of plague two years ago and their house was burnt down at the Night of the Falling Stars. I haven't heard of her since. But she will make an ideal wife—she's a noble, well educated, sociable, easy-going... and pretty and has a sad past. I must say that I've always liked her. But I couldn't show it because of my social status. It's a great choice, knight. But are you sure she will agree with the marriage?
Greetings, knight. How are you doing? I wanted to thank you one more time for finding Elisabeth for me. She will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Greetings, knight. What can I do for you?
All right, knight. But, please, be brief. I have a lot of work.
Thank you. Is there anything else you need to help with—except for Benthley of Welshrem?
I understand. Is there anything else you need to help with—except for Benthley of Welshrem?
Thank you. Is there anything else you need to help with?

Whether it is true or not, I'd like to prevent it. Supposedly there is a chief whom the rest serves. And I want the stinking hellspawn dead. I'm sure it will stop their attacks on my lands. Bring me his heart and you will get a nice reward in gold.
All right, we have a deal, Grand Duke.
Great! I knew I could ask you for help with this. And you didn't let me down. Is there anything I can do for you in return?
I'm sorry I'm not a monster hunter...
I understand. I thought you would answer that way. Forget it. What can I do for you?
Well... Is there anything I could help you with in your difficult job?
I brought you the Chief Zargh's heart, Grand Duke. That is, well that was, the infamous leader of the hellspawns in the Devil's Caverns.

Good heavens... the smell. Let me see? Terrible... only a real Beelzebub could have a heart like this... I'm really happy about this, knight. I'm sure the death of their chief will stop them in their attacks for some time—if you left any of them alive. Here is the reward I promised.
I thank you, knight. Now I have one problem less. Is there anything I can do for you?
Go to hell with the heart, knight. I feel like setting my dogs on you! Get out of my sight, you're making me sick!
You're lucky, Grand Duke—the leader of the hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns is dead. This is his heart!
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even paladins rob innocent people! Shame!

Excuse me? Did I understand you correctly, Father? You want to acquit Tinthan of the theft? You must be kidding! I must remind you that there was an eyewitness. Tinthan is probably going to be sentenced to death and the evidence is clear. There's no doubt about it!
You're welcome, Father. I really have no idea where I could have damaged the cloak...
I'm sorry, Grand Duke, I can't do that. It's a part of the investigation which is—as you certainly know—closed to the public.
As you wish, Father. I'm going to find out myself.

What do I think about the crisis? As an official of the Realm I must say that it's a disaster. A catastrophe. The Scourges of God that struck the Realm caused damage which will take years to repair. The population is decreasing, property is being damaged, the harvests are bad, the cattle are dying... and it's going to take years, maybe even decades to repair. People don't have the money to pay taxes so there is no money in the treasury. If there is no money the Realm is going down and it becomes an easy prey. I'll tell you something, Father, it will be primarily our children who will suffer the consequences of the Scourges of God—if they survive of course.

I'm not a priest, Father, so I'll leave this part of the problem to the more competent. Of course I've heard people saying that this was the end of the world and the Scourges of God was just its forerunner. I know the Holy Scripture, the Apocalypse and saint Ezechiel—but still, who can say that this is the end of the world? It's not a question I am competent to answer. I have been authorized to administer this land and I can see the effect of the plague, the famine, the rain of fire, the coming of the beasts, the loss of faith and the heresy—and of course the constant decrease in tax revenues. Glatzburg treasury is completely empty and there is no hope it will get better anytime soon. That's what I call a crisis!

I have no idea, Father, whether there will be a war or not. As far as commanding the Glatzburg regiment is concerned I only obey the orders of the First Knight from Alvaron. The orders are speaking clearly—get the regiment ready, draft and train new recruits, prepare the cavalry and the charioteers, replenish supplies and wait. And that's exactly what I'm doing—even though I must admit that it's a difficult thing to do without introducing extra taxes. I can't take from people what they don't have... and still I have to obey orders. The rumor has spread quickly and people are afraid. And I don't blame them—war is a terrible thing.
I have no idea, Father. I'd be happy if I could use the regiment against the brigands that torment Glatzburg. But the orders speak clearly—be ready. So all I can do is await more orders.

To tell you the truth I have a few suspicions of heresy. But I have no proof so I'd rather not mention them. For my own safety. I don't want to be accused of using the Inquisition to reach my own aims.
So many things have happened in Glatzburg lately, Father, that I don't know where to begin.
It's a part of my mission, Grand Duke.

Oh yes, sure... the mission of the Holy Inquisition, I forgot. The ways of the Lord are unpredictable. But to answer your question and avoid suspicion of resisting the Inquisition—I've never heard of a noble named Fae'Darlion, which of course, doesn't mean the tomb couldn't be hidden somewhere in my cellar. Glatzburg is surrounded by many relics of the past including some relics older than Ereborn. There are a few books in my library which deal with the relics of the Thron and Elenian Empires and they say that many of those relics can be found in Glatzburg and its surroundings.

Can't help you with that, Father. You'll have to look around the city, search through the woods, meadows and swamps or climb the rocks. But be careful about the dangers you can encounter there. I don't want to be solving another case of a mysterious disappearance or of a brutal murder.

Strangely, there are not many suspicions, Father. Of course they blame it all on the heretics and the infernal powers but that's a weak explanation. There are priest walking the streets of the city and their prayers and rituals should be banishing the hellspawns—as they did until recently. It's not clear why the undead appear. I believe, however, that Sheriff Smith will be able to deal with it. He's a person you can rely on.

I know which hammer you're talking about and of course I've heard that is was buried somewhere together with the rest of Bonhart von Drichtmaul's property. I found a few reports of the event in the municipal chronicle. But none of them gives any details as to where the hammer could be. So I can't help you in your investigation, Father.

I'm not going to ask what you need the wine for, Father. You'd certainly say something about your holy mission. But anyway, I haven't tried the excellent beverage for some time now. It's because you can only get it in Alvaron, the royal city, these days. Merchants are not willing to risk the loss of such precious goods by transporting it here. So I don't think you can get Chateau de Trebrechette here.
Goodbye, Father. And be careful what you do here in Glatzburg—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?!
Of course, Father. Ask Sheriff Smith. He'll tell you everything you need to know.
As you wish, Father. But please remember that I'm very busy!
Goodbye, Father. And be careful about what you do while you're here—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
As you wish, Father. But remember that I don't have much time.

By Saint Zigmund, it's him! I'd recognize his face amongst thousand of others—I dream about him almost every night! You did kill him, Father! Unbelievable... I must bow to you. You did what the best fighters couldn't do! I'm sure the death of Benthley of Welshrem will be a big blow into the face of all the bandit gangs around Glatzburg. I hope we will be able to make at least the royal roads safe again... thanks to you, Father. The whole city is indebted to you. As a token of our gratitude please accept the reward offered for the head of Benthley of Welshrem.
Goodbye, Father. And thank you one more time! But still be careful about what you do—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city, all right?
Yes, that's put nicely, Father—we'll see! And you'll see you won't like what you'll see! Goodbye!
Don't be hypocritical, Father. If you were sure my wife was innocent, you wouldn't have arrested her. I'm telling you one more time—you are not getting away with that!
Yes, I'm sure about that, Father. The sad thing is that this case might end my days in the office of the royal governor of the city.

Yes, maybe... maybe the heresy of my wife could be forgotten... if I found a decent and noble woman who would become my wife and her good reputation could improve my badly hurt status, I could hope that the consequences wouldn't be that severe... yes, that's the answer! I need to find a new wife from a good family to prove that my estate still trusts me. Can you help me there, Father? I'm not saying that it is all your fault that I'm looking for a new wife but you played your part in it...
Excellent, Father. And please, don't take too long. But still be careful who you chose because if I don't manage to win the respect back my days in the position of the royal governor are over!
I'm glad you asked, Father. Of course I would spare some gold. Don't worry.
As you wish, Father. But my time is precious. What do you want to talk about?
That'd be nice of you, Father. Is there anything I can do for you?

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course I know her, Father! How could I have forgotten about her? Why didn't I think of her earlier—I wouldn't have had to bother you. Her husband died of plague two years ago and their house was burnt down on the Night of the Falling Stars. Then she went to live to her brother in Hillbrandt and I haven't heard of her since. But she will make an ideal wife—she's a noble, well educated, sociable, easy-going... and pretty and with a sad past. I must say that I've always liked her. But I couldn't show it because of my social status. It's a great choice, Father. But are you sure she will agree with the marriage?

Great, Father. That's all I could have wished for. Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, Father.

My God! Elisabeth, is it really you? I didn't think I'd see you again. Thank you, Father, for your kindness. Here is the reward for you. And now excuse me, I must talk to Elisabeth. We have so much to talk about...
And would that help? No. So why waste words, Father?
Seeing you investigate my wife I though you knew what you were doing, Father. But obviously, I was wrong. All right then, let's go.
Greetings, Father. I'm Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor of the city. What can I do for?
Of course, Father. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.
Goodbye, Father. And be careful what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city!
As you wish, Father. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.

Sorry, Father, but solving the problems is a part of my work. I can't imagine administration of the city without problems. And as far as the Star of Doom is concerned and the rumors about the end of the world... I don't believe that. I think we have to catch and hang many bandits, thieves, murderers, villains, false prophets and cultists, but that's all. And of course we have to clean the Realm of all the hellspawns that have come lately nobody knows from where. But that's all.
I don't know, Father, I'm not an expert on religion and faith. Try talking to Cardinal Truncquillius about this topic—I'm sure his answer will make you happy.

I don't know, Father... hard to say. I just don't believe that if I start to run around with he Holy Scripture in my hands shouting that the end of the world was coming it'd help keep order in the city. That's all.
I don't know, Father, I don't care about the opinions of the others too much—as long as they're not illegal!
Me too, Father. And be careful about what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
What do you mean, Father? What kind of problems do you mean?

The worst thing is that they have joined a private army of a powerful brigand. His word is law they obey and they are willing to fulfill his craziest order without the wink of an eye. He lost his humanity. He doesn't kill for money but for killing. Sometimes I think he's not a human. He kills women, children and the elderly as well. He attacked a nearby convent and cut off the hands of all the priestesses so they couldn't pray. And then he drove them to the city walls to show us that praying was good for nothing. Can you imagine the horror, Father?
Exactly, Father. I can see that he has a reputation—unfortunately.
Are you kidding or are you serious, Father? Are you trying to tell me that you killed Benthley of Welshrem called the Bloody Butcher?
If you could really prove that you killed the worst bandit in the last three hundred years the whole of Glatzburg would be infinitely grateful, Father. Believe me!
All right, as you wish, Father. But please remember that I really have a lot of work!

What do you want, Father? I don't have much time... Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, Father.
As you wish, Father. But be brief, all right?
Hello, Father. How are you doing? I want to thank you one more time for finding Elisabeth for me. She will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. Is there anything I can do for you?
I don't see a problem in it, Father. What do you need to know?

I thought it would end with revealing and executing my wife but I was wrong—which doesn't happen too often. Who would think that the Curial Inquisitor Cardinal Truncquillius was a heretic too. Terrible...
What misunderstanding do you mean, Father? I don't know about any misunderstanding. Not counting that you arrested me and accused me of heresy!
Yes, you are certainly right, Father. I'm not going to return to it, if you wish. It's a closed chapter. After all you were only doing your duty.

I understand. You inquisitors chase heretics not monsters. Forget it. What can I do for you?
