I thank you, Father. Now I have one problem less. Is there anything I can do for you?
Go to hell with the heart, Father. I feel like setting my dogs on you! Get out of my sight, you're making me sick!

Excuse me? Did I understand you correctly, sir? You want to acquit Tinthan of the theft? You must be kidding! I must remind you that there was an eyewitness. Tinthan is probably going to be sentenced to death and the evidence is clear. There's no doubt about it!
You're welcome, sir. I really have no idea where I could have damaged the cloak...
I'm sorry, Grand Duke, I can't do that. I'm pledged to stay silent about it.
As you wish, sir. I'm going to find out myself.

What do I think about the crisis? As an official of the Realm I must say that it's a disaster. A catastrophe. The Scourges of God that struck the Realm caused damage which will take years to repair. The population is decreasing, property is being damaged, the harvests are bad, the cattle are dying... and it's going to take years, maybe even decades to repair. People don't have the money to pay taxes so there is no money in the treasury. If there is no money the Realm is going down and it becomes an easy prey. I'll tell you something, sir, it will be primarily our children who will suffer the consequences of the Scourges of God—if they survive of course.

I'm not a priest, sir, so I'll leave this part of the problem to the more competent. Of course I've heard people saying that this was the end of the world and the Scourges of God was just its forerunner. I know the Holy Scripture, the Apocalypse and saint Ezechiel—but still, who can say that this is the end of the world? It's not a question I am competent to answer. I have been authorized to administer this land and I can see the effect of the plague, the famine, the rain of fire, the coming of the beasts, the loss of faith and the heresy—and of course the constant decrease in tax revenues. Glatzburg treasury is completely empty and there is no hope it will get better anytime soon. That's what I call a crisis!

I have no idea, sir, whether there will be a war or not. As far as commanding the Glatzburg regiment is concerned I only obey the orders of the First Knight from Alvaron. The orders are speaking clearly—get the regiment ready, draft and train new recruits, prepare the cavalry and the charioteers, replenish supplies and wait. And that's exactly what I'm doing—even though I must admit that it's a difficult thing to do without introducing extra taxes. I can't take from people what they don't have... and still I have to obey the orders. The rumor has spread quickly and people are afraid. And I don't blame them—war is a terrible thing.
I have no idea, sir. I'd be happy if I could use the regiment against the brigands that torment Glatzburg. But the orders speak clearly—be ready. So all I can do is await more orders.

To tell you the truth I have a few suspicions of heresy. But I have no proofs so I'd rather not mention them for the sake of my own safety. I don't want to be accused of using false accusations to reach my own aims.
So many things have happened in Glatzburg lately, sir, that I don't know where to begin.

Can't help you with that, sir. You'll have to look around the city, search through the woods, meadows and swamps or climb the rocks. But be careful about the dangers you can encounter there. I don't want to be solving another case of a mysterious disappearance or of a brutal murder.

Strangely, there are not many suspicions, sir. Of course they blame it all on the heretics and the infernal powers but that's a weak explanation. There are priest walking the streets of the city and their prayers and rituals should be banishing the hellspawns—as they did until recently. It's not clear why the undead appear. I believe, however, that Sheriff Smith will be able to deal with it. He's a person you can rely on.

I know which hammer you're talking about and of course I've heard that is was buried somewhere together with the rest of Bonhart von Drichtmaul's property. I found a few reports of the event in the municipal chronicle. But none of them gives any details as to where the hammer could be. So I can't help you in your investigation, sir.

Are you preparing a celebration? You've chosen really an exquisite wine, no mistake! But anyway, I haven't tried the excellent beverage for some time now. It's because you can only get it in Alvaron, the royal city, these days. The merchants are not willing to risk a loss of such precious goods by transporting it here. Thus I don't think you can get Chateau de Trebrechette here in the city.
Goodbye, sir. And be careful what you do here in Glatzburg—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?!
Of course, sir. Ask Sheriff Smith. He'll tell you everything you need to know.
As you wish, sir. But please remember that I'm very busy!
Goodbye, sir. And be careful about what you do while you're here—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
As you wish, sir. But remember that I don't have much time.

By Saint Zigmund, it's him! I'd recognize his face amongst thousand of others—I dream about him almost every night! You did kill him, sir! Unbelievable... I must bow to you. You did what the best fighters couldn't do! I'm sure the death of Benthley of Welshrem will be a big blow into the face of all the bandit gangs around Glatzburg. I hope we will be able to make at least the royal roads safe again... thanks to you, sir. The whole city is indebted to you. As a token of our gratitude please accept the reward offered for the head of Benthley of Welshrem.
Goodbye, sir. And thank you one more time! But still be careful about what you do—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city, all right?
Yes, that's put nicely, sir—we'll see! And you'll see you won't like what you'll see! Goodbye!
Don't be hypocritical, sir. If you were sure my wife was innocent, you wouldn't have arrested her. I'm telling you one more time—you are not getting away with that!
Yes, I'm sure about that, sir. The sad thing is that this case might end my days in the office of the royal governor of the city.

Yes, maybe... maybe the heresy of my wife could be forgotten... if I found a decent and noble woman who would become my wife and her good reputation could improve my badly hurt status, I could hope that the consequences wouldn't be that severe... yes, that's the answer! I need to find a new wife from a good family to prove that my estate still trusts me. Can you help me there, sir? I'm not saying that it is all your fault that I'm looking for a new wife but you played your part in it...
Excellent, sir. And please, don't take too long. But still be careful who you chose because if I don't manage to win the respect back my days in the position of the royal governor are over!
I'm glad you asked, sir. Of course I would spare some gold. Don't worry.
As you wish, sir. But my time is precious. What do you want to talk about?
That'd be nice of you, sir. Is there anything I can do for you?

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course I know her, sir! How could I have forgotten about her? Why didn't I think of her earlier—I wouldn't have had to bother you. Her husband died of plague two years ago and their house was burnt down on the Night of the Falling Stars. Then she went to live to her brother in Hillbrandt and I haven't heard of her since. But she will make an ideal wife—she's a noble, well educated, sociable, easy-going... and pretty and with a sad past. I must say that I've always liked her. But I couldn't show it because of my social status. It's a great choice, sir. But are you sure she will agree with the marriage?

Great, sir. That's all I could have wished for. Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, sir.

My God! Elisabeth, is it really you? I didn't think I'd see you again. Thank you, sir, for your kindness. Here is the reward for you. And now excuse me, I must talk to Elisabeth. We have so much to talk about...
And would that help? No. So why waste words, sir?
Seeing you investigate my wife I though you knew what you were doing, sir. But obviously, I was wrong. All right then, let's go.
Greetings, sir. I'm Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor of the city. What can I do for?
Of course, sir. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.
Goodbye, sir. And be careful what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city!
As you wish, sir. I can spare some time, but please remember that I have lot of work to do.

Sorry, sir, but solving the problems is a part of my work. I can't imagine administration of the city without problems. And as far as the Star of Doom is concerned and the rumors about the end of the world... I don't believe that. I think we have to catch and hang many bandits, thieves, murderers, villains, false prophets and cultists, but that's all. And of course we have to clean the Realm of all the hellspawns that have come lately nobody knows from where. But that's all.
I don't know, sir, I'm not an expert on religion and faith. Try talking to Cardinal Truncquillius about this topic—I'm sure his answer will make you happy.

I don't know, sir... hard to say. I just don't believe that if I start to run around with he Holy Scripture in my hands shouting that the end of the world was coming it'd help keep order in the city. That's all.
I don't know, sir, I don't care about the opinions of the others too much—as long as they're not illegal!
Me too, sir. And be careful about what you do in the city—whatever your mission is. Remember that this is MY city! Understand?
What do you mean, sir? What kind of problems do you mean?

The worst thing is that they have joined a private army of a powerful brigand. His word is law they obey and they are willing to fulfill his craziest order without the wink of an eye. He lost his humanity. He doesn't kill for money but for killing. Sometimes I think he's not a human. He kills women, children and the elderly as well. He attacked a nearby convent and cut off the hands of all the priestesses so they couldn't pray. And then he drove them to the city walls to show us that praying was good for nothing. Can you imagine the horror, sir?
Exactly, sir. I can see that he has a reputation—unfortunately.
Are you kidding or are you serious, sir? Are you trying to tell me that you killed Benthley of Welshrem called the Bloody Butcher?
If you could really prove that you killed the worst bandit in the last three hundred years the whole of Glatzburg would be infinitely grateful, sir. Believe me!
All right, as you wish, sir. But please remember that I really have a lot of work!
Greetings, sir. What brought you here. Is there anything you need?
As you wish, sir. Just remember that I have a lot of work. What's on your mind?
Are you mad, sir? What on Earth did you do? Arrested my wife and accused her of heresy... did you go out of your mind? What were you thinking? Can you explain that?!

Stop this expert talk, sir. You arrested her and made her, and me as well, look suspicious. Believe me, I'm going to destroy you before you have the time to say how sorry you are for that! Nobody's going to mess with my family. My wife is completely innocent!

Stop it, sir. You arrested her and made her, and me as well, look suspicious. Believe me, I'm going to destroy you before you have the time to say how sorry you are for that! Nobody's going to mess with my family. My wife is completely innocent!
Sir, tell me that it's not true! Tell me that it's just a bad dream I'm going to wake up from in the morning and everything will be as it used to be! I can't believe my own wife could be a heretic!

It's my fault that in all the years of my marriage I wasn't able to recognize that I was having a devil in my house! But it's too late to do anything about that. I must get over it somehow. To tell you the truth, I never really loved Yulliette. It was a political marriage as it usually is amongst the nobility. But still her death means terrible complications for me, sir. You can certainly imagine the consequences the scandal will have on my position as the royal governor of the city! I can already hear all the schemers and intriguers in the royal court making plans to get me out of their way as soon as possible...

Yes, maybe the heresy of my wife could be forgotten... if I found a decent and noble woman who would become my wife and her good reputation could improve my badly hurt status, I could hope that the consequences would not be that severe... yes, that's the answer! I need to find a new wife from a good family to prove that my estate still trusts me. Can you help me there, sir? I'm not saying that it is all your fault that I'm looking for a new wife but you played your part in it...
I'm glad you are considering it, sir. I wouldn't spare on gold, of course—be sure of that.
What are you doing here, sir? Get out of here or I'll have you kicked out like a rotten beggar!
Go to hell with your questions, sir. I don't have to answer anything. And if you want to start with some legal talk I'm warning you that my dogs don't understand legal analyses and disputations!

Are you saying that I'm making it worse? Was it me who came to arrest my wife and accused her of heresy? Do you realize the situation I'm in? The wife of the royal governor of Glatzburg accused of heresy? I can already hear the slander spreading across the city! Go away, sir, before I get really mad!

Hello, sir. Have you found a good wife for me already? The longer it takes the bigger the chance is that they remove me from my office... You can't imagine how quickly they make their schemes in the royal court—especially now that the King is in... a difficult situation and gets influenced by the people around him easily.
Then keep trying, sir.

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course I know her, sir. How could I have forgotten about her? Her husband died of plague two years ago and their mansion was burnt down on the Night of the Falling Stars. She lost everything so she left to go to her brother to the North of the Realm. I haven't heard of her since. It's true that she'd make an excellent wife—she's of a noble origin, well educated, sociable, easy-going, faithful... and pretty and she had a difficult past. I must say that I've always liked her. But my social position prevented me from showing it. It really is a great choice, sir. But do you think she'd agree with the marriage? She can still be mourning her husband as a decent woman from a good society should...

Really? That's great, sir! That's all I could wish for. Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, sir, so we can get married as soon as possible.

Good heavens! Elisabeth, is it really you?! I didn't think I would ever see you again. Thank you, sir, for your help. Here is the reward for your work. And now please excuse us, me and Elisabeth must talk. We have so much to talk about...

What do you want, sir? I don't have much time... Elisabeth will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. And her sad history will make the marriage even more respectable and nobody will be able to doubt it! Bring her to me, sir.
As you wish, sir. But be brief, all right?
Hello, sir. How are you doing? I want to thank you one more time for finding Elisabeth for me. She will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. Is there anything I can do for you?
I don't see a problem in it, sir. What do you need to know?

Hello, sir. I must say that the results of your investigation are worse than my deepest fears. I thought it would end with revealing and executing my wife but I was wrong—which doesn't happen too often. Who would think that the Curial Inquisitor Cardinal Truncquillius was a heretic too. Terrible...
What misunderstanding do you mean, sir? I don't know about any misunderstanding. Not counting that you arrested me and accused me of heresy!
Yes, you are certainly right, sir. I'm not going to return to it, if you wish. It's a closed chapter. After all you were only doing your duty.

Hello, sir. Did you manage to find me a good wife? The longer it takes the bigger the chance I'm removed from my office. You can't imagine how quickly they make their schemes in the royal court—especially now that the King is in... a difficult situation and gets influenced by the people around him easily.

Elisabeth van Singier? Of course, I know her, sir! How could I have forgotten about her? Why didn't I think of her earlier—I wouldn't have had to bother you. Her husband died of plague two years ago and their house was burnt down at the Night of the Falling Stars. I haven't heard of her since. But she will make an ideal wife—she's a noble, well educated, sociable, easy-going... and pretty and has a sad past. I must say that I've always liked her. But I couldn't show it because of my social status. It's a great choice, sir. But are you sure she will agree with the marriage?
Greetings, sir. How are you doing? I wanted to thank you one more time for finding Elisabeth for me. She will make an excellent wife, I'm sure about that. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Greetings, sir. What can I do for you?
All right, sir. But, please, be brief. I have a lot of work.

Good heavens... the smell. Let me see? Terrible... only a real Beelzebub could have a heart like this... I'm really happy about this, sir. I'm sure the death of their chief will stop their attacks for some time—if you left any of them alive. Here is the reward I promised.
I thank you, sir. Now I have one problem less. Is there anything I can do for you?
Go to hell with the heart, sir. I feel like setting my dogs on you! Get out of my sight, you're making me sick!
What conditions do I have to meet to get dukedom, Grand Duke?

You're thinking of dukedom, Baron of Asherbalt? Then know that the title of a Duke can be bestowed only upon a Baron who proves his utter loyalty to the Realm and who accomplishes a task given to him. And pays 10 000 gp. for the entry into the Gold Book of the Realm, of course...
I'd like to get dukedom, Grand Duke.
Really? And do you deem yourself sufficiently loyal to the Realm, Baron of Asherbalt? Do you deem yourself ready to sacrifice yourself for your country?!
Yes, Grand Duke, I'm ready!

In that case listen carefully, Baron. I'm not sure if you've heard about it already, but the undead are walking the streets of the city at nights. You surely can imagine the panic those monstrous creatures have caused. Nobody dares to leave his house after dark and who does risks a very unpleasant death. I personally have put my mind to the case and I found out several things that alarmed me more than the presence of the undead inside the city walls. I especially noticed that they're not usual murders, committed by infernal monsters led only by an urgent lust for fresh blood. All the victims were robbed of all their valuables including brass buttons and gold teeth. At first sight it seems the undead murdered for money. But that's pure nonsense—undead bodies are led only by their murderous instinct and by nothing else.

That's why I've been so surprised by that. At first I thought the robberies are—in contrast to the murders—the work of someone else, but the testimonies of the witnesses speak otherwise. I couldn't believe there are some undead monsters which would intentionally collect valuables. And then I finally caught on to it. It's not the will of the undead that makes them steal, but the will of the one who summoned them into this world! There are many forbidden necromantic rites by which heretics are able to compel dead bodies to a new unclean life. The undead brought to life in this way obey their creator and may perform certain easy tasks for him. Fortunately that devilish ability of theirs is limited to the most basic orders, otherwise we couldn't be sure of anything. And that's why I'm sure there is a heretic standing behind the undead in the city streets and behind their attacks on the citizens. This way the heretic tries to get wealthy!
Exactly, Baron. If you manage to do that, it'll be clear evidence you're worthy to become a Duke.
Alright, Grand Duke, I'll accomplish the task. The culprit will be caught and punished!
I hope so, Baron...
Hmm... and with what evidence will you back up this accusation, Baron?

Great! I didn't hope you would manage to solve the case so quickly, Baron. There's nothing more to say. I'm free to bestow a title of a Duke upon you. That is if you have 10 000 gp. to pay for the entry into the Gold Book of the Realm...
I've found out who stands behind all the robberies perpetrated by the undead monsters wandering in the city streets at night, Grand Duke.
I'm bringing you 10 000 gp. to have my name written into the Gold Book of the Realm, Grand Duke. I hope you can bestow dukedom upon me now.
I have the money. There it is.
Never mind, Baron. In that case return to me when you have 10 000 gp. and a ducal title will be yours.

Great! By paying 10 000 gp. you got the right to be written into the Gold Book of the Realm. I hereby declare you Duke of Asherbalt! Congratulations, Duke! Accept this item as the symbol of your new standing!
When was the last time you saw your missing wife, Baron?

It was the night the orcs attacked the town, knight. Linda seemed to be rather nervous—she probably had a hunch which, unfortunately, proved to be correct. Late in the afternoon she left for town and never came back. God, I hope she's alright. What would I do without her? She means everything to me...
What do you think about the crisis that's spreading across the Realm?

The crisis is deep, knight. I would have never thought that so many disasters could happen in just a few years. The Scourges of God turned the Realm into ruins! My wife thinks... well... we think, that it's a consequence of corruptness and unfaithfulness of those who are supposed to be taking care of the Realm but they follow their own interests instead and who succumb to the powers of Satan. It's important to find those heretics and uproot them from our lands!
What kind of monsters can I encounter here in Hillbrandt?
What did you say, knight? That you wanted to encounter some kind of monsters? God, what kind of person are you?
No, I didn't mean I wanted to encounter them.
But that's exactly what you said!
Yes, but...

See? But I promise that I will never mention it to anyone. You have the word of a noble. Everybody makes mistakes and there's no need to make a big issue of it. I think you will confess to your sins soon and you will be forgiven. After all, you are God's knight!
Well, all right...
I'm looking for heretics here in Hillbrandt. Do you suspect anyone, Baron?

There is one suspicion, knight. My wife thinks—and of course I do too—that Duke Weinberg is not as innocent as he may seem. He has not been affected by the Scourges of God, knight! While the whole country is starving his granaries are always full. While everybody lost a few relatives to the plague, his family was spared. When the rain of fire fell in the spring, the flames burned everything around but his property stayed intact. But that's not everything!

Did you know that the van Gallagan family is much older and much more important than the Weinberg family? And yet it was Duke Weinberg who was designated a new liege lord of the town after the death of Grand Duke Derrick. It's obvious that he's signed a contract with devil. It's been burned by red-hot iron to his chest. That's why he wears a high collar surcoat even in the hottest summer days. I tell you, knight, he's a heretic. We just need to get some evidence against him... I should be the royal vice-governor of the town!
Anything unusual? My wife has disappeared, don't you remember? My dear Linda is gone! What am I to do without her. She was everything to me. Everything!
What do you know about Arthamon?
Arthamon? Isn't that the wax merchant from Glatzburg?
Uhm... forget it, Baron.
Aaah, you mean the rope-maker. No? Uhm... then I don't know...

The thief who stole the monstrance of Saint Orthenius must be caught and hanged. It's possible that there was more of them, so it's necessary to catch them all and get them all executed. We must show them that sacrilege won't go unpunished here!
I know exactly how has Bishop Quentinus disappeared, knight!
Really? How?
Without a trace, knight! That's how it was.
Uhm... thanks, Baron. You've been extremely helpful.
What do you think about the alleged murder of Natalia Reichmann which was supposedly committed by the landsknecht Olfghard?

What do I think of the murder of poor Natalia? My wife is sure the wild barbarian Olfghard did it. Yes, that's obvious. He did it for the jewelry her father was endowing her with. It's really a terrible case of a brutal murder. He also cut her body in pieces and buried them, so it can never be found.
How do you know what he's done with her body?

And what else could have he done with it? My wife says that if you want to hide a body of your victim so it's never found, cutting it to pieces is the best way. The small pieces rot easily or they are eaten by wild animals or by monsters. It's called a defensive dismembering of a corpse...
An interesting opinion...
Do you know how to remove a curse, Baron?
Remove a curse, you say? Have you tried a strong herb extract? My mother used to say that a strong herb extract can do miracles!
Your wife claims to be spending every night by your side. Can you confirm that?

I swear that my wife spends EVERY night by my side. She's a good wife and she knows her duties. I hold a very important position in the state administration and I can't afford any gossip. My wife lies by my side every night—you can't suspect her wondering around the town or anywhere else at nights.
Bishop Quentinus has supposedly seen your wife stealing a corpse at the cemetery. What do you think about it?

The Bishop's suspicion about my wife again? It's as ridiculous as it's absurd. I don't want you to occupy yourself with that any longer—my wife hasn't obviously done anything like that. I told that to d'Arvias—before he'd been disclosed as a heretic—and I'm telling it to you. My wife is a pious person and I want you to stop bothering her. There are others you should deal with. Otherwise I'll destroy you, understand, knight? Destroy!

Of course I know something about the murder of the merchant Ollmier, knight. He was murdered in the room he was renting in Truthorn's inn. His neck was cut through and his... well... penis cut off. Disgusting! I was there when they were examining the body and I must say that I almost threw my breakfast up. You don't see as much blood even in a slaughterhouse.

Who? Well, that's easy—demons of course. My wife thinks it was a succubus the merchant Ollmier was secretly fornicating with at night. He was an eccentric man and an adventurer, he led a wild life and it cost him his life. My wife says he brought a demon from his travels and it killed him here in Hillbrandt. That's why they didn't find any leads leading to a murderer. Because it was a demon.
You are a well educated man, Baron. You certainly know the consequences if you refuse to cooperate with me...
I know I'm not your favorite person in the world, Baron, but I would really appreciate your answer.

Dear Baron, I'm sure I don't have to explain the importance of mutual cooperation to such an educated and intelligent person—especially since cooperation from your side means giving one simple answer.

What?! What did you do? Accused Linda of heresy? But that's a complete nonsense! Where did you get that idea? How could you dare? Do you know who I am? Leave my house immediately. My wife is a faithful woman. You're going to pay for that, knight!
I'm here to uncover the truth, Baron. Goodbye.
Stop threatening me, Baron. Goodbye.
You better behave yourself, Baron, or you might follow her. Goodbye.
Thank you, Baron. Can I talk to you for a moment?
But of course, knight. What do you want to talk about?
Wait a minute, Baron. I'd like to talk to you.
OUT OF MY HOUSE!!!

I'm desperate, knight. My wife, Baroness Linda van Gallagan, got lost and she's been missing for some time. I asked Sheriff Contemburry to send his men to look for her around town but he refused. Said he needed his men in town, not spread all over the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Will you help me?
First I would like to know who you are, sir.
Forgive me, I was so upset I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Robert van Gallagan and I'm the royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt. Linda is my wife.
And did you try to find your wife yourself? Don't you know how to use a sword?
Me? Look for Linda? But then I could get killed by some wild monster. I can't risk losing my office!
If your wife is still alive I'm going to bring her back.
Then I'll repay you generously, knight.
When was the last time you saw your wife, Baron?

It was the night the orcs attacked the town, knight. Linda seemed to be rather nervous—she probably had a hunch which, unfortunately, proved to be correct. Late in the afternoon she left for the town and never came back. God, I hope she's alright. What will I do without her? She means everything to me...
If I find your wife, will there be any reward?
Of course, knight! If you manage to find Linda I'll repay you generously. Gold has no value for me.
I don't have the time to bother with the problems of all people in the town. Sorry.
Then I'm going to have to do without you, knight. Goodbye!
Wait, Baron. I would like to talk to you.
Well... as you wish. But be brief, all right? I don't have the whole day to chit-chat with you!
I found your wife, Baron. Here she is, alive and well.

Oh my God, Linda! I was so worried about you, honey. Are you all right? Thank you, knight. And of course you deserve a reward for your great deed—here you go. As you can see the van Gallagans know how to be grateful!
I found your wife, Baron. But unfortunately, I must arrest her on suspicion of heresy.
You wanna know something, Baron? I am looking for your wife already, but for a different reason... She's been accused of heresy.

What? Are you trying to tell me that my wife is a heresy suspect? That's a complete nonsense! My wife is one of the most religious people I've ever met. God knows what terrible things have happened to her and you come here telling me such terrible things instead of trying to save her. Find her and bring her back, that's all I'm asking and that's what I'm going to pay you for.
I'm sorry but I can't promise that. I have to find out whether the accusations are true.
Then leave my house immediately!
But of course, knight! If you managed to find Linda and bring her back I'd repay you generously. Gold has no value for me.
All right, I'll bring her back, Baron.
Thank you, knight. I knew one could always rely on a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Hello, Baron.
Did you find out what happened to my wife Linda, knight? I'm worried sick about her... If something's happened to her, It'd be the death of me!
I haven't found her yet, Baron.
Don't stop trying then, knight. Her life's definitely in danger!
Don't worry, Baron. Can I talk to you for a moment?
Of course, knight. Just don't waste much time because you could spend it looking for my wife.
Don't worry, Baron. Goodbye.
I found your wife, Baron. Here she is—alive and well.
You wanna know something, Baron? The situation has changed a bit. I'm still looking for your wife but for a different reason—she's been accused of heresy.

What? Are you trying to tell me that my wife is a heresy suspect? That's a complete nonsense. My wife is the most religious woman I've ever met. Of course, knight. I have nothing to do with the kidnappings, that's obvious. And the only way I'm connected to DiCerbio is by trying to get him to a trial. Take my advice, knight, don't believe a word he says!
I saw your wife, Duke, and I couldn't have missed that she was all bruised. When I asked her she hinted that you beat her up. Is that true?

What did she tell you? That I was hurting her?! I can't believe that! You know, knight, my wife is ill. She fell off a horse, got hurt and she's been mad since. She's always making things up, seeing things nobody else can see and says things my mind boggles at. But I'm a faithful man who wouldn't leave a person in need so I didn't put her in a convent which was what many had advised me to do but I'd rather take care of her myself.
And what about the bruises and welts?
My wife has been really weak since the accident and she often tumbles down. She's tumbled climbing the stairs a couple of times and hurt herself badly.
You're welcome, knight. I have nothing to hide.
I don't trust you, Duke. I'll watch out for you.
I have nothing to hide, knight.

Unfortunately, Glatzburg is ruled by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick. God knows that he doesn't deserve it. I mean, how long is it going to take before his true nature comes to light and the King stops him?
Don't you trust Grand Duke Heidrick, Duke?

First of all, I don't believe he's doing all that's in his might to improve the city. Maybe there is a reason and maybe the reason is not quite legal. There are certain people who believe he's acting in his own interest rather than taking care of the city. That's what I wanted to point out, knight.
It seems to me that you are not really objective when you're making these indirect accusations, Duke. No offense, but It'd be you who'd take up Grand Duke Heidrick's position if he were called off.

I see where you're heading, knight. It does look suspicious—a royal vice-governor accuses a royal governor of dilatoriness and of neglecting his duties and maybe of even worse things. Do you have any evidence against Grand Duke Heidrick?

The times are bad, that's true. I've never seen worse. But still I think Glatzburg—and the whole Ultherst—is going to get over it soon. Providing it's ruled by competent people who know something about ruling.

Look around, knight. The treasury of Glatzburg is empty and Grand Duke Heidrick isn't doing anything to change it. Am I supposed to sit and watch what's happening around? It's vital that we finish off the rogues and the heretics and we need an army for that. Since we can't use the royal army we must use the local militia. And such militia must be recruited and armed. Is Grand Duke Heidrick doing anything like that? No, he's not. He just keeps saying that people are poor and there's nothing to take from them. What a weakness.
I heard that there was a war brewing. Do you know any details?

But who should the war be against, Duke?
It doesn't matter, the enemy is not important. You can always find someone to send an army against. That's how it goes, knight!

Absolutely nothing. Corpses rage in the streets every night and he doesn't lift a finger!
And what do you suggest he should do, Duke?
Who, me? Well, I'd take steps! Stop their raging! Give orders to destroy them. Strike against them and uproot the evil seed from the city!
Oh... yes, sure.

It's a waste of money which is so scarce nowadays.
I must admit that I have a suspicion. But I have no proof so I'd rather not say anything.
Yes, that's understandable.

How is it possible that his property and his family have not been affected by the Scourges of God? And why isn't he doing anything to improve to situation of the city? Because I don't believe he's doing everything in his might. I tell you what I think—I think he likes it this way. I think he has a contract with the devil and he helps him ruin the Kingdom of God on Earth in exchange for riches. That's what I think!
Any evidence?
Oh... but thank you anyway.
Thank you, Duke.
You're welcome, knight. I'm a faithful servant of the Realm...

Normally, I wouldn't take it seriously but this spring the five paladins who were carrying out the investigation were murdered. So I'm afraid he really could have returned from the underworld. It looks like he did. If I were in executioner Flemberg's shoes I'd be more than worried—it was him who lead the execution.

No matter which hellspawn is behind the murder I'm going to make sure he pays for what he's done. I'm going to push Sheriff Smith until the murderer is found and the devil in him bathed in the Holy Water!

I remember a priest named Frederick living in Glatzburg some time ago. But that's all I know. If you really want to find out something about him ask somebody from the Glatzburg Diocese he belonged to.
You can't get any Chateau de Trebrechette here in Glatzburg, knight. Believe me..

Because the Grand Duke has never had a lack of anything, he's always had plenty while all the others were starving. That's why.

Better answer me now or I'll have to force you to do so.
You have all the right to dislike me, Duke. But I'm sure you don't need to love me to answer my question.

Go ahead, knight. What do you need to know?

So it hasn't been possible to purchase for some time here in Glatzburg. I'm sure, however, that Grand Duke Heidrick has a good supply hidden in his cellars.
Better answer me now, Duke, or I'll have to notify the Inquisition about your unwillingness to give a testimony.

I can hear a hidden admiration in your voice, sir. Oh yes, it is so—you admire the greatness of my plans. And my unbelievable strength. And above all—the unlimited power I'm soon going to have. Look at my great creation, my homunculus. He's the spitting image of His Highness King Edward, isn't he? To the last detail. The features of his face, the look of his eyes, the way he holds his head... it's simply him! And yet it's just a piece of clay... But I'm going to give it life now. It seems so simple and yet it has taken half of my life to find the right magical formula to give life to an nonliving matter!

Are you crazy, sir? Do you think that I'm going to surrender to a nobody such as you now that I've reached my goal? No, I'm not. On the contrary, I'm going to kill you and let your corpse rot here. Kill him my infernal servants. KILL HIM!
Of course, sir. Trust me.
Of course, sir. Anything you wish. What would you like to know?
Hello, sir. I haven't had the honor of meeting you yet. I'm Duke Rowan van Leerin, the royal vice-governor of Glatzburg.
My pleasure, sir. What's bringing you here? You're a noble, aren't you? Is there anything I can help you with?

Yes, I do. Are you offering me your help? That's very nice of you, sir. I really appreciate that. It's just that I can't think of anything I could ask you to do. Nothing I'm dealing with now needs your help. There is the case of the missing girls but master Dieter von Gelbendiel is looking into that.
No, I'm afraid not, sir. I'm working on some complicated and dangerous tasks but they concern the city treasury and taxing of the business guild in which, I'm afraid, you cannot help me.

You're right, sir. There's the income tax, the turnover tax, the import tax, the transport tax, the export tax, the storage tax, the sales tax, the purchase tax, the property tax... At least you can see what difficult tasks Grand Duke Heidrick gives me. But there's no way you can help me, sir.
A tax tax? Umm... not a bad idea! If somebody has the money to pay taxes, they will have the money to pay taxes from taxes, won't they? That's an excellent idea, sir!
You're welcome, sir. I can see you're an expert in taxes... Were you a noble I wouldn't want to be your subject!

Situation? You mean the terrible crisis we are facing—the crisis that has started a few years back in the Realm, right? As far as I can tell, the situation is serious, sir. Maybe it doesn't look like it but people are getting hopeless and desperate which is the first step to heresy. People are simply losing faith in God and satisfy their lowly drives by worshiping idols hoping it's going to save them. I've been doing everything to prevent that but my authority is limited. Grand Duke Heidrick, the royal governor of the city, keeps most power to himself, you see?

I'm saying it as if I wasn't sure that Grand Duke Heidrick's doing everything in his power for the city. Maybe there is a good explanation or maybe I'm just imagining things but there are some people who suspect him of acting in his own interest rather than in the interest of the city. I just wanted to bring your attention to the fact, sir. That's all.
No, you don't understand, sir. I was trying to imply that the Grand Duke is not doing everything to improve our lives. It almost looks like as if he liked the situation as it is!
But of course, sir, go ahead. I'd be happy to answer all your questions. What do you wish to know?
Hello, sir. How are you doing? Is there anything you need?
Go ahead, sir. What do you need to know?
Unfortunately, not, sir. I'm sorry. There's nothing I need to help with. But if something comes up I'll let you know. Trust me.

Paul Hammerhand is missing? Then he must have run away again, knight. It wouldn't be the first time. He's, well, how do you put it... a wild child. But I think he's not a bad boy. He's just neglected, I think. From time to time he joins me when I drive the Duke's herds to pasture. He's got a lot of dreams about the life of an adventurer. He likes to wander about in dangerous places such as the Dragon Rock. I told him several times to be careful and that he'd be sorry for that one day, but he never listened. If you're looking for him, try looking there...
I'm sorry, I'm not going to talk about that!

You see, knight, I don't buy many things. I don't have the money. As far as I know, the blacksmith Hammerhand sells weapons and armor. If you are interested in potions and magic items, try the herb healer Würtenrodt, the astrologist Brechthold or Father Dominicus. The innkeeper Truthorn and the stall-holder Brauchner sell and buy all kinds of things.
What do I think about the crisis? Well, I don't know about any crisis, knight. I'm only a herdsman, what would I know about a crisis. I don't even know what the word means.

There has always been loads of monsters here around Hillbrandt, knight. But it's true that it has gotten a lot worse the past few years. Strange monsters crawl out of their hideouts and eat anything that moves. Especially the Duke's sheep. I don't know where to drive them anymore to make sure nothing happens to them! The trolls are the worst, because they're made of wood and stone so the animals can't smell them. The trolls have always been here, that's true, but not like now. More and more of them are coming down the mountains as if something was attracting them here. And they hurl themselves at everything living they encounter.
Sheriff Contemburry should be paying out rewards for monsters, knight. So ask him, I don't know much.
Can you tell me one more time what you saw Judge Vallarian doing?

Early in the morning—it was still dark—I went for a walk to the palisades because I woke up early. There I saw Judge Vallarian entering the town and throwing something out to the trash dump at the palisades. He was making sure nobody could see him very carefully. Just out of curiosity, I went there to look what he was throwing out and I found the garnished dagger hilt I gave you. That's all, knight.

Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave, knight. It's been twenty years since he left this world and people used to say that he was going to return to fulfill his part of the contract he had with the Devil—and that's exactly what's happened. He wasn't exactly a good person, you see? Young girls would disappear in the town before he died and nobody ever found out what happened to them. Then later even some young boys disappeared. From time to time a body was found but it was so mutilated that nobody could tell whose body it was.

People were talking about terrible orgies he used to have in the church. It seems that he was getting drunk by the blood of young virgins and boys, fornicated with the devil and vilified the cross and the name of God. But then God finally punished him. One morning they found him dead in his bed, buried him properly in the local crypt and peace was restored. And now it seems he has returned. He wanders around the town, waiting. Nobody dares to go to the cemetery anymore because it's haunted by the awakened dead. What a horrible thing, knight.

Master Edmond d'Arvias would always treat me nice and he even helped me once when I was accused of stealing in the Truthorn's Inn. I don't think he'd do what they say he's done. And it's terrible things, they say. One could get burned for things like that. But most people think he's a devil who should be executed so that everything is the way it used to be and we're all better off.

I don't know anything about the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius, knight. But the people who stole it must have been devils because the priests who were praying for the salvation of the town in the church that night were found asleep so deep that nobody could wake them up in the morning.
I don't know whether Olfghard killed the young Reichmann or not. But he might have, I think, because people have gone completely wild nowadays.

Have you heard the legend of the Tree of Death? It's near Dragon's Rock and they say nasty things about it. Several hundred years ago at the times of the last of the Barbarian wars the defeated crowds of the pagan plunderers were running back North they came from many years before. They were mostly women, children and few warriors. A crowd like that got besieged by Duke Welliar's cavalry near Dragon Rock. The warriors were all killed and the women and children hid in a huge oak that stood there already. They surrendered and the Duke had them all hanged without mercy on the tree they were hiding in.

In the morning, when people from Hillbrandt came to bury them a surprise was waiting for them. The loops were empty and the tree looked as if it had died a long time ago. Since then people have believed that the souls of the unbaptized barbarians went into the trunk of the tree and have been waiting for the right time for revenge. The truth is that sometimes, when I drive the Duke's herd nearby the rock, I can hear unpleasant sounds and the animals get all frightened as well.
How good is your eyesight, good man?
Why are you asking about my sight, knight?

I was verifying your testimony concerning Judge Vallarian and he told me that he really wasn't in town that night and he returned in the morning, but he wasn't throwing out a dagger but a torn pair of gloves. Moreover, he said that you couldn't have seen him clearly because you can't see very well. Is that true?
Uh.. it is true, you reverence, my eyes are not very good anymore. But who else would be throwing out a broken dagger when you can have it repaired at the blacksmith's for a few gold pieces?
That is not your business. Answer my question!
It's true, knight, my eyes are not very good anymore.

Kurth Ollmier's death? Oh, that was a terrible murder, you know? They took him out in Joseph Truthorn's inn. And after they killed him they mutilated him. I saw the soldiers taking the corpse out in a sack. They were pale as if they'd seen a ghost even though they are the kind of people who must had seen a lot. It shook them a lot.
If you wanna know that, knight, it's gonna cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
Did you know, Ruphert, that refusing to cooperate with the Brotherhood of the Righteous is a severe crime? And do you know what we do with criminals? Don't make me show you!
I can see, Ruphert, that you don't like me and so you don't want to answer. But when you give it a thought, you'll find out that It'd be a good idea to answer.
You are not stupid, Ruphert. On the contrary—you seem to be very smart. That's why I don't understand why you don't want to answer my question.

You found her, knight! Thanks God Betty's back. The Duke would punish me severely if he found out one sheep of his herd was missing. In return, I'm going to tell you something which might help you with your investigation. Maybe it's a mistake and I'm playing with fire right now, but I must tell you because I haven't slept well since it happened. I keep thinking about it.

It was early in the morning after we had the terrible storm. I woke up early and I went to see what damage was done. It was still dark and people were still locked in their houses shaking with fear. There wasn't a living soul. I climbed up the palisades to be able to see well and I saw Judge Vallarian entering the town and throwing something out on the trash dump behind the palisades. It looked as if he didn't want to be seen. Then he left quietly but I couldn't get it out of my mind. I went there to see what it was he threw out.
And what was it?

You're not going to believe it, but this is what I found... a beautifully garnished dagger hilt. There was no blade, he must have broken it off somewhere. But still the hilt seemed to be pretty valuable and I didn't understand why Judge Vallarian would want to get rid of it. He must have had a good reason, I thought. So I kept the hilt thinking it might come in useful. I didn't tell anybody but you.
Are you trying to tell me that you are suspecting the inquisitorial Judge Vallarian of a crime?

I wouldn't dare, knight. I'm not suspecting anyone of anything, especially not the Inquisitorial Judge. I don't want any trouble. I just wanted to tell you what I saw. I'm sure it doesn't mean anything.
Alright, alright. Don't talk about it with anybody, understand? And I'm going to have to take the dagger, of course.
Of course, knight. I'm a humble servant of God.
You did the right thing telling me about it. But please don't mention to anybody what you've just told me. Can I take the dagger to examine it?
I don't have much to offer for your kindness, knight. But let's say I saw something which might interest you.
Sounds interesting. All right, I'll try to find the sheep.

God bless you, knight. I just hope it didn't go somewhere far from here... the surroundings of the town have been pretty dangerous lately. The damn orcs and the other hellspawns are even endangering the town now!
If you really know something important which I should know, you should tell me before it's too late.
Maybe I know something, maybe not. But unless the Duke's herd is complete I'm going to keep it to myself. Please try to understand, knight!
I'm sorry but I'm not going to help you find your sheep. Get a shepherd dog.
That's a pity. But maybe you'll change your mind later. I think you wouldn't refuse to help a neighbor in need.
Now I would like to ask you some questions, shepherd.
Of course, knight. What would you like to know from old Ruphert?
I think, good man, that I found your sheep. I sold it to the innkeeper Truthorn, however.

My God, no! Poor Betty! What have you done? He's gonna kill her and make mutton out of her. What am I going to tell Duke Weinberg? He's going to put me to pillory or maybe even at the stake. Go to Truthorn, knight, quickly, maybe it's not too late yet and Betty's still alive!
All right, I'll try to save her. I had no idea it was a Duke's sheep.
Oh my God, what a disaster! I hope Betty's all right.
Oh no, no, no! Poor Betty. What could have happened to her? Where could she have gone? I have always been so nice to her. Why did she have to do it to me? My dear girl!

Oh, excuse me, knight, I didn't see you. My name is Ruphert and I'm the municipal shepherd. I take care of the Duke's herds. It's a good job and I'm glad to have it. But right now I'm not too happy. I've lost my little Betty, you see?
Who's Betty? Your daughter?

Betty—my daughter? Oh God, no! I'm not a sodomite! I'm a truly faithful person, knight, I swear by God. Betty is one of the Duke's sheep. Could you please try to help me find her? If the Duke finds out a sheep from his herd is missing he'll have me whipped and put me to pillory, I know that!
I'll try to find the sheep, good man. Don't worry.
God bless you, knight. If you manage to find it, there will be a reward for you. I don't have much to give, but I have a piece of information you could be interested in...
I'll see what I can do. What can you give me for my help?
Is this the sheep you're talking about, good man?
Have you found the damn sheep yet, knight?
I'm trying to but when it comes to the Duke's sheep I can't help being impatient. If the Duke finds out one of his sheep is missing...
What is it, knight?
Yes, I found her. Here she is.
Hello, knight. Did you change your mind about the Duke's lost sheep?
No, good man. I don't have time to help you in your shepherding. I look for criminals, not lost cattle...
All right, all right. Maybe you'll change your opinion later...
All right, I'll look for her.
I knew you were going to help me, knight. There is something holy in you!
We'll see. What would you give me for that?
I found the sheep, good man.
Thanks for the help with the damn sheep, knight. I hope I have been helpful as well... without causing any trouble. I hate causing trouble... especially to myself.
You're welcome. Can I talk to you for a moment?
Of course. What do you need to know, knight?
Goodbye, knight.
So, knight? Did you manage to save Betty? Or did the butcher Truthorn cut her throat and make mutton out of her?
I don't know yet, good man.
So what are you waiting for, knight? If he cuts her throat I'm gonna have to confess to the Duke and I don't think he'll be happy!
Unfortunately, I came late, good man...

Oh my God... my little Betty's mutton! What am I going to tell the Duke? He will want me to pay for the sheep or put me to pillory. What am I going to do? I don't have the money to pay for a whole sheep.
I'd be happy to pay for the sheep for you, good man.
Really? Then I'd be grateful until the day I die, knight. God bless you. Go to the Duke now and ask him to forgive me. I hope he'll forgive me if you'd be so kind and pay it up for me.
I'm not responsible for you losing the sheep, good man. You need to figure something out.
What a pity. But maybe you'll change your mind later and help a neighbor in need.
Hello, knight. Did you change your mind about that sheep? I really don't have money to pay it up to the Duke...
No, I didn't. It's not my problem. Will you answer some of my questions now?
As you wish, knight. What is it? What do you want to hear from poor old Ruphert?
All right, shepherd. I'll pay for the sheep for you.
Thank you, knight! Thank you! You saved me from the Duke's wrath!
No, shepherd, it's not my problem. Goodbye.
Goodbye, knight. I hope you'll have mercy with poor old Ruphert later...
Hello, knight. Did you talk to the Duke about the damn sheep? Did you pay for it?
No, I haven't spoken to him yet. I need to ask you some questions now.
As you wish, knight. What is it? What do you need to know?
I talked to the Duke, shepherd. You don't have to worry about his wrath anymore.

Oh, thank you, knight! Thank you! You saved me from a terrible punishment! I'm going to tell you something you might find useful in your investigations in return. Maybe I'm making a mistake and maybe I'm playing with fire but I must tell you because I haven't been able to sleep well since. I keep thinking about it.

What have you done, knight? You're killing the Duke's herd! I wouldn't have thought you would... What kind of person are you?! Do you know what the Duke is going to do to me? Oh my God, my poor sheep...

Maybe I know something, maybe not. But unless the Duke's herd is complete I'm going to keep it to myself. Please try to understand, noble lord!
Of course, noble lord. What would you like to know from old Ruphert?

My God, no! Poor Betty! What have you done? He's gonna kill her and make mutton out of her. What am I going to tell Duke Weinberg? He's going to put me to pillory or maybe even at the stake. Go to Truthorn, noble lord, quickly, maybe it's not too late yet and Betty's still alive!

Oh, excuse me, noble lord, I didn't see you. My name is Ruphert and I'm the municipal shepherd. I take care of the Duke's herds. It's a good job and I'm glad to have it. But right now I'm not too happy. I've lost my little Betty, you see?

Betty—my daughter? Oh God, no! I'm not a sodomite! I'm a truly faithful person, noble lord, I swear by God. Betty is one of the Duke's sheep. Could you please try to help me find her? If the Duke finds out a sheep from his herd is missing he'll have me whipped and put me to pillory, I know that!
God bless you, noble lord. If you manage to find it, there will be a reward for you. I don't have much to give, but I have a piece of information you could be interested in...
Have you found the damn sheep yet, noble lord?
Hello, noble lord. Did you change your mind about the Duke's lost sheep?
I knew you were going to help me, noble lord. There is something holy in you!
Thanks for the help with the damn sheep, noble lord. I hope I have been helpful as well... without causing any trouble. I hate causing trouble... especially to myself.
Of course. What do you need to know, noble lord?
Goodbye, noble lord.
So, noble lord? Did you manage to save Betty? Or did the butcher Truthorn cut her throat and make mutton out of her?
So what are you waiting for, noble lord? If he cuts her throat I'm gonna have to confess to the Duke and I don't think he'll be happy!
Really? Then I'd be grateful until the day I die, noble lord. God bless you. Go to the Duke now and ask him to forgive me. I hope he'll forgive me if you'd be so kind and pay it up for me.
Hello, noble lord. Did you change your mind about that sheep? I really don't have money to pay it up to the Duke...
As you wish, noble lord. What is it? What do you want to hear from poor old Ruphert?
Thank you, noble lord! Thank you! You saved me from the Duke's wrath!
Goodbye, noble lord. I hope you'll have mercy with poor old Ruphert later...
Hello, noble lord. Did you talk to the Duke about the damn sheep? Did you pay for it?
As you wish, noble lord. What is it? What do you need to know?

Oh, thank you, noble lord! Thank you! You saved me from a terrible punishment! I'm going to tell you something you might find useful in your investigations in return. Maybe I'm making a mistake and maybe I'm playing with fire but I must tell you because I haven't been able to sleep well since. I keep thinking about it.

What have you done, noble lord? You're killing the Duke's herd! I wouldn't have thought you would... What kind of person are you?! Do you know what the Duke is going to do to me? Oh my God, my poor sheep...
An intruder in Rwhan's camp! Kill him, slaves. Kill him!
As the First Prophet said—light the flame of the just wrath and start the purgative fire of death wherever it's needed!
Huh eh... what? What did you say?
I said I was going to kill you all!
Forgive me, oh mighty Rwhan, I got lost. I didn't mean to disturb you. I'll be going.
You're not going anywhere, human worm! Rwhan is going to kill you and feed on your flesh! Kill him slaves! Kill him!
Wait, Rwhan, there's no need to kill me. Take my gold and let me go.
Your gold? Hmm... Rwhan will think about it...
Sure, Rwhan, think about it. You are going to get my gold without any effort.
All right, Rwhan is going to take your gold and let you go, human worm!
A wise decision, Rwhan. I wouldn't be an easy prey. Let me go now.
Never! Did you really think Rwhan was going to let you go, human rat? Rwhan would rather return to the Accursed depths than let any of the human race live! Kill him, slaves! Kill him!
Enough of the madness, monster. As the First Prophet said—I'm going to purge this grounds of all evil!
I'm looking for the criminals who loot the graves at the municipal cemetery and in the surroundings of the city. Do you know anything about them?
Grave looters? Yes, I know something about the case, that's right. Actually, I know exactly who the criminal is, yes!
Who is it then?

It's a man who's name is Vick Length. He boasts to be an antiquities merchant but he is really a grave looter. He tries to sell me some jewels I know. I saw them at Baron Mansfeld's funeral—the deceased was wearing them. How could Length get them if not by looting the Baron's grave?
Are you sure it was Baron Mansfeld's jewelry? You could have made a mistake?
When it comes to jewels I never make mistakes, brave knight. They were Baron Mansfeld jewels!
Thank you. Your testimony's very important.
You are welcome. I'm a good faithful person!
I'm sorry, I won't speak about that with you!

You want to buy equipment? It depend on what you want to buy. Leon van den Brooks' famous armory shop is in Alvaron. The apothecary Thelma Ulthraum and master alchemist Alberto Kelley sell potions and magic items. And the innkeepers William Burton and Salena Flock make business with everything.
A storm in Alvaron? Hmm... I haven't heard about one. And I hear about almost everything!
Fallen Angels? That is the dangerous lot of rogues in my home city Jad-Habaal, isn't it? They are terrible—chop off everybody's heads, hands and legs, rape, kill, mutilate... ouch, ouch.
Well... never mind.
I heard that Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is suspected by lot of people of heresy and treason. And he hasn't shown up in public for some time and that is very suspicious!

A terrible tragedy happened! King Edward was murdered right in the middle of his chambers and halls! Nobody has any idea who the murderer can be, the guards stand everywhere, the servants everywhere and all of a sudden the King is dead, completely murdered! Who could do that?
Sorry, I don't know the gentleman.
Sorry, I don't have these things in my stock. I do business with antiques, not roots and bodily fluids!
Priest Nicolas states he was wrongfully accused of raping Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. Do you know anything about it?

I know that if a priest take a woman by force it is a huge sin! He'll go to hell because he denies his sin and doesn't confess. He is a bad priest and a bad faithful. I'm a much better faithful even though I am from the pagan land of Jad-Habaal, because I never put a woman to bed by force!

I'm very sorry, brave knight, but I'm not a good legend teller. I'd rather listen than tell. And it's true that in Alvaron they have many legends; mainly about gold and treasures because the local people love gold and treasures!
If you really want to know that, brave knight, it will cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
In that case I'm really sorry but there is no way I can help you.
You'll tell me about that, or I'm going to kill you, you pagan worm!
I beg you, good man—answer my question. It's not going to hurt you.
You are a wise and experienced man. I can't believe you'd refuse to give your answer to a knight of God...
Yes, you are telling the truth, brave knight. I'd lose my head. But I have no reason to return—I live here in the Realm and do business like an honest and free man.
I see... actually, why not. The divine kingdom is open to all human beings whether they've been born faithful or pagans.
These are wise words, brave knight—just like the Holy Scripture says. That's why I am happy to live and work here for a bigger glory of the divine kingdom on earth!
Amen! Can I talk to you for a while?
Of course, brave knight. I'm at your... how do you call it... disposal! But before you start to talk, I have something on my mind as well.
I was pleased to meet you, good man. I wish you a long and successful life here in the Realm. Goodbye.
You wait, brave knight. I have something on my mind as well.
Tell me more about your home country. I've heard a lot about it but I haven't had a chance to speak with anybody who lived there yet.

Jad-Habaal is a country full of sun and hot sand, but it is also a country full of quiet and fertile oases. The country gave birth to a lot of good—philosophy, arts, science... but a lot of bad as well—the Holy War, intolerance, ignorance. Unfortunately there is more of the bad. The faith in Ahalaar, the only and the holy prophet know no mercy—it denies and fights everything else. Especially the true faith, that is the pain in the neck of the priests and the rulers of Jad-Habaal. They want all the nations to accept what Ahalaar says. That's why there are always wars, massacres, death and suffering.
I understand. But why did you leave? What reasons did you have?

A powerful ruler, a Sheik, got angry with me (not my fault at all) and he makes me and my whole family slaves. He make my wife and my daughters lovers in his harem and put my sons in galleons. I spent some years rowing on a galleon and it is nothing but hard work and beatings. Then one day an opportunity to run away came so I ran. Then I found out that my whole family is dead so I leave the country to die in the country of the faithful. I know that you, the faithful, have no mercy. But I am very wrong...

The monks of the Cloister of Saint Nusmiel found me half dead on the seashore. They take me in and take care of me as if I am their brother. When I am strong enough to leave they baptize me, give me some gold to go. Then I find out that the faithful are not just cruel and unmerciful warriors but they can be loving and caring as well. Unlike the faith in the Ahalaar and the Holy Prophet—they only know death and hate and more death! That's why I decide to stay here in the Realm.

As I've already implied, I do business with relics and antiques. Now I try to find these three ancient statuettes of the angels Raphael, Michael and Gabriel. They are very old, created by an unknown artist around the year 223. I want them desperately and I'm willing to pay a great sum of gold. Would you be interested in finding them and bringing them to me?
All right, I'll help you find them.
That's great. I always knew we can make an agreement, brave knight. As soon as you have one of the statuettes come to me, give it to me and I'll give you the gold.
Where do you think the statuettes could be found?
Nobody knows, brave knight. They are lost all over the Realm. You must search.
I'm sorry, I don't have time to search for antiques.
Oh... I understand your motives. If you change your mind, however, come to me and we can make an agreement.
As you wish. Can I now talk to you for a moment?
Of course, brave knight. I'm at your... how do you call it?... disposal!
Today is your lucky day, good man. I think I found one of the statuettes.
Really? Show me what you have and I tell you if it is the statuette I want.
I have the statuette of Angel Michael.
It is the one! Good heavens, it is the statuette I am looking for! Here is the reward, brave knight!
I have the statuette of Angel Rafael.
I have the statuette of the Archangel Gabriel.
All right, brave knight. You find another, bring it to me and I'll give you your gold.
All right. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Very well, it's a deal.
I thank you, brave knight. Do you have another?
I thank you, brave knight. You bring me all the three statuettes I want. You have no idea what a great deed you finished. Goodbye, brave knight—we'll probably never see each other again.

Hello, brave knight. I'm really happy that you come to see me. You are probably interested in some relics and artifacts from very old times. You come to the right place because I am Ihman ab Sahab, an antique merchant.
Ihman ab Sahab? What an unusual name... and the way you speak! Where are you from?
You be right, brave knight—as well as the whole Brotherhood of the Righteous. I come from very far, from the desert empire Jad-Habaal...
You're from Jad-Habaal? That's strange, isn't it? Your empire is the worst enemy of the whole faithful world!

Yes, that is the sad truth. Jad-Habaal fights against the whole faithful world for many centuries... and the end of the wars are not to be expected. I was born in that country, that is true. But it is not my home. I decide to leave.
Why did you become a faithful? You would surely be punished severely if you went back to Jad-Habaal.
You pagan traitor! You're going to die for daring to walk the lands of the faithful!

Stop you wrath, brave knight—I'm not a pagan traitor even though I come from Jad-Habaal. I am faithful as well as everybody else. I gave up the faith in Ahalaar and the Holy Prophet many years ago. I let myself baptized and become a faithful!
Good, I believe you. But tell me why did you become a faithful? You would surely be punished severely if you went back to Jad-Habaal.
I don't believe you. I've never heard of any pagan from the doomed country of Jad-Habaal who gave up his heresy and became a faithful!
Then I'd be the first as they say. Whether there are others or not, I am a faithful, I swear by God!
Good day, brave knight. How are you doing? I hope you are bringing a statuette of an angel as we agreed.
I'm sorry, I'm not bringing you any statuette this time.
No? It does not matter, brave knight. Do not worry, you'll be lucky next time. What can I do for you?
I would like to talk to you for a moment, good man.
You're right, I came because of the statuettes...
How do I understand that?
Hello, brave knight. How are you doing today? I hope you changed your mind and decided to help me in finding the statuettes of the angels.
I won't I'm afraid.
Oh... what a pity! But I still hope you change your mind... what can I do for you right now?
Nothing. Goodbye.
Yes, I decided to help you with the statuettes.
That is great. I was sure we could make a deal, brave knight! As soon as you have one of the statuettes come to me and I'll give you the gold.

So we do meet in the end, brave knight. It's my fault because it took me a while to figure out how to open the tomb of the Saint Orthenius with the statuettes. But as you can see I've managed to do it.
What are you trying to do? And why are you all of a sudden speaking fluently and without that ridiculous accent?

I speak the way I was taught to speak—that was just a cover. You must be a pretty gullible person, knight. Did you really think I was an immigrant who fell in love with the true faith? And did you think Ahalaar and the Holy Prophet would let me leave without punishment? Ahalaar is not weak like your God and the Holy Prophet is not nobody like your crucified First Prophet! They would never allow their country to get into the shit your Ultherst is in!
That's treachery! You are a Jad-Habaal spy!

So you finally figured that out, knight? I was afraid I was going to have to tell you so you could understood who you'd brought the statuettes to. But by the look of you I can tell that you have no idea what's going on anyway. Well then, knight, you see, these three statuettes will open the entrance to the Saint Orthenius's Tomb. And that's where, according to the Killian's chronicle, a relic called the Inquisitor, which can help you protect the Realm, should be hidden.
Are you trying to steal the relic?

Not really, knight—I was given the task of finding it and destroying it to contribute to the fall of Ultherst. If the legend of Saint Orthenius tells the truth, when the relic is destroyed it will be your end. And as you can see, I'm just a tiny step from success. Now I just need to get rid of you, and I'm there. So... as you, the faithful, would say—goodbye, knight. Now you're going to die!
I know what you're trying to do—you want to take the possession of the relic called the Inquisitor!

Yes, that is correct. I'm surprised you could figure that out. When you brought me the statuettes I thought you were the biggest fool in the world. You've just managed to somewhat improve your reputation. Not that it's going to help you anyhow—I'm still going to kill you. Ahalaar and the Holy Prophet ask for your head for getting in my way!

Yes, that's right. And a very successful spy, don't you think? I could fit in your society without much effort. I just needed to speak about penitence, correction, refusing heresy and to admire the true faith and all the doors were open to me. My task was pretty easy in the end.
But why would you want to steal the relic, filthy pagan?!

Actually, I don't want to steal it. I was given the task of finding it and destroying it to contribute to the fall of Ultherst. If the legend of Saint Orthenius is telling the truth, when the relic is destroyed it will be your end. And as you can see, I'm just a tiny step from success. Now I just need to get rid of you, and I'm there. So... as you, the faithful, would say—goodbye, knight. Now you're going to die!
Please, don't touch my goods or I get mad and call the soldiers!
When it comes to jewels I never make mistakes, Father. They were Baron Mansfeld jewels!

I'm very sorry, Father, but I'm not a good legend teller. I'd rather listen than tell. And it's true that in Alvaron they have many legends; mainly about gold and treasures because the local people love gold and treasures!

I'm investigating the case of the forged gold. It seems that some heretics can turn human excrement into gold temporarily. Is there anything you can tell me about it?

There is something I can tell you about the damn heretics, knight. A beggar named Beckham, I serve him a drink in the inn from time to time, is one them. Ever since I can remember he's always been broke, always trying to run without paying, to steal something or deceive me somehow. That's why I was pretty surprised that he came the other day with a pouch full of gold. I was wondering where he got that but he paid up his debts immediately so I didn't ask. Can you imagine the shock when the gold all of a sudden turned to—God forgive me—human excrement? I was so shocked I couldn't even catch the rascal.
Are you sure it was the beggar's money that turned to excrements?
Yes, I'm absolutely sure—I put them aside; just in case, you know?
You're welcome, knight. If you catch him give him a slap for me. Pooh, such a trickery!
The innkeeper William Burton thinks he saw his brother Ron's stuff being sold in your inn. And he thinks his brother's been murdered. What can tell me about that?

If you think I sell stolen goods you're awfully wrong, knight! Me and my husband got the thieves and traffickers out of this place once and for all. And I don't pay those hulks just to take care of the customers who don't pay. But I must admit that from time to time I take goods from people I'm afraid of even with the bouncers behind my back.
Who do you mean?

Do you know Norman, the butcher from the King's Road Inn? That's exactly the kind of person I was talking about—just the way he looks at you makes you feel uneasy. I must admit he scares me. When he came over to sell some things some time ago, I bought them without even trying to barter. It's possible that they belonged to Ron Burton even though I can't imagine how he could have got them.
You're welcome, knight. If something's happened to Ron Burton then I'm really sorry. I knew his father, he was always very nice to me.
Is there any gambling in your inn, inkeeper?
It depends who's asking and why. As you surely know gambling has been banned by the royal writ and the Holy Mother Church considers it a sin as bad as usury.
I'm asking because I'd like to play.
As you wish, knight. If you are interested, I can play the King and the Groom with you.

Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert who is the royal governor. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. I couldn't say one bad thing against the Grand Duke even though the rising of taxes is ruining my business. But the Duchess of Kenthworth is on my list, knight. I don't understand how she could get so high... well, actually I do—by going to bed with the right people. But it's a tragedy because the woman only cares about how she looks instead of looking after Alvaron!

Is Christoffer de Malamert a heretic? Well... that's hard to tell. He's never done anything bad to me and I don't want to accuse him without any evidence; but the truth is that many locals are sure he is. They think he's a traitor wishing to concentrate power in his hands. And yet more they're afraid what the future can bring because if a man so high up is a heretic who else can we trust?

To tell you the truth, knight, I have a suspicion. It's a boy called Horst. There's something wrong with him. Just take the way he looks at you, as if he wanted to throttle you. He's harassed me recently, tried to touch me and when I pushed him off he gave me this chilly grin. And then he said I'd soon be his whether I wanted or not—and he's only twelve. I'm worried about his soul—if it's not under the influence of infernal powers already.

I heard a rumor that some people who were sleeping over in the King's Road Inn got lost. It's usually single travelers but sometimes a couple disappears there. I don't know if that's true but I know that the innkeeper Bates and his hand Norman don't have a good reputation. King's Road Inn used to be a fancy place where the nobility would sleep over night when they went hunting but since Bates has bought it not many people dare to go there. All right. You play The King and the Groom with two dice and you can get either a number or a figure. The lowest roll you can get is when you get a one and a three which is a figure called the groom. Then there are numbers and the way you count them is that you multiply the higher number by ten and add the lower number. So a three and a two makes thirty-two, a four and a one makes forty-one and so on. The highest number is sixty-five. If you get two numbers which are the same, it's a figure called the chamberlain. And the number you get tells you how many chamberlains you got. That means that if you get two times one you get one chamberlain, if you get two times two you get two chamberlains and so on. The highest figure in the game is the king which is a one and a two. There's nothing higher, it's a triumph. That's why the game is called The King and the Groom—the groom is the lowest roll and the king is the highest. Understand?

I'm sorry but you can't. I'm not going to risk you coming back with soldiers. Guys, get rid of him!
Then I would like to offer you my services. As a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous I can afford to perform many things. So what's going on here?
Ehm... so you want to help us get some money out of the innkeeper Weintraum of Glatzburg, do I understand it right?
Yes, exactly. As long as there's something in it for me, of course.
