An interesting offer...

Exactly. And it will probably be the best if it's you who puts forth the proposal to Weintraum, knight. I think he's gonna treat you more carefully than if it was me or one of my boys. He might set his dogs—Beelzebub and Scamp on us...

Great. Tell him to pay 5,000 gp or else his inn is not going to stand there much longer—and he neither. Bring back the money and we'll share it. But no tricks! If I find out you tried to play me I'm going to cut your throat!
Thinking about it, I don't want to have anything to with it...
Now you gave me a difficult problem to solve, knight.
What kind of problem?
The problem what to do with your corpse so that it's never found. Guys, get rid of him!
So you want to blackmail the innkeeper Weintraum! I'm not going to allow that!
Then say hello in hell for me, knight. Guys, get rid of him!
Back again, knight? How did it go? Did the old scrooge Weintraum agree with the offer? Are you bringing the damn money?
I changed my mind. I'm not going to help you with that.

WHAT?! Do you think I'm going to believe you that you changed your mind? I don't believe that! I'm not a fool. I know exactly what kind of game you're playing here. You kept the money and you are trying to deceive us. But you are not getting away with that, knight. Now you've signed your death sentence. Kill him, guys!
I'm not bringing the money. Weintraum didn't want to pay and he was going to set his dogs on me...

WHAT?! Are you trying to tell me that he didn't give you the money? I don't believe that. You kept the money and you are trying to deceive us. But you are not getting away with that, knight. Now you've signed your death sentence. Kill him, guys!
I'm not bringing you the money. Weintraum refused to pay and he set his dogs on me...

Damn service! I don't need this! To hell with that damn tyrant. God knows one day I'm going shove the bears up his...
Uhm... sorry... I didn't want to disturb you, I was just passing by...

And so you entered a stranger's house without an invitation, right? But I don't care, anybody can just walk in here. This is Gerbert of Rowington's house. If you ever have the bad luck to meet him he probably won't forget to mention that he used to be the royal hunter. And I'm his servant Servil if you care to know. But I feel more like a slave.
It seems you don't like your master too much.

How did you figure that out, knight?! Yes you're right. A service to Baron of Rowington is a never ending nightmare. He's never happy about anything. For example let's take today; today I've been making him hard-boiled eggs the whole day and he still doesn't think they're hard enough!
Try to look at it as if it were a way to salvation, good man. God will definitely accept you in his heavenly kingdom for your eggs.
Do you think so, knight? Well, actually—my suffering is similar to the one of the First Prophet. The Baron said a couple times that he was going to have me crucified. Thank you, knight.
You're welcome. Can I talk to you?
I'm sorry I don't have time—I must cook the hard-boiled eggs. Goodbye.
God wants the servants to love their masters and be devoted to them as much as the First Prophet was devoted to his creator!
The comparison to the First Prophet is perfect, knight. The Baron said that he'd have me crucified if the eggs are not hard enough. So now I'm going to go on with my martyr's work.
Thanks for the information. Good man.
Hello, good man. Can I talk to you?
I'm sorry but I have no time. I must cook hard-boiled eggs for my master, the Baron of Rowington. If they are not hard enough he'll have me crucified.
I understand. I'm not going to disturb you then.

What do I think about the crisis? I think we got what we deserved. Or maybe what we wanted—depends on the way you look at it!

I mean that nobody can be surprised about the shit the Realm is in since everybody was treating her like a whore—abused her and didn't take care of her. Now we got what we wanted. And who can say he doesn't have a share in this?
Unfortunately, I don't watch the weather.
Interested in the Fallen Angels, my son? Then read the Holy Scripture and you'll know everything you need to know.
You're talking to a Judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition, son! Do you think if I suspected anyone of heresy I'd wait for you to come and ask me?
Of course!

The Cult of the Children of the New Order? I've heard about that before. I think it's one of the cults destroyed by the Inquisition during the Hundred Years War in the Empire, isn't? I just don't understand why are you searching for its members who must have been dead for several centuries now. Probably doing some historical research?!

The local Inquisitorial Curia is looking in vain for missing Juhasz Gotherr, the former municipal librarian and archivist who proved to be the leader of the Cult of the Pagan Night which is trying to ensure the return of the pagan beliefs and of the ancient pagan gods—probably of those from the times of the mythical Elenians. Juhasz Gotherr managed to run away during the arrest attempt and there hasn't been any news of him nor of the other conspirators since.

You want to know whether the Royal Counselor Verenicus could be somehow involved in the Prince Louis's murder? Yes, that's quite possible, son. Anything is possible these days. Just look around and try to prove me otherwise.
You are aiming dangerously high, my son. Or maybe you are an agent provocateur working for Commendoni to find out what I think about him. That's why I better not answer your question!
Priest Nicolas should be careful—no matter what he has or hasn't done. That's all I'm going to tell you about that.

You've probably heard some of the legends about Saint Orthenius people often tell. Something like that Saint Orthenius is going to come down from the Heaven at the head of an army of angels and save the Realm from all the evil, or that his follower will come from the common folks and burn the enemies of the true faith with the flame of divine justice. I don't know what's true about the legends but there is a place near to Alvaron where Saint Orthenius was buried in 223. Until recently it was one of the most sacred pilgrimage destinations and for the last thousand years crowds of the faithful would travel to see the remains of the patron of our Realm. But now...

At the times of King Henry the Third beautiful gardens were planted around the tomb. The place soon became known as the Royal Gardens. They were a place full of blooming bushes, evergreen grass, exotic trees and of wooden gazebos inviting for taking a rest. In the past generations it became a place where the nobility would spend most of their free time. But then the Star of Doom appeared in the sky and the gardens were one of the first places that has been destroyed. In the past few years the Realm was struck by the Scourges of God and the gardens have changed completely—they became known as the Gardens of Grief.
It's really a pity that such a beautiful place became a nest of evil and a hideout of infernal monsters. Saint Orthenius's tomb now lies in the middle of a doomed land where not many dare to go.
Do you think your position can protect you from the wrath of God if you refuse to answer my questions, Your Excellency?
Let's get it straight, Your Excellency—for some reason you don't like me. I assure you, however, that your answer won't hurt anybody.
Please, allow me to admire your wisdom and erudition. In fact, those were the reasons I decided to ask you the question. Please don't refuse to answer me!
I came to you because you are a member of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. I would like to show you evidence of heresy of a person that can be only accused by the Tribunal.

That's very serious, son. Do you know that the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition's function is to try the cases of the most severe crimes committed by the most important members of society? Tell me, whom do you want to accuse?
The Grandmaster of the Order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, Christoffer de Malamert.
Hmm... And what evidence against Grandmaster de Malamert do you have to support your accusation?

If that is really so, the Grandmaster must be arrested and interrogated immediately to prove or disprove the accusation. You have my consent to arrest him, son. But you must receive the consent of two more members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition—that is what the Codex of the Inquisition requires.
Hmm... I thought it'd be more difficult to gain your consent.

Why? You gave me the evidence of heresy and of treason of Grandmaster de Malamert, you asked for my consent with his arrest and with his accusation and when I gave it to you, you're surprised? I tell you one thing—not even a high position can protect anybody from the Holy Inquisition. The Inquisition is a God given most powerful judiciary and inquisitorial institution of the justice. Nobody can hide from it—not even those with the titles and degrees. Nobody, understand? Nobody!
Inquisitor General Cardinal Commendoni.
WHAT?! Are you crazy? Did you come to make fun of me? You won't get away with that. You are going to pay for your impudence, you can trust me in that!
I'm not making fun of you, Your Excellency, believe me. I have evidence. I have a testimony...
I don't care about your testimonies, son! Get out immediately or I'm calling the guards!
Are you not going to stop that nonsense? Then I have no choice. Guards, get him out!
I wouldn't do that if I were you, Your Excellency. Definitely not, unless you want the truth about yourself to come to light.
What do you mean, son? What truth? I have no idea what you're talking about.

Of course you do, Cardinal. Denying it won't help. I know everything—I even know why you don't want to give me your consent with the arrest of the Inquisitor General Cardinal Commendoni. And this is what I propose—give me your consent and I'll be quiet forever.
You're lying, son—I can tell. And I won't let you blackmail me. Go away or I'll have you carried out like a dirty vagabond—which is what you are!
As you wish, Your Excellency. It's your decision. Goodbye!

Wait, son... You wouldn't... I... I can't give the consent to arrest Cardinal Commendoni. I can't! They know too much, maybe even more than you. They know of each step I've ever done. I'm all in their hands. I can't... even if I wanted to. Except, maybe...
Except, maybe, what?

Except if you could help me with something. If you could bring me a statuette I've been trying to get hold of for many years and which became the reason the Children of the New Order started to blackmail me. Get me the statuette and I'll give you my consent with the arrest of the Inquisitor General Commendoni.
What statuette is it?

A statuette of the pagan God Bhelfelix. It's an ancient relic the pagan priests left here when they were running from the faithful armies of Ultherst together with the other barbarian raiders at the end of the tenth century. I've been searching for the statuette and if you bring it to me I'll give you my consent with the arrest of Cardinal Commendoni.
All right, I'll help you to get the statuette. Can you tell me whether you've found any information as to where the statuette should be yet?

Yes. I was lucky and I found some traces leading to Hillbrandt where the barbarian priests who were carrying the statuette back to their lands were defeated. I found a group of Glatzburg treasure hunters who probably found a map where the barbarian priests marked the place they hid the treasure in. The leader of the group is Hulph Rechtzwürther and he should be somewhere in Glatzburg or in it's surroundings. Find him, get the map and bring me the Bhelfelix's statuette. Then I'll give you the consent to arrest Commendoni.
Alright. Can I talk to you now? I have some questions.
Speak then. But speak quickly, I don't want people to see us together!
We have a deal, Your Excellency. Goodbye.
Goodbye, son. And hurry up, I can't wait for the statuette to be in my hands.
Why is the statuette so important to you?
I'm not going to tell, my son. At least not until you bring it to me.
I'm not lying, believe me—I know about the Cult of the Children of the New Order and I know why you are working for them!
You don't know anything, son! I can tell when I'm talking to a liar!
What if I paid you for the audience, Your Excellency? Could that shorten the waiting period?
Yes, actually—that would simplify the process.
Here you go then.
Good. Come now and tell me what your plea is.
I'd like to ask you a few questions, Your Excellency.
Go ahead and ask, son. What's on your mind?
I can't believe my ears—a Supreme Tribunal judge is asking for a bribe!
A bribe, son? As far as I can remember you were talking about paying an administrative fee to shorten the waiting period.
Leave, whoever you are, son. You don't have an appointment and you are wasting my precious time.
Can I ask you who you are, Your Excellency?
You don't even know me and still you dare to disturb me? You have the honor of talking to Cardinal Severtinus, a judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition!
Pleased to meet you, Your Excellency. I'd like to...

I don't care what you'd like to. I've already told you that I didn't have time for you. I consider your presence here an unbelievable impudence! You've broken the strict hearing protocol for which you can be banned from the city. So go away before I get angry!
Then I'd like to make an appointment.
As you wish, son. I'm really busy right now but sometime next month I should be able to find some time. Come after the new moon, then we can talk.
I'm afraid I can't wait that long.
And I'm afraid you'll have to. Unless you change your mind of course and find out that you actually don't need to talk to me at all.
I really need to talk to you. It's urgent, Your Excellency. Please, find some time for me.
I'm sorry, I can't. I have many important things to do.
I'm not leaving until you hear me.
I wouldn't recommend that, son. You're trying my patience. If you don't leave now I'm going to have you kicked out of here!
Hmm... Goodbye then.
I need to talk to you! Now!
How dare you speak to me like that? What do you think you're doing? You're pushing my patience. Get away or I'm calling the guards!
I'm sorry, I'm leaving. Goodbye.
What do you want here, son? Didn't I make it clear that I didn't have time for you and I don't care about your reasons? Leave!
I really need to talk to you, Your Excellency.
But I don't need to talk to you. Don't try my patience and leave!
Welcome, son. What do you need from me?
I'd like to talk to you Your Excellency.
All right, then. I can spare some time. What's on your mind?
Nothing today, Your Excellency.
Then leave me to my duties, son. Goodbye.
Hello, son. What do you need?
I brought you the statuette you asked me to get—here it is.
Oh my demons... it really is the statuette. I've never seen it before and yet I can feel the power of God Bhelfelix radiating from the statuette. Oh lord, you're coming back to your servants!
I guess I fulfilled my part of the contract. It's your turn now. Pacta sunt servanda.
What? What contract? Oh, the deal we made... well... All right, you have my consent to arrest Cardinal Commendoni. But believe me, you won't need it anyway!
No? What do you mean?

Because in a moment you'll be dead—as well as the rest of the city! Look at the statuette. Do you know what's hidden in there? The mundane form of God Bhelfelix! It was brought here from the distant ice plains to become the most powerful weapon against the faithful. Unfortunately, the priests of the Bhelfelix's cult didn't manage to free the God. That's why our ancestor were beaten!
What the hell are you talking about. Who are your ancestors? And who are you?

My real name is Aghwan-dor and I am the last priest of the Bhelfelix's cult and a descendant of the Othar tribe that has brought the statuette to Ultherst three hundred years ago. Bhelfelix, the God of Death and Destruction, is our Lord. He was brought here to destroy you which, unfortunately, didn't happen. When my ancestors were beaten in 989 and they were running back to the Moonshine Mountains, the priests of the Bhelfelix's cult who were carrying the statuette were amongst them. When they saw they couldn't cross the Mountains and they were under the siege of the Ultherst army, they decided to bury the statuette together with other valuables and relics they were carrying with them. It proved to be a wise decision because soon afterwards they were caught and massacred by the Ultherst army. All, including the women and the children.
My God... you're a pagan!

Of course I am. Didn't you know that? Well... never mind. Doesn't matter anymore. But to finish the story—a young novice managed to survive the massacre. He was lucky to be accepted into the Order of Saint Jehron. He became a member of their community. A barbaric priest who became a faithful but deep in his heart he stayed a pagan and tried his whole life to find the holy relic of his nation. The situation after the war was complicated and he had to be careful not to be discovered so he never succeeded but he found many followers amongst the assimilated remains of his nation and he made sure the Bhelfelix's cult survived. Their only aim was to find the statuette! And I—the last priest of the cult did it!
I understand. And the Children of the New Order started to blackmail you. You became their servant.

Yes, that's right. There was nothing I could do, my hands were tied. But then, all of a sudden I found a fool who brought me the statuette right into my arms—and that was you. Thanks for the help, son! Unfortunately, it's going to cost you your life! Haalbar de ghabar imhes thottor! Haalbar de ghabar imhes melittor. Haalbar de ghabar imhes savagedhor! I summon thee, oh our Lord, come to us! Haalbar de ghabar imhes ommardh. Haalbar de ghabar imhes heptarr! Haalbar de ghabar imhes loathur!
Enough of the madness, Cardinal. You are a pagan and a heretic and as such you are going to answer to the Tribunal of the Inquisition!

I don't think so—in a moment Bhelfelix will be free after many, many centuries and I'm going to offer him the hearts of all the mortals! Haalbar de ghabar imhes baronus samedus! Haalbar de ghabar imhes budikus! Haalbar de ghabar imhes pegasus!
You better stop it, Cardinal. The statuette is starting to shine in a suspicious way. You don't know what this Bhelfelix will do... Stop it!

Nothing can stop me now! Bhelfelix will eat the hearts of the faithful and I'll be ruling the whole world. Come, our Lord, come to this world! Look at all the meat and blood around you! Take what is rightfully yours! Oh, my Lord... yes! Yes! Yes! You're being born! You're coming. The spell worked and you are going to be released from your prison. Yes! Come to us!
My God... run, Cardinal. This doesn't look good!

Are you scared face to face with Death, worm? Ridiculous! Come, Bhelfelix, and feed on his meat. Come and take him... No, wait, why are you looking at me like that, my Lord? What are you waiting for? Take the poor God's knight. Wait, what are you doing? No, leave me alone, I'm your priest! No, God... Don't touch me... nooooooaaaarghhhhh... crunch!

I had no idea that the Brotherhood of the Righteous was granted the right to look through the personal belongings of judges of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition without their permission. I must read the latest King's decrees once again. But if it's not there I'll call the guards and have the whole thing investigated. In the torture chamber, of course!

Take the poor priest. Wait, what are you doing? No, leave me alone, I'm your priest! No, God... Don't touch me... nooooooaaaarghhhhh... crunch!

I had no idea that Inquisitorial Investigators gained the right to look through the personal belongings of judges of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition without their permission. I must read the Codex Inquisitorium one more time. But if it's not here I'll call the guards and have the whole thing investigated. In the torture chamber, of course!

I had no idea that the aristocracy was granted the right to look through the personal belongings of judges of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition without their permission. I must read the latest King's decrees once again. But if it's not there I'll call the guards and have the whole thing investigated. In the torture chamber, of course!
I'm going to kill you! Understand? I'm going to kill you all! I'LL KILL YOU ALL? UNDERSTAND?!
Wait, brother—your comrade Hector de Froix sent me. He wants to help you as well as I do!
Hector de Froix...? Yes, I know the name. He must die... yes, he must die! And you too, brother! All must die! Arrrggghhh!
The only thing I can do is defeat that madman and find out what caused the madness...
I don't think so!
Arrrggghhh! All must die! Arrrggghhh!
Man, you are mad!
I'm going to kill you! All of you! Arrrggghhh!
Ahhhh... Good Gracious... The pain...
I did it—the paladin is under my control! Now I'm going to look at what's causing his madness—whether it's some kind of artifact or something else...
What is it he's wearing around his neck? It looks like some kind of an ancient amulet... and it radiates such deadly cold!
Let's see what happens if I take it off his neck...

My God... the pain! What happened...? And where am I? Who are you, brother? What was happening to me? I had this terrible dream... I dreamed of killing innocent people! Me, a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous!
Unfortunately, it wasn't a dream, brother.
My God... What are you saying, brother? That it wasn't a dream? I... was really killing innocent people on sight?
You've committed many crimes—because of this necklace. Where did you get it? It's evidently cursed!
I found it in a shrine of evil I came to destroy. A dead man I found there was wearing it...
I see. Now, please, follow me, I'm going to take you back to your comrades. They are going to take care of you...

No, brother. I... can't go with you. I can't go back to my comrades. My soul has been blackened by many mortal sins which I couldn't undo if I lived for three hundred years. I have been cursed and I'm going to die cursed!
What are you going to do with that sword, brother? I hope you're not going to take your life!
What else can I do, brother? I have been doomed for the rest of eternity! Please, promise that you will take the necklace to the Knight Commander Hector de Froix so that he can destroy it!
Thank you, brother. And goodbye... Aaaahhh!
Don't do that, brother—suicide is a sin which will make you lose the chance to purge yourself! You would be doomed forever!
I already am, brother. Just promise that you will give the cursed amulet to Hector de Froix. Please, promise!
I won't touch the amulet!
Goodbye then, brother. Eternal hell awaits me... Aaaahhh!
Wait, sir knight—your comrade Hector de Froix sent me. He wants to help you as well as I do!
Hector de Froix...? Yes, I know the name. He must die... yes, he must die! As well as you, Father! All must die! Arrrggghhh!

No, noble lord. I... can't go with you. I can't go back to my comrades. My soul has been blackened by many mortal sins which I couldn't undo if I lived for three hundred years. I have been cursed and I will die cursed!
What are you going to do with that sword, knight? I hope you're not going to take your life!
What else can I do, noble lord? I have been doomed for the rest of eternity! Please, promise that you will take the necklace to the Knight Commander Hector de Froix so that he can destroy it!
Thank you, noble lord. And goodbye... Aaaahhh!
Don't do that, knight—suicide is a sin which will make you lose the chance to purge yourself! You would be doomed forever!
I already am, noble lord. Just promise that you will give the cursed amulet to Hector de Froix. Please, promise!
Toho amuletu se nikdy nedotknu!
Goodbye then, noble lord. Eternal Hell awaits me... Aaaahhh!
A girl, Francessca Gulvardi, is being held in the local jail. She's obviously innocent. I want her released at once!

What? You think Francessca Gulvardi is innocent?! Guess, you're wrong there. That devil's floozy is a damn handful, you can believe that. She attempted to murder Bishop Trevorius not long ago. She launched herself at him as if she were a wild animal and almost ripped him asunder with her teeth. She was yelling like mad and when the guards came to arrest her, three men had to hold her so she could be bound and locked up. Moreover, since I arrested her, she has been trying to seduce any man who came close to her—well, if they were only soldiers... but she attempted to seduce priests as well. She's like an animal. I'll tell you one thing—if that woman ain't possessed by dark powers, you can call me Saint Petrius.
Despite of that I want you to release her, Sheriff.
I'm sorry, but I can't. It's not in my power to release her. It's up to the inquisitorial prosecutor who ordered her to be held in custody.
I've heard that you pay rewards for apprehended bandits, Sheriff. Is it true?
Yes, you've heard right, knight. I pay rewards announced by Robert Heidrick for the heads of bandits loitering around the city. Bring me a scalp or head and I'll give you cash on the barrelhead.

Well, I'd almost forget, there's also Henry de Montreaux. Heard 'bout him? He's a former paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous; the word is that he went mad after they cast him out from that order of theirs and that he turned into a killing machine after that. That madman's loitering 'round the city and challenges anybody he meets to a duel. And kills him. I've heard rumors that he's unbeatable. That he's in league with Satan who protects him from any harm. Witnesses affirmed they had seen five swordsmen go after him and he just had them chopped into pieces. Grand Duke Heidrick offered a hefty reward for his head...
I would like to know if there are any rewards for killing monsters in the city.

Rewards for killing monsters in Glatzburg? Hmmm... depends on what you mean by monster. If you include people among them, then yes. The place is just crawling with human monsters! Grand Duke Robert Heidrick offered a reward for the head of any bandit loitering 'round the city. Bring me a scalp or head and I'll give you cash on the barrelhead.

Well, I'd almost forget, there's also Henry de Montreaux. Heard 'bout him? He's a former paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous; the word is that he went mad after they cast him out from that order of theirs and that he turned into a killing machine after that. That madman's loitering 'round the city and challenges anybody he meets to a duel. And kills him. I've heard rumors that he's unbeatable. That he's in league with Satan who protects him from any harm. Witnesses affirmed they had seen five swordsmen go after him and he just had them chopped into pieces. Grand Duke Heidrick offered a hefty reward in gold for his head...

The royal governor of the city and my immediate superior is Grand Duke Robert Heidrick. He's the supreme commander of the royal army here in the city and also the supreme commander of the Glatzburg regional armed forces—if they were mobilized. The royal vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin, I'm not in touch with him, cause he doesn't deal in anything military. He cares just about civil and business matters.

So, you'd like to do some shopping in Glatzburgu... Hmmm... depends on what you want, knight—guess it ain't vegetables, right? If it's weapons or armor, visit Hans von Drichtmaul—he runs the renowned Glatzburg armory. Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus can provide you with potions and magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum offer various wares. And Alphonso DiCerbio will also sell you almost anything—if you don't mind the origin of his wares. Anyway, it's just a matter of time for you to get enough evidence against him to send him to the gallows.
Tell me, Sheriff, what do you think about the crisis the Realm has been dragged into?

What do I think 'bout the crisis? It's a pain in the neck, knight, well, to be honest, in the ass. I'm an old guy, but I've never seen anything like that in my life. So much madness and rage... fire raining on our heads, terrible famine killing mercilessly both people and cattle, Black Death raging like a dark spirit... One can't wonder people are losing faith and are giving up. You know, despair is an ideal breeding ground for crime... Lotsa people here in Glatzburg believe that the end of the world's coming. All in all, the situation's rather desperate. The people had been hoping for a change, maybe for salvation or redemption, but nothing happened. On the contrary—it's been getting worse and worse every year. You know, knight, you won't find many people holding out hope for a brighter future.

Sure I've heard rumors 'bout war, knight. I'm a soldier and not too young so I can smell when something's brewing. Nobody's got to tell anything to me. We got the order from Grand Duke Heidrick to be on alert. That means to keep the men in the garrison and be ready to hit the road any moment. We've been also recruiting, though only volunteers so far. Cavalry needs to be replenished so we've been commandeering horses and draft cattle. We've also been trying to fill the granaries with the little we could get hold of. Well, anyway we can't afford to have big expenses, as there's almost nothing to be taxed. All in all that can mean only one thing—a war's coming. Moreover, there's word the First Knight himself should arrive from Alvaron. Don Rodrigo de Velacor, the first marshal of the royal army, is not just someone who'd be treading the Realm without a damn good reason.
Well, but against whom is the war to be waged? I don't see any enemy waiting in the field to charge.

That's the most peculiar thing about it, knight. Just as you've said—there's no sign of any enemy that would be coming and that we could face. Well, there's lotsa agitation, you know, heretics, pagans, robbers, you name it; the countryside's also crawling with hellspawns and scamps. Anyway you can't fight any of those with any army—the Inquisition and reinforced local garrisons are able to deal with them easily enough. Well, there must be something else, knight. That's just what scares me—as well as all the people in the city.
Interesting... and unsettling at the same time. Thank you, Sheriff.
You're welcome, knight. Couldn't tell you much, cause I dunno much. Well, but I can guess much.
Hmm... thanks for the information.

To tell you the truth, knight, there're so many hellspawns and monsters that I don't know where I should send my men first. There are undead crawling in the city streets Every night. If they catch someone, he's as good as dead. The same goes for the cemetery—they are rising from their graves as if the alarm were sounded in the barracks. Roads are besieged by bandits and brigands attacking merchants and solitary travelers. They take everything—both possessions and lives. Well, last but certainly not least, there are those hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns that are near the ruins of Galibornium—that pagan city. They look like a hybrid of man and basilisk and they are as mean and enraged as Satan himself. Damn them all...

Suspicion of heresy... that's a serious matter, knight. One must be careful with words when it comes to the accusations of things such as heresy or paganism. I'm a soldier, everything's black or white for me—either attack or withdraw; either ally or enemy. So I can't tell you that I suspect anyone of heresy unless I catch him with a ceremonial knife in one hand and with an innocent virgin in the other. Sorry.

Well, lotsa noticeable things have happened lately in Glatzburg. For example that murder attempt on Bishop Trevorius. A servant girl of Grand Duke Heidrick Francessca Gulvardi, a nice and good gal, launched herself at the Bishop like a wild animal. She attempted to kill him with her bare hands. She was snapping at him with her teeth like a rabid dog. If Trevorius weren't in good shape and rather well built, he wouldn't have survived. I wish you could have seen her fighting my men who came to arrest her—half a dozen men had a hard time holding her, almost got their asses kicked. Of course that wasn't normal—I'm damn sure she had to be possessed by an evil spirit. I'll tell you that I shudder to think 'bout it. If an infernal demon can possess anyone he wants, nobody can be sure to see another sunrise.

The murder of monsignor Trevorius is a rather tricky problem, knight. Very tricky. Especially because it came so soon after the attack of that possessed gal—Francessca Gulvardi. It seems somebody wanted Bishop Trevorius to be dispatched as soon as possible. Well there are dozens of questions surrounding the case...
Such as?

For example what was the Bishop doing at such a forsaken place such as Grand Duke's gazebo. Normal people have been avoiding the place for years... It's quite likely he had an appointment there. A secret one. And the one he met could have very well been his murderer... Well, anyway, those are only my speculations. I'm sure that the Inquisition won't allow the murderer to enjoy freedom for long.

The murder of Monsignor Trevorius is a rather tricky problem. Very tricky. Especially if you consider the fact that a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is supposedly involved. Don't you want to tell me something 'bout it, knight? Maybe I could help you...

I don't have anything to tell you about that, Sheriff. And if you're insinuating something in connection with the fact that I was seen near Bishop's body soon after his death, I assure you that I have nothing to do with that murder!
Yes, as I've thought. Well, then I can't help you. I know only that what you already know.

So you think that Istwan de Bragho rose from his grave and that he cannot be killed? That's bad, knight. That means that he has all those dead paladins who apprehended him years ago on his conscience... they didn't stand a chance. Damn, guess that means the city executioner, Yan Flemberg, is in mortal danger!
Well, yes, you're right... Anyway, do you think he can really be immortal?

I don't know, knight. I've never met any immortal monster—well, except for my mother-in-law, of course—so I can't tell you if it's possible or not. Nonetheless I wouldn't be too surprised if he really were immortal. Try asking Enrie Jungwirdt 'bout things like that. She knows lotsa things 'bout hellspawns and infernal stuff like that—surely more than anybody else.
Well, if you're looking for anything stolen, try asking that buffoon Tinthan if he knows something 'bout it. He steals everything he can see.

Hmmm, Hans Thomas Brookwelt as a heretic and moreover as a lecherous defiler of women? Hmmm... you know what, knight, it's quite possible. After all, who ain't suspicious nowadays, right? Anyway didn't hear gossip like that 'bout him till now. You're the first to tell me...

I don't know the servant girl Jeanette very well. Well, I've seen her several times shopping at the marketplace together with Baroness Helen von Hunth, so I don't have much intel to judge her. Nonetheless I'd say that she very well could be a witch. Who's not suspicious nowadays, right? Moreover nobody can know what she does all day—and especially night—long at that hermitage of theirs. Maybe she flies on Sabbaths... who knows?

To tell you the truth, knight, I'm no youngling, so I've heard dozens of rumors 'bout the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Well, they have one thing in common—according to all of them the hammer is buried somewhere near the city together with all the possessions Bonhart acquired during his life. Well, but the place where the treasure is buried has always been disputed. Some people think it's buried at the scaffold, others are sure it's hidden in the ruins of Galibornium. Well, and others would swear it's elsewhere. Lotsa people tried to get it—none of them succeeded. Guess the hammer will remain lost for good.

You're not the only one looking for Raquel Gielwitch, knight. I've heard that Master Dieter von Gelbendiel is personally looking into the case of those missing gals as well. Well, not that he'd be very successful—all the gals are still missing. Perhaps you'll have more luck. The only thing I know is that Raquel Gielwitch was kidnapped in the night. It seems that she had resisted, cause we found traces of blood at the crime scene and the furniture in the room was all messy. Guess she wasn't resisting for too long though, cause she was very young and tender. It saddens me that she met such a fate.
Answer me at once, Sheriff, or I'll have you racked till you change your mind!
I know that you don't like me very much, Sheriff. Nonetheless, could you, please, forget your animosity for just a minute to answer my question? I'm convinced it won't do you any harm...
I can't believe that such an experienced soldier such as you would hesitate to answer such a simple question...
Alphonso DiCerbio.
You have arrested Alphonso DiCerbio! Congratulations. Nobody was able to get any evidence against him. It'll be my pleasure to lock the bastard up!
Soldier Harph.
Why have you arrested Joah Harph? Don't be angry with me, but I don't like my soldiers to be put off duty out of the blue. The times are too rough for that. What do you think he did?
That's none of your business, Sheriff. Lock him up and keep your inappropriate comments for yourself.
Well.. as you wish, knight.
He's charged with heresy, Sheriff. He's suspected of being behind those night attacks of undead in the city streets.
Bloody hell! Pardon my swearing, knight, but that's a damn serious accusation. If it proves to be true, the reputation of the royal army, which is already rather low, will be a bit lower again...
I'm sorry to hear that, Sheriff, but I can't do anything about that.
I know. I'll lock him up.
Raimond Ventano.
Alright, knight. I'll lock him up.
Ethien de Pasque.
Do you mean Ethien de Pasque the Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?! I'm damned surprised... Very well, knight. I'll lock him up.
Yulliette Heidrick.
Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick?! It must be a mistake, right? You really don't want me to imprison Grand Duchess Yulliette, do you?
I most certainly do. And I'm not willing to discuss it with you.
Very well... as you wish. Those are bad times and I'm just doing my job. I'll lock her up.
Cardinal Truncquillius.
WHAT?! You gotta be insane, knight! Damn, he's a Curial Inquisitor! You can't just arrest him!
I assure you that I can. Do as I say!
As you wish, knight. Hope, I won't be held responsible for that!
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick.
I'm sorry, knight, but I must have heard wrong. So, again, whom do you want me to lock up?
You must be totally nuts, knight! Grand Duke Heidrick is my superior! I can't lock up my superiors. I'd be a mutiny!
No, it wouldn't be, Sheriff. I'm acting in accordance with the law—and you should do the same. Imprison him at once!
No, knight, I won't. Sorry!
Do it, Sheriff. NOW! Otherwise you're going to bear the consequences! Surely you can see that man who dared to arrest such a high ranking person won't hesitate to do anything!
Well, if you put it that way... Hope I'll get just hanged and not quartered or tortured at a breaking wheel. Sometimes, the service to the King is a bitch!
You don't have to worry, Sheriff. I'm really acting in accordance with the law—moreover I have permission to arrest the Grand Duke.
You can tell that to your grandma, knight. I know really well how those laws work. I won't put the Grand Duke into prison!
Here's a sack of gold to support your briskness, Sheriff. I hope the Grand Duke will be behind the bars soon now.
That's bribery, knight! I can't be bribed—it's against the law!
Very well, knight. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Raimond Ventano? All right, knight. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Commander Ethien de Pasque? All right, knight. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick? The wife of Grand Duke Robert Heidrick who's the royal governor of the city and one of the most powerful nobles in the Realm? Well, if you think it's wise, knight... You're gonna bear the consequences yourself. It's my duty to obey your commands. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Cardinal Truncquillius? One of the curial inquisitors? Are you really sure it's absolutely necessary, knight?
Robert Heidrick.
Ehm... Do you really wanna torture Grand Duke Heidrick, knight? You know, he's one of the most powerful men in the Realm?
Of course, Sheriff. We must attend to all our suspects regardless their social status.
Very well, as you wish. You're gonna to bear the consequences yourself—well, I'm sure you know it. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Very well, knight. I'll order the prisoner to be transported to the place of execution. You can get ready for the trial.

Guess so, knight. It's been some time since the living dead started appearing in the city streets after dusk. A terrible thing, I gotta say. First it seemed that those bastards could somehow get into the city from the cemetery, where heretics perform their dark nastiness. So I got the cemetery gates locked after dusk. Well, anyway, it didn't help and the dead can still roam the city streets at night and the people ain't safe even when they lock their doors. And those damn bastards are always gone before cockcrow. Well, I was having a hard time thinking 'bout it all, but finally I figured it out!

Yes. The rumor is that there are remnants of ancient sewer tunnels beneath the city; supposedly they were built ages ago by the founders of the city with the help of the captured pagan builders. Well, but after some church council declared everything touched by pagan hands to be pagan, the sewers were filled up and the entrances were walled. Now it seems that some sections of the sewers survived and the undead are crawling out from there!
Interesting...

Think so too. The only problem is nobody knows how to descend into those bloody sewers. I've been looking myself for an entrance for damn long and I've had no luck so far. The problem is I need damn badly to destroy that nameless evil brooding down there. If I don't manage soon enough the people are gonna flee the city and that would be the end!
I can confirm that the living dead were really coming from the city sewers. I've managed to find an entrance and so I can confirm your suspicion.

So I was right... Nonetheless we must destroy those hellspawns at any cost. If there's a single undead lurking down there, the city won't be able to rest. Would you take care of it, knight? After all, you've already been down there and you know better than anybody else what to do...
To be honest, I've already solved the problem. Those undead were indeed coming from the city sewers. I destroyed them all!
Really?! That's excellent news, knight! Finally the city will be quiet at night. I'm so much indebted to you. Of course, you'll also get your reward—here you go!
Thanks. Could I ask you some questions now?
So you disposed of some bandits, right? That's good, I can tell you. They make the royal roads damn dangerous! Well, show me what you have...
I have a bandit scalp.
Excellent, knight. Here's your reward. Another one's burning in Hell!
I have a head of one of their leaders.
Excellent, knight! Those bastards who lead the other lowlifes are a pain in the... well, you know where, knight. Here's your reward.
I have the head of Benthley of Welshrem, Sheriff.
Wait a moment, knight. Are you trying to tell me that you have the head of Benthley of Welshrem? THAT Benthley of Welshrem who's known as Benthley the Bloody Butcher?
Yes, it is so, Sheriff. There is a reward for his head, isn't there?

Well... but of course, knight! That's great news for all of us! Benthley of Welshrem is dead! Nobody's gonna die by his cursed hand anymore; that monster's not gonna cause more despair and anguish! Go see Grand Duke Heidrick, knight, and show him Benthley's head. I'm sure he's gonna drown you in gold!
Are you telling me you killed Henry de Montreaux? Ehmm, not that I would hesitate to believe you, knight, but could I see his head? You know, one needs to be sure...
Of course—here it is.
Oh my! It's really him! You did it, knight! Henry de Montreaux is dead! Here's your reward!
But of course, knight. Who's that?
I would like to interrogate one of those imprisoned in the torture chamber, Sheriff.
And who would it be, knight?
As you wish. Who would it be, knight?
I understand. I'll be glad to take care of that case myself, Sheriff.
Really? That would help me a lot, knight!
I'm glad to hear that. Could I ask some more questions?
If I decide to look into the case, is there a reward for solving it?
Well, knight, if you managed to slay all those hellspawns in the city sewers there would certainly be a hefty reward in gold waiting for you.
I'm sorry, Sheriff, but I'm not going to look into it. I must pursue my own mission.
I see. Could have guessed that. What can I do for you then?
Hello, good man.
Hello, knight. Guess I haven't had the honor of meeting you yet—the name's Gendriel Smith. I'm the Sheriff of Glatzburg.
Pleased to meet you, Sheriff. What's the situation in the city?

To be honest, I remember better times, you can bet. Well, in fact I'd never thought I'd live to see something like this. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky there have been all kinds of atrocities. Crime's on the rise—murders, robberies, fornication and shit like that are our everyday bread now. I don't know where to send my men first. And to make it worse there are the rumors about a war...
What rumors? I haven't heard anything yet...

No wonder, knight. There's nothing specific, but we got several orders from Alvaron that made us kinda nervous. We're all on standby, we're supposed to gather supplies and to recruit new conscripts. Moreover the word is that the First Knight's coming to Glatzburg... It all stinks!
Against whom should be the war waged, Sheriff?

That's the strangest 'bout it all—there's no enemy we could wage that bloody war against. Of course, we have hellspawns and other infernal brats everywhere, but you can't face them in the field. They must be caught one after another and hanged so everybody can see them—the same should be done with those darned heretics who summon them in those shameless rituals of theirs. When they are all hanging from the trees everything's gonna be calm again—I can tell you. Well, but the war that's something completely different. There must be an enemy who will lay siege to the city or who will muster in the field. The point is, there's no one like that. The people in the city are getting damn scared 'cause of that—and I can't blame them.
Hmmm... you're right. That's strange.

Damn right. Well, enough of talking like that—I'm no old gossip. When I get the order to take the field I'm gonna take my men there. Until then I gotta keep order in this city. I can tell you, knight, even that's getting harder and harder. There's not a single day passing without some kind of a problem.
What happened? Do you have something specific in mind?
The First Knight? Who's that?

The title of the First Knight is given to a carefully chosen nobleman who helped the Realm in a significant way. It's the highest rank a nobleman can achieve. The First Knight is the protector of the royal family and of the Realm itself—besides that he's also the supreme commander of the royal armies. Moreover he becomes the Lord Protector when the King dies—then it's his duty to govern the Realm until a legitimate heir can sit on the throne. These days the First Knight is don Rodrigo de Velacor. I hope that when he comes to Glatzburg I'll get some more specific intel 'bout that coming war.
Hopefully it's all going to turn good soon. Could I speak with you for a minute?
Of course, knight. I'll be glad to answer your questions. Well, but first I'd like to ask you if you could help me with a certain troubling matter.
Unfortunately I don't have time for that. I have a mission of my own.
I see. Could have guessed that. What did you want to ask then?
Sure. What have you in mind?
It seems you're rushed off your feet, Sheriff. Could I be of any assistance?
Yes, you can bet you can, knight. In times like these any help is more than welcome. Especially now when the city's trembling in fear and the people are scared to death!
Welcome, knight. Got any news from the sewers beneath the city streets? If the evil from those sewers doesn't disappear real quick, there's gonna be an exodus!
Unfortunately, I've not yet managed to cleanse the sewers.
Well, what can I do, knight. I sincerely hope you're gonna succeed in the end. Could I help you somehow?
The case is solved, Sheriff. All the undead lurking in the ancient sewers beneath the city were destroyed!
Really?! That's excellent news, knight! Finally the city will be quiet at night. I'm so indebted to you. Of course, you'll also get your reward—here you go!
I would like to get my reward for the killed bandits, Sheriff.
I killed Henry de Montreaux. I'd like to get my reward for that.
Hello, knight. How is it going? What can I do for you?
Welcome, knight. It's really admirable that you managed to cleanse the city sewers of the evil. Everybody feels much safer now. What can I do for you?
Nothing, thank you. Farewell.
I've found out that Duke Robert Heidrick is innocent. You can set him free.
Really? Good news. I didn't believe he was a heretic. I guess he is going to be a bit angry with you, isn't he? But I think he'll skip this chapter soon, ha ha...
Yes, you've heard right, Father. I pay rewards announced by Robert Heidrick for the heads of bandits loitering around the city. Bring me a scalp or head and I'll give you cash on the barrelhead.

So you think that Istwan de Bragho rose from his grave and that he cannot be killed? That's bad, Father. That means that he has all those dead paladins who apprehended him years ago on his conscience... they didn't stand a chance. Damn, guess that means the city executioner, Yan Flemberg, is in mortal danger!

I don't know, Father. I've never met any immortal monster—well, except for my mother-in-law, of course—so I can't tell you if it's possible or not. Nonetheless I wouldn't be too surprised if he really were immortal. Try asking Enrie Jungwirdt 'bout things like that. She knows lotsa things 'bout hellspawns and infernal stuff like that—surely more than anybody else.

Hmmm, Hans Thomas Brookwelt as a heretic and moreover as a lecherous defiler of women? Hmmm... you know what, Father, it's quite possible. After all, who ain't suspicious nowadays, right? Anyway didn't hear gossip like that 'bout him till now. You're the first to tell me...

To tell you the truth, Father, I'm no youngling, so I've heard dozens of rumors 'bout the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Well, they have one thing in common—according to all of them the hammer is buried somewhere near the city together with all the possessions Bonhart acquired during his life. Well, but the place where the treasure is buried has always been disputed. Some people think it's buried at the scaffold, others are sure it's hidden in the ruins of Galibornium. Well, and others would swear it's elsewhere. Lotsa people tried to get it—none of them succeeded. Guess the hammer will remain lost for good.

You're not the only one looking for Raquel Gielwitch, Father. I've heard that Master Dieter von Gelbendiel is personally looking into the case of those missing gals as well. Well, not that he'd be very successful—all the gals are still missing. Perhaps you'll have more luck. The only thing I know is that Raquel Gielwitch was kidnapped in the night. It seems that she had resisted, cause we found traces of blood at the crime scene and the furniture in the room was all messy. Guess she wasn't resisting for too long though, cause she was very young and tender. It saddens me that she met such a fate.
Well.. as you wish, Father.
Bloody hell! Pardon my swearing, Father, but that's a damn serious accusation. If it proves to be true, the reputation of the royal army, which is already rather low, will be a bit lower again...
Alright, Father. I'll lock him up.
Do you mean Ethien de Pasque the Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?! I'm damned surprised... Very well, Father. I'll lock him up.
WHAT?! You gotta be insane, Father! Damn, he's a Curial Inquisitor! You can't just arrest him!
As you wish, Father. Hope, I won't be held responsible for that!
I'm sorry, Father, but I must have heard wrong. So, again, whom do you want me to lock up?
You must be totally nuts, Father! Grand Duke Heidrick is my superior! I can't lock up my superiors. I'd be a mutiny!
No, Father, I won't. Sorry!
You can tell that to your grandma, Father. I know really well how those laws work. I won't put the Grand Duke into prison!
That's bribery, Father! I can't be bribed—it's against the law!
Very well, Father. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Raimond Ventano? All right, Father. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Commander Ethien de Pasque? All right, Father. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick? The wife of Grand Duke Robert Heidrick who's the royal governor of the city and one of the most powerful nobles in the Realm? Well, if you think it's wise, Father... You're gonna bear the consequences yourself. It's my duty to obey your commands. What kind of interrogation do you want to use? Rack, strappado, or pillory?
Cardinal Truncquillius? One of the curial inquisitors? Are you really sure it's absolutely necessary, Father?
Ehm... Do you really wanna torture Grand Duke Heidrick, Father? You know, he's one of the most powerful men in the Realm?
Very well, Father. I'll order the prisoner to be transported to the place of execution. You can get ready for the trial.

Guess so, Father. It's been some time since the living dead started appearing in the city streets after dusk. A terrible thing, I gotta say. First it seemed that those bastards could somehow get into the city from the cemetery, where heretics perform their dark nastiness. So I got the cemetery gates locked after dusk. Well, anyway, it didn't help and the dead can still roam the city streets at night and the people ain't safe even when they lock their doors. And those damn bastards are always gone before cockcrow. Well, I was having a hard time thinking 'bout it all, but finally I figured it out!

So I was right... Nonetheless we must destroy those hellspawns at any cost. If there's a single undead lurking down there, the city won't be able to rest. Would you take care of it, Father? After all, you've already been down there and you know better than anybody else what to do...
Really?! That's excellent news, Father! Finally the city will be quiet at night. I'm so much indebted to you. Of course, you'll also get your reward—here you go!
Excellent, Father. Here's your reward. Another one's burning in Hell!
Excellent, Father! Those bastards who lead the other lowlifes are a pain in the... well, you know where, Father. Here's your reward.
Wait a moment, Father. Are you trying to tell me that you have the head of Benthley of Welshrem? THAT Benthley of Welshrem who's known as Benthley the Bloody Butcher?

Well... but of course, Father! That's great news for all of us! Benthley of Welshrem is dead! Nobody's gonna die by his cursed hand anymore; that monster's not gonna cause more despair and anguish! Go see Grand Duke Heidrick, Father, and show him Benthley's head. I'm sure he's gonna drown you in gold!
Are you telling me you killed Henry de Montreaux? Ehmm, not that I would hesitate to believe you, Father, but could I see his head? You know, one needs to be sure...
Oh my! It's really him! You did it, Father! Henry de Montreaux is dead! Here's your reward!
But of course, Father. Who's that?
And who would it be, Father?
As you wish. Who would it be, Father?
Really? That would help me a lot, Father!
Well, Father, if you managed to slay all those hellspawns in the city sewers there would certainly be a hefty reward in gold waiting for you.
Hello, Father. Guess I haven't had the honor of meeting you yet—the name's Gendriel Smith. I'm the Sheriff of Glatzburg.

No wonder, Father. There's nothing specific, but we got several orders from Alvaron that made us kinda nervous. We're all on standby, we're supposed to gather supplies and to recruit new conscripts. Moreover the word is that the First Knight's coming to Glatzburg... It all stinks!

Damn right. Well, enough of talking like that—I'm no old gossip. When I get the order to take the field I'm gonna take my men there. Until then I gotta keep order in this city. I can tell you, Father, even that's getting harder and harder. There's not a single day passing without some kind of a problem.
Of course, Father. I'll be glad to answer your questions. Well, but first I'd like to ask you if you could help me with a certain troubling matter.
Yes, you can bet you can, Father. In times like these any help is more than welcome. Especially now when the city's trembling in fear and the people are scared to death!
Welcome, Father. Got any news from the sewers beneath the city streets? If the evil from those sewers doesn't disappear real quick, there's gonna be an exodus!
Well, what can I do, Father. I sincerely hope you're gonna succeed in the end. Could I help you somehow?
Really?! That's excellent news, Father! Finally the city will be quiet at night. I'm so indebted to you. Of course, you'll also get your reward—here you go!
Hello, Father. How is it going? What can I do for you?
Welcome, Father. It's really admirable that you managed to cleanse the city sewers of the evil. Everybody feels much safer now. What can I do for you?
Yes, you've heard right, noble lord. I pay rewards announced by Robert Heidrick for the heads of bandits loitering around the city. Bring me a scalp or head and I'll give you cash on the barrelhead.

So, you'd like to do some shopping in Glatzburgu... Hmmm... depends on what you want, noble lord—guess it ain't vegetables, right? If it's weapons or armor, visit Hans von Drichtmaul—he runs the renowned Glatzburg armory. Wisewoman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus can provide you with potions and magic goods. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum offer various wares. And Alphonso DiCerbio will also sell you almost anything—if you don't mind the origin of his wares. Anyway, it's just a matter of time for you to get enough evidence against him to send him to the gallows.

What do I think 'bout the crisis? It's a pain in the neck, noble lord, well, to be honest, in the ass. I'm an old guy, but I've never seen anything like that in my life. So much madness and rage... fire raining on our heads, terrible famine killing mercilessly both people and cattle, Black Death raging like a dark spirit... One can't wonder people are losing faith and are giving up. You know, despair is an ideal breeding ground for crime... Lotsa people here in Glatzburg believe that the end of the world's coming. All in all, the situation's rather desperate. The people had been hoping for a change, maybe for salvation or redemption, but nothing happened. On the contrary—it's been getting worse and worse every year. You know, noble lord, you won't find many people holding out hope for a brighter future.

Sure I've heard rumors 'bout war, noble lord. I'm a soldier and not too young so I can smell when something's brewing. Nobody's got to tell anything to me. We got the order from Grand Duke Heidrick to be on alert. That means to keep the men in the garrison and be ready to hit the road any moment. We've been also recruiting, though only volunteers so far. Cavalry needs to be replenished so we've been commandeering horses and draft cattle. We've also been trying to fill the granaries with the little we could get hold of. Well, anyway we can't afford to have big expenses, as there's almost nothing to be taxed. All in all that can mean only one thing—a war's coming. Moreover, there's word the First Knight himself should arrive from Alvaron. Don Rodrigo de Velacor, the first marshal of the royal army, is not just someone who'd be treading the Realm without a damn good reason.

That's the most peculiar thing about it, noble lord. Just as you've said—there's no sign of any enemy that would be coming and that we could face. Well, there's lotsa agitation, you know, heretics, pagans, robbers, you name it; the countryside's also crawling with hellspawns and scamps. Anyway you can't fight any of those with any army—the Inquisition and reinforced local garrisons are able to deal with them easily enough. Well, there must be something else, noble lord. That's just what scares me—as well as all the people in the city.
You're welcome, noble lord. Couldn't tell you much, cause I dunno much. Well, but I can guess much.

To tell you the truth, noble lord, there're so many hellspawns and monsters that I don't know where I should send my men first. There are undead crawling in the city streets Every night. If they catch someone, he's as good as dead. The same goes for the cemetery—they are rising from their graves as if the alarm were sounded in the barracks. Roads are besieged by bandits and brigands attacking merchants and solitary travelers. They take everything—both possessions and lives. Well, last but certainly not least, there are those hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns that are near the ruins of Galibornium—that pagan city. They look like a hybrid of man and basilisk and they are as mean and enraged as Satan himself. Damn them all...

Suspicion of heresy... that's a serious matter, noble lord. One must be careful with words when it comes to the accusations of things such as heresy or paganism. I'm a soldier, everything's black or white for me—either attack or withdraw; either ally or enemy. So I can't tell you that I suspect anyone of heresy unless I catch him with a ceremonial knife in one hand and with an innocent virgin in the other. Sorry.

To be honest, I remember better times, ya can bet. Well, in fact I'd never thought I'd live to see something like this. Since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky there have been all kinds of atrocities. Crime's on the rise—murders, robberies, fornication and shit like that are our everyday bread now. I don't know where to send my men first. And to make it worse there are the rumors about a war...

Hello, noble lord. How is it going? What can I do for you?

Really? Good news. I didn't believe he is an heretic. I guess he is going to be a bit angry with you, isn't he? But I think he'll skip this chapter soon, ha ha...

You want to shop? First of all you must know what you're looking for. If it's armor or weapons, go visit Victor Hammerhand. Potions and stuff like that can be bought from brother Dominic, and if you're lucky you could also buy those from Ellisia Würtenrodt or from Theil Brechthold, well, they're both rather moody. Joseph Truthorn and Suzan Brauchner will sell you anything.

Well, I'll tell you what I think about the crisis, knight. It's Hell on earth! God wanted to test us, but I'm sure he didn't expect what happened then. What was he thinking would happen when he took our most precious possessions—our children? What about my Natalia, knight? What did she do to him that He decided to take her to Himself just to find out how deep my faith was? Natalia was a humble and deeply faithful girl, knight. Nobody had any right to take her away from me. Nobody! Understand?!
It's a terrible plague, this crisis, I can tell you. I pray for our children to have a chance to live in a better world...

The worst monsters of all are people, knight. Of course you could admit that orcs and other hellspawns are Satan's brats longing to dip their fangs and claws into human flesh, but believe me, people are much more dangerous. The people who cast away faith and are worshiping idols, mammon, fornication and bloodshed. When you meet an orc you know your life's in danger. But when you meet a man, you can't be sure that although he's smiling today, he won't coldheartedly murder your own daughter tomorrow. Believe me, knight, beware of people!

I've heard some rumors about Duke Weinberg, knight. Well, I usually don't pay much attention to gossip, but this one seems to be not too far from the truth. I'm sure you remember the Scourges of God—people and animals dying of famine and the Black Death, rains of fire devouring dozens of cities and villages... I myself have lost most of my property. And Duke Weinberg? It almost seems as if the Scourges of God avoided him. His still rooms and granaries are full, none of his family members died, and all of his houses are standing proud and tall. That's why I think that the gossip about his compact with Beelzebub can be true.
What interesting has happened lately? My daughter was murdered if you haven't noticed!
The kidnapping of my daughter was the worst thing that happened to me in the last few years. I'm so glad it had a happy ending!

It's hard to tell whether Master Edmond d'Arvias really committed such a godless crime as people say. To be honest I wouldn't be too surprised—times are bad. I always considered him to be an honest man devoted to his holy mission. Anyway, can you believe anyone these days?!

I don't know anything about the missing Monstrance of Saint Orthenius. Somebody probably stole it. Anything's possible nowadays. It seems people went mad, losing all their virtue and humbleness. I wouldn't be surprised if somebody stole entire church.
According to the people Bishop Quentinus disappeared during the recent attack of the orcs against the town. That's why I think he's with our Lord now. May God be merciful to his soul!
Hmm... amen.
I hope you're mistaken.
I hope so too. Bishop Quentinus was a rare man.

I have no idea where you could find Paul Hammerhand. I have a feeling that he's a rather mischievous urchin. My daughter asked him to come to dinner once and since then I've been missing a golden spoon and two silver knives. But I'd hate if something happened to him, anyway...

I don't now anything about the fate of Baroness Linda van Gallagan, knight. I have no idea where she could be. She was probably killed by the orcs, or maybe they kidnapped her to torture her to death—after all, she went missing the night they attacked the town.
I'm looking for the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias, do you happen to know anything about it?

I don't know anything about the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias, knight. Nevertheless I promise that if somebody tries to sell it to me, I'll let you know. I don't know how else I could be of any help in this case.

Of course I've heard about the murder of the merchant Ollmier. It was a revolting case. Moreover the perpetrator has not been apprehended yet and it doesn't seem that he should be arrested any time soon. Sheriff Contemburry put the case on the shelf—the lack of evidence was the reason, I believe. The truth is that the murderer left no traces. That's rather strange as the murder was committed here in the attic of the Truthorn's Inn—where Ollmier had a room rented. If you ask me, I'd say that his business killed him. Nobody knows exactly what his business was, but it mostly included strange stuff from the pagan times. Artifacts, relics, holy items, scrolls, books... all in all pagan dirt.
You may earn yourself suspicion of a crime if you resist the Brotherhood of the Righteous, Reichmann. You better answer me or you're going to see for yourself...
I don't know what exactly you find repulsive about me, good man, but I sincerely believe that you'll be able to overcome your repulsion and will answer my question.
Somebody as erudite as you, Reichmann, surely shouldn't hesitate to answer my very simple question...
She's in the abandoned chapel near the Dragon Rock. Jullian took her there after he kidnapped her.
Well, could you bring her back? I doubt she could return alive on her own—you know, the countryside is crawling with orcs and other hellspawns.
Very well, I will bring her back.
I don't have time for errands like that. I'm sorry.

What? You're not going to help me?! Even though you have found out all those things? You've deeply disappointed me, knight. Well, I'll have to manage without you. I'm not going to leave my daughter prey to those monsters that are swarming behind the walls. Farewell.
I thank you with all my heart, knight! You've brought new hope into my life...
What have you just said? That if I want to prevent my daughter from coming to any harm I must pay... That's blackmail! How could you? What kind of man are you?!
Keep your breath to cool your own moralist porridge if you want to see your daughter alive.

That's heinous! I'd have never thought that a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous could sink as deep as that. What has happened to this world? Here's you dirty gold, knight. And now bring my daughter back, or else...
Else what? You'll tell someone? Who would believe you? You better hold your tongue or I'll get it ripped off!
Don't worry. Farewell.
God be with you. Farewell.
Hello, knight. What brings you here? Have you come to console the soul of an old broken man?

To tell the truth I myself don't know who I am, knight. I used to be Stefan Reichmann until recently. I had a shop in Hillbrandt before the Scourges of God struck. Anyway, although almost all my possessions were destroyed during the Night of the Falling Stars I still had the most precious treasure—my daughter Natalia. She was the treasure of my life, the light of my gloomy days. Who am I now? I don't know. Broken father? Lost soul?
What do you mean by that, good man? Is anything troubling you?
Troubling me? You bet, knight. Isn't the loss of your only daughter, the joy of your sad life, good enough reason to be troubled? She was like a fresh blossom and now she's forever gone. Dead.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?

God took her away from me. I've been a faithful believer all my life—always adhering to all the laws and God's commandments and upholding laws where others cheated. And what did I get for that? My shop was burned to the ground in the Night of the Falling Stars and my only daughter was murdered for a few trinkets not a long time ago. They have not even found her body, so I couldn't bury her. God took everything from me!
Who murdered your daughter?

Who? Who else than that wretch Olfghard. May his name be cursed thrice! Well, he denied everything when they arrested him and was asserting he was innocent, but the evidence was clear. He was apprehended soon after he tried to sell the jewelry of my daughter. I thought that justice would be served and that he would be executed at once, but he managed to escape the jail. I can't understand it. And that incompetent Sheriff Contemburry told me he had no time to look for him! Told me he needs all the men in the town. That's why I decided to help carry out justice myself. I'll pay a handsome amount of gold to anybody who'll bring me Olfghard's head!
I could do that if you wanted me to.
Wait a moment... would you really do it for me? Would you really be willing to find Olfghard and to punish him for what he did to my daughter?
Yes, without hesitation. Olfghard will pay for his crimes and you'll get your revenge!

Thank God that there's at least one man who knows that evil must be punished at all costs. If the law doesn't work it must be substituted by action. Thanks, knight. I'll reward you handsomely for Olfghard's head. God bless you!
Why not. It depends on how much you'd be willing to pay me.
Now, that my Natalia is dead, gold is worthless to me. I'll give you a big pouch of gold for Olfghard's head. I think it's a very generous offer.
I don't want to have anything to do with a blood feud. His guilt can be decided by nobody else than by an independent court!

In that case beat it! I'm not going to discuss anything with people like you, understand? I spit at your name! You call yourself a noble?! Farewell!

What? You've already managed to kill him! Heavens! My daughter is avenged. Her murderer is dead and she can now rest in piece. You've deserved my gratitude and also this pouch of gold. God bless you, noble lord.
Really? And what if you're lying? I won't believe you until you bring me his head, noble lord.
Thanks, noble lord. I must be sure the villain is really dead!
Sorry? Yes, you're probably really sorry. But that won't return her to me, noble lord. And least of all it will get Olfghard hanged. Damn life. Farewell!

Heavens, I hope my eyes aren't deceiving me! Is it really you, Natalia? God, Thank you! I'm sorry if I blasphemed, now I can see that you're just and that you've never turned your face away from me. I thank you with all my heart, noble lord. Please accept this pouch of gold as a token of my undying gratitude!
Thank you, noble lord. You've returned joy to my sad life!

What? You're not going to help me?! Even though you have found out all those things? You've deeply disappointed me, noble lord. Well, I'll have to manage without you. I'm not going to leave my daughter prey to those monsters that are swarming behind the walls. Farewell!
Hello, noble lord. Do you have Olfghard's head for me? The sooner his rotten soul burns in hell the better. He'd deserve to be burning in infernal flames for eternity for killing my daughter!
You've disappointed my hopes, noble lord. If you don't want to help me uphold justice then get lost.

That's heinous! I'd have never thought that a noble could sink as deep as that. What has happened to this world? God is going to damn you for that. Here's your dirty gold and now bring me my daughter or else...

So, noble lord, have you brought me my Natalia?

Hello, noble lord. I'm glad you killed that bastard Olfghard. The death of my daughter is avenged now. What can I do for you?

Oh my God... what are you telling me? My daughter is alive?! I thought that Olfghard murdered her. Everything indicated that. Well, but if it's really as you say and Natalia was kidnapped by Jullian... Then I ordered you to murder an innocent. Woe! I'm damned. God, please forgive me my sins... Anyway, tell me, noble lord, is my daughter alright?

That's heinous! I'd have never though that a noble could sink as deep as that. What has happened to this world? God will damn you for that. Here's your dirty gold, noble lord. And now bring me my daughter or else...
