Get lost, noble lord! I didn't say anything to anyone as you wished. Don't you dare come any closer to me or to my daughter. You've already caused more than enough suffering!

Where could you buy some goods in Alvaron? You mean... to exchange your money for someone's goods? Is that what you think? Well... yes, I think that's possible somewhere, but that's not something I would know as I never needed it...
How is it possible? Don't you ever buy anything?
No, not much. I live like our ancestors—I gather things, you know.
Well... I understand.
Well, I'm not going to talk to you about that!
Yes, I've also heard something about a war. They even told me to get recruited; but I'd have to fall down from my horse right on my head to do something so stupid...
The Fallen Angels? That's the gang of brigands that assaults people on the way to Middenheim, isn't it? Well, those are tough guys... tough as nails!

You're interested in monsters? Well, you must go to see the city cemetery—especially at midnight. It's totally flooded by evil, knight! Living dead feast there on graves and coffins during the night, ghosts fly through the air and a nameless horror is lurking in dark shadows. He who decides to go there will never be seen again—well, he actually might be seen—as one of them...

As far as I know, Grand Duke Drake Lambert set high rewards for catching the werewolves who raid not only in the neighborhood, but also in the streets of our city. Sheriff Henry Portmann pays rewards in exchange for trophies—heads of killed werewolves. It's quite a good job, but it's pretty dangerous! I think that if the reward was set for the heads of hunted people, the werewolves would soon be stinking rich...

The royal burial chamber in the city cemetery is said to be under the control of infernal powers. Since young Prince Louis and his sisters were buried there, nobody has been able to get in. I can tell you it's true—I didn't believe that so I went there to make sure about that myself!
Well, I don't deal in that fake gold, I swear! I've never counterfeited any gold, not even my feces!

Well, I don't have anything to do with that, I swear! I'm not in league with any hairy, drooling werewolf beasts. May my grandmother burn in Hell if I lie—well I'm sure she's already there, but anyway I didn't do it!
Well, I don't have anything to do with the grave robbery, I swear! I didn't rob any graves, someone else must have done that!

Do you know the tale about Wolfenburg, the mansion of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr? People say Wolfenburg has been the seat of the House of Wolfenburgs since the 7th century. Members of the House were fond of cruelty and of violence to the liege people from the beginning. It's said that the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr was the last heir of that House. His name was Duke Ronald in those times and he was even crueler than his ancestors. One day he reputedly laid his hands on a certain young and very beautiful witch who lived near his castle and raped her cruelly.

The violated witch threatened the Duke that she'd inform the Holy Mother Church about him, because it was known the Church took care of the widows and various injured women in trouble. But she shouldn't have done so, because the vicious Duke killed her immediately—without remorse. However, the witch was able to curse the Duke before she died and she changed him into an awful wolf beast. When the liege people of the Duke found out about it, they didn't hesitate and took pitchforks and flails, sharpened the pole-axes and then captured the castle of Wolfenburg. But they didn't get rid of the Duke himself. Yes, there was peace for some time, the ruins of Wolfenburg were invaded only by weeds and everything was slowly fading away, but then people started to go missing in the neighborhood and bloody pieces of their flesh or skin were to be found in the woods around. That is, Duke Ronald returned as the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr to take a bloody tax for what happened to him. And since that time his pack of werewolves has been terrorizing the countryside...

Denying an answer to a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous hasn't ever paid off for anybody. Do you realize what awaits you in that case? Interrogation, torture, imprisonment... I'm sure you don't want to taste any of that. So you should answer my question!
I probably don't belong to the group of people you'd like to talk to. Despite that I ask you to answer my question. I assure you it'll be help for a rightful cause!
I'd really like to get your answer, good man. Because it's visible at first sight that you're clever, experienced and a life-wise man.
I can see some mud on your boots. How did it happen to you?
How the mud could get on my boots? Well, look around, knight. Do you have a feeling we walk only marble roads just like in the Royal Palace?
But that type of clay I can see on your boots can't be found anywhere around. There's only one place I saw it. That is, at the cemetery...
At the cemetery? What would I do there? It's a haunted place... All reasonable people avoid the cemetery!
You lie! I found the prints of your boots around a robbed grave!
I don't know what you're talking about! I haven't been at the cemetery for years—last time I was there I was just a little whelp attending my mother-in-law's funeral!
Well... if you think so. Could I talk to you a little longer?
What do you want to talk to me about? I don't know anything. Well, but if you think so...
Hains Khobzoll alias Steinger, I arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of grave robbery. You'll come with me to face fair trial!
But that must be some kind of mistake! I didn't do anything! I don't know anything about any graves. I swear on the death of my mother-in-law!
Your boots betrayed you. There's the traces of clay on them that can be found only at one place in the city cemetery—near one of the robbed graves. Bad luck for you!

Oh my God... I told him we'd be caught one day! I told him we should go to Glatzburg and join some brigands. I told him, but he was stubborn as a mule and he said this was much safer and yielding and we'd never get caught. I was stupid when I listened to him!
I take it as the confession—and I praise you for that. However, now you should tell me who's that accomplice you talked about.

Vick, knight. Vick Length. He was the one who made me to take part in this business. He said the dead couldn't defend themselves and that they didn't need anything anyway, because they rot in the ground and their souls are either in purgatory, or in Heaven or in Hell.
I hope your testimony was true. If it was, the trial will take account of that. If you lied, you'll be tortured.

Tortured? Oh my God, no, please... I can't stand to see blood. Well, at least to see my own blood... I'm sure I would get sick! Please, knight, let me go! I'll run away as far as possible, change my life, enter the monastery, I'll do good deeds and will live according to the God's Commandments, just give me a chance, please!
Well.. maybe I could give you a chance. But you know, if I scratch your back, you'll scratch mine—your amendment is not enough for me—I would have no benefit from that!
I see. In that case I'll tell you where Vick and I have hidden most of our loot. It's big enough for you not to lack money till the end of your life, knight.
All right, let's have a deal—tell me where your loot is hidden and I'll let you go.

I agree, knight. I promise you won't hear about me again! The place where our loot is hidden is near the Citadel of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. It's under a big stone ten steps north from the hundred years old fir; and the fir is located about fifty steps east from the road to the Citadel. You can't miss it!
All right, thank you. You can go. I hope I won't hear about you again!
I promise you won't, knight. I'd say this lesson was instructive enough. Farewell!
Thank you. And now I arrest you—you'll come with me!
That's betrayal! We had an agreement...
Call it God's justice. Let's go!
I'm sorry, you're arrested. Let's go!
Pa... pardon? What do you want from me, knight? I didn't do anything! You don't have any proof against me!
Quiet, good man. Tell me who you are.
Who I am? Why do you want to know when you don't have anything against me?
I didn't say I had anything against you. I just asked you who you were.
I see... well, if you think so—my name is Hains Khobzoll, but all call me Steinger. After that renowned minstrel.
Nice to meet you. Could I talk to you for a moment?
What do you want to talk about? I don't know anything! Well, but if you insist...
I see, so you can sing and play musical instruments?

No, I can't do that. But I can get out of any trouble as well as he could. For example when he was caught with Lady Rossalinda de Winfredheim and they wanted to make a wine chalice from his skull. Not only didn't they succeed in that, but Steinger also ran away from them and composed a ballad about it; and he won the minstrel tournament in Portorian with that ballad.
And what should I have against you?
I don't know... anything. You're a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous and those often have something against various people they don't like!
Is that you, knight? What do you want from me again? I've already told you I don't have anything to do with anything...
Calm down, good man. I just want to talk to you for a moment...
I see. Well, what do you want to talk to me about, heh?
In that case I won't disturb you.
Yes, that's reasonable. Because the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous give me creeps...
Your money or your life!
Is that you, Steinger? Haven't I told you I didn't want to see you again till the end of my life?

Damned... is that you, knight? What are you doing here? I thought you had some urgent things to do in Alvaron... Well, there's nothing we can do when you're here already. So what will you choose—to give me your money, or your life? For me it's the same in fact, because if you don't give me your money, I'll kill you and take it anyway!
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to give you my money.
In that case I'll take it myself!
All right, I'll give you the money. Here you are.
You're a very reasonable man, knight. I wish more people were like you. Nowadays, people stick to each gold piece like a hungry dog to a marrowbone...
It's me, Steinger. You've already ambushed me once and I gave you all I had.

Ssssssaaaaaaaahhhhhhhh!!! Listen to me, sons and daughters of Bhelfelix. Our time has come! Time of our revenge is here! Hundreds of years of waiting have come to an end—the time of our return and of our bloody revenge has come at last! The world of men will belong to us, as it was foretold. The cult of Bhelfelix will rule and all will bow down to us!
What? Who's talking here? Who are you? Some unclean ghost or a wicked demon?

I'm the one who died to wait for the time of revenge. I'm the one who brings death as a repayment to the servants of the "one and only" God for what they did to him! And the same will be done by my brothers and sisters who died and came to take revenge on you—you'll harvest the storm you seeded when you hanged us, the men, the women and the children; hanged us on this tree as if we were scabby dogs. Now you'll get to know the anger of Bhelfelix—the time has come to the end and your God is dying. We're coming back to walk through the lands of men, to destroy and to plunder.
What? I won't allow you to do that! I'll stop you, fallen pagan souls!
Silence, poor mortal! You'll be among the first to die. Raise, brothers and sisters! In the name of Bhelfelix—charge! Unga ghar, apthor thar!!!
Wait, fallen soul—I'm sure there is a possibility to redress the wrongs that were done to you and to your fellows...

Silence, poor mortal! No time left to redress anything! Your generation will be punished for the sins of your grand-grandfathers. Raise, brothers and sisters. In the name of Bhelfelix—charge! Unga ghar, apthor thar!!!
What's happening here? What are you doing here, knight? And who is... Oh my God! This is... Bishop Trevorius! He's... dead! By all the saints, what happened here?
That's what I'd like to know too. Bishop Trevorius was assassinated, that's clear. We must find his murderers!
He was murdered? Well, really, it seems so... And his body is still warm. That's very suspicious... Lonely place, nobody around, only you, knight...
I want to tell you it seems very suspicious to me! Probably it will be best to report it to Cardinal Truncquillius immediately. He'll decide what to do with you.
If you think so, good man. I've nothing to hide.
I think it's not necessary to mention that I was here, good man.
Oh, really? And how do you want to arrange it, knight? I believe it's absolutely necessary to tell the Cardinal about it. As soon as possible.
I'll give you a pouch of gold if you won't talk about me. Please, say only that you found the Bishop Trevorius murdered.

Well... I don't like that. I won't let you bribe me, especially in the case of the murder of the Bishop of our Diocese. I can smell the scaffold from it. I'm sorry, knight. Authorities must be informed.
In that case I'll have to kill you all—you don't give me any other choice.
I'll have to kill you all—you don't give me any other choice!
What if I ask you nicely?
Keep your asking, knight. Authorities must be informed!
