Oh my God... what an awful place this is? What crimes were committed here?
It seems that some heretic ritual was performed here. Someone eviscerated thirteen newborns and put their viscera into the belly of a black goat... Oh God, what a smell...
Because of the stream of dry air flowing through the cave those bodies aren't rotten; they became mummified. According to that, one could conclude the ritual was performed several years ago.
On the other hand—someone obviously comes here from time to time to light the candles... Maybe because of some perverse piety!
Those who committed those crimes must be punished!
All right, come to me. I'll give you a soothing embrace.
Oh, really? What a surprise. Only a few men would let someone like me come closer to them...
Because most men know well what would happen to them in that case... Don't tell me you don't know what I mean!
Do you mean illness?
No. I mean death! Yeeeaaarghhh!
Silence, you infernal monster! I'm not here to satisfy your perverse lust!
Do you offend me? Excellent. I like it when a man is angry with me. You will be even angrier when I tear your bowels away from your belly and I'll be dancing with them around you! Yeeeaaarghhh!
It seems to me that nobody can satiate you anymore, princess. You're burning with infernal flame!

Yes, that's true. But on the other hand I still like to do what I want to do. Do you know, knight, what I'd like to do at the moment? I'd like to tear your bowels away from your belly and to dance with them around you. Yeeeaaarghhh!

I'm bored, I'm so terribly bored... I wish there was someone to entertain me here... And now I see, a young brave knight is coming just in the nick of time. And he's handsome! Come to me, my beloved friend, I must confess! My soul is burning and needs satiation...
Who am I? What a silly question... I'm Princess Theresia, the Grand Duchess of Vandricht and the Baroness of Dracht. Come to me, and I will whisper my professions of love into your ear...
Not a step closer, you awful monster!
I'm not an awful monster—I'm Princess Theresia, the Grand Duchess of Vandricht and the Baroness of Dracht. Come to me, and I will whisper my professions of love into your ear...
All right, confess to me. I'll listen to you gladly.
Oh, really? What a surprise. Only a few priests would let someone like me come close to them...
Because most of the clerics well know what would happen to them in that case... Don't tell me you don't know what I mean!
Do you mean a violation of the celibate?
I'm not interested in your confession, you monster of Hell. Your crimes are evident at first sight!
It seems to me that the confession can't save you from Hell, Lady Princess. Well, it seems you already belong to Hell!

Yes, that's true. But on the other hand I still like to do what I want to do. Do you know, Father, what I'd like to do at the moment? I'd like to tear your bowels away from your belly and to dance with them around you. Yeeeaaarghhh!

I'm bored, I'm so terribly bored... I wish there was someone to entertain me here... Let's see, some young priest is coming here just in the nick of time. And he's handsome! Come to me, my beloved friend, I must confess! My soul is burdened with a deadly sin and needs absolution...
Who am I? What a silly question... I'm Princess Theresia, the Grand Duchess of Vandricht and the Baroness of Dracht. Come to me, I must whisper my confession into your ear...
I'm not an awful monster—I'm Princess Theresia, the Grand Duchess of Vandricht and the Baroness of Dracht. Come to me, I must whisper my confession into your ear...

Yes, that's true. But on the other hand I still like to do what I want to do. Do you know, noble lord, what I'd like to do at the moment? I'd like to tear your bowels away from your belly and to dance with them around you. Yeeeaaarghhh!

I'm bored, I'm so terribly bored... I wish there was someone to entertain me here... And now I see, a young noble lord is coming just in the nick of time. Well, and he's handsome! Come to me, my beloved friend, I must confess! My soul is burning and needs satiation...

What do I think about the current crisis? It's a work of heretics and pagans, of godless and damned people and of other lunatics! Let them all burn at the stake, let their souls be purged and released from their sinful bodies because only after that peace and order will be returned to the Realm! The question is, when will this goal be reached. It takes more time than anybody expected and the end still seems not to be on the horizon...
I'm sorry, but I'm not interested in the weather too much.

You're interested in the Fallen Angels, my son? I must say that's a very dark part of our religion. Common people think that just saying the name of a Fallen Angel aloud can draw the attention of that terrible hellspawn to them...
Do you also think so, Your Excellency?

Me? Well... it's hard to say. Definitely it's not easy for me to say those names aloud—they belong to the most terrible servants of the Hell ruler himself! They're former Angels who were punished for their sins—together with Satan the Tempter they plotted to betray God Almighty at the Dawn of Time. The Scriptures say that because of their betrayal they were thrown down to the Earth and chained in Hell to suffer there for their sins forever. Since that time the hellspawns have been trying to get back to take control of both the Earth and Heaven. Altogether, there are four Fallen Angels—Arthamon, the Master of Ruination, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the Succubus and Fornicatress and the Archangel Azrael, Satan's Emissary and Advocate of Evil.

I don't suspect anybody in particular of heresy, son. However, it doesn't mean there can't be a dissipated heretic close to me having intercourse with demons during the night and being hidden behind the mask of a peaceful and faithful believer during the day. You must be very cautious, my son. Yes, very cautious!

The Cult of the Children of the New Order? That name really does ring a bell with me. If I remember correctly, it was a heretic cult formed and then acting in the Empire during the Hundred Years War. It was just another group of demoniacs—quite wide spread in those times. People turned to demon worshipping during times of the worst indigence—I'd say it resembled the situation in the Realm nowadays. However, the cult was nothing like a league of poor men preaching that everybody can do whatever he wanted. The cult was founded by a certain Lucius who called himself the Dark Prophet and heralded to his followers that the New Order will come and its children will rule the world—by the means of releasing Satan from his imprisonment.

The cult spread quickly after its founding and reached the highest circles of imperial society. Fortunately, all the heretics were revealed by the Papal Inquisitional Curia in the end and all of them were executed—including the prophet Lucius himself. That was the end of the whole cult. There hasn't been any news about it since that time.

Although there is some antagonism—to put it mildly—between the Inquisition and the Brotherhood of the Righteous, I can't but regret the death of the old Master Conrad von Thaum who is said to have been killed during an unsuccessful attempt to cleanse a lair of werewolves in Schwarzwald. The loss is even worse because of the fact that his renowned Decapitator Sword got into the hands of the powers of Hell. It's a great pity for the whole faithful world!
Could the Royal Counselor Verenicus be involved in the murder of Prince Louis? Yes, that's possible. I don't know any reason why he couldn't.

Because we live in the time when almost anything is possible. I must tell you, dear son, I'm terribly tired of that. I've already served almost twenty years in the Inquisition and I've started to lack the power lately... It's the same every time—suspicion, investigation, revealing the truth, arresting, torture, execution—and it's endless! In addition to that there's always a lot of betrayal, falsehood, hypocrisy, intrigues and also of blackmailing... that's why I think nobody can conclusively be said to be completely innocent.

The Inquisitor General a heretic? My God... I've never been asked that question myself. How could I answer you, dear son? Cardinal Commendoni is my superior; he's the highest representative of the institution I've been devotedly working for, for almost twenty years. Should I tell you that really anything is possible? That would be heresy... and betrayal! No, my son, I can't give you an answer for such a question. I can't. I mustn't!

Of course I've heard about the rape of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert—that is to say, the accused person is an Inquisitor! Unfortunately I don't know about any facts that would relieve brother Nicolas of the suspicion. I'm sorry.

You've probably heard some of the legends about Saint Orthenius people often tell. Something like that Saint Orthenius is going to come down from Heaven at the head of an army of angels and save the Realm from all the evil, or that his followers will come from the common folks and burn the enemies of the true faith with the flame of divine justice. I don't know what's true about the legends but there is a place near to Alvaron where Saint Orthenius was buried in 223. Until recently it was one of the most sacred pilgrimage destinations and for the last thousand years crowds of the faithful would travel to see the remains of the patron of our Realm. But now...

During the reign of King Henry the Third, beautiful gardens called the King's Gardens were planted around the crypt. The place was full of flowering bushes, evergreen grass, exotic trees and of wooden gazebos attracting people to rest. For several generations of nobles the Gardens became a place to spend most of their leisure time. When the Star of Doom appeared in the sky, the Gardens were one of the first places to be ruined. During the few years when the Scourges of God were pestering the Realm the Gardens changed beyond recognition—and they're called the Gardens of Grief now.
Don't waste your time, son—I won't let you bribe me!
You had better answer me, Your Excellency. Even your high position can't save you from the wrath of God that could strike you in the case you'd try to hide something...
I can see you don't like me very much, Your Excellency. However, I'd like to assure you that no matter what you think about me, your answer won't do any harm to anyone.
You're a very wise man, Your Excellency. So wise that you're the only one who could give me that answer. Please, answer my question.

This is a very serious decision, son. The Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition is here to judge the cases of the most serious crimes committed by the highest representatives of the society of the Realm. Whom does your accusation concern?

Really? That's very serious... although I must say I'm not surprised. I've heard several suspicions of heresy concerning Grand Master de Malamert lately. However, the investigation hasn't been started against him yet, mostly because of his high position. So tell me, what proof do you have against the Grand Master?

Petrier de Duby, a neophyte of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, confessed that Grand Master de Malamert attempts to disrupt the Realm with the help of the powers of Hell whom he serves. Moreover we found two of Grand Master's letters in which he gives instructions to his minions how they should proceed in their joint plot to disrupt the Realm.

Well... your proof speak clearly, my son. I won't try to hide I'm quite surprised that so many straight proofs were found against Grand Master de Malamert, however if that's how the things are... I don't have any other choice but to agree with this accusation. If you will be able to get the approval of two more members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition you will be approved to arrest the Grand Master. You should leave now, my son. I must think a lot about the proof you told me about.
Well... thank you, Your Excellency. However, I must say I'm surprised you gave me the approval to arrest Grand Master de Malamert so easily.

Oh, really? In that case you should think about the importance and cogency of the proof you showed me. Because the Grand Master can be accused of heresy only on the basis of those proofs and I doubt you would be in his good grace should the accusation against him be discharged! Now you should go and think what else you could do to support your statements.
Are you serious, my son, or is it some kind of a joke? If it's a joke, I'll give you good advice: don't try to be funny ever again—your jokes could easily turn against you!
It isn't a joke, Your Excellency. You're a judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition, so I'd like to show you the proof of heresy of the Inquisitor General Commendoni.
No, my son, don't do it. No matter how cogent your arguments would be I'd never give you my approval to accuse Cardinal Commendoni of heresy. Never, my son.
Why? Isn't it possible the Inquisitor General is guilty? Satan has thousands of faces...

I'm sorry, my son, but I can't tell you about my reasons. You can believe me that I'd like to do it, but I can't. Because of that I advise you to leave and to stop thinking about it. Take things as they are; Cardinal Commendoni is an unshakable pillar of the Holy Office—and thus of the Holy Mother Church—and it's unthinkable to affront such a pillar. No, it won't bring anything good, you can trust me on that! Farewell, my son.
Well... if you think so.

I've already told you, my son, that I can't agree with the accusation of the Inquisitor General of heresy or of any other crime. I simply can't—imagine how the Holy Mother Church would be affected. We can't afford such misconduct. Go away, please.
I'm sorry, Your Excellency, but I'm not going to leave till I'll get your approval. I'm sure you'll give it to me in the end. Surely you don't want everybody to get to know about your secret...
What...?! You want to threaten me?! That's unprecedented! I must protest strongly against your behavior, son! Go away and search your conscience! Our dialog is ended!
As you wish, Cardinal. But in that case I can't promise you I won't reveal your secret... Well, it's your decision!

Wait, my son! I... I didn't know somebody else could know about it except... them. But it seems that everybody around will talk about it soon. There isn't any other choice—I committed a sin and nothing in the world can help me. Any service to God can't clear me of the deadly sin I committed. I'll be judged both by the world and by God himself and I'll be thrown to Hell where I'll have to serve the dark powers forever and ever...
I'm sure you can still save your soul, Your Excellency. If you would like to do it!

Do you think so, my son? I doubt it. Fornication is a deadly sin... especially when it had such tragic consequences. I was the one who caused her death... she was unable to bear the disgrace. Why, she was a nun! And now, thirteen years later, the fruits of my crime strive after my life. Well, it's only fair. Nevertheless, I loved her so much! How could I succumb to my passion...?
It's human to err. That's why the First Prophet died on the Cross—to take our sins from us, because we would be unable to get rid of them otherwise.
Maybe you're right, my son. I made a firm decision—I must release that poor child from the curse—at all costs! Even in the case I'll die because of that!
Wait, Your Excellency—you can't die now, I need your approval to accuse the Inquisitor General of heresy. Tell me all and I'll help you, you'll see.

Oh, really? Well... why not, in fact—you know about it anyway, and if you wanted to destroy me, you had a chance to do it long ago. So—when I was a mere priest and I served as a scribe in the Archbishop's Office, I couldn't resist the wiles of eternal sin and I had a strong desire for one priestess of the nun Order of St. Bethesda. However, she didn't return my sinful desire because she was deeply devoted to her service to God. She wanted to preserve her purity, as it's right and proper for any servant of God, but I wasn't able to reconcile with her decision and led by an uncontrollable passion I laid my hands on the priestess with violence.
Go on, Your Excellency.

Immediately I was appalled by what I had done and I asked both God and the priestess to forgive me, but they didn't forgive me at all. Because of my act of violence, my daughter Joan was born after nine months, and the tainted priestess was excommunicated from her Order because of that. Moreover, she lost her sanity during childbirth and immediately after that she took her own life. But before she left our world she cursed our daughter Joan to take a terrible revenge on me. The girl died after thirteen days and was laid in a nameless grave. I thought the whole tragedy was forgotten, but I made a terrible mistake.
The curse started to take effect after many years, didn't it?

Yes, exactly. Joan didn't die, but fell into some kind of dark sleep, during which she grew up and turned into a terrible stryx. After thirteen years the girl came out from her grave and started to look for me. Maybe you've heard about the ghost of a dead girl who walked around the cemetery and was looking for the revenge on her lecherous father—that's me. The people say nobody can kill her before the curse reaches fruition—that is before I die.
I'll take care of it, Your Excellency. I'll dispel Joan's curse and you'll give me the approval to arrest the Inquisitor General.

You would do that for me, dear son? God bless you. I was praying for so many years that nothing would threaten my position. I was very ambitious, I wanted to reach as high as possible. But then I started to understand I was living with a terrible sin and now the time has come to set things right. If you are able to remove the curse from my daughter I want to take care of her, to return to her the life she lost because of me. I can't return her mother to her, but still I can be her father!
What a wise decision. Could I talk to you a little longer? I have a few questions...
Of course you can, my son.
All right, we have an agreement, Your Excellency. Farewell for now.
Farewell, my son.
Do you think that when the curse is removed the girl will become a normal human being?
I hope with all my heart, son. I expect her intellect will be on the level of a small child, but I'm ready to bring her up with a lot of patience and care to make her a human being.

No, Your Excellency, I'm not going to leave. On the contrary—I'm going to stay here and to talk to you about your true reasons why you don't want to approve the arrest of the Inquisitor General. I believe the discussion will be very interesting and full of surprise...
I've nothing to talk to you about. Please, leave—immediately!

I'm Giovanni Timore, a Pope's legate and a judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition. Come closer, my son, and tell me about the issue because of which you came to me. What do you want from me?
I'm glad to meet you, Your Excellency.
Maybe you are, son. However I can't say I have enough time to talk to all the priests I meet during the day. Thus, tell me about the issue of which you came to me about; what do you want from me?
I wanted to meet you personally, Your Excellency, and to ask you a few questions on that occasion...
Questions? What questions do you want to ask me, son? What's the matter?
I need to get a few answers from you that would surely help me in my holy mission...
All right, ask your questions, but try to be brief. I can't spend too much time with you.
I wanted to personally meet one of the most renowned members of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition in the Realm, Your Excellency.

Oh, really? That's a surprise to me... but on the other hand I can understand it. The power that the individual members of the Tribunal have in their hands is really great; but it's also a great responsibility, you can believe me of that, dear son.
How long have you been the member of the Supreme Tribunal?
The Archbishop Laurencius gave me the office of a judge of the Supreme Tribunal judge in 1120, immediately after the first Scourge of God struck the Realm.
Who can become a member of this highest trial authority of the Holy Office?

Only the best of the best, my son. I tell it without shame, because I meet those conditions. As for the formal conditions, only a canonized Bishop or a Pope's legate, id est a Cardinal, can be a member of the Tribunal. However, even then he must prove his high moral qualities, knowledge of the law and of theology... The nomination of a proper candidate must be offered as a proposal by a group of at least three Bishops or Cardinals and the decision itself belongs to the Archbishop of the Holy Mother Church who's the official head of the Holy Office.
That's interesting. Could I ask you some more questions, Your Excellency?
All right, ask your questions. But try to be brief, I don't have much time...
That's really interesting, Your Excellency. Nice to have met you, but I'll have to be going now. Duty calls.
Farewell in that case, son.
I didn't come with any specific issue, Your Excellency.
You didn't? Excuse me in that case, please, I must get back to my work. Farewell to you.
What do you want from me, my son? I don't have too much time...
All right then, ask your questions; but be brief, will you?
There's nothing in particular on my mind, Your Excellency.
Hail to you, my dear son. Can I ask you about your effort to remove the curse from my daughter Joan? Every hour is an unspeakable torment for me...
I haven't achieved any success yet, Your Excellency. I'm sorry.
Never mind... Maybe you'll be more successful in the future. So why did you come to me?
All right then, ask your questions; but be brief, will you? As a judge of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition I don't have much time to talk to you.
I found a way how to remove your daughter's curse. I need to consecrate the grave of Joan's mother and after that I must make Joan drink a flask of your blood.

Good Heavens... so you say the curse can be removed? Lord God be praised! The grave of Joan's mother is located near the scaffold... as a self-murderer she couldn't be buried in holy ground. As for the flask of my blood... wait, I'll arrange it immediately, son. Ahhh... what is a little pain in comparison to the life of my daughter? So... here is the flask, son. Take it and perform the will of God...
Thank you. Could I talk to you a little longer?
Of course. However, please, don't let me waste your precious time when you can devote it to your mission.
Farewell, dear son. God be with you. I pray for the success of your effort!
Hail to you, my son. Can I ask you if you were successful in removing the curse from my daughter Joan?
Yes, the work is done. Joan's curse was removed. She's awaiting you in the Royal Chapel at the cemetery.

Good Heavens... Lord God be praised for your noble deeds, my dearest son! Now I'll be able to atone for some of my sins and thus repay the debt I have to Joan and to her poor mother. Thank you, son. Without your help my soul couldn't even hope for salvation. I give you my approval to arrest the Inquisitor General Commendoni. May your effort be successful. I resign from any further membership in the Holy Office and to all the other activities in the Holy Mother Church—there's no place for me there anymore. I'll leave with Joan, go far away from all evil and I'll try to set right that which I caused by my sin. Farewell, son. God protect you!
Farewell, Your Excellency.
Never mind... I hope you'll be more successful in the future. What can I do for you?
I'd like to talk to you for a moment, Your Excellency.
All right. However, don't let me waste your precious time when you can devote it to your mission, please.
Nothing, Your Excellency. I just happened to come by. Farewell.
Stop acting like a fool, son. Trying to rob a member of the Supreme Tribunal of the Inquisition isn't a bright idea at all...
It's come to my knowledge you've seen soldier Harph entering the deserted city sewers accompanied by undead. Is it true?
What?! Who told you that? None of that's true, it's a lie. I don't know anything about that, and I haven't seen or heard anything. So keep such questions to yourself.
It's written in the diary of soldier Harph I found in his den deep in the city sewers. So don't pretend you haven't seen anything. What happened then?
And what'll you do with Harph if I tell you? Will he be brought to justice? Will you get me rid of him?
If he's found guilty he'll be brought to justice. And now tell me what happened.

I... caught the mongrel Harph entering the city sewers accompanied by several living dead. It was just by coincidence I was there, I didn't want to cross his path. But when I tried to make my getaway those beasts of his found me out. I thought he would let them rip me to pieces, but instead he put a pouch of gold into my hand and told me to enjoy it. And he warned me that if I said a word to anyone about what I had seen, he'd let the undead monsters eat me alive! You can't imagine the horror of seeing him. His eyes glowed like he was mad. Yes, he must be mad, there's no other explanation.
I hope you'll arrest him, knight. That you'll do something about him. If he got to know I told you...

You wanna know who rules Glatzburg? That's easy, our ruler's Grand Duke Heidrick, knight. He's the highest representative of temporal power both near and far. But he hasn't got much power left, because almost everything is a crime against the Faith now and such crimes are in the jurisdiction of the Inquisition, as you surely know. The royal vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin who squints at the governor's office. I have a feeling he's up to something...

Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned store with arms and armor. Alchemist Paolus Ventimus and the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt sell all kinds of potions and magic widgets. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum trade in all kinds of stuff, it's sort of a junk-store. But sometimes you can manage to buy something good from them. And if you don't care about the origin of the goods you buy then you may visit Alphonso DiCerbio—if he hasn't been arrested yet.

I don't know. I don't think about it much. But I'm sure it's gonna be quite inspiring for playwrights and that there's gonna be lots of plays in which I could get the lead role. I would certainly save the day in those plays and all would admire me and recognize me as a great hero.
Have you heard anything about a coming war? The word is people in the city talk about it a lot.

Yes, I've heard about the war. It's said new rookies are being recruited, all sorts of assets are being requisitioned and granaries are being filled... it will be a scuffle. As in the fifteenth year during the war against the heretics of Almadon. Duke Rowan van Leerin participated in the campaign and to this day he has been boasting about it as if the victory was his doing and not the work of Field Marshal Goffred of Auschpuck. I spoke with a landsknecht who was there during the slaughter near the Pond of Kalbern. He told me that when the Almadonians sounded the charge and stormed the right flank of the army of the Realm like hungry hounds our Duke lost all self-esteem and rushed under a wagon with provisions. Afterwards he maintained he wanted to guard it against the enemy and single-handedly killed five Almadonian soldiers there. But who would believe that?

If I were you I would be very careful where I go around Glatzburg. You may encounter monsters wanting only to feed on your entrails. For example the beasts dwelling in the Devil's Caverns not far off Galibornium. Have you heard about them? Reputedly they're some infernal bastards, crossbreeds of men and basilisks. As if an infernal lizard has fornicated with a woman and she then gave birth to a child with scales instead of skin, lizard mouth instead of face and with a long jagged tail above his ass. There must be hordes of those beasts in the Devil's Caverns because when they go hunting from time to time there is terrible havoc left wherever they come. And yes, they hunt people, whom else?
I don't know anything about rewards for killing any monsters. But sheriff Smith pays rewards in gold for catching footpads. To be precise for their heads or scalps.

In my judgement almost everybody is a heretic, knight. You'll probably be angry, but the nobility, the townsfolk, the common people and even the clergy, all are heretics with only few exceptions. Because what's the heresy? It's the deviation from that what's written in the Holy Scriptures. At least a preacher who passed through Glatzburg some time ago said so. And what do the Holy Scriptures say? That we should live in poverty and humility. Not only the common people as the nobility and the clergy say, but all of us—to a man.
Really?!

We should pray, praise our Lord and every now and then eat something in order not to starve to death. But what do people do nowadays? They have enough of all, don't deny themselves a thing, contravene all kinds of commandments and thus disobey God. And the preacher said that a heretic is not only one who praises Satan and hellspawns and kisses goats' tail on Sabbaths, but also one who has diverted from the life described in the Holy Scriptures. What have you to say about that?
I'd say that you might get accused of heresy for such opinions!
I see... that would explain why the preacher was arrested and burned by the Inquisition. So forget what I've just told you. Just to be sure.
I think you're right. At least partially.

Really? Then I don't know why the preacher was arrested and burned by the Inquisition. Well, it will be better if we both forget about our conversation. None of us can change a bit of it, so why should we care?
Who was the preacher? I think I'd like to ask him several questions...
I don't know his name. But he was burned some time ago. By the Inquisition. So they outran you, knight. Well, it will be better if we both forget about our conversation, won't it?

I've heard the city executioner Yan Flemberg is scared shitless. It seems that the executed Duke Istwan de Bragho who was the governor of Glatzburg before Duke Rowan van Leerin has risen from his grave to take his revenge on those who got him executed. Have you heard anything about it?
No, I haven't heard about that.

I see. So, the thing is that Duke Istwan de Bragho was quite an asshole. He was conspiring with dark powers and used them to kidnap girls and boys—he raped them to satisfy his perverse whims. He was a sodomite and a murderer, but he was also clever and a noble on top of it. So it took some time to find evidence against him. Several paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous decided to take care of him, tough guys, I must say, who'd beat the shit out of anybody, but for a long time even they were unable to find anything. But then a kidnapped girl managed to escape and denunciate him.

Bragho knew it's a matter of life and death and he bolted out but the paladins there were five of them overtook him and handed him over to justice. The execution was splendid, it was a perfect drama, and I'm an expert on these things. People enjoyed themselves, the Duke was gradually losing his skin, his limbs, eyes and so on, but when he was near death he uttered a terrible curse. He told them he would return and settle the score with everyone.

As I said. Certainly people got quite nervous and lost their temper. But the curse was targeted only at those who stood behind the Duke's death at those five paladins and of course at Flemberg who conducted the execution he did splendidly, by the way. Eventually the Duke went to Hell and nothing happened for several years. People almost forgot about it, but this spring tidings started to spread all of a sudden that the paladins who caught the Duke were dying one after another. And not only dying they were being murdered, and in quite a frightful way. All five of them have snuffed it by now. So it really seems the late Bragho returned from Beyond to settle the score with them. And the last one left is Yan Flemberg.
You're welcome, knight. It's a sad story, isn't it? And full of blood, I'd say.
Yes, I've heard about it.
I see. So I won't bother you.
I happen to know something about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. And I better tell you before someone starts to suspect me. Because I know who murdered the Bishop!
What? You saw the murder of Bishop Trevorius? Speak!

Yes, it's so. I was hanging around the Grand Duke's gazebo when I heard somebody coming. No sooner than I managed to hide in the nearest bush a person entered the gazebo. She was dressed in a riding habit—it was a very fine one, it had to cost quite a lot of gold. Regrettably I didn't recognize her, but I'm sure it was a woman because she walked kinda elegantly. She sat on a bench and it looked as if she was resting. After a while the Bishop appeared all of a sudden, and it seemed to me he was surprised somebody was in the gazebo. But evidently they knew each other because the Bishop entered the gazebo and they were talking for some time. The woman offered him something from her hip flask then, they drank and then she left. The Bishop stood there for a while more, then he started to rattle, fell down, held his stomach, hacked around him and then he popped off. Such horror seized me that I ran away from there as fast as I could.
So you really didn't recognize the woman?
No, knight. But she had to be from a wealthy family, given that she was able to afford such clothes...
What a pity. But thank you all the same for telling me.
You're welcome, knight. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon.

I've heard a lot about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. For example that you're in trouble, knight. They say you were caught above the Bishop's dead body even before it got cold. I tell you, it's very dangerous to let yourself be caught near a corpse. Because it's all the same if you're guilty or not the suspicion sticks to you like black pitch. But fortunately you're innocent.
Simple I saw who murdered the Bishop.
What? You saw the murderer of Bishop Trevorius? Speak!

Yes, it's so. I was hanging around the Grand Duke's gazebo when I heard somebody coming. No sooner than I managed to hide in the nearest bush a person entered the gazebo. She was dressed in a riding habit, and a very fine one, it had to cost quite a lot of gold. Regrettably I didn't recognize her, but I'm sure it was a woman because she walked kinda elegantly. She sat on a bench and it looked as if she was resting. After a while the Bishop appeared all of a sudden.

It seemed to me he was surprised somebody was in the gazebo. But evidently they knew each other because the Bishop entered the gazebo and they were talking for some time. The woman offered him something from her hip flask then, they drank and then she left. The Bishop stood there for a while more, then he started to rattle, fell down, held his stomach, hacked around him and then he popped off. Such horror seized me that I ran away from there as far as I could.
The story goes you're behind many thefts. Do you happen to know anything about the necklace of Commander Ethien de Pasque?

No, knight, I don't know a thing about the necklace of Knight de Pasque. I swear! And I feel sort of hurt that I'm being blamed for all that happens in Glatzburg. Am only I to blame for everything? If I really stole all that I'm blamed of stealing, I would already live as a rich man somewhere far away.
I'm glad, knight. I really have nothing to do with it. I'm not as crazy as to make enemies of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
I don't believe you, Tinthan. I think you're lying.
I am not lying, knight, I swear by all what's holy to me. I even haven't seen the necklace, let alone to steal it. I'm not as crazy as to make enemies of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

The name of the nobleman doesn't ring a bell to me, knight. But if you're interested in the remains of realms long dead then I advise you to search in the woods around the von Hunth's estate. I came upon all sorts of interesting things there... and I even managed to sell some of them.
I'm searching for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul. Do you have any idea where it could be? It's told Bonhart hid it somewhere before he went to the war.

All sorts of people have searched for Bonhart's hammer, knight. Even I've turned quite a few stones in the vicinity of the city, but of course I didn't find anything. Nobody knows exactly where Bonhart buried his treasure. Some say it's at the gallows, others say it's somewhere in the ruins of Galibornium. I personally think he buried it somewhere else, but I don't know where.

Have you heard the legends about the ghosts in the ruins of Galibornium, knight? It's said that when Saint Orthenius and his faithful armies conquered Galibornium in the year 223, he ordered all its inhabitants to be gathered at a large square in the middle of the burning city. There he let them choose: either they could accept baptism or be executed. Many pagans quickly thought better of their polytheism and were baptized, but there were also lots of those who didn't accept the true faith and stayed true to their gods and goddesses. And those were executed without mercy. It's said there was blood up to your knees, knight.
Yes, I can imagine that very lively. Continue.

When the war fury was over and the fires in the city died out the assembly met and decided to rename the city to Glatzburg—it reputedly means The Holy Stronghold—and settle it with the faithful. So the torn-down houses were rebuilt, the battered down rampart was piled up, the despoiled palaces were rebuilt and so on. But by some infernal plot all of a sudden ghosts of the killed pagans started to appear in the city. At first they only wailed in the streets and gave everyone the creeps, but after some time they pitched into people, smiting them hip and thigh. A fair number of other monsters that started to appear from the depths of the earth joined them, so people ran away in disorder and soon the city was empty. So the assembly met once again and decided Glatzburg would be moved several miles away and that it would be built from scratch. And Galibornium was left to its own fate.
What happened next with that place?

Well, it has been decaying, overgrowing with weeds and briars since then... but definitely it was not forgotten. Soon legends have started to spread that great treasures of pagan gold and of precious stones are aplenty in the ruins of the city. Since then Galibornium has attracted all sorts of adventurers and treasure hunters. But the truth is that not all of them have returned and only few of them managed to find something valuable in the ruins. But all who went there and returned were telling stories about dreadful ghosts, cursed souls and infernal monsters who allegedly rule the city and lurk there as the shadows of the past long forgotten. The truth is that on moonless nights you may hear frightful growls and shrieks from there that send shivers down your spine.
You may choose, Tinthan: Either you answer my question or I'll force you to comply by any means necessary. Do you understand me?
Look, Tinthan, I don't know exactly what makes you unwilling to answer my question, but I'd like to ask you to reconsider it. Your answer won't do any harm, will it?
I knew such a wise and clever man as you would act very carefully, Tinthan. But I assure you that your answer would be very valuable to me.
Alright, I'm glad we came to an agreement. When I need your help I'll let you know. Farewell.
Goodbye, knight. I'd better return to the city—the wilderness is bad for me. And when you need to obtain something, come round.
That time has come already, Tinthan.
You say you're innocent?
Exactly, knight! Absolutely innocent. I didn't steal a thing. Let alone to steal the monstrance from the episcopal temple. The leech Weintraum made it up because I owe him money for meals and drinks.
If it is so I'll clear you of blame.
Really, knight? I'd be greatly indebted to you if you did. Really!
We have a deal then. May I talk with you for a moment?
Yes, of course, knight. What do you need to know?
What would you offer me to clear you of blame?

You would do that for me? In that case I would be greatly indebted to you, knight. And what can I offer you for your help? Well... I have nothing but my services. But they may come in handy to you, that is if I'm right.
What services are you exactly talking about, Tinthan?
Well... let's say I mean the services of obtaining. I'm able to obtain anything for you in a very reasonable time, and even if it happens to belong to someone else.
Am I mistaken or do you offer me thieving for my help?
That's a very nasty word, knight. As I said, I prefer speaking about the services of obtaining. It sounds loftier and more accurately describes the meaning.
I would never accept such a dirty agreement. Moreover it proves you might have stolen the monstrance after all.
As you wish, knight. But you'll see my services will come in useful to you someday. And in that case you know where to find me.
We will see. But now I need to talk to you for a moment.
And how good are you exactly in those services of obtaining?
How good? Knight, you'll find none better, believe me! I can obtain a letter you're just writing without you even noticing it. That's for sure!
Alright, we have a deal. I'll clear you of blame and in exchange for it you'll lend me your 'abilities'.
Great, knight! I'm glad you're open to a reasonable talk.
May I speak with you for a moment more? I'd like to ask you several questions.
It's a really deeply moving story. Let's hope the truth will appear. Farewell.
Wait, knight. Could you do me a favor and settle it up somehow so that the accusation is withdrawn?

You're one of God's knights, aren't you? Shouldn't you help to administer justice? What for a paladin are you if you don't make a thing about such injustice? And moreover, if you help me, you won't be sorry.
What would you offer me for my effort?
My services of obtaining, knight. I'm not only the master of arts, but I'm also very skilled in obtaining whatever you need.
I would never accept such a dirty agreement.
As you wish, knight. But I'm sure you'll reconsider. You'll see my services will come in useful someday.
We will see. But now I'd like to ask you some questions.
What d'ya wanna know? I don't know much.
How good? Knight, you'll find none better, believe me! I can steal a letter you're just writing without you even noticing it. Well, I mean obtain it from you, not steal. You can bet on it!
Alright, we have a deal. I'll clear you of blame and in exchange for it you'll lend me your obtaining abilities.
I'm sorry, but I won't help you. Farewell.
As you wish, knight. But I'm sure you'll need my services someday. And then you'll help me whether you like it or not.

See, it's here. You need to obtain something, don't you? I wonder what it would be. Do you like something in the shop of the master armorer Drichtmaul? Or you've taken a fancy to some goods of the wise woman Jungwirdt? Just tell me, I'll obtain anything.
I'd like to get certain letters which Cardinal Truncquillius has on him.

WHAT?! What did you say? No, it's out of question! To rob the curial inquisitor... Have you gone mad, knight? We would be both executed sooner than we might shout that we were terribly sorry. I won't do that for you. Come with something different, not that madness.
I don't need anything else. I want those letters. If you don't bring them to me, I'll accuse you of some really nasty crime and I'll personally ignite the stake under you.

I understand... You want those letters. No problem. You should have told me straight off that you want them that much. There's no need to threaten me. You want the letters Cardinal Truncquillius has on him. Alright, you'll get them. I'll set to work immediately. Give me some time, I'll handle it. We'll meet beyond the town by the Grand Duke's gazebo, I'll wait for you there.
I need those letters very urgently, Tinthan. Please, only you can get them for me.
Keep your flattery to yourself, knight. That's suicide. You've to come up with something else.
I understand. What if I give you some gold for your services?
Keep your gold, knight. That'd be suicide. You've to come up with something else.
Damn me... You did it, knight! That's incredible! I'll be a handsome man. I'll be a pretty well built man. Cripple no more, but a heart-breaker of girls. I'll be a stud!
If I were you I wouldn't place great hopes in it, Tinthan. You never know how true rumors can be...

You think that such a rare substance won't work? I don't believe that. But we'll find out at once. I'm going to put it on and we'll see who is right. So... let's put some more on the forehead and on the hands and...
For goodness sake!
Damn, it itches! But otherwise it isn't painful. So what, knight? How do I look like? Am I handsome? Am I a well built stud? Tell me, knight!
I'd have never thought this possible...
So it worked? Worked? WOW!
God was merciful to you, Tinthan. Your deformity is gone...

Do you see, knight? I told you. Now I'll at last become a renowned actor and an artist. And I owe you for that. Our agreement stands good—whenever you find you need to obtain some goods you're unable to get, tell me. I'll take care of it.

In that case listen carefully, Tinthan. I need to get the statuette of the Archangel Gabriel that I found in the temple of the Holy Trinity. The guardian of the treasure, Pontifex, took it from me and I need to get it back.

You wanna say you let yourself be caught when stealing in the temple of the Holy Trinity? You must have more luck than common sense, knight. But don't be afraid, I'll help you, although I didn't think I would have to rob the guardian of the church treasure. Wait for me outside the temple, I'll bring you the statuette.
Thank you, Tinthan. I'll wait for you there.
Well... we'll see. Farewell.

And you are who, knight? I don't know you and I doubt I should. You're new here, aren't you? I've never seen you in Glatzburg, and I've been living here since I was born. But no matter what, much more important is to know what do you want of me. If they sent you to arrest me and bring me back in chains, then I assure you I don't intend doing anything like that. Do you understand?
Name's Tinthan, knight. Master Tinthan!
Master of what?
Master of arts, knight! I'm a famous actor. My name's renowned all over the Realm.
I don't believe that. Didn't you just tell you've been living in Glatzburg for the whole of your life? So how could you be known all over the Realm?
Eh... well... but in any case... sooner or later they'll know me, it's only a matter of time. I'll shine in all the plays of the renowned writer Henry Wighlett, you can take that for granted!
Nice to meet you, good man. But tell me what are you doing here? And why did you say before that you won't let yourself be arrested and brought back to the city?
What? So you didn't come to arrest me? What a relief! I feared they sent you to find me and bring back to the city.

I was accused of stealing the monstrance of Saint Rhodrick in the Episcopal temple. But that's a lie, I assure you, knight. The innkeeper Weintraum made up the accusation because I owe him money for meals and drinks!
So you're Tinthan? I've heard you're accused of sacrilege. Is it true?

Yes, it is. I was accused of stealing the monstrance of Saint Rhodrick in the episcopal temple. But that's a lie, I assure you, knight. The innkeeper Weintraum made up the accusation because I owe him money for meals and drinks!

Hi there, knight. So how's it going with that charge of mine? Have you done anything about it yet? To tell the truth I'd like to return to the city again. I really don't enjoy staying here in the wilderness.
I'm sorry, not yet.
In that case I'd like to ask you to settle this pickle more quickly, if I may.
But of course, knight. What interests you?
Goodbye, knight. And hurry up, please!
Yes, Tinthan, you're free again. Grand Duke Heidrick has withdrawn the charge against you.

Really? That's incredible. You're really smart, knight. With all respect, this was really great work. I almost thought they would burn me at the stake as some damned heathen because of that silly monstrance.

Well... I didn't want to tell it to you straight because it could make you angry... but I really stole the monstrance. But there was no devilry in it, knight, I swear! When I did it I was dead drunk. I made a bet in the inn that I would steal it during the holy service. I don't know what crossed my mind, such bunk... It was because of that wine I drank... I didn't realize it's an absolute idiocy to steal in a church during a mass. And that was the only reason the innkeeper Weintraum saw me doing it. If I had been sober no one would have seen anything.
I'm speechless! I helped to stop the criminal proceedings against the real culprit!

Don't be so sad, knight. It wasn't your fault—it's a judicial error. Moreover I'm sure there are quite a few people running about the world who are much guiltier than I am. Why, I'm quite innocent of that and I didn't do almost any harm to anybody. But as you said—it doesn't matter anymore. And for freeing me you are entitled to the reward—my services of obtaining are at your disposal. Whenever you need to steal something—I mean to obtain—just say and you'll have it in no time, knight.
I think it doesn't matter anymore...

You're right, knight. Moreover I'm sure there are quite a few people running about the world who are much guiltier than I am. Why, I'm quite innocent of that and I didn't do almost any harm to anybody. But as you said—it doesn't matter anymore. And for freeing me you are entitled to the reward—my services of obtaining are at your disposal. Whenever you need to steal something—I mean to obtain—just say and you'll have it in no time, knight.

You think you've outfoxed me, but you're wrong. I'll get a pouch of gold from you, or I'll go and find so convincing evidence against you that you'll end at the stake before you'll be able to say 'sorry'.
What? A pouch of gold? That's racketeering! And you call yourself God's knight? Where is your morality? And what about your knightly honour? Besides, where shall I get so much money?
You're a little bit much moralistic for a thief stealing in the temple, Tinthan. And you surely have some money—I think you melted the monstrance and sold the gold then.

Alright, alright... here is the money, it's useless to malign ourselves for a few coins. And naturally you still have my promise to give you the reward in the form of my skills of obtaining. When you're in need, just ask me and I'll fetch you whatever you want.
Hi there, knight. Did you reconsider my offer? Clear me of the charge and I'll lend you my services of 'obtaining'. You'll see they'll come in handy sooner or later.
Alright, Tinthan, we'll make a bargain. I'll clear you of the charge and you'll steal—I mean obtain—for me whatever I ask.
Great, knight! I knew you would eventually start to think reasonably. I can't wait to return back to the city. Staying here in the wilderness is really far from pleasant.
May I ask you several questions now?
Certainly, knight. I'll be glad to answer them all. What d'ya wanna know?
No, Tinthan, I didn't reconsider. I'd never accept such a lousy bargain.
As you wish, knight. But you'll see you'll reconsider in time.
We'll see. But now I need to talk with you for a moment.
What d'ya need to know, knight?
The future is in the hands of God. Farewell.
Welcome, knight. How's it going? Thank you once again for helping me with that unfortunate charge. May I do something for you?
Yes, Tinthan. The time has come for you to return me the favor.
May I speak with you for a moment? I have several questions.
Sure, knight, I'm at your service. What d'ya need to know?
Nothing for now. Farewell. But don't forget your promise!
Sure, knight, I didn't forget it. Whenever you need to obtain something you may just ask and it will be as if I had it ready for you already.
So how's it going, Tinthan? Do you already have what I asked of you?

Sure, knight. You wouldn't doubt my skills, would you? Here you are. But I tell you, my legs are shaking even now. I've never ever dreamed of robbing Cardinal Truncquillius himself. I have a feeling I'll better soon start to earn my living as the master of arts. I'm too old for this.
A wise decision. Anyway, I thank you. It will be probably better if we don't meet again.

You're certainly right, knight. And you know what? Why don't I start with the new life instantly? Since I was born I've been living poorly here in Glatzburg. Why not try my luck in some other corner of the Realm? Tinthan's Road Show, that doesn't sound bad, does it? I could become the master of arts I've ever dreamed of becoming. I would play parts of princes and kings, of mighty warriors and of fair lovers!
Sounds good, Tinthan. May God be with you.
Farewell, knight. And good luck—no matter what you're up to. I think you'll need it.
Do whatever you want, Tinthan. But if someone gets to know what you did for me, then I'll come and...
Sure, knight, then you'll come and I'll be sorry till my death. Don't be afraid, I'll hold my tongue. It's also my head that's at stake, isn't it?
Is it you, Tinthan? What are you doing here? Are you trying your luck in the limelight here in Alvaron?
Is that you, knight? Do you know seeing you here doesn't surprise me? I knew at once that you would come a long way—even to the Royal seat town.
Hmm... Whatever. But tell me what are you doing here?

Me? Well... I'll be frank with you, knight. We've already been through a lot, haven't we? Alright... after I left Glatzburg I wandered a little and tried my luck here and there. Of course nothing illegal, I swear! But it wasn't going too well—you won't make a fortune if you're so deformed like me.
To the point.

Sure, knight. As I said, I wasn't doing too well, and as time went by, I started to curse my appearance. And then I've learnt they have a miraculous oil here in Alvaron, that was consecrated by Pope Almod II the Miraculous himself—the man is said to be able to make miracles. The oil itself rids everyone who puts it on of all his ailments. So I've thought...
...so you've thought you would steal it here, am I right?!

Well... yes, you're right, knight. I know I'm falling into bad ways again because of it, but it would be really for the last time. As soon as I change into a handsome young man I would start to make my living by fair means, believe me.

But in the time I've been here I've just managed to find out that the oil is hidden somewhere deep in the dungeons under the archepiscopal palace where I have no chance to get. It requires someone who is able to enter the dungeons under the church without raising suspicion and to get back alive....
I hope you're not thinking of me!

Well, do you know it crossed my mind the moment I saw you here? Although a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous wouldn't be completely noteless down in the secret church dungeons, you surely can cope even with such situations.
Alright, we have a deal. I'll bring you the miraculous oil. But since that instant you'll start to earn your living honestly, do you understand?
Yes, knight, you may rely upon it. Bring me the oil and I'll show you what the life of a saint means.
What will my reward be if I bring you the miraculous oil?
As always, knight—I'll steal something for you. Well... I mean I'll obtain you goods according to your wishes. That's it.
I would never do such a thing. You better start to earn your living honestly or I'll look into it.

Gah... I thought you would say that, knight. But maybe you'll reconsider. You know my services proved helpful once. And in your holy mission there will surely be an opportunity to use them again soon.
Never! Farewell.
You're lucky, Tinthan. I've acquired the oil already. It's yours.
So what, knight, do you bring me the miraculous oil that'll change me into a handsome man and a heart breaker of girls?
What a shame. I've thought I would get rid of my ugliness at last. But perhaps you'll succeed. You're my only hope, knight!
You're lucky, Tinthan. I'm bringing you the oil. Here it is.
So what, knight? Did you reconsider about that miraculous oil?
All right, I'll bring it to you. But only under the condition that you'll start to earn your living honestly after that.
Agreed! Bring me the oil and you'll see I'll change into a downright saint!
In that case you may start immediately, Tinthan, because I'm bringing you the oil. Here it is.
I'll hope it will be so. Farewell for now.
No, I didn't!
What a shame... But maybe you'll change your mind later.
Welcome, knight. What nice weather we have today, haven't we? I've found the life is as beautiful as one's face. And for that I owe only to you.
I'm glad you're happy. And I hope you maintain yourself honestly!
Of course, knight. I started writing a drama in which I'll take the lead role of a beautiful young prince. Or maybe a king, I haven't decided on it yet.
Hmm... In that case I advise you to start learning how to write.
Yes, I've thought about it too. Thanks for the advice, knight.

I'd like to employ your services of obtaining, Tinthan. I need to get the statuette of the Archangel Gabriel that I found in the temple of the Holy Trinity. The guardian of the treasure, Pontifex, took it from me and I want to get it back.

You wanna say you let yourself be caught when stealing in the temple of the Holy Trinity? You must have more luck than common sense, knight. But don't be afraid, I'll help you, although I didn't think I would have to rob the guardian of the church treasure. To be honest, the commissions you choose are no piece of cake. Wait for me outside the temple, I'll bring you the statuette.
Well, Tinthan, do you have the statuette for me?
Of course, knight. You wouldn't doubt my skills, would you? It would hurt my feelings. Here it is.
You're welcome, knight. And if I may advise you, start to earn your living honestly—same as me.
Hmm... Farewell. And I hope you'll be tactfully silent about this incident up to the end of your life.
Rely on me, knight. There's my head at stake too, remember. We're accomplices.

You're surprising me, knight. I've thought thefts are my business, but it seems you're trying to follow in my trails. Keep it up, knight. But next time you had better choose someone else, although I can imagine that robbing a thief may not be such a grave crime in your eyes.
I hope you'll arrest him, Father. That you'll do something about him. If he got to know I told you...

You wanna know who rules Glatzburg? That's easy, our ruler's Grand Duke Heidrick, Father. He's the highest representative of temporal power both near and far. But he hasn't got much power left, because almost everything is a crime against the Faith now and such crimes are in the jurisdiction of the Inquisition, as you surely know. The royal vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin who squints at the governor's office. I have a feeling he's up to something...

In my judgement almost everybody is a heretic, Father. You'll probably be angry, but the nobility, the townsfolk, the common people and even the clergy, all are heretics with only few exceptions. Because what's the heresy? It's the deviation from that what's written in the Holy Scriptures. At least a preacher who passed through Glatzburg some time ago said so. And what do the Holy Scriptures say? That we should live in poverty and humility. Not only the common people as the nobility and the clergy say, but all of us—to a man.
I'll say that I may accuse you of heresy for such opinions!
I don't know his name. But he was burned some time ago. By the Inquisition. So they outran you, Father. Well, it will be better if we both forget about our conversation, won't it?

I've heard the city executioner Yan Flemberg is scared shitless. It seems that the executed Duke—Istwan de Bragho—who was the governor of Glatzburg before Duke Rowan van Leerin has risen from his grave to take his revenge on those who got him executed. Have you heard anything about it?

I see. So, the thing is that Duke Istwan de Bragho was quite an asshole. He was conspiring with dark powers and used them to kidnap girls and boys—he raped them to satisfy his perverse whims. He was a sodomite and a murderer, but he was also clever and a noble on top of it. So it took some time to find evidence against him. Several paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous decided to take care of him—tough guys, I must say, who'd beat the shit out of anybody, but for a long time even they were unable to find anything. But then a kidnapped girl managed to escape and denunciate him.

Bragho knew it's a matter of life and death and he bolted out but the paladins—there were five of them—overtook him and handed him over to justice. The execution was splendid, it was a perfect drama, and I'm an expert on these things. People enjoyed themselves, the Duke was gradually losing his skin, his limbs, eyes and so on, but when he was near death he uttered a terrible curse. He told he would return and settle the score with everyone.

As I said. Certainly people got quite nervous and lost their temper. But the curse was targeted only at those who stood behind the Duke's death—at those five paladins and of course at Flemberg who conducted the execution—he did splendidly, by the way. Eventually the Duke went to Hell and nothing happened for several years. People almost forgot about it, but this spring tidings started to spread all of a sudden that the paladins who caught the Duke were dying one after another. And not only dying—they were being murdered, and in quite a frightful way. All five of them have snuffed it by now. So it really seems the late Bragho returned from Beyond to settle the score with them. And the last one left is Yan Flemberg.
You're welcome, Father. It's a sad story, isn't it? And full of blood, I'd say.
No, Father. But she had to be from a wealthy family, given that she was able to afford such clothes...
You're welcome, Father. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon.

I've heard a lot about the murder of Bishop Trevorius. For example that you're in trouble, Father. They say you were caught above the Bishop's dead body even before it got cold. I tell you, it's very dangerous to let yourself be caught near a corpse. Because it's all the same if you're guilty or not—the suspicion sticks to you like black pitch. But fortunately you're innocent.
Simply—I saw who murdered the Bishop.

No, Father, I don't know a thing about the necklace of Knight de Pasque. I swear! And I feel sort of hurt that I'm being blamed for all that happens in Glatzburg. Am only I to blame for everything? If I really stole all that I'm blamed of stealing, I would already live as a rich man somewhere far away.
I'm glad, Father. I really have nothing to do with it. I'm not crazy to try to make enemies of those fanatic cutthroats from the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

I don't lie, Father, I swear by all what's holy to me. I even didn't see the necklace, let alone to steal it. I'm not crazy to try to make enemies of those fanatic cutthroats from the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

The name of the nobleman doesn't ring a bell to me, Father. But if you're interested in the remains of realms long dead then I advise you to search in the woods around the von Hunth's estate. I came upon all sorts of interesting things there... and I even managed to sell some of them.

All sorts of people have searched for Bonhart's hammer, Father. Even I've turned quite a few stones in the vicinity of the city, but of course I didn't find anything. Nobody knows exactly where Bonhart buried his treasure. Some say it's at the gallows, others say it's somewhere in the ruins of Galibornium. I personally think he buried it somewhere else, but I don't know where.

Have you heard the legends about the ghosts in the ruins of Galibornium, Father? It's said that when Saint Orthenius and his faithful armies conquered Galibornium in the year 223, he ordered all its inhabitants to be gathered at a large square in the middle of the burning city. There he let them choose: either they could accept baptism or be executed. Many pagans quickly thought better of their polytheism and were baptized, but there were also lots of those who didn't accept the true faith and stayed true to their gods and goddesses. And those were executed without mercy. It's said there was blood up to your knees, Father.
Goodbye, Father. I'd better return to the city—the wilderness is bad for me. And when you need to obtain something, come round.
Exactly, Father! Absolutely innocent. I didn't steal a thing. Let alone to steal the monstrance from the episcopal temple. The leech Weintraum made it up because I owe him money for meals and drinks.
Really, Father? I'd be greatly indebted to you if you did. Really!
Yes, of course, Father. What do you need to know?

You would do that for me? In that case I would be greatly indebted to you, Father. And what can I offer you for your help? Well... I have nothing but my services. But they may come in handy to you, that is if I'm right.
That's a very nasty word, Father. As I said, I prefer speaking about the services of obtaining. It sounds loftier and more accurately describes the meaning.
As you wish, Father. But you'll see my services will come in useful to you someday. And in that case you know where to find me.
How good? Father, you'll find none better, believe me! I can obtain a letter you're just writing without you even noticing it. That's for sure!
Great, Father! I'm glad you're open to a reasonable talk.
Wait, Father. Could you do me a favor and settle it up somehow so that the accusation is withdrawn?
You're a priest, aren't you? Shouldn't you help your fellows? What sort of priest are you when you don't do a thing about such an injustice? And moreover, if you help me, you won't be sorry.
My services of obtaining, Father. I'm not only the master of arts, but I'm also very skilled in obtaining whatever you need.
As you wish, Father. But I'm sure you'll reconsider. You'll see my services will come in useful someday.
How good? Father, you'll find none better, believe me! I can steal a letter you're just writing without you even noticing it. Well, I mean obtain it from you, not steal. You can bet on it!
As you wish, Father. But I'm sure you'll need my services someday. And then you'll help me whether you like it or not.

Damn, it itches! But otherwise it isn't painful. So what, Father? How do I look like? Am I handsome? Am I a well built stud? Tell me, Father!

Farewell, Father. And good luck—no matter what you're up to. I think you'll need it.

Sure, Father. As I said, I wasn't doing too well, and as time went by, I started to curse my appearance. The oil itself rids everyone who puts it on of all his ailments. So I've thought...

Well... yes, you're right, Father. I know I'm falling into bad ways again because of it, but it would be really for the last time. As soon as I change into a handsome young man I would start to make my living by fair means, believe me.

But during the time I've been here I've managed to find out only that the oil is hidden somewhere deep in the dungeons under the archiepiscopal palace where I have no chance of getting to because I'm no priest. And do you know it crossed my mind just as I saw you here? You would surely raise no suspicion—you're an inquisitor.

The royal vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin who squints at the governor's office. I have a feeling he's up to something...

And what do the Holy Scriptures say? That we should live in poverty and humility. Not only the common people as the nobility and the clergy say, but all of us—to a man.
I don't know his name. But he was burned some time ago. By the Inquisition. So they outran you, noble lord. Well, it will be better if we both forget about our conversation, won't it?
You're welcome, noble lord. It's a sad story, isn't it? And full of blood, I'd say.
No, noble lord. But she had to be from a wealthy family, given that she was able to afford such clothes...
You're welcome, noble lord. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon.

But fortunately you're innocent.

Am only I to blame for everything? If I really stole all that I'm blamed of stealing, I would already live as a rich man somewhere far away.
I'm glad, noble lord. I really have nothing to do with it. I'm not crazy to try to make enemies of those fanatic cutthroats from the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

I don't lie, noble lord, I swear by all what's holy to me. I even didn't see the necklace, let alone to steal it. I'm not crazy to try to make enemies of those fanatic cutthroats from the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

All sorts of people have searched for Bonhart's hammer, noble lord. Even I've turned quite a few stones in the vicinity of the city, but of course I didn't find anything. Nobody knows exactly where Bonhart buried his treasure. Some say it's at the gallows, others say it's somewhere in the ruins of Galibornium. I personally think he buried it somewhere else, but I don't know where.

Have you heard the legends about the ghosts in the ruins of Galibornium, noble lord? It's said that when Saint Orthenius and his faithful armies conquered Galibornium in the year 223, he ordered all its inhabitants to be gathered at a large square in the middle of the burning city. There he let them choose: either they could accept baptism or be executed. Many pagans quickly thought better of their polytheism and were baptized, but there were also lots of those who didn't accept the true faith and stayed true to their gods and goddesses. And those were executed without mercy. It's said there was blood up to your knees, noble lord.
Goodbye, noble lord. I'd better return to the city—the wilderness is bad for me. And when you need to obtain something, come round.

Really, noble lord? I'd be greatly indebted to you if you did. Really!
Yes, of course, noble lord. What do you need to know?

Great, noble lord! I'm glad you're open to a reasonable talk.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, knight. He's the royal governor of the city. And then there's Duke Rowan van Leerin—he's his the vice-governor. Or he was...
