The best weapons and armor are made by Hans von Drichtmaul, knight. He has an armory here—it's renowned near and far. I'd like to become his apprentice and learn all the master knows. He makes beautiful things, knight. But if you need potions, magic items and so on instead of weapons and armor then go to the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt or to the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. And you may buy various things from the innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum. And the merchant Alphonso DiCerbio may sell you anything you can imagine, although my father says he sells stolen goods and that God will surely punish him soon.
I... I don't know, knight. Sometimes it frightens me a lot. What may befall us next? Is it really the doomsday as the people in the city say, knight?
No, boy, it's not the doomsday.
I'm glad, knight. I've thought so myself. But people say many things, you know? That there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on.
That's hard to say, boy. We'll see.

Well... You're probably right, knight. But I don't think people in the city are right when they say there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on. I think God will forgive us. Yes, I'm sure he will.
Yes, boy, I'm afraid it's just so.

I don't believe that, knight. You're just frightening me, aren't you? I don't think people in the city are right when they say there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on. I think God will forgive us. Yes, I'm sure he will.
Have you heard any tidings about a war, boy?

Yes, I've heard something about a war, knight. I'm afraid they will take my father away. People say they are drafting new recruits and training them to be able to set out for a fight soon. That would be horrible...

Several days ago a terrible storm struck the city. It frightened me a lot. No one remembers such a storm. It came out of the blue, ehmm black, in the middle of the night. I think it was midnight when the wind started to shake the window shutters, there was a deafening rumbling of the thunder, the sky was all lit with sheet lightning and the horrible tumult began. I hid in my bed and my teeth clattered in fear. My father went to see what was going on outside and then he stood by the window like Lot's wife, so still I thought something bewitched him. The sky was full of demons and hellspawns screaming like it was the end of the world. I don't know how long it lasted, but when I fell asleep at last I dreamed terrible nightmares.

And you think, knight, that I stole the necklace? But that's not true, I've never stolen anything. You had better ask the comedian Tinthan, it could very well be him. They say he's able to steal your nose from between your eyes.

I know what hammer you mean, knight. Master Hans von Drichtmaul told me about it many times over. Bonhart von Drichtmaul was his ancestor, you know? I tried to find the hammer to please my master, but I had no luck. It has to be hidden very well, that's for sure. But I don't have the slightest idea where.

I'm very sorry Raquel went missing. I often played with her. She was always very nice to me, same as Lady Wanda. They would cook pea soup from time to time, the same as my mother used to cook when she still lived. I hope nothing bad happened to Raquel.

I like the legend of the Coliseum the most, knight. Do you know what the Coliseum was? It was such a large circular theatre standing in the middle of Galibornium when this country was still ruled by pagans. But there were no stage plays acted there, instead it was a place where brave heroes and warriors fought one against another. Fought to the death. In the middle there was no stage but a ring where the fights took place. People went there to see all those brave heroes fighting. Although my father said the Coliseum was firstly some sort of gallows and only later it became the entertainment for warriors, but I don't know anything about that. In any case those fights—they were called gladiatorial, but I don't know why—they were very popular and everyone went to see them. People say there used to be fights lasting several days, whole battles they were, and the victors enjoyed the glory and admiration worthy of an emperor. Ah, those were great times!
Maybe you wouldn't like them so much, son.

Maybe, but I definitely wouldn't like to live through what happened after Saint Orthenius conquered Galibornium. There reputedly was a large underground dungeon under the Coliseum where all that was related to the gladiatorial fights was done. And the last pagan defenders of the city hid there when the faithful armies overran the city walls. Saint Orthenius decided the underground would be walled up so all the pagans hiding there would be rightly punished. And so all of them starved to death. It's said that for many a long day there was crying and groans of the dying to be heard from the depths. But peace didn't come even after all of them died. Ghosts of the dead have returned to forever wander the dungeons and look for the eternal peace that was denied to them.
Please, Sir, let me go! Humbly please... I didn't do anything to anyone! So why do you hold me here among those infernal monsters and beelzebubs? I want to go home! I'm scared!
Who are you, boy?
My name's Tom Clifford, sir. Please, don't hurt me! I didn't do anything.
Don't be afraid, boy, I mean you no harm. I'll take you back to your father.
To my father? You aren't... you aren't the one who kidnapped me! Does it mean I'm saved?
Yes, boy, exactly.
Oh, thanks God! I've prayed so much for angels to come to me and bring me away from this terrible place on their wings.
Alright, boy, let's go. I'm sure your father will be glad to see you.
Tell me about your kidnapping. Did you recognize some of the kidnappers?

I... no, Sir, I didn't. They threw some bag over my head and gagged me so I wasn't able to scream. Then they tied me so hard the ropes hurt me all over my body and I wasn't able to move. I couldn't breathe and eventually I swooned away. I didn't awake until I was here, at this terrible place. All those devils were grinning at me from all sides, they showed me their teeth and hissed at me and I thought it would be my end!
Welcome, knight. I'm unable to say how much I'm grateful to you for saving me. I'd like to repay it to you somehow, but I don't know how.
Could you answer me some questions?
It doesn't matter, boy. I'm glad you're alright. Farewell.
Goodbay, knight. And thank you once more.
I didn't know the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous may search people without any reason, knight...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, Father. He's the royal governor of the city. And then there's Duke Rowan van Leerin—he's his the vice-governor. Or he was...
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, Father. He's the royal governor of the city. And then there's Duke Rowan van Leerin—he's his vice-governor. But I hope God will punish him for what he did.

The best weapons and armor are made by Hans von Drichtmaul, Father. He has an armory here—it's renowned near and far. I'd like to become his apprentice and learn all the master knows. He makes beautiful things, Father. But if you need potions, magic items and so on instead of weapons and armor then go to the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt or to the alchemist Paolus Ventimus. And you may buy various things from the innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum. And the merchant Alphonso DiCerbio may sell you anything you can imagine, although my father says he sells stolen goods and that God will surely punish him soon.
I... I don't know, Father. Sometimes it frightens me a lot. What may befall us next? Is it really the doomsday as the people in the city say, Father?
I'm glad, Father. I've thought so myself. But people say many things, you know? That there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on.

Well... You're probably right, Father. But I don't think people in the city are right when they say there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on. I think God will forgive us. Yes, I'm sure he will.

I don't believe that, Father. You're just frightening me, aren't you? I don't think people in the city are right when they say there's no hope, that the doomsday will come soon and Satan will take our souls, and so on. I think God will forgive us. Yes, I'm sure he will.

Yes, I've heard something about a war, Father. I'm afraid they will take my father away. People say they are drafting new recruits and training them to be able to set out for a fight soon. That would be horrible...

And you think, Father, that I stole the necklace? But that's not true, I've never stolen anything. You had better ask the comedian Tinthan, it could very well be him. They say he's able to steal your nose from between your eyes.

I know what hammer you mean, Father. Master Hans von Drichtmaul told me about it many times over. Bonhart von Drichtmaul was his ancestor, you know? I tried to find the hammer to please my master, but I had no luck. It has to be hidden very well, that's for sure. But I don't have the slightest idea where.

I like the legend of the Coliseum the most, Father. Do you know what the Coliseum was? It was such a large circular theatre standing in the middle of Galibornium when this country was still ruled by pagans. But there were no stage plays acted there, instead it was a place where brave heroes and warriors fought one against another. Fought to the death. In the middle there was no stage but a ring where the fights took place. People went there to see all those brave heroes fighting. Although my father said the Coliseum was firstly some sort of gallows and only later it became the entertainment for warriors, but I don't know anything about that. In any case those fights—they were called gladiatorial, but I don't know why—they were very popular and everyone went to see them. People say there used to be fights lasting several days, whole battles they were, and the victors enjoyed the glory and admiration worthy of an emperor. Ah, those were great times!
Welcome, Father. I'm unable to say how much I'm grateful to you for saving me. I'd like to repay it to you somehow, but I don't know how.
Goodbay, Father. And thank you once more.
I didn't know the inquisitors may search people without any reason, Father...

Goodbay, noble lord. And thank you once more.
I didn't know the nobles may search people without any reason, noble lord...

It's stronger than I! It's killing me, killing me a thousand times! But every time I'm born again to the new pain. Am I dead? I don't feel my body. I'm cold as a stone. My heart doesn't beat. But the pain... It's returning again and again, every time it's born again. Only blood... blood of others... may suppress it for a moment. What has happened to me?
By the First Prophet, what are you, monster?

Who am I? I don't know. I remember being someone... but it was long ago. I was Trauchmann of Asherbalt, yes that was my name. Baron Trauchmann of Asherbalt. But now I'm... a monster. Yes, I'm a monster, you told it right! My death wasn't my redemption but my curse. It was the beginning of a bad dream. Of the nightmare I won't ever awake from. And the pain... It's like orcs are still cutting me to pieces with their blades. Like the life was still running out of my body. Nevertheless I'm dead, long dead. And you're going to be dead too soon. I want your blood to escape the terrible pain for a moment.
Wait, Baron, maybe there is some way to help you.
I don't want your help, human. I want your blood! I must have your blood, I must quench the thirst!
And God said to the Prophet: That what is dead should stay in the grave forever, my son.
And God said to the Prophet: Cleanse the world of all evil, my son!

There is a certain suspicion that the alleged coming of the Fallen Angel Arthamon into this world was accompanied by a really ferocious supernatural storm occurring in Hillbrandt. Did a similar storm occur here in Glatzburg too?

Strange... there in fact was a storm not long ago, a tempest unlike anything anybody had ever seen in this town. Even the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt was very disturbed by that unholy weather. People unanimously swore there was something dancing in the sky. Maybe ghosts or hellspawns!

But I personally don't think something like that would happen. People are just terrified by all that has befallen our Realm and so they're ready to see hellspawns in every shadow. But if your suspicion concerning the Fallen Angel Arthamon were to be confirmed, then I would really shudder to think what the storm that occurred here could have meant.
I'm sorry, but I won't discuss that with you, my son!
I've overheard that a girl named Francessca Gulvardi attempted to murder you recently. What can you tell me about that?
I have nothing to say about it now, my son. I'm sorry.
To tell the truth, the girl confessed you tried to rape her and that she only defended herself.
She said that to you? I'm not surprised. Nevertheless I have nothing to say about it now, my son. I'm sorry.
The office of the royal governor of the city is held by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, son. And the vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin.
What do you think about the current crisis our Realm has been dragged in, Monsignor? Is it really the end of the world?

You ask if we're witnessing the end of the world. That's a difficult question, son. You're a priest, so you should know the Holy Scriptures and be able to read them. Yes, the Apocalypse of Saint Ezekiel mentions the Star of Doom, the Scourges of God and the end of the world, when the false prophet shall walk the world and Satan shall be freed from his prison. Sure, many events of the last few years are quite similar to that. But who can say for sure that it's really true? And who can say the Apocalypse in fact describes the end of the God's Earthly Kingdom? It's in the holy scripture and we must dedicate our whole life to studying its true meaning.
So you think the text doesn't describe the events that will happen someday?

Not necessarily. Although I can't definitely answer the question about the Apocalypse being a prophecy or a mere metaphor of the eternal fight between good and evil, I'm sure of one thing—many troubles are of people's own making. And the Holy Mother Church is no exception!

I mean that people tend to blame others for their own faults. Look at what happened in the last century—does it seem to you it has been the life of humble sheep in the God's herd? Wars, violence, frauds, crimes of the crudest sort, debauchery and blasphemy... all that's been quite common for years and no one demurs it. And what does the Holy Mother Church do? It not only countenances it, but it slowly submits to it. Utilitarianism, stinginess and selfishness, those are the traits that no priest should adhere to. But the contrary is the case!

Isn't it clear? We have to go back to the roots of the Holy Mother Church—to the life and teachings of the twelve prophets. We have to be particular about adhering to the Holy Scriptures. The Holy Mother Church exists to help people through mercy and humbleness. We have to get rid of material possessions, of political ambitions and of the lust for power. We have to cleanse ourselves. To revive the Church.
You're probably right. How can people change, when the Church doesn't change?

Exactly, my son. No pun intended, but repression and oppression aren't the right way to the correction of human soul. Only mercy, patience and the exemplary life in humility may open people's eyes. And I'll defend and promote this opinion up to the end of my life.
Doesn't that happen to be a heretical theory?

It's the theory that may lead to the correction of many wrongs, son. If someone sees anything ill in that he should scrutinize his conscience. I'll defend and promote this opinion up to the end of my life.
Hmm... I'll think about that.
You should, my son. You should.
I've heard a war is about to start, Monsignor. Do you know any details about that?

I've overheard that Grand Duke Robert Heidrick received orders concerning our royal regiment. That's all I know about it. But I'll tell you one thing, my son. Evil spawns evil and the war is the biggest evil that may befall us. All those who declare that a just war waged in the name of God is blessed are liars. No war can be the will of God, because God loves us all and if someone sins, we have to show him the way back and not break his skull with a mace!

So, you're asking me what enemies you may face here, son. Then know that the worst enemy of faithful men is unfaithfulness. Because if you lose faith in God, then you lose your soul and all hope for salvation. But that's probably not what you wanted to hear. You want to know who—or what—may kill you here in Glatzburg, am I right? Yes, I can see I am. Then be sure that there's a lot of infernal monsters and minions of Hell. But I'm no expert on this matter. Try asking sheriff Smith, he'll surely be glad to answer all your questions.

If I'm not mistaken, His Grace Robert Heidrick has offered a reward for catching footpads robbing and murdering on the roads in the vicinity of the city. If you want to know details, then ask sheriff Smith who pays the rewards in gold.
I have nothing to say about that, my son. I'll say nothing about my suspicions of heresy for now. It will be better that way—for both of us.

Lots of evil events have happened lately, son. Nevertheless, perhaps the worst is the case of girls gone missing. I don't know if you've heard about it, but several very young girls from the city and its vicinity have gone missing under strange circumstances. They barely grew too old for childrens games. They were all lambs I've known since their birth and which I myself baptized. I shudder to think about what the kidnappers want to do to them.
Do you think all those kidnappings have a single culprit?

Yes, I'm sure of it. I'm even certain it's a human and not some demon or other hellspawn. That's because minions of Hell murder everyone, they don't distinguish between men, women or children. They don't perform any occult rites, don't celebrate dark masses and don't do anything of that what's so dear to all heretics. And so I'm convinced the kidnappings are the work of a man, of a disgusting delusional heretic. And because of the similarity of all the cases I think it's one and the same culprit.
How many girls have gone missing so far?
If my information is correct there's three up to now.
I'm searching for the crypt of an Elenian nobleman named Fae'Darlion. Do you happen to know, Monsignor, where it could be found?

There are many relics of days long past in the woods around von Hunth's manor, my son. Although it's not certain the tomb you're looking for is right there I'd advise you to direct your attention there.

Father Frederick came into my diocese five years ago, just a year before the Star of Doom appeared in the sky. He wished to last out here in peace because he was very old. I was glad he came, because he was a very learned priest and famed on top of it—he was a great exorcist and demon hunter. But his behavior here in Glatzburg quite disappointed me, because he avoided people and led quite a secluded life. Nevertheless I was very aggrieved by his death three years later, because with his departure the Holy Mother Church lost a great protector of the true faith. If you want to speak about him with someone who had a closer relation with him, try speaking to Judge Welfhar. He was a disciple of his.

I'm afraid that my knowledge is too limited for coping with the unclean powers that are in control of Istwan de Bragho, my son. If what you say is true then we have to deal with a revenant, the avenger from Beyond who has come to execute his sentence on those who doomed him by this curse. Go to the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt and ask her for advice. Only she may have the knowledge necessary to send the revenant back to the Other World.

You're interested in the Fallen Angels? That's a very dark side of the true faith, my son. The Holy Scriptures refer to the Fallen Angels as the representatives of the power of Hell, the emissaries of evil and creators of all that is unholy. They're the executors of Satan's will, his minions and mighty vassals. They all used to be angels the same as Gabriel, Michael or Raphael, but they were thrown down from heaven for their crimes against God Almighty, where they have been imprisoned since then. Still they're able to infiltrate this world through the unholy powers they wield. Or through their minions, the lesser creatures of Hell.
How many of the Fallen Angels are there in all?

There are four of them. Arthamon, the ruler of ruin and destruction, Baphomet, the master of chaos and the sower of madness, Cerdie, the unholy mother of debauchery and of the original sin, and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the first of Satan's underlings, the harbinger of his will and the advocate of evil. The four horrible substances of all that's represented by evil.
Substances? What do you mean by that?!

It's a question of if they really have any material form or if they're only personified infernal powers. To know the truth church scholars have sought the answer for just that question since time immemorial. Saint Gloriefeld believes they're beings with a firm shape, although no one has ever seen them because in our world they're just a materialization of ideas of men. On the contrary, Niclas of Auxiliaris is of the opinion they have no material form, much like God himself has no material form. It's really a difficult question and I doubt someone will find any satisfactory answer to it. But whatever the truth is, the Fallen Angels really exist and constitute a great threat for God's Earthly realm.

Dead men in the city streets are yet another scourge of God falling on our heads because of sins we've committed together. But I'm also sure the presence of those infernal monsters is caused by a criminal who tries to accomplish some sinister goal of his.
Why do you think so, Monsignor?

Because there's something strange about the behavior of those monsters. They don't behave naturally. Sure, they attack innocent townsmen and take their lives—together with their entrails—but if my information is correct, there were no valuables found on the murdered people. No rings, necklaces, purses, even shiny brass buttons disappeared. And I've confirmed that street beggars and pilferers can't be blamed for those thefts. So I understand that behind the dead men in the city stand some greedy heretics not detesting even the most disgusting crimes in their efforts to get their golden calf.

I'm sorry, my son, but I don't know anything about the disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch. I only know that Dieter von Gelbendiel, the Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, has taken charge of the investigation. I hope he will succeed in his efforts and Raquel—as well as other kidnapped girls—will be found alive and well. I pray for their safe return home.
You won't bribe me, son! That's absolutely out of question!
I warn you, Monsignor. I need the answer VERY badly and I'll do anything to get it!
Please, Monsignor, let's put our possible antipathies aside and let's speak as two people wishing to help the good cause.
You're one of the most wise and learned men I've ever met, Monsignor. Please, answer my humble question.

Well... it's really a strange scroll. The parchment seems to be very old, its sides are frayed already. And the leather it's made of is unknown to me. It's really worrying. And the text... it looks like some runes or a code. It's true the Cult of the Children of the New Order used to write in the forbidden script of Satan, but it's hard to say if this is exactly that case. I'm sorry, but although the scroll is quite troubling it doesn't prove anything.

Monsignor, I would hate to be impolite, but I must insist. All that was contained in the letter from Master Edmond d'Arvias really happened and there is reasonable suspicion that the crimes of Judge Vallarian weren't of his invention. Please, help me.

No, my son, I'm sorry. You didn't give me any plausible proof confirming things Master d'Arvias writes about. On the contrary I guess it would be more than advisable to let it all be investigated by the Tribunal of the Inquisition. I will mention it to Father Truncquillius, the Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg.
Consider it well, Monsignor. I'm not so helpless as I seem. If it is necessary I'll do anything needed to make you cooperate. Do you understand me?!

Stop threatening me, son, I won't help you. You won't gain anything by force. You didn't give me any plausible proof confirming things Master d'Arvias writes about. By contrast I guess it would be more than advisable to let it all be investigated by the Tribunal of Inquisition. I will mention it to Father Truncquillius, the Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg.
I understand, Monsignor. Your cooperation naturally would be adequately compensated. Ask your price, then, I'm sure we can make a deal.

I'm sorry, son, but you didn't understand. Your money means nothing to me—mammon is a sin. You didn't give me any plausible proof confirming the things Master d'Arvias writes about. On the contrary I guess it would be more than advisable to let it all be investigated by the Tribunal of the Inquisition. I will mention it to Father Truncquillius, the Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg.
What? You want to make the Inquisition investigate me??

Indeed, my son. It's necessary to shed some light on what was going on in Hillbrandt. As I said, you didn't persuade me about the truthfulness of your words in any way. The scroll is totally insufficient as a proof, because we don't know its contents. And without it it's worthless as evidence.
But that's what I'm talking about, Monsignor. I wanted to ask you for help with deciphering that scroll. I haven't been able to do it myself.

Well... I don't know, it looks suspicious. I don't want to be pulled into some strange game you seem to have opened in Hillbrandt. But maybe you're right—deciphering that scroll would solve much. Alright, I'll help you. I can't read the runes myself and I doubt there is a book containing the transcription of this or similar script in my diocese, but I know of a person skilled in many occult and supernatural matters. It is the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt who lives here in Glatzburg. Seek her out and show her the scroll. If she is willing to help you, let her translate the scroll and then return to me.
Thanks for you help, Monsignor. May I speak with you a moment longer?
Yes, if your questions concern important matters. In any other case I'll have to excuse myself, I've much to do.
Thank you, Monsignor. Farewell.
What do you need, my son? I've been quite short on time recently, so be brief.
I've arrived from Hillbrandt, Monsignor, to give you best regards from Master Edmond d'Arvias and to deliver you his letters asking for help.

You say you've arrived from Hillbrandt? I've heard some strange events happened there. It's said Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian was executed there. He was my good friend and his death alarmed me very much. Let me see the letter of Master d'Arvias, my son.

Well... really disturbing. According to what's written here it was you that led the investigation of Judge Vallarian and who initiated his execution. I won't hide my resentment. If there really was some suspicion of heresy—and I doubt that—the situation would have to be examined by the Curial Inquisitorial Commission from Glatzburg and not by a self-appointed Inquisitorial Judge. I find your actions most inappropriate.

Don't interrupt me, son. The letter continues to say there's a suspicion Judge Vallarian concocted the invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon who is to enter this world with armies of orcs called forth from the Accursed Depths. And what's worse, along with Diocesan Bishop Quentinus you started to suspect that Judge Vallarian could be a member of the heretical Cult of the Children of the New Order.
Exactly, Monsignor.

And I should believe that? The seal on the letter seems to be genuine, but its contents trouble me. Do you really want me to believe Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian has invoked the Fallen Angel Arthamon to destroy the world? Do you want me to believe that Vallarian was a member of the heretical Cult that was destroyed several centuries ago? I'm sorry, but whatever happened in Hillbrandt, the letter from Master d'Arvias didn't convince me of anything. Do you have another proof that would assure me of verity of those events?
I do, Monsignor. We found this scroll hidden among the belongings of Judge Vallarian.
I do, Monsignor. We found a very worrying scroll among the belongings of Judge Vallarian. Regrettably I don't have it on me presently.
Well... then return when you have the scroll. Now leave in peace, my son.
What do you need, my son? Have you brought the scroll you told me about last time?
Yes, Monsignor, here it is.
No, Monsignor, not yet.
Welcome, my son. Have you managed to get the translation of that mysterious scroll already?
Yes, Monsignor, here it is. But it's content doesn't make much sense to me.

Let me see. Well... At first sight it really doesn't make much sense. Night without wood, traitors from Umbria, shadow of the dragon... But if it is interpreted correctly... Oh Goodness... It's starting to make sense!
Very well. I'm all ears.
What do you know about the Cult of the Children of the New Order, my son?
Not much, Monsignor. I expected to learn something from you.

Oh yes, naturally. Now then—the Cult was first mentioned in the Empire in the year 965, so it was more than two and half centuries ago. At that time the first members of the Cult of the Children of the New Order were uncovered in the course of inquisitorial trials with all sorts of demoniacs. But by all accounts the Cult had existed long before that and it was discovered only in the grim years of the end of the Hundred Years War.

The legend has it that in the year 965 the dark prophet Lucius foretold the end of the God's Earthly kingdom and the advent of the Dark prince, the bloody angel of revenge, who should sit on the Throne of Heaven instead of God himself. The prophecy was based on the wording of the Holy Scriptures, same as many other similar predictions, concretely on the Revelations of Saint Ezekiel—Apocalypse.
Aha?!

Lucius said that the world would end and from its ruins a new order would rise, whose children would rule the world. And that's why the Cult is named in such a way. I should note that the investigation led by the Papal Inquisition led to a shocking discovery—quite a number of mighty persons from the highest circles of imperial society were members of the Cult and the Cult alone had at its disposal immense wealth. In that way it differed very much from the other demoniac groups of that age.
Really appalling. How did it end?

The Papal Inquisition managed to get confessions of several high-ranking members of the Cult from the province of Umbria, who renounced their delusions and gave the Inquisitions enough convincing evidence. That allowed the Inquisition to convict all several hundred members of the Cult including Lucius during a monster court proceeding in the year 1021 and to burn them all in a single night. And that was the end. No historical sources have mentioned the Cult since then and it's believed it was completely wiped out.
Hmm... And what does the scroll say?

Well, let's interpret it. On the Eve of Damned Balduin, nine years after the Night without Wood... The night without wood surely means the night when Lucius and his followers were executed in Bonorium. Historical sources say the members of the Cult were so numerous that the Inquisition soon ran out of wood and it was necessary to start lumbering the orchards of Bonorium. To all appearance someone was to meet nine years after that event—at the night of saint Balduin, which is the most damned feast of all worshippers of the Dark Prince.
Great. But who was to meet whom? And why?

The following lines of the text say that. The Four Messages intact with Seals, for the men in Red Robes, for the traitors of Umbria... It's evident those traitors who denunciated the Cult in exchange for their immunity were to meet. They were four and all came from the province of Umbria. Although they weren't punished they had to wear red clothing of heretics which the scroll mentions. It makes sense, doesn't it?
Not much—why would those members of the Cult who were the cause of its fall meet?

Good question. I'm starting to suspect the reality is not such as it was believed to be. What if the destruction of the Cult was planed ahead? What if Lucius and others sacrificed themselves to allow the continuing existence of the Cult? After all as I've already said the Cult of the Children of the New Order was very powerful, its members included members of the royal family and of archiepiscopal cathedra and it had great wealth at its disposal...

I can't believe they would let themselves be caught and executed without a trace of resistance. It would make sense if those who denounced the Cult to the Inquisition did so according to a plan and so ensured that the Cult will continue to exist. To exist through the four alleged traitors of Umbria!
Let's say you're right. But why should they meet exactly after nine years?
Did those mysterious protectors of the Realm visit someone else too in Glatzburg, Monsignor?

I can't say for certain, my son. They arrived late in the evening and they backed out of the temple like ghosts, so I can't say if they visited someone else before or after it. And knowing the circumstances under which the meeting happened I rather didn't ask anybody in the city about them.

Nine is a magic number for demoniacs. Moreover it's a sufficiently long time for the excitement caused by the Cult to calm down and for the traitors of Umbria to shake off any suspicion, don't you think? They probably stayed in the safety of some monastery those nine years, waiting for their time to come. After nine years they met at the pre-arranged place and each of them took one of the sealed scrolls that were prepared there.
And one of those scrolls is now in our hands?

It's likely so. Every one of the four members who stayed alive became a continuator of the Cult and guarded its secrets—its Plan that this scroll mentions and that some historians have believed to really exist.
Plan? What plan?

Several historical sources say Lucius had a certain Plan that should have led to that what he foretold—to the end of the world—in a certain sequence of events. And according to the scroll found on Judge Vallarian it seems it is really so.

If Lucius had a plan to destroy God's Earthly realm, why didn't he execute it himself? Why would he rather let himself and most of his followers be burned and secretly pass his plan on to just a few of his followers?

I have no idea, my son. But there had to be some intention in it. Maybe Lucius found the Papal Inquisition was on his track and decided to postpone the Plan in order not to endanger its realization. Or he was aware it wasn't possible to execute the Plan offhand and that it needed some time, and because of it he did what he did—played a show for the whole world and let himself and other sectarians be burned, so that the Cult disappeared from the world and from the sight of people without ceasing to exist.
Alright. Let's suppose it happened as you said. But when was the Plan to be executed? And where?

Well... that's a good question. Let's see what our scroll says next. To the land of No Man where no stakes burned, each Twenty and One years after the Damned Balduin, nine successive followers... Lucius probably planned for the four traitors to leave the Empire to evade possible attention. In those years stakes with heretics burned almost all over the world, but here in Ultherst it was relatively quiet.
So it means the last members of the Cult left for our Realm?
It's likely. As I think about it now it was very clever of Lucius. He hid the last members of the Cult in places where no one would seek them.
But what were they to do here?

I'd say they were to wait here. The scroll reads: Each twenty-one years after the damned Balduin, nine successive followers... I would interpret it in such a way that each of the four Lucius' successors was to find one successor of his own during twenty-one years—during his lifetime. And to that successor he was to hand over the scroll and the secret tradition of the Cult.
And the successors was to be nine...

Exactly. Lucius's trial was in the year 1021 and the four followers were to pick up the copy of the Plan nine years later, in the year 1030. All in all they had nine followers and each of them had the scroll for twenty-one years. That's 189 years in total. If we add up 1030 and 189, we find the Plan should be realized in the year 1219.
My God! In that year the Star of Doom appeared in the sky!
Exactly. And in the next three years three Scourges of God struck the Realm. That can't be just a coincidence. What does the Plan say next?
In the crypt of pagans who saw the Light the Last will meet and then go in Three Directions...

That means the last of the followers were to meet again after centuries of separation, and it was to happen in a crypt of pagans who saw the light. That must mean the Paolitans. It was a religious group of heretical pagans who in the era of the pagan realm of Ereborn propagated the faith in demonical creatures and denied the pantheon. They were exterminated during the reign of Emperor Hadrimon. During the Hundred Years War they became the example for many cults of demoniacs that reassumed the teachings of the Paolitans. In facts those teachings are very similar to the teachings concerning Hell of our true faith. That means Lucius knew a secret place here in the Realm where the Paolitans met, and selected it as the place where the last followers of the Cult would meet.

And from that place they were to go in three directions. The scroll reads: Into the Shadow of a Dragon the First will step, the Second shall go where the Denhelitians once danced, and the Third must find Satan's Maw.
Exactly. Didn't you say the alleged invocation of the Fallen Angel Arthamon happened near the place named the Dragon Rock?
Yes, that's right. That could be it!

And the next—the second follower of the cult was to go where the Denhelitians used to dance. The Denhelitians were the cult wishing to transform the Holy Mother Church in their own image. Members of the cult were high church dignitaries living in luxury and prosperity and maintained that the Church is predestined to rule God's Earthly kingdom. I'd say that although they were condemned as cultists the present image of the Church is very similar to theirs.
So it means their former temple is somewhere in the Realm?
It seems so. And I'd say it's somewhere near Glatzburg, because in the 5th century the center of the Denhelitians was right here.
Great. And where was the third cultist to go?

The third must find Satan's maw. There had to be a place with such a name then. I'll try to search the chronicles, maybe I can find something there. Nevertheless it's clear the Cult really met in the year 1219 and Judge Vallarian was one of the four last followers of dark Lucius, because he found out the shadow of a dragon strictly according to the Plan.
But what are they up to?!

That we may learn from the last words of the scroll: The prison shall be opened, and vengeance will come... It seems those three are to do something at those three places that will set free a prisoner.
But Lucius lived more than two and half centuries ago. He couldn't know who would be imprisoned at the present time.
Really? On the contrary, I think Lucius knew it very well. And he even had to devise a way how to free the prisoner!
And who do you think it is, Monsignor?
The bloody angel of revenge, my son. The Dark prince of Hell. Satan!
What?! You think Lucius knew how to free Satan from his millenium long prison the Revelations of Saint Ezekiel speak about?

The text has convinced me of it, my son. I wouldn't believe someone would try to do it, but if it's the Plan of the Cult of the Children of the New Order—and we have no reason to doubt it—then I believe it.
So what we have here is a Cult long dead that's trying to destroy the world by releasing Satan. What shall we do?

I have an idea. But I don't want to speak about it here. There's too many ears here. We've already attracted too much attention. And as I personally found out recently, enemies can lurk anywhere. I don't know if you've heard about it, but a girl tried to kill me not long ago, the Grand Duke's servant girl Francessca Gulvardi. I was her confessor and she ran amok at me during a confession—like a wild animal. It was doubtless she was possessed by an unclean spirit. Up to then I hadn't believed our Realm was endangered as gravely as I was warned.
Warned? By whom?

In the early spring two men visited me. Both of them took great pains to keep their identity secret. They warned me some secret group has been established within the Realm that probably intrigues against His Majesty King Edward. The men said about themselves that they're loyal protectors of the Realm and invited me to join them. I refused because that's not my cup of tea, but I promised I'd search for members of that secret heretical society.

Your meeting with those protectors of the Realm is very similar to a certain meeting of mine—I too was sought out by two men in spring. They beseeched me to depart to Hillbrandt in the name of God's justice and to investigate the crimes that were perpetrated there.

Then it really can't be a coincidence that our paths have crossed, my son. Frankly, at first I didn't believe that, but the attempt of that mad girl to murder me seemed to me a very strange coincidence. And now, when I know the Plan of the Cult of the Children of the New Order, I'm convinced the Realm is really in a very grave danger. And it's danger not only for the reign of His Majesty, but also for the faith and for the Holy Mother Church.
So, what shall we do?

I'd rather not speak about it here. Come to the Grand Duke's gazebo outside the city, there we'll be able to speak undisturbed. And take care that nobody follows you there, my son. Our lives are in a great danger from now on!
Alright, Monsignor. Farewell.

Have you gone mad, son? Trying to rob the diocesan Bishop is a crime for which you would die very slowly. I firmly trust the disgusting act of yours was caused by some sudden mental disorder and it won't happen again!
Regrettably I don't have it on me.
I understand. In that case seek me out when you have the letter at your disposal. Goodbye for now.
What do you want, my son? I don't exactly have plenty of time. Are you bringing me the letter from Master Edmond d'Arvias?
I've brought the letter from Master Edmond d'Arvias. Here it is.
Regrettably I still don't have the letter.
In that case don't bother me. I'm really very busy!
I have to go... my son, I can't linger here any longer... they're waiting for me, I have to go... Remember, Francessca Gulvardi is the key... Father Frederick... farewell...
Farewell, Monsignor. May your soul find eternal peace.
What's going on here? Oh my God, no! You unclean spirit, you murdered Bishop Trevorius!!

Listen to me, my son... I'm the ghost of Bishop Trevorius... there's not much time left for me, they're calling me... I can resist... only for a moment... Francessca Gulvardi is the key... listen to her... relieve her body of unclean powers and hear her out... Father Frederick... will help you...
What is Francessca Gulvardi the key to, Monsignor? What did you mean by that?
Wait a moment, who's Father Frederick?
Who killed you, Monsignor? Who's your murderer?

The ruler of Alvaron is Grand Duke Drake Lambert as the royal governor of the city. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. I believe choosing Grand Duke Drake was a wise move by the King, but Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth proved to be quite an unfortunate choice. Her treasury is full all the time, but she occupies herself more with her beauty than with city administration.
I'm sorry, but I don't suspect anyone of heresy. I'm sorry.

You ask me what has happened in Alvaron recently? You mean besides the murder of King Edward? I don't know if you've heard about it, but one of the paladins lost his mind and started to murder innocent people. It's the paladin Minfred von Siegel who has returned from a long crusade against the powers of Hell recently. Presumably he brought back some demon in his head that awakened murderous tendencies in him. He killed several innocent people in broad daylight in the middle of the city. Then he allegedly ran away and now he's hiding in the vicinity of the city and cutting to pieces everyone he meets.

I'm sorry, but I don't know about any facts that could lead to the capture of those shameful criminals who allow werewolves secretly into the city. I'm sorry. Maybe you should try asking the guards who were on duty on some of the nights when there was a full moon in the sky. Maybe they saw something.
I knew Ron Burton well. I often saw him in the marketplace or in his inn, which he owned together with his brother William. So it grieves me very much he left us.
How do you know he's dead?!

I suppose so. We don't live in days when one may have false hope that a missing person will be found alive and well because he only lost his way at night. But I don't know anything particular about him.

I've heard about that accusation of rape brought by Grand Duchess Liana Lambert. I don't think Father Nicholas did what he's accused of, because Grand Duchess Liana Lambert is a deceitful and immodest bitch—God forgive me the word, but it's true. But although I greatly regret it I don't know of anything that would refute Grand Duchess's assertion...

Have you heard the legend about Duke Manfred Gotfried, knight? It was a really disgusting case of heresy—and unfortunately it has never been proven. Although all knew he was a heretic and knew about all the perversities he did, they feared him like the plague and the Inquisition never got enough evidence to convict him.
Tell me.

The Duke used to travel a lot when he was young and they say that he was one of the few who visited Jad-Habaal, the realm of the pagan dogs. From there he brought a cursed relic, a certain Necklace of Death. The necklace reputedly gave him supernatural powers allowing him to communicate with the Other World. The Baron succumbed to the temptation and started to occupy himself with necromancy.
God forbid!

Amen, knight. His heresy deepened more and more—and soon it wasn't enough for him just to speak with the dead, he wanted to have them around as his servants. So he started to use his Necklace of Death to summon the souls of the dead and then forced them to do his bidding. It's said he was served by living corpses at the table, ghosts cleaned his house and even in bed he found delight in undead harlots. Really appalling. His heresy was ended only by his death, which came for him under shady circumstances in the year 1213. Because heresy was never proven of him he was buried in a nobleman's crypt at the city cemetery.
Answer me at once, or you'll get to know my wrath!
I'm asking you sincerely, good man: answer my question. Believe me, you won't do any harm to anyone by that.
I can't believe such a wise man would refuse to answer my question...
I'm glad you ask, knight. I've been thinking a lot and then I decided to testify. I witnessed the murder of His Majesty. I know who the murderer is!
In that case tell me his name—justice must be satisfied!
I agree, knight. But there's a certain problem. The murderer of King Edward is a very powerful and hence very dangerous man. I'm afraid that if I reveal his name he'll take his revenge.
You don't need to be afraid. I'll protect you if need be. But I must get your testimony!

I don't fear for myself, knight. I'm old and the death of King Edward took away the meaning of my life. But I've a granddaughter. Her name's Adeleida and she's my most precious treasure. She's so young and innocent. I fear the murderer of King Edward will take revenge upon her if I testify against him. He'll have her kidnapped, debauched and then killed. I know the way it's done—I've heard about it so often I shudder to think of it
In that case I'll protect your granddaughter. What do you want me to do?

I want you to secretly lead her out of the town and accompany her to Hillbrandt to Monsignor Quentinus. I've arranged it with him already, I wrote him a letter and he replied me he would be glad to take care of Adeleida and to be her guardian in the case of my death. As soon as you do that I'll tell you who murdered King Edward. And I don't care for any wrath that may smite me then.
Thank you, knight. Believe me, I don't like to hinder you, but I'm afraid...
Certainly, knight. What would you like to know?
You don't have to apologize, good man. I understand you. See you soon.
Welcome, knight. What brings you to me?
I was wondering who you could be.

My name's Trisstan and I am—or I was—the chamberlain of His Majesty King Edward II. Until he was assassinated! May plague consume his murderers! Our Realm didn't deserve such a terrible loss. This will break our neck, I'm sure of it.
I'm sorry for what happened. Tell me, what was King Edward like? As a man.

What was he like as a man? A magnificent one! He was such a sovereign every land may just wish for. He was thoughtful and careful and he protected the Realm like a real father. The realm had a great support in him... until the death of his son Louis, his successor. His death broke him. When he learnt what happened, he kept himself locked in his chambers for several days and let nobody in. When he at last allowed me to bring him some food I couldn't recognize him. And since then he was only a shadow of what he had been before.
Such is the fate of humans. May I speak with you for a moment?

Fate you say? No, that wasn't fate, they were people. Only people can be blamed for crimes and sins they perpetrate. But it doesn't matter anymore, it can't bring my King back to life. So, ask away, knight.
Hello, knight. Are you looking for me?
Yes. I'd like to speak with you for a moment.
No, it's a mistake. Farewell.
Hello, knight. I've been awaiting you impatiently. Have you escorted Adeleida to Bishop Quentinus in Hillbrandt?
I am patient, knight. But you must be too—until you accompany Adeleida to Bishop Quentinus, I won't tell you the name of the murderer of His Majesty King Edward II.
Yes, I know that. May I speak with you for a momemt?
I know. I'll try to do it as soon as possible. See you soon.
Yes, I did. She will be safe with Bishop Quentinus.
I'm glad she's safe. I wouldn't forgive myself if something happened to her. I grieve to think that I may not see her ever again, but that's not as important as her safety. Thank you, knight.
You're welcome, good man. But now tell me who's the murderer of King Edward.

Certainly, knight. So then... it happened one evening when the King lingered in his study and had one of his gloomy fatalistic moods. I rather got out of his sight because he was drunk and I didn't want to get it. That was why I didn't notice a visitor come to him. I found out only because of the raised voices that woke me from slumber. The King had a quarrel with his visitor and it seemed it was getting worse and worse.
Hmm... Continue.

The visitor reproached the King for his apathy and resignation and shouted he would drive the Realm to utter ruin. The King replied the Realm already was in utter ruin and that he didn't give a damn. Then I heard sounds of fight and rushed for the study. But when I got there the King was already dead. I only saw his murderer hurrying away through the other door.

It was the First Knight Rodrigo de Velacor, knight. I know it sounds weird, because the First Knight is the highest protector of the Royal Crown and of the Realm, but it's true. He murdered the King. I don't know if he did it in cold blood, but one thing is sure—he is the murderer!
Are you sure, good man, that it really was the First Knight? You said it happened in the evening and the play of light and shadows could have cheated you.
No, knight, I recognized him reliably. Why, I met him in the royal palace every day. It was Rodrigo de Velacor, I would give my life for that!
You're welcome, knight. It was my duty. I did it for King Edward. He didn't deserve such a fate, no matter how he behaved in the last few years.
Thank you. May I speak with you a moment more?
Hello, knight. I thank you once more for helping me get Adeleida to a safe place. One can't be too careful these days. May I help you somehow?
