Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick confessed she participated in the preparation of a ritual during which the Fallen Angel Baphomet was supposedly invoked, Your Excellency. And she told me that it was you who orchestrated and planned the crime. What can you tell me about that?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick really confessed to heresy? I'm... very much surprised by that, my son. I would never think that heresy is rooted even in such high circles of society in the Realm. Really appalling. How could it get so far?
It's hard to say, Your Excellency. But tell me what do you think of the accusation brought by her. She told me that Baphomet's invocation was engineered by you.

I'm not surprised by that, my son. I have been accused of heresy many times since I've become a Curial Inquisitor. Almost every heretic forced by torture to confess tries to take revenge on various people by blackening their names and denunciating them. Last year a young boy possessed by Satan accused me of letting the infernal powers into his body during a monstrous rite. That's why in the case of Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick I'm more startled by the fact she confessed to heresy than by the fact she accused me of such terrible crimes.
So you're innocent?
Certainly, my son! How could it cross your mind to doubt it? I know your investigation puts you into difficult situations, but you always have to rely more on your faith and reason!
The Grand Duchess also confessed you have certain letters on yourself which you received this spring from someone in Alvaron and that supposedly convict you of heresy...

In fact I've really received several letters from Alvaron, but I assure you, my son, that they are in no way heretical. Inquisitor General Commendoni sent them and they contain instructions on how to proceed in the fight against the surging heresy. Every Curial Inquisitor in the Realm received similar letters.
You're welcome, my son. God bless you for your thorough investigation.
May I see those letters, Your Excellency?

I'm sorry, my son, but they're intended only for me and may not be read by anyone else. But I assure you there's nothing in them that would even remotely resemble heresy. Provided you don't think the Inquisitor General is a heretic and that he schemes with me in some infernal conspiracy.

It's alright, my son. I'm aware of the powers you must face during the investigation. But don't let yourself be led astray and act with clear mind and open heart. The heretics can't defy God's justice that we both represent!
Master Dieter von Gelbendiel maintains he saw you one evening in the episcopal garden. He insists you were giving orders there for some infernal rite to be performed. What do you think about that?

I'm not surprised in any way by Master Dieter von Gelbendiel saying something like that, my son. One may quite easily doubt the moral qualities of that man. As a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous—which is, by the way, a friary order—he should honor all virtues of the clergy, but he decidedly doesn't do so. He's a utilitarian and a careerist, and it led him to intriguing and to trying to get the office of the Seneschal. I've been watching him for years. That's why I'm not surprised he tries to defame me. But I didn't suspect he would go so far in his arrogance as to maintain I plotted some unholy rites!
So you mean to say Master von Gelbendiel lies, right?
Exactly, my son. If you spoke with him you surely observed he is concerned mainly with his own benefit. I fear for him. I think he will end very, very badly...
You're welcome, my son. I'm glad you mentioned it. I will beware of Master von Gelbendiel. I fear for him. I think he will end very, very badly...
At the present time the office of the royal governor is held by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, my dear son. His vice is Duke Rowan van Leerin as the royal vice-governor of the city.
What do you think of the current crisis our Realm has been dragged in, Your Excellency?

Do you know the Holy Scriptures, son? Yes, certainly you do. Then you surely know what Saint Ezekiel tells us in his prophecy. Yes, I'm speaking about the Apocalypse, about the revelation of the end of all things. When the Star of Doom appears in the sky, when the Scourges of God strike... and that's just what happened, son. It happened because people turned away from God Almighty and blinded by sin they started to pray to demons and hellspawns. The Realm is deeply disrupted and you can't distinguish friend from foe.

God is angry and he did well when he has punished us by the Scourges. But we will stand the test. The Holy Inquisition is an impenetrable bastion between faith and heresy, between the faithful and the heretics. We're a lit stake that will burn all that's not as clean as snow. We're a blazing torch that creates light in the darkness and destroys shadows. We'll accomplish the mission we were called to fulfill. It's only a matter of time for heretical cults to be destroyed and their members sent to the God's Justice. Yes, it's only a matter of time. And then all will return to its original state. You have my word, my son.
I've heard some tidings of a coming war. Do you know some further details about it, Your Excellency?

Yes, I too have heard about the danger of a military conflict. I spoke about it with His Grace Robert Heidrick and he assured me he hasn't received any specific information about a war so far. According to the orders of the Marshal of the Realm he shall only put the Royal regiment of Glatzburg on full alert and keep it ready. God will decide what will happen next.

If you're searching for you enemy, my son, try to remember the greatest enemies of ours are heretics. The rest is in the jurisdiction of the temporal power. The task for us, the inquisitors, is to prosecute criminals who have committed offenses against the Faith. I mean members of cults, idolaters and heathens. All those who have sinned by the most terrible sin and have rejected God Almighty as their shepherd must be redeemed by purgative flames. They are the worst beasts and we have to pursue them and free them of their sins.

The worst monsters seem to be the humans, my dear son. If I'm right His Grace Robert Heidrick has offered a reward for catching footpads robbing and murdering on the roads in the vicinity of the city. Sheriff Smith will tell you the details. He also pays the rewards in gold.
Do you suspect anyone of heresy here in Glatzburg, Your Excellency?

Your efforts to discover the utmost number of heretics is commendable, my son, but I assure you I verify all my suspicions personally, or I pass them to my Inquisitors and Prosecutors. I would hate to burden you with my own agenda. I'm sure you have—or soon will have—enough of your own tasks.
Do you know anything about the heretical cult of the Children of the New Order?
Why do you ask about the Cult of the Children of the New Order, my son?
Because I have a suspicion the Cult still exists and has its followers.

Really? That's bad news. Up till now I thought the cult was utterly destroyed in former times. They were demoniacs, worshippers of Satan, gathered in the second half of the tenth century by a certain Lucius who declared himself a Dark Prophet. This Lucius reputedly foretold the end of the God's Earthly Kingdom and the freeing of Satan from his thousand years prison—as the Holy Scriptures tell us in the Apocalypse of Saint Ezekiel.
I'd like to deepen my knowledge, nothing more. Or is it wrong?

No, surely it isn't, my dear son. I'd like to tell you all I know about the Children of the New Order. It just startled me you're asking about the cult that was destroyed so long ago. But let's speak in an ordered way. They were demoniacs, worshippers of Satan, gathered in the second half of the tenth century by a certain Lucius who declared himself a Dark Prophet. This Lucius reputedly foretold the end of the God's Earthly Kingdom and the freeing of Satan from his thousand years prison—as the Holy Scriptures tell us in the Apocalypse of Saint Ezekiel.

A very lucky event happened, my son. Although it's nothing epochal it has filled me with joy, because the matter was distressing me for a long time. It concerns the comedian Tinthan. The vile sacrilegious criminal was scoffing at justice for many years, he was boasting about his elusiveness and was stealing like a magpie. He thought his dexterous fingers could steal anything that crossed his mind and no one would catch him. But he overreached himself. He tried to steal a gold monstrance in the episcopal temple not long ago and he was sighted by witnesses. He managed to run away from the city, but it's only a matter of time before he is caught and punished. I mean executed.
May I ask you how the investigation of the murder of Bishop Trevorius is going on, Your Excellency?
Regrettably I can't reveal any details to you, my son. You're regarded as a suspect in the case. I'm sorry.
I understand...
Are there any details known about the murder of Bishop Trevorius?

Regrettably we haven't advanced much in the case of the murder of Monsignor Trevorius. We know only that the Bishop was found dead near the Grand Duke's gazebo. All evidence suggests that he was given some poison that killed him. It's a terrible loss for the Holy Mother Church. Bishop Trevorius was the man in the proper place. I didn't share some of his opinions regarding the radical changes in the Church, but it meant nothing. He had my respect and boundless confidence. I pray for the salvation of his soul and the swift punishment of those who perpetrated the worst sin imaginable and laid hands on the consecrated Bishop.

You're searching for relicts from the ages long past? Well... that's interesting. But I advise you to better put your mind to fulfilling the holy mission assigned to you by God himself. Searching for the historical legacy of the pagan era may be noble pursuit, but I'm not sure whether there isn't a slippery tentacle of sin hidden behind it. That's why you should attend to your service to God!
Do you know anything further about the Priest Frederick?

Priest Frederick? Why, he was the renowned exorcist, at least people said so. He died here in Glatzburg two years ago during a plague epidemic. I don't know much about him, he was an old eccentric man and a loner. I'm sorry I wasn't able to see him working—if he really was skilled in exorcisms, I would have surely been able to learn something from him.

I don't believe there is any hellspawn that can't be sent back from whence he came. Omnem interfici licet, solum res ad idoneum modum pertiniens est. I know well the case of Istwan de Bragho and I feel that if he really returned it happened because of his cursed desire for revenge, but I doubt his immortality. Evil has to be uprooted and utterly destroyed. Our tools for accomplishing that are prayers, flame, sword, holy water and magic. Some of that must work even against Istwan de Bragho.
Why are you asking about the Fallen Angels, my son?
I'd like to extend my knowledge, Your Excellency.

That's commendable, my son, although I must say you've chosen a very dark area for extending your knowledge. The Holy Scriptures say the Fallen Angels are Satan's minions and that they administer his will and corrupt order. They're the architects of sin, the devisers of treason and the eternal tempters. They're Arthamon, the master of Destruction, Baphomet, the ruler of madness, Cerdie, the mother of debauchery and Azrael, the Fallen Archangel and the first emissary of Satan. All four were thrown down from Heaven along with Satan for their crimes against God. God's punishment bound them in the infernal prison. Since then Hell has been their new home and their palace. From there they try to get into our world to dominate it. But they're not going to succeed, because God's Earthly kingdom is protected by the true faith that's like its angelic shield.
Does it mean that if the true faith should fade away the Fallen Angels would be able to get into this world?
I don't know, my son. The Holy Scriptures are silent about that. But even if it were possible it would never happen—the true faith is eternal just like God Himself.

I'm sorry, but I don't care for alcohol. And if I were you I would forsake it too while there's still time. I'm certain you act in good faith, but remember that infernal toils of sin are hidden even behind good intent. Better stay away from spirits!
I'm searching for Raquel Gielwitch, who is missing. Do you happen to know anything about her?

The disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch is a very sad incident. Much like the disappearance of several other girls living in this city and in its vicinity. There are certain suspicions that all those crimes are the work of the same culprits, but no evidence was found. I hope you'll manage to change that, my son.
You can't bribe me, son. I'm sorry...
Although you're a Curial Inquisitor, I have to insist upon your reply. And believe me, I know about ways how to force you to answer.
It seems you don't like me because of some reason, Your Excellency. I'm sorry about that. In spite of that I believe you'll overcome your grudge and answer my question.
I don't believe a man as learned and wise as you, Your Excellency, would refuse to help a humble servant of God...
You're welcome, my son. But now tell me, are you the paladin who came from Hillbrandt?
Yes, Your Excellency. That would probably be me.

I'm glad to meet you, my son. I received a message from Inquisitorial Judge Jeremiah. He described all your actions in Hillbrandt. My name's Cardinal Truncquillius and I'm the Curial Inquisitor in Glatzburg.
Maybe yes, maybe no. It depends on who is asking.

But yes, it is you, my son. I received a message from Inquisitorial Judge Jeremiah. It describes all your actions in Hillbrandt. My name's Cardinal Truncquillius and I'm the Curial Inquisitor in Glatzburg.
No, Your Excellency. That wouldn't be me.

To lie is a mortal sin, my son—never forget that. I know well it is you. I received a message from Inquisitorial Judge Jeremiah. It describes all your actions in Hillbrandt. My name's Cardinal Truncquillius and I'm the Curial Inquisitor in Glatzburg.

Me too, my son—in spite of all I've learned about you so far. But let's get to the point. I won't hide that I'm greatly alarmed by the events which occurred in Hillbrandt and which Father Jeremiah described in his report. The accusation and subsequent execution of several heretics including the wife of the royal vice-governor of the town, and what's worse, even of Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian. Those aren't events I can easily shrug shoulders over, even in these days. Partly because it was me who sent Judge Vallarian to Hillbrandt in the spring. He was to face the surging number of cases of heresy and apostasy there. That's why I can't believe it was him who stood behind all the crimes described in the report. What can you tell me about it, my son? After all it was you who led the investigation—it was your initiative and your effort that sent all the defendants to face God's Justice...
So it was you who sent Judge Vallarian to Hillbrandt?
Yes, as I've just said. And that's why I want to know what exactly happened in Hillbrandt to draw personal consequences from it. So, can you tell me anything about it?
During my stay in Hillbrandt I found that Judge Vallarian along with two other accomplices prepared and carried out a monstrous plan aimed at letting the Fallen Angel Arthamon enter this world.

Really?! Are you telling me the Inquisitorial Judge and the Bishop of the Holy Mother Church struggled for invoking the Fallen Angel Arthamon? I can't believe that! Who sent you to Hillbrandt anyway, my son? How come you appeared there just at the time when Judge Vallarian perpetrated—at least if what you say is true—all those crimes?
It was the will of God, Your Excellency!

Well... I can hardly object to that. Viae Domini arcanea sunt. But now reveal to me, what has brought you to Glatzburg. Did you find a suspicious trail or some evidence during those incongruous proceedings in Hillbrandt that have lead you here?

I don't know myself, Your Excellency. Two men sought me out in the spring and asked me to go to Hillbrandt and to find culprits of the crimes that took place there. That was how I got wind of Judge Vallarian.
And who were those men? Do you know anything about them?
No, Your Excellency, I didn't know them. Furthermore they took great pains over their identities staying secret.

Hmm... Really interesting. But it worries me a little bit—I don't favor anonymous denunciations a lot. If I may give you good advice: you should verify each bit of information twice and shouldn't believe anything that seems to be true at first sight. You have to be very prudent!
You may rely on me, Excellency.
But now tell me what has brought you to Glatzburg. Did you find a suspicious trail or some evidence during those incongruous proceedings in Hillbrandt that has lead you here?
Forgive me, Your Excellency, but if this isn't a part of the investigation, I'd like to keep that information to myself.

Sure, my son, as you wish. I only wanted to know who gave you an impulse to concern yourself with the Hillbrandt case. But now tell me what has brought you to Glatzburg. Did you find a suspicious trail or some evidence during those incongruous proceedings in Hillbrandt that has lead you here?
What does your questions mean, Excellency? Am I being investigated? If not, I'd like to be silent about the case.
No, you're not being investigated, my son. At least not for now. I only wanted to create some preliminary theory about what happened in Hillbrandt.

As Father Jeremiah probably wrote you in his letter, Judge Vallarian was found guilty of crimes of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King on the basis of convincing evidence and thus he was rightfully punished.

Yes, that's exactly what is written here. But I wonder what has brought you to Glatzburg. Did you find a suspicious trail or some evidence during those incongruous proceedings in Hillbrandt that has lead you here?
You're the Curial Inquisitor?

Yes, my son, that's true. I've been leading the local Inquisitorial Curia since 1221 when Inquisitor General Commendoni nominated me to take this post. I supervise all the actions of the Holy Office, and in these gloomy days it's an almost superhuman task.
I'm searching here for the Cult of the Children of the New Order, Your Excellency. I have a reasonable suspicion Judge Vallarian was its member.

The Cult of the Children of the New Order? That's a really surprising reason for your journey here to Glatzburg, my dear son. Do you know any details about that cult? Because if I'm not mistaken that demonic cult was utterly destroyed more than several centuries ago and all its members ended at the stake. Furthermore it all happened in the Empire, therefore fully outside of the territory of Ultherst. Although it's true that since the Star of Doom appeared in the sky and the Realm was punished by the Scourges of God there have been numerous attempts of heretics and apostates to resurrect many old cults and movements, but I've heard nothing of the Cult of the Children of the New Order in this respect. That's why I'm surprised by your finding that Judge Vallarian was its member.
Could you tell me something else about the Cult, Your Excellency?

Certainly. As I've already said it was a cult of demoniacs, presumably established in the second half of the tenth century by a certain Lucius who declared himself to be a Dark Prophet. This Lucius reputedly foretold the end of the God's Earthly Kingdom and the freeing of Satan from his thousand years prison—as the Holy Scriptures tell us in the Apocalypse of the Saint Ezekiel. As you can see, it wasn't any breakthrough prophecy, because it stemmed from the notorious passage of the Holy Scriptures. Likewise the teachings of Lucius didn't differ much from the teachings of other heretical sects of that era—it ran upon the saying carpe diem. That means—do what you want, there's neither Heaven nor God, and even if it existed it wouldn't matter because in a couple of years the world would become a part of Hell. And who collaborates with hellspawns will rule over enslaved souls of the faithful. The Children of the New Order behaved roughly in that way and believed that when the end of the world comes and Satan sits on the throne of Heaven and Earth, they all would have a hell of a good time.
And how did they end?

They ended in a way similar to how other cults of that era did—heretics were discovered, caught and executed to a man by the Papal Inquisition, although many of them were members of high society. Most likely one of the dark priest of the cult decided to save his life—or his soul—and denounced all his fellow cultists to the Papal Holy Office. That was why even Lucius himself was captured and along with the others burned in the year of 1021 in the Empire Square in Bonorium, the capital of the Lochland Empire. The stakes were burning there for three days and three nights then, so numerous the heretics were. And that was the end of it all. Since then there has been no mention of the Children of the New Order. That's why I'm surprised you associate Judge Vallarian with that cult.
As I've already told you, I have a reasonable suspicion it was so. And I've come to Glatzburg to find out if it is true.

Yes, you're right. We live in times too uncertain to afford ourselves premature and subjective opinions. Continue with your investigation, then—the Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.

I've found a very strange scroll on Judge Vallarian that I'd like to decipher here in Glatzburg. It will probably tell us something more about the real intentions of Judge Vallarian and about his supposed membership in the Cult of the Children of the New Order.
A scroll? What scroll is it? May I see it?
Sure, Your Excellency. Here it is.

Really strange... I've never seen any script like that. Are you sure it belonged to Judge Vallarian? In that case it's really more than important to find out what the scroll says. Stay here in Glatzburg, then, and try to shed some light on it. The Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.
I'd gladly show it to you, but I don't have it on me.

I understand. I hope you have it in a safe place. Try to find out what it says, then, and if it may show us any other tracks. The Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.
I'm very sorry, Excellency, but I'd prefer showing it to as few people as possible. I'm not sure what exactly it is.

That would probably be a wise decision, my son. I only wanted to offer you my help. But I'm sure you can cope with it without me. The Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.
Maybe you're right, Your Excellency. I have neither any hard evidence nor any tracks.

Hmm... But in any case it will certainly be better if you consider that possibility too, my son. We live in times too uncertain to be able to afford premature and subjective opinions. Continue with your investigation, then—The Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.
I've been brought here by a certain mission. But I'd like to keep its details to myself, if you won't take offense, Your Excellency.

As you wish, my son. I thought I would offer you my help. But it's your business, of course. Nevertheless if you need help with anything, just say. I'm here to serve God and the King. The Holy Office doesn't wish to inhibit the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous from taking their own way of achieving our common goal—that is God's justice. You'll probably cooperate especially with Judge Welfhar who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that everything here in Glatzburg is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those you've met so far.
I haven't been brought to Glatzburg by anything important, Excellency. I may even say I'm just passing through.

I understand. But anyway, if you need help of the Holy Office when performing your duties here don't hesitate to approach Judge Welfhar 
who is also the Chief Prosecutor of Glatzburg. Cooperate with him as much as possible. You'll surely soon find for yourself that here in Glatzburg all is much more intricate and crimes are more cunning than those happening in the northern parts of the Realm.
You're welcome, my son. Much hard and unpleasant work awaits you here, I'm sure of it. We live in days when heresy and delusions take all sorts of forms and we have to be alert.
I understand, Excellency.

But so far as the events in Hillbrandt are concerned... I can't do otherwise than to examine the matter. The execution of a Curial Judge with the delegated authority of a Curial Inquisitor is too grave a matter to be simply passed over. Less so in these days when the standing and jurisdiction of the Holy Inquisition tremble under the weight of criticism, mainly from the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I've already given orders to start the investigation in Hillbrandt. I wouldn't like you to take these steps as if I don't believe your words or actions, but as a Curial Inquisitor I can't act otherwise. And you may be sure that if the results of the investigation should concern you somehow, you'll be the first one to know.
Hmm... Thanks for the information, Your Excellency.
You're welcome, my son. Our fate is in the hands of God. But now tell me, may I do something for you?
I would like to ask you something, if it doesn't bother you.
Certainly. What do you want to know? Ask about anything.
No, Your Excellency, thank you. Farewell for now.

Farewell, my son. I believe we'll see each other soon. If you need something you know where you can find me. Although I have more work than anybody can imagine, I'll make enough time for you anytime you need.
Yes, Your Excellency. I'd like to talk with you.
By all means, my son. Although my office occupies me quite a lot, I'll gladly find some time to speak with you.
No, thanks. I was just passing by. Farewell.
Farewell, my son. And take care. Remember that heresy and delusions can wear many disguises and veils of pretense. Keep your eyes open.
Hmm... and by what evidence will you back up this accusation, my son? Remember that a Judge of the Holy Office must have all evidence gathered before he may order a trial.

Great! I can't say I'm surprised by your quick and completely precise investigation, my son, because I've never doubted your qualities. You've solved the case in a great way. There's nothing more to say. Tibi gratulor. Now you only have to demonstrate your knowledge of canon and of secular law. Come when you deem yourself ready.
Thank you, Excellency. Farewell.

As you can see, my son, it wasn't any breakthrough prophecy, because it stemmed from the notorious passage of the Holy Scriptures. Likewise the teaching of Lucius didn't differ much from the teachings of other heretical sects of that era—it ran upon the saying carpe diem. That means—do what you want, there's no Heaven nor God, and even if it existed it wouldn't matter because in a couple of years the world would become a part of Hell. And who collaborates with hellspawns will rule over enslaved souls of the faithful. The Children of the New Order behaved roughly in that way and believed that when the end of the world comes and Satan sits on the throne of Heaven and the world, they all would have a hell of a good time.

They ended in a way similar to how other cults of that era did—heretics were discovered, caught and executed to a man, although many of them were members of high society. Most likely one of the dark priest of the cult decided to save his life—or his soul—and denounced all his fellow cultists to the Papal Inquisition. That was why even Lucius himself was captured and along with the others burned in the year of 1021 in the Empire Square in Bonorium, the capital of the Lochland Empire. The stakes were burning there for three days and three nights then, so numerous the heretics were. And that was the end of it all. Since then there has been no mention of the Children of the New Order.

Your unholy words incriminate you, Cardinal! Do you confess to your sins then? Was it really you who devised the plan of the supposed invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet and who entrusted Yulliette Heidrick and other heretics to carry it out? Are you a dark priest of the cult of the Children of the New Order?

Yes, my son, exactly. I'm a dark priest of the cult of the Children of the New Order that is going to rule the Realm soon. And nothing will stop us, my son. Nothing! God is slowly dying, his Earthly kingdom is falling apart and the throne of Heaven is swaying. The time of revenge and blood has come, the time from which the New Order will be born! We were predestined to that many centuries ago and our time is almost at hand! That was why the Fallen Angels Arthamon and Baphomet were invoked. Thanks to Judge Vallarian, who managed to get the lost book Libre Daemonium of the dark prophet Lucius, we were able to perform the rites of invocation!
I don't believe you've really invoked the demons Arthamon and Baphomet!

The question of your belief is of no importance here, my dear son. Know that both Fallen Angels entered this world and they'll soon open their arms to it. The world is going to become a part of Hell. It remains only to invoke the mother of debauchery, Cerdie, and the work will be done!
Why did you decide to murder Bishop Trevorius?

Isn't it obvious? Because he posed a threat to us. He was a firm advocate of the true faith and a zealous servant of God. We couldn't risk he would denounce us and set all the remaining clergy against us. That was why I had Francessca Gulvardi kidnapped—I knew she went to confess to Bishop Trevorius. The Fallen Angel Baphomet possessed her by the means of an evil spirit that was to force her to a murderous attempt on the Bishop. Unfortunately the plan went wrong and on the top of it you arrived in the city at that time to contact Bishop Trevorius. That was why I had to act swiftly and had the Bishop removed before he was able to help you. But even so I didn't do it fast enough. As you can see, you're very successful in your efforts!
What do you aim by that disgusting Plan of yours? What is the goal of your vile conspiracy? To usurp the power in the Realm?

Of course, my son. When the Fallen Angels are invoked, nothing will hinder the Dark Prince in freeing himself of his thousand years old chains and in becoming the ruler of Heaven and Earth. How do you think it will be when God dies, my son? To tell the truth, I can't wait to see.
At whose bidding have you perpetrated all those foul deeds? Who is the head of the cult of the Children of the New Order?
I'm sorry, my son, but it's not your destiny to find the answer to that question now. But I'm sure the future will give it to you—be it in any way.
Why are you telling all that to me anyway, Cardinal? You're proving yourself guilty by that! What are you intending to achieve by that?

I believe it's important for you to understand what's going on. I believe it would be a pity to waste your talent as Judge Vallarian did. The time has come for you to be led into temptation and be able to decide on whose side you would stand in the eternal fight. So then, what path will you choose? Will you stay loyal to your God, whose Earthly kingdom is slowly perishing in the flames of doom, or will you stand on the side of those who believe in the new order whose Children will reign the world and Heaven?
That's enough, Cardinal. I arrest you for the reasonable suspicion of heresy and of conspiring against God and the King. You'll be put to prison where you'll stay for the course of investigation.

Wait, my son. You can't think I said it all to you as a confession, can you? Or that I said it to ease your position during the trial. I did it to allow you at least to partially understand what's going on. I believe it would be a pity to waste your talent as Judge Vallarian did. The time has come for you to be led into temptation and be able to decide on whose side you would stand in the eternal fight. So then, what path will you choose? Will you stay loyal to your God, whose Earthly kingdom is slowly perishing in the flames of doom, or will you stand on the side of those who believe in the new order, whose Children will reign the world and Heaven?
I would never accept such a disgusting infernal pact, Cardinal. You're arrested!

Don't be ridiculous, my son. Do you think you can defeat me? I master powers you can't even dream about! But as you wish—have it your way then. Your life's going to end here in this place! Kill him, my infernal brothers!
What could you offer me in the case that I decided to join you?

I'm glad you're trying to consider my offer before you utter your final decision. Know then that you would be heaped with gold and no sin would be forbidden to you. You would fulfill all your dreams of power, wealth and knowledge. Paths undreamed of would open to you. You would change into the man you always wanted to be. Doesn't it seem spectacular?!
Well... your offer is irresistible, Excellency. I accept. I wish to become a member of the cult of the Children of the New Order!
Optime, mi fili! I didn't doubt I would convince you. And so you'll bear the Mark of the Beast from this day on. Come closer and let me mark you by this infernal brand that'll become your new symbol!
Wait a moment. I won't let myself be branded like some cattle!
It's the part of the initiating rite, my son. Thanks to the mark of the beast we're able to recognize ourselves. You've nothing to fear, it will only hurt a little...
Alright then, brand me!
Muheheeee! You fool! Did you really think I would let you enter there where only the chosen ones may enter? Your soul now belongs to me!
I'm telling you I won't let myself be branded!
You fool! In that case you're going to die! Kill that poor wretch, my brothers!
Alright then, brand me with the mark of the beast!

Salve, serve Dei. Tuum nomen laudetur od eam causam, quam gravem casum umeris portas. Cardinalis Truncquillius inquisitor curialis Sancti officii sum. Libere gaudeo te huc Glatzburgum venisse ut nostras acies firmaret.
Excuse me, Your Excellency, but I don't understand you. I'm not well versed in the Ancient Lateran.

Really? It surprises me, my son. I've thought that all the learned advocates of the true faith, among which you concededly belong, speak this blessed language of the prophets! But I believe you'll correct this blind spot in your knowledge as soon as possible.
Yes, Excellency, I'll do my best. Thank you.
Salvete, Vestre Excellentissime Vire. Utinam ab ipso onnipotenti Deo benedicamini!
Ita, utinam tu quoque benedicaris, mi fili. Well said. Hardly any man knows the Ancient Lateran that well, although it's the blessed language of the prophets.
Canis, qui sanctus est, numquam delirat.
What did you say? The dog that is sacred never speaks deliriously? What nonsense is that?
Eh... I'm sorry, Your Excellency, but I'm not well versed in the Ancient Lateran. Excuse me.

Ain vero? Id me stupefacit, mi fili. I've thought that all the learned advocates of the true faith, among which you concededly belong, speak this blessed language of the prophets! But I believe you'll correct this blind spot in your knowledge as soon as possible.
Welcome, my son. May God bless you for your deeds. How is your search for the Cult of the Children of the New Order going? Is there something I can do for you?
No, thank you. I was just passing by. Farewell.
Welcome, my son. May God bless your path. Have you advanced in your search for the origin of that mysterious scroll? Have you found what it is?

Yes, I've found out. It really is a text written several centuries ago by the members of the Cult of the Children of the New Order. According to Bishop Trevorius it's some Plan that should lead to overthrowing God's Earthly Kingdom.
A Plan of the Cult of the Children of the New Order? I've never heard about that. What's the Plan about?
It reads that Dark Priests of the Cult of the Children of the New Order shall free Satan from his thousand years prison. It shall happen this year and God's Earthly Kingdom shall be overthrown.

Really horrifying, my son! But I must say that the idea of the end of the world and freeing Satan from his earthly prison is typical for most heretical cults these days. People in their despair lean upon beliefs that offer them certain redemption, a promise of better tomorrows and of a better life instead of the present dismal state. That's why so many fallen souls thrust their faith upon Satan, because they want to believe that if God can't give them that what they desire most—whatever it might be—His greatest rival will. And so I'm not surprised that the Cult of the Children of the New Order too foresee the end of the world and coming of something different and better in that so-called Plan of theirs.
So you think it means nothing? That it isn't dangerous?

Actually it's just the opposite, my son. I believe that any suggestion of ideas rejecting God's Earthly Kingdom and applauding the coming of the rule of the dark powers of Hell has to be uprooted as soon as possible and those who spread such delusions have to be amended and brought back into God's herd. Or we have to commit their irreparable souls to God, if there's no other way. That's why I hope you'll do all you can to discover the members of that Cult and treat them according to law. And should you need my help don't hesitate to ask. The same goes for Judge Welfhar, he's my dear friend and a loyal associate.
You're welcome, my son. Can I do something for you now?
I'm sorry, Your Excellency, but I'd rather stay silent about that. The less people who know about it the better.

Yes, you're probably right, my son. I believe you'll handle the case successfully. And should you need my help don't hesitate to ask. The same goes for Judge Welfhar, he's my dear friend and a loyal associate.
Yes, Father, I've found it. But I'd rather keep the details to myself until I verify all what I know.

Yes, that's probably a wise decision, my son. I'm glad you work systematically and don't want to release any information you haven't verified by your own investigation yet. But should you need my help don't hesitate to ask. The same goes for Judge Welfhar, he's my dear friend and a loyal associate.
No, Your Excellency, I haven't made any progress in that matter. I'm sorry.

I'm sorry to hear that. But don't give up yet, my son. I'm sure your effort will be crowned with success. And should you need my help don't hesitate to ask. The same goes for Judge Welfhar, he's my dear friend and a loyal associate. May I do something for you now?
Welcome, my son. May God bless you for your deeds. I hope your mission here in Glatzburg is drawing to a successful end. Is there something I can do for you?
Welcome, my son. May God bless you for your deeds. I hope your stay in Glatzburg will be an asset for you—much like for us. Is there something I can do for you?

Welcome, son. I believe your search for the members of the Cult of the Children of the New Order is going well. The scroll you've managed to decipher could be the key to their exposal. May I be of any help to you?

We have to talk, my dear son. I've heard very unpleasant news. Monsignor Trevorius, our beloved Diocesan Bishop, became a victim of a terrible crime. To all appearance he was assassinated near the Grand Duke's gazebo, where no one goes these days. And I've also heard that it was none else than you who was found above his cooling body. Can you tell me anything about that?
I'm sorry, Your Excellency, but I can't.

Well... as you wish, my son. In that case I can't do otherwise than to treat you as a suspect. I'm sorry, but the circumstances don't seem to favor you. I'm forced to start the investigation of your person in the case of the murder of Bishop Trevorius. Although I believe it's a mistake and you're innocent, I have to fulfill my duties. Now go and consider whether it wouldn't be wise to tell me something more about the case.
I had a meeting arranged with Bishop Trevorius near the Grand Duke's gazebo. But when I got there I found the Bishop dead...

Hmm... A meeting you say? In such a deserted place? I can't but wonder. What conditions must I meet to become an Inquisitorial Judge?

I'd like to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Excellency.

Really? In that case I hope you're ready to pass the tests examining your practical skills and theoretical knowledge. Remember that the task of an Inquisitorial Judge is mainly to receive indictments from Inquisitorial Prosecutors, investigate the indictments and then bring charges of heresy and of other crimes in accordance with the Codex of Inquisition. That's why every judge has to be able to pass muster with any felon or heathen, he also has to be able to solve even the most confounded cases. Are you really ready to pass the examination to become a Judge?

I personally have put my mind to the case and I found several things that alarmed me more than the presence of the undead inside the city walls. I especially noticed that they're not the usual murders, committed by infernal monsters led only by an urgent lust for fresh blood. All the victims were robbed of all the valuables including brass buttons and gold teeth. At first sight it seems the undead murdered for money. But that's pure nonsense—undead bodies are led only by their murderous instinct and by nothing else.

That's why I've been so surprised by that. At first I thought the robberies were—in contrast to the murders—the work of someone else, but the testimonies of the witnesses speak otherwise. I don't believe there are any undead monsters who would intentionally collect valuables. And then I finally caught on to it. It's not the will of the undead that makes them steal, but the will of the one who summoned them into this world! There are many forbidden necromantic rites by which heretics are able to compel dead bodies to a new unclean life. The undead brought to life in this way obey their creator and may perform certain easy tasks for them. Fortunately that devilish ability of theirs is limited to the most basic orders, otherwise we couldn't be sure of anything. And that's why I'm sure there is a heretic standing behind the undead in the city streets and behind their attacks on the citizens. That way the heretic tries to get wealthy.
Just so, my son. If you manage to do that, it'll be clear evidence you're worthy—and most of all, capable—to become an Inquisitorial Judge.
Alright, Your Excellency. I'll accomplish the task. The culprit will be caught and punished!
Very well, my son.
You're right, Your Excellency. I'm not quite ready yet.
In that case come when you feel you're competent enough, my son.
I've found out who stands behind all the robberies perpetrated by the undead monsters wandering in the city streets at night, Your Excellency.

I'd like to repeat the examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Excellency.

Alright. I believe you are better prepared than the last time. Do not forget that perfect knowledge of the law is absolutely crucial for an Inquisitorial Judge to effectively and righteously perform his duties. So, let's start with the examination. Pararisne, mi fili?

You're welcome, my son. But now tell me, are you the priest who came from Hillbrandt?

Are the inquisitorial proceedings governed by the principle In dubio pro reo or by the principle In dubio sequendum quod tutius est?
By the principle In dubio pro reo. It means that when there are some doubts the court should decide in favor of the defendant.
I'm sorry, my son, but you're wrong. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
By the principle In dubio sequendum quod tutius est. It means that in the case of doubts the court must adhere to the more certain.
The inquisitorial proceedings aren't governed by any of these principles. They're principles of the secular law and not of the canon law.

No, my dear son, you're wrong. They're both principles of the secular and of the canon law. But the inquisitorial proceedings are governed only by one of them, the other does not apply. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
May an Inquisitorial Judge remit a penalty already imposed on a defendant?
No, Your Honor. A judge is not authorized to remit penalties. That may be done only by the Inquisitor General.
Yes, he may. If the judge comes to the conclusion that the mere hearing of the case before the court is enough to reform the culprit, he may refrain from the punishment in its entirety.
No, my son, you're wrong. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
Yes, he may, but only in the case of minor offences.
What punishment may a judge impose if he finds the defendant guilty of heresy?

There are several punishments possible: life imprisonment, imprisonment, the donation of the amount of gold specified, the loss of title, the punishment on the pillory or even the death by hanging, beheading or burning.

No, my son. Those are punishments that a secular court may impose. The Inquisitions knows only one punishment. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
Imprisonment for life or death by burning. Nothing else can cleanse a heretic of the crimes he perpetrated.
No, my son. The Inquisition uses only one of those punishments. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
Only the punishment of death by burning. Because only the flames of the executioner's stake can purify the soul of the heretic of the body that has sinned.

The theft is of course in the jurisdiction of the temporal power, so the culprit will be prosecuted by the secular law or by the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
It's not so, my dear son. This question is not so unambiguous. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.

It depends on the circumstances of the case and the intent of the culprit. If he acted only to enrich himself, it's a secular crime. But if he stole with the aim of damaging the Holy Mother Church and the true faith, it's a crime prosecutable by the Inquisition.
Theft in the house of God is of course in the jurisdiction of the Holy Office.
How long may you question the defendant with the use of torture?
Until he confesses to the crimes he's charged with, or until he answers the question put to him.
As long as I deem fit. Codex Inquisitorium doesn't prescribe any limitation in this regard.
You're very wrong, my son. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
Only as long as not to endanger the life of the defendant.

It's not a crisis, it's a downright disaster! The end of the world, I would say. You can see it in the people here in Hillbrandt. It's said in other parts of the Realm that we are stubborn and tough and nothing can discompose us—and that's absolutely true. We're use to fighting the grudges of life, as they say. You know, no one has a bed of roses here in the north of the Realm. If you don't get used to it, you're done for. That's why we were able to endure hard times more easily than the others in the south. But now... I've never seen so much hopelessness and despair. It's like some incurable illness—it spreads fast and who gets infected is as good as gone. The Scourges of God have taken from us the most valuable thing—our hope. Hardly anyone believes anymore that it all could turn for the better.
I've heard that the miners village near the iron mines was massacred. People say the orcs did it...

Yes, you've heard well. Asherbalt was massacred by the cursed orcs. And the iron mines too. Only a few people managed to get to the safety of the town. Well, as for the safety... the orcish assault on the town several days ago has shown clearly that no one is safe now. Who would have thought it only several years ago? Business was good even here near the border, harvests were good and iron ore was plentiful... simply the Kingdom of God on Earth. And now all of a sudden all those bad things...
I'm searching for heretics here in Hillbrandt. Have you heard any gossip in your inn?

I hear so much gossip about heretics every day that I get an ear-ache, knight. One has bewitched the cow of another so that it has lost milk, someone else bedeviled a neighbor's dog and it died, and another one charmed somebody's spouse so she spreaded her thighs for him... People are so possessed by all that paganism and witchcraft that they don't hesitate to throw dirt on anybody who just slightly displeases them.
So you think there's no truth in those fables?

I didn't say that. There is some truth in everything. Take for example Duke Weinberg. I wouldn't like to say a wrong word about him, but consider it for yourself—the Scourges of God haven't hurt him in any way. While we all lost all sorts of things during those sorrowful three years, but all the scourges gave him a wide berth. He didn't lose anyone from his family, his granaries and pantries are still full, his herds are in a good shape and all his houses are where they should be... how is all that possible? That's the question!

I've heard lotsa gossip about our former Bishop Herbertius returning from the Other World. He supposedly walks around the town and looks for new victims. Just to inform you, Bishop Herbertius wasn't too popular, especially at the end of his tenure here.

People started to whisper he sold himself to Satan and that he got many forbidden pleasures in exchange for his soul. The truth is that young girls started to disappear, and later even boys, and their mutilated corpses were found from time to time deep in the woods. But it was never investigated, because there was no evidence. But one day he was found dead in his bed and since then there has been peace. Until now. They say he returned to repay what he owes the Old Nick himself. The truth is there are weird things going on at the cemetery these days and nobody dares to go there—and not even at high noon.

It may be that Master d'Arvias is innocent, knight. But it also may be he's guilty. Who could judge it? People say somebody saw him opening the gate for the orcs during their recent assault on the town. But it can be a mistake. Somebody thought he saw Master d'Arvias but in fact it was someone else. But maybe it really was him, how could I know?
Have you heard anyone talking about the stolen monstrance of Saint Orthenius?

I've heard a lot about the theft of the monstrance, knight. But if I may guess it is just gossip. They say a hellspawn did it after knocking out the priests who prayed for the salvation of the town. He reputedly did it to allow the orcs and other monsters to swiftly conquer the town. And they also say the monstrance was desecrated a long time ago by wicked rites—supposedly it was aspersed and stripped of all its sanctity. But who did it and where the monstrance is now I haven't heard. Quarim, the dwarf-man who's the jack of Raubsticht, our executioner, led the weirdest talk of all. He said he had seen who did it, but nobody believed him. He is too well known for fudging. I remember him running around the town all agog, shouting that a real dragon had broken out of the Dragon rock and that it was flying to the town. People ran away in terror, you should have seen that. But it turned out then that he was only jesting. People almost stoned him because of it.

They say Bishop Quentinus disappeared the night when the orcs assaulted the town. If that's true he has surely rendered his soul to God already. I liked the old man a lot, I always managed to come to terms with him during confessions and got absolution for cutting beer with water...
You cut beer with water?
Eh... yes, knight. Well, in fact no, not anymore, because I promised Bishop Quentinus I wouldn't do it. Instead I raised its price not to lose profit.
It's a really thorny path of penance...
Just so, knight. Life's tough...
You're welcome, knight. Do you want to know something else?
Do you happen to know anything about Paul Hammerhand going missing?

Victor Hammerhand is quite distressed because of the disappearance of his son. Paul is a brat but his father likes him, although he has already broken dozens of canes while bringing him up. He still believes he will make a dignified man and a good successor and that Paul would take over the family business. But Paul's a madcap, he has his head full of fables about crusades, brave deeds and foreign lands with sand instead of soil...
Is there any gossip going around about the disappearance of Linda van Gallagan?

I haven't heard anything particular about the disappearance of Baroness van Gallagan, knight. They say people saw her for the last time the day the orcs assaulted the town. The same as Bishop Quentinus. It's probably all over with her already, if I say it frankly. People didn't like her much, you know? She was such a would-be gentlewoman who thought she belonged at least to the royal court of His Majesty King Edward. The biggest loss is for her husband. They say he can't even, well, fulfill his morning errands, without her. With all due respect, of course. I don't want to offend the Baron in any way. I'm sure the gossip is totally untrue.
I'm searching for the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias that was stolen from him. Do you happen to know anything about that?

The sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias you say? Well, if you're hinting that I could be selling things of disputable origin, then I definitely must object. I've never seen the sword of Master d'Arvias. If I find out something about it I'll let you know immediately. You may count on me!
What do you think of the murder of Natalia Reichmann? They say the landsknecht Olfgard killed her.

People think Olfghard really did it. I mean that he killed her because of her trinkets. But I don't believe that. Yes, it's true Olfghard wouldn't hesitate to steal anything he could see and he has been punished for that several times already, but on the other hand he never stood in need of murdering, and the young girl on the top of it. He could have stolen her trinkets as easily as he could rob a child of his candy. So why would he murder her?
Are there any legends or tales about this region circulating among the people?

Legends you say? You mean superstitions, stories and such? Well, I've heard a lot of them. People say there's a treasure buried near the Dragon Rock, that there are barbarian ghosts haunting the Tree of Death, that there are cursed spirits praying for mercy in the Dead Man's Stone near the gallows... Or that there once was a pagan kingdom of Thron deep under the Moonshine Mountains and that its last King—Harlior—has been supposedly haunting there up to this day, and that a new defender of the Realm will rise from the common folk soon and restore peace and justice in these lands... Those fables are so numerous that we would be here for the whole day if I was to tell you at least a small part of what people say. Try asking around the town, someone will surely be glad to tell you something.
I've found a stray sheep, innkeeper. Do you know whom it could belong to?
A stray sheep you say? Well, if you agree I'll buy it from you.
Alright, it's a deal. It's yours.
Thanks, knight. Here's your money. It has been a long time since I offered fresh mutton in my inn!
I don't want to sell it. I just wanted to know if you know whose it might be.
In that case ask Ruphert the shepherd, knight. He cares for the Duke's herds.
Do you still have the sheep I've sold you recently, innkeeper? It belonged to the Duke and I need to get it back.
Well, I have a piece of it in the larder, but that probably isn't what you wanted to hear, is it?
Oh, so I'm too late.
I'm sorry, knight. But business is business and good mutton is good mutton...
I've heard that the soldier Jullian has deserted. Do you know where he could be hiding? Have you heard something?

There's quite a lot of talk among the soldiers about Jullian running away from the army. To tell the truth it seems to me that they all would gladly do it. To be honest, their prospects aren't very good. Most likely there are hordes of hellspawns grouping in the Moonshine Mountains to storm the town and there will be only a handful of soldiers from the thinned-down royal regiment standing in their way, along with the small group of town militia. That's why sheriff Contemburry wants to catch him and assess him an exemplary punishment so the others would think better of deserting. But you can only guess where Jullian can be. In my judgment he's headed south. What else should a man do? There's no luck waiting for anyone here.

You ask me if I know something about the death of Kurth Ollmier? My God, how could I know? The terrible murder happened right in my own inn! Ollmier had a room rented here in the attic. He paid well, I've never had any problems with him... and now he's dead.
What can you tell me about Ollmier?

He posed as a merchant, but rather he was an adventurer and a treasure hunter. As far as I can tell, he lived on selling all sorts of things that somebody ordered. They were mainly items from the ages long ago—various artifacts, relics, holy items, books, scrolls, medallions... Treasure hunting paid him quite a lot, at least as far as I can tell.
When did you find Ollmier's body?

It was in the morning, knight. I brought him breakfast every day, but there was an unusual silence in his room. It seemed strange to me, because he used to be an early riser—regardless of how long he was drinking the night before. But I thought he had just slept in and so I went on. I wanted to stand the breakfast next to his bed, but then I saw the havoc and it all fell out of my hands right onto the floor stained with blood. I've never seen so much blood, maybe not even in the slaughterhouse. The merchant lied in the middle of the room, his hands spread wide, his eyes gazing at the ceiling and there was huge pool of drying blood all around him. His throat was cut like he was a hen and in his mouth he had stuffed—god forgive me—his own manhood. I tell you flat, I'm not of a weak nature, but I was put hard to keep my knees from buckling. So I ran straight off to Sheriff Contemburry and told it all to him.
Do you know who was the last person Ollmier spoke to?

I don't remember, knight. He was in the barroom the whole evening—it was very busy there because it was the feast of Saint Hedwig. He had to go away before midnight, because he definitely wasn't among the last patrons I had to kick out after the midnight. He probably went to sleep during the evening not knowing death is waiting for him.
You're welcome, knight. I hope you'll catch those murderers as soon as possible. I'll be much more comfortable when I see their heads on the town gate.
You've surely heard, knight, that the Holy Mother Church condemned gambling as a sin and Kind Edward forbid it by his decree.
Yes, I've heard, but it can be that the Holy Mother Church isn't always right and not every law of the Realm is being adhered to...

In that case you've come to the right place, knight. I'm no criminal or something like that, you know, but here in Hillbrandt gambling is a part of the common life, you see? It offers some diversion and a chance to get some easy money. That's why I offer the game of dice to my patrons.
Wait, knight, don't hurry so much. You would be interested in some gambling, wouldn't you?
And if I did?
No, forget it.
I understand. We won't speak about it anymore. What can I do for you?
Ehm... knight, may I be so bold as to ask you for a little favor?
It depends on what it is...
I'm sorry, but I'm in a hurry. Farewell.
I hate to say it, Truthorn, but if you don't answer me, I'll have you arrested and put into prison. I wonder what would happen with your inn then. And all that because of a single answer.
I don't know what your reluctance to answer my question stems from, Truthorn, but if you think about it, you'll surely find out that your answer wouldn't hurt anyone.
You're a smart businessman. So I can't believe you wouldn't want to answer my question...
The thing is I need to borrow a certain sum of money. I know it sounds weird, we don't know each other, but as they say, asking is free.
Alright, I'll lend you the money. That's no problem. How much do you need?
Alright, here you are.
You'll really lend me the money? Many thanks, knight. I'll never forget it, you can be sure of it!
That's too much. I haven't that much money. But if I manage to raise the amount I'll surely lend the money to you.
I would be very grateful to you, knight. Really a lot!
That's too much, I won't lend you that much money.
It's no go then. Farewell. And sorry for bothering you.
And how would I benefit if I lend you the money, good man?
Well... I'm not sure of that, knight. Maybe you won't. But maybe you'll get the loan back. That's hard to say.
What do you need the money for?
A relative of mine asked me for help. I haven't much myself, so I'm asking around. But I haven't come off so far. The times are too desperate for such business...
It's out of question. I'm sorry.
Never mind. Forgive me for bothering you with that. Farewell.
I'd like to have something to drink, if I may.
And what shall it be, knight? Of course I don't have any sacramental wine, but I do have some beer, wine and mead made according to my own recipe.
In that case fetch me a tankard of beer. The golden beverage will surely refresh me.
You're welcome, knight. Can I do anything else for you?
In that case you surely understand I won't serve you. I'm sorry, but I don't sell on credit. I would be broke quite soon if I did!
I won't refuse a glass of wine, innkeeper.
I'd like to taste your home-made mead.
Here you are. And it's free. Can I do anything else for you?
You want more? As you wish... No offence, but are you really used to drinking so much?
You're welcome, knight. Business is business. Can I do anything else for you?
I'd like your home-made mead.
Well said, knight. Here you are. And it's free. Can I do anything else for you?

Don't be angry with me, knight, but I won't serve you any more drinks. Somebody could accuse me of tempting you to sin. You know how difficult it is these days. Though, could I do anything else for you?
Do you want to start playing straight away or shall I repeat the rules first?
To tell the truth, I don't have even 10 gp.
I'd rather hear the rules again.

It's easy, knight. Every player rolls two dice and the one who scores more wins. You roll first, then I. It's nothing difficult. You may wager 10 gp, 20 gp, 30 gp, 40 gp or 50 gp and you may win the same amount. If we both score the same number, then no one wins and no one loses.
I'm sorry, knight, but I won't play with you anymore. You did me out of quite a lot of money so I'll keep myself away from gambling for some time. Can I do anything else for you?
Let's see what I'll roll... Well, howsoever I count it over and over, I scored $$var:NPCHodil$$
Well... what can we do. Such is the game. Nobody won and nobody lost.
What goods do you sell, innkeeper?

All sorts of wares, knight. Just come into my shop and look for yourself. And I buy all sorts of things too, so if you want to get rid of some spare junk just come to me. You never know who can have some use for that what you don't need.
I'd like to see your wares.
By all means. What do you want to know, knight?

Hello, knight. Welcome to my inn. It's not much, that's true, but then again, it's the best tavern in the town. Maybe mainly because it's the only one, ho, ho. But you'll get here all you could need—from a good drink to every sort of arms and armor. What can I do for you?
How is it possible that there's no better inn here than this one?
Now you've hurt me a little, knight. But to answer your question—no, there's no other inn here. So either take it or leave it, as they say.
Your inn looks as good as any other, innkeeper. You've nothing to be ashamed for.
Well... maybe you're right, knight. Yes, you surely are right! Thanks. What can I do for you?
Welcome, knight. How are you? What do you think of Hillbrandt? Quite a dump, isn't it? But then again, better this subsistence than none. What can I do for you?
I've raised the money you asked me for. Here is 1,000 gold pieces.
Thank you, knight! You really helped me. God bless you! May I serve you somehow in return?
I'm afraid I don't need it anymore. The situation has changed... but thanks anyway for your effort.
Well... as you wish.
May I serve you somehow, knight?

I hear so much gossip about heretics every day that I get an ear-ache, Father. One has bewitched the cow of another so that it has lost milk, someone else bedeviled a neighbor's dog and it died, and another one charmed somebody's spouse so she spreaded her thighs for him... People are so possessed by all that paganism and witchcraft that they don't hesitate to throw dirt on anybody who just slightly displeases them.

It may be that Master d'Arvias is innocent, Father. But it also may be he's guilty. Who could judge it? People say somebody saw him opening the gate for the orcs during their recent assault on the town. But it can be a mistake. Somebody thought he saw Master d'Arvias but in fact it was someone else. But maybe it was really him, how could I know? You're an Inquisitor, you should know better, shouldn't you?

I've heard a lot about the theft of the monstrance, Father. But if I may guess it is just gossip. They say a hellspawn did it after knocking out the priests who prayed for the salvation of the town. He reputedly did it to allow the orcs and other monsters to swiftly conquer the town. And they also say the monstrance was desecrated a long time ago by wicked rites—supposedly it was aspersed and stripped of all its sanctity. But who did it and where the monstrance is now I haven't heard. Quarim, the dwarf-man who's the jack of Raubsticht, our executioner, led the weirdest talk of all. He said he had seen who did it, but nobody believed him. He is too well known for fudging. I remember him running around the town all agog, shouting that a real dragon had broken out of the Dragon rock and that it was flying to the town. People ran away in terror, you should have seen that. But it turned out then that he was only jesting. People almost stoned him because of it.
Eh... yes, Father. Well, in fact no, not anymore, because I promised Bishop Quentinus I wouldn't do it. Instead I raised its price not to lose profit.
Just so, Father. Life's tough...
You're welcome, Father. Do you want to know something else?

I haven't heard anything particular about the disappearance of Baroness van Gallagan, Father. They say people saw her for the last time the day the orcs assaulted the town. The same as Bishop Quentinus. It's probably all over with her already, if I say it frankly. People didn't like her much, you know? She was such a would-be gentlewoman who thought she belonged at least to the royal court of His Majesty King Edward. The biggest loss is for her husband. They say he can't even, well, fulfill his morning errands, without her. With all due respect, of course. I don't want to offend the Baron in any way. I'm sure the gossip is totally untrue.
Thanks, Father. Here's your money. It has been a long time since I offered fresh mutton in my inn!
In that case ask Ruphert the shepherd, Father. He cares for the Duke's herds.
I'm sorry, Father. But business is business and good mutton is good mutton...

Thank you, Father! You really helped me. God bless you! May I serve you somehow in return?

Farewell, knight. And thanks again!

Welcome, knight. My name's Yan Ulbrecht and I'm the new Sheriff of Asherbalt. And I owe it solely to you and none other for that—if you hadn't killed the orc Khan Rashgar and rout those damned green skins, I would never have gotten this chance. Thanks!
You're welcome, Sheriff. There's much hard work awaiting you here...
Yes, you're right. I have to clean out the iron mines of all the green skins that have remained there. But I trust we can do that. Frankly speaking, we won't let Asherbalt be overrun again!
I'm glad to hear that, Sheriff. May I speak with you for a moment?
I'm terribly sorry, knight, but I have much to do... I hope you won't regard it as resisting the Brotherhood of the Righteous if I don't attend to you.
Hmm... in that case farewell, Sheriff.
I'm glad to hear that, Sheriff. Farewell.
Welcome, knight. I'm glad to see you alive and well. Frankly, I need your help. Would you have some spare time?
Sure, what's the matter?

We're trying to clean the iron mines of all sorts of vermin that have wormed their way in there during the last few years, and we have some problems on the third level. It seems some spider monster has nested down there and it kills one man after another. Frankly speaking, I don't know what to do about it and I'm afraid to send more men there. Could you get rid of the monster for us? Of course for a reward!
I knew I could rely on you, knight. The reward will be yours as soon as you kill the spider demon.
I'm sorry, but I've no time for that.
I understand. I won't bother you anymore. Farewell.
I'm sorry, Sheriff. I have an important mission.
Oh... I understand. The administration of justice. I won't bother you anymore. Farewell.
Welcome, knight. May I ask how you fare with the task I've entrusted to you? I don't want to insist, but the lives of my men are at stake...
I'm sorry, but I haven't killed the spider monster yet.
Never mind, knight. You will surely do so soon.
Are you asking me if I've already slain the spider monster that was killing your men in the iron mine? Yes, I've killed it.
Really? That's great news, knight. I knew you would succeed! Thank you, you've saved the lives of many innocent men. Here's your reward—you deserve it!
I'm sorry, but I haven't killed the felonious half-ogre yet.
Are you asking me if I've already slain the evil half-ogre that was ambushing your men on the road to Hillbrandt? Yes, I've killed him.
Really? That's great news, knight! I knew you would succeed! Thanks to you it will be possible to get supplies to Asherbalt safely once again. Here's your reward. You deserve it!
Welcome, knight. Thank you for the help with the spider demon. But frankly, I have a new problem...
What's the matter, Sheriff? I'll gladly help you if it's in my power.

We have problems with supplies. It seems a half-ogre has settled down somewhere on the road to Hillbrandt and now he ambushes the supply wagons and kills their guards. But I'm unable to track him down. Could you take care of him?
Alright, I'll take care of him.
I knew I could rely on you, knight. The reward will be yours as soon as you kill the infernal villain!
I'm sorry to hear that, Sheriff. But I have no time for that at the moment.
