Oh... I understand. Some important matter of the Realm. I won't bother you anymore. Farewell.
Welcome to your domain, noble lord. May I ask how you fare with the task I've entrusted to you? I don't want to insist, but the lives of my men are at stake...
Never mind, noble lord. You will surely do so soon.
Really? That's great news, noble lord. I knew you would succeed! Thank you, you've saved the lives of many innocent men. Here's your reward—you deserve it!
Really? That's great news, noble lord! I knew you would succeed! Thanks to you it will be possible to get supplies to Asherbalt safely once again. Here's your reward. You deserve it!
Welcome to your domain, noble lord. Thank you for the help with the spider demon. But frankly, I have a new trouble...
I knew I could rely on you, noble lord. The reward will be yours as soon as you kill the infernal villain!
Welcome to your domain, noble lord. Thank you for helping me with the half-ogre. Since you've killed him the supplying of Asherbalt has been smooth.
As a ruler of this manor I would like to recruit new soldier, Sheriff.
As you wish, my lord. Do you want archer or swordman?
Swordman.
As you order, my lord!
Archer.
Although this domain belongs to you, noble lord, you don't have the right to search the pockets of people!
I found this gold earring. Do you happen to know who it might belong to?
But that's my earring I lost recently. Yes, it's the one! I've already bemoaned it and now it's back. I was angry with myself for being so careless and losing it. Where did you find it, knight?
Well... That's the thing, good woman. Have you been to Schwarzwald recently?
To Schwarzwald? No, it's been a long time since I was there. Who would dare go there when it's full of witches and all sorts of beasts? Why do you ask?
Because I found that earring of yours in Schwarzwald. Right next to paladin Richwald d'Blazier who was turned into stone!

But I... damned! I ought to have stayed silent about the earring, silly me! If it weren't for that nobody would have gotten to know anything. Why are you staring at me so, knight? Do you want to hear my confession? Alright, I'll tell you! It was I who turned the damned paladin into stone. I had it all prepared so well! I had wanted to ensnare him for a long time then—he was the second son of Duke Hyrrmann of Candra, a great opportunity for a poor girl to better herself. I just had to brew a magic potion and give it to him!
What?! You tried to seduce a paladin by means of dark magic? That's heresy!

Name it anyway you want. I think it's just another way to success and it's as good as any. Maybe even better. Wouldn't you want to be able to speak with the dead? To wade through the morning dew with the dryads? To have a good time in a wild whirl with demons as horny as stallions? Don't tell me you wouldn't, knight—you would lie to yourself. And I can do all of that. With the help of the book that has fallen into my hands by a lucky coincidence. My granny didn't know what a treasure she gave me when she taught me how to read when I was a young girl. They all laughed at me and said it would be as worthy for a poor girl as a shoe for a dead mare, but I knew it would bring me luck. And it really did!
What demonic book are you speaking about, sinner?

I speak about Libre Necronomicon, the book of the knowledge of the dead. It has opened the door to the world of the forbidden—but effective—wonders and miracles for me. It helped me to prepare the magic potion that was to win me the love of Richwald d'Blazier. And it helped me to change the paladin into stone when he slipped away from my web. It's a shame, but what could I do? Next time I'll be more cautious.
There will be no next time! I'll take care that you'll be rightly punished for your sins!
Hardly, knight. As a corpse you won't be able to do much. Unless I summon you back as my slave! My loyal servants, kill him!
Is it true you flirted with the paladin Richwald d'Blazier? And that he dismissed you because of some witch from Schwarzwald?

I flirted with the paladin Richwald d'Blazier? Who told you that? It's a blatant lie! I don't deny I liked the paladin, but I would never flirt with anyone who had made a vow of chastity. How would I benefit from that as a woman? No matter who told you that disgusting slander, he only wanted to discredit me!

Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert as the royal governor of the city. The vice-governor is Duchess Vanessa of Kenthworth. The Grand Duke is quite a classy man, but his wife is naughty—at least people say so. They say she cheats on him at every turn, but he doesn't believe that and regards his wife as a saint. And with respect to Vanessa of Kenthworth—she had to get to her office through someone's bed too, because the only thing that she really cares about is her appearance...

By my troth, Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is a heretic and a traitor, knight. All people say that—he betrayed God and started to worship Satan. Now he bows before his images and spits in the face of God! I shudder to think of what else the future will bring. Who can we trust when even the highest superior of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is a heretic?

I don't want to do harm to anyone, but I feel the innkeeper Salena Flock is the mysterious heretic who lets the werewolves into the town at each full moon. That's because I've heard weird things... They say her husband has changed into a werewolf! And Archbishop Laurencius preached that when a man has sinned, everyone in his house has sinned too. So I'd bet it's her who opens the city gates to the werewolves...

I've heard that the paladins from the Brotherhood of the Righteous are in mourning. Master Konrad von Thaum died. He was a longtime fighter against evil and an enemy of all the hellspawns. People say he fell in a battle when he along with a handful of the faithful attempted to seize the werewolf den in Schwarzwald. And the disaster is all the more grave now that his famous Decapitator sword has fallen into the hands of enemies because of that. It's a holy relic of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
I don't know anything about the murder of the paladin Richwald d'Blazier, I'm sorry. And why should I know? I'm just a common stallholder, not an inquisitor or a knight...
I search for the missing Ron Burton. Do you happen to know anything about him?

I haven't heard of Ron Burton for some time, that's true, although we used to see each other quite often because he was buying goods from me for the inn he owns together with his brother William. To tell the truth they had quite a lot of feuds between themselves because each of them envisioned the inn going another direction. I wouldn't be surprised if his brother were behind his disappearance—after all he would get the whole inn then, wouldn't he?!

Priest Nicolas may say whatever he wants, but until he delivers some evidence the Grand Duchess is lying he's practically in jail already—whatever the truth may be. I would say he didn't even touch the Grand Duchess and the harlot has made it up because of her injured vanity. People say she fornicates at every turn and someone reputedly saw her by the side of the priest Marcius, the archiepiscopal clerk and limner. So I can imagine she wanted to seduce even the innocent Father Nicolas, but he refused her and so she accused him of witchcraft and of rape.

Have you heard the legend about the treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn? It's a very gloomy tale, although it concerns a magic treasure. Baron Decard of Longhorn was a famous collector of all sorts of relics and artifacts, mostly from ages long past. But later on his collector's zeal started to become an obsession and the Baron wanted more and more. So he sold himself to dark powers and with their help he started to steal, deceive, rob and even to murder to get possession of some or other rare items.

But after he tried to rob Bishop Benedictius, he ended up in the hands of the Inquisition. When put to torture he confessed to all his crimes—and with quite a lot of pride—but even the inquisitors didn't manage to get him to reveal where he hid his raked up treasure. He was executed in the year of 1210 and although many people have tried to find his treasure since then, none has succeeded.
Don't oppose me, good woman, or you'll bring my anger upon yourself! Answer me at once!
Maybe you don't like me, good woman. All the same I'm sincerely asking you—answer my question, please.
You're beautiful and clever, Sandra. Your answer would help me a lot. Please, answer me.

Hello, knight. I haven't seen you around before. You're new in the city, aren't you? You must be, because I would know you if you weren't. I know almost all around here. My name's Sandra Ullmann, but you may call me just Sandra.
Nice to meet you, good woman. You're a stallholder, aren't you?

Exactly, knight. It's quite obvious from looking at me, isn't it? And how couldn't it be so, when I'm sitting in the square at a stall, speaking with passersby and flapping my lips. But it's an honest business in the fresh air, one meets a lot of people and all. I would be better if I was a Grand Duchess or at least a Duchess or Baroness though, but when a girl is born among the poor people she has to draw in her horns. But who knows, maybe a rich knight will notice me and I'll live happily ever after.
Yes, it's possible. The ways of our Lord are beyond our comprehension...

I think so too, knight. I've known a miller, she was such a plump girl with a blushed face, no pretty lady at all. And she boasted she would become a Baroness. And it happened exactly as she said. Before a year passed by I saw her at the fair with a butler and a servant girl. So I think that something like that may happen also to me.
Yes, it certainly is possible. May I ask you several questions now?
Sure, knight. Ask whatever you want.
I doubt that, good woman. You're too low-born to be a good match for a noble.
Oh... you savage! Just wait and see! You'll be surprised what a match I will be!
Maybe. But now I need you to answer several of my questions.
You want to ask me questions? Well, as you wish. So ask away.
I'm sorry, I didn't want to hurt you. I just expressed my opinion about how it usually works in our society.
It may work in that way, but there are exceptions. And I'll be one of them. Bet on that!
If you think so... May I ask you some questions now?
You want to ask me questions? Well, as you wish. So ask away, knight.
Well... I had better be going. Farewell.
It's none of your business who I am. I want to ask you several questions.

Yes, you're right, it's none of my business. After all, it's never wise to meddle with the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I only wanted to be nice to you, that's all. I hope you took no offense. And I'll gladly answer your questions, be sure of it
I'm glad to meet you, good woman. But I'll have to go. Farewell.

You're already leaving, knight? Why, we've hardly exchanged greetings. But as you wish. The truth is the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous have a lot of work these days. The Realm is falling apart so quickly that one's mind boggles at it. One would say people can't be like that, can they? Well, it seems I'm talking too much again. Farewell, knight.
Hello, knight. It is nice cloudy weather today, isn't it? I don't remember when the last time the sky was clear. But it surely will get better. What can I do for you?
Can you answer me some questions, please?
Certainly, knight, ask away. What do you want to know?
Well... in fact nothing. I was just passing by. Farewell.

You want to go already? Why, we've hardy exchanged a few words... But as you wish, you surely have a lot of things to do. Farewell, then. Surely we will meet again when you're passing by some next time.
But that's my earring I lost recently. Yes, it's the one! I've already bemoaned it and now it's back. I was angry with myself for being so careless and losing it. Where did you find it, Father?

I'm afraid that it was not enough...
Well... I need various herbs for my work that grow in the strangest places—for example in Schwarzwald. So what do you think I'm doing here?!
You're collecting some herbs, aren't you?
You're so clever, knight. Only rarely have I the honor to meet someone so sharp. Yes, it's exactly as you said—I'm gathering herbs. So if I may...
And may I ask you what herbs do you collect? To tell the truth I'm just searching for a herb.

You are into herbs? You've taken me by surprise a little... But after all why a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous couldn't cull herbs? Well, just to inform you, I was lucky today and I found some Trollus Bilealius, popularly called the troll bile. It's a very rare herb growing only in several places in the Realm these times and you hardly manage to find it more often than once in a few years...
The troll bile? But that's exactly the herb I need!
Really? Well... I'm REALLY sorry for that, but you'll have to find another one—if there is another one, and I doubt that. Otherwise you'll have to wait several years...
Please, good woman, give me the herb. I need it for a certain damsel in distress...
Although I'm not surprised a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous speaks about a damsel in distress, I must assure you, knight, that your damsel means absolutely nothing to me!
I'll buy the herb from you, good woman. Ask your price.
This herb is NOT for sale, knight. It's so rare that no money can buy it. I'm sorry.
I want the herb, good woman. And if I have to, I'll get it even by force. It would be enough to accuse you of witchcraft—maybe you want to practice some unclean rites with the herb...
That's ridiculous...
I wouldn't say so. Heresy is a very serious crime. So, will you give me the herb or not?!
You... you call yourself a God's knight?! You're worse than all the footpads and brigands altogether. May the plague get you! I'll remember this! Here is the herb and may you choke to death with it!
I'm glad we came to agreement by fair means. Farewell.
Hmm... alright. Keep the herb. Maybe I'll find another one...
That's a wise decision, knight. Farewell, I must go now. The way home is long... as the song says.
Welcome, good woman. May I ask you what you are doing in such a dangerous place?
It is you, knight! Well, I don't know if it's any of your business, but as you surely know, I'm an apothecary. I think I've suggested enough by that for you to guess what I'm doing here, haven't I?
Welcome, good woman. May I ask you who you are and what you are doing in such a dangerous place?
I don't know if it's any of your business, but my name's Thelma Ulthraum and I'm an apothecary. I think I've suggested enough by that for you to guess what I'm doing here, haven't I?

Do you know how someone's memory could be restored?

To improve someone's memory? Well, well, well, knight. Ain't the good old rack painful enough anymore? Maybe there is someone who can't recall his crimes even if you're crushing his fingers in a thumbscrew, right? Maybe even treating one's head in a skull-crusher can't help. Well, I'm quite surprised by that. I've always thought that paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous know the best ways how to improve one's memory...

All right, all right... something for restoring memory? Hmmm... you know what, knight, that's a tough one. Memory's not body—you can't cheat it that easily. Well, I could know a way. It's an ancient recipe—if I brew a potion according to it, it might be able to help. The problem is that the ingredients I need are rather rare.
What ingredients are you talking about?

To brew the potion I need some root of Memoricus Repeaticus—it's a rare herb, and also some powdered Moon Crystal. I don't know how proficient you are in alchemical ingredients, knight, but both the ingredients are really unique. I've not seen any Memoricus Repeaticus root for years.
If I get you the ingredients, will you make the potion for me?
Hmm... yes, I guess I could. Of course, you'll have to pay me—let's say 2,500 gp. I'm not exactly a charitable person.
I'm looking for a way to remove a stryx curse. Could you help me with that?

You mean the cursed girl Joan, right? These days there are not many people who would be trying to save possessed and cursed people without the help of a burning stake... Guess you know that better than me, right? Nevertheless as regards that problem with Joan. As you've correctly said, she's a stryx. A cursed child which became a terrifying unstoppable monster after years spent in the Netherworld. Regardless what people say, there's a cure. In fact she's still a child, although grossly disfigured in her present state due to the powerful curse of her mad mother—may God be merciful to her soul. To remove the curse you must do two things. First, you must consecrate the grave of Joan's mother and then you must force Joan to drink a vial of blood of her father who was the reason for the curse to be cast.
Thank you, good woman.

You've talked to Salena Flock, haven't you? Not a long time ago she came to ask me to brew her a potion which would cure lycantrophy. So I told her to get lost. I told her honestly that the only cure for lycantrophy is to crush the afflicted's skull. Otherwise you can't be sure that the afflicted won't relapse next full moon...
So you think that there's no cure for lycantrophy? It's a disease, isn't it? So there must be something...
Of course there is, but I'm not gonna waste any time with that. I have more important things to do than to cure hellspawns!
I really do need your help, good woman. Name your price.

Talking business, right? Well, why not... If you give me 1,000 gp I'll brew you a potion that MIGHT help. Nevertheless I need one more ingredient for it which I don't have in stock right now. It's the root of Wolverus Baenaesius, common people call the herb Wolfbane. If you bring me some, I'll brew the potion for you. It's a must.
I have both the herb and the money, good woman. You can start to brew it right now.
You've surprised me, knight. Well, it's your decision—I'll brew the potion for you. Just wait a moment.
Of course...
Well, here you go, knight. It's still boiling, be careful not to scald yourself. The afflicted must drink the potion, that's all. It'll hurt him a bit then, but there's nothing I can do about that.

Well, you should carefully observe the afflicted to see if the changes didn't go too far. In case they did you'll be talking to a lycanthrope and not to a human being. Guess you'd have a hard time convincing a lycanthrope to drink a potion that MIGHT turn him into human again... Well, you'd probably have to overpower him and force him to drink it!
Very well, when I have the herb and the money I will come to you.
I need your help and I'll get it regardless of your willingness, understood?!

No, I don't understand. On the other hand it's you who should understand that threatening me because of some hellspawn is not a wise idea. It is a rather tricky problem, knight. Someone could even say that it's cooperation with infernal powers...
I have the Wolfbane root as we've agreed. And here's the money.

So, you're asking me if I can brew you an elixir from the Devil's Root, right? Well, of course I can, knight. It's not very difficult if you know how. The difficult part is to find some Devil's Root. It usually grows at rather dangerous places—hence the name. If you find a Devil's Root, I can make you a magic elixir of it for a few gold coins.
What do I think about all that mess? Hmm... as an apothecary I'd say that a cure's gonna be damn hard to find...

I've heard some rumors that a war might be coming. It means for me, as for an apothecary, that I'll have to start an infirmary here and that I'll have to treat the wounded and dying. Almost everywhere there will be bodies of crippled soldiers who'd not hesitate to get themselves mutilated for the divine truth. I must tell you, knight, that war is the worst thing man ever invented...

Mysterious Voices

Aaaaaaaaarghhhhhhh, finally free! After so many years of agonizing waiting we're finally free! The time has come for those pitiful citizens of Hillbrandt to pay for what they did to us. What... what are you talking about?

You fool! Have you really thought you'll make us face divine justice by blessing the stone? To get to Purgatory? Fool! You only opened the way for us by blessing the cursed stone—the holy water forced us out of it. Now we'll be able to deal with the townsfolk. They got us when we lived, but they won't stand a chance against us when we're dead. The hour of revenge is upon us. You, fool, will be the first to die!
Stop, please, oh, wanderer... Please, hear our plea... hear us... Don't let our wandering souls to be forever damned to suffer... hear us, please...
By all the Saints, who are you! Wherefrom are you talking to me?

We're the lost souls trapped inside this cursed stone... We've not been allowed to rest in peace as our bodies were not properly buried in holy ground... Instead, our bodies were either thrown into nameless graves or just left to rot in the sun where ravens could feast on them... Please, free use, wanderer... We're longing to get to Purgatory and to find eternal peace... Bless this stone and end our eternal torment. Just sprinkle the stone with holy water and we'll be free... Please, hear the plea of the lost souls, wanderer, whoever you might be...
Very well, I'll help you. I'll get some holy water and I'll bless this stone so you could leave it to face divine justice.
Thank you, wanderer... Thank you...

Very well, I'll help you. By a lucky coincidence I have a flask of holy water on me. I bless this stone in the name of God Almighty, of the Archangel Gabriel and of the First Prophet. May all the souls trapped within be released and may it never bind another lost soul and prevent it from facing divine justice!
If I help you, what kind of gratitude I could expect?
We know a place where a treasure of gold and magic items is buried... Free us and we'll reveal the place to you and you'll be rich as a king!
If it's God's will you should suffer inside this piece of rock then I cannot interfere with His sentence!
Wait, don't leave... don't leave... aaaaaarghhhhhhh!!! May thousand curses strike you down! May your legs rot and may your throat be drowned in bile, you bloody bastard!
I don't believe you! I was warned not to come near this cursed stone. I won't listen to the temptations of the lost souls punished by God Himself for their crimes!

Aaaaaarghhhhhhh!!! May thousand curses strike you down! May your legs rot and may your throat be drowned in bile, you bloody bastard! We wish your mother was cut to pieces with a rusty saw the day you were conceived!

No, on the contrary. I was warned not to come near this cursed stone. I won't succumb to the temptations of the lost souls punished by God Himself for their crimes!
Bishop Vallarian, I hereby arrest you on the basis of reasonable suspicion of conspiracy against God and the King.

But quite on the contrary... you started to pursue my track.
So, is it all true? Was it really you who had planned all the crimes that Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann committed?

Crimes? No, my son, those were not crimes. It was my mission! You have no idea what's drawing near. I guess you think that my arrest and execution will end everything. Well, you're wrong. I've unleashed powers undreamt of. Everything has been done already and there's nothing you can do about it now.
No, it is you who is wrong, Your Honor. I know everything about your plans!

No, my son. You're wrong here. Do you really think Baroness Linda van Gallagan and that simpleton Sam Riemann told you anything important? I must disappoint you. They knew nothing. They were so blinded with their own opportunism and by those petty visions of theirs that I could easily convince them to believe anything I saw fit. They accepted everything and obeyed all my commands without hesitation. They murdered Kurth Ollmier because he had Libre Daemonium on him and I needed the book to perform the Rite of Summoning. They poisoned Baroness Gwenn von Weill because I needed her body. And finally, in their rapacity they helped me to celebrate the Black Mass and to summon the Fallen Angel Arthamon. Those fools thought they'd rule the world with his help, committing all kinds of perverse atrocities. How childish!
What's that book about, that Libre Daemonium? What infernal issues are discussed in it?

My dear son, Libre Daemonium is holding the secret of the Rite of Summoning which would allow the Fallen Angels to enter our world. It seemed irrecoverably lost, but I managed to get it in the end! That fool Kurth Ollmier agreed to sell it to me—he had no idea what a treasure he had found. Well, it was the book which made me realize I needed a corpse of an innocent girl which had been buried in the holy ground for thirteen days to summon the Fallen Angel Arthamon.
Where is Libre Daemonium now? What did you do with it?
I won't tell you that, my dear son. Some secrets are better left to be taken to the grave!
Why did you want to get rid of Edmond d'Arvias by falsely accusing him of heresy? Was he going to reveal the track of Linda van Gallagan?

Exactly, my son. When I found out that Bishop Quentinus had seen us taking away the body of Gwenn von Weill from the graveyard and that he had told Edmond d'Arvias about that I realized that I had to act quickly. We deceitfully lured d'Arvias out of town and then put him into a deep slumber by the means of dark magic. Then we took his sword which helped us create the Master's evil twin which looked exactly like him. We then let the creature return to town and ordered it to be seen by the people of Hillbrandt opening the gate to the orcs. Then it was not very difficult to let enough evidence of his heresy be gathered. I thought there would be nothing preventing the fool from being burnt to death as a heretic at the stake. Wouldn't it be a nice irony? A great hunter of heretics burnt for heresy. Ha!
Why did I got involved?

It was him who defiled the rest of the dead and brought them back to life. And it will be him who will soon contribute to the utter ruination of the Kingdom of God on Earth, as you mortals call it. What are you talking about? What should happen?
You're soon going to find out, my dearest son. Soon indeed!

As it seems I'm not going to have a chance to amend my mistakes in this life. I'm your prisoner, my son. Don't be too joyous about your victory, though. Remember that soon the day will come when the New Order will be born and its Children will rule the world! You cannot do anything to prevent it. The wheels have been set to motion and there's nothing anybody can do about it now. It was foretold a long time ago and now it's coming true!
As I've told you, my son. Remember my last words as everything's going to happen soon. My death won't change a thing. On the contrary—I'll prevail!
Not in this round, bishop. For an assault on a member of the Holy Inquisition I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!
No, that's you who's wrong, Your Honor. I know everything about your plans!

No, my son, I'm not going anywhere with you. On the contrary, it's you who's going to embark on a rather long journey. Did you think I was telling you all of that so that you could use it against me in a trial? Once again, you're wrong. As I've already told you, I was surprised by the success of your investigation and so I wanted to allow you to feel the joy any investigator feels when he manages to reveal a crime. Well, but that's all I wanted you to achieve. Nobody will ever know about our discussion and I doubt someone will ever find your corpse. I'll return to Hillbrandt to take back my office from Jeremiah and I'll keep waiting for the day when the New Order will rise and when its Children will rule the world. Kill him, my undead servants! KILL HIM!!!

ENOUGH! I surrender, my son. I'd have never thought you'd be able to develop your abilities to such an extent! Now I'm really sorry that I... that I underestimated you and tried to deceive you instead of persuading you to join our cause. As it seems I'm not going to have a chance to amend my mistakes in this life. I'm your prisoner, my son. Don't be too joyous about your victory, though. Remember that soon the day will come when the New Order will be born and its Children will rule the world! You cannot do anything to prevent it. The wheels have been set to motion and there's nothing anybody can do about it now. It was foretold a long time ago and now it's coming true!
Not in this round, Bishop. For an assault on member of the nobility I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go!
What can be used as evidence in an inquisitorial trial?

You can use anything that could help to clarify the case and that is directly connected to a fact or a person. Usually it's the testimony of the accused or of witnesses, examination, objects and documents related to the given case... Nevertheless it can also be your logical deduction if you manage to connect several appropriate clues and information in such a way that they prove a certain fact.
What must I do to arrest a suspect?

You can arrest only a person accused of heresy by an inquisitorial prosecutor. The accusation against a suspect can be brought only after the prosecutor is provided with sufficient evidence. We have only one inquisitorial prosecutor here in Hillbrandt—he's Father Jeremiah. You'll have to cooperate with him very closely. Seek him out and he'll tell you all the details.
When is it possible to sentence a person accused of heresy?

Final judgment can only be passed when the indicted is accused of heresy and he's proven guilty beyond doubt. In fact it means you need to acquire a sufficient number of proofs which will be used by the court to find the accused guilty.
What do you think about the crisis the Realm has been dragged into, Your Honor?

In my opinion, the situation we're in is the most difficult test God has ever decided to bestow upon us. It might seem it's no wonder that heresy has been spreading vividly in recent years as there's despair and doom all around us. Nevertheless, that's exactly the difficulty of that test, my son. We must carry on till everything turns to good. We must keep the faith without a single stain. We must not allow anyone to doubt it, let alone to dispute it or avoid it. All who have gone astray must be put into the hands of divine justice—and you too may help to accomplish that, my son!
What monsters have you met here in Hillbrandt, Your Honor?

According to the testimonies of eyewitnesses there are monsters, scamps, demons, apparitions and hellspawns galore, my son. I've personally met only orcs and giant bats. Nevertheless there are rumors about much worse monsters; about half-ogres with bodies as big as boulders, about trolls with skin of stone, about giant spiders with mandibles as big as sickles... It's hard to tell what is truth and what is just a superstition. Nevertheless the amount of hellspawns in the area is much higher than I originally expected. I'm afraid of the days to come, my son. That few soldiers who have no hope of being reinforced can't protect us against grave dangers that we'll certainly face—especially not against the orcs.
Has anything unusual happened during your stay in Hillbrandt?

I've seen many things during my long life in the Kingdom of God on Earth, my son. I've been tracking Satan and his lackeys all my life and since the day I was appointed inquisitorial judge I've faced the most heinous of crimes so many times that I almost lost my faith. Nevertheless that what I found here surpassed all my expectations—and my worries! Heresy of the worst kind infiltrated the highest ranks of the Realm. That's why we must act, my son, very quickly. Outside the walls there are legions of monsters mustering in dark holes to be led by those false idol worshippers against us—the faithful. Evil must be uprooted and burned to the ground!
What do you know about the Fallen Angel Arthamon, Your Honor?

The Fallen Angel Arthamon is a being mentioned in the Holy Scripture. He's one of the Fallen Angels who together with Satan was thrown down from the Kingdom of Heaven for their sins and for the crimes against God. For all that they must suffer in Hell wherefrom no escape is possible. Thus they at least try to ensnare people by tempting them with all the forbidden pleasures those who are weak in faith can imagine. Arthamon is Lord of Fire and Master of Despair. He's often depicted as an all-destroying flame, which is also the form he uses when entering bad dreams and unholy visions. He symbolizes the destructive power of the utter destruction, the end of all.
Do you think Arthamon could have been summoned?

To be honest I refuse to believe that any heretic group would be able to bring any of the Fallen Angels into our world—it'd be a negation of everything the Kingdom of God on Earth is built upon. Nevertheless it's quite likely heretics could be able to summon some of the Arthamon's infernal lackeys. Moreover it's possible they consider that lesser demon to be Arthamon himself. In the pantheon of the infernal beings there's quite a number of lesser demons that can be easily confused with Arthamon. The Fallen Angels themselves cannot enter our world as the shield of the true faith prevents them from doing so! Thus you can calm down, my son. Next time, don't let yourself be provoked to jump to conclusions.

No, my son, I don't know anything. The entire affair is strange indeed, though based on the experience I've gained in the service to God I suppose the Bishop is with our Lord now. I'm praying for the salvation of his soul. I know that he was a pious man and thus I hope God will mercifully accept him even though he was not buried in holy ground but torn to pieces by hellspawns instead.
Why do you think he was torn to pieces?

Because I've seen what those Beelzebubs can do to a man, my son! It took us all day to carry off the pieces of people out of the town after that attack of theirs. Keep in mind that there were only several dozens of them in that attack! Can you imagine what an army it would be if there were thousand of them marching out from the iron mines, all iron-clad, all wielding swords and shields?! It'd be the final end of Hillbrandt!

Unfortunately I don't know anything about Paul Hammerhand and his fate. I'm sure that if something happened to him, it was a divine punishment for the terrible life the young soul led. By what I've heard about him, he was a very nasty boy. He was stealing, lying, cheating, he didn't go to church and he refused sacraments. No wonder he met such a grim fate.
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of Linda van Gallagan?

It seems Linda van Gallagan disappeared during the recent attack of the orcs against the town. It's a tragedy that such a wise and selfless noblewoman who was so important for the town mysteriously disappeared. I'm praying for the salvation of her soul—I keep hope that one day she'll return to us. It's just another proof of terrible crimes committed by Master Edmond d'Arvias on the innocent people of Hillbrandt!

What?! You're looking for the sword of Master d'Arvias? That's alarming... Well, perhaps you're led by a noble notion to reveal the perpetrator of the theft. Nevertheless whoever the thief might be, don't forget that Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of heresy and your task is to acquire enough evidence against him so we could put him on trial!

No doubt it's a great tragedy. Nevertheless it's clear beyond doubt that it's not an ecclesial crime but a secular one and thus it's in the jurisdiction of Grand Duke Weinberg. That's why I'm not going to do anything about it.
Do you happen to have any idea, Your Honor, where the soldier Jullian could be hiding?

No, son, I indeed don't have any idea. It's a military disciplinary matter, my son, and thus it's fully in the jurisdiction of Sheriff Contemburry—of course if it's not found out that Jullian committed an ecclesial crime.
Do you happen to know, Your Honor, how to remove a bewitchment from a man?

Bewitchment, you say? Hmmm... I've met with real bewitchment only once in my life. It was a terrible case... the body of that poor guy got covered with festering ulcers and suddenly he got a fever. There wasn't anything that could have been done for him and he died suffering. I managed to apprehend the perpetrator after some time—it was too late though. That's why I don't have any idea how a bewitchment could be removed or disrupted. I'm sorry.

I would say so, my son. The locals are rather prone to rumors and superstitions of all kinds. It's probably caused by the lower level of education, by more simple conditions and last but not least also by a certain amount of barbarism which was inherited from the ancestors of these people. Did you know, my son, that during the Barbarian Wars many tribesmen from the Icy Plains settled here and were assimilated by the locals after some time? After all, it'd explain many strange traditions of these people which sometimes border on idolatry and heresy. If you'd like to know some of the legends regarding this region, ask the locals. I'm sure they'd be glad to tell them to you anytime.
I feel rather embarrassed, Your Honor, nevertheless I must ask you: What were you doing in the morning after that terrible storm struck Hillbrandt?
Why do you need to know it, my son?
Because the shepherd Ruphert testified he saw you early in the morning—according to his testimony you entered the town and threw something into the garbage heap...

Did he?! I'm very glad that you're pursuing your mission so studiously, investigating each and every trace. Then know that I really was in the country the night the storm struck the town. I had to investigate some traces regarding local crimes. The night caught me when I was still far from the town and thus I had to stay overnight in the open. I spent all that mayhem sitting under an old patulous spruce, absorbed deep in my prayers. I returned to town early in the morning—it was still almost dark. And the thing Ruphert saw me throwing away was a pair of my travel gloves which got torn beyond repair when I had fallen on the rocky way.
Hmmm... the shepherd Ruphert stated that he did not find gloves but a lavishly decorated dagger hilt.

My son, the shepherd Ruphert must have been mistaken. His sight is very poor and I doubt that he would be able to see anything smaller than his sheep if he were farther than ten yards from it. And even though he found a dagger there, it certainly wasn't mine. Are you satisfied, my son?
Yes, Your Honor, please accept my apology.
I don't know, Your Honor... there's something amiss.
Well, then go ask Ruphert about his eyesight yourself. You'll see!

Baroness Linda van Gallagan confessed to her sins before she died and testified that she killed the merchant Kurth Ollmier and Baroness Gwenn von Weill. She also testified that she stole her body from the cemetery and partook in a Black Sabbath at which the Fallen Angel Arthamon was supposedly summoned. Moreover she stated that it was you who planned and carefully prepared the crime. What do you think about her accusation, Your Honor?

That's absurd! I'm sure that Edmond d'Arvias is somehow involved. He must have seduced her and defiled her with sin! There's no doubt he ordered her to commit all those heinous crimes. Perhaps that devil d'Arvias confused her into believing that he's me. A disgusting case of witchcraft indeed! Nevertheless don't let yourself be confused. Heretics are ready to lie even at the moment of their death to lead us astray! We must adhere to facts and our judgment!

Sam Riemann came with a heinous accusation before he died, Your Honor. When I came to arrest him on the basis of the testimony of Linda van Gallagan, he defiantly confessed to his crimes and stated that it was you who prepared the ceremony for the supposed summoning of the Fallen Angel Arthamon...

It must be a conspiracy, my son! There's no doubt about it. I firmly believe that Edmond d'Arvias is behind all that. He's laughing in our faces while dark clouds are gathering around us. We must make sure the truth is revealed as soon as possible. Investigate with caution, but swiftly, my son. Evidence must be found and evil punished. What's worse we can't be sure what powers Edmond d'Arvias really controls. It seems that both Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann were sure it was me who was behind the crimes they committed. There's no doubt Edmond d'Arvias deceived them with infernal charms which they believed to be real.
I've heard there was a savage storm raging over Hillbrandt not a long time ago. Supposedly there were demons dancing in the sky. What do you think about it?

I'd hate to ridicule the locals, my son, but their knowledge of natural processes is rather insufficient and their ignorance and fear makes them explain natural processes by the presence of supernatural powers. I observed the foul weather myself from a rather close proximity and I must agree that the storm was frightening indeed, nevertheless I must confess that I didn't see any demons or unclean spirits prancing in the sky. I can confirm though that the clouds being lit by numerous bolts of lightning from various directions were looking rather infernal. Nevertheless if I should see a manifestation of infernal powers in an ordinary storm I'd not help the Holy Office too much in its difficult mission.
I found a place not far from Dragon Rock where a Dark Sabbath probably took place...
Yes, Your Honor. There's no doubt about it. I found a large blood-drawn ritual circle on the ground with a body of a dead girl in the middle—it was significantly decayed already...

Hmm... scary indeed. That what you describe is really a typical heretic mass which I've encountered several times during my service in the Holy Inquisition. Heretics believe they can summon infernal demons into our world by such means. It's a really alarming discovery. I'm sure Master Edmond d'Arvias attempted to summon some infernal beings at that place. You should conclude your investigation quickly, my dear son, so we can stop that wicked heretic once and for all!
Yes, Your Honor. There's no doubt about it. I found a large blood-drawn ritual circle on the ground with the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill in the middle—it was significantly decayed already.

Hmm... scary indeed. That what you describe is really a typical heretic mass which I've encountered several times during my service in the Holy Inquisition. Heretics believe they can summon infernal demons into our world by such means. It's a really alarming discovery. I'm sure Master Edmond d'Arvias attempted to summon some infernal beings at that place. You should conclude your investigation quickly, my dear son. Time is our enemy!

Yes, Your Honor. There's no doubt about it. I found a large blood-drawn ritual circle on the ground with the body of Baroness Gwenn von Weill in the middle—it was significantly decayed already. Bishop Quentinus supposes that something hatched from the body in the course of the ritual...

Hmm... scary indeed. That what you describe is really a typical heretic mass which I've encountered several times during my service in the Holy Inquisition. Heretics believe they can summon infernal demons into our world by such means... And it seems they succeeded here in Hillbrandt—of course if Bishop Quentinus isn't mistaken. Anyway, it's obvious that Edmond d'Arvias is even more dangerous than I originally thought. You must conclude the investigation as soon as possible, my son. No matter the cost. Time is our worst enemy now. Only God knows what infernal powers d'Arvias has summoned to aid him!
I spoke with Master Edmond d'Arvias, Your Honor. He asserts that he's innocent and that he's been a victim of a heretical conspiracy led by Baroness Linda van Gallagan.

That godless heretic! He's trying to avoid justice and he doesn't hesitate to utter the most terrible lies offending Our Lord Himself. The blood of those who died in the attack of the green skins is on his hands! How could he be a victim of a conspiracy when people saw him opening the gate for the orcs? And how could Baroness Linda van Gallagan be the perpetrator of the conspiracy? She's just a tender and defenseless woman! No, my dearest son, we must not be lead astray by the confusing lies of Master Edmond d'Arvias. Beware of him—he mustn't be allowed to lead you astray!

The death of Kurth Ollmier saddened me greatly, dear son. Well, not that I'd be sad he lost his miserable life. The Holy Office itself was interested in him. That is, we suspected him of heresy. And if not of heresy then of helping it—which is in fact the same.
What was the basis for the suspicion?

His business, my son. He pretended to be a merchant, nevertheless he didn't deal in anything you could buy normally. He specialized in items from the ancient times. Especially in those coming from the age of Ereborn, but also from many others, even older, pagan times. It is still not known exactly how he was able to acquire them. Nevertheless it's likely that he had black market connections or that he himself scavenged certain sites rich with remnants of those pagan realms. That's the reason the Holy Office became interested in him. There was a suspicion that he also dealt in heretical and other blasphemous items which offend God Himself by besmirching His name. I'm really sorry he fell victim to an assassin before I could ask him a few questions. With the help of the rack, of course.
Thank you, Your Honor, that's all. I'll start my investigation.
That's all for now, Your Honor. Farewell.

Wait a moment, my dear son. To pursue your investigation you'll need a bit more appropriate equipment. Keep in mind that from now on you'll be exposed to many a danger, thus you should be well prepared to face them. Here's a pouch of gold—it should be enough to buy basic equipment. Take my advice—use the money wisely!
So little? I'd expect more considering all the dangers you've just mentioned.

Be modest, my son. As a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous you should be meek and modest, same as a cleric should. Now go, you have a difficult task ahead and it's absolutely necessary for you to start your investigation as soon as possible.
Thank you, Your Honor. Do you happen to know if there're some opportunities to get some additional funds in Hillbrandt?

Remember, my son, that modesty is a virtue! Nevertheless I'm sure there are some plausible opportunities you can make use of during your investigation. Ask in town, I'm sure you'll find something appropriate. Nevertheless you certainly should not let yourself be distracted from your primary objective!
Thanks, Your Honor. Farewell.

To be honest, at first I wasn't too glad you would arrive here in Hillbrandt. The Holy Office is able to take care of the matters of heresy by itself, even here in this Godforsaken part of the Realm. But then I decided I could use your services. It would be a nice proof that the Holy Office has no secret before the Brotherhood of the Righteous and is able to cooperate with it. And it seems that we will be rather busy here. I was sent here together with my brothers by the Glatzburg Curial Inquisitor Truncquillius to investigate the local crimes. We arrived just after snow thawed and the roads became at least a little bit passable. Immediately after our arrival I realized that the town was in grave danger and that there wasn't any time to waste.
How is it possible? What happened?

It's obvious that somebody has been invoking dark powers, my son. Some perverse heretics are trying to destroy that what was firm for centuries. There's been evil gathering around the town and it doesn't seem it would be willing to back off. Someone's been attracting, luring and encouraging it. Only God can know the plans of those heretics—anyway, I'm sure that it won't be anything good!
Well, what happened in Hillbrandt anyway?

Monsters came, my son. Infernal creatures known only from the worst nightmares. Hideous hellspawns crawling from the deepest holes on the surface, spinning their dark webs around the town. At first only cattle from the pastures occasionally went missing. Then people who were unlucky enough to stay outside the town walls after dusk started to disappear. Nobody has seen them ever since. And then came that terrible blow when the miners in the iron mines got slaughtered and their village of Asherbalt was razed to the ground. There were only a few survivors who were able to tell about the atrocities they witnessed.
Who razed the village?

Orcs, my son. I know how absurd it might sound—those infernal servants of Chaos were mentioned only in the legends from the times of the fall of the pagan realms of inhuman races. Nevertheless it seems somebody had those legends revived. By all accounts orcs came somewhere from the infernal depths beneath the Moonshine Mountains. According to the recent reports from the iron mines, huge underground halls were found while mining in the lowest levels of the mines. Nobody knew then that the green skins would come from there!
How is it possible that beings of the ancient times could appear in our world?

I don't doubt heretics are responsible, my son. Somebody managed to open the gates of Hell and brought legions of those cursed beasts that had served well their Lords of Chaos in the past carrying out their destructive will, obliterating everything. Only God knows how many of them the heretics managed to summon and how many of them remain in the deep dark caverns under the Moonshine Mountains. They've managed to take control of the iron mines and of the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Since then a thick black smoke has been fuming from there. Nobody knows what infernal plots they are forging down there, but just the image is enough to make me despair. We must reveal and convict the heretics responsible for the mayhem and prevent them from carrying out their monstrous plans. Fortunately we already have a suspect. According to the investigation it seems beyond doubt that he's guilty. We just need to gather enough evidence against him.
Really? Who is it, if I may ask?

It is Master Edmond d'Arvias, the superior of the Hillbrandt Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Yes, you've heard right. I know that it sounds crazy, nevertheless it seems beyond doubt that he was the one who summoned the orcs and other hellspawns and who's using them to pursue his shameful goals which he exchanged for his holy mission and protection of divine order he swore to uphold in his monastic oath. As you can see, it's a rather delicate matter that will test your real aims—either you'll try to enforce justice or your actual intentions will come out.
Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous? I don't believe one of the highest ranking paladins of our Order would descend to something like that!

Your reaction is understandable. Masters of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are subject only to the Grand Master of the Order and to his Seneschals—they indirectly wield the Grand Master's powers. And at first Master Edmond d'Arvias seemed to me to be an honest and devote man led by the noblest notions. That's why I'd hesitate to believe the result of the investigation—if we lived in normal times. How could such a noble man be controlled by devilish temptations? Nonetheless, considering the current situation...
What do you mean, Your Honor?

I mean the shameful heretical conspiracy of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, my son! You must have heard about it, you're one of them. The highest officials of the Brotherhood of the Righteous led by Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert himself openly came out against the Holy Office! They probably want to persuade His Highness Edward the Second to restrain our jurisdiction and powers.
Why would they do that?

Your superiors reputedly claim that the Brotherhood of the Righteous has been responsible for carrying out justice since the times immemorial. Not such a long time ago they had jurisdiction over all the estates of the Realm—including the Clergy. Nevertheless after the Realm was struck by the Scourges of God and heretic intrigues began to develop into armed revolts, our Holy Mother Church persuaded King Edward to entrust the Holy Office with the investigation of heresy and to give it, in the matters connected with heresy, jurisdiction over all the estates of the Realm—including the knightly order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

It was the only way to uproot heresy from the entire society! Nevertheless the Brotherhood of the Righteous opposes the decision and tries to procure restrictions of the powers of the Holy Office. Your superiors are accusing us of pursuing our own interests and of misusing the powers entrusted to us for performing shameful deeds. They're trying to blacken us and to cast doubt upon our holy mission which was entrusted to us not only by the King but also by God Himself! What insolence!
Why would they do something like that?

Because they're afraid that their own crimes the Order has been keeping secret for so long could be revealed! I trust many paladins are loyal to the King and to God, but I doubt about the superiors of the Order. They're trying to prevent inquisitors from revealing what they're doing in their impregnable fortress—in the Citadel. They're not willing to let the truth appear and to risk that they will be rightly punished in front of the face of God. But that's where they're wrong, my son! The culprits are not going to avoid justice and people like you and me will see to that. They're going to face divine justice and Master Edmond d'Arvias will be the first!
Hmm... Why do you think the heretic you're looking for here in Hillbrandt is exactly Edmond d'Arvias?

Because the night when the green skins attacked the town Edmond d'Arvias was allegedly seen opening one of the town gates for those infernal monsters. Preliminary investigation proved that it was most likely him indeed who let them into the town allowing them to carry out their heinous destructive task. That leads me to your mission, my son. Find out if the accusation is based on truth and if so, arrest Master Edmond d'Arvias. As soon as you manage to do so, hand him over to Sheriff Contemburry and then seek me out. We'll then discuss what to do next. I believe that Master Edmond d'Arvias was ordered to perpetrate those crimes by somebody from the Brotherhood of the Righteous—I must know who it was! We must crush their conspiracy and justly punish all perpetrators!
Very well, Your Honor, I'll do my best. Could I ask you some questions before I start my investigation?
But of course, my son. I'm here to guide you. Ask about anything you'd like to know.
I see, Your Honor. I'll start my investigation immediately.
We shall see. Farewell for now, Your Honor.
It seems somewhat dubious, Your Honor. I'd rather thoroughly investigate the case first. I'd hate to misjudge anyone.

Well, that's exactly what I'm asking you to do, my son! By all means you should investigate all the details of the case. Please, consider everything I've told you about Master d'Arvias just as information I acquired during my stay in Hillbrandt. If he's proven innocent I'll be the first to admit my mistake!

Welcome to Hillbrandt, my son. I was informed that you were about to arrive. I'm glad nothing bad befell you during your journey. It's very dangerous to travel the Realm in these difficult times. It's especially dangerous here in the north. I'm Bishop Vallarian and I hold the office of Inquisitorial Judge with the delegated rights of a Curial Inquisitor here in Hillbrandt.
It's an honor to meet you, Your Honor!
Excuse me, Your Honor, but what does the title Curial Inquisitor mean?

I see. You're not yet acquainted with the hierarchy of the Holy Office—after all you're still only an inquisitorial investigator adept. Then know that a Curial Inquisitor is the highest ranking official of an inquisitorial curia, which is a basic organization unit of the Holy Office. If a large-scale heresy is proven somewhere in the Realm then an inquisitorial curia is founded there—its territory overlaps with the territory of the given diocese. No heresy has been proven yet here in Hillbrandt and thus an inquisitorial curia wasn't founded—the Holy Office is represented by me as an inquisitorial judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor.
I understand. It's an honor to meet you, Your Honor.
Greetings, my son. I hope your investigation is going well. What can I do for you?
Could I talk to you for a minute, Your Honor?
But of course, my son. I'm here to help you as much a I can with anything you might need.
I've arrested Master Edmond d'Arvias, Your Honor.

Excellent! I knew that there would be enough evidence against him. Nevertheless we must now discuss further progress, my son. We have an advantage now as the Master is imprisoned and so he can't thwart our investigation—nevertheless we need to acquire more evidence proving the heretic guilty. Without one more proof we cannot sentence such a high ranking man. His guilt must be proven beyond any doubt.
If there's such a proof, I'll find it, Your Honor.

Excellent, my son. I knew that your presence in Hillbrandt would help us solve the entire case. If I can give you advice, try interrogating Master d'Arvias with the persistent use of torture. I'm sure he's a stubborn heretic, on the other hand I doubt that anybody could resist several hours of racking.
Thanks, Your Honor.
You're welcome, my dear son. Now, what can I do for you?
It seems somewhat dubious, Your Honor. There're still many doubts...

Yes, my son, I agree with you. There are many doubts and no certainty. Nevertheless you should realize that such is the inquisitorial process. It's indeed rare that you have such convincing evidence of guilt to sleep soundly during an investigation of a heresy suspect. Believe me that I suffer from the same doubts. But it's necessary to keep to the facts and your findings and to build on them. If I can give you some advice, try interrogating Master d'Arvias with the persistent use of torture. I'm sure he's a stubborn heretic, on the other hand I doubt that anybody could resist several hours of racking.

My son, what have you done?! You arrested Baroness Linda van Gallagan and accused her of heresy! She's the wife of the royal vice-governor of the town! What were you thinking? That poor soul is in the blessed anticipation, bearing the child of her husband under her heart, and you accuse her of heresy!
I'm sorry, Your Honor, but the evidence is absolutely clear...

Her husband visited me here and insisted very strongly that she was set free and you severely punished. I believe that you were led by honest notions and that your findings might have persuaded you about her guilt, nevertheless I had no other choice. I had to set the Baroness free. I'm sorry, my son, but you'll have to focus your investigation in some other direction.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Sam Riemann.
What crimes is he accused of? And what evidence do you have against him?

Sam Rimeann is accused of evocation of Devil and his worship. He confessed he took part in heretical coven where was allegedly evoked Fallen Angel Arthamon. The same confessed Linda van Gallagan. Moreover, both of them alleged they were acting on your command...

It is obvious, that this is a conspiracy, my son! And I am firmly persuaded, that this is a work of Edmond d'Arvias. He is laughing at us, while dark clouds of evil are gathering around. We must reveal the truth as soon as possible. We can't be sure, what powers Edmond d'Arvias really disposes of. It seems both Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann were convinced, that it was me, who has planned out all these crimes. There is no doubt they were under a spell of Edmond d'Arvias that made them believe it is me instead of him. We can't judge Sam Riemann until we have proof that it was Edmind d'Arvias, who is behind all of this. Go and gather all necessary evidence, my son!

Are you trying to rob me, my son? Perhaps you're just testing my perception. I hope that it's the latter. Nevertheless I've seen you and I sincerely beg you to refrain from doing things like that in the future. Do you understand?!

As an inquisitorial investigator you can only arrest a person accused of heresy. The accusation against a suspect can be brought only by an inquisitorial prosecutor and only after he's been provided with sufficient evidence by inquisitorial investigators. We have only one inquisitorial prosecutor here in Hillbrandt—it's brother Jeremiah. You'll have to cooperate with him very closely. Seek him out and he'll give you all the details.
Is it somehow possible to become an inquisitorial prosecutor?

Of course, my son. The Inquisitorial Codex states that any inquisitor—if he proves his abilities and also his knowledge of both secular and canon law—can be named to the position of inquisitorial prosecutor, judge or of curial inquisitor. Remember though that tenure of such an office is quite demanding and that's why achieving of such a position is also appropriately difficult. Nevertheless if you believe you meet the prerequisites set forth for the office of an inquisitorial prosecutor, seek me out and I'll let you undergo the necessary tests.
What are the prerequisites for becoming an inquisitorial prosecutor?

In view of the fact that inquisitorial prosecutors bring charges against persons suspected of heresy, it is absolutely necessary for the prosecutorial adept to have perfect knowledge of both canon and secular law. Though knowledge in itself would not be enough. Just a perfect knowledge of the law does not make you a suitable candidate for the position of an inquisitorial prosecutor. It is also necessary to find out whether the adept for an inquisitorial prosecutor is capable of independent work on the most difficult cases. That's why every adept is also given a specific case to solve. Moreover he must be also able to devise a charge against a potential perpetrator. Only then can his superior inquisitorial judge decide to appoint the adept an inquisitorial prosecutor.

In my opinion, the situation we're in is the most difficult test God has ever decided to bestow upon us. It might seem it's no wonder that heresy has been spreading vividly in the recent years as there's despair and doom all round us. Nevertheless that's exactly the difficulty of that test, my son. We must carry on till everything turns to good. And not only that. We, the priests, have not just to carry on but also to keep following our holy mission. We must keep the faith without a single stain. We must not allow anyone to doubt it, let alone to dispute it or avoid it. All who have gone astray must be put into the hands of divine justice.

Really?! I'm very glad that you're pursuing your mission so studiously, investigating each and every trace. I'll be most pleased to explain—I really was in the country the night the storm struck the town. I had to investigate some traces regarding local crimes. The night caught me when I was still far from the town and thus I had to stay overnight in the open. I spent all that mayhem sitting under an old patulous spruce, absorbed deep in my prayers. I returned to the town early in the morning—it was still almost dark. And the thing Ruphert saw me throwing away was a pair of my travel gloves which got torn beyond repair when I had fallen on the rocky way.

Wait a moment, my dear son. You've become an inquisitorial investigator of the Holy Office which means that you've accepted to bear the burden of the holy mission on your shoulders and to reveal and investigate all the crimes against God and the Faith without hesitation. Your holy mission obliges you to boundless obedience to God and to your superior brother inquisitors. That's why you have to carefully consider all your deeds and to do everything in your might to truthfully and faithfully reveal every crime that comes to your notice.

Wait a moment, my dear son. To pursuit your holy mission you'll need a bit more appropriate equipment. Keep in mind that from now on you'll be exposed to many a dangers, thus you should be well prepared to face it. Here's a pouch of gold—it should be enough to buy basic equipment. Take my advice—use the money reasonably!

Be modest, my son. The Holy Inquisition should be meek and modest as is our Mother Church whose bosom nurtured us. Now go, you have a difficult task ahead and it's absolutely necessary for you to start your investigation as soon as possible.

Remember, my son, that modesty is a virtue! Nevertheless I'm sure there're some plausible opportunities which would be in compliance with your holy mission. Ask in town, I'm sure you'll find something appropriate. Nevertheless you certainly should not let yourself be distracted from your primary objective!

I'm glad you have volunteered to bolster the ranks of the Inquisition in this distant part of the Realm. It seems that the Holy Office will be rather busy here. I was sent here together with my brothers by the Glatzburg Curial Inquisitor Truncquillius to investigate local crimes. We arrived just after the snow thawed and the roads became at least a little bit passable. Immediately after our arrival I realized that the town was in grave danger and that there was no time to waste.

Of course you may ask, my son. After all it's the task I'm going to entrust to you. Listen carefully and don't let yourself be confused. The perpetrator is no one less important than Master Edmond d'Arvias, the superior of the Hillbrandt Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Yes, I know that it sounds crazy, nevertheless it seems beyond doubt that he was the one who summoned the orcs and other hellspawns and who's using them to pursue his shameful goals which he exchanged for his holy mission and protection of divine order he swore to uphold in his monastic oath.
Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous? Isn't he one of the highest ranking paladins of that Order?

Yes, you're absolutely correct. Masters of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are subject only to the Grand Master of the Order and to his Seneschals—they indirectly wield the Grand Master's powers. What's worse, at first Master Edmond d'Arvias seemed to be an honest and devote man led by the noblest notions. That's why I'd hesitate to believe the results of the investigation—if we lived in normal times. Nevertheless, considering the current situation...

I mean the shameful heretical conspiracy of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, my son! Haven't you heard about it? The highest officials of the Brotherhood of the Righteous led by the Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert himself openly came out against the Holy Office! Supposedly they want to persuade His Highness Edward the Second to restrain our jurisdiction and powers.

They're claiming that the Brotherhood of the Righteous has been responsible for carrying out justice since time immemorial. Not long ago they had jurisdiction over all the estates of the Realm—including Clergy. Nevertheless after the Realm was struck by the Scourges of God and heretic intrigues began to develop into armed revolts, our Holy Mother Church persuaded King Edward to entrust the Holy Office with the investigation of heresy and to give it, in the matters connected with heresy, jurisdiction over all the estates of the Realm—including the knightly order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

It was the only way to uproot heresy from the entire society! Nevertheless the Brotherhood of the Righteous opposes the decision and tries to procure restrictions of the powers of the Holy Office. They're accusing us of pursuing our own interests and of misusing the powers entrusted to us for performing shameful deeds. They're trying to blacken us and to cast doubt upon our holy mission which was entrusted to us not only by the King but also by God Himself! What insolence!

Because they're afraid of their own crimes being revealed! That precious Order of theirs has been keeping them secret long enough! They're trying to prevent our inquisitors from revealing what they're doing in their impregnable fortress—in the Citadel. They're not willing to confess to their crimes and they think they'll avoid the punishment God wishes to bestow upon them. But that's where they're wrong, my son! They're not going to avoid the wrath of our Lord. They're going to face divine justice and Master Edmond d'Arvias will be the first!
Hmm... Why do you think the heretic you're looking for here in Hillbrandt is just Edmond d'Arvias?
I'm ready, Your Honor.
Very well, Your Honor. We can start.
No, he can't. That's a responsibility of inquisitorial investigators. He would violate Decretum Inquisitorium by doing so.

You're wrong, my son. An inquisitorial prosecutor can decide to investigate any case himself and perform all the investigatory actions on his own. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
It's possible, Your Honor. An inquisitorial prosecutor can decide to investigate any case himself and perform all the investigatory actions on his own.
Yes, he can, but only if there's no inquisitorial investigator at his disposal or only if his superior inquisitorial judge allows it.

You're wrong, my son. An inquisitorial prosecutor can decide to investigate any case himself and perform all the investigatory actions on his own, regardless the availability of inquisitorial investigators. Also, there's no need for the consent of his superior inquisitorial judge, because it would be an unnecessary burdening of judges of the Holy Office. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
No, Your Honor. He's always obliged to follow the orders issued by his superior inquisitorial judge.
Of course, Your Honor. He wouldn't be able to perform his tasks otherwise.

No, it is not so, my son. Any inquisitorial prosecutor is always obliged to follow the orders of his superior inquisitorial judge. Judge's opinions are binding for him. Opposing the will of a judge is a transgression any inquisitorial prosecutor should strive to avoid. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

You are mistaken, my son. Crosier is not relevant in such a case. You must distinguish between our Holy Mother Church and the Holy Office. Although inquisitors were born in the womb of the Church and are still its part, we have a different hierarchy which is not affected by the Church hierarchy. A prosecutor who is a Bishop must follow the orders of his superior judge, although he's just a priest. It's true that there are not many cases like that, but it doesn't change anything. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

No, you are mistaken, my son. Only a priest and moreover a member of the Holy Office can strive to achieve the position of an inquisitorial prosecutor. Can you imagine what it would be like if the Inquisition became secular and merchants, burghers, and, God forbid, common people, riff-raff and the rabble were appointed inquisitors? The Inquisition's holy mission is to fight heresy and only the clergy is capable of recognizing it and of finding an appropriate cure. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
Any member of the Holy Office who will demonstrate his practical and theoretical knowledge of both the canon and secular law and who will solve a real case given to him.

No, you are mistaken, my son. The accusatory principle states that only persons accused by an inquisitorial prosecutor can stand inquisitorial trial. It prevents possible arbitrary behavior which could have otherwise occurred. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.
No, Your Honor. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office is absolutely exclusive and is superior to the jurisdictions of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

No, my son, you're mistaken. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office was designed to be exclusive and superior to the jurisdictions of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

It depends on who is accused. If a noble is accused, then he's tried by the local Lord. If a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is accused, then he's tried by his Order. The rest is within the jurisdiction of the Holy Office.

No, my son, you're mistaken. The person of the accused is not important. The jurisdiction of the Holy Office was designed to be exclusive and superior to the jurisdictions of both the secular Lords and of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. You have yet much to learn before you can be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor. Go away now and return when you are better prepared.

Excellent, my son! It seems that you are quite proficient as regards law—you've correctly answered all my questions. Thus all the requirements prescribed for being appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor of the Holy Office are met. I hereby bless you and name you an inquisitorial prosecutor. God bless you, son! Accept this item as a symbol of your new office. Congratulations!
Thank you, Your Honor. It's a great honor!

Yes, my son, I agree with you. There are many doubts and no certitude. Nevertheless you should remember that such is the work of inquisitors. It's indeed rare that you have such convincing evidence of guilt to sleep soundly during an investigation of a heresy suspect. Believe me that I suffer from the same doubts. Regardless your feelings it's necessary to keep to the facts and your findings. If I can give you advice, try interrogating Master d'Arvias with the persistent use of torture. I'm sure he's a stubborn heretic, on the other hand I doubt that anybody could resist several hours of racking.
I would like to become an inquisitorial prosecutor, Your Honor.
Yes, Your Honor, I'm ready.

Then I will charge you with a case which must be solved before you will be allowed to proceed to the test of the canon and secular law. Listen carefully, my son. For ages, Hillbrandt was protected by a holy relic, which shielded it from all evil. It was the Monstrance of St. Orthenius. According to an ancient legend the monstrance was consecrated by the patron saint of the Realm, St. Orthenius himself, in 221. It was carried to Hillbrandt by its first Bishop Albertinus in 339 and it became the most valued treasure of the Holy Mother Church in this part of the Realm. The monstrance was kept in the Church of St. Orthenius. Not that long ago it mysteriously disappeared. Your task will be to find the relic and to find out who was the perpetrator of that heinous crime.

By a lucky coincidence, I've already solved the case, Your Honor. The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen by priest Romius who was serving the undead Bishop Herbertius who had risen from his grave. I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Unbelievable! Bishop Herbertius risen from his grave? That's infernal! And as if it was not enough, according to your words brother Romius was commanded by that spawn of darkness to steal the monstrance. A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers... I find it hard to believe, nevertheless I can't doubt your words, my dear son. It is obvious that heresy has rooted itself deep in this town—it has infected even the ranks of the Church. Thus we must strive even more to uproot the evil before it can cause irrecoverable harm. Nevertheless I am glad to say that you completed your task with excellence! The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed which means the practical part of the test is complete. Though to be appointed an inquisitorial prosecutor of the Holy Office it is necessary to complete a test regarding your knowledge of both the canon and secular law. When you feel you are ready, come to me and we will complete your endeavor.

By a coincidence, I've already solved a part of the case, Your Honor. I found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on undead Bishop Herbertius who, according to my investigation, rose from his grave and somehow managed to get the monstrance. Anyway, I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.
No, Your Honor, I've not yet managed to find out that.
Then keep on searching till you find him, my son. I am sure you will find the perpetrator eventually.
Of course, Your Honor.
Is there anything else I could help you with, my dear son?
I will do my best to apprehend the perpetrator and to return the relic to its rightful place, Your Honor.
I have retrieved the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Your Honor. Undead Bishop Herbertius had it on him. It seems he rose from his grave.
I found out who stole the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Your Honor.
It was Romius, one of the local priests, Your Honor. He testified that he served Bishop Herbertius as a slave.

I would like to pass the test which would allow me to become an inquisitorial prosecutor, Your Honor.

Excellent. I hope that you've prepared yourself very thoroughly. You must bear in mind that only those who have mastered both the canon and secular law can perform well in a difficult office of an inquisitorial prosecutor!
Of course I did, Your Honor. We can start.
I would like to re-sit the test which would allow me to become an inquisitorial prosecutor, Your Honor.

Very well. I hope that this time you've prepared yourself very thoroughly. You must bear in mind that only those who have mastered both the canon and secular law can perform well in a difficult office of an inquisitorial prosecutor!
What crimes against God and faith is he accused of, my son? And what evidence do you have against him?

It is obvious, that this is a conspiracy, my son! And I am firmly persuaded, that this is a work of Edmond d'Arvias. He is laughing at us, while dark clouds of evil are gathering around. We must reveal the truth as soon as possible. We can't be sure, what powers Edmond d'Arvias really disposes of. It seems both Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann were convinced, that it was me, who has planned out all these crimes. There is no doubt they were under a spell of Edmond d'Arvias that made them believe it is me instead of him. We can't judge Sam Riemann until we have proof that it was Edmond d'Arvias, who is behind all of this. Go and gather all necessary evidence, my son!

Remember, my son, that modesty is a virtue! Nonetheless I'm sure there are some plausible opportunities you can take use of during your investigation. Ask in the town, I'm sure you'll find something appropriate. Nevertheless, you certainly should not let yourself be distracted from your primary objective!

To be honest, at first I wasn't too glad you would arrive here to Hillbrandt. It would be a nice proof that the Holy Office has no secret before the aristocracy of the Realm and is able to cooperate with them. And it seems that we will be rather busy here.
