As you can see, it's a rather delicate matter.

I see. As a noble you're not much acquainted with the hierarchy of the Holy Office. Then know that a Curial Inquisitor is the highest ranking official of an inquisitorial curia, which is the basic organization unit of the Holy Office. If a large-scale heresy is proven somewhere in the Realm then an inquisitorial curia is founded there—its territory overlaps the territory of the given diocese. No heresy has been proven here in Hillbrandt yet and thus an inquisitorial curia wasn't founded—the Holy Office is represented by me as an inquisitorial judge with the delegated rights of a curial inquisitor.

Yes, my son, I agree with you. There are many doubts and no certainty. Nevertheless you should realize that such is the inquisitorial process. But it's necessary to keep to the facts and your findings and to build on them. If I can give you advice, try interrogating Master d'Arvias with the persistent use of torture. I'm sure he's a stubborn heretic, on the other hand I doubt that anybody could resist several hours of racking.
I've heard that Master Armorer Leon van den Brooks owes you some money. I'd like to repay his debt.

What? You want to repay Brooks's debts?! What should I think about it? I've taken great pains to get him into a difficult financial situation and you just come here wanting to spoil my plans. No! Never!

I'm not sure what you're talking about, but repaying a debt by the third party is far from unusual. I wouldn't recommend you to refuse my quittance because as a creditor you should be aware of the legal consequences of refusing the consolidation of the hereinbefore mentioned debt portfolio.
Go to hell with your legal dodges, knight! I just want the damn armory—and I almost have it now! I won't let you take it away from me!
And I just want to repay Master van den Brooks's debts. I insist, Duchess!

That must be a bad dream! I'm sure I'm just dreaming! I've been working so hard on it and you just come and destroy it! Very well, as you wish. I'm not in a mood to argue with you. Give me 30,000 gp and get lost!
Here you go, Duchess. Take the money.
Gimme the money, I'm gonna check it. If there's just a single coin missing...
Nothing's missing. And now, if it pleases you, I'd like to ask you some questions.
Really? To be honest I hoped you were about to leave. Your presence here makes me sick. Well, if you insist...
Nothing's missing. And now excuse me, I must return to my duties.
I don't have the money on me at the moment. I'll bring it later.
As you wish, knight. Nevertheless unless I get the money the debt still exists and I can claim the armory!

You want to pay Brooks's debts?! I didn't expect that... I thought that his famous armory was almost in my hands. Well, to tell you the truth, knight, I'm no longer interested in it. Life taught me to be modest and meek.
I'm glad to hear that, Duchess.
Well, give me the money, knight. So we can forget that matter.
I believe you, knight, I'm not even going to check it.
Thank you. And now, if it pleases you, I'd like to ask you some questions.
Sure, go ahead, knight. I'll be glad to answer you.
Thank you. And now excuse me, I must return to my duties.
As you wish, knight. Come back when you have the money.

I doubt there's anybody who hasn't heard that Grand Duchess Liana Lambert was raped by that hellspawn Nicolas. A few weeks back it was a story everybody was passing on. Well, unlike most of them I didn't believe a single word of the Grand Duchess. I don't know if you've already had the opportunity to meet her, but I must assure you that she's the dirtiest woman I've ever seen. She's absolutely corrupt, she flirts with any man she meets—sometimes even with any woman—and at the same time she plays an innocent lily white girl!
I understand. Nevertheless I need some evidence...

I doubt you'll be able to find any. The Grand Duchess's lying for some reason and the fact that Father Nicolas could be arrested and sentenced leaves her calm. Unfortunately I don't know about anything that would prove Father Nicolas innocent.

Wait a moment, knight. Well, I've said I didn't know about anything that would prove Father Nicolas innocent, but that doesn't mean I can't help you. I'm sure that if you... ehm... blackmailed her a bit she would take her accusation back.
That's repulsive! I would never do anything like that!
Don't pretend to be a saint, knight. Moreover you'd be doing the right thing—you don't want Father Nicolas to be sentenced, do you? Sometimes it's necessary to fight fire with fire!
Well, how could I blackmail the Grand Duchess? I don't know about anything that could be used!

Well, I do. I know about a secret that'll surely help you. One night I managed to catch the Grand Duchess out in the city cemetery having quite wild sex with a certain man. Well, that would be shameful enough in itself, nevertheless it's even worse—do you know who that man was? It was the priest Marcius—the Archbishop's scribe and illuminator. The Grand Duchess's having an affair with a priest and moreover they're screwing in the cemetery. Disgusting!
Hmm... So you think that if I pounce on the Grand Duchess with that testimony of yours she'll take back the accusation?

It's quite likely, but if I were you I'd first try to get Marcius's testimony. If you threaten the Grand Duchess with Marcius going public about their affair she'll have no other option that to take the accusation back.
Thank you for your help Duchess.
You're welcome, knight. I'll do anything to harm the bitch. If it were not for her I'd have been in her position now—by the side of Grand Duke Drake Lambert. That swine stole him from me!
Well and what were you doing in the cemetery, Duchess?
Me? Ehm... well... I had... a rendezvous there. But you can't compare it to those obscenities they were doing there!
Grand Duke Robert Heidrick of Glatzburg is looking for a wife. You're single, aren't you?

If I understand you correctly you're asking me to think about marrying Grand Duke Heidrick, am I right? Are you kidding? Grand Duke Heidrick is ruined, discredited, politically compromised... His wife Yulliette Heidrick was sentenced to death by burning for heresy. Can you imagine how dreadful it is, knight? Grand Duke Heidrick can't survive that. He'll be removed from the office, he'll lose his standing and property. Do you think I should marry such a man?! Never!
Am I some kind of a stallholder to tell you about shopping in the city?!

That's a terrible crisis, knight. Just look at the wrinkles around my eyes the crisis has caused me. I'm using the softest, most expensive ointments and I still can't smooth them out... I hope the crisis will be over soon!

I used to think Grand Master de Malamert was such a darling. I liked him even though he was dirty and smelling of dried blood of his enemies all the time. Nevertheless since he was proven to be a monster and fiend fornicating with hellspawns and flying to Dark Sabbaths on a broomstick he has not been allowed to enter my house!

If you're looking for heretics you should arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert. Everybody knows he's a traitor and heretic! He has sold his soul to the dark powers and now he's fornicating with them somewhere deep beneath that impregnable Citadel of his. The fact he's not been seen for some time in the public just supports it. Only God knows how far he fled to avoid justice...

I've heard paladin Richwald d'Blazier was found in Schwarzwald not so long ago—he was turned into stone. Some witch named Corin is suspected of the crime—supposedly he was dating her because she charmed him with her dark spells. Just the image of the things that succubus did with him makes me shiver! Well it seems that after she satisfied her lust she turned him into stone to get rid of him. Dreadful!

You think that the royal counselor Verenicus could be a heretic? No, I can't imagine that. I know that scholarly man really well—he wouldn't be able to harm anyone—especially not the only son of King Edward whom he owes for everything he has achieved in his life. No, it's not possible.
You're asking me if the Inquisitor General is a heretic?! You're kidding, aren't you?! I'm not going to tolerate jokes like that in my house! Stop at once!

Show me the earring. Hmmm... that's a really repulsive trinket, although it's probably made of gold. I have no idea whose it could be. Nevertheless I don't believe anybody of noble birth would wear something that tasteless. I suppose some lowlife must have lost it.
Talking business, right? Well... If you really want to know that, knight, it will cost you $$moneypopTargetPop$$ gp.
I recommend you answer my question, Duchess. I assure you that I've persuaded people nobler than you to cooperate!
I sincerely urge you, Duchess—answer my question, please. I assure you that it won't cause any harm.

You're a beautiful woman, Duchess. Besides that you're also well-read and knowledgeable. No wonder you're the royal vice-governor of Alvaron. Could you please answer my question? I don't believe it would be difficult for you.
Yes, that's true. Could I first ask you with whom I have the honor of talking to?

What?! You don't know me, knight?! Have you not recognized who you're talking to? Is my face like dozens of others that you could have mistaken me for someone else? Haven't you at least seen some of my portraits?

I can see that myself, you cretin! What have you done to me? What spells have you used to bewitch me, you hellspawn?! What will I do! Nobody's going to recognize me now... moreover I'll die in a few years! You must reverse it, sir! It's all your fault, you must reverse the effect of the potion. You must return my beauty to me!

You want to bargain with my sorrow, sir? Well, you're right—I deserve it. If you help me and return me my beauty I won't spare my treasury and magic elixirs. Even though it's all your fault anyway... Will you help me?
In that case begone from my house, sir! I don't want you to stand here like that looking at me. Get lost and don't you dare to come back again!
I'm so glad to see you, sir! Have you found a cure for my ugliness? Have you found a way to restore my original beauty? I feel so ugly...
Oh, sir, please hurry! I can't live like this! Every hour is a century of suffering for me!
I'll be glad to answer all your questions, sir. Please, promise me though that you'll return to your search for a cure for my sorry state as quickly as you can!

Oh, thank you, sir! I hope with all my heart the potion will help. I'll drink it at once. Oh... it tastes great! I feel potent warmth spreading throughout my body. I feel... getting younger! My God, it works! Look at my hands... my freshness's coming back!
Go away, sir. Don't you see how tormenting your presence is? I don't want anyone to see me like that. I want to be left alone with my grief...
Haven't you heard, sir? I don't want to talk to you. I don't want to talk to anybody in the whole world. I want to be left alone...

I humbly thank you, sir. And I ask you for forgiveness for my previous behavior. You've proved to me how merciful God can be to the sinners who repent their sins. It was the most valuable lesson I've been ever given. Here's your reward, you fully deserve it.
Of course, sir. I'll be glad to talk. What would you like to know?
Goodbye, sir. And thank you once more. I think that I'm never going to forget this lesson!
Hello, sir. I'm very glad to see you again. How could I ever repay you for the great service you did to me? Could I be of any assistance?
It's the least I can do for you, sir. Ask about whatever you want. I don't have any secrets before you.

Yes, everything is absolutely ok, sir. You're so good to me. If it were not for you I'd be a hideous hag till my death! I wish everything goes well for you, sir. And by all means drop by again when you have time.
You're new to the town, Lady Baroness. What do you think about the people who live here?

The people who live here in Hillbrandt are real barbarians, knight. Excuse me for saying that, but it's true. I spent most of my life in convent schools and when I married Baron van Singier, I lived in Glatzburg for some time. It's not comparable with the conditions here. Never in my life have I seen so much atrocity, rudeness, indolence and apathy. No wonder heresy settled down here. And I wouldn't be surprised if it will be found that all the evil came from the places like this. Hillbrandt is an awful, dirty hole full of people who hardly resemble true faithful believers. Every day I spend here makes me suffer!
I've heard that your sister-in-law Linda van Gallagan is missing. Do you happen to know anything about it?

I wouldn't be surprised if devils took my sister-in-law to Hell... She was such an immoral, ruthless and cold woman who never missed an opportunity to manipulate my poor brother. Many times I offered him to move to Glatzburg where I could arrange some good position in the court of Grand Duke Heidrick for him. He always refused, because that lecherous woman—intrigued with many other men every moment—made him to stay here, in such an awful hole. God knows what plans she had here, but I'm sure she planned nothing good.
Do you want to say you doubt the faith of Linda van Gallagan?

Exactly, knight. I wasn't sure about it before I came here. However, I've been living in my brother's house for some time and I found out that my sister-in-law had well-hidden secrets. Often she crept out of the house during the night when she thought nobody could see her. Something else was always hidden behind her innocent look—disregard for me, maybe even aversion. She thought she was able to hide it all perfectly, but she didn't trick me. I used to live in the highest society in Glatzburg long enough not to be tricked by some country Baroness. I tell you, knight, the woman is engaged with Hell!
You don't have any proof of course, do you?

Oh, I'm afraid I don't, knight. I wasn't able to catch her doing anything she could be accused of. I didn't try too hard, knight. I didn't want to risk my life! The way the woman looked at me when she thought I didn't see her talked clearly enough!
Did you know that Paul Hammerhand was missing?

Yes, I've heard that the naughty son of Hammerhand the blacksmith ran away from home again. There was always trouble with that little rascal ever since I arrived in Hillbrandt. I'm sure some impure ghost must live in his body! I've never seen a child behave so terribly. He lies, steals and is wayward like Satan himself! However, I don't know anything about the reason why he's missing. He's probably doing some wicked things somewhere. Or he broke his neck at last during some devilment he tried to do!

I lost all I had during the last three years, knight. My beloved husband, all our family belongings... simply put, I lost everything. However, I don't cry, I don't take recourse to idolatry and I'm trying to strengthen my faith as much as I can. Because of that I don't think that the Scourges of God that affected our Realm are an acceptable reason for the people to become heretics using the powers of Hell just to assure better times will come. No, knight. Well, maybe there are some people of that type here, but I think most of the godless people aren't the poor ones from which life took the last things they had. The heretics are the people vicious to the marrow of their bones, the people holding various positions in the Realm's administration and society. They're among the nobles, in the Knightly Orders, even among the clerics. No offence, knight, but I'd have my eyes wide open if I were you.

I've experienced many terrible things during the last three years, but to tell the truth, the thing that scared me most was that terrible storm that drifted over the town lately in the middle of the night. All the time that terrible tempest was raging out there I was praying to the Archangel Gabriel not to let us fall into the throat of Satan. That was exactly how it looked like, knight—as if Hell opened its maw and was going to swallow up our entire world. Ghosts, phantoms and other infernal vermin flew in the air and romped about in the sky like if there wasn't God's Word that denies them to enter our world! I closed the window shutters, because I was afraid they would come into my bedroom and take my soul away with them!
How long did the tempest last, Lady Baroness?
I don't know exactly, knight, several hours at least! When the tempest was finished at least, all my body was lame because of that long kneeling.
You said you had your window shutters closed not to let those hellspawns to take your soul... In that case, How could you see the hellspawns and devils romping about in the sky?

I... it was clear to me what was going on out there, knight. Well, people in the town told me the same the next day. Not many of them were brave enough to show their face out of their door, but those who did so told me about infernal demons who cried in the sky and rampaged there like witches during some heretic Sabbath!
Thank you, Lady Baroness.
What do you think about the fact Master Edmond d'Arvias is suspected of heresy?

I don't believe Master Edmond d'Arvias would be able to commit something as terrible as the people say. Although I've known him for only a short time, I'm sure the man is one of the most faithful and honest people I've ever met. Thus it seems unthinkable to me that he's accused of something as irrational as to plot with the powers of Hell!
Well, such a crime might happen these times, Lady Baroness. Don't you think so?

Of course, you're right, I also knew people who seemed to be devoted to their mission and at the same time they reveled in hellish debauchery and godless celebrations of the Lord of Darkness in their cellars. However, that's not the case of Master Edmond d'Arvias. He's so... clean and open—talk to him for just a minute and you won't doubt he's innocent. Try talking to him, knight. You'll see he'll convince you!

I'm sorry, knight, but I'm not well versed in theology or in ecclesiastical history. Wasn't he one of the Fallen Angels? I don't know any details about him... I really don't have the slightest idea what I could tell you about him.

I don't know anything about that dirty crime, knight. Well, how could I know anything? However, I've heard some hellspawns did it—they entered the church during the night, ignored the Holy Ground, bewitched the priests and took the monstrance. At the same time they spit at the cross three times and dishonored God's name thrice!
Well... really noteworthy information.

Oh, poor Bishop Quentinus. He disappeared during that terrible attack of the orcs on the town several days ago. Surely the hellspawns killed him or they took him with them to sacrifice him to their unclean idols. He was such a kind-hearted man! Sometimes, the ways of our Lord are really inconceivable.

I'd like to agree with other people and believe that Olfghard killed Natalia Reichmann; but I can't do so—although I've had the honor to become a victim of his renowned thieving abilities myself. That is, he stole some jewelry from me during a fair. There was only one mistake he made—he underestimated a woman's wit. I had my jewelry back sooner than he was able to sell it. He even paid a compliment to me. I assure you, knight, that man doesn't need to murder young girls for money. He's not that type of man, I'm sure about that. As for me, he was accused absolutely wrongfully. Unfortunately, nobody knows what really happened to Natalia. I liked her a lot, she was one of a few unspoiled souls in this muddy stinking slum.

I don't have the slightest idea where the soldier Jullian could be, knight. In fact I wouldn't know him at all if I hadn't met him once with Natalia Reichmann. He courted her some time ago because he thought he could get to her father's money that way, you know? Well, he wasn't successful. He might have fooled Natalia with his compliments and youngster talk, but he didn't fool her father. Mr. Reichmann is a merchant too skilled to let some beginner fraudster get the better of him.
Do you want to say that Jullian courted Natalia only to get to her father's money?

Yes, exactly, knight. That dandy thought he could get right to her father's treasury through Natalia's clear heart. But he was mistaken and according to what I've heard he was really angry with Reichmann. The merchant got rid of him in such an unscrupulous way that Jullian didn't stop running until he reached the watch-house.
You're from Glatzburg, Lady Baroness. What could you tell me about Bishop Trevorius?

Bishop Trevorius is a very reputable man. He's conscientious, careful, well read and truly devoted to his work. He has a great credit for keeping peace and order in Glatzburg even after the Scourges of God struck the Realm. God knows what would happen there without his self-sacrificing approach. If you meet him, you'll see for yourself that he'd do anything to assist you.
Do you still mourn for your late husband, Lady Baroness? In the case you don't, I'd like to take the liberty to offer you a certain proposal involving Grand Duke Robert Heidrick.

I don't mourn anymore, knight. I grieved for my husband as it was proper for a faithful woman, and now I live and make good as a widow. Why do you ask me about that? What proposal do you have in mind? Robert is married, if I remember well... I won't try to hide we always used to be close to each other. With all honor, of course!
I'm glad to hear it, Lady Baroness, because the Grand Duke became a widower. Under very unpleasant circumstances, I have to say. His wife, Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, was executed as a heretic.

Oh my God... Robert's wife was a heretic? That must have politically ruined him! I never liked Yulliette much. She was a plotter and a coquette. But I would never have thought that she was a heretic. Poor Robert. It's only a matter of time when the shame ruins him. I'm sure intrigues are already plotted in the court to use his ruined marriage and cracked reputation against him.

Yes, exactly. Grand Duke Heidrick thinks exactly the same about it. However, he hopes to wed again soon, and the marriage could return to him part of the reputation and honor he lost, so that he could stay in the position of the royal governor of the city. And that's why I'm here. I'd like to ask you whether you want to become the wife of Grand Duke Heidrick.

My God... Robert and me... husband and wife? I never thought about it, not even in my dreams... However, how could I help him to get back his reputation, when I don't have any reputation myself? Well, I don't have anything in fact... Even these clothes don't belong to me in fact. How could I come to him and look into his eyes? No, that's impossible! I can't get married like some village girl... I'm sorry, knight. I can't come to Robert when I don't have anything. Not even a wedding dress... I have my honor!
I believe firmly Grand Duke Heidrick will buy you the most beautiful dress you've ever had.
I wouldn't allow that! He mustn't see me like this, without a dowry and my own dress. No, that's impossible, I'm sorry.
What if I get a really grand wedding dress for you, Lady Baroness?
Well, I've nothing to pay you with, knight. I'm sorry.
You could take it as a gift of God, Lady Baroness. Because I believe God wants to see Robert and you as husband and wife.

Oh, really? Well, in that case... In that case I agree, knight. You're very kind to offer me your help. I know an excellent seamstress who makes the most beautiful dresses the world has ever seen. Her name is Baroness Helen von Hunth. We used to be friends when I lived in Glatzburg. Find her, please, and ask her to make a grand wedding dress for me—a wedding dress worthy of the sight of Grand Duke Heidrick.
All right, Lady Baroness. I'll arrange it. You should prepare for a journey in the meantime. I'll be back sooner than you think.
Thank you, knight. As for me, I'm ready. I've nothing more, only the clothes I have on me.
I have bad news for you, Lady Baroness. Helen von Hunth is dead.
Oh my god... what a disaster! How did it happen? What happened to her?
That's not important. It means someone else must make that wedding dress.

You don't understand, knight? That's a sign from God! God doesn't want me to marry Robert Heidrick. Thus he took Helen von Hunth to him to show me my place is here, not beside Robert. I'm sorry, but I can't marry Robert. It's impossible.
I assure you that it isn't any sign from God. On the contrary, God wants you to marry each other. That's why he sent me to you.
It's nice of you to try and comfort me, knight, but I can recognize a sign from God when I see one. I'm sorry.
Don't tell me, Lady Baroness, that there isn't anybody else who could make that dress for you...
It's not the question of a wedding dress anymore, knight. There's that sign from God here that can't be ignored. I'm a humble faithful woman and so I'll do what God asks me to do.
As you wish, Lady Baroness. Farewell.

They exchanged several words and left each other like as if they didn't plan anything. But after a moment neither of them was in the tavern. I presumed they both left for the merchant's room in the attic to fornicate—because my sister-in-law is used to doing so. However, the next day Kurth Ollmier was found dead...
Do you think Linda van Gallagan could be involved somehow in that murder?

Yes, that's possible. I always believed my hard-boiled sister-in-law would be able to do something like that to get what she wanted. I don't know what Kurth Ollmier had in common with her, but they looked at least suspiciously at each other. However, there's one thing I'd like to ask you for, knight. If you talk to Linda to verify that information, don't tell her who told you, please. I'd never have enough courage to face Linda openly.
Of course, don't be afraid about it, Lady Baroness.
I'll do what I consider to be proper, Lady Baroness.
Oh... in that case I can't promise you I'll repeat that testimony in public!

Duke Weinberg rules in Hillbrandt as the royal governor of the town. My brother Baron Robert van Gallagan is the royal vice-governor, although in fact his wife Linda rules in his name. Unfortunately...
Look, Lady Baroness—you can either answer me now or you can be arrested and answer me while I'm torturing you.
It's clear to me you don't like me, Lady Baroness. However I think you can agree with me that your attitude shouldn't prevent you from answering my question.
I'd like to assure you, dear Lady Baroness, that any of your bright observations is very important for me...
Oh, knight, give me a little piece of consolation in the form of a kind word from God's knight, please!
As you wish, good woman. Don't despair—God watches over us all.

Thank you, knight. You're very kind. There is so little consolation to be found in these times... It seems to me as if the evil around us wrapped our souls up into an impermeable cloak, impenetrable even for a single beam of hope.
I don't have time to do that.
Oh... There is so little consolation to be found in these times... It seems to me as if the evil around us wrapped our souls up into an impermeable cloak, impenetrable even for a single beam of hope.
My name is Elisabeth van Singier. I'm the sister of Baron Robert van Gallagan.
You're the sister of Baron van Gallagan? You don't have the same name...
Oh, sure I don't. I was married to Baron Erwin van Singier, a former royal vice-governor of Glatzburg.
You're far from your home, Lady Baroness. What brings you here to Hillbrandt?

Death, knight. My husband died of plague two years ago; and last year I lost my home and all my belongings when our mansion was burned to ashes during the Night of the Falling Stars. Everything was razed to the ground. All I have now is my life. Because of that I came to my brother who was so kind and offered me shelter here. I even got a small annuity till the end of my life, and I'm very grateful to him for that. My brother is a really good man!
I'm sorry about your husband, Lady Baroness. I'll pray for the salvation of his soul. Could I ask you a few questions now?
Of course, knight. I'll gladly answer all your questions. What do you need to now?
Nice to have met you, Lady Baroness. Farewell.
Hail to you, knight.
Hail to you, Lady Baroness. Could I talk to you?
Of course, knight. I'll gladly talk to you. What's on your mind?
Hello, knight. I hesitate to ask you if you bring me the wedding dress from Helen von Hunth already?
Yes, Lady Baroness, I bring the dress. Here you are.
My God, it's so beautiful! I knew Helen was wonderful! Thank you, knight.
Not at all, Lady Baroness. If you agree, we could set on a way to Glatzburg now.
Yes, I agree. We shouldn't keep Robert waiting. I'm so glad I'm going to see him!
I'm afraid not, Lady Baroness. I don't bring you the dress yet.
Never mind, knight. I'm sure you'll bring it next time. Because I don't want to keep Robert waiting...
I will, you can trust me, Lady Baroness. Farewell.

You don't understand, knight, do you? That's a sign from God! God doesn't want me to marry Robert Heidrick. Thus he took Helen von Hunth to him to show me my place is here, not beside Robert. I'm sorry, but I can't marry Robert. It's impossible.
I'm so glad to see you again, knight. Robert and I are so grateful to you for what you've done for us! We'll never be able to repay you properly...
Don't worry about it, Lady Baroness. Could I talk to you for a moment?
I'm sorry, knight, but not now. I'm very busy with the wedding preparations, you now? Excuse me, please.
That's right. I'll leave you to your business. Farewell.
I did it for you gladly, Lady Baroness; moreover it was the will of God. Farewell.

My God, it's so beautiful! I knew Helen was wonderful! Thank you, Father.
Never mind, Father. I'm sure you'll bring it next time. Because I don't want to keep Robert waiting...

You don't understand, Father, do you? That's a sign from God! God doesn't want me to marry Robert Heidrick. Thus he took Helen von Hunth to him to show me my place is here, not beside Robert. I'm sorry, but I can't marry Robert. It's impossible.
I'm so glad to see you again, Father. Robert and I are so grateful to you for what you've done for us! We'll never be able to repay you properly...
I'm sorry, Father, but not now. I'm very busy with the wedding preparations, you now? Excuse me, please.

The people who live here in Hillbrandt are real barbarians, noble lord. Excuse me for saying that, but it's true. I spent most of my life in convent schools and when I married Baron van Singier, I lived in Glatzburg for some time. It's not comparable with the conditions here. Never in my life have I seen so much atrocity, rudeness, indolence and apathy. No wonder heresy settled down here. And I wouldn't be surprised if it will be found that all the evil came from the places like this. Hillbrandt is an awful, dirty hole full of people who hardly resemble true faithful believers. Every day I spend here makes me suffer!

Exactly, noble lord. I wasn't sure about it before I came here. However, I've been living in my brother's house for some time and I found out that my sister-in-law had well-hidden secrets. Often she crept out of the house during the night when she thought nobody could see her. Something else was always hidden behind her innocent look—disregard for me, maybe even aversion. She thought she was able to hide it all perfectly, but she didn't trick me. I used to live in the highest society in Glatzburg long enough not to be tricked by some country Baroness. I tell you, noble lord, the woman is engaged with Hell!

Oh, I'm afraid I don't, noble lord. I wasn't able to catch her doing anything she could be accused of. I didn't try too hard, noble lord. I didn't want to risk my life! The way the woman looked at me when she thought I didn't see her talked clearly enough!

I lost all I had during the last three years, noble lord. My beloved husband, all our family belongings... simply put, I lost everything. However, I don't cry, I don't take recourse to idolatry and I'm trying to strengthen my faith as much as I can. Because of that I don't think that the Scourges of God that affected our Realm are an acceptable reason for the people to become heretics using the powers of Hell just to assure better times will come. No, noble lord. Well, maybe there are some people of that type here, but I think most of the godless people aren't the poor ones from which life took the last things they had. The heretics are the people vicious to the marrow of their bones, the people holding various positions in the Realm's administration and society. They're among the nobles, in the Knightly Orders, even among the clerics. No offence, noble lord, but I'd have my eyes wide open if I were you.

I've experienced many terrible things during the last three years, but to tell the truth, the thing that scared me most was that terrible storm that drifted over the town lately in the middle of the night. All the time that terrible tempest was raging out there I was praying to the Archangel Gabriel not to let us fall into the throat of Satan. That was exactly how it looked like, noble lord—as if Hell opened its maw and was going to swallow up our entire world. Ghosts, phantoms and other infernal vermin flew in the air and romped about in the sky like if there wasn't God's Word that denies them to enter our world! I closed the window shutters, because I was afraid they would come into my bedroom and take my soul away with them!
I don't know exactly, noble lord, several hours at least! When the tempest was finished at least, all my body was lame because of that long kneeling.

I... it was clear to me what was going on out there, noble lord. Well, people in the town told me the same the next day. Not many of them were brave enough to show their face out of their door, but those who did so told me about infernal demons who cried in the sky and rampaged there like witches during some heretic Sabbath!

Of course, you're right, I also knew people who seemed to be devoted to their mission and at the same time they reveled in hellish debauchery and godless celebrations of the Lord of Darkness in their cellars. However, that's not the case of Master Edmond d'Arvias. He's so... clean and open—talk to him for just a minute and you won't doubt he's innocent. Try talking to him, noble lord. You'll see he'll convince you!

I'm sorry, noble lord, but I'm not well versed in theology or in ecclesiastical history. Wasn't he one of the Fallen Angels? I don't know any details about him... I really don't have the slightest idea what I could tell you about him.

I don't know anything about that dirty crime, noble lord. Well, how could I know anything? However, I've heard some hellspawns did it—they entered the church during the night, ignored the Holy Ground, bewitched the priests and took the monstrance. At the same time they spit at the cross three times and dishonored God's name thrice!

I'd like to agree with other people and believe that Olfghard killed Natalia Reichmann; but I can't do so—although I've had the honor to become a victim of his renowned thieving abilities myself. That is, he stole some jewelry from me during a fair. There was only one mistake he made—he underestimated a woman's wit. I had my jewelry back sooner than he was able to sell it. He even paid a compliment to me. I assure you, noble lord, that man doesn't need to murder young girls for money. He's not that type of man, I'm sure about that. As for me, he was accused absolutely wrongfully. Unfortunately, nobody knows what really happened to Natalia. I liked her a lot, she was one of a few unspoiled souls in this muddy stinking slum.

I don't have the slightest idea where the soldier Jullian could be, noble lord. In fact I wouldn't know him at all if I hadn't met him once with Natalia Reichmann. He courted her some time ago because he thought he could get to her father's money that way, you know? Well, he wasn't successful. He might have fooled Natalia with his compliments and youngster talk, but he didn't fool her father. Mr. Reichmann is a merchant too skilled to let some beginner fraudster get the better of him.

Yes, exactly, noble lord. That dandy thought he could get right to her father's treasury through Natalia's clear heart. But he was mistaken and according to what I've heard he was really angry with Reichmann. The merchant got rid of him in such an unscrupulous way that Jullian didn't stop running until he reached the watch-house.

I don't mourn anymore, noble lord. I grieved for my husband as it was proper for a faithful woman, and now I live and make good as a widow. Why do you ask me about that? What proposal do you have in mind? Robert is married, if I remember well... I won't try to hide we always used to be close to each other. With all honor, of course!

My God... Robert and me... husband and wife? I never thought about it, not even in my dreams... However, how could I help him to get back his reputation, when I don't have any reputation myself? Well, I don't have anything in fact... Even these clothes don't belong to me in fact. How could I come to him and look into his eyes? No, that's impossible! I can't get married like some village girl... I'm sorry, noble lord. I can't come to Robert when I don't have anything. Not even a wedding dress... I have my honor!
Well, I've nothing to pay you with, noble lord. I'm sorry.

Oh, really? Well, in that case... In that case I agree, noble lord. You're very kind to offer me your help. I know an excellent seamstress who makes the most beautiful dresses the world has ever seen. Her name is Baroness Helen von Hunth. We used to be friends when I lived in Glatzburg. Find her, please, and ask her to make a grand wedding dress for me—a wedding dress worthy of the sight of Grand Duke Heidrick.
Thank you, noble lord. As for me, I'm ready. I've nothing more, only the clothes I have on me.

You don't understand, noble lord? That's a sign from God! God doesn't want me to marry Robert Heidrick. Thus he took Helen von Hunth to him to show me my place is here, not beside Robert. I'm sorry, but I can't marry Robert. It's impossible.
It's nice of you to try and comfort me, noble lord, but I can recognize a sign from God when I see one. I'm sorry.
It's not the question of a wedding dress anymore, noble lord. There's that sign from God here that can't be ignored. I'm a humble faithful woman and so I'll do what God asks me to do.

I know something about the murder of that merchant Ollmier, noble lord. It involves my sister-in-law, Linda van Gallagan. St.Hedwika's day was celebrated the night the merchant Ollmier died. There were many people in Truthorn's tavern, but in spite of the stir there I noticed that Ollmier and Linda were looking at each other. They exchanged several words and left each other like as if they didn't plan anything. But after a moment neither of them was in the tavern. I presumed they both left for the merchant's room in the attic to fornicate—because my sister-in-law is used to doing so. However, the next day Kurth Ollmier was found dead...

Yes, that's possible. I always believed my hard-boiled sister-in-law would be able to do something like that to get what she wanted. I don't know what Kurth Ollmier had in common with her, but they looked at least suspiciously at each other. However, there's one thing I'd like to ask you for, noble lord. If you talk to Linda to verify that information, don't tell her who told you, please. I'd never have enough courage to face Linda openly.
Thank you, noble lord.
Oh, noble lord, give me a little piece of consolation in the form of a kind word of a noble, please!

Thank you, noble lord. You're very kind. There is so little consolation to be found in these times... It seems to me as if the evil around us wrapped our souls up into an impermeable cloak, impenetrable even for a single beam of hope.

Death, noble lord. My husband died of plague two years ago; and last year I lost my home and all my belongings when our mansion was burned to ashes during the Night of the Falling Stars. Everything was razed to the ground. All I have now is my life. Because of that I came to my brother who was so kind and offered me shelter here. I even got a small annuity till the end of my life, and I'm very grateful to him for that. My brother is a really good man!
Of course, noble lord. I'll gladly answer all your questions. What do you need to now?
Hail to you, noble lord.
Of course, noble lord. I'll gladly talk to you. What's on your mind?
Hello, noble lord. I hesitate to ask you if you bring me the wedding dress from Helen von Hunth already?
My God, it's so beautiful! I knew Helen was wonderful! Thank you, noble lord.
Never mind, noble lord. I'm sure you'll bring it next time. Because I don't want to keep Robert waiting...

You don't understand, noble lord, do you? That's a sign from God! God doesn't want me to marry Robert Heidrick. Thus he took Helen von Hunth to him to show me my place is here, not beside Robert. I'm sorry, but I can't marry Robert. It's impossible.
I'm so glad to see you again, noble lord. Robert and I are so grateful to you for what you've done for us! We'll never be able to repay you properly...
I'm sorry, noble lord, but not now. I'm very busy with the wedding preparations, you now? Excuse me, please.
A noble man steals?! It's unbelievable! No wonder this world is in such a bad state when even the gentry rob innocent people! Shame!
How is it possible that King Edward was assassinated? You should have protected him!

Yes, I know... it's an ineffaceable disgrace for me. That mistake sullied my honor. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, knight?
I'd like to know what is the authority of the First Knight now when King Edward is dead and there isn't any heir to the throne...

In the case the Realm loses its leader the First Knight becomes the temporary governor of the Realm. He administrates all the legislative, administrative and judicial duties of the Chief of State until the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a proper heir to the Throne from the highest ranking nobles. He's also the commander-in-chief of the Royal army, of course. Do you need to know something else, knight?
What did you do at the moment the King was murdered? Why weren't you near him to protect him?

I don't think I should confess to you where I was the moment of the King Edward's death! I've already confessed to Cardinal Letti. However, if you want to know about that, the duties of the First Knight don't entail only guarding His Majesty. I had some duties out of the Royal Palace. There was nothing I could do... However, I agree with you that what happened doesn't decrease my responsibility for it. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, knight?
I couldn't have left unnoticed the wounds on your face, Sir Knight. It looks like scratches. What happened to you?
My wound is not your business, knight! But, if you're interested in that... Not long ago I caught a thief who resisted me and he scratched my face before I killed him. Satisfied?
Yes, thank you.
Excellent. Is there anything else on your mind?

To tell the truth, I don't like that matter at all. During the inspection of dead King Edward's body I found traces of blood and small pieces of human skin under his fingernails. As if he wounded his murderer before he died...

You offend me, knight! You're not going to suspect me of anything as mad as the murder of King Edward! I'm the First Knight, the highest protector of the Realm—whatever I do, I do it for the benefit of the Realm. If you're going to continue offending me, your audience will be terminated before you can say Jack Robinson!
A common thief wounded you?
Yes, he did. He used the moment of my incaution and tried to blind me. However, he didn't succeed—I killed him immediately!

What do I think about the current crisis? I don't know. I'm not a cleric, I'm a soldier—thus I don't analyze the basis of the matter, I'm trying to solve emerging troubles immediately. I see an enemy—I attack. I've been using this simple rule all my life and I don't see the slightest reason why to change it!
I'm sorry, but revealing a military secret could mean a threat to the safety interests of the Realm. Because of that I can't answer your question, knight. I'm sorry!

Christoffer de Malamert a heretic? What nonsense! I've known him for many years and I had the honor of fighting by his side; I could swear to the cross of the First Prophet that he's an honest and noble man. However, it's true that most of the people in Alvaron don't think the same, on the contrary they believe he's a traitor who sold out his own people. I wish they knew what mischief they commit...

You can run into many various monsters in Alvaron and around, knight. I've been a soldier for almost twenty years, but I'm still scared of the undead. You can kill a living opponent with a single well-directed blow, no matter what the opponent looks like. The undead are something completely different. You must hack the dead like a butcher to get them down, and even on the ground they wriggle and kick around themselves like a wild mare. Not talking about the damned souls, horrors and shadows, knight. There's nothing more terrible than an ethereal opponent...
Yes, I agree with that.

And you're right to agree! Be careful not to stay at the city cemetery after dusk, knight. Living dead feast there on graves and coffins during the nights, spirits flow through the air in the graveyard and nameless horrors lurk in the shadows. He who decides to go there is never seen again—or he's seen as one of them! Even during the day it's not a safe place at all...

Grand Duke Drake Lambert set reasonably high rewards for catching the werewolves who rampage not only around the city, but unfortunately also in the streets. Sheriff Henry Portmann pays the reward in exchange for trophies—heads of killed werewolves—brought to him. I don't expect it could completely solve the troubles the pack of the wolf-prince Wulfhyrr causes us, but I'm sure there will be some effect...
I'm sorry, knight, but the knowledge of heretic cults doesn't belong to my priorities. I've never heard about that cult...

My friend Baron Mansfeld died some time ago. We've known each other since childhood and we grew up together; his death broke my heart. When we became adults, our lives became very different. I devoted my life to the service to our Realm and he started to make business and gather more and more property. I must say he was successful. Thanks to several good decisions he made a lot of money; many high noble Houses could only dream about something like that.

Unfortunately, the Baron didn't have a very good relationship with the rest of his family and because of that he decided to hide all his gold somewhere near Alvaron, not to let it get in the hands of his wicked relatives. And so he did—the Baron buried his treasure and died untroubled. I'm sure you can imagine, knight, that people are turning twice every stone in the neighborhood as they're trying to find that treasure...

I can't stand the fact that as the temporary commander-in-chief of the Royal army I can't prevent the werewolves from getting into the capital of the Realm. I take it as my personal failure and I'm doing all I can to prevent it. However, I can't send the whole Royal regiment to watch the city gates. Even if I strengthen the watch, we found the guards the next day sleeping due to some wicked spell. I wish to get those malevolent heretics into my hands. I would show them how much pain can they experience in this world before they get into Hell!

I've heard about the case of the violation of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert, knight. It's sad that something of that kind could happen—no matter what the truth is. In case Father Nicolas is guilty it would hurt the reputation of the Inquisition. In case Grand Duchess Liana lied it would hurt the reputation of her husband as he's the royal governor of our city. Because of that I must say I'm very sorry the scandal happened—nothing good will come from that.

Have you heard the tale about Duke Manfred Gotfried, knight? It was an awful case of a hidden heresy. All the people knew he was a heretic and what terrible things he made, they were afraid of him like the devil is afraid of the cross, but the Inquisition was never able to gather enough evidence to prove him guilty. The Baron traveled a lot when he was young and he was said to be one of a few faithful people who visited Jad-Habaal, that Realm of the pagan dogs. He was supposed to have brought a damned relic from there, a certain Necklace of Death. The necklace was rumored to bestow supernatural abilities on him—reputedly it allowed him to establish contact with the Other World. The Baron succumbed to the temptation and started to deal with necromancy...
Farewell, knight. God preserve the Realm!
The First Knight cannot be bribed!
You had better answer me, Sir Knight. You can't imagine the troubles you would get into in the case you deny to cooperate with me!
I ask you frankly, Sir Knight, answer my question—it's for the righteous cause!
Your wisdom and experience are renowned, Sir Knight. Your answer would help me a lot...
To tell the truth, I'd like to talk to you for a moment.
Well... all right, I'll give you a moment of my time. But try to be brief, will you? I've too much work, there are SO MANY things that need to be done... The Realm was kept in ruins for so long!
No, I don't need that. Farewell.
Don Rodrigo de Velacor, I arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of the murder of His Majesty King Edward the Second. You'll come with me to be put before a fair trial!

You... you found out about it, knight? Oh my God... not yet, please! There's so much I still have to do and so little time left... However, I'm glad it came so soon. I wouldn't be able to carry that burden for long. I'm a sinner and I must be punished. Well, I hoped I'd be able to save the Realm first. Or at least to try to save it. Maybe it's still not too late!

Yes, knight, I confess. It was me who killed King Edward the Second. I'm deeply sorry about that, but there was nothing else I could have done. I must protect the Realm—even from His Majesty himself, if it's necessary! In this case there was nothing else to do—King Edward was ready to allow the Realm to be completely destroyed!
What are you talking about, Sir Knight?

You don't have the slightest idea what's happening, knight. You think I'm a devious murderer who took the life of King Edward either because of selfish incentives or in the service of the powers of Hell. But I can assure you that's not true. I killed King Edward whom I loved and respected above all, because my oath of the First Knight obliged me to do so!
You must explain that to me!

The First Knight is the highest defender of the Realm and of the Crown, knight. This position obliges its representative not only to protect His Royal Majesty and the Royal family, but also to protect the Realm as such. That's exactly what I had to do—to protect the Realm! Believe me that I loved King Edward like my own father, but I couldn't let him destroy our Realm that I swore to protect!
How could King Edward threaten Ultherst? I don't understand it... that is to say, he was our King!

I didn't understand it as well, knight. Unfortunately,the King's heart was broken when his children died two years ago—he grieved especially for Prince Louis. He changed a lot since that time. He wasn't interested in anything, tried to drown his sorrow in wine... and he didn't realize dark clouds were gathering above Ultherst!
Do you mean the spread of heresy?

No, knight—although heresy is involved directly in the matter. I'm talking about the crusade. The Pope Alessander the Third proclaimed the crusade against Ultherst several months ago. In the Empire, which used to be our ally for ages, armies of crusaders are gathered even now to invade Ultherst and to perform the Will of God—to kill, to plunder and to destroy!
Oh my God... A Crusade against Ultherst!? I don't believe that! Why should one faithful country attack another?

It is as I've told you, knight. I got to know about it thanks to my loyal allies abroad only several weeks ago. I informed the King immediately, but he refused to believe me. I was able to convince him in the end, but he didn't do anything. He told me it was the Will of God. He told me Pope Alessander was right—that we all are sinners and godless people who deserved to die by the swords of crusaders!
That sounds like High Treason!

Yes, that's exactly what I told the King. He laughed at me. He shouted at me that he was the King and he could do what he wanted to his land—and that he wanted it vanished in the flames of the Crusade. Can you imagine that, knight? Ultherst would fall under the hoofs of the knights from the other faithful countries! I couldn't just watch it without trying to do anything!
So you killed the King...

Yes, I did. There was nothing else I could do at that moment. I could not overcome my anger. I became a murderer. I'm sincerely sorry about it, but I can't take it back. Immediately after my deed I went to Cardinal Letti and confessed to him. I decided to hand myself over to the justice, but later I realized I wouldn't help anything that way. With the King dead, great part of his authority was passed over to me and I found out I could do something for the Realm. I could try to save it! Thus I postponed the penance. I must secure the defense of the Realm!
Do you want to oppose the crusaders? That would be a deadly sin...

Yes, that's exactly what I want to do, knight. I swore to defend the Realm from both outer and inner enemies and I'm not going to break my oath! I'll prepare the Royal army to fight and I'll march to the field with them. I will lead my men to battle against the imperial crusaders, to fight for our homeland! For Ultherst! God save the Realm!
But that would mean I'd have to let you go...

Yes, that's true. You found out about my crime and came to arrest me. That would mean the end of my effort and probably the end of the Realm. In that case I'd be executed, the new King could name his new First Knight. The new King must be elected by the Realm Assembly of Estates, and just summoning the Assembly would take several months. At that time our Realm would be burned by the fire of war already... completely defenseless and left at the mercy of the rampaging hordes of the plundering crusaders!
I understand. In that case, I'll let you go, Sir Knight, even though I'll never become the Seneschal of the Brotherhood of Righteous. And I hope God will punish you and you'll die in the battle...

I... I don't know what to say, knight! Thank you. Not for myself—my life is meaningless. Thank you for the Realm, knight. With this decision you've done for the Realm more than most of the other people did together! You're a real patriot! I assure you that I'll do all I can not to let the Realm fall! God be with all of us!
I can't let you go, Sir Knight. You're a murderer and you must stand the trial, no matter what your intentions were...

I... yes, knight, you're right. It would be naive to think that I could help the Realm as a sinner—as a murderer. God is angry with me and the time has come to pay for what I did. However, realize one thing, knight—I can't let you arrest me. I can't blacken the honor of the First Knight by letting you put me in chains. There's only one thing I ask from you—challenge me to a duel and let me fall as a Knight! The crime will be punished and the honor of the First Knight will be preserved...
All right, I agree. Sir Rodrigo de Velacor, I challenge you to a duel. Let our weapons decide our case!
Thank you, knight. Farewell to you...
I'm sorry, Sir Knight—you must go with me as a prisoner!

I understand... I that case you don't give me another chance but to commit suicide. My soul will be damned forever, but the honor of the First Knight will be preserved! Farewell, knight... Aaaaaahhhhhhhh...

Who are you, knight? What do you ask from me? I'm very busy at the moment, as you can see! Now, when most of the Royal authority has passed over to my hands I don't have much time for unregistered visitors...
Could I know who you are, Sir Knight?
I'm Don Rodrigo de Velacor, the First Knight of the Ultherst Kingdom, the Grand Duke of Aurelia and the Duke of Ostrakovice, the titular Baron of Olmin and Griss.
I'm honored to meet the highest defender of the Realm...
Wait, knight—did you come to exchange polite phrases with me or do you really want something from me?
I wanted to meet in person the man who should have defended His Majesty King Edward the Second and who obviously failed...

You're right, knight... it's an ineffaceable disgrace for me. That mistake sullied my honor. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, knight?
I'd like to know what is the authority of the First Knight now that King Edward is dead and there isn't any heir to the throne...

In case the Realm loses its leader the First Knight becomes the temporary governor of the Realm, knight. He administrates all the legislative, administrative and judicial duties of the Chief of State until the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a proper heir to the Throne from the highest ranking nobles. He's also the commander-in-chief of the Royal army, of course. Do you need to know something else, knight?
What did you do the moment the King was murdered? Why weren't you near him to protect him?

I don't think I should confess to you, knight. I've already confessed to Cardinal Letti. However, if you want to know about that, the duties of the First Knight don't consist only of protecting His Majesty. I had some duties out of the Royal Palace. There was nothing I could do... However, I agree with you that what happened doesn't decrease my responsibility for it. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, knight?
Nothing specific, in fact.
In that case you'll have to excuse me, knight. I'm very busy, you know? Maybe we'll have an opportunity to talk to each other sometime later.
If you think so, Sir Knight. Farewell.
You have an exotic name, Sir Knight, and the salutation "Don" isn't commonly used in the Realm as well...

You're right, knight. My grandfather was Diego de Velacor, one of the Grand Dukes of the Calmariland Kingdom. During one tournament in Alvaron he met my grandmother, a daughter of the Duke of Mantt, and he decided to stay here in Ultherst when they were married. Since that time the House of Velacor resides here in the Realm, although its roots are deep in the history of the Calmariland Kingdom.
Is that you again, knight? What do you want? I've a lot of work to do...
I'd like to talk to you for a moment, Sir Knight. Would you find some time for me?
All right, as you wish, but try to be brief, will you?
Aaaaahhhhhhh... thanks... thank you, knight... you must... must save Ultherst! I... I failed... God save the... Realm!
Leave in peace, Sir Knight!
Hail to you, knight. I'd like to assure you once more that you made the right decision—I'll prepare the Realm to defend against the Crusade, believe me!
All right. Could I disturb you and talk to you for a moment?
I trust you, Sir Knight. Farewell.

Yes, I know... it's an ineffaceable disgrace for me. That mistake sullied my honor. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, Father?

He administrates all the legislative, administrative and judicial duties of the Chief of State until the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a proper heir to the Throne from the highest ranking nobles. He's also the commander-in-chief of the Royal army, of course. Do you need to know something else, Father?

However, if you want to know about that, the duties of the First Knight don't entail only guarding His Majesty. I had some duties out of the Royal Palace. There was nothing I could do... However, I agree with you that what happened doesn't decrease my responsibility for it. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, Father?
My wound is not your business, Father! But, if you're interested in that... Not long ago I caught a thief who resisted me and he scratched my face before I killed him. Satisfied?

You offend me, Father! You're not going to suspect me of anything as mad as the murder of King Edward! I'm the First Knight, the highest protector of the Realm—whatever I do, I do it for the benefit of the Realm. If you're going to continue offending me, your audience will be terminated before you can say Jack Robinson!
I'm sorry, but revealing a military secret could mean a threat to the safety interests of the Realm. Because of that I can't answer your question, Father. I'm sorry!

You can run into many various monsters in Alvaron and around, Father. I've been a soldier for almost twenty years, but I'm still scared of the undead. You can kill a living opponent with a single well-directed blow, no matter what the opponent looks like. The undead are something completely different. You must hack the dead like a butcher to get them down, and even on the ground they wriggle and kick around themselves like a wild mare. Not talking about the damned souls, horrors and shadows, Father. There's nothing more terrible than an ethereal opponent...

And you're right to agree! Be careful not to stay at the city cemetery after dusk, Father. Living dead feast there on graves and coffins during the nights, spirits flow through the air in the graveyard and nameless horrors lurk in the shadows. He who decides to go there is never seen again—or he's seen as one of them! Even during the day it's not a safe place at all...
I'm sorry, Father, but the knowledge of heretic cults doesn't belong to my priorities. I've never heard about that cult...

Unfortunately, the Baron didn't have a very good relationship with the rest of his family and because of that he decided to hide all his gold somewhere near Alvaron, not to let it get in the hands of his wicked relatives. And so he did—the Baron buried his treasure and died untroubled. I'm sure you can imagine, Father, that people are turning twice every stone in the neighborhood as they're trying to find that treasure...

I've heard about the case of the violation of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert, Father. It's sad that something of that kind could happen—no matter what the truth is. In case Father Nicolas is guilty it would hurt the reputation of the Inquisition. In case Grand Duchess Liana lied it would hurt the reputation of her husband as he's the royal governor of our city. Because of that I must say I'm very sorry the scandal happened—nothing good will come from that.

Have you heard the tale about Duke Manfred Gotfried, Father? It was an awful case of a hidden heresy. All the people knew he was a heretic and what terrible things he made, they were afraid of him like the devil is afraid of the cross, but the Inquisition was never able to gather enough evidence to prove him guilty. The Baron traveled a lot when he was young and he was said to be one of a few faithful people who visited Jad-Habaal, that Realm of the pagan dogs. He was supposed to have brought a damned relic from there, a certain Necklace of Death. The necklace was rumored to bestow supernatural abilities on him—reputedly it allowed him to establish contact with the Other World. The Baron succumbed to the temptation and started to deal with necromancy...
Farewell, Father. God preserve the Realm!

You... you found out about it, Father? Oh my God... not yet, please! There's so much I still have to do and so little time left... However, I'm glad it came so soon. I wouldn't be able to carry that burden for long. I'm a sinner and I must be punished. Well, I hoped I'd be able to save the Realm first. Or at least to try to save it. Maybe it's still not too late!

Yes, Father, I confess. It was me who killed King Edward the Second. I'm deeply sorry about that, but there was nothing else I could have done. I must protect the Realm—even from His Majesty himself, if it's necessary! In this case there was nothing else to do—King Edward was ready to allow the Realm to be completely destroyed!

You don't have the slightest idea what's happening, Father. You think I'm a devious murderer who took the life of King Edward either because of selfish incentives or in the service of the powers of Hell. But I can assure you that's not true. I killed King Edward whom I loved and respected above all, because my oath of the First Knight obliged me to do so!

The First Knight is the highest defender of the Realm and of the Crown, Father. This position obliges its representative not only to protect His Royal Majesty and the Royal family, but also to protect the Realm as such. That's exactly what I had to do—to protect the Realm! Believe me that I loved King Edward like my own father, but I couldn't let him destroy our Realm that I swore to protect!

I didn't understand it as well, Father. Unfortunately,the King's heart was broken when his children died two years ago—he grieved especially for Prince Louis. He changed a lot since that time. He wasn't interested in anything, tried to drown his sorrow in wine... and he didn't realize dark clouds were gathering above Ultherst!

No, Father—although heresy is involved directly in the matter. I'm talking about the crusade. The Pope Alessander the Third proclaimed the crusade against Ultherst several months ago. In the Empire, which used to be our ally for ages, armies of crusaders are gathered even now to invade Ultherst and to perform the Will of God—to kill, to plunder and to destroy!

It is as I've told you, Father. I got to know about it thanks to my loyal allies abroad only several weeks ago. I informed the King immediately, but he refused to believe me. I was able to convince him in the end, but he didn't do anything. He told me it was the Will of God. He told me Pope Alessander was right—that we all are sinners and godless people who deserved to die by the swords of crusaders!

Yes, that's exactly what I told the King. He laughed at me. He shouted at me that he was the King and he could do what he wanted to his land—and that he wanted it vanished in the flames of the Crusade. Can you imagine that, Father? Ultherst would fall under the hoofs of the knights from the other faithful countries! I couldn't just watch it without trying to do anything!

Yes, that's exactly what I want to do, Father. I swore to defend the Realm from both outer and inner enemies and I'm not going to break my oath! I'll prepare the Royal army to fight and I'll march to the field with them. I will lead my men to battle against the imperial crusaders, to fight for our homeland! For Ultherst! God save the Realm!
I understand. In that case, I'll let you go, Sir Knight, even though I'll never become Curial Inquisitor because of that. And I hope God will punish you and you'll die in battle...

I... I don't know what to say, Father! Thank you. Not for myself—my life is meaningless. Thank you for the Realm, Father. With this decision you've done for the Realm more than most of the other people did together! You're a real patriot! I assure you that I'll do all I can not to let the Realm fall! God be with all of us!

I... yes, Father, you're right. It would be naive to think that I could help the Realm as a sinner—as a murderer. God is angry with me and the time has come to pay for what I did. However, realize one thing, Father—I can't let you arrest me. I can't blacken the honor of the First Knight by letting you put me in chains. There's only one thing I ask from you—challenge me to a duel and let me fall as a Knight! The crime will be punished and the honor of the First Knight will be preserved...
Thank you, Father. Farewell to you...

I understand... I that case you don't give me another chance but to commit suicide. My soul will be damned forever, but the honor of the First Knight will be preserved! Farewell, Father... Aaaaaahhhhhhhh...

Who are you, Father? What do you ask from me? I'm very busy at the moment, as you can see! Now, when most of the Royal authority has passed over to my hands I don't have much time for unregistered visitors...
Wait, Father—did you come to exchange polite phrases with me or do you really want something from me?

You're right, Father... it's an ineffaceable disgrace for me. That mistake sullied my honor. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, Father?

In case the Realm loses its leader the First Knight becomes the temporary governor of the Realm, Father. He administrates all the legislative, administrative and judicial duties of the Chief of State until the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a proper heir to the Throne from the highest ranking nobles. He's also the commander-in-chief of the Royal army, of course. Do you need to know something else, Father?

I don't think I should confess to you, Father. I've already confessed to Cardinal Letti. However, if you want to know about that, the duties of the First Knight don't consist only of protecting His Majesty. I had some duties out of the Royal Palace. There was nothing I could do... However, I agree with you that what happened doesn't decrease my responsibility for it. Thus I'll leave public life as soon as the Assembly of Estates is gathered to elect a new King from the highest ranking nobles. Until that time I'll do my best not to let the Realm suffer because of the absence of the Chief of State! So I swear! Do you need to know something else, Father?
In that case you'll have to excuse me, Father. I'm very busy, you know? Maybe we'll have an opportunity to talk to each other sometime later.

You're right, Father. My grandfather was Diego de Velacor, one of the Grand Dukes of the Calmariland Kingdom. During one tournament in Alvaron he met my grandmother, a daughter of the Duke of Mantt, and he decided to stay here in Ultherst when they were married. Since that time the House of Velacor resides here in the Realm, although its roots are deep in the history of the Calmariland Kingdom.
Is that you again, Father? What do you want? I've a lot of work to do...
Aaaaahhhhhhh... thanks... thank you, Father... you must... must save Ultherst! I... I failed... God save the... Realm!
Hail to you, Father. I'd like to assure you once more that you made the right decision—I'll prepare the Realm to defend against the Crusade, believe me!

Amen, sir. His heresy deepened more and more—and soon it wasn't enough for him just to speak with the dead, he wanted to have them around as his servants. So he started to use his Necklace of Death to summon the souls of the dead and then forced them to do his bidding. It's said he was served by living corpses at the table, ghosts cleaned his house and even in bed he found delight in undead harlots. Really appalling. His heresy was ended only by his death, which came for him under shady circumstances in the year 1213. Because heresy was never proven of him he was buried in a nobleman's crypt at the city cemetery.
Farewell, sir. God preserve the Realm!
