Could you tell me what did you do that night when that terrible tempest raged above the city? There's a certain suspicion that you were seen near the scaffold in that time together with a group of hooded people carrying some big bag into the night; a bag big enough to contain a human body...

What? Why are you disturbing me with such nonsense? That's a nasty lie and nothing else! What insolence! How can you accuse me—the descendant of the House Ventano—of something like that! Who told you such a lie? What scoundrel took my name in his mouth?
That's not important. Answer my question.
So you believe that absurdity? Well, all right, if you really want to know what I did, I'll tell you—I was in the city tavern throughout the evening! And now you better leave me alone.
Yan Flemberg, the city executioner, told me about that.

Well, I can't say I'm surprised. I never thought anything good about that man and I'm glad it was affirmed at last. You should be careful about him, knight—his lies could certainly bring misfortune to someone!
So you deny that accusation?

Of course I do, knight. Yan Flemberg is a liar—we played cards and he lost a nice sum of money, so he tries to get me back. That evening when the tempest was raging I was in the city tavern all the time!
Not at all, knight!

Who rules in Glatzburg? Why, Grand Duke Robert Heidrick does, who else should rule here? He's the royal governor of the city. If you're interested in who's the vice-governor, Duke Rowan van Gallagan is. Well, to tell the truth, someone more competent should have been given that position—me, for example. I'll take care about it as soon as I get the title! I'll start as the royal vice-governor and then... who knows what the future will bring...

You want to buy some goods? What do you have in mind? Weapons and armor? In that case go to Hans von Drichtmaul. Or do you want potions and magic items? In that case Enrie Jungwirdt or Paolus Ventimus might help you. You might also find some usable goods in the shops of Wanda Gielwitch or Ludwig Weintraum—they're local innkeepers. Or you can go to Alphonso DiCerbio if you don't mind the origin of his goods.

You want to know what do I think about the current situation in the Realm? Well, I can tell you—I'm not interested much in that, to tell the truth. It's a spiritual question, not a business one, and I'm a businessman. Sure, there are those heretics here and so on, but as far as they pose a threat only to my faith and not to my property, I think you should worry about them instead of me. Well, there's something else—the people in the city tell that the End of the World is coming. But I think that no matter what you're going to call it, it's the time of change that will come. Now we'll see who's well prepared and who isn't. No matter what will happen, you could bet on me—I will be prepared, you can trust me.
I've heard some talk that a war could come. Do you happen to know anything about it?

People talk a lot about a war these days, that's true. Nobody knows anything for sure, all is just unfounded information, but it's true that many things look like as if a war was about to start. However, any war is like blessing for the business. The orders will come one after another. I already have orders for a lot of goods and I'm quite busy to deliver all of it in time. Quilts, boots, belts, covers... various things. God bless us!

Do I suspect someone of heresy? Well... if I were you, I'd be very careful about Enrie Jungwirdt. I'm not some superstitious fool, but if the woman doesn't flirt with the devil then every fish can fly. Have you heard about those visions of her? She's said to be able to see what's happening miles away from her... or even what hasn't happened yet at all. And as for those magic potions of hers... she must have some pact with Satan, that's clear!
Do you have any proof?

No, I don't have any... but if you search her house, I'm sure you'll find some forbidden books, occult items, pagan ritual tools and a lot of other devilment because of which the justice could be satisfied!
Thanks. I'll surely check her.
Yes, knight, you should. It would be better for all of us if she were put to the stake as soon as possible.

Yes, many things have happened that I could talk about. For example, the taxes were raised, as well as the duty, toll and warehousing payments. An absolute disaster! Fortunately I'm a too skilled a businessman to let those obstacles do me too much harm—nobody will get my money so easily!

Do you know Francessca Gulvardi? I suppose you do. She's that possessed girl who tried to kill Bishop Trevorius. Imagine that I succeed to exorcise the impure powers from her and she testified that you arranged her kidnapping. What could you tell me about that?

You mean that I arranged the kidnapping of that lunatic murderess Francessca Gulvardi? That's the greatest nonsense I've heard lately, knight. However, it's a pretty dangerous nonsense, I must say. I wonder you occupy yourself with that—who would believe some bitch possessed by impure spirits? And as for exorcising the impure powers from her... Excuse me, knight, but are you really so sure about it? Satan is a tricky bastard and he's pretty able to pretend what he wants you to see. Many times he can stand even the holy water and in that case there's no way how to find out whether the demon left the possessed body or not. In addition to that you aren't any exorcist. Thus, I dare to doubt your results—no offence. I'm sorry, but you're talking to the wrong person.

I've heard about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, of course, but I don't know any details about it. I've heard the hellspawns killed him somewhere near the Grand Duke's gazebo. What a bad idea, going to such lonely places where death could be hidden almost everywhere...
I've heard about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, of course. I've heard you're suspected of killing him. What will you tell me about that?
I'm the one who asks the questions here.
Yes, I expected something like that. Unfortunately I can't help you anyhow.
I'm not involved in the murder in any way.
Yes, I expected something like that. Well, no offence... In any case I hope the murderer will be caught soon. Bishops shouldn't be murdered on someone's whim.
You're asking me about those dead who walk around the city every night? I think someone should stop them at last. Man shouldn't have to fear for his life when he goes home from the tavern.

Someone stole the Chain of Order from Commander Ethien de Pasque? Well, bad luck for the Commander. I've heard that the Chain of Order is one of the signs of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, something like a relic. He must be very angry. If you want to help him find the thief, knight, go to Tinthan the actor and threaten him properly. I believe he stole the Chain. He's the most skilful thief in the city—or at least he's said to be the most skilful one. He could steal your nose from your face without letting you notice that.

So you're trying to get Chateau de Trebrechette, knight. I must say it won't be easy, I'm sorry. It's the most exquisite wine man can get in the Realm and it's very, very expensive. It's imported to Alvaron by sea from the southern provinces of the Empire and I doubt any merchant would dare to carry such a precious cargo through the roads of our Realm in these days. I haven't seen it being sold for a long time here in Glatzburg. I'm sure you would get it in Alvaron—if you were able to get there alive...
I'm not interested in fairy tales and superstitious rumors. They're good only for small children.
I'm not sure if you realize that if you deny me the answer, some very unpleasant things could happen to you...
I understand—you don't like me. However, I don't see a single reason why you couldn't give me the answer to this question—it won't do anyone any harm!
You're wise and brave, Ventano, that's apparent at first sight. I believe you won't be reluctant to answer one question to a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous...
Nice to meet you, good man. I'm honored to meet a descendant of such a renowned House!

Oh, really? Well... in fact you're right—everyone should be honored to meet me! I wish local so-called nobles realized it too and granted me the title of Baron that should be mine by right. Without my ancestors who helped to build this city by their own hands probably none of them would sit here nowadays. However, things will be changed and I'll be respected, you can bet I will!
What do I mean? I mean that a high noble title will be granted to me for my deeds! Who else other than me would deserve it? Just consider what I've done for the future of our Realm!
Well, what have you done, if I may ask you?
You will see soon yourself, knight. I promise. I can't tell you more at the moment. It's a secret, you know.
Oh, I see. Could I ask you a few questions now?
Questions? What questions? Well, maybe I could give you a bit of my precious time...
You told me you were a merchant. Could I look at your goods in that case?
Yes, so I firmly believe. Could I ask you a few questions now?
If that's the Will of God... Farewell.
The House Ventano? I've never heard of it...
No doubt, knight. God knows where you are from. It's obvious you're not from Glatzburg but from God-knows-where.
Yes, you could say so. In any case I'm honored to meet you.
All right, all right. Tell me, what do you want from me?
I'd like to ask you several questions, if I can.
Enough of the offence! Do you know who you are talking to?
All right, all right, no need to be angry immediately, knight. Your attitude isn't very friendly as well, after all... Tell me, what do you want from me?
My goods? No, I'm afraid you couldn't. I doubt anything I deal in would be useful to you.
Can I ask what you sell?
I make a large-volume business with those articles that are advantageous at the moment. No retail, I'm sorry. Building materials, textiles, carpets...
Raimond Ventano, you're arrested in the name of justice. You were accused of the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi. You'll come with me!

How... pardon? What are you talking about...? I didn't commit anything like that, it's a nasty lie! Who could have told you anything like that? Francessca Gulvardi is possessed by the dark powers, everyone knows that! The bitch tried to kill Bishop Trevorius!
No matter what's the truth, you're arrested, Raimond Ventano. You'll come with me!
Never!
Francessca Gulvardi was exorcised, cleansed of the dark powers that controlled her and so she could testify who arranged her kidnapping. Because of that you'll come with me!
Who are you? What do you want? I have no time, I must attend to my business!
Sorry to bother you. I was interested in who you might be...

You're interested in who I am? Can you tell me why? Is that any business of yours? Do you think you can come here and ask me questions without me knowing who you are and what you want from me? Well, when you've already asked who were you honored to meet, I'll tell you. My name is Raimond Ventano, when you want to know. Yes, you've heard well—Ventano! I'm the heir of the ancient House Ventano who helped to found this city entire millennium ago!
Tell me who you are immediately! Don't you see who you are honored to talk to?

I don't see a single reason why I have to answer your rude question! But if you really want to know, I'll tell you. My name is Raimond Ventano. Yes, you've heard well—Ventano! I'm the heir of the ancient House Ventano who helped to found this city entire millennium ago!
I'm sorry, I didn't want to bother you. I can see you've more important things to do. I'd better go.
Yes, you're right, knight, I have VERY important things to do. After all, a man of such an origin and importance such as me has some important things to do ANYTIME!
Yes, that's true. Could I ask what your name is, Sir Baron? Or Sir Duke? Or maybe even...

Oh no, don't exaggerate, knight. I'm not a noble man... although doubtless any of those titles should belong to me—rightly! Because I'm Raimond Ventano. Yes, you've heard well—Ventano! I'm the heir of the ancient House Ventano who helped to found this city entire millennium ago!
It's you again, knight? What do you want? Can't you see I must devote myself to my business?
Well, as you want, but try to be brief, knight. I'm a very busy man!
I just happened to come by, I didn't want to disturb you. Farewell.
Behold, knight, I give up! Mercy! I'll come with you, just don't kill me!
I'm glad you've decided to surrender, Ventano. However, for an assault on me I sentence you to forfeiture of property. Let's go.

Well, I can't say I'm surprised. I never thought anything good about that man and I'm glad it was affirmed at last. You should be careful about him, Father—his lies could certainly bring misfortune to someone!

Of course I do, Father. Yan Flemberg is a liar—we played cards and he lost a nice sum of money, so he tries to get me back. That evening when the tempest was raging I was in the city tavern all the time!
Not at all, Father!
Yes, Father, you should. It would be better for all of us if she were put to the stake as soon as possible.

You mean that I arranged the kidnapping of that lunatic murderess Francessca Gulvardi? That's the greatest nonsense I've heard lately, Father. However, it's a pretty dangerous nonsense, I must say. I wonder you occupy yourself with that—who would believe some bitch possessed by impure spirits? And as for exorcising the impure powers from her... Excuse me, Father, but are you really so sure about it? Satan is a tricky bastard and he's pretty able to pretend what he wants you to see. Many times he can stand even the holy water and in that case there's no way how to find out whether the demon left the possessed body or not. In addition to that you aren't any exorcist. Thus, I dare to doubt your results—no offence. I'm sorry, but you're talking to the wrong person.

Someone stole the Chain of Order from Commander Ethien de Pasque? Well, bad luck for the Commander. I've heard that the Chain of Order is one of the signs of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, something like a relic. He must be very angry. If you want to help him find the thief, Father, go to Tinthan the actor and threaten him properly. I believe he stole the Chain. He's the most skilful thief in the city—or at least he's said to be the most skilful one. He could steal your nose from your face without letting you notice that.

So you're trying to get Chateau de Trebrechette, Father. I must say it won't be easy, I'm sorry. It's the most exquisite wine man can get in the Realm and it's very, very expensive. It's imported to Alvaron by sea from the southern provinces of the Empire and I doubt any merchant would dare to carry such a precious cargo through the roads of our Realm in these days. I haven't seen it being sold for a long time here in Glatzburg. I'm sure you would get it in Alvaron—if you were able to get there alive...
You're wise and brave, Ventano, that's clear at the first sight. I believe you won't be reluctant to answer one question to a humble priest...
You will see soon yourself, Father. I promise. I can't tell you more at the moment. It's a secret, you know.
No doubt, Father. God knows where you are from. It's obvious you're not from Glatzburg but from God-knows-where.
All right, all right, no need to be angry immediately, Father. Your attitude isn't very friendly as well, after all... Tell me, what do you want from me?
Yes, you're right, Father, I have VERY important things to do. After all, a man of such an origin and importance such as me has some important things to do ANYTIME!

Well, as you want, but try to be brief, Father. I'm a very busy man!
Behold, Father, I give up! Mercy! I'll come with you, just don't kill me!

There are many legends told about Glatzburg, knight. It's an ancient city with roots stretched as far to the past as the year 223 when the nearby town of Galibornium was captured—it was the capital of the Erebornian province Filkland in those days. I'm sure you know about it. Well, many people use the legends and tales as a source of entertainment or thrill, but I'm always trying to find a grain of truth in every legacy of the past. To tell the truth, I've found many interesting facts or at least assumptions thanks to this approach. Look at the legend of St. Orthenius, for example. I'm sure you've heard it already, haven't you?

Oh yes, sure. The hero will come in hard times who will take up the relic of St. Orthenius, which is called the Inquisitor, and with the help of this relic he will defeat the enemies of the faith and of the Realm.

Yes, exactly. Nicely summarized, I must say. However, you must realize that what you've just said are tales that have been passing on via oral tradition from one generation to another for many hundred years! How could we be sure St. Orthenius really foretold something like that? What if some people who just needed to tell a good story inserted some words into his mouth?
So you think the legend isn't true at all?

I didn't say that, knight. On the contrary, I think there's quite a lot of truth to that legend. However, the grains must be separated from the chaff at first. I spent quite a long time dealing with that legend and I studied its sources and other related links in the process. I concluded that the reference about the Inquisitor relic is true. Orthenius really had to have some very powerful weapon, otherwise nobody would mention it and the people would talk about superhuman power of his arms and so on. However, I don't believe the fate of our faith and of our Realm depends on the qualities of the weapon as such—no matter how excellent the qualities of the weapon were. That's nonsense, of course.
Where do you think the relic could be right now?

That's the question I tried to answer by the means of studying sources from that period, as well as tales of common people. Unfortunately I wasn't successful. There isn't a single reference where the relic could be and what happened to it after St. Orthenius died. However, I believe one source exists that contains this information—or at least a hint of it. It's the original text of the legend, written by Killian the chronicler in the 3rd century—that is immediately after Orthenius's death. I was looking for that source carefully in all the libraries and archives I could get into, but I didn't find it. I ran into some hints that the original handwritten work of Killian the chronicler could be deposited in the secret libraries of the Holy Mother Church somewhere in the Archbishop's Palace in Alvaron. That means it's absolutely inaccessible for me, so I've stopped my research regarding the matter.
I'd like to hear it, if you agree.

Of course, knight. Well, the legend about St. Orthenius tells how this great holy man, warlord and later also the patron of our Realm led the armies of all the faithful men to victory over the pagan realm of Ereborn here in the Filkland Peninsula in the year 223. He fought in the first line in most of the battles and he always was the one who caused the victory because he was able to get his fellow fighters into some kind of battle frenzy. However, he was a renowned fighter especially thanks to a powerful relic called The Inquisitor, reputedly blessed by the First Prophet himself.

Nobody knows exactly what the weapon looked like, but legend says it was able to destroy dozens of pagans with each strike and it spread death wherever it was swayed. Soon the people started to believe that thanks to that relic Ereborn was defeated here in the Filkland Peninsula and that the relic was a gift from God given to St. Orthenius to ensure protection of the faith, church and of the Realm itself—as became obvious in the end. The legend further says that St. Orthenius foretold on his death bed that when the true faith would be threatened again, his follower would be found among the common people and he'd take over the relic to fight the enemies and to achieve another glorious victory.
That sounds promising, doesn't it?

No, knight. The whole thing is pure nonsense. Just imagine it—a savior will appear in the time of danger to save everyone. This theme can be found in almost any folk tale. Common people want to be comforted by the vision that in the time of the greatest need someone will come and do something to bring the good times back. But it doesn't work that way, as all of us know so well.

I didn't say that, knight. On the contrary, I think there's quite a lot of truth in that legend. However, the grains must be separated from the chaff at first. I spent quite a long time dealing with that legend and I studied its sources and other related links in the process. I concluded that the reference about the Inquisitor relic is true. Orthenius really had to have some very powerful weapon, otherwise nobody would mention it and the people would talk about superhuman power of his arms and so on. However, I don't believe the fate of our faith and of our Realm depends on the qualities of the weapon as such—no matter how excellent the qualities of the weapon were. That's pure nonsense, of course.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of the city, knight. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor. According to what I've heard they don't like each other very much. Politics, you know... Thank God I'm a scientist and so I can leave these profane things to other people.

As for weapons and armor, you can buy the best goods from Hans von Drichtmaul, who has his renowned armory here in Glatzburg. Potions and magic items—similar to my own goods—can be bought also from Enrie Jungwirdt the wise woman—if you don't mind her erratic nature. Wanda Gielwitch and Ludwig Weintraum, our local innkeepers, both have shops with various goods. And you can exchange many things with Alphonso DiCerbio, if you don't mind the origin of his goods. Several times I bought my own property from him.

To tell the truth, knight, I knew very well that the crisis would come. No need to be surprised—I'm the Master of Alchemy and thus I must be prepared for such events. A long time before the Star of Doom appeared in the sky in 1219, I was finding signs everywhere in the Realm that could have meant only one thing—great shift in the Power. The change of the whole Pondus aeternum, the eternal balance. Erebornian philosophers called it diespothe malcius—the time of the change. However, no matter what you're going to call it, it had been clear for a long time that something big and really unpleasant would happen. And so it did—the Scourges of God shook the Realm like the ship in the tempest.
What do you think it was caused by? Why did the Power—as you call it—start to shift? What's behind the change?

I don't know, knight. I can't tell you. I can tell you that God is the source of all the Power and that it all was the will of God, if you want to hear something like that. However, I don't believe it personally. I believe God is a part of the Power, he isn't the Creator of Power. No need to be shocked, knight—I'm not preaching any heretic heterodoxy to you. Many renowned and wise clerical thinkers wrote about this theory—for example Jacob of Ayolla or Giorgio de Companella. It's only a part of the scientific theory; it isn't a dogma. But to return to the issue—I really don't know what caused such a shift of the Power. Who can tell why a volcano erupted? Who knows why the earthquake occurs? Really, I don't know, knight.
Well... You're talking about very strange things. What about the faith? What about the Scriptures? Are they not involved?

Of course they are, knight. Because faith—in the way you look at it—is a part of the Power too. It's a component of the momentum of our Universe—maybe the most important one. The Scriptures discuss faith—and from this point of view I dare say it's somewhat mystically written alchemical work. I admit the matter is very complex, knight. I wasn't able to fathom it completely myself, although I devoted almost all my life to the studies of alchemy.
Well, how do you see the things?

The fact is that there is an all embracing and all permeating Power here that has been changing the World around us as well as the movement of the Earth has been changing the landscape during the eons. Something important happened before the Scourges of God came—the shift of Power was accompanied by some external manifestations—the signs that skilled alchemists, astrologers or even common village wise women could see and recognize. It was like as if the swallows were flying low above the ground before the storm...
I've heard some talking that a war would come. Do you happen to know anything about it?
I've heard some talking about a war, but I'm not much interested in it. The war isn't my field of interest.
Maybe it's not your field of interest, but if the war does come, it will affect you anyway...

Yes, you're right, knight—the demand for the healing potions would increase, as well as the prices. Nevertheless I hope there won't be any war. In addition to that it isn't clear to me whom should be the war declared to. There isn't a single enemy around here. The pagan from the Far East aren't a threat to us, I can't see anyone marching to the Realm... so I don't have the slightest idea whom should be the war waged against.

From time to time the hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns attack people around Glatzburg. Maybe you've already heard about them—they dwell in deep caverns located near the ruins of Galibornium. I was lucky enough to get the body of one such beast and could study it properly. You'll be surprised, knight, but I found out they aren't hellspawns of any kind—at least they didn't come from the Hell. Although they look like devils at the first sight, because they have scales on their skin, lizard head and a long tail with prickles, many of their inner parts are human-like, as I found out during the autopsy.
What do you want to say, Master Alchemist?

I want to say those lizards are human in fact. Yes, it may sound like a heresy, because human was created according to the image of God, but it is as I say—the science proved it clearly! Long ago, somebody—or something—changed them into the form in which we know them nowadays. It's hard to say what changed them. Maybe a curse, or some pagan mages and alchemists... who knows? However, no matter what the truth really is, they're bloodthirsty invaders now and there isn't any place for them in God's Kingdom on Earth. Unfortunately, I've heard they multiply quickly, their assaults from the Devil's Caverns to the neighborhood of Glatzburg occur much more often now and the creatures are more courageous than they used to be.

To tell the truth, knight, I've heard many funny accusations of heresy lately that I can't help myself but laugh. For example that someone's cow was bewitched by someone not to give milk anymore; that someone infatuated someone's wife to spread her legs for him; that Enrie Jungwirdt makes hellish potions and uses her broom to fly to Sabbaths; that Grand Duke Heidrick sold his soul to Satan in exchange for the rule over Glatzburg for the rest of his life...
You don't believe anything of that?

All those accusations are pure nonsense, of course, but shiver runs down my spine when I realize that a lot of people were burned for similar nonsense. Because of that I'm somewhat cautious as for the accusation of heresy and I prefer to think about it before I tell something like that to someone. It's beneath my dignity to try to get rid of people I don't like by the means of the Inquisition.
That's reasonable. However, not all suspicions are either fabricated or pure nonsense...

Yes, that's true. You can trust me that if I had a reasonable suspicion that someone I knew was a heretic or a cultist, I'd tell the Holy Office immediately. Well, I'm frankly glad I don't know any heretic, because any contact with the Inquisition can be dangerous for a common mortal. You must know it well yourself—sometimes there isn't much difference between the witness and the accused.
I agree with that. Thanks.
What has happened here lately? You mean this spring?

Well... what could be interesting enough for you? I'm not going to cloy you with my success to distill fluidum glaviernicum et malifaciarum, or with the fact I was able to improve the recipe of Master Giovani Abrachiaci. You might be interested in crimes and things like that, right? In that case I must say there was an attempt to kill Bishop Trevorius. Maybe you've heard about it already... people talk about it a lot now. A Grand Duke's maid—Francessca Gulvardi—tried to murder the Bishop of our diocese. I know it sounds strange, but it really happened!

That quiet and delicate girl attacked the Bishop during confession, cracked the confessional and scattered its pieces all around. She tried to bite the Bishop's neck with her teeth. Fortunately, His Excellence has not only a strong soul, he has also good physical strength and constitution, so he was able to defend himself, although he had to struggle with all his might. No doubt the girl was possessed by some impure spirit, incubus or some other demon, because how could she be so wild and powerful otherwise? I've already heard about such cases... but I'd have never thought one day I'd see it happen so near to me.

I don't know much about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, knight. Only the same as others know—that he was found near the Grand Duke's gazebo. God knows why he went to such a place... Well, to tell the truth, I can't say I was surprised. Francessca Gulvardi tried to murder the Bishop not long ago. The Bishop must have known someone—or something—tried to kill him, so he should have been very careful about where to go and who to meet. However, how could I judge the incentives of a servant of God?
You don't suspect anyone in particular?

No, knight. I don't know about anybody who would do that. The Bishop had some enemies, that's true. Surely you've heard he belonged to the radical priests who strive for the return to the original mission of the church—to the service to God and to people. Many clergymen don't like it, of course. Why should a high priest want to give his property away, to stop collecting the tithes, leave the politics and go to serve the ill and people in need? Thus I think the murder of the Bishop can have something to do with that.
Not at all, knight. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon. Monsignor Trevorius was an admirable man.

I've been studying the history of the pagan civilization of the Elenians for some time and I was surprised how many references pointed exactly here, to the neighborhood of Glatzburg. Before the Scourges of God stroke, I succeeded to explore the large area around the mansion of Baron Edgar von Hunth and I must say I found a lot of remains of the realm of the Elenians. Although I didn't find what I was looking for, I was fascinated. Because of that, I recommend you to focus your search for the burial chamber of that Elenian noble in this direction.
Do you happen to know some details about the priest Frederick?

I knew the priest Frederick in person, knight. Not too well, because he was only less than three years here in Glatzburg, but we talked about demons and about exorcising them quite often. He used to be a renowned exorcist, in case you didn't know. During the time when he practiced those dangerous rituals he succeeded in banishing dozens of demons from bodies of possessed people. He wasn't any quack who only pretended the exorcism—he was a real exorcist, an expert in the right place, although he was a bit eccentric. I was very sorry when death took him two years ago—he was a real well of knowledge for me in the areas I hadn't explored much yet.

I'm not an expert in the area of the after-death revenge, knight. It's out of my field of interest. I'm interested in materium, in the matter—I don't study religion and spiritual aspects of our existence. Because of that I can't advise you how to get rid of Istwan de Bragho. I suppose you tried everything you were able to try. However... try asking Enrie Jungwirdt to help you. She's the most skilled person in that area of expertise.
Do you want to hear what I really think about the Fallen Angels, or what does the Scriptures say?
I'd like to hear both of it.

I see. So—the Scriptures tell us that the Fallen Angels are the servants of Satan, executors of his will, and disseminators of sin. They're former angelic beings, but when God threw them down from the sky for the sins they committed against him, they became the hellspawns. They're chained in Hell and try to get to our world from there, using their impure powers and plenty of minions. They can't enter our world themselves because our true faith is guarding God's Kingdom on Earth like an angelic shield—it prevents them from doing so.
I see, and what about your opinion?

That's a little bit more complicated, knight. The Scriptures consider the Fallen Angels to be some kind of beings, creatures having certain characteristics and rather specific look. I don't think it's so simple. I don't want to say it's not true at all—that would be close to heresy, of course. I'm only trying to look at it from another—strictly scientific—perspective. Look at the thunder and at the lightning, for example—primitive pagans believed some God of Thunder existed who sometimes got angry, thundered with his terrible voice and threw lightning bolts all around. They projected that God with many details, so that man could think he really was their fellow. However, all of us know what thunder and lightning really are. What if there's something like that for the Fallen Angels?

Look at it in detail, knight. We have Arthamon here, the Lord of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the devilish Queen of Fornication, and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the First Emissary of Satan's will. Arthamon embodies the element of ruination, of total doom, destruction, the manifestation of the anti-matter. What if I told you any of the Fallen Angel didn't exist—that he was just a personification of the powers that harmed and thwarted all what existed? It's the same for Baphomet—surely madness is an element of Chaos, thus it's condemnable and it was personified into Baphomet to let the faithful set their hate upon a specific creature. Even more easy it's for Cerdie—she's a courtesan of Hell who tempts both men and women to infidelity, destroys marriages and turns people to the Chaos. The Fallen Angel Azrael is the personification of all bad things Satan has on his conscience, that is all evil not being attributed to any of the other Chaos elements.
Do you want to say the Fallen Angels don't exist themselves? That there's no need to fear them? That's a heresy!

Not at all, knight. I don't declare they don't exist—exactly to the contrary. We must fear them and we must face their plots. I only want to say I don't believe that these beings exist in the material conception. I don't believe there's a person named Arthamon or Baphomet in some infernal cavern. Look at the examples of the summoning of Hell forces—lower demons always take the appearance that their summoners imagined. So you can meet for example the demon Gaugliel described both as a horned multi-head beast and like a huge black snake singing with a velvet voice; and that's exactly what I think about the Fallen Angels.

To tell the truth, knight, I'm looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul myself. I hope you won't be angry when I keep my results to myself. I'll tell you just some of the facts you probably know already—the hammer was made for Bonhart by one of the most renowned Masters of Alchemy, André Juliano Vestrenniol, who lived in 899–988. That's why I'm trying to find the hammer—I'd like to study it and try to reveal some of Vestrenniol's secrets. The hammer should be buried somewhere around Glatzburg together with the Bonhart's treasure—but I'm not interested in the treasure. All I want is the hammer.

Where you could get Chateau de Trebrechette? It's easy, knight. Go to Alvaron, the royal capital where the wine is brought from the Southern Empire, and buy some there. Of course you'll have to be lucky to get some, because I've heard the trade has been diminishing since the Scourges of God. You won't get it here in Glatzburg anyway—it's hard to buy basic food nowadays, not talking about such an exquisite wine. The city will be starving soon if things keep going the direction they are.
I found this piece of strange ore, master blacksmith. Do you happen to know what it could be?
Show me what you have, knight... why, this is the Philosopher's stone! Yes, no doubt it is!

It is a rustic name for a rare mineral Astratus Lungis. The secret of the origin of this mineral hasn't been discovered yet, but it is true that there's a lot of magic in it. With a dash of craftsmanship it can be turned into any other metal—gold is most popular, of course, but smiths like to use it for forging weapons and armor. I could turn each Philosopher's stone you bring me into gold for you, if you wish—for a small fee, of course.
Of course, knight. I can turn each Philosopher's stone you bring me into gold for you.
I'd answer if I were you, Master Alchemist. You never know what unpleasant things could happen to you when you impetuously refuse to give information to the Brotherhood of the Righteous...
It's your right not to like me, Master Alchemist. However I believe you're intelligent enough to realize your answer won't do any harm to anyone.
Your wisdom and erudition is renowned, Master Alchemist. I would be honored if you answered my question
For example?

Six-legged bulls with several heads and many pairs of horns, winged women with lion claws and lizard legs, ten-headed snakes having bodies of basilisks, animals similar to those which lived in our world in times long before the era of the first pagan civilizations... Well, when I studied all those fragments of the past, I concluded that the gladiator games in Galibornium were renowned exactly thanks to the monsters the gladiators fought against.
I understand—but I still don't see the connection with the Chalice of Metamorphosis.

I'm getting to the point, knight. It wasn't clear to me where the monsters came from. For a long time it was a mystery for me, but one day I found a certain scroll mentioning the Chalice of Metamorphosis. Probably it was some relic or an alchemical artifact thanks to which the Erebornian clerics and alchemists were able to turn a living creature into any monster they wanted! Do you understand, knight? They were able to morph living beings according to their mad ideas and thus they created the warriors fighting the gladiators in the Coliseum! That was the source of the renowned gladiator games of Galibornium! I found other details during my studies and many years of difficult investigations. The Chalice of Metamorphosis was kept in Galibornium just under the Coliseum, in deep cellars where the Erebornian priests performed their mad experiments.
Now I understand it all. You would like to study that artifact and to reveal its secret, wouldn't you?

Yes, exactly, knight. I believe that if I could puzzle out its secret, I could reveal new horizons of the modern alchemy this way. Maybe I could look behind the horizon of the Principle of Godly Creation itself... That would be an epochal discovery, knight! However, I need to get the Chalice of Metamorphosis first to do that. I've heard you solved many troubles... Because of that I thought you could help me.
All right, I agree. I'll look for the Chalice.

Excellent, knight! I knew you would help me; and not only me—if you'll be able to find the Chalice, you'll help science as a whole. If I'll be able to reveal its secret, of course! With such a discovery I surely could get to a leading position in the Royal Alchemists Guild!
We'll see if our search will be successful. Could I ask you a few questions now?
Of course you can, knight. I'll gladly answer all your questions, just ask.
I must find the Chalice first. I'd rather start immediately. Farewell for now.
Where do you think the artifact could be located? Maybe it was destroyed or lost forever?

I don't think so, knight. All the references regarding the Chalice of Metamorphosis suggest that it was kept in Galibornium just under the Coliseum. When the armies of the faithful seized Galibornium in 223, St. Orthenius ordered the dungeon, as a symbol of pagan decay and perversity, to be immured not to let anybody in—but also not to let anybody out. Thus he sentenced all the Erebornian people who were currently in there to a terrible death of starvation. It's said that the souls of the dead there have not found eternal peace and wander through the cellars even nowadays. Some people who went to the ruins of Galibornium to search for hidden treasures declared they had heard strange noises and moaning from the dungeons under the Coliseum...
I think I don't like it at all... Some secrets should stay unrevealed. The Principle of Creation belongs to our God and trying to reveal it is very close to heresy!

No, I don't think so, knight. Why in that case would God give man the thirst for knowledge, as well as the unfaltering will to reveal all the hidden secrets? If our God didn't want man to reveal the principles of function of the surrounding world, surely he would prevent him from doing so.
If I bring you the Chalice of Metamorphosis, you'll surely reward me, won't you?

Of course I will, knight! I'll reward your effort gladly. What would you say to a pouch of gold and some magic item in addition to that? I think it would be more than a generous reward for your effort, don't you think so?
I'm sorry, but I'm not going to accept your quest. You'll have to find some solution yourself.
Well, what can I do. However, I'm not going to stop my investigation until I get and inspect the Chalice of Metamorphosis!
You have the right to do it, of course. However, I'd like to ask you a few questions now.
All right, knight, ask me. Maybe you'll be lucky to find some answers you seek.
Sure. Good luck. Farewell.
Have you ever heard about the Chalice of Metamorphosis?
The Chalice of Metamorphosis? No, it doesn't ring the bell. What should it be?

It's a relic from the pagan realm of Ereborn. You know, knight, I spend a lot of time studying the Erebornian art of alchemy. You can't imagine how many things were invented several millennia ago—there are even areas in which we're still behind them. Many secrets were forgotten or even lost forever during the bloody year 223 when Ereborn was defeated. I study existing fragments of the past carefully, because new knowledge can be often found that way and from time to time a really great secret is revealed.
It says nothing to me, but it sounds somehow... pagan.

Yes, you're right, knight. It's a relic from the pagan realm of Ereborn. You know, knight, I spend a lot of time studying the Erebornian art of alchemy. You can't imagine how many things were invented several millennia ago—there are even areas in which we're still behind them. Many secrets were forgotten or even lost forever during the bloody year 223 when the Ereborn was defeated. I study existing fragments of the past carefully, because new knowledge can be often found this way and from time to time a really great secret is revealed.
I'm sorry, but I don't have much time to do that. I've an urgent mission.
I see. Forget it in that case. What did you want to ask?
Well... don't you think it's close to heresy? To highlight the pagan arts in comparison with the faithful ones...

No, knight, I don't think so. There's nothing forbidden in it. In 1107, King Raul the First approved the Royal Alchemist Guild to investigate and to study the Erebornian science. You can't imagine what secrets are hidden deep in the past...
How is it connected with the Chalice of Metamorphosis, Master Alchemist? Is it some forgotten Erebornian secret?

Yes, exactly, knight. I'm sure you know the ruins of the ancient Erebornian town of Galibornium are located near Glatzburg. It used to be the province capital and thus it was a jewel among other towns here in the Filkland Peninsula. Above all, the gladiator games were the source of its power and glory. You know what the gladiator games were, don't you?
I don't know much about it to tell the truth.

Gladiator games were a bloody entertainment of the fallen Erebornian society. Games were performed in the Coliseum, round building with many tribunes and the battle arena in the middle. Even now the remnants of the building can be found in the ruins of Galibornium. The first gladiators were slaves, war prisoners and criminals convicted to find death in the middle of the Coliseum for the amusement of Erebornian people. It was a kind of execution in fact. Erebornian soldiers fought unarmed convicts and competed in the number of killed people.

However, the Erebornians soon found out that it was much more fun to give weapons to the convicts who fought each other for the amusement of the audience. The victor was allowed to stay alive; it was a good incentive for the gladiators to fight really hard. That popular means of execution led to the founding of the gladiator games in the form we know from the late Erebornian literature.

To keep the audience satisfied as much as possible, new terrible enemies were sent to fight the gladiators—fierce beasts, wild monsters and a lot of various vermin common in those days. The more dangerous enemy, the better was the entertainment. According to the dangerousness of the enemies the gladiator slaughtered he gained the favor of the audience. During several hundred years of the existence of the gladiator games some gladiators became so popular that they were even more famous than many politics or warlords.
Thanks for the explanation. Go on, please.

Oh, sure. Well, as I've already said, the gladiators didn't fight only human enemies, but also various beasts imported from every corner of the known world. However, the one who would study all the available sources regarding that abhorrent entertainment carefully would find out that during the last several decades of the existence of Ereborn there were so bizarre monsters sent to fight gladiators that neither the nature nor some mad pagan God could have created something like that.
Of course I know what the gladiator games were. Go on.

In that case you probably also know that the gladiators fought not only against humans—as it used to be at the beginning of this bloody entertainment—but also against other various enemies: fierce beasts imported from every corner of the known world or wild monsters living in the world in those times. However, the one who would study all the available sources regarding that abhorrent entertainment carefully would find out that during the last several decades of the existence of Ereborn there were so bizarre monsters sent to fight gladiators that neither the nature nor some mad pagan God could have created something like that.
I have a philosopher's stone here, master alchemist. I'd like to have it transmuted into gold.
As you wish, knight. There's nothing more powerful than a good chest of gold, is there? Wait a moment, please...

That's no ordinary stone, knight—just to the contrary. It's an extremely precious substance which is renowned for it's ability to be turned into almost any other unliving substance. The only limitation is to find new substances to turn it into. Well... it's finished, knight. Here's your gold. If you wouldn't object, I'd just take my share as a reward.

I can see I have a special guest here today—a member of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Welcome, knight. Guests are always welcome at my home. I don't think we know each other yet. My name is Paolus Ventimus, and I'm the Master of Alchemy. What can I do for you?
You're the Master of Alchemy? Surely you sell various potions, don't you?

Oh yes, of course. I sell some potions. I can prepare quite a lot of various potions and elixirs in fact. I'm a student of the best Masters of the Royal Alchemist Guild in the Realm and I'm the most renowned alchemist here in Glatzburg. If you're interested in something, just tell me. My shop is always at your disposal.
Thank you. Could I look at the goods you offer?
Of course, knight. Come closer. Well, but you better don't forget the customers have to pay also for the goods they break.
I'm sure I'll use your offer in the future. I'd like to ask you a few questions now.
As you wish, knight. Both my shop and my alchemy laboratory are at your disposal whenever you need. However, before you start questioning me, could I have a question for you?
It was nice meeting you, Master Alchemist. I'll surely come back when I'll need your services. Farewell for now.
Farewell, knight. I'm sure we'll see each other again soon.
Hello, knight. How are you? Do you need anything from my shop? Or maybe you bring me good news, such as you found the Chalice of Metamorphosis, right?
I'm sorry, but I don't bring you the Chalice of Metamorphosis yet.
Never mind. I'm sure you'll be lucky enough to find it in the end. Now, what can I do for you?
Yes, It is as you say. I have good news for you. I found the Chalice of Metamorphosis. Here you are.

Oh, really? Aren't you joking, knight? You really found the Chalice of Metamorphosis?! That's absolutely fantastic! Show it to me... Oh my God! I never thought it would get into my hands... that's phenomenal! It hides so many secrets and mysteries... I'll start investigating them immediately. It must give away the knowledge it's hiding! The secret of Metamorphosis must be revealed once and for all!
I'm glad you're happy, Master Alchemist.
Happy? I'm absolutely overjoyed, knight! Here's a pouch of gold for your effort—and here's a very rare relic in addition to that. I'm sure you can use it.
Thanks. Could I interrupt your studies and ask you a few questions? I promise it won't take much time.
Oh yes, sure... but be brief, will you? I'd like to start revealing the mysteries of the Chalice of Metamorphosis as soon as possible!
My goods? Oh yes, sure. My goods. Could you look at it quickly, please? I'd like to start revealing the mysteries of the Chalice of Metamorphosis as soon as possible!
I have a few questions I'd like you to answer.
Questions, you say? All right, you can ask. Maybe you'll find what you seek.
I'll answer your questions gladly, knight. However, before you start questioning me, could I have a question for you?
I'd like to see your goods, if you won't mind.
To tell the truth, knight, I'm very busy at the moment. I'm fully devoted to solving the mysteries hidden in the Chalice of Metamorphosis. What would you like?
I'd like to talk to you, Master Alchemist.
As you wish, knight. Well, but try to be brief, will you?
Well, but try to be brief, knight.
Nothing in fact. I'll leave you to do your research. Farewell.

Of course. First we crush the root in the Petri dish and pour it into the flask. Then we spill in some crushed stardust and a Gautieria fungus, add some clean water and let it stand for a while. Then we'll pour the solution into the boiler and let it distill... Well, it's done. Here's the potion from the magic mandrake root. Use it cautiously, knight it's a powerful essence alluring evil powers!

It's an ancient city with roots stretched as far to the past as the year 223 when the nearby town of Galibornium was captured—it was the capital of the Erebornian province Filkland in those days. I'm sure you know about it. Well, many people use the legends and tales as a source of entertainment or thrill, but I'm always trying to find a grain of truth in every legacy of the past. To tell the truth, I've found many interesting facts or at least assumptions thanks to this approach. Look at the legend of St. Orthenius, for example. I'm sure you've heard it already, haven't you?

I didn't say that, Father. On the contrary, I think there's quite a lot of truth to that legend. However, the grains must be separated from the chaff at first. I spent quite a long time dealing with that legend and I studied its sources and other related links in the process. I concluded that the reference about the Inquisitor relic is true. Orthenius really had to have some very powerful weapon, otherwise nobody would mention it and the people would talk about superhuman power of his arms and so on. However, I don't believe the fate of our faith and of our Realm depends on the qualities of the weapon as such—no matter how excellent the qualities of the weapon were. That's nonsense, of course.

Of course, Father. Well, the legend about St. Orthenius tells how this great holy man, warlord and later also the patron of our Realm led the armies of all the faithful men to victory over the pagan realm of Ereborn here in the Filkland Peninsula in the year 223. He fought in the first line in most of the battles and he always was the one who caused the victory because he was able to get his fellow fighters into some kind of battle frenzy. However, he was a renowned fighter especially thanks to a powerful relic called The Inquisitor, reputedly blessed by the First Prophet himself.

No, Father. The whole thing is pure nonsense. Just imagine it—a savior will appear in the time of danger to save everyone. This theme can be found in almost any folk tale. Common people want to be comforted by the vision that in the time of the greatest need someone will come and do something to bring the good times back. But it doesn't work that way, as all of us know so well.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of the city, Father. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor. According to what I've heard they don't like each other very much. Politics, you know... Thank God I'm a scientist and so I can leave these profane things to other people.

To tell the truth, Father, I knew very well that the crisis would come. No need to be surprised—I'm the Master of Alchemy and thus I must be prepared for such events. A long time before the Star of Doom appeared in the sky in 1219, I was finding signs everywhere in the Realm that could have meant only one thing—great shift in the Power. The change of the whole Pondus aeternum, the eternal balance. Erebornian philosophers called it diespothe malcius—the time of the change. However, no matter what you're going to call it, it had been clear for a long time that something big and really unpleasant would happen. And so it did—the Scourges of God shook the Realm like the ship in the tempest.

I don't know, Father. I can't tell you. I can tell you that God is the source of all the Power and that it all was the will of God, if you want to hear something like that. However, I don't believe it personally. I believe God is a part of the Power, he isn't the Creator of Power. No need to be shocked, Father—I'm not preaching any heretic heterodoxy to you. Many renowned and wise clerical thinkers wrote about this theory—for example Jacob of Ayolla or Giorgio de Companella. It's only a part of the scientific theory; it isn't a dogma. But to return to the issue—I really don't know what caused such a shift of the Power. Who can tell why a volcano erupted? Who knows why the earthquake occurs? Really, I don't know, Father.

Of course they are, Father. Because faith—in the way you look at it—is a part of the Power too. It's a component of the momentum of our Universe—maybe the most important one. The Scriptures discuss faith—and from this point of view I dare say it's somewhat mystically written alchemical work. I admit the matter is very complex, Father. I wasn't able to fathom it completely myself, although I devoted almost all my life to the studies of alchemy.

Yes, you're right, Father—the demand for the healing potions would increase, as well as the prices. Nevertheless I hope there won't be any war. In addition to that it isn't clear to me whom should be the war declared to. There isn't a single enemy around here. The pagan from the Far East aren't a threat to us, I can't see anyone marching to the Realm... so I don't have the slightest idea whom should be the war waged against.

From time to time the hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns attack people around Glatzburg. Maybe you've already heard about them—they dwell in deep caverns located near the ruins of Galibornium. I was lucky enough to get the body of one such beast and could study it properly. You'll be surprised, Father, but I found out they aren't hellspawns of any kind—at least they didn't come from the Hell. Although they look like devils at the first sight, because they have scales on their skin, lizard head and a long tail with prickles, many of their inner parts are human-like, as I found out during the autopsy.

To tell the truth, Father, I've heard many funny accusations of heresy lately that I can't help myself but laugh. For example that someone's cow was bewitched by someone not to give milk anymore; that someone infatuated someone's wife to spread her legs for him; that Enrie Jungwirdt makes hellish potions and uses her broom to fly to Sabbaths; that Grand Duke Heidrick sold his soul to Satan in exchange for the rule over Glatzburg for the rest of his life...

Yes, that's true. You can believe me that if I had a reasonable suspicion that someone I knew was a heretic or a cultist, I'd tell the Holy Office about it immediately. Well, I'm frankly glad I don't know any heretic, because any contact with the Inquisition can be dangerous for a common mortal. No offence, Father. You must know it well yourself—sometimes there isn't much difference between the witness and the accused.

I don't know much about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, Father. Only the same as others know—that he was found near the Grand Duke's gazebo. God knows why he went to such a place... Well, to tell the truth, I can't say I was surprised. Francessca Gulvardi tried to murder the Bishop not long ago. The Bishop must have known someone—or something—tried to kill him, so he should have been very careful about where to go and who to meet. However, how could I judge the incentives of a servant of God?

No, Father. I don't know about anybody who would do that. The Bishop had some enemies, that's true. Surely you've heard he belonged to the radical priests who strive for the return to the original mission of the church—to the service to God and to people. Many clergymen don't like it, of course. Why should a high priest want to give his property away, to stop collecting the tithes, leave the politics and go to serve the ill and people in need? Thus I think the murder of the Bishop can have something to do with that.
Not at all, Father. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon. Monsignor Trevorius was an admirable man.

I knew the priest Frederick in person, Father. Not too well, because he was only less than three years here in Glatzburg, but we talked about demons and about exorcising them quite often. He used to be a renowned exorcist, in case you didn't know. During the time when he practiced those dangerous rituals he succeeded in banishing dozens of demons from bodies of possessed people. He wasn't any quack who only pretended the exorcism—he was a real exorcist, an expert in the right place, although he was a bit eccentric. I was very sorry when death took him two years ago—he was a real well of knowledge for me in the areas I hadn't explored much yet.

I'm not an expert in the area of the after-death revenge, Father. It's out of my field of interest. I'm interested in materium, in the matter—I don't study religion and spiritual aspects of our existence. Because of that I can't advise you how to get rid of Istwan de Bragho. I suppose you tried everything you were able to try. However... try asking Enrie Jungwirdt to help you. She's the most skilled person in that area of expertise.

That's a little bit more complicated, Father. The Scriptures consider the Fallen Angels to be some kind of beings, creatures having certain characteristics and rather specific look. I don't think it's so simple. I don't want to say it's not true at all—that would be close to heresy, of course. I'm only trying to look at it from another—strictly scientific—perspective. Look at the thunder and at the lightning, for example—primitive pagans believed some God of Thunder existed who sometimes got angry, thundered with his terrible voice and threw lightning bolts all around. They projected that God with many details, so that man could think he really was their fellow. However, all of us know what thunder and lightning really are. What if there's something like that for the Fallen Angels?

Look at it in detail, Father. We have Arthamon here, the Lord of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the devilish Queen of Fornication, and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the First Emissary of Satan's will. Arthamon embodies the element of ruination, of total doom, destruction, the manifestation of the anti-matter. What if I told you any of the Fallen Angel didn't exist—that he was just a personification of the powers that harmed and thwarted all what existed? It's the same for Baphomet—surely madness is an element of Chaos, thus it's condemnable and it was personified into Baphomet to let the faithful set their hate upon a specific creature. Even more easy it's for Cerdie—she's a courtesan of Hell who tempts both men and women to infidelity, destroys marriages and turns people to the Chaos. The Fallen Angel Azrael is the personification of all bad things Satan has on his conscience, that is all evil not being attributed to any of the other Chaos elements.

Not at all, Father. I don't declare they don't exist—exactly to the contrary. We must fear them and we must face their plots. I only want to say I don't believe that these beings exist in the material conception. I don't believe there's a person named Arthamon or Baphomet in some infernal cavern. Look at the examples of the summoning of Hell forces—lower demons always take the appearance that their summoners imagined. So you can meet for example the demon Gaugliel described both as a horned multi-head beast and like a huge black snake singing with a velvet voice; and that's exactly what I think about the Fallen Angels.

To tell the truth, Father, I'm looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul myself. I hope you won't be angry when I keep my results to myself. I'll tell you just some of the facts you probably know already—the hammer was made for Bonhart by one of the most renowned Masters of Alchemy, André Juliano Vestrenniol, who lived in 899–988. That's why I'm trying to find the hammer—I'd like to study it and try to reveal some of Vestrenniol's secrets. The hammer should be buried somewhere around Glatzburg together with the Bonhart's treasure—but I'm not interested in the treasure. All I want is the hammer.

Where you could get Chateau de Trebrechette? It's easy, Father. Go to Alvaron, the royal capital where the wine is brought from the Southern Empire, and buy some there. Of course you'll have to be lucky to get some, because I've heard the trade has been diminishing since the Scourges of God. You won't get it here in Glatzburg anyway—it's hard to buy basic food nowadays, not talking about such an exquisite wine. The city will be starving soon if things keep going the direction they are.
Show me what you have, Father... why, this is the Philosopher's stone! Yes, no doubt it is!
Of course, Father. I can turn each Philosopher's stone you bring me into gold for you.
