I never thought it would get into my hands... that's phenomenal! It hides so many secrets and mysteries... I'll start investigating them immediately. It must give away the knowledge it's hiding! The secret of Metamorphosis must be revealed once and for all!
Happy? I'm absolutely overjoyed, Father! Here's a pouch of gold for your effort—and here's a very rare relic in addition to that. I'm sure you could use it!
I'll answer your questions gladly, Father. However, before you start questioning me, could I have a question for you?
To tell the truth, Father, I'm very busy at the moment. I'm fully devoted to solving the mysteries hidden in the Chalice of Metamorphosis. What would you like?
As you wish, Father. Well, but try to be brief, will you?
Well, but try to be brief, Father.

There are many legends told about Glatzburg, noble lord. It's an ancient city with roots stretched as far to the past as the year 223 when the nearby town of Galibornium was captured—it was the capital of the Erebornian province Filkland in those days. I'm sure you know about it. Well, many people use the legends and tales as a source of entertainment or thrill, but I'm always trying to find a grain of truth in every legacy of the past. To tell the truth, I've found many interesting facts or at least assumptions thanks to this approach. Look at the legend of St. Orthenius, for example. I'm sure you've heard it already, haven't you?

I didn't say that, noble lord. On the contrary, I think there's quite a lot of truth to that legend. However, the grains must be separated from the chaff at first. I spent quite a long time dealing with that legend and I studied its sources and other related links in the process. I concluded that the reference about the Inquisitor relic is true. Orthenius really had to have some very powerful weapon, otherwise nobody would mention it and the people would talk about superhuman power of his arms and so on. However, I don't believe the fate of our faith and of our Realm depends on the qualities of the weapon as such—no matter how excellent the qualities of the weapon were. That's nonsense, of course.

Of course, noble lord. Well, the legend about St. Orthenius tells how this great holy man, warlord and later also the patron of our Realm led the armies of all the faithful men to victory over the pagan realm of Ereborn here in the Filkland Peninsula in the year 223. He fought in the first line in most of the battles and he always was the one who caused the victory because he was able to get his fellow fighters into some kind of battle frenzy. However, he was a renowned fighter especially thanks to a powerful relic called The Inquisitor, reputedly blessed by the First Prophet himself.

No, noble lord. The whole thing is pure nonsense. Just imagine it—a savior will appear in the time of danger to save everyone. This theme can be found in almost any folk tale. Common people want to be comforted by the vision that in the time of the greatest need someone will come and do something to bring the good times back. But it doesn't work that way, as all of us know so well.

I didn't say that, noble lord. On the contrary, I think there's quite a lot of truth in that legend. However, the grains must be separated from the chaff at first. I spent quite a long time dealing with that legend and I studied its sources and other related links in the process. I concluded that the reference about the Inquisitor relic is true. Orthenius really had to have some very powerful weapon, otherwise nobody would mention it and the people would talk about superhuman power of his arms and so on. However, I don't believe the fate of our faith and of our Realm depends on the qualities of the weapon as such—no matter how excellent the qualities of the weapon were. That's pure nonsense, of course.

Grand Duke Robert Heidrick is the royal governor of the city, noble lord. Duke Rowan van Leerin is the vice-governor. According to what I've heard they don't like each other very much. Politics, you know... Thank God I'm a scientist and so I can leave these profane things to other people.

To tell the truth, noble lord, I knew very well that the crisis would come. No need to be surprised—I'm the Master of Alchemy and thus I must be prepared for such events. A long time before the Star of Doom appeared in the sky in 1219, I was finding signs everywhere in the Realm that could have meant only one thing—great shift in the Power. The change of the whole Pondus aeternum, the eternal balance. Erebornian philosophers called it diespothe malcius—the time of the change. However, no matter what you're going to call it, it had been clear for a long time that something big and really unpleasant would happen. And so it did—the Scourges of God shook the Realm like the ship in the tempest.

I don't know, noble lord. I can't tell you. I can tell you that God is the source of all the Power and that it all was the will of God, if you want to hear something like that. However, I don't believe it personally. I believe God is a part of the Power, he isn't the Creator of Power. No need to be shocked, noble lord—I'm not preaching any heretic heterodoxy to you. Many renowned and wise clerical thinkers wrote about this theory—for example Jacob of Ayolla or Giorgio de Companella. It's only a part of the scientific theory; it isn't a dogma. But to return to the issue—I really don't know what caused such a shift of the Power. Who can tell why a volcano erupted? Who knows why the earthquake occurs? Really, I don't know, noble lord.

Of course they are, noble lord. Because faith—in the way you look at it—is a part of the Power too. It's a component of the momentum of our Universe—maybe the most important one. The Scriptures discuss faith—and from this point of view I dare say it's somewhat mystically written alchemical work. I admit the matter is very complex, noble lord. I wasn't able to fathom it completely myself, although I devoted almost all my life to the studies of alchemy.

Yes, you're right, noble lord—the demand for the healing potions would increase, as well as the prices. Nevertheless I hope there won't be any war. In addition to that it isn't clear to me whom should be the war declared to. There isn't a single enemy around here. The pagan from the Far East aren't a threat to us, I can't see anyone marching to the Realm... so I don't have the slightest idea whom should be the war waged against.

From time to time the hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns attack people around Glatzburg. Maybe you've already heard about them—they dwell in deep caverns located near the ruins of Galibornium. I was lucky enough to get the body of one such beast and could study it properly. You'll be surprised, noble lord, but I found out they aren't hellspawns of any kind—at least they didn't come from the Hell. Although they look like devils at the first sight, because they have scales on their skin, lizard head and a long tail with prickles, many of their inner parts are human-like, as I found out during the autopsy.

To tell the truth, noble lord, I've heard many funny accusations of heresy lately that I can't help myself but laugh. For example that someone's cow was bewitched by someone not to give milk anymore; that someone infatuated someone's wife to spread her legs for him; that Enrie Jungwirdt makes hellish potions and uses her broom to fly to Sabbaths; that Grand Duke Heidrick sold his soul to Satan in exchange for the rule over Glatzburg for the rest of his life...

I don't know much about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, noble lord. Only the same as others know—that he was found near the Grand Duke's gazebo. God knows why he went to such a place... Well, to tell the truth, I can't say I was surprised. Francessca Gulvardi tried to murder the Bishop not long ago. The Bishop must have known someone—or something—tried to kill him, so he should have been very careful about where to go and who to meet. However, how could I judge the incentives of a servant of God?

No, noble lord. I don't know about anybody who would do that. The Bishop had some enemies, that's true. Surely you've heard he belonged to the radical priests who strive for the return to the original mission of the church—to the service to God and to people. Many clergymen don't like it, of course. Why should a high priest want to give his property away, to stop collecting the tithes, leave the politics and go to serve the ill and people in need? Thus I think the murder of the Bishop can have something to do with that.
Not at all, noble lord. I hope you'll catch the murderer soon. Monsignor Trevorius was an admirable man.

I knew the priest Frederick in person, noble lord. Not too well, because he was only less than three years here in Glatzburg, but we talked about demons and about exorcising them quite often. He used to be a renowned exorcist, in case you didn't know. During the time when he practiced those dangerous rituals he succeeded in banishing dozens of demons from bodies of possessed people. He wasn't any quack who only pretended the exorcism—he was a real exorcist, an expert in the right place, although he was a bit eccentric. I was very sorry when death took him two years ago—he was a real well of knowledge for me in the areas I hadn't explored much yet.

I'm not an expert in the area of the after-death revenge, noble lord. It's out of my field of interest. I'm interested in materium, in the matter—I don't study religion and spiritual aspects of our existence. Because of that I can't advise you how to get rid of Istwan de Bragho. I suppose you tried everything you were able to try. However... try asking Enrie Jungwirdt to help you. She's the most skilled person in that area of expertise.

That's a little bit more complicated, noble lord. The Scriptures consider the Fallen Angels to be some kind of beings, creatures having certain characteristics and rather specific look. I don't think it's so simple. I don't want to say it's not true at all—that would be close to heresy, of course. I'm only trying to look at it from another—strictly scientific—perspective. Look at the thunder and at the lightning, for example—primitive pagans believed some God of Thunder existed who sometimes got angry, thundered with his terrible voice and threw lightning bolts all around. They projected that God with many details, so that man could think he really was their fellow. However, all of us know what thunder and lightning really are. What if there's something like that for the Fallen Angels?

Look at it in detail, noble lord. We have Arthamon here, the Lord of Destruction, Baphomet, the Ruler of Madness, Cerdie, the devilish Queen of Fornication, and the Fallen Archangel Azrael, the First Emissary of Satan's will. Arthamon embodies the element of ruination, of total doom, destruction, the manifestation of the anti-matter. What if I told you any of the Fallen Angel didn't exist—that he was just a personification of the powers that harmed and thwarted all what existed? It's the same for Baphomet—surely madness is an element of Chaos, thus it's condemnable and it was personified into Baphomet to let the faithful set their hate upon a specific creature. Even more easy it's for Cerdie—she's a courtesan of Hell who tempts both men and women to infidelity, destroys marriages and turns people to the Chaos. The Fallen Angel Azrael is the personification of all bad things Satan has on his conscience, that is all evil not being attributed to any of the other Chaos elements.

Not at all, noble lord. I don't declare they don't exist—exactly to the contrary. We must fear them and we must face their plots. I only want to say I don't believe that these beings exist in the material conception. I don't believe there's a person named Arthamon or Baphomet in some infernal cavern. Look at the examples of the summoning of Hell forces—lower demons always take the appearance that their summoners imagined. So you can meet for example the demon Gaugliel described both as a horned multi-head beast and like a huge black snake singing with a velvet voice; and that's exactly what I think about the Fallen Angels.

To tell the truth, noble lord, I'm looking for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul myself. I hope you won't be angry when I keep my results to myself. I'll tell you just some of the facts you probably know already—the hammer was made for Bonhart by one of the most renowned Masters of Alchemy, André Juliano Vestrenniol, who lived in 899–988. That's why I'm trying to find the hammer—I'd like to study it and try to reveal some of Vestrenniol's secrets. The hammer should be buried somewhere around Glatzburg together with the Bonhart's treasure—but I'm not interested in the treasure. All I want is the hammer.

Where you could get Chateau de Trebrechette? It's easy, noble lord. Go to Alvaron, the royal capital where the wine is brought from the Southern Empire, and buy some there. Of course you'll have to be lucky to get some, because I've heard the trade has been diminishing since the Scourges of God. You won't get it here in Glatzburg anyway—it's hard to buy basic food nowadays, not talking about such an exquisite wine. The city will be starving soon if things keep going the direction they are.
Show me what you have, noble lord... why, this is the Philosopher's stone! Yes, no doubt it is!
Of course, noble lord. I can turn each Philosopher's stone you bring me into gold for you.
I'd rather answer if I were you, Master Alchemist. You never know what unpleasant things could happen to you when you impetuously refuse to answer the question of a noble...

I'm getting to the point, noble lord. It wasn't clear to me where the monsters came from. For a long time it was a mystery for me, but one day I found a certain scroll mentioning the Chalice of Metamorphosis. Probably it was some relic or an alchemical artifact thanks to which the Erebornian clerics and alchemists were able to turn a living creature into any monster they wanted! Do you understand, noble lord? They were able to morph living beings according to their mad ideas and thus they created the warriors fighting the gladiators in the Coliseum! That was the source of the renowned gladiator games of Galibornium! I found other details during my studies and many years of difficult investigations. The Chalice of Metamorphosis was kept in Galibornium just under the Coliseum, in deep cellars where the Erebornian priests performed their mad experiments.

Yes, exactly, noble lord. I believe that if I could puzzle out its secret, I could reveal new horizons of the modern alchemy this way. Maybe I could look behind the horizon of the Principle of Godly Creation itself... That would be an epochal discovery, noble lord! However, I need to get the Chalice of Metamorphosis first to do that. I've heard you solved many troubles... Because of that I thought you could help me.

Excellent, noble lord! I knew you would help me; and not only me—if you'll be able to find the Chalice, you'll help science as a whole. If I'll be able to reveal its secret, of course! With such a discovery I surely could get to a leading position in the Royal Alchemists Guild!
Of course you can, noble lord. I'll gladly answer all your questions, just ask.

I don't think so, noble lord. All the references regarding the Chalice of Metamorphosis suggest that it was kept in Galibornium just under the Coliseum. When the armies of the faithful seized Galibornium in 223, St. Orthenius ordered the dungeon, as a symbol of pagan decay and perversity, to be immured not to let anybody in—but also not to let anybody out. Thus he sentenced all the Erebornian people who were currently in there to a terrible death of starvation. It's said that the souls of the dead there have not found eternal peace and wander through the cellars even nowadays. Some people who went to the ruins of Galibornium to search for hidden treasures declared they had heard strange noises and moaning from the dungeons under the Coliseum...

No, I don't think so, noble lord. Why in that case would God give man the thirst for knowledge, as well as the unfaltering will to reveal all the hidden secrets? If our God didn't want man to reveal the principles of function of the surrounding world, surely he would prevent him from doing so.

Of course I will, noble lord! I'll reward your effort gladly. What would you say to a pouch of gold and some magic item in addition to that? I think it would be more than a generous reward for your effort, don't you think so?
All right, noble lord, ask me. Maybe you'll be lucky to find some answers you seek.

It's a relic from the pagan realm of Ereborn. You know, noble lord, I spend a lot of time studying the Erebornian art of alchemy. You can't imagine how many things were invented several millennia ago—there are even areas in which we're still behind them. Many secrets were forgotten or even lost forever during the bloody year 223 when Ereborn was defeated. I study existing fragments of the past carefully, because new knowledge can be often found that way and from time to time a really great secret is revealed.

Yes, you're right, noble lord. It's a relic from the pagan realm of Ereborn. You know, noble lord, I spend a lot of time studying the Erebornian art of alchemy. You can't imagine how many things were invented several millennia ago—there are even areas in which we're still behind them. Many secrets were forgotten or even lost forever during the bloody year 223 when the Ereborn was defeated. I study existing fragments of the past carefully, because new knowledge can be often found this way and from time to time a really great secret is revealed.

No, noble lord, I don't think so. There's nothing forbidden in it. In 1107, King Raul the First approved the Royal Alchemist Guild to investigate and to study the Erebornian science. You can't imagine what secrets are hidden deep in the past...

Yes, exactly, noble lord. I'm sure you know the ruins of the ancient Erebornian town of Galibornium are located near Glatzburg. It used to be the province capital and thus it was a jewel among other towns here in the Filkland Peninsula. Above all, the gladiator games were the source of its power and glory. You know what the gladiator games were, don't you?
As you wish, noble lord. There's nothing more powerful than a good chest of gold, is there? Wait a moment, please...

That's no ordinary stone, noble lord—just to the contrary. It's an extremely precious substance which is renowned for it's ability to be turned into almost any other unliving substance. The only limitation is to find new substances to turn it into. Well... it's finished, noble lord. Here's your gold. If you wouldn't object, I'd just take my share as a reward.

I can see I have a special guest here today—a citizen of a high standing. Welcome, noble lord. Guests are always welcome in my house. I think we don't know each other yet. My name is Paolus Ventimus, and I'm the Master of Alchemy. What can I do for you?
Of course, noble lord. Come closer. Well, but you better don't forget the customers have to pay also for the goods they break.
As you wish, noble lord. Both my shop and my alchemy laboratory are at your disposal whenever you need. However, before you start questioning me, could I have a question for you?
Farewell, noble lord. I'm sure we'll see each other again soon.
Hello, noble lord. How are you? Do you need anything from my shop? Or maybe you bring me good news, such as you found the Chalice of Metamorphosis, right?

Oh, really? Aren't you joking, noble lord? You really found the Chalice of Metamorphosis?! That's absolutely fantastic! Show it to me... Oh my God! I never thought it would get into my hands... that's phenomenal! It hides so many secrets and mysteries... I'll start investigating them immediately. It must give away the knowledge it's hiding! The secret of Metamorphosis must be revealed once and for all!
Happy? I'm absolutely overjoyed, noble lord! Here's a pouch of gold for your effort—and here's a very rare relic in addition to that. I'm sure you can use it.
Greetings, noble lord. What can I do for you?
I'll answer your questions gladly, noble lord. However, before you start questioning me, could I have a question for you?
To tell the truth, noble lord, I'm very busy at the moment. I'm fully devoted to solving the mysteries hidden in the Chalice of Metamorphosis. What would you like?
As you wish, noble lord. Well, but try to be brief, will you?
Well, but try to be brief, noble lord.
Do you really think it's necessary to ask the royal counselor such questions, knight?! I'm sure you'll find out yourself where to get any goods you need in Alvaron!

I don't know any details about the war preparations, knight. King Edward didn't plan to wage a war. The preparations started when His Majesty was assassinated and the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor became the temporary army leader. Well, and he didn't consult anything with me.

Because of that, the only thing I know is that the royal army regiments in the whole Realm were ordered to replenish their numbers, to requisition horses and cattle, to refill all rations and gather some supplies... to prepare for the war, in fact. However, the question is—against whom will the war be waged? Because there isn't a single enemy around that could be defeated on the battlefield...

The Cult of the Children of the New Order? Yes, that name rings the bell to me. If I remember the Empire history well, it was a demoniac cult founded in the tenth century around the self-appointed prophet Lucius who predicted the End of the World and the coming of the New Order. The Children of the New Order should have ruled the conquered world alongside the released Dark Prince of Hell. Soon the cult affected the whole society of the Empire, but the Pope's Inquisitorial Curia succeed in catching and executing all members of the cult in the end—including Lucius himself. It was the end of the whole cult and nobody has heard about it since that time.

I'm sure you've heard some rumors about the counterfeited gold that appeared in the city. It seems that some unknown heretics can turn common... well... human feces to gold for a short time and use it to pay with it like with a real gold. Because of that the mistrust in the Realm gold coins spreads in the city and the trade as a whole is seriously threatened. Grand Duke Lambert is deservedly very unhappy about it.
I wish I could help you with the investigation of the murder of our King Edward, knight. Unfortunately I don't know any facts that could help you to find the killers and to prove them guilty...
I'm really sorry, knight. However, I believe firmly you'll succeed in the end!
What did you do in the evening when the King was murdered?

I was in my study, knight—like every other evening when our leader didn't need me. Well, he didn't seek my services too often in the last several years, to tell the truth. He was drowning in pain because of the death of his children, and he preferred to be left alone...

I knew this Juhasz Gotherr—from time to time I went to him to borrow some odd book or a scroll, as he was the city librarian an his library was always well stocked. He was fond of pagan texts, so we used to discuss the Elenians and their significance in the world's history for long hours. I never thought he was a heretic, even the leader of the cult of Pagan Night himself! I really don't know where he could be now, but the people say he can be seen from time to time creeping through the city streets under the veil of darkness. I must say the image of a heretic able to commit any crime creeping under my windows is quite terrifying!
I'm sorry, but I don't know anything about Ron Burton. I even didn't notice he was missing. I hope nothing bad happened to him...

I don't know Father Nicolas too well, but I know Grand Duchess Liana Lambert quite well and I can swear she's the most noble woman in the whole city and she would never fabricate something so shameless. Thus, no doubt Father Nicolas is lying—he must really have committed the terrible crime the Grand Duchess accused him of. You should focus your investigation in that direction, knight.

Many tales are told about the manor of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich. Maybe you saw it yourself—it's such an awful ruin on the outskirts of Alvaron, a scar on the face of the city that used to be so beautiful. The people say that the Baron's impure ghost dwells in the manor, and it's true that terrible screams and crying is heard from there at nights, so the people got used to avoid the place...

The Baron's ghost was imprisoned in the house after the Baron was poisoned and cursed by his last—thirteenth—wife. She accused him of terrible things he was supposed to have done to his twelve ex-wives and children. She testified that she found their remains in the cellars of her husband's house. But her testimony didn't save her from the fate all the poisoners meet—no matter what was their motive for the murder. Before she died, however, she cursed her husband and it made his ghost return to the family mansion which soon became a house of horror.
Don't try to oppose me! Refuse me the cooperation I need and I'll destroy you!
I ask you frankly, answer my question, please.
I hoped I could get an appropriately sound answer from the King's counselor... You have great reputation, you know. Answer me, please.

I'm Verenicus, the Baron of Earia and the titular Duke of Khentt, personal counselor of His Majesty King Edward the Second. Well, the former counselor, of course... That's why I mentioned Domitius Ulpianus. We have surprisingly much in common. Sometimes, a shiver runs down my spine because of that...

Ulpianus Domitius was born in a modest place, in the family of an impoverished country nobleman—as well as me. He was predestined to have as boring life as me—he was supposed to become a scribe in a nearby town. His parents couldn't afford better education for their child. Soon he began to stand out because of his intellect—a Pope's legate noticed him and took him to the capital to study law and philosophy at the best universities. Something like that happened to me as well, so I could become the personal counselor of His Majesty King Edward the Second in the end. Let our Lord be so merciful and care for his soul on the other side... However, my fate is even more similar to Ulpian's. Terrible tragedy happened to him as well as to me, when his beloved emperor died.
So you are the personal counselor of His Majesty? Nice to meet you. The death of His Majesty must have hit you harshly...
Yes, that's true. I didn't expect God would call him to the Heaven so quickly. There was so much he could do... but there's nothing to do about it. The Realm will have to do without him.
Yes, it will have to. Could I ask you a few questions? As the personal counselor of His Majesty you must have great knowledge...
If you really think I'll be able to answer your questions, you can ask me of course, knight.
Your story sounds like a fairy tale to me—about a poor boy gone lucky. How did you become the personal counselor of His Majesty?

I owe a lot to my patron, Duke Abram of Longham. It was he who helped me out of the hole where I attended the scribing school as a boy and brought me here to Alvaron. He gave me the education and taught me all man needed to live in high society. Everything else I reached thanks to my diligence and intensive hard work. From a common royal scribe I became the royal counselor in the matters of law—as well as Domitius Ulpianus—and the King got to like me so much in the end that he made me his personal counselor.
That's really impressive. Could I ask you a few questions? As the personal counselor of His Majesty you must have great knowledge...
What are you going to do now when the King is dead?
Well, I already plan something—I'd like to move on a little, since I have some energy left. I'll see if it will be possible.
What's the matter, if I can ask you?
Of course, you can ask, knight, but I'm not going to tell you. Excuse me, but it's my secret. If I told you, you could outrun me or use the secret some other way, and I don't think I'd like that.
I understand. Could I ask you a few questions? As the personal counselor of His Majesty you must have great knowledge...
I understand, and I wish you good luck. Farewell.
I'm glad to have met you, but I have to go. Farewell.

Farewell, knight. By the way, if you'd like to study the curricula vitae of renowned Erebornian people, come to me. Maybe we could also find for you an analogue with the life of someone renowned. It's a fascinating reading.
Duke Verenicus of Khentt, I came to arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of heresy and a plot against God and the King. You'll come with me now, to be put before a fair trial!
What are you talking about, knight? What plot against God and the King? What heresy? I'm the royal counselor and a noble man! I refuse your accusation completely. You have no proofs for that!

You are mistaken, Duke. I questioned a girl named Corin Morray who witnessed you two years ago performing some occult ritual in the bedroom of Prince Louis—a ritual that caused immediate death of the prince!

That's nonsense! Corin Morray was accused herself of helping the other girl, Kathryn Winhold, to kill Prince Louis! She's the murderer, not me! Moreover, she escaped two years ago and was proclaimed an escaped prisoner of the Inquisition. You should detain her, not believe her lies! But even if that was true, that questionable proof wouldn't approve you to accuse me of heresy and of the plot against God and the King!
I have another proof. I acquired also the testimony of Kathryn Winhold who confirmed it all and marked you as the murderer!
What nonsense is that? Kathryn Winhold was executed as murderer and heretic! How could she give you her testimony?!
I was able to establish a contact with her in the Other World. Her ghost appeared before me and yielded her terrible testimony.
Are you mad? You want to tell me you talked to ghosts? Do you want to show that proof at the trial? They will laugh at you! You'll look like a fool!

I doubt it. The Code of Inquisition counts everything that can prove the accused person is guilty—or innocent—to be a valid proof. Thus, I arrest you for a reasonable suspicion of heresy and of the plot against God and the King. Let's go!

Well... let's see, the parallel of my fate with Domitius Ulpianus starts to fill up. He was also arrested in the end of his life and judged for the betrayal of the imperial Crown. Did you know about it?
That's not important now. You'll come with me to confess your sins!

That's what you imagine, knight, but you are mistaken. I'll come with you now, because I don't want to be killed by an impetuous, mad brained paladin who thinks he's doing the right thing, but soon the situation will change. I know what I'm saying. Unlike Ulpian I won't be executed, but set free and promoted as I deserve. You'll get to know about all that in time. Now, let's go—it's not respectable to stand here like that.
Do you know, knight, who was Domitius Ulpianus?
Well... no, I don't, but maybe you'll tell me...

He was an excellent lawyer and the personal counselor of the Erebornian Emperor Alexander Severus. Nobody knows exactly when he was born—it's usually an unimportant date which only mothers remember—but he died in the year 122 of the new era, less than five years after the death of his Emperor. You know, knight, story of his life is a source of never-ending inspiration for me...
That's interesting. However, tell me who you are?
You told Domitius Ulpianus was an excellent lawyer. Sounds a little like heresy, to talk like that about a pagan.

Why do you think so, knight? I don't know what do you know about the history of law, but the law of the Realm is fully built up on the heritage of the Erebornian law system. It was transformed into the orthodox law codex, of course, but the main principles of the civil law are based on the laws formulated and written down by the lawyers during the last century of the Erebornian Realm—including Ulpian's laws. His most renowned quotation is Dura lex, sed lex—hard law still is the law. Well, the whole Inquisition law is based on this principle, isn't it?
Yes, I know. But still I don't know who you are...
Is that you, knight? I could lend you the curricula vitae of some renowned people from the Erebornian Realm if you want. Maybe you could also find an analogue of your life with someone renowned...
Maybe later, if I'll have more leisure time. Now I'd like to ask you a few questions.
I understand. Ask your question in that case, knight.
Thanks for the proposal, but I don't have enough time to study the curricula vitae of renowned Erebornian people. Maybe later. Farewell.
Do you really think it's necessary to ask the royal counselor such questions, Father?! I'm sure you'll find out yourself where to get any goods you need in Alvaron!

I don't know any details about the war preparations, Father. King Edward didn't plan to wage a war. The preparations started when His Majesty was assassinated and the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor became the temporary army leader. Well, and he didn't consult anything with me.
I wish I could help you with the investigation of the murder of our King Edward, Father. Unfortunately I don't know any facts that could help you to find the killers and to prove them guilty...
I'm really sorry, Father. However, I believe firmly you'll succeed in the end!

I was in my study, Father—like every other evening when our leader didn't need me. Well, he didn't seek my services too often in the last several years, to tell the truth. He was drowning in pain because of the death of his children, and he preferred to be left alone...

I don't know Father Nicolas too well, but I know Grand Duchess Liana Lambert quite well and I can swear she's the most noble woman in the whole city and she would never fabricate something so shameless. Thus, no doubt Father Nicolas is lying—he must really have committed the terrible crime the Grand Duchess accused him of. You should focus your investigation in that direction, Father.
If you really think I'll be able to answer your questions, you can ask me of course, Father.
Of course, you can ask, Father, but I'm not going to tell you. Excuse me, but it's my secret. If I told you, you could outrun me or use the secret some other way, and I don't think I'd like that.

Farewell, Father. By the way, if you'd like to study the curricula vitae of renowned Erebornian people, come to me. Maybe we could also find for you an analogue with the life of someone renowned. It's a fascinating reading.
What are you talking about, Father? What plot against God and the King? What heresy? I'm the royal counselor and a noble man! I refuse your accusation completely. You have no proofs for that!

That's what you imagine, Father, but you are mistaken. I'll come with you now, because I don't want to be killed by an impetuous, mad-brained cleric who thinks he's doing the right thing, but soon the situation will change. I know what I'm saying. On the contrary to Ulpian I won't be executed, but set free and promoted as I deserve. You'll get to know about all of it in time. Now, let's go—it's not respectable to stand here like that.
Do you know, Father, who was Domitius Ulpianus?

He was an excellent lawyer and the personal counselor of the Erebornian Emperor Alexander Severus. Nobody knows exactly when he was born—it's usually an unimportant date which only mothers remember—but he died in the year 122 of the new era, less than five years after the death of his Emperor. You know, Father, story of his life is a source of never-ending inspiration for me...

Why do you think so, Father? I don't know what do you know about the history of law, but the law of the Realm is fully built up on the heritage of the Erebornian law system. It was transformed into the orthodox law codex, of course, but the main principles of the civil law are based on the laws formulated and written down by the lawyers during the last century of the Erebornian Realm—including Ulpian's laws. His most renowned quotation is Dura lex, sed lex—hard law still is the law. Well, the whole Inquisition law is based on this principle, isn't it?
Is that you, Father? I could lend you the curricula vitae of some renowned people from the Erebornian Realm if you want. Maybe you could also find an analogue of your life with someone renowned...
I understand. Ask your question in that case, Father.

Thank you for setting me free! I was about to think they will torture me to death down here...
Freedom, at last! I was rotting down here for a couple of years... and God knows I will have my revenge now!
I am free! My prayers and dreams have been fulfilled!
Put your hands out of my pockets!!!
In the case the vagrant named Steinger told me the truth there should be a stash in this place where he, together with Vick Length, hid his loot.
Yes, it's here! Oh my God, it's proper treasure... I'll take it all—these are great exhibits!

We have very bad times now, that's true. Several years ago things looked like if we all should be happy soon—business was good, as well as the harvests, there were almost no signs of the hellspawns... And now? All is ruined, disasters and despair everywhere. I can tell you, knight—God prepared a really hard test for us!

There are many hellspawns lurking around Hillbrandt, knight. This spring the orcs came out from the entrails of the Moonshine Mountains and killed everybody both in the iron mines and in the miners' village Asherbalt. Since that time, thick black smoke rises to the sky in the mountains, so I'm sure—because I'm the blacksmith—they process iron ore there. God knows what do they need it for. If there were people in the mountains, I'd say they want to equip an army. But the orcs are not people, so it's hard to say what devilment are they preparing. I fear we'll get to know soon anyway.
What do you know about the orcs, master blacksmith?

What do I know about the orcs? Well, nothing special, knight. The people say it were the orcs who destroyed the ancient Realm of Thron ages ago in the times of wars of non-human races. I'm sure you've heard about it already—it's a very sad story. However, the legends don't say where the orcs came from. To tell the truth, for a long time I thought the tales were nothing more than fiction. I didn't have the slightest idea the orcs really existed and that I'd see them myself one day. Well, as far as I watched them during the attack, there are both common orcs and some big warriors with hands as big as tree trunks and also some clerics with deadly spells. Be careful about them, knight. I saw what they could do to an adult. And you can believe me it wasn't a pleasant sight!

I'm sorry, knight, but I don't suspect anyone of heresy. Well, I've heard a lot of things. About Master d'Arvias, about Duke Weinberg... but I don't believe anything of that, you know? I'm a humble man and the only things I believe are those which I can see with my own eyeballs. I didn't catch anyone doing anything bad, so I don't want to do any harm to anyone talking bad about him. There are many others in the town to do so...

The orcs attacked Hillbrandt several days ago, knight. The people say someone let them into the town, and I think it's quite possible. I faced them myself in the streets of the town, and I killed several of them. I think there was something strange about this attack.

I'm not a soldier, knight, but I know a lot about fighting. Thus, it seems very strange to me such a small army tried to conquer the town. Of course we don't know exactly how many orcs there are down under the mountains and who is in charge there, but it's clear they couldn't seize the town during that attack, no matter they were able to get inside the walls and leave so many dead behind. In addition to that, in the end they turned in the middle of the fight without a good reason and ran for their lives, as if hell itself was burning right behind them. I must say, knight, it seems to be very strange in my opinion.

I don't believe Master Edmond d'Arvias is a heretic. I've known him since he came here to Hillbrandt and took over the local chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. He's an honest man with the heart of a lion. He devoted all his life to the just fight and I don't see a single reason why he should change sides at once. Got a feeling somebody tries to set something up on him.

Of course I've heard about the theft of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius—everybody heard about it. However, I don't know any details about the thief. I remember I heard Quarim, the apprentice of the Master Executioner, boasting in the Truthorn's tavern that he knew something about it. I think Quarim just spins a yarn, but you can try asking him. You'll find him at the scaffold probably...

I saw Bishop Quentinus last time the night before the orcs attacked the town. I fear those hellish pagans killed him and chucked his body somewhere—if they didn't eat it immediately. God save his soul.

I haven't heard anything about Baroness Linda van Gallagan, knight. The people say she's been missing since the night the orcs attacked the town—as well as Bishop Quentinus. Maybe the orcs got her, and in that case we'll probably never hear of her again. To tell the truth—I wouldn't mind it at all. I didn't like her too much. She was a nasty plotter...
I'm really sorry, knight, but I didn't hear about the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias. Someone stole it from him? That's unprecedented...

You mean, whether Natalia was murdered by the landsknecht Olfghard? Well... as for me, he didn't do such a thing. I know Olfghard well. He wouldn't do anything like that, although he did some quite wild things in the past. Why would he murder young girls? To rob them—yes, that sounds like him. As well as to flatter them and get under their skirts. But to murder a girl? No, he wouldn't do that, there was no good reason...

I doubt we'll hear about the soldier Jullian again. I bet he's already on his way south, probably to Glatzburg. He knows very well what would happen to him if he was caught. As for the deserters, Sheriff Contemburry has a strict opinion.

As for the tales and legends, our Paul is really keen on them. When someone starts to tell him a story, he's quiet for a while, like if he was another human being. I don't remember many stories. All the stories seem the same to me—there is some evil somewhere, someone brave will come and face it and he'll either die like a hero or he'll win and get some gold, girls and so on. Well—it wouldn't be bad to be such a legendary hero, would it?

The merchant Kurth Ollmier used to buy some equipment for his journeys from me from time to time. He was more like a traveler and adventurer than a stall-holding merchant from the square. I can't tell you whether he was a good man or not, but I don't think he deserved such a terrible death. Someone cut his throat in the Truthorn's tavern—in the attic room he rented. Those butchers also cut off his manhood and inserted it into his mouth. I've never heard something like that—and this has been a wild country last couple of years, with all those orcs and monsters—God knows where they came from.
You found strange ore, you say? Show it to me, knight... it's the Philosopher's stone!

It's a common name for a rare mineral having a strange feature: it can be turned into any other metal—it depends on the processing temperature and on the way of hardening. I don't have the slightest idea where the mineral comes from, but there must be some magic in it, because all weapons and armor forged from such a mineral are magic. So, I can make you one magic item from each Philosopher's stone you bring me, if you want.
Of course I could process some Philosopher's stone for you, knight. I could make you one magic item from each piece you bring me.
It has never paid off for anybody to oppose the Brotherhood of the Righteous, master blacksmith! Answer me immediately, or there will be serious consequences for you!
Maybe you don't like me, Hammerhand, but that isn't a reason good enough to refuse to answer me, is it?
I don't believe a man so rational and skilful like you could have some serious reasons why not to answer my question...

Thanks to God you found him, knight. I don't want to know how he could get so far from the town. Once more you run from home, Paul, and I'll break the cat-o'-nine-tails on your back! As for you, knight, please take this item as the expression of my deepest thanks. I also hope some gold won't offend you—it's the compensation of the expenses you had during the search for my son.
Thank you, master blacksmith. Could I talk to you for a moment?
Thank you, master blacksmith. Could I look at your goods now?
Farewell. Watch your son more carefully in the future.
I have one piece of the Philosopher's stone here, master blacksmith. I'd like to have something forged from it.
Thank you, master blacksmith. No need to hurry. Take your time and do the best you can.

Of course, knight... Well, here you are. This was the only thing I was able to make from the stone. It changed the shape right before my eyes, as if the stone had its own free will. I hope you'll be satisfied. Or I can buy it back from you. Is there something else I could do for you?
Welcome, knight. I'm Victor Hammerhand, the town blacksmith. If you need some weapon, or maybe an armor, come to me. I have the best goods you can get in this God forsaken part of the Realm.
I'm glad to meet you. Could I talk to you?
Of course, knight, but first there's something I'd like to ask you for. Do you think you could spare some of your time? It's important.
Of course, what's on your mind?

It's about my son Paul, knight. You know—he isn't a bad boy. He's quite wild and short-tempered, that's true. Often he's stubborn and nobody can convince him to do something, but he's a good boy in the core. Probably it's my fault, I didn't spent enough time with him, there was too much work around the anvil. His mother died when he was a little child and I didn't have enough time for him. He learned to take care of himself and he rambles around the town quite often. Maybe that's why some people think he's so bad. However, he wouldn't hurt anybody—I'd put my own hand into the fire if he ever did.
Where's the problem, master blacksmith?

You know, we had a quarrel some time ago and he ran from home. This isn't the first time he did so, but he always returned soon. This time he didn't. I fear for him. I tried to convince Sheriff Contemburry to help me, but he doesn't want to hear anything like that. He said there's enough trouble in the town so he can't let his soldiers look for some damned urchin who ran from his home into the neighborhood.
I understand. I'll look for him, master blacksmith.
I would reward you of course, if you could find him, knight. You can believe me!
It depends on what you would offer me...
Well... I refuse to believe a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous would ask a reward from a neighbor in the time of need. However, I will reward you, you can trust me. I won't spare my purse.
I'm sorry. I don't have time to do things like that.
What a shame. I hoped that you could... well, what can I do. It's your decision, I'm not going to urge you.
That's nice of you. Could I talk to you a little longer?
As you wish, knight. What would you like to know?
To tell the truth, Sam Riemann warned me about your son...

Yes, I suppose he did. Paul isn't very popular around here. However, believe me, he isn't a bad boy. People say a lot of things about him, but most of them are just slanders. No matter what is missing or broken, Paul is always the one who caused it according to them. His behavior helps these tales a lot, but he isn't as evil as he's said to be. In addition to that, Sam Riemann is rather an eccentric person and it has seemed to me lately that he'd like to do some harm to Paul, but I don't know the reason.
I found your son, master blacksmith. He was hiding in an abandoned log cabin near the Dragon rock.
Don't waste my time, master blacksmith. You're not here to ask questions. I'm going to ask questions here!
Well, all right, knight. As you wish... what do you need to know?
What do you sell, master blacksmith?

As I've already said, you can get all the weapons and armor I can produce. Daggers, swords, axes, bows... everything you can imagine. To tell the truth, I'm no match for the blacksmith workshops in the East, but as for the weapons and armor you can get here in Hillbrandt—my products belong to the best goods all around.
I'd like to talk to you, master blacksmith.
Nothing in fact. Farewell.
Do you want something, knight?
As you wish. What would you like to know?
I found your son, master blacksmith. He was hiding in an abandoned log cabin near the Dragon rock. I promised him to take him back to you.
No, I think I don't. Farewell.
Hello, knight. Thank you once more for my son—for finding him and bringing him back home. Would you like something?
Of course. What would you need to know, knight?
I don't have that much time, master blacksmith. I'd like to see your goods!
Well, all right, knight. As you wish...

Probably it's my fault, I didn't spent enough time with him, there was too much work around the anvil. His mother died when he was a little child and I didn't have enough time for him. He learned to take care of himself and he rambles around the town quite often. Maybe that's why some people think he's so bad. However, he wouldn't hurt anybody—I'd put my own hand into the fire if he ever did.
I would reward you of course, if you could find him, noble sir. You can believe me!
Of course, noble sir. What do you need to know?
Well... It should have struck me at once that a noble would ask a reward from a neighbor in the time of need. However, I will reward you, you can trust me. I won't spare my purse.
As you wish, noble sir. What would you like to know?

Yes, I suppose he did. Paul isn't very popular around here. However, believe me, he isn't a bad boy. People tell a lot of things about him, but most of them are just slanders. No matter what is missing or broken, Paul is always the one who caused it according to them. His behavior helps these tales a lot, but he isn't as evil as he's said to be. In addition to that, Sam Riemann is rather an eccentric person and it has seemed to me lately that he'd like to do some harm to Paul, but I don't know the reason.
Well, all right, noble sir. As you wish... what do you need to know?
Do you want something, noble sir?
Hello, noble sir. Thank you once more for my son—for finding him and bringing him back home. Would you like something?
Of course. What would you need to know, noble sir?
Well, all right, noble sir. As you wish...
Although you are a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, knight, I'll give you a piece of advice—stay out of trouble!
And if I won't?
Then you might become the trouble—I assure you that you wouldn't like it!
Yes, I'll try to. Farewell.

I would have never thought that traveling the Realm would be as dangerous as these days—with all those werewolf packs one would rather stay in the city. And I'm military... can you imagine how the common folks must be scared?!
Yes, that's terrible...
Damn right!
Hold on, it'll get better soon.
Hope so too... Because if it were to get worse... I just can't imagine how it would be...

Now, when the King is dead, the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor is the supreme commander of the royal armies. I'm proud I can serve under him, knight. He's soldier to the bone. I'm sure he'll lead us to victory—whoever the enemy might be!

Did you know that the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor became the supreme commander of the royal armies after King Edward's death? It's gonna be better now... Well, I don't wanna speak ill 'bout the dead, but the word is that in his last months the King wasn't interested in military very much... Well, he wasn't interested in anything except for booze!
Long live the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor, the supreme marshal of the royal armies! May God protect the Realm!
Well said!
Now, when the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor is dead, the royal army is without its supreme commander. I hope nobody attacks us now—it'd be the end of Ultherst...

Who's gonna lead us now, when the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor is dead? The royal army is without its supreme commander... and any army without command flees when it comes to the first charge...
I see you're an inquisitor, Father—anyway, stay out of trouble!

It's harder and harder to keep the army in order. Defeatism spreads like cancer...

I'm sorry, knight, I can't spend any time chatting with you. I'm busy drilling my men. It's damn hard to keep at least a semblance of discipline and order. Damn times...
I understand. It's not easy to make your men perform their duty when everything around you goes to hell. Farewell.
With you in command the men don't have to fear anything, officer. Farewell.
Discipline is a must! Without discipline, they'd be climbing trees like squirrels! Not gonna happen!
I see. I wish you good luck, officer. Farewell.

Unfortunately yes...
Hmm... that means I gotta drill my man a bit more before it comes. Farewell, knight.

Yes, that's right. Orcs indeed appeared there...
Then I hope God's gonna save us. When even monsters from legends appear the Realm must be in a really bad shape...
Don't lose faith, soldier!
Yes, you're probably right. We must believe in our Lord!

I don't think it might be true, I know it! I was there fighting the orcs...
Oh my god! So it's really true! The Realm must be in a really bad shape, when even monsters from legends appear...

I'd have never thought that the roads around Glatzburg will be as dangerous as nowadays. Just imagine that—the last week an entire squad got massacred when delivering a message to Hillbrandt. Never heard about anything like that...
Everything will be alright, eventually. Nevertheless we must do something for that, soldier!
Yes, you're right...
Yes, the situation is terrible...
Well, when even God's knights admit it, there must be something to it...

Hello, knight. I tell you straight, knight, be careful behind the city walls—there are swarms of brigands who'd kill you before you could say Amen. And what's worse there are monsters crawling from every hole to feast on human flesh and blood! I can't help myself not to tremble in fear.
Yes, you're right. Farewell.
Don't be low, good man.
You're right. One should keep good mood and strong faith. Well, but to be honest, the last man talking like that was found cut into pieces by brigands. There wasn't much left of him, I can tell you!
Do you think there is any hope the Realm will be saved, knight?
Most certainly, soldier!

I'm glad to hear that. Now I may die more happily. We're gonna to deliver a message to Hillbrandt tomorrow and I'm sure I won't make it there... But a brighter future is doubtlessly awaiting our children. Farewell!
No, I don't think so. There isn't any hope.

Really? That's a pity, knight. We're gonna to deliver a message to Hillbrandt tomorrow and I'm sure I won't make it there... I am afraid there probably isn't any brighter future for our children. Farewell!
The service in the royal army is harder than ever these days, knight. I'd be so grateful if anything of those terrible things of the last few years did not happen...
Don't lose hope, soldier!
Easier said than done—you're a God's knight and God favors you. But nobody's interested in a poor footman... not even God himself!
I'll kill those bastards. Kill them all!
About whom are you talking, soldier?
Whom? All of them!!!
Right you are, soldier.

Of course they are! Do you think it could be otherwise?
Ehm... well, you've surprised me. I thought that you were still looking for infernal monsters. But if you say you got them all...

Just too many!
Hold on, good man. God won't let us falter on our way.
Yes, sure... God won't let us falter, that's right. Well, I'd like to get a more tangible assurance. Let's say a Glatzburg company of the royal army.

Well, it's almost certain... No, I'm sure of that!
I have no idea. Farewell.
Suppress your fear, good man. The Realm needs you.
Well, I guess you're right. Thanks, knight.

I'm afraid those orcs will attack us again soon, knight. Who can know how it's gonna end this time... Can you feel the ground trembling? I'd bet the greenos are up to something in their caves under the Moonshine Mountains...
Calm down, good man. Everything's going to be alright.
I'd love to be calm like you, knight. I hope you're right...
Then you must be ready to sacrifice your life in the defense of the town!
Yes, that's true. We're gonna show those infernal bastards!
Hillbrandt ain't my town. I'm from Ollheim, a small village near Glatzburg. I'm just doing my military service here... I don't wanna die here. My fiancé's waiting for me at home...

Where are they? Why ain't they attacking us again? I know they're lurking out there! Watching us with those green eyes of theirs, waiting. Come on, you bastards! I'm gonna chop you to pieces, you beasts. You're gonna vomit your own blood! Gonna kill you all!!!
Calm down, good man.

Can you feel the ground trembling? They're preparing some mischief. And that thick smoke coming from the iron mines... I can smell brimstone even here! That waiting's killing me. Let them attack, I'm gonna chop them to pieces then!
Excellent, good man. Your resolve does you credit. Farewell.

There're too few of us, noble lord. Damn few. While our numbers are thinning out every day, they're growing stronger out there. Soon they'll be stronger than us—I know it! Everything was heralded by that terrible storm. Till then, no monster had tried to attack the town. But everything changed after that storm. Dead left their graves, mines got flooded by orcs, the Moonshine Mountains are swarming with half-ogres and trolls, giant bats are circling the town at night... There're too many of them. Just too many!

Could you tell me, noble lord, if the end of the world is really coming, as our military chaplain keeps saying? One can't be sure these days—there're too many monsters out there to let one sleep soundly. Since that attack of the bloody greenos on the town, I've not slept much. How many of them can be hiding in the mountains? What do you think? More than us? I hope not. But it might be so. Well, it's almost certain... No, I'm sure of that!
Well, I guess you're right. Thanks, noble lord.

Where are they? Why ain't they attacking us again? I know they're lurking out there! Watching us with those green eyes of theirs—waiting. Come on, you bastards! I'm gonna chop you to pieces, you beasts. You're gonna vomit your own blood! Gonna kill you all!!!

Hello, noble lord. These are damn hard times we're living in—I can tell you. One can't be sure to see another morning. Those monsters are all around us... Where the hell are they coming from, anyway? A few years back, one would not have believed that all that fairytale stuff for children was true. Well, would you believe back then that you'd meet an orc one day? Nowadays they'd love to rip your head off if they meet you. Those are damn bad times, noble lord, I can tell you!
Let's hope everything will be alright, soldier.
I'm glad to hear that, soldier. Farewell.

Hello, knight. I admire you for what you did—defeating the orcish Khan Rashgar is quite a heroic deed. I'm sure that sneaking through the iron mines to the orcish caverns to slash Rashgar required quite some bravery!
It was God's will...
Yes, of course. Even though you've my admiration. Now we can take care about reopening the mines. And I tell you, if we meet any greenish monster there, we're gonna show it!
It was nothing...

Nothing?! I certainly wouldn't call it nothing, knight. I've never heard in my life about anybody who'd be able to do something like you did. Now we can take care about reopening the mines. And I tell you, if we meet any greenish monster there, we're gonna show it!

Halt! Theft is a terrible crime! You'll lose your right hand for that!
What?! That's some kind of a misunderstanding...
It's not a misunderstanding—you've committed a crime and you will be punished for it!
I'm afraid I will need my hand... Can we settle this problem in a different way?
Very well... instead of cutting off your hand I sentence you to an alternative punishment—forfeiture of property!
Agreed. Take everything I have...
Wise decision. And don't do it again!!!
I'm afraid I will need my stuff too!
Do you resist the royal authority?! In that case you lost your head!!!
Never!!!
At your service, noble lord! God protect the King!
What monsters have you met here in Hillbrandt?

There's lots of them, knight, I can tell you. You can run mostly into those stinky greenos who appeared not a long time ago marching from below the Moonshine Mountains like an army of bloody ghost massacring the iron mines and the mining village of Asherbalt. Since then they've been up to no good down there, cuz there's been thick black smoke coming from the mines. But the orcs ain't the only ones who could whack you near Hillbrandt. There are other monsters.

Trolls, knight. I'm sure you've heard 'bout them—at least from legends. My granny used to tell me that Old Nick himself created them from stones and wood as an anti... er... thesis of the human beings, who are made of bones and flesh. They can rip you in half in the blink of an eye. They're coming down from the mountains in packs to get their fill of flesh—no matter whose flesh it is. You can find lotsa those beast throughout the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains these days.

Wait a moment, knight, that's not all. You should also mind those giant bats. They're as big as a dire eagle and a whole lot more dangerous. They have maws full of sharp teeth and they attack in big flocks. They used to dare to attack only cattle or a solitary traveler—an only at night. These days you can't be sure even at high noon. Well, and if your duty calls you out of the town you should beware those giant spiders. The beasts are lurking behind every other rock and their poison's damn deadly.
Very well, I'll be careful. Thank you.
What can you tell me about orcs, soldier?

They're cursed beasts, knight. Nobody knows how it's possible they appeared out of the blue. Well, the miners had been telling stories about huge uncharted caverns beneath the mines which might be the antechambers of Hell itself. Anyway, who could have known that legions of bloodthirsty monsters our mothers used to tell fairytales about were going to swarm out of there?
That's true. Nevertheless, I'd like to hear something a bit more specific.

Of course, knight. Well, according to my observations there're several kinds of 'em bastards. I've met mostly warriors—huge toughguys seven feet tall swinging giant axes as if it were just sticks. Well, I've also met their priests, or whatever they call them. They're smaller, hunched and thinner. The problem is they know spells. Very nasty spells. They can turn you into a pool of stinky piss or set you afire just as one would light a torch. I tell you straight—I'd much rather end up chopped into pieces than to get into the claws of those dark priests of theirs. The word is they kidnap people to do terrible things to them. They torture and maltreat them so long that they get mad. Terrible. May the Archangel Gabriel himself protect us!

Yep, sure there are. Duke Weinberg offered rewards for killed orcs. Our Sheriff Contemburry pays them. Well, there ain't many guys getting rich that way. There were some adventurers and mercenaries who decided to go hunting orcs in the Moonshine Mountains, but only a few of them made it back alive. Anyway, I got some gold from that recent attack at the town, but I can tell you, it's a damn dangerous job.
I heard that not a long time ago orcs attacked the town and got behind the walls. How did it happen?

Yep, that's absolutely true, knight. I was guarding the Lower Gate that infernal night. It was raining as if some bloody flood was to come and so we were huddling around the fire. All of a sudden there was shouting and then wild roaring of those beasts coming from the north. We immediately sounded the alarm and headed there, but even on the way we meet the first orcs. It was clear as day that they somehow managed to get into the town. They spread throughout the town and killed everybody they met. Well, we were fighting scattered all over the town for some time until Sheriff Contemburry and Duke Weinberg rallied us. Well, then we pushed them out of the town pretty quickly. They were jumping off the stockades as if the Archangel Gabriel himself was swinging his flaming swords behind their sorry asses. After the battle we found out that the Upper Gate had been opened wide. The word is Master Edmond d'Arvias had done that...

To tell the truth, knight, I probably know something 'bout that brat. A few days back I saw him running out of the town along the old road that leads to the Dragon Rock. I told myself then that he were heading in a damn dangerous direction, well, on the other hand there ain't any safe place these days... Hope nothing happened to him. Well, he was a spoilt brat, but I'd hate of something bad happened to him.

No, I don't know anything about the theft of the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius. But the word is that it was a hellspawn pinching it—those priests praying in the church for the salvation of the town that night were damn hard to wake up the following morning. Somebody cast an unholy sleep spell to get rid of them!
I've heard he disappeared the night the greenos attacked the town. If they managed to get him alive I'm sure they sacrificed him to Old Nick himself...

The word is people saw her for the last time the night before the greenos attacked the town. Guess her fate was rather gruesome—if they managed to get her alive they could have done lotsa nasty thing to her. Poor Baron van Gallagan, what will he do without his wife? The word is she was everything to him... and also that she was behind everything, if you get me, knight... Anyway, I don't know anything 'bout her fate, so I can't help you.

There's no doubt Olfghard murdered her, knight. Her jewelry was found on him when he was trying to sell it to the stallholder Suzan Brauchner. But there's one thing I don't get—how could he escape from the jail? He must have gotten to the keys during that ruckus when the greenos attacked the town. I hope we're gonna catch and execute that loser real soon.

Got absolutely no idea, knight. The last time I saw him was when he returned from the merchant Reichmann—he said he wanted to ask him to give him his daughter. The guy was pretty outraged. Old Reichmann told him to bugger off before he could open his trap. Soldier's work wasn't good enough for him I guess. Maybe he thought that he could get a good dowry if he married into a rich family. What a dandy. Well, he was wrong. Anyway, haven't seen him since then.

Hello, knight. How is it going? You're coming to the town in damn bad times, I can tell you. It used to be rather calm in here, but things are different these days. Guess it's same in the rest of the Realm. Since the Scourges of God struck and those infernal beasts came out of their dark holes terrible atrocities have been happening. It's a shame they can't send us reinforcements. There're damn few of us here and the monsters are just growing in numbers.
Are you talking about orcs?

Not only orcs. If there were only those bloody greenos we could be able to do something to stop 'em. But there are other beasts. Much more dangerous, if you ask me. The mountains are infested by trolls. I remember my granny talking 'bout them. She used to make the sign of the cross every time she thanked God for destroying the infernal lot. Well, you see, they're back. And they're not alone. These are damn bad times, I can tell you. Who knows how that's gonna end?
We shall see. Thank you a lot.
Of course. I don't have anything better to do anyway. Nothing happens during the day... usually.
Hello, knight. It's a damn bad duty, if you ask me. All those monsters around us... one can't be sure to live to see retirement.
That's true. Could I ask you a few questions?
You're right, soldier. Farewell.

We meet at last, knight. I've been awaiting your arrival quite impatiently. I'm glad I can finally look into your eyes. To be honest, I get a lump in my throat when I'm looking into the face of my murderer from such a close distance—but the joyful image of you hanging at the scaffold makes me feel better!
What? Who are you and what are you talking about?

Names aren't important, knight. Don't try to make me think you remember the names of your victims. I doubt a professional killer such as you would remember the names of those who fell by his hand. So, why should you know my name? It's much more important that we've finally met here and that you're going to kill me here!
I'm no murderer. And I have absolutely no idea why I should take your life...

No murderer? Ha ha... allow me a little laugh. You're a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous—you know, all of them are murderers! You harass innocent people thinking that nobody can stop you. You're wrong. The Holy Scripture says that no crime shall be left without due punishment. And in your case it won't be different. You'll be hanged for murdering me!
I have no idea why I should take your life...

Oh, he has no idea! All right, I'll tell you—if you don't kill me, I'll kill you. Well, I doubt that I could, as I'm just a poor merchant. Nevertheless if you don't defend yourself, you're going to die. If you're going to defend yourself, I'm going to die. Either way I win, as you're going to die anyway. There are two witnesses over there in that bush. In case you kill me, they will testify that you blasphemed and decided to kill me because of your infernal lust for my blood. Isn't it ironic to die because of such a blatant lie? Well, that's exactly what's going to happen... the death of my brother, who was executed because a Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous accused him of a crime against the Realm to get hands on his wealth, will be avenged. Farewell, knight, give my regards to Grim Reaper, or to the executioner!
You are mistaken, the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous aren't murderers. Yes, they may make mistakes sometimes, but to err is human!

Shove your mistakes up your ass, knight. I know damn well how it's done. If you want to get somebody's property, you come and accuse him of a crime against the Realm. Then you torture him till he pleads guilty which means you can confiscate his property. That's exactly what you did to my poor brother. He professedly conspired against the King.
