But his death won't be left without punishment—at least in your case. You'll be hanged for murdering me!
You're not going anywhere, noble lord. I won't let my murderer leave like that. Murder must be punished!

I'd like to ask you to give my regards to my wife when you die. Tell her I loved her and I never wanted to hurt her... I wanted to tell it to her myself before God took her during the plague, but I didn't manage. I know that I'm going to get to Hell for how I treated her, but I'd like her to forgive me. Could you seek her out in Heaven and ask her to forgive me?
I'd love to help you out, good man, but my time here is not over yet and you could be waiting for years before our Lord calls me to him...
Well, that's where you are wrong, knight. I decided to ask you for help because I know that you're going to die soon and that as God's knight you're going straight to Heaven...
I don't understand... How can you be so sure that I'm going to die soon?

Because I'm going to kill you just here, knight! Tell my wife that although I'm going to burn in hell for this I loved her and that I didn't want to hurt her... Now, make yourself ready for the longest journey, knight!!!
Are your sins so great that you don't believe you could pass through Purgatory and be made one with your wife in the Kingdom of Heaven?
No, knight, I'm a real sinner. There's no other way than to ask you to pray for my salvation in Heaven instead of me. Could you do it for me?
Knight, could I ask you to do me a favor? It's terribly important and you as God's knight really can help me!
What do you need, good man?
I am sorry but I don't have time just now.
Then please make some, as this matter cannot be delayed. I've been waiting too long already...
Very well. What's the matter?
Don't bother me!

Don't worry, I'll make it quick—I'd like to ask you to give my regards to my wife in Heaven. Tell her I loved her and I never wanted to hurt her... I wanted to tell it to her myself before God took her during the plague, but I didn't manage. I know that I'm going to get to Hell for how I treated her, but I'd like her to forgive me. Could you seek her out in Heaven and ask her to forgive me?
Well, that's where you are wrong, Father. I decided to ask you for help because I know that you're going to die soon and that as a priest you're going to get straight to Heaven...

Because I'm going to kill you just here, Father! Tell my wife that although I'm going to burn in hell for this I loved her and that I didn't want to hurt her... Now, make yourself ready for the longest journey, Father!!!
No, Father, I'm a real sinner. There's no other way than to ask you to pray for my salvation in Heaven instead of me. Could you do it for me?
Father, could I ask you to do me a favor? It's terribly important and no one else than a priest can help me!
Well, that's where you are wrong, noble lord. I decided to ask you for help because I know that you're going to die soon and that as a noble you're going straight to Heaven...

Because I'm going to kill you just here, noble lord! Tell my wife that although I'm going to burn in hell for this I loved her and that I didn't want to hurt her... Now, make yourself ready for the longest journey, noble lord!!!
No, noble lord, I'm a real sinner. There's no other way than to ask you to pray for my salvation in Heaven instead of me. Could you do it for me?
Noble lord, could I ask you to do me a favor? It's terribly important and you as a noble really can help me!
Because I'm going to kill you—that's why! I got paid rather handsomely to help you out of this world and I'm going to take care of it just now!
Attacking a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous is the most serious crime, for that I declare your life forfeit!
What? Who paid you for my death? What a disgusting conspiracy is it?!
That's none of your business, knight. You're going to be dead anyway!
Hello, knight. I've been waiting for you so long. You're the paladin who has recently arrived to Hillbrandt, aren't you?
Yes, that's me. Why are you waiting for me?
No, it's not me, you've mistaken me for someone else...
Wait a moment, oh, no, it must be you, knight. I've never seen you around and I know every God's knight in this bloody diocese!
Then tell me why are you waiting for me?
Attacking an inquisitor is the most serious crime—for that I declare your life forfeit!
That's none of your business, Father. You're going to be dead anyway!
Hello, Father. I've been waiting for you so long. You're the priest who has recently arrived to Hillbrandt, aren't you?
Wait a moment, oh, no, it must be you, Father. I've never seen you around and I know every priest in this bloody diocese!
Attacking a noble is rebellion—for that I declare your life forfeit!
That's none of your business, noble lord. You're going to be dead anyway!
Hello, noble lord. I've been waiting for you so long. You're the noble who has recently arrived to Hillbrandt, aren't you?
Wait a moment, oh, no, it must be you, noble lord. I've never seen you around and I know every noble in this sleepy hollow!
Mad butcher Norman didn't lie—this must be the secret entrance into the hidden cellars under the innkeeper Bates's tavern!
Only God knows what horrors I'll find down there...
This secret entrance will allow me to descend into the hidden cellars under the innkeeper Bates's tavern.

These stairs would allow me to descend into the Royal Burial Chambers. Unfortunately it's beyond any doubt that the holy place, where the remains of the members of all the ruling houses of Ultherst used to be buried, has been taken by dark powers. The infernal flames won't allow me to enter...
I must keep praying for the salvation of this place. I hope that one day I'll be able to liberate it from the tainted influence of the Beast! Nevertheless I can't do anything about it right now...

These stairs will allow me to descend into the Royal Burial Chambers. It's beyond any doubt that the holy place, where the remains of the members of all the ruling houses of Ultherst used to be buried, has been taken by dark powers. Nonetheless it doesn't seem anything is preventing me from descending down there...
May the Archangel Gabriel himself light my way into the infernal abyss...
I think it'll be better if I stay away from it... at least for now!
This entrance leads to the secret underground chambers of Duke Rowan van Leerin.
But I'm not going down there right now.
It's locked. I must bring the key chamberlain Johaness Clifford gave me.
It seems I've discovered a forgotten entrance to the ancient sewers under Glatzburg.
It seems I've discovered a forgotten entrance to the Glatzburg underground... where does it go?
This entrance leads to the ancient sewers under Glatzburg.
Do you suspect anybody of the locals of heresy, Your Grace? Your testimony would be very valuable...

Do I suspect anybody of heresy? Well, it's hard to say. Of course I heard about Master Edmond d'Arvias. Supposedly he was seen letting the orcs into the town during their recent attack. I didn't see it myself and I hesitate to believe it, nevertheless I must admit that these times I wouldn't be too surprised at anything. Anyway, I definitely cannot testify against him because I didn't see him doing anything illegal. Nevertheless I must admit that those rumors about the conspiracy of the Brotherhood of the Righteous are troubling me. If it were proved that Master d'Arvias really is a heretic it'd explain many speculations...
Do you think that those accusations of heresy are true? That the Brotherhood of the Righteous is pursuing its own goals and is afraid that the Inquisition could reveal their crimes...

As I've already told you—it's hard to tell without evidence, nonetheless the behavior of the Order is at least strange when it comes to its relationship with the Holy Office. The one who has nothing to hide needn't be afraid...
Tell me, Your Grace, what do you think about the crisis the Realm has been dragged into?

Since I was appointed royal governor here in Hillbrandt I've not faced anything that terrible, knight. As the royal governor of the town I have almost unlimited power and I still can't cope with all the troubles plaguing us. The hellspawns outside the town walls almost have us in their grip. I believe they're going to besiege us soon. Then there's that heresy problem. If it were just a question of faith it certainly wouldn't be such a danger. Nevertheless, as the heretics allied themselves with hellspawns to destroy the town I can't be sure that I won't awake with an orcish saber on my throat. God made us face a really difficult trial, knight, that's for sure!
I've heard, Your Grace, that the Scourges of God didn't harm you at all. Don't you think it's a bit strange? You've lost no family members, your property is intact and your granaries full...

It seems you had a word with Baron Robert van Gallagan or with someone who helps him spread those nasty slanders. So to make it clear once and for all—I couldn't have lost any family members because I don't have any family. Me and my father were the last living Weinbergs and since his death I've been the only one. I have neither wife nor children so I could have hardly lost anyone during the plague. I admit that my granaries are full, but I doubt that any royal governor suffers from hunger even in these difficult times. After all, I'm a high ranking noble so I can get money if I need it. I can levy taxes, tolls, duties... whatever.

The fact my house wasn't burnt down during the Night of the Falling Stars and my herds of cattle was left unscathed can be attributed to plain luck. Your suggestion would mean that anybody with a house to stay in is a Satan worshipper. And as regards Baron van Gallagan himself—he's been pale with anger for years because he wanted to be given the office of the royal governor when Duke Derreck died. Do you know why His Highness Edward II appointed me and not van Gallagan? Because he's a totally incompetent half-wit! After all he can't control even his own wife—she can do with him whatever she wants. How could he be able to rule the town and the surrounding numerable domains?
That sounds reasonable. Nevertheless you wear your surcoat buttoned up even in the hottest summer days. Why?

Oh, you mean that rumor that I have the contract with Satan written all over my body? Don't be ridiculous, knight. My entire upper body has been mutilated since my participation in the royal campaign against the Kelbeginians. They poured hot pitch over me when we laid siege to Uprecht. It was a miracle I survived. Can you imagine how my skin looks?
Yes, I certainly can. Sorry for bothering you with that, Duke.
That's alright. I'm glad you perform your duty so thoroughly.
Would you mind if I took a look?
No, of course not. If you have nothing better to do, I'll gladly show you my mutilated body! Look... This is how God rewards those faithfully serving the King. Are you satisfied?!
Yes, Your Grace, please accept my apology.
That's alright, knight. You're doing JUST your duty, right?!
What monsters must you deal with in Hillbrandt, Your Grace?

Hillbrandt and its surroundings are drowning in monsters, knight. Until recently there had been just solitary cases of attacks caused by individual hellspawns, such as giant bats and spiders. Nonetheless it all changed and now we're facing enemies in rather military numbers. I've served in army so I know pretty well what I'm talking about. Everything seems to be pointing at a coming war—whatever may be behind it. I've sent several messages to Grand Duke Heidrick of Glatzburg describing in detail our situation and asking him to send reinforcements. Nonetheless I can't shake the feeling that they consider my reports to be at least exaggerated. Anyway, the truth is there are unconceivable hordes of enemies gathering in the mountains.

Yes, it is so, knight. I've not been to Glatzburg or to any other region of the Realm since the first Scourges of God struck us and thus I cannot judge how bad are the manifestations of infernal powers there, but here in Hillbrandt a war is inevitable. The thick black smoke that has been coming from inside the mines since the orcs massacred the miners and ransacked Asherbalt can't mean anything good. If you ask me, I think that the green skins are smelting iron and tempering steel—that's it! It's only a matter of time before we're stormed by an army of iron-clad devils.
What do you know about orcs?

I'm neither historian nor lore keeper to tell you about all the references to orcs. I'm a pragmatic man. When I see an enemy I must find a way how to defeat him. I don't care wherefrom the green skins came—if they were summoned from Hell or from a distant past. All that matters is that they're here and that I must find a way how to pave the road to Glatzburg with their skulls!

There are many strange things that happened during the last three years I could tell you about. Nonetheless the scariest thing that happened lately was that fierce storm that came rolling from the Moonshine Mountains. I had a feeling that the end of the world is coming. I've heard people talking about demons dancing in the sky that night. I'll tell you straight, knight, I'm not sure what I should think about such rumors. To be honest I also glimpsed something. I can't explain why I opened the window and looked outside despite the raging gusts of wind and pouring rain—I'd swear that for a second I saw the grinning face of a laughing demon in the sky. I know, it could have been just the play of light and shadows or a cloud lighted by a lightning bolt, but anyway... I can't shed the feeling the storm was just heralding something really bad. I've never seen a scarier storm in my life. Well the things happened rather quickly after it—orcs appeared, undead rose from their graves, trolls and half-ogres started coming in packs from the mountains...
Do you think there could be a connection?
Maybe. But I have no idea what connection it could be. Maybe it's just a coincidence. I really don't know.

Master Edmond d'Arvias as a heretic? I don't know, it's hard to tell. I've heard that some people saw him opening the gate for the orcs the night they attacked the town. I didn't see him myself and I hesitate to believe it, nevertheless I must admit that I wouldn't be surprised by anything these days. I definitely cannot testify against him because I didn't see him doing it myself.
Do you happen to know anything about the disappearance of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius?

You better don't mention the theft of the Monstrance of St. Orthenius aloud. Just thinking about it makes me so angry that I'd kill someone—sorry for the expression, but it's rather accurate. The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was providing the citizens of Hillbrandt with protection—especially spiritual and moral. Without it the locals quickly lose their faith and I've heard some rebellious talking that it'd be better to flee south, leaving the town to monsters. If we don't find the thief and the Monstrance as soon as possible I'm not sure how it could end. Unfortunately, despite my personal intervention in the case I had no luck and I don't have the slightest idea where the Monstrance could be hidden.

According to my investigation Bishop Quentinus disappeared the night the orcs attacked the town. I'm afraid they killed him—we weren't able to properly identify some of the bodies after that terrible bloodshed.

To be honest I didn't look for Linda van Gallagan too intensively. I know that she most likely disappeared during the attack of the orcs and to tell the truth I don't give a damn. I know that it's a sin to talk about my neighbors like that, but I can't help myself. Please, knight, forgive me my blasphemy, but Linda van Gallagan did all she could to set her husband against me, and she succeeded. That's why I cannot honestly feel pity that she disappeared without a single trace. I hope God will forgive me.
Someone stole the sword of Edmond d'Arvias. Do you know anything about it?

So you're investigating the theft of the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias. That's quite a suspicious case... I'd think that those paladins' swords are, as the symbols of the Order, carefully guarded by their owners. Moreover making an enemy of one of the most powerful men around by stealing his most precious treasure doesn't seem very wise to me—whoever the thief might have been. I smell brimstone in that, knight. God knows what those hellspawns are capable of in these hard times.
I've heard about the alleged murder of Natalia Reichmann which was supposedly committed by landsknecht Olfghard. What's your opinion?

The murder of Natalia Reichmann was not alleged—it was absolutely real! Too real, I'm afraid. Stefan Reichmann, Natalia's father, hasn't recovered from it yet. The tragedy has completely changed him. Natalia was everything to him; she was to become the sole heir of his considerable wealth and now she's up there. And all that because of that brigand Olfghard! I'm really sorry I didn't let him get executed the day he was apprehended. Instead he was allowed to escape and only God knows now where he's hiding.
Do you happen to have any idea, Your Grace, where the soldier Jullian could be hiding?

No I have no news about the whereabouts of the soldier named Jullian, knight. He's a deserter. I hope Sheriff Contemburry catches him really soon and his punishment makes an example of him. I don't want something like that to happen in my army again. I have enough problems with keeping up the morale of my men even without deserters.
I found a stray sheep, Your Grace. Is it yours by chance?
My sheep? I'm sorry, knight, but I don't know all the sheep in my flocks. Ask the shepherd Ruphert, he's taking care of them for me.
The shepherd Ruphert lost one of your sheep, Your Grace. I promised him to pay you for it. Could we settle it somehow?

Knight! You don't think that I'd accept money for a lost sheep from you, do you? It was you who killed the orcish Khan Rashgar... It'd be an insult. Don't be afraid about the sheep. I have so many sheep that it can't hurt me to have one less.
Very well, knight. Give me 20 gp and the debt will be settled. The shepherd Ruphert was lucky to have met you.
Here's the money, Your Grace.
Thank you, knight. Consider the sheep problem solved. I wish all my problems were like that!
I don't have that much, Your Grace.
Well, what can I do, knight?. Come back when you have the money. Or just forget about it. It's the shepherd Ruphert's problem.

If you're interested in clues and traces connected to the murder of the merchant Ollmier I have to disappoint you, knight. I don't know anything that could help the investigation. Nevertheless, if you'd like to know general aspects of the case, ask Sheriff Contemburry. I can tell you only that what others know—the murder was committed in the attic of the Truthorn's Inn and the method was quite contemptible. I've been trying very hard to apprehend and punish the perpetrator, unfortunately I've had no luck so far.

The rumors about a war are true. I indeed received orders from the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor not too long ago. The orders were unambiguous—we are to prepare for a campaign. My task is to put the Hillbrandt regiment on alert, to reinforce the defensive posts throughout the town, to commandeer horses and draft cattle and to fill up granaries and build up supplies. So it really seems a war is at hand. Only the enemy was not mentioned in the orders of the First Knight. It's strange because the monsters plaguing Hillbrandt can't be faced in the field of battle—that's absolutely obvious...
I'm sorry, but I can't speak about that—it's classified information!
You're a high ranking noble, Your Grace. Nevertheless I'm sure you know that even the nobility may be accused of heresy. You don't want to risk something like that for one simple answer, do you?
You don't like me, Your Grace, and I fully accept it. Nevertheless it's no reason to deny me the answer to my question. You're certainly well aware it's in the interest of justice.
You're a wise man, Your Grace. Somebody that clever certainly wouldn't refuse to answer someone such as me.
Orcish Khan Rashgar is dead, Your Grace. I killed him!
You killed... orcish Khan Rashgar, knight?! I find it hard to believe. After all, legends describe Rashgar as the terrible ruler of all the orcs who cannot be killed by any mortal hand!
Legends were wrong. Here's the proof—his head.

Goodness Gracious! May the Archangel Gabriel protect us! Never in my life have I seen an orc so hideous... Really, may Hell swallow me up, if it's not the head of the orcish Khan... Eh, God forgive me the blasphemy. It's really unbelievable news! I hope that without their Khan the infernal lot will crawl back into the holes which they came from in spring! It will be possible to reopen the iron mines! You must be a godsend, knight! Here's your reward—it's as much as I dare to take from the town treasury. The entire town is indebted to you, knight! I'll immediately send a company of soldiers into the mines. Hopefully we'll be able to reopen them soon.

Welcome to Hillbrandt, knight. I am Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. I'm really glad the Brotherhood of the Righteous strengthens its ranks in Hillbrandt. I hope it'll help to bring more safety into the town and to solve all the crimes Judge Vallarian and his inquisitors came to investigate more quickly. A few years ago I wouldn't be able to imagine in my wildest dreams that something that bad could happen in my domain. Nevertheless, now when it seems that the entire Realm is on the brink of destruction it doesn't surprise me that much. Why should Hillbrandt be spared of the rampage of heretics and pagans?
I'm sure you must be busy these days. Is there anything I could help you with?

I have been wrestling with many difficulties here in Hillbrandt lately, knight. Believe me, nothing was ever easy here, the less is it now when the Scourges of God have struck. The greatest danger is the damned green skins that have recently appeared in the Moonshine Mountains and massacred the whole mining village Asherbalt. You must have heard about that. No one knows where they came from. Maybe they really came from Hell itself as many people believe... In any case they have occupied the iron mines and have been preparing some devilish trick there since then.
Could I talk to you for a moment, Your Grace? I have some questions...
But of course, sir. Ask me about whatever you want. It's in my best interest to acquaint you with the situation in the town.
I would like to have a little talk with you, Your Grace. Of course only if you don't have anything urgent to attend to.
Go ahead, knight. I'll be glad to answer all your questions. The rest can wait...
I've heard that landsknecht Olfghard was charged with the murder of Natalia Reichmann.

Yes, that's true. He was apprehended when he was trying to sell some of the jewelry he had taken from her. A revolting case. The merchant Reichmann is one of the most respectable citizens of Hillbrandt. Why did it have to be his daughter that became the victim of such a terrible crime?!

Olfghard is innocent, Your Grace. Natalia Reichmann was kidnapped by the soldier Jullian, so he could get to the money of her father. I found him hiding together with kidnapped Natalia in an abandoned chapel near the Dragon Rock.
Really? Natalia was kidnapped by that deserter?! In that case Olfghard is innocent and all the accusations were false! I'm glad the truth was revealed. I'd hate to make a judicial error...
Me too, Your Grace. Farewell.
I understand. Nevertheless what could I do for you in that matter?

Well the rumor is the orcs are led by the legendary Khan named Rashgar. As a former soldier I'm sure that if you were able to kill that grand orc his lot would flee and scatter throughout the mountains, and I'd be able to retake the iron mines. Do you think, knight, that you could try to do it? I mean to eliminate that Rashgar and bring me his head.
Very well, I'll take care of it.

Really? I knew the task would be a challenge you would welcome... If you manage to kill him, you'll become part of the history of the town! Can I do something for you now or are you going to stalk that hellspawn right away?
It depends... Would there be any reward for it?
If you succeed you can count on a significant reward in gold. And if you fail I guarantee you a splendid funeral!
I'm sorry, but I'm no beast hunter.
Really? I've thought killing monsters is one of the duties of the Brotherhood of the Righteous... But what can I do? Anyway, can I help you somehow?
Greetings, knight. Have you good news for me? I mean, have you, by any chance, brought me the head of that grand orc Rashgar?
Unfortunately not yet, Your Grace.
No problem, knight. I'm sure you'll manage to succeed eventually. I'm sure it's divine will. Anyway, what can I do for you?
It certainly sounds like a good idea...
Indeed, knight. We will be finally able to stop waiting in the town to be slaughtered—we will be able to launch a counterstrike instead! Can I, my dearest knight, do anything for you now?

I'll immediately send a company of soldiers into the mines. Hopefully we'll be able to reopen them soon.

Welcome to Hillbrandt, Father. I am Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. I'm rather glad Judge Vallarian has another man at his disposal. I hope it'll help to solve all the crimes that have happened lately in my town. A few years back I wouldn't be able to imagine in my wildest dreams that something that bad could happen in my domain. Nevertheless, now when it seems that the entire Realm is on the brink of destruction it doesn't surprise me that much. Why should Hillbrandt be spared of the rampage of heretics and pagans?

I have been wrestling with many difficulties here in Hillbrandt lately, Father. Believe me, nothing was ever easy here, less now that the Scourges of God have struck. The greatest danger is the damned green skins that have appeared in the Moonshine Mountains recently and massacred the whole mining village of Asherbalt. You have surely heard about that. No one knows where they came from—maybe they really came from the Hell itself as many people believe... In any case they have occupied the iron mines and have been preparing some devilish tricks there since then.
But of course, Father. Ask me about whatever you want. It's in my best interest to contribute to the investigation of all the crimes.
Go ahead, Father. I'll be glad to answer all your questions. The rest can wait...

Well the rumor is the orcs are led by the legendary Khan named Rashgar. As a former soldier I'm sure that if you were able to kill that grand orc his lot would flee and scatter throughout the mountains, and I'd be able to retake the iron mines. Do you think, Father, that you could try to do it? I mean to eliminate that Rashgar and bring me his head.

Really? It's a pleasant surprise, Father. I know that work like that is not very typical of inquisitors... Nonetheless if you managed to kill him, you'd become part of the history of the town! Can I do something for you now or are you going to stalk that hellspawn right away?
I understand, Father. I know that you inquisitors have a bit different mission. Anyway, could I help you somehow?
Greetings, Father. Have you good news for me? I mean, have you, by any chance, brought me the head of that grand orc Rashgar?
No problem, Father. I'm sure you'll manage to succeed eventually. I'm sure it's divine will. Anyway, what can I do for you?
Indeed, Father. We will be finally able to stop waiting in the town to be slaughtered—we will be able to launch a counterstrike instead! Can I, my dearest Father, do anything for you now?

Since I was appointed royal governor here in Hillbrandt I've not faced anything that terrible, sir. As the royal governor of the town I have almost unlimited power and I still can't cope with all the troubles plaguing us. The hellspawns outside the town walls almost have us in their grip. I believe they're going to besiege us soon. Then there's that heresy problem. If it were just a question of faith it certainly wouldn't be such a danger. Nevertheless, as the heretics allied themselves with hellspawns to destroy the town I can't be sure that I won't awake with an orcish saber on my throat. God made us face a really difficult trial, sir, that's for sure!

Oh, you mean that rumor that I have the contract with Satan written all over my body? Don't be ridiculous, sir. My entire upper body has been mutilated since my participation in the royal campaign against the Kelbeginians. They poured hot pitch over me when we laid siege to Uprecht. It was a miracle I survived. Can you imagine how my skin looks?
That's alright, sir. You're doing JUST your duty, right?!

Hillbrandt and its surroundings are drowning in monsters, sir. Until recently there had been just solitary cases of attacks caused by individual hellspawns, such as giant bats and spiders. Nonetheless it all changed and now we're facing enemies in rather military numbers. I've served in army so I know pretty well what I'm talking about. Everything seems to be pointing at a coming war—whatever may be behind it. I've sent several messages to Grand Duke Heidrick of Glatzburg describing in detail our situation and asking him to send reinforcements. Nonetheless I can't shake the feeling that they consider my reports to be at least exaggerated. Anyway, the truth is there are unconceivable hordes of enemies gathering in the mountains.

Yes, it is so, sir. I've not been to Glatzburg or to any other region of the Realm since the first Scourges of God struck us and thus I cannot judge how bad are the manifestations of infernal powers there, but here in Hillbrandt a war is inevitable. The thick black smoke that has been coming from inside the mines since the orcs massacred the miners and ransacked Asherbalt can't mean anything good. If you ask me, I think that the green skins are smelting iron and tempering steel—that's it! It's only a matter of time before we're stormed by an army of iron-clad devils.

There are many strange things that happened during the last three years I could tell you about. Nonetheless the scariest thing that happened lately was that fierce storm that came rolling from the Moonshine Mountains. I had a feeling that the end of the world is coming. I've heard people talking about demons dancing in the sky that night. I'll tell you straight, sir, I'm not sure what I should think about such rumors. To be honest I also glimpsed something. I can't explain why I opened the window and looked outside despite the raging gusts of wind and pouring rain—I'd swear that for a second I saw the grinning face of a laughing demon in the sky. I know, it could have been just the play of light and shadows or a cloud lighted by a lightning bolt, but anyway... I can't shed the feeling the storm was just heralding something really bad. I've never seen a scarier storm in my life. Well the things happened rather quickly after it—orcs appeared, undead rose from their graves, trolls and half-ogres started coming in packs from the mountains...

To be honest I didn't look for Linda van Gallagan too intensively. I know that she most likely disappeared during the attack of the orcs and to tell the truth I don't give a damn. I know that it's a sin to talk about my neighbors like that, but I can't help myself. Please, sir, forgive me my blasphemy, but Linda van Gallagan did all she could to set her husband against me, and she succeeded. That's why I cannot honestly feel pity that she disappeared without a single trace. I hope God will forgive me.

So you're investigating the theft of the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias. That's quite a suspicious case... I'd think that those paladins' swords are, as the symbols of the Order, carefully guarded by their owners. Moreover making an enemy of one of the most powerful men around by stealing his most precious treasure doesn't seem very wise to me—whoever the thief might have been. I smell brimstone in that, sir. God knows what those hellspawns are capable of in these hard times.

No I have no news about the whereabouts of the soldier named Jullian, sir. He's a deserter. I hope Sheriff Contemburry catches him really soon and his punishment makes an example of him. I don't want something like that to happen in my army again. I have enough problems with keeping up the morale of my men even without deserters.
My sheep? I'm sorry, sir, but I don't know all the sheep in my flocks. Ask the shepherd Ruphert, he's taking care of them for me.

Sir! You don't think that I'd accept money for a lost sheep from you, do you? It was you who killed the orcish Khan Rashgar... It'd be an insult. Don't be afraid about the sheep. I have so many sheep that it can't hurt me to have one less.
Very well, sir. Give me 20 gp and the debt will be settled. The shepherd Ruphert was lucky to have met you.
Thank you, sir. Consider the sheep problem solved. I wish all my problems were like that!
Well, what can I do, sir?. Come back when you have the money. Or just forget about it. It's the shepherd Ruphert's problem.

If you're interested in clues and traces connected to the murder of the merchant Ollmier I have to disappoint you, sir. I don't know anything that could help the investigation. Nevertheless, if you'd like to know general aspects of the case, ask Sheriff Contemburry. I can tell you only that what others know—the murder was committed in the attic of the Truthorn's Inn and the method was quite contemptible. I've been trying very hard to apprehend and punish the perpetrator, unfortunately I've had no luck so far.
You're a high-ranking noble, Duke. Nevertheless I'm sure you know that even the nobility may be accused of heresy. You don't want to risk something like that for one simple answer, do you?

You don't like me, Duke, and I fully accept it. Nevertheless, it's no reason to deny me the answer to my question. You're certainly well aware it's very important for the investigation I'm conducting.
You killed... orcish Khan Rashgar, sir?! I find it hard to believe. After all, legends describe Rashgar as the terrible ruler of all the orcs who cannot be killed by any mortal hand!

Goodness Gracious! May the Archangel Gabriel protect us! Never in my life have I seen an orc so hideous... Really, may Hell swallow me up, if it's not the head of the orcish Khan... It's really unbelievable news! I hope that without their Khan the infernal lot will crawl back into the holes which they came from in spring! You must be godsend, sir! Here's your reward—it's as much as I dare to take from the town treasury. The entire town is indebted to you, sir!

Welcome to Hillbrandt, sir. I am Duke Weinberg, the royal governor of the town. I impatiently awaited your arrival—I was told you were to take over Asherbalt, the small domain in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Congratulations, although I won't hide that you'll have to fight out your domain first. At the beginning of the spring it has fallen into the hands of orcs who had crawled out of the dark bowels of the Moonshine Mountains. Nobody in Asherbalt survived their attack.
Well... that isn't good news at all. I'm sure you must be busy these days, Duke. Is there anything I could help you with?

I have been wrestling with many difficulties here in Hillbrandt lately, sir. Believe me, nothing was ever easy here, the less is it now when the Scourges of God have struck. The greatest danger is the damned green skins that have recently appeared in the Moonshine Mountains and massacred the whole mining village of Asherbalt. You must have heard about that. No one knows where they came from—maybe they really came from Hell itself as many people believe... In any case they have complicated my life a lot by occupying the iron mines.
Go ahead, sir. I'll be glad to answer all your questions. The rest can wait...

Well the rumor is the orcs are led by the legendary Khan named Rashgar. As a former soldier I'm sure that if you were able to kill that grand orc his lot would flee and scatter throughout the mountains, and I'd be able to retake the iron mines. Do you think, sir, that you could try to do it? I mean to eliminate that Rashgar and bring me his head.

Really? That's a pleasant surprise, sir. I know such work isn't quite typical for a noble... If you manage to kill him, you'll become part of the history of the town! Can I do something for you now or are you going to stalk that hellspawn right away?
I understand. Nothing can be done then. Anyway, can I help you somehow?
Greetings, sir. Have you good news for me? I mean, have you, by any chance, brought me the head of that grand orc Rashgar?
No problem, sir. I'm sure you'll manage to succeed eventually. I'm sure it's divine will. Anyway, what can I do for you?
Indeed, sir. We will be finally able to stop waiting in the town to be slaughtered—we will be able to launch a counterstrike instead! Can I, my dearest sir, do anything for you now?

The title of a Baron can be bestowed only upon a Squire who proves his utter loyalty to the Realm and who accomplishes a task given to him for the greater good of the Realm. And pays 5,000 gp. for the entry into the Gold Book of the Realm, of course...
I'd like to get the title of a Baron, Duke.
Really? And do you deem yourself sufficiently loyal to the Realm? Do you deem yourself ready to sacrifice yourself for your country?!
Yes, Duke, I'm ready!

In that case I'll give you a task that'll test your loyalty and devotion. For ages, Hillbrandt was protected by a holy relic, which shielded it from all evil. It was the Monstrance of St. Orthenius. According to an ancient legend the monstrance was consecrated by the patron saint of the Realm, St. Orthenius himself, in 221. It was carried to Hillbrandt by its first Bishop Albertinus in 339 and it became the most valued treasure of the Holy Mother Church in this part of the Realm. The monstrance was kept in the Church of St. Orthenius. Not a long time ago it has mysteriously disappeared. Your task will be to find the relic and to find out who was the perpetrator of that heinous crime.

By a lucky coincidence, I've already solved the case, Duke. The Monstrance of St. Orthenius was stolen by priest Romius. He was serving the undead Bishop Herbertius who had apparently risen from his grave. I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Unbelievable! Are you telling me that Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? That's infernal! And as if it was not enough, according to your words priest Romius was commanded by that spawn of darkness to steal the monstrance. A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers... I find it hard to believe, nevertheless I can't doubt your words, sir. It is obvious that heresy has rooted itself deep in this town—it has infected even the ranks of the Church. Nevertheless I am glad to say that you've completed your task with excellence! The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed. That means I'm free to bestow the title of Baron of Asherbalt upon you. That is if you have 5,000 gp. to pay for the entry into the Gold Book of the Realm...

By coincidence, I've already solved a part of the case, Duke. I found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on undead Bishop Herbertius who apparently rose from his grave and somehow managed to get the monstrance. Anyway, I killed him and brought the monstrance back. Here it is.

Indeed?! Are you telling me that the former Hillbrandt Bishop Herbertius rose from his grave? And that you found the Monstrance of St. Orthenius on him? Diabolical indeed! Nevertheless it's good that the monstrance is back. Hopefully it will help Hillbrandt to rest once again under the divine protection. Did you manage to find out who had stolen the monstrance? Because it's obvious that Herbertius could not do that—such an infernal abomination could not have set its foot on the holy ground...
No, Duke, I've not managed to find out yet.
Then keep on searching till you find him, sir. I am sure you will find the perpetrator eventually.
Of course, Duke. Farewell
I will do my best to apprehend the perpetrator as soon as I can and to return the relic to its rightful place, Duke. Farewell.
I have retrieved the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Duke. The undead Bishop Herbertius had it on him. It turned out he rose from his grave.
I found out who stole the Monstrance of St. Orthenius, Duke.

What?! A priest of the Holy Mother Church enthralled by infernal powers? I find it hard to believe... though I believe your words, sir. It is obvious that heresy has rooted itself deep in this town—it has infected even the ranks of the Church. In any case I am glad to say that you've completed your task with excellence! The monstrance is back and the perpetrator is revealed which means I'm free to bestow the title of Baron of Asherbalt upon you. That is if you have 5,000 gp. to pay for the entry into the Gold Book of the Realm.
I'm bringing you 5,000 gp. to get my name written into the Gold Book of the Realm, Duke. I hope you can bestow the title of a Baron upon me now.
Never mind, Baron. In that case return to me when you have 5,000 gp. and the baronial title will be yours.

Great! By paying 5,000 gp. you got the right to be written into the Gold Book of the Realm. I hereby declare you Baron of Asherbalt! Accept this item as the symbol of your new standing! I'll also send a company of soldiers and Sheriff as a new crew of Asherbaltu. And don't forget you can now recruit one soldier to your party.
Thank you, Duke. Farewell.
What conditions do I have to meet to get a baronial title, Duke?

All the same I hope you'll manage to take over the rule in Asherbalt and that you contribute to strengthening the King's power in this God-forsaken corner of the Realm. Only several years ago I would never had dreamt of something like that happening on my domain... But now, when the Realm is on the verge of destruction, it doesn't seem all that much strange. Why should only Hillbrandt be left untouched by the rampage of heretics and hellspawns?
Has something noteworthy happened in Glatzburg recently?

To tell the truth I'm quite disturbed by how Johaness Clifford has behaved recently, knight. I don't know what happened to him but he has been acting as if he were someone else. We've known each other since our childhood and we're good friends. We've always been honest and frank with each other and confided everything to ourselves. But now Johaness is a changed man—he's gloomy, doesn't go out and he doesn't talk with anybody. Something had to happen to him, I know him too well to think otherwise. But I can't imagine what it could be.
You're welcome, knight. Maybe you should pay him a visit and try to find out what's going on...

So you want to know if something noteworthy has happened... Well, I personally can't understand how it's possible the soldier Harph, who used to owe me a great amount of money for drinks until recently, is now splashing out gold with both his hands. It can't be his soldier's pay—soldiers live in misery and squalor—and he has been never good at gambling. So I'm asking where he got all the gold of his? He's paying like a lord now... He's my most generous customer! Well, I certainly don't complain, that's true, at least as long as he pays me!
I've heard you accused Tinthan the Comedian of theft, innkeeper.

Yes, that's true. I caught the petty scrub stealing in the episcopal cathedral. It was his turn finally! He stole all sorts of things here in Glatzburg, but no one caught him in the act. He was laughing into our faces for a lot of years, damned vulture. But now he's gonna get what he deserves. God's justice is slow but sure. I'll gladly go to have a look at his execution!
Tinthan asserts it's only your personal revenge, for him owing you money for meals and drinks. What can you tell me about that?
Yes, he owes me some money, that's true. But I saw him stealing, it's as sure as there's God above me. His debt has nothing to do with that.
I think you're lying, innkeeper. I want you to take your testimony back!
And why should I do that, knight? With all due respect—I caught the thief in the act and I don't see a single reason to let him get away with that!
I appeal to your conscience, good man—don't allow an innocent man to be sentenced only because of your personal revenge. Take your testimony back, please!
And why should I do that, knight? What's wrong with me testifying against the thief I caught in the act?! I won't take my testimony back!
Maybe you're telling the truth, and maybe not. In any case I want you to take the testimony back.
Do you offer any gambling here? I'd like to get some money.
Gambling in my inn? What a strange idea is that, knight? This is a decent establishment!
What a shame... I was looking for some reasonable use for my gold...

Really? Then wait a moment, knight. I thought that... well, it doesn't matter what I thought. If you are really interested we certainly can come to terms. You know, I don't want to get into trouble. But now and then a customer plays the Devil's Emissary with me. So if you're interested just tell me. Discreetly, of course!
I've thought so. I've never asked about that, right?
And if some, ehm... gambling... was played here, knight, would you be interested?
Yes, I'd like to play.

Really? It surprises me... and pleases too. If you're really interested we certainly can come to terms. You know, I don't want to get into trouble. But now and then a customer plays the Devil's Emissary with me. So if you're interested just tell me. Discreetly, of course!
Of course not! Gambling is a sin and a crime!
Certainly! And that's the reason I don't offer any here.

By the grace of God our ruler is His Serene Highness Grand Duke Robert Heidrick—may he live forever. He holds the office of the royal governor. His vice is Duke Rowan van Leerin. It's said he seeks after the office of the governor himself, but he doesn't have the necessary support in the royal court for that.
Who will sell me some goods here in Glatzburg? Except for you, of course.

My shop isn't enough for you, knight? I assure you all my wares are of the first-class quality and by far the best far and near. Nevertheless there are other shops around. Hans von Drichtmaul has a renowned armory in Glatzburg. The wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt and the alchemist Paolus Ventimus will sell you potions and various magic items. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch, and of course myself, sell all sorts of things. And if I may give you advice, avoid Alphonso DiCerbio. He sets up for a tradesman but in truth he's a mere thief and brazenly sells stolen goods.

Don't be angry with me, knight, but I hate to talk about such things as the crisis the Realm has been dragged into. Those things aren't my cup of tea. I'm only a common and humble man trying not to lose his livelihood in these terrible times. I go to church regularly, make confessions, pay the tithes... and I don't care about anything else. All that's the work of heretics and heathens consorting with demons at nights, holding up their wanton asses for them and getting various devilish advantages for that. May plague and smallpox get them, knight. I hope they all fly out the chimney, if you know what I mean.
I've heard some tidings about a war coming. Do you know anything about that? Maybe you have heard something more...

There's much talking about a war, that's true. The whole royal regiment is on alert and no soldier may leave the city so they visit my inn more often than the drill-grounds. And they keep talking about various things—they say that the new commands from Alvaron have come to get ready and stay, so that new soldiers are being recruited and drilled to be ready for marching out and that horses and draft cattle are being requisitioned... I myself have lost two geldings and three oxen that way. But such it is these days, we can't do anything about it. People are quite terrified by all that silent humbug. It would be really bad if the war was to start. The strangest thing is that there's no enemy around to wage the war against. It's all quite weird.

If I remember it right Sheriff Smith pays rewards in gold for heads or scalps of the footpads rampaging by the roads in the vicinity of the city. The reward was announced by His Serene Highness Grand Duke Robert Heidrick—may he live forever—in an effort to crack down on the waylaying that has spread far too much recently. Hardly any merchant or wayfarer is able to walk the roads without losing his belongings or his life—perhaps even both.

If I have some suspicions of heresy? Well... a man hears many things, especially here in the inn after guests have a few pitchers of beer in them. They often speak about Enrie Jungwirdt. Those prophecies of hers reputedly have something to do with the idolatry and she's said to brew poisons and various devilish potions and to have all sorts of unclean filth inside her house... But even Master Raimond Ventano gets his batch of gossip. Hardly anybody enters his house, he stays there locked whole days and you can hear weird sounds from there at night. But I don't give much about those gabbles. I gladly serve them beer and lay the table for them when they occasionally pay my inn a visit, or sell them something they need. But one may never know... Maybe you should check them out, knight.

Many evil things have happened here lately, that's true. For example that wild tempest that raged above the city several days ago. It was so furious that there were demons and hellspawns dancing in the sky like Hell itself opened and the infernal parade went out to have fun in the night air. People have been timorous since then and the already ill humor got even worse. And my income with it. If it continues that way I will have to close the place in a couple of months...

The murder of reverend Monsignor Trevorius is the worst disaster that could befall us. What will we do now without His Excellency? Who will pour hope into our bleeding hearts during masses? Why had it to go so far that even diocesan Bishops are becoming victims of murders? What will we do...

Those dead men in the city streets—that's all we need, really. One is afraid to open his door at night, and even so many people lost their lives... God knows what a devilry it is. People say the dead men behave quite weirdly. Not that they aren't killing and eating brains and such—they do that, of course. But reputedly they do other things too, and that's weird. They for example rob their victims. That's not normal, is it? That a dead man will kill you and deprive you of your bodily entrails, that's sort of expectable. But that he will then rob you? I've never heard about that. What do they do with all that money? Don't pretend to me that someone in the city sells them something for it. I would never serve them if they marched in here. This is a decent establishment!

If you're looking for a stolen jewelry, then try asking the mongrel Tinthan. He's pretending to be an artist, a great actor, but he's just a thief. He would easily steal the nose from between your eyes and when you looked for it, he would maintain that you never had it there.

I think that the accusation of Hans Thomas Brookwelt is damned nonsense. I've known him personally for many long years and I swear he's no damned heretic. Just to the contrary—he's a diligent and religious man, although of low descent. His craft of carpentry is now paying more than anytime before because coffins are in high demand. So if he wanted to marry a woman he would only have to clatter the coins and she would draw him to the church herself. No, that man doesn't stand in need of trying some witching tricks on anybody. He's a toiler and a good churchgoer.

It seems there's been heaps of those suspicions of heresy lately. Do you mean Jeanette, the servant girl of Baron von Hunth? It doesn't seem probable to me. I don't know the girl well, she comes here only occasionally with Baroness Helen von Hunth during the market days, but I haven't heard a single bad word about her. She's quite sheepish and not too beautiful, so she probably doesn't have many suitors, but that doesn't mean she has to be a witch flying to Sabbaths at full moons. No, I don't believe that.
I almost forgot, knight—I have a letter for you here.
Look, innkeeper—either you'll answer me or I'll ensure this day is the worst one in your whole life!
Maybe you don't like me, innkeeper, but if you think about my question you surely will find out your answer won't do any harm.

You're a cautious man, innkeeper, I can see that at first sight. And it's quite a laudable quality, especially in the days we're living in. But I'm sure that in my case you don't need to be so wary. Your answer would really help me a lot.
A letter? What letter?
Just a letter, knight. For you. Here it is.
And is it really addressed to me? I've not been here in Glatzburg for too long...
You've recently come from Hillbrandt, haven't you? In that case it's for you.
Who gave you the letter?

A messenger, knight. He came several days ago, gave me the letter and told me you would surely come here. And as you can see, he was right. Moreover he told me you would be waiting for the letter. Is it true?
Yes, in fact that's true.
That's none of your business, innkeeper!
Well... you're right, knight. I'm sorry.
Maybe. I'm not sure.
Hmm... In any case it's none of my business, right?!
Who is the letter from?
How do I know that? Do you think I read letters belonging to others? Moreover it's sealed, as you can see.
Hmm... thanks, innkeeper. Farewell.
Hmm... thanks, innkeeper. Now I'd like to see your wares.
Look, innkeeper—either you'll take your testimony back, or you'll get yourself into quite a messy situation, I guarantee it!

I?! And for what?! I didn't rob anybody. What justice is this? A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous threatens me with arrest because I testified against a notorious thief whom I caught in the act! But as you like, knight, I'll take my testimony back, if you wish so. I don't want to get into trouble because of that damned scrub...
That's a wise decision, good man.
If my words can't persuade you, I'm willing to pay you for the cooperation. What would you say if I offered you 250 gp?
You're offering me a bribe for taking back my testimony against Tinthan? I've never seen something like that before... But as you wish, sir knight. Give me 2,000 gp and we have a deal.
Wise decision, good man. Here is yur money and good bye!
And what will it be, knight? Beer or mead?
Here you are, knight. I kindly request you to pay me 1 gp.
In that case you surely understand I won't serve you. I'm sorry, but I don't sell on credit. Otherwise I would be broke really fast! May I do something else for you?
In that case you surely understand I won't serve you. I'm sorry, but I don't sell on credit. Otherwise I would be broke in no time! May I do something else for you?
I understand, you want something stronger. Here you are, knight. I kindly request you to pay me 1 gp.
Here you are, knight. It will be 1 gp.
Don't be angry with me, knight, but I won't sell you any more drinks. Somebody could accuse me of tempting you to sin. You know how difficult it is these days. Though, can I do anything else for you?

I take several cards from the deck—you decide how many, but five at the most. One of them is the Devil's Emissary. The cards are put on the table, turned and I shuffle them before your eyes. And you have to decide what card is the Devil's Emissary. The bet is always 10 gp. and in the game two, three, four or five cards are used. According to that you may win 20 gp, 35 gp, 50 gp or 65 gp.
I'm sorry, knight, but I'm not going to play with you any more. You deprived me of too much money for me to play on. I'll stay away from gambling for a while. May I do something else for you?
In that case come back when you have at least 10 gp, knight. Farewell.

Damned villains! Disgusting footpads! Filthy scavengers! May the plague kill them, treacherous scoundrels! What will I do? Now, when my precious goods are in the hands of mean criminals?! What will the nobility of Alvaron think of me now? I can tell you! They'll think what kind of establishment is this that they don't have any wine worthy of real aristocrats? What a God-forsaken back of beyond is this? And I endeavored so much! It cost me a fortune and now it's gone because of those sods who rob and murder on the royal roads!
Hello, innkeeper. What's going on? What has happened to you?

Ah... forgive me, knight, I didn't notice you. Welcome to the King Edward's Inn. I'm Weintraum the Innkeeper—at your service. What can I do for you? Would you like to rent a room or maybe to buy some food or drinks, to your heart's content? Every single one of our dishes is exquisite, as you're surely going to find out for yourself. Or maybe you want to buy or sell some goods? My shop is fully at your service...
Maybe later, good man. But now tell me why did you lament so much? What has happened to you?

You want to know what has happened to me? Don't even ask, knight. It was a terrible accident. It will cost me all the reputation I've been building for all my life. I'm done for, totally done. Unbelievable! But in these hard times our Holy Mother Church is willing to accept even such hardened and unfaithful men back to our ranks. The heart of this sinful man may be purified by the purgative flames of justice that will relieve it from the sinful body. Hence I sentence Raimond Ventano in the name of God Almighty to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. May God be merciful to his soul.

The man has perpetrated really terrible deeds, although he took an oath to the King and God! At least if what the prosecution claims is true. Because the evidence presented is not enough to prove the guilt beyond reasonable doubt—although they raise just suspicion...

I know, Your Honor. But there's another evidence. Commander Ethien de Pasque was arrested on the basis of the suspicion of heresy and put to torture. In that case I can't do otherwise but to declare the guilt of Commander Ethien de Pasque was proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Let's look at the monstrous disguise the man used to conceal his deeds. He in his disgusting pride didn't detest the most condemnable crimes!

How disgusting! If it really was so, it would mean that heresy of the worst kind is able to penetrate even the hearts of high-ranking persons in the Realm. What other evidence does the prosecution have that could convince us of the guilt of Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick?

Dietrich the gravedigger confessed he purveyed the dead body of a mad girl for the Grand Duchess and her henchmen, and that he did it for a payment. The heretics needed the corpse for invoking the fallen angel Baphomet.

I must say I'm disgusted at the crimes Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick is charged with. At the same time I must express doubts she really perpetrated them. The evidence brought forth—although it raises some suspicions about the Grand Duchess—isn't enough to prove the guilt. Does the prosecution have any other convincing proof?

And those creatures in fact came to help her during the torture!

God! What terrible crimes Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick did perpetrate! Of what disgusting offences against God's name, and against all what's sacred was the woman able to do! Hence I in the name of God and by virtue of the authority given to me sentence Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to her soul. Ignite the stake, son!

Thank you, Your Honor. With your kind permission I'd like to present the evidence against the defendant Cardinal Truncquillius.

Your Honor, allow me to bring forth the first proof of the guilt of Cardinal Truncquillius. Yes, that's possible. But there's also the possibility the Grand Duchess lied in her perversity and tried to defame Cardinal Truncquillius, who has always seemed to be the firm bastion in the fight against heresy. What would you say to that, brother?

Yes, it's impossible to forego that possibility. But there is yet other evidence that convicts Cardinal Truncquillius. There were certain letters found on him in which he's instructed in great detail, what steps shall be undertaken to successfully invoke the fallen angel Baphomet.
Hmmm... it's really alarming. But the letters may be fabricated, forged or replaced to deceive the attentive sight of the Holy Office. Don't you think so, son?!

It's possible, Your Honor. But let me continue. As more proof I'd like to present the testimony of Master Dieter von Gelbendiel, the highest superior of the local chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. It's beyond reasonable doubt the other heretic was Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick and that they spoke about the invocation of the fallen angel Baphomet. And the Grand Duchess along with Commander Ethien de Pasque and Raimond Ventano really performed the said rite later on!

Oh... I have to admit it's really very convincing proof. Certainly nobody would have the nerve to dispute the testimony of the Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. But you've said, brother, that Master Dieter von Gelbendiel witnessed the alleged talk in the evening time. It's possible he mistook Cardinal Truncquillius for somebody else, isn't it?

Yes, Your Honor. But I have proof Master Dieter von Gelbendiel wasn't mistaken and that he saw exactly that what he's now saying he did. Cardinal Truncquillius confessed to all his sins! But that was not enough! He subjected me to the infernal seduction and tried to win me for his cause!

Oh my God! If it's really true... then Cardinal Truncquillius is guilty beyond reasonable doubt! Alas for us who blindly believed his words! Alas a hundredfold for all those who weren't able even to dream about disputing that, what in his case seemed indisputable—the strength of his faith and the purity of his soul! Now, in the light of the evidence brought forth, I have no other choice than to find Cardinal Truncquillius guilty of all the points of the indictment. Hereby I, in the name of God and by the power invested in me sentence Cardinal Truncquillius to be burned to death. The sentence is to be executed immediately. Let God be merciful to his soul. Ignite the stake, son!
Can you show those letters to the court?
Yes, I can. But I would like to have the letters back for the reason of further investigation.
Unfortunately not, Your Honor. I don't have them on me.
In that case I suspend the proceeding until you bring the letters. Otherwise I can't accept them as an evidence against cardinal Truncquillius.
I ask the prosecution, if they are able to show us the letters proving the guilty of cardinal Truncquillius now?
Can you show the diary to the court?
Here it is!

Can you show the fiary to the court?
Do you happen to know some details about the priest Frederick, Your Honor?

I know about Father Frederick more than anyone else, son. Why, he was my longtime tutor and mentor! His name will stay engraved in my memory as long as I live. It was he who led me to the bosom of the Holy Mother Church and it was he who at the end of his life greatly encouraged me to become a member of the Holy Office. Father Frederick was a very wise man. He traveled a lot. He visited the Empire and dwelt at the Papal Court. He traveled through all the faithful realms of Kalmariland and talked with their highest church officials. According to his words—and I definitely don't doubt them—he visited even the Holy Grave of the First Prophet in Jevaran and bowed before his remains. He was the most educated and the most wise man I've ever met. And moreover he was as modest as every priest should be.
I understand. He had to be a man worthy of following.

Exactly, son. But he was also a fierce enemy of dark powers, a soldier of God. Do you know he was one of the last priests able to perform the rite of exorcism? Yes, it's true! During his lifetime he managed to free dozens of possessed people of demons and other unclean powers. He was good at it as nobody else was. Regrettably he had no successor. All the more I'm saddened God summoned him to his kingdom two years ago—he took to his grave all his knowledge and skills. I miss him greatly. I often used to go to pray to his grave in the Sepulcher before the cemetery succumbed to the power of the Beast. I hope his remains and souls remained untouched by the powers of Hell.
I found out that the accusation of the trickster Tinthan, of stealing the Monstrance of Saint Rhodric from the Bishopal temple was false. I would like to acquit him.

That's noble of you, son. But tell me, why are you telling it to me? Crimes not regarding the faith are in the jurisdiction of the temporal power, not in the jurisdiction of the Church. Turn to Grand Duke Heidrick with that case.

The Temporal power in this city is represented by Grand Duke Robert Heidrick in the office of the royal governor. The vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin. But otherwise we are all in the hands of God, of course.

It depends on what exactly are you asking about, son. You want to know my opinion about what's the cause of all what has befallen the Realm? Alright, I'll tell you. The cause of all that is the smallness of people. People are creatures that have to be led. As a herd of sheep—by the firm hand of the shepherd. Only then the herd thrives, grows and is content. It's not in vain that the Holy Scriptures say: God is our shepherd and we're his humble sheep. And behold! The firm hand of the shepherd has relaxed and the herd has scattered. Some sheep got the impression they are shepherds themselves and started to preach their own words. Other sheep were strangled by hungry wolves. But most sheep have just scattered in the woods in fear and now they're at a loss. It's clear the hand of the shepherd has relaxed...
Have I heard wrong or have you just criticized the Church? Because it's just the Holy Mother Church who's the extended hand of the shepherd...

You're very sharp, son. But don't try to find any words undermining the authority of the church in my speech. I'm trying to say people have erred and they need to be called back into the herd by their shepherd. And those who are the most savage must be destroyed! That's the task of the Holy Office, son. That's your task and the task of all my brother inquisitors. If you too do well what the Shepherd called us to do our reward will be the return of God's Earthly kingdom to the Earth.
I've heard some tidings about a coming war. Do you happen to know anything about that?

I've heard such tidings too, that's true. And it has greatly alarmed me. Although there's not much information, the few I've heard really suggest that the war may be coming. I won't hide my opinion and I'll tell you frankly, son, that I disapprove of war in the same way as the First Prophet did. He let himself be arrested and crucified without a trace of fight because he knew the faith was undying and the humbleness was the way to salvation. I wish all who strive after a war would realize this truth and abandon their futile actions.
But if nobody drew up arms, who would stop monsters and infernal demons peering out of the earth's bowels these days and threatening people?

If nobody drew up arms it would mean all are living in accordance with the Holy Scriptures and there would be no infernal demons. Because it was just the loss of faith and deviation from the Holy Scriptures that caused all what has befallen the Realm.

There are more than enough hellspawns in Glatzburg and its vicinity, son. As well as enough heretics and apostates. There are footpads and brigands waiting by the roads, there are hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns raiding the woods... But what worries me most are the living dead in the city cemetery. It seems the shadow of the Beast has stained even that holy place and the dead are raised back to the unclean life to become a tool of destruction. Who falls into their hands has his fate sealed. It worries me because there is nowhere to bury the dead. And if the deceased are denied eternal rest in the holy ground their souls won't find peace...

Trading with death isn't among the things I'd like to be informed about, son. But to satisfy your curiosity I must tell you, Sheriff Gendriel Smith pays rewards in gold for dead footpads. Ask him about details if you really need to know.
I'm searching for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you have any suspicions, Your Honor?
I verify my suspicions myself or I ask my prosecutors or inquisitors to do that. So I won't burden you with them, if you don't mind.
Do you know anything about the Cult of the Children of the New Order?

The Cult of the Children of the New Order? I've heard about it, of course. It's one of the historically important cases of the growth of a demonic sect and of the fight against it. It all happened in the second half of the 9th century of the Empire. It was at the end of the Hundred Years War, when the whole faithful world was burdened with bloody wars and despair was breaking human hearts like deadwood. At that time a certain Lucius, who deemed himself as a Dark Prophet, preached the end of the God's earthly kingdom and the freeing of Satan from his thousand years prison. With this teaching, that denied the Holy Mother Church, the Holy Scriptures and God himself, and urged the indecent and depraved life, he gathered around him a numerous group containing even the members of the imperial court. The Papal Holy Office was hard put to destroy the cult, but eventually it succeeded and during great proceedings it sentenced all the members of the cult—including Lucius himself—to be burned to death. As far as I know there have been no mention of the cult since then. Why are you asking?
I believe the cult still exists and has its followers. That's why I came to Glatzburg—I'm searching here for the Children of the New Order.

Really? That surprises me. Through my lifetime I haven't come across a single case concerning the Children of the New Order. But that doesn't mean you can't be right. Maybe the cult really has its followers, but I wouldn't worry much about that, because if there has been no mention about the Children of the New Order until now, they won't be too numerous.
I wanted only to broaden my knowledge.
Yes, that's commendable. Although I'm a bit surprised by that in a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.

Francessca Gulvardi, the chambermaid of the Grand Duke, attempted to murder our Bishop Trevorius. Can you imagine the horror, son? She laid her hands on the highest priest of the Holy Mother Church, here in the city! And it's the work of infernal powers, I'm sure of that. The girl surely was possessed by an unclean spirit, because how else could such a slender body be so powerful as to scatter the confessional all over the episcopal temple?

The attempt was made during a confession on the holy ground of the episcopal temple. And imagine, son, that the poor soul tried to tear the Bishop's throat like some fierce beast! Fortunately Bishop Trevorius is a man of strong arms and of the stout heart. He resisted the attack and helped the guards to arrest the girl. She's being kept in the city jail since then. But it puzzles me why the Bishop used his powers to forbid the Inquisition to hear and sentence the girl. It's such an obvious case of a possession that she can be freed of the unclean spirit, only by the purgative flame.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a hard blow for the Holy Mother Church. We've lost a great man who has never stopped before any difficulty, not even before the criticism of the Church itself. It does him credit only God judges our actions. Regrettably the investigation hasn't progressed much yet. We know only that the Bishop was poisoned near the deserted Grand Duke's Gazebo, in the woods behind the city.

I would say that you're the one suited to answer that question. As far as I'm familiar with the records of the case, you were found over the Bishop's dead body not long after he died. What can you tell me about that? What did you do there and how did you know you would find him there?
If I'm not indicted I'd rather refrain from testifying.
Certainly, as you wish. But remember that everything you confess voluntarily will serve to your advantage during the trial...
I can't reveal what I was doing there. It's only between me and Bishop Trevorius.
Hmm... as you wish. But remember that everything you confess voluntarily will serve to your advantage during the trial...
I had a secret meeting arranged there with Bishop Trevorius. I can't say more about it.

Secrecy is Satan's companion, as the Holy Scriptures say. But as you wish, keep the secret for yourself. But remember that everything you confess voluntarily will serve to your advantage during the trial...

I had a secret meeting arranged there with Bishop Trevorius. We wanted to consult about how to proceed with the search for the Cult of the Children of the New Order. But when I arrived there the Monsignor was already dead.

Really? Well... interesting. And suspicious too. The whole case starts to smell of deep heresy. I advise you well, son—be careful and go to confession as soon as possible. Preferably to Cardinal Truncquillius.
I've found out that Istwan de Bragho came out of his grave to take revenge on those who caused his apprehension and execution. And it seems he's immortal. Do you happen to have a good advice for me?

Is it really true that Istwan de Bragho has risen from his grave? That would be bad news, son. I would have never though that there's any truth in the tales of the revenge of executed Istwan de Bragho. But it's clear now I was mistaken, and it grieves me. Maybe it was possible to do something about it, although I doubt that...

So, now we face an undead who has already managed to execute a great portion of his revenge—I've heard that all the five paladins who convicted him of terrible crimes years ago were murdered this spring. There remains only the executioner Yan Flemberg who conducted the execution. We have to safeguard him at any costs, son. If you're saying Istwan de Bragho is really invulnerable by sword and magic, then there has to be some other way. But regrettably I don't have such knowledge.
And someone else could advise me?

I'm saying it quite unwillingly, because it's unusual for the Holy Office to turn for help to seculars, but try asking the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt. She's versed in demonology and dark spiritualism more than anyone else.
Never mind. Thank you.

But I may advise you to try asking Enrie Jungwirdt. Although I'm saying it quite unwillingly, because it's unusual for the Holy Office to turn for help to seculars, there's no other way out in this case. Enrie Jungwirdt is versed in demonology and dark spiritualism more than anyone else.

God protect us against the Fallen Angels and the infernal powers they wield! As you surely know, they're the former angels who were thrown out of Heaven, along with Satan at the beginning of time for crimes against God. By falling into the bowels of Hell they've become demons, ugly horned monsters and beelzebubs wielding immense powers of chaos and evil. Arthamon is the ruler of the utter ruin, Baphomet rules the madness, Cerdie is the mistress of debauchery and the fallen archangel Azrael administers the will of Satan himself and is his first emissary.

They all together struggle for disrupting God's order and for destroying God's kingdom on the earth and in Heaven. For this purpose they're trying to enter our world, but they cannot do that because the true faith in God the Redeemer, inhibits them from doing that. So they're at least trying to sow the seed of sin into hearts of men, they're trying to entice the God's sheep and lead them astray. And that's the task of us, the servants of God, to guard seculars—and each other—against that terrible evil.
Do you think it's possible to invoke the Fallen Angels?

No, son, that's impossible. Heretics may at most draw their attention by performing certain rites, but they can't break the restrictions by which the Fallen Angels are bound. That's why they send their minions instead of themselves. Regrettably those lesser demons, for example Gaugliel, Mazriel, Proctfor or Elgheborth, can in fact be invoked. But it's impossible to invoke the Fallen Angels themselves. That would be the end of it all...
I'll be frank with you, Your Honor. Either you'll answer my question or you'll bear the consequences of your impetuousness. Do you understand me?!
It seems you don't like me, Your Honor. Nonetheless I'd like to appeal to you to answer me, because you surely realize that your answer would help the mission that's common to both of us.
You're very wise, Your Honor, that may be seen even at first sight. May I ask you to answer my question? It would help me greatly...
I'm searching here for the cult of the Children of the New Order. I have a reasonable suspicion some of its members are hiding here in Glatzburg.

Well... interesting. To tell the truth I don't remember coming across a single case concerning that ancient cult of demoniacs through my lifetime. We had here in Glatzburg some heretics endorsing the legacy of the cult of the Dark Sunrise and of the Movement of the Damned, we convicted even some Derbigenians, Haradians and several worshippers of the Cult of the Dead... but no followers of the cult of the Children of the New Order. Are you really sure you're searching for the Children of the New Order? Why, the last mentions of them are from the last days of the Hundred Years War, when they all were caught and executed. And it happened in the Empire and not here in Ultherst.
Yes, it's really the cult of the Children of the New Order.

Well... that's alarming. It seems someone is trying to revive the cult. Heretics are completely mad these days in their efforts to destroy the true faith, and to disrupt the Holy Mother Church. As if we haven't been doing enough for them for long centuries. This disgusting unfaithfulness must be completely uprooted! I hope you'll reveal them and hand them to justice, son!
I'll do my best, Your Honor.
You're probably right, I must have been mistaken.

I think so too. But on the other hand we can't ignore the possibility that someone is really trying to revive the legacy of the cult. But I wouldn't be too worried by that. Heretics are reviving all kinds of old demonic traditions these days, but without deeper knowledge of infernal practices. In any case you won't do wrong if you ask Cardinal Truncquillius about the cult of the Children of the New Order. He knows more than anyone else about heretical cults and movements—he has dedicated his whole life to fighting heresy and he was working abroad for the Papal Inquisition for several years.
I've been led here by a certain mission, but I'd like to keep the details to myself.
I understand. Your mission is only your business, of course. But if you should need any help, just ask. I'm here to serve!
Altogether it's nothing important. You may say I'm only passing through.
I understand. In that case I hope your journey will lead you to a successful end, whatever it may be.
Anyway, I'd like to speak with you now about another thing. Could you spare a little of your time?
What's the matter, Your Honor?
Do you know the history of the pagan city of Galibornium whose ruins can be found near Glatzburg?
