I've heard something about that already. Galibornium reputedly used to be the capital of this province at the time when the Filkland Peninsula belonged to the pagan realm of Ereborn. In the year of 223 it was conquered by the faithful armies led by Saint Orthenius.

Very well, son. It seems you're versed in the local history. In that case you surely know the city wasn't populated again. Although there were attempts made to settle it again, there hanged the shadow of the pagan curse above the ruins. Instead of the city becoming a beautiful new faithful town as it happened in the case of Alvaron people had to abandon it and lay the foundations of Glatzburg several miles away in a place that was much less favorable.
Regrettably...

The reason was that some unnamed evil crept into the city, and especially into its underground. Ghosts, demons, shadows from pagan mythology, beasts from Erebornian menageries... all that sneaked in among the burnt city walls blackened by smoke, leaving their hiding places at nights to leave bloody tracks in the shape of the dead faithful behind them. That's why the town has been deserted forever and left at the mercy of demons and ghosts.
No, I don't know any details about the history of Galibornium.

Then know it used to be the capital of this province at the time when the Filkland Peninsula belonged to the pagan realm of Ereborn. In the year of 223 the city was conquered by the faithful armies led by Saint Orthenius, and burned to the ground in order for it not to be inhabited ever again. Although there were attempts made to settle it again, there hanged the shadow of the pagan curse above the ruins. Instead of the city becoming a beautiful new faithful town, as it happened in the case of Alvaron people had to abandon it and lay the foundations of Glatzburg several miles away, in a place that was much less favorable.
It's a grim history. But why are you telling it to me?

Because I'm not sure you've heard about the Temple of All Gods in the main square of Galibornium. It was the most imposing pagan sacral building in the whole Filkland Peninsula. Even the faithful had to admire it in spite of themselves, because it really looked like a respectable house of God, although it was devoted to pagan gods. When the city was conquered and its inhabitants either killed or converted, the faithful priests decided to let the temple stand and to consecrate it, to turn it into a magnificent divine sanctuary.

But when the ceremony came, attended by most of the faithful inhabitants, some dark pagan powers appeared next to the altar—they were maybe some ghost or demons—and terrible slaughter started. The faithful priests attempted to consecrate the temple twice more in all, but with the same result. I deduce from it that some ancient pagan evil settled down in the temple, and that it has been attracting to it, all what's evil and infernal since then.

Yes, it's quite possible. If the temple has been possessed by pagan unclean powers, it's probably the reason why there have been infernal creatures lingering in its vicinity for centuries. Evil attracts evil, no matter what its origin is!

That's exactly my opinion, son! I'm sure that if we could wipe out the evil from the Temple of All Gods it would be long step forward in the many centuries long fight against the unclean powers that have found their home in the ruins of Galibornium. And that's exactly what I'd like to speak with you about.
I think I'm starting to guess what's your point here, Your Honor.

Yes, I think my point is quite obvious. I'd like to ask you to dare and do what the Holy Mother Church has tried to no end several times during the last centuries. To consecrate the Temple of All Gods and make it a divine sanctuary. Would you accept such a demanding task?
I'll do what you ask of me, Your Honor.

I knew you wouldn't fail me, son. You're a true example for us all! May Archangel Gabriel himself and all the Saints protect you. Here accept the sprinkler with holy water that will allow you to fulfill the task. As soon as the Temple of All Gods is consecrated I'll send several of our priests to start with repairing it, and to keep the flame of the true faith burning amidst infernal darkness.
Alright, Your Honor.
May I do something for you now, son?
That depends on what the reward would be...

A reward? Your reward would certainly be the fastening of the power of the Holy Mother Church, the annunciation of the glory of our Lord and the reinforcement of the influence of the true faith on the area affected by infernal powers.
I'm sorry, but I don't think I would succeed where so many priests before me didn't. The place is lost for the true faith!

Alright... I'm not surprised. I myself have not found enough courage to undergo such a hard task. Maybe you're right and the place is really lost forever for the Holy Mother Church. We can't do anything else.
Exactly, Your Honor.
Forget it. Can I do something for you?
I'd like to ask you several questions, if I may.
But sure, son. There's nothing easier. What do you want to know?
I'd like to charge Alphonso DiCerbio with the kidnapping of Tom Clifford.
Yes, I have. Guss Halworth witnessed DiCerbio and several others kidnapping Tom Clifford when the boy was returning from master armorer Hans von Drichtmaul in the evening.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of kidnapping against Alphonso DiCerbio. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Raimond Ventano with the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi, Your Honor.

Yes, I have. I managed to free Francessca Gulvardi of the dark powers that possessed her. Then she testified Raimond Ventano was one of the kidnappers who dragged her to the place where the unclean spirit entered her body.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of kidnapping against Raimond Ventano. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Commander Ethien de Pasque with heresy and kidnapping, Your Honor.

Yes, I have. According to the testimony of Raimond Ventano Ethien de Pasque was his accomplice in the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi and participated in the purported invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet, that reputedly occurred in the disgusting sanctum near the city gallows. I found the Chain of the Brotherhood belonging to the Commander there. He believed it was stolen from him.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of heresy against Ethien de Pasque. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick with heresy, Your Honor.

What?! Are you serious or are you only joking, son? Do you realize what you have just said? Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick is the wife of the royal governor of the city, Grand Duke Robert Heidrick! And that means she belongs to the highest circles of the society and has connections with the king's court!

Yes, I realize that, Your Honor. But even she falls within the jurisdiction of the Holy Office and since I've gathered the required evidence against her I'm determined to arrest and question her with your permission!
As you wish, son. But I have to ask you what evidence have you gathered against her.

Raimond Ventano and Ethien de Pasque confessed that all the crimes they perpetrated they did at Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick's bidding. They say she's the high priestess of the Cult of Chaos of the Fallen Angel Baphomet. Allegedly it was she who came up with the idea of invoking the terrible demon and of usurping the power with his help.
Hmm... that's... alarming. But it's not enough to arrest her. Do you have any other proof of her guilt?
Certainly, Your Honor. Dietrich the gravedigger confessed he procured for the Grand Duchess a dead girl's body that was lying in the grave for thirteen days and that she paid him for it.
My God! If all you've just said is really true it's my duty to bring a charge of heresy against Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. You have my permission to arrest her, son.
I'd like to charge Cardinal Truncquillius of heresy, Your Honor.

WHAT?! Cardinal Truncquillius? I must say you've taken me aback, son! You can't accuse the Curial Inquisitor of heresy, can you?! Why, he's my superior! I'm obliged to obey his orders! This would be disobeying a superior and there's only one punishment for that, death!

But not in the case when there's a suspicion that he perpetrated a crime, Your Honor. That Inquisitorial Codex of yours allows to temporarily suspend a Curial Inquisitor of his powers if there's an allegation brought against him. And then his subordinate inquisitors aren't obliged to obey his orders any more until he's exonerated.

I know what the Codex of Inquisition says, son. But still he's the Curial Inquisitor! He's a man I deeply respect and he's a great support in the fight against heresy! You can't charge him with heresy! Not him! That's madness!

You Honor, I appeal to you to thoroughly perform your duties. You well know yourself you have to examine each allegation that is brought. As the Prosecutor General of local Curia and the Inquisitorial Judge you have to bring a charge against Cardinal Truncquillius!
Tell me, then, what evidence do you have against him, son. And choose your words carefully!

So then... Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick confessed he reputedly performed the rite of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet, with whom she then fornicated and therefore gave birth to monstrous unclean creatures. And she confessed that she prepared and performed the rite of invocation at Cardinal Truncquillius's bidding.
That's not enough. Continue.
I've acquired certain letters addressed to Cardinal Truncquillius. An unknown heretic encourages him in the letters to take all the steps needed to invoke the Fallen Angel Baphomet.
That's still not enough to accuse the Cardinal, son. Do you have some other evidence against him?

Yes, Your Honor. Dieter von Gelbendiel testified he saw Cardinal Truncquillius one evening in the episcopal garden when the Cardinal was giving orders to one of his accomplices for performing the unclean rite.

Well... the arguments brought forward by you is too cogent and the allegation too grave for me to act otherwise. Although I trust in Cardinal Truncquillius's innocence I have to grant your suit. I bring a charge of heresy against Cardinal Truncquillius. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
And at the same time I have to—although I do it very unwillingly—temporarily assume the authority of a Curial Inquisitor according to the Codex of Inquisition.
Exactly, Your Honor. Congratulations.
There's no need to congratulate me. I know that nothing good will come from it. And now excuse me, please!
Certainly, Your Honor. Farewell.
Why you, Your Honor? I've been already named an Inquisitorial Judge and so I'm in the same position as you!

In that case you surely know the Codex of Inquisition requires that a temporarily freed office of a Curial Inquisitor, is taken over by the judge with the longest period of activity with the Holy Office. And presently it's I who satisfy this requirement.
Indeed, I understand. Farewell.
I'd like to charge the soldier Harph with heresy, Your Honor.

Yes, I have. In the disgusting sanctum in the center of the city sewers I found the diary in which the soldier Harph indecently confessed to all the crimes he perpetrated by means of the undead monsters.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of heresy and of consorting with dark powers against the soldier Harph. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to charge the soldier Harph with heresy, Your Honor. I suspect him of standing behind the assaults perpetrated after dark by undead monsters.
That's great, son! And do you have enough supporting evidence?

Yes, I have. In the disgusting sanctum in the center of the city sewers I found his diary in which he indecently confessed to all the crimes he perpetrated by means of the undead monsters in his wicked lust for wealth.
I'd like to charge the servant girl Jeanette with witchcraft, Your Honor.
Yes, I have. Hans Thomas Brookwelt testified the servant girl Jeanette attempted to bewitch him by dark magic and thus to get to his saved gold.
Well... the evidence brought forward by you speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of witchcraft against the servant girl Jeanette. You have my permission to arrest her, son.
I'd like to charge Hans Thomas Brookwelt with witchcraft, Your Honor.
Yes, I have. The servant girl Jeanette testified Brookwelt seduced and violated her with the help of infernal powers he wields.
Well... the evidence brought forward by you speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of witchcraft against Hans Thomas Brookwelt. You have my permission to arrest him, son.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Alphonso DiCerbio.
It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment, son.
Yes, I have. Guss Halworth witnessed DiCerbio kidnapping the little Tom Clifford. DiCerbio later confessed to the crime.
Yes, the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Alphonso DiCerbio!
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against the soldier Harph.

Yes, I have. The soldier Harph was seen descending into the Glatzburg underground accompanied by several undead. When I explored the hive of depravity I found the soldier's diary in it. In the diary he confesses to all his crimes!
The evidence speaks clearly. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against the defendant soldier Harph.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Raimond Ventano.
Yes, I have. Francessca Gulvardi convicted Raimond Ventano of complicity in her kidnapping. And Ventano later confessed to that crime.
Yes, the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Raimond Ventano.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Commander Ethien de Pasque.

Ethien de Pasque holds the office of the Commander in the knightly order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, son. It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial Judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment.

Yes, I have. I've found the knight's necklace in the place where a monstrous heretical sabbath took place. Moreover Raimond Ventano confessed it was Ethien de Pasque who helped him to kidnap the servant girl Francessca Gulvardi. And the Commander eventually pleaded guilty of all the crimes.
In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Ethien de Pasque.
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick.

Your decision to accuse the wife of the royal governor of the city is a serious one. It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial Judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment. You surely can imagine the consequences of such an action.

I have plenty of evidence, Your Honor. Dietrich the gravedigger testified the Grand Duchess paid him a fat prize for procuring a corpse of a mad girl for her.Other evidence against the Grand Duchess are the confessions of Commander Ethien de Pasque and the merchant Raimond Ventano. They both confessed it was Grand Duchess Yulliette who planned the purported rite of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet, and the kidnapping of the servant girl Francessca Gulvardi. As the last proof there is the confession of Grand Duchess Yulliette herself.
I won't try to hide my surprise, but your evidence is convincing. Hereby I, as the judge of the Holy Office, order the trial to be held against defendant Yulliette Heidrick. God's will be done!
I'd like to submit a proposal for court proceedings against Cardinal Truncquillius.

Son, your decision will have grave consequences. Very grave consequences that will shake the confidence in the Holy Office. It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial Judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment of Cardinal Truncquillius.

Yes, I have. Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick confessed it was Cardinal Truncquillius who orchestrated the purported rite of invocation of the Fallen Angel Baphomet and all the other crimes. Another evidence against the Cardinal is the testimony of Master Dieter von Gelbendiel who witnessed him giving orders to one of his accomplices. Moreover I found incriminating heretical letters on Cardinal Truncquillius that prove his guilt beyond reasonable doubt. And as the last proof I have the confession of Cardinal Truncquillius himself.
I'm shocked! I can't say anything else. In that case I, as the judge of the Holy Office, have to order the trial to be held against defendant Cardinal Truncquillius.
Nothing, Your Honor. Farewell.

Welcome, son. Can I help you somehow? I guess you're new to Glatzburg. I'm Welfhar and I'm the Judge of the Holy Office. Glatzburg is in my judicial jurisdiction and presently I hold the office of the General Prosecutor in Glatzburg too. If I'm not mistaken you don't belong to the local chapter of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, do you?
No, Your Honor. I've just arrived from Hillbrandt.

From Hillbrandt? I've heard some news that some unfortunate incident happened there... They say Bishop Vallarian was sentenced and burned there. I must admit it was my close friend and his death quite unsettled me. Weren't you involved in that case somehow, son?
No, Your Honor, I wasn't.

Hmm... I wish I had enough time to study the case. I've always esteemed and admired Judge Vallarian. But due to my working load here in Glatzburg I will hardly have some spare time to look at it. What a pity! Hopefully Cardinal Truncquillius, the Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg, will take some action in this matter. Anyway, I'm glad to meet you, son. What was it that brought you to Glatzburg?
Yes, Your Honor. It was I who accused Judge Vallarian of heresy and who brought forth the incriminating evidence during the inquisitorial trial.

Really?! In that case I assure you that you owe me many answers! I've always deemed Judge Vallarian a very honorable, though quite willful man, who's completely devoted to his mission. I'll find enough time to ask you VERY specific questions concerning reasons leading to that unfortunate incident!
I have nothing to say to you about that case!

We will see, son, we will see. I'll take care his death is properly investigated! I presume Cardinal Truncquillius, the local Curial Inquisitor, is thoroughly informed about the matter and that he'll decide what has to be done. But now tell me what was it that brought you here to Glatzburg?
I acted in conformity with the law, Your Honor. I have nothing to confess to before God.

Hmm... only the investigation will show that. I presume Cardinal Truncquillius, the local Curial Inquisitor, is thoroughly informed about the matter and that he'll decide what has to be done. But now tell me what was it that brought you here to Glatzburg?
Why, I didn't do anything wrong, did I? I'm completely innocent, Your Honor. I swear!

The investigation will show if it's true. I presume Cardinal Truncquillius, the local Curial Inquisitor, is thoroughly informed about the matter and that he'll decide what has to be done. But now tell me what was it that brought you here to Glatzburg?
No, I don't, Your Honor.
I immediately thought so. What was it then that brought you here to Glatzburg?
Welcome, son. I hesitate to ask if you've already achieved some success in your noble effort to consecrate the pagan temple in Galibornium...
Not yet, Your Honor. But I'm working on it.
Optime, mi frater! I'm glad to hear that. I'm sure your efforts will be crowned with success. What can I do for you in this instant?
Yes, Your Honor. The pagan temple is freed of unclean powers and consecrated as the Church of the Sacred Heart of our Lord.

Really? I can't believe that... Have you really managed to wipe out evil from that ancient dark place? And to consecrate a new sanctuary of God there? Unbelievable! The whole Holy Mother Church, not only here in Glatzburg will be indebted to you forever, son! You're a real example for us all!

Don't thank me, son—you don't have to. I and the whole Holy Mother Church should be grateful to you instead. I'll arrange at once some priests from the Glatzburg Diocese to move into the consecrated temple and to start with its reconstruction.
Welcome, son. I thank you all the time in my prayers for what you've done for our Holy Mother Church. Can I do something for you?
What do you need, son? If I'm right you should now be in the pagan temple in the ruins of Galibornium trying to consecrate it...
That's true, Your Honor.
In that case, if I were you, I would consider if I'm spending wisely the time our God Almighty has given us for our mission. Can I do something for you now?
It's done already, Your Honor. The pagan temple is freed of unclean powers and consecrated as a Church of the Sacred Heart of our Lord.

Really? I can't believe that... Could it be that you really managed to wipe out evil from that ancient dark place? And to consecrate a new sanctuary of God there? Unbelievable! Well... if it's true the whole Holy Mother Church will be indebted to you forever, son! You're a real example for us all!
Good day, son. What can I do for you?

Welcome, son. I must thank you again for consecrating the pagan temple in Galibornium. I'm sorry a man of such exceptional abilities is at the same time gathering evidence against Curial Inquisitor Truncquillius. But God will judge if your deeds are proper. What can I do for you?

I must apologize to you, dear son, for my initial mistrust concerning the accusation of Cardinal Truncquillius. It was so... shocking that I refused to believe it at first. How deeply is this age rotten when heresy infiltrates even such high circles of the Realm's society? Unbelievable... and utterly grueling. How shall I fulfil my mission when I can't be sure we're carrying out the will of God?
Trust in your intellect and your faith, Your Honor! They will always lead you out of all creeks and baits of lies!
Yes, you're right, son. I deeply apologize to you once again!
That's your problem, Your Honor!
I understand your anger, son. You surely take it ill of me that I wasn't able to accept the fact Cardinal Truncquillius is guilty. Nevertheless I hope you'll forgive me. Farewell.
I'd like to charge Robert Heidrick with heresy and with conspiring against God and the King.
WHAT?! You want to charge Grand Duke Robert Heidrick of heresy? The royal governor of the city? You must be joking!
I'm not. The evidence speaks clearly.
I thought you would say that. So, what evidence is it, son?

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick confessed she found an unfinished letter addressed to the marauding knight, Benthley of Welshrem in the study of her husband. Moreover I found a tatter of Heidrick's cloak in the city cemetery not far from the place where one of the graves was robbed and desecrated. The Grand Duke's presence in the cemetery was further confirmed by Commander Ethien Pasque who witnessed the Grand Duke performing a dark Sabbath.
Shocking! Your evidence is really convincing. Let the truth be told in the inquisitorial proceedings. You have my consent to arrest Grand Duke Robert Heidrick.
A paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous steals?! I'm shocked! Go confess your sins immediately, son! I won't allow something like that!
What prerequisites must I meet if I want to become an Inquisitorial Judge?

You're thinking about the black gown of a judge of the Holy Inquisition, my son? That does you credit. God wishes us Inquisitors to improve constantly in our holy mission that He has put on our shoulders, in his divine wisdom. Every prosecutor of the Holy Office may become an Inquisitorial Judge, if he solves an assigned case under the supervision of the Curial Inquisitor, and then passes an examination of canon law and of secular law.
Since you're the provisional Curial Inquisitor I'd like you to examine me to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Excellency.

Really? In that case I hope you're ready to pass the tests. They will examine your practical skills and theoretical knowledge of the inquisitorial process and of canon law and secular law. Remember that the task of a Inquisitorial Judge is mainly to receive indictments from Inquisitorial Prosecutors, investigate the indictments and then bring charges of heresy and of other crimes in accordance with the Codex of Inquisition on their basis. That's why every judge has to be able to pass muster with any felon or heathen, and why he has to be able to solve even the most confounded case. Furthermore he has to be well versed in the whole of canon law and secular law. Are you really ready to pass the examination to become a Judge?
Yes, I'm.

Optime. In that case listen carefully. I'm not sure if you've heard about it already, but there are undead walking the streets of the city at night. You surely can imagine the panic those monstrous creatures have been causing. Nobody dares to leave his house after dark and who does, risks a very unpleasant death. I personally have put my mind to the case and I found several things that alarmed me more than the presence of the undead inside the city walls.

I especially noticed that they're not usual murders, committed by infernal monsters led only by an urgent lust for fresh blood. All the victims were robbed of all valuables including brass buttons and gold teeth. At first sight it seems the undead murder for money. But that's a pure nonsense—undead bodies are led only by their murderous instinct and by nothing else. That's why I was so surprised by that. At first I thought the robberies were the work of someone else, but the testimonies of the people who accidentally witnessed the crimes spoke otherwise. I couldn't believe there were any undead monsters who would intentionally collect valuables. And then I finally caught on to it.

The undead don't steal on purpose, but by the order of the one who has summoned them into this world! There are many forbidden necromantic rites by which heretics are able to compel dead bodies to a new unclean life. The undead brought to life that way obey their creator and may perform certain very easy tasks for them. Fortunately that devilish ability of theirs is limited to the most basic orders, otherwise we couldn't be sure of anything. And that's why I'm sure there is a heretic standing behind the undead in the city streets, and behind their attacks on the citizens. That way the heretic tries to get wealthy!
I understand. And my task is to find out the heretic, get enough evidence against him and turn him over to justice.
Exactly, my son. If you manage to do that, it'll be clear evidence you're worthy—and most of all, capable—of becoming an Inquisitorial Judge.
Alright, Your Honor. I'll accomplish the task. The culprit will be caught and punished!
Very good, brother.
To tell the truth, Your Honor, I've already found the culprit of all those crimes by a coincidence. I have a proof against the soldier Harph.
Very good, brother. But it's necessary you present yet another proof supporting your suspicion—such is the requirement of the Codex of Inquisition.
Yes, that's true. I'll take care of that.
Optime. I have no doubt you'll be successful in your effort.
By chance I've already worked on that case. The culprit of all those crimes has been already found.
Really? That's great! So, who is it? Who's the wicked culprit?

It's the soldier Harph of the Royal garrison of Glatzburg. I found his diary, hidden in his disgusting den deep in the deserted sewers under the city. In the diary he confesses to all his crimes. Moreover a witness who told me he saw Harph descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of undead monsters.

Great! Your investigation seems to be completely precise. You've solved the case without a glitch. There's nothing more to say about it. Congratulations! Now you only have to demonstrate your knowledge of canon law and of secular law. Come when you deem yourself ready enough.
Alright, we may start.

Optime. In that case listen carefully. It concerns the case you're already familiar with—it's the case of the undead walking the streets of the city at night. You surely can imagine the panic those monstrous creatures have been causing. Nobody dares to leave his house after dark and who does risks a very unpleasant death. I personally have put my mind to the case, and I found several things that alarmed me more than the presence of the undead inside the city walls.

The undead don't steal on purpose, but by the order of the one who has summoned them into this world! There are many forbidden necromantic rites by which heretics are able to compel dead bodies to a new unclean life. The undead brought to life that way obey their creator and may perform certain very easy tasks for them. Fortunately that devilish ability of theirs is limited to the most basic orders, otherwise we couldn't be sure of anything. And that's why I'm sure there is a heretic standing behind the undead in the city streets and behind their attacks on the citizens. That way the heretic tries to get wealthy!
Yes, that seems to fit. The soldier Harph confessed exactly to that crime in his diary, I found inside his disgusting den deep in the middle of the deserted sewers under the city.

Whatever the truth is, your task is to find out the heretic standing behind those crimes and to convict him. If you manage to do that, it'll be clear evidence you're worthy—and most of all capable—of becoming an Inquisitorial Judge.

Yes, that seems to fit. The soldier Harph confessed exactly to that crime in his diary I found inside his disgusting sanctum deep in the middle of the deserted sewers under the city. Moreover a witness who told me he saw Harph one night descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of undead monsters.

Really? But in that case you've proven the guilt of the soldier beyond reasonable doubt. Great, brother! Your investigation seems to be completely precise. You've solved the case without a glitch. There's nothing more to say about it. Congratulations! Now you only have to demonstrate your knowledge of canon law and of secular law. Come when you deem yourself ready enough.

Really? I'm very glad to hear that, brother, because I believe you're going to be a great Inquisitorial Judge. Frankly speaking, you've already convinced me of your qualities by solving the case of the soldier Harph. You revealed and convicted him without a glitch, so you don't need to prove your practical knowledge of the inquisitorial process to me anymore. I've already checked you're familiar with it. But now you have to pass the examination of canon law and of secular law that you must be well versed in. Come to me when you deem yourself ready enough.
In that case I'm going to ask you several questions about canon law and secular law. You must answer them all correctly, if you don't, you'll have to repeat the whole examination another time.
I've found who's behind the robberies perpetrated in the city streets after dark by the undead monsters, Your Honor.

It's the soldier Harph of the Royal garrison of Glatzburg. I found his diary, hidden in his disgusting den deep in the deserted sewers under the city. In the diary he confesses to all his crimes. Moreover I've heard a witness who told me he saw Harph descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of undead monsters.

If I remember right, there was the soldier Harph accused in the connection with that crime, and the accusation was your initiative. Was his guilt proven in the end? Did you find any evidence convincing him beyond reasonable doubt?
Yes, I did. I've heard a witness who told me he saw Harph descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of undead monsters.
I'd like to pass the examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Honor.

Optime, mi frater! I hope you're well prepared. Remember that knowledge of the law is absolutely crucial for a Judge of the Holy Office. Without it you couldn't properly fulfill your holy mission and you would be a burden for the Holy Inquisition instead of an asset. Shall we start?
I'd like to repeat the examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Honor.

I'm glad to hear that. I trust you are better prepared than the last time. Do not forget that perfect knowledge of the law is absolutely crucial for an Inquisitorial Judge to effectively perform his duties. So, let's start with the examination. Pararisne, mi fili?

Since you provisionally assumed the duties of the Curial Inquisitor I'd like you to finish my examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Honor. I started the examination with Cardinal Truncquillius.
Certainly, brother. What was your task?
I was to reveal and convict the heretic standing behind the robberies perpetrated in the city streets after dark by the undead monsters, Your Honor. And I succeeded.

If I remember rightly, there was the soldier Harph accused in the connection with that crime and the accusation was your initiative. Was his guilt proven in the end? Did you find other evidence convicting him beyond reasonable doubt?
Yes, I did. I had a witness who asserted he saw Harph descending into the city sewers accompanied by a group of the undead.

Since you were provisionally named a Curial Inquisitor I'd like you to finish my examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge, Your Honor. I've already solved the case assigned to me by Cardinal Truncquillius.

Optime, mi frater! In that case you have to pass the examination of canon law and secular law. Remember that this knowledge is absolutely crucial for a Judge of the Holy Office. Without it you couldn't properly fulfill your holy mission and you would be a burden for the Holy Inquisition instead of an asset. Shall we start?
Yes, we shall.
Since you were provisionally named a Curial Inquisitor I'd like to pass the examination to become an Inquisitorial Judge with you, Your Honor.

I'm glad to hear that, brother. I trust you're well prepared. Remember that a perfect knowledge of law is required for an Inquisitorial Judge to correctly and rightly perform his duties. So then, let's start the examination. Are you ready, my son?
Yes, Your Excellency, I'm ready.

I know about Father Frederick more than anyone else, brother. Why, he was my longtime tutor and mentor! His name will stay engraved in my memory as long as I live. It was he who led me to the bosom of the Holy Mother Church and it was he who at the end of his life greatly encouraged me to become a member of the Holy Office. Father Frederick was a very wise man. He traveled a lot. He visited the Empire and dwelt at the Papal Court. He traveled through all the faithful realms of Kalmariland and talked with their highest church officials. According to his words—and I definitely don't doubt them—he visited even the Holy Grave of the First Prophet in Jevaran and bowed before his remains. He was the most educated and the most wise man I've ever met. And moreover he was as modest as every priest should be.

Exactly, brother. But he was also a fierce enemy of dark powers, a soldier of God. Do you know he was one of the last priests able to perform the rite of exorcism? Yes, it's true! During his lifetime he managed to free dozens of possessed people of demons and other unclean powers. He was good at it as nobody else was. Regrettably he had no successor. All the more I'm saddened God summoned him to his kingdom two years ago—he took to his grave all his knowledge and skills. I miss him greatly. I often used to go to pray to his grave in the Sepulcher before the cemetery succumbed to the power of the Beast. I hope his remains and souls remained untouched by the powers of Hell.

That's noble of you, brother. But tell me, why are you telling it to me? Crimes not regarding the faith are in the jurisdiction of the temporal power, not in the jurisdiction of the Church. Turn to Grand Duke Heidrick with that case.

It depends on what exactly are you asking about, brother. You want to know my opinion about what's the cause of all what has befallen the Realm? Alright, I'll tell you. The cause of all that is the smallness of people. People are creatures that have to be led. As a herd of sheep—by the firm hand of the shepherd. Only then the herd thrives, grows and is content. It's not in vain that the Holy Scriptures say: God is our shepherd and we're his humble sheep. And behold! The firm hand of the shepherd has relaxed and the herd has scattered. Some sheep got the impression they are shepherds themselves and started to preach their own words. Other sheep were strangled by hungry wolves. But most sheep have just scattered in the woods in fear and now they're at a loss. It's clear the hand of the shepherd has relaxed...

You're very sharp, brother. But don't try to find in my speech any words undermining the authority of the church. I'm trying to say people have erred and need to be called together to the herd again by the shepherd. And those who are the most savage must be destroyed! That's the task of the Holy Office, brother. That's your task and the task of all our brother inquisitors. Do your work well and your reward will be the return of God's Earthly kingdom to the earth.

I've heard such tidings too, that's true. And it has greatly alarmed me. Although there's not much information, the few I've heard really suggest that the war may be coming. I won't hide my opinion and I'll tell you frankly, brother, that I disapprove of war in the same way as the First Prophet did. He let himself be arrested and crucified without a trace of fight because he knew the faith was undying and the humbleness was the way to salvation. I wish all who strive after a war would realize this truth and abandon their futile actions.

There are more than enough hellspawns in Glatzburg and its vicinity, brother. As well as enough heretics and apostates. There are footpads and brigands waiting by the roads, there are hellspawns from the Devil's Caverns raiding the woods... But what worries me most are the living dead in the city cemetery. It seems the shadow of the Beast has stained even that holy place and the dead are raised back to the unclean life to become a tool of destruction. Who falls into their hands has his fate sealed. It worries me because there is nowhere to bury the dead. And if the deceased are denied eternal rest in the holy ground their souls won't find peace...

Trading with death isn't among the things I'd like to be informed about, brother. But to satisfy your curiosity I must tell you, Sheriff Gendriel Smith pays rewards in gold for dead footpads. Ask him about details if you really need to know.

Yes, that's commendable. God's servant—and especially those whose task is to fight heresy—has a duty to learn all he can to keep such knowledge that's necessary for fulfilling his holy mission. I bless you, brother.

Francessca Gulvardi, the chambermaid of the Grand Duke, attempted to murder our Bishop Trevorius. Can you imagine the horror, brother? She laid her hands on the highest priest of the Holy Mother Church, here in the city! And it's the work of infernal powers, I'm sure of that. The girl surely was possessed by an unclean spirit, because how else could such a slender body be so powerful as to scatter the confessional all over the episcopal temple?

The attempt was made during a confession on the holy ground of the episcopal temple. And imagine, brother, that the poor soul tried to tear the Bishop's throat like some fierce beast! Fortunately Bishop Trevorius is a man of strong arms and of the stout heart. He resisted the attack and helped the guards to arrest the girl. She's being kept in the city jail since then. But it puzzles me why the Bishop used his powers to forbid the Inquisition to hear and sentence the girl. It's such an obvious case of a possession that she can be freed of the unclean spirit, only by the purgative flame.

The murder of Bishop Trevorius is a hard blow for the Holy Mother Church. We've lost a great man who has never stopped before any difficulty, not even before the criticism of the Church itself. It does him credit—only God judges our actions. Regrettably the investigation haven't progressed much yet. We know only that the Bishop was poisoned near the deserted Grand Duke's Gazebo, in the woods behind the city.

I would say that you're the one suited to answer that question. As far as I'm familiar with the records of the case, you were found over the Bishop's dead body not long after he died. What will you tell me about that? What did you do there and how did you know you would find him there?

A secret meeting you say? Interesting... and suspicious. Inquisitors aren't in the habit of meeting anyone secretly. Secrecy is Satan's companion, as the Holy Scriptures say. But as you wish, keep the secret to yourself. But remember that everything you confess voluntarily will serve to your advantage during a trial...

Really? Well... interesting. And suspicious too. The whole case starts to smell of deep heresy. I advise you well, brother—be careful and go to confession as soon as possible. Preferably to Cardinal Truncquillius.

Is it really true that Istwan de Bragho has risen from his grave? That would be bad news, brother. I would have never though that there's any truth in the tales of the revenge of executed Istwan de Bragho. But it's clear now I was mistaken, and it grieves me. Maybe it was possible to do something about it, although I doubt that...

So, now we face an undead who has already managed to execute a great portion of his revenge—I've heard that all the five paladins who convicted him of terrible crimes years ago were murdered this spring. There remains only the executioner Yan Flemberg who conducted the execution. We have to safeguard him at any costs, brother. If you're saying Istwan de Bragho is really invulnerable by sword and magic, then there has to be some other way. But regrettably I don't have such knowledge.

No, brother, that's impossible. Heretics may at most draw their attention by performing certain rites, but they can't break the restrictions by which the Fallen Angels are bound. That's why they send their minions instead of themselves. Regrettably those lesser demons, for example Gaugliel, Mazriel, Proctfor or Elgheborth, can in fact be invoked. But it's impossible to invoke the Fallen Angels themselves. That would be the end of it all...

Well... that's alarming. It seems someone is trying to revive the cult. Heretics are completely mad these days in their efforts to destroy the true faith, and to disrupt the Holy Mother Church. As if we haven't been doing enough for them for long centuries. This disgusting unfaithfulness must be completely uprooted! I hope you'll reveal them and hand them to justice, brother!

Very well, brother. It seems you're versed in the local history. In that case you surely know the city wasn't populated again. Although there were attempts made to settle it again, there hanged the shadow of the pagan curse above the ruins. Instead of the city becoming a beautiful new faithful town as it happened in the case of Alvaron people had to abandon it and lay the foundations of Glatzburg several miles away in a place that was much less favorable.

That's exactly my opinion, brother! I'm sure that if we could wipe out the evil from the Temple of All Gods it would be long step forward in the many centuries long fight against the unclean powers that have found their home in the ruins of Galibornium. And that's exactly what I'd like to speak with you about.

I knew you wouldn't fail me, brother. You're a true example for us all! May Archangel Gabriel himself and all the Saints protect you. Here accept the sprinkler with holy water that will allow you to fulfill the task. As soon as the Temple of All Gods is consecrated I'll send several of our priests to start with repairing it, and to keep the flame of the true faith burning amidst infernal darkness.
May I do something for you now, brother?
But sure, brother. There's nothing easier. What do you want to know?
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of kidnapping against Alphonso DiCerbio. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of kidnapping against Raimond Ventano. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of heresy against Ethien de Pasque. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.

What?! Are you serious or are you only joking, brother? Do you realize what you have just said? Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick is the wife of the royal governor of the city, Grand Duke Robert Heidrick! And that means she belongs to the highest circles of the society and has connections with the king's court!
Yes, I realize that, Your Honor. But even she falls within the jurisdiction of the Holy Office and since I've gathered the required evidence against her, I'm determined to arrest and question her!
As you wish, brother. But I have to ask you what evidence have you gathered against her.
My God! If all you've just said is really true it's my duty to bring a charge of heresy against Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick. You have my permission to arrest her, brother.

WHAT?! Cardinal Truncquillius? I must say you've taken me aback, brother! You can't accuse the Curial Inquisitor of heresy, can you?! Why, he's my superior, and yours too, after all! We both are obliged to obey his orders! This would be disobeying a superior and there's only one punishment for that—death!

But not in the case when there's a suspicion that he perpetrated a crime, Your Honor. The Codex of Inquisition allows to temporarily suspend the powers of a Curial Inquisitor in the case there's an allegation brought against him. And then his subordinate inquisitors are obliged to obey his orders no more until he's exonerated.

I know what the Codex of Inquisition says, brother. But still he's the Curial Inquisitor! He's a man I deeply respect and he's a great support in the fight against heresy! You can't charge him with heresy! Not him! That's madness!
Tell me, then, what evidence do you have against him, brother. And choose your words carefully!
That's still not enough to accuse the Cardinal, brother. Do you have some other evidence against him?

Well... the arguments brought forward by you is too cogent and the allegation too grave for me to act otherwise. Although I trust in Cardinal Truncquillius's innocence I have to grant your suit. I bring a charge of heresy against Cardinal Truncquillius. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.
Well... it seems the evidence speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of heresy and of consorting with dark powers against the soldier Harph. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.
That's great, brother! And do you have enough supporting evidence?
Well... the evidence brought forward by you speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of witchcraft against the servant girl Jeanette. You have my permission to arrest her, brother.
Well... the evidence brought forward by you speaks clearly. In that case I bring a charge of witchcraft against Hans Thomas Brookwelt. You have my permission to arrest him, brother.
It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment, brother.

Ethien de Pasque holds the office of the Commander in the knightly order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, brother. It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial Judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment.

Brother, your decision will have grave consequences. Very grave consequences that will shake the confidence in the Holy Office. It's my holy duty as an Inquisitorial Judge to ask you if you have enough evidence for the indictment of Cardinal Truncquillius.
I'm sorry, brother, but you are wrong. You have much to learn before you can be named an Inquisitorial Judge. Go away and return when you are better prepared.

No, brother, you're wrong. They're both principles of the secular law and the canon law. But the inquisitorial proceedings are governed only by one of them, the other does not apply. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
No, brother. A judge is not authorized to remit penalties. That may be done only by the Inquisitor General.
Yes, he may. If the judge comes to a conclusion that mere hearing of the case before the court is enough to reform the culprit, he may refrain from the punishment in its entirety.
No, brother, you're wrong. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.

There are several punishments possible: life imprisonment, imprisonment, the donation of the amount of gold specified, loss of the title, punishment on the pillory or even death by hanging, beheading or burning.

No, brother. Those are punishments that a secular court may impose. The Inquisition knows only one punishment. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
The imprisonment for life or death by burning. Nothing else can cleanse a heretic of the crimes he perpetrated.
No, brother. The Inquisition uses only one of those punishments. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
When somebody commits a theft in a house of God, will that crime be prosecuted by the secular law, by the Brotherhood of the Righteous, or by the Holy Office?
The theft in a house of God is of course in the jurisdiction of the Holy Office.
You're very wrong, brother. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.
You're wrong, brother. You have much to learn yet before you can become an Inquisitorial Judge. Go now, and return when you're better prepared.

Optime, mi frater! You correctly answered all the questions about the canon law and the secular law and so I don't doubt your qualities. So I bless you and name you a Judge of the Holy Office. Benedictione te inquirentem iudicem eo nomino. Utinam deus te benedicat, fili. God bless you, brother! Take this item as the insignia of your new position. Congratulations!
Thank you, Your Honor. It's great honor for me!

Welcome, brother. May I help you somehow? I guess you're new to Glatzburg. I'm Welfhar and I'm a Judge of the Holy Office. Glatzburg is in my judicial jurisdiction and presently I hold the office of the Prosecutor General in Glatzburg too. If I'm not mistaken you don't belong to the local Inquisitorial Curia, do you?

From Hillbrandt? I've heard some news that some unfortunate incident happened there... They say Bishop Vallarian was sentenced and burned there. I must admit it was my close friend and his death quite unsettled me. Weren't you involved in that case somehow, brother?

Hmm... I wish I had enough time to study the case. I've always esteemed and admired Judge Vallarian. But due to my working load here in Glatzburg I will hardly have some spare time to look at it. What a pity! Hopefully Cardinal Truncquillius, the Curial Inquisitor of Glatzburg, will take some action in this matter. Anyway, I'm glad to meet you, brother. What was it that brought you to Glatzburg?

We will see, brother, we will see. I'll take care his death is properly investigated! I presume Cardinal Truncquillius, the local Curial Inquisitor, is thoroughly informed about the matter and that he'll decide what has to be done. But now tell me what was it that brought you here to Glatzburg?
Welcome, brother. I hesitate to ask if you've already achieved some success in your noble effort to consecrate the pagan temple in Galibornium...

Really? I can't believe that... Have you really managed to wipe out evil from that ancient dark place? And to consecrate a new sanctuary of God there? Unbelievable! The whole Holy Mother Church, not only here in Glatzburg will be indebted to you forever, brother! You're a real example for us all!

Don't thank me, brother—you don't have to. I and the whole Holy Mother Church should be grateful to you instead. I'll arrange at once some priests from the Glatzburg Diocese to move into the consecrated temple and to start with its reconstruction.
Welcome, brother. I thank you all the time in my prayers for what you've done for our Holy Mother Church. Can I do something for you?
What do you need, brother? If I'm right you should now be in the pagan temple in the ruins of Galibornium trying to consecrate it...

Really? I can't believe that... Could it be that you really managed to wipe out evil from that ancient dark place? And to consecrate a new sanctuary of God there? Unbelievable! Well... if it's true the whole Holy Mother Church will be indebted to you forever, brother! You're a real example for us all!
Good day, brother. What can I do for you?

Welcome, brother. I must thank you again for consecrating the pagan temple in Galibornium. I'm sorry a man of such exceptional abilities is at the same time gathering evidence against Curial Inquisitor Truncquillius. But God will judge if your deeds are proper. What can I do for you?

I must apologize to you, dear brother, for my initial mistrust concerning the accusation of Cardinal Truncquillius. It was so... shocking that I refused to believe it at first. How deeply is this age rotten when heresy infiltrates even such high circles of the Realm's society? Unbelievable... and utterly grueling. How shall I fulfil my mission when I can't be sure we're carrying out the will of God?
Yes, you're right, brother. I deeply apologize to you once again!
I understand your anger, brother. You surely take it ill of me that I wasn't able to accept the fact Cardinal Truncquillius is guilty. Nevertheless I hope you'll forgive me. Farewell.
I thought you would say that. So, what evidence is it, brother?
The Inquisitor of the Holy Office steals? I'm shocked! Go to confess your sins immediately, brother. I will not allow this!

You're very sharp, son. But don't try to find any words undermining the authority of the church in my speech. I'm trying to say people have erred and they need to be called back into the herd by their shepherd. And those who are the most savage must be destroyed! That's the task of the Holy Office, son. That's your task and the task of all my brothers inquisitors. If you too do well what the Shepherd called us to do our reward will be the return of God's Earthly Kingdom to the Earth.
Yes, that's commendable. Although I'm a bit surprised by that in a member of the aristocracy.

A secret meeting you say? Interesting... and suspicious. I've thought that nobles of the Realm aren't in the habit of meeting anyone secretly, provided they're not preparing a revolution or conspiracy. Secrecy is Satan's companion, as the Holy Scriptures say. But as you wish, keep the secret for yourself. But remember that everything you confess voluntarily will serve to your advantage during the trial...

WHAT?! Cardinal Truncquillius? I must say you've taken me aback, son! You can't accuse the Curial Inquisitor of heresy, can you?! Why, he's my superior! I'm obliged to obey his orders! This would be disobeying a superior and there's only one punishment for that—death!

Welcome, son. Can I help you somehow? I guess you're new to Glatzburg. I'm Welfhar and I'm the Judge of the Holy Office. Glatzburg is in my judicial jurisdiction and presently I hold the office of the General Prosecutor in Glatzburg too. If I'm not mistaken you don't belong to the local gentry, do you?
A noble steals?! I'm shocked! Go confess your sins immediately, son! I won't allow anything like that!
Come, friend, I'll play with your bowels!
Put away your weapon, friend, and you won't come to any harm. I promise I will take it as a mitigating circumstance.
Enough of such talking, little soldier! Prepare to die! I'll make a necklace from your entrails!
Wait, good man. I don't want to measure my strength with you. Take this pouch of gold and let me pass, please!
If you have money I'll take it from you anyway, little soldier. You're gonna die!
I'm sorry, you rogue, but I'll have to cross your wicked intentions!
Really? And how do you wanna do that? Will you hit my fist with your face?
Abandon your malicious intention, good man, and you won't come to any harm. It's still time to take the path of penance and ask God for forgiveness.
Enough of such talking, josser! Prepare to die! I'll make a necklace from your entrails!
If you have money I'll take it from you anyway, josser. You're gonna die!
I'm sorry, my son, but I'll have to cross your wicked intentions!
Really? And how do you wanna do that? Will you pray so hard that I get a heart attack?
If you desist from your intent to commit an illegal act on me, good man, the court will surely take it as a mitigating circumstance.
Enough of such talking, little prince! Prepare to die! I'll make a necklace from your entrails!
Who summons me into this world? Who disturbs my eternal peace and forces me to linger here, in the bitter and vile world? I want to go away, release me at once and abandon your intentions!
I need your testimony, poor soul. I need you to answer several questions.
I don't want to answer your questions, mortal. I want to return back, away from this world...
Withdraw from vainly trying to resist me, stray soul, and answer my questions! Because I wield the power that won't allow you to lie!
Aaaaahhh! Your words are tormenting me, mortal. I want to go away, but I can't. I can't go back, I'm being kept here against my will. Ask then. Ask your questions and release me from this world!
Do you know Corin Morray, stray soul?
Corin Morray? The name... sounds familiar. Yes, I remember the girl. She was my... friend. Yes, I remember her. We served together at the royal court as servant maids.
Can you remember what happened in the royal palace two years ago? What did you witness?

It's so long ago... I feel the memories flowing around me. They're icy cold but nevertheless the pain is like red-hot iron. Yes... I recollect what happened. I remember... We saw dark shadows moving through the royal palace. Someone let them inside on a moonless night. There were no guards, the entrance was not being watched. But we saw them. We followed them like a moth follows the flame of a candle. And much like the moth we sealed our fate by that.
What happened? What did you witness? Corin Morray spoke about a dark ritual...

Oh yes, the ritual... They lit black candles, sprinkled the floor with fresh blood, scattered narcotic spice into bowls and sang dreadful chants in some unknown language. In the chamber of Prince Louis. He was not yet fifteen years old, he was so young and innocent... His body hovered above the bed and there were demons and unclean powers consorting all around him. They played with his body, tortured him and caressed him at the same time. It was macabre... and fascinating. I wanted to scream in horror, but instead I nearly gave in to the singing. Corin held me... She held her hand over my mouth and was biting her lips not to scream so hard, that she started to bleed.

Prince Louis died. I saw his deadly pale face. I almost heard it when his heart ceased to beat. Then we ran away at last. They didn't see us, they were too inebriated by what they had just done. They dragged themselves away like old men. But we didn't see that, we ran away back to our chamber and there we silently wept till the morning because of what we witnessed. We shouldn't follow those men. We shouldn't entangle ourselves into something that terrible. Because then the punishment came. The punishment for those who can't stay silent. And I wasn't able to. For some time I fought with that, but after the funeral of Prince Louis I wasn't able to be silent any longer. I confessed.
Who to?

I don't know. The priest was hidden in the confessional. But the same day I was arrested and put in chains. Then they put me to torture. They burnt me with hot iron. They crushed my fingers. They whipped off pieces of skin from my back. They poured boiling water into my mouth. And they raped me. Again and again. I couldn't endure that. I wanted to die so it would end at last. That's why I said all they wanted to hear. I confessed I made it all up. I confessed I myself revel in infernal powers and I denunciated Corin as my perverse companion and lover. I don't know what happened to her. They probably executed her too. They'll execute all of them. Same as they did to me. They tied me to a post at the stake, passed the sentence and watched as flames were swallowing me. I suffocated with smoke, the blaze was consuming me. I sensed my skin broiling. I felt the stink of my own burned body. It took a very, very long time before I blacked out. And the whole time I screamed in pain like an animal. But at last the merciful wings of death took me away and then there was nothing...
Did you recognize some of the men performing the ritual in the chamber of Prince Louis?

Yes, I recognized one of them. We both did. We often saw him in the royal palace, we knew his voice and the way he walked. It was impossible for him to hide from us in the black cloak. It was the Royal Counselor Verenicus, the snake and a rat of a person! It was him who let the heretics into the castle and led them to the chamber of Prince Louis. It was him who arranged for them not to run into any guards. He and only he, is the direct deviser of the death of Prince Louis!
You didn't recognize anyone else but the Counselor Verenicus? Try to remember, it's important!
No, I didn't recognize anyone else. Only the snake of a person, Counselor Verenicus. May he strangle with his own poison!
How many people participated in the heretical rite?

They were three all in all. Three dark cloaks silently moved through the palace corridors. Stilly like bat wings, like the breath of death. There were three like the fallen angels. Three like the Scourges of God.
What did Corin Morray do then?

My dear Corin... She was like my older sister. More experienced, more grown up. She advised me to be silent. She knew well that such secrets must not be revealed. But I wasn't able to help myself. I had to open my heart to someone... and it was the death of me. Oh, those flames burned so much... The pain was unbearable!
I thank you for you testimony, stray soul. Hereby I release you from my power. You may return to whence you've come from. Rest in peace!
Who will sell me some wares here in Alvaron?

You want to know if Christoffer de Malamert is a heretic? I dunno. People say that about him. Many townsmen are convinced he's a heretic and a traitor. But the more they shout it into the world the more they fear what the future will bring them. Because if it's true, then where will heresy stop when it is able to taint the heart of the Grand Master of a knightly order?
I don't remember any fierce storm occurring recently, knight. It's true that sometimes quite a scuffle breaks loose above Alvaron, but nothing of that sort has happened lately.
I'm sorry, but I have no suspicions of heresy. I'm at the very end of the investigation procedure and not at its beginning—I don't care about any suspicion because I have plenty of my own work!

Surely you have heard King Edward II was murdered not long ago. And in the midst of his own chambers in the royal palace. I absolutely don't understand how someone could do it when the whole palace was guarded so rigorously. But it doesn't matter now... The Realm lost its leader and it will take some time before the Assembly of the Realm convenes and selects a new king from its members. Maybe it won't ever happen because the gentry are so set by the ears lately, that they can't agree upon anything. God protect our Realm!
You ask me if Verenicus is mixed up in the murder of Prince Louis? Hmm... I really have no idea. But if he is, then I suppose he'll end up in my hands eventually, won't he?

Inquisitor General could be a heretic? I would be greatly surprised by that. I mean I would be surprised if someone found out, not if he was a heretic. But to tell the truth I've never had in my hands, such a high ranking inquisitor, even the very head of the Holy Office. It surely would be an interesting experience...

I've heard Juhasz Gotherr appears somewhere in the city now and then, of course cloaked by night and only in the darkest streets. It's said he's grubbing for something, but no one knows what it could be. Some say he's searching for victims that he could use in his dark pagan rituals, others say he's looking for some ancient artifact or a grimoire. God knows what's true. Maybe he isn't even in the city.
I'm searching for missing Ron Burton. Do you happen to know anything about him?
I've heard Ron Burton went missing. It certainly is a hard blow for his brother—especially when the whole inn bequeathed to them by their father, is going to belong to him now...
Nothing. Only that someone's misfortune may be some other's luck. But it's quite possible his brother was eaten by wolves or killed by some other infernal vermin...
Do you happen to know some way how to improve a man's memory?
To improve memory you say? I personally suggest the rack. There's nothing better for improving memory than a well stretched body and dislocated limbs...
Better answer me or you'll going to deplore not doing so!
I ask you sincerely, good man, answer my query.
I don't want to flatter you in any way, but I assure you that an answer from a man so experienced and worldly-wise would help me a lot.
Welcome, knight. What do you need? Do you have some work for me?
You're the executioner?
Yes, it happens to be so. The name's Charles Winston III.
Do you have much work here in Alvaron?
I would say so. Just look around here and you can see I certainly don't suffer from boredom. And I feel you're gonna gimme some more work...
Maybe. May I talk with you for a moment?
Well, as you wish, knight. It's up to you...
You're a nobleman?
No, but the executioner's craft is inherited in our family from father to the firstborn son, who's named Charles. Hence the number.
No, not now. Farewell.
I don't remember any fierce storm occurring recently, Father. It's true that sometimes quite a scuffle breaks loose above Alvaron, but nothing of that sort has happened lately.
Welcome, Father. What do you need? Do you have some work for me?
Well, as you wish, Father. It's up to you...
I don't remember any fierce storm occurring recently, noble sir. It's true that sometimes quite a scuffle breaks loose above Alvaron, but nothing of that sort has happened lately.
Welcome, noble sir. What do you need? Do you have some work for me?
Well, as you wish, noble sir. It's up to you...
What can you tell me about the orcs?

Shamans say the orcs are an ancient race originating in the Accursed Depths, from where they were set free at the beginning of days by the Cursed Flame who then became their master. Under his leadership the orcs conquered the realm of Thron under the Mountains. It was in the era when God of the humans was only one of many gods present in the world. But gods punished orcs for destroying the realm of Thron and threw them down again to the Accursed Depths. The orcs had waited there since then, for the Cursed Flame to release them again and lead them to their final reckoning with the world. Then the time of bloodshed shall come and the orcs would walk together with people branded by the Mark of the Beast. And so it happened. The race of orcs again entered this world not to leave it any more!
What plans do the orcs have?

According to the shamans they're waiting for the Sign of Blood that shall be sent them by their master, the Cursed Flame. Then they shall walk the world again and along with other infernal legions and people branded with the Mark of the Beast, shall reckon with the whole world. Wrang thinks the time will come quite soon!
Do you know any people conspiring with the orcs?

No, Wrang doesn't know any people with the Mark of the Beast, who order the orcs in the name of the Cursed Flame. Wrang has never met such people. Only once he saw a human female going to Khan Rashgar.
Is there something noteworthy going on in the orcish realm?

It's said there's a place where the ghost of the last King Under the Mountains appears. He swore before his death that he wouldn't leave the realm of Thron until it is avenged by the death of Khan Rashgar. The legends from the ancient era of the Great War say the ghost guards the mythic treasure of Thron that has been never found by orcs.
That's all I needed to know, orc. You may go now.
Wait, human, don't harm poor Wrang. Leave poor Wrang to his own damned fate!
Peace, orc, I don't mean you any harm. For now. Tell me who you are and what are you doing here.

Ah, you're asking who Wrang is and what he's doing here? Wrang's poor orc working all his life and not doing anything else but slaving and working like a beaver. A scourge and whip above him and for all the work he was getting only disdain, ingratitude and rotten meat. Last time they forced him along with the other workers to dig in the human iron ore mines, because they wanted to make enough weapons and armor for the army of Khan Rashgar that was soon to rise to the world from the Accursed Depths. Wrang saw only unbelievable grind there, only work and nothing but work and death. And the cruel boss Gubring didn't let anybody rest a bit!

We were mining iron ore for him and he was sending it below to the orcish realm. One day Wrang couldn't stand it any more and he ran away. Gubring had no mercy with anybody, he beat orcs and tortured them. Only thing he wanted was to have enough of iron ore. And when somebody wasn't able to work any more Gubring ordered him killed and wolfed by others. Wrang didn't want to end that way and so he ran away. But he knows well Gubring's gonna search for him and eventually he'll find him and kill him. Provided that someone won't kill Gubring instead.
It seems you really hate Gubring's guts, orc.

Oh yes, Wrang hates Gubring to the bottom of his rotten soul. He wishes rats had eaten his mother alive before she managed to bear him. I wish someone would wring Gubring's neck or stick a jagged knife into his back!
If you wish so, I'll murder Gubring...

WHAT?! Gentleman would do it for poor Wrang? In that case Wrang would be the happiest orc in the whole world! As a reward Wrang will reveal to the gentleman all he knows about the orcs and where they dwell and what they plan. Gentleman won't regret it. Wrang knows it all, he has been everywhere and has heard a lot. Gentleman just bring Gubring's head. He'll find Gubring in the labor camp surrounded by guards and workers. Gentleman goes and kills him!
Well... maybe I could kill that Gubring. What would you give me for bringing you his dead head?

Gentleman would do it for poor Wrang? In that case Wrang would reward him greatly. Although he doesn't have much, he may reveal to the gentleman all he knows about the orcish race and the orcish realm and the orcish plans. And the gentleman's heading there, isn't he? What else would he want so deep under the mountains?
I would never accept such a disgusting deal!
You wouldn't? So let Wrang be, human. If you don't want to help Wrang then be gone to burning Hell and die there, you fool!
You're right, I'll better leave you to your fate, orc!
Not so fast, orc. It's not me who's going to go to Hell—it's gonna be you!
In that case I have a good news for you, orc. Gubring's dead. I killed him.
Wrang doesn't believe you! Show Wrang his head! Show! Show!
Here it is, orc.
You've made it, human! You murdered Gubring who almost tortured poor old Wrang to death. Wrang is so thankful to you! He'll tell you all he knows!
Alright, I'll bring it.
Gubring's dead, orc. But I assure you I didn't do it because I wanted to help you. There's no place for orcs in this Kingdom of God. Nevertheless I'll spare you.
Oh... Wrang thanks you, human. He's better gonna go out of your sight.
Gubring's dead, orc. But I assure you I didn't do it because I wanted to help you. There's no place for you here same as for him and hence, I'm going to send you now to God to be judged.
Your ill fortune hasn't mollified me, orc. You and your race have tainted the Realm and deserve to burn in the infernal flames for that!
Be quiet, infernal monster, and prepare to die swiftly. Soon you're going to be judged by God himself!
Are you bringing Wrang Gubring's head, human? Kill Gubring and bring me his head!
Don't worry, orc. I'll bring you Gubring's head.
Here's Gubring's head, orc.
You've made it, human! You murdered Gubring who almost tortured poor old Wrang to death. Wrang is so much thankful to you! He'll tell you all he knows about orcs and their plans as a reward!
I've thought it over. I'll send your soul to burning hell!
Let Wrang be, human. You didn't want to help him, so let him be and make off!
Be gone to hell, monster.
Wrang is happy Gubring's dead and his body is being eaten by worms. Wrang owes you, human!
Of course you may talk with Wrang, human. What d'ya need?
In that case you'll pay me with your life, you monster!
Wrang doesn't have anything. It's useless to search him...
Yes? Whhrrgghhh... that's good. It has been long since I ate human flesh. You came at the right time. Yes, I'll feast on your heart, human! WHAAAUUUURRRGGGHHH!!!
How's it possible my den has been stained by the stench of a human body?! How's it possible a human intruder has managed to come so deep into the Urrm's sanctum? Whhhrrrggghhh!
I came to cleanse this disgusting dirty kennel, full of evil of all that fouls the face of the God's earthly kingdom!
God sees this infernal place and his wrath is terrible! And he wishes no seed of sin would come out of here anymore!
I'm here to wrest from your ugly paws the holy relic of the Brotherhood of the Righteous—the Decapitator sword!
Hold back, Duke Ronald! I know about the curse that has changed you into this ugly beast. Maybe it's possible to free you of your damnation...
Damnation?! It's no damnation you wretch, it's a gift! God Urrm has endowed me, to allow me to become his chosen one!
Chosen for what?!

You don't understand?! I've become the one who's going to perform the rite of the Wolf's Might. I was destined to find this wolfish sanctum and to decipher the Urrm's ancient message. I've become the executor of his will and I'll become the one who'll lend his body to Urrm, to allow him to return to the Earth. There's only one thing left to do—to do one more sacrifice to Urrm. For the thirty and three full moons I've been abducting human females from Alvaron and its vicinity, and sacrificed them to god Urrm. And as soon as I sacrifice the last one Urrm will awake and enter my body!
In that case you don't give me any other choice, hellspawn!

Quiet, knight! You shouldn't utter the name of the Fallen Angel Arthamon aloud... Because he may hear us and send some unclean spirit to tear out our soul from our body and drag it away to burning Hell! Arthamon is one of the Fallen Angels who together with Satan were thrown down from Heaven by God for disobeying His words and working against His will. Since then they've been dwelling in Hell, the antipode of Heaven, and they've been trying to infiltrate our world to seize it and make it their kingdom. It's said that if they really managed to enter our world the powers of ruin, chaos and eternal sin would be unleashed here, that would destroy all that our faithful world is built upon. And there would be nothing left. But why are you asking about Arthamon, knight?
Baroness Linda van Gallagan confessed she helped to invoke Arthamon some time ago. Presumably he is now present in our world!

Woe, thrice, knight! The beast has been unchained! My fears have come true. I had a dream... The dream in which I saw earth opening and the ruler of flame, Arthamon, coming out of it to throw his destructive powers upon our world. Woe betide us all, ruin has entered the world!
Wait, good woman... Do you really think the Fallen Angel may enter our world? Why, the gospel and the true faith impede him from doing it!
Really, knight?!
If the Baroness spoke the truth and Arthamon was indeed invoked, where could he be hiding?
I don't have the slightest idea, knight. But I suppose he's hiding somewhere deep underground, as close to his infernal home as possible.
Even if it was true, maybe it would not be late yet to destroy Arthamon somehow?!
To destroy the Fallen Angel? Hardly so, knight. The Fallen Angels represent the worst of all dark powers. How could ordinary mortals stand up the power nearly as great as the God's?
I apologize for being so curious. It was just because I had a dream about Arthamon recently.
What dream?
I had a dream in which I saw earth opening and the ruler of flame, Arthamon, coming out of it to throw his destructive powers upon our world. Woe betide us all if ruin has entered the world!
If it really happened, where could Arthamon be hiding?
Even if Arthamon managed to get into our world, maybe it would be possible to destroy him somehow.
To destroy the Fallen Angel? Hardly so, knight. The Fallen Angels represent the worst of all dark powers. How could ordinary mortals stand to the power nearly as great as God's?
I've encountered a case of bewitching. Do you happen to know how to relieve the victim of the spell?

Are you telling me you've encountered a bewitched person, knight? That's a serious matter... You need quite a lot of knowledge of the forbidden arts to do it. That who bewitched the person is more than well versed in using dark powers. He had to obtain some item belonging to the victim. Then he put the item into a clay doll and spoke a cursed word. The victim will stay bewitched until the doll is destroyed.
I met the undead Bishop Herbertius who has risen up from the dead. And it seems there's nothing that can do him any harm. Could you give me some advice about how I can fight him?

You're telling me Bishop Herbertius has risen from his grave. And that nothing can harm him. Well... that doesn't sound good. When mighty and evil people die and then return back from beyond, they tend to change into very abhorrent creatures. According to what you say I think he may be a vampire. What did the Bishop look like? Was his body in a good state or was it decaying?
His body was in quite good state, but he was deadly pale and he stank.

Then woe betide us, knight! He's a vampire! That's bad, very bad... Vampires are a very mighty sort of undead. They will even stop fearing the sunlight over time. And to kill a vampire is not an easy task. Their unclean lives are cursed inside their damned hearts and they often take their heart and store it in a safe place. Thus they become invulnerable. A vampire can be killed only after his heart is destroyed.

I'd like to ask you about a discovery that I've made near the Dragon Rock. It's probable that a heretical sabbath occurred there because I found a dead girl in the middle of the circle, drawn most likely with human blood. The heart was taken out of the body and a great black egg inserted instead of it. Do you happen to know what meaning such a rite has?
