Holy Heaven! A black egg inserted in the place of the heart of the dead girl? Oh my God! What you've just told me reminds me of the rite of invocation of Satan, as described by Saint Aquistus in his tractate On the Invocation of Satan and Other Infernal Minions!
I haven't read that...

I'm not surprised, knight. For several centuries—to be specific since the third council of Trenevir—it has been a forbidden book. Saint Aquistus devoted himself to the analysis of pagan and heretical rites during which heathens tried to make contact with Hell and its creatures. And one of those rites is very similar to that you've just described to me, knight. During the rite a black cock's egg is inserted into the body of a dead girl and after uttering the correct formulas, the gate connecting this world with the world of hellspawns will open...
It's hard to believe that, don't you think?

Hard to believe? Why do you think so, knight? Nobody believed fire could rain instead of water. And lo! The rain of fire came upon us. I don't think we live in days when we may afford to doubt anything, knight. I warn you—the ritual is as real as the rain of fire! Satan will come and will bring an army with him to settle the score with the world! I had a dream and my dreams have never lied.

A crisis... yes, knight, you've given it the right name. That what we face really is... a crisis. And it's so much worse that I'm not sure if it will end someday. It may very well be that we will live dozens more years in this slush. Who can know for sure for how long God decided to test our faith? But frankly, knight, if it's really so, I doubt the true faith will survive here in Hillbrandt. It's getting weaker every day. I feel it although I'm no priest. Nobody believes the situation will eventually get better.
If you're searching for heretics, then if I were you I'd watch out for Lotti Frankmüller, knight.

Because everything's not such as it seems to be at first sight! Not everything that seems to be beautiful really is such. Even the reddest apple may be rotten with worms. Beware of her, knight, I advise you well!
Suzan Brauchner told me Lotti Frankmüller had been a secret lover of the murderer Hans Falkner. Is it true?
I don't know, knight, if she was a lover of the killer Falkner. Maybe she was, maybe not. But I definitely advise you to beware of her!
You're right, good woman. In all likelihood she has bewitched Raubsticht the executioner for executing her secret lover, the murderer Hans Falkner.
I don't know anything about that, but I definitely advise you to beware of her!

You want to know if something unusual has happened... well, yes, knight, it really has. Evil has entered our world from the depths of Hell itself! The tempest that blew over Hillbrandt several days ago was the indication of terrible things to come! Heaven will shake and the riders of Apocalypse will come forth again and this world will be no more!

I speak of the end of the world, knight! I know well what the storm meant. I know well why hellspawns and horned demons romped about in the sky! I understand well the meaning of their devilish laughter! The end draws near and we will be its witnesses!
That's blasphemy!
Blasphemy? Maybe... but certainly it's true. My dreams never lie.
Hmm... thank you.
An innocent soul is dead and evil dances around us like a Satan's harlot!
Do you want to say you believe Master d'Arvias is innocent?
I don't know, knight... it's hard to say. In these times everything's possible. And my dreams have told me nothing about the knight clad in steel.

Yes, I know the monstrance of Saint Orthenius has disappeared. I had a dream... and I saw a Beast's minion walking the town streets. It was he who seized the monstrance and brought it to his master, the faceless monster whose name was forgotten and found again!
What are you talking about? Who stole the monstrance?
I don't know anything more. I'm sorry. It was only a short dream...

My God! Deep the Bishop's soul dwells, deep... Dived into the earth like a coffin in the grave. And there's only sin and debauchery around, raping and brimstone. Thrice woe... where the Bishop's soul has gone!
Do you want to say the Bishop's dead?
I don't know, knight. Maybe. My dream didn't tell me more.

I see him... I see Paul Hammerhand. He's... lying... silently. He's huddled and sleeping. My God, his body's burning! His body's flouncing in flames! His soul's leaving our world! Quickly, knight, go and give him this potion before it's too late!
What are you talking about? Where will I find Paul?
If only I knew, knight! You must hurry... you must find him or else he's going to die. Give him this potion, it will save him.
I don't know anything about Linda van Gallagan, knight. She's clouded in darkness. I can't see her...
Do you have any suspicion who could have stolen the Master Edmond d'Arvias' sword?

As concerns the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias... I had a dream, knight. An evil dream... I saw a steel-clad knight lying in a deep unclean bed of sin and darkness where he was immersed by those standing around him. One of them took hold of the Master's sword while another one uncovered her shameless and unclean loins, and pressed them hard against the knight's groins... They dishonored him, stained and humiliated him. Woe to the knight who lost his sword! Woe to the land that lost its protector!

Wait... Master d'Arvias told me he lost his sword after being lured out of the town by heretics and put to sleep by some unclean magic. And that's exactly what you've just described. Who were those heretics? Who stole the Master's sword?
I don't have any idea, knight. I saw only black cloaks dark as night... dark as the souls of those wearing them. I saw only that they were three and there was one woman among them...
It's weird, knight, but everytime somebody from the town dies I have a dream from which I get to know about it. But I haven't dreamed about Natalia...
What? Are you telling me, it means Natalia wasn't murdered?
I don't know, knight... I only wanted to say nobody has ever died without me knowing about it. That's all.

You're asking me where the soldier Jullian is? Well... where he could be? Where's the blackest darkness?! Just under the candlestick! The soldier Jullian is near, knight. Very near... and he's not alone! His mind's full of lust and mammon! He's up to something bad...
But where is he? Do you know it?!
No, knight, I don't.
He's not alone? So who's with him?
I don't know, knight. I haven't the slightest idea. But it's not a man and she's not there from her own choice!

Do you want to hear a legend of the oath that outlasted eons? Of the oath uttered on the brink of ruin? Then hear the tale of Harlior, the last King of the mysterious race of Thron living in the Moonshine Mountains, when mankind still walked the path of deep paganism. The realm of Thron was magnificent... and it was all underground.
Underground?

Yes, just so. The Throns built fascinating palaces in the bowels of the world, they excavated breathtaking halls and fostered unbelievable crafts. Their pagan gods favored them and so the Throns thrived undisturbed in their subterranean seclusion. But it was the thorn in the side of the Cursed flame, the terrible ruler of nonexistence, and he decided to destroy all that beauty. He summoned the orcs, his loyal servants, from the Accursed Depths, and opened the paths to the realm of Thron for them. The orcs led by their eternal Khan Rashgar, burst into the Realm like a plague. They were destroying, plundering and killing all that they came across. Not even the pagan gods were able to stop the destruction because the Cursed Flame was mighty indeed!
Terrible... continue, please.

The fall was imminent. The realm was at the verge of the last battle. The Throns, those brave heroes, were lining up to valiantly enter the Hall of Ancestors and to feast there forevermore. Then the King of the Throns by name of Harlior, swore before the gods themselves that he wouldn't leave his realm until Khan Rashgar was dead. Then the armies clashed. The ironclad Throns fought against much greater numbers of orcs like the gods. But they were defeated all the same. But when cursed Khan Rashgar searched for the body of King Harlior, he didn't find it. The King's oath changed him into a phantom in the instant of his death. He became a ghost without the body and he has been walking in the ruins of his realm since then. For he may not sit at the Table or Feast in the Hall of Ancestors until his oath is fulfilled.
Fascinating... What happened to the orcs then? How's it possible that legends haven't mentioned them after that and that they appeared only now in the world they don't belong to?

They belong to every world, knight! They're creatures from the Accursed Depths where nothing exists, not even time. They serve those who know about them. And the fact someone summoned them into our world means only one thing—they are to destroy all that comes across their path!
I've heard some legends about the Dead Man's Stone standing near the gallows. What do you know about that stone?

Woe, knight—better not go near the Dead Man's Stone! There are souls of murderers and villains imprisoned there, of all the men ever executed in Hillbrandt. They're evil souls, damned by God. They are bound to haunt that piece of cursed rock forever. I have had countless nightmares about them... They screamed at me to go and release them, but I know well that what God has condemned, man has to leave alone.
I saw priest Romius and I'm worried about his health. Has he come to you for an advice lately?

Priest Romius hasn't asked me for any advice about his health recently, knight. But to tell the truth I too noticed him not looking good lately. He's very pale, queasy and he seems tired all the time. As if he had anemia. But that's apparently nonsense because he was completely healthy not long ago.
Anemia?
Just so, knight. Anemia has exactly these symptoms. It's also similar to sick people after the medic performed bloodletting by leeches on them, to lower the fever.

I'm not sure if it bears some relation to that but maybe I can tell you something about the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, knight. On top of that what you already know, of course—that Ollmier was murdered in Truthorn's inn in a rather wicked way. It's said they even stuck his manhood into his mouth... But what I want to tell you doesn't concern the way he was murdered but the reason why someone did it.
Really? So, why?

It's only my guess, of course, but it's possible it had some relation to his way of making his livelihood. Although he was a merchant he dealt in the items that definitely weren't intended for your everyday use. Magic scrolls, grimoires of witches, magic charms, mystic symbols, religious items... and all that originating from the days long ago. I'm sure the man crawled through many an ancient cemetery, many a ruin and through various black markets. And that became his doom. Because some secrets are to stay hidden and if someone unauthorized gets near them it may cost him his life!

Show me the root, knight... But why, it's the root of the herb called diabolicus magnificatum, popularly known as the Devil's root! It's very rare and very magic. I may brew a rather powerful boosting potion from it.

Are you asking me if I'm able to brew magic potions from the devil's root? But yes, of course, knight! To brew miraculous potions from the Devil's root is quite easy. Much more difficult is to find one. It usually grows in rather dangerous places—hence its name. If you manage to find any Devil's root I'll prepare a miraculous potion from it for several gp.
Tell me at once, or I'll put you on the rack, you old hag!
You don't like me, Ellisia, and I respect that. But I don't see any reason why you shouldn't answer my question. You know it would help a good cause!
Someone as wise as you, Ellisia, certainly wouldn't hesitate to answer my question...
No, that's untrue, I don't do anything like that! Who told it to you?!
It doesn't matter. To brew potions prolonging human life goes against God's law. You flirt with heresy, woman. It would be better for you to confess now.
I have nothing to confess. I have no potion of long life and I've never had any.
It's your last chance to give me the potion voluntarily. If you don't do so, I'll have to hand you over to the Inquisition. Then you'll be accused of heresy and tortured till you confess.
Heigh-ho, here it is...
See, at last you've grown wise. Farewell.
Alright, I believe you. There's probably no such potion at all. Farewell.
It was the astrologer Theil Brechthold.
The old rotten plotter. It's just like him. He set you onto me to get the potion for himself, am I right?
So you confess you have the potion?!
Oh... yes, I have such a potion, indeed.
Then give it to me at once!
Here it is, knight. But believe me—you don't do well to associate with persons like Theil Brechthold!
There's no point in getting excited, nothing's going on. Farewell.
The story goes that you brew a potion for yourself that prolongs your life...
I have a Devil's root on me. I'd like you to brew that miraculous potion from it for me, as you promised.
Nothing for now. Thanks.
If it has to be, knight. What do you want to know?
I have nothing to discuss with you, knight.
I won't trade with you, knight. Find someone else.
Good. I'll do it immediately...
It will cost you 1,000 gp.
I agree. Here is the money.
Really, it is the one! Thank Heaven it came into my hands at last! I'll be able to tap the mysteries of herbs with its help, like none of my ancestors ever did. Thank you, knight!
You've nothing to thank me for, good woman.
But I do. I'll prepare a miraculous potion from Devil's root as your reward. You'll see you'll find it useful!
Don't mention it, knight. Can I do something else for you?

I'm glad you've arrived at last, knight. I've been impatiently expecting you. I'm sure there's great power inside you even in your young age. The power that's able to front the darkness slowly enshrouding this town. Oh yes, you'd like to know who I am. My name's Ellisia Würtenrodt and I'm the local herbalist.
How could you know I would arrive in Hillbrandt, good woman?

I had a dream, knight. And in that dream I saw you coming to the gates of the town. Darkness was enshrouding you much like the whole town, but there was a lit torch in your hand and that means defiance and power. That's why I think you've brought us the light of hope.
Interesting. Do you have such dreams often?

Only every so often, knight. But they never lie. They're like the apparitions of the Holy Ghost—they always herald something that is to happen and what is going to happen. Sometimes I even don't know the persons or places I dream about. But then I always get to know that it happened exactly as it did in my dream. Or that something happened that corresponds with the symbolic meaning of my dream. And similarly it was with the dream about you—I dreamt about you coming to the city. It was several days ago.
You told me you're a herbalist. In that case you surely sell some potions and magic items, don't you?

Yes, it's so. I inherited the craft of brewing potions and making magic items of my mother just as she inherited it from my grandmother. The craft has been in our family for whole generations. If you need you may look into my shop. Maybe there's something that'll interest you, knight.
You look somewhat dismal. Is there something that's worrying you?

You're right, there's really something worrying me. It's the ancient herbarium written by the alchemist Semiel del Turquist of Ashton. I've managed to obtain a copy of that famous and matchless book for quite a lot of gold. But the merchants who were to bring the precious book to the town never arrived. Apparently they became victims of one of the orcish ambushes that are so common lately. And so my book is probably lost beyond redemption.
Maybe there's still hope. If I find the herbarium I'll certainly bring it to you.
Really? In that case you would earn my most sincere thanks, knight. God bless you. Can I do something for you?
Can I bank on some reward if I find your herbarium?
Certainly, knight. If you bring me my herbarium I'll brew you one of my magic potions. It will surely come in handy.
I'm sorry, but I definitely can't help you in any way.
What a shame. I felt you could be able to help me in this matter. But never mind, I'll find some other way.
I found an old herbarium on the orc by name of Rwhan. Is it what you're looking for?
Hello, knight. I hesitate to ask if you've already found my lost herbarium.
Not yet, good woman.
Never mind. Hopefully you'll find it. Can I do something for you?
Here's your herbarium.
What do you want, knight? You have the courage to come to me even after you took away my potion? I don't suppose you're bringing me my lost herbarium.
No, I haven't found your herbarium yet, good woman.
I would have thought so. Because it's more difficult than to rob old people. So, what do you want from me?
I've found your herbarium. Here it is.
Welcome too, knight. What can I do for you?
What do you want, knight? I've no time for you after what you did to me with that potion...
Greetings, knight. Thank you once more for finding my herbarium. What can I do for you?
Friedrich Raubsticht asks you to prepare a cure disease potion for him. Could you do this for him?
Yes, I could. But it will cost 500 gp.
Here is the money.

Good. I will give you the most powerful cure disease potion I can prepare. It helped even late duke Knutt who was the greatest philanderer of his time—he caught probably all venereal diseases I know... If this potion doesn't help, Raubsticht is lost.
Thank you, I'll tell him that. I'm sure he will be glad.
I don't have that money.
Than come back when you earn enough—if Raubsticht is still alive.

Quiet, Father! You shouldn't utter the name of the Fallen Angel Arthamon aloud... Because he may hear us and send some unclean spirit to tear out our soul from our body and drag it away to burning Hell! Arthamon is one of the Fallen Angels who together with Satan were thrown down from Heaven by God for disobeying His words and working against His will. Since then they've been dwelling in Hell, the antipode of Heaven, and they've been trying to infiltrate our world to seize it and make it their kingdom. It's said that if they really managed to enter our world the powers of ruin, chaos and eternal sin would be unleashed here, that would destroy all that our faithful world is built upon. And there would be nothing left. But why are you asking about Arthamon, Father?

Woe, thrice, Father! The beast has been unchained! My fears have come true. I had a dream... The dream in which I saw earth opening and the ruler of flame, Arthamon, coming out of it to throw his destructive powers upon our world. Woe betide us all, ruin has entered the world!
Really, Father?!
I don't have the slightest idea, Father. But I suppose he's hiding somewhere deep underground, as close to his infernal home as possible.
To destroy the Fallen Angel? Hardly so, Father. The Fallen Angels represent the worst of all dark powers. How could ordinary mortals stand up the power nearly as great as the God's?
To destroy the Fallen Angel? Hardly so, Father. The Fallen Angels represent the worst of all dark powers. How could ordinary mortals stand to the power nearly as great as God's?

Are you telling me you've encountered a bewitched person, Father? That's a serious matter... You need quite a lot of knowledge of the forbidden arts to do it. That who bewitched the person is more than well versed in using dark powers. He had to obtain some item belonging to the victim. Then he put the item into a clay doll and spoke a cursed word. The victim will stay bewitched until the doll is destroyed.

Then woe betide us, Father! He's a vampire! That's bad, very bad... Vampires are a very mighty sort of undead. They will even stop fearing the sunlight over time. And to kill a vampire is not an easy task. Their unclean lives are cursed inside their damned hearts and they often take their heart and store it in a safe place. Thus they become invulnerable. A vampire can be killed only after his heart is destroyed.

I'm not surprised, Father. For several centuries—to be specific since the third council of Trenevir—it has been a forbidden book. Saint Aquistus devoted himself to the analysis of pagan and heretical rites during which heathens tried to make contact with Hell and its creatures. And one of those rites is very similar to that you've just described to me, Father. During the rite a black cock's egg is inserted into the body of a dead girl and after uttering the correct formulas, the gate connecting this world with the world of hellspawns will open...

Hard to believe? Why do you think so, Father? Nobody believed fire could rain instead of water. And lo! The rain of fire came upon us. I don't think we live in days when we may afford to doubt anything, Father. I warn you—the ritual is as real as the rain of fire! Satan will come and will bring an army with him to settle the score with the world! I had a dream and my dreams have never lied.

A crisis... yes, Father, you've given it the right name. That what we face really is... a crisis. And it's so much worse that I'm not sure if it will end someday. It may very well be that we will live dozens more years in this slush. Who can know for sure for how long God decided to test our faith? But frankly, Father, if it's really so, I doubt the true faith will survive here in Hillbrandt. It's getting weaker every day. I feel it although I'm no priest. Nobody believes the situation will eventually get better.
If you're searching for heretics, then if I were you I'd watch out for Lotti Frankmüller, Father.

Because everything's not such as it seems to be at first sight! Not everything that seems to be beautiful really is such. Even the reddest apple may be rotten with worms. Beware of her, Father, I advise you well!
I don't know, Father, if she was a lover of the killer Falkner. Maybe she was, maybe not. But I definitely advise you to beware of her!

You want to know if something unusual has happened... well, yes, Father, it really has. Evil has entered our world from the depths of Hell itself! The tempest that blew over Hillbrandt several days ago was the indication of terrible things to come! Heaven will shake and the riders of Apocalypse will come forth again and this world will be no more!

I speak of the end of the world, Father! I know well what the storm meant. I know well why hellspawns and horned demons romped about in the sky! I understand well the meaning of their devilish laughter! The end draws near and we will be its witnesses!
I don't know, Father... it's hard to say. In these times everything's possible. And my dreams have told me nothing about the knight clad in steel.
I don't know, Father. Maybe. My dream didn't tell me more.

I see him... I see Paul Hammerhand. He's... lying... silently. He's huddled and sleeping. My God, his body's burning! His body's flouncing in flames! His soul's leaving our world! Quickly, Father, go and give him this potion before it's too late!
If only I knew, Father! You must hurry... you must find him or else he's going to die. Give him this potion, it will save him.
I don't know anything about Linda van Gallagan, Father. She's clouded in darkness. I can't see her...

As concerns the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias... I had a dream, Father. An evil dream... I saw a steel-clad knight lying in a deep unclean bed of sin and darkness where he was immersed by those standing around him. One of them took hold of the Master's sword while another one uncovered her shameless and unclean loins, and pressed them hard against the knight's groins... They dishonored him, stained and humiliated him. Woe to the knight who lost his sword! Woe to the land that lost its protector!
I don't have any idea, Father. I saw only black cloaks dark as night... dark as the souls of those wearing them. I saw only that they were three and there was one woman among them...
It's weird, Father, but everytime somebody from the town dies I have a dream from which I get to know about it. But I haven't dreamed about Natalia...
I don't know, Father... I only wanted to say nobody has ever died without me knowing about it. That's all.

You're asking me where the soldier Jullian is? Well... where he could be? Where's the blackest darkness?! Just under the candlestick! The soldier Jullian is near, Father. Very near... and he's not alone! His mind's full of lust and mammon! He's up to something bad...
No, Father, I don't.
I don't know, Father. I haven't the slightest idea. But it's not a man and she's not there from her own choice!

They belong to every world, Father! They're creatures from the Accursed Depths where nothing exists, not even time. They serve those who know about them. And the fact someone summoned them into our world means only one thing—they are to destroy all that comes across their path!

Woe, Father—better not go near the Dead Man's Stone! There are souls of murderers and villains imprisoned there, of all the men ever executed in Hillbrandt. They're evil souls, damned by God. They are bound to haunt that piece of cursed rock forever. I have had countless nightmares about them... They screamed at me to go and release them, but I know well that what God has condemned, man has to leave alone.

Priest Romius hasn't asked me for any advice about his health recently, Father. But to tell the truth I too noticed him not looking good lately. He's very pale, queasy and he seems tired all the time. As if he had anemia. But that's apparently nonsense because he was completely healthy not long ago.
Just so, Father. Anemia has exactly these symptoms. It's also similar to sick people after the medic performed bloodletting by leeches on them, to lower the fever.

I'm not sure if it bears some relation to that but maybe I can tell you something about the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, Father. On top of that what you already know, of course—that Ollmier was murdered in Truthorn's inn in a rather wicked way. It's said they even stuck his manhood into his mouth... But what I want to tell you doesn't concern the way he was murdered but the reason why someone did it.

Show me the root, Father... But why, it's the root of the herb called diabolicus magnificatum, popularly known as the Devil's root! It's very rare and very magic. I may brew a rather powerful boosting potion from it.

Are you asking me if I'm able to brew magic potions from the devil's root? But yes, of course, Father! To brew miraculous potions from the Devil's root is quite easy. Much more difficult is to find one. It usually grows in rather dangerous places—hence its name. If you manage to find any Devil's root I'll prepare a miraculous potion from it for several gp.
It's your last chance to give me the potion voluntarily. If you don't do so, I'll have to accuse you of heresy and torture you till you confess.
Here it is, Father. But believe me—you don't do well to associate with persons like Theil Brechthold!

You're wrong, faithful. I'm not a spawn of Hell, although my body is long dead. I personally have put it into that state to wait until someone opens the entrance into this dungeon and allows me to return to the earth's surface—back to the life! And you did just that...
What?! What are you talking about? Are you saying you've managed to outsmart Death? But that's a sin!

You orthodox people... Those sins of yours are ridiculous. They always have been. You're totally obsessed by them. You're forbidden to commit them but your life is in fact a way from one sin to another... But that's unimportant now. Are you asking how I managed to outsmart Death? Simply—I own the relic named the Chalice of Metamorphosis. It's also called the Vessel of Pearin or the Chalice of the Creator, because thanks to the power of the god it's possible to change a man or an animal into any being—it's only needed to drink from the chalice!
Oh God...

And just thanks to the magic effects of the Chalice of Metamorphosis I willfully changed myself into an undead to wait for the day the gates of my involuntary prison open. The perfidious Orthenius made them magically sealed for us all to starve here to death. But now the time of revenge has come. I'm going to rise again, create a new body for myself and then I'll muster an army with the help of the chalice to overthrow the orthodox dogs and return the rule over the world to the Pantheon. A new Ereborn will rise and I'll be its emperor! And you're going to be the first of the orthodox who'll pay for all what you did to Ereborn! You'll die!

What?! Are my senses deluding me?! A mortal inside the Temple of the Creation? But that's not possible! That would mean... the seal has been broken! Yes, there's no other explanation! Oh great Pearin, thank you for rescuing me! I've known the day would come for me to walk the surface again! This day is the last one of my prison! Aloha etrribe!
Who are you, wandering soul? And what are you talking about?!

I'm Yrrmaxius, the high priest of the god Pearin, the Great Creator. Or I used to be when I was alive. That was in the era when the realm of Ereborn ruled the world—before the madman named Orthenius came and destroyed all what he saw in the name of the First Prophet and God the Savior. Including the magnificent Galibornium, the city of my birth. It's queer you orthodox are able to perpetrate the worst crimes in the name of the love of the Savior...
You're really the right one to say that—as a spawn of Hell you're committing the most disgusting crime against God!
Enough! I won't hear such disgusting talk. And moreover from a hellspawn such as you!
My husband, Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, is the royal governor of Glatzburg at the moment. The vice-governor is Duke Rowan van Leerin.

Weapons and armor are sold mainly by Hans von Drichtmaul in Glatzburg, knight. He's renowned far and wide. At the wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt and at the alchemist Paolus Ventimus you may get potions and various magic things. The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch and the landlord Ludwig Weintraum both run shops with everything you can imagine. And then there is Alphonso DiCerbio here, who is said to sell stolen goods.
What do you think of the current crisis our Realm has been dragged into, Grand Duchess?

It's regrettable that the Realm has got into such a woeful state. And it's the work of all those criminals and heretics who are so numerous in the world these days. I unlike others firmly believe everything will get back square again. I pray for that every day, knight.
That's commendable.
Just so, knight.
I've heard a war is coming, Grand Duchess. Do you know something further about that?
My husband has mentioned some orders from Alvaron that seemed to be indication of a war. But I don't know any details.
I'm searching for heretics here in Glatzburg. Do you suspect someone, Grand Duchess?
Are you asking me if I suspect some heretics? Do you mean aside from my husband? No, knight... I can't think of anyone. God, it's so terrible... What will I do if it shows that my husband... oh God!

Maybe I'm going to repeat myself a bit, knight, but the worst thing that happened here recently is the suspicion of heresy that hangs over my husband. I shudder to think about him being... about me being married for so long to... a heretic!

The merchant Raimond Ventano was accused of heresy, Grand Duchess. During torture he confessed he along with you invoked the fallen angel Baphomet into this world. What can you tell me about this accusation?

It's absurd! That common swain has the nerve to charge me with something like that?! How could he... I hope you don't believe that nonsense. No matter what the villain is guilty of, his denunciation of my person is evidently made-up. Don't you know who I am, knight? You can't think I would descend to heresy, moreover to such monstrous one as the invocations of demons, can't you? I'm sure he did that confession in a state of mental disorder or that he tried to take innocent people like me with him to the burning Hell!
Yes, that's probable. Nevertheless I needed to be sure.

I'm glad, knight, that you don't give any weight to those lies. No one can be sure these days that some of the hunted-down heretics won't frame him up of his own committed crimes just to do him wrong.

We will see? What do you mean by that, knight? Isn't it clear that the hooligan's telling downright lies? Don't you feel that the accusation of his smells of brimstone? That it's a temptation you've been led into? Raimond Ventano's apparently lying, whatever his motives are! That's all I'm going to say about that!
I don't believe you, Grand Duchess. I think you're guilty and it's only a matter of time for me to get enough evidence against you!

What?! You can't be serious about that! I'm Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, not some village charlatan flying on a broom to sabbaths at night. And I deem your efforts to discredit me as an attack on my honor! You'll take the consequences of that, be sure of it!

Another fabricated accusation against me? That's unbelievable... Someone must put a stop to that! No one may disparage my name, no repulsive heretic and Satan's minion! But I won't just sit watching it—I'm going to take care that there won't be any more of those foul charges!
Do you know Commander Ethien Pasque was charged with Heresy, Grand Duchess? He confessed he participated in the invocation of the fallen angel Baphomet...
Did Commander Ethien Pasque really confess to heresy? That's shocking... I wouldn't have ever thought something like that's possible. But why do you tell me, knight? What are you aiming for?
The Commander confessed during the questioning that it was you who allured him to partake in that mad plan, and that it was you who led the dark mass during which Baphomet was allegedly invoked!

That's absurd! That treacherous heretical knight has the nerve to accuse me of heresy?! How could he... I hope you don't believe that nonsense. I don't believe you, Grand Duchess. I think you're guilty and it's only a matter of time to get enough evidence against you!
Dietrich the Gravedigger confessed he obtained a dead body of a virgin from the city cemetery for you and that you paid him for it. What can you tell me about that?

I was to compound Dietrich the Gravedigger to get a corpse of a virgin?! What nonsense is that? Why would I do something like that? That's absurd! I have nothing to say about it. Of course it's a lie, a bald-faced lie. I don't know who paid the gravedigger to spread such allegations about me, but one thing is certain—it's all a lie!
Alright, I believe you.
I'm glad to hear that, knight. After all you're a sensible man—you just can't believe something like that.
I don't believe you, Grand Duchess. The testimony of Dietrich the Gravedigger is trustworthy. It's only a matter of time to get enough evidence against you!

Another accusation against me, knight? And this time it was brought by such a low-bred man as the gravedigger Dietrich? By such an indigent and a hobo? What nonsense is that? Why would I do something like that? That's absurd. I have nothing to say about it. Of course it's a lie, a bald-faced lie. I don't know who paid the gravedigger to spread such allegations about me, but one thing is certain—it's all a lie!

The murder of Monsignor Trevorius is a terrible disaster! I can't imagine anything more dreadful, knight! What's happening with this world that murderers aren't shy to lay hands even on the diocesan Bishop? Is it really the end of the world? Who could do such a thing? May God strike him with a lightning and may his soul burn in Hell...
I know something about the murder of Bishop Trevorius, knight. But I don't dare to utter it aloud...
You may speak openly, Grand Duchess.

Alright then. It's said that it is you who's somehow mixed in the murder of Bishop Trevorius. I don't believe that, but after the dreadful experience with my husband… I don't know who I should believe and who not!
I haven't anything to do with that murder!
Yes... surely you haven't. I believe you, knight. Who else should have my trust than a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous?
Try to find comfort in prayers, Grand Duchess.
Yes, you're right. Maybe I'll find in them the much-needed peace I lack so deeply in recent days. There are such terrible things going on...
Trust only God and his mercy.
Oh yes, you're right, knight. I have to trust firmly that God's providence will eventually put all in order. Thank you.
Do you happen to know anything about Priest Frederick?
I'm sorry, but I don't know Father Frederick. I don't remember ever meeting a priest by that name.

You can't even imagine, knight, what all we had to endure here in Glatzburg. A famine, a plague, a rain of fire, footpads, heresy... and to cap it all the undead have come and started to murder in the city streets after dark. It's terrible! You can't leave your house at night, and moreover, you can't even be sure the dead men won't force your door and rip you to pieces in your own bed. When is somebody going to do something about that? We can't let them murder reinlessly, can we?
I haven't heard that Hans Thomas Brookwelt would seize a woman against her will. In fact I haven't heard even that he would seize any WITH her content. So I can't confirm that suspicion in any way.

I know the servant maid of Baroness Helen von Hunt quite well—she accompanies her mistress during every visit to the city. She's not very beautiful girl and she seems to be quite gray, even sheepish. But that's no reason to suspect her of heresy. No, knight, that must be some mistake.

No, knight, I don't know a thing about the disappearance of Raquel Gielwitch. I've only heard that several other young girls have gone missing too. These are terrible days... I wish the things would change for the better soon. I can't wait to see that.
You're a distinguished woman, Grand Duchess, but I assure you it means nothing to me. If it's necessary, I'll force you to cooperate by VERY blunt ways!
Please, Grand Duchess, answer my question. It's really very important to me!
I'm sure a woman so beautiful and learned won't refuse to answer my question...
You have to worry no more, Grand Duchess.

I thank you once again, knight. I don't know what I'm going to do now, but I know my fate is in the hands of God. Perhaps it all can be explained somehow. If it showed that my husband is a heretic... God, what dark days have come upon us! And if I think that mere couple of years ago... I'm glad you've come to visit me. I didn't know whom to confess to. What are you going to do now? I mean with my husband. I fear to stay in his house!
If it shows he's guilty he'll stand before a court and answer for his deeds!
Oh God, it's a nightmare! I wish I could wake up and find out nothing of that has happened! I would give anything for that...
I'm really sorry, Grand Duchess. But the truth about your husband won't be uncovered until the case is fully investigated.
Yes, certainly... But even so it's horrible... I have to be strong!
May I ask you several questions, Grand Duchess?
But certainly, knight. It would be pleasure to answer all your questions. Ask away.
Farewell, Grand Duchess.
Goodbye, knight. If you're ever passing by be sure to visit me again!

Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, in spite of all you've just told me I arrest you on the basis of reasonable suspicion of heresy and of orchestrating a conspiracy against God and the King. You're coming with me!
I beg you pardon? Is it some sort of joke? I assure you, knight, I have no mood for such jesting now. You can't imagine what all I've gone through in recent days... I'd like to confess to you.
Do you want to confess to all crimes you're accused of?

What are you talking about, knight? What crimes should I confess to? Do you realize who you're talking to?! Your accusation—whatever it may concern—is ridiculous. Leave immediately or I'll have you removed by the guards!
Hardly so, Grand Duchess. I've come to arrest you and take you to prison where you'll wait during the course of investigation. Will you go with me voluntarily or will I have to force you?

How can you dare...?! You would lay your hands on the wife of a governor of the royal city? You... But you will regret it, I guarantee you! Alright, if you stick to your delusional charges, let's go. The sooner I see you in the prison instead of myself the better!
I'm very sorry, Grand Duchess, but within the scope of investigation I have to verify your accusation too. If it shows it's erroneous you'll be released immediately. But now please follow me.
As you wish, knight. But you'll regret it. You will, and terribly, I promise you that!
There's no time for that now. You're coming with me, Grand Duchess.
What are you talking about, knight?! I won't go anywhere with you. Do you know who I am?!
Yes, Grand Duchess, I'm aware of that. However I have enough evidence against you to arrest you. Please, come along, or I'll have to use force.
Stop talking, Grand Duchess. You're coming with me or else I'm going to drag you to prison unconscious and in chains!

Oh, knight, I must confide to you immediately! I can't be silent about it any more! Such horror! Please, hear me out!
First tell me who you are, good woman.
Oh, I'm sorry, I forgot my manners. I'm Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, the wife of Grand Duke Robert Heidrick, the royal governor of the city and a liege of His Majesty King Edward II.
I'm honored to meet you, Grand Duchess. Now tell me what's on your heart.

I... haven't known what to do for a long time, knight. The sacrament of marriage is inviolable for me and I know I should honor and love my husband. But that what I've witnessed... The faith lead us above all to the obedience to our Lord, doesn't it?!
Exactly. Tell me then what's the matter. What did you witness?

But in time it started to be suspicious. He secretly disappeared from our house at nights and returned only before the dawn. When I sometimes asked him where he was he denied it all or came with some yarn. As a jealous woman I gathered from it he has a lover! I know I shouldn't do that, but I had to find out who she was. I secretly searched his belongings, looked into his study and checked contents of his pockets. I had to find some proof!
And did you find any?

No, knight. In fact yes, but not the one I was looking for. Once when my husband was in his study writing something he was all of a sudden called away to some important matter. He left the unfinished letter in his study, which he locked properly, not knowing I had secretly made a copy of the key. I entered the study and read the letter. Then I thought I would turn into a pillar of salt!
Really? What was in the letter?

My husband, whom I always deemed an incorrupt man of high morals, wrote in the letter about the preparation of some monstrous act that was to happen soon and that consisted of invoking, God forgive me, one of the three fallen angels to the world!
Who was the letter addressed to?

It was intended for, what a horror, knight Benthley of Welshrem. Yes, for that wanted murderer and a dreaded footpad who has probably all the mortal sins that the Holy Scriptures speaks of on his conscience!
Are you sure it was really your husband who wrote the letter? Couldn't somebody have slipped it there secretly?
Hardly, knight. It was written by his hand and the ink was still wet. After all, you may see for yourself. I have the letter here.
Well... really odd.
Yes, knight, it really is. I hope you understand my fear and my concerns. And I hope God will forgive me my faults because I have sinned against the sacrament of marriage.
Yes, he surely will forgive you. You atone for your sins by telling me about them.
Do you think so, knight? I've been agonizing so much...
If your soul feels guilty, pray ten times to Saint Paulius. All your sins and faults will be forgiven then.
Your sin is a grave one, Grand Duchess. To free yourself of guilt you'll have to donate to the Brotherhood of the Righteous—that is, to me—2,000 gp. for the fight with crime.
Certainly, knight. I'll readily pay if justice asks it. Here is the gold. I'm glad I'm going to be free of the qualm at last. I've been agonizing so much...
Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick, I arrest you on the basis of reasonable suspicion of heresy and of orchestrating of a conspiracy against God and the King. You're coming with me!
Welcome, knight. I'm so glad to see you again. You're bringing at least a little ray of hope into my sorrowful life. What can I do for you?
I'd like to talk with you for a moment, Grand Duchess.
I'll gladly answer all your questions, knight.
Nothing this time, Grand Duchess. I've been just passing by.
It was nice to see you, knight. Farewell. May the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you!

I beg you pardon? Is it some sort of joke? I assure you, sir, I have no mood for such jesting now. You can't imagine what all I've gone through in recent days... I'd like to confess to you.

What are you talking about, sir? What crimes should I confess to? Do you realize who you're talking to?! Your accusation—whatever it may concern—is ridiculous. Leave immediately or I'll have you removed by the guards!
As you wish, sir. But you'll regret it. You will, and terribly, I promise you that!
What are you talking about, sir?! I won't go anywhere with you. Do you know who I am?!
Oh sir, I must confide to you immediately! I can't be silent about it any more! Such horror! Please, hear me out!

I... haven't known what to do for a long time, sir. The sacrament of marriage is inviolable for me and I know I should honor and love my husband. But that what I've witnessed... The faith lead us above all to the obedience to our Lord, doesn't it?!

No, sir. In fact yes, but not the one I was looking for. Once when my husband was in his study writing something he was all of a sudden called away to some important matter. He left the unfinished letter in his study, which he locked properly, not knowing I had secretly made a copy of the key. I entered the study and read the letter. Then I thought I would turn into a pillar of salt!
Hardly, sir. It was written by his hand and the ink was still wet. After all, you may see for yourself. I have the letter here.
Yes, sir, it really is. I hope you understand my fear and my concerns. And I hope God will forgive me my faults because I have sinned against the sacrament of marriage.
Yes, he surely will forgive you, Grand Duchess. You atone for your sins by telling me about them.
Do you think so, sir? I've been agonizing so much...
If your soul feels guilty, pray ten times to Saint Baudolinus—he has a soft spot for sinners.
Your sin is a grave one, Grand Duchess. To free yourself of guilt you'll have to donate an exceptional tax in an amount of 2,000 gp. to the treasury of the Realm—that is, to me...
Certainly, sir. I'll readily pay if the Realm asks it. Here is the gold. I'm glad I'll be free of the qualm at last. I've been agonizing so much...
Welcome, sir. I'm so glad to see you again. You're bringing at least a little ray of hope into my sorrowful life. What can I do for you?
I'll gladly answer all your questions, sir.
It was nice to see you, sir. Farewell. May the Archangel Gabriel himself protect you!
What?! What are you talking about?!
I'm saying I've been awaiting you to prematurely rid the world of you. So if I may, let's proceed with the business...
Why do you want to kill me? We even don't know one another...
That doesn't matter, knight. I've got paid for sending you directly to Hell and I'm gonna do just that. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
Hold you horses! I'll pay you if you let me go!
I've already got paid for dispatching you. And frankly, I would really hate to disobey my boss. So I'm sorry, knight. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
It's suicide to attack a paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. If you really want to leave this world, I'll gladly help you find the way!
We will see!!
You're here at last, knight. I started to fear I won't live to see you coming...
Who are you, good man. I don't think we have a meeting arranged.
That's true. But I think you're gonna pay attention to me. Because there's your life at stake!
Don't bother me, you villain. I've much to do.
No chance, knight. I've been waiting for you here for quite a while and I'm not in the mood for squabbling. So pay attention to me—after all it's your life that's at stake!
That doesn't matter, Father. I've got paid for sending you directly to Hell and I'm gonna do just that. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
I've already got paid for dispatching you. And frankly, I would really hate to disobey my boss. So I'm sorry, Father. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
God sees your deeds and his wrath is great. I'll pay you back in the same coin. I'm going to punish you for your sins!
You're here at last, Father. I started to fear I won't live to see you coming...
No chance, Father. I've been waiting for you here for quite a while and I'm not in the mood for squabbling. So pay attention to me—after all it's your life that's at stake!
That doesn't matter, noble sir. I've got paid for sending you directly to Hell and I'm gonna do just that. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
I've already got paid for dispatching you. And frankly, I would really hate to disobey my boss. So I'm sorry, noble sir. Pleasant journey to the Other World!
No common villain will attack a noble! I'll have to teach you how to behave, you scoundrel!
You're here at last, noble sir. I started to fear I won't live to see you coming...
No chance, noble sir. I've been waiting for you here for quite a while and I'm not in the mood for squabbling. So pay attention to me—after all it's your life that's at stake!
Nothing important, knight—only to kill ya! Give my best regards in Hell!!
Knight, can you spare a moment? I need to talk with you...
Sure, what do you need, good man?
I'm sorry, I have no time. Farewell.
That's a load of cobblers, knight. You're gonna stay here 'till I'm finished with you!
And what is it you need, good man?!
Nothing important, only to kill ya! Give my best regards in Hell!!
Father, can you spare a moment? I need to talk with you...
That's a load of cobblers, Father. You're gonna stay here 'till I'm finished with you!
Nothing important, noble lord—only to kill ya! Give my best regards in Hell!!
Noble lord, can you spare a moment? I need to talk with you...
That's a load of cobblers, noble lord. Ya gonna stay here 'till I'm finished with you!
I hope ya already managed to do a good turn today, knight.
Because ya won't have time for that any more. I'm gonna kill ya!
I hope ya already said your prayers today, Father.
Because ya won't have no time for that any more. I'm gonna kill ya!
I hope ya have already managed to levy all taxes today, noble lord.
In that case give my best regards there—'cause this is your last moment in the world of living. I'm gonna kill ya!
Where do you think yer gonna go after ya die? To Hell or to Heaven?
Naturally to Heaven, I'm a humble knight of God!
Probably to Hell, I have killed several people in a fit of anger because they asked wrong questions, if you get my point...
Naturally to Heaven—I'm a humble servant of God!
Probably to Hell—my soul isn't free of mortal sins...
Naturally to Heaven—I live in accordance with the Holy Scriptures!
Probably to Hell—that's for all those taxes...

You're lying! This is a fake, a false scroll to confuse me, put me off! But you won't succeed—I'll get the real scroll! Kill him, my faithful! May the Elenian Gods rise and dance in the eternal pagan night!
So you won't surrender the scroll to me?! In that case the wrath of Elenian Gods will strike you! Kill him, my faithful! May the Elenian Gods rise and dance in the eternal pagan night!
Juhasz Gotherr alias Zan'Drem, I arrest you on suspicion of heresy. You'll go with me to appear before a just court!
No, I'm not going with you anywhere, knight. I just want the scroll. Give it to me and you may leave. Refuse and the Elenian Gods will punish you severely!
The scroll isn't what you're looking for. Actually, it's a mere shopping list of some long-dead Elenian merchant. It is no prophecy nor anything similar...

You think you can deceive me, knight? I know very well how slimy you paladins can be, when it comes to words! No, you won't delude me! I know what's in the scroll and no lies will prevent me from getting hold of it!
You are mistaken—the scroll isn't what you're looking for. See for yourself what's in it—three threescores of nuts, five cubits of fabric, six carafes of wine...
If you think so... I was just trying to bring into light the fallacies you believe so blindly. Now you'll come with me to appear before a just court!
Enough words, you're coming with me!

Halt, knight! In the name of the prophet Son'Traedamus I ask you to give me voluntarily the scroll you hold and that was given to you by a man named Alberto Kelley! Surrender the scroll to me and you may leave in peace. Refuse and the Elenian Gods will strike you with their wrath!
Who are you?!

I am Zan'Drem, the High Priest of the Cult of the Pagan Night. The scroll you hold is a relic the appearance of which our Cult has been awaiting for millennia! It is the genuine text of the Son'Traedamus's prophecy, according to which the Elenian Gods will soon rise again and they will dance in the night forever...
What abhorrent heresy is this?!

It is no heresy at all! It is an ancient prophecy which will soon gain fulfillment. You will see before your very eyes the decline of your civilization and the Elenian Gods walking the world in an eternal night dancing to the sounds of their pipes! That's how Son'Traedamus spoke! But now give me the scroll!
I'll hand the scroll over to you, but I want some money for it...
The deputy of the Elenian Gods is not to be haggled with, knight! Give me the scroll!
All right, I'll give you the scroll. Here it is...

Excellent! After so many years of seeking the original ancient Son'Traedamus's prophecy fell finally into my hands! Listen, what Son'Traedamus said—three threescores of nuts, five cubits of fabric, six carafes of wine... What? What abominable fake is this?!
It is no fake, but the real content of the respective scroll. It is a shopping list of some long-dead Elenian merchant...
Sorry, but you'll NEVER get the scroll!
In that case I'll take it myself! Kill him, my faithful! May the Elenian Gods rise and dance in the eternal pagan night!
Is this an attack?!

Yes, strictly speaking, yes. But nothing will happen to you if you hand the scroll you hold over to me. It's a relic the appearance of which our Cult has been awaiting for millennia! It is the genuine text of the Son'Traedamus's prophecy, according to which the Elenian Gods will soon rise again and they will dance in the night forever...
Son'Traedamus the Prophet? I've never heard of him...

No wonder... You paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous care only for your petty missions and forget that you're just a grain of sand in the ocean of time. You forget there were civilizations that overtook yours by several classes. And though it may seem they are irretrievably gone, it isn't true. Be aware that thousands of years ago the Elenian prophet Son'Traedamus predicted the fall of the Elenian Gods in the struggle with human population, but they'll be brought back to life again and they will dance in the night for eternity! And now give me the scroll, knight!
No, I'm not going with you anywhere, Father. I just want the scroll. Give it to me and you may leave. Refuse and the Elenian Gods will punish you severely!

You think you can deceive me, Father? I know very well how slimy you orthodox priests can be, when it comes to words! No, you won't delude me! I know what's in the scroll and no lies will prevent me from getting hold of it!

The deputy of the Elenian Gods is not to be haggled with, Father! Give me the scroll!

No wonder... You orthodox priests care only for your twelve prophets and forget that your 'True faith'—as you haughtily call it—is just a grain of sand in the ocean of time. You forget there were civilizations that overtook yours by several classes. And though it may seem they are irretrievably gone, it isn't true. Be aware that thousands of years ago the Elenian prophet Son'Traedamus predicted the fall of the Elenian Gods in the struggle with human population, but they'll be brought back to life again and they will dance in the night for eternity! And now give me the scroll, Father!
No, I'm not going with you anywhere, sir. I just want the scroll. Give it to me and you may leave. Refuse and the Elenian Gods will punish you severely!

You think you can deceive me, sir? I know very well how slimy you nobles can be, when it comes to words! No, you won't delude me! I know what's in the scroll and no lies will prevent me from getting hold of it!

Halt, sir! In the name of the prophet Son'Traedamus I ask you to give me voluntarily the scroll you hold and that was given to you by a man named Alberto Kelley! Surrender the scroll to me and you may leave in peace. Refuse and the Elenian Gods will strike you with their wrath!
The deputy of the Elenian Gods is not to be haggled with, sir! Give me the scroll!

No wonder... You nobles care only for your domains and forget that you're just a grain of sand in the ocean of time. You forget there were civilizations that overtook yours by several classes. And though it may seem they are irretrievably gone, it isn't true. Be aware that thousands of years ago the Elenian prophet Son'Traedamus predicted the fall of the Elenian Gods in the struggle with human population, but they'll be brought back to life again and they will dance in the night for eternity! And now give me the scroll, sir!

Zzzaaarrrggghhh! Who dared to enter our sanctuary?! Who desecrated our holy place with his presence?! Chief Zargh commands that he is immediately killed and his entrails laid on the altar of the Cursed Flame!
Who are you, hellspawn?! What sort of right entitles you to dwell in the Kingdom of God on Earth?!

I am Chief Zargh, the liege of the Cursed Flame. My race of lizards is ready to join the Legions of Death as soon as they leave the Kingdom of Destruction. And you dared to defile our sanctuary with your presence. Chief Zargh commands you to be instantly killed! Kill him, my faithful!
I came to punish this abhorrent Satan's breed for the sins committed against God Almighty. Die, monster!
Chief Zargh is laughing at you, worm! You're standing in the sanctuary of the Cursed Flame—you have no power here. Kill him, my faithful!
We'll see!
I am sorry, I didn't mean to bother you. I'll come later. Farewell!
You are laughing at Chief Zargh, the liege of the Cursed Flame?! What impudence! Before you die, you'll taste the infinity of pain! Grasp him, my faithful!
It seems that this grave was desecrated. Someone dug up the coffin and stole the dead body from it.
I should take a look to see if there are any traces here...

It seems that this grave has been robbed recently... It's possible that the criminals I promised Brother Augustin to apprehend have this on their conscience. I should take a look around here, if there are any traces...
Hmm... as for the traces—the soil around the grave is stamped with many footprints. And the soil seems unusually clayey here... unlike the rest of the cemetery or anywhere near Alvaron.
It means that if the Lord is with me, I will find out who exactly has this clay on his shoes, it will be obvious evidence of his complicity in this crime!
My Lord, what kind of heretic could have committed such a heinous crime like the violation of this grave?! For what ungodly purposes did he need the body that was buried here?!
I should take a look around here if there are any traces that could lead to the revelation of the perpetrator of this disgusting sacrilege!

My Lord, what kind of heretic could have committed such a heinous crime like the violation of this grave?! If I am not mistaken, here exactly had been buried Baroness Gwenn von Weill, before her body was stolen.

If I am not mistaken, here exactly had been buried Baroness Gwenn von Weill, before her body was stolen by Baroness Linda van Gallagan and her accomplices. A terrible case of heresy! How far the human madness can go?!
I should take a look around here if there are any traces that could lead to the conviction of Baroness Linda van Gallagan's accomplices!
It seems that the broken blade I found here was used to pry open the coffin lid in this violated grave... Yes, there's no doubt about it!

It seems that the broken blade I found here matches the handle of the dagger said by Ruphert the shepherd to belong to Judge Vallarian. It was used to pry open the coffin lid in this violated grave... Yes, there's no doubt about it!

Amethysts are rich, purple colored gems belonging to the quartz family of minerals. In the past, Amethysts were believed to possess certain magical properties. Now, however, they are used mainly as sobriety charms.
Amethyst
This silver amulet sports an image of Saint Gustaph giving alms to the poor. Though the amulet itself is not of fine make, the quality of the carving is exquisite.
Braham's Silver Amulet

This beautiful amulet would prove a suitable addition to any noble lord or lady's collection, were it not for a single, yet quite considerable, flaw; anyone who places the amulet around his or her neck is immediately stricken with murderous rage. Though none could say for sure, it is likely that the amulet dates back to the ancient Erebornian empire. The pagans of Ereborn were quite fond of such trinkets.
Cursed Amulet of Murderous Rage

It is clear from the engraving in this magnificent weapon's hilt that it belongs to none other than Master Edmond d'Arvias. This is a sword without equal. The blade itself, while richly ornamented, is perfectly balanced and sharper than a courtesan's wit. Upon second glance, however, you notice something rather... perturbing. The symbols etched into this weapon's blade are remarkable, but they do not resemble the typical markings found on a brother paladin's sword. Why would that be?
Master Edmond d'Arvias's sword
There is nothing at all remarkable about this boulder. It is largely made of stone—as one would expect—and likely contains traces of iron ore.
Boulder

Betheal Temporarum is a precious herb once used by the ancient Elenians to brew magnificent potions. Though many of the complex formulae which made use of this particular herb were lost when the Elenian civilization fell, a handful of recipes have survived the test of time. Subsequently, these discoveries have led to the brewing of a wide array of potions which mainly affect the physiology of the human body. It is safe to say, then, that the handling of Betheal Temporarum is best left to trained alchemists.
Betheal Temporarum

The battle axe is a unique variety of combat axe designed with two—usually symmetrical—killing edges and a single, top-mounted bayonet. Most battle axes are between a meter and a meter-and-a-half in length. The battle axe is believed to have originated from a more primitive weapon used by the sub-human Thron species, who once inhabited the depths below the Moonshine Mountains.\\n\\nThough deadly, the battle axe has never become a piece of standard-issue equipment, due mainly to the difficulty troops experience when attempting to use the weapon, which requires a great deal of space to be effective, in the tight confines of formal battle lines. From time to time, it is employed by mercenaries and executioners in the place of the two-handed sword, which handles in much the same way but requires a much smaller swing-arc to be used effectively.
Battle Axe

The stiletto is a much lighter variant of the standard-issue dagger with an extremely specialized purpose. The main difference between the two weapons lies in the unique shape of the stiletto's blade. The edge of a stiletto is usually symmetrical and is used primarily for piercing, rather than slashing.\\n\\nDue to its specialized nature, it is safe to assume that the use of the dagger far predates the invention of the stiletto, which was developed to puncture the protective clothing of modern combatants. Used mainly by infantry in close quarters, the stiletto is the perfect weapon for executing a knight pulled from his steed. Designed to kill quickly and efficiently, the stiletto is capable of puncturing everything from the softest leather to the sturdiest plate.
Stiletto

Though combat staves are as deadly as a properly wielded blade in the right hands, they are used primarily for training. In fact many travelers use combat staves in place of walking sticks due to the dependability of their make. While not used often by infantrymen, members of the clergy and nobility prefer them to other less elegant weapons. While most combat staves are carved from sturdy wood and reinforced with metal braces, the staves of messengers are often hollow and can be used to smuggle secret documents and valuables through hostile territories.
Combat Staff

Combat axe is a catch-all term for any battle-worthy weapon with a flat, curved blade set into a haft, rather than a hilt. While standard-issue axes have always been the weapon of choice for infantry and local militia, knights and lords often prefer using larger, more elegant blades.\\n\\nWhile certainly not the most graceful instrument of death, the combat axe trumps most other weapons on the battlefield in terms of shear versatility. Well-made axes can be used to execute both slashing and crushing attacks, and as such, are more useful than swords for shattering limbs and breaking armor. While wonderful offensive tools, axes are less favorable than swords in close-quarters combat due their relative inability to parry incoming attacks. Still, when the thirst for blood outweighs the need for safety, hearty warriors will find few friends more reliable than a well-made axe.

As any peasant soldier campaigning in winter will tell you, boots are an invaluable piece of equipment. Though a standard pair of leather traveling boots will serve the needs of most adventurers, those willing to spend extra coin will find that added protection in the form of plated heels, toes, and shinguards can make all the difference in battle.
Boots

Black pearls are a rare form of pearl, made from calcium carbonate deposited within the shell of the Pinctada Margaritifera breed of oyster. Pinctada Margaritifera are native to the seas that surround the pagan empire Jad-Habaal, and are highly sought after by the faithful for their rarity and brilliant shine.
Black Pearl

”Devil's Root” is the colloquial term for the roots of the Radix Diaboli herb, renowned throughout the Orthodox world for its ability to permanently alter the human mind and body. The name “Devil’s Root” is derived not from any negative side effect of ingesting the root, but from the Radix Diaboli herb’s appearance itself—that of a horned, grinning devil. Though trained alchemists are capable of producing potions with miraculous effects from Devil’s Root extract, even novices can produce rudimentary healing salves just by grinding or squeezing the root into a paste.
Devil's Root

This appears to be the diary of Father Frederick. Though you feel a twinge of guilt at the thought of reading another man’s private thoughts, you proceed to thumb through the pages until something of interest catches your eye. It seems that Father Frederick was capable of performing the rite of exorcism: The rite which allows an arbiter of the True Faith to force demons out of the bodies of the faithful. In one of the entries, Father Frederick details an exorcism of particular note:\\n\\nBless me, Heavenly Father, for I have seen the devil’s face. Today, I encountered the dread demon, Beelzebub, living in the flesh of a young girl. From the child’s innocent lips, he spat profanities like skipping stones and besmirched the name of God in ways that made my very soul tremble. Nevertheless, I held my ground and held the beast’s gaze, for I carry the Revelation of the Divine Mercy in my heart. With the Holy Scriptures in hand, I hung my rosary around my neck and sprinkled the body of the innocent girl with Mandrake Root broth, which turned the devil red with anger. The fiend screamed and cursed my name, but, alas, he could not best me. Three times did he try to tear the Scripture from my hands, and three times in vain. After I doused him with Holy Water for a third time, he fled back to the depths of Hell, leaving the girl’s tormented soul free at last. The entry ends with Father Frederick recounting a rather peculiar incident involving a set of stairs which took place shortly after the exorcism. What a strange, strange man.
Father Frederick's Diary

After reading but a handful of entries, there can be no doubt that the author of this diary—the soldier Harph—is not only a madman, but also a heretic and a traitor to his fellow man. How else could one describe the fiend behind the undead plague afflicting Glatzburg? One passage in particular details Harph’s madness in the fullest:\\n\\nToday, with His blessing, I raised the Gerswood family from their eternal slumber—father, mother, and three sons. They were taken by the plague two years ago, and there was very little left of their bodies, but their bones were well enough intact to fill with unholy life. Now they’ve joined the rest of my pawns, fetching whatever I wish from the corpses of the fallen. The true beauty of the cycle is that every fool slain eventually finds his way into my army of the damned, taking to the streets from their graves at my command! Yes... beautiful. Never will I forget to whom I owe every ounce of this decadence—every morsel of tender flesh and every drop of chilled wine. Without His love, I would still be wasting away, a slave to the fool king, Edward. Hail Satan, my new lord and master; do with this wicked soul as you please, Dark Prince, and fill my cup forevermore!
Soldier Harph's Diary

This is obviously the diary of Duke Rowan van Leerin, as it was found on his person during his arrest. And, as if that were not proof enough, there is also an inscription scrawled hastily on the diary’s first page: “If found, please return this diary... erm... this JOURNAL to Duke Rowan van Leerin. No, seriously. Please.”\\n\\nAccording to van Leerin’s diary, the fool attempted to give life to a statue of King Edward II in hopes of overthrowing the true king and having his creation rule in the man’s stead! Apparently, he needed the blood of at least three girls in order for the ritual to succeed. To this end, he had his lackey, Alphonso DiCerbio, bring the girls to him. Who could have imagined a fellow with such feminine handwriting (a fellow who kept a diary, no less!) would be capable of committing such a heinous crime? I’ll be sure to keep a note of van Leerin’s treachery in my... erm... journal. For future reference, of course.
Duke van Leerin's Diary

As the old saying goes, every kiss begins with Ka—Er... rather, ‘diamonds are forever.’ And forever, as any loose-moraled heathen in confession will tell you, is a very, very long time. Sometimes referred to as God’s Tears, the Holy Mother Church teaches that diamonds were formed as our Lord mourned the betrayal of Satan—his most faithful archangel. Our Lord’s tears fell for days and days, scattering themselves across the Earth so that the faithful might one day find them and be reminded of the evil that nearly unmade us all. The Royal Alchemist Lorenzzo Graffiti challenged this opinion in 1145, claiming that diamonds were merely a form of the mineral “graphite” which had been exposed to tremendous amounts of both heat and pressure over centuries. The poor sod was tried and burned at the stake for heresy that same year. To think: Graphite! What utter nonsense.
Diamond

The modern lance is a simple, yet elegant, weapon consisting of a gradually thinning wooden shaft tipped with an iron head. Lances themselves, however, are as old as time itself, with the earliest references to mounted lancers dating back to the Erebornian Empire. Once the weapon of choice for pagan leaders, the lance was also greatly favored by kings and noblemen alike for the power and majesty they conveyed to loyal troops.n\\nThough pagan warriors often used lances in the same way that modern infantrymen use spears, as the weapons became more and more readily available to civilized cavalrymen, the modern style of “lancing” came into being; that is, the concept of using the lance itself to direct the force of a mounted rider and his horse into a single, devastating blow. At more than two meters long, the lance proves a deadly weapon even when broken.
Lance

The bow has been a staple of warfare since the first savage discovered that a taut string could sling sticks. There is evidence of the bow having been used as far back as the founding of the Erebornian Republic. The Erebornians themselves were believed to have created the first versions of the standard bow, while the subhuman Elenians are credited with the discovery of reflex, or composite, bows. The warriors of the Jad-Habaal empire, on the other hand, were said to have created the first ‘shortbows,’ which were easier for their mounted archers to use on the fly. Regardless of who created them or how they’re used, one thing is certain: The sight of bows on the battlefield is as common as piss, blood, and fear.\\n\\nBows are often made of hard, flexible woods such as yew, elm, or rowan. Well made bows bend, even at the grip, just enough to allow the maximum amount of tension to build along the drawstring; poorly crafted bows, however, bend too much along their grips, creating a great deal of recoil which can drastically affect an archer’s aim. A common mistake among idiots using the bow for the first time is to hold the grip near the body while nocking an arrow to the drawstring, which is most often pointed in general direction of the enemy. Though not terribly effective, this tactic has been used time and time again by drunkards, fools, and the sons of haughty Glatzburgian noblemen.
Long Bow

The standard longsword is the bread and butter weapon of modern infantry and cavalry alike. Aside from its obvious worth as killing utensil, the longsword is also valued as a symbol of the true faith, due to its resemblance to the cross upon which the First Prophet was crucified. While favored greatly by commoners over the axe and the mace due to its relatively versatility, the longsword has long been the symbol of noble-birth as well; in fact, many noble houses possess a single, finely-crafted blade which is passed from father to eldest son at the dawning of each new generation.n\\nAs varied as the men who wield them, longswords are as much symbols of status and worth as they are dangerously efficient weapons. Though the size and shape of blades vary widely from one sword to the next, most are roughly a meter in length. While much can be determined from the shape of a sword’s edge or the carving of its pommel and guard, much more can be learned from the way a man carries his blade. Even in the wrong hands, a well-made longsword is as deadly as any case of the flux; in the right hands, however, even mass-produced slag-iron blades can fell strong men like withered saplings.
Long Sword

Making note of the richly embellished handwriting, it is clear to you that the author of this letter is likely a man of sophistication. The letter reads:\\n\\nMy son,\\n\\nBe wary of who you trust in Glatzburg. The wolf wears the lamb’s skin, and waits with bared fangs! Beware the clergy especially; I fear their bleating grows nearer to growling with every passing hour.\\n\\nSincerely,\\nA Friend.
Letter of Warning

This letter is addressed to Cardinal Gustapho Letti, from Christoffer de Malamert, Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. The Grand Master is asking his friend to grant me the utmost possible assistance in the search for the Children of the New Order:\\n\\nDear Gustapho,\\nIt seems that the Archangel Gabriel keeps watch over us still, for he has sent us a blessing in our darkest hour. Though the gift is but one man, his knowledge and expertise will prove invaluable in our—as of yet fruitless—search for the order of heretics currently plaguing our Realm. Please grant him your full support, and use the services he provides to their full potential so that we might free ourselves from the lingering shadow of evil that much sooner.\\nEver Your Faithful Servant,\\nChristoffer
Letter for Cardinal Gustapho Letti

This is Edmond d'Arvias's letter to Bishop Trevorius in Glatzburg. It reads:\\n\\nDear friend,\\nI sincerely hope you receive this letter in kind health and fair circumstance, despite the evils plaguing us all. I would trouble you, Trevorius, to aid the bearer of this letter with an investigation of the utmost importance. Though I tremble to write the words which follow, I fear even more your disbelieving them, old friend. There has been a conspiracy in Hillbrandt to invoke the fallen angel, Arthamon—a conspiracy, I fear, which has likely succeeded. What makes the case all the more troubling is that Bishop Vallarian, who you know well from the Inquisitorial Curia of Glatzburg, has been convicted of the crime.\\nAs you can see, this is no petty case of hearsay heresy. Though the betrayal of an inquisitorial judge frightens me to no end, Trevorius, certain truths which have come to light bring a chill to my very soul. Though it may only be the rambling of a doomed man, Judge Vallarian left a warning for the bearer of this letter; the Children of the New Order, of which you certainly know more than I, walk the Earth again.\\nI would ask you to afford the bearer of this letter all possible assistance with his investigation, and to help him discover the truth behind Judge Vallarian’s betrayal. I fear more than my peace of mind hangs in the balance, old friend.\\nEver Yours, Edmond
Letter to Bishop Trevorius

This letter simply reads:\\n\\nKill him, he knows too much.\\n\\nT.\\n\\I must uncover the true identity of this “T” as quickly as possible. I pity the fool who dares come between me and my investigation.
Assassin's Letter

These letters are addressed to Glatzburg's Curial Inquisitor, Truncquillius, from an unidentified heretic in Alvaron. One of them reads:\\n\\nMy dearest,\\nNow is the time. The rooks are rising, and the dragon has laid her golden egg. The time has come to throw open the floodgates and let the dark currents wash over the towns and the cities of Ultherst. You know your duty. The book which was lost and found again states your purpose. The search has come to an end, and with it, the Kingdom of God on the Earth. Prepare yourself for the unlocking, and hurry, for the shadows of the past nip at our heels, even as the noose slips ‘round their necks.\\n\\nThe Fisher
Incriminating Heretical Letters

The first recorded use of chain mail comes from the earliest days of the Erebornian empire. However, it is now believed that the people of Ereborn first learned the craft of making chain mail from the pagans of Jad-Habaal. After the downfall of the Ereborn, for a time, the craft was thought lost, but a handful of armories scattered throughout the faithful world retained the secret to forging and linking chain rings.
