The process of forging chain mail has since spread to the rest of the faithful world, where it is now mass produced for the first time since the fall of the pagan kingdoms.\\n\\nThe production of chain mail is an extremely demanding process. Due to the intense level of skill and attention to detail needed to forge chain mail, a full suit is often very expensive. Highly sought after by heavy infantry and cavalry alike, chain mail is only now becoming a common addition to the modern warrior’s arsenal.\\n\\nThe earliest incarnations of chain mail were essentially metal “dresses” which draped to the wearer’s knees in order to protect the torso and the soft flesh of the thighs. As plate leg guards became more and more common, the length of chain mail shortened. Though most knights prefer a steady helm of plate, for extra coin, suits of mail can be specially crafted with chain hoods for added protection.
Chain Mail

Thorn apples are a type of magical herb used often, and only, for the spreading of mischief. Thorn apple clouds the mind, causes hallucinations and brings about mad visions of the future. These effects can be induced by inhaling, eating, or applying the herb to one’s body in the form of a cream. All of these methods are forbidden by the Holy Mother Church, and no one seems to know just how ten barrels of thorn apple wound up in the cellars of the Bishop’s palace in Glatzburg.
Thorn Apple

Double blades are curious weapons, scarcely recognized and infrequently used by warriors of the faithful world. As the name suggests, double blades are swords forged with two edges each set into either side of a single hilt.\\n\\nThe double blade was first introduced to the faithful world after the crusades, suggesting that the pagans of Jad-Habaal made use of double blades in the ninth or tenth centuries. Among the faithful, the double blade has become the accepted weapon of journeymen, adventurers, and landsknects who often come into contact with the desert pagans. The double blade has also become the favored weapon of the brother paladins of the Order of the Holy Cross, who protect the Divine Grave from the pagan dogs.
Double Blade

The double=bladed axe is a rather rare variant of the standard combat axe, believed to have been created by the subhuman Thron, who once lived beneath the Moonshine Mountains. The weapon consists of a single meter long shaft bedecked with two symmetrical blades. The mere sight of a double-bladed axe strikes fear into the hearts of those who have not yet committed themselves to dying a bloody death.
Double-bladed Axe

The dagger is an ancient and time-honored weapon, first developed when our oldest ancestors fashioned sharpened stones into blades to kill their prey. Formed by fastening a symmetrical blade to a short, stocky hilt, daggers are most effective when used as piercing weapons. Though entirely different from the standard knife in terms of use and purpose, the first recorded differentiation between the two weapons came from the chronicler, Hermann, who described the dagger with the Old Latern “sica,” meaning “piercer,” rather than the more common “culter,” which roughly translates to “slashing blade.”
Dagger

This is the hilt of a once magnificent dagger. The craftsmanship... the intricate carving and the fine forgework; this was clearly, at one time, a very expensive weapon. Jagged edges at the base of the dagger suggest the blade was snapped, but why? Why would someone destroy such a beautiful weapon?\\n\\nRupert, the shepherd, found the hilt at the municipal garbage heap near the gates of Hillbrandt. The shepherd thinks Judge Vallarian discarded it there as he was returning to the town in the morning. How would Vallarian have broken his dagger, and more importantly, what was he doing outside the town’s walls after dark? Curious... very curious.
Magnificent broken dagger

Judging from the workmanship, this blade once belonged to an exquisite dagger. Though the steel is of a fine make, the edge of the blade is jagged, suggesting that it was likely snapped under terrible duress. The open grave and empty coffin nearby seem to legitimize this theory. But why would someone use such a dagger for the sole purpose of desecrating a grave... and who could possibly afford to waste what was clearly, at one time, such an expensive weapon?
Magnificent dagger blade

I received this scroll, containing a full translation of the ancient Elenian language, from the seer, Enrie Jungwirdt. With it, I should be able to find the tomb of the pagan noble, Fae'Darlion. The Elenian “alphabet,” if it could be called as such, is wildly different from any human language I’ve ever seen. Compared with the Moon Runes—The Elenian name for their own beautiful script—the writing of the faithful seems... primitive. Clumsy, even. In the interest of self-preservation, I would do well to keep that opinion to myself.
Elenian Script Transcription

This letter, from Grand Duke Heidrick to Benthley of Welshrem, reads:\\n\\nBrother!\\nThe hour of the wolf has come, it is time to get ready. Let the Blood Moon rise, the thunder roar and the lightning strike from the clear sky. Prepare the blood feast, the black mass and the Sabbath of the loyal where we shall dance around our idol and bow to our new lord who will finally come to us! Hurry for the time has come!\\nRobert
Grand Duke Heidrick's letter

This mountain crystal flask is filled with the blood of a member of the Highest Inquisitional Tribunal—his name is Giovanni Timore. If I should succeed in the task I was given and remove the curse from the terrible stryx that lives in the municipal cemetery, I must make poor Joan drink the flask. Only her father's blood can remove the horrible family curse from her. Raphael, watch over me... I cannot believe what I am doing.
Flask of blood

This flask contains an extremely precious substance—an oil blessed by Pope Almod the Second, the Miraculous. Almod the Miraculous was considered the mortal embodiment of the Holy Spirit by many of the faithful due in large part to his wondrous healing abilities. Some say Almod blessed this oil himself before his passing, leaving behind not only an enduring legacy but also a potion of healing capable of removing even the foulest of human maladies. Simply holding the flask, I feel safer. May Almod shed his mercy over me, and as he did this oil so long ago, so bless and guide me through my sojourn into the heart of darkness.
Flask of Blessed Oil

Garnets are gems of a deep crimson color which are said to bring health, strength and a “rosy” disposition to those who wear them. Perhaps that is why individuals with garnets in their treasuries are healthier, stronger and often happier than those too poor to afford them. For some inexplicable reason, garnets can only be found in the Realm and nowhere else. As such, the garnet has become something of a state jewel. The largest garnets ever discovered are now included among the crown jewels. They are called simply “the Crimson Eyes,” due in large part to their size and in part to the eerie nature of the gems. Some report feeling the sensation of being watched while in their presence.
Garnet

Halberds are a relatively new addition to the arsenal of men. Introduced to standard infantry near the end of the Hundred Years War, the halberd is a piercing/slashing polearm weapon. The word halberd is derived from the Erstwick word “halm,” meaning pole, and “barte,” meaning axe. Used primarily by infantrymen, halberds fill an interesting niche between the more defensive pike and the hyper-aggressive greatsword.
Halberd

This precious herbal was put together by the famed alchemist Semiel del Turquist of Ashton, known far and wide for both for his skill as an apothecary and for his rather detestable taste in poetry. Having been excommunicated from the church no less than twelve times for his lecherous writings, Semiel del Turquist was arguably the most “forgiveable” man to have ever lived. Each count of excommunication was interposed for by a high ranking member of the clergy. Some tales claim these clergymen were beset by diseases of the wanting flesh... and illness that Semiel would have been all too familiar with curing, but no one would have ever dared to make such accusations openly, lest they risk besmirching the name of Semiel “the Untouchable.”
Herbal

The severed head of the Bloody Butcher, Benthley of Welshrem, should be proof enough that the bane of Glatzburg has been dealt with. Only God knows how many innocent lives he took before I put him down. The church will likely excuse his madness on the grounds that he believed our Lord God was commanding him to commit murder.
Benthley of Welshrem's Head
This is the severed head of the orc, Gubring. Never again will he profane God’s creation.
Gubring's Head
This is the severed head of Baroness Helen von Hunth. What sort of creature lays hands on a woman only to remove her head? God save her tortured soul; may she ever rest in peace.
Helen von Hunth's Head

This is the severed head of one of the rogues plaguing Glatzburg. It burdens my wounded soul to look upon this wretch’s face, features contorted by an agony that has come and gone forever. The word “shocking” could never adequately describe the number of men who have resorted to petty crime. Worse, not all of these brigands are failed beggars and runaway soldiers; members of the gentry—knights and barons, once godly men—have cast aside their lots as well. Now they lead companies of bloodthirsty highwaymen, scouring the king’s roads for the bittersweet glimmer of stolen gold... or the promise of unprotected flesh.
Head of a Rogue

This is the severed head of Henrey de Montreaux, ex-paladin of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. Brother Henrey walked a path from whence he could never return; a path that many before him have walked and—God forgive us—many more will walk after his passing. The righteous should hang their heads in prayer to see such a man fall. He could have been so much more, had he devoted himself to the ideals of worldly justice and our Lord God Almighty’s peace.
Montreaux's head
This is the severed head of the landsknecht Olfghard. God save his soul if his soul be worth the trouble. Elsewise, damn him and his dark deeds for all eternity. In your name, amen.
Olfghard's head

This is the severed head of Orc Khan Rashgar, and never have I laid eyes on something at once so equally horrifying and uplifting. The “Immortal” Rashgar was old when the first man took his first breath, and never did a beat of his black heart sound without a whisper of hate for all of God’s creation. It was he who led the greenskin’s genocidal campaign against the savage proto-men of the Thron Empire, destroying them to the last child. In his time, Rashgar carried out the will of his dark masters with ruthless efficiency and absolutely remorselessness. That time—praise God—is at an end.
Rashgar's head

This is the severed head of an orc warrior, and I for one am thankful to see the greenskin horde short one more head. In life, this beast possessed the strength to crush a human skull with childlike ease, but that might was nothing compared to the power of our Lord. His will be done on Earth as it is in Heaven.
Orcish head

This is the severed head of an orc shaman. In all of my years, I have witnessed few things more terrifying to behold. It calms the nerves a touch, however, to know the orcs are bereaved of one of their unholy scions. Never again will this beast foul our Lord God's creation.
Orcish shaman's head

This is the severed head of a werewolf, but not that of a simple beast. What I hold now is all that remains of what was once a man and I would do well to remember that as I continue my journey. The evils of this world and those that lurk beyond it never rest. Neither must I, lest I fall as well. This particular abomination, however, will never again prowl the Schwarzwald in search of human flesh; perhaps with its passing, the innocent might sleep a little more soundly.
Werewolf head

These are the bloody jowls of the slain Wolf Prince, Wulfhyrr. Never again will this creature separate loved ones from their families or pierce the night with his inhuman cries. Though the ancient wood of Schwarzwald is far from safe, it is far safer with the Prince of Wolves dead and gone.
Wulfhyrr's head

Chateau de Trebrechette, an opulent wine that shares a name with the vineyard which produces it, is a rare commodity in these troubled times. In times of peace, the wine was often delivered by sea, though, from time to time, the occasional trader with more brass than sense would smuggle a bottle or two through the treacherous passes of the Moonshine Mountains. Not a single drop has been seen in Hillbrandt since the coming of the Scourges of God, for no trader in his right mind would risk losing a single bottle of Chateau de Trebrechette—let alone his life—to the Hellspawn running rampant in the countryside.
Chateau de Trebrechette
A Potion of Strength will temporarily increase the Strength of anyone who drinks it. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Strength
A Potion of Dexterity will temporarily increase the Dexterity of anyone who drinks it. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Dexterity
A Potion of Constitution temporarily improves the Constitution of anyone who drinks it. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Constitution
A Potion of Intelligence will temporarily increase the Intelligence of anyone who drinks it. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Intelligence
A Potion of Speed will temporarily increase the Speed of anyone who drinks it. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Speed
A Potion of Healing will restore one's lost Hit Points. The number of Hit Points restored depends on the quality of the potion. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Healing
A Potion of Mana will restore one’s lost Mana Points. The amount of Mana restored depends on the quality of the potion. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Mana
A Potion of Stamina will restore one’s Stamina. The amount of Stamina restored depends on the quality of the potion. This is a basic non-blended potion.
Potion of Stamina

A Purifying Potion will remove the effects of all other potions as long as their quality is the same or lower than the quality of the Purifying Potion. Due to the totality of its cleansing effects, these concoctions are sometimes referred to as Potions of Disillusion.
Purifying Potion

A Potion of Accuracy temporarily increases the imbiber’s “to hit” attribute: the higher the quality of the potion, the greater the accuracy of the imbiber. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Strength and Potion of Dexterity.
Potion of Accuracy

A Potion of Frost Protection will temporarily increase the imbiber’s Frost Resistance: the higher the quality of the potion, the higher the resistance. This is a dual-component potion be obtained by mixing a Potion of Strength and a Potion of Constitution.
Potion of Frost Protection

A Potion of Mind will temporarily increase the imbiber’s maximum Mana Points. As with other potions, the quality of the potion determines how many extra Mana Points the imbiber will receive. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Strength and a Potion of Intelligence.
Potion of Mind

A Potion of Tirelessness temporarily grants the imbiber a decrease to the amount of Stamina lost when running. The quality of the potion determines the rate at which Stamina will be lost. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Strength and a Potion of Speed.
Potion of Tirelessness

A Potion of Poison Protection temporarily increases the imbiber’s Poison Resistance: the higher the quality of the potionThis is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing the potions of Dexterity and Constitution.
Potion of Poison Protection

A Potion of Perception will temporarily improve the reaction speed of the imbiber: the higher the quality of the potion, the faster the reactions. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Dexterity and a Potion of Intelligence.
Potion of Perception

A Potion of Defense will temporarily increase the Armor Class of the imbiber. The quality of the potion determines the Armor Class bonus. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Dexterity and a Potion of Speed.
Potion of Defense

A Potion of Fire Protection will temporarily increase the imbiber’s resistance to fire: the higher the quality of the potion, the higher the resistance to fire. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Constitution and a Potion of Intelligence.
Potion of Fire Protection

A Potion of Electrical Protection will temporarily increase the imbiber’s resistance to electrical damage. As with other resistance potions, the degree of resistance is determined by the quality of the potion. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Constitution and a Potion of Speed.
Potion of Lightning Protection

A Potion of Witchcraft will temporarily increase the recovery speed of the imbiber’s magical energy. As with other potions, the rate at which magical energy is restored is determined by the quality of the potion. This is a dual-component potion obtained by mixing a Potion of Intelligence and a Potion of Speed.
Potion of Witchcraft

A Potion of Invulnerability will temporarily increase the imbiber’s resistance to physical harm. As with other potions, the degree of resistance is determined by the quality of the potion. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity and Constitution.
Potion of Invulnerability

A Potion of Wizardry will temporarily increase the imbiber’s ability to pierce foes with magical attacks. Higher quality potions increase the magnitude of piercing further. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence.
Potion of Wizardry

A Potion of Blood will temporarily increase the imbiber’s chance of landing a critical hit. Higher quality potions increase this chance further. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity and Speed.
Potion of Blood

A Potion of Endurance will temporarily increase the imbiber’s maximum Stamina. The quality of the potion determines the maximum amount of Stamina gained. This a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Constitution and Intelligence.
Potion of Endurance

A Potion of Regeneration allows the imbiber to gradually recover lost Hit Points for a short period of time. The quality of the potion determines how much lost health is regained. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Constitution and Speed.
Potion of Regeneration

A Potion of Mana Restoration allows the imbiber to gradually recover lost Mana Points for a short period of time. The quality of the potion determines how much lost mana is regained. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Intelligence and Speed.
Potion of Mana Restoration

A Potion of Magic Resistance will temporarily increase the imbiber’s Magic Resistance. The quality of the potion determines the amount of added resistance. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Dexterity, Constitution and Intelligence.
Potion of Magic Resistance

Potions of Invincibility will temporarily increase the imbiber’s Armor Class and reduce his or her chance of being critically hit. The quality of the potion determines how much extra Armor Class is gained and how much the chance of being critically hit is lowered. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Dexterity, Constitution and Speed.
Potion of Invincibility

Potions of Mastery will temporarily increase the level of all of the Imbiber’s active skills. The quality of the potion determines the degree to which these skills are increased. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Dexterity, Intelligence and Speed.
Potion of Mastery

Potions of Elemental Resistance will temporarily increase the imbiber’s resistance to Fire, Frost, Poison and Electricity. The quality of the potion determines the increase of these resistances. This is a three-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Constitution, Intelligence and Speed.
Potion of Elemental Resistance

An Elixir of Strength will permanently increase the Strength of the imbiber by one point. This is a four-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution and Intelligence.
Elixir of Strength

An Elixir of Constitution will permanently increase the Constitution of the imbiber by one point. This is a four-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution and Speed.
Elixir of Constitution

An Elixir of Intelligence will permanently increase the Intelligence of the imbiber by one point. This is a four component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Constitution, Intelligence and Speed.
Elixir of Intelligence
An Elixir of Speed will permanently increase the Speed of the imbiber by one point. This is a four-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence and Speed.
Elixir of Speed

An Elixir of Dexterity will permanently increase the Dexterity of the imbiber by one point. This is a four-component potion obtained by mixing potions of Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence and Speed.
Elixir of Dexterity
Potions of Treatment are a more potent blend of Potions of Healing, used to much greater effect. They are two-component potions, obtained by mixing potions of Healing and Strength.
Potion of Treatment
Potions of Concentration are a more potent blend of Potions of Mana, used to much greater effect. They are two-component potions obtained by mixing potions of Mana and Strength.
Potion of Concentration

Potions of Courage are a two-party remedy, simultaneously increasing the imbiber’s Fear Resistance while removing any lingering fear effects. They are two-component potions produced by mixing potions of Strength and Stamina.
Potion of Courage
Potions of Antidote will slow the effects of any poison currently effecting the imbiber. They are two-component potions obtained by mixing potions of Healing and Dexterity.
Potion of Antidote
Potions of Freedom remove any movement-hindering effects from the imbiber. They are two-component potions obtained by mixing potions of Mana and Dexterity.
Potion of Freedom
Potions of Resting are more potent versions of the Potion of Stamina. These potions are created by mixing potions of Stamina and Dexterity.
Potion of Resting

Potions of Cure Disease, under the correct circumstances, can cure any disease currently affecting the imbiber. The quality of the potion determines the strength of the cure—certain diseases can only be cured by the strongest Potions of Cure Disease. These potions are created by mixing potions of Constitution and Healing.
Potion of Cure Disease

Every night is a terrible night for a curse—why suffer? Potions of Broken Curse, as the name suggests, lessen the effects of any curse currently afflicting the imbiber. The quality of the potion determines how drastically the symptoms of said curse are reduced. These potions are produced by mixing potions of Mana and Constitution.
Potion of Broken Curse

A well-brewed Potion of Sobriety can clear the head of any wayward drunk, much to the chagrin of angry housewives and head-shaking priests the world over. As the name suggests, these potions permnanently remove the effects of drunkenness. They are produced by mixing potions of Stamina and Constitution.
Potion of Sobriety

Potions of Sanity, when ingested, possess the ability to cure any malady of the human mind. While the permanence of the effects lies in questions, recreational users have reported a twenty-five percent decrease in mad visions of tentacle-waggling gods from beyond the depths of space within forty-eight hours of consumption. These potions are created by mixing potions of Healing and Intelligence.
Potion of Sanity

Feeling confused? Have a drop or two. Potions of Resolution will cure any imbiber’s confusion, allowing for the delivery of swift, clear-headed retribution. This dissolution of confusion is far from obtrusive, though it proves quite a nuisance for those who make use of elusion and illusions. These potions are created by mixing potions of Mana and Intelligence.
Potion of Resolution

Potions of Sight are capable of curing unnatural or premature blindness. The quality of the potion determines how much of the imbiber’s sight is returned. Potions of Sight are produced by mixing potions of Stamina and Intelligence. Currently, they can do nothing to prevent blindness brought about by idle hands.
Potion of Seeing
Potions of Survival are a more potent blend of the standard Potion of Healing formula which affects the body more rapidly. Potions of Survival are produced by mixing potions of Healing and Speed.
Potion of Survival

Potions of Magic are a more potent blend of the standard Potion of Mana which regenerates a user’s magical energy at a much quicker rate. These potions are produced by mixing potions of Mana and Speed.
Potion of Magic
Potions of Energy are a more potent blend of the standard Potion of Stamina which restores the imbiber’s vigor much faster. These potions are produced by mixing potions of Stamina and Speed.
Potion of Energy

Never before has an object so simple fostered such... bewilderment. Painted thick with the countless sighs and groans of those who have attempted to open this small box before, the locking mechanism—if indeed there is one—seems impossible to find. With your ear pressed to the box, you hear a faint whispering. The words, however, are thoroughly alien. Was this box forged to hold something? Or was it meant simply to confound? Only by destroying it will the answer be made clear. Do you dare?
Magical Box

The name “Drichtmaul” has been carved with great care into the ornamented pommel of this hammer. The weapon itself is magnificent, to say nothing of its obviously magical nature. There’s no telling what a talented blacksmith could forge from this enchanted steel. I trust the Drichtmauls must have missed this weapon terribly.
Drichtmaul Family Hammer
This large metal key is worn and rusted from years of use. The distinctive markings on its surface indicate that this key likely opens one of the doors in the mine.
Mine Gate Key
A small, ordinary steel key. The distinctive markings on its surface indicate that this key likely opens one of the doors in the mine.
Rusty Mine Key

There can be no doubt this key was crafted by inhuman hands. Too large to fit comfortably in a grown man’s hand, yet too small for a troll’s, it’s likely this key was forged by the ancient sub-human Thron who once inhabited the depths of the Moonshine Mountains. If the size of the key is any indication, the lock it fits and the door it opens must be positively gargantuan.
Ancient Key

This massive key once belonged to lord Zargh, the Tyrant of the Lizardmen inhabiting the Devil's Caverns. The crude, almost impractical nature of the thing indicates that the Lizardmen are not accustomed to the concept of locking things away. It would be foolish, however, to believe a species as crafty as the Lizardmen would forge a useless key.
Devil's Caverns Key

I received this key from Johaness Clifford, Duke Van Leerin's chamberlain. He claims that it unlocks the entrance to a dungeon beneath the Duke's residence where Van Leerin performs dark rituals. According to Clifford, the rituals are cruel and complex. The key, on the otherhand, is rather plain. So much for showmanship.
Secret Entrance Key

This key could never have been shaped by human hands. It’s cold to the touch—like ice at times—but seems to hum with energy just the same. I swear sometimes I can feel it tugging at my thoughts, shaping the very world around me. Things like eyes misplaced on certain faces, angles and shapes that should not exist in places they should not appear; these odd happenings began when I first touched the key and seem to grow more intense as I turn it over in my fingers. I shiver to think of what this dreadful thing unlocks.
Key of Madness

With a great deal of certainty, I can say I’m one of few humans to have ever held this key. I take little pride in that fact. Though made of simple steel, it chills the flesh to the bone. All the same, it crackles with a foreign energy, the likes of which I’ve never known. The voices, though... the voices are the worst of it. Lingering whispers haunt my dreams, taunting and torturing me at every turn. A few of them I recognize. Voices of the fallen, of those I’ve persecuted. Others... well, others are closer to the heart. The sooner I part with this damnable thing, the better.
Key of Insanity

I can scarcely contain myself. Something about this key makes me... makes me want... to laugh. I can’t for the life of me say why—it’s made of simple iron; slightly cold to the touch, but no different from any other key I’ve ever held. It tingles, though. Tingles—what a funny word. Tingles. Tingles! The key tingles when I touch it. There’s something about it. Oh, I’ve said that already haven’t I? It’s just the tingling, you see. The tingling! Ha!
Key of Lunacy

My hands and eyes would have me believe this... thing is a key. It looks and feels like any other I’ve ever held, but it’s the other senses—God given senses, the sense of right and wrong—which trouble me. I feel incomplete when I touch it. I can think of no other way to describe the sensation. It’s as if a piece of me is dying, or perhaps, already dead. What could it possibly unlock, or more to the point, would I even care to find out?
Key of Sin

Though its shaped like a key, I have to wonder if this thing isn’t actually some sort of weapon. The emotion it radiates (in-so-far as a key can radiate, at least) leaves me ill. Ill... and well... just ill. I cannot bring myself to describe the other sensations it fills me with. Needless to say, parting with it will prove sweet sorrow.
Key of Lechery

It’s been quite some time since I last laid with a woman, hasn’t it? The company of men and animals has been little comfort thus far, but perhaps that’s because I haven’t yet tried... no. What am I thinking? This key is something else entirely. I cannot believe... cannot listen to the things it begs me to do. Oh, but the begging is so sweet. I cannot wait to unlock whatever it desires. Insert and twist the... God, save me.
Key of Lust

How anyone could have forged this key, I’ll never know. Simply holding it fills my mind with visions of things no God-fearing man should ever find himself dreaming of. I must discover what it unlocks quickly before I succumb to thoughts of... Gabriel, preserve me.
Key of Dissolution

I wish I could just abandon this quest and find a fit, fiery-haired girl to—God, what am I saying!? This key is bloody terrifying... I mean, er—quite terrifying. I should set about discovering what it unlocks before I call the whole thing off and go get my staff pol—Good heavens! That’s certainly enough of that.
Key of Shamelessness

If any other key I’ve ever held has frightened me, none has so much as prepared me for being near this one. I dare not touch it anymore than is absolutely necessary. The film it leaves on the tips of my fingers burns and even when it’s pressed against my clothing, I can feel it eating away at the linen and leather. I must discover what this key unlocks before it undoes me.
Key of Corruption

This is a key... how foolish of me. Of course it’s a key; what am I saying? Alas, I feel the need to remind myself. It is obviously the craft of hellspawn, this infernal device. When I hold it, I can feel the weight of dozens of eyes upon me. Their sorrow, their regret, overwhelms me and I can do naught but shiver. I sense great loss associated with the object. I must discover what it unlocks, though I tremble to imagine the gate it must open.
Key of Decimation

This key is... This key—oh God, how could you let such terrible things transpire under your careful watch? Such death! I have never witnessed such suffering; it is as though a forest of men sprang up in the world and was hacked down—all of them cut at the knee, the groin and the chest—like kindling! Kindling to fuel the fires of war... I cannot bear to look at this key any longer. I simply do not have the will. Without a doubt, this device was made to the detriment of the True Faith.
Key of Annihilation

Instinct dictates that this... thing is a key. If anything can be said of the occult, they loathe wasting their power on worthless objects. Judging from its shape alone, however, it could be anything. Holding the thing hasn’t yet granted me visions or filled me with any particular emotion, as most occult objects do. In fact, the only thing I feel at all is profound anger when I behold it. How dare these cultist mongrels threaten MY religion? I vow to see these lickspittles driven before me before the fall takes me.
Key of Destruction
Having found this key on the body of an orc, it’s safe to assume the thing is of their make and design. The metal is plain—grimy, but plain. I wonder it opens?
Orcish Key

Yet another key of inhuman make. If the crude design or monstrous size had not given it away, then the grisly runes scratched into its surface would have been clue enough. Needless to say, it must open an absolutely massive door.

This enormous key—crudely fashioned and adorned with bits of tarnished metal—opens an orcish door. Of that, I have no doubt. But the orcs have never been known for their appreciation of embellishment. The door this key unlocks must either guard something very precious to the orcs... or perhaps keep something they respect—or fear—caged. Neither seems a more pleasant option.

Whatever this opens must be important to the orcs. They usually put little thought into embellishing their creations, but the metal ornaments adorning this key show it was made with great care. By orc standards, at least.
Orcish key

Using the religious markings found on the surface of this key as a guide, I can tell it unlocks a church’s tomb. The inclusion of the insignia of the Glatzburg diocese makes determining which tomb that may be that much easier, though by no means simple. It is beautifully made—too beautiful for a common smithy, certainly. Interesting. This key was likely fashioned by a royal smith; a high honor... and none too cheap.
Ecclesiastical Tomb in Glatzburg Key

The mixture of secular and religious motifs found on the surface of this key indicate that it likely belongs to the tomb of an aristocrat. The insignia of the city of Glatzburg lies nearly hidden among them. Marked so intricately, and being of such extraordinary make and design, this key was almost certainly shaped by a royal smith.
Secular Tomb in Glatzburg Key

The religious motifs found on the surface of this key indicate that it most likely belongs to one of the Lord’s holy houses. The symbol of the Glatzburg diocese is engraved upon it, narrowing the search for said house quite substantially. The key shines and has evidently been well cared for, meaning that it probably sees frequent use.
Glatzburg diocese key

This key, while massive, was very poorly made. It likely fits one of the doors or chests in the Devil’s Caverns, where the Lizard men nest. Whichever of the beasts made it is clearly obsessed with the idea of snakes. The key itself resembles a knot of the little buggers, writhing about as though they were throwing a tantrum.
Lizards' Key

This key, while massive, was poorly made. It likely fits one of the doors or chests in the Devil’s Caverns, where the Lizard men nest. Whichever of the beasts made it is clearly obsessed with the idea of snakes. The key itself resembles a knot of the little buggers, writhing about as if they were throwing a tantrum.

This key, while massive, was very poorly made. It likely fits one of the doors or chests in the Devil’s Caverns, where the Lizard men nest. Whichever of the beasts made it is clearly obsessed with the idea of snakes. The key itself resembles a knot of the little buggers, writhing about as if they were throwing a tantrum.

Well, judging from where I found this particular key, it’s probably safe to say it wasn’t used for anything wholesome. The Bloody Butcher — what a disgusting creature. Needless to say, the world is a safer, better place without Benthley of Welshrem in it. A key, though? That’s odd. The rogues themselves don’t seem to fear the notion of being robbed. I can only assume that it unlocks something in Welshrem’s settlement then: personal belongings, maybe... or a cage of some description?
Rogue Keep Key

There’s a thick coat of rust and grime on this key. From the looks of it, it hasn’t been used in ages. That would make sense, considering how long the coliseum has lain empty, but it’s odd nonetheless to find a key just lying around. And what a key it is. The make, the craftsmanship—it’s unlike any other I’ve ever held. Fascinating. Galibornium... what other secrets do you hold?
Coliseum Key

There are scratches on the surface of this key, and if I had to guess, I’d say they probably weren’t made by iron-chewing rat monsters. I really hope they weren’t made by iron-chewing rat monsters. Seriously, I really — actually, they seem rather shallow. Maybe someone was just cleaning it and scrubbed a little too vigorously. As much as I hate to admit it, that does seem like a more reasonable circumstance. Cleaning a key, though... a key to what? The sewers, perhaps?
Key from the Glatzburg's Sewers
The den beneath Wolfenburg reeks of werewolf musk and age old rot, but the passages are lined with doors and cages. Any of them might be opened by this very key.
Wolfenburg Key

I’m sure an expert in heraldry could tell me a thing or two about this key. I can tell it opens one of the Noble Tombs in the Royal Cemetery, but other than that, I don’t have much to go on. A locksmith would probably have a fair amount to say as well, but judging from the looks of this key and regardless of how old it is, someone has taken very good care of it.
Alvaron Tomb Key

There is, beyond the shadow of a doubt, absolutely no reason a key should ever be this... fabulous. Why would the Brotherhood fashion something so expensive only to leave it their dungeon? Mind you, it’s a very nice dungeon... but it’s not that nice. There are noble manors in Glatzburg worth less than this key – I’d lay coin on it. Well, despite its location, it has to be important to the brothers. Either that or the Brotherhood is in desperate need of a new financier. Either way, note to self: If this Inquisitor business doesn’t pan out, take up locksmithing.
Citadel Key

Regardless of what one may think of the clergy, none can deny that the Holy Mother church takes very good care of her dead. This key is proof of that. Smithed from the finest gold and polished to a brilliant shine, it looks as if it were made yesterday. It opens one of the many doors beneath the Royal Cemetery, though I can’t be sure which.
Ecclesiastical Tomb Key

If the gate this key opens is half as beautiful as this little gemmed darling, I could scarcely imagine the Pearly Gates being any grander. There are thieves in this world who would kill their own mothers just for the chance to hold something this valuable for an instant. I could only imagine what they’d do to see the gate. Thankfully, it’s as far removed for them as the notion of Heaven. And thankfully you’ve no interest in stealing it. Besides, who would you market a giant, jeweled gate to, anyway?
Magnificent Archiepiscopal Dungeon Key

Thousands of men, women, and children starve to death daily, and here I hold in my hands a key worth more than ten thousand meals. The Holy Mother church obviously places an unearthly importance upon the doors to her holdings. Which does this particular beauty unlock, I wonder?
Archiepiscopal Dungeon Key

The Church is obviously obsessed with producing keys worth more than entire trade caravans. This one, though well-kept, bears the signs of use. It likely opens more than one door in the Archiepiscopal Dungeon.

This key belongs to the Brotherhood of the Righteous’s tower in Hillbrandt. Only the most holy and worthy of men are ever granted access to its sacred secrets. It bears an inscription: “Welcome, Brother.” Welcome Brother, indeed.
Key to Hillbrandt’s Tower

This key belongs to the Brotherhood of the Righteous’s tower in Glatzburg. Only the most holy and worthy of men are ever granted access to its sacred secrets. It bears an inscription: “Welcome, Brother.” Welcome Brother, indeed.
Key to Glatzburg's Tower
Key to Alvaron's Tower

This key bears a tiny inscription: “This key, and indeed, any other key of similar make and jewel-encrusted nature, service and belong exclusively to the Archiepiscopal Dungeon.” That’s a rather long-winded way of saying “don’t take the keys outside, you bloody prat.”
Key of Archiepiscopal Dungeon

I must not allow myself to fall to the petty temptations of common men. Oh, who am I kidding – it’s a treasure map!A real treasure map! I’m so excited.And judging by the looks of it... yes! This is no ordinary treasure map. This is barbarian treasure. When the Barbarians were driven from Ultherst back in 988, they hid the loot they’d pillaged from northern villages in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Rumor has it that a statuette of the pagan god Bhelfelix was hidden along with the rest of the barbarian’s plundered cache. They must have made a map in hopes of returning someday, but as fate would have it, they never showed. Instead, the map passed into the hands of the infamous treasure hunter, Hulph Rechtzwürther, and from his hands into mine.
Barbarian treasure map

This is the testament of Father Bartholomeus, first Superior of the Order of Saint Orthenius. By all rights, the man should have been considered a saint himself. The order was established to preserve the heritage of the Great Liberator, and legends say Father Bartholomeus was among the most dedicated to protecting Orthenius’s legacy. However, according to this text, the order may have had another purpose — one I’ve certainly never heard of. It reads:\\n\\nNightmares haunt my rest, chilling visions of the death awaiting all who share the Order’s secret. The secret of the keys! Oh, cruel fate; why must you destroy those who throw themselves willingly at your mercy? No matter. We must never risk disclosing the secret of the keys to our enemies — even in death. I shall pen it here, in my Final Testament of Faith, to be buried alongside me in the impenetrable tomb which awaits my aging flesh. If you lay eyes upon this holy document, I charge you – if you be a God-fearing servant – to avenge our murder and to take up the mantle we have relinquished. If you be foe, I pray that the Lord God strips the flesh from your worthless bones and burns your peeled rind in Hell for all eternity for seeking our death.Steady yourself, traitor hand – death is but God’s path to immortality.\\n\\nForgive me my mortal weakness.\\n\\nThe first thing you must know, brother-champion, is this: the three keys are actually jade statuettes fashioned in the image of the three emissaries of God – Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael. Each statuette lies in a different corner of the Realm, hidden away and guarded by contraptions guaranteed to kill any intruder weak of mind or conviction. Their locations are as follows:\\n\\nThe Statuette of Raphael was buried beneath the Sacred Tree near the village of Hillbrandt, nestled in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. In the shade of that very tree, St. Orthenius converted hundreds of pagan warriors to the True Faith after besieging their fortress stronghold.\\n\\nThe Statuette of Michael rests in Galibornium, in the former Temple of All Gods, which St. Orthenius cleansed and consecrated personally in the name of the Holy Mother.\\n\\nFinally, the Statuette of Gabriel was hidden in the first Episcopal temple built upon the shores of Filkland Peninsula, in the city now known as Alvaron, where the Orthodox Patriarch Basilian erected his residence as the new Rex.\\n\\nIf these keys you seek, brother champion, be wary – that which lies in wait cares none for the purity in your heart. To claim the statuettes, you will need to treat-lightly and with the grace of God. Go now, with my blessing if you be a friend of the Faith, or my blackest curses otherwise.
Bartholomeus' Testament

This map should lead me to the treasure of the late Decard of Longhorn. Apparently the treasure is buried in Schwarzwald, near the coaching inn... assuming the werewolf Kenthwaar was telling the truth. I doubt many intelligent men have ever had that same thought cross their mind. Well, how many of those men were rich? Probably a few...
Treasure map

If all goes well, this map should lead me to the treasure of the infamous tomb-robber, Vick Length. It claims the treasure is buried near the bridge leading to the Citadel of Brotherhood of Righteous – ugh, what a mouthful. I say claims only because I have trouble believing that rogue Steinger would tell anyone the truth, let alone me. Still, it couldn’t hurt to look.

This jewel-encrusted key unlocks the Royal Tomb, the most prestigious burial site in all of Alvaron. The remains of great kings and, by extension, some terrible ones, are interred here.I received the key from Cardinal Letti shortly after the Archbishop Laurencius locked himself inside the tomb. Rather a foolish plan, when you consider it.
Royal Tomb key

To some, this key is worth more than my very life. It unlocks one of the gates leading to the Royal Burial Chamber, where the greatest men and women to have ever ruled Alvaron lay in eternal repose. Once inside, I must pay my respects to these noble lords and ladies with my caution and discretion. Their rest means more to me than my safety.
Royal Burial Chamber key

This map should lead me directly to the treasure of the late Baron Mansfeld. At least, I would assume so, considering I took the map from him after returning his corpse to its grave. If the instructions are correct, the treasure should be found in a stump near Alvaron’s gallows. They should be right. Right? I don’t see why a dead man would go to the trouble of lying to me.

There’s no mistaking it. This grimoire once belonged to the Elenian noble, Fae'Darlion. His sigil is painted across every blank space within, and for good reason. The Elenians were famous for their magical abilities and for their restrictive caste system: The aristocracy of Elenian society was composed entirely of priestly wizards. While possessing an aristocracy comprised entirely of wizards is not altogether uncommon among pagan cultures, the Elenians were a truly unique Magocracy.\\n\\nUnder penalty of death, Elenian nobles were forbidden from sharing the contents of their grimoires with anyone. While it sounds ridiculous to a human, the Elenians lived in constant fear of falling under the power of a single Mage Lord. While this prohibition protected the Elenians from themselves, it also proved to be their downfall. During times of war, coordinating the defense of their homeland proved almost impossible as no two wizards could ever work side by side for fear of having their spells stolen. As such, the Elenian Empire was reduced to a Lone Wolf state – a loose confederation of arrogant wizards who were systematically picked apart by their unified enemies. The wizards’ draconian laws did provide one thing, however: no two Elenian grimoires were ever the same, and each is now a treasure beyond reckoning to the mortal races that survived them. In death, the Elenian’s many varied magical tomes have achieved the immortality they could never keep for themselves.
Fae'Darlion's Spell Book

Spears are the common man’s lance, in most respects. Their long reach and piercing heads make quick work of enemy cavalry charges. However, due to their unwieldy nature in close-quarters combat and the difficulty required to extract them from fallen foes, many infantrymen consider spears to be expendable weapons, useful only in the initial phases of combat.\\n\\nComposed of a wooden shaft, usually 1-2 meters in length, and a piercing metal head, spears are effective – if somewhat simple – weapons. However, due to their expendable nature, many infantrymen now prefer modern alternatives such as the halberd or the glaive. Not only are these weapons more efficient killers of men, they are also easier to extract from a victim’s corpse.
Spear

As the name suggests, Mandrake Roots are the roots of the Madrake Officinarum herb—simply referred to as “Mandrake” by most. The roots themselves come in a variety of shapes and sizes, most resembling the human form. Many suppose this is because Mandrake Root tends to grow near places of human suffering, such as gallows or hangman’s trees.To preserve a Mandrake Root’s magical properties, the root itself must be exhumed at precisely midnight. Prior to digging the root from the earth, however, it must be beaten three times with a willow switch. Many believe this ritual deters imps, notorious little Hellspawn who thrive in the dirt, from clinging to the root as it’s extracted.
Mandrake Root

Leather armor, depending on the hide it’s crafted from, can be an affordable alternative to scale and plate mail. As such, most modern armies clothe their infantry entirely in leather made from cured sheep or cow skins. Padded thickly to protect vital organs, leather armor gives its wearer a degree of mobility unheard of with stronger, more unwieldy suits of armor. That mobility comes at a price, though. While most infantrymen pay little mind to enhancing their armor – many swear that leather is little more than a second skin, after all – the dependability of leather can be improved by adding protective plates of steel or strips of lamellar over exposed joints or vital organs. While these minor improvements increase the strength of the armor, they also restrict mobility.
Leather Armor

Sabers are strange, curved swords first introduced to the Faithful by Crusaders returning from the deserts of Jad-Habaal. Though their strange shape made them initially difficult to wield in one-to-one melee, cavalry throughout the civilized world soon recognized the value of curved, aerodynamic blades. While heavy cavalry prefer long sabers as secondary weapons, light cavalry and skirmishers prefer short sabers as primary weapons due to their shear killing power. Few sights inspire as much dread as a mounted rider bearing a curved blade, and few things kill quicker than a saber with a horse’s speed behind it.
Short saber

The warriors of Jad-Habaal are famous for a great many things, namely their strange curved swords and penchant for impressive facial hair. But one invention in particular separates the Jad-Habaali warriors from any other fighter in the known world: the short bow. Sacrificing strength for versatility, the warriors of Jad-Habaal have made use of mounted archers for generations thanks to the aid of the shortbow. Its size, weight, and strength make it an incredible utility in the field. The concept of horseback archery has yet to catch on in the realm of the Faithful, mainly because the training is excruciatingly demanding both on the warrior and the mount. Give me solid ground any day, am I right?
Short Bow

Very little separates the standard short sword from its “long” equivalent. The variance in blade size is negligible for the common fighter. However, for the uncommon warrior, short swords can be exceedingly deadly weapons. Lighter and swifter than their larger cousins, a well-made short sword possesses all of the strengths of a sword and a dagger. Modern shortswords are likely based upon the ancient Erebornian’s standard sword design. The Erebornians were exceptional warriors, and in their hands, short swords were both weapons and tools of artistry. It was once said that a trained Erebornian with a well made short sword could hold his own against any number of men wielding two-handed blades. Curious, how the weapons managed to outlive their prideful masters with the odds so grossly weighed in their favor.
Short Sword

Crystals are a transparent variety of quartz, believed to be the mineral’s purest form. They are revered by the faithful for their supposed ability to hinder dark magics. They also, depending on the region, harm evil spirits, ward off demons, enlighten their wearer or charm angels. Of course, if you’re not one to go believing everything you hear, they also fetch a pretty penny. Those do the same thing no matter where you find them, or so I’m told.
Crystal

What a treasure! This volume is immensely valuable, not only to me but the Faith as a whole. This is the Chronicle of Father Killian, a master historian who lived centuries ago. It details the period between the Rise of the True Faith and the Fall of the Erebornian Empire. Of particular importance are the years 180-236 of the New Era, when Saint Orthenius, Patron and Protector of the Realm, walked the earth spreading the True Faith with blade and tongue. Were it not for the wiles of Orthenius, Ultherst may never have risen from the ashes of Ereborn.\\n\\nBut Killian was not simply one of Orthenius’s contemporaries; he was also one of the saint’s followers. As such, the tales found in his Chronicle are the source of many of the more recognizable stories involving the Great Saint’s travels.\\n\\nPerhaps the most popular tale taken from Killian’s Chronicle is the legend of the Successor, the one who was destined rise in St. Orthenius’s absence as Patron and Protector of the Realm. According to the legend, the Successor would some day come to possess a powerful relic known as “the Inquisitor” – an artifact of immense power which would allow him to destroy any evil as St. Orthenius destroyed the ancient Erebornians. Killian’s telling of the tale, however, dispels much of the superstition that age and countless re-tellings have attached to the legend:\\n\\nOn the day of his death, the Saint Orthenius climbed a small hill near Alvaron and lay down at a the base of a massive pine tree.\\n-'Today I will leave this world,' he told his companions. 'But shed not a tear for me, for it is the Will of the Lord which compels me to rest. It is He who measures our time and rations it to us, each the length he or she requires to do what is necessary.\\n-'But what will we do without your guidance,' asked the one they called Despairer. 'The pagans will rally at your death! They will return and slaughter us as lambs; the Faith will surely perish!\\n-If you heed these words, never shall the Faith fall,' replied Orthenius. 'First, you must construct me a tomb from the stone of the Earth and bless it three times in the name of God Almighty. Bury me within and bless the tomb thrice more. Once my body is at rest, set about carving three statuettes from the purest jade under the stars, one for each of God’s mighty archangels,’ Orthenius said, staring into the bark of the great pine. ‘Bless them and bind them to my tomb so that it may never be opened without them. If ever an enemy should rise to challenge the Faith, break the seal on my tomb and retrieve from my grave a weapon, the very manifestation of God’s wrath. You will know it when first you lay eyes upon it, and it will likewise know You. It will answer to “Inquisitor.” Do not hesitate to use it! In idle hands, the Inquisitor will prove as deadly to the innocent as the guilty, for so is God’s Word mighty in calloused hands and dangerous in those which are soft.'\\n\\nAnd the companions did what he said. At the site of his death they constructed a majestic tomb and laid the body of their master within. They then sealed the tomb using the three statuettes – one carved in the image of Raphael, Gabriel, and Michael each. Afterward, they hid the three statuettes and vowed never to relinquish the secret of their whereabouts so long as they all should live. Their final act was to form a pact, the Order of Saint Orthenius, and swear an oath to defend their master’s secret for all eternity. I, Killian, bear sacred witness to these deeds, and so these deeds took place. Amen.
Killian's Chronicle

An Aspergillum, known to some as the “Holy Man’s Mace,” is a ritual tool used to sprinkle sacred holy water. Taking its name from the Lateran “asperege,” meaning “sprinkle,” many priests use aspergillums to sanctify altars and the freshly dead. In a pinch, an aspergillum can also be used to ward off the undead, who fear Holy Water as mortal men fear the fires of Hell itself.
Aspergillum

If you’ve ever had the misfortune of staring down a light cavalry charge, between bouts of crying and pissing yourself, you likely noticed someone carrying a round shield. Lighter and easier to wield than their larger, infantry-focused cousins, round shields have long been the go-to choice for mounted warriors looking for speedy combat. The only exceptions to this rule are heavy cavalry which usually consists of mounted knights. In a situation of that magnitude, a small round shield would simply be a liability.
Round Shield

This is the skull of the former royal chambermaid, Kathryn Winhold. The scorch marks say it all. Her death must have been horrifying, but whose isn’t, these days? I found her skull (oddly enough) with the rest of her blackened remains in a grave on the fringe of Alvaron’s place of execution.
Skull of Kathryn Winhold

Saint Baudolino was a controversial saint. So controversial, in fact, that many scholars agree he likely never existed at all. I couldn’t say; I never met the man. I can, however, say that this particular skull is a fake made by Heins Schiebell, who intended to “return” it the Holy Mother Church for a hefty “finder’s fee.” Trading fake relics for church gold is nothing new, although the practice is abhorrent. The chance of possessing a genuine relic is too great to pass up. For instance, there’s a cathedral on the border of the Empire which bought three crosses in the same year. They swear the First Prophet was crucified on each of them. Likewise, Heins Schiebell swears there’s nothing wrong with trading in fake relics, and he would know. He’s quite the expert in religious matters, especially those involving the flexibility of imagination. Note to self: burn Schiebell if you ever get the chance. I’m sure more than a few churches would pay well for his particular brand of “relics.”
Skull of St. Baudolino

Even the oldest crones and buzzards in Hillbrandt remember being children when they first met the old woman, Ellisia Würtenrodt, who even then was more wrinkle than face. Well, her secret’s out. This potion, strange as it may be, supposedly grants its imbiber extended life. As enticing as that sounds, I question the morality of such an undertaking. On the one hand, God allots us all our time and expects us to serve it... but he also gives us the freewill to search for our own truth, as well as the hearts and minds to handle whatever we come across in our journey.
Longevity Potion

According to Thelma Ulthraum, this disgusting-looking potion possesses the power to cure lycanthropy. That being said, even she has her reservations. For one thing, testing it has proven almost impossible. Realistically, what half-human beast with the strength of ten men would trade its unholy power to walk among the living as a mortal again? Second, who would willingly drink this, regardless?
Cure Lycantrophy Potion

This is an extract taken from a sprig of Mandrake Root. This particular potion is used, most often by heretics to induce mad visions in hapless victims. According to the diary of Father Frederick, though, Mandrake Root can also be used to drive demons from an innocent host. It says something that the concoction is so foul it frightens even demons.
Mandrake Potion

According to Master Alchemist Alberto Kelley, Master of the Royal Alchemist Guild of Alvaron, this potion will reverse the effects of certain metamorphosis spells. On the plus side, even if it doesn’t work, it certainly won’t do any harm to Baroness Vanessa; she already looks like the southern end of a north-bound mule. With the flux. And smallpox.
Dispel Magic Potion

According to the label, this potion cures forgetfulness, either brought about by the coming of age or senility, or the unnatural memory loss caused by certain spells. The label also reads: Shake before use! I’ll have to remember that.
Anti-forgetfulness Potion

This potion was brewed by the herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt for Hillbrandt's executioner, Friedrich Raubsticht. It’s meant to cure a particular illness, though which, I can’t be sure. A note enclosed with the potion reads:\\n\\nIndicator Group: Male Diseases\\n\\nDo not ingest if: Prior hypersensitiveness to the primary medicinal ingredient or any secondary ingredient.\\n\\nPrimary ingredient:Sildenafilum\\n\\nSecondary ingredients: Microcrystallic cellulose, calcium hydrogenphosphate, sodium salt of croscarmellose, magnesium-octadecanoate\\n\\nAdverse side-effects: None. At least no one has complained so far.\\n\\nRecommended dosage: Bottoms up\\n\\nDoses per package: 1\\n\\nManufacturer: Ellisia Würtenrodt, Hillbrandt.
Raubsticht's Potion

This amulet wasn’t made by human hands. The attention to detail, the delicate ornamentation – no, this was made by something with long, graceful fingers. Something Elenian. The moon runes are a dead giveaway. Beautiful as it is, it radiates a deathly cold, and cold, in terms of Elenian magic, is rarely ever good.
En'Lenius's Amulet

A single glance at this abominable volume would likely drive a normal man insane. The book itself is bound in human flesh, and painted with scenes of the most unimaginable depravity. The scenes, painted in blood which never dries, swirl and slither across the book’s ghastly, writhing cover. If what I know of the book is true, it was written in the year 850 by the Dark Prophet, Lucius, founder of the Children of New Order. Judging from the living script, it seems to detail the rise of the fallen angels, Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie.\\n\\nLucius describes the rites for summoning the fallen angels in the most thorough... and sickening terms. His descriptions and instructions as to how the Children should go about committing the atrocities needed to bring Hell to Earth are terrifying, in a word. This Dark Prophet, this Lucius, could never have been a man of flesh and blood like me. The implications of that possibility are... are too frightening to even consider.\\n\\nLord protect me, there’s more. Apparently, one of the Children will be “Marked by the Beast,” and it will be his or her duty to perform the ritual necessary to bring Hell to our world:\\n\\n”Blessed are the chosen, the vessels of corruption! Carry on your person, marked champion, this tome, for through it are channeled the powers which will open the way. To open the gates of Hell, you must be willing to sacrifice. First, you must make an offering of the blood of your brow, breast, and loins. When the unclean blood has mixed at your feet, use it as ink to inscribe the drawn mark upon the gateway. Your mortal form will be consumed, for great and powerful are the fires of Hell, but your spirit will live forever among the princes of the damned, and your sacrifice will bring about the end of God’s feeble, flawed creation.”\\n\\nMay the angels forgive me for what I have read, and may God shed his mercy over me. I must end this, once and for all.
Libre Daemonium

The Theologia Arcanea was penned by the greatest mind to ever grace the faithful world, SaintEfarius. It deals heavily with the relationship between the blessing we know as the “Divine Presence” and the whole of God’s creation. Several logical arguments for the existence of God precede a detailed theoretical explanation as to why the Divine Presence, believed by many to the Holy Ghost itself, manifests in mortals as a form of expendable energy.\\n\\nThe Theologia Arcanea is the cornerstone for the understanding of the mystical powers contained within the rites and symbols of the Holy Mother Church. The text is considered to be almost as important as the Scriptures themselves. A comprehensive understanding of the principles described in the book would be nearly impossible for the common man to come by, yet, anyone who can fully grasp the concepts could master them.\\n\\nThough an invaluable asset to the defense of the Faith, there are many who worry that uncontrolled exposure to the book could lead to the manipulation of its incantations by heretics and traitors who would use the secrets therein to bring the Church to its knees.
Theologia Arcanea

Episkopos Invociren wrote Adversum Maleficarum as a guide for those who devote their lives to battling the forces of evil, particularly those who become conduits for unholy magic. Many of the chapters detail the performing of rites and prayers needed by warriors of God to protect and deliver themselves from evil, but a few of the later chapters also deal with the performance of certain rites of exorcism. Such rites are said to be able to cleanse entire villages, driving legions of demons out of unwilling or unknowing hosts with relative ease.\\n\\nThe book became an indispensable tool of the True Faith’s defense soon after its publication. The Holy Council declared that the work had been written under the influence of Divine Inspiration, and vowed that the volume would stand beside the Scriptures and the Theologia Arcanea as one of the cornerstones of the Church’s defense.\\n\\nPope Urbianus II ordered that copies of the Adversum Maleficarum be sent to every holding from Empire of Lochland to the most remote villages on the fringes of the Orthodox world with the express intention of spreading the Faith and its protection as far as humanly possible.
Adversum Maleficarum

Adanabius of Hognar, the Seeking Mystic, was made rather infamous for hisDiquisitiones Magicae, which the Church originally considered heretical due to Adanabius’s “devaluation” of miracles. Nevertheless the book was deemed acceptable by the Adavian Council in 1008 as one of the paths of discovering Divine truth.\\n\\The text describes, in Adanabius’s own words, how angels and other beings touched by the Lord’s grace are capable of performing miracles – not because they are blessed, but because they possess the faith and temperament required to perform the casting of certain “spells” which manifest themselves in the form of the Divine Presence, which is in turn the physical manifestation of the Holy Ghost. While accepted as truth, this text directly contradicts previous Church dogma, which states that only the Lord God Almighty is capable of performing miracles. The Church has yet to provide a feasible response to this contradiction of truths.
Diquisitiones Magicae

Directorium Inquisitorum, also known as the Golden Tome of the Defender of the Faith, was written between 241 and 250 by Ruphiel, a monk of Saint Marchiel Monastery in the Moonshine Mountains. Ruphiel, who belonged to the Order of Saint Orthenius, spent a great deal of time studying the life and deeds of the Patron, and penned this work as a guide for inquisitors and other defenders of the Faith.//n//nThe church claims that Ruphiel wrote the book under the influence of Divine Inspiration, and the text has become one of the cornerstones of the Inquisitorial office of the Papal Cathedral.\\n\\nThe text outlines the signs an inquisitor should be wary of when investigating the goings-on of heretics and the unclean. Things like twitching, unnatural movements, or an aversion to holy symbols... even the description of those imbued with unholy resistance to torture; the book contains everything a discerning inquisitor would ever need to know to root out and destroy any infestation of heretical belief.
Directorium Iquisitorum

The first, best dissertation on the practices and effects of heretical magic was the Liber Artum Magicarum Prohibitarum, penned by Abbot Ruffus, formerly of the Lochland Cloister of Saint Jillian. Abbot Ruffus, who would later become Pope Nicholas IX, considered the book a stepping stone toward defeating the rise of heretics in the Empire of Lochland in the ninth century. The dissertation was designed to allow the Church’s faithful to identify and bring to justice sorcerers and other practitioners of evil magic.\\n\\nThe dissertation is a treasure trove of information regarding the uses, effects and defenses against the magic of death and decay. It was stolen from the Papal Library in 905, and though it was rediscovered some years later, the Church has no doubt that several copies were made during these “Lost Years.” The Papal Inquisition is, and always has been, on the lookout for these supposed counterfeit copies, for should the text ever fall into the wrong hands, it could prove immensely dangerous for inquisitors in the field.
Liber Artum Magicarum Prohibitarum

In times long past, when the young Church waged an intellectual war with many pagan races and societies, a priest of the Lord named Arkinodos wrote “Revelation of the False Teachings,” or Elenchós Tés Pseudonymú Gnóseós. The text contains not only detailed descriptions of Erebornian cultic rites, but also lists several contradictions contained within them. Most famous, however, are the supposed dialogues between an Erebornian cultist and Arkinodos himself, which reveal the nature of Erebornian lies and refute them with the Creator’s Truth, written by the First Prophet himself.\\n\\nThough Arkinodos’s work was well-intentioned, the Church would eventually outlaw his text, for in the writing of it, Arkinodos forgot an easily overlooked truth: Heretics can read, too. Over the years, the Church saw a drastic increase in the number of heretical rites being performed within Church territories, but only when the matter was investigated further did it become apparent that a terrible mistake had been made. Many of the culprits were working with a copy of “Revelation” in hand, using the thoroughly researched and corrected hexes within not to disprove the strength of Paganism, as Arkinodos had intended, but instead to wallow in the unhindered glory of their own cruel gods. For that reason, Arkinodos is oft-remembered as “The Thoughtless Thinker,” and his Revelation, little more than an interesting, if forbidden, read.
Elenchós Tés Pseudonymú Gnóseós

No four words elicit more fear from the Holy Mother Church than “Liber Lucifer Ordinis Novi,” and with good reason. Penned in the 9th century by an unnamed heretic, the Liber Lucifer is a call-to-arms against the Church, invoking and inviting any sin which will weaken God’s hold over the Earth. Listed within are the rituals required to summon entities representing every vice known to man. Alongside these are simple instructions designed to teach and instruct even the simplest of creatures as to how they might best damage the Church, from within and without. Understandably, the Holy Council banned the book the moment its existence was made known, though the Church has never succeeded in destroying every copy ever made. To this day, the eyes and ears of the Papal Inquisition scour every inch of the known world, searching for any surviving copies of the text so that they might bring to justice any who adhere to that which lies within.
Liber Lucifer Ordinis Novi

Scrolls, like the magic they contain, have a long and storied history. No one can say for sure when the first was penned, but they have witnessed the rise and decline of masculine magic worshippers who burned women as witches; the founding and strengthening of every religion known to man; scrolls were even used by the First Prophet himself. They might contain the ritual required to perform a certain spell, or simply the formula of ingredients required, but every well-written scroll will allow the chosen to wield the magic of Creation. The concept of a “chosen” one is no romantic story-telling device, for even those who wield “evil” magic are the chosen of God. The Church teaches that no man is born a sinner, and that even those who were destined by God to do great things will and will continue to fall and become scions of the darkness. Thankfully, only the chosen who master, remember, or read well-written scrolls are capableof performing spells. No matter how gifted, without the correct knowledge, a chosen one is much like the head of a mace with no handle: Intimidating, but utterly without purpose.
Magic Scroll

The origins of the term “bastard sword” are as many as the designs of the weapon itself. The most widely accepted reasoning behind the name is that the blade, commonly referred to as a “one-and-a-half-hander”, is the bastard child of a two-handed sword and a standard long sword. Another popular origin theory stems from the fact that the bastard sword is widely used by both members of the peasant serf class and members of the nobility despite their rather plain make. Many grizzled veterans will happily tell you that the swords aren’t made pretty so that any poor bastard can use them without having to worry about being called a thief.
Bastard sword

The Decapitator Sword is one of the most powerful artifacts in the arsenal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. The blade’s previous owner, Master Konrad von Thaum, wielded it for nearly thirty years before falling at the hands of the infamous Wolf-Prince. Though old beyond reason and growing blind in both eyes, Von Thaum still managed to decapitate a number of the Wolf-Prince’s bestial spawn before succumbing to his wounds. Such is the might of the sword that even the elderly and infirm become mighty weapons of God when wielding it in good faith.
Decapitator Sword

This is an excellent specimen of root from the Memoricus Repeaticus herb. Renowned for its silly Lateran name and its supposed incredible ability to return lost or shrouded memory, the Memoricus Repeaticus is the go-to herb for the elderly or weak-minded. The Church, however, seems to put little faith in the herb. The Holy Mother often resorts to tried and true remedies to recall misplaced or muddled memories, namely the rack and the strappado. It’s amazing what a heretic might remember when the right pressure is applied, and no known herb gives an interrogator quite the same degree of satisfaction.
Memoricus Repeaticus root

Moon crystals are semi-precious stones used by herbalists and lay-healers to treat common maladies – most usually those of the flesh, including pock-marks and scarring brought about from urban diseases. Moon crystals can be used in a variety of ways, though most often the stones are simply rubbed across a patient’s body. Sometimes, however, a remedy will call for the stones to be ground into powder and taken as an analgesic. Unfortunately for most peasants, that particular term is rarely if ever explained for them ahead of time.
Moon crystal

The Chalice of Metamorphosis is a powerful pagan artifact from the era of the Erebornians. Legend holds that anyone or anything that drinks from the chalice will be transformed, sometimes into a creature of the imbiber’s choosing and sometimes not. The gold from which the chalice is made is cursed beyond a doubt, shaped as it is like folds of living skin. Though the object could prove useful in the future, I would prefer if it stayed buried firmly in the Erebornian’s twisted past.
Chalice of Metamorphosis

The Monstrance of St. Orthenius is one of the most valuable holy relics in all of Utherst, having been blessed by Orthenius himself in the year 221. It was brought to Hillbrandt in 339 by Father Albertinus, the first Bishop of Hillbrandt, and soon became the most valued treasure of the newly-formed diocese. According to local legends, the Monstrance is imbued with tremendous power which prevents the town of Hillbrandt from falling so long as the relic rests within her walls. It mysteriously vanished in the spring of 1223, sending the small mountain village into a bit of a panic. With good reason, no less, as the village was shortly thereafter attacked by a warband of orcs. I fear no one in Hillbrandt will rest easy until I return the artifact to the church’s care. Though,I can’t help but to imagine the power of a single man, utterly unconquerable while in the possession of a lone relic. The implications are tempting... and utterly corrupting.
Monstrance of St. Orthenius

Normally a fine piece of jewelry like this would be found in a noble lord or lady’s collection, but this particular amulet is different. It’s been enchanted, either by a priest or an alchemist. One must always take care when examining and wearing strange jewelry, for certain curses mask themselves brilliantly, taking the form of increased emotion or decreased discretion. Some cursed objects are said to contain shards of the Dark Prince himself, though said jewelry is almost as rare as sightings of the devil himself.
Amulet

The brother who lost this amulet must be kicking himself, assuming his fellow brothers haven’t already done it for him. It’s beautifully crafted, and the religious symbols etched into the metal are without a doubt signs of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. These amulets are often used as symbols of rank, belonging to either a knight-commander or even in some cases, masters. Who would allow such a thing to be taken from them? Such a shame... would be almost too much to bear. And why was it found near a ritual site. Some would say that’s evidence enough to warrant an arrest...
Magnificent amulet

This golden amulet gleams in the sunlight, a stark contrast to the lifeless black stone set into its center. Both sides of the amulet are marked with the strange scrawling of the Jad-Habaal, which only the wisest Viziers ever learn to write. It was most likely brought to the realm by the Duke, Manfred Gotfried and subsequently buried with him in the Alvaron cemetery. What his fascination with the Jad-Habaal could have been, I will certainly never know, though one could scarcely believe it was a wholesome thirst for knowledge.
Necklace of Death

This tombstone is made of solid black marble and etched with gold-leaf lettering. The grave of Baron Mansfeld; he must have been the richest old sod in Ultherst before he died. Er... I mean... God rest his soul.
Tombstone

There’s nothing out of the ordinary about this earring... except its location. I can’t help but to think that the petrified paladin nearby isn’t its original owner. At least, I hope not. He’d look awful in jewelry. Well, the trick is to find the earring’s twin. When I find its actual owner, she’ll have quite a bit of explaining to do.
Golden earring

The Libre Necronomicon is a collection of Old Lateran texts dealing with death, the afterlife, demons and the “netherworld.” There are several rites and incantations detailed within, most dealing with the summoning of lesser demons and the preparation of heretical masses. One spell, however, deals with the summoning of dead spirits. The text itself is rather gruesome...\\n\\nLet he who fears not the gaze of death look upon these words and marvel. To perform this particular rite, one must be in possession of the skull of the deceased in question and the Necklace of Death, an artifact which must have been crafted beyond the sight of God consisting of bits of bone and rotten flesh. Once the necklace is fitted over the incanter’s neck and the skull of the deceased is taken in hand, the necromancer must sing the litany penned below at the site of the deceased’s fall.
