Among them were several saints, including Saint Jakob, the Holy Smith. Saint Jakob, at the behest of his beloved king, forged a glorious shield to compliment David’s own favored axe. The shield, which one rested in the treasure of Bonorium, has been lost since the Barbarian occupation. Now, it would appear, it has been found again. Glory be.
King David's Shield

The art of crafting reflex bows was copied by Erebornian bowyers from the Elenians, a mysterious non-human race. Though Elenian bows remain unsurpassed in their craftsmanship, having been enchanted by now-lost druidic magic, the Erebornian’s modern equivalent is still comparable in terms of strength.\\n\\n Perhaps the best known (and most feared) bow among the Erebornians was the reflex bow of Grand Duke Liun'Dren, an Elenian noble, named String of Death. The Grand Duke used it tirelessly to defend his homeland until the Erebornians conquered the Elenian capitol in 395. The Grand Duke, ushering the rest of his forlorn people to safety, carried the bow with him to the Filkland Peninsula, where it was thought to be lost forever.
String of Death

The church claims this spear, golden, stained with blood that refuses to peel or flake, was used to pierce the First Prophet’s flesh as he hung from the cross in Jevaran. The deed was reportedly done by Effiteus, an Erebornian soldier, who sought to end the prophet’s suffering. He was crucified as well for his mercy, and was sainted in the year 223. After his death, Effiteus's spear was hidden by the faithful and supposedly blessed by the Second Prophet in the 35th year of our Lord. Since then, the spear has been passed from father to son, stolen, lost, found and lost again, but always it finds its way into the hands of those who would use it to defend the True Faith. Glory be!
Holy Spear

Urrm was an ancient wolf demon, worshipped both those who trace their lineage back to the Barbarian occupation in the 900s. Though his cult was largely destroyed many centuries ago, the worship of Urrm has continued in certain portions of the known, thanks in large part to an artifact known as Urrm's Eye.\\n\\n According to barbarian folklore, the eye was created by a pagan god called Odeman as a wedding gift for his terribly ugly wife, Uglinia. The relic was meant to shift Uglinia's physical form to match the shape of her soul. Urrm, true to his nature as a thief and liar, stole the eye and has used it since to bind all things evil and animalistic.\\n\\n It is believed that werewolves and Lycans will exist so long as the eye remains on this plane of existence. Whether there’s truth in that belief or not, few would argue that the Eye is as unsettling as it is sinister.
Urrm's Eye

Greater Morningstar, like it’s equally-poorly named cousin Lesser Morningstar, was crafted by Bonhart von Drichtmaul, the legendary blacksmith of Glatzburg. Both relics were powerful flails made to help Ultherstian defenders drive back the barbarian hordes of the early 900s. The magic power of the flails was granted by the Angel, Michael, who watched over Bonhart as he worked.\\n\\nGreater Morningstar is a two-handed flail, the counterpart of its one-handed cousin. Von Drichtmaul intended for both weapons to be used by the righteous, but they were lost relatively early in the Barbarian Wars. They were only reclaimed in 989, in the closing days of the war. It’s said neither weapon ever tasted of the blood of Von Drichtmaul’s intended victims.
Greater Morningstar

Venerius was an inquisitor who led trials against the Cult of the Derbingenians from 1055 to 1079. The Derbingenians, a cult based upon the tenants of maintaining a loose moral fiber and multiple partners, reigned largely from the shadows. In truth, an entire generation of youth was lost to the wiles of the Derbingenians before Venerius received the aid of Heaven itself.\\n\\n One evening, the Archangel Gabriel appeared before Venerius and bid him to embark without hesitation on a journey into the Moonshine Mountains where he was to spend thirteen days and thirteen nights immersed in prayer at the summit of the Moonshine Mesa. If, and only if, Venerius fulfilled the angel’s wishes, Gabriel promised to reveal the names and locations of every member of the Derbingenian cult. Venerius, overjoyed to hear his search was at an end, did as the angel commanded.\\n\\n For thirteen days and thirteen nights, Venerius prayed, fasting all the while with barely a drop of water to sate his thirst. When he awoke on the fourteenth morning, beside his head lay a golden necklace, thrumming with divine energy.\\n\\n The necklace was imbued with countless enchantments and Venerius used it to reveal all the Derbingenians, including Grand Duke Longhart of Glatzburg who had, according to witness testimony, upwards of sixty wives. When asked how he uncovered the cult’s leadership, Venerius responded that the angel Gabriel had come to him in a dream and bestowed upon him the knowledge. When church scholars later discovered the amulet’s powers, they named it “Venerius’s Dream” as a knowing jest.
Venerius's Dream

Victor's Pride was originally a gift from the Emperor of Lochland, Friedrich II, to Wilhelm II, rewarded for lending his aid against King Emmanuel of Calmariland. The weapon, consecrated by the Archbishop of Bonorium Clement III, who would later become Pope Paolus II, was intended to stand as a symbol of Ultherst’s unflinching dedication to the True Faith. When the Artheim Peace treaty ended the conflict, Wilhelm II fell into a dark depression. Rumor has it that he sold Victor’s Pride to help pay off Ultherst’s war debts. What self-respecting nobleman would buy a weapon from his king...?
Victor's Pride

Wolf Fang was the prized creation of the legendary blacksmith, Thaguul, who rose to fame after defeating Gorbul, the vengeful barbarian god of bravery and strength. The smith forged Wolf Fang for his son, Orth, knowing that one day, Gorbul’s revenge would fall upon his house. Little did Thaguul know just how thorough that revenge would be.\\n\\n After several years of being hounded and harassed by ice giants, the servants of Gorbul, young Orth vowed to reap a slice of revenge for himself. One evening, he allowed himself to be swallowed by an ice giant. Hiding in the creature’s belly, Orth made his way to Gorbul’s palace, where he freed himself from the ice giant’s stomach in the middle of the night. Orth went from room to room, slaying giants and their servants, before ending the night by stealing Gorbul’s jewels of power. Without them, Gorbul was something more than man but something less than a god, and the Pantheon, unwilling to belittle itself to keep him, cast Gorbul out. According to the legends, Gorbul went on to became a famous bard with an incredible falsetto.\\n\\nWolf Fang found its way to the Realm during the Barbarian Invasion of 951. After the defeat of the pagan intruders, it was lost together alongside many other barbarian treasures.
Wolf Fang

History remembers few men so well as King David, the Erebornian noble-son who killed his Emperor and founded a nation of his own design. Three pieces of wargear made David a tyrant on the battlefield: His mighty axe, which tasted the blood of the last of Ereborn’s Emperors; His shield, powerful beyond mortal comprehension and capable of deflecting even the deadliest of blows; and his mail, forged by Saint Jakob the Wondersmith, which many claim became a second skin for the young king. There is no greater honor than to hold his armor... save perhaps wearing it for yourself.
King David's Mail

Iron Mantle is a powerful relic that was bestowed upon Wilhelm van den Fergusson by the Grandmaster of the newly founded Order of the Holy Cross Geoffrey de Duby for lending his aid during the siege of Jevaran. According to historical resources, Wilhelm van den Fergusson was born in Ultherst and returned there after the Crusade to found the Brotherhood of the Righteous.\\n\\n Iron Mantle was supposedly blessed by Saint Desdemonus who also participated in the First Crusade and died at the walls of Jevaran during the final battle for the Holy Grave.
Iron Mantle

Brettonia, a province of Calmariland, has long been recognized as a breeding ground for masterful archers and the home of unsurpassable war bows. Perhaps the most renowned bow ever crafted in Brettonia is Royal Bane, which took lives of over twenty rulers of several countries during its 400 year lifespan. Royal Bane was the favored weapon of many assassins over the course of those four centuries, well-liked for its many enchantments and its unbelievable range. A skilled archer wielding Royal Bane can supposedly hit targets from a distance of several hundred yards. More than one monarch fell prey to Royal Bane while overseeing a battle or watching the walls of his keep. How did it find its way here, though?
Royal Bane
This ring is a symbol of your newfound office. Wear the rank of Inquisitorial Prosecutor with honor and distinction.
Prosecutor ring
This ring is a symbol of your newfound office. Wear the rank of Inquisitorial Judge with honor and distinction. May the ring’s many enchantments lead you swiftly to the course of justice, Your Honor!
Judge ring
This ring is a symbol of your newfound office. Wear the rank of Curial Inquisitor with honor and distinction. May the enemies of god tremble when they hear your name, Inquisitor!
Curial necklace
This ring is a symbol of your newfound office. Wear the rank of Commander Knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous with honor and distinction. God save the king!
Commander ring
You have been granted this valuable ring as insignia of your position after being promoted to Master Knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. God save the king!
Master ring
This bracelet is an insignia of your newfound office. Wear the rank of Seneschal Knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous with honor and distinction, always. God save the king!
Seneschal bracelet

This ring, bestowed upon only a handful of men in the past, is a symbol of your enduring service to the title of Baron of Asherbalt. May your noble guidance and powerful influence serve as an example for your fellow nobles.
Baron ring

This ring commemorates and celebrates your title as the Duke of Asherbalt. As a duke, you control a hold and all of the judicial and administrative powers that come with it. May your grace and civility serve as an example for your fellow lords.
Duke ring

As Grand Duke of Asherbalt, your lordship commands respect that most men could only ever dream of. As Grand Duke, you are eligible to serve in a multitude of royal offices, including the position of Royal Governor. Wear your heraldic ring with dignity and honor, my lord.
Grand duke ring

A Flail consists of a weight attached by a chain to a long pole. The weight is usually a metal ball with sharp spikes. Many versions of the flail incorporate several iron weights attached with multiple chains.\\n\\n Flail weapons were developed relatively recently, probably as a modification of the standard mace and club variants. The flail was likely a response by master weaponsmiths to the increasing protective quality of armor in the ninth century. Abnormal weight distribution gives a flail enough kinetic energy to cause terrible damage even to a heavily armored opponent.\\n\\n One-handed flails became rather popular with both heavy cavalry and infantry. In line with the perpetual evolution of warfare, after a time, infantrymen began to favor the two-handed flail. The larger, more unwieldy weapon allowed infantrymen one advantage other, shorter weapons had never before given them – the ability to take on cavalry without a pole weapon.
Flail

Rubies derive their name from the ancient Lateran word “Rubeus,” meaning red. These gems have been coveted since the dawn of pagan civilization both for their rich color and their rarity. Rarely are rubies larger than a single karat ever found, though large rubies often sell for more than similar sized diamonds. \\n\\n Flawless rubies of more than 20 carats are considered natural miracles. The biggest rubies are, as a symbol of the First Prophet's blood, often used in the crowns of monarchs and in ecclesiastical symbols of the Holy Mother Church. It’s ironic, or rather, a shame that the largest ruby ever discovered sits in the crown of Shah of Jad-Habaal. Rumor has it the Shah’s ruby is larger than a pigeon egg. Anyone who’s ever seen the Shah fight, however, can attest that the ruby in his crown is by far the largest of his... erm... stones.
Ruby
Five fingers and a palm guard. Enough said.
Gloves

The rosary—rosarium in Ancient Lateran—is a tool of the Holy Mother Church used by the faithful for counting uttered prayers. It consists of a string and a certain number of beads made of wood, metal, nacre or of other materials. It is said that a rosary worn around one's neck can protect the wearer from dark powers. Such theories, as of yet, have never been proven.
Rosary

A traditional suit of full plate mail consists of a cuirass with breast and back plates; a gorget; pauldrons; sleeves; vambraces with couters which cover elbows and forearms; a tasse; culets; a fauld; cuisses; and of course, greaves.\\n\\nA full suit of plate armor is often supplemented by an emblazoned surcoat. This tradition was born during the Crusades. Warriors returning from the Holy Land often kept their underclothing stylized after wearing it for added protection in the Holy Land, where the sun kept their metallic armor unbearably hot. An emblazoned surcoat resembles a tunic, variably with or without short sleeves. In the mild climate of the faithful world, with the exception of sunny Calmariland, the emblazoned surcoat surrendered much of its protective function.
Full Plate Mail

Sapphires are the second hardest material known to man. They’re so hard, in fact, that they can only be cut with diamond-coated tools, thus making cut sapphires a rare commodity. Superstitions claim the sapphire grants a multitude of pleasant powers, including a trend toward luck and protection from betrayal. They say women in love take chances only with drinking offered wine from sapphire cups, though where that particular belief originated, none can say.
Sapphire
Saber

Though the club is wildly believed to be man’s first crafted weapon, the axe was certainly the second. From cutting trees to killing prey, the axe is one of the cornerstones of human civilization. On the battlefield, axes are deadly, fear-inspiring space-controllers. Their range, swing breadth and power are absolutely unmatched in the modern world.
Axe

This strange arrow was used to kill the paladin, Eradim d'Chambrie. The arrowhead is serrated, making it difficult to remove. Moreover there's a cavity in the arrowhead in which poison was most likely stored. Enough to ensure a death, at least, if not a perfect shot.
Killer Arrow

Arrows speak for themselves. Their power and utility is unmatched in all of human history. When a men first spied distant prey, once hungered for flesh beyond his grasp, the first arrow was born – if only in spirit. They will and have revolutionized warfare. Given their ease of use, stopping power and ranged capability, there is little doubt the arrow will some day kill the sword.
Arrows

A backsword is a stabbing weapon with a long, straight blade. Together with sabers, the backsword is one of the principal weapons of cavalrymen, especially heavy cavalry.\\n\\n The average backsword is a little heavier than a saber and is crafted specifically for stabbing. One of the cavalry commanders of King Jonathann III, the renowned Grand Duke Horst van den Brecht, was quoted as saying that the only true weapons were stabbing weapons – other blades and blunts were the weapons of cowards. That particular commander trained his heavy cavalry in the art of backsword fighting to the exclusion of fighting with spears or standard swords. Despite the prevalence of bows on the battlefield, the backsword is still the favored weapon of cavalry charges looking to inspire fear.
Backsword
This is the scalp of a footpad, one of the many small-minded tyrants hunting the roads in and out of Glatzburg. Disgusting? Possibly. Barbaric? Certainly. Proof of services rendered? Most definitely.
Footpad Scalp
The scalp of an orc – probably worth some coin to the right collector.
Orc Scalp

This amulet, according to the assertion of the wise woman, Enrie Jungwirdt, was made by the ancient non-human Elenians. The wonderfully decorated charm shows the shining sun, its rays intertwined with the Elenian lunar runic script. There is a large cut diamond embedded in the middle of the sun; no doubt the relic is incredibly valuable.
Sun Charm

The Sun Crystal is a precious quartz gem with powerful magic effects – or so the Alchemists Guild claims. It it said the Sun Crystal possesses outstanding healing effects and is generally well-accepted by the human body. It’s used as an ingredient in multiple salves and poultices, and is found just about everywhere. Because of its ubiquitous nature, pinpointing the origin of sun crystals has been nearly impossible. The Holy Mother Church regards it as a gift of the Archangel Michael, but the Alchemists, to their peril, disagree...
Sun Crystal

Emeralds are precious stones prized for their magnificent green color. Prevalent jewelcutter wisdom indicates a well-cut emerald should shine the color of a spring meadow, but larger, different cuts change the light reflected. A single stone, depending on its cut, could appear as a shadow of blue, green, or yellow. Magical power is ascribed to the emerald as it is with other precious stones. Common thought describes the emerald a a stone of harmony, friendship, honesty and loyalty. It is said to protect against the evil eye and is worn to protect against epilepsy and cramps.
Emerald

This is a statuette of a strange barbarian god from the far North and distant past, named Bhelfelix. It’s made of polished jade and leavess a very gloomy impression. Watching the statuette, gazing into its cold, lifeless eyes, gives the sensation of being spoken to by someone standing a great distance away. Peculiar... and utterly sinister.
Bhelfelix Statuette

This is one of three Jade statuettes said to portray the three Archangels of the True Faith. This one is a representation of Gabriel, the Emmissary. Given its timeless stylization, the statuette is very difficult to age. It was probably carved many centuries ago, by an unknown master who drew inspiration from the then-prevalent Erebornian style of sculpting. It radiates a strange, cheerful energy, and clearly wasn’t made for the sake of decoration.
Statuette of Gabriel

This is one of three Jade statuettes said to portray the three Archangels of the True Faith. This one is a representation of Michael, the Warrior. Given its timeless stylization, the statuette is very difficult to age. It was probably carved many centuries ago, by an unknown master who drew inspiration from the then-prevalent Erebornian style of sculpting. It radiates a strange, cheerful energy, and clearly wasn’t made for the sake of decoration.
Statuette of Michael

This is one of three Jade statuettes said to portray the three Archangels of the True Faith. This one is a representation of Raphael, the Farseer. Given its timeless stylization, the statuette is very difficult to age. It was probably carved many centuries ago, by an unknown master who drew inspiration from the then-prevalent Erebornian style of sculpting. It radiates a strange, cheerful energy, and clearly wasn’t made for the sake of decoration.
Statuette of Raphael

This wax figurine is meant to represent the executioner, Friedrich Raubsticht. Although made from beeswax and crafted by someone clearly ignorant of any concept or notion of artistic virtue, the thing is clearly the Hillbrandt executioner. Though I’m no genius sorcerer or mad alchemist, I can say with some certainty that a wax doll with pins jabbed into its heart probably isn’t a harmless toy.
Wax figurine of Raubsticht

Under normal circumstances, there would be little to differentiate this heart from any other. It maintains the same weight, the same size, the same shape as any other I’ve ever seen. The lack of a body – and more so, the fiendish red glow of the thing – are offset only by its interminable beating. It’s intriguing and terrifying in the same instance. I should distance myself from it as quickly as possible, but after only I’m sure it isn’t of use.
Cursed Heart

Glaive is the general term for any of the various stabbing or cutting polearms whose popularity grew during the 11th century.n\\nGlaives are a typical infantry weapon due to their length. A typical weapon used is the so-called big-eared glaive, the blade of which is combined with two side spikes—ears.
Glaive

Where the armorer's opportunity to use thick leather ends, starts the manufacture of scale armor. This is a name for quite a wide variety of protective clothing comprising of a leather or flaxy coat fitted with smaller segments of hard thick leather or metal—scales, lamellas, discs—interconnected by sewing, leather string or sewn or riveted on the leather or flaxy coat itself.\\n\\nLikewise chain armor, this type of armor is ancient—it was already widely used by the warriors of the ancient world, e.g. the Erebornians called it lorica squamata. The production technology of scale and similar armor (eg. lamella armor) survived the decline of the Erebornian Empire. Any skilful provincial armorer can hammer small lamellas and cut out scales. Although the more perfect chain and later plate armor have massively spread during the last millenium, scale armor remained popular among warriors due to its lower acquisition cost.\\n\\nDespite its popularity scale armor has many disadvantages—it's usually heavier and compared to a chain armor it allows a lower level of dexterity. Another disadvantage is the hand protection—if the armor has any sleeves at all, the design of the scales rarely permits them to reach the elbows, so that every warrior has to solve the protection of hands and forearms separately. The layout of the scales also doesn't permit it to fasten the amour with a belt. Of course it is possible, but with tiny scales only. The bigger ones usually get stuck preventing the belt from being tightened and the warrior then has to bear the whole weight of the armor only on his shoulders.
Scale armor

This wedding dress was sewn by Baroness Helen von Hunth herself. Absolutely stunning... It's hard to believe what splendor the Baroness must have been able to embody in such a simple cut. She seems to have been inspired by the Vandenian Period, when simple dresses with scarce decorations were the dominant fashion. It's obvious that looking back into the past in combination with modern elements suits the fashion best. Of course... I’d know nothing about fashion.
Wedding Dress

The Holy Scriptures are the linchpin of the orthodox religion, thirteen books in total. They were written between 29 of the Old Era and 223 of the New Era. Within the many tomes comprising the Holy Scriptures are written the basic ideas, notions and principles of the orthodox religion, from the Creation of the World to the apocalyptic texts of the Book of Revelation. The Scriptures explain—or rather show—the essence of the orthodox religion, its principles and thesis, recommendations for the lives of ordinary people and strict rules for the lives of clergy and earthly rulers.\\n\\n It is a historic record of the life of the First Prophet and his twelve apostles supplemented with their ideas, visions and revelations. Throughout the whole Old World—neither in its pagan part—there is no such religious compilation existing in such a massive and comprehensive form like the Holy Scriptures. Not even the Jad-Habaal Ahran, reputedly the oldest religious book in the world and basis of this pagan desert realm's religion, is as rich in religious ideas and thesis as presented in the Holy Scriptures.\\n\\n That is why there's no need to explain why it became the linchpin not only of the whole orthodox religion but also of the whole world, interconnected inseparably with religion and the Holy Church. The Holy Scriptures consist of thirteen books written not only by the thirteen Prophets, but also by a multitude of their apostles and followers, thanks to whom were the Holy Scriptures integrated in the form we know today.\\n\\nThe Holy Scriptures consists of thirteen books written by the Thirteen Prophets and a large number of their followers, who rounded off The Holy Scriptures to the form we know nowadays.\\n\\nThe thirteen books of the Holy Scriptures are as follows:\\n\\nAnterima\\nSepria\\nBaktar\\nHepreth\\nKunkvas\\nHevlet\\nIbhar\\nShriva\\nTrina\\nNecra\\nJesmis\\nMalchra\\nApocalypse
Holy Scriptures

This little flask contains perhaps the most precious substance produced by the Church: Holy Water. It is used in almost every liturgical right, from baptism to the last unction. The bravest Inquisitors use it even to interrogate demons, or so the stories hold. Methods, however, vary from one source to the next...
Holy Water

This mysterious scroll is written in the ancient Elenian runic script. In the opinion of Albert Kelley, Master of the Royal Alchemist Guild, it is likely the formula, alchemical or otherwise, for a unique elixir. Regardless, the scroll itself is positively ancient; an archival treasure, if ever I’ve held one.
Mysterious Scroll

A Falchion is a short bladed cutting weapon. The origin of a Falchion is unclear; some master armorers suppose it developed from a sax once used in the Erebornian Empire. The blade is shorter than a sword or a cutlass, straight or slightly curved and usually single edged, though examples of double-edged hunting knives are known as well. A Falchion can be found in the Realm since the fourth century in the equipment of militia, i.e. the poorest warriors.\\n\\nA Falchion is supposed to have been used as a hunting weapon earlier than for military purposes. This is testified among others by Hermann the chronicler, who describes the murder of Grand Duke Brechthold II in the sixth century. The murderous weapon in this act was a Falchion, which Hermann describes like this: ...and suddenly Lork, ungodly villain sent by Satan, jumped out of his hideout with a sword at his side and with all his strength he stabbed the Grand Duke with a Falchion directly into his entrails... However, it was probably a special case and the Falchion still wasn't commonly used in the sixth century battlefields. Not even Hermann describes the weapon more carefully. On the other hand, he mentions another kill with a Falchion in similar circumstances, when King Varthold's retinue member... thrust a wide Falchion into Beneda as if he was a boar dashing against him...
Falchion

Topazes are beautiful gems, highly sought after by collectors and jewelers alike. In antiquity, they were referred to as chrysolite. According to the Erebornian philosopher Plinius, Topaz could be found on an island in the Great Sea that was named Topazos—from the word “topazien” that means “to assume”, because the island was allegedly difficult to find. Crusaders called this volcanic island the Isle of St. John and in present maps it is the Isle of Ziberget. However, as more and more Topazes found their way into the Realm, the Faithful soon realized that Topazos was not the only deposit of gems.
Topaz

Tridents are one of few “strange” weapons carried over from the Erebornian empire. It's a variant of a shorter infantry pike set not only with a single spike, but with three lined up on a single socket.\\n\\nHistoric sources regard tridents as the weapons of gladiators, the famous slave fighters who braved the arenas of the Erebornian cities. Historically, tridents weren’t used by Ereborniam infantrymen and fighters who mastered the use of a trident were dangerous both for the weapon’s tremendous killing power and for the exotic awe it inspired in foes.
Trident

The Troll Bile Herb, aptly named for its misshapen, stinking leaves, is used in various alchemical concoctions. I’m not sure who came up with the name... or how, for that matter. Most people’s first experience with actual troll’s bile is a long trip down a short throat, filled with slime from tongue to gullet.
Troll Bile Herb

Without a doubt, the worst-smelling part of a troll would have to be the gall bladder. The refuse they eat... gut-wrenching even to imagine. Of course, this assumption is made with the belief that somewhere, hidden in the twisted mass of malformed organs, lays an actual troll gall bladder. Dubious, but a subject of great debate.\\n\\n I can’t imagine what any God-fearing man or woman could possibly do with this... filth, but I do this know: it stinks like hell, and feels like fresh dung between the fingers. Disgusting.
Troll Bile

The crafting of Warhammers, more so than any other weapon in history, was a call of challenge from smiths to their fellows. These broad, crushing hammers were forged to combat the ever-increasing strength of plate mail. Needless to say, a weapon crafted to destroy plate mail could – and will – more than easily crush the thing wearing it.\\n\\nOne could say that a cavalry war hammer is a successor to the so-called Ultharian mace. This was a hammer-like weapon, which enabled Grand Duke Ulfmar and his mean to defeat the armies of King Philip Gaspar I in 1001.\\n\\n A classical war hammer is completely made of steel with roundels protecting and reinforcing the haft. The roundels are small, often decoratively formed, metal rings. The haft is approximately half a meter long.
Warhammer

War bows are a unique brand of weapon, recognized at once as the mark of a skilled archer and a discriminate killer. War bows, which are derived from the concept of the Elenian “Assassin Bow,” are powerfully built frames strung with only the strongest of twine.\\n\\n Many men will attest that an arrow loosed from a war bow is the equivalent of sword swing from thirty yards away.
War Bow

Great axes are the common man’s weapon of choice. Bearing the same shape and fuction as regular axes, the added strength of a longer haft and bigger blade make great axes excellent killing machines. Few men live to tell the tale after squaring off against an enemy wielding one of these terrible, maiming monsters.
Great Axe

Carrying a great club can potentially signify a great many things about a man.\\n\\n One, that he speaks softly. With a weapon of such incredible girth and power, the need to raise one’s voice becomes nonexistent.\\n\\n Two, that he walks tall. Men with proficiency wielding a great club rarely fear other, lesser warriors.\\n\\n And three, that he knows his business, and business is good. That’s really all there is to it.
Great Club

A large shield is an inherent part of every well-situated armored knight's equipment. It protects against the blows of enemy weapons as well as against bow fire. It developed from the so-called kite shield used approximately up to the tenth century. At that time the shields became smaller, thanks to the improving protection of the warriors with armor, and gradually lose the typical rounding of the upper edge.\\n\\nA large shield is used especially by the heavy cavalry, but it is favored among the infantrymen as well, because it offers much better protection than smaller round shields. In horseback fighting it's more difficult to handle and usually it doesn't allow cavalrymen to ward off on both sides, but the knights can compensate this with a suitable fighting skills and command of the horse.\\n\\nA large shield is made of wooden boards or plates so that the typical bulging out is reached. A shield of this construction protects its bearer better than a flat one, because hits can slip off it better. When composing a shield, it is necessary to glue the individual boards together and join them with an interlaid wooden rib or ironwork. The thickness of the shield varies, nevertheless, considering its large size, it usually isn't too thick, because its weight together with the ironwork would then become troublesome even for a knight.\\n\\nThe shield is covered with thick leather, usually cow skin—raw or soaked—so that it could better stretch and strain to the wood when it dries out. Instead of leather, thick canvasses or cloths are used as well. The leathering of the shield considerably improves its resistance, because the wood doesn't chop off or crack so easily under the blows.\\n\\nEdges of a covered shield are further reinforced with leather or metal and its surface is fitted with an umbo or a rib. At the end the shield is affixed with a sling to hang it on a warrior's shoulder and with handles that can be either leather, metal or wooden ones. A wooden horizontal handle is good for handling the shield in man-to-man combat, but it is practically useless when fighting on horseback.
Large Shield

According to folk tales, the Wolfsbane herb is effective against werewolves. Its smell is said to repel werewolves like plague winds, any weapon coated in Wolfsbane venom is said to kill the beasts in a single strike. The reliability of these tales is another question entirely.
Wolfsbane

From classical melee daggers used in face-to-face combat and classified as stabbing weapons, special types of throwing daggers developed in time to be used in ranged combat. Throwing daggers are lighter than normal daggers and their centre of gravity is moved to the upper part of the blade so that the weapon could rotate well and thrust better.\\n\\nUnlike standard daggers the throwing daggers usually lack the guard—it is useless for throwing, because its function is to protect the warrior's hand in melee combat. In other aspects the design of a throwing dagger corresponds to that of a classical one. Now and then double-bladed throwing daggers show up—the chance of hitting an opponent is increased and thus they are meant for fighters less skilled in throwing weapons.
Throwing Daggers

From classical hand axes used in face-to-face combat and classified as cutting weapons, special types of throwing axes developed in time to be used in ranged combat. Throwing axes are lighter than the common hand axes and their centre of gravity is moved so that the weapon could rotate well and thrust better.\\n\\nThrowing battle axes are usually all-metal; the classical wooden helve is missing and it's replaced with a metal handle furnished with spikes on each side. The axe itself can have only one blade with a counter-spike on the other side, or two blades. Thus the axe is conformed to the aim to hit the opponent almost every time with a blade or a spike, even when handled by a warrior unskilled in this type of combat.
Throwing Axes

Padded armor is the cheapest and subsequently least-effective armor at an infantryman’s disposal. Padded armor is little more than a second skin; a second skin that molds, freezes when wet and generally stinks. It is, however, better than wearing nothing at all. Only just, though. Only just.
Padded Armor

This stone stele is decorated with archaic ornaments and is covered in inscriptions from the Holy Scriptures. Judging from the Ancient Lateran used for the inscriptions, the stele must have been created very long ago—in the earliest days of the orthodox religion. The inscription... the inscription claims it is one of the foundation stones of the Temple of the First Prophet. I... I can scarcely believe it.
Foundation Stone of the Temple of the First Prophet
This monstrous, mutated heart once belonged to Lord Zargh, the unclean ruler of the hellspawn inhabiting the Devil's Caverns, near the ruins of the pagan city of Galibornium.
Lord Zargh's Heart

This is the last will of Father Bartholomeus, the first prefect of the Order of Saint Orthenius. This monastic order was founded to attend to the memory of Saint Orthenius, great liberator and patron of the Realm. Nevertheless, as one can read out from the text of the last will of Father Bartholomeus, the order had also another—secret—mission. Consider it by yourselves:\\n\\nRecently, horrible dreams have been haunting me and bringing me great pain. Of a death I dream that from the hands of unknown assassins came for all of my brothers that guard a great mystery along with me. The secret of the keys! It can never be revealed, nor forgotten. That is why I, Bartholomeus, the first prefect of the Order of Saint Orthenius, am writing this last will for it to rest with me in my grave for all of eternity thus preserving the secret of the keys. Let it be known to those who want to look for them that they have a form of jade statuettes and represent three emissaries of God—Raphael, Michael and Gabriel. Each of these statuettes rests in a different corner of the Realm, hidden and furnished with deadly traps for all those who are not from the Order of ours.\\n\\nThe statuette of Raphael was buried on the slopes of Moonshine Mountains at a holy tree near a village called Hillbrandt. That place was sacred, because it was there where Saint Orthenius himself converted to the one true faith hundreds of pagans that were resisting in a nearby stronghold until then.\\n\\nThe statuette of Michael was hidden in Galibornium, in a former Temple of all Gods, which was consecrated to the orthodox Temple of the Saint Mother of God by Saint Orthenius himself.\\n\\nLastly, the statuette of Gabriel was hidden in the first episcopal temple built on the Filkland Peninsula, in a city christened Alvaron, where an orthodox patriarch Basilian as a new Rex built his residence.
Bartholomeus's last will
Happiness is always something to yearn for... but I’ll be damned if it sells!
Gold

Master Edmond d'Arvias denies all accusations of heresy. He maintains that he is, and ever has been, the victim of heretical intrigues. However, he also claims to know who is truly responsible for the evil which has befallen Hillbrandt. According to d'Arvias, the Bishop Quentinus saw the Baroness, Linda van Gallagan, carrying the body of Gwenn von Weill away from the town cemetery one evening. The trouble is, before Master d'Arvias could find further evidence of the Baroness' guilt, Bishop Quentinus vanished and the Master himself came under suspicion. To prove that d'Arvias is innocent, I must first find the missing Bishop. However, if the evidence proves Master d'Arvias guilty, I will have no choice but to dismiss his testimony.
I've encountered an infernal creature, a lifeless homunculus which was indistinguishable from Master Edmond d'Arvias in every way.
I've encountered an infernal creature, a lifeless homunculus masquerading as a knight of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Balthazar confessed to overhearing Downay the gardener preaching that the rule of the Children of the New Order would soon come, allowing him to exact his revenge upon those most deserving.

Baron Dawn von Blutenreich was apparently cursed by his last wife, Miriam, for the alleged murders of his twelve former wives and their children. According to the tenets of the curse upon him, his unclean spirit shall haunt the Von Blutenreich family estate until the remains of his victims have been buried in a family grave.

The mad innkeeper, Bates, confessed that he and Norman the butcher have been murdering guests of the King's Road Inn in order to make various dishes from their flesh. The two performed their grisly deeds in a secret underground chamber, no doubt to further satisfy their own disgusting appetites.
Beckham the beggar confessed that although he paid his tab at the"The Hanged Man" inn with counterfeited gold, the coin had originally belonged to the priest, Gilbert.
Beckham the beggar allegedly overheard the merchant, Ihman ab Sahab, persuading Father Gilbert to deliver him the text of St. Orthenius' legend from Killian's Chronicle at any cost.
Braham the beggar reputedly overheard Dietrich, the gravedigger from Glatzburg, claiming he knew well who was behind the evil befalling the city.
Braham the beggar told me where the marauding knight, Benthley of Welshrem, dwells.
The stallholder, Suzan Brauchner, claims that Lotti Frankmüller was once the lover of Hans Falkner. Falkner, a convicted murderer and ravisher, was recently put to death by Hillbrandt's executioner.
Theil Brechthold, the alchemist of Hillbrandt, is able to turn any Philosopher's Stone I bring him into gold.
The Royal Master Armorer, Leon van den Brooks, identified the arrow that killed the paladin, Eradim d'Chambrie. He made it specially for Sven Larsen.
Leon van den Brooks of Alvaron is able to forge magical items from each Philosopher's Stone I bring him. For a considerable fee, of course.
Hans Thomas Brookwelt claims that Jeanette, the chabermaid, tried to bewitch him with dark magic.

William Burton, the landlord, asserts that he saw the innkeeper, Salena Flock, selling pieces of his missing brother's equipment. Consequently, he assumes that his brother, Ron, was robbed and murdered.
The time has come for me to make for the capital of the Realm, Alvaron, to uncover the author of the heretical letters sent to the executed Cardinal Truncquillius.
I have the consent of Inquisitor General Commendoni to arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert.
Inquisitor General Commendoni flatly denies the accusations of heresy raised against him and disavows any association with the Children of the New Order.

Cardinal Commendoni confessed that he is the dark high priest of the Children of the New Order. He also masterminded the grand heretical conspiracy which has robbed Ultherst of her innocence and left countless people dead. Commendoni claims that the goal of the Children is to release the Dark Prince, Satan, from his thousand-year imprisonment. The fool truly believes that the Prince of Darkness will allow the Children to rule over their fellow men as kings upon the Earth. Better a king in Hell than a servant in Heaven, thinks the man farthest from God's light; Commendoni would have traded all of our souls for the false promise of glory.
Sheriff Contemburry in Hillbrandt is paying a reward for every slain orc. A simple trophy, such as a scalp, will suffice for proof of a fresh kill.

I have heard that the soldier, Jullian, has not reported for duty in some time. He was allegedly courting the daughter of the merchant Stefan Reichmann, but was flatly refused by her father. The girl's father threatened him, stating that if he ever went near Natalia again, he would be killed.
I found the diary of Father Frederick. It contains, among other things, a very detailed description of the rite of exorcism—the cleansing of a human soul possesed by unclean spirits.

I have discovered the secret diary of the mad Duke, Rowan van Leerin. It contains a detailed description of the Duke's gruesome plan to dispatch His Majesty King Edward II and to usurp the throne of Alvaron.
I have discovered that the kidnapped child, Tom Clifford, was left among the infernal beasts inhabiting the Devil's Caverns. May God have mercy on his young soul.
Alphonso DiCerbio confessed that he has committed several crimes at the behest of Duke Rowan van Leerin, including the kidnapping of several innocent girls and little Tom Clifford.

Dietrich the gravedigger confessed that he was paid for supplying Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick with a corpse from the Glatzburg cemetery. Apparently, the Grand Duchess needed the body of a tainted girl which had been lying in sacred ground for exactly thirteen days in order to perform some wicked rite. How could such an upstanding woman have fallen so far? Are there no decent souls left in all of Utherst?

A stranger left a letter for me with Glatzburg's innkeeper, Weintraum. The letter warned me to be wary of Bishop Trevorius. Could it be that this letter was left by the same unknown patrons who initially tasked me with the investigation of Hillbrandt?

Downay the gardener confessed to being a member of the Children of the New Order. He also stated that he commited various crimes against God and King at the behest of the Seneschal, Jean de Guise of the Brotherhood of the Righteous.
Hans von Drichtmaul, the armorer, told me that no one has seen little Tom Clifford for some time. Tom is the son of Johaness Clifford, a servant of Duke Rowan van Leerin.
Grand Duke Drake Lambert claims that Inquisitor Nicolas raped his wife through the use of infernal powers known only to heretics.
Master armorer Hans von Drichtmaul is able to create various magical items from the Philosopher's Stone.

I found the broken blade of a magnificent dagger in Hillbrandt's cemetery. Beyond the shadow of a doubt, the blade was used to pry open the lid of a nearby coffin. A body... appears to have been stolen from within.
Baron Edger von Hunth possesses several bottles of Chateaux de Trebrechette.

The executioner, Yann Flemberg of Glatzburg, claims to have seen a group of hooded individuals not far from the gallows one night. They were carrying a large sack, inside of which could have been a human body. Flemberg thinks that Raimond Ventano was among them, but he could not be sure.

Flitz the beggar does not believe that the landsknecht, Olfghard, robbed and murdered the daughter of Stefan Reichmann. He does not believe that Oldghard is capable of commiting such a terrible crime.
Flitz the beggar witnessed the orcs dragging Bishop Quentinus out of Hillbrandt Cathedral during their last attack on the town.

The night Kurth Ollmier was murdered, Flitz the beggar witnessed someone climbing out of the merchant's window in Hillbrandt's inn. Although Flitz did not recognize the person in question, he remembers that the individual then met with the soldier, Millward, who may know the intruder's identity.
Lotti Frankmüller confessed to bewitching the executioner, Friedrich Raubsticht of Hillbrandt, because he executed her former lover, Hans Falkner.

Master Dieter von Gelbendiel witnessed a secret meeting between Cardinal Truncquillius and one of his minions. The Cardinal commanded the other individual to carry out all necessary preparations to perform a heretical mass.
Master Dieter von Gelbendiel supposes that the Cult of the Children of the New Order perished long ago and that it has no followers in the present day.
According to innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch, the gravedigger Dietrich from Glatzburg insisted that he knew well who was behind the evil plaguing the city.

Wanda Gielwitch thinks that the suspicion of heresy concerning the chambermaid Jeanette may very well be true because the maid wanted to buy from her an assortment of occult-related items, including bat's wings, snake's skin and moon crystal.
When arrested, the priest Gilbert pleaded guilty to all his sins and confessed that it was he who, with the help of dark powers, changed human ordure into gold.
I found out that the unknown patron who put me on the trail of the Cult of the Children of the New Order's crimes was in fact seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, Jean de Guise.
Petrier de Duby confessed that he had served as messenger for Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert and that he had delivered messages to other conspirators.

There were two letters from Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert found in a secret hiding place. In the letters, he gives instructions to his minions on how to proceed with their joint plan to disrupt the Realm.
According to the statement of Jean de Guise, Cardinal Gustapho Letti is conspiring with Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert and I should be wary of him.

Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous Jean de Guise confessed to his sins and admitted that he is a member of the heretical cult, the Children of the New Order. De Guise claims that he committed all of his crimes at the bidding of Cardinal Commendoni, the dark high priest of the cult.

As soon as the Grand Duke's maidservant Francessca Gulvardi was freed of the unclean powers that drove her to attack Bishop Trevorius, she confided in me the name of one of her tormentors. It was none other than the merchant, Raimond Ventano.
Guss Halworth witnessed the kidnapping of young Tom Clifford, the son of the servant Johaness Clifford. The alleged kidnapper was Alphonso DiCerbio.
According to Guss Halworth, the treasure of Bonhart von Drichtmaul is buried near the Devil's Caverns.

From the diary of the soldier Harph, I learned that it was he who committed the robberies and murders taking place after nightfall in the streets of Glatzburg. His undead monsters, once citizens of Glatzburg, were the result of numerous necromantic rituals.

From the diary of the wicked soldier Harph, I discovered, among several other gruesome details, that he had been caught by Tinthan the comedian upon entering the deserted sewers with his undead minions in tow.
Some of the soldiers in Glatzburg are intrigued by the rather large sum of money their fellow Harph has suddenly acquired. While others are living hand to mouth, Harph is spending money like water.

I found a scrap from a beautifully embroidered cloak beside a desecrated grave in the Glatzburg cemetery. Evidence suggests that it is a scrap from the cloak of a heretic, who no doubt stole a buried body from the grave. Later, I discovered that the fabric came from the cloak of Grand Duke Robert Heidrick.
A culprit has left deep footprints in the clay around one of the robbed graves. This particular type of clay can only be found here in the cemetery and nowhere else in the vicinity of Alvaron.
Before he died, Kurth Ollmier allegedly mentioned that he had found a buyer for a certain book that had come into his possession after many years of strenuous searching.

Although appearances are often deceptive, the twelve-year old, Horst, is in fact a son of the Wolf-Prince Wulfhyrr. It was he who allowed Wulfhyrr and his pack entrance into the town upon the eve of every full moon, allowing them to seize their innocent victims!

It's likely that it was Lotti Frankmüller who cursed executioner Raubsticht. She was, as I've discovered, the lover of the late Hans Falkner, a murder who was recently executed in Hillbrant. The curse, therefore, may be Frankmüller's misguided attempt at exacting revenge for the death of her nefarious lover.

I have found the  blade of a magnificent dagger in the cemetery. Beyond a reasonable doubt, it was used to pry open the lid of a coffin from which a dead man's body was unceremoniously disinterred. Later, I discovered that the dagger belonged to Judge Vallarian.
The chambermaid, Jeanette, claims that she is the victim of Hans Thomas Brookwelt's witchcraft. She claims that Brookwelt "got ahold of her" with the aid of infernal powers.

Johaness Clifford confessed that his master, Duke Rowan van Leerin, has been keeping girls imprisoned in the secret sanctum beneath his home. Apparently, the Duke threatens to sacrifice them. If true, then this madman must be stopped before innocent lives are lost.

The soldier, Jullian, kidnapped Natalia Reichmann to extort her father, Stefan Reichmann. Julian is hiding together with the kidnapped girl in a deserted chapel near the Dragon Rock. There is a madness in the boy's eyes beyond anything I have ever witnessed. For Natalia's sake, I must either take him into custody or else see him cut down. I fear there can be no reasoning with him.

The wise woman, Enrie Jungwirdt, claims to have had a vision. In it, the Archangel Gabriel appeared to her and heralded the coming of the dreaded fallen angels: Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie. Should her dreams become reality, I dare not think of what is to come.
The wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt advised me that the undead Duke Istwan de Bragho could only be slain with holy water.
The wise woman Enrie Jungwirdt is able to brew miraculous potions from sprigs of Devil's Root.
Enrie Jungwirdt had a vision in which she witnessed the kidnapping of Raquel Gielwitch. She saw two men carrying the girl's unconscious body to the house of Duke Rowan van Leerin.

If I find a rare herb, known only as "Troll's Bile," the alchemist Alberto Kelley can brew a magic potion from it that will reverse the negative effects of the spell Vanessa of Kentworth cast upon herself. The herb can be found growing somewhere in Schwarzwald.
Master of the Royal Alchemist Guild, Alberto Kelley of Alvaron, is able to turn any Philosopher's Stone I bring him into gold.

Kenthwarr the werewolf told me where the treasure of the executed Baron Decard of Longhorn is buried in the Schwarzwald. I also received a map which will no doubt lead me to it, should I prove incapable of finding it on my own.
The members of the Highest Inquisitorial Tribunal are the Inquisitor General, Cardinal Commendoni, and the Cardinals Gustapho Letti, Giovanni Timore and Severtinus.
Sven Larsen confessed that Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, Jean de Guise, paid him to murder Eradim d'Chambrie.

Linda van Gallagan maintains that she, along with her fellow heretics, invoked the fallen angel, Arthamon, near the Dragon Rock. I should speak with someone more well-versed in demonic lore to ascertain the threat this terrible evil poses... and to better understand the dark ritual which may have ushered it into our world. First Prophet, watch over me.

Baroness Linda van Gallagan confessed that she murdered the merchant Kurth Ollmier to retrieve the "Libre Daemonium," written by the dark prophet Lucius. She also confessed to poisoning Baroness Gwenn von Weill and then, along with Sam Riemann, removing the poor girl's body from its grave. All of this she did, supposedly, at the bidding of Judge Vallarian in order to perform a heretical mass. According to Van Gallagan, during the mass, the three allegedly invoked the fallen angel, Arthamon, the dreaded Demon of Fire and the Master of Ruin. I pray that the Baroness is mistaken.
Linda van Gallagan denies the charge of heresy raised against her and asserts that she has an alibi which her husband, Baron Robert van Gallagan, can confirm.
Cardinal Gustapho Letti told me that during a confession, the First Knight, Rodrigo de Velacor, admitted to murdering His Majesty, King Edward II.

Cardinal Gustapho Letti is convinced that I must fully investigate the suspicions surrounding the Inquisitor General, Cardinal Commendoni. It is of the utmost importance that I discover if he truly is the dark high priest of the Children of the New Order or not.

It is doubtless that Cardinals Severtinus and Giovanni Timore were corrupted by the Children of the New Order. I must pressure them to grant me their consent to charge and arrest Inquisitor General Commendoni at any cost!
I managed to get Cardinal Letti's consent to arrest the Inquisitor General Commendoni.

Cardinal Letti is convinced that with the aid of the Libre Daemonium, we will be able to confirm—or refute—whether or not there is any merit to the claims that heretics belonging to the Children of the New Order have summoned the fallen angels to our world.
Cardinal Letti is certain that Inquisitor General Commendoni is hiding in the Archiepiscopal Dungeon.
Grand Duchess Liana Lambert confessed that the charge of rape brought against the priest Nicolas was, in fact, based upon a lie.

According to Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert, the priest Marcius may be the only person capable of identifying the author of the heretical letters sent to Cardinal Truncquillius in Glatzburg. As an Archiepiscopal clerk, he may recognize the handwriting of the letters.

Jean de Guise lied to me—he is not the unknown patron who put me on the trail of the Children of the New Order. It was, in fact, the Grand Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, Christoffer de Malamert. Jean de Guise is a heretic who has betrayed his Brotherhood and become a servant of infernal powers.
While arresting Vick Length, I found an ancient Elenian amulet on him.

The archiepiscopal clerk, Marcius, certified that the handwriting found in the heretical letters addressed to the executed Cardinal Truncquillius belonged to none other than the Inquisitor General, Cardinal Commendoni.
Father Marcius confessed that he is the lover of Grand Duchess Liana Lambert and that they revel in perverse bodily delights in the city cemetery.

Cardinal Truncquillius had several anonymous letters on his person. In said letters, an unknown heretic from Alvaron encourages him to proceed with the realization of the plan and to continue as planned with the invocation of the fallen angel, Baphomet, in Glatzburg.
The soldier, Millward, stated that he saw Master Edmond d'Arvias opening the town gate for the orcs during their recent attack on Hillbrandt.
The night Kurth Ollmier was murdered, the soldier, Millward, caught Baroness Linda van Gallagan climbing out of the window of the merchant's room in Hillbrandt.

Nina Monthreass was kidnapped by werewolves after they were allowed into Alvaron by Horst, a child with sinister ambitions. The werewolves entered the city through a small gate after the devilish little heretic used a dark spell to lull the gate guards into a deep slumber.

Two years ago, Corin Morray witnessed a gathering of heretics in the chambers of Crown Prince Louis' in the royal palace. They were performing an unholy rite which eventually led to the prince's death. Morray claims to have identified one of the heretics as the royal counselor, Verenicus.

I wish that I could have spoken with Kathryn Winhold. She, along with Corin Morray, witnessed the performing of heretical rite in the royal palace two years ago which left the crown prince, Louis, dead. Regrettably, she was executed that same year. There may yet be a way to discover what she knew, though... I should ask Cardinal Letti for guidance.

According to the historian, Killian, Saint Orthenius was entombed in the year 235 alongside a relic known only as "the Inquisitor." The tomb was then sealed by members of the Order of Saint Orthenius using magical jade statuettes of the angels Gabriel, Michael and Raphael. The statuettes were subsequently hidden in different locations throughout the Realm where they were to remain until the day a new protector of the Realm rises to claim them.
I found someone's necklace in the heretical sanctum near the Glatzburg gallows. I have no doubt that a witches' sabbath took place there recently.
I found someone's necklace in the heretical sanctum near the Glatzburg gallows where a witches' sabbath took place recently. As it happens, the necklace belongs to Commander Ethien de Pasque.
I have found the testament of Saint Bartholomeus. It contains the location of the jade statuettes of Gabriel, Michael and Raphael. With it, I should have no trouble finding them.
At the scene of the crime—where the paladin Richwald d'Blazier became the victim of an unknown heretic's dark magic—I found a golden earring.

I found a scrap from a beautifully embroidered cloak beside a desecrated grave in the Glatzburg cemetery. Evidence suggests that it's a scrap from the cloak of the heretic who absconded with the missing corpse.

I have discovered that the Children of the New Order have truly invoked the fallen angel, Arthamon. I fear that the darkness I have witnessed thus far pales in comparison to the shadow cast by this... abomination.
I have discovered that the Children of the New Order have invoked the fallen angel, Baphomet. My soul quakes to imagine their evil plot drawing nearer to fruition!
I have discovered that the Children of the New Order have successfully invoked the Succubus, Cerdie. I must undo this terrible evil if ever the souls of men are to be free again!
I have found the spellbook of the Elenian Grand Duke, Fae'Darlion.
If I could determine to whom the arrow used to kill Eradim d'Chambrie belonged, I would have solid evidence against the murderer.

I have managed to lay hands upon a copy of the cursed "Libre Necronomicon," which is used by the heretics in their foul necromantic rites. There is a method described within which details how one might summon the ghost of a deceased man and force it to answer his or her questions!

I have stumbled across a clearing not far from Hillbrandt where a witches' sabbath must have taken place. Upon the ground, a large pantagram has been etched in blood. The corpse lying at its center has had its heart rather cruelly...removed. It also appears that a great black egg was inserted in its place. Angel's mercy, what is this? Something appears to have hatched from it!

It seems that a witches' sabbath similar to the one which took place in Hillbrandt was performed in Glatzburg as well! This discovery is ill-received. The sabbath in Hillbrant allegedly invoked the fallen angel, Arthamon. What unclean spirit, then, did this ritual bring forth?

Norman the butcher confessed that he, along with the innkeeper, Bates, have been murdering guests of the King's Road Inn. The two have been making various dishes from the flesh of their victims. How depraved must these two men be to dine on the flesh of their fellow man?

If the mad butcher Norman was telling the truth, there should be an entrance located in the kitchen of the Bates's inn which leads to a secret underground chamber. Apparently, that is where the murderers have been performing their unthinkable deeds.

An investigation is underway in the case of the murder of Bishop Trevorius. As it stands, I am the primary suspect. I should unmask the true culprit as quickly as possible, lest I feel the merciless pull of the rack!
Sheriff Gendriel Smith in Glatzburg is paying for the death of local rogues. Vigilantes presenting Smith with proof of their kills will be rewarded with a rather hefty sum of gold.

Sherrif Henry Portmann is offering a substantial reward to anyone who can present him with a trophy from a slain werewolf. Werewolves have been terrorizing the areas surrounding Alvaron, and have even been found in the city's streets. Any aid I can provide to the local guardsmen would be greatly appreciated.

While examining the body of King Edward II, I discovered traces of skin and dried blood beneath his nails. It is clear that the king wounded his murderer in the throes of his own assassination. The wound was likely inflicted to the suspect's face, judging from the nature of their struggle.

I found the landsknecht, Olfghard, who is accused of murdering Natalia Reichmann. According to his testimony, however, the daughter of the merchant Stefan Reichmann was kidnapped by the soldier, Jullian.

Although Olfghard is uncertain, he believes he may have seen the missing Baroness, Linda van Gallagan, making her way toward the iron mines in the company of orcs. He insists that she went willingly, as she showed no signs of struggle or distress.

Paul Hammerhand, the blacksmith's boy, witnessed a heretical sabbath near the Dragon Rock. He swears that the ritual called forth a winged demon, but other than a handful of vague details, the child could offer no true description of the beast. The poor lad must have been scared senseless by what he saw.

In an abandoned home in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains, I came across Paul Hammerhand, the son of Hillbrandt's blacksmith,Victor Hammerhand. The child was positively exhausted and burning with fever when I found him. Apparently, he hid to stay out of sight of the heretics he saw performing a witches' sabbath near the Dragon Rock. In the process, and chilled to the bone, the boy must have taken ill. The poor thing; no one should ever be forced to witness the things young Paul must have seen that night, let alone a child.

Commander Ethien de Pasque confessed under pain of torture that he sold his soul to Satan when he, along with two other heretics—the merchant, Raimond Ventano, and Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick— invoked the fallen angel, Baphomet, in the Sanctum of Chaos. The three hoped to curry favor with the demon lord so that they might use his power to quicken the rise of evil upon the Earth.

Commander Ethien de Pasque claims to have witnessed a terrible crime committed by the Grand Duke, Robert Heidrick. De Pasque claims that he witnessed Heidrick desecrating a grave in the Glatzburg cemetery. He also claims to have seen Heidrick carrying away the corpse, afterward.

May the angel Michael bear witness to my deeds: I have achieved the unthinkable! I have banished the three fallen angels—Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie—back to the pit from whence they came! The Children of the New Order have failed to bring Hell to our world. Praise be to God Almighty, and may the angel Gabriel watch over my weary soul!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for the renegade soldier, Harph. I simply have to ask Sheriff Smith to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for the merchant, Alphonso DiCerbio. I have but to ask Sheriff Smith to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for defendant Raimond Ventano. I simply have to ask Sheriff Smith to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for Commander Ethien de Pasque. I have but to ask Sheriff Smith to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!

I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for the Grand Duchess, Yulliette Heidrick. I have but to ask Sheriff Smith to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!

I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for defendant Downay, the gardener. I have but to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for defendant Sven Larsen. I simply have to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for Duke Verenicus of Khentt. I have but to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for Father Gilbert. I simply have to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for defendant Steinger. I have but to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
I now possess enough evidence, as a Judge of the Holy Office, to hold a trial for defendant Vick Length. I simply have to ask Sheriff Portmann to deliver the prisoner and the trial may commence!
The Sheriff of Alvaron, Henry Portmann, pays a substantial reward to anyone that brings him a trophy from a slain werewolf.
The varlet, Quarim, believes that the curse placed upon Friedrich Raubsticht the executioner is an act of revenge. However, Quarim has no suspicions as to whom the dark magic might belong.

The executioner's varlet, Quarim, testified that the night the monstrance of Saint Orthenius was stolen, he witnessed the priest, Romius, leaving Hillbrandt's cathedral. Supposedly, the priest was hiding something beneath his cowl.

Bishop Quentinus witnessed a band of heretics stealing the corpse of the late Baroness Gwen von Weill from the cemetery in Hillbrandt. The Bishop testified that one of the heretics was undoutedly the Baroness, Linda van Gallagan.

After carrying out the autopsy of Baroness Gwenn von Weill, Bishop Quentinus believes that an infernal creature must have hatched from the black egg imbedded in the late Baroness' chest during the heretical rite performed near the Dragon Rock.

Many members of the royal regiment of Glatzburg are curious as to how their fellow soldier, Harph, managed to accrue such an impressive fortune in such a short amount of time. Whereas other soldiers are living hand to mouth, Harph is spending money like water.

It is likely that Hillbrandt's executioner, Friedrich Raubsticht, was bewitched by someone close to Hans Falkner, the convicted murderer and ravisher. At the gallows, Falkner threatened Raubsticht, stating that his death would be avenged.

Friedrich Raubsticht claims to have witnessed Suzan Brauchner skulking near the mass grave in Hillbrandt's cemetery one evening. She was apparently looking for something, though what, he could not say.

Thomas Reitdorf alleges that he saw, with his own eyes, Edmond d'Arvias opening the gates of Hillbrandt to the orcs during their recent attack on the town. Many of Hillbrandt's citizens claim that Reitdorf's opinions are wild and unfounded, but I can let no mention of heresy go unnoticed.
Sam Riemann is convinced that the blacksmith's son, Paul Hammerhand, is possessed by unclean spirits. He advised me to be wary of the child. Could the boy's mischief truly be so threatening?

Sam Riemann pleaded that he, along with Baroness Linda van Gallagan, attended a witches' sabbath near the Dragon Rock. During the rite, the inquisitorial judge, Vallarian, supposedly invoked the fallen angel, Arthamon.

Sam Riemann refuted Linda van Gallagan's accusation that he both prepared and attended a heretical sabbath near the Dragon Rock. It is worth noting that Riemann stated only that the Baroness lied, but mentioned nothing of his own innocence.

Sam Riemann swore that he witnessed Edmond d'Arvias commanding the orcs during their recent attack on Hillbrandt. In his opinion, there can be no doubt that Master d'Arvias was in complete control of the brutish beasts.

The royal vice-governor of Hillbrandt, Baron Robert van Gallagan, suspects Duke Weinberg of committing heresy most foul. According to Van Gallagan, the Duke must be conspiring with infernal powers because his family and his possessions have been miraculously unharmed by the Scourges of God. A strange coincidence, perhaps, but heresy? I should investigate to be sure.

While examining the body of King Edward II, I discovered traces of skin and dried blood beneath his nails. Doubtless, the King wounded his murderer during the attack—likely across the face, judging from the nature of their struggle. Consequently, I have discovered that Rodrigo de Velacor possess facial wounds; wounds which could have easily been made by the desperate clawing of a man destined for death. I should investigate further...

The priest, Romius, confessed to serving the vampire Herbertius, the former Bishop of Asherbalt. Apparently, he had been satiating the abomination's damnable thirst with offerings of his own blood. Romius also confessed to stealing the monstrance of Saint Orthenius at the bidding of his master. How could two men who were once so blessed fall so far from the light of God? Such a shame.

Duke Rowan van Leerin pointedly denies the allegations brought forth by Alphonso DiCerbio. According to DiCerbio's testimony, the Duke is behind the kidnappings of young girls in Glatzberg. The Duke, in turn, claims that DiCerbio is trying to ruin him for attempting to disclose the trader's less than savory business affairs.

Duke Rowan van Leerin pleaded guilty to kidnapping several innocent girls in Glatzberg, claiming that he needed them in order to perform a perverse heretical rite. Through said rite, he hoped to animate a statue of King Edward II. He then intended to use the resulting homonculus to seize control of the throne.
Several residents of Hillbrandt reputedly saw Master Edmond d'Arvias opening the town's gates for the orcs during their last raid.

There is a rumor in Hillbrandt that Herbertius, the former Bishop of Asherbalt, sold his soul to Satan in exchange for tremendous power and eternal life. Now, if the rumor holds true, his broken body has risen from the grave to repay his end of their devilish bargain. The word "vampire" hangs from several lips, but few dare speak it aloud.

If I require weapons or armor during my stay in Hillbrandt, I should look to the blacksmith, Victor Hammerhand, for assistance. Potions and spells are sold by the herbalist, Ellisia Würtenrodt, the priest, Father Dominicus, and by the alchemist, Theil Brechthold. The stallholder, Suzan Brauchner, reputedly sells almost anything which can be sold, and the same can be said for the innkeeper, Joseph Truthorn.
A deep despair has settled over Hillbrandt. The faith is waning and the people are disillusioned. I fear that dark days lay before us.

The residents of Hillbrant have recently been plagued by roving bands of trolls who have come down from the mountains. The troll tribes are growing more aggressive by the day and will soon become a more serious threat if left unchecked.
The inhabitants of Asherbalt were massacred by the orcs. No one knows from whence the devils come, but they seem to have taken up residence in the abandoned iron mines.
Sheriff Contemburry is offering a reward for slain orcs. Interested parties need only bring a trophy from every kill to earn their coin.

A vicious storm darkened the skies over Hillbrandt recently, but the accounts of its passing are as varied as they are strange. A handful of locals attest that it was an ordinary, albeit extremely powerful, gale. They say the winds were brutal, but not altogether outside the realm of the natural. Others swear that they saw the silhouettes of demons dancing in the clouds. The one fact that everyone seems to agree upon, however, is that the storm was accompanied by a terrible racket, a sound that many described as "a mad shrieking." No mention of demons should be taken lightly, and never have I witnessed a "shrieking" storm. I should press the townsfolk for more information.
It seems that Father Quentinus, the Diocesan Bishop of Hilbrant, went missing during the recent orc attack.

I have heard that the landsknecht Olfghard robbed and murdered the daughter of Stefan Reichmann. He was recently taken into custody, but managed to escape and has now gone into hiding. If I can find him, I can press him for answers... and, perhaps, grant the peace that both Natalia and Stefan Reichmann deserve.

Hillbrandt was recently sacked by a horde of orcs. The beasts managed to infiltrate the town under the cover of darkness, catching the town's guardsmen unawares. Many innocent lives were lost before the infernal creatures were driven back.

There are still a few residents of Hillbrandt who believe that Master Edmond d'Arvias is innocent, despite several eyewitness accounts that he opened the town's gates for the orcish horde. They are convinced that he could, or rather, would never surrender himself to infernal forces, and attest that the man would sooner die than allign himself with the pawns of Satan. A noble sentiment, indeed... but is there any truth to it?

I have heard several people discussing the tale of Saint Orthenius as of late. According to legend, at the dawn of Alavaron's recorded history, St. Orthenius defeated the pagans with the aid of a powerful relic known only as "the Inquisitor." Before his death, St. Orthenius foretold that when the true faith was most endangered, the Inquisitor would find its way into the hands of a new protector who would wield it against the enemies of man and God alike.

According to legend, the Tree of Death which stands near the Dragon Rock is inhabited by the spirits of fallen marauders. They are the remnants of the barbarian army which was routed and slaughtered there in the year of 988 by the cavalry of Duke Welliar as they attempted to flee north of the Moonshine Mountains.

I have heard the story of the Dead Man's Stone, which stands near Hillbrandt's gallows. According to legend, the lamentations of tortured souls can be heard there. People say, if you listen closely, you can hear the mournful whispers of the sinners bound to the stone by God's wrath.

I have heard the legend of King Harlior, the last ruler of the Thron Empire. According to the tale, King Harlior swore an oath never to leave his realm until the orcish ruler, Khan Rashgar, whose armies crushed the Thron Empire long ago, lay dead. Since his death, Harlior's spirit has supposedly wandered the vast honeycomb of passages beneath the Moonshine Mountains, awaiting the coming of a savior to slay the orcish Khan and release him from his self-imposed torment.

I have heard the townsfolk spreading disturbing rumors concerning Duke Weinberg. The people think it quite strange that while others have suffered greatly from the Scourges of God, Duke Weinberg seems entirely untouched. There have been no reports of the man losing either family or property as of late, nor has he made any mention of his own losses. A curious turn of events, to be sure, but could it be the trappings of some foul bargain?
The foothills of the Moonshine Mountains are said to be infested with giant spiders and bats. I should take care when venturing beyond Hilbrandt's walls.

I've heard rumors of buried treasure near the Dragon Rock. Supposedly, the barbarian marauders left it behind during their rout at the hands of Duke Welliar's calvary more than four centuries ago. Despite their best efforts, the Duke's men never found it. All the more reason to try finding it for myself. Perhaps I'll prove a sharper detective than Duke Welliar's calvarymen.
Hillbrandt is ruled by Duke Weinberg, the acting royal governor. The Duke's vice-governor is Baron Robert van Gallagan, and there is little love lost between the two gentlemen.

Hans von Drichtmaul sells weapons and armor in Glatzburg. The wise woman, Enrie Jungwirdt, and the alchemist, Paolus Ventimus, will sell me potions and various magic wares at reasonable prices. The innkeeper, Wanda Gielwitch, and the landlord, Ludwig Weintraum, both trade in odds and ends, and Alphonso DiCerbio is more than willing to offer his wares as long as I leave alone the question of their origin.

The people of Glatzburg are in a state of perpetual fear. Whatever darkness has befallen the realm has left their once eager hearts barren and cold. They move about with eyes downcast, and smiles are a commodity rarer than twice-blessed gold. If ever there was doubt that our world is in need of hope, the commonfolk of Glatzburg are proof to the contraire.

The people of Glatzburg are being terrorized by the living dead. The fiends come at night and stalk the city streets, brutalizing baron and beggar alike. No one seems to know from where they come or to where they go before the coming of dawn each morning, but the fact remains: no one is truly safe within the walls of Glatzburg under cover of night.

The people of Glatzburg believe that Satan himself dwells in the caverns near the ruined pagan city of Galibornium. They call them the "Devil's Caverns," and refuse to go near them for fear of their lives.

Some of the residents of Glatzburg are so frightened by the coming dark that they have begun labeling their brothers and sister heretics for fear of being labeled themselves. This madness, this betrayal of Reason, must come to an end.

It seems that a storm much like the one seen over Hillbrandt blew through Glatzburg recently, as well. Everyone who saw the storm claims to have seen demons dancing in the clouds, and to have heard the very same shrieking associated with the Hillbrandt gale. This cannot be a coincidence. I fear that some terrible evil is afoot in Glatzburg.

There are bands of bloodthirsty rogues led by the marauding knight, Benthley of Welshrem, stalking the woodlands near Glatzburg. They attack merchant caravans and lone wanderers alike, and few of their victims escape with their lives. They have a base of operations somewhere deep in the forest outside Glatzburg, but no one has pinpointed the exact location.
