The greatest number of remnants from the ages long past is said to be found in the woods around the estate of the von Hunths family.

I've discovered that Father Frederick, the fellow mentioned by the spirit of Bishop Trevorius, was a rather... odd priest. He fell victim to the plague two years ago, but was supposedly quite a reputable exorcist in his time.
Francessca Gulvardi apparently attempted to murder the Diocesan Bishop Trevorius recently. There are rumors that she's been possessed by dark powers, but none can be sure.

I've heard that several young girls have disappeared from Glatzburg and its surrounding holdings recently. No one seems to know where they've gone, but the implication is that they were kidnapped. The question is, were they taken by lusty rogues? Or by the servants of a darkness most foul? In truth, neither answer is more comforting.

The ruins of an ancient pagan city, Galibornium, are said to be located near Glatzburg. The city stood for centuries before the fall of the pagan kingdom of Ereborn, which was conquered by the armies of St. Orthenius. Galibornium, like so many other pagan strongholds, was sacked by the armies of St. Orthenius during their glorious march across the continent, leaving the city little more than a bare and desolate ruin. No man has dared settle within her since. Devoid of human life, and home only to lost souls, the city's sun-bleached innards are now the plaything of wayward demons. Those in search of the lost city should be wary, for one can never be too sure what will turn up where the pagans once dared to tread.

I have heard stories of the ancient sewer systems beneath Glatzburg. They were built shortly after the city was founded, but were eventually sealed and filled. They have since fallen into distant memory. Could it be that sewers were not so thoroughly sealed as everyone seems to believe? Could there be evil lurking, even now, just beneath the surface of the Earth? I should investigate the matter myself.

The residents of Glatzburg are positively terrified of an evil they claim is inhabiting the city's ancient sewer system. According to eyewitness accounts, the living dead are rising from the sewers, once thought to be sealed, under the cover of night to murder and wreak havoc. Many fear to open their doors after dark, and only the bravest—or most foolish—dare to walk the streets of Glatzburg by the light of the moon.
It is rumored that the freshly dead have a habit of rising from their graves in Glatzburg.
I've heard rumors that the former royal vice-governor of Glatzburg, Istwan de Bragho, has risen from his grave to exact his revenge upon those who orchestrated his capture and execution.

Glatzburg is ruled by the royal governor and Grand Duke, Robert Heidrick, and the royal vice-governor, Duke Rowan van Leerin. The locals seem to care little for either, though, and suspicion hangs heavily over the heads of both. The situation in Glatzburg is dire, indeed.

Apparently, there is a series of caves near Glatzburg which the locals refer to as "the Devil's Caverns." Legend has it that they lead directly to Hell and are populated by hordes of filthy, flesh-eating demons. The townspeople of Glatzburg refuse to go anywhere near them as a result.

I have been told by the locals that there may be lost souls trapped beneath the Colosseum of Galibornium; souls whose remains were left unburied after the dreadful gladitorial bouts for which the city was famous. Perhaps in death I can give them the peace they never knew in life.

The people of Glatzburg, disillusioned though they be, seem to believe that a new Protector of the Realm is destined to rise. According to the legend of Saint Orthenius, a new Protector of the Realm will rise when the true faith is most in danger, and that he will come bearing an ancient relic to cleanse our world of the enemies of man and God alike. I'm not sure how much faith I place in legends, but if a Protector were to rise, now would seem the perfect time...

The people of Glatzburg are distressed by the tidings of war's approach. No one is sure against whom it will be waged, but suspicion abounds and none of it good. The best advice I could hope to give them is to pray... and to prepare.

It appears that the "uncatchable" thief, Tinthan, has been accused of stealing from the episcopal temple. He is currently in hiding, but none can say where. I hear tale that Tinthan is also quite the comedian. Hmm. It would appear that this is one instance where the joker is, indeed, wild. I... should return to my investigation.
I've heard that there may be an entrance to the ancient sewer system near the city's garbage heap.

It is possible that Commander Ethien de Pasque's necklace was stolen by the comedian Tinthan. Rumor has it that the man could steal a letter from under the nose of an Inquisitorial investigator as it was being written. If I search for this comedian-turned-thief, I should be sure to keep my personal belongings, and any unfinished letters for that matter, close at hand.
It seems that one can only find bottles of Chateau de Trebrechette in Alvaron.
The city of Alvaron is ruled by Grand Duke Drake Lambert, and his royal vice-governor, Duchess Vanessa of Kentworth.

Leon van den Brooks owns a famous armory in Alvaron. If I need weapons or armor, he is the man to see. The apothecary, Thelma Ulthraum, and the master alchemist, Alberto Kelley, can both sell me a wide variety of potions and magical goods, and if I require their services, the landlord William Burton and the innkeeper, Salena Flock, both deal in odds and ends.

Until recently, many of Alvaron's residents dismissed claims that the Realm was in terrible danger. After the murder of King Edward II, however, opinions quickly began to change. The city has since descended into a state of panic, and her people live in constant fear. Never before have I witnessed terror on such a grandiose scale. It chills the blood to see the men and women of such a proud culture crawling about on their hands and knees like frightened vermin at the very mention of heresy.
The residents of Alvaron are troubled by the news of coming war. No one is sure against whom it is to be waged, but everyone fears that they will soon discover the answer.

Many of Alvaron's residents believe that Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is, in fact, a heretic and a traitor. The notion of seeing one who was once so blessed brought so low fills them with utter dread.
Only a handful of Alvaron's residents believe that Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert is innocent and that the accusations of heresy and treason raised against him were judicial misgivings.
It seems that Alvaron hasn't yet experienced a storm akin to the ones seen near Hillbrandt and Glatzburg. There is some mercy in that, but I'll be keeping one eye fixed to the sky, just in case.

It seems that the people of Alvaron and its surrounding holdings have been the victims of recent werewolf attacks. According to witness testimony, the beasts infiltrate the city on the eve of every full moon to kill and kidnap victims. Those captured are no doubt carried off to the creatures' hovel, located somewhere in Schwarzwald. Wulfhyrr, the wolf-prince, is said to lead the pack in question. I should tread lightly if ever I dare to wander into this den of wolves.
I've heard that the freshly dead have a habit of rising from their graves in Alvaron. No living thing is safe in the city's cemetery after dark.

Many people suspect Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert of heresy and high treason. Moreover, he has not shown his face in public since the initial accusations were raised. Could it be that the man is truly as corrupt as everyone seems to believe?

I've just discovered that His Majesty, King Edward II, was murdered recently in his own chambers in the royal palace. So brazen an attack... are heretics to blame? Or was Edward the victim of political intrigue?

Several people have been found murderered in the streets of Alvaron. The local authorities believe that at least the same number of people have gone missing, as well. Both crimes are ascribed to the wolf-prince, Wulfhyrr, and his roving pack of half-beasts.

The paladin Richwald d'Blazier was discovered in Schwarzwald some time ago. His body had been turned entirely to stone. The primary suspect is the witch, Corin, because she had purportedly been meeting with the paladin in secret.

The stallholder, Sandra Ullmann of Alvaron, was supposedly trying to ingratiate herself with the paladin Richwald d'Blazier. Word on the street is that he refused her advances, however, because his heart was already spoken for. People claim that his true lover was an unidentified witch from Schwarzwald.

It would appear that a band of heretics in Alvaron is using infernal magic to turn human ordure... into gold. For a short while, at least. As a result, there is a great deal of mistrust among the commonfolk, and merchants, understandably, seem less willing to bite their coins in order to expose potential counterfeits. Do these foul blasphemers know no shame? To think... how utterly disgusting.
Upon the eve of the last full moon, Nina Monthreass of Alvaron disappeared. It seems as though she was kidnapped by the kin of the wolf-prince, Wulfhyrr.
More and more graves are defiled and robbed in the cemetery of Alvaron on a daily basis. As a result, the sightings of living dead there have drastically increased night after night.
Rumor has it that an ancient evil stalks the streets of Alvaron by night, searching for something which was stolen from it.

I have heard the tale of the rogue paladin, Minfred von Siegel, who apparently went mad and took the lives of several innocents in Alvaron. Shortly after the massacre took place, Von Siegel fled the city. Now he resides in the countryside beyond the reach of the Sheriff, murdering all who dare cross his path!

It's said that the fortune of Baron Mansfeld is buried somewhere near Alvaron. Mansfeld apparetly buried the treasure, rather than allowing it to fall into the hands of his "less deserving" relations. In some ways, the act was commendable... and in others, quite plainly mad.
I've heard that lone wanderers who stay the evening at the King's Road Inn in Schwarzwald have a habit of disappearing in the night.

Many of Alvaron's residents are shocked by the death of the old Master, Konrad von Thaum, who fell during a failed attack on the den of the wolf-prince, Wulfhyrr, in Schwarzwald. His renowned blade, Decapitator, is still missing, and has likely fallen into the hands of the enemy.

I have heard talk of the Cult of the Pagan Night, a cruel society which longs for the return of pagan society and its vicious, unclean gods. Although dozens of vile crimes can be ascribed to the cult, the Inquisition has, as of  yet, failed to bring even a single member to justice. Curious... but not altogether surprising, given the recent troubles befalling the Realm.
The Royal Tomb in Alvaron's cemetery has been cursed for quite some time. No one has been able to enter since Prince Louis and his royal sisters were entombed there over two years ago!

It seems that the death of Prince Louis two years ago was accompanied by rather strange circumstances. Although two young maidservants, Kathryn Winhold and Corin Morray, were eventually convicted of the murder, rumor has it that it was Kathryn Winhold herself who initially accused the Royal Counselor, Verenicus, of the crime. But what did either of the accused stand to gain from the death of a prince? The shadows lingering over the Royal Family seem to grow darker and deeper with every new detail brought to light.

In Alvaron, I heard the tale of "Cursed Joan," a young girl who was awakened from her eternal slumber by a terrible curse. Reborn in the form of a stryx, she searches, desperately trying to find her wanton father so that she may exact her revenge upon him for ravishing her mother and driving her to suicide so many years ago. The cruelty of men, it seems, is on par only with that of demons. The poor child... may her soul someday find the peace it so rightfully deserves.

The late Duke Manfred Gotfried was reputedly a heretic who often summoned spirits to do his bidding with the aid of his necromantic trinket, the Necklace of Death. He died under strange circumstances in the year 1213, and was entombed in the Secular Tomb.

There is a cursed manor in Alvaron, once belonging to the late Baron von Blutenreich. It is said to be haunted by the Baron's unclean spirit, which many believe was imprisoned there by his thirteenth wife. Von Blutenreich's last wife purportedly poisoned and cursed the man as he lay dying, condemning him for the deaths of his twelve previous wives and their children, whom many believe were murdered by the Baron himself.

I now know that the treasure of Baron Decard of Longhorn is hidden somewhere in Schwarzwald. Decard was renowned for being both terribly rich and a heretic. He was executed in 1210, for one or the other.

People say that the tomb of St. Orthenius, the patron of the Realm, is located within the remains of an ancient royal garden that is now beset by hellspawn. It used to be a popular place of pilgrimage, but now the very ground is cursed by the infernal beasts which take up residence nearby. Is nothing sacred? If he could see the state of our world, Orthenius would surely be turning over in his grave.

I've listened to the legend of Wolfenburg, the "royal seat" of the wolf-prince,Wulfhyrr. According to the tale, Wulfhyrr is in fact the former Duke, Ronald of Wolfenburg, who was cursed by one of his serfs after he allegedly raped the poor girl. What curse more befitting a lecher than to suffer the wolf's hunger for all eternity? It would seem, however, that Wulfhyrr found little humility wearing the skin of a beast. It's well past time, then, that someone put this dog down.

I've acquired the hilt of a magnificent dagger from Ruphert the shepherd. The blade, however, is missing. Ruphert swears that the dagger belonged to Judge Vallarian, who tried to rid himself of it by tossing it into the garbage heap near Hillbrandt's stockade.

Ruphert the shepherd told me that Blacksmith Hammerhand's lost son, Paul, was fond of wandering into the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains, especially near the Dragon Rock. Perhaps I can find some trace of him there.
According to the testimony of the merchant, Ihman ab Sahab, Vick Length tried to sell him some of the jewels he took from the grave of Baron Mansfeld.
According to the testimony of the innkeeper, Salena Flock, Beckham the beggar paid her with counterfeit coins which eventually turned into human ordure. How disgusting!

Salena Flock believes that the apothecary, Thelma Ulthraum, is capable of curing her husband's lycantrophy. However, when the poor woman asked the apothecary for help, Ulthraum threw her out on the streets, claiming that she would "aid no hellspawn or their kin." Apparently, this is the way earnest requests for aid are answered in our day and age; at the end of a sharp blade, or an even sharper tongue.

Salena Flock thinks that the belongings of Ron Burton were sold to her by Norman, the rather... eccentric butcher in the employ of innkeeper Bates, proprietor of the King's Road Inn. I should investigate further.
I have received Cardinal Severtinus's consent to arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert.
I have received Cardinal Severtinus's consent to arrest Inquisitor General Commendoni.

Cardinal Severtinus asserts that there is treasure buried somewhere in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. Allegedly, this treasure contains a statuette of the barbarians' god, Bhelfelix. According to the Cardinal, there is a map in the possession of the treasure-hunter Hulph which details the location of both the statuette and the treasure. Luckily, Hulph is currently staying in Glatzburg.

Sheriff Gendriel Smith is offering a reward to anyone who slays one of the bloodthirsty rogues plaguing Glatzburg and her holdings. A simple trophy, such as a scalp or head, will suffice as proof of a fresh kill.

Stefan Reichmann is thoroughly convinced that his daughter Natalia was robbed and murdered by the landsknecht, Olfghard, and with good reason. As of yet, her body has not been found, and Olfghard hismelf was arrested after trying to sell some of the girl's stolen jewels in Hillbrandt.

Stefan Reichmann has a strong dislike for the soldier, Jullian, who apparently plotted to secure his own portion of the Reichmann fortune by asking for Natalia's hand in marriage. The young soldier was not only rebuked by the girl's father, but was also threatened by him. Reichmann stated in no uncertain terms that he would kill the boy if he ever came near his daughter again.
I have discovered that Steinger's boots are caked with the same peculiar sort of clay found only near the defiled graves in Alvaron's cemetery. This cannot be a coincidence.
Steinger confessed to robbing both the graves within Alvaron's cemetery and those beyond her walls. Together with his companion Vick Length, the two men amassed a small fortune in misbegotten loot.

The villain Steinger told me where he and his accomplice, Vick Length, buried all of their stolen treasure. It's hidden near the Citadel of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, by the bridge spanning the dry brook. I also received a map of the treasure's location, in case I couldn't find it of my own accord. What sort of detective does he take me for?

I have learned that the rather eccentric alchemist and astrologer, Theil Brechthold of Hillbrandt, is actually one of the most preeminent scholars of our time. He was even the Master of the Royal Alchemists Guild at the court of His Majesty, King Edward II, in Alvaron for a time.
I have received consent from Cardinal Giovanni Timore to arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert.
I have received consent from Cardinal Giovanni Timore to arrest Inquisitor General Commendoni.

I've heard that the comedian, Tinthan, was charged with the theft of the Monstrance of Saint Rhodrick. According to local legend, the man's no stranger to high profile theft, but the fool might very well lose his head over this one. For his sake, I pray the judge in his case has a wonderful sense of humor, or else a very weak heart.

Tinthan, the comedian, caught the soldier Harph entering the deserted sewers in Glatzburg with his undead minions in tow. He claims it was apparent at first glance that the creatures obeyed the soldier's every word without question. This had better not be a joke...

Tinthan offered me his services as a thief in exchange for acquitting him of the charge of theft. He stated that if I ever needed something stolen, I could turn to him without hesitation. I'm sure there's a beautiful irony in rewarding acquittal with the promise of theft, and I can definitely see the humor in it, but the thought of a comedian running about, stealing at my every whim is... disturbing. And in more than one way. Nonetheless, I shall keep his offer in mind.

Tinthan is certain that the Holy Mother Church possesses a sacred oil which can cure any disease or bodily ailment. The precious substance is said to be hidden somewhere in the dungeons of the cathedral in Alvaron, though precisely where, the thief cannot say.

The chamberlain, Trisstan, overheard a heated argument between His Majesty and Rodrigo de Velacor the night of King Edward II's murder. Afterward, the chamberlain saw the First Knight sneaking out of the king's study.

When I attempted to arrest him, Cardinal Truncquillius confessed that he is a dark priest of the heretical cult, the Children of the New Order, and that he devised all of the crimes which led to the invocation of the fallen angel, Baphomet, the Demon of Madness and Lord of Chaos.

Cardinal Truncquillius is certain that the Realm will only be free of evil when the purging flames of the Inquisition have melted away the imperfections of man. He also believes it's only a matter of time before the last of the heretics is caught and their dark delusions suppressed forever. His optimism is admirable; I wish that I could share it.

I found a golden earring in the very clearing where Richwald d'Blazier was turned to stone. Later, I discovered that it once belonged to Sandra Ullmann. Beyond the shadow of a doubt, the presence of the earring proves that she must have partaken in the ritual that left the brother paladin encased in stone.
Sanda Ullmann confessed to turning the paladin Richwald d'Blazier to stone for resisting her dark temptation.
The apothecary, Thelma Ulthraum, requires a moon crystal and the root of the "Memoricus Repeaticus" plant in order to brew a potion that prevents memory loss.

To remove the curse from Cardinal Timore's daughter, I must first find and consecrate the grave of her mother. Then, I must overpower Joan and force her to drink a flacon of her father's blood. A grisly task, to be sure, but it must be done if ever the girl is to know peace.
The apothecary, Thelma Ulthraum of Alvaron, can brew a potion which cures lycanthropy. First, however, I must bring her a Wolfsbane root.
The apothecary, Thelma Ulthraum of Alvaron, promised me that she would brew a miraculous potion from every sprig of Devil's Root I bring her.

Judge Vallarian is absolutely certain that Master Edmond d'Arvias is the driving force behind the atrocities committed in Hillbrandt as of late. Presumably, d'Arvias has conspired with dark powers to summon the orcs, creatures of Old Era legend, from their infernal nest in the ruins of the ancient Thron empire. Understandably, the Brotherhood of the Righteous does not share Vallarian's suspicion.

Judge Vallarian resisted arrest and had to be subdued. In a moment of depraved clarity, he confessed that it was he who had conceived all of the crimes committed by Linda van Gallagan and Sam Riemann. Their purpose was to invoke the fallen angel, Arthamon, the Demon of Ruin and Lord of Fire. If he speaks truthfully, the three supposedly succeeded in their task. I pray that he is ever the liar.
Judge Vallarian has called upon me to gather more evidence against Edmond d'Arvias in order to hasten the Master's trial.

After his arrest, Judge Vallarian mentioned something about the day when a new order would rise. An order whose children would rule over the ashes of our world. For all of our sakes, I pray these are but the fatalistic rantings of a doomed man.

I've heard that the Brotherhood of the Righteous was trying to persuade King Edward II to restrict the Holy Office's powers. According to Vallarian, it was all a heretical conspiracy concocted with the aim of making the treacherous knightly order all but untouchable. Surely there must have been some ulterior motive. Could the Brotherhood truly be so fraught with heretics as to turn against the Inquisition?
Duchess Vanessa of Kentworth is positive that the only person capable of returning her back to her original form is the Master of Alchemy, Alberto Kelley.
Vanessa of Kentworth believes that the Grand Duchess, Liana Lambert, will withdraw the charges raised against Nicolas if I threaten to divulge the details of her love affair with Marcius.

Baroness Elisabeth van Singier suspects her sister-in-law, Baroness Linda van Gallagan, of committing some sort of mischief. According to Van Singier, Lady Van Gallagan was often seen sneaking out of her house under the cover of night. In a town the size of Hillbrandt, there could scarcely be many reasons to leave one's home after dark. None of them, unfortunately, are very godly in nature.
The First Knight, Rodrigo de Velacor, confessed to the murder of His Majesty King Edward II.

When put to torture, the merchant Raimond Ventano pled guilty to the kidnapping of Francessca Gulvardi. He also confessed that he—along with his accomplices, Ethien de Pasque and Yulliette Heidrick—invoked the fallen angel Baphomet, the Demon of Madness and the Lord of Chaos, during a heretical mass.
Raimond Ventano told me that in order to enter the Sanctuary of Chaos, I must speak in an ancient tongue.

Paolus Ventimus is certain that the method of obtaining St. Orthenius' fabled "Inquisitor" relic is detailed in the saint's own legend. According to Ventimus, the key to locating the device lies within the original text of St. Orthenius' tale, written centuries ago by the historian Killian. After Killian's death, the tale was rewritten several times until the truth of the Inquisitor relic was buried beneath the oft-quoted fairytale of a Protector who would rise to free the poor and the oppressed from their servitude. While certainly not the savior the people are hoping for, the true Protector will be the one they need most. Perhaps one day, they will see that.
The alchemist, Paolus Ventimus of Glatzburg, is able to turn every Philosopher's Stone I bring him into gold.

According to the assertions of the Royal Counselor, Verenicus, Crown Prince Louis is not truly dead. He was merely enthralled by a dark spell which left his spirit lingering feebly between the bounds of life and death. Because the Royal Apothecary could not distinguish true death from the unnatural stillness caused by the spell, the prince was declared dead and buried in the Royal Tomb alongside his sisters. No matter how small the chance, if the Crown Prince yet lives, I must find him and undo the spell which binds him. The Realm has never been in greater need of a ruler; in the meanwhile, I can only pray that Louis is the man his people desperately need him to be.
Royal Counselor Verenicus confessed that he, along with Jean de Guise and Cardinal Commendoni, performed a heretical rite two years ago which left the Crown Prince, Louis, in a state of near-death.
If I bring Victor Hammerhand a Philosopher's Stone, he can forge a magical item from it.

There is supposedly a former paladin of the Brotherhood, a man by the name of Hanrey de Montreaux, who wanders the woodlands near Glatzburg, always in search of a fight. Locals say that he's become a fanatic—obsessed with the art of dueling—and that he uses his obsession as a means to commit murder. If the stories ring true, the man is apparently unbeatable. If I happen across him in my travels, I'll be sure to put those stories to the test.

I've heard rumors that Ultherst is on the verge of war. Granaries are being filled, royal troops have taken up arms, and conscriptionists travel from town to town, making soldiers out of plowshares. But what does it all mean? With whom are we at war? I fear the answer almost as much as I fear being left ignorant.

My greatest fears have become reality. The Pope, Alessander III, has called for another Crusade. On the borders of the Empire, our age-old ally, an army of the faithful gathers from every corner of the Orthodox world. Every sword, every shield, every steed, banner and battlecry calls out for retribution. Retribution from Ultherst, a land—in the eyes of the Papacy—which is beyond redemption. The faithful believe that the evil plaguing Ultherst poses a danger to every civilized nation in the Orthodox world, and through fire and flame, they will see Ultherst cleansed... of innocents and evildoers alike. May God watch over us, and may the archangel Michael fight alongside those who seek only to defend what they love from those who are misguided.
The soldier, Volter, told me that some time ago, he saw the blacksmith's boy running out of Hillbrandt in the direction of the Dragon Rock.
I found the statuette of the archangel, Gabriel, but it was immediately taken from me by the church's treasure-keeper, Pontifex.

Weintraum told me that his friend, Johaness Clifford, hasn't been himself lately. According to Weintraum, the man has been uncharacteristically grim as of late, and that he refuses to leave his home or even to speak with his closest friends.
The innkeeper, Weintraum, has withdrawn the charges he raised against Tinthan.

I've learned from Weintraum that his most generous patron is, surprisingly, the soldier, Harph, who has been known to squander lavish sums of money on a whim. Though not the strangest thing I've ever heard, I must admit that there's something terribly odd about a run-of-the-mill soldier spending money like a drunken nobleman in a brothel. Perhaps I should investigate the source of his newly found wealth.

I discovered that Father Frederick, mentioned by the ghost of Bishop Trevorius, was once a great teacher and counselor to Judge Welfhar. He was said to be the last priest in the Realm capable of performing the ancient rite of exorcism. Two years ago, however, he succumbed to plague and was buried in the sepulchre beneath the city's graveyard.

Kathryn Winhold has given her posthumous testimony about the nature of Royal Counselor Verenicus' crimes. According to Winhold, two years ago, Verenicus took part in a dark ritual which resulted in the death of Crown Prince Louis.
Wrang the orc told me of a noblewoman who came to see the orcish Khan, Rasghar, some time ago. The orc claims that she is one of the heretics who commands his former brethren.

I've heard that somewhere in the Orcish kingdom, the tortured spirit of King Harlior dwells. Harlior was the last ruler of the Thron Empire, which thrived under the Moonshine Mountains before the coming of the orcs. His spirit is said to be guarding a legendary treasure, waiting for some brave soul to fulfill his age-old promise of seeing the orcish Khan, Rashgar, dead. Only then, when Rashgar's body grows cold and still, will Harlior's self-imposed torment come to an end.

According to Scripture, Arthamon, along with the demons Baphomet and Cerdie, are the three fallen angels who were cast down alongside their master, Satan, at the dawning of time. Guilty of crimes against God, their Father, they were banished forever from His side and the glory of Heaven, doomed to dwell in eternal darkness. Ever since, they have been trying to seize our world and make it their own, a bitter testament to their hatred of God. If Arthamon has truly been invoked, we shall all soon feel the keen sting of his fiery temper.

According to Ellisia Würtenrodt, the fallen Bishop of Asherbalt, Herbertius, has risen as a vampire! As a child of the night, Herbertius can only be slain by destroying his cursed heart. It's likely, therefore, that the fiend keeps the putrid organ nearby at all times. I must be wary when approaching this beast, for vampires can be dangerously persuasive killers.
Ellisia Würtenrodt, the herbalist of Hillbrandt, promised to prepare a magic potion for me from every sprig of Devil's Root I bring her.
The witches' sabbath, the remains of which I found at the Dragon Rock near Hillbrandt, is said to have summoned a powerful demon to our world. At least, that's what Ellisia Würtenrodt claims.
I've learned from Ellisia Würtenrodt that the only way to cure bewitchment is to find and destroy the bewitcher's mommet, a small figurine meant to represent the afflicted.

Ellisia Würtenrodt tried to discourage me from going near the Dead Man's Stone near the Hillbrandt gallows. Supposedly, there are souls bound to it which long only for the chance to exact revenge upon those they consider responsible for their deaths.

The Grand Duchess, Yulliette Heidrick confessed that she, together with Raimond Ventano and Ethien de Pasque, invoked the fallen angel, Baphomet, in the Sanctuary of Chaos. She also claimed to have committed her terrible crimes at the bidding of Cardinal Truncquillius. For the Church's sake, I pray she is ever the liar.

An abhorrent letter has found its way into my hands. In it, the Grand Duke Robert Heidrick commands the marauding knight, Benthley of Welshrem, to carry out all necessary preparations to perform a heretical mass. The Grand Duke, it would seem, intends to invoke the very powers of Hell itself.
I have freed the spirit of Baron Dawn von Blutenreich from its worldly bonds.
When confronted, Cardinal Commendoni chose to resist arrest. I was left with no choice but to kill him to preserve my own life.

I now have enough evidence to formally accuse Master Edmond d'Arvias of heresy and conspiracy to commit crimes against God and King. As a result, I can arrest the man at my leisure.

I have been ordered to arrest the Inquisitorial Judge, Vallarian, under the reasonable suspicion of heresy and conspiracy to commit crimes against God and King.

It seems that the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius, a sacred relic said to safeguard the town of Hillbrandt, disappeared recently from the Hillbrandt Cathedral. The town's residents are in a state of panic, fearful that, without the Monstrance, their walls will protect them little from the threat of orcish invasion.
What happened to Linda van Gallagan?
Baron Robert van Gallagan is heartbroken. His wife Linda has been missing for quite some time, and he's desperate to find out what's become of her. He's asked for my assistance in the investigation.
Bring a memory loss cure potion to Balthazar

In order for old man Balthazar to tell me the name of a potentially dangerous heretic, I have to bring him a memory loss cure potion. Hopefully, he won't remember this was all just an elaborate joke to waste a wandering soul's time, or I'll be forced to forget he isn't the one I'm looking for.
Find a cure for the executioner Raubsticht

It seems that the Hillbrandt's executioner Friedrich Raubsticht has been stricken by a rather... ugly disease. His whole body is covered in dripping sores, and he's in terrible pain, though he can't bring himself to leave the executioner's yard to rest. He's asked me to bring him a curative potion from the herbwoman, Ellisia Würtenrodt.
Fetch the sword of Master Konrad von Thaum
Master Kirk von Haubersacht has asked me to help the Brotherhood of the Righteous recover the mighty Decapitator which has fallen into the hands of werewolves.
Fetch the holy oil
I promised Tinthan I would fetch him holy oil. The precious substance, produced by the Holy Mother Church, has the power to cure any ailment.
Find the statue of the pagan god Bhelfelix
If I bring the statue of the pagan god Bhelfelix to Cardinal Severtinus, I'll have his consent to charge the Inquisitor General Commendoni with heresy.
Bring a bottle of Chateau de Trebrechette wine to Weintraum
I'm to obtain a bottle of Chateau de Trebrechette wine for the innkeeper, Weintraum. The bottle he ordered from Alvaron has fallen into the hands of bandits.
Apprehend Duke Rowan van Leerin

Several young girls have gone missing in and around Glatzburg recently. If I apprehend the culprit and see justice done, Master Dieter von Gelbendiel has promised me information which may prove crucial to my investigation.
Catch the leader of the Cult of the Pagan Night
I've been ordered to catch the leader of the Cult of the Pagan Night, Juhasz Gotherr, who along with his heretical companions plans to see the world plunged into eternal darkness.
Accompany Linda van Gallagan back to town
I promised Baroness Linda van Gallagan I would accompany her back to Hillbrandt and her husband.
Accompany Helen von Hunth back to her husband
I promised Baroness Helen von Hunth I would accompany her back to her husband.
Accompany Natalia Reichmann back to town
I agreed to accompany Natalia Reichmann back to Hillbrandt and her father.
Escort Paul Hammerhand back to town
I promised to escort Paul Hammerhand back to his father's smithy.
Find the werewolves' secret ally in town
Sheriff Henry Portmann has promised me a reward if I can uncover the identity of the traitor who’s been ushering werewolves into the city from the Schwarzwald.
Who stole the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius?
In order to be named the Inquisitorial Prosecutor, I have to demonstrate my abilities by bringing back the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius and apprehending the thief who took it.

To be named the Commander of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, I must demonstrate my capabilities by returning the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius, apprehending the culprit who stole it from Hillbrandt's church, and killing a given number of enemies of God and King in the process...

To earn the title of Baron, I must demonstrate my loyalty to the Realm by returning the Monstrance of Saint Orthenius and apprehending the culprit who stole it from Hillbrandt's church some time ago. Also, I must pay a fee of 5,000 gold pieces. Some would say buying a title cheapens it… to those people, I say ‘5,000 gold isn’t nearly cheap enough.’
Who killed the merchant Kurth Ollmier?
Strangers calling themselves friends of the Realm have asked me to investigate the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier in the hamlet of Hillbrandt.
Find Joachym

The old miner, Graubner, is worried about his companion Joachym who left some time ago to fetch food. He’s yet to return, and the old man grows more worried by the hour. I promised Graubner I'd try to find his friend.
Find Jullian
Sheriff Jacob Contemburry is missing a young soldier, Jullian, who hasn't yet reported for duty. I'm to find out where the runaway is hiding and bring him back in one piece.
Find Paul Hammerhand
The blacksmith Victor Hammerhand asked me to find his son, Paul, who ran away from home some time ago. The blacksmith fears something may have happened to the boy.
Find the statuettes of the angels of the Holy Trinity
The merchant Ihman ab Sahab is searching for three ancient jade statuettes of the angels Raphael, Michael and Gabriel. He's willing to pay a large sum of gold for each of them.
Feed the ogre Fathor
Fathor the ogre won't eat me if I bring him a meal of sheep. Or so he says.
The Summoning of Arthamon

I must discover the truth of the rumor that the Fallen Angel Arthamon has been summoned by pagans living in Hillbrandt. Arthamon is the Demon of Ruin and the cursed Master of Fire. If he truly walks the Earth, we are all in grave danger.
The Summoning of Baphomet

I must uncover the truth and determine whether the Children of the New Order have truly summoned the Fallen Angel Baphomet. Baphomet is the Demon of Madness and the Master of Chaos. If he truly stalks the hills of Glatzburg, sanity may be a quickly fading luxury.
The Summoning of Cerdie

I must determine whether or not the Succubus, Cerdie, was truly summoned by Alvaronian cultists. Cerdie is the Mother of Debauchery and the Lady of Eternal Sin. If she truly walks the Earth, mankind is surely doomed. I pray it is only a rumor, but I greatly fear uncovering the truth.
Search for the hammer of Bonhart von Drichtmaul

The armorer Hans von Drichtmaul asked me to find his great-grandfather’s magic hammer. Bonhart von Drichtmaul was a beast of a man, and the hammer holds tremendous significance to Hans. It should be buried somewhere in the vicinity of Glatzburg along with Bonhart von Drichtmaul’s other belongings.
Find the paladin Minfred von Siegel

It seems the paladin Minfred von Siegel has descended fully into madness. He has resorted to murdering innocents along the road. Commander Hector de Froix ordered me to find him and bring him back at any cost. I fear it will have to be in pieces.
Find the sword of Master Edmond d'Arvias
Masted Edmond d'Arvias is missing his weapon, the Sword of the Brotherhood. He’s asked me to help him get his weapon back and, if possible, to determine who stole it.
Return the amulet to the undead Elenian noble
I promised the undead Elenian noble En'Lenius that I would return his magic necklace. It was stolen from him by grave robbers, and he cannot rest without it.
Look into the disappearance of Ron Burton

For all intents and purposes, Ron Burton has vanished. He was set to return from a business trip not long ago, but never returned to Alvaron. His brother, William, has asked me to find out what happened to him.
Look into the disappearance of Bishop Quentinus

Father Dominicus is one of the few citizens of Hillbrandt who believe that the missing Bishop Quentinus is still alive. He asked me to find the Bishop and bring him back safely. I promised to do what I could.
Cure the lycanthrope
I promised the innkeeper Salena Flock I would try to cure her husband Alwar of his lycanthropy. He was bitten by a werewolf, and his wife fears he is too weak to resist the creature’s unholy illness.
Identify the Dark High Priest of the Children of the New Order

To thwart the Children of the New Order’s dark plans, I must first uncover the identity of their Dark High Priest. By severing the serpent’s head, perhaps the coils will unwind from the heart of the Realm.
Denounce the soldier Harph

To become an Inquisitorial Judge, I must prove myself by denouncing the heretical necromancer who plagues the city of Glatzburg. By night, the fiend commands the dead to steal and murder. The Church cannot abide such evil.

To be knighted Master of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, I must prove myself by denouncing the heretical necromancer who plagues the city of Glatzburg. Only by putting an end to his dark reign, and slaying the poor souls he’s enslaved, will I earn my place as a Master.

To earn the title of Duke, I must prove my loyalty to the Realm by denouncing the heretical necromancer who plagues the city of Glatzburg. Also, for some reason, I must pay a fee of 10,000 gold pieces as well. It takes money to make money, I suppose…
Purvey a human body for Pteremon
The undead Erebornian nobleman, Pteremon, longs to wear the flesh of a human body once more. He has asked me to claim one for him.
Free Francessca Gulvardi
I promised Francessca Gulvardi I would arrange her release from prison. She appears wholly innocent, and I for one believe her.
Free Baroness Helen von Hunth
Baron Edger von Hunth beseeched me to rescues his wife. She has fallen into the hands of the marauding knight, Benthley of Welshrem, and lord Von Hunth fears for her wellbeing.
Free Olfghard

Olfghard asked me to help find evidence that would acquit him of the murder of Natalia Reichmann. He is ragged, unkempt, and uncultured… but I am not entirely convinced he’s a killer. I promised him I would do what I could.
Catch the money forgers

Grand Duke Drake Lambert of Alvaron has hired me to hunt down the forgers in Alvaron. For some time, the infernal counterfeiters have been turning human waste into gold and putting it into circulation. Disgusting, but an interesting thought, nonetheless – imagine a noble family that could literally excrete gold.
Kill all the monsters in the Glatzburg cemetery
I promised Dietrich the gravedigger I would kill every monster roaming about the Glatzburg cemetery. If only every task were so simple; what a dull world we would live in!
Kill the giant bats surrounding Hillbrandt
To show my good will to the guards of Hillbrandt and earn my passage into the hamlet, I must kill the giant bats surrounding the town. This should be simple work.
Kill the infernal minions
To prevent Pteremon’s return to Hell, I must kill the minions of darkness sent to claim him. Any blow struck against the Dark Prince is a victory for the Church and the Realm.
Help Ulm von Grimschloss clear the dungeon beneath the pagan watchtower
I promised the paladin Ulm von Grimschloss from the order of the Brotherhood of the Righteous that I would help him purge the dungeon beneath the ruins of an ancient pagan watchtower.
Punish Hans Thomas Brookwelt

Jeanette the chambermaid has implored me to bring Hans Thomas Brookwelt to justice for the crime of seducing and dishonoring her with the aid of infernal powers. Apparently, he has done the same to many of the other women in Glatzburg.
Punish Jeanette the chambermaid

Hans Thomas Brookwelt turned to me to bring Jeanette the chambermaid to justice. He claims she is a witch, and has attempted on multiple occasions to bring him under her control with the aid of dark spells and rituals.
Give the cursed necklace to the paladins of the Brotherhood of the Righteous
I promised the paladin Minfred von Siegel I would give Hector de Froix his cursed necklace. Apparently, the thing has driven poor Minfred completely mad...
Bring the herbarium

Ellisia Würtenrodt, the herbalist, has been waiting in vain for several weeks. She ordered a rather precious herbarium that was to be brought to her by way of a merchant caravan from Glatzburg. She's afraid the caravan was ambushed by orcs and has asked me to find the book and bring it to her.
Find the spellbook of the Elenian Prince Fae'Darlion
If I bring the spellbook of the Elenian Prince Fae'Darlion to the wise woman, Enrie Jungwirdt, she'll help me with the translation of the encrypted message found in the belongings of Judge Vallarian.
Bring back Ethien de Pasque his necklace
Commander Ethien de Pasque asked me to find his Chain of the Brotherhood. He believes it was probably stolen.
Bring the Chalice of Metamorphosis

The alchemist Paolus Ventimus asked me to find the Chalice of Metamorphosis for him. It is an artifact from the height of the Erebornian Empire. According to Ventimus, it should be somewhere in the ruins of Galibornium.
Bring the ring of Archbishop Matroiani

If I bring the ring of the late Archbishop Matroiani to the priest Marcius, he may be able to identify the author of the heretical letters sent to Cardinal Truncquillius in Glatzburg. I would much rather carry on with my investigation than retrieve lost jewelry, but this may be my only lead.
Bring a Mana Potion to Bishop Quentinus
I found Bishop Quentinus tired beyond witlessness. I must find a Mana Potion for him in order to raise his spirits enough to return home.
Bring back the foundation stone

I promised the priests from the newly consecrated Church of the Sacred Heart of our Lord that I would find and bring them the foundation stone of the temple, consecrated in the year 223 by Saint Orthenius himself.
Find the gold ring of Guss Halworth

Guss Halworth was recently ambushed by bandits on the road to Glatzburg. Although he escaped unharmed, the bandits took his gold seal–the signet ring of the Knights of Archangel Gabriel. I promised him I would return it if I happened across it.
Bring back the stray sheep
One of the duke's sheep is missing! I promised Ruphert the shepherd I would look for it.
Decipher a mysterious scroll

The alchemist Alberto Kelley charged me with translating a mysterious scroll he found in the ruins of an ancient Elenian sanctum. He believes it could be the key that unlocks some of the great mysteries surrounding the pagan culture’s magical heritage.
Remove the curse from the house of Baron von Blutenreich
I'm to remove the curse from the house of Baron von Blutenreich.
Remove the curse from the daughter of Giovanni Timore

In order to have Judge Giovanni Timore of the Highest Inquisitorial Tribunal to cooperate, I must remove the curse from his illegitimate daughter, Joan. She… has transformed into a Stryx after thirteen years spent in her grave. To tell the truth, I’m not terribly sure what a Stryx is… but I’ll deal with it, nonetheless.
Remove the curse from the executioner Raubsticht

It seems someone has bewitched Executioner Friedrich Raubsticht, for he suffers from an illness that is seemingly incurable by practical means. I promised him I would try to save him from his affliction, but I’ll admit, the disease is beyond my understanding.
Find a cure to reverse the spell of ugliness

Duchess Vanessa of Kentworth has trifled with pagan magic and in so doing changed herself into an ugly hag. I promised her I would find a potion to reverse the effects of the spell, but I must admit: ugly suits a woman who dabbles in evil affairs.
Find magic ingredients

Vanessa of Kentworth has asked me to deliver several magical ingredients. They're needed to prepare the spell of eternal beauty. The ingredients are as follows: a Betheal Temporarum blossom, a sun crystal, and troll bile.
Find a wife for Grand Duke Heidrick
I promised Grand Duke Robert Heidrick I would find a suitable wife for him. He believes marrying will do wonders to improve his damaged reputation.
Sell a bogus relic
I linked up with the relic forger Heins Schebell and agreed to help him sell the fake skull of Saint Baudolinus to the Holy Mother Church.
Hide Adeleida

I was asked by the Royal Chamberlain Trisstan to hide away his granddaughter, Adeleida. He fears for her safety more than he fears for the Royal Family, and believes someone might try to harm her to strike back at him.
Deposit the remains of Baron Liam von Hunth
Edger von Hunth asked me to put the remains of his father into the Von Hunth family sarcophagus in the secular tomb under the Glatzburg cemetery.
Put the zombie back into its grave
I promised the undead Baron Mansfeld that I would put him back in his grave.
Kidnap Helen von Hunth
I've associated with the soldier Harph in his effort to kidnap Baroness Helen von Hunth. I'm to deliver her to a location of our agreeing.
Find the heretics and prove them guilty

I must apprehend the heretics responsible for committing the disgusting crimes which have befallen Hillbrandt as of late. It seems the murder of the merchant Kurth Ollmier, and the strange circumstances surrounding the death of Baroness Gwenn von Weill and the theft of her body are all somehow connected. None of those crimes may be left unpunished.
Heal Paul Hammerhand
I must cure Paul Hammerhand's fever. A healing potion should do the trick...
Return the silver amulet to the beggar
The innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch seized the beggar Braham's silver amulet. I've decided to remedy that injustice and return the amulet to the beggar at once.
Blackmail the merchant Stefan Reichmann
I've associated with the soldier Jullian in his effort to blackmail the merchant, Stefan Reichmann. I'm to deliver the ransom for his daughter Natalia to Jullian as soon as possible.
Blackmail the landlord Weintraum
I've associated with the criminal Hermann Schultz in his effort to blackmail the landlord Ludwig Weintraum. I'm to hand over a letter of blackmail to him and retrieve the due ransom.
Seek Bishop Trevorius

I should seek out Bishop Trevorius of Glatzburg. I am told he can help me in my hunt for conspirators from the Children of the New Order. I'm to deliver Trevorius a letter from Edmond d'Arvias and explain my situation.
Win the duel with Hanrey de Montreaux
The marauding knight Hanrey de Montreaux challenged me to a duel. God be with the lesser of us.
Cure the werewolf Kenthwarr
I promised the wounded werewolf Kenthwarr I would bring him a Potion of Cure Disease and a Potion of Healing.
Decipher the Plan of the Cult

To win the confidence of Bishop Trevorius, I must show him evidence supporting my suspicion concerning the Cult of the Children of the New Order. I can likely obtain such evidence by deciphering the mysterious encrypted message I found in the belongings of the late Judge Vallarian.
The exorcism
The ghost of the murdered Bishop Trevorius asked me to perform exorcism on the possessed Francessca Gulvardi. She seems to be the key to continuing my investigation.
Cleanse the Glatzburg sewers of evil
Sheriff Gendriel Smith ordered me to cleanse the deserted sewers beneath Glatzburg. Thankfully, he was referring to the evil dwelling within, and not… well, you know.
Find the murderer of King Edward II

If I solve the murder of His Majesty King Edward II and pass the exam of Canon and Secular Laws, I'll be named Curial Inquisitor. Such an opportunity comes but once in a lifetime, and very, very early in my own. I would do well to see this through to the end with all due diligence. God be with your servant.
If I solve the murder of His Majesty King Edward II and bring divine justice to his killers and their servants, I will be named the Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous. I shall not fail.

If I can solve the murder of His Majesty King Edward II and pay 15,000 gold pieces to the Royal Treasury, I'll earn the title of Grand Duke. Such a title would make me a made man for life. That’s a gamble I have to bet on.
Consecrate the pagan temple
I was asked to consecrate the temple in the ruins of the pagan town of Galibornium. Judge Welfhar is confident that consecration will cleanse the evil within.
Free the evil spirits
I promised the souls imprisoned in the Dead Man's Stone I would free them from their earthly prison. Sprinkling the stone with holy water should be enough to release them.
Summon the ghost of Kathryn Winhold

By performing a necromantic rite, I might be able to summon the ghost of the executed Kathryn Winhold and hear her testimony regarding the crimes of the Royal Counselor Verenicus. I should be able to learn the rite from a tome known as the Libre Necronomicon.
Kill Benthley of Welshrem
I promised Lothard Luisse I would help him avenge the death of his mother and sisters. They, and many others, were murdered by the marauder Benthley of Welshrem.
Kill Gubring
I promised the orcish worker Wrang that I would murder his boss. The orc I'm meant to kill goes by the name of Gubring.
Kill the ghost of the Dwarfish king Harlior
The Orcish leader Horth has promised to reward me richly for slaying the ghost of King Harlior.
Kill Helen Von Hunth
Benthley of Welshrem has asked me to kill Baroness Helen von Hunth. Life is a crime; she must be punished for her transgression.
Kill Istwan de Bragho
Yan Flemberg, the executioner of Glatzburg, has implored me to destroy the cursed Duke Istwan de Bragho who has risen from his grave with the intent of taking revenge upon his slayers.
Kill the spider demon
Sheriff Ulbrecht has asked me to destroy the spider demon killing his men in the mines. Spiders, demons? No problem. Spider demons? I may need to bring fire for this one…
Kill Olfghard
Stefan Reichmann has charged me with finding and killing the runaway prisoner Olfghard. Olfghard stands accused of murdering Reichmann's daughter, Natalia, and has fled to avoid execution.
Restore the supply to Asherbalt
Sheriff Ulbrecht asked me to kill the half-ogre endangering the transportation of supplies to Asherbalt.
Kill the Orcish leader Khan Rashgar
The ghost of pagan King Harlior has asked me to grant him eternal peace by killing the Orcish leader Khan Rashgar once and for all.
Kill Kenthwarr the werewolf
Paladin Gerhard de Blanc called upon me to help him track down the wounded werewolf Kenthwarr and finish him off.
Kill Lord Zargh
I promised Grand Duke Heidrick of Glatzburg that I would bring him the heart of the Lizardmen’s leader. I’ll find the beasts in the Devil’s Caverns.
Save Corin Morray from being executed

Paladin Brian de Gawais and his fellows from the Brotherhood of the Righteous are on the verge of executing Corin, a seemingly moonstruck girl, for turning brother Richwald d'Blazier into stone. I must prove the girl’s innocence to the brothers.
Rescue Nina Monthreass
I promised Nina Monthreas I would escort her back to the city.
Save Raquel Gielwitch
Innkeeper Wanda Gielwitch has asked me to find out what has happened to her missing sister.
Save paladin Scott de Ormand

Paladin Scott de Ormand from the Brotherhood of the Righteous was overpowered by trolls and dragged away to their den in the foothills of the Moonshine Mountains. I promised his wounded companion Rivien d'Ardrieaux that I would try to save him. I have very little hope of finding him alive, though. Trolls are notoriously vicious creatures, especially when faced with the challenge of debasing good men.
Pay the debt of Leon van den Brooks

If I pay the debt Leon van den Brooks owes to Vanessa of Kentworth, he has promised to reveal the name of the customer who had ordered the poisoned arrow which killed Paladin brother Eradim d'Chambrie.
Stop Archbishop Laurencius
If Archbishop Laurencius’s devious plan comes to fruition, the entire Realm will be thrown into chaos. He must be stopped at any cost.
Stop the orcs
I promised Duke Weinberg that I would bring him the head of the Orcish leader Khan Rashgar. Rashgar has plagued the countryside for too long; his reign of terror must come to an end.
Arrest Master Edmond d'Arvias

Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian has charged me with finding and arresting Master Edmond d'Arvias. By all accounts, it seems d’Arvias conspired with dark powers to kidnap the Diocesan Bishop Quentinus. Why would a Paladin Brother turn his back on his fellow man in such a dark time? The crime seems… almost out of place, but it is not for me to judge.
Arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert

Jean de Guise, the Seneschal of the Brotherhood of the Righteous, has ordered me to request permission of the Highest Inquisitorial Tribunal to arrest Grand Master Christoffer de Malamert on the basis of incriminating evidence. After receiving the Tribunal’s permission, I am to arrest him.
Arrest the grave robber
There has been an increasing number of grave robbings in Alvaron as of late. Father Augustin has ordered me to find and arrest the culprit or culprits.
Retrieve the incriminating letters
I must retrieve the letters Cardinal Truncquillius carries on his person at any cost. Grand Duchess Yulliette Heidrick asserts that they convict him of heresy and of conspiring against God and King.
Get the Potion of Longevity

The astrologer Theil Brechthold suspects the herbalist Ellisia Würtenrodt has been secretly brewing something he calls a “potion of Longevity.” If what he says is true, drinking such a potion could extend one’s life by several generations. He has asked me to retrieve the forbidden potion for him so that he might be young forever.
Find the author of the letters sent to Cardinal Truncquillius

I must find the author of the heretical letters sent to Cardinal Truncquillius. Only then will I have direct and incriminating evidence against the unknown heretic spreading corruption through the Realm.
Discover the names of members of the Children of the New Order

I must find out who's behind the murder of Bishop Trevorius and discover what other atrocities the culprit plans to commit. If the Cult of the Children of the New Order is behind this crime, then it is my duty to see justice done and the offenders executed.
Exculpate Nicolas of his charge
To free the priest Nicolas, I must exculpate him of the charge of raping Grand Duchess Liana Lambert.
Exculpate Tinthan of charge

Tinthan the comedian has implored me to exculpate him of the charge of theft for which he is to be executed. In exchange for that, he will lend his thieving skills to my services. He claims to be able to steal anything in the world–that could prove exceedingly useful.
