The year 1223 has finally come. The whole Kingdom of Ultherst is drowning in chaos and the end of the world is getting nigh. In some it arouses hope, in others fear. But you are being preoccupied with a problem much more mundane—to stay alive. You have fallen into the hands of the Holy Office which means only one thing these days—torture and death. Of course, you could try to prove your innocence, but who would listen to reason these days? The Scourges of God have stricken and there are hellspawns lurking high and low. But don't you dread, the Inquisition is here to restore peace and order, and each and every sinner shall be redeemed in the flames of divine justice—even though he might seem innocent at the moment. God will be able to tell…\\n\\nStrangely enough, you were saved from the torture and the final judgment by two mysterious men who explained to the industrious servants of God, whose company you were enjoying, what a miscarriage of justice means.

In the end, a pouch of gold turned out to be the best proof of innocence. The result of this seemingly simple transaction was one of the very few release orders ever issued by the Holy Inquisition. Nevertheless, as you soon found out, the price for the mercy was to be high. It looked quite innocent at first—you were to go to Hillbrandt, a mountain town at the northern border of the Realm, and shed some light on the death of a certain merchant by the name of Kurth Ollmier. Why you? Because you were nobody! You were insignificant and replaceable—as your saviors had said. But what the hell! You were alive!\\n\\nSo you set off for a journey to Hillbrandt to find the Inquisitorial Judge Vallarian whose errand boy you were supposed to become to hide your real mission—just as you were told to do. Your saviors promised to contact you soon to see the results of your investigation.
And then you were supposed to be free. But everything was to turn out in a really, really different way. Why? Because it is the year 1223; the year when the world is to end.

Although the mad Judge Vallarian was executed and his soul is now about to face the final judgment, your quest has not been completed yet. Not by far. The mysterious cipher found on the heretical judge, his remarks of some kind of a New Order and of children who should rule the world when it comes, and above all the claim that the fallen angel Arthamon has been summoned suggest that Vallarian's crimes were not just a coincidence and that they had deeper roots.\\n\\nSo you set off for a journey to Glatzburg, the second biggest city of the Realm, to find the key to the whole mystery and to follow the track discovered in Hillbrandt. You keep asking in vain whether your saviors knew how important the task they gave you in a good faith was or whether you have accidentally come across something nobody had any idea about before.\\n\\nMaybe Bishop Trevorius, whom you are supposed to contact in Glatzburg, can answer that.

Your experience tells you, however, that prudence and a certain degree of paranoia are important for your survival. It is not the first time you have found yourself at the centre of a scheme of someone you trusted to be your ally. You must not forget that the devil is cunning and it has thousands of faces. It is, after all, the year 1223 and the end of the world is supposed to come... as is the traditional tax raise.

There is no doubt that the heretical Cult of the Children of the New Order has spread as far as to Alvaron, the capital of the Realm, and permeated the highest ranks of the society. The evidence found during the investigation of Cardinal Truncquillius's crimes suggests that. Will the summoning of the third fallen angel—succubus Cerdie—really mean the end of the Kingdom of God on Earth as their disgusting plan supposes? Anyway, the mission has become more important than you have ever dreamt of. And yet it seems that most people in the Realm have no idea that they are balancing on the edge of doom and keep living in their everyday sin.\\n\\nThe only people who could have foreseen the plans of the Children of the New Order were your mysterious patrons who entrusted you with the investigation of the crimes in Hillbrandt.

However, they have not contacted you since your rescue—although they promised to do so. Could it be that they were discovered by their heretical opponents and crushed before they could have warned you? But that does not change anything—you have already ventured too far to leave the game now. It seems that the fate of the whole Realm depends on you. Everything you do now can have fatal consequences!\\n\\nOr is it not so? After all, it is the year 1223 which has—besides the announced tax raise—brought a lot of unexpected events already.
